# Dialogue changes in 1.0.0

First release: every NPC line, narration and answer option rewritten shorter, base game and all three story DLCs.

**39,650 lines changed.** Each entry shows the text before this release (the original game text) and after, grouped by conversation.

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "After the ritual, an Astropath is assigned their position. At this or that Adeptus, an Astropathic relay, or a ship. More often than not, our first place of service is also our last."
  - After: "Then we're posted to an Adeptus, relay or ship. Usually for life."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That said, there are other options. Blasphemous, forbidden options." {n}The Choirmaster grimaces.{/n} "Unsanctioned psykers.   - After: "Or forbidden ones." {n}He grimaces.{/n} "Unsanctioned psykers, who rarely survive. With the warp this rabid, we may need them soon."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is a sacred compiler that helps us record, store, and, to an extent, unriddle messages.   - After: "A sacred compiler. It records our dictated visions and partly decodes them in its thesaurus core, a catalogue of symbols."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I suppose you have a better idea of that than I do. It is something I have never thought about before and on which I hardly have an opinion worth sharing, Lord Captain."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Weisz's face twists into a bitter grimace.{/n} "My duty is to shield you from the monstrous communications that filter through the warp.   - After: {n}Bitterly:{/n} "I shield you from the warp's horrors: dead men's screams, {g|Encyclopedia:WarpGlossary}Sea of Souls{/g} visions, cursed symbols, abominations hunting minds. Hiding that is my duty."

  - Before: {n}You feel a strange anxiety as the old man's burnt-out eyes seem to probe your inner self.{/n} "Your intentions are fairly easy for me to infer. You are looking for mutineers, and the only reason you would come to your Choirmaster is to order me to turn to the warp for answers."
  - After: {n}His eyes probe you.{/n} "You want me to find mutineers through the warp."

  - Before: "Your predecessor came to me with the same orders once. Nothing good came of it. Please believe me, Lord Captain, when I say a mountain of corpses was the least of the problems we faced that time."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Choirmaster makes a wry face, as though you have caught him doing something reprehensible.{/n} "Apologies, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It was... force of habit. I swear I will never again intrude upon your mind's peace without permission."
  - After: {n}Caught.{/n} "Apologies, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Habit. Never again."
- **Master Herimon**
  - Before: "And that is glorious, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! A thousand thanks to you for liberating me from my former master! Living at the court of Governor Iskandor is... indescribable.   - After: "Glorious, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Governor Iskandor's {g|Encyclopedia:WarpGlossary}Immaterium{/g}-fed perversions are behind me. My life is yours."

  - Before: "You saved me from a life of service that would have been a hundred times worse than the cruellest of deaths, and I am indebted to Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. If I have to lay down my life to repay that debt, then so be it."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is my wish to be useful to Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but what you have come for... will put the ship in peril. A ritual of this kind can — and certainly will — go the worst way possible."
  - After: "I wish to serve, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but this ritual will imperil the ship."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, do you know the proverb about staring too long into the abyss? What you are asking for is tantamount to plunging the entire Choir into that abyss. Human minds fusing into one another, vitrified organs inside still-living bodies, perverse fantasies manifesting in the flesh...   - After: "One careless thought and the warp sweeps the ship. Minds fusing, flesh twisting..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And even if I agreed... it would be impossible. I would need a second powerful telepath as a defender to shield my mind. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Choirmaster's face is twisted into a mask of horror, which quickly turns into a grimace of wholehearted anger.{/n} "This is a mistake, {name}. You have no idea what you are dooming us to! Dooming this ship! And your dynasty!"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Absolutely not!" {n}This is the first time you have ever heard the Choirmaster raise his voice.{/n} "She is a witch... an abomination! She will only make the situation worse! The beasts of the warp will sense her heresy-prone soul and descend upon us in droves."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You have signed our death sentence." {n}Weisz's anger almost seems to ignite his otherworldly gaze, making it burn right through you. However, his face does not stay contorted with fury for long. There is a distinct coldness to his voice as he says,{/n} "Well, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... Bring your witch here."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Why, the abyss will do so much more than stare at us today. We will be throwing stones into it and begging it to devour us." {n}The Choirmaster speaks the last few words with the bitter smirk of a condemned man who has just been told the day of his hanging.{/n}
  - After: "Today we beg the abyss to devour us." {n}A condemned man's smirk.{/n}
- **Idira**

  - After: "The great Choirmaster, scared of my whispers!" {n}Idira laughs.{/n} "Relax, old man. I'll protect you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Weisz frowns, clearly tormented by dark suspicions.{/n} "I am worried by all this reticence and omission, but... I will not presume to argue with Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The journey from Janus will take some time. I will report back when Lady Vyatt arrives."

  - Before: "He is right, {name}. I know some of the fundamentals, but this isn't my primary field."
  - After: "He's right, {name}. Not my field."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Weisz chews his lips, as though tasting your words.{/n} "I suppose you could, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. However, I would not dare put your safety at risk. What kind of a Choirmaster gets their own Lord Captain killed?"

- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "As you please. Master Herimon will welcome the news of his forthcoming release. His present lord is quite... unpleasant. I will report back once Master Herimon has been brought on board."
  - After: "As you please. Herimon will welcome it. I'll report once he's aboard."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, I do not for a moment doubt your powers, but I insist that you refrain from taking this unnecessary risk."
  - After: "Lord Captain, please avoid this needless risk."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "My little whispers are crazy excited at the mere possibility that your precious head will be the next one they get to drop by. You might want to think again if it's really what you want."
  - After: "My whispers would love your head next. Think again."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}The Interrogator looks at you with unabashed curiosity.{/n} "Considering the combat experience we've had together, {name}, I'm sure that if anyone is up to a challenge like that, it's you. On the other hand, is it really worth it to tempt the {g|Encyclopedia:ChaosGlossary}Archenemy{/g} when you don't have to?"
  - After: {n}Curious.{/n} "You could, {name}. But why tempt the {g|Encyclopedia:ChaosGlossary}Archenemy{/g}?"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "The Emperor would not send a gruelling challenge to one who was not up to it. Sometimes the thorniest path is also the most righteous one."
  - After: "The Emperor sends no trial one cannot bear. The thorny path is righteous."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Choirmaster's face grows gloomy. For a long time, he stares at the floor, saying nothing. Finally, he raises his head to look at you. His much-wrinkled face is relaxed. A reverent expression has come over it, and there is a hint of a smile on his lips.{/n} "So be it, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: {n}A long silence, then reverent calm.{/n} "So be it, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Master Herimon is a seasoned telepath, but his lord would never part with such an incredibly valuable specialist. A sizeable amount of money will be necessary to organise Master Herimon's... escape."
  - After: "Master Herimon, a telepath. His lord won't release him. His escape will cost plenty."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Choirmaster raises his eyebrows.{/n} "Lady Vyatt? The governor? As far as I know, she is not a psyker."
  - After: {n}Surprised.{/n} "Governor Vyatt? She's no psyker."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lady Vyatt has already begun to prepare for the ritual." {n}Weisz points to the dark red inscriptions in an unfamiliar language.{/n} "I sense a strange and distant power in these glyphs... An otherworldly, unholy might... And I pray to the Emperor that you know what you are doing."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Master Herimon, assigned to the chapel upon your orders for the purposes of performing the ritual, has almost finished his preparations, Lord Captain."
  - After: "Master Herimon is nearly ready, Lord Captain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Choirmaster lets out a deep sigh.{/n} "Well. You made this choice, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}A sigh.{/n} "Your choice, Lord Captain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Captain. Do you still wish to perform the ritual?"
  - After: "Lord Captain. Still want the ritual?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I managed to send out a call for help and did my best to contain the phantoms on my own before Lady Theodora arrived. I was the only survivor out of the entire Choir. Her Ladyship allowed me to spend a month in a secluded cell upon whose floor and walls I drew the most powerful protective hexagrams I knew. I was crushed. I was broken. And, worst of all, I was afraid. Afraid of meeting the same fate as Adeline and my other apprentices... An Astropath must never be afraid, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}.   - After: "I held the phantoms off until help came, the sole survivor. A month in a warded cell, broken and afraid. An Astropath must never fear, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

  - Before: "Oh yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, the Choirmaster has described the ritual to me in a wealth of detail. I might even say a slight excess of it." {n}Vistenza smiles coyly like a card-sharper at a gambling table.{/n} "I am familiar with certain techniques that could... curb the {g|Encyclopedia:WarpGlossary}Immaterium{/g}'s rapacious interest during the ritual."
  - After: "Oh yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, at length." {n}A card-sharp's smile.{/n} "I know ways to curb the {g|Encyclopedia:WarpGlossary}Immaterium{/g}'s interest."
- **Vistenza Vyatt**
  - Before: "Thank you for this opportunity to serve for your dynasty's benefit, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Vistenza bows before you with a radiant smile.{/n} "Your invitation was incredibly thrilling. I do not often get a chance to leave Janus."
  - After: "Thank you for this chance, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}She bows, beaming.{/n} "I rarely leave Janus."
- **Master Herimon**
  - Before: "Greetings, {name} von Valancius. I will be honoured to serve my saviour." {n}A middle-aged psyker bows to you passionately. His plump face carries many marks of indulging in all manner of vice.{/n}
  - After: "Greetings, {name} von Valancius, my saviour." {n}A vice-worn psyker bows.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lady Theodora bombarded the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratumGlossary}Adeptus Administratum{/g} for months with requests to provide her with a new Astropathic Choir.   - After: "Lady Theodora pressed the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratumGlossary}Adeptus Administratum{/g} for months. The new Choir must never learn the details."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That is the harsh truth, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It must not be done."
  - After: "It must not be done, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "I remember that day, Lord Captain. When we arrived at the chapel, there was blood and human remains everywhere. But that was the least of the terrifying things we saw there."
  - After: "I remember. Blood everywhere, and that was the least of it."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta makes the sign of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aquila}Aquila{/g}.{/n} "Protect the souls of the stricken and take them under Your wing, that Your faithful servants may find peace..."
  - After: {n}Argenta makes the {g|Encyclopedia:Aquila}Aquila{/g}.{/n} "Grant the stricken peace..."
- **Vistenza Vyatt**
  - Before: "Most certainly, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! The chartists who took me here were quite forthcoming and... attentive to my exacting tastes. But most importantly, they were fast, as I wouldn't dare keep you waiting for a second longer than necessary."
  - After: "Certainly, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! The chartists were attentive and fast."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Pity..." {n}The Choirmaster's shoulders go limp and his face resumes its usual sullen expression.{/n} "I was hoping that curious dispatch would distract you from the dangerous idea that brought you here, and I would not have to implore you to reconsider."
  - After: "Pity..." {n}He slumps.{/n} "I hoped that dispatch would distract you from your dangerous idea."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Choirmaster Weisz starts the conversation before you have opened your mouth to speak.{/n}
  - After: {n}Weisz speaks first.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It takes the entire Choir's power to invade such a prodigious number of minds at once. I weave their voices into a chord and steer it into the murky sea of other people's souls. Together, we read tens of thousands of thoughts, emotions, and intents, looking for the thing we are after. The seed of corruption you are interested in."
  - After: "I weave the whole Choir into one chord and search thousands of minds for the seed of corruption."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I—" {n}The Choirmaster cowers, as if cornered.{/n} "I did find it. But the price... The price! Yes, Lady Theodora got the names she wanted, but was it worth it?   - After: "I—" {n}He cowers.{/n} "I found it. Theodora got her names, but the ship nearly died for them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Weisz is silent for a few seconds, his face lowered toward the floor, his hands trembling.{/n} "You are right. I do not absolve myself of my own guilt. And may His punishment strike me if I forget about it for even a moment."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Please, Lord Captain, learn from her mistakes instead of committing your own."
  - After: "Please, learn from her mistakes."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And who is it?" {n}The Choirmaster's smile, though courteous, seems ever so slightly sarcastic.{/n}
  - After: "And who?" {n}A faintly sarcastic smile.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is not heresy, but it is indeed a dangerous tool that will only yield to a mighty hand. That time, things were going all too well. The Choir was many-voiced like never before. Adeline and my other talented apprentices sounded louder than the rest of Astropaths in all of the Expanse. We were strong and confident enough to take a bold gamble, and we lost."
  - After: "Not heresy, but dangerous. With Adeline, the Choir was at its strongest. We gambled, and lost."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Weisz frowns gloomily as he listens to Vistenza's equivocations punctuated by glowing smiles. Shadows of dark suspicions have fallen on his face, but he keeps a mournful silence.{/n}

- **Idira**
  - Before: "The Lord Captain helped me {d|Encyclopedia:CompIdira_DamperOn}overcome{/d} my curse, old man," {n}Idira says coldly through her teeth, and drums her fingers on her psy-stifler.{/n} "This thing here protects me from the warp, which means I can protect you as well... if you ask me nicely."
  - After: "The Captain helped me {d|Encyclopedia:CompIdira_DamperOn}overcome{/d} my curse, old man." {n}She taps her psy-stifler.{/n} "I can protect you, if you ask nicely."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "The Asuryani spend decades tempering their spirits before touching the veil. You lack the gift of time, yet you seek to harness powers that are only too pleased with your ignorance."
  - After: "Asuryani train for decades before touching the veil. You grasp at it ignorant."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Perhaps you have some {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}useful contacts{/d} at your disposal who could assist the unfortunate Herimon with his situation."
  - After: "Perhaps your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}useful contacts{/d} could help Herimon."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You summon your will and drive out the unpleasant sensation. The Choirmaster smiles sadly.{/n} "You shroud your mind well, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, and yet I can guess why you have come. With all due respect, I am asking you to reconsider."
  - After: {n}You force him out. He smiles sadly.{/n} "You shroud your mind well, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but I can guess. Please reconsider."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The lines on Weisz's brow disappear.{/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I realise that this ritual may be your only chance of finding the mutineers, but is their plot so threatening as to risk dooming the entire vessel? I do not think so."
  - After: {n}Relieved.{/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The mutineers aren't worth dooming the ship."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Weisz bows solemnly.{/n} "As you will, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. By your leave, I will return to my duties."
  - After: {n}He bows.{/n} "As you will, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Weisz freezes with his mouth agape, then grimaces in irritation.{/n} "I should not have said anything. I... dare not object to your will. However, I must remind you that performing the ritual is impossible without a psychic protector."
  - After: {n}He grimaces.{/n} "I won't object. But I need a psychic protector."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Blood begins to seep out of the corners of Idira's eyes.{/n} "The poison of the undiscovered mystery is eating away at the steel insides and the lifeblood that courses within them. Within kindred flesh lurks a strange mind, waiting for its prey to fall asleep. What is tomorrow worth, O child of Humanity? Rouse the slumbering trouble and find out, or else carry on in ignorance until you lose yourself." {n}As she regains her senses, Idira inhales sharply, then glances sideways at you:{/n} "Do think it over, Lord Captain. We're on the verge of letting the last thread slip from our hands. And if my little voices' whispers are anything to go by, without the ritual, things will get very bad."
  - After: {n}Idira's eyes bleed.{/n} "Poison eats the steel. In kindred flesh a strange mind waits." {n}She gasps.{/n} "Captain, without the ritual, it gets very bad."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix casts a tired and almost irritated glance at you.{/n} "There have been millions of people who neglected to remove a hidden threat — and were themselves removed from existence before their due time as a result. Do you value your dynasty? For that may well become the price of indolence and cowardice. Perform the ritual."
  - After: {n}Irritated.{/n} "Ignored threats erase dynasties. Perform the ritual."
- **Jae**
  - Before: {n}Jae's expression becomes unusually serious.{/n} "I'm not keen on toying with the powers of the warp either, shereen. But ignoring the raised dagger in an enemy's hand is an idea I like even less."
  - After: {n}Jae turns serious.{/n} "I don't like the warp, shereen. But I like ignoring a raised dagger less."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Internal strife and lurking enemies stole my home from me." {n}Despite her efforts to hide it, you notice a slight tremble in the Lady Navigator's voice.{/n} "If that ritual can uncover the threat, then we must act on it.   - After: "Hidden enemies stole my home." {n}Cassia's voice trembles.{/n} "Better some casualties than losing everything."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Domin, the Undying One's will has led us to Veni'Zacchary, and He bids us walk a path that is both narrow and bloody. If we stray from this path now, our mark will disappear forever..."
  - After: "Domin, the Undying One led us to Veni'Zacchary. Stray from His bloody path and our mark is lost..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That means we will have to cancel the ritual." {n}A faint hopeful smile appears on his lips.{/n}
  - After: "Then we cancel the ritual." {n}A hopeful smile.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That would be in order, considering all the dangers of the ritual."
  - After: "Wise, given the dangers."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/AstropathicChapel/DrumMalfunction/DrumMalfunction_dialogue

  - Before: "What is going on here?"

  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} prays in {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Techna-Lingua{/g}.{/n}

  - Before: {n}The Enginseer stares at you sullenly.{/n} "False. I record a three point eighty-four percent decrease in the mechanism's efficiency as a result of the Rogue Trader's manipulations. I also record several blasphemous violations of the Catechism of Maintenance and Operation."
  - After: {n}Sullen.{/n} "False. Efficiency down three point eighty-four percent. Catechism violated."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Unit Sigma-AR87 is currently in a tech-trance of shared comprehension with the spirit of the {g|Encyclopedia:ArcheotechGlossary}archeotech device{/g} catalogued under the name of 'Streamspindle.' Disturbing the unit is not recommended." {n}Pasqal falls silent for a few seconds.{/n} "However, a preliminary diagnostic has revealed several algorithmic faults that are in conflict with the sacred mechanism's processes. A practical intervention into certain cycles will likely aid the release of the accumulated burden."
  - After: "Sigma-AR87 is in tech-trance with the {g|Encyclopedia:ArcheotechGlossary}archeotech device{/g} 'Streamspindle.'" {n}Pause.{/n} "Fixing faulty cycles should help."
- **Sigma-AR87**
  - Before: "It will be done, Lord Captain. Initiating a ship-wide summons of locally available {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} units."
  - After: "It will be done. Summoning all {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} units aboard."
- **Astropath**
  - Before: "The esteemed Enginseer is in a state of tech-prayer trance and hasn't moved from the spot for a day now..." {n}He shrinks his head into his shoulders timidly.{/n} "I had the audacity to think the sacred compiler could be better helped by examining its parts... but who am I to question the secret knowledge of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g}?"
  - After: "He's prayed a full day..." {n}Timid.{/n} "I'd check the parts, but I can't question the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g}."
- **Sigma-AR87**
  - Before: {n}The Enginseer eyes you respectfully but with very sincere and poorly concealed confusion.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Enginseer looks confused.{/n}
- **Astropath**
  - Before: {n}His head bowed and his shoulders twitching, the {g|Encyclopedia:AstropathGlossary}Astropath{/g} cuts a sorrowful and anguished figure.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... the sacred mechanism, it..."
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:AstropathGlossary}Astropath{/g} looks anguished.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... the mechanism..."
- **Sigma-AR87**
  - Before: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} rises proudly to his feet and says in Low Gothic, a language he clearly has not had much practice in,{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} have rejected my pleas. The sacred mechanism will continue in its cycle of suffering."
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} rises.{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} rejected my pleas. It will keep suffering."
- **Astropath**
  - Before: "Forgive me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but I do not know the answer." {n}The Astropath lowers his voice to a whisper, glancing at the praying Enginseer.{/n} "I'm afraid even the Adeptus Mechanicus don't fully comprehend the workings of this mechanism. We're only knowledgeable on the surface-level machines: the receivers commit the messages to paper, the transcribers sort the mental imagery by semantic category and feed it into the thesaurus core, and then the sacred compiler supplements the messages with a list of symbols and their interpretations. However, the mechanism extends far deeper, into the bowels of the ship... Therefore I wouldn't even venture a guess at the possible source of this trouble."
  - After: "I don't know, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Whispering.{/n} "Even the Mechanicus barely understand it. It runs deep into the ship."
- **Astropath**
  - Before: {n}The Astropath is shaking. He bows to you hurriedly.{/n} "Thank you for your invaluable help, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I will make sure to tell Master Weisz that everything is working again!"
  - After: {n}He bows.{/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I'll tell Master Weisz!"
- **Astropath**
  - Before: {n}Horror twists the Astropath's face.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I implore you! I will work harder! I will pray more fervently!"
  - After: {n}Horror.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, please! I'll work harder!"
- **Sigma-AR87**
  - Before: {n}The Enginseer's facial augmentation emits a series of clicks.{/n} "Estimated likelihood of successful machine spirit placation by sacrificial means: greater than zero. It will be done, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}Clicking.{/n} "Sacrifice success likelihood: above zero. It will be done."
- **Astropath**
  - Before: {n}The young man exclaims in astonishment,{/n} "Imagine a single extra character creeping its way into the coordinates for a warp jump, and sending the flagship to the centre of a star! Imagine the word 'disloyal' becoming 'is loyal,' resulting in thousands of your faithful servants falling victim to treachery! Nothing is a trifle to an Astropath!"
  - After: {n}Aghast.{/n} "One wrong character could jump the flagship into a star! Nothing is a trifle to an Astropath!"
- **Astropath**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!" {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:AstropathGlossary}Astropath{/g} smiles at you — the shy, awkward smile of someone unused to smiling.{/n} "The sacred mechanism is working again with no disruptions!" {n}With a trembling hand, the psyker hands you a strip of paper with smooth rows of etched characters, this time containing no errors.{/n}
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!" {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:AstropathGlossary}Astropath{/g} smiles shyly.{/n} "It works!" {n}An error-free strip.{/n}
- **Sigma-AR87**
  - Before: "I recommend installing two incense-burning units in this compartment to prevent the spirit's continued anger. The unit Zacchary Weisz will be provided with a list of minor recommendations, one hundred and forty-two in total, for improvements to this compartment's maintenance. Failure to implement will result in sanctions on the part of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} priesthood."
  - After: "Install two incense-burners here. Zacchary Weisz gets one hundred and forty-two maintenance recommendations, or {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} sanctions."
- **Astropath**
  - Before: {n}The Astropath grows pale.{/n} "Apologies, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! It's a... regrettable necessity..."
  - After: {n}He pales.{/n} "Apologies, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! A regrettable necessity..."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/AstropathicChapel/HauntedMemories/HauntedMemories

- **Player**
  - Before: "Choirmaster Weisz, I order you to banish the warp spawn!"
  - After: "Weisz, banish the warp spawn!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Adeline is dead, and so are the rest of them. Live with your guilt. Do not let it consume you."
  - After: "Adeline's dead. Live with the guilt; don't let it consume you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What about the other voices? Were they your apprentices as well?"
  - After: "The other voices: your apprentices too?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Zacchary Weisz, I find you guilty and condemn you to death."
  - After: "Zacchary Weisz, I condemn you to death."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You do not deserve absolution. Your service will continue."
  - After: "No absolution. Your service continues."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will find your Adeline and bring her out into the light."
  - After: "I will find Adeline and bring her into the light."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If you got your freedom, why did you stay on the ship?"
  - After: "If you were freed, why stay aboard?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You must help me heal Kibellah, Weisz."
  - After: "Help me heal Kibellah, Weisz."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Touch Weisz's hand] "It's not her. You cannot wallow in your own guilt forever. There are people, out there and in here, who depend on you. Living people."
  - After: [Touch Weisz's hand] "It's not her. Living people need you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Choirmaster? What is going on?"
  - After: "Choirmaster? What's happening?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You have already condemned yourself to years of torment. I cannot give you a new punishment — only forgiveness. And you must forgive yourself."
  - After: "I can't punish you more, only forgive. Forgive yourself."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You have not allowed the warp to break you, and I believe the Emperor's light is strong in your soul. Continue your service, for Humanity needs you, and in duty you will find redemption."
  - After: "The Emperor's light is strong in you. Keep serving; duty brings redemption."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your ambition was worth the risk, you were simply unlucky with your students. The weak are destined to be stepping stones for others on the path to knowledge — accept this sacrifice and live without regret."
  - After: "Your ambition was worth it; the weak are stepping stones. Live without regret."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Astropath, remember the golden radiance of Holy Terra. Remember your own oaths. He wants you to be steadfast."
  - After: "Remember Holy Terra and your oaths. Be steadfast."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Execute Weisz] "I am sorry, Weisz. You have left me no choice."
  - After: [Execute Weisz] "Sorry, Weisz. You leave me no choice."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}An unpleasant heaviness grows in your head, as if a vice were slowly tightening its grip on your mind. The Choirmaster is kneeling, his burnt-out eyes peering into the void. He raises his head, and you see a weary old man, weak and frightened. He whispers,{/n} "She is here. Adeline has returned. She is asking me for help. But you... You scare her. She is hiding from you. You will not harm her, will you?"
  - After: {n}A vice grips your mind. Weisz kneels, frail.{/n} "Adeline has returned. She fears you. You won't harm her?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Weisz's breathing is laboured.{/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The burden was too heavy for me to bear." {n}On the verge of fainting, he musters the last of his strength to sit down on the steps.{/n}
  - After: {n}Gasping.{/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It was too heavy." {n}He sits.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}From every direction, every shadow, comes playful girlish laughter. At times it transforms into an old man's rueful weeping; at other times, into a deep growl of annoyance. The sounds form cold, malicious words:{/n} "The sorrow will be eternal."
  - After: {n}The shadows laugh and weep:{/n} "The sorrow will be eternal."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The mocking laughter of an old man turns into a moaning whisper:{/n} "I am the victims. I am the murdered innocents. I am his guilt!"
  - After: {n}A whisper:{/n} "I am the murdered innocents. His guilt!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The rest were my voices. Antonius was the youngest. He had been in the Choir for only a short while. When the situation turned dire, fear got the best of him, and I... was infuriated by his weakness. I dominated Antonius's mind and impelled him to use up every spark of his life force for the ritual. Annis's doom came even earlier. She was the one person who told me, in front of the Choir, that the ritual was madness. In my anger, I ordered her {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitorised{/g}. I believed I had to protect my authority. She died on the spot where you're standing now. I think she was still aware..." {n}More scarlet drops seep through the Choirmaster's red-stained blindfold.{/n} "All my voices... I remember the name of each one whose life I cut short within these walls."
  - After: "Young Antonius panicked; I seized his mind and burned out his life for the ritual. Annis called it madness, so I had her {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitorised{/g}. She died where you stand." {n}His blindfold bleeds.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That is for the best. I can no longer carry this burden alone. With Lady Theodora dead, the thought of my crime being forgotten, erased from history, is unbearable! I want to be judged and condemned!"
  - After: "Good. With Theodora dead, my crime mustn't be forgotten. Condemn me!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Not all of them. Stavros was the oldest in the Choir — he had been on the ship even longer than I. Mighty, wise man, if acrimonious. He envied me and criticised my ambition, but I was fond of him all the same. Thaddeus was the ship's confessor. Theodora had insisted on his presence. When it was over, he was the only other survivor, and he confronted me with angry accusations. I could not bear to listen to him, so... I silenced him. Killed him."
  - After: "Not all. Stavros, the eldest, envied me; I liked him anyway. Thaddeus, the confessor, survived and accused me. So I killed him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Tears of blood are streaming down the Choirmaster's face, dissolving what was left of the inscriptions on his time-worn blindfold. {/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: {n}He weeps blood.{/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Choirmaster lifts up his blood-smeared face toward you. He says faintly,{/n} "You are cruel. But I bow to Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s will."
  - After: {n}Faintly:{/n} "You are cruel. But I bow to Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s will."
- **Zacchary Weisz**
  - Before: {n}Weisz's expression is a mixture of pain, horror, and grief. He lowers his arms slowly.{/n} "I... know, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I know this is not Adeline, but an echo of the one who devoured her soul. I just wanted to see her again, hear her voice again for a brief moment." {n}With jerky movements, as though shaking off shackles of ice, he picks up his staff.{/n} "Ghost of my failure, now is your time to vanish."
  - After: {n}Weisz lowers his arms.{/n} "I know, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It's an echo of what devoured her. I just wanted to hear her." {n}He raises his staff.{/n} "Vanish."
- **Zacchary Weisz**
  - Before: "She is no warp spawn!" {n}Weisz howls in desperation.{/n} "She is my apprentice!"
  - After: "She's no warp spawn!" {n}A howl.{/n} "She's my apprentice!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The shadows croak hoarsely in an old man's voice,{/n} "Why do you seek his redemption? He was always a terrible leader and talentless mentor! He doomed everyone!" {n}The indignant tremble grows into a roar of righteous condemnation:{/n} "He was arrogant! Having no notion of his own wretchedness, he did not put his faith in the Emperor, but instead believed himself to be invincible!" {n}The voice grows weaker. It is now a young man's, soft and full of anguish:{/n} "And he paid for his mistake with our lives... It was cruel and painful."
  - After: {n}Croaking:{/n} "Why redeem him? A terrible mentor!" {n}Roaring:{/n} "Arrogant, faithless!" {n}Anguished:{/n} "We paid with our lives."
- **Zacchary Weisz**
  - Before: "I see her with my own sight, unknown to ordinary people. She is as alive to me as you are, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "To my sight she's as alive as you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Zacchary Weisz**
  - Before: "Light? There is no light here, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, not anymore. Only shadows of the past."
  - After: "No light here, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Only shadows."
- **Adeline**
  - Before: {n}The ghost stares at Weisz mournfully. The muffled sob coming from the apparition almost seems to take physical form as it drifts toward the Choirmaster and envelops him.{/n}
  - After: {n}The ghost sobs over Weisz.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Sevitia was an ordinary servant. She fought the Immaterium's monsters until the warp began to prevail. She tried to save me, to lead me away, but I did not listen. She stayed at my side until the last moment and died a terrible death... all because of my accursed pride."
  - After: "Sevitia, a servant, begged me to flee. I refused; she stayed and died, for my pride."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Choirmaster's mind fades swiftly and eagerly, weary from suffering, and the otherworldly horror lurking in the shadows dissipates. No longer do the daemons who haunted Zacchary Weisz reign supreme in this chapel.{/n}
  - After: {n}Weisz's mind fades; the chapel's daemons dissipate.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The voice grows heavy with a metallic clang:{/n} "We begged him to reconsider, but he took our minds away as punishment." {n}The shadows' speech is now gentler and more feminine:{/n} "But we were loyal to him regardless. We tried to save him even though he had not saved us..." {n}The voice becomes cold, resonating with sorrow from beyond this world:{/n} "He is guilty."
  - After: {n}Metallic:{/n} "He took our minds." {n}Gentle:{/n} "We still tried saving him." {n}Cold:{/n} "He is guilty."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am guilty. I wronged them. I had been promised a great future at the Scholastica Psykana, for my talents were exceptional. But fate would not have it, and instead of serving on {g|Encyclopedia:HolyTerraGlossary}Holy Terra{/g}, I ended up here in the Expanse, where barely a gleam of the {g|Encyclopedia:AstronomicanGlossary}Astronomican{/g} reaches. My pride took a heavy blow, but my spirit was not cowed. I set about to assemble a Choir unlike any yet seen here. A mighty, resonant, astounding Choir. Lady Theodora expended tremendous resources bartering with captains and governors to procure Astropaths of my choosing. I brought together talents and budding geniuses under my authority. They were to ensure I would make a triumphant comeback."
  - After: "I am guilty. Denied {g|Encyclopedia:HolyTerraGlossary}Holy Terra{/g}, I was sent to the Expanse, far from the {g|Encyclopedia:AstronomicanGlossary}Astronomican{/g}. So Lady Theodora bought me gifted Astropaths, a Choir to win my comeback."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A reckoning, Lord Captain. A reckoning for my great arrogance. Daemons have been pursuing me for years, following my scent, sending me dire messages, hunting me... And now they have me. The entities that manifested here during the ritual were banished, but a lingering echo of their presence has latched onto the shadows. It has sprouted in the darkness and pounced upon my mind."
  - After: "A reckoning for my arrogance. Daemons hunted me for years. The ritual's echo lingers in the shadows and has seized my mind."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "At first, Lady Theodora wanted to have me executed for what had happened, but then she regained her composure and graciously agreed to honour our deal. But... where was I to go? My dead were all here."
  - After: "Theodora spared me and honoured our deal. But my dead are here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After a long silence, he says in a hollow voice,{/n} "In a bodily sense, yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: {n}Hollowly:{/n} "Bodily, yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Weisz merely covers his ears with his hands.{/n} "Please... I am guilty... Adeline!" {n}The Choirmaster is unlikely to be of any help in this state.{/n}
  - After: {n}He covers his ears.{/n} "Adeline!" {n}He's no help now.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After a moment's hesitation, the old man holds out his staff to you.{/n} "Please take it. This mighty instrument is the last reminder of Adeline and the others, of my guilt. It was with this that I performed the last ritual. I have no right to carry it any longer and would like it to be yours. A reminder of the painful lesson my pride has taught me."
  - After: {n}He offers his staff.{/n} "Take it. I performed the last ritual with it. Let it remind you what my pride cost."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Choirmaster raises his grief-stricken face. The droplets of blood trickling from under the bandage land on the deck with a ringing sound.{/n} "Your words... are medicine for my soul, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: {n}He bleeds.{/n} "Your words heal me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Choirmaster grips the Aquila on his belt so tightly that the gold wings draw blood from his fist.{/n} "You... are right, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Wishing to abandon my post is cowardice and an offence against Him."
  - After: {n}He grips his Aquila, bleeding.{/n} "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Deserting is cowardice."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Choirmaster falls silent for a moment, trying to make sense of your words.{/n} "It is true. They are dead, and to follow them would be to undo all I have achieved. Thank you for believing in me. I will not fail Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} again."
  - After: {n}He ponders.{/n} "True. Following them undoes everything. I won't fail Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} again."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Adeline? She is there, in the shadows..." {n}A tortured sigh escapes his feeble body.{/n} "Many shadows lie. The true ghosts are hiding among the false ones. But I hear... I hear! I hear Thaddeus's earnest prayer and old Stavros's words of disappointment — he always doubted my talents as a mentor."
  - After: "Adeline? In the shadows..." {n}A sigh.{/n} "Many shadows lie. I hear Thaddeus praying, and Stavros doubting me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Weisz mutters incoherently, consumed by his frightful reverie.{/n}
  - After: {n}Weisz mutters.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I hear poor Antonius's scream... the scream he let out when he unwillingly gave up the last of his vitality. Annis's pleas — I condemned her to an existence as a half-machine. I can even... I almost sense Sevitia's touch. She tried to save me, but she fell instead. So many voices, all condemning me for what I did! Find them... Separate the true voices from the false echoes!"
  - After: "Antonius screaming, Annis pleading, Sevitia, who fell saving me. All condemn me! Separate the true voices from the false echoes!"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta's scornful laughter cuts through the sinister whispers.{/n} "Sorrow? To perceive corruption is a triumph, for once you perceive it, you can eradicate it! Cower, blasphemous spawn! I hear your voices, and I follow the trail!"
  - After: {n}Argenta scoffs.{/n} "Corruption perceived is corruption eradicated! I'm on your trail, spawn!"
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai hisses, glancing at the shadows anxiously.{/n} "I can almost feel the claws of She Who Thirsts clamping around our souls! The sooner we leave this place, the better. Have your servants void this compartment once we are gone."
  - After: {n}Marazhai hisses.{/n} "She Who Thirsts is near! Leave, then void this compartment."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "The whispers keep saying we should kill old Weisz. They're just so giddy about it... I guess we shouldn't kill him, then? The whispers never get excited about anything good."
  - After: "The whispers are giddy to kill Weisz. So we shouldn't?"
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "His is such a terribly wounded soul... It has all but sunk beneath the grey-blue blisters of guilt, and they are swelling ever so rapidly. The last silvery speck of hope could fade at any moment."
  - After: "Guilt is drowning his soul. Its last hope could fade any moment."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And they could do that for me, that team of brilliant Astropaths whose talents were honed to perfection. Adeline, Annis, Antonius... Every one of them surpassed myself as I used to be. I saw that my time was coming, and... I lied when I told you it was Lady Theodora who had forced us to go through with the ritual. The idea had been mine. When, in her paranoia, Her Ladyship set out to find spies aboard the ship, I made her an offer. A ritual that would give her the names, in exchange for my fledglings' freedom and my own. It was... a good deal. She was willing to trade seven Astropaths for the names of traitors. And I doomed them all. My pride killed them."
  - After: "My Astropaths, Adeline, Annis, Antonius, surpassed me. And I lied: the ritual was my idea. To name Theodora's spies, in exchange for our freedom. She traded seven Astropaths for it. My pride killed them all."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He chuckles bitterly, and scarlet stains bloom on his blindfold made of sacred manuscripts.{/n} "Adeline was my ritual protector, only to become my greatest vulnerability. When the mad stream of other people's thoughts started to disorient my Astropaths, I became frightened for her. I hesitated, I wanted to spare her... and I lost control. The right thing to do would have been to sacrifice her, but... I couldn't. I had always had a soft spot for her. Her genius had made her my favourite."
  - After: {n}A bitter laugh.{/n} "Adeline, my favourite, guarded the ritual. When it overwhelmed us, I should have sacrificed her. I hesitated, and lost control."
- **Zacchary Weisz**
  - Before: {n}Weisz blocks your path, extending his arms in a gesture that both calls for restraint and pleads for mercy.{/n} "Do not harm her! Please! The poor girl is frightened to death! Let me talk to her! I cannot fail her again!"
  - After: {n}Weisz blocks you.{/n} "Don't harm her! Let me talk to her! I can't fail her again!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Weisz says nothing. His otherworldly gaze is directed through you and past you, to a spot further inside the chapel. His lips silently whisper a name over and over.{/n}
  - After: {n}Weisz silently whispers a name.{/n}

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/AstropathicChapel/TelepathicSearch_Beggining/TelepathicSearch_Beggining_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Balanced on the brink, your gaze falters and slides down into the depths. Billions of pitch-dark non-minds stare back at you. A shapeless mass of wrongness. Purple worms of aberration encased in carapaces of otherness.{/n}

  - Before: "No, this is not my ritual!" {n}Panic rings in the Choirmaster's voice inside your mind.{/n} "This is his spell! An invasion of our minds! While I was seeking it with my power, it found us with its own! And I... cannot stop it! I cannot force it out of our heads!"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A blind man clad in green appears between you and the croaking Nothingness, shielding you.{/n} "What manner of abomination are you? I cannot sense you. You are not of the warp. What is your twisted nature?"

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/Bridge/AccidentEmergencyMeeting/AccidentEmergencyMeeting_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I wish to know what disaster has befallen us."
  - After: "What disaster has befallen us?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Was this an accident or was it sabotage?"
  - After: "Accident or sabotage?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "We must come up with a plan of action."
  - After: "We need a plan."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Save the vessel. The enforcers must quell the riots and ensure that the work is done."
  - After: "Save the vessel. Enforcers, quell the riots."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Rescue the crew members from the damaged compartments. Either we all survive or we all perish."
  - After: "Rescue the trapped crew. We all survive or perish."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Seal the bay doors and mine the shuttles. Let them know that I mean to leave them no choice but to carry out their duty in the Emperor's name."

- **Player**
  - Before: "Let them go. I will stay here with those who still believe in our success."
  - After: "Let them go. I stay with those who believe."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell them they have my permission. Gather them all in one compartment, then seal it and vent it into the void. I have no need for cowardly refuse."
  - After: "Let them. Gather them in one compartment, then vent it. No cowardly refuse."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do hope it is obvious to everyone that my treasures, trophies, and relics are to be rescued first! Everything else comes second!"
  - After: "My treasures, trophies and relics are rescued first!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Assume command] "We will begin with emergency countermeasures. Here are your orders!"
  - After: [Assume command] "Emergency countermeasures. Here are your orders!"

Only the Master Helmsman looks curiously unperturbed — Ravor's ever-scowling face clearly cannot hold any more grim dissatisfaction.{/n} "I'm glad you've made it here in one piece, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: {n}Turmoil on the bridge. Only Ravor seems unperturbed.{/n} "Glad you made it, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "While we do not know this for certain, I am convinced that we have been attacked from within. We are now more vulnerable than ever."
  - After: "I'm convinced we were attacked from within."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your {g|Encyclopedia:CommBead}comm-bead{/g} springs to life.{/n} "Infernus Master speaking. There have been several large explosions throughout the ship.   - Before: {n}Her voice is followed by a hiss from the vox-caster:{/n} "It might have been a chain reaction caused by an accidental failure. The ship is old — that sort of thing can happen. But I commend Mistress Sauerback's vigilance. It is appropriate at this hour."
  - After: {n}The vox hisses:{/n} "Maybe an accidental chain reaction; the ship is old. Still, vigilance is wise."
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**

Sadly, the optimal survival strategy for the vessel does not include the survival of those poor sods."
  - After: "Repairs are ranked, but riots slow us. Saving the ship means losing those trapped."
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**

- **Master Helmsman Ravor**

  - After: "We'll stay and report readings. We have void suits."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}She barks orders into the vox and is answered immediately by a staccato of gunfire. After a while, she nods in satisfaction.{/n} "The crowd has been pacified, Lord Captain. A clear demonstration of our resolve and a few public executions have tempered their fervour."
  - After: {n}Orders, then gunfire.{/n} "Crowd pacified, Lord Captain. A few executions helped."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}Having given the order, Sauerback listens in to the vox with a furtive smile, then nods contentedly.{/n} "The compartment has been vented. The vessel has been purged of the spineless wretches."
  - After: {n}Sauerback smiles furtively.{/n} "Vented. The spineless wretches are purged."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}Sauerback grits her teeth and hisses into the vox,{/n} "Let them through... Remove the cordon... Provide enough oxygen, water, and rations... for eight watches. And nothing else for those traitors!"
  - After: {n}Sauerback hisses into the vox,{/n} "Let them through... Supplies for eight watches. Nothing else for traitors!"
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}The Master-at-Arms glares furiously at the vox-caster.{/n} "The enforcers... will do their duty. Aid will arrive shortly."
  - After: {n}She glares at the vox.{/n} "The enforcers... will help."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}Sauerback's personal vox bursts into life. Her face contorts with rage as she listens to the report.{/n} "There's been an incident on the flight deck. A mob of voidsmen and labourers, despicable cowards all, are trying to break through to the shuttles! The enforcers are holding them back for now, but the cordon is in danger of being overrun."
  - After: {n}Sauerback's vox bursts in; she seethes.{/n} "A mob is storming the flight deck shuttles! The cordon may break."
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**
  - Before: "Right now, we are a blind, unpowered, defenceless, sinking spittoon drifting through the abyss. The total volume of outages was nearly enough to turn us into an adamantine casket."
  - After: "We're a blind, powerless, sinking spittoon. Nearly a casket."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "The crew has suffered heavy casualties due to explosive depressurisation, loss of air supply to the compartments, multiple fires, and failures in the transportation systems. The numbers are getting worse by the minute."
  - After: "Heavy crew casualties, and rising by the minute."

  - Before: {n}During your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Navy}time in the Navy{/d}, you have encountered more than a few critical failures. As a result, you know exactly how to redistribute the system power to help you buy whatever time and resources might be needed to address priority issues. Your plan succeeds, and the ship now stands a better chance of not collapsing into a pile of scrap within the next few hours. You can tell from the officers' voices that they are very glad to be under the command of someone who knows what they are doing.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Navy}time in the Navy{/d} taught you to reroute power in a crisis. It works; the ship holds, and the officers are relieved.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A moment's silence fills the bridge. Finally, a cautious response comes from the vox-caster:{/n} "Copy that, Lord Captain. Every effort will be made to save your treasures and preserve the cultural heritage of the dynasty."
  - After: {n}Silence. Then the vox:{/n} "Copy, Lord Captain. Your treasures will be saved."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "At the time of the accident, Danrok was on the freight line inspecting warehouses. He has not been in contact since. We are assuming... the worst."
  - After: "Danrok was inspecting freight warehouses. No contact since. We fear the worst."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}Sauerback grabs the vox-caster and snarls,{/n} "All enforcers are to don full gear, spread out among the compartments, and maintain discipline at all costs. If anyone dares to distract the Infernus Guild from their emergency work, shoot them. Record this order, hand it to the servo-skulls, and distribute it across the decks. Now."
  - After: {n}Sauerback snarls into the vox,{/n} "Enforcers, full gear, keep order. Shoot anyone hindering the Infernus Guild."

  - Before: {n}A new burst of hisses emanates from the vox-caster:{/n} "Jocasta, we are running short on brave men. We would be grateful if your people would lay down their weapons and come to assist the Infernus Guild. The sooner you come, the more lives we can save."
  - After: {n}The vox hisses:{/n} "Jocasta, we need hands. Send your people to help the Infernus Guild."

The honourable Vox and Infernus Masters have departed for the affected compartments to take charge of their subordinates, but remain present on the vox-line."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/Bridge/ChirurgeonMajoris/ChirurgeonMajoris_dialogue

  - After: "You earn your keep, at least."

  - Before: {n}He nods, brushing away invisible specks from his white gloves.{/n}
  - After: {n}He nods, brushing his gloves.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I hope I have satisfied your curiosity."

  - After: "I don't confess, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I serve the Emperor with work, not words."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Naturally, House Chorda still has need of people like me — educated and capable of intellectual thought. However, anyone who is permitted to learn does so under strict supervision.   - After: "Chorda still needs the learned, but watches them. Lady Incendia's sages live in a prison of a librarium."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My job is to save lives. Heal wounded officers, develop vaccines for onboard epidemics, discover new methods of healing. However...   - After: "I should be finding cures. Instead I hear complaints and decide who matters. Irritating."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Forius takes one look at your hand and immediately produces a syringe from the folds of his robe.{/n} "Ordinary vesticula scarabis, or 'void leprosy,' in common terms. Still in the early stages. One injection will suffice."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I would not have become a chirurgeon if I was afraid of death. It is an unavoidable side effect of my profession."
  - After: "A chirurgeon can't fear death. It comes with the job."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He shrugs indifferently.{/n} "A straightforward case."
  - After: {n}He shrugs.{/n} "A straightforward case."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}His colourless eyes flash indignantly.{/n} "My expertise is the result of hard work and accumulated wisdom, not some paltry sorcery! I employ my craft to save His children. That should serve as a better proof of my innocence than any show of piety."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "'You teach a man to read, you raise a bright heretic,' I believe was one of the favourite local sayings. As for demonstrating the superiority of knowledge over the advice of holy ecclesiarchs, well... that kind of defiance was sure to put my life at risk."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Are you interested in a general report on the ship as a whole or in hearing about how your immediate subordinates are faring?"
  - After: "A report on the ship, or your officers?"

- **Player**

  - Before: "I wish I could have finished him off with my own hands."

  - Before: {n}The Master-at-Arms stands at attention, ignoring the wounds and burns covering her face and body.{/n} "Lord Captain, the vessel has been secured. - **Jocasta Sauerback**

  - After: "He's cornered in Bay 45-F-1. We'll get him."
- **Einrich Monteg**

- **Einrich Monteg**

It's a pity I couldn't share the blessing of purity with you and make you part of our family. A pity, too, that we couldn't kill you either. But we all must play the cards we are dealt. And now we take our leave the way the true masters of fire should."
  - After: {n}Gunfire nears.{/n} "Goodbye, {name}. Pity we couldn't convert or kill you. We leave as masters of fire."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "And then what? Will you spare us?"
  - After: "Then what? Will you spare us?"
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: {n}Einrich winces angrily.{/n} "We all felt every single moment of the blessed angel's agony. And then he died, and our dream died with him. You snuffed it out and stomped on it like a lho-stick butt. Now, his song will not return to our dreams. The Many-Armed Emperor will not see us."
  - After: {n}Einrich winces.{/n} "We felt his agony. Our dream died with him."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: {n}A tear rolls down his cheek, leaving a damp trail through the soot covering his face. Yet his voice remains steady:{/n} "Was that really necessary? Did Nemi and Mia have to die?"
  - After: {n}A tear streaks the soot on his face.{/n} "Did Nemi and Mia have to die?"
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: {n}The lho-stick in his fingers is shaking.{/n} "Of course not. Why would they?"
  - After: {n}His lho-stick shakes.{/n} "Of course not."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "He has been here a long time — longer than you or anyone else. His blessed feet crossed these decks centuries ago, when Theodora's predecessor still called himself Lord Captain. He came from the stars where the Many-Armed Emperor dwells to bear His word, but then he faced a great massacre at the hands of the wicked."
  - After: "He's walked these decks for centuries. He came from the Many-Armed Emperor's stars, but the wicked massacred his kind."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "You can always count on veterans. I will present the old man with an award. Throne knows he has earned it, and then some."
  - After: "I'll give the old veteran an award."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "A brave heretic is no better than a craven one. And that is what he was: a heretic and an abomination."
  - After: "Brave or not, a heretic."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "I wish you could too, Lord Captain."
  - After: "So do I, Lord Captain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Her servo-skull rattles to life and projects a hologram onto the deck. A blurred replica of Einrich Monteg stares at you, blood oozing from a wound on his temple.   - After: {n}A servo-skull projects a bleeding Einrich Monteg.{/n} "Bridge, copy? Celebrating, {name}?"
- **Jocasta Sauerback**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The renegades stormed the bridge and then brought that thing in. We held our ground, but as soon as the monster looked at us, my mind went blank. It was like being a puppet. Damn those xenos tricks!"

- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "In that case, we will die together as a family."
  - After: "Then we die together, as a family."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "I'm also a liar and a manipulator. All of this is true, but it no longer matters."
  - After: "And a liar. No matter now."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "Will you grant me mercy, {name}? I doubt it."
  - After: "Will you grant mercy, {name}? I doubt it."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "Your arrogance never fails to amuse. Yes, I underestimated you, as well as your retinue, those bloody zealots, and that sadist Jocasta. Who would have expected such fierce resistance from a bunch of false believers?"
  - After: "Yes, I underestimated you, your zealots and Jocasta."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: {n}The Infernus Master appears serious, sombre. The usual cheerful insolence has vanished from his face.{/n} "I wanted you to see my face before I die. Commit it to memory. One day, you will realise what sacrilege you have committed, and in that moment, you will remember me."
  - After: {n}Einrich is grim.{/n} "Remember my face when you see your sacrilege."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "No, I know I'm a dead man walking. But there are unarmed people here with me: our families, who have neither the desire nor the ability to fight. Our children, our elderly. People like my sister and niece. Do you want their blood on your hands as well? Will you take revenge on them, too, or is my life enough?"
  - After: "I'm dead anyway. But our unarmed families are here: children, elders, my sister and niece. Is my blood enough?"
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "And yet the venerable Sire kept His message safe and took refuge on this vessel, away from the persecution of heretics. When that false Lord Captain let our ancestors on board, the Sire heard their pain and answered their pleas, blessing them with genetic purity. He protected us after that, joining our thoughts together into a single song. He was the true Lord Captain of this ship."
  - After: "The Sire hid aboard. He blessed our ancestors with purity and joined our thoughts in one song. He was the true Lord Captain."

  - Before: "Do not even think about showing mercy to a single offshoot of this menace, {name}." {n}Heinrix's voice rings with cold fury.{/n}
  - After: "No mercy for this menace, {name}." {n}Heinrix is icy.{/n}

  - Before: "You addled, pathetic ashmag..." {n}Jae shakes her head.{/n} "Just do yourself a favour and give up the ghost, Einrich..."
  - After: "Pathetic ashmag..." {n}Jae shakes her head.{/n} "Give up, Einrich."

  - After: {n}Argenta is sombre.{/n} "Death freed them from that beast."

  - Before: "First you consign your family to the clutches of unspeakable heresy, and now you weep for their deaths?" {n}The Seneschal's voice rings with icy castigation.{/n} "I see that any further dialogue with you would be pointless, Monteg."

  - Before: "Does this primitive piece of technology give you a good view of your precious monster's corpse?" {n}Marazhai smiles with satisfaction upon seeing the pain in Einrich's face.{/n}
  - After: "Enjoying the view of your monster's corpse?" {n}Marazhai smiles.{/n}
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Remember you, kraken spawn? You are a brazen one!" {n}Ulfar bursts into laughter.{/n} "I will compose a fine verse about this day — about the bloody battle and the victory over your abominable master. But you, spouter of lies and betrayer of Humankind — there won't be a single line about you."
  - After: {n}Ulfar laughs.{/n} "I'll sing of this victory, but not of you, traitor."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "You don't know when to stop, do you, {name}? Fine, I'll tell you. We were close to our goal — a few more years, a few more pure converts to the true faith... But the spinners pulled that stunt with the bath and you seized on their tip-off right away. When it came to the telepathic ritual, it became clear that you weren't going to leave us alone and that we'd have to start the harvest season early."
  - After: "Fine, {name}. We were close. Then the spinners' bath stunt tipped you off, and after the ritual we had to harvest early."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "Our old Magus appeared to you during the rite and led you on a false trail. He lulled you into a false sense of security by throwing a small portion of our forces to the wolves and sacrificing himself to buy time to prepare for the harvest. We orchestrated the elevator accident, but you survived, and then I almost intercepted you there on the freight line, but the Bloodspun Web interfered again. You could have been part of us — part of something great, something real. But you ruined everything. Everything."
  - After: "Our Magus misled you and died to buy time. We rigged the elevator; I nearly had you on the freight line, but the Bloodspun Web interfered. You ruined everything."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}While talking to Ravor, you do not immediately notice the familiar otherworldly flicker — Trazyn is examining the fallen Patriarch with moderate interest.{/n} "I have a similar one in my collection, only larger and of a different phenotype. His brood was trying to clear out one of the sleeping tombs... and since I just happened to be there for the purpose of expropriating historical treasures, I thought the moment was worth preserving."
  - After: {n}Trazyn appears, studying the Patriarch.{/n} "I have a larger one in my collection."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "I am pure. My mother and father both trace their lineage back to the ones who received the gift of genetic perfection from the Sire himself. Had there been a few more generations between us, I would have resembled the Sire more closely, but... each of us has their own calling. I look almost like a false believer..." {n}Einrich lifts the welding goggles from his forehead, exposing the rudiments of a purple crest.{/n} "...which means that I was destined to be a spy among you."
  - After: "Pure, from the Sire's first blessed. I look almost human..." {n}He lifts his goggles: a purple crest.{/n} "...so I was your spy."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "The finger of truth has three sorrowful phalanges. One is shattered, but..." {n}The Infernus Master smiles widely, pulls a remote control from his pocket, and pushes a button. There is a sharp beeping of detonators, a monstrous roar, and the projection disappears. For a while, the sound of flames crackles from the speaker before abruptly cutting off.{/n}
  - After: "The finger of truth has three sorrowful phalanges. One is shattered, but..." {n}He grins and detonates. Then silence.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}Sauerback mutters something into the comm-bead, then hisses angrily:{/n} "Thermal charges. The void rat blew up the compartment, along with himself and the entire assault team."
  - After: {n}Sauerback hisses:{/n} "He blew himself up with the assault team."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "No, we will merely fade away. The Sire is dead and his pureblood offspring have been butchered. They alone, our pristine kin, could bestow the kiss that allowed his song to be heard. The orphans and widows are of no threat to anyone. Drop them off in any remote wilderness."
  - After: "We'll fade. The purebloods are dead. Widows and orphans threaten no one; leave them somewhere wild."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}Sauerback grimaces.{/n} "He was always a self-important bastard and a sycophant, but he honoured the Creed. Even he did not deserve to become one of those creatures."
  - After: {n}Sauerback grimaces.{/n} "A sycophant, but faithful. He didn't deserve that."

  - Before: "Not in the usual way. My ancestors wronged yours and were appointed inferni as a result. Hard labour, deadly risks, plenty of opportunities to atone. Those criminals have been dead for generations, but we are still serving their time. Maybe we will find redemption one day."

- **(conversation owner)**

  - Before: "I hear that you too have had to deal with {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}injustice{/d} and badmouthing in your time. I hope people will stop judging you for your past mistakes in less than a couple of centuries." {n}Einrich gives you a sympathetic smile.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Life has been tough for those two. I take care of them as best I can, but at that moment, I was powerless. There is only one other time I ever felt so helpless. Thank you for standing up for them. I will never forget this. Ever since Elsie died, they are all I have left."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Of course, the job description doesn't allow me to risk my life now." {n}He smiles sadly.{/n} "It is all about management these days, sending the boys and girls into the fire. But it's all nonsense, and if the going gets tough, I won't leave them there alone."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Elsinora, my wife. She died saving the ammo depot, back in Lady Theodora's time." {n}The smoke from the lho-stick mercifully obscures Einrich, hiding the traces of emotion on his face.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Infernus Service is split into different brigades according to duties.   - After: "Liquidators fight fires and rescue people; repairmen fix doors, leaks, vents; inspectors keep passages clear."

  - Before: {n}Jocasta Sauerback is the very picture of discipline. Her uniform is exquisitely pressed, her armour is polished, and her posture is imposing and rigid.   - After: "Certainly. He trusted others. I trust only you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am responsible for upholding safety and order aboard the ship. Guard duties, patrols, finding and punishing troublemakers...   - After: "Order: patrols, guards, punishment. Disobedience today is riot tomorrow."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Two words, Lord Captain: suppression and fear. The base nature of the rabble cries for an iron grip, lest they give in to their animal urges.   - After: "Suppression and fear. Night searches, interrogations, floggings, executions — officers included."

  - Before: {n}There is a long pause. Then, Sauerback smiles grimly.{/n} "I do not intend to mourn Macharius's death, although I will miss the insufferable snob.   - After: {n}A grim smile.{/n} "I won't mourn Macharius. I'll redeem our name serving Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I inherited it from the previous Master-at-Arms. Like the esteemed Seneschal, he left the Navy to serve Lady Theodora. He brought quite a few officers with him and established a tradition: upon the death or resignation of an enforcer, his or her armour would be passed on to a fellow officer who had distinguished themselves in the course of their duties. I was awarded armour in this way in my time, and upon the death of my predecessor, I inherited his personal armour."
  - After: "Inherited. Tradition passes a fallen enforcer's armour to a distinguished one. My predecessor's came to me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But for now the steel in his spine remains unbending as ever — Werserian has been staunchly defending the crew in disputes with Master Anthar. I admire the Arbitrator's dogged pursuit of order, his hard-nosed severity, his implacability..." {n}The admiration in Sauerback's voice is unmistakable.{/n} "But the esteemed Seneschal is right — while our enforcers may not be as superbly trained as the Adeptus Arbites, our strength lies in our unquestioning loyalty to the dynasty. It is not for the esteemed Proctor to interfere with centuries of tried and tested practice."
  - After: "Werserian still defends the crew against Master Anthar. The Arbitrator impresses me..." {n}Admiringly.{/n} "But our strength is loyalty. The Proctor shouldn't meddle."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}She cocks an eyebrow.{/n} "Please repeat your orders, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}She cocks an eyebrow.{/n} "Repeat your orders, Lord Captain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Proud to serve the dynasty!"
  - After: "For the dynasty!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I come from the noble Sauerback family of the capital world of Dargonus. I dare say that our house is renowned for its loyalty and strict adherence to the law, and the members of my family have been your faithful enforcers for centuries. I am honoured to be the sixth Master-at-Arms named Sauerback to serve on this ship." {n}Jocasta speaks the words with unmistakable pride.{/n}
  - After: "A Sauerback of Dargonus, loyal to your line for centuries. Its sixth Master-at-Arms aboard." {n}Proudly.{/n}

  - Before: {n}An exact copy of you sits on the throne, a sinister double, crawled into this reality from behind the looking glass. {mf|His|Her} gaze meets yours, and the world expands sharply, crushing you with an overwhelming sense of your own insignificance. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your twin leers back. With razor-sharp teeth, {mf|his|her} grin rips open your mind, and a primal dread slithers in through the gap. It is a terror woven into the genes of every living thing, the paralysing fear of the natural predator of one's species. There is nothing human in the smile emanating from that face you know so well.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}With a tremendous {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}mental{/d} effort, you pry open the invisible jaws locked on Ravor's mind. You only manage to hold the unknown entity's monstrous power back for an instant, but it is enough to free your helmsman's consciousness from its prison.{/n}

- **Master Helmsman Ravor**

  - After: "Lord Cap'n? Then who's on the throne?" {n}He recoils, then collapses, ears bleeding.{/n}

  - After: "Groxshit! The Lord Captain never left. We dropped that elevator!"
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**
  - Before: {n}Ravor tries to catch you in his sights, but falls to the deck before he can steady his hand. There is bloody foam bubbling from his mouth.{/n} "No! The Lord Captain is in danger! I must... protect..." {n}He stops, his chest rising and falling heavily. He is badly wounded, but he will live if he receives help soon.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ravor falls, foaming blood.{/n} "Must... protect..." {n}He'll live with help.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your doppelganger remains seated and motionless on the throne, but {mf|his|her} posture betrays the tension of a predator ready to pounce. {mf|He|She} catches your gaze, and the vessel of your soul overflows with a cascade of images and feelings. You hear a song, a chorus of countless whispers that weave a tantalising melody. You feel a unity with something great and beautiful. It is bigger than you, bigger than this ship and everyone on it.{/n}
  - After: {n}{mf|He|She} sits poised, {mf|his|her} gaze flooding you with a whispering song of vast, beautiful unity.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The doppelganger's eyes grow wider and deeper, like twin purple lakes. You step into them, and the Meaning begins to permeate every fibre of your being. You dive head-first into the bliss, never to come out again.{/n}
  - After: {n}You sink into its purple eyes and the Meaning, never to return.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The bridge shudders as a crushing roar billows across it. Behind the facade of that leering face, you glimpse the monstrous shadow — the shadow in the void that wants only to devour you.{/n}
  - After: {n}A roar shakes the bridge; a devouring void-shadow looms.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}The Seneschal adjusts his grip on his weapon and growls,{/n} "Only one {mf|man|woman} may sit on the throne of the Rogue Trader, and that is {name} von Valancius. Wretched pretenders, craven xenos, enemies of Humanity — their only rightful place is in a pool of blood at the {mf|lord|lady} of the dynasty's feet!"
  - After: {n}Abelard growls,{/n} "One {mf|man|woman} sits here: {name} von Valancius. Pretenders bleed at the {mf|lord|lady}'s feet!"
- **Nemi Monteg**
