  - After: "Amateur. Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, may I show him how it's done?"
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Many-Armed?" {n}A deep furrow appears on Sauerback's brow.{/n} "Blast it! Lord Captain, we are dealing with an extremely dangerous xenos cult that excels at hiding among humans."
  - After: "Many-Armed?" {n}Sauerback frowns.{/n} "Blast! A dangerous xenos cult that hides among humans."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Very little. As per regulations, every Master-at-Arms passes on special instructions to their successor — instructions that more resemble disturbing tales. Some of them mention genetic cults — covert clans, cliques, and sects that all share one common trait: xenos infestation."
  - After: "Little. Masters-at-Arms pass down tales of genetic cults: secret sects infested by xenos."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We believe... in the Many-Armed Emperor... He who waits... for His children, cast out into the unknowable abyss. He is kind... merciful... He uproots tyrannies of evil... He sends His angel to the righteous, and angel's kin follow..." {n}The man lowers his gaze with an expression of surprise. It seems he has described his paltry religion in its entirety.{/n}
  - After: "The Many-Armed Emperor... waits for His children... merciful... He sends His angel and angel's kin..." {n}That's all of it.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Their arms, Lord Captain. These xenos have more arms than normal. They twist and pervert our faith, probably for the sole reason that it gives them blasphemous pleasure."
  - After: "These xenos have extra arms. They pervert our faith for pleasure."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Genestealers, {name}. That is what these enemies of Humanity are called. When such a creature bites its victim, it injects its gene into their body and dominates their mind. Or, more accurately, it binds it to the shared mind of the Brood. The victim undergoes no visible change, but their offspring will carry the brand of inhuman nature. Bestial maws, extra limbs, or something worse at times — horrific genetic outliers. However, the cult makes sure to keep any of their kind with unnatural appearance out of sight. After several generations, the mutants become practically indistinguishable from humans, but then something in their genes once more begets fully developed xenos capable of beginning the cycle of infestation anew."
  - After: "Genestealers, {name}. Their bite binds victims to the Brood. Their children are monstrous; over generations they look human, until pure xenos are born again."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "The lower decks have plenty of dark corners for the xenos to lie in wait. Commoners are too dull-witted and spineless to identify the threat before it is too late. And at the same time, they are dull-witted and spineless enough to serve as cannon fodder to be thrown at the cult's enemies when the uprising begins."
  - After: "Dark corners, dull commoners — and cannon fodder for the uprising."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}The Interrogator slowly shakes his head.{/n} "It's too early for that... Let's see what he has to say first."
  - After: {n}Heinrix shakes his head.{/n} "Too early. Let him talk first."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "These things pass themselves off as ordinary people, as rabble or preachers, corrupting new groups. They pray to their unholy idol, which they often refer to as the Many-Armed Emperor. They create ever-growing families and produce offspring — hideous at first, but with each new generation, more and more human in appearance. And then, they rise up."
  - After: "They pass as rabble or preachers, breeding offspring more human each generation. Then they rise."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}In lieu of answering, Sauerback nods grimly, lost in troubling thoughts.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sauerback nods grimly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In a sanctuary... A tomb... for heretics... A quiet place..."
  - After: "A sanctuary... a tomb... for heretics..."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}Sauerback glares at him with visible jealousy, but Einrich just keeps grinning smugly.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sauerback glares jealously; Einrich grins.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Their end goal is always mutiny. They can prepare for many generations, accumulating weapons and numbers, until one day, they attack. That day is their 'day of revelation,' the apotheosis of their profane faith. They think that on that day, their blasphemous 'Star Children' will descend from the void and elevate their worshippers."
  - After: "Mutiny. For generations they arm, then strike, expecting 'Star Children' from the void to elevate them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The prisoner jerks as if trying to point at you with his tied hands.{/n} "You're a false believer, a fake captain! You're leading people into the gloom of heresy, away from salvation!"
  - After: {n}He jerks at you.{/n} "Fake captain! Heretic!"
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}The Master-at-Arms says with a warm smile,{/n} "Please, allow me. He won't die by my hand. I won't let him."
  - After: {n}Sauerback smiles.{/n} "Allow me. I won't let him die."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "The creatures that infect the first victims act as scouts for a xenos race known as Tyranids. After creating a Genestealer Cult, the scout... 'evolves' into something more complex, an entity called the Patriarch. The collective mind of the Brood becomes a psychic beacon for the Tyranids, a beacon that marks the planet as vulnerable. Once the xenos fleet approaches the infected world, the rebellion begins. The cult strikes the world's defenders in the back while the xenos devour all life on the planet. And the cult's true believers certainly do not find the ascension they were promised. Instead, they all become a bioresource. Food."
  - After: "The first creature scouts for the Tyranids, then becomes a Patriarch whose Brood-mind beacons them in. When they come, the cult strikes from within, and all are devoured, faithful too. Food."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I fear you are right, Mistress Sauerback. This— actually, please, continue. I will correct you should your information contradict credible intelligence."
  - After: "You're right, Mistress Sauerback. Continue; I'll correct errors."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The pigment of the tattoo looks fresh, standing out starkly against the colour of his skin, which means that it is a very recent addition. You look closely and you notice a pair of scars at the base of his neck, suspiciously reminiscent of an almost healed bite.{/n}
  - After: {n}Fresh tattoo. Two neck scars, like a healed bite.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I am finished, {name}. If that didn't suffice, I do not recommend applying biomancy again — we may lose the prisoner."
  - After: "Done, {name}. More may kill him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You notice a strange mark on the man's neck: it looks like a superficial burn, or yet another pestilence from the lower decks.{/n}
  - After: {n}A mark on his neck: a burn or pestilence.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "He has proved far more useful than I expected. He must have been in the cult only for a short time, and the psychic connection to his brethren had not taken root in his mind. No amount of torture would have loosened his tongue otherwise..." {n}Heinrix frowns.{/n} "Things are progressing too smoothly. I don't like it."
  - After: "He was new, the Brood bond unrooted." {n}He frowns.{/n} "Too smooth. I don't like it."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}Casting a glance at the prisoner whispering incoherently under his breath, Sauerback adds off-handedly,{/n} "And this vile scum, with your permission, I'll throw out of the airlock. I doubt he will be of any further use."
  - After: {n}Sauerback shrugs.{/n} "With your permission, this scum goes out the airlock."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "The speeches of your enemies, mon-keigh, sound just like your own. Fanatical, composed of nothing but rage and contempt. Is even that not enough to make you wonder?"
  - After: "Your enemies sound like you, mon-keigh: all rage. Doesn't that give you pause?"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta exhales hoarsely:{/n} "Damn you all, distorters of holy words!"
  - After: {n}Argenta rasps:{/n} "Damn you, distorters of holy words!"
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Snarling furiously, Ulfar clenches his fist.{/n} "Many-armed poison... I smell the foul seed of the xenos. The Iron Priests say it once fell into the waters of Fenris, and from it came the terrible sea krakens. Well, Fenris is here, Fenris is ready to hunt."
  - After: {n}Ulfar snarls.{/n} "Xenos seed, like the one that spawned Fenris's krakens. Fenris hunts."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: {n}Cassia whispers in mesmerised horror,{/n} "His soul is pale, almost colourless, but alien hues have seeped into it. Unthinkable and insane... and they came from without."
  - After: {n}Cassia, horrified:{/n} "His soul is stained with alien hues."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I have heard of them, and every tale was awash in blood. They are the reapers of the Great Devourer — predators that have bloomed from its seed, beasts whose gift is to turn the weak-spirited into their enthralled fighters. Beware of them, elantach. When they are near, even a loyal friend may turn out to be a messenger of death."
  - After: "Reapers of the Great Devourer. Beware, elantach: near them, even a friend may bring death."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}At a barely noticeable gesture from the Proctor, Glaito lunges at the prisoner, bites down, and starts violently shaking his arm. You hear the man's bones break and his flesh tear apart, but his screams are filled with horror rather than pain — so overpowering is his fear of this living weapon of the Lex Imperialis that knows no pity.{/n}
  - After: {n}Glaito savages the prisoner's arm. He screams in terror.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Glaito, heel. The miscreant can't take any more. What we need is answers, not execution."
  - After: "Glaito, heel. We need answers."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}A barrage of hissing discharges surges from Eogunn's mechadendrites and hull, enveloping the prisoner in a dazzling, lethal web. The biting smell of ozone drifts through the air, mingling with the thick vapour of burning hair. Strange, livid scars swell up on the man's skin one after another, branching in different directions, as if the current were burning its way through his flesh. {/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn's mechadendrites crackle; ozone and burnt hair. {/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I believe forced galvanisation of the nervous system will serve as sufficient impetus to arrive at a consensus. If you don't wish to kill this... person, then the current level of severity is enough."
  - After: "Galvanised nerves bring consensus. More would kill him."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "The dynastic crypt! The vermin have infiltrated the crypt holding the bodies of the worthiest servants of the dynasty! No one is allowed inside save for the Lord Captain's personal retinue, and they dared... But how? The crypt's defences are impenetrable..."
  - After: "The dynastic crypt! Only the Lord Captain's retinue may enter. How? Its defences are impenetrable..."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "I wouldn't say that these improvised webbers are that much better than fighting with bare hands, but... until we are done with the clean-up, every enforcer will carry a combat knife fit for cutting through nets."
  - After: "Crude webbers. Until the clean-up's done, enforcers carry net-cutting knives."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The light from the Infernus Master's lho-stick reveals his surprised but amiable expression. Einrich's lip is split and a fresh bruise is blossoming on his cheekbone.{/n} "Lord Captain? Didn't expect to see you in this compartment. Are you out on a stroll, taking in the sights of your domain? The blue glow of plasma is especially striking at this time of the watch."
  - After: {n}Einrich, bruised, lip split, smokes a lho-stick.{/n} "Lord Captain? Touring your domain?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Einrich rubs his grazed knuckles.{/n} "A little gift to remember the enforcers by. We've had a small disagreement. They thought they had the right to beat and starve innocent people while investigating the incident in Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s bathchamber. I thought their noses were too straight and they had too many teeth. So, we politely exchanged opinions."
  - After: {n}Einrich rubs his knuckles.{/n} "Enforcers beat innocents over Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s bathchamber incident. I objected."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "An enforcer's baton is pretty sturdy, but not as thick as the skull of a hard-boiled infernus. I have to give it to Jocasta, her officers earn their rations. They clobber you good."
  - After: "An infernus skull outlasts a baton. Jocasta's officers hit hard, though."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "As Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} wishes. I might as well carry out a bay inspection, then, since I'm here. I won't interfere in your business."
  - After: "As Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} wishes. I'll inspect the bay."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Found me out, have you?" {n}Einrich gives you a wink and pulls on his lho-stick.{/n} "I'm not really here about the reactor. Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} is accustomed to associating with people of your rank, or officers at the very least, but here... This place is home to voidfarers of simpler manners, whose clan customs may be unfamiliar to you."
  - After: {n}Einrich winks.{/n} "I came to smooth things over. Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} knows officers; folk here have rough clan customs."

  - After: {n}Nije frowns.{/n} "Our customs are decent, Master Monteg! I'd boil in plasma before harming the Lord Captain!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Einrich rolls his lho-stick back and forth, thinking.{/n} "I've also seen it on some bulkheads, crates, doors. I just assumed it was the mark of some small clan — many voidsmen mark their workplaces with family symbols."
  - After: {n}Einrich thinks.{/n} "I've seen it on crates and doors. Thought it was a clan mark."

  - After: {n}Nije bows.{/n} "How goes the search, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Einrich chuckles.{/n} "I think you've found someone's secret stash. What was it? A mouldy nutribar, lho, a few thrones?   - After: {n}Einrich chuckles.{/n} "Someone's secret stash, marked to find later."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No offence, Nije, but if you can find even three people in this bay who can give a report without turning the air blue, I'll gladly admit I was wrong." {n}Einrich grins at the now silent Nije.{/n} "You're a good bunch, I'd hate to see you insult {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} with some foolishness and not even realise it."
  - After: "No offence, Nije, but few here can report without cursing." {n}He grins.{/n} "I'd hate you to offend {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}."

  - Before: {n}Einrich deftly examines the weapon.{/n} "Interesting. Nije is right — this could get a whole bay executed. No wonder these scoundrels are so cautious."
  - After: {n}Einrich examines it.{/n} "This could get a whole bay executed."

  - After: "I'll wait for your cue."

  - Before: "Permission to kick off our little operation, {name}?"
  - After: "Shall we start, {name}?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm just keeping an eye out, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Feel free to ask old Nije any questions you may have — he knows the plasma drive chambers like the back of his hand."
  - After: "Just watching, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Ask Nije — he knows these chambers."
- **Shift Foreman Nije**
  - Before: "That's just what we need, more secret stashes. I hope there was nothing forbidden in it? Forgive me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but voidsmen are simple folk. I've been trying to wean them off their grubby habits for years. But give them anything worth having and all they want to do is hide it in a hole like a rat!"
  - After: "More stashes! Forgive them, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Voidsmen hoard like rats."
- **Shift Foreman Nije**
  - Before: "What is that?" {n}Nije's thick eyebrows knit together angrily, and you almost think you see a power charge jolt across them.{/n} "We've got smugglers on the loose! Who else would be hiding these strange messages? I'll have them all drawn and quartered on the turbine, I will! Now I'd like to find out what they're smuggling..."
  - After: {n}Nije scowls.{/n} "Smugglers! I'll quarter them on the turbine! But smuggling what?"
- **Shift Foreman Nije**
  - Before: {n}Nije holds the weapon as if it is going to bite him, sweat beading on his forehead.{/n} "Machine spark shake me! A homemade weapon, and assembled right in this compartment — the markings are the same as those on local machine parts. This is a very serious matter — it seems someone is plotting a riot and secretly building their own arsenal from scavenged materials right under our noses!"
  - After: {n}Nije sweats.{/n} "Machine spark shake me! Homemade, from local parts. Someone's arming for a riot!"
- **Shift Foreman Nije**
  - Before: {n}The shift foreman shrugs sheepishly.{/n} "I... To tell you the truth, I'm no good at hunting rule-breakers. It's not what I do. You give the orders, and we will do it."
  - After: {n}Nije shrugs.{/n} "I'm no hunter. You order, we follow."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Clenching his fists until his knuckles crack, Einrich resolutely says,{/n} "We'll help. I have a couple of people in mind, tough lads. I'll get them here right away."
  - After: {n}Einrich cracks his knuckles.{/n} "I'll fetch some tough lads."
- **Shift Foreman Nije**
  - Before: {n}The shift foreman's voice grows quieter.{/n} "I just wish I knew who to trust with it... Our villain could be anyone from the bay crew. If we pick the wrong person, we'll blow the whole ambush. We need someone from the outside who won't draw attention to themselves."
  - After: {n}Nije whispers.{/n} "Any crewman could be the villain. We need outsiders."
- **Shift Foreman Nije**
  - Before: "That's right, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. If something isn't to your liking or if you find anything suspicious, come to me at once!"
  - After: "Find anything suspicious, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, come to me!"
- **Shift Foreman Nije**
  - Before: "We'll spook them, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. By the time the enforcers finish their search, all the rats will have scattered and covered their tracks."
  - After: "The rats will scatter, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Shift Foreman Nije**
  - Before: "We are proud of our chambers. Power feeds the ship's main engine from here. There are other drives on the ship, but ours is the mightiest. That's to say, we do important work."
  - After: "We power the ship's main engine — the mightiest drive aboard."
- **Shift Foreman Nije**
  - Before: {n}Nije looks at you in confusion.{/n} "I'm... I'm a voidsman, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Grew up on Footfall, joined the crew at fourteen, spent my whole life in this bay. I've raised no family and made no fortune, but I've climbed my way up the ranks. I don't know anything but my trade and this compartment... I am my trade and this compartment, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}Nije blinks.{/n} "A voidsman, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Footfall-born, crew at fourteen. I am my trade and this compartment."
- **Shift Foreman Nije**
  - Before: "Working with plasma is dangerous, but we have a good crew, and not too many incidents. The esteemed Tech-Priests are satisfied with us, the machine spirits are all working as they should. The inferni don't complain about us either — we fix cracks in the reactor vessel on time, and we fix leaks."
  - After: "Plasma's dangerous, but we're good. Few incidents, leaks fixed on time."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Is it just the power surging in the bay, or was there a spark between us just now, Einrich?" {n}Jae bites her lip dramatically.{/n}
  - After: "Power surge, or a spark between us, Einrich?" {n}Jae bites her lip.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Einrich matches her with a theatrical sigh.{/n} "Either could start a dangerous fire, Mistress Heydari. Someone could get hurt, and we can't let that happen, now can we?"
  - After: {n}Einrich sighs theatrically.{/n} "Both start fires, Mistress Heydari."
- **Shift Foreman Nije**
  - Before: "You're the most mawkish infernus I've ever met, Master Monteg." {n}A burly man in coveralls furrows his bushy eyebrows. His sparse hair stands on end.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, welcome. I'm Shift Foreman Nije, in charge of this section. If you need anything, I'm here to help."
  - After: "Mawkish as ever, Master Monteg." {n}A burly man in coveralls.{/n} "Welcome, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Shift Foreman Nije, at your service."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm carrying out a routine drive inspection. The regulations require scheduled checks to make sure the insulation isn't weakened, the sensors haven't been tampered with, and the reactor isn't about to blow anytime soon. Just business as usual."
  - After: "Routine drive inspection. Business as usual."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is strange that the senior officer is conducting the inspection alone. According to the regulations, there should be an entire squad of inferni, and the personal presence of the Infernus Master is necessary only in emergencies.{/n}
  - After: {n}Odd: inspections need a squad; the Infernus Master comes only in emergencies.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Plasma drive inspections are a regular requirement — the ship's power-generating heart cannot be allowed to stop beating.{/n}
  - After: {n}Plasma drive inspections are routine.{/n}
- **Shift Foreman Nije**
  - Before: "Somebody keeps daubing it on the equipment and bulkheads. If I find the scoundrels, I'll tear their hands off and send them for servitorisation." {n}The shift foreman frowns.{/n} "Is it some kind of sedition? I didn't know. If you see one of these, let me know, we'll try to find these artists."
  - After: "Someone daubs it on equipment. I'll have their hands!" {n}He frowns.{/n} "Sedition? Tell me if you see it."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/ExplorationEvents/AstrolabyTreasure/AstrolabyTreasure_EPP

- **Player**
  - Before: Examine the room and the body.
  - After: Examine the room and body.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Overgrown trees and ivy-covered roots conceal an ancient bio-dome nestled in one of the crevices. It would have been impossible to locate this place without the precise coordinates from the armillary sphere.
  - After: The armillary sphere's coordinates lead to an ancient, overgrown bio-dome.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The structure is in a state of gross disrepair. Creepers cover the walls and ceiling, and pungent flowers and berries hang from beams and equipment alike. The centre of the structure reveals a sealed chamber where vegetation has yet to break through. Inside is a humble bunk — a decayed body sprawled over it — tables with blueprints, parts and tools, and a great number of chests containing treasure.
  - After: Inside a sealed chamber: a decayed body on a bunk, blueprints, tools and chests of treasure.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Judging by the dead man's clothes, the diary pages, and the monograms on the blueprints, you realise that you have found the final resting place of the legendary Captain Bartholomeus Ort. During his long and adventurous life, he travelled the entire Expanse, mapping out numerous star systems and, in his later years, realising his life's work: the armillary sphere that he imbued with the sum of his knowledge. The device on your ship is undoubtedly his creation.
  - After: It is legendary Captain Bartholomeus Ort, who mapped the Expanse and built the armillary sphere on your ship.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: While the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} were still hotly debating whether or not he had committed the crime of invention, Bartholomeus disappeared without a trace, leaving only a single message: "I have gathered treasures from hundreds of worlds, but they will not be handed over to the covetous lords of the Expanse. Instead, I bequeath my riches to one who cherishes the shine of the stars more than any gold or rubies." It seems that you happen to be this very person.
  - After: Accused by the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} of invention, he vanished, leaving his riches to one who loves the stars more than gold. You.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The shuttle's hold is bursting with untold riches. You leave the forgotten dome at the mercy of the invading wilderness and its inhabitants.
  - After: Your hold bursts with riches. The dome is left to the wilds.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Only the rustling of leaves and the chirping of insects respond to the roar of the shuttle taking off. The dome waits motionless in the embrace of roots and vines.
  - After: The shuttle lifts off. The dome waits in the vines.

  - Before: A squad of enforcers and Tech-Priests put on their void suits and dock with the ship. The vessel is empty except for the frozen and desiccated corpses of the crew. Some retain human features, but others are easily recognisable as genetic aberrations. They have been dead for centuries.

  - After: No life signs. Cold, dark, silent.

  - Before: An all-out barrage turns the Finger of Sorrow to space dust, forever erasing its sinister secrets from the history of the Koronus Expanse.
  - After: A barrage turns the Finger of Sorrow to dust, secrets and all.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Finger of Sorrow was a common merchant vessel. The log records its travels along many of the trade routes of the Calixis Sector. The last entry states that the ship departed from Port Wander on the border between the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanseGlossary}Koronus Expanse{/g} and the {g|Encyclopedia:CalixisGlossary}Calixis Sector{/g}. The Tech-Priest notes that the protocols for undocking from the station were not followed, indicating either a hasty escape or blatant disregard for the covenants of the Omnissiah.
  - After: A Calixis merchant ship. Last entry: fleeing Port Wander, between the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanseGlossary}Koronus Expanse{/g} and the {g|Encyclopedia:CalixisGlossary}Calixis Sector{/g}, in haste.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The hold is empty, apart from a few open containers. However, careful examination points to three opened service hatches that bear claw marks. Venturing deeper into the service tunnels, the enforcers find three empty nests with chunks of purple chitin and dried traces of dark slime that has eaten through the metal panels. There can be no doubt that Genestealers once lurked here.
  - After: Clawed hatches lead to three empty nests with purple chitin and acid slime. Genestealers.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Many of the cabins have become tombs for the bodies of the crew. They asphyxiated when the ship's life support systems failed. One of the enforcers notices a cache marked with the symbol of a fanged serpent with a sharp tail and three clawed limbs. The cache contains an amulet and a miraculously preserved diary.
  - After: The crew suffocated in their cabins. A cache marked with a clawed, fanged serpent holds an amulet and a diary.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The diary was kept by one of the missionaries of a Genestealer Cult. According to the entries, this cult secretly spread throughout much of the Calixis Sector, although the author does not mention any specific infected worlds. He recalls with reverence "the promised land, the cradle of faith, salty as the tears of righteous martyrs." The author's branch of the cult had settled on Port Wander Station, the last threshold between the Calixis Sector and the Koronus Expanse.
  - After: A Genestealer Cult missionary's diary. The cult spread secretly through Calixis; his branch settled on Port Wander Station.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The cult grew and gained followers among the workers and the poor, and even managed to infiltrate powerful trade guilds. However, their plans fell apart when the Genestealer's Kiss was granted to an unworthy candidate. This oversight led to the discovery of the cult and a bloody purge. The author of the diary recalls with horror and sorrow how many of the pureblood children of the Star Saviour perished in the massacre.
  - After: It infiltrated workers and guilds, until the Genestealer's Kiss went to an unworthy candidate. A purge killed many pureblood children of the Star Saviour.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The story ends by chronicling the escape of a small group of heretics who managed to save three purebreds and steal a merchant ship under heavy fire from the station. They narrowly navigated the Maw, but the ship's damage was too severe. "The three phalanges of the Finger of Sorrow," the pureblood Star Children, fell into a long sleep and became dormant. Meanwhile, the cultists humbly watched the ship's life support systems fade away one after another. In the last lines, the author welcomes death in the name of the Many-Armed Emperor with solemnity and elation.
  - After: A few fled with three purebreds, barely crossing the Maw. "The three phalanges of the Finger of Sorrow" went dormant as life support failed. The author died praising the Many-Armed Emperor.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The enforcers plant melta charges at key points on the vessel, and the explosion rips the Finger of Sorrow to pieces that are obliterated by strikes from the macro-cannons.
  - After: Melta charges and macro-cannons obliterate the ship.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The ship watches you silently with the dead visors of its {g|Encyclopedia:Augur}augur{/g} systems.
  - After: The ship watches with dead {g|Encyclopedia:Augur}augur{/g} eyes.

  - Before: "From what I can tell, it's something like a prayer with several verses that tell about the life of one of the cult's saints. Erianne, or the Matriarch Spider, as they call her."
  - After: "A prayer about their saint, Erianne, the Matriarch Spider."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The blood that was used to paint the symbol is still fresh, but you see no clues as to who left it here or what their intentions were.{/n}
  - After: {n}Fresh blood, no clues.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}In other words, it is an invitation. It is only too {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}obvious{/d} that cultists obsessed with mysticism would never use prose to mark the way to their temple — they are too fond of their obscure chants and cryptic verses.{/n}
  - After: {n}An invitation. {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}Obviously{/d}, mystics mark their temple's path in verse.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Maybe it has something to do with them inviting you to visit their temple. Maybe they're trying to get your attention? Apologies, Lord Captain, I'm no good at deciphering their disturbing riddles."
  - After: "An invitation to their temple? I can't read their riddles."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah carves the same symbol on the back of her hand with a knife and whispers a prayer.{/n} "Domin'{name}, remember this sign. It is the beginning of your quest, the first blood trail."
  - After: {n}Kibellah carves the symbol into her hand.{/n} "Remember it, Domin'{name}. The first blood trail."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "When I took up my post here, I made sure to familiarise myself with all the... particular qualities of this compartment. I soon heard about the verse and decided to investigate. I questioned a number of people who follow the Bloodspun Web as I was trying to figure out if there was anything pernicious about it, and eventually I learned the whole thing." {n}He frowns.{/n} "The words are certainly strange, but it's nothing worse than that, it seems."
  - After: "I questioned followers to check it was harmless and learned it." {n}He frowns.{/n} "Strange, nothing worse."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_DTSearching/DTS_BurntMan

- **Player**
  - Before: "The spinner whispered a verse to you? Can you repeat it for me?"
  - After: "The spinner whispered a verse? Repeat it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I begged him to save me, but he just turned and left... Why?" {n}He coughs and starts feverishly scratching the same symbols you saw into his flesh.{/n} "Please, help me! I want to live..."
  - After: "He left me... Why?" {n}He scratches the symbols.{/n} "Help me!"

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_DTSearching/DTS_BurntMan/DTS_BurntMan_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Switch on your vox] "Get some enforcers and medicae personnel in here, now. There is a man in need of revival. Once he has recovered, assign him to be a scribe's apprentice — he is too badly injured to go back to a worker's life."
  - After: [Switch on your vox] "Enforcers and medicae here, now. Revive this man, then make him a scribe's apprentice — he can't work anymore."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Assess the man's chances of survival]
  - After: [Assess his chances of survival]
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you know anything about the mark next to you?"
  - After: "Know anything about this mark?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Leave] "All of us must face our fated outcome."
  - After: [Leave] "We all face our fate."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Who are you and what happened to you?"
  - After: "Who are you? What happened?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Help is on the way. Just hold on a little longer."
  - After: "Help is coming. Hold on."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Mercy... Please, save me..." {n}The young man gasps for air through burnt lips, slipping in and out of delirium. His skin is dripping from his gaunt body like melted wax from a candle. His eyes, somehow intact, alive, clear, and filled with pain, stare at you from under his caked eyelids.{/n}
  - After: "Mercy... save me..." {n}A burnt young man, skin melting, stares in pain.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He begins to whisper, his lips twisted in pain:{/n}
"To soot-smirched soul... her mercy she did grant.
Last breath expressed, knife met heart:
removed from chest... passed on to death.
Her duty blessed, a balm for those
who suffer... anguish and distress...
A longing brought to rest:
of mortal bonds the soul divest..."
  - After: {n}He whispers:{/n}
"To soot-smirched soul... her mercy she did grant.
Knife met heart...
of mortal bonds the soul divest..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He might survive, but he will be maimed for life. Too much of his muscle has been charred down to the bone — even if he does retain some ability to move, pain will be his constant companion. His motor skills have been damaged beyond repair. A broken man or a corpse, time will soon tell.{/n}
  - After: {n}He might live, maimed and in constant pain.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No! Mercy..." {n}Horror flashes in the man's eyes, but once he sees your calm expression, he lets go of the fear and bows his head in resignation.{/n} "So be it... I can't... take this pain anymore... I'd rather... die..."
  - After: "No!" {n}Seeing your calm, he yields.{/n} "So be it... I'd rather die..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He tries to turn his head, his blackened skin crunching as it opens into scarlet cracks.{/n} "A spinner came... He painted the symbol... Then he gave me water... and whispered a strange verse... He told me to memorise it and to recite it later... so that help would come. And here you are! Then I should..."
  - After: {n}His skin cracks.{/n} "A spinner painted it... taught me a verse to summon help. And here you are!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: "I wonder how long he's been sitting here like this. A watch? Three? The whispers say nobody cared because he didn't matter, but they also say he's somehow supposed to matter to us... Strange."
  - After: "The whispers say nobody cared, yet he matters to us. Strange."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Never forget the mercy that the Lord Captain has granted you."
  - After: "Never forget the Lord Captain's mercy."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm Vayle, a cleaner... I was in my house, asleep... enforcers came... set fire to it... I didn't... make it out in time..."
  - After: "Vayle, a cleaner... enforcers burned my house while I slept..."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "When the Undying One is ready to accept a soul, it must be sent forth, and so will it be freed from the torment of the flesh. Yet you have chosen to... prolong this one's suffering. Your intentions perplex me."
  - After: "His soul should be freed to the Undying One. You prolong his suffering. Perplexing."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man shakes his head desperately, ripping open the crust that has just begun to form over his burns.{/n} "No... Please... I'm begging you!"
  - After: {n}He shakes his head.{/n} "No... I'm begging you!"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "There is no curse more terrible than an existence between unlife and undeath. You have liberated a tormented soul, Domin'{name}. The Undying One sees the good you have wrought."
  - After: "You freed a tormented soul, Domin'{name}. The Undying One sees."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "You soulless ashmag..." {n}Jae mutters under her breath.{/n}
  - After: "Soulless ashmag..." {n}Jae mutters.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}More verses. The crux of this test is {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}clear{/d}: in order to follow in the saint's footsteps, you are supposed to kill the young man and thus release him from his suffering. The cultists want to see if you understand the philosophy of those you seek.{/n}
  - After: {n}The test is {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}clear{/d}: like the saint, kill him to end his suffering.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "O-of course! Thank... thank you..."
  - After: "Th-thank you..."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "The prognosis is unfavourable, Rogue Trader. I could... " {n}Seeing the look in the young man's eyes, the Manipulus trails off.{/n} "But no, I could not. While there is some hope of survival for this man, it is most likely illusory."
  - After: "Prognosis unfavourable. I could..." {n}Eogunn trails off.{/n} "No. His hope is illusory."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A blissful smile twists the man's lips, and a tear forms at the corner of his ruined eye socket.{/n} "The God-Emperor has sent you to save me... You are His light... You are His grace... Thank you... Thank you for not leaving me here..."
  - After: {n}He smiles, tearful.{/n} "The God-Emperor sent you... Thank you for not leaving me..."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "The death cultists want us to end the poor man? Those sick lunatics! Anyone can be saved as long as they still want to live!" {n}Jae's fingers move toward her neck augment instinctively.{/n} "At the very least, they deserve an attempt to save them before you discard their life."
  - After: "Kill him? Lunatics! Anyone who wants to live can be saved!" {n}Jae touches her neck augment.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "There are times when death is more merciful than a life of perpetual agony."
  - After: "Sometimes death is kinder."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The chances of this unit surviving are slim. Functional usefulness in the event of stabilisation of vital processes is minimal. Disposal is recommended."
  - After: "Survival unlikely. Disposal recommended."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Brownish-yellow pus has collected under his scorched skin. His wounds have already been touched by the rot of the lower decks, and even if his body survives transport to the medicae facility, the man will still die of either shock or infection.{/n}
  - After: {n}His burns fester. Shock or infection will kill him.{/n}
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai approaches the mutilated man, closes his eyes, and takes a deep breath. The corners of his lips curve into a satisfied smile.{/n}
  - After: {n}Marazhai inhales near the man, smiling.{/n}

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_DTSearching/DTS_DeadlyLeap/DTS_DeadlyLeap_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Shout into the shaft] "I've had it with this madness and with your riddles! I am not going to risk my life just for the sake of finding some temple!"
  - After: [Shout into the shaft] "Enough riddles! I won't risk my life for some temple!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Call upon the Ruinous Powers] "I am willing to take the risk so that I might learn the secrets of the Bloodspun Web, but I need your aid!"
  - After: [Call upon the Ruinous Powers] "I'll risk it to learn the Bloodspun Web's secrets. Aid me!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Pray to the Emperor] "I put my life in Thy hands, for I believe truly that Thou wilt protect."
  - After: [Pray to the Emperor] "My life is in Thy hands; Thou wilt protect."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The rotating blades promise nothing but a senseless and brutal death. Slipping past them would require some unreasonably precise calculations... or blind luck. While listening to the air currents, for a moment you think you hear Zdena's whispered prayer rising from the depths of the shaft.{/n}
  - After: {n}Spinning blades promise death; passing needs precision or luck. Zdena's prayer echoes below.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}All you hear back is the echo of your own words.{/n}
  - After: {n}Only your echo answers.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The words come easily, and all of your doubt fades away. Somehow, you know with certainty that your life will not end here.{/n}
  - After: {n}Doubt fades. You won't die here.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A confident smile that is not your own appears on your lips. The rumbling blades no longer seem dangerous, and the prospect of jumping becomes a mere trifle.{/n}
  - After: {n}A smile not your own. Jumping seems trivial.{/n}

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_DTSearching/DTS_FormerCultist/DTS_FormerCultist_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Your eyes always return to that blood symbol. What do you know about it?"
  - After: "What's that blood symbol to you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "As the Emperor's anointed, I hereby overturn the Vizsier's verdict. The cult ruined your life, and for what? For a few mere killings?"
  - After: "As the Emperor's anointed, I overturn the Vizsier's verdict. Ruined over a few killings?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do you think you are doing?"
  - After: "What are you doing?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Leave] "I doubt that you can be of any help to me."
  - After: [Leave] "You can't help me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You know the symbols of the Bloodspun Web. You bear similar scars. Are you a spinner?"
  - After: "Bloodspun Web symbols, matching scars. A spinner?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You look like you are about to take your own life. Are you having a rotten day?"
  - After: "Suicidal? Rotten day?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You were ordered to die? For what reason?"
  - After: "Ordered to die? Why?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "So the spinners simply let you go? They made no attempts to find you and kill you?"
  - After: "The spinners never hunted you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are disgusting. I will not grant you the release you crave so much. May you live on in suffering, fearful of every shadow."
  - After: "Disgusting. No release for you. Live in fear."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are a coward and a butcher of the innocent. I will purge my ship of your existence."
  - After: "Coward and butcher. I'll purge you from my ship."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Have you killed any more innocent souls since you ran?"
  - After: "Killed more innocents since?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You do not sound particularly remorseful."
  - After: "You don't sound remorseful."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will not judge you, nor will I decide your fate. Farewell."
  - After: "I won't judge you. Farewell."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do not even think of marring the underside of my train with your entrails!"
  - After: "Don't mar my train with your entrails!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A sinewy middle-aged man watches the bustle of the bay with a detached expression. Every so often, whenever his eyes linger on the blood mark inscribed nearby, his face changes strangely and his hands clench into fists.{/n}
  - After: {n}A sinewy man eyes a blood mark, fists clenched.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A dead man. I lost my name years ago. I've been just another dead man ever since."
  - After: "A dead man, nameless for years."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You... you're right, Lord Captain! The Vizsier taught me to serve. To kill. I did what I was chosen to do... and they punished me for it. They've kept me living in fear almost my whole life!" {n}The man's colourless eyes fill with malice.{/n} "Thank you for opening my eyes. It's time for Sebreid to return... and for the dead man to disappear, along with his creators."
  - After: "You're right! They taught me to kill, then punished me!" {n}Malice fills his eyes.{/n} "Sebreid returns. His creators die."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Vicious ashmag! You used people's faith in the Exalted One to justify abusing the power that was given to you!"
  - After: "Ashmag! You twisted the Exalted One's faith!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What? I... I didn't..." {n}The man starts and almost falls, but manages to keep his balance. In the dim {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumen{/g} light, you notice old scars scattered all across his body. The scars seem vaguely familiar.{/n}
  - After: "I didn't..." {n}He stumbles. In {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumen{/g} light, familiar scars show.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The scars all vary in length, width, depth, and shape. However, you notice a pattern in the way the scars are aligned, as well as a series of faded symbols on the man's rough skin. Death cultists bear similar marks on their bodies.{/n}
  - After: {n}Patterned scars, faded symbols: death cultist marks.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "You dare insult the Rogue Trader with your impudence? Your body may already be covered in scars, but your tongue seems to be asking for more."
  - After: "Insolence? Want more scars?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Vizsier told me to kill the one who would be at a certain junction of the utility tunnels at a certain hour. I went to the appointed spot. Then I waited. An hour. Two. Five. The junction was still empty. Nobody came. After hours of waiting, I finally realised: the person at the junction had been me the whole time. It was my turn to go to the Undying One. But I was... afraid. I couldn't do my duty. I ran."
  - After: "The Vizsier ordered me to kill whoever came to a tunnel junction. Nobody came. It was me. My turn to die. I ran."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My whole life has been rotten. And I only have myself to blame. I've tried to change things, fix things. But I always ended up here, so eventually, I accepted the truth."
  - After: "My life's rotten, my own fault."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "If Humankind followed its own Paths as the Children of Asuryan do... this mon-keigh would be one who has lost his Path."
  - After: "This mon-keigh has lost his Path."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "If this were an interrogation, I would welcome such a response. But in this case we are merely wasting our time."
  - After: "A waste of time."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah briefly studies the man's face, then turns away.{/n} "I do not know you. Death's gaze is not upon you."
  - After: {n}Kibellah turns away.{/n} "Death's gaze is not upon you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He bows half-heartedly.{/n} "I can't even be of any help to myself."
  - After: {n}He bows.{/n} "I can't even help myself."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I was. But I failed to complete my final assignment, so I was... exiled from the cult."
  - After: "I was. I failed my final task and was exiled."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There was no pursuit. I thought I'd see their black blades the very next day. Instead, years passed without them taking my heart. I tried starting a new life, but the terror never stopped eating away at me. When I got truly desperate, I went to the temple of death myself. But no one there would speak to me. When I gave them my name, they just whispered, 'Sebreid has gone to the Undying One.' They looked through me like I wasn't even there. I've lived like this for twenty years. Like a coward. Like a dead man."
  - After: "Nobody came. At the temple of death they whispered, 'Sebreid has gone to the Undying One,' and ignored me. Twenty years a dead man."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No! What about the symbol? The portent? You... you were supposed to..." {n}The man's tired eyes fill with horror that quickly turns into hysteria. His knees buckle, and he staggers heavily before falling onto the tracks with a pitiful cry.{/n} "No! Help!"
  - After: "No! You were supposed to..." {n}He falls onto the tracks.{/n} "Help!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I've spent years in remorse. I'm tired of it."
  - After: "I'm tired of remorse."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No. I've been afraid to touch my own knife since that day. Thought it might just stab me on its own... But the temptation is always there."
  - After: "No. But I'm tempted."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Oh, you poor thing, I think I'm gonna cry. You couldn't stop slicing people up! That must have been so hard for you! Even my whispers have nothing to say to a pathetic tale like that. I bet they're thinking, 'What a lousy, self-absorbed sack of scum!'"
  - After: "Poor thing! Even my whispers call you scum!"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah appears behind you and watches the man leave.{/n} "He severed souls from bodies before their fated time. Not because he honoured death, but because he enjoyed killing. He did not have that right. No one does."
  - After: {n}Kibellah watches.{/n} "He killed for pleasure. No one has that right."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man looks at you.{/n}
"But some would choose to leave the righteous path.
These earned penance in due time:
her whip sings vengeance on renegade menace.
Her blades pass sentence.
For cowards seek to hide their hearts,
but death makes no pretendence;
it takes what it is due in essence."
{n}He stops, then adds hoarsely,{/n} "The third verse of the Song of Trailing Blood. The Vizsier recited it to me before sending me on my final assignment. I didn't realise at the time that it was my judgement."
  - After: {n}He looks at you.{/n}
"But some would choose to leave the righteous path.
These earned penance in due time:
her whip sings vengeance on renegade menace.
Her blades pass sentence.
For cowards seek to hide their hearts,
but death makes no pretendence;
it takes what it is due in essence."
{n}Hoarsely:{/n} "The Song of Trailing Blood, third verse. My judgement."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Another verse, another step along the trail of blood. The riddle is {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}trivial{/d}: it is time for death to take what it is due, and the Vizsier is waiting expectantly for you to carry out the sentence he passed years ago.{/n}
  - After: {n}A {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}trivial{/d} riddle: the Vizsier wants his sentence carried out.{/n}
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah stares at the remains of he who was once her brother in service.{/n} "Truly, it is better to die for Him than to live for yourself. This, he forgot."
  - After: {n}Kibellah eyes the body.{/n} "Better to die for Him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}But spinners are constantly renewing their wounds, while this man's look long since healed.{/n}
  - After: {n}But these scars healed long ago.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's vox-synthesiser springs to life with an indignant binharic trill.{/n} "I am registering this unit's intention to use the train tracks for purposes other than those intended by their design. I categorically demand that the unit's self-disposal be carried out using methods that do not violate the Catechism of Maintenance and Operation."
  - After: {n}Pasqal trills.{/n} "Self-disposal on tracks violates the Catechism of Maintenance."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man freezes a step away from oblivion, listens, then recoils and goes still once more.{/n}
  - After: {n}He freezes at the edge, then recoils.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man's wandering gaze turns to you as if he is expecting a question of some kind.{/n}
  - After: {n}He looks at you expectantly.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard barks out,{/n} "In the name of the dynasty, I command you to step away from the edge and explain the misdeed you were about to commit!"
  - After: {n}Abelard barks,{/n} "Step away and explain!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Just as you begin to hear the rumble of an approaching train, the man's gaze turns toward the tracks. He leans forward...{/n}
  - After: {n}A train nears. He leans toward the tracks...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man's faded eyes go wide as he notices Kibellah. His voice quivers:{/n} "You... Have you come to take me to the other side?"
  - After: {n}He sees Kibellah, trembling.{/n} "Are you here for me?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man lets out a dull groan and turns to look at the symbol again.{/n} "But then why... why is it here?"
  - After: {n}He groans at the symbol.{/n} "Then why is it here?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It's a symbol of the Bloodspun Web. I come here every watch, but it hasn't been here before now. I guess today must be a special day." {n}He smiles strangely.{/n}
  - After: "A Bloodspun Web symbol. New today." {n}He smiles strangely.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There were plenty of reasons. I sowed death. I offered Him the souls of the most pleasing men and women I could find because it kindled my passions. I killed well-off crewmen who didn't deserve their wealth, and I took their thrones. I killed enforcers who looked into my eyes without fear — because I wanted to be feared! I revelled in bloodshed. I betrayed the Tenets. I realised it, but I couldn't help it... because I enjoyed it."
  - After: "I killed for pleasure: rich crewmen, fearless enforcers. I betrayed the Tenets."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_Default/LT_Beggars/LT_Beggars_dialogue

  - Before: "Praished be the Lord Captain!" {n}The poor descend on the alms like a pack of gutter rats, each one scurrying off to their own corner with what they grabbed.{/n}

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_Default/LT_BlindMan/LT_BlindMan_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I did not mean to alarm you. I simply wish to learn more about my people's lives."
  - After: "Don't be alarmed. I'm learning about my people."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Throw a strip of dried ration meat into his mug] "Here. Have something to eat."
  - After: [Throw a strip of dried ration meat into his mug] "Eat."
- **Player**
  - Before: "How does a blind old man manage to survive in a place like this?"
  - After: "How does a blind man survive here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is that junk you are making such an effort to hide?"
  - After: "What junk are you hiding?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Place a stack of ration cards in his mug] "Perhaps a gift for you will convince you to show me?"
  - After: [Place a stack of ration cards in his mug] "A gift, to persuade you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius. And you will show me whatever I tell you to show me."
  - After: "I'm Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius. Show me what I ask."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Kill the old man] "I grow tired of you."
  - After: [Kill the old man] "I tire of you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "There, next to you — weapons are usually transported in crates like those. I want to look inside."
  - After: "Those crates carry weapons. Let me look."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will simply look into that crate of yours. I will not take anything."
  - After: "I'll just look in the crate. I won't take anything."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}An old man in pitiful rags listens intently to the sound of your footsteps. A stinking piece of cloth is wrapped around his eyes, with greenish pus oozing out from under it. The old man lays his trembling hands protectively on the heap of junk that serves as his bed as well as his table. An empty beggar's mug makes a clinking sound next to his withered leg.{/n}
  - After: {n}A blind, rag-clad old man guards a heap of junk.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Rogue... Trader?" {n}The old man's face widens in astonishment, and he bows reverently, whispering,{/n} "I've waited... I've waited for so long, hoping to one day serve you, Lord Captain! The crate—"
  - After: "Rogue Trader?" {n}He bows.{/n} "I've waited to serve you! The crate—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The old man ravenously sinks his remaining teeth into the meat's tough fibres, but soon gives up on chewing and swallows the piece whole.{/n} "Could this be a true miracle of the Emperor? Or... is it just another dream?"
  - After: {n}He swallows the meat whole.{/n} "A miracle of the Emperor? Or a dream?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The void rats gnawed them out while I was asleep. And the sewer water my wounds were washed with was infected, turns out. The pain became a stinging feeling that wouldn't go away... And only got worse."
  - After: "Void rats ate them while I slept. The wounds got infected."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "People help me. Good people. Not-so-good ones, too." {n}He sweeps his withered arm vacantly around the slum.{/n}
  - After: "People help me. Good and bad." {n}He gestures vaguely.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The old man sinks his chipped fingernails into the rotted crate.{/n} "I heard the sound of your footsteps. The creak of your well-made soles against the metal is pleasing to the ear. You walk with confidence. You have everything you need. Don't take everything from this old man who has nothing."
  - After: {n}He clutches the crate.{/n} "You have everything. Don't take mine."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The old man scoops up the greasy cards, grins happily, and moves aside to count them, smacking his lips.{/n} "Benefactor! Nourisher! May the Lord Captain protect you!"
  - After: {n}He grabs the cards, grinning.{/n} "Benefactor! May the Lord Captain protect you!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The old man carries on listening to the clamour of the slum for a long time, whispering an almost silent prayer to the God-Emperor all the while.{/n}
  - After: {n}He listens to the slum, praying silently.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The skin shrunken around the man's hunched skeleton is almost translucent. That heap of junk really is likely to be everything he owns in this life.{/n}
  - After: {n}Skin and bone. The junk is likely all he owns.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, the only thing he has to share with you is a long list of infectious diseases. May I offer you a breathing mask?" {n}Abelard produces an actual gold-encrusted mask from his pouch.{/n}
  - After: "He offers only diseases. A mask, Lord Captain?" {n}Abelard offers a gilded one.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The old man shakes his grey head vehemently.{/n} "Take me for a fool, do you? What would the Rogue Trader be doing down here? Liar!"
  - After: {n}He shakes his head.{/n} "The Rogue Trader, down here? Liar!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Glaito's whole body leans in the direction of the crates sitting next to the man, and Solomorne directs your attention toward them with a nod.{/n} "Some curious things he has stored in there. I suggest you give the old man a good shake and see if he is as harmless as he wants to appear."
  - After: {n}Glaito strains toward the crates.{/n} "Shake him. See how harmless he is."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}No matter how innocuous or wretched the old man's appearance, it will take more than that to deceive you. Trained always to look for {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Arbitrator}criminal intent{/d} first and foremost, you cast a suspicious eye at the crates — these look too much like reinforced containers used for transporting weapons.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your eye for {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Arbitrator}criminal intent{/d} spots it: those are weapon crates.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No!" {n}The old man shakes his head furiously.{/n} "Retribution! You won't escape His retribution for this!"
  - After: "No!" {n}He shakes his head.{/n} "His retribution awaits!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your people? Could it be... Our Lord Captain, our benefactor, is it really you?" {n}The old man looks shocked.{/n} "Our gracious {mf|lord|lady}, we know you well! Your charity gets us through the day, and we pray for you always! But what are you doing down in this... Please, hurry away before they know you're here! They are plotting something terrible. This crate, it's where they hide their—"
  - After: "Our benefactor?" {n}He's shocked.{/n} "We pray for you, {mf|lord|lady}! Hurry, they're plotting. This crate hides their—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Or rather, that is what someone with no experience in the art of {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}smuggling{/d} would think if they were in your place. Hiding contraband in caches without leaving a watcher is a short-sighted gamble, as there is always a chance that some lucky scoundrel or patrolman might stumble upon the goods. Someone suitably repulsive and miserable, like this old man, often acts as the perfect deterrent.{/n}
  - After: {n}Or so a novice at {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}smuggling{/d} would think. A repulsive wretch makes the perfect cache guard.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Weapons?" {n}The old man's voice sounds frightened and pitiful.{/n} "How would something like that wind up in our bottom-of-the-bilge compartment?"
  - After: "Weapons?" {n}He cowers.{/n} "Down here?"

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_Default/LT_EnforcerChief/LT_EnforcerChief_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "What is the situation on the lower decks?"
  - After: "How are the lower decks?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do the lower deck officers think of Jocasta Sauerback?"
  - After: "What do officers here think of Jocasta Sauerback?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Not every voidship can boast of its own railway."
  - After: "Few voidships have a railway."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Cult of the Bloodspun Web has a presence in this compartment, does it not?"
  - After: "The Bloodspun Web is present here, isn't it?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The rabble cause you no problems, I hope?"
  - After: "The rabble give you no trouble?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am only going to ask this once. How did wretches from the lower decks get their hands on a crate of autoguns?"
  - After: "I'll ask once. How did lower deck wretches get a crate of autoguns?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Mutinous rabble? How paranoid of you."
  - After: "Mutinous rabble? Paranoid."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Be steadfast in your duty, Captain Frensoe."
  - After: "Stay steadfast, Captain Frensoe."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have learned enough."
  - After: "I've learned enough."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am satisfied in all regards. Carry on in your duty as before."
  - After: "I'm satisfied. Carry on as before."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I came across a drawing of a worker in a red mask. What does it mean?"
  - After: "I saw a drawing of a worker in a red mask. Meaning?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Don't be shy, Frensoe. Just tell me what you think we could do to make those people's lives at least a little better."
  - After: "Don't be shy, Frensoe. How could we improve their lives?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Medicine is in such short supply that people are killing each other for it. Perhaps there is a way out?"
  - After: "People kill for scarce medicine. Any way out?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Those are excellent ideas! I commend you, Captain. Get it done."
  - After: "Excellent ideas, Captain. Do it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I hereby offer you my assistance, Captain. I shall conduct an inspection and then share my thoughts on how to change this place for the better."
  - After: "I'll help, Captain: inspect, then advise how to improve this place."
- **Player**
  - Before: "A secret cell of mutant conspirators was operating in your jurisdiction. They were armed with autoguns and refused to surrender peacefully."
  - After: "A cell of armed mutant conspirators operated here. They refused to surrender."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Rejoice, Frensoe, for the Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} has deigned to deal with your problems! Rest assured, I will provide you some crucial guidance once I am done inspecting the bay."
  - After: "Rejoice, Frensoe, the Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} will fix your problems! Guidance after my inspection."

  - After: "The bay doesn't interest me. I'm here on business, briefly."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have finished inspecting this bay."
  - After: "I've finished inspecting this bay."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The workers are to be provided with everything they need to service the freight line properly. Food and medicine will be delivered to the bay, and you are to demote any enforcers found to be abusing their authority to the status of workers."
  - After: "Give workers what they need to run the freight line. Deliver food and medicine, and demote abusive enforcers to workers."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Let's consider these two problems: not enough food in the vat and too many starving people around it. What could you do?"
  - After: "Too little food in the vat, too many starving around it. What could you do?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Enforcers have been appropriating ration cards from workers returning from their shifts. Why is that? Are you short on provisions?"
  - After: "Enforcers take ration cards from workers after shifts. Why? Short on provisions?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Smile insinuatingly] "The source of all of this compartment's woes are hunger and poverty, which are driving those people to commit petty crimes. I am sure you would have done something by now, but there are certain rules you have to follow that are simply too... limiting. Isn't that right?"
  - After: [Smile insinuatingly] "Hunger and poverty drive petty crime here. You'd have acted, but the rules are too... limiting. Right?"

  - Before: "Only harsh measures will bring order to the bay. Establish an execution quota, strip all corrupt enforcers of their rank, and burn away all crime. Any idlers are to be given a job, and if they cannot do anything useful, servitorise them. Organise mandatory sermons and spread the word of faith."
  - After: "Only harsh measures work. Execution quotas, strip corrupt enforcers, burn out crime. Idlers work or get servitorised. Mandatory sermons."
- **Player**
  - Before: "He is more than just a legend. He is real, and he is a dangerous rebel."
  - After: "He's no legend. He's real, a dangerous rebel."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Roll your eyes] "The fantasies of the common folk... 'Protector of the poor'? Please."
  - After: [Roll your eyes] "'Protector of the poor'? Please."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The cultural heritage of this compartment is... interesting."
  - After: "Interesting local heritage."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I find these sentiments disconcerting. Stay vigilant, Frensoe."
  - After: "Disconcerting. Stay vigilant, Frensoe."

  - Before: "It seems you were prepared for my visit. How did you and Sauerback know I was coming now?"
  - After: "You expected me. How did you and Sauerback know?"

  - Before: "Why are you worried? Is there a problem with this compartment?"
  - After: "Why worried? A problem here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am here to inspect the entire compartment. I am curious to see how people on the lower decks live."
  - After: "I'll inspect the whole compartment. I'm curious how the lower decks live."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Were you in a shootout?"
  - After: "A shootout?"
- **Player**

  - Before: "Learn from this mistake, and ensure that no 'Nemesite' is ever allowed to appear again."

  - Before: "What do you know about the death cultists?"

  - After: "My reasons are none of your business."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I encountered mutants in the pestilence pit. They seemed to be under the influence of unholy powers."
  - After: "Mutants in the pestilence pit, under unholy influence."
- **Player**
  - Before: "There were thieves in one of the technical rooms. I have already dispatched them."
  - After: "I dispatched thieves in a technical room."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Foreman believes that the people who stole the autoguns are connected to Nemesite."
  - After: "The Foreman ties the autogun thieves to Nemesite."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It seems to me that there is a mutiny brewing in your compartment."
  - After: "A mutiny is brewing here."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Now you see the whole picture. Deal with this menace."
  - After: "Now you see it all. Deal with it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The details are irrelevant."
  - After: "Details are irrelevant."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Being assigned here seems almost like exile. Did you commit an infraction?"
  - After: "This post seems like exile. An infraction?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you not take issue with death cultists killing people on your territory?"
  - After: "Death cultists killing on your turf doesn't bother you?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A sturdily built man with an augmented jaw stands at attention. The dark circles under his eyes speak to many sleepless nights, but his voice is loud and spirited:{/n} "Welcome to Freight Hub LD-987/A14, Lord Captain! I am Eddock Frensoe, captain of the enforcers in lower deck bay LD-A14. The Master-at-Arms has assigned me to be your liaison for the duration of your stay here."
  - After: {n}A tired, jaw-augmented man salutes.{/n} "Welcome to Freight Hub LD-987/A14, Lord Captain! Eddock Frensoe, enforcer captain, your liaison."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Most of the locals unload trains and sort provisions. We give maintenance jobs to the more capable ones. The rest... are reserve workforce. Whenever crew are lost on a deck, we find replacements from among those rats. And if extra hands are needed anywhere else, there are always more than enough volunteers eager to work for rations. They even queue for jobs."
  - After: "They unload trains and sort provisions. The rest are reserve labour, begging for work."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Hub LD-987/A14 connects the lower decks' freight, residential, and artillery bays. Our task is to monitor the flow of the labour force and prevent supply disruption between bays."
  - After: "It links freight, residential and artillery bays. We keep labour and supplies moving."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Traffic controllers. They're {g|Encyclopedia:Technomat}technomats{/g} trained by priests of the {g|Encyclopedia:CultMechanicus}Machine Cult{/g} to keep the sacred cogitators in working order and prevent train collisions. The consequences of an accident like that... would be easy to imagine. Especially if one of the trains were carrying macro-cannon ordnance."
  - After: "{g|Encyclopedia:Technomat}Technomats{/g} of the {g|Encyclopedia:CultMechanicus}Machine Cult{/g}. They prevent collisions, even with ordnance trains."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Mistress Sauerback possesses all the personal and professional qualities required to lead the enforcers efficiently, Lord Captain!" {n}He enunciates each word with pride, but you note drops of sweat on his brow.{/n}
  - After: "Mistress Sauerback is fully qualified!" {n}He sweats.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That is true. Usually higher-class ships are the ones that get trains, but it's far from the greatest thing a Rogue Trader's {g|Encyclopedia:WarrantGlossary}Warrant{/g} can see done. The credit here goes to Lady Theodora's predecessor, on whose orders the Adeptus Mechanicus assisted in birthing this miracle of sacred engineering from the womb of the dynasty's flagship."
  - After: "True. Lady Theodora's predecessor used the {g|Encyclopedia:WarrantGlossary}Warrant{/g} to have the Mechanicus build it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh, another thing the bastards do on a regular basis is build their shacks in front of service tunnel entrances. That has delayed the arrival of infernus brigades during several emergencies, and caused air and power supply problems in adjacent bays. We burn those saboteurs along with their shacks, but they just keep pressing on regardless."
  - After: "They build shacks over service tunnels, blocking emergency crews and air. We burn them. They persist."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That is correct. The enforcers... do not bar them from carrying out their sacred duties..." {n}He scowls.{/n} "As irregular as it is to have armed crew members set up a secret hideout forbidden to the enforcers, and that they can go around dispensing bloody justice."
  - After: "Yes. We don't interfere..." {n}He scowls.{/n} "Irregular, armed killers with a secret hideout."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To the best of my knowledge, being paranoid is practically a requirement in our line of work. In any case, the rabble are always plotting. Take my word for it."
  - After: "Paranoia is part of the job. The rabble always plot."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Always at your service, Lord Captain!"
  - After: "At your service, Lord Captain!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Autoguns?" {n}Purple spots appear on his face.{/n} "Warp take me, they couldn't have bypassed the security of a munitions train and walked away with the cargo without help from someone in the enforcers. I executed one reprobate who was trafficking in weapons not too long ago, but even that moron wasn't so greedy and stupid as to arm the rabble with autoguns. So there is another who dishonours the enforcers' uniform. I will find the maggot and shove their head under a passing train."
  - After: "Autoguns?" {n}He flushes.{/n} "Then an enforcer helped. I'll find the traitor and shove their head under a train."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A deep furrow cuts through the captain's forehead. Then his eyes light up with a spark of curiosity, and he says tentatively,{/n} "We could... shorten the queue to the vat. And fill the vat... with the acquired resource. While they are alive and... have nutritional value." {n}He casts an enquiring look at you.{/n}
  - After: {n}He brightens.{/n} "We could... fill the vat with the queue. While they're still nutritious." {n}He looks to you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The captain frowns.{/n} "It's a figure of local legend, known as Nemesite, protector of the poor and oppressed. Ever since I was a child, desperate people have been drawing his portrait on the walls hoping to summon a defender to punish those who wronged them. We've had thirteen or so fools calling themselves 'Nemesite' over the past five years. We... disburdened ourselves of them, just to be sure."
  - After: {n}He frowns.{/n} "Nemesite, a legend, protector of the oppressed. Thirteen fools claimed the name in five years. We disposed of them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We are short on purified air. It currently goes through three sacred cycles of filtration but... that takes a long time. Would a single sacred cycle be... too egregious of a departure from the sanitation code? The circumstances being what they are..."
  - After: "Air is short. One filtration cycle instead of three?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We have faith healers in this bay practising superstition-based medicine that learned specialists have deemed to be useless at best. At present, enforcers are forbidding these quacks from healing people, but... lifting the ban on their absurd potions would somewhat alleviate the medicine shortage." {n}He stops, apparently surprised by his own boldness.{/n}
  - After: "Lift our ban on faith healers' potions?" {n}He's surprised at himself.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Inspired by your approval, Frensoe exclaims enthusiastically,{/n} "At once, Lord Captain!"
  - After: {n}Frensoe beams.{/n} "At once, Lord Captain!"

This compartment has always been a troublesome one, and the Master-at-Arms assigned me here because she thought highly of my merits. I am honoured to have earned Mistress Sauerback's trust."
  - After: {n}He shakes his head.{/n} "No, I was commended. Mistress Sauerback trusts me."

  - Before: "I most certainly do, Lord Captain. I've heard they choose their victims based on omens, and that just screams trouble to me. What if they decide to kill someone they're not supposed to? That's the only way we can protect the mindless herd from themselves."

  - Before: "Also employed here are an enforcer squad, a team of inferni, the clerks who keep cargo records, and a medicae officer. A fine chap whose medicine of choice is a bullet, may the God-Emperor forgive him."
  - After: "Also enforcers, inferni, clerks, and a trigger-happy medicae."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Just thinking about the prospect of walking around the lower decks wounds your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}refined senses{/d}. Your mind conjures vivid images of filth and poverty hanging in the air, seeping out of every crack, gnawing their way through your skin.{/n}

  - Before: {n}The captain nods eagerly.{/n} "Will do! We will increase the pressure on the untrustworthy element, conduct searches and interrogations to uncover criminals. We will herd the rabble to prayer services and remind them that Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s law is a stern one."

  - Before: "Lord Captain, {mf|sir|ma'am}!" {n}Eddock Frensoe stops perusing the reports on his data-slate.{/n} "I hope being in this bay has not caused you any inconvenience."
