- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He frowns slightly.{/n} "I will admit that I have been occasionally tempted to... overstep certain boundaries in the ship's regulations."
  - After: {n}He frowns.{/n} "I've been tempted to overstep regulations."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The captain shrugs.{/n} "Not much can be expected from simple-minded serfs."
  - After: {n}He shrugs.{/n} "Simple-minded serfs."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Master-at-Arms ordered us to be on standby after the Bloodspun Web openly invited you to visit their temple. We have been awaiting your arrival every day since then, Lord Captain."
  - After: "Since the Bloodspun Web invited you, we've been on standby."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The compartment has just enough food to avoid starvation, Lord Captain. This is why the enforcers are making sure that no serf has more cards than they're supposed to. They used to rip out people's tongues for it, but I reduced the punishment to simply beating the thieves and confiscating all their cards. The orders are to give these cards to workers who are starving due to a lack of work shifts — not that it helps them much, but it's better than nothing." {n}Frensoe scoffs.{/n} "Are there enforcers guilty of misappropriating the confiscated items? Yes. Do those caught stealing receive severe punishment? Absolutely."
  - After: "Food is barely enough, so we cap cards. I swapped tongue-ripping for beatings. Seized cards go to starving workers." {n}He scoffs.{/n} "Thieving enforcers get punished."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm sorry, Lord Captain, I do not. No one knows — the cultists are too adept at hiding and keeping their secrets. And it worries me that you might have to walk around the entire compartment looking for the temple."
  - After: "Nobody knows where it is."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The lower decks are not suitable for someone of your status. And it's not just the grime or the crowds of brutish labourers — I suspect that the entrance to the temple of death is hidden in some dark corner where you might encounter criminals or contagious outcasts. With the kind of riffraff that dwells there, you might even be attacked."
  - After: "The lower decks are beneath you. The temple likely hides among criminals and outcasts. You could be attacked."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He frowns.{/n} "To put it bluntly, although the bay performs its functions well, even its more civilised sections are sorely lacking in discipline. I was only assigned recently, so I haven't had time to straighten everything up, since doing so will require making some serious changes. I am not inventing excuses, Lord Captain — as the officer in charge, I accept full responsibility for what takes place in this compartment."
  - After: {n}He frowns.{/n} "The bay works but lacks discipline. I'm new. I take full responsibility."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Frensoe glances at you warily.{/n} "As you will, Lord Captain. Still, out of concern for your safety, I must warn you that you should avoid the farthest sections of the bay. They are ridden with disease, and the locals can be particularly unpleasant to deal with. With the kind of riffraff that dwells there, you might even be attacked."
  - After: {n}He looks wary.{/n} "As you will. Avoid the far sections. Disease, hostile locals."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Captain Frensoe has acquired a few wounds since your last conversation. Half of his ear is gone, and you notice that he is wearing bloodied bandages under his uniform. Seeing you, he quickly injects himself with a stimulant and straightens.{/n} "How may I serve you, Lord Captain?"
  - After: {n}Frensoe, wounded, injects a stimulant.{/n} "How may I serve, Lord Captain?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes, there's been a raid on a local gang. We've finally cleared out the scoundrels who were smuggling goods to neighbouring compartments. No one escaped." {n}Frensoe permits himself a brief smile of grim satisfaction.{/n}
  - After: "A raid on smugglers. None escaped." {n}He smiles grimly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes, Lord Captain. And as soon as my back has healed, I will repeat this punishment once for every so-called Nemesite we've had by my count."
  - After: "Yes. Then again for every Nemesite."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are too lenient on me, Lord Captain." {n}Frensoe sounds completely devastated.{/n}
  - After: "Too lenient, Lord Captain." {n}He's devastated.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Not much, but I'm always trying to learn more, given that they like to pay visits to my compartment." {n}Frensoe scratches his head, thinking.{/n} "The spinners honour the Emperor through death: they kill notorious reprobates and heretics. Sometimes they kill righteous folk, and other times even seemingly at random... Their rituals are morbid and their prayers are strange — anyone not initiated in their rites would struggle to make any sense of them."
  - After: "Little." {n}He thinks.{/n} "Spinners honour the Emperor through death: heretics, reprobates, sometimes the righteous or random folk. Morbid rites."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You... went to the pestilence pit. You. Into the pestilence pit." {n}Frensoe stares off into the distance as he speaks.{/n} "Pardon me, Lord Captain. I just can't even begin to find the words I would use if I had to tell the Master-at-Arms that you had perished in there." {n}He rubs his temple wearily.{/n} "The enforcers do regular checks to see if there are any dangerous blight-stricken rejects hiding at the bottom of the bay. I implore you, Lord Captain — leave this job to us."
  - After: "You went into the pestilence pit?" {n}He stares.{/n} "If you died there..." {n}He rubs his temple.{/n} "Leave that to us."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thieves... I just had an enforcer hanged for dealing with a local gang. I had hoped that the lesson had been learned." {n}Frensoe winces as if from pain.{/n} "By the Emperor, Lord Captain, why must you be so unconcerned with your own safety? It's our duty to find and shoot lawless scum. Throne, you are going to become the best enforcer in the bay at this rate!"
  - After: "I just hanged an enforcer for that." {n}He winces.{/n} "Throne, your safety, Lord Captain!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I can't argue with the fact that these people are truly devout and that they help to uphold order around here in their own way, but the sight of them still chills my blood."
  - After: "Devout, orderly, and chilling."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Frensoe avoids looking at Kibellah.{/n} "I do, Lord Captain. But the cult is authorised to exist on the ship, which means their activities down here are not to be interfered with."
  - After: {n}He avoids Kibellah's eyes.{/n} "I do. But the cult is authorised."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The threat of mutiny is always there, Lord Captain. We have uncovered several cells over the past month, although, admittedly, none of the traitors were armed with autoguns. We will redouble our efforts. The bastards will pay dearly for stealing our munitions."
  - After: "Always. Several cells this month, none with autoguns. They'll pay."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Foreman... You wouldn't believe the kinds of thugs he welcomes at his vat. I agree that sympathisers of Nemesite's anarchic cause may be involved in this outrage, but I don't trust that Foreman character. He knows everyone in the bay; he sees everything, but he never informs on one of his own. He only complains about problems I am already well aware of."
  - After: "The Foreman shelters thugs. He sees everything and never informs."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Frensoe lets out a menacing growl as his face fills with blood.{/n} "Who dared?"
  - After: {n}Frensoe flushes, growling.{/n} "Who dared?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Frensoe grinds his teeth in fury.{/n} "I will find them. Every single one of them. And I will destroy them all."
  - After: {n}He grinds his teeth.{/n} "I'll find and destroy them all."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The captain grumbles sullenly under his breath.{/n}
  - After: {n}The captain grumbles.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: {n}Cassia shivers.{/n} "Such ghastly places you describe... We are not headed there, are we, Lord Captain?"
  - After: {n}Cassia shivers.{/n} "We're not going there, are we?"
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Cass, knowing the Lord Captain, I wouldn't get my hopes up... Just think of it as an exotic outing."
  - After: "Cass, knowing the Lord Captain... think of it as an exotic outing."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "You treat most members of your own species as either a resource or a parasite. It is unsurprising that the world of humans is so filthy and dark."
  - After: "Your kind are resources or parasites to you. No wonder your world is dark."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Well, they stopped doing that recently, and what a relief it was for me. I couldn't exactly breathe easy with trained killers walking about."
  - After: "They stopped lately, thankfully."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Infernus Master salutes you cheerfully with his lho-stick.{/n} "Lord Captain, what an unexpected encounter! What brings you to this compartment? The famous cuisine and magnificent vistas, no doubt?"
  - After: {n}The Infernus Master salutes with his lho-stick.{/n} "Lord Captain! Here for the vistas?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I don't have the foggiest idea, and that's probably for the best. I have my hands full as it is."
  - After: "No idea. My hands are full."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm here to patch up Savage, locomotive number three, under the Tech-Priests' supervision. That old grump is my personal favourite on the entire freight line. Every couple of years, Savage gets mad: his boiler catches fire and starts spitting steam at the repairmen. Guess who they call to take care of him in these situations. The inferni, of course! And after I've done all the most dangerous work, that's when the iron brains come in. But that's all right. I love Savage."
  - After: "Fixing Savage, locomotive three, my favourite. Sometimes his boiler catches fire, and we inferni handle it before the Tech-Priests."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The stubborn machine does indeed seem remarkably similar to a wild beast. The roar of the mechanism resembles hoarse growling, and the scarlet glow of the lumens on the control panel makes you think of the malicious glare of a predator. The spirit of this machine is vicious, but strong and lively.{/n}
  - After: {n}The machine growls like a vicious, strong beast.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You know, that might be for the best. The dynasty needs a Rogue Trader, not a charred piece of ember."
  - After: "Wise. The dynasty needs a Rogue Trader, not an ember."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A deafening clang resounds from Savage's innards, and the train shudders underfoot, as if preparing to leap forward.{/n} "Whoa! Careful, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Don't let this monster smash us against the nearest wall."
  - After: {n}The train lurches.{/n} "Careful, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh, I refuse to believe Savage would dare scald the Lord Captain. He definitely should not."
  - After: "Savage wouldn't dare scald you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The panel before you is covered with technical runes, {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumens{/g}, and levers. The platform shakes with the boiler's mighty vibration as the iron beast beneath your feet growls and snorts ferociously.{/n}
  - After: {n}Runes, {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumens{/g} and levers. The beast growls underfoot.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "When he's in a good mood, the feeling you get standing at his levers and speeding down the freight line is indescribable... I envy those Tech-Priest drivers who get to operate him every day — the roar of the boiler, the wheels thumping like mad, and all that furious power pulsing in your hands, responding to the slightest movement. How about..." {n}There is a mischievous spark in Einrich's eyes.{/n} "...I introduce you?"
  - After: "When he's happy, driving him is indescribable." {n}Einrich's eyes spark.{/n} "Shall I introduce you?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "As you command. I do hope you're leaving with a favourable impression. Enjoy your walk! Meanwhile, I will take a ride on the freight line and see how our little rascal here behaves at full throttle."
  - After: "As you command. I'll take him down the line at full throttle."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Do you feel it? There is so much energy and defiance in him... This is a rocket, not a locomotive — unruly and enamoured with speed, but... quite willing to submit to a strong hand." {n}There is almost a loving tenderness in Einrich's voice.{/n} "Pull the lever toward you, smoothly but firmly. Then, pump the fuel with this command rune."
  - After: "Feel it? Speed-mad, but he yields to a strong hand." {n}He speaks tenderly.{/n} "Pull the lever firmly, then pump fuel with this rune."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A roguish gleam appears in his eyes.{/n} "You don't say?"
  - After: {n}He grins.{/n} "You don't say?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A torrent of steam bursts from the slit in front of your face, but Einrich deftly covers you with his shoulder. A moment later, you realise that you cannot hear a thing... Or rather, you hear only one thing: the roar of the engine, triumphant and powerful.{/n} "Looks like Savage has agreed not to kill us both. His Tech-Priest guardians will be pleased."
  - After: {n}Steam bursts; Einrich shields you. The engine roars triumphantly.{/n} "Savage agreed not to kill us."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Not quite, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I said Savage is not dangerous, but 'not dangerous' ends right here. He might just pull a stunt and bake us to death during the ride, and it would be better if the ship did not lose another Lord Captain."
  - After: "Not quite, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. He might bake us. The ship can't lose another Lord Captain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Everything is going to be all right. Savage would never fry me... Right, Savage?"
  - After: "He'd never fry me... Right, Savage?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "All hail the Lord Captain! You have subdued a mighty beast today. Now, I'm sure you have urgent business to attend to, and it's time for me to drive Savage down the line and see if he is feeling cranky."
  - After: "All hail the Lord Captain, beast-tamer! Now I'll drive Savage down the line."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet tilts her head to the side in confusion.{/n} "Is this still a conversation about mon-keigh machines, or something else?"
  - After: {n}Yrliet tilts her head.{/n} "Still about machines?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In that case, I hope that you at least had some fun. Good luck, Lord Captain."
  - After: "Hope you had fun. Good luck."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Einrich squints contentedly and whispers the litany of ignition before turning to you.{/n} "The machine is angry and refuses to obey. Right now, Savage is powered only by the auxiliary manoeuvring engine. We will need to start the main rotor if we want to take a trip down the freight line."
  - After: {n}Einrich whispers the litany of ignition.{/n} "He's angry. We must start the main rotor to ride."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Then you've picked the most unassuming part of it. My mentor used to say that a ship is like the human body. If that's the case, we are definitely standing inside its iron bowels right now."
  - After: "If a ship's a body, this is its iron bowels."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Put your hand on the big lever and gently give it a pull. Very gently!" {n}Einrich's face is focused, but his voice has not lost any of its playful cheer.{/n} "Savage does not like being hassled."
  - After: "Pull the big lever. Gently!" {n}He grins.{/n} "Savage hates being hassled."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A few erratic jolts shake the platform, and an indignant groan emanates from the depths of the machine. An intense shudder passes through the lever and into the palm of your hand, and there is a strange feeling of emptiness in your stomach. Savage's fiery heart is stirring.{/n}
  - After: {n}The lever shudders in your hand. Savage's fiery heart stirs.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Einrich lowers his eyes and grins.{/n} "Could I have wished for anything more, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"
  - After: {n}Einrich grins.{/n} "What more could I wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Savage lets out an angry rumble, and the boiler mounts rattle pitifully. One nut snaps off its threads and flies past your head toward the platform like a bullet. You hear a scream followed by panicked cries.{/n} "Another accident to your name, eh, Savage?" {n}Einrich quickly adjusts the lever, reducing the fuel supply.{/n}
  - After: {n}A nut flies past your head; someone screams.{/n} "Another accident, Savage?" {n}Einrich cuts the fuel.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A new explosion inside Savage shakes his iron body, causing your eyes to see double from the vibration.{/n} "Now you are feeling his real power. He can run down the entire freight line in a minute, given the chance... And kill everyone who rides him at that speed. Now, try applying some thrust to the main rotor — grab those paired levers and give them a firm tug."
  - After: {n}Savage shakes.{/n} "His real power. He'd kill riders at full speed. Now tug the paired levers for the main rotor."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "I have had experiences with mechanisms that preferred to be turned on quickly and boldly. I guess this engine has a different design." {n}Jae innocently runs a finger along the control panel.{/n}
  - After: "Mechanisms I've known liked a bold start." {n}Jae innocently strokes the panel.{/n}

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_Default/LT_KibellahRecruit/LT_KibellahRecruit_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Thank you for your assistance against the mutineers."
  - After: "Thanks for your help."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Perhaps you might help me find the entrance to your temple after all?"
  - After: "Help me find your temple?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have changed my mind. I will permit you to accompany my retinue."
  - After: "Join my retinue after all."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I must take my leave now."
  - After: "I must go."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is the situation on the lower decks?"
  - After: "How are the lower decks?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Watching time slip away. People never pause to consider how many breaths they have left to take before they feel the kiss of death. Ignorance... has its own form of beauty."
  - After: "Watching time slip. Ignorance is beautiful."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I was simply following the thread of the Web. For their time had come, and the Undying One reached out a hand to receive their souls."
  - After: "Their time had come."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My duty to the Undying One prevents me from interfering in the Vizsier's design. I cannot become the thread that guides you. But I can be at your side as you walk that path."
  - After: "I can't guide you. But I'll walk beside you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Bloodspun Web has heeded your orders. The spinners are no longer ushering souls to the other side. Not everyone in the cult was ready for the change, and the tunnel-dwellers were less ready still."
  - After: "The spinners obey you and kill no more. Not all accepted it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Walk with silent footsteps amid the whispers of the Undying One."
  - After: "Walk silently amid His whispers."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The weak and miserable grasp at the chance to live another watch. The strong and cruel threaten them with swift death. Neither realise that the end of the thread is true freedom from fear and pain."
  - After: "The weak cling to life. None see death is freedom."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Go forth and I will follow you."
  - After: "Go. I will follow."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The threads of our destinies have been woven together again. But for how long?"
  - After: "Our threads rejoin. For how long?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "They believed the Undying One had cursed them and revoked His mercy. They thought murderers and other wrongdoers now had free reign. Fools. There are many ways to serve Him without severing souls from bodies."
  - After: "They felt cursed. Fools. He can be served without killing."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_Default/LT_Oppressed/LT_Oppressed_dialogue

- **Player**

  - After: "Enforcers take workers' earnings after shifts?"

  - Before: [Strike the enforcer] "Consider yourself discharged, thief. Tomorrow you are to stand here and queue for a work assignment like the others."

  - Before: [Stop the enforcer] "I intend to hear this man out."
  - After: [Stop the enforcer] "I'll hear this man out."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Let the enforcer do his job] "Make it quick. I have places to be."
  - After: [Let the enforcer do his job] "Make it quick."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Kick the worker] "Out of my way, blasted filth!"
  - After: [Kick the worker] "Out of my way, filth!"

  - Before: [Address the enforcer] "Return the cards and do not dare abuse your position again."
  - After: [Address the enforcer] "Return the cards. Never abuse your post again."

  - After: [Address the worker] "Crimes get punished. I don't protect thieves."

  - After: [Leave] "No time for this."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Raise your voice] "The Imperium is surrounded by enemies! They are many, they are cunning, and they are spiteful! Who is to blame for your hungry days? They are! But we, the Emperor's faithful servants, are stronger than their scheming ways! We are steadfast! We will not yield! We will tighten our belts, stand as one, and prevail! Who is with me?"
  - After: [Raise your voice] "The Imperium's cunning, spiteful enemies are to blame for your hunger! But we, the Emperor's faithful, are stronger! We'll tighten our belts, stand as one, and prevail! Who is with me?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Add a note of sagely depth to your voice] "Society, you see, is much like a boot. Its toe proudly directs the foot of the Imperium forward, and yet it needs a sole to stand on. You are the sole, good people. That you are down here choking on dirt without ever seeing a sliver of light is not the result of someone's ill will, but rather, it is the logical order of the world. I hope that understanding this fact will help you make peace with your destiny and free you of all spite."
  - After: [Add a note of sagely depth to your voice] "Society is a boot. The toe leads the Imperium forward; you are the sole it stands on. Choking in the dirt isn't malice, just the world's logical order. Make peace with your destiny."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Gaze proudly and solemnly at the crowd] "Would I have achieved glory if I had complained about every hardship along my path? No! I pressed ever onward in spite of all the adversity! So must you — and we will remember your names for it!"
  - After: [Gaze proudly and solemnly at the crowd] "Did I win glory by complaining? No! I pressed on despite adversity. So must you, and we'll remember your names!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You both deserve punishment. Strip the arbitrary enforcer of his rank and give lashes to the thief."
  - After: "Both deserve punishment. Strip the enforcer's rank and lash the thief."
- **Twelve**
  - Before: {n}The battered worker throws himself at your feet and touches the toe of your boot with his dirty palms.{/n} "Your gracious {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Hand of the God-Emperor! Save your unworthy servant!"
  - After: {n}A battered worker grovels.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Save me!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A murmur of discontent breaks out among the gawkers who have gathered around. None of the other workers dare come closer, but the anger on their faces is plain to see.{/n}
  - After: {n}Onlookers mutter angrily.{/n}
- **Irritated Enforcer**
  - Before: "We appropriate nothing. We just monitor and redistribute," {n}the enforcer mutters gloomily.{/n} "The rabble are a lying and thieving lot. We have instructions to stay alert for people holding more than the standard amount of ration cards. To prevent supply embezzlement and famine."
  - After: "We just redistribute," {n}he mutters.{/n} "Rabble steal. Extra cards mean embezzlement."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A sullen, red-bearded man with keen black eyes draws your attention. His oddly piercing gaze seemed to size you up the whole time you were speaking, but now he has hastened to conceal himself behind the gawkers. The next thing you know, you are watching him hurry deeper into the tunnels.{/n}
  - After: {n}A red-bearded man who was watching you slips into the tunnels.{/n}
- **Twelve**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I work hard, never even take breaks to rest, and all I earn is seven ration cards with fifteen mouths to feed back home! The enforcers shake me down every shift, just like they do every other honest hard worker who—"
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, seven cards for fifteen mouths, and enforcers shake us down—"
- **Irritated Enforcer**
  - Before: "Enough whining! You and your pals lifted a box of nutribars a few watches ago, and two canisters of water before that. I didn't beat the life out of you because I took pity on you, and this is the thanks I get?"
  - After: "Enough! You stole nutribars and water. I spared you!"
- **Twelve**
  - Before: "I didn't do them in, it was an acc—" {n}The worker stops himself, cowers, and whimpers,{/n} "They got their heads bashed in by crates! The dead don't need rations!"
  - After: "It was an acc—" {n}He cowers.{/n} "Crates fell on them! The dead don't eat!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The clamour rises, becoming too persistent, deafening, suffocating... Then a baton lands a crunching blow somewhere in the crowd, and everyone quiets down.{/n}
  - After: {n}The clamour swells until a baton cracks. Silence.{/n}
- **Irritated Enforcer**
  - Before: {n}The enforcer hastens to remove one of his gloves, then starts shining your boot.{/n} "Almost d-done, Lord Captain!"
  - After: {n}The enforcer shines your boot.{/n} "Almost d-done!"
- **Twelve**
  - Before: {n}With a crunch, your boot breaks the bridge of the unfortunate man's nose.{/n} "I'b sorry, please, I'b sorry! It hurts so buch..."
  - After: {n}Your boot breaks his nose.{/n} "I'b sorry!"
- **Twelve**
  - Before: {n}The terrified man glances furtively at the enforcer, who is grinning.{/n}
  - After: {n}He glances at the grinning enforcer.{/n}
- **Twelve**
  - Before: "May the God-Emperor protect you and all of House von Valancius, Lord Captain!"
  - After: "God-Emperor protect you, Lord Captain!"
- **Irritated Enforcer**
  - Before: {n}The enforcer hisses at the worker vindictively,{/n} "Oh yes, Twelve. This time I'm gonna break thirteen of your fingers and ribs, as a lesson to your slimy accomplices."
  - After: {n}The enforcer hisses,{/n} "Twelve, I'll break thirteen of your fingers."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your inspiring visage, just like the one they used for the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Glory}propaganda poster{/d}, sends the serfs into a frenzy of rapturous cries. You hear them channelling all their hopes to overcome the odds just as you did. Even the beaten man stares at you with a wistful smile on his lips.{/n}
  - After: {n}Like your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Glory}propaganda poster{/d}, you send the serfs into rapture.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Alas, the ungrateful rabble is incapable of fathoming the sheer grandeur of your views on social structures. Blinking their ignorant eyes dully, the serfs continue to stare at you without proper respect.{/n}

  - Before: {n}The worker snarls at the enforcer, who has suddenly gone pale.{/n} "Didn't expect that, now did you? Once my back stops hurting... we'll see how brave you are without your baton."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The discharged enforcer, surrounded by spiteful leers, glowers at the crowd as the beaten worker laughs uproariously, seemingly far more pleased with the other's misfortune than troubled by his own sentence.{/n}

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_Default/LT_Outcasts/LT_Outcasts_dialogue

  - After: "Why did you kill this man?"

  - Before: "I am the Lord Captain of this ship. On your knees, insolent scum!"
  - After: "I'm the Lord Captain. Kneel, scum!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "The ship will be a little cleaner without you."

  - Before: "You need medicine and food. I shall have them brought to you."

  - Before: {n}The specimens before you must be the most repellent inhabitants in the compartment — they are covered in sores and bald patches glistening with pus, and the stench of unwashed bodies brings a tear to your eye. One of them glowers at you and grunts,{/n} "Wotcha want?"

  - After: {n}He bites the throne.{/n} "Don't expect thanks."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What the..." {n}The man breaks off, and then his ugly face spreads into a sly grin, and his numerous sores begin to fill with pus.{/n} "It's true, isn't it? Yes... Someone is watching over us, keeping us safe. How did I not realise it before?"

  - Before: {n}Grinning, the leader spits out,{/n} "For the crime of wealth. That dead bastard had rations and fuel cells. We'll trade them for porridge."
  - After: {n}The leader spits,{/n} "For wealth. Rations and fuel cells, for porridge."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The outcasts look at one another and burst into hoarse, gurgling cackles.{/n} "The Lord Captain in our shithole! And I'm Saint Drusus, and here's my rigalia!" {n}The man exposes an armpit riddled with boils.{/n}

- **Cassia**
  - Before: {n}Cassia lets out a faint sigh, hastily covering her face with her hands.{/n} "Gracious Emperor... Why are we talking to these horrible people?"
  - After: {n}Cassia covers her face.{/n} "Why are we talking to them?"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta towers over the freak, looking immaculate and unaffected.{/n} "Even meeting wretched heretics such as this brings me joy. Wiping out even a drop of corruption is still a worthy deed."
  - After: {n}Argenta is unmoved.{/n} "Purging corruption is a joy."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard attentively holds out a snow-white handkercher to her.{/n} "I fear, Lady Cassia, that these and many other questions will be left unanswered."
  - After: {n}Abelard offers a handkercher.{/n} "Unanswerable, Lady Cassia."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The mutant bares the black stumps that are his teeth.{/n} "We'll gut you and trade what you have on you for a pile of scran. Hey, outcasts, come on up if you want a share in the spoils!"
  - After: {n}He bares black stumps.{/n} "We'll gut you for scran. Outcasts, come!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The longer you stare at the man, the more deviations from the human form you detect. Wretches such as this, disfigured by genetic abnormalities and disease, are the perfect breeding ground for true corruption.{/n}
  - After: {n}Such deformed wretches breed true corruption.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The outcast licks his lips and you see a tongue studded with small, underdeveloped teeth. This is no disease, but an obvious mutation.{/n}
  - After: {n}His tongue has tiny teeth. A mutation.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man bares his teeth malevolently.{/n} "Will you now? We know your kindness — you'll douse us with poison and leave us to die. So we don't sully your ship."
  - After: {n}He snarls.{/n} "Your kindness? Poison."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If we're blessed, then we can live in this hole. We can live... and share our blessings." {n}The mutant's gaze lingers on you, his eyes glistening with slime.{/n} "Thank you."
  - After: "Blessed, we can live... and share it." {n}His slimy eyes linger.{/n} "Thank you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You detect a note of hysteria in the vagrants' laughter. The fingers of many are convulsively trembling. And there is something in the fearless way they look at you, an indifference to death... too strange and unnatural.{/n}
  - After: {n}Hysterical laughter, trembling fingers, unnatural calm about death.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}From the vagrants' mouths comes the most repulsive laughter you have ever heard.{/n}
  - After: {n}Repulsive laughter.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Mould-eaters. Outcasts. Folk who have no place even among the lowest of the low. Some were born that way, some were driven out to keep them from spreading the contagion. The Foreman won't let us near the vat, the enforcers try to shoot us on sight. As if it's our fault that we were born in a terrible place... We are worms in the rotten belly of this ship, fodder for disease."
  - After: "Mould-eaters, below the lowest. Born so, or cast out as contagious. Barred from the vat, shot on sight. Worms in the ship's belly."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_Default/LT_Pariah/LT_Pariah_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Why are you wearing chains and a mask? You haven't escaped from the enforcers, have you?"
  - After: "Why the chains and mask? Escaped?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is this repulsive place? Do you live here?"
  - After: "What foul place is this?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Peer into the darkness] "I cannot fathom what I am meant to see here..."
  - After: [Peer into the darkness] "What am I meant to see?"

  - Before: "You are insane. Out of my sight!"
  - After: "You're insane. Begone!"
- **Player**

  - After: "That blood symbol: part of the Song of Trailing Blood?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A figure in decaying tatters is rocking to and fro, muttering indistinctly in several different voices, occasionally breaking into hoarse laughter. As you come closer, she freezes and turns slowly to look at you. An ugly, rusted mask covers her face.{/n} "Are you... here to take Zdena to the other side? No. No no no."
  - After: {n}A rust-masked woman mutters.{/n} "Here to take Zdena beyond? No no."

  - Before: "You're just wandering around in the dark. Looking for the light... but it's nowhere to be found. Do you really not see it?"
  - After: "Seeking light in the dark. Don't you see?"

  - Before: {n}The woman starts chanting hurriedly:{/n}
"She wandered an eternity in dark,
yet was consoled. Web foretold:
Undying One's blood-secrets glowed,
a light to guide her faithful fold.
But threads must end. And so the spider
did that which was owed:
her life and death to ship bestowed..."
  - After: {n}She chants:{/n}
"In dark she roamed;
blood-secrets glowed
to guide her fold.
The spider paid what's owed:
her life and death to ship bestowed..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Old Zdena. Zdena the Outcast. Zdena the Mad. Zdena the Disaster. Zdena the Curse. Zdena the Spurned." {n}The woman hugs her arms to her chest and starts cackling loudly. Broken chains clink at her emaciated wrists and neck.{/n} "A ghost of the past? A shadow of the present? Only the Undying One knows. He alone..."
  - After: "Zdena the Mad." {n}She cackles; chains clink.{/n} "Only the Undying One knows what Zdena is."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman scratches her neck nervously. You note her deformed fingers, ravaged by some unknown disease.{/n} "Here, where the unfortunate meet their undeath. Here, a dumping ground for the bodies of those the Undying One rejects. Here, where pestilence dwells. Zdena welcomes them all. Talks to their ghosts. Here, where Zdena... lives? Yes. That sounds right."
  - After: {n}She scratches diseased fingers.{/n} "The Undying One's rejects are dumped here. Zdena talks to their ghosts."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Ah, these. Gifts, they are. The chains clink to announce Zdena's approach. For others to hear." {n}She slides her disease-darkened palm down the rough, rusted metal of her mask.{/n} "They hide, fearful of becoming like Zdena. Afraid of losing face... ha ha ha!"
  - After: "Chains warn others." {n}She strokes the mask.{/n} "Losing face... ha!"

  - After: "You can't hear them?" {n}She laughs.{/n} "They dislike visitors."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Zdena breaks into hysterical laughter.{/n} "You'll be back! Everyone who's looking for something comes back. Or... do they? Why come back when you've found what you were seeking?"
  - After: {n}She laughs.{/n} "Seekers always come back! Or not?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You peer into the darkness, and are gradually able to make out the outlines of objects hidden in the shadows. Rotting corpses. Rough walls. The twitching death throes of infected people left here to die. You see no light in this place, only more darkness and despair.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "You don't see!" {n}She tears off rags and skin.{/n} "Become the ship's blood, like Zdena!"

  - After: "Zdena will show you. Come!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman turns away and starts talking to someone only her eyes can see.{/n}
  - After: {n}She talks to someone unseen.{/n}

  - After: {n}Ulfar grips his amulet.{/n} "Spirits gnawed her mind. Madness spreads."

  - After: {n}Zdena laughs.{/n} "Yes! The song... Listen!"

  - After: "She's ill, Lord Captain. Leave her."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}She laughs again.{/n} "And you'll see, you'll see if you learn to see! Look into the darkness, look, look!"
  - After: {n}She laughs.{/n} "Look into the darkness!"

If one were to {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}interpret{/d} this entire mystical search as a repetition of the saint's journey, then the logical conclusion is that you are supposed to sacrifice yourself — to merge with the blood that has drenched the flagship from bow to stern.{/n}
  - After: {n}The final test: sacrifice. {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}Interpreted{/d} as the saint's journey, you must give yourself to the flagship's blood.{/n}

  - Before: {n}The flute player smiles mysteriously and brings the flute to his lips. A simple, brisk melody pours out of the instrument, the glum faces of workers and traders soften a little, and the tunnels around you seem less squalid than before. Long after the music has stopped, many continue to whistle the unassuming ditty.{/n}
  - After: {n}His brisk melody softens glum faces; many whistle it long after.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You manage even better this time. You shout at the rat, nearly prompting it to hide in the hole along with the ball — and yet, a moment later, the game ends with the ball stuck in a dead end once again.{/n}
  - After: {n}You shout the rat nearly into the hole, but the ball sticks again.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}The Interrogator's lip curls, but he remains silent, his icy gaze not leaving the man.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Interrogator stares icily, silent.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "This flute player is not as simple as he pretends to be, {name}. I am most curious to know what he's really doing here. I will have him monitored."
  - After: "He's not as simple as he seems, {name}. I'll have him monitored."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The people cast their eyes down in unison, their intent gazes threatening to burn new holes in their worn-out shoes. Their haggard faces show fear, but not remorse.{/n}
  - After: {n}The people look down, fearful but unrepentant.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The people stare shamefacedly at the floor like guilty children. One of the elders in a tattered robe reaches for the homemade Aquila around his neck, whispering a penitential prayer.{/n}
  - After: {n}The people look down in shame. An elder prays.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The people whisper excitedly as they discuss Twelve's miraculous rescue. The crowd looks at you in awe.{/n}
  - After: {n}The crowd whispers of Twelve's rescue, awed.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The people murmur their halting agreement with your words. There is not an ounce of sincerity in this rumbling — the rabble simply does not dare challenge the words of the Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself}.{/n}
  - After: {n}The crowd murmurs insincerely, fearing the Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself}.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The flute player bows his head so low you cannot see his face.{/n} "My humble flute is not worthy of singing the Lord Captain's tune. But since it is your will, I will compose a new melody. I hope it will be so good that it will be heard on every deck."
  - After: {n}He bows low.{/n} "My flute is unworthy, but I'll compose your melody for every deck."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The flute player smiles regretfully.{/n} "I think the song just died. But I won't despair — life always suggests new melodies that people will like."
  - After: {n}He smiles regretfully.{/n} "The song just died. There'll be others."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The flute player's clear eyes widen in surprise. Then, with an open and friendly smile, he says,{/n} "Many a grand story of the Lord Captain's generosity is told, and, I swear on my own flute, today I will add another! To a fortune peddler, the Lord Captain's grace is a gift from fate itself!" {n}He applauds you with gratitude, and the workers timidly join in.{/n}
  - After: {n}He smiles, surprised.{/n} "Another tale of the Lord Captain's generosity!" {n}Workers applaud.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It's simple: on this board, you play with fate. Choose a ball and give it to Bolts, my rat. If she rolls your ball into the pocket marked in red within three minutes, you win. If she doesn't, you lose. Simple."
  - After: "Give Bolts, my rat, a ball. If she sinks it in the red pocket within three minutes, you win."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Perhaps you would like to trade us some of that captain's fortune of yours, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?" {n}The flute player bows respectfully and gestures at the game board. The crowd buzzes with anticipation.{/n}
  - After: "Care to trade some of that captain's fortune, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?" {n}He gestures at the board.{/n}

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_Default/LT_Thieves/LT_Thieves_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell me why I shouldn't execute you on the spot."
  - After: "Why shouldn't I execute you now?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Abelard, help these wretches realise the full extent of their unenviable position."
  - After: "Abelard, explain their position to these wretches."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, and you will explain what is going on here."
  - After: "I am Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius. Explain this."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Who I am does not matter. What are you doing here?"
  - After: "Never mind who I am. What are you doing?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Today is your lucky day — put down what you hoped to steal and walk away."
  - After: "Lucky day — drop the loot and walk away."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I suppose you may be of some use. I shall permit you to take a few of the more basic weapons and leave. Serve the ship well."
  - After: "You may be useful. Take a few basic weapons and go. Serve the ship."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "Criminals on my ship have a single fate — death."
  - After: [Attack] "Criminals on my ship die."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Take a closer look at the suspicious individuals]
  - After: [Examine the suspicious individuals]
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why do you want my weapons? Are you going to rebel?"
  - After: "Why my weapons? Planning a rebellion?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You all have your little fingers cut off. What does it mean?"
  - After: "Why are your little fingers cut off?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "I have few words to say to the likes of you."
  - After: [Attack] "I have little to say to you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You obviously did not expect anyone to be here. Are the enforcers providing cover for you?"
  - After: "You didn't expect anyone. Are the enforcers covering for you?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Several people are eagerly rummaging through a rack filled with weapons from the enforcers' arsenal. A big man with a pockmarked face is the first to react to your presence — he attracts the others' attention with a piercing whistle and barks out,{/n} "Who are you? There's not supposed to be anyone h— ah, it doesn't matter. Identify yourself!"
  - After: {n}Thugs loot an enforcer weapon rack. A pockmarked brute whistles.{/n} "Identify yourself!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Hard Nines, a gang... I mean, a brotherhood from Transport Bay 9. Don't think we're parasites. We do our bit for the prosperity of the ship. We're sort of... er... assistants to the enforcers. Self-appointed. We make sure that order is maintained in compartments where the enforcers are too lazy or greedy for bribes. We put a stop to robbery and freethinking, and well... we accept a small contribution as a show of thanks."
  - After: "The Hard Nines, Transport Bay 9. Self-appointed enforcer helpers, for a small thanks."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Have it your way, then!" {n}The pockmarked thug grins crookedly and rushes over to the weapon rack.{/n}
  - After: "Your way, then!" {n}He rushes to the rack.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Before you stands Lord Captain {name} von Valancius, {mf|master|mistress} of this vessel and everything on it, including those goods you are pawing at with your unwashed hands, and your miserable lives as well."
  - After: "Lord Captain {name} von Valancius, {mf|master|mistress} of this vessel and your lives."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The people turn to stare at you in disbelief and exchange heated whispers. The excitement is interrupted by the leader's roar:{/n} "What are you gawping at? Hurry up and bend your backs as is right and proper!"
  - After: {n}They stare. The leader roars:{/n} "Bow!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The leader looks at your gear appraisingly and frowns.{/n} "It matters. You better answer, or this conversation won't last long at all."
  - After: {n}The leader eyes your gear.{/n} "It matters. Answer."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}rumours about you{/d} are true, then you yourself know how it goes. There are criminals, and then there are criminals."
  - After: "If the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}rumours about you{/d} are true, you know: there are criminals, and criminals."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The leader nods readily.{/n} "I'll mark today as my second birthday — I saved my skin and I saw the Lord Captain, all in one day. Long live Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: {n}He nods.{/n} "My second birthday! Long live Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Hear that, boys? The Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} is expecting good things from us. We can't let {mf|him|her} down." {n}His cronies make sounds of approval.{/n} "We will fulfil your command to the letter."
  - After: "Hear that, boys? The Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} trusts us. Won't fail {mf|him|her}." {n}Cronies cheer.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The leader spits on the ground in annoyance.{/n} "What in the void have I been standing here making speeches for? I thought we had ourselves an all right Lord Captain, but no, {mf|he|she}'s the strait-laced type! Bring it on, then, Your {mf|Lordliness|Ladyness}."
  - After: {n}He spits.{/n} "Strait-laced, {mf|he|she} is! Bring it on, Your {mf|Lordliness|Ladyness}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Makeshift armour peeks out from beneath their ragged clothes, and their battered weapons display a patchwork of crude repairs. The group stares longingly at the rack where the good plasteel gleams, restlessly clutching their humble weapons.{/n}
  - After: {n}Makeshift armour, patched weapons. They eye the rack hungrily.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You notice that the little finger on every person's right hand has been cut off. It is hardly a coincidence.{/n}
  - After: {n}Each lacks the right little finger. No coincidence.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Even shooting them feels like a waste of bullets. I doubt these bottom-feeding degenerates have ever heard of the Lex in their lives."
  - After: "Not worth the bullets. They've never heard of the Lex."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Lex, eh? What kinda crew is that? They with the Rust Rats from Freight 10 or with the Piperunners from the main sorting hub?"
  - After: "The Lex? With the Rust Rats from Freight 10 or the Piperunners?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It's our gang's initiation rite, a fine tradition. By voluntarily removing a finger, the newcomer shows their determination and willingness to join us forever. It's also a badge of honour." {n}He proudly shows off the stump of his little finger.{/n}
  - After: "Initiation: a finger means you're in for life." {n}He shows his stump.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Erm... You could execute us, but who would take our place? Shameless scum who rob and kill to their hearts' content. Bastards who accept mutants into their gangs and pray to the Archenemy. There have always been outlaws on this ship. You're better off with outlaws like us, who don't go too far and who keep the heretics down."
  - After: "Kill us and worse take our place: Archenemy worshippers. Better outlaws like us."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Why stop there? You might as well call yourselves saints and say the fate of the whole dynasty rests on your shoulders!"
  - After: "Why not call yourselves saints, too!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To do business." {n}The gang leader smiles ingratiatingly.{/n} "We're no rebels. If anyone blasphemes against Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, we call the troublemakers to order. And we shed blood for the flagship without fear. I suppose that makes us... defenders of the ship?" {n}The thug raises his eyebrows questioningly and looks at you expectantly.{/n}
  - After: "Business." {n}He smiles.{/n} "We silence blasphemers against Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Defenders, really." {n}He looks expectant.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you must excuse these blockheads. I was taken aback myself — it's not every day you see the Rogue Trader in the flesh. And as for this..." {n}The man casts a grim glance at the rack.{/n} "I won't insult you by denying it — you've caught us red-handed."
  - After: "Forgive these blockheads, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}He glances at the rack.{/n} "You caught us red-handed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I wish... Frensoe, the newly appointed captain, had our informant strung up. He's tightening the screws, damn it, we can barely breathe. Today's the last time we'll come to pick over this compartment."
  - After: "I wish... New captain Frensoe hanged our informant. Last raid."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_Riot/DeathCultist_Escape/DeathCultist_Escape_dialogue

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_Riot/EnforcerTurrets/EnforcerTurrets_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Give me a situation report, soldier."
  - After: "Situation report, soldier."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I attribute your inability to defeat the enemy on your own to a lack of commitment. All survivors are subject to disciplinary action."
  - After: "You lacked commitment. Survivors face discipline."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am glad I was able to help. What comes next?"
  - After: "Glad to help. What next?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How did you end up in this compartment, soldier?"
  - After: "How did you end up here, soldier?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How did the mutineers manage to take over the post?"
  - After: "How did mutineers take the post?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I could swear I saw you get killed."
  - After: "I swear I saw you die."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What kind of propaganda was Frensoe spreading?"
  - After: "What propaganda did Frensoe spread?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "As far as I knew Frensoe, those speeches of his were completely out of character."
  - After: "That wasn't like Frensoe."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}From the sound of his voice, you recognise him as Captain Klein, the man who performed the autopsy on the mutant during the investigation.{/n}
  - After: {n}It's Captain Klein, who autopsied the mutant.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The enforcer post has been lost and is swarming with mutants. Alas, the only ways to the upper decks lie either through the post or through the transport tunnels, but there are enemies there as well."
  - After: "Mutants hold the post. The other way up, the tunnels, is enemy-held too."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "She sacrificed herself, covering our sally from the upper decks. She wanted to tell me something before it happened, something important — I could see it in her eyes — but she didn't get the chance. Now, I will never know." {n}Klein clenches his teeth and winces in pain.{/n}
  - After: "She died covering us. She wanted to tell me something, but never could." {n}Klein winces.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He grimaces.{/n} "A talented enforcer. And a good friend."
  - After: {n}He grimaces.{/n} "A good enforcer and friend."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Insert the data-key into the cogitator by the entrance, and the post will be hit with a devastating pulse that is lethal to {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g}. It will burn out the detonators and turn mines into harmless chunks of fyceline-stuffed iron."
  - After: "Insert it into the entrance cogitator. Its pulse kills {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g}, burning out the mines."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He nods curtly.{/n} "Harsh, but fair, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Permission to report."
  - After: {n}He nods.{/n} "Fair, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Emperor protect you, Lord Captain. We will cover the rear if the enemy comes out of the tunnels. Be careful: the mutants have mined the guard post. But there is something they didn't know." {n}Klein squints nastily and hand you a small copper rod with a connector.{/n}
  - After: "Emperor protect you. We'll guard the tunnels. The post is mined, but..." {n}He hands you a copper rod.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This is Frensoe's data-key that activates the Eclipse protocol. The train control node is vulnerable. If something were to anger or confuse the machine spirits, it could easily lead to a catastrophic accident — a trainload of crashing shells, for instance, or worse. That's why there are Tech-Priests' creations embedded in the walls: they are potent enough to rip the power out of any device."
  - After: "Frensoe's Eclipse protocol key. Tech-Priest wall devices can drain all machine power."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You see eyes framed by scars and wrinkles above the respirator.{/n} "Captain Klein, enforcer of the officers' deck, at your service, Lord Captain!"
  - After: {n}A respirated, scarred face.{/n} "Captain Klein, enforcer, at your service!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Mistress Sauerback sent my squad and me to the freight line to take charge of the situation. She heard that you had been spotted here and wanted us to lend you support."
  - After: "Mistress Sauerback sent us to support you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I agree, Lord Captain. We found a bite mark on his body... one that we've seen before. I suspect he was compromised against his will."
  - After: "Agreed. He had a familiar bite mark."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I could swear the same. I suppose the Emperor's protected me." {n}He touches one of his fresh wounds cautiously. Glistening pus remains on his fingers. A fresh wound could not have taken this little to fester. As you look closer, you notice clear signs in the wound's ooze. The foulness you let into this bay has already latched onto Klein and shared its gifts with him.{/n}
  - After: "The Emperor protected me." {n}His wound already festers. The foulness you let in has claimed him.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The enforcer whom you clearly saw die a minute ago gets up from the ground. Reeling and noticeably astonished, he feels his body with his hands and sticks his fingers into his fresh wounds. Having ascertained that he is alive, he resets his dislocated shoulder with a cracking sound.{/n}
  - After: {n}The enforcer you saw die rises, astonished, and resets his shoulder.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I thank Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} for the timely assistance. I thought it was my fate to go down an aberration's gullet, like poor Jinevri, but the Emperor had other plans for me."
  - After: "Thanks, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I nearly ended up like poor Jinevri."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Wretched scum! I fought worse than you on Dargonus!" {n}With a look of disgust, the enforcer in the protective mask grinds his boot into a lump of mutant flesh.{/n}
  - After: "Scum! I fought worse on Dargonus!" {n}He grinds mutant flesh underfoot.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "By treason. Captain Frensoe ordered the enforcers to leave the outpost and led them into a tunnel under the pretext of suppressing a mutiny. As soon as they reached it, however, he began spreading propaganda in an effort to stir up irreverence among the soldiers. He urged them to join the mutiny and eliminate the senior officers."
  - After: "Treason. Captain Frensoe led the enforcers out, then urged them to mutiny and kill their officers."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "He claimed that the enforcers were being pressured into oppressing their fellow crewmen for the benefit of their greedy superiors. He called for a change of order, including reprisals and penance for anyone who had participated in the crimes of the ship's rotten hierarchy." {n}Klein pulls his respirator aside and spits morosely.{/n}
  - After: "That enforcers serve greedy superiors. He wanted reprisals against the ship's hierarchy." {n}Klein spits.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I arrived just in time to execute the traitor Frensoe and reclaim control. I ordered the squad to return to the post and take up a defensive position, but it was already overrun by mutants entering through the elevator shaft. They lured us out and then seized our fortifications."
  - After: "I executed Frensoe, but mutants from the elevator shaft had seized the post."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_Riot/Factotum_Riot/Factotum_Riot_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Janris Danrok puts down the rifle and dabs his forehead with a silky handkercher, before shoving it under the tight band of the ammunition belt across his chest. His gilded frock coat is overlaid with a bullet-riddled and melted flak vest that barely fits around his voluminous waist. Behind him, a motley band of enforcers, armed clerks, and labourers greets you with enthusiastic shouts. A group of captives, silent and dejected, sits a short distance away.{/n}
  - After: {n}Janris Danrok, in gilded coat and tight flak vest, lowers his rifle. His motley militia cheers; captives sit nearby.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thanks to your order to put the enforcers on high alert, the traitors were unable to take them by surprise. I watched them take back the bays in full assault gear, sparing neither themselves nor their enemies. That was a wise decision indeed."
  - After: "Your high-alert order let the enforcers retake the bays. Wise."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I should warn you that many of the rebels were carrying enforcers' equipment during the battle. Apparently, they took it from the soldiers assisting in the rescue efforts. Those traitors from the Infernus Guild stabbed them in the back. Be careful."
  - After: "Beware: rebels wear enforcer gear stolen by the treacherous Infernus Guild."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Janris points courteously to a pile of relics, trophies, and chests overlaid with gold.{/n} "Following your instructions, we were able to evacuate some of your riches in time, as well as the sacred unguents and ammunition from the damaged compartments. Use whatever you like as you see fit. I can assure you that the rest will remain with me in perfect safety."
  - After: {n}Janris points to gilded chests.{/n} "We saved some of your riches, unguents and ammunition. Take what you need."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The kindly inhabitants of Depot 4 are unpretentious but loyal people..." {n}The Factotum nods casually toward the ragged labourers.{/n} "They have generously agreed to join my improvised posse to 'beat the mutinous scum bloody raw,' as they put it. A most honourable clan indeed. I shall order that they be assigned additional water and oxygen rations."
  - After: "Depot 4 folk are humble but loyal." {n}He nods at the labourers.{/n} "They'll get extra water and oxygen."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You see familiar faces among his escort. Lieutenant Avrilla Vent of the enforcers stands shoulder to shoulder with one of the leaders of Depot 4, an elderly woman whom everyone referred to as Old Nan.{/n}
  - After: {n}Among them: Lieutenant Avrilla Vent and Depot 4's Old Nan.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Factotum loosens the straps on his flak vest slightly and gives a satisfied groan.{/n} "It was going splendidly until we were rudely interrupted by the traitorous mutants. I am afraid I have temporarily had to requisition weapons and uniforms for myself and my militia. But do not worry: every spent bullet will be accounted for and added to the 'unplanned extermination of heretics' column in the ledger."
  - After: {n}He loosens his vest.{/n} "Mutants interrupted. Every bullet is logged as 'unplanned extermination of heretics'."
- **Old Nan**
  - Before: {n}The old woman raises her shotgun.{/n} "And we're eager to serve. One must keep one's house in order, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, and you {d|Encyclopedia:CompAbelard_Q1_GaveWeapons}gave us weapons{/d} for a reason! So, Stager came to us all quiet, and he brought some lads along with him. They started talking, telling us how oppressed and deprived we all were. They tried to incite rebellion, you see? And so, we blew their heads off."
  - After: {n}She raises her shotgun.{/n} "You {d|Encyclopedia:CompAbelard_Q1_GaveWeapons}gave us weapons{/d} for a reason, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Stager and his lads preached rebellion, so we blew their heads off."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "I must emphasise that it is a miracle that these commoners have joined us and not the rebellion. For the Emperor's sake, do not go arming every commoner on the ship after this, Lord Captain."
  - After: "A miracle they didn't join the rebels. Don't arm every commoner, Lord Captain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Why, I intend to die for you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Every member of the militia, from burly enforcer to puny clerk, nods in sombre agreement with the High Factotum.{/n} "But I must admit, we are quite exhausted from fighting our way here, and we are not really suited to being an assault squad."
  - After: "Die for you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}The militia nods.{/n} "But we're exhausted."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I think Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} should head for the enforcers' post. You will be safer there. Meanwhile, we will take a breather and smoke a few more dozen heretics out of their holes. God-Emperor willing, I will not have to die a glorious death with your name on my lips after all and will instead begin auditing the damage the ship has suffered, as well as the losses among the crew. It is a routine procedure — one in which I have become quite proficient."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} should head for the enforcers' post. We'll rest, hunt heretics, then audit the damage."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am flattered, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I can assure you that smiting heretics is no more difficult than shooting up serfs at my aunt's birthday party. In fact, fighting an armed opponent may even add a certain spice."
  - After: "Flattered, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Like shooting serfs at my aunt's party, only spicier."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Quite bad, but it could have been far worse if it were not for Mistress Sauerback's paranoia and insufferable temper. As you well know, she has a nasty habit of expecting betrayal from everyone except Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. She had therefore taken care to draw up special protocols for all sorts of mutiny, and had stationed agents on every deck."
  - After: "Bad, but Mistress Sauerback's paranoia saved us. Trusting only Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, she put agents on every deck."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You have a discerning eye, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Only a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}true aristocrat{/d} versed in the sophisticated art of hunting would appreciate the perfection that is this handsome toy! May I direct your attention to the filigree on the stock? Made by Master Gorenov himself! A superb weapon for—" {n}He stops himself and suddenly goes pale.{/n} "How utterly boorish of me! Such a tactful intimation, and I have made a fool of myself... Please, accept this weapon as a gift!"
  - After: "A {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}true aristocrat{/d}'s eye, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Master Gorenov's filigree—" {n}He pales.{/n} "How boorish! Please, take it as a gift!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Janris lets out a sigh of relief.{/n} "Rest assured, this rifle will serve House von Valancius well in my hands."
  - After: {n}Janris sighs, relieved.{/n} "It will serve House von Valancius well."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Serve your new owner faithfully, my dear rifle! Please, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, do not forget to apply the finest oils, or she might get right cranky." {n}Janris dabs his eyes with one hand and snaps his fingers with the other, commanding the nearest servant to give him their weapon.{/n}
  - After: "Serve well, dear rifle! Oil her finely, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Tearful, he takes a servant's weapon.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Factotum blows the head off a heretic with a precise shot, then lowers his rifle.{/n} "Much obliged."
  - After: {n}The Factotum shoots a heretic.{/n} "Much obliged."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "You have yet to learn the art of subtly hinting at desirable gifts, shereen..."
  - After: "Learn subtler gift-hinting, shereen..."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar makes a patronising gesture.{/n} "Not bad, coffer keeper. I wouldn't have thought there was such a taste for bloodshed in your heart. I approve of your vigour."
  - After: {n}Ulfar gestures.{/n} "Not bad, coffer keeper. I approve."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Janris swells with pride.{/n} "After being praised by the Angel of the Emperor himself, I simply must end no fewer than a dozen mutineers myself!"
  - After: {n}Janris swells.{/n} "Praised by the Angel of the Emperor! I must kill a dozen more!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne gives a nod of respect.{/n} "Meticulous adherence to procedure. It's a shame you don't serve in the Administratum — I imagine your department would be a true example of efficiency and order."
  - After: {n}Solomorne nods.{/n} "Meticulous. The Administratum could use you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am delighted to see you in good health, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I am afraid my report on the inspection of the ship's storehouses will be slightly delayed due to extraordinary circumstances."
  - After: "Glad you're well, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! My storehouse report is delayed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The enforcers reported that you had been sighted in this compartment, and I humbly believed it was my duty to head for the freight line with this very modest army... Would you kindly move a little to the right, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"
  - After: "I heard you were here, so I brought an army... Step right, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are indeed correct, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Serfs, enforcers, officers, Tech-Priests, and tunnel rats have all united in their fight against the rebellious scum. The only ones missing are the inferni. It seems they were the backbone of this mutiny... And they strangled all those who were not privy to their dastardly plan."
  - After: "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Every clan fights the rebels except the inferni, who led the mutiny and strangled the uninvolved."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Danrok glances at the wounded prisoners.{/n} "Yet, as you can see, our enemies also include those who swore an oath to you not so long ago — crew members who fell for the rebel propaganda. It is your choice whether to sentence them yourself, or to leave the execution to me after you have departed on your business."
  - After: {n}He glances at the prisoners.{/n} "Sworn crew turned by propaganda. Sentence them yourself, or leave it to me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "When the riot began, these agents took out many of the seditious officers and mounted a defence. In addition, I have been informed of at least three cases in which the officers inciting the enforcers to mutiny were shot by Jocasta's personal aides. It looks like she had already been keeping an eye on her least reliable subordinates. I should give the Emperor a candle in gratitude for making her such a suspicious hag."
  - After: "Her agents and Jocasta's aides killed seditious officers. Thank the Emperor she's a suspicious hag."
- **Old Nan**
  - Before: "It cost us, though. Our Rivet was made of heroic stuff: he pounced on Stager, screamed, roused the crowd to a fight. He didn't make it, of course, but at least we shot the doubters and our unwanted guests then and there."
  - After: "It cost us. Brave Rivet jumped Stager and roused us. He died, but we shot the traitors."
- **Avrilla Vent**
  - Before: "That fortune was Mistress Sauerback, Lord Captain. She assigned me to keep an eye on the captain of Depot 4, with special powers. The captain had become compromised, so I eliminated him. I then opened a special package with instructions to follow in case of mutiny, formed a defence squad, and joined the battle."
  - After: "Mistress Sauerback had me watch Depot 4's compromised captain. I killed him and formed a defence per her orders."

- **Player**
  - Before: [Reset the dislocated elbow]
  - After: [Reset the elbow]

  - Before: [Inspect the elevator wreckage]
  - After: [Inspect the wreckage]

I wish your mon-keigh technologies delivered such surprises more often."
  - After: {n}Marazhai is spotless.{/n} "Death came tantalisingly close. Delightful."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The bone crunches unpleasantly, and a sharp pain pierces your arm, but you manage to reset the elbow. It has swollen and still looks worrisome, but at least you can move your arm now.{/n}
  - After: {n}Painfully, you reset the elbow. Swollen, but usable.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The bone crunches unpleasantly, and a sharp pain pierces your arm: it seems that your efforts have only made it worse. You can still hold your weapon, but each careless movement fills your veins with molten lead.{/n}
  - After: {n}You make it worse. Every move burns.{/n}
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "How titillating. Now do the same to your other arm, {name}."
  - After: "Titillating. Now the other arm, {name}."
- **Heinrix**

  - After: "{name}... allow me..." {n}Heinrix's chill touch resets the bone.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is a miracle you have survived. Guide rails lie in a twisted pile over a crown of shattered plasteel.{/n}
  - After: {n}A miracle you survived the wreck.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The elevator was equipped with safety devices meant to stop the cabin inside the shaft, but at least half of them have failed. Your fall was no accident.{/n}
  - After: {n}Half the safety brakes failed. No accident.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Smoke and darkness limit your vision, but, judging by the stench of rust and unwashed bodies, you are somewhere on the lower decks. You can hear the crackling of flames, groans, screams, and the rumble of falling beams coming from the distance. The disaster has not spared this compartment.{/n}
  - After: {n}Smoke and stench: the lower decks. Flames and screams nearby.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:CommBead}comm-bead{/g} emits only unintelligible hissing. Either it was damaged in the fall or the communication lines in this compartment have failed.{/n}
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:CommBead}comm-bead{/g} only hisses. Damaged, or lines down.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The elevator shaft has expelled you into the dim of the emergency lights. The smell of {g|Encyclopedia:Promethium}promethium{/g} and burnt flesh only adds to the nausea, confirming that you have suffered a concussion. Your elbow is twisted at an odd angle, and your body is wracked with pain. But there is a silver lining to all the agony: it means you are not dead yet.{/n}
  - After: {n}{g|Encyclopedia:Promethium}Promethium{/g} reek. Concussed, elbow twisted, agonised, but alive.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}This ship is indeed old. Apparently, this cascade of accidents was the last straw for the aged elevator's {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g}.{/n}
  - After: {n}The old lift's {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g} finally gave out.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The elevator shaft has expelled you into the dim of the emergency lights. The smell of promethium and burnt flesh hits your nostrils, but... there is no pain. Not a single broken bone, not even a scratch on your whole body. It is as if your body became as strong as your faith during the fall, and nothing could have harmed you. Even the ringing echo of the crashed lift resembles the glorious tolling of a bell.{/n}
  - After: {n}You land unhurt, as if your body grew strong as your faith. The crash rings like a holy bell.{/n}

Einrich Monteg is not human, and he seeks your demise."
