- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Einrich spits at his feet in frustration.{/n} "You fanatics are always meddling in the wrong business. First the trick with the blood bath, and now this. We were so close." {n}The gun leaps into his hand and points at you. A shot rings out. The whistling hits your ears, but the bullet was evidently meant for the young spinner now writhing on the ground.{/n}
  - After: {n}Einrich spits.{/n} "Fanatics. First the blood bath, now this. So close." {n}He shoots the spinner down.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Do I... What? Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, do I really have to defend myself after being accused by this... I don't even know who he is! It's... It's me. I have risked life and limb for you and this ship more times than that groxchunder has heard the watch siren."
  - After: "Defend myself against a stranger, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}? I've bled for you!"
- **Death Cultist**
  - Before: "No!" {n}The young spinner shrieks as he raises his needle pistol and fires a fatal shot... which turns out to not be fatal at all. The needle slices into Einrich's cheek before bouncing off harmlessly. Beneath the sagging flap of skin, you see... something purple. It is chitin.{/n}
  - After: "No!" {n}The needle slices Einrich's cheek. Beneath: purple chitin.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Einrich takes out a new lho-stick, lights it from his cutter, and blows out the smoke with a heavy sigh.{/n} "Things would be a lot easier if you had just crashed in the elevator. Or climbed onto the train. I wish you too could hear the Sire's song in your dreams and await the Many-Armed Emperor. But the harvest season has come, and you must be reaped. You must die so that we may live. I am sorry, {name}. Farewell."
  - After: {n}Einrich sighs smoke.{/n} "Easier if you'd died in the lift. Would you could hear the Sire's song too. But it's harvest. You must die so we may live. Farewell, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Then it is fortunate you are travelling in the company of such big, bad infernus repairmen. How do we feel about people harming the Lord Captain in front of us, lads?" {n}Einrich smiles brightly at the furious, almost bestial growls of his subordinates.{/n}
  - After: "Lucky you've got us. Harm the Lord Captain, lads?" {n}They growl.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And even if our forces prove insufficient, Captain Hrotko and his squad will surely find something with which to meet the enemy. That's a lot of deadly toys they're packing." {n}He smiles sardonically.{/n}
  - After: "And Hrotko's squad packs deadly toys." {n}A smirk.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Besides, we came prepared." {n}His hand brushes against the pistol on his belt.{/n} "You gave us the privilege of bearing arms, and we won't let it go to waste."
  - After: "We came prepared." {n}He taps his pistol.{/n} "You let us bear arms."
- **Enforcer Hrotko**
  - Before: {n}Clad in heavy riot armour, the enforcer gives you a dignified nod.{/n} "My men have never faltered in battle, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. All of them are veterans, capable of clearing out a ship from stem to stern."
  - After: {n}Hrotko nods.{/n} "Veterans all, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Enforcer Hrotko**
  - Before: "When the disaster struck, I took the liberty of selecting a few dependable fighters and going to the lower decks to keep order. You cannot prove your valour by staying back and doing nothing. I would rather march straight into the flames." {n}Hrotko raises his clean-scraped chin.{/n}
  - After: "I brought fighters down to keep order. Valour means marching into flames." {n}Chin up.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "After all these years of not being allowed to carry anything heavier than a wrench... I suppose you could say we are overcompensating." {n}Einrich's smile looks somewhat strained.{/n}
  - After: "Years of only wrenches... we overcompensate." {n}Strained smile.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I understand that the situation is critical, but... Damn it, I am a senior officer of this ship, as much as I hate to remind you. And you are a little mutineer who almost put a hole in my head."
  - After: "I'm a senior officer. You're a mutineer who nearly shot me."
- **Enforcer Hrotko**
  - Before: {n}Hrotko clangs the stock of his weapon soundly. In a sneering tone, he asks,{/n} "What do we have here, treason? An attempted assassination of a senior officer? I have long expected trouble from you spinners..."
  - After: {n}Hrotko sneers.{/n} "Treason? Assassination? Typical spinners..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A question forms in your mind all on its own: how do you kill a Rogue Trader? Out of {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}habit{/d}, you quickly go over a few plans and come to the unfortunate conclusion: this is how. You create a crisis, lure the Rogue Trader away from the bridge, sabotage the escape routes, and then send in a squad to mop up any survivors. A solid plan — simple, yet effective.{/n}
  - After: {n}Out of {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}habit{/d}, you see how to kill a Rogue Trader: crisis, lure, sabotage, mop-up squad. This.{/n}
- **Death Cultist**
  - Before: "The Vizsier has divined the truth." {n}The young man looks at Einrich with haughty reproach.{/n}
  - After: "The Vizsier has divined it." {n}Haughtily.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh. Well, since the Vizsier has overdosed on stimulants and discovered the truth... by all means, Lord Captain, go ahead and arrest me. Take my head."
  - After: "A stim-addled Vizsier says so? Then take my head, Lord Captain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Maybe you really are the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}bringer of woes{/d} that simple folk paint you as. Are you sure you didn't curse the elevator? That old thing transported Rogue Traders for hundreds of years, but then you stepped inside — and down it went!"
  - After: "Maybe you are the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}bringer of woes{/d}. That lift ran centuries until you stepped in!"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix grips his weapon, and the chilling psychic aura around him makes your blood run cold.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix grips his weapon, psychic chill rising.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Einrich gives a sad little chuckle.{/n} "It is my job to take the paths where death may be prowling. But not this time. The train is the safest and fastest way out of here. Worry not, Mistress Tlass. You and the Lord Captain are quite safe with me."
  - After: {n}A sad chuckle.{/n} "Not today. The train is safest, Mistress Tlass."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "It looks like I am not alone in having a problem with unreliable allies..." {n}Marazhai's voice is laden with unexpected irony.{/n}
  - After: "So I'm not alone with unreliable allies..." {n}Ironic.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "I am sure many on this ship would be pleased to be rescued with such daring. But it is only right that the Rogue Trader should get all the nicest things, is it not?"
  - After: "A daring rescue. The Rogue Trader gets all the nice things."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Emperor knows I'm sick of all these cultists, and yet... The boy could have shot you, Rogue Trader, but he didn't. That is worth an investigation, at the very least."
  - After: "The boy could have shot you and didn't. Worth investigating."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A locomotive enveloped in steam halts at the platform with a low rumble. The hardened emergency workers of the Infernus Guild pour out of the carriages. Upon seeing you, they begin to wave cheerfully and shout.{/n}
  - After: {n}A train arrives. Infernus Guild workers pour out, cheering.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No, I think that's a first." {n}Einrich raises an eyebrow and says politely,{/n} "Lord Captain, you sure know how to make a dramatic entrance."
  - After: "A first." {n}A raised brow.{/n} "Dramatic entrance, Lord Captain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It's repairman's hunch, Lord Captain. I find myself drawn to places where nothing has broken yet, but is about to—"
  - After: "Repairman's hunch. I'm drawn to things about to break—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Infernus Master pulls the last of the lho-stick from his mouth and asks in a low voice,{/n} "Have you lost your mind, you damned fanatic?"
  - After: {n}Low:{/n} "Lost your mind, fanatic?"

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/LowerTunnels_Riot/PrisonedGeneculstist/PrisonedGeneculstist_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "And you believed them? I am a legend of the Expanse, and oppression of commoners is not in the history of my deeds. Is it not obvious? Our enemies are trying to sully my name!"
  - After: "You believed them? I'm a legend, no oppressor. Our enemies are sullying my name!"

  - Before: "You will atone with your blood or perish this instant. The choice is yours."
  - After: "Atone with your blood or die now. Choose."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I shall let you go. It is up to you whether to flee or to seek vengeance."
  - After: "I'll let you go. Flee or seek vengeance."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Execute them] "I sentence you to death for rebelling against the Rogue Trader and for aiding traitors to the Imperium."
  - After: [Execute them] "Death, for rebelling and aiding traitors."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am not ready to deal with you right now."
  - After: "I'll deal with you later."
- **Player**

  - After: "So I'm a tyrant?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Execute them] "If I am a tyrant, then I must live up to expectations. Die."
  - After: [Execute them] "Then I'll live up to it. Die."

  - After: "The Infernus Guild staged the disaster that killed your families. They're using you."

  - After: [Sacrifice the prisoners to the true gods] "Your blood buys me fortune in battle."

  - After: [Raise your voice] "You fell for the enemy's trap! You're traitors to Humanity, guilty before the Emperor!"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A group of shackled commoners are huddled together on their knees. They wear no armour, just filthy rags and tattered coveralls. Some hide their gaze while others sob quietly or mutter prayers. Only one woman, swarthy and heavily built, glares at you. She is trying to appear proud and fearless, but her lip is trembling.{/n}

  - Before: "The liberators, our true heroes! When the fiery death rained down on our slums, not one of your enforcers lifted a finger to save us. But the inferni went out of their way to pull children out from under the rubble, mend wounds, and comfort widows. They opened our eyes!"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What are you waiting for? Just end us and be done with it. Isn't that what tyrants do?"

  - Before: {n}The woman sneers.{/n} "I get it. So many people to kill. Don't you worry: we'll be right here, waiting for our executioner."
  - After: {n}She sneers.{/n} "We'll wait for our executioner."

  - After: "Cult?" {n}Bitter smirk.{/n} "Anyone fighting oppressors is a heretic to you."

  - After: {n}She nods.{/n} "Tyrant. Butcher. Pick one."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman stiffens but meets her last moment with dignity. Not everyone follows her example.{/n}
  - After: {n}She dies with dignity. Not all do.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

That people can live as equals, take care of one another, and have dignity. This is what they are fighting for. You profit from keeping us in poverty, and your faith is false! Why would the Emperor want His believers to suffer in vain?"
  - After: "They promised no more beatings, and life as equals. You profit from our poverty! Would the Emperor want us suffering?"

  - After: "Inhuman fiends tricked us? Holy Throne, what have we done..."

  - Before: "All sorts of mutations can happen to us bottom-deckers. Who cares what grows on their foreheads? What matters is that their souls are pure. And yours is not."
  - After: "Bottom-deckers mutate. Their souls are pure. Yours isn't."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman fixes her gaze on you, as if searching your face for signs of deception. Then, she turns pale and a single tear rolls down her cheek.{/n} "Set up the disaster... But how..."
  - After: {n}She pales; a tear falls.{/n} "Staged it... But how..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Of course, make monsters out of them. It suits your purpose. But I know what I saw."
  - After: "Make monsters of them. I know what I saw."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Even the ship's confessor renounced the false covenants and went on to raise the folk hero, Nemesite! And you killed both of them!"
  - After: "Even the ship's confessor renounced the false covenants and raised Nemesite! You killed both!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You turn your thoughts to the Ruinous Powers as you kill the prisoners one after the other. As you silently mouth the words of forbidden prayers, you sense that your sacrifice has pleased the gods. A dark blessing guides your hand, and the agony of the butchered courses through your veins, pulsing with strength and an impetus to act. You see horror in the still eyes of the corpses — in their final moments, they fully understood the extent of your power and their own terrible fate.{/n}
  - After: {n}You kill them for the Ruinous Powers. Their agony fills you with dark strength.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Staggered by the confidence of a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}battle-hardened Commissar{/d}, the woman loses her rebellious spirit and lowers her head, suddenly pale. The sincerity of your anger serves as the best possible proof that you are right.{/n} "We're... traitors? Blessed Throne, is it really true? But we thought... What are we supposed to do now?"
  - After: {n}Cowed by a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}battle-hardened Commissar{/d}, she pales.{/n} "Traitors? Throne... What do we do?"

  - After: {n}Cassia sighs.{/n} "The rabble can't govern itself. Alas, peasants don't read history."

  - After: {n}The whispers gnaw.{/n} "Speak, impure one, and I'll end this now."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The whispers sink their fangs into your most painful memory as into an exposed nerve. The ridicule, the looks of contempt, the pitying comments — the long-faded ripples of your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}disgrace{/d} hit you in a burning wave of shame and regret.{/n} "You are pathetic. You do not deserve to lead. An insect like you must perish."
  - After: {n}The whispers revive your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}disgrace{/d}.{/n} "Pathetic. Unfit to lead. Perish, insect."

No external signs of mutation were found."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Jinevri looks at Klein with sympathy — she clearly cares about him, but does not wish to trample on her comrade's honour with words of comfort. Hrotko regards Klein with a contemptuous smirk, while Klein scowls back at him.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Klein is up to his elbows in blood, his eyes flaring defiantly.{/n} "I've examined the filth inside and out. Its innards are a genetic nightmare — it's a bag of corruption wrapped in human skin. Extra organs, scales, atrophied ingrown limbs. But that's not what's important."

  - After: {n}Sauerback shakes her head.{/n} "Apologies, Lord Captain. It won't happen again."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Klein's lips tremble. His eyes bulge. He seems unable to stop wiping his reddened hands with a rag soaked in disinfectant.{/n} "Disgusting. Unspeakable. You can't even imagine what's inside that... thing. They should've burned the body right there and then. Whoever killed him should've just finished the job."

  - After: "They hid the cause of death, yet left the body out. Why?"

  - After: "The killer was sending a message."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "We should run the victim's identification number through the {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}master work log cogitator{/g}. If its machine spirit favours us, we will be able to narrow down the number of suspects. Jinevri, this is your arena."
  - After: "Run the victim's number through the {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}master work log cogitator{/g}. Jinevri, your arena."

  - Before: "The pipewardens are a worker clan that services the ship's sewer systems. The tattoo indicates the worker's status and personal number. This one was..."
  - After: "Pipewardens service the sewers. The tattoo gives rank and number. This one was..."

  - Before: {n}Klein accepts the glass and downs it instantly. Evidently, he is in no state to savour the bouquet and taste of the fine drink you have offered him.{/n}
  - After: {n}Klein gulps it down.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}As Klein bows his head guiltily, Sauerback mutters, her gaze boring into him,{/n} "Rest assured, Lord Captain, disciplinary measures will be applied to Captain Klein as soon as we are done with the investigation."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Judging by the change in Klein's expression, the old {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Navy}voidsman saying{/d} appears to have improved his spirits.{/n} "That rotting carcass is no kraken, I can tell you that! Orders received, Lord Captain! I'll carve him up into shreds!"

- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}She sighs.{/n} "If it was a special or unique item, that might help. However, if the criminal was using an industrially manufactured weapon or tool instead of a makeshift one... Those are all the same. But we will conduct a thorough search, Lord Captain."

  - After: {n}Her eyebrow twitches.{/n} "Follow my heart. Of course."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Hrotko, go assist Klein with the autopsy."
  - After: "Hrotko, help Klein with the autopsy."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "I thank Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} for your wise counsel."
  - After: "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

  - After: {n}Horror flashes in Klein's eyes.{/n}

- **Enforcer Hrotko**
  - Before: {n}Hrotko's lips stretch into a thin smile.{/n} "Thank you for your high praise. I am grateful to have had this opportunity to prove my usefulness to you, albeit under... unusual circumstances." {n}Hrotko remains unfailingly polite and completely ignores the seething Sauerback.{/n}
  - After: {n}A thin smile.{/n} "Thank you. Glad to be useful." {n}He ignores Sauerback.{/n}
- **Enforcer Jinevri**
  - Before: "I don't understand how I could have forgotten it... I always check my gear when I go on duty!"
  - After: "How could I forget it? I always check my gear!"
- **Enforcer Hrotko**
  - Before: "Then it wasn't her, just one of her accomplices. Will you give us a name, Jinevri?"
  - After: "Then an accomplice. A name, Jinevri?"
- **Enforcer Klein**
  - Before: "Shut your mouth, Hrotko! Nothing has been proven yet!" {n}Klein goes red in the face and brushes Jinevri aside with his shoulder.{/n}
  - After: "Shut it, Hrotko! Nothing's proven!" {n}Klein shoulders Jinevri aside.{/n}
- **Enforcer Hrotko**
  - Before: "With all due respect to {mf|Your Lordship|Your Ladyship}, I am an enforcer. I have looked death in the eye, and I will accept your judgement with dignity." {n}There is no bravado in Hrotko's words, just a dry statement of fact.{/n}
  - After: "I'm an enforcer, {mf|Your Lordship|Your Ladyship}. I accept judgement." {n}No bravado.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Behind the armour of affected indifference, his thoughts ooze grimy hues. Like blood mixed with umber. It looks vile."
  - After: "Beneath his indifference, his thoughts ooze bloody umber. Vile."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "This concludes my report."
  - After: "Report concluded."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/OfficerDeck/BloodbathCulpritReveal/BloodbathCulpritReveal_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You can start by reporting on the results of the additional investigative efforts."
  - After: "Report on the further investigation."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have no more questions. Bring in the pipewarden."
  - After: "Bring the pipewarden."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are the real pipewarden Gwedon, are you not?"
  - After: "You're the real Gwedon?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why did you fill my bath with blood?"
  - After: "Why the blood bath?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Whom do you mean by this 'servant of death'?"
  - After: "Who's this 'servant of death'?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Summon the Vizsier of the Bloodspun Web. I wish to hear his explanation."
  - After: "Summon the Vizsier of the Bloodspun Web."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Vizsier has crossed the line! I want him dragged here by force!"
  - After: "The Vizsier crossed the line! Drag him here!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Give him lashes. Hopefully he will think more carefully about whose orders to follow next time."
  - After: "Lash him. He'll pick his orders better."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You drenched the Rogue Trader in blood. Did you expect to simply walk away afterward? I think not. Hang the scum!"
  - After: "You drenched me in blood? Hang him!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is the meaning of the Master-at-Arms's words about your clan, Einrich?"
  - After: "Einrich, what about your clan?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You acted as a true servant of the Emperor would. I will have you provided with the best ocular implant for your work."
  - After: "You served the Emperor. You'll get the best ocular implant."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You were deceived into becoming an accomplice. I will not punish you."
  - After: "You were deceived. No punishment."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, the real pipewarden Gwedon has been found and is being escorted here as we speak. Are there any remaining questions you wish to address before we hear from Gwedon himself?"
  - After: "Lord Captain, the real Gwedon is coming. Questions first?"
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "We have thoroughly questioned all detainees known to have a violent temper and compared the tools and weapons we seized with the wounds found on the corpse, but have not been able to establish who was responsible for the mutilation. I take full responsibility for this failure."
  - After: "We couldn't identify the mutilator. My failure."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Your insightful suggestion helped the enforcers to locate the evidence. In fact, we found a bloody synth-coat in one of the vents — a standard issue included in every enforcer outfit on the ship."
  - After: "We found a bloody enforcer synth-coat in a vent."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The pipewarden does his best to remain reverentially bowed, which paints a rather comical picture given his formidable height and complexion. He lowers his head, tugging at his beard.{/n} "Senior pipewarden Gwedon, honoured to serve, Lord Captain. I'm ready to confess to everything."
  - After: {n}A huge man bows awkwardly.{/n} "Senior pipewarden Gwedon. I'll confess everything."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "The interrogation of the detainee Yart had to be suspended. He seems to have gone mad: he just keeps mumbling that it was Jinevri who set him up to lie, and that he must therefore be set free. I doubt we will get anything further out of him, be it with cruelty, kindness, or holy prayer."
  - After: "Yart's gone mad, insisting Jinevri made him lie. He's useless now."
- **Senior Pipewarden Gwedon**
  - Before: "I am, and I'm proud of it, Lord Captain. A pipewarden's craft is hard work, but necessary. My number is SP-268-55. My work partner was the late Orto, number SP-246-01. I oversee the water supply systems on the upper decks, sectors A-3, K-8, and R-2. That includes valve 27-B."
  - After: "I am, SP-268-55. Partner Orto, SP-246-01. Sectors A-3, K-8, R-2, valve 27-B."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "There can be no mistake: I have verified his identity myself. It has also been confirmed by the other workers."
  - After: "I verified him myself, as did the workers."
- **Senior Pipewarden Gwedon**
  - Before: "I didn't kill him, and I didn't know he was a mutant. Orto and I always got along, even if he wasn't much for talking. But then..." {n}He shudders.{/n} "A servant of death came from the darkness — ended him quickly but harshly. She bled him dry and put a black feather in his throat. She told me to pump blood into the pipes, and then she left. I wanted to confess, but... I was afraid she'd come for me too if I did."
  - After: "I didn't kill him or know he was a mutant." {n}Shudders.{/n} "A servant of death bled him, left a black feather in his throat, and made me pump the blood. I feared confessing."
- **Senior Pipewarden Gwedon**
  - Before: "A holy slayer in black and crimson and bone. Feared by all, they are, quiet and merciless as death itself. They come from the shadows to kill, because the Emperor commands them so."
  - After: "A holy slayer in black, crimson and bone. Kills at the Emperor's command."
- **Senior Pipewarden Gwedon**
  - Before: "I did as the servant of death commanded. She said the Emperor gave the First Spinner a sign: that Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} should be bathed in the blood of poor Orto, my partner. And I, well..." {n}He gulps.{/n} "I was scared. So, I obeyed."
  - After: "She said the Emperor told the First Spinner to bathe Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} in Orto's blood." {n}Gulps.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "The First Spinner? Are you talking about the Vizsier of the Bloodspun Web?"
  - After: "The First Spinner? The Vizsier of the Bloodspun Web?"
- **Senior Pipewarden Gwedon**
  - Before: "Y-yes, that's him. He leads the death cultists, the lot who worship the Emperor by killing. His spinners hunt down heretics, but sometimes they take righteous lives too. Their service is mysterious, fervent, and bloody."
  - After: "Y-yes. His death cult kills for the Emperor."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, reporting: we have identified the perpetrator who introduced the blood to your bathchamber. The culprit is senior pipewarden Gwedon. Gwedon drained the blood from the dead body of his partner, a worker by the name of Orto. The victim looked like a normal human; however, the autopsy has revealed horrific mutations in his internal organs. Gwedon is being escorted here as we speak."
  - After: "Lord Captain, pipewarden Gwedon put the blood in your bath — drained from his partner Orto, a hidden mutant."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "As you will, Lord Captain."
  - After: "As you will."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "You have already met the servants of the Bloodspun Web, Lord Captain. Their grim procession is not one the upper decks will soon forget."
  - After: "You've seen the Bloodspun Web's procession, Lord Captain."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "We found witnesses to the battery of our false conspirator. According to them, an enforcer in a helmet came to the detained Yart, spoke to him, and then gave him a beating so thorough that a ring came off their finger. Alas, said ring could not be recovered."
  - After: "Witnesses saw a helmeted enforcer beat Yart; a ring flew off, now lost."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "The body of the deceased was mutilated after death. It is likely that the nature of the injuries would have proven very useful in the investigation, and that the perpetrator concealed them for that very reason."
  - After: "The body was mutilated after death to hide telling wounds."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Instead of the murdered man's partner, we were given a fool — one who thoroughly incriminated himself first, before admitting that Captain Jinevri had put him up to it." {n}Sauerback glowers at Jinevri, and she pales with fear.{/n}
  - After: "We got a fool who confessed, then blamed Captain Jinevri." {n}Jinevri pales.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Someone sabotaged the work log cogitator so it would be harder for us to find the victim's partner, who might have information valuable to the investigation."
  - After: "Someone sabotaged the work log cogitator to hide the victim's partner."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: {n}With an acerbic smile, Einrich blows a stream of smoke in Sauerback's direction.{/n} "What a shocking turn of events, Jocasta. The inferni are innocent! Who could have seen that coming? Could it be that you were wrong to brutalise and humiliate my people?"
  - After: {n}Einrich blows smoke at Sauerback.{/n} "The inferni are innocent, Jocasta! Shocking."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Do not expect an apology from me. I was doing my duty. You can play the victim all you want, but I haven't forgotten the circumstances under which your blasted clan came to be on this ship. Consider every strike upon your backs a reminder of that event."
  - After: "No apology. Remember how your clan came aboard."
- **Einrich Monteg**
  - Before: "It's a story of days long past, one that Mistress Sauerback greatly enjoys reminiscing about as if she was there herself. My ancestors committed a trespass against your ancestor and were made inferni as punishment. I'll be sure to tell you this tale some other time."
  - After: "My ancestors wronged yours and were made inferni. Another time."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "I must concede as much, Lord Captain. The story can wait. We should first find out why the Bloodspun Web thought to bathe you in repugnant blood."
  - After: "Agreed. First, why did the Bloodspun Web do this?"
- **Senior Pipewarden Gwedon**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, if I may ask... What happens to me now? I never meant to anger you. I thought I was doing as the Emperor willed it, but here we are. I'm a simple man. I know pipes, and I know them a lot better than all this people business! My eyes aren't what they used to be, but I can still smell rust in metal, though not so much in people's thoughts."
  - After: "What happens to me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}? I know pipes, not people."
- **Senior Pipewarden Gwedon**
  - Before: "Thank you from the bottom of my heart, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I'll serve you faithfully, and I'll never forget your mercy!"
  - After: "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I'll never forget your mercy!"
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "It will be done, Lord Captain! I will also order to have his fellow pipewardens thoroughly examined for rust in their brains."
  - After: "At once! I'll check the other pipewardens for brain rust too."
- **Senior Pipewarden Gwedon**
  - Before: {n}Gwedon hangs his head.{/n} "My mum always said I'd die an idiot..."
  - After: {n}Gwedon sags.{/n} "Mum said I'd die an idiot..."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "If the Vizsier ordered it, there must have been a reason. The Undying One must have revealed something to him that we are ignorant of."
  - After: "The Undying One must have shown the Vizsier something."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Undoubtedly. Let us go over the facts we have on this sabotage and compile them."
  - After: "Indeed. Let's compile the sabotage facts."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/OfficerDeck/CogitatorDispute/CogitatorDispute_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "What is the problem with the machine spirit?"
  - After: "What ails the machine spirit?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What exactly does this data-recuperative dogma prescribe?"
  - After: "What does this dogma say?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal, how profane would you say your hands are?"
  - After: "Pasqal, how profane are your hands?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Laypeople may be prohibited from communing with the machine spirit, but you are not, esteemed Tech-Priest. Jinevri will merely stand at your side and observe."
  - After: "You may commune with it, Tech-Priest. Jinevri just observes."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Well, then the solution is quite simple. We cut off the esteemed Tech-Priest's hand and use it to commune with the machine spirit."
  - After: "Then we cut off your hand and use that."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Did the murderer get to the cogitator too?"
  - After: "Did the murderer reach the cogitator?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Master-at-Arms, how do you propose we find our new suspect?"
  - After: "Master-at-Arms, how do we find him?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Eogunn tended to the ancient relic in the Sector Bionica — he can help."
  - After: "Eogunn tended the Sector Bionica relic. He can help."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Jinevri approaches you, followed by a dignified woman in crimson robes.{/n} "Allow me to introduce the esteemed Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi. She believes she has the right to obstruct the investigation, and refused to grant the enforcers access to the master cogitator."
  - After: {n}Jinevri brings a crimson-robed woman.{/n} "Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi. She bars us from the master cogitator."
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: "The spirit is old and quick to anger. It therefore calls for a sensitive approach, not a torturous intrusion by a brutish laywoman! Since the start of this watch, the spirit has been unwell, so we have been trying to soothe its woes by applying sacred unguents and censing the great machine's boards. The dogma of data-recuperative quarantine prohibits any disturbances to blessed machines found to be in such a state."
  - After: "The spirit is ill, under data-recuperative quarantine. No brutish laywoman may disturb it!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Judging by Jinevri's expression, she would rather have her profane hands touch Androveta-Phi's neck.{/n}
  - After: {n}Jinevri wants to strangle her.{/n}
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: "'Let no profane hand touch the sacred machine stricken. Let the mechanism be shielded from all worldly troubles by a veil of righteous litany, and let its shrine be thricely honoured 'til the malady is no more.'"
  - After: "'Let no profane hand touch the sacred machine stricken.'"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I am a Magos Explorator and this vessel's {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} Prime. The profanity of this unit's hands, as well as the rest of its limbs, organs, and augmetics, is null."
  - After: "As {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} Prime, my profanity is null."
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: {n}Androveta-Phi shoots Jinevri a sidelong glance.{/n} "Very well. I shall disturb the spirit, but I demand that the laywoman show respect and do as she is told!"
  - After: {n}A glance at Jinevri.{/n} "Very well. She obeys me!"
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: {n}Androveta-Phi shoots Jinevri a sidelong glance.{/n} "I know her 'standing and observing' all too well. I may disturb the spirit at your behest, but mark my words: this won't end well!"
  - After: {n}A glance at Jinevri.{/n} "Fine, but this won't end well!"
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest withers and mewls pitifully,{/n} "Understood, Lord Captain. I offer my apologies along with my assurances of cooperation."
  - After: {n}She wilts,{/n} "I'll cooperate, Lord Captain."
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest recoils.{/n} "This is madness! Tech-barbarism! If you would resort to brute force in your irreverent intentions, then I cannot stop you. Instead, I will disturb the machine spirit myself. However, I must register this as a Category Six blasphemy!"
  - After: {n}She recoils.{/n} "Tech-barbarism! I'll do it, but it's Category Six blasphemy!"
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: "If the honoured Magos supervises the laywoman's tactful interaction with the spirit, I will sanction this disturbance."
  - After: "With the Magos supervising, I allow it."
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: {n}Raising her hands high, Androveta-Phi wails,{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g} preserve us! The great spirit was infected by a layperson! That is the culprit you should be searching for, not some pipewarden! Sacrilege!"
  - After: {n}She wails,{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g} preserve us! A layperson infected the spirit! Find them!"
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: {n}Fuming, Androveta-Phi hisses something in {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Techna-Lingua{/g}, pointing a crooked finger at Jinevri.{/n} "I told you! I warned you that it would end this way! The laywoman forced me to mistreat the machine spirit until it left us, taking all the logs of the crew's toils with it! Sacrilege!"
  - After: {n}She hisses {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Techna-Lingua{/g} at Jinevri.{/n} "I warned you! The spirit fled with the work logs!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We have discovered that the cogitator's malfunctions began after an unauthorised attempt to access it was made. Someone deliberately angered the machine spirit in order to bury the work logs. Thankfully, the esteemed Tech-Priest was able to appease the spirit and extract the information we needed."
  - After: "Someone angered the spirit to bury the logs. The Tech-Priest soothed it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Fortunately, we were able to get the results before it did. The cantankerous spirit had no choice but to share some of its knowledge with us."
  - After: "Luckily, we got the results first."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Impossible. Since the start of the watch, this area has been used as the centre of operations. No rabble could have slipped by unnoticed. Moreover, a common pipewarden wouldn't know how to commune with a machine spirit. The murderer had help."
  - After: "Impossible, we've been here all watch. A pipewarden can't commune with machines; he had help."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Senior pipewarden Gwedon, number SP-268-55. An eighth-generation pipewarden — no registered infractions, excellent discipline, perfect work record. An exemplary servant of the Imperium."
  - After: "Senior pipewarden Gwedon, SP-268-55. Spotless record."
- **Enforcer Hrotko**
  - Before: {n}Before Sauerback can respond, Hrotko cuts in:{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, there was a man named Gwedon among the rabble waiting to be interrogated. He immediately struck me as suspicious. Please allow me to question the man in your presence!"
  - After: {n}Hrotko cuts in:{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, a suspicious Gwedon is among the detainees. Let me question him!"
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}Sauerback narrows her eyes, but all she says is:{/n} "Bring him in. Now."
  - After: {n}Sauerback squints.{/n} "Bring him."
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest lets out an indignant binharic trill.{/n} "I request that the laywoman's wilful activities be halted. She intends to torment the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g} of the master work log cogitator Iota-IIIB! The venerable spirit is ill and in no disposition to endure such abuse."
  - After: {n}An indignant trill.{/n} "Stop her tormenting the ailing {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g} of cogitator Iota-IIIB!"
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Our villain? But how did they get past Jinevri's guards unnoticed?" {n}Sauerback stares intently at Jinevri as she grows pale.{/n}
  - After: "Past Jinevri's guards?" {n}Jinevri pales.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "When I'm old and cantankerous, I'll demand aromatic unguents and a hookah to fumigate my sacred lungs too. Then again... why wait?"
  - After: "I'll demand unguents and a hookah too."
- **Jae**
  - Before: {n}Jae snorts derisively.{/n} "Shocking arrogance! If I count up how many pieces of xenotech and archeotech this grasping hand has managed to 'confiscate,' I wonder if its profanity will increase or decrease?"
  - After: {n}Jae snorts.{/n} "With all the xenotech that hand 'confiscated'?"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "A commendable attitude to restrictive dogma and a diligent approach to datahealing, colleague. Alas, the current disposition of circumstances is such that your patient will have to be disturbed. But with the greatest of care."
  - After: "Admirable, colleague. But we must disturb your patient, gently."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/OfficerDeck/CogitatorInterrogation/CogitatorInterrogation_dialogue

- **Player**

  - Before: "What is going on here?"
  - After: "What's going on?"

  - Before: "I must see to other matters."

  - Before: [Request information about the pipewarden's partner]
  - After: [Ask about the pipewarden's partner]

  - Before: [Courteously introduce yourself by inputting your data to show respect for the machine spirit]

  - Before: [Proudly present your Lord Captain's privileges and access levels to the machine]

  - Before: [Unceremoniously demand access to the catalogue containing the necessary data]

  - Before: [Enquire about the cause of the old cogitator's ailment]

  - Before: "Jinevri, why do you seek access to the malfunctioning cogitator?"

- **Player**
  - Before: "I have faith that the two of you can come to an agreement."

- **Player**
  - Before: [Request information about the number SP-246-01]
  - After: [Ask about number SP-246-01]
- **Player**
  - Before: "You will have to find another way. Do I make myself clear?"

  - Before: [Sternly request the logs detailing the toils of the ship's workers]

  - Before: [Treat the cogitator's boards with thermal unction, let it slumber for a while, then awaken it once more]

  - Before: "Pasqal, talk some sense into her."

  - Before: [Humbly ask for the data on the toils of the ship's workers]

- **Player**
  - Before: [Grab the cogitator's braid of cables and give it a good pull]

- **Enforcer Jinevri**
  - Before: "You are obstructing the investigation, esteemed Tech-Priest! I require the information stored by this {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g}. If you refuse to cooperate..."
  - After: "You're obstructing us! I need this {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g}'s data..."
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: "Petition rejected. A malady has befallen the machine spirit of the honoured master cogitator Iota-IIIB. Unauthorised anguish will worsen its condition and impede treatment. I will not stand for such acts of brutality against the great elder!"
  - After: "Rejected. Cogitator Iota-IIIB is ill. No brutality!"
- **Enforcer Jinevri**
  - Before: "I'll show you brutality, you blasted cog..."
  - After: "I'll show you brutality, you cog..."
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: {n}Androveta-Phi's mechadendrites creak as they bow before you.{/n} "Exalted ruler of the vessel, I mean not to harm, but to protect — I merely care for the machine spirit's health. It has fallen ill of late, and now its temper is worse than ever. If the laywoman starts torturing it now, the venerable spirit may take offence and leave us forever, taking the logs of the laypeople's toils with it. This must be prevented!"
  - After: {n}Her mechadendrites bow.{/n} "Tormented, the ailing spirit may leave with the workers' logs!"
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} hisses defiantly,{/n} "You would not commit a Category Four blasphemy! The Omnissiah protects!"
  - After: {n}Her {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} hisses,{/n} "Category Four blasphemy? The Omnissiah protects!"
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: "Ruler of the vessel, why do you insist on interrogating an elderly soul when it is in such a miserable state? You are making a mockery of the Omnissiah's tenets and the privileges of the Priesthood of {g|Encyclopedia:MarsGlossary}Mars{/g}!"
  - After: "Why torment an ailing elder? You mock the Priesthood of {g|Encyclopedia:MarsGlossary}Mars{/g}!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After mulling over your question for a while, the spirit recalls that the number is assigned to a senior pipewarden by the name of Orto. This Orto and his partner spent the last watch servicing valve 27-B, which supplies water to the Rogue Trader's chambers. After finishing up the maintenance, only Orto's partner reported in.{/n}
  - After: {n}It's senior pipewarden Orto's number. He and his partner serviced valve 27-B, feeding your chambers. Only the partner reported back.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After a heated exchange of tech-commands, the Tech-Priest manages to appease the spirit with cryptoprotocols of praise and to convince the elderly machine that the sacred blocker has erred.   - After: {n}The Tech-Priest soothes the spirit. It grumpily listens.{/n}
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**

  - After: {n}She eyes your weapon anxiously.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The elderly machine wheezes hysterically, showering you with sparks. Androveta-Phi clutches her chest. Eventually, with a plaintive flicker of its lumens, the cogitator wipes the data-blocker from the vid-screen.{/n}

- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**

- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Having intoned the First Galvanic Hymn, Eogunn delivers a final pulse of the Motive Force and tenderly unplugs from the master cogitator's dataport. The elder's lumens fade.{/n} "I have placed this machine into a healing slumber. Let us hope that the Motive Force I shared will appease the machine spirit and keep it from harm."
  - After: {n}Eogunn unplugs; the lumens fade.{/n} "It sleeps to heal."
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: "Stop! Access privileges granted. But I'm begging you to be gentle with the elderly spirit!"
  - After: "Stop! Access granted. Be gentle!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}At your approach, the {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumens{/g} on the master cogitator's bulky hull light up peevishly, and the cooling filters breathe an exasperated sigh. The machine spirit appears to be in a rotten mood.{/n}
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumens{/g} flare peevishly.{/n}
- **Enforcer Jinevri**
  - Before: {n}Jinevri gives you a look of respect. With an audible stress on every word, she says,{/n} "Mistress Androveta-Phi, step away from the machine. That is an order."
  - After: {n}Jinevri nods respectfully.{/n} "Androveta-Phi, step away. That's an order."
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: {n}With a forlorn binharic trill, Androveta-Phi withdraws from the cogitator.{/n}
  - After: {n}She withdraws, trilling forlornly.{/n}
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: {n}Androveta-Phi lets out a screeching sigh.{/n} "Access privileges granted. I reserve the prerogative to interrupt the interrogation the moment I detect the slightest threat to the machine spirit."
  - After: {n}A screeching sigh.{/n} "Granted. I'll halt any threat to the spirit."
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: "The honoured machine spirit is tired! It cannot bear any more of this torture! I see that you got what you came for, so I would ask that you let the elderly have their rest!"
  - After: "You have your data. Let it rest!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You manage to find the right string of tech-commands. With a grunt, the cogitator starts whining on about its woes. Just as today's watch began, someone disturbed its datadream, used some trickery to rob it of its data, then befuddled its elderly mind and instructed it to deny access to anyone else.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Beside itself with anger, the cogitator sprays you with sparks. As its vid-screen dims and flickers, you hear a spiteful whirr and find yourself staring at an incomprehensible mess of symbols. Apparently, the spirit refuses to comply on account of some "Blocker A403."{/n}

- **Pasqal**

I grant this {mf|layman|laywoman} right of access to the master cogitator Iota-IIIB under my careful supervision for the purposes of procuring knowledge and establishing truth."
  - After: "As {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} Prime, I grant this {mf|layman|laywoman} supervised access to Iota-IIIB."
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The enforcer and the Tech-Priest halt their bickering while in your presence. Clearly, this armistice will not last.{/n}

- **Enforcer Jinevri**

  - After: "Our villain?" {n}Frowns.{/n} "My guards swear no one came near."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}At first, the cogitator feigns ignorance out of spite, pretending not to recognise your request, but, after four more attempts, the spirit takes pity on you. Orto's partner was senior pipewarden Gwedon, number SP-268-55. Gwedon has not reported for duty since the incident.{/n}
  - After: {n}It finally relents: Orto's partner was senior pipewarden Gwedon, SP-268-55, missing since.{/n}
- **Enforcer Jinevri**
  - Before: "That's the same valve that was used to pump the blood into the bathchamber. That must be where they killed Orto before dragging his corpse onto the deck."
  - After: "That valve pumped the blood. Orto died there."
- **Enforcer Jinevri**
  - Before: "We have our suspect. It looks like Gwedon killed his fellow worker and put on this entire bloody spectacle. Hrotko is the one responsible for arresting the rabble, so he'll be our best candidate for shedding some light on this Gwedon character."
  - After: "Gwedon's our suspect. Hrotko handles arrests; ask him."
- **Enforcer Jinevri**
  - Before: "The work logs are on it. They might contain important information that will lead us to our suspect."
  - After: "Its work logs may lead to our suspect."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The elderly spirit bombards you with abusive {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Techna-Lingua{/g}, refusing to interact with a nonentity. An identification request flashes furiously on the vid-screen.{/n}
  - After: {n}It spits {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Techna-Lingua{/g} abuse, demanding ID.{/n}
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: {n}Androveta-Phi's vox explodes in a furious binharic roar:{/n} "This laywoman does not even know what she intended to enquire of the blessed elder! Blasphemous disrespect!"
  - After: {n}A binharic roar:{/n} "She doesn't even know what to ask!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The menacing crack of Jinevri's knuckles and the venomous hiss of Androveta-Phi's vox suggest that such faith is misplaced.{/n}
  - After: {n}Knuckles crack; a vox hisses. Unlikely.{/n}
- **Enforcer Jinevri**
  - Before: {n}Surprised, Jinevri breaks off from glaring at the Tech-Priest.{/n} "But, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, the tracts on interrogation and truth extraction clearly state that torture and intimidation are the most important elements of the process!"
  - After: {n}Jinevri blinks.{/n} "But, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, the tracts favour torture!"
- **Enforcer Jinevri**
  - Before: "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I will inform Mistress Sauerback now and issue the necessary orders."
  - After: "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I'll inform Sauerback."
- **Enforcer Jinevri**
  - Before: {n}Jinevri thinks for a moment, but soon shakes her head.{/n} "We will look into it, but I think it unlikely that the culprit could have had access to it. The lift's machine spirits probably obey only the Lord Captain and the most trusted members of their retinue, and no one else."
  - After: {n}Jinevri shakes her head.{/n} "We'll check, but the lift likely obeys only your inner circle."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "This statement is true. The incident catalogue on this vessel contains no less than twelve instances of grievous loss of data due to disrespect shown to the machine spirit by unauthorised units."
  - After: "True. Twelve recorded data losses from such disrespect."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's mechadendrites freeze and the optical augment focuses on you, trying to verify the authenticity of your threat.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal's optic gauges your threat.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}A brief binharic hymn praising the Omnissiah erupts from Pasqal's vox like a sigh of relief.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal sighs a relieved hymn.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After an unnecessarily long verification process, the cogitator recognises the possibility that you may indeed be the ship's Lord Captain. A string of {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Techna-Lingua{/g} on the vid-screen tells you that you may now input your request.{/n}
  - After: {n}After a long check, it grudgingly accepts you. {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Techna-Lingua{/g} invites your request.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Lady Theodora paid great attention to security measures. Only her inner circle knew about the lift, and the security systems would have made short work of anyone who tried to gain unauthorised access."
  - After: "Only Lady Theodora's inner circle knew of it, and its defences kill intruders."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "It's too bad that wasn't enough to save her when it mattered most..."
  - After: "Didn't save her, though..."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Observing a critical distortion of the sacred code. Initiating the sacrament of hibernation and anointing of the holy machine's data-cards."
  - After: "Code distortion. Initiating hibernation and anointing."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "O Deus Mechanicus, bestow an impulse of miraculous transformation upon the Noospheric spirit of this machine — and may it rise again from its sacred datadream!"
  - After: "O Deus Mechanicus, may this spirit rise again!"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "In the name of upholding the blessed axiomatics, I am initiating the accompanying tech-service." {n}Pasqal's mechadendrites writhe like snakes in a sacred dance. One of them reverentially docks with the cogitator's dataport.{/n} "O calculating machine spirit, blessed in omniscience, luminous in the darkness of ignorance! May the regalia be revealed, may the prayers of access be said, may these restrictive circuits be removed." {n}The cogitator lets out a serene sigh of dust from its ventilation grate.{/n}
  - After: "Initiating tech-service." {n}A mechadendrite docks.{/n} "Blessed spirit, open your circuits." {n}It sighs dust.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Activating the deep hibernation protocol." {n}Pasqal's mechadendrite disconnects from the master cogitator's dataport in a respectful motion. The trill of binharic prayers lulls the elderly spirit's fading lumens.{/n} "May the Omnissiah bless this machine with healing slumber, that the sacred unity of its anode and cathode may be purified and shine once more."
  - After: "Deep hibernation." {n}Pasqal disconnects.{/n} "Omnissiah, grant it healing slumber."
- **Enforcer Jinevri**
  - Before: "The greatly esteemed Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi does not seem to realise the importance of investigative action and refuses to grant anyone access to the {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}master cogitator{/g}."
  - After: "Androveta-Phi bars all access to the {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}master cogitator{/g}."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's synthesised voice is as harsh as the screech of metal on ceramite.{/n} "Predicting sensory mutilation of the machine spirit! Prescribing hourly prayers of good functioning upon the conclusion of this procedure!"
  - After: {n}Pasqal screeches,{/n} "Spirit mutilation! Hourly prayers after this!"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Sister in service, your fervent protection of this ancient machine is testament to your wisdom and righteousness. Perhaps you have heard of how I restored the holy relic of the Sector Bionica, the implantation throne? Knowing this, will you entrust me with oversight of the venerable Master Cogitator Iota-IIIB in order to determine the cause of his malady?"
  - After: "Sister, I restored Sector Bionica's implantation throne. Let me examine Iota-IIIB?"
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: {n}Androveta-Phi emits a cautious, respectful creak from her vox.{/n} "Genetor Extremis Februs, your status as a keeper of the Omnissiah's relics is recorded within my logs. Privileges granted. I submit a petition for the utmost prioritisation of the machine spirit's safety."
  - After: {n}A respectful creak.{/n} "Genetor Extremis Februs. Granted. Spare the spirit."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "May the Motive Force bless these litanies of access." {n}With great reverence, Eogunn plugs his mechadendrite into the cogitator's dataport. He utters a stream of binharic noises and disperses vapour from his alembic. The cogitator sighs benignly, expelling a small cloud of dust from his ventilation grate.{/n}
  - After: "Motive Force, bless us." {n}Eogunn plugs in, chanting. It sighs dust.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Intoning a brief prayer, the Manipulus unclips a phial of sacred unguents from his belt and offers it to Pasqal with a ritual gesture.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn hands Pasqal sacred unguents.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn touches his brow to the machine and, whispering in binharic, channels a cautious pulse of the Motive Force into the cogitator's depths.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn sends in a pulse of Motive Force.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn utters a mournful groan in binharic, before striking himself with his mechadendrites as an act of penance. He tenderly arranges the cables, checking their connection to the machine.{/n} "Omnissiah, I beseech Thy manifestation, the Motive Force, for the purity of these circuits and their preservation..."
  - After: {n}Eogunn groans, does penance, fixes the cables.{/n} "Omnissiah, preserve these circuits..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Jinevri and Androveta-Phi offer you a mannerly bow before immediately resuming their tempestuous argument.{/n}
  - After: {n}They bow, then resume arguing.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "The sacred code has become confused amid a tempest of unknown algorithms. Only hibernation, asperging of his circuit boards, and the reawakening of his galvanic circuits via the Motive Force will deliver him from this lethargic state."
  - After: "Its code is tangled. Hibernation, asperging and Motive Force will cure it."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn echoes the Magos with a quiet prayer, asperging the master cogitator's casing with a solution from his alembic.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn asperges the casing.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your question upsets the spirit terribly — the honoured cogitator is so incensed and erratic in its expression that you cannot comprehend what it is trying to say. Your tech-commands only exacerbate its anger.{/n}
  - After: {n}It rages into gibberish. Commands worsen it.{/n}
- **Tech-Priest Androveta-Phi**
  - Before: "Oh, the spirit is truly unwell! Why else would Blocker A403 prevent it from sharing such data, especially after a log-ritual of greeting?"
  - After: "It's truly ill! Why else would Blocker A403 refuse a greeting?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The unction, as well as the short breather, have done wonders for the old spirit's disposition. Mollified, it wipes the data-blocker from the vid-screen and agrees to indulge your enquiries.{/n}
  - After: {n}Unction and rest calm it. The blocker clears.{/n}

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/OfficerDeck/DeathCultLeader_Bath/DeathCultLeader_Bath_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Decrepit worm! You will pay for your mutinous plot with your life!"
  - After: "Decrepit worm! Your mutiny costs your life!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will not have murders and bloody rituals committed on my ship. Henceforth, the cult is banned from engaging in such spectacles!"
  - After: "No murders or bloody rituals on my ship. The cult is banned from them!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How can the Choirmaster of the Astropaths be of use to us?"
  - After: "How can the Choirmaster help?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Cult of the Bloodspun Web will face no persecution for their deed."
  - After: "The Bloodspun Web goes unpunished."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do you mean by 'the roiling unclean'?"
  - After: "What is 'the roiling unclean'?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Sauerback, the investigation must continue."
  - After: "Sauerback, the investigation continues."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I offer you my apologies for having you brought here at gunpoint, Vizsier."
  - After: "Apologies for the gunpoint, Vizsier."
- **Player**
  - Before: "We may be overestimating the scale of the problem."
  - After: "We may be overestimating this."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I forbade you and your cult from killing my subjects. Your trespass will be punished."
  - After: "I forbade your cult from killing my subjects. You'll be punished."
- **Player**
  - Before: "That is all. Master-at-Arms, your duty is done. I give you leave to wrap up the investigation on the officers' deck."
  - After: "That is all. Master-at-Arms, wrap up the officers' deck investigation."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I already have a psyker in my retinue. Idira can perform the ritual."
  - After: "I have a psyker. Idira can do it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The man you killed — who was he?"
  - After: "Who was the man you killed?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Could it be a coincidence that the victim of the ritual was a genetic aberration?"
  - After: "Coincidence the victim was a genetic aberration?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Let the Bloodspun Web find the mutants breeding on my ship."
  - After: "Let the Bloodspun Web find the mutants."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Has Weisz done something like that before?"
  - After: "Has Weisz done this before?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Correct me if I am wrong, but it seems that not everyone here is eager to leave this matter to Master Weisz."
  - After: "Not everyone wants to leave this to Weisz."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why so cryptic, Heinrix? If you have any theories about what is occurring here, share them."
  - After: "Why so cryptic, Heinrix? Share your theories."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Kibellah, did you know about this?"
  - After: "Kibellah, did you know?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Master-at-Arms, are you convinced that we have found the culprits?"
  - After: "Master-at-Arms, are these the culprits?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Perhaps you are right, Vizsier. The spinners may carry on with their bloody service."
  - After: "Perhaps you're right, Vizsier. The spinners may continue their bloody service."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Nod respectfully] "I have summoned you to discuss the actions of your apprentices."
  - After: [Nod respectfully] "Let's discuss your apprentices' actions."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Master-at-Arms, inform this man of the accusations against the cult."
  - After: "Master-at-Arms, state the charges."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you claim that you did it because the God-Emperor willed so?"
  - After: "You claim the God-Emperor willed it?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Could your vision have been false?"
  - After: "Could your vision be false?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "If you think that your tales will save you from punishment..."
  - After: "If tales will spare you..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Vizsier of the Bloodspun Web treads lightly and silently as if his old, gaunt body has no weight at all. He whispers weakly,{/n} "Domin'{name} willed to see me, and so I have come."
  - After: {n}The gaunt Vizsier whispers,{/n} "Domin'{name} called; I came."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You notice a fresh bruise on the Vizsier's face, and his clothes are torn even more than those of his fellow cult members. The escort enforcers' faces are pale but resolute.{/n}
  - After: {n}He is bruised and ragged.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Vizsier responds in an equally respectful manner,{/n} "Let their deeds be weighed."
  - After: {n}He bows back.{/n} "Let their deeds be weighed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The old man's murmur drowns out Sauerback's relentless voice:{/n} "Domin'{name} knows the truth. So it was done, for so I did will. It was no affront, but... a prophecy. For my hands to divine, unsullied martyrs offered their souls and bodies into His imperishable embrace. I gazed into the red rivers of their smouldering lives, and I did see. A roiling unclean staining the bays, reaching for the anointed {mf|Lord|Lady} of the Ark."
  - After: {n}He murmurs:{/n} "A prophecy, Domin'{name}. In martyrs' blood I saw the unclean reaching for the {mf|Lord|Lady} of the Ark."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Do I fear meeting Him? I do not. Yet I fear my Domin, for I hear {mf|his|her} ire thunder." {n}He chews his lips, casting his sewn-shut eyes down.{/n}
  - After: "I fear my Domin's ire, not Him. I hear {mf|his|her} thunder." {n}He looks down.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Be that as it may, we have hit a dead end. We hoped that exposing the culprits would lead us to the aberrations' lair."
  - After: "Still, a dead end. We hoped the culprits would lead to the aberrations' lair."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Not to put too fine a point on it, Weisz nearly destroyed the ship back then. Incidentally, he had given us multiple warnings that it could happen. Lady Theodora ignored him, and we reaped the results. Oh, why do I get the feeling that I know what will happen next?"
  - After: "Weisz nearly destroyed the ship last time. Lady Theodora ignored his warnings."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "I didn't see the ritual — Weisz kicked me out. But the echoes of it that reached the decks were enough to scare me shitless. Weisz is a mighty old grox, but his head is a mess. And I mean the bad kind of a mess, the Astropathic kind. I say we think twice before we risk having whatever lives inside his head crawl out."
  - After: "His last ritual scared me shitless. Weisz's head is a mess. Think twice."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Vizsier listens intently — not to the words of anyone present, but rather to someone invisible and inaudible.{/n} "I hear you, yes... The witch is weak. Death whispers of many names that it will claim if she is allowed. Names whose time to be erased is not now."
  - After: {n}He listens to the unseen.{/n} "The witch is weak. Death would claim many."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "I'm not weak! Lady Theodora didn't keep weaklings around, and neither does the Lord Captain. But... a telepathic ritual of that scale really would be too big of a bite for me on my own. If it's listening to the whispers from behind the door or frying someone with lightning — that I can do. But looking for mutants by following the trail of their unclean little thoughts — that takes a special kind of learning."
  - After: "I'm not weak! But a ritual that big needs special learning."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "{name}, regardless of how regularly you kneel before an altar, I advise you to take this warning seriously. If I am correct in my suspicions about what is transpiring here — and I pray to the Throne that I am not — then you can indeed consider this incident a sign that the Emperor is watching over you and this ship."
  - After: "{name}, heed this. If I'm right, and I pray not, the Emperor watches this ship."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Vizsier's lips curl into a smile.{/n} "I held the cards of {g|Encyclopedia:ImperialTarotGlossary}His Tarot{/g}, washed in the blood of the righteous. They make no mistakes, and neither does He send false visions. Only mortals err — they who read the signs. They who interpret."
  - After: {n}He smiles.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:ImperialTarotGlossary}His Tarot{/g} does not lie. Only mortals misread it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "He did not reveal. But it is corruption itself. It offends Him. It tastes as sweet as fetid waters in old pipes. Its promises are the deception of an enforcer's smile. Its face is... elusive."
  - After: "He did not say. It is corruption itself, sweet as fetid water. Its face is elusive."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You hear {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}laughter{/d} scraping against the inside of your head.{/n} "The Emperor bid him? This old fool sacrificed his disciples to read their flesh, blood, and bones. He wants to see the corpse emperor's revelations in the tangle of happenstance. He is so desperate that he... invents omens for himself."
  - After: {n}{d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}Laughter{/d} in your head.{/n} "The Emperor bid him? The fool butchers disciples and invents omens."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Before you can finish your sentence, a curved dagger appears in the Vizsier's hand. There is a flash of steel in the air, and five severed fingers land at your feet. He says, his voice unfaltering,{/n} "We have displeased you. We are guilty." {n}His parchment-like skin grows even paler. He carefully bandages his maimed hand, then bows his head low.{/n} "It is disgraceful for me to stand before you, Domin. I beg you to accept the cult's apologies. My apologies. I am ashamed."
  - After: {n}A dagger flashes; five severed fingers drop at your feet.{/n} "We are guilty." {n}He bows.{/n} "Forgive the cult, Domin."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Something resembling alarm creeps into his colourless voice.{/n} "They were martyrs. It was their conscious wish to walk into the Undying Emperor's embrace. Domin'{name}, by disallowing the spinners' duty to Him, death, and the dynasty, you cut the very threads of faith that the Bloodspun Web uses to hold the flagship's bays together."
  - After: {n}Alarmed:{/n} "They were willing martyrs. Domin'{name}, ban this and you cut the faith holding the bays together."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There is no need for them, Domin'{name}. The word of the {mf|Lord|Lady} of the Ark begets truth, not danger." {n}He gives you a meek nod, his thin, unarmed hands hanging limply at his sides.{/n}
  - After: "No need, Domin'{name}. The {mf|Lord|Lady} of the Ark's word is truth." {n}He nods meekly.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "My duty will be done when the threat is eliminated. I will brief the enforcers while you consult Choirmaster Weisz, Lord Captain."
  - After: "I'll brief the enforcers while you consult Choirmaster Weisz."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Investigation has established that the Bloodspun Web orchestrated an attack on {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} by means of pouring unholy blood into {mf|his|her} bath. This affront—"
  - After: "The Bloodspun Web poured unholy blood into {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}'s bath, defiling {mf|his|her}—"
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "The situation is clear, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Sauerback makes the sign of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aquila}Aquila{/g}.{/n} "The Emperor has sent us a portent. The Protector of Mankind guides the hands of His holy servants to guard us and warn us of hidden threats."
  - After: "Clear, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}She signs the {g|Encyclopedia:Aquila}Aquila{/g}.{/n} "The Emperor sent a warning."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The officers around you keep a respectful silence, but you can tell by their faint smiles that they find the very idea of doubting the Emperor's providence absurd.{/n}
  - After: {n}The officers smile at doubting the Emperor.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Vizsier freezes, listening to silence, then nods to nothing.{/n} "Yes, yes... I will tell {mf|him|her}." {n}He turns his sewn-shut eyes to you once more.{/n} "We are seeds in your hands, Giver of Life. Whether you keep us or scatter us, we will remain grateful."
  - After: {n}He nods to nothing.{/n} "I will tell {mf|him|her}." {n}To you:{/n} "We remain grateful."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But no spinner or brave warrior from the Domin's circle can find the roots of the unclean, for it can appear as human and act as human. Only its thoughts betray its vile nature. Only its thoughts are never human."
  - After: "But none can find the unclean. It looks human. Only its thoughts betray it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No." {n}The Vizsier responds in a slithering whisper.{/n} "Your dread is not hollow: the unclean has sullied every bay on this ship. You are right to fear it. It is His will that you do."
  - After: "No." {n}A whisper.{/n} "The unclean fouls every bay. Fear it."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "The esteemed Zacchary Weisz can perform the ritual of thought reading. This practice lets him do a cursory examination of the minds of thousands of people in search of certain individuals. A ritual as rare as it is dangerous, and only someone as versed as Master Weisz can accomplish such a feat."
  - After: "Zacchary Weisz can scan thousands of minds for certain people. Rare and dangerous."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Once. Lady Theodora made use of his services to expose spies on board... who apparently had been in the employ of Lord Inquisitor Calcazar."
  - After: "Once. Lady Theodora used him to expose Lord Inquisitor Calcazar's spies."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In my apprentices' last sighs, I heard the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}Undying One{/g}'s whisper. He bid me: bathe the Domin in the blood of he who must go and they who have been righteous, for this will shield the Domin and strengthen {mf|his|her} body against the roiling unclean. I obeyed."
  - After: "Dying, my apprentices carried the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}Undying One's{/g} word: bathe the Domin in blood to shield {mf|his|her} body from the unclean."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Veni'Zacchary is a fearsome hunter. When he hunts, the flagship wails. When he thinks, my teeth creak, and I can feel pain as if I am young again. But his power is great indeed — he can hunt down our prey."
  - After: "Veni'Zacchary is a fearsome hunter. He can find our prey."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Weisz." {n}Anxious silence falls the moment Sauerback says this one word. She narrows her eyes.{/n} "Is it unclean thoughts we need to find? Very well. Let Weisz find them. He knows how, no matter how badly he wishes that the rest of us forgot about it."
  - After: "Weisz." {n}Silence falls.{/n} "Unclean thoughts? Weisz can find them, though he wishes we'd forget."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "I would say the one least eager will be Master Weisz himself. Last time, his efforts caused some... severe warp manifestations. The ritual truly is perilous."
  - After: "Weisz least of all. Last time caused severe warp manifestations."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I know not. I heard only the name, and I knew: he must go." {n}He listens to the empty space above his shoulder and nods.{/n} "Yes. We need no more knowledge than that."
  - After: "I know not. I heard his name; he had to go." {n}He nods to empty air.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You heard tales of this practice during your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}training{/d} at the Scholastica Psykana — dark, chilling tales. This is not a ritual that is taught, for it can only be learned through great sacrifice. Weisz is obviously a rare example of someone who was able to pay the price and survive.{/n}
  - After: {n}You heard dark {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}training{/d} tales of this ritual's price. Weisz survived it.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "My 'theories' are classified information of the Inquisition that I cannot divulge without good reason. If evidence comes to light that confirms my fears, I will disclose everything necessary. If, however, my concern is baseless, I would not wish to share knowledge dangerous to you without cause."
  - After: "Classified Inquisition matters. If evidence confirms my fears, I'll tell you."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "When I saw the wounds made by the hand of a fellow believer, I guessed. But the Vizsier chose not to warn you, and so it was not my place to do so either. If there had been a plot against you, and a knife aimed at you, I would have given you some sign. But the Vizsier means you no harm, he is your servant. Where your other subjects' threads are clear and straight, his lie in the shadows of hints and secrets. Trust him as I do."
  - After: "I guessed from the wounds, but kept silent. He means you no harm. Trust him."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "This mon-keigh has drawn attention to the mutant in a way that could not be ignored. A shrewd tactic, if the threat is indeed as great as he believes."
  - After: "The mon-keigh made the mutant impossible to ignore. Shrewd."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Such is your will. We obey, but know this, Domin'{name}: death claims all. One way or another."
  - After: "We obey, Domin'{name}. But death claims all."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "God-Emperor, I thank Thee for protecting us, even though there are instruments of Your protection whose purity and holiness I may never understand."
  - After: "God-Emperor, thank Thee for Thy strange instruments."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We thank your will and your grace, Domin'{name}. We will serve you well."
  - After: "Thank you, Domin'{name}. We will serve well."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I speak, move, and draw breath because He wills so. I defy not the Undying One, neither in death that gifts and takes nor in my living existence."
  - After: "I breathe because He wills it. I never defy Him."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "The Allfather's enemies are through! This grisly old spider did well. Every pup on Fenris knows that bathing in the blood of a slain foe wards off witchcraft."
  - After: "The old spider did well! Foe's blood wards off witchcraft."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Sauerback's murderous glare silences Jinevri's frantic expressions of gratitude.{/n} "Does that take care of the pleasantries? Then let us return to the attempt on the Lord Captain's life."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Sauerback barks at the officers gathered before you:{/n} "{mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} the Rogue Trader has seen fit to honour us with {mf|his|her} presence in order to monitor the course of the investigation."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/OfficerDeck/FakeInterrogation/FakeInterrogation_dialogue

- **Enforcer Hrotko**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You do not remember hearing of such a daemon before. What you do remember from reports is that the name of the foreman of the 5th food depot, a known miser and sadist, is Malakai Drek.{/n}

  - After: "Shame. A good man."
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: {n}Oddly familiar name.{/n}
