  - After: {n}He smiles warmly.{/n} "I could talk about the chapel for hours."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira scoffs contemptuously.{/n} "For once in your life, you could just admit that it doesn't take a tongue calloused from prayer to handle the warp's dangers!"
  - After: {n}Idira scoffs.{/n} "Admit it, prayer isn't what handles the warp!"

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/ShipTemple/ShipConfessorDead/ShipConfessorDead_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "We will do as Kibellah proposes."
  - After: "We'll do as Kibellah proposes."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Enough blood has been spilt. I hereby pardon this deluded fool, to show the rest of the vessel that I am not the monster that Nemesite paints me to be."
  - After: "Enough blood. I pardon this fool, to prove I'm not the monster Nemesite claims."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Sauerback, get him an escort so that he may tell the lower decks that Nemesite is a liar and a scoundrel. You will persuade him to be eloquent, will you not?"
  - After: "Sauerback, escort him to tell the lower decks Nemesite is a liar. Make him eloquent."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Creed must be strictly observed aboard the vessel. Since the voidsmen are wavering in their faith, let the High Factotum find a true servant of the Ecclesiarchy elsewhere."
  - After: "The Creed must be upheld. Let the High Factotum find a true Ecclesiarchy servant elsewhere."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Appoint a loyal crew member who is known for the strength of their faith — someone the children of the void will recognise as their own. We do not want any outsiders."
  - After: "Appoint a devout crew member the voidborn see as their own. No outsiders."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I trust the Bloodspun Web and grant the cult the honour of guiding the congregation aboard my ship."
  - After: "I grant the Bloodspun Web the honour of guiding my ship's congregation."
- **Player**
  - Before: "We are done here. Come."
  - After: "We're done. Come."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It is not my place to judge."
  - After: "It's not my place to judge."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are different. He is a murderer, but you understand the true value of human death."
  - After: "You differ. He murders; you understand death's true value."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are indeed alike. And it is up to you to prove before the God-Emperor's gaze that the Tenets of the Web are stronger than whatever Nemesite believes in."
  - After: "You are alike. Prove before the God-Emperor that the Tenets of the Web are stronger."
- **Player**
  - Before: "To equate a true servant of the God-Emperor with this apostate is a heresy unto itself!"
  - After: "Equating a true servant of the God-Emperor with this apostate is heresy!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I want you to find a preacher on Dargonus who would kill their own mother for me. I will accept nothing less than absolute loyalty. Is that clear?"
  - After: "Find me a preacher on Dargonus who'd kill their own mother for me. Absolute loyalty. Clear?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Hrotko, how did you come to be here at just the right moment?"
  - After: "Hrotko, how were you here just in time?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Are there any other senior officers helping you?"
  - After: "Are other senior officers helping you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How many more of you mutineers are hiding on my ship? I want to know your names, I want to know where you meet — everything."
  - After: "How many mutineers are on my ship? Names, meeting places — everything."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address Ziek] "I have questions for you, traitor."
  - After: [Address Ziek] "Questions for you, traitor."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have learned all I need."
  - After: "I've learned enough."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Yes, both of you have been brainwashed. Stop looking for omens and try using your own judgement instead."
  - After: "You're both brainwashed. Stop seeking omens; use your judgement."
- **Player**
  - Before: "So he was connected to the genetic aberration as well. Delightful."
  - After: "So he was tied to the aberration too. Delightful."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Nod at Ziek] "Now, let us decide what to do with our surviving traitor."
  - After: [Nod at Ziek] "Now, what to do with our surviving traitor."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Were you serving Nemesite for a cause or simply for money?"
  - After: "Did you serve Nemesite for a cause or money?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "They were waiting for us. It was a trap."
  - After: "They were waiting. A trap."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}Her ruminations are interrupted by a furious hiss. Sauerback snarls a curse through her teeth and spits at Adalbert's smoking remains. Her left arm hangs limp and her face is mangled by shrapnel.{/n} "Lord Captain, we have a prisoner." {n}She points her weapon at the man standing hunched over in pain.{/n} "Permission to finish off the cur."
  - After: {n}Wounded, Sauerback spits on Adalbert's remains.{/n} "A prisoner, Lord Captain." {n}She aims at him.{/n} "Permission to finish him."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "We will make certain that the lower-deckers believe their 'hero' to be dead. We will leave the body to hang for a good long while, that the hopes of the mutineers may rot along with the corpse."
  - After: "We'll hang the body, so the mutineers' hopes rot."
- **Initiate Ziek**
  - Before: "P-pardon? Does this mean I can go?" {n}Ziek glances nervously about like a harried animal.{/n} "Have you really... Forgive me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... I thought you... But then... I'm so sorry!"
  - After: "P-pardon? I can go?" {n}Ziek glances about.{/n} "Forgive me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!"
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "That is one traitor dealt with, Lord Captain, but how many more have been poisoned by the false confessor's heresy? A new spiritual shepherd must be appointed quickly to banish any mutinous thoughts sown by the traitor from the minds of the crew and to strengthen their faith and obedience. Without the ship's confessor, the rabble will begin to whisper that the Emperor has forsaken us, and such doubts will only play into the rebels' hands."
  - After: "One traitor down, Lord Captain, but his heresy spread. Appoint a new confessor fast, or they'll say the Emperor forsook us."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "You honour us with this boon, Domin. I will relay your words to the Vizsier so that he may choose someone worthy."
  - After: "An honour, Domin. The Vizsier will choose someone worthy."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "As you command! I will order the chapel be restored as well."
  - After: "As you command! I'll restore the chapel."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "I will send agents to every deck. The next time Nemesite rears his head — which, I am certain, will happen sooner rather than later — we will be one step ahead of him, and not the other way round."
  - After: "Agents on every deck. Next time, we'll be ahead of Nemesite."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "I am thinking about Nemesite, my adversary. The more I learn about him, the more I see a vague reflection of myself. A twisted reflection, perhaps... but all too familiar. Like me, he was forced to tread the path of servitude from an early age, stripped of anything that might stand in the way of duty — a champion and a zealot left with nothing but an idea, forged and tempered by his mentor."
  - After: "Nemesite. I see myself in him, twisted: raised to serve, left only an idea forged by his mentor."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "This is true. Like a puppeteer, he pulls at the threads of other people's destinies, tangling and severing them. When I cut these threads, it is only as the Undying One commands: with timely precision. I must stop Nemesite so that I might save your subjects from premature death."
  - After: "True. He severs threads; I cut only as the Undying One commands."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Yes, Domin'{name}. Your words echo through my soul, and we are in accord. Nemesite will fall, for his ways are dark and have led him astray." {n}Kibellah trails a metal claw across her lips, sealing her promise with blood.{/n}
  - After: "We are in accord, Domin'{name}. Nemesite will fall." {n}She seals it in blood.{/n}
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Sauerback staggers away, and your gaze turns to the motionless Kibellah, staring at her own reflection within a pool of blood.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sauerback leaves. Kibellah stares into a pool of blood.{/n}
- **Initiate Ziek**
  - Before: "Down... with the tyrant..." {n}The broad-shouldered initiate who calls himself Ziek clutches a deep wound, glaring at you with hatred.{/n}
  - After: "Down... with the tyrant..." {n}Wounded Ziek glares.{/n}
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "All warriors fight for something, be it fame, life, wealth, or their loved ones. Nemesite cares nothing for these things: he sacrifices his kin, scorns glory, and amasses no riches. I am sure he would gladly give up his own life if necessary. Nemesite fights for an idea, and so that is where we must strike. Make his idea bleed, and he will be obligated to respond. And whoever is forced to react instead of acting, dies."
  - After: "Nemesite fights for an idea. Make it bleed and he must react. Whoever reacts instead of acting dies."
- **Initiate Ziek**
  - Before: {n}Ziek flashes you a bloody grin.{/n} "He promised us freedom!"
  - After: {n}Ziek grins bloodily.{/n} "He promised us freedom!"
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Yes, Lord Captain. Adalbert had been warned, yet he chose not to flee. Instead, he stayed behind to set a trap for us. Did he really believe this madness would succeed and he would somehow survive?"
  - After: "Yes. Adalbert was warned, yet stayed to trap us. Did he expect to live?"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "He did not want to survive. His only hope was to kill. Nemesite managed to turn his adoptive father into a blade pointed squarely at the Domin's throat, just as Adalbert himself had once turned Nemesite into a weapon. Neither of them feared death."
  - After: "He wanted only to kill. Nemesite made his adoptive father a blade, as Adalbert once made him."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}She looks away... but then turns back to you as if remembering something.{/n} "Domin'{name}... our conversation is not yet over. Please, stay with me for a few moments. There is something I want to ask."
  - After: {n}She turns back.{/n} "Domin'{name}, stay. I must ask something."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "You may be right. Perhaps we are defined not by what we are, but by what we serve. Thank you for this insight, Domin."
  - After: "Perhaps we're defined by what we serve. Thank you, Domin."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Do not kill him in vain." {n}Kibellah shakes her head.{/n} "Those who follow the Tenets of the Web know that, just as we serve death, so too does it serve us. Allow the death of this man to become an instrument in your hands, Domin'{name}. Pass off the traitor's body as that of Nemesite. Instil fear in his supporters. The enemy will be forced to act to undo this deception, exposing himself in the process."
  - After: "Don't waste his death, Domin'{name}." {n}She shakes her head.{/n} "Pass his body off as Nemesite's. The enemy must act, exposing himself."
- **Enforcer Hrotko**
  - Before: "I was praying, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Ever since you spared me, I have been praying a lot." {n}Hrotko's groomed face now looks haggard. His cheekbones jut out, and his former well-off appearance has taken on an air of noble piety.{/n} "And when I saw those vermin pull out their weapons, I considered it unacceptable to stand aside. I may have been found a bad officer, but not once have I been called a bad fighter. I am glad to see you in one piece. Today, I will be praying to the God-Emperor for your health."
  - After: "I was praying, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, as I have since you spared me." {n}Hrotko looks gaunt.{/n} "A bad officer, never a bad fighter."
- **Enforcer Hrotko**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, are you unharmed?" {n}Hrotko, formerly an enforcer and now an {d|Encyclopedia:HrotkoPriest}initiate{/d}, has not lost his usual cold composure, despite the fact that his white robes are stained with blood.{/n}
  - After: "Lord Captain, unharmed?" {n}Hrotko, now an {d|Encyclopedia:HrotkoPriest}initiate{/d}, is calm in bloodied robes.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "That devious, mind-twisting beast..." {n}Sauerback frowns with worry.{/n} "I have been going through my predecessor's archive recently, and I may have an idea as to what manner of creature this Nemesite is. We are dealing with a Kelermorph — a special variety of mutant filth in service of genetic cults. These creatures are made and raised to play the part of the people's leader, an inspiration for the mutinous rabble. A Kelermorph's purpose is to sow disorder and use the rebellion to eliminate the ruling elite, those who might be capable of opposing the xenos."
  - After: "That beast..." {n}Sauerback frowns.{/n} "The archives suggest a Kelermorph — a cult mutant bred to lead rebellions and kill rulers."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Too much evidence points to Nemesite being a Kelermorph, a special xenos unit bred for subversion. A Kelermorph utilises the discontent of the masses and incites them to revolt, with the end goal of removing local rulers loyal to the Imperium and installing Genestealer cultists in their place. This creature wears the mask of a populist leader, one who inspires the mutinous rabble. It will not stop until one of you is dead, {name}."
  - After: "Nemesite is likely a Kelermorph, bred to incite revolt for Genestealer cultists. It won't stop until one of you dies, {name}."
- **Initiate Ziek**
  - Before: "Even the confessor didn't know where it is. He was afraid of spies, or of giving his son's secrets away under torture. You see? You can't get to our champion!"
  - After: "Even the confessor didn't know, fearing torture. You'll never reach our champion!"
- **Initiate Ziek**
  - Before: "Officers? Ha! There is no one else among them who is pure! They only care about power and gorging themselves on the scraps you throw them, or else they would have long... long since turned against you." {n}Ziek can barely finish the sentence before he is beset by a torrent of gurgling coughs.{/n}
  - After: "Officers? None are pure! They gorge on your scraps." {n}He coughs wetly.{/n}
- **Initiate Ziek**
  - Before: "The confessor said every compartment has people who fight for our cause. They promised to take me into the circle of our most devoted believers. Then I would know... But even then, I would tell you nothing, not even under torture!"
  - After: "Every compartment has our fighters. But I'll tell you nothing!"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "This mon-keigh makes her traps deftly — with sharp edges and relentless bonds. Yet, once again, she uses blood. Blood and death... Not as a hunter, but as a killer."
  - After: "Deft traps. But blood again... a killer, not a hunter."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "You hunt with skill, blood scryer." {n}Ulfar nods in approval.{/n} "To smoke the foe out of his putrid burrow and provoke him to fight? Much smarter than chasing him around dark corners!"
  - After: {n}Ulfar nods.{/n} "Smart, blood scryer. Smoke him out!"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "You ought to see this, Domin'{name}." {n}Kibellah leans over the confessor's body and slices off the edge of his collar with her blade, revealing a tiny scar on the back of his neck. It looks just like the one the captured worker in the plasma drive chambers had, except that this one clearly healed a long time ago.{/n}
  - After: "Look, Domin'{name}." {n}Kibellah bares a healed scar on the confessor's neck, like the plasma drive worker's.{/n}
- **Initiate Ziek**
  - Before: "I doubt you'll like the answers."
  - After: "You won't like the answers."
- **Initiate Ziek**
  - Before: {n}The initiate only looks at you sullenly.{/n}
  - After: {n}He glares sullenly.{/n}
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "We now know much more about the enemy." {n}Kibellah ponderously runs her finger along the flat of the blade.{/n} "About just how deep the poison of conspiracy runs within the veins of your ship. But the Bloodspun Web has wrapped itself around its bays too tightly, and Nemesite can no longer hope to escape."
  - After: "Now we know how deep it runs." {n}She traces her blade.{/n} "But the Web holds the ship. Nemesite can't escape."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}Sauerback gives Ziek a bloodthirsty smile.{/n} "Did you hear that, wretch? It is not over for you yet. You are mine now, so you had best sing sweetly about your Nemesite. You may yet earn yourself an easy death."
  - After: {n}Sauerback smiles.{/n} "You're mine, wretch. Sing about Nemesite and earn an easy death."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah gives a barely perceptible nod of agreement but maintains an aloof expression.{/n}
  - After: {n}Kibellah nods, aloof.{/n}
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Omens are not just the idle whimsy of a sluggish mind. They appear everywhere to those who have eyes to see them. And yet, your words ring true. Thinking about how alike Nemesite and I are is deeply distressing to me, and this is a weakness. I must instead focus my thoughts on the thread that will lead us to victory."
  - After: "Omens are real. But dwelling on our likeness is weakness. I'll follow the thread."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The battle is over, and silence descends once again upon the chapel. Flakes of ash whirl quietly in the air before coming to rest on the blood trickling slowly across the floor.{/n}
  - After: {n}Silence. Ash settles on blood across the chapel floor.{/n}

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/ShipTemple/ShipConfessorTraitor/ShipConfessorTraitor_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "So, Nemesite is just a man? Excellent. It is harder to kill a legend."
  - After: "Nemesite is just a man? Good. Easier to kill."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you serve Nemesite or do you command him?"
  - After: "Do you serve Nemesite or command him?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are responsible for the deaths of countless people. The time has come for a reckoning."
  - After: "Countless died because of you. Time for a reckoning."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I demand an explanation, Confessor. This instant."
  - After: "Explain yourself, Confessor. Now."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Kibellah, it was you who found him. Therefore, it is up to you to pass judgement."
  - After: "Kibellah, you found him. You judge him."
- **Player**
  - Before: "How did your deception go unnoticed?"
  - After: "How did no one notice?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Any last words, Adalbert?"
  - After: "Last words, Adalbert?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Are you hoping he will save you now?"
  - After: "Hoping he'll save you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "For betraying the faith, I hereby excommunicate you from the Emperor's light and name you an abomination! And now — die, heretic."
  - After: "I excommunicate you from the Emperor's light, abomination! Die, heretic."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Despite your crimes, I will keep you alive. Sauerback, arrest the traitor."
  - After: "I'll keep you alive. Sauerback, arrest the traitor."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Any rebellion is a strike against the Imperium, to the advantage of the enemies of Humanity. Repent, for there is no fate worse than to be deprived of His light."
  - After: "Rebellion aids Humanity's enemies. Repent, lest you lose His light."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I too desire a better life for my subjects. The path to that need not be violent — let us make peace and change life on the ship together."
  - After: "I want a better life for them too. Let us make peace and change the ship together."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Face the facts — you are no champion of justice. You are a manipulator who raises himself up by standing on the corpses of others. I am not judging you. On the contrary, I could use a man of such talents. Together we could accomplish a great deal..."
  - After: "You're no champion of justice — you climb on corpses. I could use such talents. Together we could do much..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your 'liberation' is rooted in betrayal and bloodshed."
  - After: "Your 'liberation' is betrayal and bloodshed."
- **Player**
  - Before: "To separate a family would be cruel. You and your son will see each other soon enough."
  - After: "I won't separate a family. You'll see your son soon enough."
- **Player**
  - Before: "And you were so good at moaning about the servants he killed..."
  - After: "And you mourned the servants he killed so well..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "So, you are a heretic, then?"
  - After: "So you're a heretic?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are not even trying to lie. This is commendable."
  - After: "Not even lying. Commendable."
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: {n}Adalbert meets Kibellah's words calmly, with almost majestic resignation.{/n} "A defender of the people and a tyrant's minion are two faithful servants of opposing ideas, two souls that have rejected everything else for the sake of duty. I now truly see that your collision with him was inevitable."
  - After: {n}Adalbert, resigned.{/n} "Defender and minion. Your clash with him was inevitable."
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: "And it was by the Emperor's command that I took Adalbert's place through deception, pretending to be him. The dead man had inherited much influence and many thrones from his clan, which hastened my successful rise through the ranks. But it was not for wealth and power that I did this! I accepted the burden of hard work to empower the common people, to pave the way for liberation from oppression and injustice. And my part is almost done."
  - After: "By the Emperor's command I became Adalbert, to free the common people. My part is almost done."
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: "This is a war, {name}. The war for our liberation, and we are willing to die and to kill for it, because our enemy is brutal and deaf to our pleas. You have deserved it." {n}He resolutely places his hand over his heart.{/n}
  - After: "This is war, {name}. For liberation we kill and die. You deserved it." {n}Hand on heart.{/n}
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: "Your pet tormentor who extols death is right. I know Nemesite, and I assist him. Just like him, I am your enemy, {name}." {n}Adalbert raises his voice, and in the soft tenor, you hear notes of accusation as deep as rolling thunder.{/n} "And I am also the enemy of your cruel regime, where life is dirt under the enforcers' feet, where a man has nothing to eat, writhes in fear, and knows no hope!"
  - After: "Your tormentor is right. I aid Nemesite. I am your enemy, {name}." {n}His voice thunders.{/n} "And your regime's!"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah extends a finger topped with a metal claw toward Confessor Adalbert.{/n} "The divination has revealed that you stand beside the enemy Nemesite. Speak only the truth before the Domin and the Undying One."
  - After: {n}Kibellah points a claw at Adalbert.{/n} "You stand with Nemesite. Speak truth before the Domin and the Undying One."
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: "I follow him as he once followed me. Nemesite is my son, if not by blood then in spirit. I took him in as a wilful child, and I fostered the best in him... a passion for justice, the indomitable flame of a fighter, and unyielding determination. I have been preparing him for years."
  - After: "I follow him as he once followed me. Nemesite is my son in spirit."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, this is an ambush! They have been waiting for us!" {n}Sauerback's shout hits your ears, drowning out hurried footsteps and the clanking of gun plasteel.{/n}
  - After: "Lord Captain, ambush!" {n}Footsteps, clanking guns.{/n}
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah whispers to you,{/n} "I sense no lie in his voice or bearing, Domin'{name}. He feels and welcomes death with open arms. The moment favours us. We must learn more. He who betrayed his oaths will not deliver Nemesite to us, but from his words we may divine knowledge of our enemy."
  - After: {n}Kibellah whispers,{/n} "He tells no lie, Domin'{name}. His words may reveal Nemesite."
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: "The shackles will fall, and there will be nothing left of your tyranny. Nor of you." {n}Adalbert speaks without hatred. His even voice is that of a martyr on his way to glory.{/n}
  - After: "The shackles will fall, and your tyranny. And you." {n}Calm, a martyr.{/n}
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: "One last confession? Why not?" {n}He frowns and pulls back his collar, as if he were short of breath.{/n} "I am not Adalbert. That was the name of an initiate from a clan of confessors who passed away from disease many years ago. I was born in squalor on the lower decks, and at the behest of the M—" {n}He falters, as if he wanted to add something else.{/n}
  - After: "One last confession?" {n}He tugs his collar.{/n} "I am not Adalbert; he died of disease. I was born on the lower decks, and at the behest of the M—" {n}He falters.{/n}
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: "No, we decided otherwise. I am not worth him risking his life, so do not expect to capture him through me. My son has no attachments, for they would only make him weak. He will gladly sacrifice himself for his dream of liberty and equality, and I must do the same. I only grieve that, thanks to your efforts, I cannot be near my son and ease his burden."
  - After: "No. My son has no attachments; he'll die for liberty, as I must. I only grieve I can't be near him."
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: "You seem to have mistaken my humility in the face of death for submission." {n}Adalbert smiles weakly.{/n} "It is not for you to decide my fate. I will make the choice myself — I will surrender my life in the fight for our future. I will die, but I will take you with me." {n}He clicks his fingers, and the initiates who have been standing humbly around turn in your direction, their white robes opening to reveal a variety of weapons.{/n} "For Nemesite, brothers and sisters! For freedom!"
  - After: "Humility is not submission." {n}Weak smile.{/n} "I die, and take you with me." {n}The initiates draw weapons.{/n} "For Nemesite! For freedom!"
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: "I grieved for them, but... they were unreliable. They could have compromised us. They had to die, but the fault for their deaths lies with you and your enforcer dogs, for fear of whom we are forced to hide."
  - After: "They were unreliable. They had to die. The fault is yours."
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: "No. Heresy is what you and your fellow bloodsuckers believe in. The {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorumGlossary}Ecclesiarchy{/g} has turned faith into a whip to drive the powerless, the aristocracy has turned it into a shield to cover their transgressions, and the enforcers have turned it into a club with which to beat those who dare to raise their voices. Your faith is an instrument of lies and suppression, and I renounced it long ago. My faith promises salvation, not thraldom."
  - After: "No. Your {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorumGlossary}Ecclesiarchy{/g} made faith a whip. Mine promises salvation."
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: {n}Adalbert shrugs, his kindly face growing harder.{/n} "Why would I? If the dogs have come looking for blood, they will not leave without a kill. Such is your vicious nature."
  - After: {n}His face hardens.{/n} "Why bother? Dogs want a kill."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You were not there for those years of pestilence. Confessors attended every deck and died in multitudes. New ministers were recruited in every port, at every station. Their names and faces blurred together, and we recognised our kin only by their robes. No one who knew Adalbert's true face survived that time. The Emperor saved me from being exposed."
  - After: "Plague killed the confessors. No one who knew Adalbert survived. The Emperor hid me."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}Sauerback reacts to his gesture with due suspicion, sharply gripping her weapon, prepared to eliminate any threat to you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sauerback grips her weapon.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta's eyes flash.{/n} "Betrayer of the faith! Your blasphemous words will perish with you!"
  - After: {n}Argenta's eyes flash.{/n} "Betrayer! Your blasphemy dies with you!"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Even when it is fighting injustice, your kind only manages to foster more evil in its midst."
  - After: "Even fighting injustice, your kind breeds evil."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "You holy people are all bloody hypocrites!" {n}Idira spits at the confessor's feet.{/n} "You go on about how rotten we are, but take a knife and scratch your surface a little — and we'll find the worst heretic of all!"
  - After: "Holy hypocrites!" {n}Idira spits.{/n} "Scratch you, find the worst heretic!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I doubt it. People like you only ever see what they want to see."
  - After: "I doubt it. You see what you want."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "You have raised a living instrument that serves a purpose without question." {n}Kibellah speaks cautiously, as if not entirely sure of her judgement.{/n}
  - After: "You raised a living instrument." {n}Kibellah, unsure.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am bathed in His light as never before! You worship lies, while the true Emperor desires otherwise for his children!" {n}It takes an effort for him to regain his composure.{/n} "Your light is darkness, {name}. And I am sorry you are unable to see the truth."
  - After: "I am bathed in His light! You worship lies!" {n}He calms.{/n} "Your light is darkness, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Tortured doubt lingers on the confessor's face for a moment before being superseded by his former conviction.{/n} "Even if your intentions are pure, you are too tainted... Poisoned. No, the matter is clear — you or us. Peace and coexistence are impossible."
  - After: {n}Brief doubt.{/n} "You're poisoned. You or us. No peace."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He shakes his head, looking crestfallen.{/n} "I almost pity you — such blind conviction that nothing matters more than power... I will prove that not everyone is as flawed as you."
  - After: {n}He shakes his head.{/n} "Power isn't everything. I'll prove it."
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: "The words of a tyrant inebriated with power and impunity." {n}He smiles bitterly.{/n} "Nemesite is an idea. And you have the arrogance to believe you can kill an idea made flesh. It is better this way, so keep underestimating him."
  - After: "A tyrant's words." {n}Bitter smile.{/n} "Nemesite is an idea made flesh. Keep underestimating him."
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: "My son, the protector of those whose blood you feed upon, whose hard work has paid for your content life on the upper decks of this ship."
  - After: "My son, protector of those you feed upon."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}Sauerback clenches her fists until her knuckles crunch.{/n} "You treasonous impostor! To think that I listened to your sermons and was anointed by your hand. You will choke on your words along with the teeth I am about to knock out!" {n}Adalbert dignifies her with neither a word nor a glance.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sauerback clenches her fists.{/n} "Impostor! I'll knock your teeth out!" {n}Adalbert ignores her.{/n}
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: "Such is his purpose: to be the hope, to break the shackles, to end the centuries of torment that have passed aboard this ship. A great sacrifice for a great cause." {n}He falls silent, looking at Kibellah expectantly.{/n} "You should be familiar with his ways, except that instead of a sower of freedom, you were raised to be an executioner's sword."
  - After: "He was raised to break the shackles." {n}He eyes Kibellah.{/n} "You, to be an executioner's sword."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah takes a step forward and makes a straight, sharp sweeping gesture, as if crossing Adalbert's figure or severing an invisible thread.{/n} "Death has whispered your name, betrayer of vows. The judgement of the Undying One awaits you."
  - After: {n}Kibellah slashes the air.{/n} "Death whispers your name, oathbreaker. The Undying One awaits."
- **Confessor Adalbert**
  - Before: {n}Adalbert shifts his gaze to you and lets out a mournful sigh.{/n} "I was warned about your visit, {name}. As well as its purpose."
  - After: {n}Adalbert sighs.{/n} "I was warned of your visit, {name}. And its purpose."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Attachment makes us weak." {n}Kibellah's whisper is barely audible, and you see her face grow more dismal still.{/n} "You made a weapon out of him, just as he made a weapon out of you."
  - After: "Attachment makes us weak." {n}Kibellah, grim.{/n} "You made him a weapon, as he made you."

## DLC/DLC1/Narrative/ShipTemple/TrialOfFaith/TrialOfFaithDialog

- **Player**
  - Before: "You look unwell, Marius. How long since you last slept?"
  - After: "You look unwell, Marius. When did you last sleep?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You deign to speak to me out of turn?"
  - After: "You speak out of turn?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am unimpressed, Marius. You do not belong among the missionaries. Return to your duties."
  - After: "Unimpressive, Marius. You're no missionary. Back to your duties."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Prove to me that your epiphany was real. Put your faith to the test."
  - After: "Prove your epiphany. Test your faith."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Kill the officer] "All I see in you is dangerous madness."
  - After: [Kill the officer] "I see only dangerous madness."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have no time for this and no desire to deal with you. I am leaving."
  - After: "No time for this. I'm leaving."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I see you are going to persist. Fine. I will give you a chance to prove your faith."
  - After: "You persist. Fine. Prove your faith."
- **Player**
  - Before: "My decision stands. Now get out of my sight."
  - After: "My decision stands. Out of my sight."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You speak of your great-great-grandfather with particular enthusiasm. What makes him so important?"
  - After: "Why is your great-great-grandfather so important?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell me more about the vision you had."
  - After: "Tell me about your vision."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Sister Argenta, I entrust you with the test."
  - After: "Sister Argenta, you test him."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Take my blessing, along with any weapon you like from the ship's reliquary. Quench its thirst with the blood of those you deem unworthy."
  - After: "Take my blessing and any reliquary weapon. Bleed the unworthy."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your courage and resolve are beyond reproach. You will make a fine officer. Trust me."
  - After: "Your courage is beyond reproach. You'll make a fine officer."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am ready to pass my verdict."
  - After: "I'm ready to judge."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Medicae Officer Marius Clemence Sorne Keblau, you have convinced me of your genuine faith. I hereby give you my blessing as Rogue Trader and order you to take up missionary service."
  - After: "Medicae Officer Marius Clemence Sorne Keblau, your faith is genuine. I bless you and order you into missionary service."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You were assigned a position on this ship. That is your place in the Imperium's design. And you seek to upset that order? I ought to have you executed for such impudence."
  - After: "Your place here is the Imperium's design. Upset it? I should execute you for impudence."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Marius, you can do good without having to leave the ship. You have enough work here to fill the rest of your life. Cure people and strengthen their faith: is that not enough?"
  - After: "Marius, do good here. Cure people, strengthen their faith. Is that not enough?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A young man is praying beside the reliquary. His hair is dishevelled and his sweat-stained uniform is crumpled. Dark circles have formed underneath his eyes. As you approach, he jumps up from his knees and makes the sign of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aquila}Aquila{/g} with a jerky motion.{/n} "Lord Captain! You are here! I believed— nay, I knew you would come!"
  - After: {n}A haggard youth at the reliquary leaps up, making the {g|Encyclopedia:Aquila}Aquila{/g}.{/n} "Lord Captain! I knew you'd come!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I require neither rest nor sleep! I feel energised and alive like never before. I— I'm overflowing with faith!"
  - After: "I need no sleep! I'm overflowing with faith!"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah approaches the officer without making a sound.{/n} "Death is the faithful companion of those who sow the seeds of faith amid the stars. Though it has a thousand faces, I will show you but one... The one you fear most. The one you have seen in your nightmares."
  - After: {n}Kibellah approaches silently.{/n} "I will show you the death you fear most."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}His bloodshot eyes, slightly twitching fingers, and nervous agitation point to chronic sleep deprivation or the gruelling strain of too much work.{/n}
  - After: {n}Bloodshot eyes, twitching: sleeplessness or overwork.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Whatever happened to this officer, it has him in quite a state.{/n}
  - After: {n}He's in quite a state.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The officer tries to smooth his hair with one hand and straighten his collar with the other.{/n} "B-but who else if not one of the Emperor's anointed? The vision... I must bring this matter to your attention. You are the only one I can ask."
  - After: {n}He smooths his hair.{/n} "B-but who else? The vision... only you can answer."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The medicae officer looks away, struggling to comprehend what he has just heard. A deep furrow appears on his brow — a rare occurrence in someone of his age.{/n} "You are right. There's a lot I could do for my home ship. But I can't just turn my back on the sign I was given and make do with a compromise. The Emperor commands that I dedicate every part of me to His faith, so that's how it must be."
  - After: {n}He frowns.{/n} "I could do much here. But I can't ignore my sign."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira smiles back at you.{/n} "Indeed, why not look into this wannabe fanatic's future?" {n}She closes her eyes and rubs her temples theatrically.{/n} "Oh yes! The whispers tell me that you, Marius, will embarrass yourself on the very first planet you go to, and come crawling back to this ship burdened with debt and disburdened of breeches!"
  - After: {n}Idira grins.{/n} "His future?" {n}She rubs her temples.{/n} "You'll crawl back in debt and without breeches!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marius wrings his hands.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! You have turned my inner eye to things I've never reflected on before. I think... you're right. I am not ready to be a missionary." {n}He smiles a tired smile.{/n} "A vision brought me to you, and you have shown me the truth. Correcting the flaws in my faith is what I must turn my efforts toward."
  - After: {n}Marius wrings his hands.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you're right. I'm not ready." {n}A tired smile.{/n} "I must mend my faith."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your words leave the officer awestruck. He freezes in place, waiting.{/n}
  - After: {n}Awestruck, he waits.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marius grabs onto the hem of your clothes.{/n} "I implore you! This is my calling!"
  - After: {n}He grabs your hem.{/n} "I implore you! This is my calling!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "He had the honour of helping an ancestor of yours capture this relic." {n}Marius points piously toward the reliquary.{/n} "In that gruelling fight, he not only treated the wounded soldiers but shed blood for the cause himself."
  - After: "He helped your ancestor take this relic." {n}He points.{/n} "He healed and bled for it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The officer raises his eyes to the ceiling and recollects with rapt abandon:{/n} "First I noticed a faint light out of the corner of my eye, but thought it was a surgical {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumen{/g} someone had turned on. The light grew brighter, and when I turned toward it, it shone right through me! I saw my muscles, organs, and bones under my skin. I was bared, body and soul, as if I was standing by the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThroneGlossary}Throne{/g} itself."
  - After: {n}He gazes up.{/n} "A light like a {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumen{/g} shone through me. I was bared, body and soul, as before the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThroneGlossary}Throne{/g}."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}An inner fire lights up Argenta's face.{/n} "You believe you have been chosen for missionary work? Do you know what hardships the bringers of His word must endure? Words alone will not make the faithless fall to their knees. Countless righteous men and women have died at the hands of those they were trying to save! Other foes lurk on remote worlds as well. Disease. Hunger. Destitution. The smallest flaw in your faith will be enough for them to break you and turn you away from the Throne. Do you think you have what it takes to overcome these challenges?"
  - After: {n}Argenta burns.{/n} "Missionaries die by those they save, or by disease. Any flaw in your faith will break you. Can you endure?"
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Easy, paragon of faith. I was just testing how frayed your nerves are."
  - After: "Easy, paragon. Just testing your nerves."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marius's eyes glaze over, and his lips start moving in silent prayer.{/n}
  - After: {n}Marius prays silently.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The young man makes no effort to shield himself from your strike, accepting death with an expression of genuine surprise on his face.{/n}
  - After: {n}He dies unresisting, surprised.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The young man takes an almost ludicrously deep breath and says solemnly,{/n} "I am Marius Clemence Sorne Keblau, medicae officer. I have had a vision. My great-great-grandfather appeared before me and bid me seek your blessing to become a missionary! Please grant me your gracious leave to embark on my journey." {n}He freezes and stares at you without blinking.{/n}
  - After: {n}Solemnly:{/n} "I am Marius Clemence Sorne Keblau, medicae officer. In a vision my great-great-grandfather bid me seek your blessing to become a missionary!" {n}He stares.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marius makes an effort to stifle the protest within him before it can burst into words.{/n} "Thank you for the honour, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I will serve you diligently."
  - After: {n}He stifles a protest.{/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I will serve."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Tears glisten in Marius's eyes as he stands to attention and makes the sign of the Aquila again.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! It has been a great honour to serve you. Faith takes time to cultivate on faraway worlds, but one day you or your descendants will hear of my deeds."
  - After: {n}Teary, he salutes.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! One day you'll hear of my deeds."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marius sputters in astonishment,{/n} "Chosen one? I— you— anything you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I must tell my family at once!"
  - After: {n}He sputters,{/n} "Chosen? Anything, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I must tell my family!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is hard to tell if Marius is more intimidated by the Sister of Battle or the hardships she speaks of. However, he juts out his chin and replies in a firm voice,{/n} "I will drink my cup of sorrows, no matter how bitter it may be, and will praise the Emperor for every trial."
  - After: {n}He juts his chin.{/n} "I will praise the Emperor for every trial."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your stern tone frightens Marius.{/n} "I am a loyal son of the Imperium and have, until now, never entertained the idea of abandoning my duties on this ship. But what if mine is a different calling? How could I ignore a message from Him?"
  - After: {n}Frightened.{/n} "I'm loyal. But how could I ignore His message?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "An ancestor of mine stepped out of that most pure light." {n}Marius pauses, his voice faltering.{/n} "And he said, 'My child! Your destiny is to bring faith to distant worlds. Seek the Rogue Trader's blessing and set out on your journey.' The words didn't seem to be coming from his mouth but from every direction at once, and other strong and pure voices echoed them, and, and—" {n}For a moment Marius looks like he's about to faint, but he finishes his speech in a tone that is almost serene.{/n} "It was a miracle."
  - After: "My ancestor stepped from the light." {n}He falters.{/n} "'Bring faith to distant worlds. Seek the Rogue Trader's blessing.'" {n}Nearly fainting:{/n} "A miracle."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marius is silent for a long time, then smiles timidly.{/n} "If it were someone else, I would try to insist... But if you really believe that I will... Throne, who am I to doubt the words of a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Navy}conqueror of the void{/d} like you? Thank you for your guidance, Lord Captain. I will not fail you."
  - After: {n}A timid smile.{/n} "Who am I to doubt a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Navy}conqueror of the void{/d}? I won't fail you, Lord Captain."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Right you are, Aett-Vater! Everyone on Fenris knows: they who seek a great destiny must first face a great trial! Many of our heroes covered themselves in glory by accepting harsh challenges and proving their valour."
  - After: "Right, Aett-Vater! On Fenris, great destiny demands great trial!"
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "His colours burn brightly and feverishly, his zealous gold ready to consume all other hues. A beautiful sight, if somewhat frightening."
  - After: "His colours burn feverish gold. Beautiful, frightening."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "The ray of his soul is so thin and pure, so fragile... A rare glow in the guts of an iron ship."
  - After: "His soul is thin, pure, fragile. Rare here."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "Easily remediable." {n}Marazhai continues critically examining his sharp claws.{/n}
  - After: "Easily remediable." {n}Marazhai eyes his claws.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta nods in satisfaction.{/n} "Spoken like a righteous man!"
  - After: {n}Argenta nods.{/n} "Spoken like a righteous man!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}One swift movement, and a cold needle flashes by Marius's neck. His eyes roll up and his body convulses. Nothing happens for several long seconds, until he finally forces out,{/n} "O Emperor! What an abomination, what unbearable, Throne-offending blasphemy!" {n}He clenches his teeth and mutters stubbornly on through the froth forming on his lips.{/n} "And I shall fear no corruption, and I shall face my death as His faithful servant!"
  - After: {n}A needle at his neck; he convulses.{/n} "O Emperor! Blasphemy!" {n}Frothing:{/n} "I fear no corruption! I die His servant!"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}With another swift movement, Kibellah administers an antidote to the officer.{/n} "This one has gained knowledge of one of death's manifestations. Another of his weaknesses has died off, making room for service."
  - After: {n}Kibellah gives an antidote.{/n} "He has met death. A weakness died."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marius clenches his fists, gnashes his teeth, and says,{/n} "That will never be! The cursed spirits are lying to you! They seek to lead me astray, as they do any fervent believer. Drown out their voices with prayer and don't let them make you an instrument of their evil!"
  - After: {n}He clenches his fists.{/n} "Never! The spirits lie. Drown them with prayer!"

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/AdministratumPalaceArbites/APA_TasseraReport/APA_TasseraReport_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You are biased against Solomorne."
  - After: "You're biased against Solomorne."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Solomorne, tell the prefect everything."
  - After: "Solomorne, tell her everything."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What fantastic advice you gave me, Solomorne. I should not have listened to you."
  - After: "Fantastic advice, Solomorne. I shouldn't have listened."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Lean toward Solomorne and whisper] "You shouldn't have taken all the blame like that."
  - After: [Whisper to Solomorne] "You shouldn't have taken all the blame."
- **Player**
  - Before: "A heretic had seized power on Thassera. I had him executed."
  - After: "A heretic seized Thassera. I executed him."
- **Player**
  - Before: "A heretic had seized power on Thassera. I had him executed and assigned a representative in his place."
  - After: "A heretic seized Thassera. I executed him and appointed a replacement."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I discovered a warp-active mineral on Thassera and ordered it be studied. If this resource proves sufficiently useful to the Imperium, you must include it in the tithe."
  - After: "I found a warp-active mineral on Thassera and ordered it studied. If useful, tithe it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I discovered a material on Thassera known as thassertium, a potent psy-focus. I had it destroyed in the interests of the Imperium's security."
  - After: "I found thassertium, a potent psy-focus, on Thassera and destroyed it for security."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I discovered a unique material, a natural psy-focus called thassertium. I ordered it be included in Thassera's planetary tithe."
  - After: "I found thassertium, a natural psy-focus, and added it to Thassera's tithe."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What got into you back then, by the way? You were so aloof."
  - After: "Why were you so aloof back then?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "That is unacceptable. Find yourselves another Arbitrator to deal with your problems."
  - After: "Unacceptable. Find another Arbitrator."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I see. Good luck on your assignment, Solomorne."
  - After: "Good luck on your assignment, Solomorne."
- **Player**
  - Before: "One way or the other, we can consider the matter of Thassera closed. Am I correct?"
  - After: "Either way, Thassera is closed, correct?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What gives you the right to evaluate Solomorne?"
  - After: "What right have you to evaluate Solomorne?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Solomorne did nothing that could be considered a violation of the Lex Imperialis!"
  - After: "Solomorne never violated the Lex Imperialis!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Someone has finally caught you by the scruff of the neck, eh, lawman? Let's see how this plays out."
  - After: "Caught by the scruff at last, lawman? Let's watch."
- **Player**
  - Before: "That is the Administratum's responsibility — handle it yourselves."
  - After: "That's the Administratum's job — handle it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "One of the Rogue Trader's many duties is to mete out justice. I agree."
  - After: "Justice is a Rogue Trader's duty. I agree."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I hope we can get this over with quickly. As important as these cases may be, my personal business is even more so."
  - After: "Let's be quick. My own business matters more."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You still shouldn't have said anything. I can take care of myself."
  - After: "You shouldn't have spoken. I can handle myself."
- **Player**
  - Before: "My Seneschal will give you an account of it. Reporting to anyone in person would be beneath my station."
  - After: "My Seneschal will report. In person is beneath me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Are you not being a little harsh on yourself, Solomorne?"
  - After: "Too harsh on yourself, Solomorne?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "If you think the Thasserian mineral is so important to the Imperium, make it part of the tithe. What is the problem?"
  - After: "If the mineral matters so much, tithe it. What's the problem?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The tithe deliveries from Thassera will be restored to their former capacity. This is all you need to know."
  - After: "Thassera's tithe will be restored. That's all you need."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The audience is with the Master of Seals, not the prefect. It would appear you... misspoke?"
  - After: "The audience is with the Master of Seals, not the prefect. You... misspoke?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How dare you reprimand me for a wicked man's death! It would have been the duty of any servant of the Emperor to cleanse the heretic with fire and plasteel — or are you going to brashly and blasphemously claim otherwise?"

  - Before: {n}As she speaks, Prefect Vultur's augmented hands constantly fidget with a tattered piece of paper that may have once been a report:{/n} "But for how much longer might we have to wait for the Rogue Trader? Ten turns? Thirty? Thrice that? Time is an invaluable commodity, and we currently have none, esteemed Marshal. Not to mention that Decree RP/84-289 explicitly states—" {n}She stops abruptly when she sees you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Vultur fidgets with a tattered report.{/n} "Wait how long? We have no time. Decree RP/84-289—" {n}She sees you.{/n}
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal raises his chin.{/n} "Rogue Trader. The Adeptus Arbites request your immediate cooperation. The {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGlossary}sacred tithe{/g} collected from the Koronus Expanse is in danger, and you are the only one who can negate this threat."
  - After: {n}The Marshal raises his chin.{/n} "Rogue Trader. The {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGlossary}sacred tithe{/g} is in danger. Only you can save it."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "Extraordinarily so, and there is no guarantee that we are not already too late." {n}The prefect's glare bores into Strachs's grim figure.{/n}
  - After: "Very. We may be too late." {n}She glares at Strachs.{/n}
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal's face is impenetrable.{/n} "The disagreement between the prefect and myself was put to rest the moment you arrived. Now, to the issue at hand."
  - After: {n}Impassive:{/n} "Our dispute is over. To business."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: {n}The raspy voice of the prefect cuts across the Marshal's speech:{/n} "If I may provide certain details: as per regulations, prior to being sent to this temporary depot, all tithe shipments were first brought to Dargonus. These deliveries were made using barges crewed by servitors, with the only people on board with the privilege of autonomous behaviour being key officers and an Arbitrator escort. In other words, the location of both the system and the planet was strictly classified. A special pact was made with the {g|Encyclopedia:NavisNobiliteGlossary}Navigator House{/g}... Even I was not entrusted with the coordinates..."
  - After: {n}The prefect cuts in:{/n} "Its location is secret, by pact with a {g|Encyclopedia:NavisNobiliteGlossary}Navigator House{/g}. Even I lack it."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal looks straight at you.{/n} "Given the scarcity of our resources, absolute secrecy is Leethus's main line of defence. However, we are detecting... increased activity near the storage world's location. I do not want to do this, but I am, quite plainly, forced to ask for your help: go to Leethus and organise the extraction of the Imperial Tithe to Dargonus for further safekeeping."
  - After: {n}He looks at you.{/n} "Secrecy protects Leethus, but activity nearby is rising. Go there and move the Imperial Tithe to Dargonus."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "Enough with your insinuations. I make my own decisions!" {n}With his chin proudly set, the Marshal strives to avoid looking at the prefect.{/n}
  - After: "Enough. I decide for myself!" {n}He avoids the prefect's eyes.{/n}
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "All of the Expanse is ablaze, Rogue Trader. This state of disorder jeopardises a critical strategic location: the planet Leethus, a clandestine world provided by Theodora von Valancius for the purpose of storing the tithe collected from the worlds of the Koronus Expanse." {n}Strachs's cheek twitches.{/n} "At present, the planet is overflowing with the sacred tribute, amassed over the course of decades. After we lost contact with every single ship sent through the {g|Encyclopedia:Maw}Maw{/g} in recent years, the decision was made to cease all attempts to transport the tithe out of the Expanse until the route is once more secure. It was for just such periods of the Maw's impassability that the storage world of Leethus was devised."
  - After: "Chaos threatens Leethus, Theodora von Valancius's secret tithe world." {n}His cheek twitches.{/n} "Ships through the {g|Encyclopedia:Maw}Maw{/g} vanished, so decades of tribute wait there."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: {n}The prefect looks at them and snaps her fingers. The fighters immediately make the sign of the Aquila.{/n} "These are my bodyguards, members of the Fangs of the Expanse. They are here to demonstrate my willingness to offer the Adeptus Arbites whatever cooperation I can."
  - After: {n}She snaps her fingers; the fighters make the Aquila.{/n} "My bodyguards, Fangs of the Expanse. A sign of cooperation."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "That is an acceptable option — one with which we are prepared to proceed. The Adeptus Administratum has requisitioned mercenary troops of the highest calibre. Under extreme circumstances, the Lex Imperialis permits—"
  - After: "We would. We've hired top mercenaries. The Lex Imperialis permits—"
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "Out of the question." {n}There is steely ringing in Strachs's voice.{/n} "In the Koronus Expanse, there exists a strict separation of authority between the Adeptus Arbites and the Administratum, as certified by the von Valancius dynasty and formalised in the Lex Dargonus. Transporting the tithe to and from Leethus and maintaining its security is the duty of the Adeptus Arbites. Aside from the head of the dynasty, only we have the right to set foot on Leethus or to know its coordinates. Such is the word of the law."
  - After: "Out of the question." {n}Steel in his voice.{/n} "By the Lex Dargonus, Leethus is Arbites duty. Only we and the dynasty head may know of it."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "And I hope that you have since drawn some conclusions about the importance of guarding your key worlds. The entire Expanse is on fire. Your capital remains the safest place in Koronus." {n}The prefect attempts to speak, but the Marshal presses on, enunciating each word:{/n} "And this is not open to discussion."
  - After: "Still the safest place in Koronus." {n}He talks over the prefect:{/n} "Not open to discussion."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal sighs in anguish.{/n} "Enough to instantly turn anyone who captured it into a force more intimidating than the {g|Encyclopedia:KasballicaMissionGlossary}Kasballica{/g} Shadow Barons. A tempting prize, as you can see."
  - After: {n}He sighs.{/n} "Enough to make its captor mightier than the {g|Encyclopedia:KasballicaMissionGlossary}Kasballica{/g} Shadow Barons."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "A fringe world of no value to the Imperium. By order of Lady Theodora, it was stricken from all astrogational data." {n}The Marshal grimly works his jaw as he looks away.{/n} "Its security was considered beyond doubt. Until now."
  - After: "A worthless world Lady Theodora erased from all charts." {n}He looks away.{/n} "Secure. Until now."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal nods.{/n} "I will have the coordinates and passwords transferred to you. They are for your eyes only. Once you have arrived at the location, you are to oversee the tithe's transportation to Dargonus. We will meet the barges here and then redirect them to secure vaults."
  - After: {n}He nods.{/n} "Coordinates and passwords, for you alone. Ship it to Dargonus; we'll vault it."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "I must ask that you hurry, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... before all is lost." {n}The prefect bows.{/n}
  - After: "Hurry, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}She bows.{/n}
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal draws a sharp breath.{/n} "Impossible. That would mean that someone commanding vast resources and influence knows of its existence. We have no evidence that could support this conjecture. Considering the current state of the Koronus Expanse, with pirates and xenos roaming where they please, it is far more likely that the storage world will be discovered by accident."
  - After: {n}He breathes sharply.{/n} "Impossible. More likely pirates or xenos stumble on it."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "I..." {n}The Marshal freezes with his mouth open, then closes it with a snap and says quietly, with surprising sincerity,{/n} "My duty demanded it. I understand you have the right to be angry with me, but... we must not let the interests of the Imperium suffer as a result of your antipathy. I beg you."
  - After: "I..." {n}He freezes, then quietly:{/n} "Duty demanded it. Be angry, but don't let the Imperium suffer. I beg you."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: {n}The prefect clasps her hands.{/n} "Lady Theodora was fond of secrets... and good at keeping them. You inherited those secrets when you ascended her throne... but there are so many of them that apprising you of them all would be an impossible task, as is determining the scope of your knowledge."
  - After: {n}She clasps her hands.{/n} "Lady Theodora loved secrets. You inherited too many to list."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal gives a taut nod, a look of wary relief on his face.{/n}
  - After: {n}A taut, relieved nod.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The hastiness of the Marshal's rejection of your theory is the best proof that he himself considers a deliberate search to be a plausible explanation. But it seems he is unwilling to admit it, even to himself.{/n}
  - After: {n}His haste betrays that he thinks it plausible, but won't admit it.{/n}
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "If there is a possibility of protecting the tithe until it can be shipped to the Imperium, I would prefer to do just that."
  - After: "I'd rather guard the tithe until it ships."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "Mercenaries." {n}The Marshal spits the word out in disgust.{/n}
  - After: "Mercenaries." {n}He spits it.{/n}
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: {n}Vultur sighs.{/n} "Gregoras, you know we need every fighter we can get these days. You have precious few people at your disposal, and every year, fewer still remain. The Adeptus Administratum regulations do not prohibit the employment of hired force." {n}She meets the Marshal's fierce gaze with calm composure.{/n}
  - After: {n}Vultur sighs.{/n} "Gregoras, your ranks dwindle. We need fighters." {n}She meets his glare.{/n}
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "You clearly {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Navy}have an eye{/d} for practical issues. Lady Theodora assured me that Leethus had some kind of unique system for barge automation. We have no choice but to put her words to the test."
  - After: "You {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Navy}have an eye{/d} for it. Theodora claimed Leethus automates its barges."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "To be honest, this is the first time I am hearing of this planet as well. Leethus must have been one of those secrets whose details only a select few are privy to — and even fewer among those few ever get to live once their purpose has been fulfilled."
  - After: "New to me too. A secret few know, and fewer survive knowing."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal turns again to look at you.{/n} "There is another reason. Under the present circumstances, only you can provide the necessary level of security for the Imperium's property stored on your world. The Arbites are too few, and our forces are stretched too thin, as we must see to the stability of tithe deliveries from other worlds — and prevent any attempts to disrupt said stability. Thus, we are humbly asking you to help us."
  - After: {n}He turns to you.{/n} "And only you can secure it; the Arbites are stretched thin."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "In other words, they are here in case the diplomatic approach fails and you need a show of force instead."
  - After: "Force, should diplomacy fail."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}His eyes glittering, the Marshal says curtly,{/n} "I am unable and unwilling to discuss the subject."
  - After: {n}Eyes glittering:{/n} "I won't discuss that."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Arbitrator maintains an air of haughty imperturbability, but you catch the worried glance he casts in the prefect's direction. The Marshal is clearly discomfited by being the sole focus of your fire.{/n}
  - After: {n}He glances worriedly at the prefect, uneasy under your fire.{/n}
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Arbitrator's entire being exudes haughty self-assurance.{/n}
  - After: {n}He exudes haughty assurance.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "To save an unimaginable treasure hoard, just as a change of pace? Why not? If you were to offer us a modest share of the cargo, we would be..." {n}Jae catches the Marshal's icy glare.{/n} "...outraged! We require no compensation at all, for we operate solely for the good of the Imperium!"
  - After: "For a modest share we'd be..." {n}Jae catches the Marshal's glare.{/n} "...outraged! We serve only the Imperium!"
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "The {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g}'s resources are not limitless, nor is this within their jurisdiction. The matter is delicate, however, and calls for the utmost secrecy. It is also intimately related to your dynasty and its ancient covenant with the Adeptus Arbites. We indeed require your personal assistance."
  - After: "Not the {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g}'s business. It's secret, tied to your dynasty's covenant with us."

  - After: {n}A red light flashes, like a melta charge.{/n}

  - After: [Unleash powers of the warp against your enemies] "Fall, worms!"

  - After: "Indulge me with a few questions?"

  - Before: "You are not very talkative for someone who is about to die."

  - After: [Address the pirates] "Bring me Sargona's head for a pardon and a place on my crew!"

  - After: [Give Solomorne a three-finger signal and attack the guard] "A waste of time... Now!"

  - Before: [Charge into battle] "Enough! I am carrying out your sentence!"
  - After: [Charge into battle] "Enough! I carry out your sentence!"

  - Before: [Strike the barricade] "You coward, Sargona! Do you think this pitiful trap will keep you safe?"

  - After: "Your ploys won't keep me from my recaf!"
- **Player**

  - After: [Fill your voice with the promise of inexorable punishment] "Who dares raise a hand against a disciplinary officer and learn the death I've prepared?"

  - After: "Who helped you steal the tithe? Not Governor Medineh."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Nod at the strange machines] "An interesting choice of decorations for a ship's bridge..."
  - After: [Nod at the strange machines] "Odd decorations for a bridge..."

  - After: [Destroy one of the suspicious devices] "Fascinating toys. Let's see inside."

  - After: [Look at Sargona's henchmen] "Tired of piracy? Fight with me. The right to come aboard is earned with blood."
- **Player**

  - After: "Take the ship into the warp? Fool, you don't know what lurks there. I do."
- **Captain Sargona**
  - Before: {n}Sargona's forehead is covered in sweat, and his expensive jacket is mottled with burn marks. His hands are in constant movement as he works the controls for the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp engine{/g}.{/n} "So, von Valancius, you think you have won? Think again — I still have one last card to play."
  - After: {n}Sweating, Sargona works the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp engine{/g}.{/n} "Think you've won? I have one last card."
- **Captain Sargona**

  - After: {n}Your warp power passes through the screen harmlessly.{/n}

  - Before: {n}{d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}Sorcerous power{/d} spills out into realspace and crashes against the minds of those who have dared oppose the von Valancius dynasty.{/n}
  - After: {n}{d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}Sorcerous power{/d} crashes into your foes' minds.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: {n}Your foes scream in terror.{/n}
- **Captain Sargona**

  - After: {n}Sargona flinches.{/n} "We'll both die. I won't say. You don't know who you face."
- **Captain Sargona**
  - Before: "If there is even the slightest chance that I might live... I would rather keep my mouth shut."
  - After: "If I might live... I'll stay quiet."
- **Captain Sargona**
  - Before: {n}Sargona bares his teeth.{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} of these 'decorations' will accelerate the start of my warp engine... and our deaths, von Valancius. Take a good look at the last thing you'll ever see."
  - After: {n}Sargona grins.{/n} "Their {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} speed my engine. And our deaths."
- **Captain Sargona**

  - After: {n}He pulls the warp lever.{/n} "To the abyss, von Valancius!"

Sargona casts a quick glance at one of the generators off to the side, as if checking that it is still intact.{/n}
