## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/BoardingShip/BS_KTCStolenTithe_dialogue/BS_KTCStolenTithe_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Hmm. So, you're offering me a ship that I have to capture myself? Hardly a profitable bargain, is it?"
  - After: "A ship I must capture myself? Hardly a bargain."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Any tactical recommendations for the assault?"
  - After: "Tactical advice for the assault?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell me more about the ship you are promising me."
  - After: "Tell me about this ship."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I may have other matters to attend to en route to the Mundus Nullius. Will you be able to accompany me?"
  - After: "I may have stops before the Mundus Nullius. Will you come along?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "That is an impressive dog you have."
  - After: "Impressive dog."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Give me the rundown on Sargona."
  - After: "Brief me on Sargona."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Well, where is the Marshal? Why send a Proctor with this request?"
  - After: "Where's the Marshal? Why send a Proctor?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why have you approached me and not Winterscale? Rykad Minoris was his world."
  - After: "Why me, not Winterscale? Rykad Minoris was his."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I don't want the ship — I want a cut of the tithe."
  - After: "Not the ship — a cut of the tithe."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It is a pleasure to see you, Solomorne. And you, Glaito."
  - After: "A pleasure, Solomorne. And Glaito."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Counter-offer: I get the ship, and an Arbitrator joins my retinue as well."
  - After: "Counter-offer: the ship, plus an Arbitrator in my retinue."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will help the Adeptus Arbites. What is the plan?"
  - After: "I will help the Adeptus Arbites. The plan?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I expect to be well compensated for my efforts, or else I shall be severely displeased. Now tell me the particulars."
  - After: "I expect good pay, or I'll be displeased. Details."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are here to beg for my help? Well, go on, then, make your case. Perhaps you have found me in a helpful mood."
  - After: "Here to beg? Make your case. I may be in a helpful mood."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Return the data-slate] "I remember all the commands perfectly well."
  - After: [Return the data-slate] "I remember all the commands."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I need more information about the thief."
  - After: "More on the thief."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have no more questions. Board the flagship and await my command."
  - After: "No more questions. Board the flagship and await orders."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I knew you would be back, begging another boon... First the rescue from Rykad, now this."
  - After: "Back begging again... First Rykad, now this."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It is poor form for a Rogue Trader to refuse to help servants of the law."
  - After: "A Rogue Trader shouldn't refuse servants of the law."
- **Player**
  - Before: "So, you've lost a ship and you want someone else to solve your problem?"
  - After: "You lost a ship and want someone else to fix it?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I dislike my call sign. A Rogue Trader needs something grand — Emperor's Eagle, for example."
  - After: "I want a grander call sign — Emperor's Eagle."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Greetings, Proctor. You did the right thing in coming to me."
  - After: "Greetings, Proctor. You were right to come."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I suggest we move to a more private location where we can provide you with the case files."
  - After: "Somewhere private, for the files."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The formidable-looking man offers you a salute. His armour is immaculately polished, and a hulking cyber-mastiff sits at his feet. The Arbitrator's face reveals nothing but imperturbable equanimity, and his gaze is cold and weighty as befits an enforcer of the law.{/n} "Proctor-Exactant Solomorne Anthar. I greet you on behalf of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusArbitesGlossary}Adeptus Arbites{/g}."
  - After: {n}An impassive Arbitrator salutes, cyber-mastiff at heel.{/n} "Proctor-Exactant Solomorne Anthar, {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusArbitesGlossary}Adeptus Arbites{/g}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you for responding to my request, Rogue Trader. I am here on the orders of Marshal Strachs to ask for your help. We are in pursuit of a tithe thief. We must board the thief's ship, execute the heretic for his crimes, and return the sacred tribute to the protection of the Adeptus Arbites. The reward for your assistance in this matter will be the thief's frigate, the Heartless, which we will capture in the course of the mission."
  - After: "Marshal Strachs asks your help catching a tithe thief: board his ship, execute him, recover the tithe. Your reward: his frigate, the Heartless."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "From Rykad Minoris. The tithe ship departed shortly before the world fell and has not been in contact since. Our investigation revealed that the ship was plundered and destroyed. I already know the name and approximate location of the culprit."
  - After: "From Rykad Minoris. The tithe ship left before the fall and was plundered. I know the thief and roughly where."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What I am offering is the coordinates of your future trophy and a team of Arbitrators to help you take the vessel. You will be enriched and you will be continuing the alliance formed by Lady Theodora with the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusArbitesGlossary}Adeptus Arbites{/g}. It is for you to judge the value of this opportunity."
  - After: "I offer coordinates, Arbitrators, and Lady Theodora's alliance with the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusArbitesGlossary}Adeptus Arbites{/g}. You judge."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Do not mistake this as an attempt at bargaining, but I promise you — if you agree to help us, you will see how truly impressive Glaito is in action."
  - After: "Help us and see Glaito in action."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No. I'm still on mission, and in your absence, my subordinates and I will be checking weapons and finalising tactics for the assault. In other words, we will be wholly occupied with preparations."
  - After: "No. We'll be preparing the assault."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Heartless is the enemy flagship. It has been corrupted with inhuman technology, but you have the necessary resources to purge it of xenos filth and make it serve the Imperium once more. Even if you don't wish to own a ship previously crewed by pirates, you will have prospective buyers lining up to take it off your hands."
  - After: "The enemy flagship, xenos-corrupted. Purge it, or sell it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "He is a former privateer and a fugitive psyker. At one time he was involved in the {g|Encyclopedia:ColdTrade}Cold Trade{/g} and the supply of xenos mercenaries, but his pirate habits got the better of him and he started robbing his associates. Now even among the criminal rabble he is known as a nasty piece of work — something of an achievement, you will agree. Sargona is cunning, cruel, and unpredictable."
  - After: "Ex-privateer, fugitive psyker. Ran xenos mercenaries in the {g|Encyclopedia:ColdTrade}Cold Trade{/g}, then robbed partners. Cunning, cruel."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Marshal Strachs is not on Dargonus at present, so he appointed me to speak on his behalf — time is of the essence when there is a heretic to catch. I am sure he will present himself to you as soon as he returns to your capital world."
  - After: "He's off Dargonus; time is short. He'll see you later."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I did and I was rebuffed. As Rogue Trader Winterscale rightly pointed out, from the moment of the tithe's collection, responsibility for it transfers to the Adeptus Arbites. He also noted that the loss of a world is not an inconsiderable detriment to his protectorate, and he has no intention of expending resources to recover something that no longer belongs to him."
  - After: "He refused: the tithe is now the Arbites' problem, and he's already lost a world."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm no expert on ships, but when I questioned the captains on Footfall about the Heartless, they were almost salivating as they listed its virtues."
  - After: "Footfall's captains drool over the Heartless."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Out of the question. The tithe is inviolable and belongs to the Imperium. No faithful servant of the Emperor would dare take any part of the sacred tribute."
  - After: "Out of the question. The tithe is inviolable."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I do not have the power to choose my assignments, Rogue Trader. However, if the mission is successful, the Marshal is unlikely to refuse to deploy me as your escort."
  - After: "Not my choice. But succeed, and the Marshal will likely assign me to you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Without so much as a flicker in his expression, Solomorne commands,{/n} "Glaito, speak! Not every cyber-mastiff receives a personal greeting from a Rogue Trader — such an honour warrants a response."
  - After: {n}Deadpan:{/n} "Glaito, speak! A Rogue Trader greets you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Shortly after the fall of Rykad Minoris, I questioned the Liege of Footfall. He supplied me with exhaustive information about Sargona and his ship and gave the Arbitrators full access to the docks. I suspect Tocara's compliance stems from some bad blood between him and Sargona. Scum eating scum — nothing new there."
  - After: "The Liege of Footfall gave me Sargona's file and the docks. Bad blood between them. Scum eating scum."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Indeed. One {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Arbitrator}never truly leaves the Arbites{/d}." {n}Solomorne gives you a deferential nod.{/n} "I meant no disrespect to your skills, but I prefer to err on the side of caution."
  - After: "Indeed. One {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Arbitrator}never truly leaves the Arbites{/d}." {n}He nods.{/n} "Merely caution."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Under similar circumstances in the past, our arrangement would have obliged us to turn to Lady Theodora. She was a key figure in supporting the {g|Encyclopedia:LexImperialisGlossary}Lex Imperialis{/g} in the Koronus Expanse."
  - After: "Once, we'd have asked Lady Theodora, a pillar of the {g|Encyclopedia:LexImperialisGlossary}Lex Imperialis{/g}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Good. Do you have any further questions?"
  - After: "Good. Questions?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Captain Sargona and his flagship, the Heartless, are concealed in the Mundus Nullius. The exact location can only be determined with your ship's augurs when we enter the system."
  - After: "The Heartless hides in the Mundus Nullius. Only your augurs can find it."

- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "I can't fault your reasoning."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The ship was not lost — it was stolen. If breaking the law were an impossibility, there would be no Adeptus Arbites. In the Calixis Sector, our forces would have caught up with that heretic by now and brought him to justice, but the Arbitrators here do not have such resources."
  - After: "Stolen, not lost. Calixis Arbites would have him by now; we lack resources."
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "No Footfall ship has {g|Encyclopedia:Augur}augurs{/g} strong enough. Yours does."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In a tactical assault, the shorter the call sign, the lower your chances of getting shot while you're saying it. But so be it, Emperor's Eagle."
  - After: "Long call signs get you shot. So be it, Emperor's Eagle."
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: {n}Pasqal's vox hisses.{/n} "Purging a blasphemous ship is our sacred duty... and the Emperor's."

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/BoardingShip/BS_Outcome/BS_Outcome_dialogue

  - Before: "The sacred Warrant has wiped {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}your slate{/d} clean. Now you have been summoned to serve the Emperor — and I'll be damned to the void if I ever once rebuke you for your past deeds."

- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**

  - After: "Also provisions, weapons, xeno—" {n}He eyes Solomorne.{/n} "Valuables."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne raises his eyes to the ceiling.{/n} "I swear on the Emperor's light, I wasn't trying to express any kind of personal interest. I was simply doing my duty."
  - After: {n}He rolls his eyes.{/n} "It was just duty."

  - After: {n}He squints.{/n} "Agreed. And you, after battle?"

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/BoardingShip/BS_Start/BS_Start_dialogue

- **Player**

  - After: [Smile] "How gallant, taking the fire to spare me."

  - Before: [Smile even more widely] "Your professionalism is terribly charming."
  - After: [Smile even more widely] "Your professionalism is charming."

  - Before: "Why not go all together? We can overwhelm them with our numbers."
  - After: "Why not all go together and overwhelm them?"

  - Before: "You do not know me well enough yet. It remains to be seen who will need saving, trust me."
  - After: "You don't know me yet. We'll see who needs saving."

  - After: "Below sounds more dangerous. Why not switch?"

  - Before: "I am not accustomed to receiving such attentions from brave Arbites warriors. It is quite a pleasure."
  - After: "Such attention from brave Arbites warriors is a rare pleasure."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I don't want you to die, Solomorne, so be careful. Don't risk your life on my account."
  - After: "Be careful, Solomorne. Don't risk your life for me."

  - Before: [Address Solomorne's squad] "Arbitrators, I expect every heretic on this ship to come to know the implacability of justice. Today, the Emperor Himself heeds your verdicts — so go and deliver death unto the enemy!"
  - After: [Address Solomorne's squad] "Arbitrators, make every heretic here know implacable justice. The Emperor heeds your verdicts — deliver death!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "It seems your main formation is going to be A-48. I will plan my squad's tactics with this in mind to maximise our effectiveness during the advance. The Arbitrators' strength is in coordinated action — the enemy will fall under our joint onslaught."
  - After: "You'll use formation A-48. I'll plan my squad around it; Arbitrators excel at coordination. Together we'll crush them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}With the sparest of movements, Solomorne attracts your attention.{/n} "I will lead Delta-Xi squad along the lower deck, through the tight passageways, promethium pipework, and service areas where the enemy is most at home. We will take that difficult ground. Your squad — call sign Rho-Theta — will proceed along the upper deck. The objective is to reach the elevator. Rogue Trader, I request that you personally do not put yourself in the line of fire or take any unnecessary risks — we cannot afford to lose you. Once the deck sweep is complete, we'll rendezvous to regroup and launch the assault."
  - After: {n}Solomorne signals.{/n} "Delta-Xi takes the lower deck, Rho-Theta the upper. Meet at the elevator for the assault. Rogue Trader, take no risks."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Clenching his jaw, his face impenetrable, Solomorne says,{/n} "If you encounter especially stubborn resistance, summon me. I will come to your aid."
  - After: {n}Jaw clenched:{/n} "Call me if stuck."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne stares at you in silence for a long time, then mutters,{/n} "Charming, indeed. I've been called many things, but that is a first."
  - After: {n}A long stare.{/n} "Charming. That's a first."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No, we will focus all their fire on us. Splitting up grants us tactical advantages — I know this based on dozens of successful assaults."
  - After: "No; they'd focus fire."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I don't doubt your skills in combat." {n}The corner of Solomorne's lips lifts ever so slightly in a quizzical, not-quite-smile.{/n}
  - After: "I don't doubt your skills." {n}A not-quite-smile.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I will not send a Rogue Trader into danger — not even if {mf|he|she} requests it. Your survival is a priority."
  - After: "I won't endanger a Rogue Trader, even if {mf|he|she} asks."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If you get into trouble, call us immediately." {n}Solomorne taps his finger on his vox. Turning to his squad, he sucks in a lungful of air and roars,{/n} "Delta-Xi squad — formation A-48! Go, go, go!"

- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "I'm not—" {n}He sighs.{/n} "An honour to serve the Emperor's anointed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne puts two fingers to his ear, listening to his {g|Encyclopedia:CommBead}comm-bead{/g}.{/n} "Another Arbitrator squad has been hit hard. Find a way to open the door for us — there should be a cogitator or control panel nearby. But first, we will go down and get into position — we need to overwhelm the enemy with a surprise attack."
  - After: {n}He checks his {g|Encyclopedia:CommBead}comm-bead{/g}.{/n} "A squad's been hit. Open the door via a nearby panel. We'll wait in position below."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}At your words, the Arbitrators, whose presence was already formidable, begin to radiate danger. The Proctor strikes his chest with his fist.{/n} "A speech from a seasoned {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}Commissar{/d} is exactly what we needed. By the Lex, we will not fail you!"
  - After: {n}He thumps his chest.{/n} "A true {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}Commissar{/d}! By the Lex, we won't fail!"
- **(conversation owner)**

And not just mine — isn't that right, Arbitrators?" {n}Solomorne's squad responds with a jubilant roar, and for a moment, you feel as though you are carrying the Marshal's mantle again.{/n}
  - After: "{d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Arbitrator}No longer wearing the insignia{/d}, but our {mf|brother|sister} in arms. Right, Arbitrators?" {n}They roar.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne nods, relief written in his gaze.{/n}
  - After: {n}He nods, relieved.{/n}

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/BoardingShip/BS_Xenocogitator/BS_Xenocogitator_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Step away from the cogitator]
  - After: [Step away]
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The black cogitator you are looking at is clearly not Imperial technology. With its unnatural curves and a surface smooth like solid mercury, nothing about this machine suggests sacredness. The device has no vid-screen, but you notice the presence of dry, rust-coloured spots on the control panel.{/n}
  - After: {n}A black, mercury-smooth xenos cogitator. No screen; dry rust-coloured spots on the panel.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You remain standing next to the cogitator. The panel is being fed by your pain, and you send a request: "Shut down life support systems." Instantly, you see — or rather sense — several people inside a crew cabin gasp for air, then sink to their knees, turn blue, and collapse lifeless to the floor. A quick death would have been too good for those traitors. You can feel their pain. You open your mind to it... The memory ends abruptly.{/n}
  - After: {n}You order life support shut down and savour the traitors suffocating. The memory ends.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A mental image comes to life: you are on your knees, your hands tied behind your back. Your wrists are painfully swollen, and your face stings with numerous abrasions. A finely dressed man stands with his back turned, but it is clearly you he is talking to.{/n} "Did you think you could betray me and get away in one piece? You were never smart, but I had no idea you were an idiot. There's nothing wrong with a bit of greed, my dear fellow. Stupidity, on the other hand... Think of this as me doing you a favour." {n}You barely have time to register the glint of a weapon in the captain's hand before a burst of pain shatters the traitor's skull — your skull — and your mind is released from the grip of the shared memory.{/n}
  - After: {n}You kneel, bound and beaten. A finely dressed captain speaks:{/n} "Betray me? There's nothing wrong with greed. Stupidity, though... Consider this a favour." {n}A shot shatters your skull, and the memory releases you.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "No!" {n}Breathing heavily, Cassia covers her eyes with her hand as crimson tears seep through her thin, trembling fingers.{/n} "Such rotten, rusty colours cannot possibly exist... It's all madness and lies. A mockery!"
  - After: "No!" {n}Cassia covers her eyes, crimson tears seeping through.{/n} "Such rotten colours can't exist... Madness and lies!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The machine is refusing to let you go. It drives its needles deeper still into your flesh, trying to reach the nerve endings, and drinks greedily. You are overcome with a sensation of boundless hunger. When at last you manage to jerk your hand free, a fan-shaped splash of blood hits the panel. The machine's agony retreats from your consciousness.{/n}
  - After: {n}The needles dig deeper, drinking with boundless hunger. You jerk free, splashing blood on the panel.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You place your hands on the panel and transmit a series of mental commands into the machine, bidding it to open the sphere. Immediately, dozens of tiny needles shoot into your palms. An acrid liquid spreads through your veins. Then, a whispering thought forms in your head: access has been revoked.{/n}
  - After: {n}You command the sphere open. Needles pierce your palms, acid floods your veins. A whisper: access revoked.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's vox lets out a mournful binharic groan.{/n} "The rite of sacred diagnostics has been interrupted. Cause of interruption: a primitive method of disposal was employed against the object of study..." {n}The Tech-Priest's visor flashes red before dimming wearily.{/n} "...which had a ninety-eight percent chance of being of anathematic origin."
  - After: {n}Pasqal groans in binharic.{/n} "Diagnostics interrupted by primitive disposal of an object..." {n}His visor dims.{/n} "...ninety-eight percent likely anathematic."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}This machine is controlled by pain, and you have fed it sufficiently. You place your hand on the panel — only for an instant — and send a single thought into the cogitator: "Open up." A barely audible click rises from the sphere's shell, and the walls of the prison move slowly apart, revealing a desiccated corpse. The dead man's body has stiffened in a huddled-up position, his fingers wrapped tightly around a metal object.{/n}
  - After: {n}Fed with pain, the sphere opens, revealing a desiccated corpse clutching a metal object.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You touch the leather-bound buttons. In an instant, tiny needles sink into your fingers, and the machine greedily absorbs the seeping blood. A whisper-like mental echo rustles in your head: access has been granted.{/n}
  - After: {n}Needles sink into your fingers, drinking blood. A whisper: access granted.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Contact with the object is categorically forbi— undesirable!" {n}Pasqal's mechadendrites freeze, scanning the foreign code greedily.{/n} "Or so it was. Omnissiah authorise and preserve us."
  - After: "Contact is forbi— undesirable!" {n}Pasqal scans the code greedily.{/n} "Omnissiah preserve us."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "The very sight of that... mechanism... defiles us. One moment of stupidity will spell an eternity of cursed existence for all of us. Is that what you want, elantach? We must destroy it! Before the darkness of this creation touches our souls."
  - After: "That mechanism defiles us, elantach. Destroy it, before its darkness touches our souls!"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}The Manipulus uses his auspex to scan every contour of the machine's casing with unhurried attention.{/n} "The ergonomics... are far removed from the sacred canons of the STC. It is evident we are in the presence of xenos technology. Yes, Nuncius, let me be more specific: the xenos in question is the Drukhari species. If my hypothesis holds true, this blasphemous device is governed by the nociceptive systems of a living donor. In other words, the machine is powered by the pain of another."
  - After: {n}Eogunn scans it with his auspex.{/n} "Drukhari technology, Nuncius. Likely powered by a living donor's nociceptive systems — by another's pain."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Pray continue your experiment, Rogue Trader. After all, what are the torments of the flesh if they serve the Quest for Knowledge? Nuncius and I can always furnish you with worthy augmetics in the event of loss of limb or irreversible nervous degradation."
  - After: "Continue, Rogue Trader. Torment serves the Quest for Knowledge. We can always furnish augmetics."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Colleague, I register regrettable lacunae in your knowledge which the sacred diagnostics of this xeno-object are unlikely to ever complete. However, if you will permit it, I stand ready to transmit a portion of my wisdom to you, provided you swear the appropriate data-vows."
  - After: "Colleague, your knowledge has lacunae. Swear the data-vows, and I'll share some wisdom."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A cacophony of screams explodes inside your head. Images swarm in your mind's eye — bodies... lots of bodies... your hands covered in warm blood that is not your own — the memories of the machine's first owner. The images flicker out as suddenly as they appeared. The machine has sneaked its way deep inside your consciousness, where it awaits your next command.{/n}
  - After: {n}Screams. Bodies. Hands slick with others' blood — the first owner's memories. Then silence; the machine waits inside your mind.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}In one swift movement, you draw your weapon and rid the world of the corrupting xeno-abomination.{/n}
  - After: {n}You draw your weapon and destroy the xeno-abomination.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You are lying in a fetal position, surrounded by pitch darkness. From all sides, the metal walls of the spherical prison bear down on you, their cold surfaces scalding the raw lesions on your skin. They are separating you from the world outside. Worse still, they have cut you off from the warp. The deafening silence presses down on your skull, making your mind scream in agony. You are aware of your body still existing, but your consciousness is already slowly dissolving inside a cocoon of emptiness... and then, the sphere opens up slightly. Blue light comes flooding in, blinding you. You hear a grating, non-human voice:{/n} "A disappointing result. The amplifier has next to no effect. The test subject is too weak. Leave him." {n}The sphere slams shut again, and you are forcefully ejected, or so it feels, from the memory.{/n}
  - After: {n}Curled in the dark sphere, cut off from the warp. It opens; an inhuman voice:{/n} "Disappointing. Amplifier ineffective. Subject too weak. Leave him." {n}It slams shut; the memory ends.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's augmetics become instantly more animated, clicking, whirring, and flickering ecstatically.{/n} "Initiating observation log. No data-connectors or sacred Noospheric corona detected. Tech-nature: unknown. I declare Category Epsilon-Alpha secrecy. In accordance with the Canon of Technological Security, this object must be isolated and subjected to the rite of sacred diagnostics. All witnesses will be extermi— warned."
  - After: {n}Pasqal whirs ecstatically.{/n} "Tech-nature unknown. Category Epsilon-Alpha secrecy declared. It must be isolated for sacred diagnostics. Witnesses will be extermi— warned."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai grins at the sight of the peculiar machine, then glances at you.{/n} "A most curious item. What are you waiting for, {name}? Come closer. It does not bite."
  - After: {n}Marazhai grins.{/n} "Curious. Come closer, {name}. It does not bite."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix raises his eyebrows.{/n} "If only every xenoheresy were as blatant as this one... I hope I don't need to spell out what must be done with this perverse construct."
  - After: {n}Heinrix raises his eyebrows.{/n} "Blatant xenoheresy. You know what must be done."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "That thing — it pretends to be silent, then explodes with echoes of voices. Then, it goes quiet again... And then comes another flash of pain... The pain of another! It knows something, keeps it inside. And... it wants to show it to you, I think."
  - After: "It's silent, then bursts with voices... another's pain! It's hiding something. It wants to show you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The needles slide deeper into your palm, and you feel that your pain is no longer the only thing they are collecting. The thought that the accursed machine is draining the very life out of you makes you break out in a sweat. The pain remains, but the strange sensation is succeeded by weakness. From deep inside the device, a string of data surfaces: the machine is awaiting further orders.{/n}
  - After: {n}The needles drain not just pain but life. Weakness follows. The machine awaits orders.{/n}

  - After: {n}{petname} cries out, wings spread, blessing you back.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}When you approach, {petname} sends out a piercing screech and throws something at your feet. You reach down and realise that your bird has brought you a gift. As for where and when {petname} could have found it, you will probably never know.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} drops a gift at your feet. Where {petname} found it, who knows.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A fierce battle is unfolding on {petname}'s perch. The giant bird's two heads have clashed in a bitter fight. It is impossible to determine the cause of this conflict, but you feel certain you should intervene!{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname}'s two heads are fighting on the perch. You should intervene!{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The yellow-eyed head starts tearing through metal with redoubled fury, until its opponent is forced to yield. Shrinking away in a pitiful attempt to save itself, the machine half of the eagle admits defeat. The victor lets out a triumphant squawk and mercifully relents.{/n}
  - After: {n}The living head tears into metal until the machine half yields.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The living symbol of the Imperium gazes at you with seeming indignation at the frivolous gesture. {petname} permits your touch, but you can tell that no further reaction will be forthcoming.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} permits your touch, indignant, and nothing more.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} responds with a nod of calm dignity and a clack of the hooked beak. The second, mechanical head repeats the living one's gesture.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname}'s heads both nod with calm dignity.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Both of {petname}'s heads let out a fearsome cry. Beating its wings, the mighty bird takes flight...{/n}
  - After: {n}Both heads cry out as {petname} takes flight...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servo-head immediately obeys your command as it lunges and snaps at its living counterpart's throat. The metal beak tightens like a vice until the victim gives a plaintive shriek. Having asserted its dominance, the machine lets go of its other half, leaving it bloodied and maimed.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servo-head mauls its living twin's throat.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}When the eagle returns to its perch, it drops a trophy on the floor: a severed arm. You notice ship gang symbols tattooed across the wrist — this limb belonged to one of the lawbreakers who torment righteous servants of the Rogue Trader and often descend into outright heresy. It seems your companion has reminded the presumptuous rabble about the consequences of disobeying the law of the Imperium.{/n}
  - After: {n}The eagle drops a gang-tattooed severed arm — a lesson for lawbreakers.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Upon its return, the eagle throws a mutilated piece of a person's chest at your feet — a trophy from the hunt. An Aquila on a leather strap glints in the mangled mass of skin and flesh, and you barely identify the bloodstained shreds of fabric as a fragment of the robes of an Ecclesiarchy servant. Looking at the grim wounds gives you a good idea of how much torture this sanctimonious fool must have suffered before their untimely demise.{/n}
  - After: {n}The eagle drops a mangled chest in Ecclesiarchy robes. The priest died slowly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your stern voice has an immediate effect, and the fighting stops. Nevertheless, the living bird continues to shoot looks of deep-seated hatred at its servo-twin.{/n}
  - After: {n}The fighting stops, but the living head glares hatefully at its servo-twin.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The giant bird observes you with unblinking eyes.{/n}
  - After: {n}The bird watches you, unblinking.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The eagle returns looking somewhat ruffled after its long and swift flight. It flaps its wings a few times, then settles comfortably onto its perch.{/n}
  - After: {n}The eagle returns ruffled and settles on its perch.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Expecting a servitorised animal to appreciate your affectionate gesture would be folly, and yet, as you gently brush {petname}'s feathers, one of the heads tilts to one side as if leaning into your touch.{/n}
  - After: {n}As you stroke {petname}'s feathers, one head leans into your touch.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As your fingers brush against the rough feathers, {petname} lets out a chilling screech. You feel as if the bird is about to sink its talons into you... but then, under its master's commanding gaze, it quells its bloodlust.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} screeches, nearly striking, but your gaze quells its bloodlust.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Having returned to its perch, the eagle throws a bloody scrap at your feet — all that remains of a particularly large void rat. These parasites can grow to frightening sizes and are a true scourge of the lower decks. It looks like your companion has just eased the lives of the ship dwellers, if only a little.{/n}
  - After: {n}The eagle drops the remains of a huge void rat, a scourge of the lower decks.{/n}

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/CaptainQuarters/CQ_Pet_MastiffRVR/CQ_Pet_MastiffRVR_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You are my most loyal friend, {petname}."
  - After: "My most loyal friend, {petname}."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Well done! Be sure to give all my enemies the same treatment!"
  - After: "Well done! Do the same to my enemies!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "{petname}, stop that immediately! Don't attack things just because you feel like it!"
  - After: "{petname}, stop! Don't attack things on a whim!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cyber-mastiff lifts its head from its bed, looking at you with the dispassion of a pict-recorder.{/n}
  - After: {n}The cyber-mastiff looks up, dispassionate as a pict-recorder.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cyber-mastiff makes a sound that reminds you of a dog's whimper combined with the screeching of metal. You feel confident that {petname}'s servo-protocols have registered your every word.{/n}
  - After: {n}A metallic whimper. {petname} has registered every word.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The dog's attention instantly focuses on the thrown object. A moment later, {petname} leaps and snatches it from the air. Even before the metal legs hit the floor, your glove is reduced to tiny shreds — a transparent reminder that the cyber-mastiff takes every command extremely seriously.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} snatches the glove midair and shreds it before landing.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It takes you a moment to notice that something is amiss in your chambers. Finally, your gaze comes to rest on a torn cushion from one of the chairs. Your combat beast must have had too strong a reaction to the smell of real down filling. {petname} looks at you from the usual spot, unflustered as ever.{/n}
  - After: {n}A chair cushion lies torn, its down filling too tempting. {petname} watches, unflustered.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} remains cold and impassive as if you touched an inanimate slab of metal. Only the slight twitch of the cyber-mastiff's tail indicates that your affection has been acknowledged and appreciated.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} stays impassive; only a tail twitch acknowledges you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname}'s red visors turn to you. You know full well that a cyber-mastiff is an instrument of His will, not a comrade; nevertheless, just as one can grow fond of one's trusted bolter, so too can an instrument be shown sympathy.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname}'s red visors turn to you. An instrument of His will, not a comrade — yet one can grow fond of it.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} looks at you expectantly. Evidently, the servo-protocols refuse to acknowledge an unknown command, and so, the cyber-mastiff is simply ignoring it.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} ignores the unknown command.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} carefully drops something at your feet. The cyber-mastiff must have picked it up somewhere aboard the ship or on a battlefield. Whatever the case may be, this unexpected trophy will prove useful.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} drops a useful trophy at your feet.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Upon receiving your command, {petname} leaps onto all fours with a low growl and runs out of your chambers...{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} growls and runs out...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} returns after a while, covered in blood and scraps of flesh. You do not know — or particularly care — where and under what circumstances the cyber-mastiff caught up to its prey. What matters is that your beast, an extension of your will, has taught your servants an excellent lesson and gorged itself on the suffering of its victims in the process.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} returns covered in blood and flesh — a lesson to your servants, and a feast of suffering.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} is gone for a long time. Meanwhile, the open vox-line reports several incidents on one of the middle decks, mostly involving obscura dealers and smugglers who have suddenly let themselves be exposed. The vox is still talking about how the enforcers are in the process of apprehending the criminals when {petname} crosses the threshold of your quarters and walks back over to you.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} is gone long. The vox reports obscura dealers and smugglers exposed on a middle deck; enforcers are still arresting them as {petname} returns.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} returns after a couple of watch hours. The cyber-mastiff's route is familiar to you by now — you know it has done a circle around the bridge and the upper decks, inspecting the various stations. Half beast, half machine, it is an embodiment of devotion to the ideals of the Imperium and the unbending will of its most faithful servants. The sight of it strikes awe and terror into any idling officers, compelling them to return to their duties as quickly as possible.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} returns from circling the bridge and upper decks, striking awe and terror into idle officers.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cyber-mastiff simply continues watching you as you turn away from the cushion.{/n}
  - After: {n}The cyber-mastiff just watches you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You take some time to learn how {petname} executes basic commands. The cyber-mastiff follows your exact instructions, leaving you convinced that the servo-protocols are working correctly... and yet there is a small deviation from the norm: the dog's tail keeps wagging, as if {petname} were pleased to be spending time with you.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} executes every command correctly — yet its tail keeps wagging, as if {petname} enjoys your company.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cyber-mastiff's servo-protocols have undergone a few notable changes. Throughout the training session, the beast repeatedly displays extreme aggression and ferocity, as it shreds anything you throw yet seems to remain unsatisfied. {petname} hungers for blood. Real blood.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servo-protocols have changed: {petname} shreds everything with unsatisfied ferocity. It hungers for real blood.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You try out the cyber-mastiff's commands one after the other, thoroughly checking the servo-protocols. {petname} obeys every order without the slightest error, relentless as any other tool created for His service. The beast remains perfectly focused until the very last command — this machine is ready to serve the Rogue Trader.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} obeys every command flawlessly, ready to serve the Rogue Trader.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cyber-mastiff seems uninterested in your words, but you know that its servo-protocols have carefully recorded everything you said.{/n}
  - After: {n}The cyber-mastiff seems uninterested, but recorded every word.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cyber-mastiff — a hulk of muscle, metal, and wire — is resting in its designated spot. {petname} tracks your every gesture, as if logging your movements using some sophisticated device that never stops watching.{/n}
  - After: {n}The cyber-mastiff rests in its spot, {petname} logging your every move.{/n}

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/CaptainQuarters/CQ_Pet_Psyber-Raven/CQ_Pet_Psyber-Raven_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell me what the future holds for us, {petname}."
  - After: "What does the future hold, {petname}?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How does it feel to be imprisoned in the body of one of my servants?"
  - After: "How does it feel, trapped in my servant's body?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I grow tired of you. Rid my raven of your presence!"
  - After: "I tire of you. Leave my raven!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are a servant of the Weaver of Destinies, are you not? Do you have the power to save me from death?"
  - After: "You serve the Weaver of Destinies. Can you save me from death?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Thank you, {petname}. I wonder what you will bring me next time."
  - After: "Thanks, {petname}. What will you bring next?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "{petname}, that's enough. Petty thievery presents neither you nor your owner in a favourable light."
  - After: "{petname}, enough. Petty theft shames us both."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} watches you intently from up above. The jet-black bird remains almost perfectly still, giving you the sense of looking at a stuffed mount or a statue instead of a living creature. Suddenly, its beak opens, and you hear a distorted, barely intelligible{/n} "{name}."
  - After: {n}{petname}, statue-still, croaks:{/n} "{name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} looks at you without making a sound and straightens up. Then, the bird spreads its wings as if trying to appear larger. Presumably, this dignified silence is supposed to demonstrate the grim respect that your subjects have for their Rogue Trader.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} silently spreads its wings: grim respect.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} stares off into space without blinking. A barely distinguishable {d|Encyclopedia:CQ_RavenDemonDecision}whisper{/d} comes from the raven's half-open beak, filling the entire room. As soon as you approach, the sounds stop, and the bird turns its head to you sharply.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} {d|Encyclopedia:CQ_RavenDemonDecision}whispers{/d}, then turns sharply to you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The raven's beak yawns open unnaturally wide, its tongue lolling out and its wings trembling in agony. The eye under its tongue pierces you with its stare, and the sound of the voice that comes from the bird's throat pulls your muscles taut and twists your bones out of their joints.{/n} "Taunting a Lord of Change is unwise. My confinement within the weapon of the dancing souls lasted far longer, yet still, I found a way to exact my revenge. But I am not offended — I yearn to see you touch upon the Primordial Truth. The rest is insignificant, Child of the Dawn."
  - After: {n}An eye stares from under the raven's tongue; its voice twists your bones.{/n} "Taunting a Lord of Change is unwise. I escaped the dancing souls' weapon and took revenge. Still, I yearn to see you touch the Primordial Truth, Child of the Dawn."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That is impossible, Child of the Dawn — it was you who wove this fate into being. Now and for all time, this vessel is one of thousands of my eye's pupils." {n}The raven's head cracks and falls to one side, as if something invisible had snapped its neck. For a few seconds, the bird stares at you with dead eyes, before suddenly jerking back to life and raising its head once more.{/n}
  - After: "Impossible, Child of the Dawn — you wove this fate. This vessel is mine forever." {n}The raven's neck snaps, then it jerks back to life.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A whispering host of voices erupts from the raven's throat, caressing your ears, slithering into your mouth and nose.{/n} "A true Child of the Dawn who craves to take hold of the threads of the future... You ask for much, and great will be the price to pay. But the champion's desire is my desire."
  - After: {n}Whispering voices:{/n} "You grasp at the future's threads, Child of the Dawn. The price will be great. But the champion's desire is mine."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Something within the raven laughs softly, before the bird shakes itself as if to clear its head. It looks the same as before, but for the faint, mocking blue glow now emanating from its black eyes.{/n}
  - After: {n}Soft laughter; a mocking blue glow lingers in its eyes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The raven suddenly shrieks and stretches its wings wide. From under its black feathers, dozens of glimmering, otherworldly eyes stare at you.{/n} "Power over destiny, Child of the Dawn! No more and no less!"
  - After: {n}Otherworldly eyes stare from its feathers.{/n} "Power over destiny, Child of the Dawn!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The raven's head turns to you with a crack, and you hear a many-voiced {d|Encyclopedia:CQ_RavenDemonDecision}whisper{/d} emanating from its half-open beak.{/n}
  - After: {n}The raven's head cracks toward you; a many-voiced {d|Encyclopedia:CQ_RavenDemonDecision}whisper{/d}.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...a thin, sharp blade — one of Kibellah's many tools of death.{/n}
  - After: {n}...one of Kibellah's blades.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The raven's black eyes glitter with what seems like excitement.{/n}
  - After: {n}Its eyes glitter excitedly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...a cluster of torn multi-coloured wires. It matters little where {petname} ripped these from — you had better hide them. Pasqal will be incensed if he hears about such a show of disrespect toward sacred machines.{/n}
  - After: {n}...torn wires {petname} ripped out. Hide them from Pasqal.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The raven turns its head, looking at you with each eye in turn, then cranes its neck as if trying to bow. It seems it has heard an abundance of flattering words about you and is now attempting to express reverence to the best of its ability.{/n}
  - After: {n}The raven bows clumsily: they flatter you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The raven flaps its wings and takes off from its perch...{/n}
  - After: {n}The raven takes off...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...a worn bookmark. Was {petname} really brazen enough to snatch it right from Cassia's book while she was reading it?{/n}
  - After: {n}...Cassia's bookmark. Did {petname} snatch it mid-read?{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The feathers feel rough to the touch. {petname} catches one of your fingers with a beak that could easily slice a digit clean off — this is merely a warning, for now.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} nips your finger — a warning.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The raven lets out a sullen, almost aggrieved croak.{/n}
  - After: {n}A sullen croak.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} avoids looking you in the eye. A disturbing feeling pierces your body.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} avoids your eye. Unsettling.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The raven starts beating its wings as if preparing to take flight. A few words fall from its beak:{/n} "Three stars! Burning! Burning! Burning into one!"
  - After: {n}It flaps:{/n} "Three stars! Burning into one!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The raven bows its head. This time, the voice you hear is not the usual deafening croak, but a quiet rattle, as if {petname} were afraid of being heard by the wrong ears:{/n} "Ancient one. Death of the galaxy."
  - After: {n}{petname} rattles quietly:{/n} "Ancient one. Death of the galaxy."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As soon as you step closer, the raven flaps its wings in agitation, as if eager to give you something. A curious object falls into your hand...{/n}
  - After: {n}The raven drops something into your hand...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...a cracked spirit stone. Marazhai's armour bears many such adornments — grim reminders of his triumphs over his distant craftworld kin.{/n}
  - After: {n}...a cracked spirit stone, like Marazhai's trophies.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...a strange bauble made from an unusual substance. After getting a better look, you recognise the material as wraithbone. It looks like Yrliet may now be one weapon ornament short.{/n}
  - After: {n}...Yrliet's wraithbone weapon ornament.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...a torn scroll containing a work schedule for one of the upper decks. Abelard must be looking everywhere for the document, stolen by {petname} when he wasn't looking.{/n}
  - After: {n}...Abelard's work schedule, stolen by {petname}.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...a slightly bent, Aquila-shaped pin. You cannot imagine how {petname} managed to steal it right off Heinrix's jacket.{/n}
  - After: {n}...Heinrix's Aquila pin. How did {petname} manage?{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...a scrap of fur, unmistakably from Ulfar's cloak. You find yourself wondering what the mighty Astartes would have had to say about {petname}'s antics had he caught the thief in the act.{/n}
  - After: {n}...fur from Ulfar's cloak. Lucky he didn't catch {petname}.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...an empty ammo casing. You recognise the weapon — {petname} must have sneaked into the training chamber in the middle of Sister Argenta's routine session.{/n}
  - After: {n}...a casing from Sister Argenta's training. {petname} snuck in.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...an empty flask smelling of cheap amasec. Idira would probably laugh if she heard how much your raven "cares" about her health.{/n}
  - After: {n}...Idira's empty amasec flask.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...a sharp-smelling biscuit. Solomorne uses these when he is training with Glaito. It has been nibbled on — the raven must have got hungry in the middle of its shenanigans.{/n}
  - After: {n}...Solomorne's nibbled Glaito treat.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...a fine gemstone earring. The back looks bent beyond use, so returning this to Jae would probably serve no purpose at this point...{/n}
  - After: {n}...Jae's earring, bent beyond use.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Quiet laughter breaks the silence. The raven's jaws part, and under its tongue, you see a daemonic blue-grey eye open sluggishly.{/n} "The Child of the Dawn has come to speak with me. I will answer your call."
  - After: {n}A daemonic eye opens under the raven's tongue.{/n} "The Child of the Dawn calls. I answer."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} lets out a piercing croak, beak agape. The sound is surprisingly reminiscent of mocking laughter. With its talons digging into the perch and its wings beating frenziedly, the raven looks as if it has grown used to people cowering in terror upon its arrival. It appears that its master instils the same fear in {mf|his|her} subjects.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} croaks mockingly, expecting cowering — the fear its master instils in {mf|his|her} subjects.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} watches you approach with keen attention.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} watches keenly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{petname} returns after a watch hour has passed. Before landing back on the perch, the raven drops its trophy at your feet — following your command, it has indeed found something to offer its master.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} returns with a trophy.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}With a short croak of gratitude, {petname} catches the food and instantly tears it to pieces.{/n}
  - After: {n}{petname} tears the food apart.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The raven cranes its neck, staring into your face. Its black beak opens:{/n} "Darkness marching over fading suns."
  - After: {n}It stares:{/n} "Darkness marching over fading suns."

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/CaptainQuarters/CQ_Pet_ServoskullSwarm/CQ_Pet_ServoscullSwarm_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Do something... unusual. Dance with me!"
  - After: "Something unusual. Dance with me!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Examine the servo-skulls for any information on the people they were made from]
  - After: [Examine the servo-skulls for who they were made from]
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have work to do. Come, you will help me clear my backlog of paperwork."
  - After: "Come, help me clear my paperwork."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I wish to be entertained. Sing something for me."
  - After: "Entertain me. Sing something."
- **Player**
  - Before: "All right, that's enough singing! Enough!"
  - After: "Enough singing! Enough!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Since you have your quills ready, I shall dictate my memoirs to you. Let us start with my childhood..."
  - After: "Quills ready? I'll dictate my memoirs, starting with childhood..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Inspiration has returned to me. It is time we continued writing my memoirs."
  - After: "Inspiration's back. Let's continue my memoirs."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servo-skulls greet you with a chorus of binharic trills as you approach.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servo-skulls trill in binharic.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Judging by the buzzing of servo-motors, your metal servants are struggling to process an unfamiliar command. Then, one skull stirs into motion, followed by another — the two of them drift around you in something resembling a ceremonial procession. The third and largest servo-skull remains in place, watching the silent parade.{/n}
  - After: {n}Two skulls drift around you in a ceremonial procession; the largest watches.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Several hours pass in the blink of an eye. Your head feels heavy from the volume of decisions you have made in this span of time — and from the incessant buzzing of servo-skulls by your ear. However, you have nothing to rebuke your assistants for: thanks to their help, you have managed to make a considerable dent in the impregnable wall of bureaucracy that serves as the lifeblood of voidship captaincy.{/n}
  - After: {n}Hours later, head aching, you've dented the wall of bureaucracy.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The panels containing the data close with a quiet click.{/n}
  - After: {n}The data panels click shut.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Loyal servant of the Imperium, Administratum adept, Grand Chronicler Avangeline Aivic. Cause of death: suffocation."
  - After: "Administratum adept, Grand Chronicler Avangeline Aivic. Died: suffocation."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The metallic plate merely reads,{/n} "Data deleted."
  - After: {n}The plate reads,{/n} "Data deleted."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Inside every skull, you find a small panel containing a cast-metal plaque.{/n}
  - After: {n}Each skull holds a cast-metal plaque.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After a few seconds, the skulls begin "singing" some kind of hymn, drilling the same, constant note into your temples, which quickly start throbbing with pain. You see no indication that they are ever going to stop.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your attempt is doomed from the start — you are not a Tech-Priest, and lack the knowledge to service these sacred machines. The sheer arsenal of buttons and wires on the back of every skull leaves you dazed, and you give up halfway through your examination.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The skulls' humming grows louder. The lumens in their eye sockets dim, then light up brighter than before. The swarm's flight patterns seem noticeably more chaotic now.{/n}
  - After: {n}The skulls flare and fly more chaotically.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A spark runs under your fingers, and one of the servo-skulls begins shaking violently. Afraid of irreparably damaging the machine, you cease your intrusion.{/n}
  - After: {n}A spark; a skull shakes violently. You stop.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Defender of the Golden Throne and of all Humanity, brave member of the Imperial Guard Bapask Yeronis, melee combat expert. Cause of death: killed in an ambush."
  - After: "Imperial Guardsman Bapask Yeronis, melee expert. Died: ambush."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servo-skulls obediently let themselves be held by your hands. It takes you a good deal of time, but you finally gain an understanding of the litanies and rituals that were used to tame their machine spirits.{/n}
  - After: {n}With time, you learn the litanies that tame their machine spirits.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Several hours later, your throat is sore, and the creaking of the quill on the parchment has taken on a faintly sad undertone. It seems both you and the sacred machine are in need of a break.{/n}
  - After: {n}Hours later, you both need a break.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Three watch hours later, the servo-skull ends the epic work of chronicling the many hardships and adversities of your life. Your magnum opus is complete, and although it may look like metres and metres of jumbled parchment now, you know it for what it truly is: the memoirs of the greatest Rogue Trader to have ever lived, carefully recorded by a servo-skull's quill!{/n}
  - After: {n}Hours later, the memoirs of the greatest Rogue Trader ever are complete!{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sounds crawling out of their vox-machines drop to a rattle, then stop completely. Blessed silence returns to your chambers.{/n}
  - After: {n}The vox rattles to silence. Blessed quiet.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Behind the fake slate stating that all data on this servo-skull's provenance was deleted, a hidden section is revealed. An inscription inside it reads,{/n} "Adept of Inquisitor [redacted] of the Ordo [redacted] Havrilius Smiroth."
  - After: {n}Behind the fake slate:{/n} "Adept of Inquisitor [redacted] of the Ordo [redacted] Havrilius Smiroth."

  - After: {n}A compartment clicks open inside a skull.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/Commorragh/PitSolomorne/PitSolomorne_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You are a human in a city of Drukhari. It is enough to break anyone. But Glaito led me to you, and I am going to get us out of here. You gave up hope too soon."
  - After: "This city would break anyone. But Glaito led me here, and I'll get us out. Don't give up hope."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If an Arbitrator from your squad was in your position, would you abandon them?"
  - After: "Would you abandon one of your Arbitrators here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Drukhari have been perfecting their art of killing for centuries, whereas you are wounded and exhausted — abandon your dream of a lone crusade against the xenos."
  - After: "You're wounded; the Drukhari are master killers. Drop this lone crusade."
- **Player**
  - Before: "And what do I tell the Marshal? That his top Arbitrator died in this squalid hole? Or that he — void take me — fashioned himself a ladder of corpses and climbed out of this pit?"
  - After: "What do I tell the Marshal? That you died here, or climbed out on a ladder of corpses?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you wish to die a hero? The Drukhari will catch you and break you, and you will die licking their feet."
  - After: "A hero's death? They'll break you, and you'll die licking their feet."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You scarcely recognise the formerly sanguine and imperturbable Arbitrator in the frenzied, roiling mass of rage before you. Solomorne's face is twisted in a savage snarl:{/n} "I'll kill every last one of you! I'll kill you all! Where's my dog, you scum? WHERE IS HE?"
  - After: {n}Solomorne snarls in rage.{/n} "I'll kill you all! Where's my dog?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Execution. I am my own executioner, and the city of the xenos will be my tool. I will kill as many of the spawn and their human servants as I can, and then I will go to the Emperor for my final judgement."
  - After: "Execution. I'll kill all the xenos I can, then face Him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I don't remember. It was dark. I was being dragged somewhere. I called Glaito and I was struck, and then..." {n}Solomorne grips the back of Glaito's neck with a trembling hand.{/n} "I remembered the trap. And I started fighting. I felt no pain or fear, only rage. I came to in a different place and I searched, and searched, and searched..."
  - After: "I was dragged off..." {n}He grips Glaito.{/n} "Then rage. I woke and searched..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And you, you xenos scum. Why are you still breathing, wretch?"
  - After: "And you, xenos. Why still breathing?"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "The elantach has chosen not to cut off my breathing. It is not for you to challenge {mf|his|her} decision."
  - After: "The elantach spared me. Respect {mf|his|her} choice."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne shakes his head.{/n} "I gave up hope long before now. Our world holds no less foulness than here — there, it is merely diluted."
  - After: {n}He shakes his head.{/n} "I lost hope long ago. Our world is just as foul."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have judged myself and handed down the sentence. This accursed place is not the cause of it, though it did push me past breaking point. I cannot do it anymore — I cannot look at the lying governors, the scoundrels who succumb to corruption, the people who become the playthings of xenos..."
  - After: "I've sentenced myself. I can't face the corruption anymore..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Like his master, there's something wrong with him." {n}His metal fingers trace over the stitches on the cyber-mastiff's forehead.{/n} "But he is not beyond repair. Take him — maybe you'll escape this place, and then the Tech-Priests on the flagship can fix him... I can't even guess at what the xenos have done to him."
  - After: "He's broken too." {n}He touches the stitches.{/n} "Take him to your Tech-Priests."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Great. An error. Our synchronisation is broken, and now he..." {n}His voice rises to a roar:{/n} "Will this damned day ever end? My dog, the only one I would trust with my life — he..." {n}Solomorne shakes his head furiously.{/n}
  - After: "Our sync is broken..." {n}He roars:{/n} "My dog, the only one I trust..." {n}He shakes his head.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No. He's not guilty. He never was and never will be. It's just... You can see I have a problem, can't you? What kind of Arbitrator turns into a quivering mess over a cyber-mastiff? It's a dependency, a weakness... I'm no longer fit for purpose."
  - After: "He's innocent. But an Arbitrator undone by a dog? I'm unfit."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne glowers at you.{/n} "You escaped the xenos' clutches somehow. So, it's too early to write me off as well."
  - After: {n}He glowers.{/n} "You escaped. Don't write me off yet."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "One outcome is worse than the other — are those my options?"
  - After: "Bad or worse — those are my options?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No!" {n}The Arbitrator growls through his teeth.{/n} "That won't happen. Ever."
  - After: "No!" {n}He growls.{/n} "Never."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "This statement is false. The unit is still fit to serve as high-quality base material for the purpose of servitorisation," {n}Pasqal interjects for seemingly no particular reason.{/n}
  - After: "False. The unit remains fine servitor material," {n}Pasqal interjects.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "To die a true defender of Imperium is to die a heroic death. But it seems to me that to carry on living in the name of Humanity is no less-honourable a feat. Take heart, Proctor — do not let this place destroy you."
  - After: "Living for Humanity is honourable too. Take heart, Proctor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Proctor grins crookedly.{/n} "A ladder of corpses. How does that sound, Glaito?"
  - After: {n}He grins.{/n} "A ladder of corpses. Hear that, Glaito?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne does not lift his heavy gaze from the cyber-mastiff.{/n} "It would be nice to at least know that I did everything I could to get Glaito out of here. Beyond that... we'll see."
  - After: {n}He watches Glaito.{/n} "I'll get Glaito out. Then... we'll see."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No. I wouldn't listen to them. I'd haul them out of here on my back. I'd defend them to the last."
  - After: "No. I'd carry them out."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Not a chance. I've got enough strength to take on at least one more scrawny Drukhari... but I'll admit, that still sounds like a terrible idea."
  - After: "I can take one more... but yes, it's a bad idea."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No one else will witness my judgement. Farewell, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "My judgement needs no witness. Farewell."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne's nostrils flare in anger. Barely regaining control of his emotions, he mutters,{/n} "Even if you insist on my return, that won't change the crucial fact that I am no longer fit to serve the Lex. There is only one sentence for me — to stay here and send as many xenos to the abyss as I can."
  - After: {n}He seethes.{/n} "I'm unfit for the Lex. I'll stay and kill xenos."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne accepts his death without a single sound, wearing a crooked smile on his face. Glaito does not even snarl, but simply goes still at his master's feet. Drops of blood slowly seep from the stitches on the dog's head.{/n}
  - After: {n}Solomorne dies silently, smiling. Glaito goes still, stitches bleeding.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Metal fingers close around Glaito's collar.{/n} "Your words have been heard. I will rise above this foul city and everything in it — and return to my duties."
  - After: {n}He grips Glaito's collar.{/n} "Heard. I'll return to duty."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To collect and guard the tithe. That does not mean we ignore other violations of the Lex Imperialis — we simply act within the scope of our limited resources, the first of which being our small numbers. Here in the Expanse, many believe themselves to be too far from the civilised parts of the Imperium to have need of the law. The presence of the Adeptus Arbites helps to remind those people that the Lex Imperialis is in effect wherever there is at least one human being."
  - After: "Guard the tithe and enforce the Lex as our few numbers allow, reminding the Expanse the law reaches everywhere."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I believe you. A Rogue Trader's throne does not tolerate weaklings or idiots."
  - After: "I believe you."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Fortune has little to do with it. You have formed an alliance with the Arbites, just as your predecessor did. My presence here is only the expected result of your decisions."
  - After: "Not fortune. You allied with the Arbites."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I just hoped it would discourage you. I only know how to give a full and exact account, and this story about lost limbs and odious abominations... I wasn't sure if a Rogue Trader would appreciate having to listen to all that."
  - After: "I hoped to discourage you. It's a gory story."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Very well." {n}He raises his metal hand and slowly clenches it into a fist.{/n} "Have you ever been eaten alive? I have."
  - After: {n}He clenches his metal fist.{/n} "Ever been eaten alive? I have."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You know where to find me, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "You know where I am."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Proctor looks you straight in the eye with cold impassivity.{/n} "Your suggestion that I could have prevented the disappearance of a star sounds almost flattering. And yet, I never dodge responsibility. Let the Emperor, in the hour of His final judgement, determine the measure of my guilt in what happened."
  - After: {n}He stares coldly.{/n} "Stop a star vanishing? Flattering. Let the Emperor judge my guilt."

  - Before: {n}Glaito tolerates your touch for exactly one second before jerking his head away, tossing your hand away from him.{/n}
  - After: {n}Glaito jerks away after a second.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You want to repeat your triumph? I cannot guarantee Glaito will be so calm this time."
  - After: "Again? He may not be calm."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I must admit, I was pleasantly surprised. I had expected something far less civilised, given that the Koronus Expanse is on the outskirts of the Imperium. Instead, Dargonus may even compare to some Calixian worlds in status and stability."
  - After: "Surprising. Dargonus rivals Calixian worlds in stability."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Leaning over Glaito, Solomorne carefully feels every stitch on the cyber-mastiff's body.{/n} "A lump here, and here... And what the Throne is this?" {n}His iron fist slams into the floor, leaving a dent.{/n} "Bloody freaks! Gutted my dog! I'll— Ah, Rogue Trader... How long have you been... standing there?"
  - After: {n}Solomorne checks Glaito's stitches.{/n} "Freaks gutted my dog!" {n}His fist dents the floor.{/n} " I'll— Ah, Rogue Trader... how long were you there?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have told myself that so many times, I don't know what the words mean anymore. Speaking of words..."
  - After: "Words lose meaning. Speaking of words..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne responds with an equally curt gesture, signalling his assent.{/n}
  - After: {n}He signals assent.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am beginning to think you enjoy pain."
  - After: "You like pain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "So do I. I'm more used to having orders and a plan of action — and elimination targets instead of interlocutors. But, every now and then, I have to suffer through these bouts of downtime."
  - After: "So do I. I prefer targets to talk."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne raises an eyebrow.{/n} "A Rogue Trader and an Arbitrator — you have an interesting notion of normality. Well, I'll try not to disappoint you with my conversation skills."
  - After: {n}An eyebrow rises.{/n} "Normal? I'll try."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "From what my father told me, she was a principled woman of poor health. She died in childbirth. Not having known her might be the sole regret of my life."
  - After: "Principled, frail. She died bearing me. My only regret."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A heavy sigh comes from Solomorne's chest, but a moment later, he is back to his calm self. His voice is steady as he speaks:{/n} "How... unfortunate. Well, I am ready to satisfy your curiosity, but I would plead for some privacy."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "As you will. We can have this conversation later." {n}Though Solomorne's expression does not change, you notice that he is trying not to meet your eyes too often.{/n}
  - After: "Later, then." {n}He avoids your eyes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am not going to call the prefect's judgement into question, but..." {n}Solomorne peers at you.{/n} "You had to make a difficult decision, and you made it. You took responsibility. I appreciate such qualities in people."
  - After: {n}He peers at you.{/n} "You made a hard call and owned it. I respect that."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You stated as much to the prefect, and it went down in my record. If that is insufficient and you expect me to comment, then I will."
  - After: "It's on my record. Want my comment?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne raises his chin with dignity.{/n} "You may consider my recommendation flawed; however, I did not force you to act on it. I have nothing more to add."
  - After: {n}Chin raised.{/n} "I didn't force you. Nothing to add."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are the ruler of an entire protectorate — I would not presume to judge you based on a single incident. If it seems like I am censuring you, that's just my face. And voice.   - After: "I won't judge you on one incident. Seeming censorious is just my face — years of interrogation rooms."
- **Glaito**
  - Before: {n}The cyber-mastiff gnashes his fangs a hair's breadth away from your fingers, preventing you from touching him.{/n}
  - After: {n}Glaito snaps at your fingers.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Proctor pauses before giving a response.{/n} "To assist the Rogue Trader in claiming new worlds in the God-Emperor's name is precisely why I am here."
  - After: {n}A pause.{/n} "That's why I'm here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Dead silence falls over the bridge in the wake of the loud noise, but it lasts only a moment. The officers hurry to return to their duties for fear of drawing your attention.{/n}
  - After: {n}The bridge falls silent; officers hurry back to work.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne touches his cheek with his metal fingers.{/n} "I would have preferred a shot in the leg instead... Ah, that's right — I am not allowed to object. In that case, thank you for teaching me a lesson — this brazen detractor is sure to benefit from it."
  - After: {n}He touches his cheek.{/n} "I'd prefer a shot in the leg. But I may not object. Thanks for the lesson."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne looks slightly puzzled by your response.{/n} "I am not really in a position to edify a Rogue Trader, but... Well, when it comes to honesty and impartiality, you can count on me."
  - After: {n}Puzzled.{/n} "For honesty and impartiality, count on me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I do not know. It was one of those tough situations where only time will tell how well you handled them."
  - After: "I don't know. Time will tell."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He freezes, beads of sweat forming on his brow.{/n} "I need to tell you something about my past... if you care to listen, that is."
  - After: {n}He sweats.{/n} "I must tell you about my past."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If I were in your position, I would take the prefect's evaluation in stride and learn from your painful experience on Thassera. Sometimes, life knocks the wind out of you in a way that can't be dodged, so it helps to learn how to take a hit."
  - After: "Learn from Thassera. Some hits can't be dodged — learn to take them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "By the way, I ran into that young woman recently, {d|Encyclopedia:CQ_LizzyOnBoardDecision}Maive{/d}. Curtsies to anyone she meets, big smile on her face.
