  - After: "I met {d|Encyclopedia:CQ_LizzyOnBoardDecision}Maive{/d}. Irritating, but harmless — and useful."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You {d|Encyclopedia:CQ_LizzyServDecision}servitorised{/d} that young woman, Maive — a severe measure, but it was the right call. Now the enemy won't be able to take advantage of her naivety again."
  - After: "You {d|Encyclopedia:CQ_LizzyServDecision}servitorised{/d} Maive. Severe, but right."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We could discuss something else?"
  - After: "Something else?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I suppose I have what you would call a proven and diverse track record: investigations, rebel suppressions, punitive raids — dozens of completed operations," {n}Solomorne concludes dryly, without any hint of pride.{/n}
  - After: "Investigations, suppressions, raids — dozens," {n}he says dryly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I was on a mission, not attending to pointless amusements."
  - After: "I was on a mission, not at play."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are quite right, and I am almost proud of it — what kind of Arbitrator would stoop to idle revelry, or, Throne forbid, dancing?"
  - After: "Proudly. An Arbitrator dancing? Throne forbid."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "When I think back to Thassera, I can recall only one moment of joy, and that was when we returned to the ship." {n}Solomorne responds curtly, his gaze directed somewhere over your shoulder.{/n}
  - After: "Only returning to the ship," {n}he says curtly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Very well, if you insist, let me think about it one more time... The wine smelled like wash, the Impostor Hunt was a plot — I fail to see anything appealing there — and the rest of the festivities had all the characteristics of degradation. I believe that covers everything."

  - Before: "Yes, I've been looking for a chance to have this conversation." {n}Solomorne's nostrils flare, his eyes darting uneasily around the bridge.{/n} "I must tell you something about my past, so that we might consider the matter closed. If you agree to hear me out, that is."

Only when Glaito lets out a low growl, drawing Solomorne's attention, does he break his stillness and raise his eyes.{/n} "Come with some parting words, Rogue Trader? Now is the time — there may not be another opportunity."
  - After: {n}Solomorne stands still until Glaito growls.{/n} "Parting words? Now's the time."

  - After: {n}He ruffles Glaito, smiling sadly.{/n} "With you both, I'll die well or prevail. Enough."

- **Solomorne**

The rote gesture looks unexpectedly heartfelt.{/n} "It has been an honour to serve in your retinue, and it does not matter what lies ahead. Isn't that right, Glaito?" {n}Without a direct command, the cyber-mastiff barks his assent.{/n}

  - Before: "You have entrusted me with the leadership of the Adeptus Arbites in the Expanse — whether I become the next Marshal or not, I will have to leave your retinue and devote myself entirely to my new post."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To purge the Arbitrators' ranks of those who have strayed in their service to the Lex Imperialis. Conducting the required investigations and enquiries will not be compatible with keeping my place in your retinue — if we return to the Expanse, I will leave the flagship and work to restore order in the Adeptus Arbites."
  - After: "Purge the strayed Arbitrators. I'll leave your flagship to restore order."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Glaito bares his metal fangs, and Solomorne's mouth broadens into a dangerous, death-or-glory grin.{/n} "Let those who hide from us at the edge of the galaxy be afraid — we will bring the Lex Imperialis to them whether they want it or not. So, {name} shall we show them all?"
  - After: {n}Both bare teeth.{/n} "Let the galaxy's edge fear the Lex. Shall we, {name}?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne and Glaito exude steely confidence — both akin to living embodiments of duty and order.{/n} "The doctrine of the Adeptus Arbites commands that I cast aside doubt and fear for the sake of service, so you won't see even a hint of such criminal hesitation from me. I am ready to carry the Emperor's justice into the heart of darkness."
  - After: {n}Steely duty.{/n} "Doctrine forbids fear. I'll carry the Emperor's justice into the dark."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Suddenly, Solomorne throws back his head and laughs. His laughter, unusually sincere and gleeful, rolls across the bridge.{/n} "Will you now? As if I'd let Glaito die while I still live!"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You know I am." {n}Solomorne places his hand firmly on his weapon, and Glaito stands at attention, echoing his master's determination.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "Or..." {n}His gaze pierces.{/n} "Order me to stay, and my place is at your side."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He folds you into a tight embrace, his voice dropping to a whisper:{/n} "Try to survive. If you don't, I'm going to kill everyone down there, and I won't care if they're guiltless under the Lex or not."

  - Before: {n}Solomorne nods in understanding.{/n} "I agree — words are unnecessary. It's time to descend to Epitaph and face the final test."
  - After: {n}He nods.{/n} "No words needed. To Epitaph."

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/FeudalWorld/FW_BackToBody/FW_BackToBody_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "All of you are going to pay for everything you have done to me!"
  - After: "You'll all pay for this!"

  - Before: "You have stolen something from me, Ruoldo! I have come to reclaim it."
  - After: "You stole from me, Ruoldo! I'm taking it back."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Surrender now and confess everything, Governor. Perhaps, then, I will convince Solomorne to kill you swiftly."
  - After: "Confess, Governor, and maybe Solomorne kills you swiftly."

  - Before: "Well done, Solomorne! How did you know that would work?"
  - After: "Well done, Solomorne! How did you know?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address Tavrisk] "Hey, psyker! Return me to my body at once, and I will grant you an easy death!"
  - After: [Address Tavrisk] "Psyker! Restore my body, and die easy!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your conspiracy almost entertained me. Fine, I suppose I will add this victory to my list of accomplishments."
  - After: "Your conspiracy almost amused me. Another victory."
- **Player**
  - Before: "EMPEROR KNOWS I was trying to give you a chance."
  - After: "EMPEROR KNOWS I gave you a chance."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Governor Ruoldo! For the crimes of stealing my body from me, practising heresy, and all-round monstrousness, you are hereby sentenced to death! Attack!"
  - After: "Governor Ruoldo! For body theft and heresy, you die! Attack!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Has anyone got a lho-stick? I badly need a puff."
  - After: "Anyone got a lho-stick?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "But why did you not get out of the cage earlier? You could have..."
  - After: "Why not leave the cage earlier?"
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "Let's go with an old Thasserian proverb: 'do not feed the horse you cannot outrun.'"
  - After: "Thasserian proverb: 'do not feed the horse you cannot outrun.'"
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "One last stick before you go? I approve — let us respect that tradition! Somebody fetch me a—"
  - After: "One last stick? Tradition! Fetch me a—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}When the dust clears, you see the familiar hall. From the shadows, the jester's eyes spark with malice as they meet yours. Behind him stands a cage, in which you, or rather your body, is sitting. Your face is awash with tears, your lip is split, and a vox lies next to you. In another cage to the side stands Solomorne, glaring through the bars at the true governor of Thassera. Upon seeing you and Glaito, the Proctor straightens. It seems he was just waiting for your return. Without taking his intent gaze off you, he gives you a slow nod: he is ready to fight.{/n}
  - After: {n}The hall. Behind the glaring jester, your tear-stained body sits caged. Solomorne, caged too, nods: ready.{/n}
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: {n}The fool mockingly sticks out his chin.{/n} "And how, may I ask, do you intend to do that? Only Tavrisk and myself know how the ritual works; certainly, he is the only one who can perform it. And it just so happens that we don't feel much inclined to cooperate."
  - After: {n}The fool smirks.{/n} "How? Only Tavrisk can do the ritual, and we won't."
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: {n}Ruoldo's loud cackling reverberates around the hall, creating a thousand echoes.{/n} "Sculptor! You may begin!"
  - After: {n}Ruoldo cackles.{/n} "Sculptor! Begin!"
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "How very generous! Allow me to repay you in kind. If you leave now, you may live out the rest of your days on my planet as that dunce of a woman! No, wait. I've changed my—"
  - After: "Generous! Leave and live as that dunce woman! No, wait—"
- **Maive**
  - Before: {n}Maive, the real Maive, looks at you through watering eyes.{/n} "Myself again... It was so... so..." {n}She lacks the strength for anything more, and her body collapses to the ground.{/n}
  - After: {n}The real Maive weeps.{/n} "Myself again..." {n}She collapses.{/n}
- **Tavrisk the Sculptor**
  - Before: {n}Without removing his hands from the stone in front of him, the heavily augmented old man turns around to look at you, an expression of utter amazement spreading across his face.{/n} "But why? Why would I negotiate with a corpse-to-be? You are the past, and the governor and I are bound for the future!"
  - After: {n}The old man turns, amazed.{/n} "Negotiate with a corpse-to-be? We are the future!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}The metal of the cage emits a piteous creak as Solomorne slams his entire weight against the bars...{/n}
  - After: {n}Solomorne slams the bars...{/n}
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: {n}The court fool snaps his fingers, and the guards ready their weapons. In the tense silence that follows, every sound, every movement can be clearly heard. And then...{/n}
  - After: {n}The fool snaps; guards raise weapons. Silence. Then...{/n}
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: {n}Ruoldo casts a furtive glance out the window and lets out a hesitant giggle.{/n} "Decided to show a little decorum, my celestial guest? It is a little late for tha—"
  - After: {n}Ruoldo giggles nervously.{/n} "Decorum now? Too late for tha—"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I didn't. But the heretics were so obsessed with this lump of stone, I figured their sorcery would be ruined without it."
  - After: "I didn't. I figured breaking their stone would ruin their sorcery."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "How dare you order anyone around in my own palace! Tavrisk, do it!"
  - After: "Orders in my palace? Tavrisk, do it!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I don't know, Rogue Trader. My finger might twitch, and Glaito will think it's an order to spill his guts."
  - After: "My finger might twitch, and Glaito will gut him."
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "But how did you... the elevator! Damn it, why did you have to make all this commotion? Why couldn't you just sit in a cage, out of the way, and wait for the ritual to be completed?" {n}The fool looks back at the altar.{/n} "Tavrisk, move!"
  - After: "The elevator! Why not stay caged?" {n}He turns.{/n} "Tavrisk, move!"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "There is truth in his words: it is senseless to negotiate with a corpse-to-be." {n}Kibellah runs her fingers along the edge of her blade with a slow, almost caressing motion.{/n}
  - After: "True. No use bargaining with a corpse." {n}Kibellah strokes her blade.{/n}
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "What is that old louse muttering now? Judging by that fulsome sneer of his, it's not the praises of the Allfather."
  - After: "What's the old louse muttering? Not the Allfather's praises."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Your tongue is a quite superfluous part of your body, Vil'Ruoldo. Worry not — this flaw is easy to correct."
  - After: "Your tongue is superfluous, Vil'Ruoldo. Easily fixed."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "The term 'cooperation' is hardly applicable in this circumstance, Ruoldo." {n}As Heinrix speaks, his gaze, focused and grim, sweeps over the hall, the altar, and Tavrisk's decrepit frame.{/n}
  - After: "Not 'cooperation', Ruoldo." {n}Heinrix eyes Tavrisk grimly.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "You're really, really not going to like that future, old man. The ones beyond the door already send their regards. They say they can't wait to meet you and this little king of yours."
  - After: "You'll hate that future, old man. Those beyond the door await you."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "They would be of no help to him now. Nothing would." {n}Argenta's eyes are ablaze, her hands firmly clutching her weapon.{/n}
  - After: "Nothing can help him." {n}Argenta grips her weapon.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "More often than not, there is a ravine of differences lying between us, Master Interrogator. But right now, I am prepared to cross it, so that we may stand together and give this one's motley posterior the beating it deserves." {n}Jae's crooked smile is as grim as Heinrix's.{/n}
  - After: "For once, Master Interrogator, let's beat this one's motley posterior together." {n}Jae grins.{/n}
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: {n}Ruoldo angrily grits his teeth as he shoots them both a withering look.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ruoldo glares.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I have heard plenty of nonsense spoken by convicts, but that drivel wins first place."
  - After: "That drivel wins first place."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Ah!" {n}Cassia flinches and shields her eyes with her hand.{/n} "The deathly light of thassertium... It is all around him, permeating his soul, melding into his colour, his essence..."
  - After: "Ah!" {n}Cassia shields her eyes.{/n} "Thassertium light fills his soul..."
- **Tavrisk the Sculptor**
  - Before: {n}The psyker's cracked skin seems ready to crumble to dust, but his thassertium eyes burn with an otherworldly fire.{/n} "The ritual is nearly complete, my lord. The Altar of Change is ready to irrevocably switch the threads of fate."
  - After: {n}Tavrisk's thassertium eyes burn.{/n} "The Altar of Change is nearly ready, my lord."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I doubt it. Loosening the cage's fastenings without being noticed proved to be quite difficult. Besides, without you and Glaito there, the outcome would have been too unpredictable, and I had no room for error. But there was one thing I knew for sure: Glaito's implants and mine were exchanging data logs, which meant you were alive. So I waited."
  - After: "Loosening the cage unseen was hard, and acting without you too risky. Glaito's implants told me you lived. I waited."
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "So the rumours were true? I'll remember that arrogant tone when I'm the one flaunting your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_GreatDeed}exploits{/d} in your body!" {n}The fool laughs, but the laughter sounds nervous.{/n}
  - After: "I'll flaunt your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_GreatDeed}exploits{/d} in your body!" {n}He laughs nervously.{/n}
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: {n}The fool delivers a mocking bow, as if inviting you to dance.{/n} "Dying was not among my plans tonight. Sculptor, get to work!"
  - After: {n}The fool bows.{/n} "Not dying tonight. Sculptor, work!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You struggle to open your eyes. After the world has once again taken shape, you realise that you are staring at your own palms, from your own eye sockets. You move a hand, and each muscle responds gratefully, filling with warmth. The others watch you with a mixture of hope and dismay.{/n}
  - After: {n}You wake in your own body. The others watch, hopeful.{/n}

Would you lend it to her?" {n}The one-eyed bandit glances at your dirty yet expensive clothes. Something tells you that these people would gladly peel the dress off you, right along with your skin.{/n}

- **One-Eye**

- **One-Eye**
  - Before: {n}Several bandits at once break into howling laughter.{/n} "Oh, that sure gave me a fright, it did," {n}says the leader through the tears, casually pulling a knife from his sleeve. Glaito, standing by your leg, lets out a rumbling growl, and the laughter stops.{/n}

  - After: "Behold Cogicor, the scrolls' mechanical sage! It knows all, commands machines, foretells the future!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The box in front of you, presumably the Cogicor they speak of, exudes a strong odour of ritual oils. Made of thin planks, it is covered in so many purity seals that it seems to be held together by them alone. A stack of flimsy rough paper lies atop it, and there is a mica panel with malachite buttons attached to the front. A thin slit is visible among the buttons.{/n}
  - After: {n}A flimsy, oil-reeking box held together by purity seals, with buttons and a paper slit.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard sighs heavily and leans over to you.{/n} "Sometimes, when information reaches the more backward worlds, it undergoes strange metamorphoses in the minds of unfortunate and regrettably parochial laypeople... Have mercy, Lord Captain. They probably have been trying to please you."
  - After: {n}Abelard sighs.{/n} "Backward worlds garble things. Have mercy, Lord Captain."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix shrugs.{/n} "I've seen quite a few distortions of Gothic on primitive worlds... But I do not recall ever seeing such a miscomprehension of the Omnissiah's gifts."
  - After: {n}Heinrix shrugs.{/n} "Never seen the Omnissiah's gifts so misunderstood."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}There is a barely audible breathing coming from the box. Whoever is inside wants very much not to be noticed.{/n}
  - After: {n}Faint breathing: someone hides inside.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Surprisingly, the quiet rustle coming from the box does in fact resemble the hum of a cogitator.{/n}
  - After: {n}It does sound like a cogitator.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If I may advise the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}... In order to receive an answer, one should take a piece of paper and slide it into the hole here. Then, touch this stone and ask the question loudly and clearly."
  - After: "Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}, slide paper in, touch this stone, and ask clearly."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sheet you offer is consumed with a speed beyond that of an ordinary autoquill. After a few moments, the sheet returns with a single notation: "LOTS."{/n}
  - After: {n}The sheet returns: "LOTS."{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sheet shoots back out of the box and falls to the ground. It bears a solemn inscription: "GLORY EVERLASTING."{/n}
  - After: {n}The sheet shoots out: "GLORY EVERLASTING."{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The box holds the paper for a long time. When the sheet finally emerges from the slot, it is visibly shaking. You see the words "IMMOLATION. PLEASE DON'T."{/n}
  - After: {n}A trembling sheet: "IMMOLATION. PLEASE DON'T."{/n}
- **Young Nobleman**
  - Before: "As you wish. Do not hesitate to pose more questions! It has enough ink for many more answers."
  - After: "As you wish. It has ink aplenty!"
- **Young Nobleman**
  - Before: "Who? What poor soul? I do not..." {n}The young nobleman addressing you withers under the scathing gaze of his partner.{/n}
  - After: "What soul? I..." {n}His partner glares.{/n}
- **Grey-Haired Nobleman**
  - Before: "As you command, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}. Forgive us... We wished only to delight you by reproducing an otherworldly miracle we had read about in an ancient chronicle..."
  - After: "As you command, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}. We only copied an ancient miracle..."
- **Young Nobleman**
  - Before: "Our hearts flutter at the opportunity to please the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}! May this sagacious machine assist you in your endeavours."
  - After: "We're thrilled to please the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The box's thin walls splinter under your blows, and the ink-stained body of an old man falls to the paving stones. The two noblemen look away nervously, but they do not risk fleeing your wrath.{/n}
  - After: {n}The box splinters; an ink-stained old man tumbles out. The nobles cower.{/n}
- **Grey-Haired Nobleman**
  - Before: "We did not mean to offend! We only wished to please..."
  - After: "We only wished to please!"
- **Grey-Haired Nobleman**
  - Before: {n}As you approach, the nobles bow gracefully. Their sewn-on faces are wrapped tightly around their skulls, and their eyes gleam with earnest subservience. One dares to address you:{/n} "O Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}, grace us with your regard! When my brother and I heard of your arrival, we immediately sought to surprise you with an exceptional gift."
  - After: {n}Two nobles with sewn-on faces bow.{/n} "O Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}! We have a gift for you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The miraculous device reluctantly accepts the offered paper and makes a vague moan-like sound. After a languid moment of waiting, you are presented with a sheet that reads "ERR" — which most likely means "error."{/n}
  - After: {n}It moans: "ERR."{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}After a chrono-turn of heavy silence, Pasqal finally intones,{/n} "I am registering an act of... imitation of sanctity. This cultural phenomenon is typical of underdeveloped tribes. I also anticipate the discovery of cave pictograms dedicated to the divine arrival of the more advanced units."
  - After: "Imitation of sanctity, typical of underdeveloped tribes," {n}Pasqal intones.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne folds his arms and leans toward the slot, his voice ringing with steel:{/n} "Machines cannot feel fear, 'Cogicor.' They can only meekly accept their fate." {n}The Proctor catches your gaze and shrugs.{/n} "I couldn't help myself."
  - After: {n}Solomorne, to the slot:{/n} "Machines don't fear, 'Cogicor.'" {n}He shrugs.{/n} "Couldn't resist."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Glaito stalks toward the box and bares his fangs, while Solomorne frowns grimly at the device:{/n} "Really? Then again, what else could you expect from this ignorant world..."
  - After: {n}Glaito bares fangs. Solomorne:{/n} "Typical of this ignorant world..."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn gleefully throws his hands in the air.{/n} "Nuncius, witness the act of creating a primitive technological idol! Please record everything carefully — this is a unique opportunity to observe how a culture deprived of the Omnissiah's light attempts to interpret His design!"
  - After: {n}Eogunn beams.{/n} "Nuncius, record this primitive techno-idol!"

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/FeudalWorld/FW_Daemon/FW_Daemon_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You are nothing but a worm in the shadow of the Golden Throne! Reveal yourself to me, and let us fight! Or is hiding like a coward in the back of a person's thoughts all you are capable of doing?"
  - After: "Worm beneath the Golden Throne! Show yourself and fight, or keep hiding in minds, coward?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I need no protection, daemon. People are stronger than you think."
  - After: "I need no protection, daemon. People are stronger."
- **Player**
  - Before: "My gratitude will not be long in coming, Master."
  - After: "My gratitude will come soon, Master."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A moment of ringing silence — and then, a thousand shards pierce your mind. A familiar voice coils around your thoughts, drowning them out:{/n} "Are you leaving without even conversing with me, Child? Without even asking yourself how such a vivid soul managed to remain intact after wandering in the darkness's embrace and donning another's guise? Such rare luck for a mortal."
  - After: {n}A voice pierces your mind:{/n} "Leaving, Child? Don't you wonder how your soul survived intact?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And their time is so fleeting..." {n}The echo of the entity's voice lingers for a while, like the sound of distant thunder.{/n}
  - After: "So fleeting..." {n}It echoes like thunder.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}In the icy silence, you are struck with a series of incredibly lifelike recollections. You are not alone, and you never were. It was always there, in your shadow, in your blood, inside you.{/n} "...Yes, {name}. This luck is named the Edge of Daybreak. Had it not been for my sleepless gaze, your mind would have long since joined the mournful host of those who are no more. It was I who kept it whole and unharmed, for I could not allow such a radiant destiny to fall to some absurdity. But at times, I do wonder: is it worthy of my protection?"
  - After: {n}It was always within you.{/n} "Yes, {name}. The Edge of Daybreak. I kept your mind whole for your destiny. But are you worth it?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There it is: the ingratitude and obliviousness of the insects that call themselves Humanity. I am no corporeal body that can be slain, Child. All of time belongs to me, as does every thread in the tapestry of destinies. I need but touch one of them..." {n}You feel a sharp pain, and a trickle of blood runs down your temple. A taste of grim solemnity permeates the silence of your unseen interlocutor.{/n} "But I am generous: I give my chosen Children time to understand..."
  - After: "Ingrate. I have no body, Child; all fate's threads are mine." {n}Blood trickles from your temple.{/n} "But I give my Children time..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Naivety is a bold luxury... Is it not time to face the truth, Child? The threads of fate will not obey your desire alone. But I can help you to grasp them, once you are ready. Thankfully, I am generous: I give my chosen Children time to understand. After all, human souls are so fragile..." {n}You feel a sharp pain, and a trickle of blood runs down your temple.{/n}
  - After: "Naive, Child. Fate won't obey you alone; I'll help when you're ready. Souls are fragile..." {n}Blood trickles from your temple.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Soon. Very soon now, Child." {n}Ravenous sparks of foreign visions illuminate your mind.{/n} "You are not yet able to fathom the grand design of the Weaver of Destinies, but you may already relish this taste of power, of triumph, of true freedom, Child!"
  - After: "Soon, Child." {n}Visions flare.{/n} "The Weaver of Destinies' design eludes you, but taste this power!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You feel a sharp pain, and a trickle of blood runs down your chin — absorbed in the sudden cascade of images, you did not notice yourself biting your lip. Your patron has departed your mind.{/n}
  - After: {n}You bit your lip bloody. Your patron is gone.{/n}

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/FeudalWorld/FW_DrinkFountain/FW_DrinkFountain_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you always have amasec flowing from that fountain?"
  - After: "Does amasec always flow?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Drink] "Your 'enjoyments' and 'entertainments' are impossible to watch in a sober state."
  - After: [Drink] "Your 'entertainments' need drink."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Step away] "I prefer to keep my mind clear."
  - After: [Step away] "I'll stay clear-headed."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Come on, Solomorne. Just one cup."
  - After: "Come on, Solomorne. One cup."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Step away] "I think I have had enough."
  - After: [Step away] "Enough for me."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Drink] "I am ready to celebrate my glorious self!"
  - After: [Drink] "To my glorious self!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Hand the cup to Solomorne] "The duty of a valued guest is calling, Proctor."
  - After: [Hand the cup to Solomorne] "Guest's duty, Proctor."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Hand the cup to Solomorne] "Let us give our hosts their due and raise a toast to companionship, shall we? Let us lock our arms together and seal this solemn ritual with a kiss!"
  - After: [Hand the cup to Solomorne] "To companionship! Arms locked, sealed with a kiss!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The fools of this backward world won't be the only ones insulted should you refuse."
  - After: "Refuse, and you insult more than these fools."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are such a bore."
  - After: "You're such a bore."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Dark-maroon amasec is pouring out of the ridiculously gaudy fountain. An eager cup-bearer hands you a goblet filled to the brim.{/n} "Have a taste, if you please, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}! This vintage had been maturing ever since we laid the cornerstone of our citadel. We tapped it to celebrate you."
  - After: {n}A gaudy amasec fountain. A cup-bearer offers a goblet.{/n} "Taste, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}! Aged since our citadel's founding!"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Thank you, Lord Captain, but we need one of us to remain sober." {n}The Interrogator gives you a mildly reproachful look.{/n}
  - After: "Someone must stay sober, Lord Captain." {n}Heinrix looks reproachful.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet looks at the cup of amasec with what seems to be desperation. Finally, she twists her lips and utters a forced but firm{/n} "No."
  - After: {n}Yrliet hesitates.{/n} "No."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A pleasant warmth spreads through your body. The liquor is surprisingly palatable. The servant fills another cup and exclaims,{/n} "May your spirit be stronger than any amasec!"
  - After: {n}Warm and smooth. A refill:{/n} "May your spirit outlast any amasec!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I dare not protest! Should you change your mind, I am always at your service."
  - After: "As you wish! I'm at your service."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai wrinkles his nose in disgust.{/n} "I could smell the reek of this awful slosh from orbit. Do not insult me with the suggestion that I might want to drink it."
  - After: {n}Marazhai sneers.{/n} "I smelled this slosh from orbit. Don't insult me."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Request denied. I am registering a number of mind-altering substances in this preparation that act as cognitive suppressants." {n}Pasqal casts a long glance at the fountain.{/n} "The layman or woman who conceived the idea of installing a poisonous fountain in a public place must have been under the influence of the poison themselves."
  - After: "Denied. Cognitive suppressants detected." {n}Pasqal eyes the fountain.{/n} "Its builder was surely poisoned too."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Amasec clouds the mind and darkens the eye. I will refrain, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "Amasec clouds the mind. I'll refrain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You lean over the parapet with elegance, or what feels like it, and catch the amasec in your mouth. The dumbstruck servant sends the cups crashing to the ground. Anyone else who wants a drink will have to wait, or else follow your brilliant example.{/n}
  - After: {n}You elegantly catch the stream in your mouth. The stunned servant drops the cups.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your mind is a little hazy, and a drunken flush brightens your cheeks. The amasec may go down deceptively smoothly, but its strength is already making itself known.{/n}
  - After: {n}You feel hazy and flushed.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cup-bearer beams.{/n} "Has your promenade put you in the mood for a drink, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}?"
  - After: {n}The cup-bearer beams.{/n} "A drink, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The world around you begins to swim before your eyes, and the sight of the maroon liquid makes you a little nauseous. You probably should not drink any more of it.{/n}
  - After: {n}The world swims. No more.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sight of the liquor makes you a little nauseous. You probably should not drink any more of it.{/n}
  - After: {n}You feel queasy. No more.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Your head feels light and pleasantly empty. It looks like you are more than a little tipsy. A heavy hand is laid on your shoulder, and Solomorne's voice comes in cold and insistent:{/n} "You ought to stop, Rogue Trader. We still have business to attend to."
  - After: {n}You're tipsy. Solomorne grips your shoulder:{/n} "Stop. We have business."
- **Maive**
  - Before: {n}The young woman's cheeks flush a bright red as she accepts the drink from you.{/n} "Thank you, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}. Here's to you prospering forever, and Thassera always serving you truly and faithfully..." {n}Maive takes a sip and coughs, but upon noticing your gaze, she bravely downs the drink after all.{/n}
  - After: {n}Maive blushes.{/n} "May Thassera serve you forever, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}..." {n}She coughs, then downs it.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A stream of alcohol hits your nose. Your hands slip off the parapet. In full dress and along with all your weapons, you fall into the fragrant liquor, making a terribly loud splash.{/n}
  - After: {n}You slip and fall into the fountain, fully armed, with a huge splash.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "You are just like Glaito when he sinks his teeth into a heretic." {n}The Proctor takes the cup and downs it in one long, powerful gulp.{/n} "Are you sure this is amasec? It is a tad watery. Trust a planet that underpays its tithe to dilute its liquor as well."
  - After: "Like Glaito with a heretic." {n}He downs it.{/n} "Watery. Tithe-dodgers dilute their liquor too."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cup-bearer refills your goblet. Then, with a sudden soulfulness, he looks into your eyes and sighs,{/n} "May you, unlike the rest, always be the {mf|master|mistress} of your fate."
  - After: {n}The cup-bearer sighs,{/n} "May you always be {mf|master|mistress} of your fate."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar frowns sceptically before taking a powerful swig. He grimaces with contempt and spits on the ground.{/n} "Serving this sour hogwash to mighty warriors is a disgrace. Such tasteless slop can do nothing to raise the spirit."
  - After: {n}Ulfar swigs and spits.{/n} "Sour hogwash!"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "It is an honour to accept a gift from you, Domin." {n}Kibellah looks pensively at her own reflection in the cup and, with a swift motion of her hand, pours its contents into her ceremonial flask.{/n}
  - After: "An honour, Domin." {n}Kibellah pours it into her flask.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "By no means! Such frivolous excess would impede us in carrying out our burden of service to the Emperor. It is only on truly great days, such as today, that the fountain pours forth this noble beverage. Besides, even the sturdiest of servants could not work the pump for days on end."
  - After: "No! Only on great days like today. And the pump workers tire."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Naturally, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}! It requires the gruelling labour of dozens of sturdy workers to create an upward movement of the liquid in the pipes! It is a most useful contraption!"
  - After: "Yes, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}! Dozens of sturdy workers push the liquid up!"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I was planning to simply refuse... but I am nonetheless glad that the truth has been spoken." {n}Yrliet and Marazhai exchange knowing glances.{/n}
  - After: "I'd have just refused, but I'm glad it was said." {n}She and Marazhai exchange glances.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Azhi eat my eyes!" {n}A delighted Jae hands Cassia another brimming cup.{/n} "Keep going, shereen! You're doing great, but you're capable of so much more! Another couple of swigs, and the fire will warm your whole body and soul!"
  - After: "Azhi eat my eyes!" {n}Jae refills Cassia's cup.{/n} "Keep going, shereen!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}After casting a sidelong glance at you, Solomorne dips his head deferentially.{/n} "I apologise, I did not mean to be rude." {n}He accepts the cup, intertwines his arm with yours, and downs the amasec in a mighty gulp. Then he gives you a quick and not overly heated kiss and immediately averts his eyes.{/n}
  - After: {n}Solomorne bows.{/n} "Apologies." {n}Arm in arm, he drinks, kisses you quickly, and looks away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Perhaps a fountain of amasec is considered the height of luxury here on Thassera, but to you, one who has mastered the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}art of social libation{/d}, the amount of drink seems rather meagre.{/n}
  - After: {n}A master of {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}social libation{/d}, you find it meagre.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn inserts the tip of his augmetic finger into the goblet and pauses for study.{/n} "Analysis reveals traces of metals and organic compounds in the composition, the very same that coat the fountain's inner workings. Alas, this substance will give the drinker nothing but veisalgia and utter disappointment in the local customs of amasec making. No, Nuncius, my analysis does not require your revision."
  - After: {n}Eogunn tests it.{/n} "Pipe metals. It yields only veisalgia. No, Nuncius, no revision needed."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Once I am back on your flagship, I will raise a glass to the success of this mission. That is, I might raise a glass. Of water."
  - After: "On your flagship I might raise a glass. Of water."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "No. And not just because I am on a mission." {n}Solomorne studies the fountain with a critical eye.{/n} "This is nothing more than carousal on a backward world, no matter how many court fools are singing our glories. There is neither honour nor pleasure in partaking of local liquor."
  - After: "No. Not just for my mission." {n}He eyes the fountain.{/n} "Backward-world carousal holds no honour."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira shrinks from the amasec and hesitates for a short while before resolutely shaking her head.{/n}
  - After: {n}Idira shakes her head.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: {n}Cassia's eyes widen in dismay. She stares intently at the cup, then screws up her eyes and downs the contents in one gulp.{/n} "My throat is... on fire..."
  - After: {n}Cassia gulps it.{/n} "My throat... on fire..."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard accepts the cup with great decorum, takes half a gulp, and grunts thoughtfully,{/n} "An interesting bouquet. Not particularly refined, but quite potable, in my uninitiated opinion."
  - After: {n}Abelard sips.{/n} "Unrefined, but potable."
- **Jae**
  - Before: {n}Jae downs the cup and looks around her with melancholy eyes.{/n} "What can I say? Footfall isn't the only place that knows how to have a good time."
  - After: {n}Jae downs it wistfully.{/n} "Footfall's not the only place for a good time."

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/FeudalWorld/FW_Entry/FW_Entry_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Nod at the servitor orchestra] "Fascinating. How did you manage to acquire something like that?"
  - After: [Nod at the servitor orchestra] "How did you get those?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Can't wait to meet some kindred spirits?"
  - After: "Eager to meet kindred spirits?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You heard the Proctor. Take us somewhere we can have a serious conversation."
  - After: "Take us somewhere to talk seriously."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell me your gossip, then."
  - After: "Tell me your gossip."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Ruoldo, I'm sure you know why we are here."
  - After: "Ruoldo, you know why we're here."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do your servants often interrupt their rulers' conversations without permission, Governor?"
  - After: "Do servants often interrupt you, Governor?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You mentioned entertainment. Tell me more."
  - After: "Tell me about the entertainment."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Very well. I would like to see what this place has to offer."
  - After: "Show me what this place offers."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Let's go, then. We must not miss the biggest local spectacle."
  - After: "Let's go. Can't miss the big spectacle."
- **Player**
  - Before: "We have plenty of time. First, I will inspect every nook and cranny in this place."
  - After: "First, I'll inspect every corner here."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Abelard, announce the purpose of our visit to these provincials."
  - After: "Abelard, announce our purpose to these provincials."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What an exquisite necklace! I think it would look better around the neck of your Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."
  - After: "Exquisite necklace! It would suit your Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} better."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I thank you for the courteous welcome, Governor; however, we have come here to address a grave concern."
  - After: "Thank you, Governor, but we're here about a grave concern."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Glance around with a bored expression] "Might we proceed inside now? I find all this squalor rather tiring."
  - After: [Look bored] "Can we go inside? This squalor tires me."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Wave in Abelard's direction] "Seneschal, you take it. I do not wish to soil my hands."
  - After: [Wave at Abelard] "Seneschal, take it. I won't soil my hands."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Remember, Maive: I do not want to hear a word out of you unless I give you explicit permission or ask a direct question."
  - After: "Maive: not a word unless I allow it or ask."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your face is your own. Why is that?"
  - After: "Your face is your own. Why?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have absolutely no interest in your base entertainments. The sooner we start reviewing the tithe documents, the better!"
  - After: "No base entertainments. Show me the tithe documents."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You put on other people's skin out of a desire to look younger? You will declare this vile practice banned — today."
  - After: "Wearing others' skin to look younger? Ban this vile practice — today."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Grant each 'rejuvenated' individual a regular youth levy and overtime duties — after all, what good are health and long life to the servants of the Imperium?"
  - After: "Give each 'rejuvenated' a youth levy and overtime — long life should serve the Imperium."
- **Player**
  - Before: "A fine tradition indeed... I hope the subjects are conscious when you peel their skins off? I would love to attend such a procedure myself sometime and enjoy the show."
  - After: "Fine tradition... Are they conscious when peeled? I'd love to watch."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Smile] "Relax, Maive. Just pretend that you are giving a good friend a tour of the place."
  - After: [Smile] "Relax, Maive. Pretend you're touring a friend."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If it will help the investigation, we should not dally."
  - After: "If it helps the investigation, let's not dally."
- **Player**
  - Before: "'Celestial Highness.' What kind of an address is that?"
  - After: "'Celestial Highness'? What sort of address is that?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I believe there was something else the esteemed governor wished to say?"
  - After: "The governor had more to say?"
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "I am most flattered by your attention, esteemed judicator — and by this opportunity to serve the Imperium with even greater dedication than before. Speaking of dedication, we are already conducting a thorough inspection to see which scribe it was that bungled the tithe calculation. Fear not: the scoundrel shall soon be—"
  - After: "Most flattered, judicator! We're already hunting the scribe who bungled the tithe—"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Enough. According to data-protocol Calixis-Sigma UX 11-4, this Mu-class planet, type 'feudal,' {g|Encyclopedia:AestimareGlossary}Aestimare rating{/g} E874, with an assigned {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGradeGlossary}tithe grade of Solutio Extremis{/g}, has not provided its due tithe amount in full. You have violated the Lex and are hereby under investigation. You are to present all related customs reports and shipping manifests. Immediately." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:ProctorGlossary}Proctor{/g}'s voice carries no emotion, and Glaito silently bares his teeth, completing the image of the implacable hand of justice that has arrived on Thassera.{/n}
  - After: "Enough. This world, {g|Encyclopedia:AestimareGlossary}Aestimare rating{/g} E874, {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGradeGlossary}tithe grade of Solutio Extremis{/g}, has underpaid its tithe. You are under investigation. Present all manifests. Immediately." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:ProctorGlossary}Proctor{/g} is cold; Glaito bares teeth.{/n}
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "Though at most only once in a generation, even Thassera receives visits from time to time, Your Celestial Highness. One day, an entire delegation from a foreign world arrived with these mechanical musicians in tow. We were immediately smitten with them! Sadly, our performers have now fallen into a sorry state. Thassera's humid air makes their preservation difficult, you see, and we don't have a single {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}crimson-clad{/g} holy man or woman left. All we can do now is offer up prayers of our own, burn oils, and do everything else the old writings say, even though we have no hope of understanding them..."
  - After: "Foreign visitors brought them once. Now they rot in our damp air, and no {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}crimson-clad{/g} priest remains. We just pray and burn oils."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The governor's heavy gold-stitched jacket adds a certain presence to his figure, but it cannot hide how poor of a rider he is. The way his boots dig into the horse's sides, his hands fiddling with the reins, his trembling fingers — all speak of nervousness and a lack of control.{/n}
  - After: {n}Fine jacket, poor rider: he's nervous and lacks control.{/n}
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "Thank you, Your Celestial Highness! We know your journey here must have been an arduous one. As a sign of our appreciation, we have prepared a veritable... constellation of enjoyments in your honour! We humbly invite you to taste of our amasec, along with our finest dishes, and may you likewise savour some of the local entertainment. One of the court ladies will accompany you so as not to let even a single word or wish of yours linger without attention."
  - After: "Thank you! We've prepared amasec, feasts and entertainment. A court lady will attend you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The governor's gold-stitched jacket bears a skilfully depicted Aquila encircled by glittering stars, each of which has been cut from a different type of gemstone — a remarkable luxury for someone who governs a world devoid of the light of civilisation.{/n}
  - After: {n}His jacket bears a jewelled Aquila — rare luxury on a backward world.{/n}
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: {n}Ruoldo touches his stretched-out countenance.{/n} "Ah, this is a fine tradition that I myself brought to this world! You see, there is a way to tame the merciless passage of time: all you need is to find a young and healthy face, appropriate it, and attach it over your own fading skin. The local nobility eagerly took to this art of extending one's life and youth, and I, once a Celestial Lord myself, now promote this custom by personal example so I may showcase its wonderful properties!"
  - After: {n}Ruoldo touches his stretched face.{/n} "My tradition! Wear a young face over your own. The nobles love it!"
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: {n}The fool parts with his offering and then jumps away with an irritating giggle.{/n}
  - After: {n}The fool hops away giggling.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Before you can even blink, the cyber-mastiff beside him sinks its teeth into Bluff's forearm, jerking it back and forth in a fury. The attack lasts only for a moment, but when Glaito lets go, the fool's limb is already torn to shreds. With a cry of pain, Bluff leaps away and melds into the roiling crowd.{/n}
  - After: {n}Glaito savages Bluff's forearm. Shrieking, the fool flees.{/n}
- **Maive**
  - Before: {n}A thin woman emerges into the torchlight, looking at you with a mixture of fear and awe. Her diminutive figure is practically drowning in her velvet and silk dress, and a resplendent necklace of blue stone adorns her neck.{/n} "Maive, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}, at your service!"
  - After: {n}A thin, awed woman in silk and a blue-stone necklace steps forward.{/n} "Maive, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}, at your service!"
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: {n}Daunted by your silence, the governor squirms nervously in his saddle.{/n}
  - After: {n}The governor squirms in his saddle.{/n}
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "Well, slap my grox! Fine, then, listen to this: One-Eye, terror of the common man, went out a-thieving one day. He sneaks into a hut, itching to fill up his sack, and what sees he? A scary big shadow on the floor! He turns around, and right behind him... a giant! A monster! With hands like Imperial columns! It grabs him by the throat and starts beating the air out of him like he's a ball of dough... Turns out, he's popped by Murgeth's place, and she used to work the bone mill no worse than ten men could when she was young. The fellow's been One-Eye ever since. And hoo, is he glad he's not One-Arm or One-Leg!"
  - After: "Slap my grox! One-Eye the thief robbed a hut, and a giant pounded him like dough — old Murgeth, strong as ten at the bone mill. Glad he's not One-Arm!"
- **Maive**
  - Before: "Such living masks are the privilege of the high nobility. I may not be a commoner, but to be entitled to a change of face... That is something I have yet to earn." {n}Maive casts a fascinated eye over the nobles whose faces — inasmuch as they are theirs — are stretched tight over metal fixtures. Many have their mouths frozen in an unnatural smile, and it is hard to tell whether this is a consequence of the tightness, or simply an eager show of delight.{/n}
  - After: "Living masks are for high nobility. I've yet to earn one." {n}She gazes at the nobles' stretched faces.{/n}
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: {n}A richly dressed man riding a sinewy horse breaks off from the procession. When he approaches, you immediately notice a strange detail: the man's face is pinned to his head with precious fastenings that stretch the skin across his skull.{/n} "Celestial guests, there is no higher honour for us than to extend our hospitality to such noble eminences! {mf|His|Her} Celestial Highness the Rogue Trader, and an illustrious judicator of the Imperium! All of Thassera clamours, trembles, and cheers! Ruoldo the Fair-Faced, Governor of Thassera, at your service!"
  - After: {n}A rider approaches, his face pinned taut with jewelled clasps.{/n} "Welcome, {mf|His|Her} Celestial Highness the Rogue Trader, and judicator! Ruoldo the Fair-Faced, Governor of Thassera, at your service!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "It's not a question of preference, but of what might help the investigation. The execution will gather a crowd, and we in turn will gather information. That will prove useful, considering how eager everyone was to make their exit."
  - After: "It's for the investigation. Executions draw crowds, and crowds talk."
- **Maive**
  - Before: "Taddua the Scorched is hosting a public trial for a few guilty wretches today. I also overheard that the council of Thasserian nobility was preparing a special gift for you... Besides those, our mechanical orchestra, the only one on Thassera, will be playing all evening! And of course, you will also get to see the crowning jewel of Lord Ruoldo's collection: his maimed, metal-harnessed beasts!"
  - After: "Taddua the Scorched holds a public trial today. The nobles have a gift for you, the orchestra plays, and Lord Ruoldo shows his maimed, metal-harnessed beasts!"
- **Maive**
  - Before: {n}Maive fidgets anxiously with her dress.{/n} "Perhaps my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} would like to attend the feast? Or the execution?"
  - After: {n}Maive fidgets.{/n} "The feast, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}? Or the execution?"
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "Look at this one! She has barely risen above the bottom, and already she shoots for the privileges of the top! Greedy hands are wont to get chopped off!"
  - After: "Barely off the bottom and reaching for the top! Greedy hands get chopped!"
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "Well, well! Our Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} is not one to mince words — {mf|he|she} up and tells the specks on the soles of {mf|his|her} shoes where they belong!"
  - After: "Our Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} puts the specks on {mf|his|her} soles in their place, {mf|he|she} does!"
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "But of course, Your Celestial Highness! It would be my pleasure to discuss whatever topic you have in mind. That said, you have had such long and perilous journey behind you! Like any self-respecting host, I must first propose—"
  - After: "Of course! But after such a journey, I must first propose—"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne ruffles Glaito's neck and turns to you.{/n} "Feudal worlds are rarely known for their bureaucratic precision. Reconnaissance on the ground will tell us more than any report hastily scribbled down by these blockheads. I suggest we attend this trial and see how the laws of this planet are enforced."
  - After: {n}Solomorne pats Glaito.{/n} "Feudal reports are worthless. Let's attend the trial and see their law."
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "Mhmm, I can tell by what I'm hearing that our executioner has already lit up the Phesmophorius, ready to give the condemned a warm welcome! Which means the governor's official whisper collector — that's me — has a whole lot of important business to get to. And so, I must leave you now, good sirs and ladies, lest I miss out on a hot batch of juicy tales. Terribly pleased to meet you all! Honoured judicator!" {n}Bluff grasps Solomorne's hand and gives it a vigorous shake.{/n}
  - After: "The Phesmophorius is lit! I must go gather tales. Honoured judicator!" {n}Bluff shakes Solomorne's hand.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I see no reason not to. Who knows what evidence we might discover — or what secrets of her lord our guide might share." {n}Solomorne gives Maive an ominous look that makes her shudder timidly.{/n}
  - After: "Why not? We may find evidence — or our guide's secrets." {n}Maive shudders.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Just professional intuition. Shall we go?"
  - After: "Intuition. Shall we go?"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Excuses are the hallmark of the guilty. Do not make your situation worse, Governor."
  - After: "Excuses mark the guilty, Governor."
- **Maive**
  - Before: {n}Maive gasps. With trembling hands, she removes her necklace and offers it to you with a curtsy.{/n} "Lord Ruoldo generously gave it to me... This stone is a thassertium shard — the rare crystal our planet is famed for. Truly, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} is more deserving of such a gift..."
  - After: {n}Trembling, Maive offers the necklace.{/n} "A thassertium shard, our famed crystal. You deserve it more, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "As you wish. However, I should warn you that sudden 'handshakes' like that are considered tantamount to assaulting an Arbitrator on duty — there are contact poisons out there that can kill you in a couple of heartbeats. Be on your guard, Rogue Trader: festivals like these are ideal settings for assassinations."
  - After: "As you wish. But such 'handshakes' may carry contact poisons. Festivals suit assassins."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Judging by the stench, the servitors — or, more specifically, the parts of them made of flesh — will not last much longer. Slime oozes from rust holes, every other lifeless eye is adorned with cataracts, and their mouths are like corpse dumps filled with shards of rotten teeth. Every wrong note their instruments play is accompanied by the mournful screeching of servo-motors and sparks flashing from dangling wires.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servitors' flesh is rotting; servos screech and spark at every wrong note.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}A furrow appears on Heinrix's brow.{/n} "But that is devoid of all sense... What is this, some travesty of rejuvenat treatments? All the procedures I have heard of are far more complex and laborious..."
  - After: {n}Heinrix frowns.{/n} "Senseless. A travesty of real rejuvenat treatments."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard, wearing a grim expression, accepts the gift in your stead. Through comically exaggerated gestures, the fool displays his grief at having been unable to hand you the key directly, then steps back into the governor's shadow.{/n}

- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "Oh, the embarrassment!" {n}The governor leans down from his horse and grabs the fool's hand. Having wrenched the key from Bluff's grasp, Ruoldo raises his hand to strike, and the fool quickly backs off. Finally, the governor offers the gift to you with a reverential bow.{/n}
  - After: "The embarrassment!" {n}Ruoldo wrenches the key from Bluff, shoos him, and offers it to you with a bow.{/n}
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: {n}You miss your mark as the fool jumps away with surprising agility, dancing and jeering as he goes.{/n}
  - After: {n}The fool dodges, jeering.{/n}
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "Being the paragon of grace that {mf|he|she} is, would my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}, perhaps, also deign to feast {mf|his|her} ears on the latest Thasserian gossip to go with my gift?"
  - After: "Would my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} have gossip with {mf|his|her} gift, if {mf|he|she} please?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Having finished his nonsensical tale, the fool erupts into acerbic giggling.{/n}
  - After: {n}The fool giggles.{/n}
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: {n}Ruoldo nods, somewhat perplexed.{/n} "I, well, I do have certain suppositions—"
  - After: {n}Ruoldo, perplexed:{/n} "I have suppositions—"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's optical visor fills with deep red, and his vox-speaker erupts into a howl of pained fury:{/n} "I am registering heretical sacrilege born from the stupidity of self-entitled laity! The commandment 'Offend not the Omnissiah by negligent misservice' has been trampled!" {n}His wail turns into an angry, stifled wheeze:{/n} "What scoundrel was it that thought to burn sacred unguents instead of incense?"
  - After: {n}Pasqal's visor flares red.{/n} "Sacrilege!" {n}He wheezes:{/n} "Who burned sacred unguents instead of incense?"
- **Maive**
  - Before: {n}Maive opens her mouth to say something, but catches herself, drops her gaze, and gives a sad nod.{/n}
  - After: {n}Maive stops herself and nods sadly.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne looks at the throng currently staring at you in wonder and trepidation.{/n} "So, 'Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}'... Your coming is a historic event for these people. Rest assured: the locals will be watching your every move, and a single word or careless gesture from you may well transform their lives on this underdeveloped world."
  - After: {n}Solomorne eyes the crowd.{/n} "You're history to them, 'Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}'. Mind your words."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "Oh!" {n}Ruoldo looks confused for a few moments.{/n} "Yes! Yes, of course, this very day..."
  - After: "Oh!" {n}Ruoldo is confused.{/n} "Yes, today..."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "Most assuredly, Your Celestial Highness! I shall proclaim this decree this very day..." {n}Ruoldo smiles, causing his attached face to crease in an unsettling way.{/n}
  - After: "Assuredly! I'll proclaim it today." {n}His attached face creases.{/n}
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: {n}A smaller figure steps out of the crowd, dressed in the motley attire of a court fool and wearing a sneering mask.{/n} "My name is Bluff! I am Lord Ruoldo's good mood. I tickle His Governorship with well-spouted jests and itty-bitty gossip. And now, I merrily doff my cap to our Celestial Lords and Ladies and hand them this here key to Thassera as a token of our boundless loyalty." {n}The fool bows and offers you his gift.{/n}
  - After: {n}A masked fool in motley steps out.{/n} "I'm Bluff, Lord Ruoldo's good mood! Here's the key to Thassera, for our boundless loyalty." {n}He bows, offering it.{/n}
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: {n}Ruoldo's eyes nearly pop from their sockets at your words. He gulps and nods awkwardly.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ruoldo gulps and nods.{/n}
- **Maive**
  - Before: {n}Maive smiles sheepishly.{/n} "I'm afraid that is easier said than done, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} — it would be like trying to imagine a mighty sun as a tiny ember. But I will do my best not to anger you by acting too nervous."
  - After: {n}Maive smiles sheepishly.{/n} "Like seeing the sun as an ember, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}. But I'll try."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I am pleased to see that you prefer to continue our mission over all the idle pastimes of this world."
  - After: "Good. The mission first."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "That is what we call the highborn who come down to us in their wondrous vessels... Of course, I am not a native of Thassera, and thus, was once a Celestial Lord myself. I have grown used to the local customs, however, and so, I address you like any Thasserian would."
  - After: "Our name for highborn from the stars. I was one myself, but follow local custom."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: {n}Ruoldo clasps his hands together and says meekly,{/n} "Of course, Master Judicator, I will provide you with all the documents as soon as our internal review is complete. I assure you it won't take long, and the report itself will be exhaustive!"
  - After: {n}Ruoldo, meekly:{/n} "You'll have every document once our review is done, Master Judicator!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne leans closer and says in a lowered voice,{/n} "Based on my experience, I would say we have been assigned a spy under a pretence of generosity, but this is a good thing. We will use this young woman as our source of information about the world. For now, it would be wise to play along and question her thoroughly once we are away from prying ears."
  - After: {n}Solomorne whispers,{/n} "She's a spy. Good. Play along; we'll question her privately."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The governor's clumsy attempts to stay in the saddle and his utter lack of noble bearing are {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}bewildering to you{/d}. It appears that the upbringing of the Thasserian aristocracy is as unimpressive as this world's technological state.{/n}
  - After: {n}His clumsy riding {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}bewilders you{/d}. Thassera's nobility is as backward as its tech.{/n}
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "From a distant civilised world — yes, Thassera lacks much of what I was accustomed to, yet after my appointment here, I quickly grew to love this planet with all my heart. I hope that during your visit you, too, will come to feel at least some affection for Thassera."
  - After: "A distant civilised world. But I love Thassera now. I hope you will too."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ruoldo abruptly changes the subject, unwilling to say more about his native world. The reason for this is unclear.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ruoldo avoids talk of his homeworld. Why is unclear.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard clears his throat.{/n} "{mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} {name} von Valancius, inheritor of the greatest protectorate of the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g} and bearer of the sacred {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g}, has graced Thassera with {mf|his|her} presence in order to discuss matters pertaining to this planet's tithe—"
  - After: {n}Abelard clears his throat.{/n} "{mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} {name} von Valancius, of the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}, bearer of the {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g}, honours Thassera with {mf|his|her} presence regarding its tithe—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ruoldo does not seem in the least disheartened — exchanging the gleaming spires of a hive for the dark towers of a feudal world would have broken the spirit of many.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ruoldo seems content, despite trading a hive for a feudal world.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I am surprised they're still functioning." {n}Eogunn's facial muscles twitch, as if the Manipulus is making a titanic effort not to grimace in disgust.{/n} "Perhaps the air here is conducive to the slow decay of the organic matter... or perhaps even servitors possess something akin to a will to live. What's that, Nuncius?" {n}The Genetor turns to his servo-skull.{/n} "No, this particular phenomenon does not seem anything like a machine miracle after all."
  - After: "Surprising they still work." {n}Eogunn hides a grimace.{/n} "Perhaps servitors have a will to live." {n}He turns to Nuncius.{/n} "No, not a machine miracle."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Temper yourself, colleague. You are making a category error, thinking that the indigenous population is capable of observing the rituals of service to the fullest extent. The best that an ignorant layperson can do for a working mechanism is to leave it well alone. The burning of sacred unguents, however, is... quite unnecessary."
  - After: "Temper yourself, colleague. Laity should leave machines alone. Though burning unguents is... unnecessary."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "N-now, Your Celestial Highness, we truly tried our best to put together a celebration worthy of our honoured visitors. But the news of your coming reached us so late! All I have left is a single talentless Astropath. We had to rush the preparations. Nevertheless, we have managed to put everything, everything Thassera is proud of on display here for you! I must ask—"
  - After: "N-now, we tried! But news came so late. I must ask—"
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "Well, in that case... please proceed to the castle. All of Thassera has been awaiting your arrival, busily preparing the finest dishes and entertainments in your honour, so I fear it may be challenging for you to avoid attention. Let us have a court lady accompany you..."
  - After: "Then proceed to the castle. All Thassera awaits you. A court lady will accompany you..."

And his voice — a true delight! I'll wager people must stand in line for a chance to confess to 'his holiness' in private. ## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/FeudalWorld/FW_FinalJudgement/FW_FinalJudgement_dialogue

- **Player**

  - Before: "In the end, he realised thassertium was a potent {g|Encyclopedia:PsyfocusGlossary}psy-focus{/g}. A magnificent artefact; a door to eternity! No more limitations imposed by our mortal bodies. No ailments, no injuries! If your flesh is worn... just swap it for new flesh! Don't like your lot in life? Choose from a thousand others! No longer just a dream, but its most perfect realisation. Immortality in stone..."
  - After: "Thassertium is a {g|Encyclopedia:PsyfocusGlossary}psy-focus{/g}. After many sacrifices, Tavrisk made the Altar of Change: swap worn flesh, choose another life. Immortality in stone!"

  - Before: "This statement is false, for it is incomplete. The rite of Servitude Imperpituis does not inhibit the unit's communication abilities — it replaces the decay of worldly notions with sacred logo-algorithms. Flesh-speak is flawed and redundant."
  - After: "Incomplete. Servitors' speech isn't removed; flesh-speak becomes logo-algorithms."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Be silent, heretic. Or you will find yourself washing away your blasphemies with tears of blood until the pain makes you beg the Emperor for death."
  - After: "Silence, heretic, or weep blood."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "You were an accomplice to the heretics, and you have been touched by sorcerous blight. In your position, I would beg for a swift execution." {n}There is no hatred in Solomorne's words, only total conviction about their truth.{/n}
  - After: "You aided heretics and are tainted. Beg for a swift death." {n}He says it calmly.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Agreed. Anything even remotely connected to the heresy that was committed here must be destroyed down to the last fragment — and to the last participant."
  - After: "Agreed. Destroy every fragment and participant."
- **Maive**
  - Before: "I understand. Thank you... for your mercy, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}." {n}Maive curtsies, staring straight ahead in confusion.{/n}
  - After: "Thank you for your mercy, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}." {n}She curtsies, dazed.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "The heretic mentioned that destroying the altar would risk deaths among the local population. Whether he was lying or trying to manipulate us is irrelevant: the abomination must be destroyed. As for any casualties... The Emperor will know His own."
  - After: "He said destroying the altar could kill locals. Irrelevant. The Emperor will know His own."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As you approach the damaged altar, you feel an unpleasant weakness. You hear a faint ringing in your ears, as if the smooth surface of the stone is groaning from the wounds it has suffered.{/n}
  - After: {n}Near the altar, you feel weak; the stone rings.{/n}
- **Maive**
  - Before: "Y-yes... as you command... But my brother wasn't the traitor — the man who killed him was..." {n}The young woman's shoulders continue to shake a little, but she makes no more sounds.{/n}
  - After: "Y-yes... but his killer was the traitor..." {n}She trembles.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As you look up at the altar, the ringing in your ears intensifies for a moment. Rupturing your eardrums, the altar roars, threatening, promising to take thousands more with it. But you are deaf to its pitiful threats.{/n}
  - After: {n}The altar roars, threatening thousands. You ignore it.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As you lean over the shards, the ringing in your ears intensifies for a moment. A quiet voice promises you strength and power, asks you to save it from oblivion, and you graciously fulfil its request. Once the largest of the shards is in your hands, it falls silent, pacified.{/n}
  - After: {n}A voice begs, promising power. You take the largest shard; it quiets.{/n}
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "Of course, this game involved one key piece. The embodiment of freedom of choice — my magnificent Altar. So much accumulated potential from years of experimentation. It is damaged, but it still beckons, waiting to be used..." {n}Ruoldo looks you in the eye with a caustic smile.{/n} "I advise you to keep it safe — who knows how many thousands of lives it will claim if something happens to it, unleashing all that power?"
  - After: "My damaged Altar still holds great power." {n}He smirks.{/n} "Keep it safe, or thousands may die."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The strange ringing stops, leaving behind an unpleasant echo in your ears — your head must still be suffering from the effects of moving between bodies.{/n}
  - After: {n}The ringing fades: body-swap aftereffects.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta closes her eyes and utters a prayer:{/n} "Emperor, have mercy on the unfortunate souls who found themselves trapped in the grasp of the Archenemy. Have mercy, for they knew nothing and had nowhere to go..."
  - After: {n}Argenta prays:{/n} "Emperor, have mercy on these unknowing souls."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "To cut the thread of an entire world but prevent the spread of corruption is to please the Undying Emperor. The Domin's will be done, and may Thassera accept its sacred death."
  - After: "A world's death to halt corruption pleases the Emperor. May Thassera accept it."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Elantach, your desire to understand rather than destroy out of fear does your credit, but... take heed: the minds of mon-keigh are fragile and ill-equipped to withstand something with such a strong connection to the veil."
  - After: "Elantach, curiosity is admirable, but mon-keigh minds can't withstand the veil."
- **Maive**
  - Before: {n}A timid prayer falls from Maive's lips:{/n} "Emperor on the Golden Throne, my whole life I was mistaken in my ways of honouring You, but now I pray to You... not for my own soul, but for his..."
  - After: {n}Maive prays:{/n} "Emperor, I pray for his soul, not mine..."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Thank you, Rogue Trader. This is the right choice."
  - After: "Thank you. The right choice."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}The Proctor swiftly kills the young woman before she is able to comprehend what you said. She sinks to the floor like a broken doll. Solomorne looks away, not resting his gaze on her even for a moment.{/n}
  - After: {n}Solomorne kills her instantly and looks away.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Ruoldo, you have committed unthinkable heresy, and I refuse to acknowledge you as a human being or read your verdict as befitting a criminal. You are a stain on Thassera's history, and it is time—" {n}You point your weapon and put the governor to death right as Solomorne finishes speaking:{/n} "—to wipe you from it."
  - After: "Ruoldo, you're a stain on Thassera. Time—" {n}You kill him as Solomorne finishes:{/n} "—to wipe you away."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ruoldo's eyes widen with terror. Drops of sweat run down his pathetically shaking chin. You could drink his fear and despair like rich wine. A moment later, blood gushes from the governor's absurdly gaping mouth, gurgling and bubbling as it splashes onto the stone... Far at the back of your mind's velvety darkness, a voice cackles briefly. It is pleased. It is sated.{/n}
  - After: {n}You savour Ruoldo's terror as he bleeds out. A sated voice cackles in your mind.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne looks at you intently.{/n} "An... interesting verdict, Rogue Trader. Nevertheless, the criminal has been punished, and that is all that matters now."
  - After: {n}Solomorne stares.{/n} "Interesting verdict. Still, justice is done."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I will readily admit that the lack of speech in servitors is more of a disadvantage than a plus. However, if the Rogue Trader so bids, I can certainly leave her vocal cords intact or even make some improvements to them during the servitorisation process."
  - After: "Mute servitors are a drawback. I can keep her voice, if the Rogue Trader wishes."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Your latest thesis perfectly explains why your attempts to communicate with the laity are so woefully ineffective, colleague."
  - After: "That explains your poor rapport with the laity, colleague."
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "A governor attracts too much attention, and I wanted my hands to stay untied. So, I offered my court fool a fair bargain: he would become me — ruling the planet, living the good life, getting whatever he wanted — while I would be out there, flying toward the stars. We traded faces, clothes, and lives. And because I had gotten the local nobles into the habit of sewing other people's mugs on their heads, the switch went unnoticed."
  - After: "A governor draws attention. So my fool became me while I fled. Here, nobles wear others' faces; no one noticed."
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "But the switch was only the first part of the deal. Naturally, I didn't mention the second part: the removal of witnesses. If someone is going to turn against you the moment there's a knife at his beloved sister's throat, you can't afford to keep him alive." {n}Ruoldo casts a hateful glance in Maive's direction.{/n}
  - After: "Part two: kill the witness. A man who'd break for his sister can't live." {n}He glares at Maive.{/n}
