  - After: "Then, the shortest Hunt ever! Straight to the finale!"
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: {n}Ruoldo waves a hand at Maive:{/n} "Be a darling and tell our guest about our amusements. I am a little... exhausted."
  - After: {n}Ruoldo waves at Maive:{/n} "Explain, darling. I'm exhausted."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Down, Garra! Bad beast, very bad! I apologise, Your Celestial Highness. How is your Impostor Hunt going?"
  - After: "Down, Garra! Apologies. How goes your Impostor Hunt?"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Did you just admit that there is masquerading rabble among the Thasserian nobles? Illiterate, with no idea how to collect tithes or... By the Throne, that actually explains so much." {n}The Proctor scoffs and glances at the enthusiastic guests.{/n} "Go ahead, Governor. Commence your charade. The sooner we start, the sooner we finish."
  - After: "Rabble posing as nobles? That explains the tithes." {n}He scoffs.{/n} "Start, Governor."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: {n}The governor lets out an audible gulp.{/n} "It shall be done, Master Judicator."
  - After: {n}He gulps.{/n} "Yes, Master Judicator."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "If I can amuse the esteemed judicator with conversation, I will be only too glad to..."
  - After: "I'd be glad to amuse the judicator..."
- **Maive**
  - Before: "Perhaps you should stay here, my lord?" {n}Maive's gaze is full of genuine concern.{/n}
  - After: "Stay here, my lord?" {n}Maive looks concerned.{/n}
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "I feel you may be right, Maive. I will be waiting here, surrounded by savoury dishes and plentiful amasec. Have a fruitful hunt, Your Celestial Highness!"
  - After: "Yes, Maive. I'll wait with the food. Happy hunting!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "But of course. I have always wanted to try my hand at casual small talk." {n}Solomorne folds his arms imperiously over his chest, somehow becoming even taller in stature and broader in the shoulders.{/n} "Tell me about the laceraxes, Governor. Such fascinating creatures — where did you get them from?"
  - After: "Small talk. Novel." {n}Solomorne looms.{/n} "Where are the laceraxes from?"
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "Oh, yes! The famous Idexian pearls of revelation. I often use them myself to keep my mind receptive to new ideas."
  - After: "Ah, Idexian pearls of revelation! I use them too."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "Since laceraxes are used for entertainment, they do not last long on Thassera, and they are brought in batches, hence the 'long ago.' Honestly, beasts from faraway worlds are not that interesting a topic of conversation. Let us talk about something else, shall we?"
  - After: "They die fast here, so they come in batches. Dull topic. Something else?"
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "Ehm, I think they were the red robes who arrived to celebrate the ascendance of a new governor. That's me." {n}Ruoldo's wistful gaze follows a shrimperius fleeing the table.{/n}
  - After: "The red robes came to celebrate a new governor. Me." {n}He watches a shrimperius flee.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Indeed. The Tech-Priests are famous for having many vocations outside of pursuing technology and discovering new knowledge. Like music, and visits of courtesy..."
  - After: "Indeed. Tech-Priests love music and courtesy visits..."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "Marvellous! As soon as you are done with your search, I will be..." {n}The governor attempts to rise from the table, but gravity proves to be his superior.{/n}
  - After: "Marvellous! When you're done, I'll..." {n}Gravity keeps him seated.{/n}
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: {n}The governor throws up his hands.{/n} "Can they? And I was sure they were a common beastie! I might have embarrassed myself there, but I would be glad to talk about something else."
  - After: {n}He throws up his hands.{/n} "Really? I thought them common! Something else?"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Do not judge me harshly. I am just trying to get into the festive mood as best I can. We can certainly change the subject. I would like to note that I find your youth-extending face transplant procedure amazing. Does Thassera possess any other unique knowledge or items brought over from your homeworld? What is that world called, by the way?"
  - After: "Just festive. Your face transplants are amazing. Anything else from your homeworld? Its name?"
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "They are not exactly Idexian garments, but who cares? Just say the word, and the hold of your celestial vessel will soon be bursting with Thasserian vestments. After the celebration, of course."
  - After: "Not Idexian, but say the word and your hold will burst with vestments."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "I... do not know? I would rather tell you about things I am much better acquainted with, like Thasserian amasec, for example."
  - After: "I... don't know? Let me tell you about Thasserian amasec."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: {n}The governor takes a big sip from his cup.{/n} "I am a bit tipsy, so I cannot help it! On a day like today, it would be criminal not to toast such important guests!"
  - After: {n}He sips.{/n} "I'm tipsy! Criminal not to toast such guests!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne leans over to you:{/n} "Rogue Trader, once you've had your fill of the governor, let me ask him a few questions."
  - After: {n}Solomorne leans in:{/n} "When you're done, let me question him."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "Ah, my native Idesk... Idex. Unfortunately, I have not introduced much from it beyond the art of changing faces. But perhaps the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} has taken a liking to some of Thassera's original creations?"
  - After: "My native Idesk... Idex. I brought only face-changing. Like anything of Thassera's, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}?"
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "Your Celestial Highness must have been listening to a lot of gossip. Who cares where the rabble goes afterward? However, I can assure you that the victors are often sent into my personal service. We call it the Highest Favour, and today, it will be up to you to choose whom it should be bestowed upon!"
  - After: "Gossip! Victors enter my service — the Highest Favour. Today you choose!"
- **Maive**
  - Before: "By the way they talk, by their lack of restraint — the unfamiliar delicacies overwhelm them so much that they lose control. Impostors are often scared of the responsibility that has fallen on their weak shoulders, and they try to stay close to the real nobles and imitate their rarefied manners. During the hunt, it is most worthwhile to pay attention to separate groups where conversation has already started — a frightened impostor will probably try to hide behind other people's backs... That's all I know, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."
  - After: "They lose restraint over strange delicacies. Scared ones cling to real nobles and hide in groups already talking. That's all, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The governor is dragging out his words, as if he is not entirely sure of them himself — or is not telling you something.{/n}
  - After: {n}He drags his words, unsure or hiding something.{/n}
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "What?" {n}A shrimperius wriggles free of the governor's fork and drops into his goblet.{/n} "Yes, it was foreigners who delivered the mechanical musicians... I'm sure I have not mentioned them yet..."
  - After: "What?" {n}A shrimperius lands in his goblet.{/n} "Yes, foreigners brought the musicians..."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: {n}The man's face becomes stretched to the limit on its fastenings, signalling deep offence.{/n} "My Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}! I ask that you do not insult me so! I may not be used to having such lofty conversations, but believe me: I am definitely the governor of Thassera!"
  - After: {n}His face strains on its fastenings.{/n} "My Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}! I am the governor of Thassera!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Thank you for the conversation, Governor. I have learned everything I wanted to know."
  - After: "Thank you, Governor. That's all."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I would never question your title, Governor." {n}Solomorne gives you a long look.{/n} "And the Rogue Trader hardly wishes to offend you either."
  - After: "I'd never question your title." {n}He eyes you.{/n} "Nor would the Rogue Trader."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The governor's voice is unsteady. He seems to be already well in his cups.{/n}
  - After: {n}He's well in his cups.{/n}
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: {n}With a distracted smile in the direction of his orchestra, the governor adds as if in passing:{/n} "Music... It lifts the spirit, improves digestion, and allows one to refresh oneself between courses by having a nice dance with a gallant partner." {n}He casts an intent look at Solomorne standing beside you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eyeing the orchestra:{/n} "A dance between courses aids digestion..." {n}He looks at Solomorne.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "It would be my honour." {n}Solomorne's face is an impenetrable glower. He takes your hand, his palm firm and covered with calluses from his weapon grip.{/n}
  - After: "My honour." {n}Glowering, he takes your hand.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne is clearly trying to move to the beat of the music but meeting with little success — his stiff movements make him look like a broken servitor. His hold on you is delicate, as if you were a fragile vase, but there is no thrill of passion in his touch. He avoids meeting your eye, instead looking off to the side, monitoring the assembled guests. During the next step, he treads heavily and very painfully on your foot.{/n}
  - After: {n}Solomorne dances like a broken servitor, eyes on the guests, then stomps your foot.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Scowling even more, Solomorne sullenly mutters,{/n} "I apologise."
  - After: {n}Solomorne mutters,{/n} "I apologise."
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: "I recommend you try the fried alcedont, whose horns were still goring my hunters just the other day. And here, we have some five-tailed shrimperiuses in stewed black-eye sauce. These fellows need to be eaten quickly, before they scurry off the plate! As for the side dishes, you simply must have a taste of these crispy blaberid shells seasoned with blue glut. This spice scorches your tongue, but follow it with some amasec, and it will feel like the waters of life itself!"
  - After: "Try the alcedont, shrimperiuses — eat them before they flee! — and blaberid shells with blue glut. Chase it with amasec!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I feel like these people have scopes instead of eyes. And you and I are a paired target."
  - After: "They have scopes for eyes. We're a paired target."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}You manage to sweep Solomorne along on your sudden charge, his movements becoming more graceful, your eyes meeting his... until a new jolt of pain stabs through your other foot.{/n}
  - After: {n}Briefly graceful, then he stomps your other foot.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}The music fades, and Solomorne lays his hand on his weapon with obvious relief, his movements immediately regaining their predatory fluidity.{/n}
  - After: {n}The music ends; relieved, he grips his weapon.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Analysing... This brand is the property of the Idex-Venteris food factory. It was used to mark the meat of high-protein specimens of the planet's fauna. The inscription in proto-Gothic translates to: 'grox on corpse-feed.'"
  - After: "Analysing... An Idex-Venteris meat brand. It reads: 'grox on corpse-feed.'"
- **Jae**
  - Before: {n}Jae huffs gloomily.{/n} "A revelation like that puts a whole new perspective on this quaint little game."
  - After: {n}Jae huffs.{/n} "That changes this quaint game."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai cocks his head to one side, looking at Maive in bewilderment.{/n} "You really are a primitive species if your pretenders are so easy to expose."
  - After: {n}Marazhai eyes Maive.{/n} "Primitive, if pretenders are this easy to spot."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Abominations like you will never see the true light of righteous faith. We are the children of the God-Emperor, and you are a festering wound on the body of the galaxy whose fall is only a matter of time."
  - After: "Abomination. You are a festering wound on the galaxy, and your fall is coming."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "You see a beast devoid of free will as an example to follow? All I see is a broken spirit bound in the chains of cruelty."
  - After: "Your ideal is a broken spirit in chains?"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "If your blade does not obey your hand, it may one day pierce your throat." {n}Kibellah's words cause the governor to shudder.{/n}
  - After: "A disobedient blade may pierce your throat." {n}The governor shudders.{/n}
- **Governor Ruoldo**
  - Before: {n}The governor shakes his head sadly.{/n} "Oh, what a shame! But perhaps you would at least—"
  - After: {n}He sighs.{/n} "A shame! Perhaps—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The tables are buckling under the spread of steaming hot dishes, oozing with grease and exuding tantalisingly spicy aromas. Quite the challenge for an uninitiated stomach, but {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}you{/d} have taken part in feasts far grander than this.{/n}
  - After: {n}Greasy, spicy dishes; {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}you{/d} know grander feasts.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Would you rather I question you instead of the Rogue Trader? Be advised, I am a man of action, not words."
  - After: "Shall I question you instead? I act."

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/FeudalWorld/FW_HideAndSeekAftermath/FW_HideAndSeekAftermath_dialogue

- **Player**

- **Player**
  - Before: "When my ship carries me between the stars, cutting through the endless void, I ask myself what the new day might bring. Well, my wish is to be off this planet as soon as possible. The end."

  - Before: "However, while most of us were indulging — I would even say wallowing — in the thrill of the Impostor Hunt, {mf|His|Her} Celestial Highness turned {mf|his|her} lofty thoughts away from these motley diversions and toward duty. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cyber-laceraxes' lumens glow blood red. Before the condemned can even scream, the beasts pounce on their prey with hungry snarls.{/n}
  - After: {n}The laceraxes' lumens flare red. They pounce.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You hear venomous laughter from among the crowd and recognise Bluff's voice. As the square drowns in the clamour and applause of gawkers who were spectating the game, you look around for the court fool but cannot spot him anywhere.{/n}

Still, knowing their penchant for such games, I do suspect they tried to make their guesses anyway — quietly, among themselves."

  - After: "I need to look around."

  - After: "I obey, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."

He keeps muttering these awful rhymes about blood and fate. And it's like he's waiting for something, but I just can't understand what."

- **Solomorne**

  - After: "The court fool is your brother?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My brother's, my {mf|lord|lady}. I had a feeling he wasn't acting himself lately. If I'd known he had fallen in with scoundrels, I would have found them and strangled them with my own hands!"
  - After: "My brother's, my {mf|lord|lady}. If scoundrels misled him, I'll strangle them!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Are you ready, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}?"
  - After: "Ready, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}No sooner have you stepped into the elevator than a short metallic clang comes from somewhere above you...{/n}
  - After: {n}Metal clangs above...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Lying nearby is the lifeless body of lacerax "Number 4," which you released from its cage. Its fur is clumped and sticky with blood, its vicious eyes glazed over. Giving its own life to protect another was a stunningly human act for a beast.{/n}

  - After: "A kind side, my lord judicator?" {n}Maive smiles, unafraid.{/n}

Or maybe..." {n}Solomorne looks pensive as he straightens Glaito's collar.{/n} "Maybe it was a fine animal that was unlucky enough to have bad masters. This is the first creature I've met on Thassera that has been worthy of respect."

  - After: {n}He glances at her.{/n} "Or I hate people."

  - After: "So confused!" {n}She stares at the corpse.{/n} "I thought— No."

  - After: "I thought Daen, my brother, called me. But he wasn't there."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You think back to Ruoldo's last moments. It is hard to tell for certain, but it really did seem as though his voice had changed, that it sounded younger and less strained — as if he had cast off a mask.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ruoldo's dying voice sounded younger, unmasked.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Maive puts a handkercher to her mouth and grows pale, most likely recalling the grotesque sight of the governor's violent demise.{/n}
  - After: {n}Maive pales, recalling the gore.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The young woman shuts her eyes tightly and begins to whisper a silent prayer.{/n}
  - After: {n}She prays silently.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}At his master's command, Glaito directs his scan rays at the dead man's severed hand, which has somehow avoided being reduced to shreds along with the rest of the body. The cyber-mastiff's augmetics emit a warning signal.{/n}
  - After: {n}Glaito scans the severed hand. A warning sounds.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Ruoldo was branded too. He couldn't have known, or else he would not have doomed himself like that. I assume this is likewise the work of that buffoon — the only question is whether he was acting of his own accord or at the behest of someone more important."
  - After: "Ruoldo was branded unknowingly. The buffoon — alone, or for someone higher?"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "That is what any cornered heretic would swear to try to save their life."
  - After: "Any cornered heretic says that."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If only I knew, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}. If only I knew..." {n}Maive's glistening eyes are full of shock.{/n}
  - After: "If only I knew, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}..." {n}Shocked.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "O God-Emperor!" {n}Maive presses her hands to her chest in the sign of the Aquila. Her lips whisper a prayer:{/n} "Forgive and protect his soul! Forgive and protect..."
  - After: "O God-Emperor!" {n}Maive prays:{/n} "Protect his soul!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes, my lord." {n}Maive lowers her eyes.{/n} "We are lower nobility, and it is a high honour to be the governor's own court entertainer..."
  - After: "Yes, my lord." {n}She looks down.{/n} "A high honour for lower nobility..."

  - After: "My dear, weren't you watching the Rogue Trader?"

  - Before: {n}Heinrix's lip curls as he looks at you.{/n} "Warp emanations... strong ones at that. Sorcery at work... before our very eyes." {n}His fingers tighten on his weapon.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix sneers.{/n} "Strong warp. Sorcery." {n}He grips his weapon.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Isn't that the meek little lady-in-waiting that was assigned to my shereen? Looks like she's lost the Lord Captain too... and her sanity to boot."
  - After: "My shereen's lady-in-waiting? Lost her, and her sanity."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard scowls.{/n} "You could have memorised a few facts from the Lord Captain's biography... Are we to play guessing games now?"
  - After: {n}Abelard scowls.{/n} "Anyone could memorise that. Guessing games?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix frowns.{/n} "She is not lying about the sorcery. There is a strange current of warp energy flowing from her, leading somewhere... up there."
  - After: {n}Heinrix frowns.{/n} "Real sorcery. Its warp current leads... up there."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Do not weep, child. I will cut your thread quickly and painlessly before your soul succumbs to corruption."
  - After: "Do not weep, child. I will end you before corruption does."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Not the most skilful attempt, little mouse. Our shereen would have come up with something better."
  - After: "Clumsy, little mouse. Our shereen would lie better."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "This statement... is potentially true. Cyber-mastiff protocols are difficult to breach and override, much less..." {n}Pasqal casts a gloomy look at his surroundings.{/n} "In a primitive culture such as this."
  - After: "Potentially true. Mastiff protocols resist override..." {n}Pasqal glances around.{/n} "Especially here."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "The evidence is difficult to argue with... unless the Arbitrator was forced somehow."
  - After: "Hard to argue... unless the Arbitrator was forced."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "If anything could cause Solomorne to be parted from his faithful dog, it would be a threat to the Lord Captain..."
  - After: "Only a threat to the Lord Captain would part Solomorne from his dog."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The vox in your companion's hand is speaking in your own voice:{/n} "There is no need for concern! The Proctor and I are in the middle of examining the documents... together with the governor. I will be back as soon as we are done here..." {n}There is a loud click, indicating that the other side has cut the connection.{/n}
  - After: {n}The vox, in your voice:{/n} "No concern! The Proctor, governor and I are reviewing documents. Back soon." {n}Click.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As soon as you approach, everyone's attention shifts to you. For now, their reaction feels closer to pent-up irritation than outright hostility.{/n}
  - After: {n}Everyone turns, irritated.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your pompous declaration silences the group momentarily and they stare at you in utter bewilderment. Someone lets out an awkward chuckle.{/n}
  - After: {n}Stunned silence. An awkward chuckle.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your words are greeted with looks of bewilderment. Even the sight of Glaito standing at your side seems only to raise more questions.{/n}
  - After: {n}Bewilderment. Even Glaito raises questions.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}They take no notice of you at first. But after a moment, one by one, they turn their gazes to you. Silence falls over the street.{/n}
  - After: {n}They turn to you. Silence.{/n}
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Feeble worms! Do you feel brave, testing my patience so? Present the Aett-Vater! Go on, make {rt_mf|him|her} come down here — it is a short enough trip!" {n}Ulfar's voice is like a thunderclap, the walls themselves seeming to shake with its mighty echo.{/n}
  - After: "Worms! Make {rt_mf|him|her}, the Aett-Vater, come down!" {n}Ulfar's voice shakes the walls.{/n}
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Strange little bird! Everyone wishes to wear the Aett-Vater's mantle, but few could bear its weight. Go and tell your tales elsewhere."
  - After: "Strange bird! Few can bear the Aett-Vater's mantle. Begone."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Activating standby mode." {n}Pasqal emits a quiet hum as he begins his binharic prayer.{/n}
  - After: "Activating standby mode." {n}Pasqal hums.{/n}
- **Voidsman-at-Arms**
  - Before: {n}You see your trusted shuttle pilot — it seems he went looking for his Lord Captain when you disappeared. You hear a voice coming out of the vox in his hand — your own voice, telling the pilot that everything is in order and that you will return to the shuttle once you are done examining the tithe documents. Judging by his furrowed brows, the pilot has some reservations about following the orders he is receiving.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your pilot, searching for you. His vox, in your voice, says you'll return after the tithe documents. He frowns.{/n}
- **Voidsman-at-Arms**
  - Before: {n}The pilot stares at you in bewilderment as he tries to fathom how a local stranger knows his name, but his confusion only lasts a moment. With a nod of grim determination, he grabs you by the elbow and hurries down the street with you toward the shuttle.{/n}
  - After: {n}Surprised, the pilot hurries you to the shuttle.{/n}
- **Voidsman-at-Arms**
  - Before: {n}The pilot gapes at the madwoman before him, but the mention of the Rogue Trader dynasty shakes him out of his bafflement. He unceremoniously pulls you to your feet, grabs your elbow, and hurries down the street with you to where the shuttle is waiting.{/n}
  - After: {n}The pilot gapes, then hauls you up and hurries you to the shuttle.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "An extremely atypical presentation for the Rogue Trader, dearest colleague." {n}Nuncius, hovering nearby, expresses his silent agreement.{/n} "The cadence of the voice differs from the norm, and such indecision is uncharacteristic of {rt_mf|his|her} personality... Psychosis? A curious hypothesis."
  - After: "Atypical, colleague." {n}Nuncius agrees.{/n} "Odd cadence, unlike {rt_mf|his|her} decisiveness... Psychosis?"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Let me take a closer look." {n}Eogunn floats over to you, his hulking form bristling with manipulators as he looms overhead.{/n} "Hmm... complex polytrauma... possibly cardiogenic shock... Hysterical twilight state or oneiroid delirium? Or something truly inconceivable? Quite right, Nuncius, a cursory examination is not enough!"
  - After: "Let me look." {n}Eogunn looms.{/n} "Polytrauma... shock... delirium? Quite right, Nuncius, I need a closer look!"

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/FeudalWorld/FW_Lizzy/FW_Lizzy_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Let's continue our walk."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Noticing your gaze, Maive turns to you.{/n} "My Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}..." {n}She hesitates before continuing.{/n} "They say you are the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g}'s anointed. Have you... truly seen Him?"
  - After: {n}Maive turns.{/n} "Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}..." {n}She hesitates.{/n} "Have you seen the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g}?"

  - Before: "My Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}? Did you want to ask me something?"
  - After: "My Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}? A question?"

  - After: "He gave me a thassertium necklace just before you came. Strange. And he knows me too well now."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Forgive me, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}... Did you wish to ask me something?"
  - After: "Forgive me, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}... A question?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What would you like me to do, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}? I was taught how to dance and sing..."
  - After: "What would you like, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}? I can dance and sing..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A blush erupts on Maive's cheeks.{/n} "Thank you, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}! For me, there is no reward greater than your praise!"
  - After: {n}Maive blushes.{/n} "Your praise is my greatest reward, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}!"
- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Maive's eyes are like two moons, shining with wonder and curiosity. She bites her lip in an obvious attempt to restrain herself and not pepper you with more questions.{/n} "Pardon me. Did you... wish to ask me something?"

- **(conversation owner)**

With great care, she sings a passage from some local hymn about how the Emperor, who holds the Key to all Destinies, locked the heavens against invisible monsters and enemies of Humanity. Her voice, though trembling with nerves, is surprisingly pleasant to listen to.{/n}

  - Before: "Let's give it a try!" {n}Maive smiles cheerfully.{/n} "The movements are simple. Watch: you put this foot here, and you stretch your arms out like this..."

  - After: {n}Maive bites her lip.{/n} "Forgive me, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."

  - Before: "It is an honour to entertain the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."
  - After: "An honour to entertain the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."

  - Before: {n}When she comes to a stop before you in a final curtsy, her cheeks are flushed.{/n} "I hope this humble dance was worthy of your eyes, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}!"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "He is... the best among all the court servants." {n}Maive looks down, but you catch the fear in her eyes.{/n} "He always knew how to make the noble lords laugh. But at first, Daen's jokes were just funny pranks and puns. Those were wonderful, almost impossible times..."

My own brother..." {n}Having said all this, she freezes in fear, turning white as a sheet.{/n} "Apologies for my lack of restraint..."

- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "Court has stories, but you've better things to do, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."
- **(conversation owner)**

He Himself sits at the very top of the Great Tower of Humankind, from there gazing out over the worlds and stars of His domain. He sees all, knows all, and a bloody tear rolls down His cheek when He reads our shameful thoughts and deeds in the annals of our lives."
  - After: "Preacher Antiochus says so, my {mf|lord|lady}. He sits atop the Great Tower of Humankind, weeping blood at our sins."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "'The Story of Humanity's Deliverance From Darkness.' It is sung once a moonlife as a reminder of the great deed of the God-Emperor, who used the Key to all Destinies to lock the world away from wicked things. He walled Himself up in the Great Tower of Humankind along with all the people. He could have ascended to the stars, but He chose to stay, for our sake, though we are unworthy. We must remember this deed."
  - After: "'Humanity's Deliverance From Darkness.' The God-Emperor used the Key to all Destinies to lock out evil, staying with us in the Great Tower of Humankind."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh, how embarrassing! My Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}, I apologise for offending your ears!" {n}Cheeks burning with shame, Maive casts her eyes down.{/n}
  - After: "Forgive me, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}!" {n}Maive blushes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is my pleasure to serve the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."
  - After: "My pleasure to serve the Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But those who strive, who do not let the seed of evil into their hearts, He will reward with a new destiny, a new life, higher and better than the one before — with a turn of His Key, he unlocks the dungeon of their souls. I live in hope that, one day, He will come to my door." {n}Maive's smile is one of sad resignation.{/n}
  - After: "The virtuous He rewards with a better destiny. I hope He comes for me." {n}A sad smile.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In the time of darkness, the God-Emperor walled up the Tower of Humankind against fiends and monsters to keep it safe from evil. But evil had already planted its seed in thousands upon thousands of human souls. He locked them in the dungeon of the Tower, so that they might first eradicate the evil in their thoughts. All our lives, we atone for our transgression against the God-Emperor. And after death, we return to His judgement. But that is our burden to bear, my {mf|lord|lady}. When I see you and realise that before me stands His anointed, one blessed by His godly hand — there is no one happier than I!"
  - After: "The God-Emperor walled the Tower against monsters and jailed evil-tainted souls in its dungeon. We atone for life. But seeing His anointed, my {mf|lord|lady}, I'm overjoyed!"

  - Before: {n}Solomorne casts a quick glance around, as if looking for someone, and then nods at you confidently.{/n}
  - After: {n}Solomorne glances around, then nods.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "How fascinating. And what are you going to do to get a better destiny?"
  - After: "Fascinating. How will you earn a better destiny?"

  - After: "The governor never favoured you before? And escorting the Rogue Trader?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Maive blinks in astonishment.{/n} "That is so, my lord judicator. I still wonder why the God-Emperor saw fit to bestow such a tremendous honour upon me."
  - After: {n}Maive blinks.{/n} "True, my lord judicator. Why me, I wonder."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}For a brief moment, a deep wrinkle cuts across Solomorne's forehead.{/n} "So, your brother is not his usual self. This world is a tangled web indeed."
  - After: {n}Solomorne frowns.{/n} "Her brother changed too. A tangled web."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You speak the words that have sounded countless times from {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Ministorum}your lips{/d}, echoing off the walls of cathedrals, and Maive listens in fright and awe.{/n} "Could it really be true? There is no Tower, and all people's destinies are preordained? Forgive me, my {mf|lord|lady} — if you say so, then it is the truth. I will relearn how to pray and believe, I swear!"
  - After: {n}You preach {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Ministorum}the Creed{/d}.{/n} "No Tower? Then I'll relearn faith, my {mf|lord|lady}!"
- **Argenta**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes, my {mf|lord|lady}." {n}Maive throws a despairing glance at you, but dutifully bends down and licks the clods of mud from the soles and heels of your shoes, crawling at your feet until her lavish hem is in tatters. Now your shoes shine like new. Wiping her muddied lips with her sleeve, Maive slowly rises to her feet, staring dully ahead.{/n} "How else may I serve you, my {mf|lord|lady}?"
  - After: "Yes, my {mf|lord|lady}." {n}Despairing, Maive licks your shoes clean.{/n} "What else, my {mf|lord|lady}?"
- **Kibellah**

  - After: "Begging blessings, not trials, insults the Undying One."
- **Idira**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Though the Thasserians honour the God-Emperor, their interpretation of the Creed verges on heresy. Serving Him is already the reward, and only the desire to serve longer and with greater zeal is worthy of pursuit.{/n}
  - After: {n}Thasserian belief verges on heresy: serving Him should itself be the reward.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Indeed, the saying holds: as many the worlds, so many the paths of faith in the God-Emperor. Thus, it is no surprise that Thasserian doctrine is cast in an almost poetic form.{/n}
  - After: {n}Many worlds, many faiths. Thassera's is poetic.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I dare not complain, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}. Lesser nobles such as myself sometimes receive punishment for angering our lords, but that is good, in a way.   - After: "Punishment cleanses me to serve the God-Emperor, Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}." {n}She makes the Aquila.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "My {mf|lord|lady}? Oh..." {n}Maive goes quiet.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That is excellent, my {mf|lord|lady}!"
  - After: "Excellent, my {mf|lord|lady}!"

I only heard about the attack after it had already begun, and the elevator might as well not have been moving at all, it was so slow..."

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/FeudalWorld/FW_NewBody/FW_NewBody_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your mind is a loose shard, cast out into nothing, screaming in the voices of thousands of lives... Are they your lives? Or do they belong to another? The blood cracks branch out, biting into every scrap of disjointed thought, ravaging, hungering to shatter what little of your own self remains. A cry gurgles in the depths: a plea to make the torment stop and let you dissolve in unconsciousness... But something has sunk its claws into you, keeping you in place, fusing you back together piece by piece. Methodically and tortuously, it continues to skewer the shreds of your identity onto the thread of existence in an attempt to outpace the all-consuming void.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your mind is a shard in the void, screaming with thousands of lives. Something holds you, stitching you back together.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You are wrenched suddenly out of oblivion by a blunt, merciless bite. You try to breathe and hear your own ragged wheeze. Sight gradually returns to you, and an angry horse's head emerges from the mist. You are back. You are alive.{/n}
  - After: {n}A bite wrenches you awake. An angry horse looms. You are alive.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You try to shove the head away from you, but your hand veers off. Your palms feel nothing, because the skin on them is just some unwieldy meat cover forcibly pulled onto your frame. Your fingers curl up of their own accord.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your hand veers off. The skin feels like a foreign meat cover.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your shout is as thin as a death cry and unbearably shrill. Still, it is just strong enough to make the creature stop trying to bite you and back off.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your shrill shout drives the creature back.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Slowly, your eyes begin to put together a sordid image: everything around you is brown and disgusting. Hay, wood, blood, dirt... horse: the trapdoor you jumped down has led you to a stable.{/n}
  - After: {n}Hay, blood, dirt, horse: the trapdoor led to a stable.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You sway, as if from sickness, all your limbs feeling impossibly fragile. Scrawny legs, frail arms — these do not belong to you. This is a costume, and it is not yours: it does not fit your status, it is the wrong size, and it still carries greasy traces of its former owner inside. You are overcome with the urge to tear off your flesh and throw it away like a worn glove.{/n}
  - After: {n}You sway. These frail limbs aren't yours: an ill-fitting costume. You want to tear the flesh off.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You gather your will and repress the desire to peel all the skin off. The mad impulse recedes. The memories that linger in this body may yet prove useful.{/n}
  - After: {n}You repress the urge. This body's memories may prove useful.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your hand finds something on your chest, something so cold it burns your fingers. For a moment, you think that it is the real you — the shard of your will lost in the flow — but it turns out to be nothing more than a thassertium necklace.{/n}
  - After: {n}Something icy on your chest: not your lost self, just a thassertium necklace.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Memories that are not your own tear into your mind, replacing your thoughts. It occurs to you that someone else used to scare all the monsters away — a big brother, so funny and always smiling. With some effort, you manage to force his gentle face out of your head.{/n}
  - After: {n}Alien memories: a smiling big brother who scared monsters away. You push him out.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A stable is a place for peasants, not sovereigns. But, somehow, your body remembers the scents of poverty. Your consciousness expands heavily, like sick lungs. You remember a large basket, bundles of food clutched in your hands, and the grateful smiles of the hungry.{/n}
  - After: {n}This body knows poverty: a food basket, the grateful smiles of the hungry.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As you look at it, the crystal stares back at you with its still blue eye. The fool's wrinkled face suddenly emerges from the reflection, and his gloating voice seems to hang at the edge of your awareness. This body remembers pain and electrified air... Something bad.{/n}
  - After: {n}The crystal's blue eye shows the fool's gloating face. This body remembers pain and electrified air.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}To complete the picture, you have no choice but to look into a nearby water trough at your reflection. You see familiar features: some unnatural force has dragged you out of your body and into that of Maive, Ruoldo's lady-in-waiting. Now that you have spent some time in this stable, you feel a little more accustomed to your new limbs. But where is your own mortal shell?{/n}
  - After: {n}A water trough shows your reflection: you are in the body of Maive, Ruoldo's lady-in-waiting. But where is your own body?{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your muscles cramp in bitter agony — you could swear you hear the gnashing of bones and the wailing of stretched tendons. The reward for your suffering is a clumsy turn to one side, and then, your strength leaves you once more.{/n}
  - After: {n}Through cramping agony, you manage a clumsy roll.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You dig unfamiliar nails deep into thin skin, trying to scrape someone else's face off yourself. The pain in your cheeks has a sobering effect. You see blood on your fingers. This may not be your body, but it can still prove useful to you.{/n}
  - After: {n}You claw at this face. The pain sobers you. This body may still prove useful.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}This strange flesh obeys you reluctantly, as if receiving your commands with a delay. It takes all your grit to raise a dainty hand and place it on the horse's muzzle. The animal snorts and tosses the hand away with ease.{/n}
  - After: {n}You lift a sluggish hand to the horse's muzzle; it tosses it away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your memories of the last several minutes are incoherent and painful. The flash of sorcery, the leap into the unknown, Solomorne shouting something — he gave Glaito an order, but what order was it? Any attempt you make to process what happened only pulls you deeper into unconsciousness.{/n}
  - After: {n}Fragments: sorcery, a leap, Solomorne shouting an order to Glaito — what order? Thinking drags you under.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}iron will{/d} immediately rejects the shameful weakness, and you give yourself an order: to steady yourself and to probe the memories of the previous owner of this body.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}iron will{/d} rejects weakness. You probe this body's memories.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your attempt at twisting your body around only ends in a racking pain shooting through your back. The most you can achieve is a lurch upward accompanied by a piercing crunch somewhere in the spine.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pain shoots through your back; your spine crunches.{/n}

If only I could also taste the stardust from the soles of the Celestial {rt_mf|Lord|Lady}'s boots! You're so lucky, Maive!"
  - After: {n}They gasp.{/n} "Ruoldo's nothing to {rt_mf|him|her}! The Celestial {rt_mf|Lord|Lady}'s stardust! Lucky Maive!"

  - After: "Told you! {rt_mf|He|She}'s a Celestial {rt_mf|Lord|Lady}, the Emperor's anointed!"

  - Before: {n}The people recoil in fear and cast anxious glances about them. You make use of the confusion to successfully sneak away.{/n}

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/FeudalWorld/FW_Sculptor/FW_Sculptor_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not quite understand. Are you a psyker?"
  - After: "Are you a psyker?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The glorious deeds of my future."
  - After: "My future glories."
- **Player**
  - Before: "All that I am accomplishing in the present."
  - After: "My present deeds."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am here to look at the sculpture. What has my destiny got to do with it?"
  - After: "I came for the sculpture. Why my destiny?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What can you tell me about this material you are working with?"
  - After: "What's this material?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your hand augmetics are most impressive. Such implants are impossible to come by on a feudal world. Where are you from?"
  - After: "Fine augmetics, rare on a feudal world. Where are you from?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Did you capture the governor's destiny in sculpture too?"
  - After: "Did you sculpt the governor's destiny?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Solomorne, how would you prefer to see me portrayed?"
  - After: "Solomorne, how should I be portrayed?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "This is ludicrous! You do not decide my destiny. Nor do I need a monument."
  - After: "Ludicrous! You don't decide my destiny."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sculptor's mechanical hands crawl over the rough stone, their many-jointed metal fingers remaining in constant motion. Even now, you recognise your own features in the unfinished piece — it seems someone commissioned a statue of you the moment you set foot on the planet. The old man turns his wrinkled face to you, and you see crystals where his eyes should be.{/n} "Is my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} here to gaze upon {mf|his|her} destiny? Alas, my creation is not yet complete."
  - After: {n}A crystal-eyed sculptor carves your likeness.{/n} "My Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} comes to see {mf|his|her} destiny? It's unfinished."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "When I sculpt, Your Celestial Highness, I see people's destinies in the forms I create. The visions that come to me shape not only the stone, but the person's fate as well. Your image was indistinct when it appeared before me, and my work is not yet done. What do you wish to behold?"
  - After: "I sculpt destinies, Your Highness. Yours is unclear. What would you see?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "These musings on destinies and fates remind me of a heretical cult that has been plaguing the von Valancius domain of late... Your visions, sculptor, are whispers of the warp." {n}Heinrix glares ominously at the old man.{/n}
  - After: "Warp whispers, like the cult plaguing the von Valancius domain." {n}Heinrix glares.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have passed through the halls of the Black Ship. My Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady} may be certain that my creations bear no evil within them. Tell me, what do you wish to see shaped in stone?"
  - After: "I passed the Black Ship, my Celestial {mf|Lord|Lady}. What shall I shape?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sculptor's hands scuttle over the stone like huge metal spiders. Somehow, his sightless gaze perceives exactly those details of your appearance that you are proud of the most.{/n} "Your destiny will soon be complete, my {mf|lord|lady}. I will have it delivered to your celestial vessel."
  - After: {n}His hands capture your proudest features.{/n} "Soon done, my {mf|lord|lady}. I'll send it aboard."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sculptor's hands scuttle over the stone like huge metal spiders. Somehow, his sightless gaze envisions the exact version of you that you wish to see.{/n} "Your destiny will soon be complete, my {mf|lord|lady}. I will have it delivered to your starfaring vessel."
  - After: {n}His hands shape you as you wish to be.{/n} "Soon done, my {mf|lord|lady}. I'll send it aboard."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "As Your Celestial Highness desires. However, there is no escaping your fate." {n}The old man shrugs, his worn augmetics creaking.{/n}
  - After: "As you wish. Fate is inescapable." {n}He shrugs.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Ruoldo had my limbs replaced before he took me from my home planet. It was so long ago, I have since forgotten what my land is like to the touch."
  - After: "Lord Ruoldo gave me these limbs and took me from my long-forgotten homeworld."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, all that about the soul? That wasn't a metaphor, you know. This one channels his own mind through the stone and then sees what comes of it. You should be careful around this sorcerer — I don't like how my whispers have taken a fancy to him."
  - After: "Captain, he literally pours his mind into stone. Careful — my whispers like this sorcerer."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Hmm... he carves his works using the psyker abilities he is cursed with. An astonishingly frivolous application of warp powers."
  - After: "He sculpts with psyker powers. Frivolous use of the warp."

Such neglect often poses a serious threat to the person's life, and yet, the old man's skin looks relatively healthy in the spots where flesh and metal meet.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}This man appears to belong to a rare variety of psykers — biomancers capable of recovering even from otherwise deadly wounds and diseases.{/n}
  - After: {n}He's a biomancer, a psyker who heals even deadly wounds.{/n}

  - Before: {n}His mouth stretches into a cryptic smile.{/n} "I have made thousands of statues for Ruoldo, but Thassera's stone flesh can never seem to sate his great ambitions."
  - After: {n}He smiles.{/n} "Thousands of statues, yet Thassera's stone never sates Ruoldo."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The old sculptor once more turns his unseeing gaze to the patterns in the stone before him.{/n}
  - After: {n}He returns to the stone.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My lord governor calls me a foreteller and creator — others, a wicked {g|Encyclopedia:PsykerGlossary}sorcerer{/g}. But there is no cause for concern: my abilities are sanctioned, and I am pure before the Emperor's celestial eye." {n}He gestures at the tubes on the back of his head, as if to prove the truth of his words.{/n}
  - After: "Some call me a {g|Encyclopedia:PsykerGlossary}sorcerer{/g}. I'm sanctioned and pure." {n}He shows his head tubes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}There is no embellishment in the old man's words — he shares a special bond with his creations, one that {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}you can sense{/d} as clearly as any other breath of the warp.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A humble creator, the governor's first sculptor, Tavrisk, who has the honour of shaping the destinies of others but not his own." {n}Tavrisk the sculptor turns his head to you, but you see no pupils in his crystal ocular augmetics.{/n}
  - After: "Tavrisk, the governor's first sculptor. I shape every destiny but mine." {n}His eyes are crystal.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This is thassertium — a fascinating stone born from the bowels of this planet. Like any other kind, it bends and melts beneath the sculptor's tool, but for the sculpture to come to life in earnest, they must put their very soul into it." {n}One of his hands emerges from behind the statue and gently touches his head, seemingly of its own volition.{/n} "The soul, however, obtains calluses the more the sculptor works, and mine has long since become covered in scabs."
  - After: "Thassertium, local stone. It lives only if you pour your soul in." {n}He touches his head.{/n} "Mine's all scabs."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira clutches her head and wheezes:{/n} "Be wary when toying with destiny. What gives a boon now will come back to collect later. So may the opposite be true — to harvest sweet fruits in the future, one must first drink one's fill of bitter things. Watch your words!"
  - After: {n}Idira clutches her head.{/n} "Destiny's boons come due later. Watch your words!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The old man whispers without taking his eyes off the stone,{/n} "The sculpture is not quite ready yet."
  - After: {n}He whispers,{/n} "Not ready yet."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}That this old man has not yet rotted alive is an incredible stroke of luck.{/n}
  - After: {n}Lucky he hasn't rotted alive.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The blue veins of the statue flare faintly under your gaze. The stone undoubtedly possesses {g|Encyclopedia:PsyfocusGlossary}psy-focus{/g} properties, allowing the old man to concentrate warp energies in it and amplify them.{/n}
  - After: {n}The stone is a {g|Encyclopedia:PsyfocusGlossary}psy-focus{/g}, amplifying his warp power.{/n}
- **Solomorne**

  - After: {n}Solomorne frowns.{/n} "Exactly as you are." {n}He looks away.{/n} "I don't get art."

  - After: "And I was meant to die." {n}He raises his data-branded palm.{/n}
- **Bluff the Court Fool**

- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "Times are troubled, as you know. I want everything to go according to plan."
  - After: "Troubled times. I want it all to go to plan."
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "To serve the Imperium faithfully and honestly, why else? Our all-knowing Administratum benefits if the feudal throne is occupied by someone with an intelligence level higher than a grox's. A golden shove for all my diligent service on Idex. I packed my bags and came here to govern this backwater. What a joke..."
  - After: "The Administratum wanted someone smarter than a grox ruling here. My reward for Idex. A joke..."
- **Bluff the Court Fool**
  - Before: "Don't be ridiculous — I couldn't swallow a man whole even if I wanted to!" {n}Bluff throws up his arms in an exaggerated fashion.{/n}
  - After: "I couldn't swallow a man whole!" {n}He throws up his arms.{/n}

  - Before: {n}There is a {d|Encyclopedia:FW_ShotJesterDecision}gunshot wound{/d} in his shoulder surrounded by singed threads. His garish outfit is soaked with blood.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Bluff ignores the Arbitrator, his gaze fixed on you — more specifically, on the {d|Encyclopedia:FW_TookAmuletDecision}necklace on your chest{/d}.{/n} "A lovely piece, isn't it?"
  - After: {n}Bluff eyes the {d|Encyclopedia:FW_TookAmuletDecision}necklace on your chest{/d}.{/n} "Lovely, isn't it?"

  - Before: {n}Bluff ignores the Arbitrator, his gaze fixed on Maive — more specifically, on the necklace on her chest.{/n} "A lovely piece, isn't it?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You are surrounded by the smell of old rust. The darkness reluctantly retreats: the pain comes first — throbbing in your head; then the metallic taste in your mouth; and finally the feel of the hard floor, chafing your stinging cheek.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Staring daggers at you, Ruoldo shrieks,{/n} "Seize her! Seize Maive!"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You look over to where Solomorne indicated. Glaito lies motionless in the middle of the room. Judging by the flickering lumens on his implants, the dog is still alive.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The piercing pain in your head makes it hard to parse Solomorne's cryptic signals.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The guard takes a heavy step in your direction. The look on his face promises nothing pleasant.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A sweet, melodious voice rings out — not yours.{/n}
  - After: {n}A sweet voice — not yours.{/n}
- **Bluff the Court Fool**

  - After: "Who heeds a jester? Unnoticed, I prepared our grand finale. And hid my tracks..."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Much more. You see, with the right knowledge, the right tools, and some complex rituals, people can transform a simple, dirty blue pebble from the depths of Thassera into something truly special. However, it's a bit late for you to do anything with that information."

  - After: {n}Taddua the executioner smirks behind him.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}There are markings on the floor at your feet: a crooked circle bordered by unholy symbols. Bluff is standing in the centre of an identical circle. You hear a quiet, measured scraping sound and an old man's muttering coming from the depths of the hall — the few words you manage to catch sound nothing like Gothic.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You are bobbing like a boat tossed upon the waves. Colours and sounds meld into a cacophony, stirring up nausea in this exhausted body. - **Tavrisk the Sculptor**
  - Before: "The preparations are complete, my lord." {n}Barely able to take his eyes off the dark altar, the sculptor hobbles toward the edge of the balcony.{/n}
  - After: "Ready, my lord." {n}The sculptor hobbles forward.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}At your feet lies a gaudy mask that has fallen from the fool's face. Covering his wrinkled visage with both hands, the ugly and enraged governor of Thassera rises hastily on trembling legs.{/n}
  - After: {n}The mask has fallen. Thassera's enraged governor rises, face hidden.{/n}
- **Bluff the Court Fool**

These rain-worn mechanisms never fail to disappoint — creaking one moment, failing the next."

The crystals in his eye sockets gleam and go dark in time with the flashes.{/n}

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/FeudalWorld/FW_StableGuard/FW_StableGuard_dialogue

- **Player**

  - Before: "Let me out this instant! I am the Rogue Trader! They have put me in this body..."
  - After: "Free me! I'm the Rogue Trader, body-swapped!"

  - Before: "Please, let me out! I can make you rich."
  - After: "Free me! I'll make you rich."

  - Before: "Glaito? You have recovered?"
  - After: "Glaito? Recovered?"

  - Before: "Stay back, or you'll be sorry!"
  - After: "Stay back!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "My servants will find me. And when they do, they will cut you to ribbons, unless you let me go right now!"
  - After: "Free me, or my servants will cut you to ribbons!"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You take a deep breath and scream as loud as you can. Your voice rings pitifully. This cry may be your last.{/n}
  - After: {n}You scream pitifully.{/n}

  - After: {n}Your punch is too weak. He grabs your wrist.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You dash forward, but your weak legs fail you. The man grabs your hair with his free hand. Black spots dance before your eyes.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your legs fail. He grabs your hair.{/n}

  - After: {n}Glaito barks, awaiting orders.{/n}

  - After: {n}A pause.{/n} "No more trading, then."

  - After: "Stop whining. Die quickly."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You notice a dent in one of the cyber-mastiff's implants: he has taken a beating. It is hard to say whether he received this injury at the time of your capture or during his escape from the castle.{/n}
  - After: {n}One of Glaito's implants is dented.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You try to hit him in the jaw, but miss your punch — Maive is a lady-in-waiting, not a fighter. The man grabs your wrist.{/n}
  - After: {n}You miss — Maive's no fighter. He grabs your wrist.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: {n}You trip. He grabs your hair.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cleaver, raised for a strike, falls from the man's hand as he screams, assailed by a whirlwind of fangs, fur, and metal. Having emerged from the gloom, the cyber-mastiff does not give the stable hand even a single chance: after ripping out a part of his spine, the beast spits out the corpse and looks up at you.{/n}
  - After: {n}The cyber-mastiff lunges from the gloom, rips out the stable hand's spine, and looks at you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}An abrupt metallic clang rattles the stable. Something very heavy is coming your way at terrifying speed.{/n}
  - After: {n}A clang. Something heavy charges.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: {n}Cyber-mastiffs obey only their master. Is Solomorne dead?{/n}

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/FeudalWorld/FW_Trap/FW_Trap_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I am uneasy as well, on account of certain unusual circumstances."
  - After: "I'm uneasy too. Some things are unusual."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The governor's strange behaviour. The remarkably lavish gifts, the change in personality... and all of that just before our arrival."
  - After: "The governor's lavish gifts and changed personality, just before we arrived."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not like the way the governor is using every means possible to stall our enquiry into the tithe."
  - After: "The governor keeps stalling our tithe enquiry."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The governor is not Thasserian. And yet, he seems utterly clueless about what is happening outside this planet."
  - After: "The governor isn't Thasserian, yet knows nothing of the outside."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The sculptor, like Ruoldo, is not a local. But more importantly, he is a sanctioned psyker."
  - After: "The sculptor is no local either. And he's a sanctioned psyker."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Remember the last mutant from the public execution? Something was off about him, and it wasn't just the physical deformity."
  - After: "The last mutant at the execution. Something was off about him."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If you have suspicions about the Thasserians, why have you not taken any action so far?"
  - After: "If you suspect the Thasserians, why haven't you acted?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are the most suspicious person here, Solomorne. Take a deep breath."
  - After: "You're the most suspicious one here, Solomorne. Breathe."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The local beliefs. What is this tripe about 'altering your destiny'?"
  - After: "What's this tripe about 'altering your destiny'?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "My words will be 'The Emperor knows.'"
  - After: "My words: 'The Emperor knows.'"
- **Player**
  - Before: "No. We are going to resolve all issues peacefully."
  - After: "No. We resolve this peacefully."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You tell me! You're the sleuthing Arbitrator!"
  - After: "You tell me! You're the Arbitrator!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "We are being led into a trap of some sort."
  - After: "We're being led into a trap."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will take a drag on a lho-stick. That will be the signal to strike."
  - After: "When I light a lho-stick, strike."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do not forget that the Thasserians have been nothing but cordial to us so far."
  - After: "The Thasserians have been nothing but cordial."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Thasserians have failed to gather their tithe and are now distracting us with smoke and mirrors."
  - After: "They failed their tithe and are distracting us."
- **Player**
  - Before: "There is something in Thassera's atmosphere that alters the human brain. Sooner or later, anyone who lives here becomes a clumsy idiot."
  - After: "Something in Thassera's air turns everyone into clumsy idiots."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Have you seen the writings of that madman, Falt? The Chronicle of Fates? It is lunacy bordering on heresy."
  - After: "Falt's Chronicle of Fates? Lunacy bordering on heresy."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I would wager that this is a cult. The predicaments I get into usually involve a cult of some description."
  - After: "It's a cult. My troubles usually involve a cult."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The tithe is a ruse. The governor is fully aware that with every hour that passes without him providing a report, his sentence only becomes more severe. Which means he is not even trying to account for the shortage. I suspect that there is some goal he is pursuing in trying to keep us here on Thassera."
  - After: "The tithe is a ruse. Every unreported hour worsens his sentence, yet he isn't trying to explain the shortage. He wants to keep us on Thassera for some goal."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The fact there was a mutant attack during a public execution, with no clear or evident cause."
  - After: "A mutant attack at a public execution, with no clear cause."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The governor barely manages to stay in his saddle, which is odd for a local nobleman."
  - After: "The governor barely stays in the saddle. Odd for a local noble."
- **Player**
  - Before: "This is what they call a persecution complex, Solomorne."
  - After: "That's a persecution complex, Solomorne."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Thassera is not what they are making it out to be — not a feudal world with a primitive populace but a forge world. Or else, an industrial one. The point of the deception is to pay a smaller tithe!"
  - After: "Thassera isn't a primitive feudal world but a forge or industrial one. The deception lowers their tithe!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will shout, 'ATTACK!'"
  - After: "I'll shout, 'ATTACK!'"
- **Player**
  - Before: "It is how I want it done."
  - After: "It's how I want it done."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Everyone needs rest sometimes, Solomorne. When one is constantly on edge, one starts to imagine things."
  - After: "Everyone needs rest, Solomorne. Constant tension breeds imaginings."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Maive, bring me a cup of {g|Encyclopedia:Amasec}amasec{/g} — and make sure it's filled to the brim," {n}comes an unexpected order from Solomorne.{/n}
  - After: "Maive, {g|Encyclopedia:Amasec}amasec{/g}, filled to the brim," {n}Solomorne orders.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "His work with locally mined stone may be a harmless pursuit... or it may not be. In any event, the fact that the governor employs a sorcerer who is working on his own project is enough to raise questions."
  - After: "A governor's sorcerer with his own project raises questions."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "My hypothesis is that this is not about the tithe. That is merely a pretext to keep us here long enough — but what for? We should play along for now. Let them think we've taken the bait while we wait for an opportunity to seize control of the situation. For that, we need to agree on a signal to launch a coordinated attack."
  - After: "The tithe is a pretext to hold us. Play along, then strike together. We need a signal."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I should rather call it vigilance. Strange situations may seem inconsequential now, but when the time comes for the looming threat to reveal itself, we will realise they were warning signs — or, indeed, warning shouts. Experience tells me we won't have long to wait for proof to emerge."
  - After: "Vigilance. Warning signs. Proof will come."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Fair enough. It is my direct duty to draw conclusions and pass verdicts."
  - After: "Fair. Verdicts are my duty."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne pauses, then asks with pointed courteousness:{/n} "May I conclude that you have observed nothing that struck you as suspicious?"
  - After: {n}A pause.{/n} "So you've noticed nothing suspicious?"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne waits until Maive is some distance away, then turns to you.{/n} "I wanted to talk to you without the observer they have attached to us overhearing." {n}He casts a sweeping glance around the courtyard and lowers his voice.{/n} "Do you get the sense that what is happening raises questions that lack coherent answers?"
  - After: {n}Maive leaves.{/n} "Away from our observer..." {n}He lowers his voice.{/n} "Does this all add up to you?"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "You are not wrong. In particular, I would like to note the governor granting preferential treatment to our attendant. Perhaps he needs her unconditional trust... to ensure that she does something or, on the contrary, remains uninvolved at just the right moment."
  - After: "And he favours our attendant. Perhaps he needs her trust."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I see. Then I will not initiate combat, but neither will I stand back if the other side initiates."
  - After: "I won't start a fight, but I'll answer one."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Indeed. At first, one could mistake it for sycophancy and an attempt to appease the 'celestial guests,' but the longer it goes on, the more apparent the criminal intent behind this stalling of the inevitable becomes."
  - After: "Indeed. Not sycophancy: criminal stalling."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Without a word, the Arbitrator hurls the drink on the pavement. The splash of amasec is like a scarlet wound upon the stone that has been polished by a thousand soles.{/n}
  - After: {n}He hurls the amasec down like a scarlet wound on the stone.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I have been gathering information. Taking any steps before doing that would have been reckless. Now is the time to coordinate our actions and discuss the risks — which are high, considering we are both outnumbered and in unknown territory."
  - After: "I was gathering facts. Now we plan. We're outnumbered here."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Not too odd considering Ruoldo's ravenous fondness for food and amasec... but an astute observation nonetheless."
  - After: "Ruoldo loves food and amasec. But astute."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have a theory, but I would like to hear yours first, lest my opinions influence your reasoning."
  - After: "I have a theory, but tell me yours first."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "An Arbitrator cannot be bribed — neither with gold nor with special treatment. Doing our duty is all that concerns us. The locals' affability is not conducive to obtaining data on the tithe, and that is what matters to me."
  - After: "Arbitrators can't be bribed. Affability yields no tithe data."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I take that as a no. Understood. No further questions."
  - After: "I take that as a no."
- **Maive**
  - Before: {n}Maive returns, taking quick careful steps along the paved road, a brimming goblet in her hands.{/n} "Your amasec, my lord. I haven't spilt a drop!"
  - After: {n}Maive returns with a goblet.{/n} "Your amasec, my lord. Not a drop spilt!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne looks at you, his doubt evident.{/n} "Certainly a bold theory, but I would be wary of such far-reaching speculations."
  - After: {n}Solomorne looks doubtful.{/n} "Bold. Too speculative."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Likely so. But while we are ignorant as to the nature and purpose of this trap, we have nothing concrete to go on and can only stay on our guard."
  - After: "Likely. Until we know more, stay on guard."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "That is possible. But how can they ever expect it to work? Tithe evasion cannot be covered up, especially not by eliminating our delegation. It is as though the governor is painting himself into a corner..."
  - After: "Possible. But evasion can't be hidden, even by killing us."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Believe it or not, I have seen worlds like that. Colonies do not tend to last very long on them, so I cannot second your hypothesis."
  - After: "I've seen such worlds. Their colonies don't last."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Not bordering — they are heresy writ large. But that is not what troubles me. What troubles me is that the madman succeeded in publishing them."
  - After: "Heresy writ large. Worse, it got published."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Heretical cults are not the only threat by far. But there is enough heresy on Thassera either way."
  - After: "Cults aren't the only threat. But there's heresy enough."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The fact that the court fool is Maive's brother only adds to the suspicion, as do the alleged changes in his behaviour. There is some connection between the governor and these two — a buffoon who is permitted to run wild and a minor noblewoman who has unexpectedly been given an important role in the festivities."
  - After: "And Maive's brother, the court fool, has changed. The governor ties to both: a buffoon running wild, a minor noble given a key festival role."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne chuckles.{/n} "Expertly noted. It somehow slipped my mind that {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Arbitrator}you collected tributes{/d} from just as many worlds as I have in your time. I do not have a strong hypothesis for why the governor is stalling us, but I would like to propose a plan: let's not give away the fact that we are aware of his ploy and wait for an opportune moment to strike — we do not know the territory, so we should act suddenly and take no chances. Now let's decide on a signal we will use when the time is right."
  - After: {n}Solomorne chuckles.{/n} "Right, {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Arbitrator}you collected tributes{/d} too. Let's feign ignorance and strike suddenly. We need a signal."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Precisely. Either he has had an experience so traumatic as to cause him to altogether lose his memory, or we are being played for fools."
  - After: "Either trauma wiped his memory, or we're being played."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Yes. Mutation is a corruption that seldom leaves a person with a sound mind, but what the madman spouted on the scaffold, and what he had done to himself, was beyond the pale."
  - After: "Mutants are rarely sane, but his was beyond the pale."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "The God-Emperor alone knows how many different cults of Him there are. No two planets worship Him in quite the same way. But only a heretic would wax poetic about altering a fate that was ordained by the Emperor once and for all."
  - After: "Only a heretic speaks of altering a fate the Emperor ordained."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "The attack is unlikely to have been planned. It looked too... messy, shall we say. On the other hand, perhaps that's the best this backwater planet can do when it comes to plotting and scheming."
  - After: "Too messy to be planned. Or backwater scheming."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Which ones in particular?"
  - After: "Which ones?"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Thus forewarning the enemy as well. What would be the point?"
  - After: "And forewarn the enemy?"

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/PenalWorldArbites/PWA_Solomorne/PWA_Solomorne_dialog

  - Before: "We are getting reports... of it being an order of the Adeptus Administratum. We have received several official forms to the effect that Dargonus's orbit is currently deemed unsafe for tithe storage due to an unspecified threat that has sprung up on the world in your absence."
  - After: "Administratum orders. Dargonus's orbit is deemed unsafe for the tithe."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The vox is silent for several minutes.{/n} "The messages have no discernible structure or cause. Professions of loyalty. Audience requests. Even pleas for leniency... One thing is clear, Lord Captain: something has agitated the upper echelons of the nobility. In other words... they are scared."
  - After: {n}Silence.{/n} "Oaths, pleas, requests... The nobles are scared."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are requested to come to the Palace of Justice in person. The prefect speaks of a terrible heresy that is threatening the von Valancius protectorate. While you were away, steps were taken to prevent the spread of the corruption; however, your presence is required to make the final decision. Prefect Vultur will meet you in person for a confidential conversation."
  - After: "Prefect Vultur summons you to the Palace of Justice. A heresy threatens the protectorate; you must decide."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The vox is silent for a while.{/n} "It appears you have no choice if you want to help your subjects. Although I don't like what is going on, I would advise you to go to the Palace — if nothing else, to find out what you can do to protect your people."
  - After: {n}Silence.{/n} "I don't like it, but go — for your people."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It seems the law faltered on Dargonus as soon as its {mf|master|mistress} left it unattended. The disjointed reports from the ground sound strange, if not outright suspicious... but only you can put an end to any heresy on your own planet."
  - After: "The law faltered once its {mf|master|mistress} left. Only you can end this heresy."

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/RaycadMinorisArbites/RM_AlternativeArbitesFirstMeeting/RM_AlternativeArbitesFirstMeeting_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I want you and your unit to escort me to the governor."
  - After: "Escort me to the governor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A man in Adeptus Arbites armour raises the visor on his helmet and regards you with a harsh look.{/n} "Thank you for your cooperation. Proctor Garren. Now, state your name and the purpose of your stay on Rykad Minoris."

  - After: "An investigation. Arbites business only."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This world is in the throes of rebellion and madness. Whatever the cause may be, we will not risk the success of our mission to address it. But if the governor does not re-establish a semblance of control by the time we are done, we will see to it ourselves."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The huge cyber-mastiff immediately stops snarling in your direction and goes quiet at its master's foot, its stillness punctuated only by the thick globules of blood dripping from its metal fangs.{/n}

  - After: "Answer my question first."
- **(conversation owner)**

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/RaycadMinorisArbites/RM_ArbitesRescue/RM_ArbitesRescue_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Those wounds look bad. Let me offer you first aid."
  - After: "Those wounds look bad. Let me help."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It has been a pleasure to make your acquaintance. Do try to survive, will you?"
  - After: "A pleasure. Try to survive."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is happening in the starport?"
  - After: "What's happening in the starport?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I sincerely hope that you die out here."
  - After: "I hope you die out here."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I see you are not trying to flee and have chosen to fight instead. I commend your resolve."
  - After: "You chose to fight, not flee. Commendable."

  - Before: "Rykad Minoris is doomed. There is no time for heroics. We need to leave!"
  - After: "Rykad Minoris is doomed. We leave now!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Very well. You and your people may come with me."
  - After: "Very well. Your people may come."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will consider it an honour to assist you."
  - After: "An honour to assist you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your problems do not concern me."
  - After: "Your problems don't concern me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "That's better. Welcome aboard."
  - After: "Better. Welcome aboard."
- **Player**
