  - After: "You, your Marshal and your Arbitrators can go to the warp. No alliance."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It appears your investigation has hit a dead end."
  - After: "Your investigation hit a dead end."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I could use a personal lawman at my beck and call — especially one who is in my debt."
  - After: "A personal lawman in my debt could be useful."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I won't wish you luck — with a dog like that, you clearly do not need it."
  - After: "With that dog, you don't need luck."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne's chestplate is punctured in multiple places and his face stained with blood, but his gaze remains clear and firm.{/n} "Still alive, Rogue Trader? Good."
  - After: {n}Solomorne is bloodied, gaze firm.{/n} "Still alive, Rogue Trader? Good."
- **Glaito**
  - Before: {n}You spot just as many wounds on Glaito: there are burns and cuts all over the coat, and one of the visors is broken. And yet, there is nothing in the cyber-mastiff's straight posture that would indicate pain — if pain is even something this dog can feel.{/n}
  - After: {n}Glaito is wounded, but unbowed.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Panic and heresy. The people are ready to crush each other to reach the shuttles, which makes them easy targets for the enemy."
  - After: "Panic and heresy. People trample each other for shuttles."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To die would be to fail my mission, and I cannot let that happen. Emperor protect you, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "Dying would fail my mission. Emperor protect you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I do not know. He waited for you — under Arbites escort — to burn the heretic's body and conclude the ceremony. But when the sun went out and enemies came at us from every crack in the rockcrete, he panicked and ran. Not the smartest choice — he would have been safer with us."
  - After: "Unknown. When the sun went out, he fled his escort. Foolish."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Keep hoping," {n}Solomorne responds calmly, as if commenting on the weather, then turns away.{/n}
  - After: "Keep hoping," {n}he says calmly, turning away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Actually, our plan is to retreat. The rebels are one thing, but there is nothing we can do against the warp forcing its way in, and that's a fact." {n}Solomorne spits out a mouthful of blood.{/n} "This battle was forced on us — we had to keep the heretics away from the terminal until the machine spirits finished transferring the data to our shuttle."
  - After: "We're retreating; we can't fight the warp." {n}He spits blood.{/n} "We held the terminal for the data."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Speaking of shuttles, the ship we hired has turned tail and left orbit, so I must turn to you with a request: take my squad aboard, and we will disembark on the first world or station with access to a voidship. We cannot die here while whoever stole the tithe is enjoying their freedom."
  - After: "Our ship fled. Take my squad to the next voidport. The tithe thief runs free."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Emperor knows I am no orator, so I will ask you again, as well as I can. I need your help, not to save myself, but so that I may continue serving the Lex Imperialis. The Marshal must receive the information I have obtained here. If you want me to beg, I will — my pride means nothing compared to my duty."
  - After: "I need your help so the Marshal gets my information. I'll beg if I must."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A vein pulses violently on the Proctor's temple, but his voice is calm:{/n} "You have my thanks, Rogue Trader. You should press forward — we won't keep you waiting."
  - After: {n}A vein pulses.{/n} "My thanks. Go, we'll follow."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We need time to dress our wounds and regroup. We will cover your retreat and make sure there is no attack from the rear. Get to the shuttle first; we'll be right behind you."
  - After: "We'll cover your rear. Get to the shuttle; we'll follow."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man rests his bloodied hand on the cyber-mastiff's shoulders.{/n} "We always knew it would end like this, didn't we, Glaito?" {n}Solomorne turns away as if you had ceased to exist.{/n}
  - After: {n}Hand on the mastiff.{/n} "We knew it would end like this, Glaito." {n}He ignores you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Not yet, it hasn't." {n}A crooked smile crosses his face.{/n} "We did find something on the port terminal... Shortly after the tithe was hauled away, a suspicious ship took off from the planet. And I already know how to track it down."
  - After: "Not yet." {n}A crooked smile.{/n} "A suspicious ship left right after the tithe vanished. I can track it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My squad and I will dress our wounds, regroup, then try to break through to our shuttle. I recommend you do that last part as well, and soon."
  - After: "We'll regroup and reach our shuttle. Do the same."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You helped us to fight them off, so, instead of words of gratitude, let me offer you something more substantial." {n}Solomorne hands you a heavy shotgun.{/n} "It belonged to a bloody good Arbitrator. May it serve you now."
  - After: "Instead of thanks..." {n}He hands you a shotgun.{/n} "A good Arbitrator's. May it serve you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I would have accepted your offer, but we still have medicae kits. Not many, but it should last us until we get to the shuttles — which is all we need."
  - After: "We have medicae kits enough."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I agree. In that case, you may add my luck to your own so you can get out of here."
  - After: "Agreed. Take my luck too."

He carries his helmet in the crook of his arm, but his stern facade serves him as well as any visor could. He bows to you sharply.{/n} "Marshal Strachs of the Adeptus Arbites."

- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: {n}Your eyes drift shut. You slowly plunge ever deeper into the darkness of sleep, while a voice, growing more and more distant, continues to wish you and your progeny epiphanies and boons of every kind... until an awkward cough jerks you suddenly out of your sweet torpor. The prefect, who appears to have finished speaking some time ago, is looking at you wordlessly, as is the Marshal, along with everyone else in the room.{/n}
  - After: {n}You doze off, until a cough jolts you awake. Everyone is staring at you.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "A delegation of the Adeptus Administratum and the Adeptus Arbites is accommodated in the von Valancius territory so that they may tally and collect the {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGlossary}Imperial Tithe{/g} from your worlds, Lord Captain. Lady Theodora graciously provided them with premises where they could perform their duties and authorised them to restructure the dynasty's archives."
  - After: "An Administratum and Arbites delegation collecting the {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGlossary}Imperial Tithe{/g}, Lord Captain. Lady Theodora housed them."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal leans forward. His voice is low, and when he speaks, it feels as though the marble tiles of the palace had begun to vibrate.{/n} "The Adeptus Arbites delegation has arrived to greet Lady Theodora's successor and to see to the extension of our decades-long arrangement."
  - After: {n}The Marshal's deep voice rumbles.{/n} "We came to greet Lady Theodora's successor and extend our long arrangement."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "If I may continue for you." {n}The prefect steps forward, dragging her feet slightly.{/n} "As per the decree of Theodora von Valancius ORD-037/ЗN, the representatives of the Adeptus Administratum and the Adeptus Arbites are sanctioned to use the Palace of Justice, oversee {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGlossary}tithe{/g} collection in the protectorate, and review any and all cases of tithe avoidance, tithe exceedance, or other irregularities. These rights have been formalised in numerous pacts and statutes under the main decree — considering your new position, you may have yet to acquaint yourself with all these documents."
  - After: "If I may." {n}She shuffles forward.{/n} "Decree ORD-037/ЗN grants us the Palace of Justice and oversight of {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGlossary}tithe{/g} collection and irregularities."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: {n}The prefect's lips contort into a twist.{/n} "Our work has been disrupted by unforeseen setbacks regarding communication and transportation. As our requisitioned assets were not adequately prepared, we have lost some of our personnel and resources as a result."
  - After: {n}Her lips twist.{/n} "Transport setbacks cost us people and resources."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal nods — he seems more accustomed to the tone you have chosen than to wordy pleasantries.{/n} "Warp storms ravaging the Koronus Expanse have deprived us of ships, people, and resources. And so, we must approach you as the inheritor of the pact we made with Lady Theodora."
  - After: {n}The Marshal nods.{/n} "Warp storms cost us ships and people. We turn to you, heir to Theodora's pact."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "The Arbitrators are too short-handed to perform all the duties expected of them. Since they first arrived in the Expanse, their numbers, limited from the outset, have only continued to dwindle... After analysing the situation in accordance with Amendment FS/89З-24 to Decree ORD-037/ЗN, we have decided to notify you of a tithe violation committed by one of the worlds in the region. This regrettable lapse must be rectified as quickly as possible." {n}The old woman shivers and rubs her augmented hands together with an unnerving creak.{/n}
  - After: "The Arbitrators are dwindling. We notify you of a tithe violation by a nearby world. It must be rectified." {n}Her augmented hands creak.{/n}
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "Not at all. You are the Emperor's anointed, and you act solely of your own volition." {n}The Marshal's voice makes the enforcers in the room flinch.{/n}
  - After: "Not at all. You are the Emperor's anointed." {n}The enforcers flinch.{/n}
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: {n}The prefect, on the other hand, speaks softly, and yet, you can hear every word as if she were standing directly beside you:{/n} "Your predecessor, Lady Theodora — may the light of the Throne illuminate her path in death — always sought to address the needs of both the Adeptus Administratum and the Adeptus Arbites, because she realised how blessed and important our work is for the good of the Imperium — to say nothing of the fact that she honoured the laws of her own dynasty."
  - After: {n}The prefect, softly:{/n} "Lady Theodora, Throne light her path, always served our needs and honoured her dynasty's laws."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "Thassera, a feudal world far from the main routes that was bereft of the Imperium's light, then rediscovered less than two centuries ago. It supplies agricultural resources and manpower."
  - After: "Thassera, a remote feudal world rediscovered under two centuries ago. Crops and manpower."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "This is not a von Valancius world — the system is located just outside the border of your protectorate. The Imperium is built upon strict and unfailing abidance by the {g|Encyclopedia:LexImperialisGlossary}Lex Imperialis{/g}, and a planet's tithe, even one that is relatively small, must be provided in full."
  - After: "It lies just outside your border. Under the {g|Encyclopedia:LexImperialisGlossary}Lex Imperialis{/g}, every tithe is owed in full."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal inclines his head.{/n} "If you were to break this pact, the Adeptus Arbites would no longer consider itself obligated to provide you with support, such as by bolstering your personal retinue with Arbitrators."
  - After: {n}He inclines his head.{/n} "Break the pact, and the Arbites owe you no support, no Arbitrators."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "Furthermore..." {n}The prefect licks her finger out of habit, as though she were about to turn an invisible page.{/n} "Decree ORD-037/ЗN 'On Mutual Benefaction and Cooperation Between the Rogue Trader and Representatives of the Adeptus Administratum and the Adeptus Arbites' was created and personally certified by Theodora von Valancius for good reason. If we were to disregard this measure, we would risk having... any of the aforementioned parties sink back into pernicious freethinking. I am sure I need not to tell you what a great undertaking it is to establish any semblance of order. I strongly urge you to reconsider."
  - After: "Furthermore..." {n}She licks a finger.{/n} "Lady Theodora certified Decree ORD-037/ЗN for good reason. Without it, order crumbles. Reconsider."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: {n}Before you even finish speaking, the prefect's cogita-quill begins scratching at her data-slate, likely recording your refusal and making corrections to various decrees. The Marshal merely bows, and the delegation of lawkeepers leaves the room.{/n}
  - After: {n}Her cogita-quill scratches out your refusal. The Marshal bows, and the delegation leaves.{/n}
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "An Arbitrator will be assigned to you for increased security. Proctor Anthar, front and centre!" {n}The Marshal's voice thunders over the Arbitrator ranks, and Solomorne Anthar marches over to your throne, his cyber-mastiff at his heel.{/n}
  - After: "An Arbitrator will guard you. Proctor Anthar!" {n}Solomorne marches up, mastiff at heel.{/n}
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "Proctor Anthar's capacity is not that of a spy, but that of a representative of our organisations who will help you to navigate the many nuances of the Imperial Law and, if the need arises, direct you down the just path."
  - After: "Not a spy — a guide through Imperial Law, and down the just path if needed."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "The Emperor protects!" {n}The Marshal makes the sign of the Aquila in a motion so sharp that you can practically hear it cutting the air.{/n}
  - After: "The Emperor protects!" {n}The Marshal makes a sharp Aquila.{/n}
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: {n}The prefect adjusts her ocular lenses with a weary sigh.{/n} "And once again, no specifics given — of course. And my reports? Nobody ever stops to think—" {n}She quickly catches herself and offers you a bow.{/n}
  - After: {n}The prefect sighs.{/n} "No specifics, of course. And my reports? Nobody thinks—" {n}She catches herself and bows.{/n}
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "For thirty-four generations, my family has served in the Adeptus Administratum. I was given a name befitting one who comes from a long line of scribes." {n}The prefect looks at you without blinking — she is either ignoring your disrespectful tone or has genuinely failed to notice it.{/n}
  - After: "Thirty-four generations of scribes. My name befits them." {n}She stares, unblinking.{/n}
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "You are the successor to Lady Theodora, whose alliance with our two sacred organisations forever glorified her as a Rogue Trader closely tied to the executors of {g|Encyclopedia:HolyTerraGlossary}Holy Terra{/g}'s will. And we as representatives of the Adeptus Administratum and the Adeptus Arbites must verify that you are able to maintain this alliance that has brought such repute to your dynasty." {n}The prefect scrutinises you as if trying to estimate your proportions and weight.{/n} "That is why we have arrived in person, as the present circumstances have provided us with a chance to see if your intentions concord with those of the late von Valancius."
  - After: "Lady Theodora's alliance with us served {g|Encyclopedia:HolyTerraGlossary}Holy Terra{/g}. We came to see if you can keep it." {n}She sizes you up.{/n}
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: {n}The prefect bows to you.{/n} "The material compensation... should satisfy you."
  - After: {n}She bows.{/n} "The compensation should satisfy you."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal gives you a terse nod.{/n} "Indeed, and I should offer you our thanks once again. I have read the report on the operation, and it is worth noting that {g|Encyclopedia:ProctorGlossary}Proctor{/g} Anthar spoke highly of you and your talents."
  - After: {n}A terse nod.{/n} "Indeed, our thanks. {g|Encyclopedia:ProctorGlossary}Proctor{/g} Anthar's report praised you."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "Though, having once saved him and the other Arbitrators from a dying planet, your character should require no further affirmation."
  - After: "You saved him from a dying planet. Your character needs no proof."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You enunciate an impressively long and ornate list of all the blessings and encouragements that have been {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}showered upon you since birth{/d}. Those in attendance listen with bated breath. With each passing minute, the prefect's face falls lower and lower, but she dares not utter a word throughout your speech, which takes a good quarter of an hour.{/n}
  - After: {n}You recite a quarter-hour of every blessing {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Nobility}showered upon you since birth{/d}. The prefect's face falls, but she stays silent.{/n}

His meticulously polished jaw augmentation reflects the palace's interior as sharply as a mirror.{/n} "Allow me to introduce myself! I am Lussarius Karmelan, a collector of curiosities. Perhaps Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} will find something useful among my offerings."

  - After: "The broadest choice in the Expanse! But even I have limits..."

  - Before: {n}The merchant bows, still smiling: the light makes his prosthetic jaw sparkle.{/n}
  - After: {n}He bows, jaw sparkling.{/n}
- **Curiosity Merchant**

  - After: "Tithe destruction, unlicensed breeding, defaming the Arbites. No mercy."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Your choice was between starving to death and desecrating the tithe. This mitigating circumstance will be taken into account during your sentencing."
  - After: "Starve or desecrate the tithe. That mitigates your sentence."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "They should have hanged a few of your unauthorised families. You would have learned an important lesson in maintaining order, without falling below your initial head count."
  - After: "A few hangings would have kept order."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The madman raises his only remaining eyebrow in mock surprise.{/n} "Pray tell, where on this Emperor-cursed world do you mean to go? Perhaps to the Arbites? Then, allow us to take you there. With such an esteemed guest for a hostage, I won't have to storm their fortifications: they will open the gates themselves. Stepchildren, kill our guest's retinue. They would encumber the negotiations."
  - After: {n}He smirks.{/n} "The Arbites? With you as hostage, they'll open the gates. Stepchildren, kill the retinue."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Self-proclaimed Captain Walz, a Stepchild of the Imperium, as we all are here. A living tithe abandoned to his fate. And a death world veteran who ended up among recruits by mistake."
  - After: "Captain Walz, self-proclaimed. A Stepchild of the Imperium. A death world veteran."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That's what you emissaries of the Riven Sky always say, because you're afraid of one who knows the truth."
  - After: "Riven Sky emissaries always say that. You fear the truth."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Of course you do. Where else? I know the way. I dream of their little fortress at night, overwhelmed and aflame. The avenues of approach, the adjacent high grounds, the shelters — they are all burned into my mind because of how often I think about that place. The Stepchildren and I will arrive there very soon."
  - After: "I know the way. I dream of it burning."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I will raise the bloodied head of the false law on a spike and destroy the illusion that the Riven Sky has any power left in it. Then, the other Guard units will join me, and our march toward the stars will begin!"
  - After: "I'll spike the false law's head. Then the Guard joins me, and we march to the stars!"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}After examining the Guardsman, Kibellah gives a thoughtful nod.{/n} "The blood of a madman is hot, and his organs stay warm for longer... Useful for divinations."
  - After: {n}Kibellah nods.{/n} "A madman's organs stay warm. Good for divinations."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Our illusions were shattered. The Arbites brought us here and left us to rot. For years, we waited for our chance to die heroically in the name of the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g}, until we realised: the Imperium is gone. All there is... is the Riven Sky."
  - After: "Left to rot, we waited years to die for the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g}. It's gone. Only the Riven Sky remains."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "A warrior robbed of his right to perform feats in battle is akin to a caged beast. First, it is madness that gnaws at his heart, and then, it is Morkai, the bringer of death."
  - After: "A warrior denied battle goes mad, then Morkai takes him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The revolting semblance of a smile appears on his melted face.{/n} "Look around you! Everything you see was a tithe — a sacred payment to the Imperium. And what became of it? Why did it never travel to other worlds as we'd been promised? Why are we starving here instead of doing battle among the stars? Because there's nothing there, that's why..."
  - After: {n}He grins.{/n} "All this tithe never left. Why do we starve here? Because there's nothing out there."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Riven Sky. You children of the abyss like to toy with our minds. You keep bringing new garbage here and dumping it on our heads — all just to maintain the feeble facade of your lies! And you keep talking about a future that will never come... Enough!"
  - After: "The Riven Sky. You dump garbage on us to prop up your lies. Enough!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We break the containers open, and we get our own sustenance. At least the food we have here is real. Your minions, the Arbites, toss us some rations, but they aren't enough for the whole regiment. There are too many of us now."
  - After: "We loot containers. Rations can't feed us all."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Conspiracy to murder members of the Adeptus Arbites. The sentence is death. Further questioning would be pointless, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "Conspiracy to murder Arbitrators. Death. Questions are pointless."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne rubs the bridge of his nose wearily.{/n} "I have no further questions for anyone who is clearly out of their mind. The question I would like to ask is if there was ever a way to prevent this ugly situation."
  - After: {n}Solomorne sighs.{/n} "No questions for madmen. Could this have been prevented?"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Oh no. First, I will disembowel you in front of your Guardsmen. Then, I'd like to see what passes for the Arbites around here. I will ask them this: why in the void's name does rabble dare to speak of Arbitrators with anything other than terrified reverence?"
  - After: "I'll gut you first, then ask the Arbites why rabble doesn't fear them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Me? No, no, we need each other! Only together can we take on the Riven Sky and its emissaries. First we take out the Arbites, then we fly to the steel star in the sky. There, we will strike down the false rulers and begin our restoration of the true Imperium!"
  - After: "We need each other! Take the Arbites, then the steel star, and restore the true Imperium!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The madman's face breaks into a smile.{/n} "Ah, I'm sure that's what you think! You have one of the law dogs at your side. So, you are their commander, emissary of the Riven Sky! With you as my hostage, the Arbites will open their gates to me without a fight. Take this one alive, Stepchildren. We don't need the rest of them."
  - After: {n}He smiles.{/n} "You command the law dogs! As hostage, you'll open their gates. Take this one alive, Stepchildren."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Our sergeant... We strung up our sergeant. The Arbites gave him to us. They serve the Riven Sky, and nothing comes from the Sky but evil..." {n}The Guardsman's one eye studies your squad intently, as if calculating something.{/n}
  - After: "We strung up our sergeant. The Arbites serve the Sky." {n}He sizes you up.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The soldiers exchange anxious glances. There are hints of doubt and shame in their discordant voices.{/n}
  - After: {n}The soldiers waver, ashamed.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The soldiers stare at you silently with stern, judging eyes devoid of any remorse.{/n}
  - After: {n}The soldiers stare, unrepentant.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A sweet lie told by servants of the Riven Sky. Over and over... But not to worry: their end is nigh."
  - After: "A Sky lie. Their end nears."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are wasting your breath. None will renounce the truth once it has been revealed to them."
  - After: "Wasted breath. None will recant."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "And that outcome is far from the worst."
  - After: "Far from the worst outcome."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Guardsman's face stretches into a merciless sneer.{/n} "You think I am the monster here, three-eyed thing?"
  - After: {n}He sneers.{/n} "I'm the monster, three-eyed thing?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Commander? No, the enemy! He was hiding the truth from us and prevented us from taking action. His death opened the way to freedom and made us realise that there is nothing up there — we are on our own."
  - After: "He hid the truth. His death freed us. We're alone."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard assumes a most stern expression and proclaims vociferously:{/n} "Guardsman, before you stands Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, by the will of the Emperor the ruler of millions of subjects and the sovereign of many planets, Leethus included! From now on, you will show {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} proper deference and obey any order without question."
  - After: {n}Abelard, sternly:{/n} "This is Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, sovereign of Leethus! Obey {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man scrutinises you from top to bottom.{/n} "Yes, I see... I see the crux of the matter: you are someone very important, someone whose arrival can turn the tide. This is even more than I expected."
  - After: {n}He studies you.{/n} "Someone important. Better than I hoped."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Shamed by your words, the Guardsmen avert their eyes from you, a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Militarum}great Astra Militarum commander{/d}, obeying whose orders comes as naturally as breathing to any private.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Guardsmen look away from a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Militarum}great Astra Militarum commander{/d}.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A tremor runs across the man's burned face.{/n} "You are not lying. We have both tasted {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Torture}pure agony{/d} and are forever changed by it. Yes, you are a dangerous opponent."
  - After: {n}He twitches.{/n} "We've both known {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Torture}pure agony{/d}. You're dangerous."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are not {mf|him|her}, just another of the Sky's tricks!" {n}But the captain's voice is unable to drown out the whispers of the Guardsmen, who are already recounting your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Glory}story{/d} to each other.{/n}
  - After: "You're not {mf|him|her}, just a Sky trick!" {n}His men whisper your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Glory}story{/d}.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "These Guardsmen refer to you as captain — I do not know by whom or with what right that rank was given to you, but it means nothing to me. Every living tithe unit must be commanded by a sergeant — where is yours? I need them to take us to the Arbites outpost."
  - After: "Your 'captain' means nothing. Where's your sergeant? We need the Arbites outpost."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne turns to you and comments in a flat voice,{/n} "Murder of a superior officer. Desertion of living tithe quarters. Defamation of {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusArbitesGlossary}Adeptus Arbites{/g} members. More than enough for a verdict."
  - After: {n}Solomorne, flatly:{/n} "Murder, desertion, defaming the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusArbitesGlossary}Adeptus Arbites{/g}. Enough."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Guardsman chuckles.{/n} "Don't try to fool me. We both know the truth: the Riven Sky is the abyss that has devoured everything outside — the primordial darkness. Sometimes, the Sky sends people, but they're imitations — shadows wearing human skins. They don't know that they don't exist, but I... I see right through them. They come from the steel star with the scarlet overseeing eye: from your rulers' throne."
  - After: {n}He chuckles.{/n} "The abyss that devoured all. It sends shadows in skin from the steel star with the scarlet eye."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "At last, the puppet master has decided to face me. How does it feel to look into the eyes of the last loyal sons and daughters of the Imperium? Don't answer that. I can see all the hate and greed eating you up inside."
  - After: "The puppet master at last. I see your hate and greed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That perfectly captures your rotten essence! You take true words and twist them into lies! No, we will put an end to the madness. Stepchildren, attack!"
  - After: "You twist truth into lies! Stepchildren, attack!"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "There is no truth in your doomed mind, Guardsman. By succumbing to doubt, you have embarked on the path of the wicked — and now, you will not escape judgement. For so it is said that all who despair shall betray, and all betrayal shall draw His retribution."
  - After: "Your doubt made you wicked, Guardsman. All who despair betray, and betrayal draws His retribution."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "You are not marred by the scabs of corruption, but you still chose to become a monster who would find no rest... Why?"
  - After: "Uncorrupted, yet you chose to be a monster. Why?"

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/TreasureWorld/TW_MadClerk/TW_MadClerk_dialogue

  - Before: "I have come for the inventory."
  - After: "I'm here for the inventory."

  - Before: "You face Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, peasant! On your knees is how you are to greet me! And I will be expecting an inventory of this place's riches from you."

  - Before: "I have no time for this!"
  - After: "No time for this!"

  - Before: "There is no cogitator with the inventory, is there?"
  - After: "There's no cogitator, is there?"

  - Before: "Not another word. And do not even think about falling behind."

  - Before: "How did ambulls get here in the first place?"
  - After: "How did ambulls get here?"

  - Before: "Well, let us see what you have to say."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The grey-clad man taps his fingers on his data-slate. His bulky head {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}implant{/g} showers the surroundings liberally with sparks.{/n} "Two hundred million... No! Didn't account for corrosion... But where?"
  - After: {n}A clerk's {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}implant{/g} sparks.{/n} "Two hundred million... where?"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}The Seneschal's booming voice causes a small avalanche of grain in one of the opened containers.{/n} "{mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, bearer of the sacred Warrant, has come to collect the inventory of the tithe shipment."
  - After: {n}Abelard booms.{/n} "{mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} {name} von Valancius wants the tithe inventory."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The clerk winces and mutters mechanically,{/n} "Tertius Quart, rank three scribe of the Departmento Catalogus, quantity: one! The inventory— it—"
  - After: {n}He winces.{/n} "Tertius Quart, scribe, one! The inventory—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Another unauthorised addition to the living tithe?" {n}The clerk waves you off, annoyed.{/n} "Your turn is in eight cycles! Shoo!"
  - After: "More tithe?" {n}He waves you off.{/n} "Eight cycles! Shoo!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}His dry, reddened eyes fix upon you.{/n} "There is no Rogue Trader on the inventory! I can't give you anything before I fill in the forms! So, let's start with the retinue..."
  - After: {n}He stares.{/n} "No Rogue Trader on file! Forms first. Retinue..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A woman of benign appearance, quantity: one. An opulence of golden Aquilas and Imperium-standard skulls suggests an affiliation with the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorumGlossary}Adeptus Ministorum{/g}. What department are you from?"
  - After: "Benign woman, one. {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorumGlossary}Adeptus Ministorum{/g}? Department?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The clerk nods quickly, pressing his fingers to his split lips.{/n}
  - After: {n}He nods, holding his lips.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A mutant with albinism, quantity: one. The gill slits suggest an ocean world origin. Note: skin desiccated. Placement in a liquid-filled tank recommended to avoid spontaneous disposal."
  - After: "Albino mutant, one. Gills. Tank recommended."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Guard private, aged, quantity: one. Deterioration: high. Unfit for duty..."
  - After: "Guard private, aged, one. Unfit..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A Rogue Trader, quantity: one. Bloodstain count on attire: twenty... Could you turn around?"
  - After: "Rogue Trader, one. Bloodstains: twenty... Turn around?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes! Death! But, with you gone, the tithe would've stayed here! It would've given me time... Meeting the target, filling in the last form: those are the only things that matter!"
  - After: "Yes! Without you, the tithe stays! Only the last form matters!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There used to be more of us. Five died of exhaustion. Three were killed in collapses of tithe assets. Two were eaten by ambulls. Another ten... no, elev— I don't know! Administratum replenishments are too rare! This world is too highly classified!"
  - After: "Exhaustion, collapses, ambulls killed them. No replacements!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The clerk gives you a hounded look, his implant crackling ominously.{/n} "You've eliminated the ambulls? G-good. I'm crossing them off the inventory. How many injuries have you sustained? I must account for the units of blood spilt..."
  - After: {n}Sparks.{/n} "Ambulls crossed off. Injuries? I must count the blood..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Please understand: I need time for additional inventory-taking! Just a little. A couple of... years. No, decades..."
  - After: "I need more time! Years. Decades..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Tertius's face brightens suddenly as his implant flashes again.{/n} "Ah, yes! Yes, of course... Let me open the path to the... the cogitator! That's where the inventory is."
  - After: {n}He brightens.{/n} "It's in the cogitator! I'll open the way."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The clerk's eyes well up.{/n} "I thought it would stop you! I have a job to finish!"
  - After: {n}Teary:{/n} "I thought it'd stop you! I must finish!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It's incomplete!" {n}The scribe recoils and clutches his head with a moan.{/n}
  - After: "It's incomplete!" {n}He clutches his head.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The inventory is in my implant. And it's notifying me of unaccounted-for assets — all the time!" {n}The clerk whimpers; his implant creaks in response.{/n} "My head is the inventory..."
  - After: "The inventory's in my implant!" {n}It creaks.{/n} "My head is the inventory..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The clerk sobs and lowers his sparking head, ready to follow you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sobbing, he follows.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Inventory of the Rogue Trader: complete. Thank you for your cooperation. Now, regarding the tithe..."
  - After: "Rogue Trader: done. Now, the tithe..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The clerk gets to work enthusiastically, as if he hadn't heard you.{/n}
  - After: {n}He ignores you, eager.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "An Ogryn, quantity: one, extra shaggy. Hazy-eyed, unencumbered by intelligence. Everything within the norm. Equipped with Adeptus Astartes power armour from the Space Wolves arsenal. Note: send an enquiry to Fenris regarding possible theft."

  - Before: "A servitor of non-standard configuration, quantity: one. Frame: feeble. Functionality: dubious. Signs of subpar lobotomy evident."
  - After: "Odd servitor, one. Feeble. Bad lobotomy."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A sister of the Adepta Sororitas, quantity: one. Beauty: indescribable. Grace: perfect. Majesty: extraordinary."
  - After: "Sororitas sister, one. Beauty: indescribable."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A member of the Adeptus Arbites, quantity: one. A non-standard-issue cyber-mastiff, quantity: one. Physical integrity: below average. Configuration: secondary. Jaw: prognathous and powerful. All of the above applies to both units."
  - After: "Arbitrator and cyber-mastiff, one each. Jaws: powerful."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A mutant most abominable, quantity: one... Scrawny, ugly, and underfed. Adding a recommendation for disposal..."
  - After: "Abominable mutant, one. Scrawny. Dispose..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And other hired personnel of no note."
  - After: "And hirelings of no note."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This concludes the inventory of the retinue. Proceeding to taking inventory of the Rogue Trader."
  - After: "Retinue done. Now you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The scribe frowns.{/n} "Abominable, scrawny, quantity: two."
  - After: {n}He frowns.{/n} "Abominable, scrawny: two."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...Twenty-six. Equipment condition: excellent. Limb count: satisfactory. Appearance: unremarkable. Self-importance: elevated."
  - After: "...Twenty-six. Looks: unremarkable. Self-importance: elevated."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You can't imagine how hard this is — the workload, the responsibility! Please understand: I'm on my own here! Well, almost..." {n}The clerk adds in a conspiratorial whisper,{/n} "There's another scribe here. He works at night and litters the reports with errors!"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A-ambulls! Repulsive, aggressive pests! They adapt to any environment... This world is infested with them! They got to the tithe and gobbled up everything they saw. And I had to update the inventory!" {n}The clerk's voice falters and turns into inconsolable weeping.{/n}
  - After: "Ambulls ate the tithe, and I had to update it!" {n}He weeps.{/n}

  - Before: "Lord Captain, why can't you be like other Rogue Traders in how you express your eccentric side? You could reserve a deck for grox races. You could use your crew members as human pieces in games of regicide. At a pinch, you could have your face carved into an asteroid!"
  - After: "Lord Captain, couldn't you just race grox instead?"

  - Before: {n}The clerk grabs his quill greedily, ready to catalogue your every birthmark and scar.{/n}
  - After: {n}He grabs his quill eagerly.{/n}

  - Before: "A man of worn-out appearance with a heavy stare, quantity: one... What department are you from, colleague?"
  - After: "Worn man, one. Department, colleague?"

  - Before: "A pale, lanky woman, quantity: one. Multiple signs of battery, evidence of malnourishment. Best category fit: Servants. Subcategory: Idlers."

- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}The Proctor's heavy fist crashes into Tertius's jaw, and a bloodied tooth clangs against the wall of a nearby container.{/n} "Account for this. No more evasiveness or asinine excuses. The Rogue Trader asks, and you answer. Is that understood?"
  - After: {n}Solomorne punches him.{/n} "The Rogue Trader asks, you answer."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "He has lost his mind and is unlikely to recover it. I see no point in judging a madman. I suggest simply collecting the inventory and leaving."
  - After: "He's mad. Take the inventory and go."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Your confession does nothing to diminish your guilt. You will die for what you did, either here or following your return to the Administratum and a lengthy investigation."
  - After: "You'll die anyway, here or after an Administratum inquiry."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Just one question: are you aware that this will go into the report to the Marshal?" {n}Solomorne's iron palm covers his face.{/n} "Or, worse, do you actually want this in the report?"
  - After: "This goes to the Marshal." {n}He facepalms.{/n} "Or is that the point?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Th-the Administratum? No! Let me finish the inventory, or kill me... What do I have to sign?"
  - After: "The Administratum? No! Let me finish, or kill me!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "He is stalling. He will continue to chatter away unless harsh action is taken."
  - After: "He's stalling. Be harsh."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The clerk's tense shoulders relax a little.{/n} "I believe you... But the report... Just one more tiiiny bit of stock-taking, all right?"
  - After: {n}He relaxes.{/n} "Fine... Just a tiiiny bit more?"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "I am not even sure which offends me more: your invaliding me or your mistaking me, an officer of the Navy, for an expendable Guardsman."
  - After: "Unfit? And a Navy officer, a Guardsman?"
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar makes a superstitious gesture to ward off evil.{/n} "Spilling the blood of a harmless fool is a bad omen. The feebleness of mind might spread to the killer. And that is the only thing saving this filthy-tongued louse's life."
  - After: {n}Ulfar wards off evil.{/n} "Killing a fool is bad luck."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The unit's degraded cognitive capacity is confirmed. The unit's functional value is unconfirmed. Requesting termination of vital functions in the name of mercy."
  - After: "Unit degraded. Requesting merciful termination."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "This servant's colours are mad— Wait, did I just get called a fish?"
  - After: "He's mad— Did he call me a fish?"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Perhaps I should carve your words into his skin with my blade, Domin? He seems to want..." {n}Kibellah grins darkly.{/n} "...a written request."
  - After: "Shall I carve it into him, Domin?" {n}She grins.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "There's irony in a complete lunatic being the only one who thinks me normal."
  - After: "Only a lunatic thinks I'm normal."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "You are inventing some lady of the court in the place of the warrior you are looking at! What is this so-called inventory?"
  - After: "I'm a warrior, not a court lady!"
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Do not protest, sweet-voiced sister! Has the scribe said a word of untruth?"
  - After: "Hush, sister! Did he lie?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Put 'N/A' in that field, 'colleague.' And add a note at the top of my sheet that says, 'burn before reading.'"
  - After: "'N/A,' colleague. Add: 'burn before reading.'"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "No offence, but I would not trust you with an inventory of Glaito's shit, what with how deranged you are. And to think that someone gave you the Expanse's entire tithe to freely desecrate."
  - After: "I'd not trust you with Glaito's shit, let alone the tithe."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "The deeper my knowledge of your species becomes, the more often I ask myself: how have you colonised so many worlds? How did you reach the stars to begin with?"
  - After: "How did your species ever reach the stars?"
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "'Disposal'... Your mon-keigh threats could at least use some variety. But even there, your imagination goes no further than a trite promise of premature demise."
  - After: "'Disposal'... Mon-keigh threats lack imagination."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Benign appearance? Yes, that's me! Put down 'Adeptus Amasecus' as my department, esteemed one."
  - After: "That's me! Department: 'Adeptus Amasecus.'"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Relax, Tertius. There is no time for any further inventory-taking. Just give us the report, and we will take you to the shuttles without any trouble."
  - After: "Relax, Tertius. Report, then shuttle."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The sub-items have been entered, thank you for your cooperation." {n}Under Solomorne's judgemental gaze, the clerk pokes his finger at the data-slate.{/n}
  - After: "Entered." {n}Solomorne glares.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne sighs helplessly.{/n} "Mercy, Rogue Trader, I beg you."
  - After: {n}Solomorne sighs.{/n} "Mercy, Rogue Trader."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The clerk yanks the data-slate away with surprising agility and hunches protectively over it.{/n} "No! This device is already on the inventory list and must not be removed! I— I? Yes, I must make a note of attempted theft on the record! Please state clearly the offender's name and occupation."
  - After: {n}He snatches it.{/n} "It's inventoried! Attempted theft! Your name?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Trazyn's irascible grumbling sounds in your head a little before the glowing silhouette appears.{/n} "Rudimentary, very rudimentary. This hoard of rotting banality does not even approach one hundredth of the scale of my collection, and yet Humanity cannot even cope with such a paltry little... how to label it... dust heap."
  - After: {n}Trazyn appears.{/n} "Rudimentary. Humanity can't even manage a dust heap."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A Tech-Priest of the Adeptus Mechanicus, quantity: one. Organic limbs: standard quantity. Mechadendrites: within normative parameters. Head..." {n}The clerk squints at Nuncius.{/n} "One unit in excess of the required complement. I will log this with the annotation 'recommended for removal.'"
  - After: "Tech-Priest, one. Head..." {n}He eyes Nuncius.{/n} "One extra. Remove."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Nuncius is not subject to removal, and the removal of my own head would do little to restore your cognitive functions, layperson, even if I were to graft it onto you. There are cases, it seems, where even my skills prove powerless."
  - After: "Nuncius stays. Nothing fixes your mind, layperson."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A human torso is built into the massive cogitator. Countless cables entangle the shrivelled body and snake under the pale skin.{/n} "Identification: Rogue Trader von Valancius. At last, everything ends."
  - After: {n}A torso wired into a cogitator.{/n} "Rogue Trader von Valancius. Oblivion directive: final stage." {n}Bilious:{/n} "At last, offspring."

  - Before: {n}The man announces in a mechanical voice:{/n} "Supreme ordinance: the arrival of the head of the von Valancius dynasty with the purpose of extraction of the tithe triggers the immediate activation of the Oblivion directive by the watcher of Leethus.   - After: {n}Mechanically:{/n} "Ordinance: when the dynasty's head comes for the tithe, the Oblivion directive triggers, locked by unbreakable cogni-shackles. You get the assets; Leethus dies, blamed on Humanity's enemies."

  - Before: "At first I thought Theodora was going to pay me visits so she could gloat, but she never once appeared on the station.   - Before: "When Theodora was young, I was brought to Dargonus to be trained for the role of Seneschal. When she became the Rogue Trader, she refused to recognise me as her kin. She needed an obedient servant who wouldn't challenge her rule. Had I behaved myself, perhaps Theodora would have condescended to call me her brother and heir on her deathbed."
  - After: "I trained as her Seneschal. As Rogue Trader, she disowned me for an obedient servant."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You... are a better person than Theodora was. Do not take this as a compliment — it is an extremely detrimental quality for a Rogue Trader."
  - After: "You're better than Theodora. Bad for a Rogue Trader."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are a worthy successor to the great Theodora von Valancius, whether it pleases you or not."
  - After: "A worthy heir to Theodora, like it or not."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Then you will change nothing. The directive cannot be stopped — the cogni-shackles, once applied to the initiation systems, are unbreakable. Accept your fate, offspring. I accepted mine long ago."
  - After: "Pointless. The cogni-shackles are unbreakable. Accept it, offspring. I did."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "At least you're alone in that corridor and will never have to wonder who's banging on the door from the other side — and how long the flimsy hinges of your mind will hold."
  - After: "At least no one bangs on your mind's door."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I must refuse. The supreme ordinance states that if the head of the dynasty has declared the tithe's evacuation, I am to destroy the planet. You are the one who announced to the Arbitrators that you were taking the tithe with you. The directive has been initiated and the cogni-shackles placed. It cannot be stopped."
  - After: "No. If the dynasty's head takes the tithe, the planet dies. You told the Arbitrators. It can't be stopped."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "But you wanted her throne, didn't you? Her whole life, she was surrounded by scoundrels who envied her, ready to devour her without a second thought the moment she made a single misstep."
  - After: "But you wanted her throne. Scoundrels like you circled her."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Worthy and unyielding even under the heavy burden of power. But surely you remember, shereen, that Jae Heydari is always at your service? That is what partners are for: to share their heavy burdens between them."
  - After: "Worthy. But Jae shares your burden, shereen."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "Sisters... Such maddening creatures. At least they cause the mon-keigh just as much trouble."
  - After: "Sisters... maddening. Mon-keigh suffer them too."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "I do not know what kind of person you were, but... I feel sorry for you. To be reduced to an expensive doll, a toy in someone's hands... No one deserves such a fate."
  - After: "I pity you. An expensive doll."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Such a waste of the sacred current of the Motive Force is unacceptable. I demand the immediate cessation of this unit's vital processes without the right to atone for its personal inefficiency."
  - After: "Wasted Motive Force! Terminate this unit."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Thank the Emperor for ending this brief spell of madness. Give the order to the watcher. We have lost enough time here already."
  - After: "Thank the Emperor. Order the watcher."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne stiffens, struggling to say a word. After a long pause, he speaks slowly, almost laboriously:{/n} "You are assuming a very broad interpretation of your authority, Rogue Trader. I do not believe that even the Warrant and the alliance with the Arbites give you the authority to take control of the tithe. However, the situation with the {g|Encyclopedia:Maw}Maw{/g} is a matter of urgency, and you are the only person in the Expanse who can take on this enormous responsibility. I hereby authorise your decision, but you will have to get approval from the Marshal as well."
  - After: {n}Solomorne stiffens.{/n} "The Warrant doesn't grant the tithe. But the {g|Encyclopedia:Maw}Maw{/g} is urgent, and only you can bear this. I authorise it; the Marshal must too."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I will not authorise such a heinous violation of the Lex Imperialis." {n}Solomorne stubbornly juts out his chin.{/n} "It is within your power to plunder the tithe, but the consequences will be inevitable. Such a transgression cannot be concealed, and the Adeptus Arbites will demand answers. I have failed to convince you, but I trust the Marshal will change your mind."
  - After: "I won't authorise breaking the Lex." {n}He juts his chin.{/n} "The Marshal will change your mind."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "{name}... No, asking you to come to your senses won't do. I know you won't give up." {n}Solomorne presses a fist to his chest, his voice momentarily trembling with pain.{/n} "I will authorise your decision and assume full blame for what happens next. You may take the tithe, but do not deny me that."
  - After: "{name}... You won't give up." {n}Voice trembling:{/n} "I'll authorise it and take the blame."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes, I needed to exchange codes with the flagship in order to identify the vessel and its owner. I had to sift through onboard communication channels and systems to verify the new Lord Captain's data and {mf|his|her} right to be one."
  - After: "Yes. I checked codes with the flagship to verify {mf|his|her} claim."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne does not take his eyes off you, as if he had been hypnotised.{/n} "May the Lex strike me down! Even allowing for the Warrant and everything that you have single-handedly accomplished in the Expanse..." {n}He shakes his head, unable to break out of his stupor.{/n} "I'll be damned, but your every word rings with truth that I cannot dispute... Of all the people in this sector, you are the only one who can rightfully lay claim to the tithe, and I, Proctor Solomorne Anthar, hereby acknowledge this."
  - After: {n}Solomorne stares.{/n} "May the Lex strike me..." {n}He shakes his head.{/n} "Only you can claim the tithe. I, Proctor Solomorne Anthar, acknowledge it."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "{name}, your soft-heartedness is beyond the pale! You dare interpret the Lex Imperialis this way?" {n}Solomorne covers his face with the palm of his hand, trying to reign in his emotions.{/n} "No matter what words you may use, this is still theft, and you are asking me to be an accomplice. Throne's blood..." {n}He lowers his hand, and there is an immense weariness in his gaze.{/n} "So, you put before me a choice: the death of many worlds, or a heinous violation of His Law. I am siding with you, and may the Emperor have mercy. This crime now falls on us both, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "{name}, soft-hearted fool!" {n}He covers his face.{/n} "It's theft." {n}Weary:{/n} "Dying worlds or His Law. I side with you. This crime is ours."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I have witnessed your deeds that honour the God-Emperor, and I believe that you exercise the power of the Warrant justly — but what you are about to do is unthinkable... And you would have me risk everything: my honour, my life, and the very future of the tithe." {n}Solomorne falls silent and fixes you with his gaze.{/n} "Nevertheless, in the name of the Lex Imperialis, I hereby authorise your decision. All that remains is to pray that the rest of the Arbites see you for the same person I do: a loyal servant and a true conduit of His will."
  - After: "This is unthinkable." {n}He holds your gaze.{/n} "Still, by the Lex, I authorise it. Pray the Arbites see His servant in you, as I do."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And so, Theodora's plan is accomplished: the tithe of the Koronus Expanse now belongs to the dynasty. Whether her intentions were the same as yours, offspring, I know not, but that matters little."
  - After: "Theodora's plan is done: the tithe is the dynasty's. Whether her aims were yours matters little."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "In other words, the station is, in a manner of speaking, an augmetic of colossal proportions. A curious experiment, yet I am confident I could devise a more elegant method of achieving the same end."
  - After: "A colossal augmetic. I'd do it more elegantly."
- **Jae**
  - Before: {n}Jae lets out a whistle.{/n} "Now that's ambition — you can't even call it theft! Just an ingenious redistribution of resources on a sector scale. Ingenious and audacious..."
  - After: {n}Jae whistles.{/n} "Not theft: redistribution. Audacious!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "This qualifies for a culprit's confession, except the culprit herself is dead and judging this creature would be pointless. Still, we must decide what to do next, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "A confession, but the culprit's dead. We must decide, Rogue Trader."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "An outrageous accusation! Lady Theodora never would have sullied herself with such heresy. Stealing the sacred tithe? Never!"
  - After: "Outrageous! Theodora would never steal the tithe!"

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/TreasureWorld/TW_SpaceAssault/TW_SpaceAssault_Dialogue

  - Before: "What ships are they?"
  - After: "What ships?"

  - Before: "How did they find us? This system's coordinates are classified!"
  - After: "How'd they find us? This system is classified!"

  - After: "Prepare for battle. I'm coming."

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/TreasureWorld/TW_TankChoice/TW_TankChoice_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal, you are the best candidate."
  - After: "Pasqal, you're best."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Abelard, I entrust the tank to you!"
  - After: "Abelard, it's yours!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Lady Cassia, can you handle it?"
  - After: "Lady Cassia, can you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Sister Argenta, you know what to do."
  - After: "Sister Argenta, go."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Heinrix, can you figure it out?"
  - After: "Heinrix, can you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Jae, don't fail me now!"
  - After: "Jae, don't fail me!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Kibellah, have you ever shot from a tank?"
  - After: "Kibellah, ever shot a tank?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Solomorne, you will drive the tank."
  - After: "Solomorne, you drive."
- **Player**
  - Before: "This is a task for a Rogue Trader."
  - After: "A job for a Rogue Trader."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I know who I definitely wouldn't trust to cover me in that thing. I mean you, Solomorne."
  - After: "Not you, Solomorne. I don't trust you."
- **(conversation owner)**

See those cables and counterweights? They're what's keeping the containers suspended. We get rid of the counterweights, and the containers will fall and block the passages. Someone will have to climb into this semblance of a tank and open fire on these targets while the rest activate the shell loading system using the cogitators and hold off the enemies. Choose who will man the tank."
  - After: {n}Solomorne turns.{/n} "Shoot those cable counterweights; the containers drop and block their reinforcements. One takes the tank, the rest load shells at the cogitators and hold. Who?"

- **Marazhai**

  - After: {n}Jae smirks.{/n} "Private Heydari reporting!"

- **(conversation owner)**

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/VigilPalace/VP_Greetings/VP_Greetings_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Are there any other such institutions elsewhere in my protectorate?"
  - After: "Are there other such institutions in my protectorate?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What kinds of cases are usually heard here?"
  - After: "What cases are heard here?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You are greeted by an impeccably dressed man with a perfectly straight back. An Arbites scale emblem is embroidered on his clothes.{/n} "Glory to House von Valancius! We are honoured to welcome you to the Palace of Justice, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Do you wish to proceed to the session at once, or will you grace me with any questions I might humbly answer?"
  - After: {n}A prim Arbites official greets you.{/n} "Welcome to the Palace of Justice, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Begin now, or ask first?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. As is the case with the rest of the Imperium, worlds make do with the traditional method: the accused are not allowed to say a word, and executions are carried out as ordered by planetary authorities or by powerful organisations of the Imperium. Only here on Dargonus does such an unusual ceremony exist — Benefaz von Valancius was known for his eccentricities. It is said that he invented this system himself and started this glorious tradition in which you are to take part today."
  - After: "No, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Elsewhere the accused stay silent. Only Dargonus has this ceremony, Benefaz von Valancius's invention."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This is the Palace of Justice: the ninth residence of House von Valancius, erected by your esteemed ancestor Benefaz von Valancius and handed over by Theodora von Valancius — ever may she bask in the Throne's radiance — to the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusArbitesGlossary}Adeptus Arbites{/g} and the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratumGlossary}Administratum{/g} for judiciary use. Cases of special interest are heard at this Palace. Sentences are carried out here also."
  - After: "The Palace of Justice, built by Benefaz, given by Theodora to the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusArbitesGlossary}Adeptus Arbites{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratumGlossary}Administratum{/g}. Special cases are tried here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Only the most important ones that involve the interests of the highest-born persons and prominent factions of the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g}: disputes between noble houses that go on for generations; conflicts between the God-Emperor's servants who are vested with authority and whose disagreements affect trade and security in the protectorate; and other litigations of supreme significance!"
  - After: "Only the gravest: feuds of nobles and great factions of the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g}."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "The cases litigated at the Palace of Justice quite literally concern matters of life and death. In such instances, there is always a guilty party whose lies, connivances, or negligence have caused damage to the protectorate. The task of the judge is to establish guilt and pass a stern sentence, as order cannot be imposed without these, or without summary executions."
  - After: "Life and death. Someone is always guilty. The judge finds guilt and sentences sternly."

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/VigilPalace/VP_PrefectTrial

- **Player**
  - Before: "Marshal Strachs! You have heard my arguments and the prefect's distorted version of the truth. Do you require yet more information before you denounce the real culprit?"
  - After: "Marshal Strachs! You've heard us both. Need more before you denounce the real culprit?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "By the God-Emperor's will, the von Valancius dynasty was granted a Warrant of Trade. Go against me, and you go against the God-Emperor. Marshal Strachs and Prefect Vultur are hereby sentenced to death. Those who aided and abetted them in this plot will share the same fate."
  - After: "The God-Emperor granted my dynasty its Warrant. Defy me, defy Him. Strachs and Vultur are sentenced to death, with all who aided them."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Arbitrators! Vultur and Strachs believe that the Lex Imperialis is but a collection of letters and forms to be played with as they please. They believe that you must blindly follow their orders. But whom do you defend? Humanity or these prefects? I call upon you to stand with me in the name of Humanity, not the soulless machine of the Administratum!"
  - After: "Arbitrators! Vultur and Strachs toy with the Lex Imperialis and demand blind obedience. Whom do you defend? Stand with me for Humanity, not the Administratum's machine!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your evidence, arguments, witnesses, and even the Lex Imperialis are just a pathetic attempt to gain the upper hand over someone like me. There is only one law in the Expanse and I am it! And I sentence you all to death for insubordination!"
  - After: "Your evidence and Lex are pathetic. There is one law in the Expanse: me! I sentence you all to death for insubordination!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do apologise for putting a brain in your mechanical soldier's head."
  - After: "Sorry for putting a brain in your mechanical soldier's head."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Solomorne is his own master — I do not choose for him. But if you think that an Arbitrator's tenets can be so easily broken by any passing stranger, then you insult the very core of the Adeptus Arbites."
  - After: "Solomorne chooses for himself. If any stranger can break an Arbitrator's tenets, you insult the Adeptus Arbites."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You can lie and implicate me all you want. But I will not forgive you for using Solomorne and Glaito like this."
  - After: "Implicate me all you want. I won't forgive you using Solomorne and Glaito."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Those words were indeed spoken in our conversations. Our private conversations."
  - After: "Those words were spoken. In our private conversations."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Very well, let's do it your way."
  - After: "Very well, your way."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The right to judge is granted by the God-Emperor. Can you swear that at this moment you are guided by the Lex Imperialis and not someone else's intent?"
  - After: "The God-Emperor grants the right to judge. Swear you follow the Lex Imperialis, not another's intent."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It is a difficult thing to admit that one is in the wrong, Marshal. You have stumbled by putting your trust in Vultur, but I have faith that you will make the right choice now."
  - After: "Admitting error is hard, Marshal. You trusted Vultur, but I believe you'll choose rightly now."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You have demonstrated clearly that your vaunted Lex is worth nothing — you bend and mould the law to suit your desires. And yet, power is so intoxicating, so difficult to give up... Am I wrong, Strachs?"
  - After: "Your Lex is worthless; you bend it to your desires. And power is so hard to give up... Am I wrong, Strachs?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You should have joined my side while you still had the chance."
  - After: "You should have joined me while you could."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Attempting to manipulate the Marshal's sense of professional pride. Recorded and added to the case."
  - After: "Manipulating the Marshal. Recorded."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Disrespect toward the doctrine of the esteemed Adeptus Arbites has been recorded."
  - After: "Disrespect to Arbites recorded."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The prefect straightens in her chair with such force that you hear the arduous grinding of her implants. Her voice is cold and slightly tremulous:{/n} "Decree GC-781/89, Supplement 982. For tithe theft, participation in foul sorcery, and other crimes against the Imperium {name} von Valancius is sentenced to death. The property of the dynasty is hereby confiscated and placed under the oversight of the Adeptus Administratum. Any last words, convict?"
  - After: {n}The prefect stiffens.{/n} "Decree GC-781/89, Supplement 982: for tithe theft and sorcery, {name} von Valancius dies. Last words?"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Stop, {name}. The Arbites were following Strachs's orders, following the law. To condemn them just for that is unfair. Show them the leniency that you once showed me, or else this long road we have travelled together will have been for nothing."
  - After: "Stop, {name}. They obeyed the law. Show them the mercy you showed me."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Surprisingly moderate words after all we have seen. You will not restore order this way. Now is the time for harsh and decisive measures, or else your subjects and allies will continue to rebel against you."
  - After: "Too soft. Only harshness ends rebellion."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "No, {name}. What you are proposing is not the God-Emperor's justice. You are distorting the Lex Imperialis and placing your own ego above all else, even His will. I cannot accept this outcome."
  - After: "No, {name}. That's your ego, not His justice. I refuse."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Then our paths diverge. I will find a way to rectify the flagrant violations of the Lex Imperialis, but without you, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "Then I go on without you, Rogue Trader."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne turns to the Arbitrators. The Proctor's eyes are blazing, his voice thundering with unusual passion:{/n} "Arbitrators of the Adeptus Arbites, by turning against the prefect and the Marshal, you will not be in violation of the Lex Imperialis, on the contrary — we are governed by the Emperor's will alone, and He is pleased by order and stability on His vassal worlds. We must not allow this crude power grab to succeed. Our task is to protect the legitimate ruler of the protectorate and to restore justice."
  - After: {n}Solomorne turns to the Arbitrators.{/n} "The Emperor wants order. Stop this power grab! Protect the rightful ruler!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Everyone who sided with Vultur and Strachs must die. They have earned neither mercy nor the privilege of a trial. Their execution will be a lesson to anyone who would ever again attempt to assassinate a Rogue Trader or manipulate the Lex Imperialis."
  - After: "Their allies die untried. A lesson."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "For Prefect Vultur and Marshal Strachs, the sentence for attempting to pervert the Lex Imperialis is death. The others must face your judgement in accordance with the Emperor's Law."
  - After: "Death for Vultur and Strachs. Judge the rest."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "The Rogue Trader is right. If the Arbitrator has dared to stray from the Lex, then he never was an Arbitrator. The fault lies with me for not seeing the weakness in his heart in time."
  - After: "The Rogue Trader is right. He was never an Arbitrator."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I must refuse. Marshal Gregoras Strachs, I charge you with treason against the Imperium and conspiring with a heretic! Fangs of the Expanse, to battle!"
  - After: "I refuse. Strachs, traitor! Fangs of the Expanse, attack!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Glaito looks at Solomorne and lets out a grinding whimper. The Proctor sighs heavily, covering his eyes with his hand.{/n} "Fine... To the void with it! Unlike the Marshal, you haven't failed me yet."
  - After: {n}Glaito whimpers.{/n} "Fine... You haven't failed me yet."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne casts you a look of gratitude.{/n} "Don't waste your breath, Rogue Trader. She'll get her due."
  - After: {n}Solomorne nods gratefully.{/n} "She'll get her due."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A moment of silence. Suddenly, one by one, the Arbitrators raise their weapons and point them at the Marshal and the prefect.{/n}
  - After: {n}One by one, the Arbitrators aim at Strachs and Vultur.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your words fall on deaf ears. No Arbitrator moves from where they stand.{/n}
  - After: {n}No Arbitrator moves.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I will appeal to the Arbitrators — I'm sure many of them are already convinced that the prefect is manipulating the Lex Imperialis for her own ends."
  - After: "I'll appeal to the Arbitrators. Many already doubt the prefect."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne nods and raises his weapon.{/n} "Glaito, ready!"
  - After: {n}Solomorne raises his weapon.{/n} "Glaito, ready!"
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "Your words have been heard, Rogue Trader. However, you are the real criminal now. You stole the Expanse's tithe, of which there is irrefutable evidence including the testimony of Proctor Anthar; therefore you are to be punished to the fullest extent of the Lex Imperialis."

  - After: "Our paths diverge, {name}."

  - After: "Even if the prefect's guilty, your charges stand."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "Are those your last words?"
  - After: "Your last words?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Inscribia heaves in a breath, ready to launch into a vehement tirade, but the Marshal raises his right hand and everyone falls silent.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Marshal raises a hand, silencing Inscribia.{/n}
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**

When my every action became subject to your avaricious schemes rather than the Lex.   - After: "Enough. Vultur, you served your greed." {n}Strachs clenches his fist.{/n} "You made me a puppet!"
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "Prefect Inscribia Vultur. You are charged with fraud, attempted assassination of the Emperor's anointed, and undermining the foundations of the Lex Imperialis. Surrender now and accept a dignified death."
  - After: "Prefect Inscribia Vultur, you're charged with fraud and attempted murder. Surrender and die with dignity."

  - Before: "Heretic! Traitor! Marshal, execute them! All of them!"
  - After: "Heretic! Traitor! Marshal, execute them all!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Anyone who dares to join the heretic is condemned to death! Marshal, carry out the sentence!"
  - After: "Heretic's allies die too! Marshal, execute them!"
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "Arbitrators. The sentence is death. Carry it out."
  - After: "Arbitrators. Carry out the death sentence."
