  - After: "Lady Molles-Secundas dies for forgery! Arbitrators, carry it out!"
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: {n}As the last attendants leave the courtroom, the prefect turns to you with a delighted expression.{/n} "Lady Theodora held court sessions like this to strengthen her subjects' faith in the Lex Imperialis and their fear of breaching it. A most useful practice, wouldn't you agree?"
  - After: {n}The prefect beams.{/n} "Lady Theodora held these sessions to instil fear of the law. Useful, no?"
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "Of course, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I dare not take up any more of your time."
  - After: "Of course, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I won't keep you."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "Your enthusiasm is laudable, but, as I'm sure you understand, any manner of procedure requires prior registration — which, in turn, involves filling out official forms and signing regulation-approved documents. It is for this reason that I am, alas, unable to honour your request. With your permission, I will now return to my duties. Thank you."
  - After: "Laudable, but cases need prior registration. Alas. Good day."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "Delivering justice is incredibly demanding work that requires in-depth knowledge of the Lex Imperialis. Today, you merely touched upon a small fragment of this sacrament. Thank you for your participation. And now, it is time for me to return to my duties. Good day to you."
  - After: "Justice is demanding. You touched only a fragment. Good day."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "That is correct. In addition, he insists on your subjects bearing witness to it — as a lesson to them, so to speak. To refuse a cardinal is impious in itself, but to execute one who is a saint in all but name..."
  - After: "Correct, publicly. Refusing a cardinal is impious, but executing a near-saint..."
- **Court Administrator**
  - Before: "All arguments have been acknowledged. Let the Rogue Trader's verdict be delivered."
  - After: "Arguments heard. The Rogue Trader's verdict."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: {n}A modicum of respect can be glimpsed in the prefect's gaze in your direction.{/n} "A very balanced decision. It sets a precedent that, through reasoning by analogy, will help in optimising other court cases on Dargonus."
  - After: {n}A hint of respect.{/n} "Balanced. A useful precedent."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, without a Choirmaster, the power of Dargonus's Astropaths would be significantly diminished. Unless a worthy replacement is found for Master Pras, he cannot be executed." {n}The Seneschal frowns.{/n} "There is a Chorda world that owes us an old debt which can be repaid with a seasoned Astropath. We can make the request, although it would leave the planet in question with barely any means of communication."
  - After: "Without its Choirmaster, Dargonus's Choir weakens. Pras needs a replacement." {n}Abelard frowns.{/n} "A Chorda world owes us an Astropath, though it'd leave them nearly mute."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "If Lady Molles-Secundas is right, then her children are the impostor's accomplices and are guilty of defaming the authenticity of Administratum documents." {n}Now Solomorne has enough sang-froid in him for a regiment.{/n} "Let the woman know that her heirs must face the same fate as the criminal, for so stipulates the Emperor's Law."
  - After: "If she's right, her children are accomplices." {n}Solomorne, ice-cold.{/n} "By the Emperor's Law, they share the criminal's fate."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira hugs herself, rocking back and forth.{/n} "No more does the blind man listen to the distant light... Concealed behind the false gold, abomination lies at his heart, and it's burning, burning, burning!" {n}The psyker's entire body shudders.{/n} "Oh my, Lord Captain. Looks like our Astropath really is lost to corruption. I swear he's hiding something under that robe of his — either an amulet or some unholy mark! And those rabid zealots are going to find it on him, alive or dead. But the little voices are laughing, saying you may kill the traitor but don't expect any good to come of it..."
  - After: {n}Idira shudders.{/n} "Behind false gold, abomination burns! The Astropath's corrupted, Lord Captain. But the voices laugh: kill him, yet expect no good of it..." {n}She rocks.{/n}
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "The {g|Encyclopedia:AstropathGlossary}Astropathic Choir{/g} hardly needs an introduction. They are some of the most valuable servants of the Imperium, without whom any and all communication between your worlds would collapse. The Dargonus Choir took horrific casualties in the recent major warp storm. Master Pras made an enormous effort to at least partially restore communication. While we may not have proof of his innocence, Pras's dedication to his duty is beyond doubt." {n}The old woman locks her shrivelled fingers together.{/n} "As you can see, this is an intricate situation."
  - After: "The {g|Encyclopedia:AstropathGlossary}Astropathic Choir{/g} links your worlds. Pras laboured to restore it after the storm. Innocence unproven, dedication certain." {n}She knots her fingers.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Choirmaster Weisz has known Master Pras for quite a long time.   - After: "Weisz says Pras's images grew anxious and detached, maybe from the {g|Encyclopedia:WarpGlossary}warp storm{/g}, but something still sets them apart."

  - Before: "Unfortunately, Acting Choirmaster Qadd is unable to present any reliable information. He barely knows Master Pras, and the late Zacchary Weisz never provided a detailed assessment of the Astropath you are asking about."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You see clearly now that no matter what decision you make, it will backfire on you. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You have no way of knowing what the correct decision should be. This does look like a complicated case.{/n}
  - After: {n}You can't tell the right choice.{/n}
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "Spoken like a true heir to Lady Theodora, who could squeeze gold out of a rock. Sister Juth would never recant her statement. She will have no choice but to accept your conditions."
  - After: "Worthy of Lady Theodora. Sister Juth won't recant; she must accept."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Situation analysis complete. Let the paradox cease; let functionality triumph. Suggestion: use the unit Cardinal Anvylas's organic remains to construct a servo-skull herald and place it in an automated chapel. The status of sainthood will be extended to the liturgical mechanism."
  - After: "Suggestion: make Cardinal Anvylas's remains a servo-skull herald in an automated chapel. Sainthood transfers to the mechanism."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta shakes her head.{/n} "Wise counsel is required here, and it is not to be found within these walls. Reverend Hieronymus would understand the workings of the cardinal's soul. Entrust him to the good shepherd of the Drusians."
  - After: {n}Argenta shakes her head.{/n} "Entrust him to Reverend Hieronymus of the Drusians."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "The head of the Drusians would hardly deny the cardinal's peculiar request. However, the matter will be outside our jurisdiction at that point, and Reverend Hieronymus will appreciate your high trust in him when it comes to questions of faith."
  - After: "He'd grant it. Out of our jurisdiction, and he'll value your trust."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "How could the woman have possibly known for sure her husband would make it out of a major dustup like that? The business had ground to a halt, so she took things in her own hands. Actually, shereen, on Efreet you're allowed to take several spouses precisely in case this happens. It would be a trifle for you to amend the laws of Lady Molles-Secundas's homeworld. Let her continue to fill your coffers — she's more than able to handle two husbands!"
  - After: "Business stalled, so she acted. Shereen, Efreet allows several spouses for this. Amend her homeworld's laws; she can handle two husbands!"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix rubs the bridge of his nose, looking tired.{/n} "This absurdity has dragged on for too long... So be it. The Emperor as my witness, I am reluctant to revisit my early training experience in the Administratum, but I am going to have to. Does Lady Molles-Secundas have a paper that certifies she is alive? If not, the defendant is to be deemed dead, with all that entails."
  - After: {n}Heinrix sighs.{/n} "Fine. Does Lady Molles-Secundas have a paper certifying she's alive? If not, she's dead."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Lady Molles-Secundas's talents are self-evident — she could easily boost production on any planet. What might be called her promotion under the guise of punishment would bring tangible benefits. You just so happen to think of several backwater worlds that have good potential but lack the capable stewardship to match it.{/n}
  - After: {n}Her talent is obvious: 'punish' her with backwater worlds needing stewardship.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As much as you would like to turn the situation to your advantage, you cannot think of a solution.{/n}
  - After: {n}You find no advantage here.{/n}
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "Well, a gesture like that is certain to reverberate throughout the protectorate, but a verdict is a verdict. This session is now concluded!"
  - After: "That will echo, but a verdict is a verdict. Session concluded!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Both parties have shown disrespect for the Imperium's authority. The Doleful Host is engaging in mob justice, and the defendant did not even deign to stand trial in person. Sentence them both to death — that would be the optimal outcome."
  - After: "Both defy Imperial authority: mob justice, and a no-show. Execute both."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: {n}The dumbstruck prefect opens and closes her mouth like a fish out of water.{/n} "I... am struggling to comment on that. Will somebody share the incredible news with Lady Molles-Secundas? This session is now concluded!"
  - After: {n}The prefect gapes.{/n} "I... Someone tell Lady Molles-Secundas. Session concluded!"
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "Lady Molles-Secundas will depart for her place of exile before today ends. Arbitrators, carry out the sentence!"
  - After: "She leaves for exile today. Arbitrators, carry it out!"
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "As you wish." {n}The prefect's dry fingers tap quickly on her data-slate. Soon afterward, she looks up from the vid-screen and says in a colourless voice,{/n} "Lady Molles-Secundas has confessed to bribing an Administratum official and is pleading for her offspring to be spared."
  - After: "As you wish." {n}She taps her slate.{/n} "Lady Molles-Secundas confesses to bribing an official, and begs mercy for her children."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The indignant prefect shakes her head energetically.{/n} "She is a mother trying to save her children! That may have been a false confession! And, what is worse, a false accusation against the sacred service of the Administratum!"
  - After: {n}The prefect shakes her head.{/n} "A mother saving her children! A false confession slandering the Administratum!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The old woman presses her lips into a thin line.{/n} "Perish the thought. Your position as an Emperor-blessed judge is unquestionable."
  - After: {n}Lips thin.{/n} "Never. Your judgement is unquestionable."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "No. Such a verdict will remind your subjects that only the Rogue Trader has the right to administer justice. That is why I advise you to be stern — the Lex is on your side."
  - After: "No. Justice is yours alone. Leniency breeds vigilantes or heretics. Be stern."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "I imagine the verdict will horrify the cardinal, but on the other hand, centuries from now, his followers will still be able to listen to his recorded sermons and worship his remains with the same fanatical zeal as in the notional saint's lifetime. Expect generous donations toward the construction of the automated chapel, since many will want to have a part in such a momentous event."
  - After: "He'll be horrified, but his flock will hear him for centuries. Expect donations for the chapel."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "The Bloodspun Web is knowledgeable in ways to torment one's flesh without going to the Undying One before due time. Domin, allow us to help Cardinal Anvylas attain enlightenment and experience the purity of a near-death state. Undergoing our rite should make him realise it is not in his gift to sever his own thread."
  - After: "Domin, let the Bloodspun Web bring Cardinal Anvylas near death. He'll learn his thread isn't his to sever."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "This is a complicated situation, but... Lady Molles-Secundas was acting in the Imperium's interests. She had shouldered the duty of care for the family business, and was in no position to wallow in her grief for cycles upon cycles." {n}Cassia throws back her shoulders and says in a dignified voice,{/n} "A marriage between people of noble birth is a union of two servants of the Emperor. Duty toward the Imperium is at the heart of that union. If there comes a long period of time when one of the spouses is unable to fulfil their obligations, the marriage loses its meaning. If you could codify this understanding in law, that would help resolve this situation."
  - After: "She served the Imperium; she couldn't grieve forever." {n}Cassia straightens.{/n} "Noble marriage is duty. Make that law."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "This sounds like a decision that is favourable in the eyes of the Emperor. Moreover, I imagine it will make kidnappings for ransom substantially rarer. This session is now concluded!"
  - After: "Pleasing to the Emperor, and fewer ransom kidnappings. Session concluded!"
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "Again? I'm afraid they have already said what they had to say and are humbly awaiting their fate. Whatever questions you have, you may pose to me."
  - After: "Again? They've spoken. Ask me instead."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "If that is the Astropath I am thinking of, the Dargonus Choir is going to be headed by a much stronger psyker than Pras. That will definitely improve communication between the protectorate's worlds."
  - After: "A far stronger psyker than Pras. Communications will improve."
- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**
  - Before: "A harsh verdict, but from now on your subjects will hardly dare escalate situations to the point of open clashes — in cases similar to this one, of course."
  - After: "Harsh, but it will deter open clashes."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The cardinal was quite desperate to be relieved of his mortal life. But now that both the Ecclesiarchy and the Rogue Trader have refused him, he has no choice but to remain a living paragon of holiness."

- **Prefect Inscribia Vultur**

  - Before: "A loose description of the events, and yet one that is remarkably close to the truth. Surely you do not think that Lady Molles-Secundas herself orchestrated her husband's kidnapping? Although, one might say you are an {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}expert{/d} on such incidents."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}In your days {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Ministorum}serving as an archdeacon{/d}, you resolved far more precarious religious disputes than this. The cardinal has admitted to his intention of killing a great and righteous man, and that is enough for you to render a decisive verdict.{/n}

You immediately hatch an audacious plan: send Lady Molles-Secundas to one of the fringe worlds under the pretext of exile and have her set up the production of rations there.{/n}

  - Before: "The protectorate isn't yours, and it never was. Have you not read your own Warrant, even once? The limitless potential of the protectorate is wasted in the hands of spoilt fools... And I am tired of watching you desecrate the very foundations of the Imperium. If it weren't for you, the protectorate would be operating for the good of the Throne as impeccably as a sacred machine of the Omnissiah!"

  - Before: {n}The prefect's eyes narrow spitefully. She opens her mouth to say something but is cut off before she can utter a single word.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Inscribia Vultur gives no reply — she meets her death with her head proudly raised and her lips pursed in contempt.{/n}
  - After: {n}Vultur dies head high, contemptuous.{/n}

  - Before: {n}The prefect grimaces.{/n} "To be spared for the rest of my life from having to watch you bring the Imperium's territories to ruin? That is a reward, Rogue Trader. But I suppose you are right — cataloguing shipment chronicles is an art long overdue for some rigorous supervision, and none except me in your entire domain is capable of performing this function adequately."
  - After: {n}She grimaces.{/n} "Spared watching you ruin things? A reward. Only I can keep those records anyway."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vultur chuckles.{/n} "Never. The counterparty always bends the terms to its advantage..."
  - After: {n}Vultur chuckles.{/n} "Never."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**

  - After: {n}Fist to chest:{/n} "Your judgement is final. Find the Arbites a better Marshal."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}Strachs instantly snaps in a steely voice,{/n} "No. I have shamed the Adeptus Arbites by yielding to Prefect Vultur's manipulation. I have betrayed the Lex Imperialis, the very law I was duty-bound to uphold. I am guilty. I insist that you pass the sentence and carry it out immediately."
  - After: {n}Strachs snaps,{/n} "No. I yielded to Vultur and betrayed the Lex. Sentence me now."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I accept death for staying loyal to the true Lex Imperialis, and I do so without regrets. My only request is this: take care of Glaito." {n}Solomorne closes his eyes and shouts a command:{/n} "Rejection protocol: leave DX-1. Farewell... my friend."
  - After: "I die loyal to the Lex. Take care of Glaito." {n}He commands:{/n} "Rejection protocol: leave DX-1. Farewell... my friend."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}For a time, Solomorne says nothing.{/n} "I admit defeat. I admit that you are a Rogue Trader, one who is beyond my judgement. I gratefully accept my pardon and swear an oath of service to you."
  - After: {n}Silence.{/n} "I admit defeat. You're beyond my judgement. I swear to serve you."
- **Solomorne**

Otherwise, we Arbitrators will not accept these changes. Until my official assignment, though, I will lead as acting head of the Adeptus Arbites."
  - After: "It takes time. Without precedent, we need a new procedure. Until then, I'm acting head."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Arbitrators accept your decision stoically: no one says a word in protest, no one reaches for their weapon.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Arbitrators accept it in silence.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I will personally see to the execution of your order, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "I'll see to it personally, Rogue Trader."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A whisper runs through the room, turning slowly into a murmur of approval. No one dares resist the will of the newly proclaimed sole judge of the Koronus Expanse.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The rest of the room stands still, all eyes turned to you. The final verdict. What you say next will decide the fate of not just the Adeptus Arbites, but of justice in the Koronus Expanse as a whole.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Only the guilty try to defend themselves, whereas I acted in the interests of the Imperium. - **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}Without waiting for you to address him, Marshal Strachs does not plead so much as give you an order:{/n} "Judge me, {name}. Now that the dust has settled, I can see everything clearly. I thought my actions were in service to the Lex, but in truth, only one person has ever benefitted from them. That mistake deserves no pardon, and I have earned my punishment."
  - After: {n}Strachs all but orders you:{/n} "Judge me, {name}. Vultur used me to seize your protectorate. I earned punishment."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne bows his head low.{/n} "I am grateful... for us both. Farewell, Rogue Trader. May none but the Emperor Himself be your judge."
  - After: {n}Solomorne bows.{/n} "Thank you, for us both. May only the Emperor judge you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The last shreds of the dog's mind contained in the body of a living weapon compel him to be with his master. Though too wounded to run at full speed, Glaito dashes forward nonetheless, his blood drenching the cold stone floor of the palace.{/n}

- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne goes quiet as a statue. Slowly, in a voice that does not sound like his own, he says,{/n} "Order received, Rogue Trader."
  - After: {n}Solomorne goes still.{/n} "Order received, Rogue Trader."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Before the sound of the cannon blast can subside, you hear the clanging of metal claws and a howl of rage.{/n}
  - After: {n}As the blast fades: clanging claws, a howl of rage.{/n}
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal looks directly at you, with a strange emptiness in his eyes.{/n} "I see. Not only has the Rogue Trader turned out to be a criminal, but Vultur as well. However, I am the one most to blame for what happened, having been swayed by the manipulations of one heretic while failing to stop another violator of the Lex Imperialis. Rogue Trader, if you have a shred of honour left, have me executed, and may the Emperor judge my soul."
  - After: {n}Empty eyes.{/n} "So you're a criminal too. But I'm most to blame. If you have honour, execute me."

  - After: "Inglorious, but... I won't be alone. Thank you for Glaito."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Among the broken fragments of the great scales and the burning Arbites banners, the people kneel as one. The verdict has been announced. Whatever the future may hold, one thing is certain: the Koronus Expanse will not be the same.{/n}

- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "Even in this, you went against the Emperor's Law. But I accept the sentence." {n}The Marshal presses a fist to his chest and solemnly declares,{/n} "May He shorten my days; may He summon me to His judgement."
  - After: "Against the Emperor's Law again. But I accept." {n}Fist to chest:{/n} "May He summon me to His judgement."
- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: {n}Strachs presses a fist to his chest and solemnly declares,{/n} "And your judgement is final. I was protecting the Lex Imperialis and its guardians. I erred on that path. May the Emperor send the Arbites a worthier Marshal."
  - After: {n}Fist to chest:{/n} "Your judgement is final. I erred. May the Arbites get a worthier Marshal."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You might have understood my perspective. The way you managed to expose my plans before the trial confirms your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}extraordinary intelligence{/d}. But it is poisoned by your self-interest, which makes it all the more painful for me to lose this battle of wits for power."
  - After: "Exposing me proves your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}extraordinary intelligence{/d}. Pity it serves only you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Marshal meets his death with dignity, standing tall as befits an Arbitrator. A flash of melta imprints his silhouette on your retinas. When you open your eyes again, Gregoras Strachs is gone.{/n}

- **Marshal Gregoras Strachs**
  - Before: "I consider this measure unduly lenient, but I have no right to protest your decision." {n}The Marshal brings a closed fist to his chest and adds solemnly,{/n} "For your judgement is final."
  - After: "Too lenient, but I can't protest." {n}Fist to chest:{/n} "Your judgement is final."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As the weapon roars, Inscribia Vultur's body is reduced to dust.{/n}
  - After: {n}The weapon roars; Vultur turns to dust.{/n}
- **Solomorne**

## DLC/DLC2/Narrative/VoidshipBridge/FirstInvestigation/VB_InvestigationFirst_ktc

- **Player**
  - Before: "How did a criminal from Calixis find his way onto my ship?"
  - After: "How did a Calixis criminal get on my ship?"

  - Before: "Solomorne, why are you so certain that this is the man you're seeking?"
  - After: "Solomorne, why are you sure it's him?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Ravor, did you know about this?"
  - After: "Ravor, did you know?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Accused, do you have anything to say?"
  - After: "Accused, anything to say?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Ravor, this talented voidsman is your responsibility. Should he commit any misdeeds henceforth, you will have to answer for them."
  - After: "Ravor, he's your responsibility. His misdeeds are yours to answer for."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not trust this man to remain in the Master Helmsman's crew... but I cannot allow such talent to go to waste. Hand him over to the Factotum, he will find a use for him."
  - After: "Not in the helm crew, but don't waste him. Give him to the Factotum."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The fugitive criminal must be punished. Execute him."
  - After: "The fugitive must be punished. Execute him."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Cease any 'investigations' behind my back. If I hear of such a thing again, Arbitrator, you will be put off this ship — and not via shuttle, but through the airlock."
  - After: "No more 'investigations' behind my back, Arbitrator, or you leave through the airlock."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why did you unleash a cyber-mastiff on my subjects, Solomorne?"
  - After: "Why set a cyber-mastiff on my subjects, Solomorne?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "It is not for you, Solomorne, to judge a man trying to escape the claws of dishonour. They tried to write me off once too. Let the voidsman be — I won't say it again."
  - After: "Don't judge a man fleeing dishonour, Solomorne. They wrote me off too. Let him be."
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**
  - Before: "Lord Cap'n, I beg you to look into this outrage! This cyber-horror nearly chewed up my assistants — and one of them's been left without two of his fingers. Instead of calming his beast, the Arbitrator attacked my crewman!"
  - After: "Lord Cap'n, outrage! That cyber-horror maimed my men, and the Arbitrator attacked one!"
- **Solomorne**

He is accused of subverting {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGlossary}sacred tithe{/g} shipments, smuggling, kidnapping the Imperium's subjects, and bribing officials. Were we not on your flagship, I would have executed the heretic on the spot, but here, you are the authority, and you are the court."
  - After: {n}Solomorne:{/n} "He's wanted for subverting {g|Encyclopedia:TitheGlossary}sacred tithe{/g}, smuggling, kidnapping, bribery. You are the court here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}With an impassive gesture, Solomorne points at the condemned man — and the cyber-mastiff launches himself off the deck.{/n}
  - After: {n}Solomorne points; the cyber-mastiff leaps.{/n}
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**
  - Before: {n}A deep crease runs down the Master Helmsman's forehead.{/n} "You're throwing away a crewman, Lord Captain... for what? To indulge that lump? Well, have it your way."
  - After: {n}Ravor frowns.{/n} "Wasting a crewman for that lump? Fine."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Because I was personally involved in tracking down and purging the Shadows of the Abyss crime syndicate to which the perpetrator belongs. The case was in {g|Encyclopedia:CalixisGlossary}Calixis{/g}, on the world of Helvica Prime, but for Arbitrators, time and distance do not mitigate guilt."
  - After: "I helped purge his syndicate, Shadows of the Abyss, on Helvica Prime in {g|Encyclopedia:CalixisGlossary}Calixis{/g}."
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**
  - Before: "If I went sticking my beak into the pasts of every one of the hundreds of people in the crew, I wouldn't have time to steer your ship. All I know is that when everything went to groxshit on Rykad Minoris, this one oversaw the work at the docks so that the fools didn't trample each other to death in their panic. And later he ran into a friend at the port on Footfall, and they found us some parts within a day. He's even got arms growing out of the right places. He might make it to junior helmsman, if he keeps it up."
  - After: "I don't dig into pasts. He kept order on Rykad Minoris and found parts on Footfall."
- **Convicted Voidsman**
  - Before: {n}The long-haired voidsman flinches when you address him.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, the governor of Helvica Prime was a scumbag who abhorred the light of the God-Emperor — the things he did to the people under him... We only survived by stealing from him, or else we'd have ended up in a corpse pit, like one in four did after a distribution station accident. But once I'd got out of there, that was it, I was out of that business for good. And when I found myself in your service, I realised that it was a gift of fate, and I'd be a fool if I didn't repay such good fortune with my wholehearted toil..."
  - After: {n}He flinches.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, Helvica Prime's governor was a monster; we stole to survive. That's behind me. I'll serve well..."

  - Before: {n}The voidsman's face pales and he falls to his knees.{/n}
  - After: {n}The voidsman pales and kneels.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Rogue Trader, will you carry out the sentence yourself, or do you order me to deliver justice?"
  - After: "Will you do it, or shall I?"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "The bastard tried to run when he saw me. His fellow crew members hesitated and didn't make way for me — there was no time to find out if they were abetting the perpetrator or just panicking, so I had to use Glaito for suppression purposes."
  - After: "He ran; his crewmates blocked me, so I used Glaito."
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**
  - Before: {n}The Master Helmsman shoots a look of naked dislike at Solomorne.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ravor glares at Solomorne.{/n}
- **Convicted Voidsman**
  - Before: {n}The man's eyes fill with tears of gratitude.{/n} "You understand... You know what it's like {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}to rise from the ashes{/d} to a new life. I swear I'll write over my past with hard work!"
  - After: {n}Grateful tears.{/n} "You know how {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}to rise from the ashes{/d}. I'll redeem myself!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "The man before you is the former captain of a smuggling ship owned by the syndicate. Check the heretic's left arm — every syndicate member had a distinctive implant by which they recognised each other. It was that implant's signature that Glaito picked up on during his patrols."
  - After: "He captained their smuggler. Their implant is in his left arm; Glaito sensed it."
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**
  - Before: "Yes, Lord Cap'n." {n}Ravor's disgruntled grimace momentarily dissipates.{/n}
  - After: "Yes, Lord Cap'n." {n}Ravor eases.{/n}
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**
  - Before: "Give my best crewman to that... bureaucrat to use as an errand boy? I'd rather see him fed to the dog, honestly..."
  - After: "My best man as that bureaucrat's errand boy? Better feed him to the dog..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The criminal manages to sigh a few words of prayer as you draw your weapon.{/n}
  - After: {n}He prays as you draw.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "He was among the servants sent to you by Governor Medineh."
  - After: "He came with Governor Medineh's servants."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ravor looks grimly at the body.{/n} "Well, Lord Cap'n, I'll try to find a replacement for the poor sod. I hope your lawman doesn't go after the next one."
  - After: {n}Ravor eyes the body.{/n} "I'll replace him. Hope the lawman spares the next."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Then this case is closed. With your permission, I will return to my duties."
  - After: "Case closed. Back to my duties."
- **Solomorne**

  - After: {n}Silent disappointment rolls off him.{/n}

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/ColonyChronicles/Zarkov/Zarkov_Part_1/Zarkov_Part_1_dialogue

  - After: "Has this happened before?"

  - After: "Solomorne, your plan. Organize defences and strike teams."

  - After: "Burn and poison this world with promethium and chem-bombs."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Soon, within the root system of Zarkov, entire bastions of plasteel and adamantine rose. However, their defensive lines were not directed outward, but inward. The fighting was bloody and ferocious, yet, despite the losses, the Drovers were nearly exterminated.{/n}

  - After: {n}The lances never missed. Abelard praised the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperialNavyGlossary}Imperial Navy{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:AstraMilitarumGlossary}Astra Militarum{/g} cooperation.{/n}

The moment the expedition set about destroying them, entire swarms of Drovers rushed into the depths of Zarkov, as if desperately seeking to stop the effort. As the last construct collapsed, every single creature froze and fell limp, as though its nervous system had briefly failed. The surviving members of the expedition hastened to return, unwilling to await the Drovers' reawakening. Since that day, attacks on the settlements have become markedly less frequent.{/n}
  - After: {n}Deep below, the expedition found alien constructs emitting the signal. Drover swarms rushed to defend them, but when the last fell, every creature went limp. Attacks have been rarer since.{/n}

  - After: "The Omnissiah's wrath shall smite the xenos."

  - Before: {n}The mobile teams were equipped with powerful vox-hailers. The sequence of sound waves broadcast through the speakers disrupted the signal received by the Drovers.   - After: "Perhaps your kind may yet live in harmony with its worlds."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn screws up his face as if seized by intense pain.{/n} "I... No. I cannot. That is a powerful, if utterly sordid, argument on your part, {name}. Commendable! Very well, I will go through with this deception, but solely for Nuncius's sake."
  - After: {n}He winces.{/n} "Sordid but powerful, {name}. Very well, for Nuncius."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A commendable effort at manipulation. But if you intend to exploit my emotions to sway my judgement, then no, you will not succeed. I am convinced Nuncius would act precisely as I have."
  - After: "Nice manipulation, but no. Nuncius would do the same."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Then let us not delay. Do me the favour of inviting my esteemed colleague over — I am, as is evident, in no position to do so myself."
  - After: "Then summon my esteemed colleague; I clearly can't."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}The Haemonculus's face betrays nothing but contemptuous arrogance.{/n} "You have but a few moments of my precious time, {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}. Speak."
  - After: {n}Contemptuous.{/n} "Speak quickly, {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I... offer my sincere apologies, Haemonculus. Your mastery is far beyond my own; I should never have doubted that fact." {n}The Manipulus stares at the floor, avoiding the xenos's gaze.{/n}
  - After: "I apologise, Haemonculus. Your mastery exceeds mine." {n}Eyes downcast.{/n}
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}For a moment, malicious triumph twists Tervantias's already mutilated features into a grotesque mask.{/n} "Oh, finally I hear a shred of reason from your lips, you miserable creature. But you lack zeal. Repeat it once more, loudly and clearly. So that I may catch your babbling without having to strain my ears."
  - After: {n}Malicious triumph.{/n} "Finally, reason. But louder, with zeal."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: "It is more than just 'not enough.' It is woefully inadequate, mon-keigh. I want your kinsman to grasp the true depth of his worthlessness and I wish to behold it first-hand."
  - After: "Woefully inadequate. I want to watch him grasp his worthlessness."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest continues.{/n} "My conduct was beneath my station, Haemonculus, and my judgement... altogether lacking."
  - After: {n}He continues.{/n} "My conduct and judgement were lacking, Haemonculus."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: "You have moved from simple reasoning to objective facts, yet you have still failed to state the conclusion." {n}Tervantias speaks almost tenderly, openly relishing the humiliation of his opponent.{/n} "Do it then. Admit that you are a mentally deficient nonentity, whose entire body of knowledge is nothing but a pile of dubious guesswork and foolish rituals."
  - After: "Now conclude." {n}Relishing it.{/n} "Admit you're a deficient nonentity of guesswork and foolish rituals."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Manipulus looks up, his eyes filled with a focused scorn that verges on rage. In a heartbeat, he will put that scorn into words; unless you step in now, any hope of freeing Eogunn will be completely destroyed.{/n}
  - After: {n}Rage fills Eogunn's eyes. Intervene now or lose him.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn fixes the xenos with a gaze so lethal that, were such things possible, naught would remain of the creature but a smouldering pile of greasy soot. He remains silent, his face a mask of steel as his eyes drill into the Haemonculus.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn glares murder at the Haemonculus, silent.{/n}
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: "Do not test my patience, mon-keigh. Unless forming a coherent sentence from a collection of sounds is a task too daunting for a mind as rudimentary as yours?"
  - After: "Don't test me, mon-keigh. Is one sentence too hard?"
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}Tervantias hisses in displeasure, clenching and unclenching his clawed hands.{/n} "I am uncertain what gave you the impression that you are entitled to raise your voice, but your insolence is amusing. His words, however, are not. This conversation is becoming tedious."
  - After: {n}He hisses.{/n} "Your insolence amuses. His words don't. Tedious."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}Tervantias's lip twitches, and his voice sharply drops an octave, becoming a low, menacing hiss.{/n} "You presume to make choices for me, specimen? Meddle again, and I will graft your lips to your eyelids."
  - After: {n}He hisses.{/n} "Meddle again and I graft your lips to your eyelids."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}The Haemonculus turns away from Eogunn, instantly losing all interest in him.{/n} "If you value this heap of meat and scrap metal so highly, I will order it reassembled. Never speak of it to me again."
  - After: {n}He turns away.{/n} "Fine, I'll have this scrap reassembled. Never mention it again."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are correct, my esteemed colleague: I am indeed a short-lived, absurd creature with a rudimentary mind and utterly questionable cognitive abilities..."
  - After: "Correct, esteemed colleague: I am a short-lived creature with a rudimentary mind..."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}Tervantias nods approvingly, savouring every word the Manipulus utters.{/n}
  - After: {n}Tervantias nods, savouring it.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...but you, xenos, are a mockery of knowledge. A pathetic butcher incapable of creating anything new. All your so-called 'research' produces nothing but dysfunctional cadavers, monuments to your own vanity. In the name of the Omnissiah, be damned, vile spawn! May your works turn to dust and sink into oblivion!" {n}Eogunn speaks these words with sudden, startling volume, the skin of his mangled throat bulging from the strain.{/n}
  - After: "...but you, xenos, are a butcher of cadavers. In the Omnissiah's name, be damned! May your works turn to dust!" {n}Eogunn roars.{/n}
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: "What?" {n}Tervantias's mask of civility shatters. Livid, he looms over Eogunn, his many limbs splayed wide and hisses,{/n} "The next experiment will be your very last, mon-keigh."
  - After: "What?" {n}Livid, he looms.{/n} "Your next experiment is your last, mon-keigh."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}Tervantias fixes you with a piercing stare.{/n} "Triumph can only be won over an equal. I lowered myself to this miserable specimen's stature by calling for its admission, yet it is nothing but a thing. Now, this thing has grown as tiresome to me as your whimpering. Take it away."
  - After: {n}He stares at you.{/n} "Triumph needs an equal; this is a tiresome thing. Take it away."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: "A pathetic attempt to turn the situation in your favour, specimen. Speak again and you will be part of the next experiment yourself."
  - After: "Pathetic. Speak again and you join the next experiment."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}Without sparing Eogunn a glance, Tervantias snaps,{/n} "Your apologies failed to satisfy me, mon-keigh. The only thing you have earned is the removal of your tongue, but I will attend to that later."
  - After: {n}Tervantias snaps,{/n} "Your apology failed, mon-keigh. I'll take your tongue later."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}With a nauseating smirk, Tervantias looks on as blood spurts from Eogunn's mouth, leaving him nearly drowning in it.{/n} "Good specimen, you know how to please, unlike this wretch. It no longer amuses me; consider it your reward."
  - After: {n}Eogunn chokes on blood.{/n} "Good specimen. This wretch bores me; take it."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}Your fist slams into the metal plate in Eogunn's skull, leaving him unharmed. Tervantias watches you with utter indifference.{/n} "If you thought this would amuse me, specimen, you have failed to do so."
  - After: {n}Your fist hits his skull plate harmlessly.{/n} "Not amusing."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I refuse to endure this humiliation any longer, {name}. There is lying, and then there is the desecration of oneself. I... I simply cannot."
  - After: "Enough, {name}. Lying is one thing; self-desecration another."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}A complacent smile plays across the Haemonculus's face. He is visibly pleased by your subservience.{/n} "So, that is how it is? This scrap of flesh is of such value that you would grovel in the dirt to secure his release? Truly... entertaining. I think I will grant your request, purely for the pleasure of reclaiming him later and savouring the spectacle once more."
  - After: {n}He's pleased.{/n} "You'd grovel for this scrap? Granted, so I can reclaim him later and enjoy this again."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The scene elicits no reaction from Tervantias. The Haemonculus watches your struggles with utter indifference.{/n}
  - After: {n}Tervantias is indifferent.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Manipulus raises his gaze to you, looking weary.{/n} "Everything has its breaking point, Rogue Trader. Including my patience. As I am now... I cannot... I cannot govern my feelings well enough. I am sorry."
  - After: {n}Weary.{/n} "My patience broke. As I am, I can't govern my feelings. Sorry."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am ready to embrace death by your hand... Yet, if there is but a flicker of hope for survival, I must seize it. For Nuncius's sake."
  - After: "I'd accept death, but if I can survive, I must. For Nuncius."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A final request, {name}." {n}In the moments before death, Eogunn's voice suddenly regains its former strength and resonance.{/n} "Take care of Nuncius."
  - After: "A final request, {name}." {n}His voice regains its strength.{/n} "Take care of Nuncius."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A gloating smile touches Eogunn's lips.{/n} "It galls him beyond measure."
  - After: {n}Eogunn gloats.{/n} "It galls him beyond measure."

Only once I have exhausted all possibilities and examined the full range of data will I be prepared to admit defeat."
  - After: "We must repeat it, with control groups. One failure proves nothing. Only with all data exhausted will I admit defeat."

  - Before: {n}Eogunn smiles.{/n} "Perhaps. But it is what I truly believe. Only time, the most dispassionate arbiter of all, will be able to judge us."
  - After: {n}Eogunn smiles.{/n} "Perhaps. Time will judge us."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn raises a finger.{/n} "Precisely. A man chooses what he is made of — regrets for his past mistakes, or the experience he gained from them. Only those who choose the latter course can attain true wisdom."
  - After: {n}Eogunn raises a finger.{/n} "Precisely. Choose experience over regret. That is wisdom."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We have managed to reach a consensus on the root of the problem — the rest can be overlooked. He is not convinced by all my conclusions, but that is no terrible thing — he and I share a common path, but we each have our own methods of comprehending it."
  - After: "We agree on the root. Our methods differ, our path doesn't."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn looks at you dully.{/n} "Yes, it is long past time. I only ask for the privilege of privacy — this admission is difficult for me to make, and I can confide only in you."
  - After: {n}Eogunn looks at you dully.{/n} "Yes. In private, please — only you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "His refusal to repair Nuncius is an outrage and a violation of the vows he has sworn to the Machine God. I will summon him to the bridge immediately, in the hope that he will not dare to prevaricate in the presence of the Rogue Trader!"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Without Nuncius, Eogunn cuts a rather strange and lonely figure. I am relieved that I have at last {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_EogunnFinalAcceptance}managed to make peace{/d} with mine."
  - After: {n}Without Nuncius, Eogunn seems lonely, yet smiles placidly.{/n} "We all carry phantoms. I'm relieved I {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_EogunnFinalAcceptance}managed to make peace{/d} with mine."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn is absorbed in prayer. Nuncius floats over his shoulder — the real Nuncius now. Mine were the ruin of Nuncius, but they also {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_EogunnFinalService}brought me back to the path of purity of thought and deed{/d}. I grieve and feel grateful.   - After: {n}Eogunn prays. The real Nuncius floats nearby, his skull deformed but human.{/n} "My mistakes ruined Nuncius, but {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_EogunnFinalService}brought me back to the path of purity of thought and deed{/d}. I grieve, and I'm grateful."
- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But can anyone truly know the essence of another person? For a veil of words often shrouds meaning that cannot be discovered in one brief conversation. Then again, all the greatest works on human nature began with scant material. Ask your questions, Rogue Trader."

  - Before: "Stygies VIII is a {g|Encyclopedia:ForgeWorldGlossary}forge world{/g} located on one of the moons of a gas giant in the binary star system of Vulcanis. A magnificent place! - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I may not look it, but I am a wanderer and a pilgrim. Nuncius and I have led research expeditions with the aim of finding relics and artefacts and advancing the Quest for Knowledge. We have visited more than one world, voyaged on more than one ship, and got our hands dirty more than once, both literally and figuratively."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have come to the conclusion that the only correct decision in the context of this experiment was not to conduct it in the first place. I was attempting to wring usefulness out of people like charge from a dying battery. But regardless of how well and long a battery served before, when it is finally depleted, isn't the more rational response to dispose of it and replace it with a new one? Righteousness is a trait of these people, but it is not their primary function. I see that now."
  - After: "The experiment should never have happened. I clung to my hypothesis against Nuncius and reality, draining people like a dying battery. Righteousness is their trait, not their function. I see that now."
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "Heresy — often hurled at us. A tool to condemn the misunderstood. Rogue Traders have power precisely to go where line-toers can't. Absurd times."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You have heard from drunken voidfarers dread tales and speculation about metal creatures that do not know death. None of these stories ever sounded plausible, let alone convincing.{/n}
  - After: {n}Drunken voidfarers told of deathless metal things. Implausible.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have encountered inconsistencies in my research. Ghost colonies with fresh tracks that match the descriptions of these xenos from various sources. Adeptus Mechanicus expeditions that plunged into obsidian ruins, never to return. Gaps in the knowledge repositories of individual worlds, as if someone had been trying to hide information. In isolation, all these are unexplained coincidences, but if I analyse the cumulative frequency of the events and the systems in which they occurred, and compare them to the few things I do know, I can detect certain patterns. The ancient xenos are exhibiting activity."
  - After: "Ghost colonies with fresh tracks. Expeditions lost in obsidian ruins. Archive gaps, as if hidden. Together, they form patterns. They're active."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I thought I could benefit the Imperium by creating truly righteous people. But I did not consider that each person in the Imperium already has a role and function. Trying to assemble them into something new robs them of their functionality and, consequently, of their spiritual purity. I have committed the transgression of innovation, but with human beings, for which I have already assigned myself appropriate penance."
  - After: "I sought to create righteous people. But those fulfilling their function already are. Reassembling them stripped that purity. I sinned by innovating upon humans, and have set my penance."

  - Before: {n}This sounds like more than a belief — he has encountered these mythical xenos, or come very close to doing so.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And that is what unites us. A sincere answer — it is a rare ruler who will admit that {mf|he|she} fears anything at all."

Triasomata, before you stands {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTraderGlossary}Rogue Trader{/g} {name} von Valancius, Lord Captain of this vessel and sovereign of its crew. Solely by {mf|his|her} grace do you still live — one wrong word, one wrong movement, and I will personally call the enforcers down upon you."
  - After: {n}Abelard glares at Nuncius.{/n} "Allow me. This is {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTraderGlossary}Rogue Trader{/g} {name} von Valancius. You live by {mf|his|her} grace — behave."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The mumbling and head thumping stop. The man shifts his clouded gaze to you, and you see recognition in his eyes.{/n}

  - Before: "The Lord Captain...? I serrrve the dynasty!" {n}With an unpleasant clang, the man slams his augmented hand into his chest implant in a military salute. He freezes, like a stalled machine man — then an agonising shudder runs through his entire body, and blood trickles from the corner of his mouth.{/n} "Is this a p-p-punishment? Am I not permitted to... to die? I will not fear! Eiderdown and shroud..."
  - After: "Lord Captain! I serrrve the dynasty!" {n}He salutes, then shudders, bleeding.{/n} "May I not die? I will not fear!"
- **Triasomata**
  - Before: {n}Something akin to resolve appears in the man's eyes as his face is seized by spasms.{/n} "A h-hero... is to b-be... emulated. A h-hero... overcomes. Where's your helmet, soooldier?" {n}He hammers his fist again into his steel chest.{/n} "God-Emperor, I will not be afraid! Emperor... I will... be afraid..."
  - After: {n}Resolve flickers.{/n} "A hero overcomes. Where's your helmet, soldier?" {n}He pounds his chest.{/n} "I will not fear!"

- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}On the operating tables, several bodies are laid out, their mutilations exposed to the chill air. Their chest and abdominal cavities yawn wide, excavated of their augmented organs, which now nestle in flasks, still connected to the bodies by tubes and cables. Judging by the rhythmic contractions, the organs are still functioning. Eogunn hovers beside the tables, assiduously taking measurements and jabbing {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g} into the extracted organs or inside the bodies. Nuncius keeps stoic vigil nearby, an impassive observer of this grotesque spectacle.{/n}
  - After: {n}Opened bodies lie on tables, augmented organs pulsing in flasks. Eogunn probes with {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g}; Nuncius watches.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}Three men of differing ages lie before you: young, middle-aged, and old. If you look closely, you can see that they still have a semblance of life about them. Each one has had the top of his skull delicately removed, and electrodes are now attached to the blush-hued brain tissue latticed with blood vessels. Below the neck is one continuous gaping wound, the edges spread and held in place by a complex system of clamps. {/n}
  - After: {n}Three men — young, middle-aged, old — barely alive, skulls and bodies opened.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your {g|Encyclopedia:CommBead}comm-bead{/g} crackles to life, carrying the Vox Master's anxious voice:{/n} "Lord Captain, an urgent report from Mistress Sauerback. A strange creature resembling a malfunctioning {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitor{/g} is heading toward the lower decks, shouting pleas that make reference to you and Genetor Februs. Enforcers have been dispatched to intercept it, but they assumed that you would prefer to assess the situation personally."
  - After: {n}Your {g|Encyclopedia:CommBead}comm-bead{/g} crackles:{/n} "Lord Captain, Mistress Sauerback reports a {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitor{/g}-like creature heading below, shouting for you and Genetor Februs. Enforcers await you."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The pathologically emaciated build and spindly, almost transparent limbs indicate that this is a voidborn. A glance into the open ribcage reveals signs of damage — the sac around the heart is torn and the vessels have been reinforced with metal staples. The poor youth's heart is half {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}augment{/g} — both ventricles have been replaced by pumps, which are connected to opaque tubes that run to the medicae device's reservoir. The young man's neck is tattooed with his bay code and job title. It seems he is a common worker from the lower decks.{/n}
  - After: {n}An emaciated voidborn youth, heart half {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}augment{/g}. A tattoo marks him a lower-deck worker.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Two reasons. The first is that they were previously fatally injured. I have performed numerous rites and manipulations to ensure that each was able to avoid a fatal outcome. The second is that I have been conducting the necessary measurements to fully assess the compatibility of the configurations of Ferrum Sanctum and organic components for an optimal experimental result. This often requires the extraction of said components."
  - After: "They were dying; my rites keep them alive. And I extract parts to test Ferrum Sanctum compatibility."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "There are strong arguments in favour of each of them." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Genetor}Genetor{/g} raises a clawed mechadendrite and begins flexing its manipulators in time with his words.{/n} "Firstly, they have all performed their service impeccably, which suggests outstanding human qualities. Secondly, each body is robust enough to receive the Blessing of the Omnissiah. And thirdly, there is no other chance of salvation for any of them."
  - After: "Each is strong." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Genetor}Genetor{/g} flexes a mechadendrite.{/n} "All served impeccably, all can bear the Omnissiah's Blessing, and none has another hope."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn raises his mechadendrites in anticipation.{/n} "Who will form the basis of the Triasomata?"
  - After: {n}Eogunn waits.{/n} "Who will form the basis of the Triasomata?"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "A natural reaction, wholly understandable. Natural, but precipitate. Let me ask you a question: what is Humanity's primary mission? What are we striving for?"
  - After: "Precipitate. Tell me: what is Humanity's primary mission?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The combination of countless factors that unite the thoughts and deeds of a person into the quintessence of the worth of his being within his specific society. I am at a loss to provide a less broad definition, but no matter. Much more important is how you define righteousness. The subject you choose will determine the answer to that question."
  - After: "What gives a person worth in his society. But your definition matters more — your chosen subject will give it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Pressing his lips together, the Manipulus grunts out,{/n} "To condense his overly pedantic response: Nuncius does not consider righteousness to be in any way a significant factor in this research. Had I any less respect for my dearest colleague, I would say that this constitutes an egregious misunderstanding of the concept of the Triasomata, and is indicative of extreme closed-mindedness. But such remarks are beneath me."
  - After: {n}The Manipulus grunts,{/n} "Nuncius thinks righteousness irrelevant here. A grave misunderstanding — but I won't say so."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Finally, Eogunn touches the voidborn youth.{/n} "Mikosh, a ventilation shaft crawler from Sorting Hub 10. He dutifully burned mouldslime and vermin, and would be the first to climb into blocked ducts, risking his life to deliver recycled air into the sector. He was a true believer and never lamented his lot. On his final foray, he saved hundreds of workers by using his body to plug a hole in a combustible gas pipe. The toxicity led to cardiac arrest and blood poisoning."
  - After: {n}Eogunn touches the youth.{/n} "Mikosh, a vent crawler from Sorting Hub 10, faithful and uncomplaining. He saved hundreds by plugging a gas pipe with his body. The toxins stopped his heart."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn stares after him in amazement. {/n} "Impossible! The calculations were perfectly calibrated, all factors taken into consideration! Was the specimen defective? I must find the Triasomata immediately and determine what went wrong!"
  - After: {n}Eogunn stares.{/n} "Impossible! The calculations were perfect! I must find the Triasomata!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is as if a light has gone out inside Eogunn. Visibly repressing a sigh, he turns to his subjects. {/n} "It is frustrating that you failed to understand my intent, but perhaps it was indeed questionable. I accept your verdict, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}Eogunn dims.{/n} "A shame. Perhaps it was questionable. I accept your verdict, Lord Captain."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn closes his organic eye, deep in thought. Finally, his face breaks into a smile.{/n} "Thank you, {name}. This is it, the solution to our dilemma. I will begin the triasomia procedure. May organic flesh and sacred machinery be one!"
  - After: {n}Eogunn smiles.{/n} "Thank you, {name}. I begin the triasomia. May flesh and machine be one!"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}With a barely audible crunch, Eogunn's injector mechadendrite pierces the brain tissue. The man's face contorts in anguish, and his back arches in a fit of spasms. His brows furrowing, the Genetor delivers a powerful pulse of the Motive Force, and the unfortunate man drops limply back down on the table. The Tech-Priest's manipulators dart between the three bodies, separating organs, augmetics, and limbs, and transplanting them to the new host. Discharges of energy coruscate around Eogunn's hulking figure, growing brighter and brighter until the final flash leaves you temporarily blinded. When your vision returns, you see the Manipulus carefully releasing the subject's limbs from their restraints.{/n} "The process is complete."
  - After: {n}Eogunn pierces the brain; the man convulses, then stills. Organs and limbs are transplanted amid a blinding flash. Eogunn releases the restraints.{/n} "The process is complete."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The creature, which a second ago resembled a humanoid lump of bloody meat studded with metal, suddenly leaps up with unexpected vigour, tossing Eogunn backward and letting out an unintelligible howl of suffering. Before anyone can react, the amalgam man barrels toward the entrance of the Sector Bionica, filling the deserted corridors with his plaintive moans.{/n}

- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "A decisive one! I can detail the composition and humour ratio of each experimental subject, measure the mass of their frontal lobe, or answer with picosecond accuracy how often their heart contracts. But how does one calculate a man's righteousness? How do you weigh diligence of service? You will help me answer these questions by choosing the basis for the Triasomata. Your assessment will be the linchpin upon which this experiment hinges."
  - After: "A decisive one! I can measure organs, but not righteousness. Choose the Triasomata's basis — your judgement is the linchpin."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "One way or another, we must see the experiment through to the end."
  - After: "We must finish the experiment."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Survival, {name}. Among myriad enemies who seek to exterminate us, among cruel stars that harbour unknowable horrors, among traitors who promise death to our fellow humans. We want to survive. Death is inevitable — it is an incontrovertible fact. But to survive long enough for those who remain to achieve what we failed to — that is an endeavour worthy of Humanity."
  - After: "Survival, {name}. Death is certain, but surviving long enough for others to finish our work — that is worthy of Humanity."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "These three are doomed. If you tell me to stop the experiment, I will obey without question and terminate their life functions. But then their sacrifice will have been in vain. If you allow me to see this through to the end, one of them will survive — no, he will become something greater than he was before."
  - After: "They are doomed. Say stop, and I end them, their sacrifice wasted. Let me finish, and one becomes something greater."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Recalling your comment, Eogunn disperses some kind of caustic vapour from an alembic on his shoulder. Your nose goes numb for a moment, but the smells no longer trouble you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn sprays a vapour; the smell fades.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Nuncius obediently turns on his built-in {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumen{/g}, illuminating the subjects on the tables. It seems he is unwilling to divulge the subtleties of the experiment, silently ceding the right to answer to Eogunn.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nuncius lights his {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumen{/g}, leaving the answer to Eogunn.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The crux! All three organisms were found in critical condition. I asked myself: is their usefulness and productive capacity truly at an end? Nonsense. To move from a state of being to a state of non-being entails no benefits or meaning. I personally ensured that their vital functions were preserved. Our goal could not be simpler — to vanquish death by creating the perfect righteous man, that which I have dubbed the Triasomata."
  - After: "The crux! All three were dying, yet still useful. I preserved them. Our goal: vanquish death with the perfect righteous man — the Triasomata."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}With his well-developed musculature and strong bones, this man presents a stark contrast to the others. His left arm is missing, along with part of his shoulder. Shreds of major vessels protrude from the neatly trimmed stump — they have been closed off with bizarre-looking endcaps that are wired to a metal arm lying nearby. The enforcers' emblem is tattooed on the man's neck, topped with the von Valancius coat of arms.{/n}
  - After: {n}A muscular man missing his left arm, a metal arm wired nearby. His neck bears the enforcers' emblem and von Valancius arms.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In their current state, each of the subjects is doomed. But just as the parts of dying mechanisms can be combined again to create a functioning machine, so too can these subjects be combined into a single entity, granting them continued life through the correct configuration of the Ferrum Sanctum and organic components of all three. The only thing I require to continue the experiment is a solution to my dilemma: which subject should serve as the basis?" {n}Eogunn turns his burning gaze to you.{/n}
  - After: "Each is doomed. But like parts of dead machines, they can be combined into one living whole. I need one answer: which subject is the basis?" {n}He looks to you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}An angry spark zips along the pistons in the Manipulus's beard. He floats higher, turning his glowering gaze on the sector's ceiling.{/n} "Because I cannot abide the senseless waste of potential. I cannot accept that a foolish accident and the fragility of organic flesh can — in an instant — deprive the Imperium of worthy servants. And if I am able to extend their service life, I will do so. Whatever the cost."
  - After: {n}Sparks crackle in his beard.{/n} "I cannot abide frail flesh robbing the Imperium of worthy servants. If I can extend their service, I will. Whatever the cost."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn's passionate speech could be mistaken for pride and conceit. But something else lies behind it, a doggedness born of some deeply personal experience. This man carries a heavy burden, and the experiment is but one of his many attempts to relieve himself of it at last.{/n}
  - After: {n}Behind the pride lies a personal burden; this experiment is an attempt to shed it.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Drifting lower once more, Eogunn calmly asks,{/n} "Any more questions plaguing you, Rogue Trader?"
  - After: {n}Eogunn drifts lower.{/n} "More questions?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Hedonism is an understandable urge. A desire to experience life to the fullest. But at the root of this lies another, more primitive drive."
  - After: "Understandable. But a more primitive drive lies beneath."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Cohesion leads to increased potential. The whole is greater than its individual parts. But where does the urge to stand together come from? The answer is extremely simple."
  - After: "Unity strengthens. But whence that urge? Simple."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Struggling, striving to be at the top of the food chain. An understandable answer. But at the root of that urge lies another, more primitive one."
  - After: "Understandable. But a more primitive urge lies beneath."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My dearest colleague and I have had more than one consilium, but we have never reached a consensus. Nuncius is a sceptic, and our positions rarely align, but we tend to reach a compromise in the end. But, alas, not on this occasion. The only thing we agree on is the need for a third opinion. Only you can furnish us with said opinion — this is an incontrovertible fact."
  - After: "Nuncius and I can't agree this time. We need a third opinion — yours."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Three minds cannot coexist in one body. Setting aside the fact that even I would not be capable of achieving such a feat in practice, in theory it would certainly lead to the complete deconstruction of all three minds. Some... less flexible thinkers might even consider it heresy."
  - After: "Three minds in one body would destroy all three. Some would call it heresy."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The old man's eyelids are closed and his face is serene. He might appear to be sleeping peacefully, were it not for the deathly pallor of his face and his monstrously mangled neck. He had been fitted with a voice implant at some point previously, but it had recently been wrenched from the unfortunate man's body. Every so often, the metal hose now serving as his trachea emits a reedy whistling sound. He is clutching something tightly in his right hand — it is an ornate set of prayer beads, the kind used by ordained servants of the Ecclesiarchy.{/n}
  - After: {n}A pale old man, voice implant torn out, a hose whistling in his throat. He clutches Ecclesiarchy prayer beads.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You sense some agreement in Nuncius's silence.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nuncius silently agrees.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "As my dearest colleague rightly notes, we have encountered many such... points of contention... over the years."

  - Before: {n}The Genetor speaks rapidly, his words almost merging into an indistinct buzz.{/n} "Lord Captain, operations in the Sector Bionica have practically stalled. Genetor Extremis Eogunn Februs is unilaterally experimenting with the implantation throne, drawing the Motive Force from the compartment's circuitry and thereby hindering proper administration of the augmentation rite."
  - After: {n}He buzzes rapidly.{/n} "The Sector Bionica has stalled. Eogunn Februs is draining the implantation throne for experiments."
- **(conversation owner)**

Violations of the Catechism of Maintenance and Operation have been recorded, along with restricted access for other Tech-Priests. However, the rank of the life-form designated 'Eogunn Februs' is too high to be impeded without intervention from the life-form designated 'Lord Captain.'"
  - After: "Analysis..." {n}A pause.{/n} "Insufficient data. Rites violated, others locked out. Only the Lord Captain outranks him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Attesting: according to the logs of the Sector Bionica systems, Genetor Eogunn Februs is undertaking unauthorised use of the implantation throne contrary to its designated purpose. Recommended sanctions: imposition of a techno-penance combined with temporary rank reduction."
  - After: "Logs confirm misuse. Recommend techno-penance and demotion."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "As you will, Lord Captain."
  - After: "As you will."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "He is playing with death, in fact, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. He keeps trying to catch it, but it runs away from him, and flies over his shoulder, but it will never leave him completely. I thought I was cracked in the head, but no, that tin can must have bigger problems than me, if he can't decide whether to live or die."
  - After: "He's playing with death, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. That tin can can't decide to live or die."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Companion/CompanionQuest/Manipulus_Q2/ML_NunciusFinal/ML_NunciusFinal_dialogue

- **Player**

  - After: "What did you whisper?"

  - After: "End the experiment, Eogunn. What now?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Then do not delay. Do what you must."
  - After: "Then do what you must."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Actually... Do as you wish."
  - After: "Actually... as you wish."

  - Before: "You don't have much time. Say what you have to say."
  - After: "Time is short. Speak."

  - After: "His implant melted. You carry remains. Nuncius is dead."
