  - After: "Say goodbye and let him go, for both of you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You have been working toward this for fifty years and you want to give up now? Are you or are you not a great Genetor? Save him!"
  - After: "Fifty years, and you quit? Save him, Genetor!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Deliver it to the ship and make a weapon."
  - After: "Take it aboard. Make a weapon."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Smile] "I have heard much about you. Eogunn is forever talking about you."
  - After: [Smile] "Eogunn talks of you constantly."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What will you do with the artefact?"
  - After: "What of the artefact?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Is the melodrama over? Can we leave now?"
  - After: "Melodrama over? Can we go?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Draw your weapon] "This was a mistake. I shall end his suffering."
  - After: [Draw your weapon] "A mistake. I'll end his suffering."
- **Player**
  - Before: "And you left him like this? That's monstrous."
  - After: "You left him like this? Monstrous."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Eogunn, he does not want this."
  - After: "He doesn't want this."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why are mutations continuing even while in stasis?"
  - After: "Why mutate in stasis?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Something is enveloped within the sarcophagus's stasis field, something that one would struggle to identify as a human being. The body is locked in a foetal position, the mouth open in mute agony, and only the tears streaming from the eyes, reminiscent of some weeping holy statue, reveal that the person is alive. Merciless waves of transmutation slowly and inexorably remake the body — the augmented fingers are covered with veins, vessels, and bones, and the blood that drips from them turns to mica. All in sepulchral silence, broken only by the breathing of the stasis sacellum apparatus. A funeral dragging on for half a century, attended by no one. Until today.{/n}
  - After: {n}In the stasis field lies something barely human, curled, weeping in mute agony as transmutation remakes it. A fifty-year funeral, unattended until today.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn touches the sacellum delicately with the tips of his fingers, as though fearing that the machine and its contents will crumble to dust.{/n} "We meet again, dearest colleague. I would give anything to have you look at me now, your eyes brimming with reproach, resentment, even hatred. But all I see in them is pain and yearning. Is it yearning for life or for oblivion? I do not know. I stopped understanding myself long ago — madness and guilt are bewildering, they muddle the brain. I have grown accustomed to it. But that I stopped understanding you — I can never forgive myself for that."
  - After: {n}Eogunn touches the sacellum gently.{/n} "We meet again, dearest colleague. I see only pain in your eyes. I stopped understanding you, and can never forgive myself."
- **Nuncius**
  - Before: {n}With his last vestiges of strength, Nuncius clasps a mangled hand over Eogunn's and nods.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nuncius clasps his hand and nods.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I will save Nuncius. Fifty years of searching, calculating, and experimenting cannot have been for nothing — I have travelled too far to surrender at the very end. This is a debt I owe to my colleague. No, to humanity. If I master death here and now, then I will pave the way for a new age in the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g}. {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_EogunnFinalMadness}The methods do not matter{/d}. Does anyone remember the hundreds of failed attempts and sacrifices that are made in the search for a solution to a problem, if that solution ends up being the only correct one?" {n}Eogunn asks vehemently, without looking at Nuncius.{/n}
  - After: "I will save him. Fifty years cannot be for nothing. Master death, and the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g} enters a new age. {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_EogunnFinalMadness}The methods do not matter{/d}." {n}He won't look at Nuncius.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Xenotechnology bound Nuncius and me together, and it also doomed us. Believing that it was possible to master the technology of the {g|Encyclopedia:XenosGlossary}xenos{/g} and use it for good, I allowed corruption to enter me and I cultivated it for years until it reaped its harvest. This entire place, along with the xenos and his cursed artefact, should have been {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_EogunnFinalService}burned to the ground{/d} as soon as we set foot on this world. It was not the xenos that killed Nuncius, or the transmuter, or even the {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g}'s avarice. It was me. Every choice, every decision I made, ultimately formed an equation with only one possible answer: the death of Nuncius. What is left of him? A mangled shell that has known nothing but torment for these last fifty years."
  - After: "I thought {g|Encyclopedia:XenosGlossary}xenos{/g} tech could serve good, and let corruption in. This place should have {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_EogunnFinalService}burned to the ground{/d}. Not the transmuter, nor the {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g}: I killed Nuncius. He's a tormented shell."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I have grown accustomed to playing the role of mentor, and this habit has done me a cruel disservice — if only I had stopped talking and listened, I could have learned a great deal. From you I have learned {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_EogunnFinalAcceptance}acceptance and mercy{/d}. Survival does not equal life. I have argued that death has no meaning — it still doesn't, it is unfathomable and merciless. However, the same is true of life — meaning is something we give it, whether it be service to the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g}, the Quest for Knowledge, or forging bonds stronger than blood. I have made my meaning self-destruction through guilt and false hope."
  - After: "I should have listened. You taught me {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_EogunnFinalAcceptance}acceptance and mercy{/d}. Survival is not life. Life means what we give it: the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g}, knowledge, bonds. I gave mine to guilt."
- **Nuncius**
  - Before: {n}The corner of his lips where flesh remains struggles to lift in a grateful smile. Struggling to force out each word, Nuncius rasps,{/n} "I'm glad... that he was... not alone..."
  - After: {n}He rasps, half-smiling:{/n} "Glad... he wasn't... alone..."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Yes, it is long past time."
  - After: "Yes, long past time."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I thought our views on the situation were similar. What do you propose?"
  - After: "I thought we agreed. What do you propose?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn lets out a rumbling laugh, as if you had told some ridiculous lie.{/n} "Absurd, {name}! How can he be dead if I can see him before me, feel him within me? Yes, Nuncius, that's what I told {mf|him|her} — you are alive, we are both alive! This is an incontrovertible fact."
  - After: {n}Eogunn laughs.{/n} "Absurd, {name}! He lives within me! I told {mf|him|her}, Nuncius: we're alive!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servo-skull is grimly silent. His eye sockets are as empty as a desecrated grave.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servo-skull is silent.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn frowns, closes his organic eye, and sits in deep thought for a while.{/n} "I... have reassessed the situation. I am plagued by doubts, and I am not entirely sure I am doing the right thing. But I will trust you. This is my final decision."
  - After: {n}Eogunn ponders.{/n} "I doubt, but I'll trust you. Final."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn shakes his head.{/n} "With all due respect, Rogue Trader, this is not your choice. Nuncius is my responsibility, and I will decide for myself what to do with him. Do not deny me this. And now I must begin."
  - After: {n}He shakes his head.{/n} "Not your choice, Rogue Trader. He's mine. I begin."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Nuncius struggles to say something, but Eogunn does not give him the chance. The mechadendrites dig into his flesh, extracting and replacing organs one by one — Eogunn rips something right out of his own body, quickly replacing it with implants or strange objects of apparent xenos origin. One of the mechadendrites continuously emits the Motive Force, targeting organs and augments, compelling them to function against all odds. Eogunn does not make a sound during the entire operation.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn's mechadendrites swap organs between them and xenos objects, Motive Force forcing them to work. He makes no sound.{/n}
- **Nuncius**
  - Before: {n}Nuncius seizes the Tech-Priest's hand with immense effort.{/n} "Eo... gunn... Just... let... me... go..."
  - After: {n}Nuncius grips his hand.{/n} "Eo... gunn... let... me... go..."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn closes Nuncius's eyes. He stares at the body in silence for a time, then summons the {g|Encyclopedia:ServoSkulls}servo-skull{/g} and issues a command in binharic. The servo-skull's eye socket goes dark and its manipulators freeze, and the Tech-Priest places it at the foot of the sacellum.{/n} "Now I have let him go for good. {name}, thank you for this opportunity. And thank you for being here with me."
  - After: {n}Eogunn closes his eyes and sets the dark {g|Encyclopedia:ServoSkulls}servo-skull{/g} by the sacellum.{/n} "He's free. {name}, thank you for being here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My heart rate is higher than usual, and my mind is awash with grief. But I also feel... relieved. It may sound strange or cynical, but now that I have let him go, I feel that I can go on living. But I will never dare to forget Nuncius ever again — it is a pain I will carry inside me until the end, and I will be... glad to have it with me."
  - After: "I grieve, yet feel relieved. Now I can live on. I'll carry his memory gladly."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn examines the stump of his mechadendrite.{/n} "It is dangerous. The risk of a similar situation happening again is high. I suggest we bury it here. But if you decide otherwise, I believe I could study its properties and develop a weapon based on it. I will trust your decision."
  - After: {n}He eyes his stump.{/n} "It's dangerous. Bury it here, or I could make a weapon. Your call."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn takes Nuncius's hand gently in his own. He leans closer and whispers something, then pulls away:{/n} "It's time. You were not always right, and neither was I, but you were never wrong about the things that truly matter. Forgive me, and farewell, dearest colleague."
  - After: {n}Eogunn whispers to Nuncius.{/n} "You were never wrong about what mattered. Forgive me. Farewell, dearest colleague."
- **Nuncius**
  - Before: {n}With his last scraps of strength, Nuncius gives Eogunn's hand a barely perceptible squeeze, before letting his arm fall to the cold metal of the sacellum. One last attempt at a smile frozen on his lips.{/n}
  - After: {n}A faint squeeze; his arm falls, a smile frozen.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes, Rogue Trader. All that remains is the matter of the artefact."
  - After: "Yes. Only the artefact remains."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn places a hand on Nuncius's chest.{/n} "Hush, old friend. I have returned to end your agony. You will die by my hand, not of the xenos' filth. Here to witness is {name}, who reunited us."
  - After: {n}Hand on his chest:{/n} "Hush, old friend. You'll die by my hand, not the xenos'. {name} will witness."
- **Nuncius**
  - Before: {n}Perhaps it is just a glint or a reflection from one of the devices, but for a moment, a shaft of light seems to illuminate Nuncius's face. His pupils dilate, and his hand reaches up, as if trying to touch something. His breathing becomes clearer and more even. Barely audibly, he whispers:{/n} "Omnissiah... at last... I comprehend..."
  - After: {n}Light touches Nuncius's face; he reaches up, whispering:{/n} "Omnissiah... I comprehend..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Clutched in his hands — no, fused with his fingers — is a black cube of unnaturally smooth black material. In the endless cycle of excruciating metamorphoses, it is the only object that is unmoving and unchanging.{/n}
  - After: {n}Fused to his fingers is a smooth black cube, unchanging.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Genetor Extremis Nuncius, by the Emperor's Mercy, I hereby end your algorithms and cognitive processes. By the right granted to me by the rank of {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magos{/g}, before the all-seeing gaze of the all-thinking Machine God, I name you a martyr worthy of sanctification as a {g|Encyclopedia:ServoSkulls}servo-skull{/g}. Your Quest for Knowledge has come to an end, but your service is not over." {n}Laying both hands on Nuncius's chest, Eogunn asks gently,{/n} "Are you ready, dearest colleague?"
  - After: "Nuncius, by the Emperor's Mercy I end your processes. As {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magos{/g}, I name you a martyr, worthy of a {g|Encyclopedia:ServoSkulls}servo-skull{/g}. Your service continues." {n}Gently:{/n} "Ready, dearest colleague?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn's galvanic coils crackle, and a powerful discharge passes from his hands directly into Nuncius's chest in a flash of azure. Nuncius's entire body shudders, then goes still forever. Gently removing the dead man's hand from his own, Eogunn stares at him for a time. Finally, with a decisive swing of his mechadendrite, he cuts off his colleague's head, and takes it. Then, he takes the servo-skull that has been hovering at his shoulder and sets it at the foot of the stasis sacellum.{/n} "I have done what I had to do. Now I am ready to walk the path of atonement myself. I excommunicate myself from the xenarite sect and dedicate myself to the Quest for Knowledge as it has been established in His covenants. {name}, thank you for being with me."
  - After: {n}An azure discharge; Nuncius stills. Eogunn takes his head and leaves the old servo-skull.{/n} "It is done. I renounce the xenarite sect for His covenants. {name}, thank you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes. For the first time in a long time, my mind is completely clear. I have no regrets about what I have done. Nuncius is free of corruption at last, and I am pleased that I had the fortitude to end his life myself. I have learned a harsh lesson that I will not dare to forget, but should my memory begin to fade, I will always have a reminder of what deviation from dogma leads to." {n}Eogunn looks mournfully at Nuncius's head.{/n}
  - After: "My mind is clear. No regrets. He's free of corruption, by my hand. I'll keep a reminder of where heresy leads." {n}He eyes the head.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I want it! Nuncius... will thank me later."
  - After: "I want it! He'll thank me later."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Suddenly, Nuncius begins thrashing around in convulsions — a seizure so intense that he bites off his mutated tongue and begins choking on his own blood.{/n} "No, blast it, no!" {n}Eogunn roars gutturally, sending his mechadendrites swarming in panic. After a moment, Nuncius's body goes still.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nuncius convulses, choking on blood.{/n} "No, blast it!" {n}He goes still.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I'm still... Yes, Nuncius, yes, endure a little longer, we will be one..." {n}The Manipulus has lost his final shred of rationality — his gaze is now in full thrall to madness. He desperately extracts the distorted augments from the corpse and mercilessly reattaches them inside himself, heedless of the pain and blood. Last of all, he removes the cortical implant from Nuncius's head — a melted piece of dead metal covered in lumps of brain matter. Whispering words you cannot make out, Eogunn solders it next to his heart.{/n}
  - After: "Endure, Nuncius, we'll be one..." {n}Mad, Eogunn grafts the corpse's augments into himself, the melted implant beside his heart.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Don't you dare! I'm on the verge of a breakthrough!"
  - After: "Don't you dare! I'm close!"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Coughing up blood, Eogunn collapses heavily to the floor.{/n} "The Triasomata... is complete. Nuncius is in me."
  - After: {n}Eogunn collapses, coughing blood.{/n} "The Triasomata... complete. Nuncius is in me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A refractive transmuter. I had to confine it together with Nuncius — if it were removed, death would follow almost instantly. Of course, this is only a hypothesis based on an analysis of my colleague's condition. A hypothesis I have no desire to test."
  - After: "A refractive transmuter. Removing it would likely kill him. I won't test that."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am the Triasomata, redemption from death. Nuncius and I are forever one, I will not be parted from him again." {n}Looking somewhere beyond you, Eogunn smiles blissfully.{/n} "I am so glad I was finally able to save you, dearest colleague."
  - After: "I am the Triasomata, redemption from death. We are one." {n}He smiles at nothing.{/n} "I saved you, dearest colleague."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am ecstatic! Now that Nuncius is with me forever, together we can refine the triasomia procedure. How many triumphs await us, how much good we will deliver to Humanity! And for that we have you to thank, {name}. Isn't that right, Nuncius?"
  - After: "Ecstatic! Together we'll perfect triasomia for Humanity! Thanks to you, {name}. Right, Nuncius?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I don't know. This device is older than Humanity itself — who knows what else it is capable of? Stasis can only slow its effects."
  - After: "Unknown. It's older than Humanity. Stasis only slows it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes, it is. Monsters are born of hope and fear. I was driven by both."
  - After: "Yes. Hope and fear breed monsters."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "He cannot hear you. But I appreciate that you still see him as a human being."
  - After: "He can't hear. Thank you for seeing him as human."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Something only the two of us would understand. Allow me to keep this mystery unsolved. I want to have a memory of him that belongs only to me."
  - After: "Something just ours. Let me keep it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I know, old friend. I've come to release you. {name}, Rogue Trader, has given me the chance to do this."
  - After: "I've come to release you, old friend, thanks to {name}."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Companion/CompanionQuest/Manipulus_Q2/ML_ReserveGenerator/ML_ReserveGenerator_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Scowl] "This place is nothing but disappointment. So, what do we do now?"
  - After: [Scowl] "Nothing but disappointment. Now what?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Apparently, the passage to the camp is blocked. Any suggestions on how to get through?"
  - After: "The camp passage is blocked. Ideas?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Won't the battery in your guts power the lift?"
  - After: "Can't your battery power the lift?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you know where to find it?"
  - After: "You know where it is?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The plan is solid. Let's move out."
  - After: "Solid plan. Move out."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn makes a low, resonant grunt filled with frustration.{/n} "A deplorable situation. The lift's {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g} has lain in deep hibernation since the grace of the Motive Force abandoned it. We are stranded on this side of the chasm without it."
  - After: {n}Eogunn grunts.{/n} "The lift's {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g} sleeps unpowered. We're stranded."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Know it?" {n}Eogunn smiles sadly.{/n} "For Nuncius and myself, this place was long our dwelling place, and our dungeon. Every corridor is etched into my memory's archives with pictographic precision."
  - After: "Know it?" {n}A sad smile.{/n} "It was our home and dungeon."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The central generator once blessed the research camp with power. After so many years of solitude, its machine spirit has likely forgotten the words of the Galvanic Hymns and fallen dormant. I can remind it of its duty and share the Motive Force from my own flesh. But, to do that, we must reach it first."
  - After: "The camp's central generator is dormant. I can rouse it with my own Motive Force, once we reach it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn casts a wary glance toward the laboratory beyond the chasm and nods.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn nods warily.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "An obvious solution, one would think, colleague." {n}He taps the casing of his battery with a mechadendrite.{/n} "But, alas, an inapplicable one. All the Motive Force stored within my galvanic coils would sustain the lift for but a moment, since its hunger is too great. Only the generator can truly sate it."
  - After: "Alas, no." {n}He taps his battery.{/n} "It'd last a moment. Only the generator suffices."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But of course! We simply need to trigger a rapid release of a vast amount of energy in a confined space. To put it plainly, we blow it to the warp!" {n}Eogunn grins with sudden enthusiasm.{/n} "I recommend melta charges. If memory serves, there should be a crate outside; it may still hold a few."
  - After: "We blow it to the warp!" {n}He grins.{/n} "Melta charges. Check the crate outside."

  - Before: "The Manipulus has modified the ship's servitors in ways that deviate from the permissible standards for their construction. The arguments he has presented are heretical, the results are blasphemous, and his speech is profane."
  - After: "The Manipulus altered the servitors heretically. Blasphemous."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This statement is true. Other means of bringing Genetor Februs into compliance have already proven ineffective, having had an adverse effect on the productivity of the engine compartments."
  - After: "Correct. Other measures failed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I request an audience with the Rogue Trader. Genetor Extremis Eogunn Februs has committed a Category Five blasphemy by violating the precepts of the Catechism of Maintenance and Operation. The offender persists in denying his distortion of the Omnissiah's design and insists on resolving the conflict with third-party mediation."
  - After: "Rogue Trader, Genetor Februs has committed Category Five blasphemy. He denies it and demands mediation."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Companion/CompanionQuest/Manipulus_Q2/TruthAboutNuncius/TruthAboutNuncius_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You have betrayed my trust. I want you to leave my retinue."
  - After: "You betrayed me. Leave my retinue."
- **Player**
  - Before: "So you have been lying to me all this time?"
  - After: "You've been lying all along?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are speaking too rationally about your insanity."
  - After: "Too rational about insanity."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will help you return to Nuncius. We will go to Amsanct as soon as we find a way through the gate."
  - After: "I'll take you to Nuncius, past the gate to Amsanct."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Eogunn, I need the truth. What really happened on Amsanct?"
  - After: "Eogunn, the truth. What happened on Amsanct?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Then tell me what really happened on Amsanct."
  - After: "Then tell me about Amsanct."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will not be swayed by your excuses."
  - After: "Your excuses won't sway me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You cannot reconstruct them here on the ship?"
  - After: "Can't you rebuild them here?"

  - Before: "Very well, I will take you to Aviorus."
  - After: "Very well, to Aviorus."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why haven't you performed your ritual this time?"
  - After: "Why skip your ritual now?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How does one get to Amsanct?"
  - After: "How does one reach Amsanct?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How did you come to be on the planet?"
  - After: "How did you get there?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You said that Nuncius was between life and death — what happened?"
  - After: "Between life and death — how?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What was he like, the real Nuncius?"
  - After: "What was the real Nuncius like?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You said that treating your insanity would make it worse — explain."
  - After: "Why would treatment make it worse?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have heard all I wish to."
  - After: "I've heard enough."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Execute him] "I sentence you to death for heresy."
  - After: [Execute him] "Death for heresy."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You mean to tell me that you left a man in agony for fifty years and still haven't gone back to him? A fine friend you are."
  - After: "Fifty years of his agony and you never went back? Fine friend."
- **Player**
  - Before: "We will make a stop there if it's on our way."
  - After: "We'll stop if it's on our way."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If you keep forgetting the real Nuncius, why do you still seek a way to save him?"
  - After: "If you keep forgetting him, why still try to save him?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn looks aged — the {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumen{/g} light on his wasted face casts each crease, furrow, and implant scar into stark relief. His hands, usually resting contentedly on his stomach or pensively tweaking the pistons on his chin, now hang limply at his sides. He hovers barely above the floor, as if some unbearable weight were on the verge of crushing him into the deck. He does not look at Nuncius.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn looks aged and crushed in the {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumen{/g} light. He does not look at Nuncius.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thesis one: my mind is sick. This is an incontrovertible fact. I deduced it long ago — 49 years and 138 days ago, to be precise. After weighing all the arguments, I chose inaction — a decision egotistical in its rationality. I believe that, had I attempted to cure my insanity, I would have declined all the sooner."
  - After: "Thesis one: my mind is sick. I knew it 49 years and 138 days ago, and chose not to treat it. Treatment would hasten my decline."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Not intentionally. I lied to both of us. I did not recall those details until today."
  - After: "I lied to us both. I only remembered today."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Nuncius and I belong to a secret sect of xenarites. Our path of Knowledge is the study of xenotechnology for the benefit of the Imperium. Many of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Priesthood of Mars{/g}, who interpret the precepts of the Omnissiah very narrowly, deem our path a heretical schism. After our ordination on Stygies VIII, Nuncius and I went searching for samples of Necron xenotech — a nearly impossible task, and thus, a fascinating one. On one such expedition, we came into conflict with other Tech-Priests — we were close to death, but the Inquisition, who had been observing our research in secret, decided that we would be more useful alive. Of course, it was only once we arrived on Amsanct that we learned that the Inquisition had been behind the confrontation."
  - After: "Nuncius and I are secret xenarites — heretics to the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Priesthood of Mars{/g}. Rival Tech-Priests nearly killed us hunting Necron tech; the Inquisition saved us. On Amsanct we learned they'd staged it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "How else am I to speak of it? My condition is a known fact. I have discovered it, assessed its impact, weighed all the variables, and settled on the most rational plan of action. Which is to remove information about it from my memory by means of a ritual of transcranial electroconvulsive self-flagellation that I designed myself. The ritual is dangerous and unreliable, but it is better than the alternative."
  - After: "How else? The rational course: erase it with my own ritual of transcranial electroconvulsive self-flagellation. Dangerous, but better."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Won't you allow me to explain myself? But, then, I have no right to criticise you."
  - After: "Won't you let me explain? Though I've no right to object."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn stares through you, looking lost — difficult memories are dragging him away from the here and now.{/n} "Yes, of course, we must get to... to Nuncius. I have to find him and finish what I started, don't I?"
  - After: {n}Eogunn stares, lost.{/n} "Yes... Nuncius. I must finish what I started."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn bends his entire body in a deep bow.{/n} "I understand, and I thank you for your merciful judgement, Rogue Trader. I will treasure the time we spent together on the path of Knowledge. Perhaps someday this experience will help me find a solution, and I will be able to tell Nuncius about you."
  - After: {n}Eogunn bows deeply.{/n} "Thank you for your mercy, Rogue Trader. Someday I'll tell Nuncius of you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm afraid not. They were wholly unique. It would take me years to find new samples and regain what was lost. I am certain they are still there, which is why I am asking you for this courtesy."
  - After: "No. They were unique; it'd take years. They must still be there."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you, {name}. If I may, I will leave you now. I have much to think about."
  - After: "Thank you, {name}. I'll go think."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Amsanct is a planet in an uncharted sector of space, home to the ruins of a civilisation of technologically advanced xenos — the ordained call them Necrons. There we set up a research camp under the supervision of the {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g}, and we set about searching for surviving samples of xenotechnology. And we found them. One of them led to the tragedy that resulted in Nuncius being caught between life and death, and me talking to a servo-skull." {n}He says this in an uncharacteristically dry monotone.{/n} "Ask your questions, {name}, I will answer them all."
  - After: "Amsanct: uncharted Necron ruins we searched for the {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g}. One find left Nuncius between life and death, and me talking to a servo-skull." {n}Flatly.{/n} "Ask, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your trust in me has already been shaken — you worked out on your own that there was something amiss with me. If I do not tell you the truth, then it will be irretrievably lost. The scenario in which I tell you everything is the only one where there is a chance of us being on good terms once more."
  - After: "You already sensed something wrong. Only the truth can restore us."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After pausing, he adds,{/n} "The decision to eradicate a newfound knowledge is never easy. I understand why I must, but each time it feels like I am killing an important part of myself. I am afraid of knowing the truth about Nuncius, but I'm also afraid that if I forget it, I'll never remember it again. And that fear is not groundless."
  - After: {n}He adds,{/n} "Each erasure kills part of me. I fear the truth — and losing it forever."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The intervals between my realising the truth are becoming longer all the time. I used to uncover my secret about once every two months. That quickly turned into four. Now it takes as long as eight. This shows that the deterioration of my mind is accelerating." {n}He raises his colourless gaze to you.{/n} "So far, I have failed to find an effective countermeasure. I do not know if I will ever find one."
  - After: "I rediscover the truth every two months, then four, now eight. I'm failing faster." {n}He looks up.{/n} "I've found no cure."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Not was — is," {n}comes Eogunn's mild yet emphatic correction.{/n} "Everything I said about him before is true. He complements me in all that I cannot foster in myself. He is also my staunchest opponent — his scepticism and caution have always balanced my scientific optimism and audacity. We rarely completely agree on anything, but I believe that without our conflicts, we both would have discovered and achieved far less. Ours is a symbiotic relationship — together we form a whole that is more powerful than its individual parts."
  - After: "Not was — is," {n}Eogunn corrects.{/n} "His caution balances my audacity. Our quarrels made us both greater. Together we are more than our parts."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "From the bits of information I was able to piece together, I came to the conclusion that the Inquisition was interested in that sector of space as a whole, and that Amsanct was only a small part of the operation. We were transported there on a certain Chartist vessel for the purposes of secrecy — I suspect the Chartists were just a cover. Our expertise was invaluable for the study of xenoruins, so Nuncius and I were placed in charge of the research team and provided with all the necessary equipment."
  - After: "The Inquisition wanted the whole sector. A Chartist ship brought us; we led the research."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We discovered a rare specimen in the ruins — a critically injured but still functioning xenos, and some kind of artefact with it. The xenos called it a refractive transmuter. Understanding how this artefact functioned was our primary objective. We imprisoned the xenos and tried to uncover its secrets, but our equipment was incapable of hurting or granting us any insight into the device. We experimented with the refractive transmuter almost blindly."
  - After: "We found a dying xenos with an artefact it called a refractive transmuter. It told us nothing; we tested the artefact blindly."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The artefact. Nuncius and I had a disagreement — I was frustrated by the lack of progress, and I wanted to take a more radical approach to studying it. I wanted to experiment on myself. Nuncius was vehemently opposed — he argued that it was reckless, with insufficient data and unpredictable outcomes. Of course, he was right. In my stubbornness and arrogance, I did not heed him. I removed the artefact from the stasis sacellum and reached for it with a mechadendrite. Nuncius tried to intercept it and inadvertently touched the artefact. That moment has haunted me for the past fifty years."
  - After: "The artefact. I wanted to test it on myself. Nuncius called it reckless — rightly. I took it from the stasis sacellum anyway; he tried to stop me and touched it. It has haunted me fifty years."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The refractive transmuter began to rearrange Nuncius's body on a molecular level. Metal turned to flesh, and flesh to metal in a monstrous cycle of wicked infinity. At times, he would produce a scream, but after a second his vocal cords would turn to lead and his tongue to tin, and the screams would abruptly cut off. I had no time to reflect — to save his life, I had to hastily modify the stasis sacellum and immerse Nuncius in it along with the artefact. It did not stop the agony, but it did stop him from dying. It gave me the chance to find a solution."
  - After: "It remade his body — metal to flesh, flesh to metal, endlessly, his screams dying in a leaden throat. I sealed him in the stasis sacellum with it. The agony went on, but he lived."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Locked away in the laboratory, I tried to find ways to reverse the artefact's effects. None of them worked. I turned to the xenos, demanding information — with threats, requests, pleas. But its only response was contemptuous silence. I was utterly powerless. And then I decided to flee."
  - After: "Nothing reversed it. The xenos answered my pleas with contempt. Powerless, I fled."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Silence. An empty gaze. Finally, a reply:{/n} "New knowledge, tools, experience — I needed more. My staying on Amsanct would not fix the situation. I decided to flee to the Expanse and seek answers there. I couldn't take Nuncius with me, so I secretly diverted the Motive Force from the main generator to support the stasis sacellum, placing the main camp on reserve power, then closed up our laboratory."
  - After: {n}Silence. Then:{/n} "Staying fixed nothing. I diverted the main generator's Motive Force to his stasis sacellum, sealed the lab, and fled to the Expanse."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn avoids meeting your eye.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn avoids your eye.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What are you going to do now? I have no more secrets from you."
  - After: "What now? I have no more secrets."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "These memories are painful. Forming a rational understanding of the world — breaking it down into hypotheses, facts, conclusions — is not just my vocation, it is the essence of my existence. I have power over my thoughts. But my emotions — they bring chaos to my existence. They tear through logic and trample over calculations. If I rid myself of the Nuncius figment, I will be left facing a monstrous, insurmountable task alone. My efficiency will plummet, and the path to Knowledge will be shrouded in mist. Paradoxically, my insanity is the key to preserving my mind and soul."
  - After: "Emotion wrecks my reason. Without the Nuncius figment I'd falter alone. My insanity preserves my mind."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn's ponderous body drops to the deck with a clang. The servo-skull he called Nuncius continues hovering silently above him. The machine's empty eye sockets stare blankly into the distance, awaiting new commands.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn's body clangs to the deck. The servo-skull hovers on.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Every few months, I once again spontaneously deduce that I am insane, as I have just done. And I arrive at the same conclusion as before."
  - After: "Every few months I rediscover my madness, and decide the same."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thesis two: there are two Nunciuses. This is also an incontrovertible fact. The first Nuncius is a figment of my imagination, the product of my insanity and, at the same time, the anchor that keeps my mind from further degradation. I project it onto a servo-skull, a model with no additional features other than an auxiliary lumen and an autoquill. It is incapable of conducting a conversation or holding an opinion. I do not even know from whose skull it was made."
  - After: "Thesis two: there are two Nunciuses. One is my figment, my anchor, projected onto a plain servo-skull. It cannot talk. I don't know whose skull it is."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The second Nuncius is a {g|Encyclopedia:Genetor}Genetor{/g} Extremis of the Adeptus Mechanicus. My dearest colleague, the person who could cope with my temperament, walking shoulder to shoulder with me on the path of Knowledge. The only person whose presence ever made me feel alive. For the last half century, he has been in unending agony, caught between life and death, at the secret site Amsanct. Because of me. All this time, I have been searching for ways to save him. He exists and is still alive, this is another..." {n}Hesitation. A tiny moment that holds fear and hope — doubts heavier than an entire world. Eogunn finishes quietly,{/n} "It's a fact."
  - After: "The other is a {g|Encyclopedia:Genetor}Genetor{/g} Extremis, my dearest colleague, fifty years in agony between life and death on Amsanct. Because of me. He's alive, this is..." {n}He hesitates, then whispers,{/n} "It's a fact."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That part of space can only be accessed through a special dimensional gateway. I do not know its exact coordinates or how to activate it — I assume that only the highest ranks of the Inquisition can answer this question."
  - After: "Only via a dimensional gateway. Its location and key are likely known only to the Inquisition's highest ranks."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After a moment's hesitation, Eogunn returns his attention to you.{/n} "I have a request — I need to prepare before this journey. Before I joined the clergy of Altar-Templum-Ext-17, I had a small laboratory in the Aviorus System. I was forced to leave it in haste for my own safety, and important samples and records of my experiments remained there. If we want to help Nuncius, we must retrieve them."
  - After: {n}Eogunn turns back.{/n} "Before Altar-Templum-Ext-17, I had a lab in the Aviorus System. I fled, leaving vital samples and records. We need them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Of course, I can wait. However, without the samples, the journey to Amsanct is futile — without them, I cannot help Nuncius."
  - After: "I can wait. But without the samples, I can't help him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The memory of an organic brain is not as malleable as mathematically sound data stored in cogitators. Memory cannot be fully exterminated, only... mutilated. Moreover, it is not my goal to forget Nuncius completely, but rather to obscure my memories of him. I usually can recollect that there is someone in a similar state, and that this experiment is a priority for me and Nuncius the servo-skull. The sense of time slipping through my fingers, the thrill of research, and an inexplicable sense of the import of the outcome all urge me to conduct these experiments, even if I do not remember for whose sake they are being done."
  - After: "Organic memory can only be mutilated, not erased. I still sense someone suffers and the work matters, even when I forget who."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Then, by means of deception and cunning, I managed to stow away on a Chartist vessel that had been delivering supplies and equipment to Amsanct. I disembarked on {g|Encyclopedia:FootfallGlossary}Footfall{/g}. I have not returned to Amsanct since. All the experiments you have witnessed, I have conducted them for one purpose — to find a way to save my dearest colleague."
  - After: "I stowed away on a Chartist supply ship to {g|Encyclopedia:FootfallGlossary}Footfall{/g} and never returned. Every experiment since was to save him."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Companion/CompanionQuest/Manipulus_Q2/WhyRunEogan/WhyRunEogan_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Funny, you failed to ask yourself that question when you condemned Nuncius to torment."

  - After: [Pull out your chrono] "You have one minute to explain."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am sure that you had your reasons. I should like to hear them."
  - After: "You had your reasons. Let's hear them."

  - Before: "There never was any laboratory, or any samples, was there?"
  - After: "There was never any lab or samples, was there?"

  - Before: "I have had enough of your antics. Go wherever you wish, but I will not be joining you."
  - After: "Enough antics. Go where you like, without me."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Look at the chrono] "Time's up. Is that all you have to say to me?"
  - After: [Look at the chrono] "Time's up. Is that all?"
- **Player**

  - After: "I listened. Now you listen."

  - After: "You're a coward. You butcher your memory and stall while your friend suffers. Return to Nuncius and let him go."

  - After: "You've achieved much. Stop doubting. You'll save Nuncius — the end justifies the means."

  - Before: "You will not be alone. We will do this together."
  - After: "You won't be alone. We'll do this together."

  - Before: "I hope you mean it. I won't give you another chance."

- **Player**
  - Before: [Glance at the chrono] "Next time, try to be quicker about realising that I am always right."
  - After: [Glance at the chrono] "Next time, realise I'm right quicker."
- **Player**
  - Before: "So be it, forget about Nuncius. You may remain on the ship as long as you wish and continue your research."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Zeta-42//33-Mu, I repeat! I, Genetor Extremis Eogunn Februs, am requesting an escort to the flagship of the {g|Encyclopedia:ExploratorsGlossary}Explorator{/g} Cognisance Fleet."
  - After: "Zeta-42//33-Mu! Genetor Extremis Eogunn Februs requests escort to the {g|Encyclopedia:ExploratorsGlossary}Explorator{/g} Cognisance Fleet."

  - Before: {n}Eogunn's galvanic cell crackles angrily.{/n} "This is absurd! Appalling! I need to..." {n}Then he notices you.{/n} "Rogue Trader... I..."

- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Magos Februs, do you truly believe flight is the best course? You know too much.   - Before: "I'm not ready. I'm sorry, {name}. I need more time — a few years to research, perhaps more. Nuncius's life is at stake, I cannot decide his fate with incomplete data. I panicked and named a system where trading vessels often pass through, so I can get to {g|Encyclopedia:FootfallGlossary}Footfall{/g} and from there join the Explorators in the hope of buying time and discovering new knowledge.   - After: "I'm not ready, {name}. I need more data to decide Nuncius's fate. Amsanct terrified me. I panicked, planning to reach {g|Encyclopedia:FootfallGlossary}Footfall{/g} and the Explorators."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No, there was not. I do not have a solution to Nuncius's problem. If such materials had existed, I never would have left them behind. Never."
  - After: "No. I have no solution for Nuncius."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Please understand — is it possible to conduct an experiment without having all the relevant data? I must prepare."
  - After: "Without data, how can I experiment? I must prepare."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn nods curtly.{/n} "Perhaps that is for the best. I thank you for everything, {name}. I hope one day I can find the answer that eludes me, and tell Nuncius of your outstanding qualities. Farewell." {n}He turns around and beckons 'Nuncius' after him. The servo-skull's empty eye sockets express nothing.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn nods.{/n} "Perhaps best. Thank you, {name}. Farewell." {n}He leaves; 'Nuncius' follows.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes. I only apologise for burdening you with my troubles, and then daring to betray your trust again. Flesh is weak, and mine is no exception."
  - After: "Yes. Forgive me for betraying you again. Flesh is weak."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn meets your eye with a haunted expression on his face.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn looks haunted.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn goes pale. He opens his mouth silently, unable to find a response. When the shock wears off, he closes his organic eye and the wrinkles on his face smooth out.{/n} "You are right. I cannot run forever. I keep insisting that this is all for Nuncius, but I am not only a coward, I am a consummate liar. I think only of myself. I choose a phantom to hide from the pain. It is time to finally choose my dearest colleague. And... to say goodbye."
  - After: {n}Eogunn goes pale.{/n} "You're right. I'm a coward and a liar, hiding behind a phantom. Time to choose my dearest colleague. And... say goodbye."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My duty... Heresy of my own making. I have elevated myself and Nuncius above mere components in a mechanism. Every screw can be replaced by another, no matter how useful it may be. It is my duty to replace the screw, to purge the corrosion from my soul. Even if I must sacrifice... a colleague. The Omnissiah commands it."
  - After: "My heresy... Every screw is replaceable. I must purge the corrosion, even at the cost of... a colleague. The Omnissiah commands it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Of course... I have been plagued by doubt for so long, but why? Is it because I have lost my mind that I have lost my ability to think? I am Genetor Extremis Eogunn Februs, sage and alchemist. The Omnissiah has granted me knowledge and the ability to comprehend, and I dare not doubt. For I am a conduit of His design, and if I doubt myself, I doubt the Machine God. I have spoken."
  - After: "Why doubt? I am Genetor Extremis Eogunn Februs. To doubt myself is to doubt the Machine God. I have spoken."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Shock is replaced by peals of laughter.{/n} "Sobering honesty, {name}! If a machine does not fulfil its function, it should be repaired. I fell into an abyss of emotion and doubt, failing to consider the situation pragmatically. After all, to you, I am a tool. Of course you will not let me just walk away. Which means I can only move forward. I will have to take the risk simply because I have no other choice."
  - After: {n}He laughs.{/n} "Sobering honesty, {name}! A broken tool gets repaired. Forward it is — no choice."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you. I have realised my purpose. I will not flee again until I see this through to the end. That is my vow."
  - After: "Thank you. I won't flee again. My vow."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest bows decorously.{/n} "Then all that remains is to find a way to Amsanct."
  - After: {n}He bows.{/n} "Now, a way to Amsanct."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are cruel, {name}. Cruel, but correct — I was rash and self-absorbed. I cannot afford to behave that way again. Only calculation and preparation will help me this time."
  - After: "Cruel, {name}, but correct. This time, only calculation."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "The flickers of colour, so bright and so frantic, they shift and bleed into one another, forming one ugly blot... He is on the edge, Lord Captain. At his limit." {n}Cassia whispers so quietly that her words reach you alone.{/n}
  - After: "His colours bleed together... He's at his limit, Lord Captain." {n}Cassia whispers.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Great relief shows on Eogunn's face.{/n} "{name}, thank you. I hoped you would understand, though I did not expect such a generous offer. I will only ask for your mercy — do not remind me of the truth. Sooner or later, I will remember it myself. But until then, I prefer to believe that my dearest colleague is still with me. Isn't that so, Nuncius?"
  - After: {n}Eogunn looks relieved.{/n} "Thank you, {name}. Don't remind me of the truth. Let me believe my dearest colleague is with me. Right, Nuncius?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servo-skull is silent. As always.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servo-skull is silent.{/n}

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Companion/EogannFarewell/EogannFarewell_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Let me guess, the words of yet another wise man?"
  - After: "Another wise man's words?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Eogunn, I am glad that we crossed paths."
  - After: "Eogunn, I'm glad we met."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If we survive, what will you do after?"
  - After: "If we survive, what then?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Prepare yourself, Eogunn. A difficult battle lies ahead — this is an incontrovertible fact."
  - After: "Prepare, Eogunn. A hard battle lies ahead — incontrovertible fact."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Nuncius, I will not forget you."
  - After: "Nuncius, I won't forget you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn is levitating, with his arms folded over his belly and his organic eye closed.{/n} "{name}, on this occasion, I have no words of wisdom, no valedictions, or ready answers. I choose to forget the perfection of statistics, to throw off the shackles of probability, and to reject the cold flawlessness of mathematics, abandoning attempts to calculate the odds of victory. There is a time for contemplation. That time is at an end. May the Omnissiah guide our deeds."
  - After: {n}Eogunn levitates, eye closed.{/n} "{name}, no wisdom this time, no odds. Contemplation is over. Omnissiah guide us."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Everyone's hospitality has its limits — I will leave your retinue and continue my research. I have learned much on your ship, but my hunger for knowledge is not yet sated; it draws me onward. Thank you, Rogue Trader, may the Omnissiah light your path."
  - After: "I'll leave to continue my research. Thank you, Rogue Trader. Omnissiah light your path."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Manipulus smiles mischievously.{/n} "{name}, let me tell you a secret. Not every fact declared to be incontrovertible is actually so. Let us test the robustness of your claim together, as befits two colleagues."
  - After: {n}He grins.{/n} "{name}, not every incontrovertible fact is. Let's test yours, colleague."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Nuncius was but one of many — the Imperium is full of people whose suffering is unbearable. The Omnissiah has blessed me with skills that can alleviate that suffering, or end it through a merciful death. You have given me the resolve to follow this path. I will embark on my wanderings, and let the inscrutable currents of the Motive Force guide me to those in need."
  - After: "Many suffer like Nuncius. My skills can ease it, or grant merciful death. I'll wander where the Motive Force leads."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I will set foot on the path of redemption. The lessons I have learned from my attempts to create the Triasomata will allow me to direct my skills in a course pleasing to the Omnissiah. I will grant longevity to the worthy, enabling them to defy death in service to the Imperium. In the likeness of the Motive Force, I will nourish the key elements of the Imperium's machinery so that their functions will be carried out to the last."
  - After: "I'll seek redemption, using my Triasomata lessons to grant the worthy longevity in the Imperium's service."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Nuncius and I will continue to refine the triasomia procedure. In order to do so, I will require a great deal of technologies that are... not Imperial in origin. I will seek them out, continuing to experiment on myself, and I will achieve perfection! Even if the Imperium misunderstands me, I will defy death — it is my duty."
  - After: "Nuncius and I will perfect triasomia with... non-Imperial tech, testing on myself. I'll defy death — my duty."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I was pleased to share my thoughts, deeds, and silence with you, {name}. There is no higher good than to know oneself and to be known by another — for knowledge is the providence of the Omnissiah."
  - After: "I was glad to know you, {name}, and be known. Such is the Omnissiah's providence."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servo-skull remains true to himself, staying silent until the last. Perhaps he simply hates goodbyes.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servo-skull stays silent. Perhaps he hates goodbyes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You could say that. Nuncius spoke those words to me the first time we met. Now I say them to you in farewell."
  - After: "Nuncius's words when we first met. Now my farewell."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Companion/KTCTechpriestDebate/KTCTechpriestDebate_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I see you are consumed with anger, but I do not understand why. Kindly explain yourselves."
  - After: "You're furious, but why? Explain."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Enough. I am ready to adjudicate between you."
  - After: "Enough. I'll adjudicate."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Eogunn, your experiments are indeed dangerous. Henceforth, you shall not conduct them outside the laboratory."

  - After: "I can't judge this; I lack knowledge of the Machine God's mysteries."
- **Player**

  - After: "Eogunn, why experiment outside the laboratory?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "If you call each other colleagues, why do you not work together?"
  - After: "If you're colleagues, why not work together?"

  - Before: "I believe the least-biased participant should speak first. Nuncius?"
  - After: "The least-biased speaks first. Nuncius?"

  - Before: "Pasqal, what makes Eogunn's experiments so dangerous?"
  - After: "Pasqal, why are Eogunn's experiments dangerous?"

  - Before: "Nuncius, what do you think?"
  - After: "Nuncius, your view?"

  - After: [Ostentatiously listen to Nuncius] "The Magi are squabbling children? I agree."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal, do not hinder Eogunn in his research."
  - After: "Pasqal, don't hinder Eogunn's research."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Spare me your petty bickering. Pasqal, what exactly has Eogunn done?"
  - After: "Spare me the bickering. Pasqal, what did Eogunn do?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal, you will oversee the righteousness of Eogunn's experiments. Together, you will stabilise and improve the servitors."
  - After: "Pasqal, oversee Eogunn's experiments. Together, improve the servitors."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You're exhausting me. Sort this out yourselves and do not dare disturb me with such trifles again."
  - After: "Sort it out yourselves and never bother me with trifles again."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The very air between the two {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} seems to crackle with tension. The glares Eogunn and Pasqal exchange could melt steel.{/n}
  - After: {n}The two {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} glare at each other.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal straightens up more than usual, as if trying to match the height of his hovering opponent.{/n} "Lord Captain, as an ordained Magos, I bear witness against Genetor Extremis Eogunn Februs. He conducts research that negatively impacts the productivity of the holy rites of {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitor{/g} maintenance and distorts the visage of the Machine God's creations. Such blasphemy tramples the tenets of faith and may lead to critically unpredictable consequences."
  - After: {n}Pasqal stands tall.{/n} "Lord Captain, I accuse Genetor Extremis Eogunn Februs: his research disrupts {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitor{/g} rites. Blasphemy."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Out of respect for Magos Haneumann, I will not respond to such a blatant provocation with aggression. That would be counterproductive. However, I would note that my esteemed colleague is fundamentally mistaken in his interpretation of my actions. I have followed the Quest for Knowledge, serving the Machine God as befits a Genetor Extremis. No blasphemy against His commandments has been committed, as Nuncius can attest."
  - After: "Magos Haneumann misreads me. I serve the Quest for Knowledge. No blasphemy, as Nuncius can attest."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The prerogative of oversight to ensure compliance with the rites is accepted. I request full access to Magos Februs's research. Under these conditions, cooperation will be deemed productive and feasible."
  - After: "Oversight accepted, given full access to his research."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I refuse." {n}Pasqal raises a {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrite{/g} in warning.{/n} "This decision leads to an irresolvable conflict. Cooperation is impossible."
  - After: "I refuse." {n}Pasqal raises a {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrite{/g}.{/n} "Impossible."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Their very nature is blasphemous through committing the heresy of invention. Genetor Februs was supposed to completely eliminate the source of the malign code that had infiltrated the servitors' neural implants. Instead, he altered their mortal flesh in such a way that it is no longer subject to the Machine God's imperatives as transmitted by the implants."
  - After: "Heresy of invention. He was to purge malign code from their implants; instead he freed their flesh from the implants' commands."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "A reasonable question, Rogue Trader, and I believe the answer will prove most satisfactory. After the Triasomata reconstruction {nc|failed to confirm my hypothesis|ended in failure}, I spent considerable time drawing conclusions from it. The fruit of my labours is a formula for bionic synergy that enhances the efficiency of augmetic integration with the host."
  - After: "After the Triasomata {nc|failed to confirm my hypothesis|ended in failure}, I devised a bionic synergy formula for better augmetic integration."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn flares with indignation, poised to launch into an impassioned tirade... but abruptly catches himself, instead gazing dejectedly at the servo-skull.{/n} "Very well, Rogue Trader. I will submit to your decision. You are right, Nuncius. Scaling unproven solutions could lead to unfortunate consequences."
  - After: {n}Eogunn bristles, then deflates.{/n} "Very well. You're right, Nuncius. It's risky."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Nuncius, the issue of productive integration of augmetics into the living flesh of a host is the cornerstone of all my endeavours!" {n}Eogunn falls silent for a few seconds, as if processing his interlocutor's response.{/n} "I am disappointed by your attempts to remain neutral in this debate."
  - After: "Nuncius, augmetic integration is my life's work!" {n}A pause.{/n} "Your neutrality disappoints."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I am afraid you will have to accept the status quo, esteemed colleague." {n}Eogunn makes no effort to conceal the smugness in his voice.{/n} "Thank you for your agreement, Rogue Trader. I will immediately resume my work of implementing the formula in the remaining servitors."
  - After: "Accept it, colleague." {n}Smugly.{/n} "Thank you, Rogue Trader. Back to the servitors."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I do not deny my actions, Rogue Trader. Indeed, I have introduced several experimental modifications to the servitors' construction, modifications that increase their productivity and task efficiency. But does this not enhance their utility? The essence of Magos Haneumann's accusations eludes me."
  - After: "Yes, I modified the servitors to work better. Isn't that useful?"
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priests bow and depart together, conversing quietly in {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Lingua-Technis{/g}. It is uncertain how long this fragile peace between them will last, but there is hope that their collaboration will bear fruit.{/n}
  - After: {n}They leave together, murmuring in {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Lingua-Technis{/g}. A fragile peace.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Genetor Extremis Februs was summoned to pacify a group of frenzied servitors. Given his rank and presumed breadth of knowledge, the risk of disruption to the sacred rites was deemed minimal. However, the Genetor exceeded his remit and performed rites on several servitors that do not conform to the paradigm of the Cult Mechanicus, replacing some of their blessed implants with organic matter."
  - After: "Sent to calm frenzied servitors, he replaced blessed implants with organic matter."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servo-skull tactfully remains silent, granting the opposing parties complete freedom to express their views.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servo-skull stays tactfully silent.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Several indignant bursts of binharic chatter precede Pasqal's response.{/n} "Directive acknowledged, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}Angry binharic.{/n} "Acknowledged, Lord Captain."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn nods reluctantly.{/n} "The requirement is satisfactory. I am prepared to share my knowledge and methods with Magos Haneumann, provided this allows me to continue my experiments and convince him of the purity of my thoughts and deeds. Nuncius will bear witness to this tech-oath."
  - After: {n}Eogunn nods reluctantly.{/n} "Acceptable, if I may continue. Nuncius will witness this tech-oath."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Out of the question." {n}Eogunn shakes his head.{/n} "The outcome of the proposed cooperation is predetermined, and it is most unfavourable, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "Out of the question." {n}He shakes his head.{/n} "It would end badly."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Is that a rhetorical question?" {n}The alembic on Eogunn's shoulder hisses, releasing a cloud of acrid vapour.{/n} "No, I see that you truly wish to hear the answer. Each follows their own path to knowledge, comprehending existence through the wisdom of the Omnissiah. My path and that of Magos Haneumann diverged at the very beginning."
  - After: "Rhetorical?" {n}His alembic hisses.{/n} "Our paths to knowledge diverged from the start."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The vox-emitters on both Tech-Priests emit brief binharic arias, signifying the end of the conversation. Pasqal and Eogunn depart swiftly, avoiding any interaction with one another.{/n}
  - After: {n}They chirp binharic farewells and leave separately.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servo-skull remains silent, unwilling to enter the argument.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servo-skull stays silent.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}After a brief pause, Eogunn adds, addressing the servo-skull,{/n} "Yes, Nuncius, bone tissue is no less vital and stable, but it would have been less convincing in this particular case."
  - After: {n}To the servo-skull:{/n} "Yes, Nuncius, bone too, but less convincing."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Both Tech-Priests turn toward the servo-skull, which has not uttered a single word. Pasqal glares malevolently while Eogunn opens his mouth to object, then thinks better of it.{/n}
  - After: {n}Both turn to the silent servo-skull. Pasqal glares; Eogunn bites back an objection.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The operational stability of the resulting modified servitors cannot be prognosticated. The ship's machine spirits may find themselves defenceless and fall victim to entropy, which would begin to multiply within the computational cycle."
  - After: "Unpredictable. Entropy could spread to the machine spirits."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Is productive efficiency not the highest value for a servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g}? Servitor malfunctions will occur less frequently, shorter maintenance times will be required, and the labours of the {g|Encyclopedia:Technomat}technomats{/g} will be optimised. The utility of such a solution is indisputable and therefore requires no preliminary investigation."
  - After: "Isn't efficiency the {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g}'s highest value? Fewer malfunctions, optimised {g|Encyclopedia:Technomat}technomats{/g}. Indisputable."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Unthinkable." {n}Pasqal's visor flashes crimson.{/n} "I assess collaboration with Genetor Februs to be counterproductive. His willingness to distort dogma in order to justify his own flaws borders dangerously on heresy."
  - After: "Unthinkable." {n}Pasqal's visor flashes.{/n} "He bends dogma. Near heresy."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "This statement is false. Efficiency is a consequence of observing proper rites, not a cause for worship. The rejection of standardised methods of service in the pursuit of increased productivity is a Category Five blasphemy. Optimising the labour of technomats is not the prerogative of a Genetor Extremis. Each serves according to their function." {n}Magos Haneumann's visor flashes red for a fraction of a second.{/n} "This alone is an incontrovertible fact."
  - After: "False. Efficiency follows rites. Abandoning them is Category Five blasphemy, and technomats are not a Genetor's concern." {n}His visor flashes.{/n} "An incontrovertible fact."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn raises a finger in a didactic manner.{/n} "My intervention did not violate the protocols of servitorisation. Their minds still follow the machine algorithms. No heresy has been committed. Colleague, you are overly accustomed to relying upon the cold orderliness of the Ferrum Sanctum and you perceive organic matter as something mutable and unreliable. Yet the living cell is one of the most perfect and stable aggregates created by the Omnissiah."
  - After: {n}Eogunn raises a finger.{/n} "Their minds still obey; no heresy. You trust only the Ferrum Sanctum, but living cells are stable too."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}Both Tech-Priests stare at you intently.{/n}
  - After: {n}Both Tech-Priests stare at you.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I am registering a high level of sound judgement in the stated decision." {n}Pasqal bows almost imperceptibly.{/n} "The consequences of Genetor Februs's malfunction and irrelevant decisions will be rectified immediately, and the functioning of the ship's machine spirits will be optimised according to sacred protocols."
  - After: "Sound judgement." {n}Pasqal bows slightly.{/n} "Genetor Februs's errors will be rectified."

  - After: {n}The Tech-Priest snaps his fist shut on the sparks: a stout, hovering {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} priest, bearded in cables.{/n}

- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest steadily exhales and opens an eye.{/n} "You are correct, Nuncius, I risk boring the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTraderGlossary}Rogue Trader{/g} with my protracted ruminations.   - Before: "Correct, entirely correct! Rarely do I meet such astute interlocutors among the laity." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Manipulus}Manipulus{/g}'s eyes light up. There is no hint of sarcasm or condescension in his praise — Eogunn is genuinely pleased, like a proud mentor commending a student on their insight.{/n} "I respectfully initiate a request for an audience — I must discover what other gems of knowledge are hiding within your rich mind."

  - After: {n}Argenta raises an eyebrow.{/n} "It doesn't answer? Peculiar!"

  - Before: "The Bloodspun Web also speaks to its departed brothers and sisters. But the answer we receive is the silence granted by the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}Undying One{/g}."
  - After: "The Bloodspun Web speaks to its dead too. The {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}Undying One{/g} answers with silence."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Your thanks are accepted, but my service is not yet at an end."
  - After: "Thanks accepted, but I'm not done."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Not quite. I humbly ask that you hear my petition."
  - After: "Not quite. Hear my petition."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "The clergy of the Altar-Templum-Calixis-Ext-17 cloister, in gratitude for the tidings of the sacred archeotech, request that you be attended by Magos Eogunn Februs and the unit Nuncius.   - After: "My cloister offers Nuncius and me to the von Valancius dynasty, to tend the Sector Bionica and experiment for Knowledge."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "It is my creed. The incontrovertible fact that has defined my existence for as long as I can recall, and I recall a great deal.
