I am intimately familiar with machines such as the one that I restored to life — I will school the members of the priesthood on board in its litanies of maintenance and operation, and reveal the secrets of the command runes so they may operate it themselves."
  - After: "My creed: the union of flesh and metal. I'll teach your priests to run the machine I restored."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "An excellent observation! My technical designation is Manipulus." {n}His {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g} spring to life, pointing at his augmented abdomen.{/n} "And here is the galvanic cell, the repository of the Motive Force. It — no, that will take too long, better to give a demonstration. Observe!"
  - After: "Excellent! I am a Manipulus." {n}His {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g} point to his abdomen.{/n} "My galvanic cell holds Motive Force. Observe!"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's vox emits a binharic trill, solemn and oppressive.{/n} "Confirmed: the sacrament of tech-relic maintenance has been performed correctly. Protocol for exchange of sacred regalia initiated." {n}The Tech-Priest's gaze fixes on Eogunn's robe.{/n} "Registering the affiliation of this blessed tech-unit to the clergy of the {g|Encyclopedia:ForgeWorldGlossary}forge world{/g} Stygies VIII." {n}A scarlet spark flickers in his blue optical augmetic, almost as if Pasqal has narrowed his eyes in suspicion.{/n} "Requesting confirmation of the unit's familiarity with the standards of the Catechism of Maintenance and Safety in effect on this vessel."
  - After: {n}Pasqal trills.{/n} "Maintenance correct." {n}He eyes the robe.{/n} "Unit of {g|Encyclopedia:ForgeWorldGlossary}forge world{/g} Stygies VIII." {n}His optic flares.{/n} "Confirm you know this vessel's safety Catechism."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "It is my pleasure to confirm the protocol for the exchange of sacred regalia and greet my brother in ministry." {n}There is no tension detectable in Eogunn's voice — rather, there is inexplicable excitement.{/n} "The vows taken in this temple are known to me, and I promise to honour them. I request a meeting with my esteemed colleague to facilitate knowledge exchange and to discuss values."
  - After: "Confirmed, brother." {n}Eogunn sounds excited.{/n} "I'll honour the vows. Let us exchange knowledge."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Folding his arms over his stomach, the Tech-Priest addresses Nuncius:{/n} "Scepticism is undeniably one of the instruments of Knowledge, dearest colleague. It guards us against many heresies, preventing ego and vanity from clouding reason on the path of service. But as you see, Nuncius, it is not justified in every circumstance." {n}After a moment's silence, Eogunn nods.{/n} "Rogue Trader, Nuncius states that you are a person of rare perspicacity and prudence. I record this as an incontrovertible fact and thank you for your hospitality."
  - After: {n}He addresses Nuncius.{/n} "Scepticism was unjustified here, colleague." {n}He nods.{/n} "Rogue Trader, Nuncius calls you rarely perceptive. Thank you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest twists the bolt on his beard one final time, then nods politely.{/n}
  - After: {n}He twists his beard bolt and nods.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}A faint smile plays on Eogunn's lips.{/n} "Declined with gratitude and due reverence. The tech-unit Nuncius is designated as a personal instrument of the quest for the divine, which confers the privilege of privacy. That includes privacy from intrusion by entities of equal standing."
  - After: {n}Eogunn smiles.{/n} "Declined. Nuncius is my personal instrument, privileged with privacy — even from equals."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Manipulus}Manipulus{/g} looks blankly at you, then tilts his bulk forward, reducing his hovering height so that his feet almost brush the deck.{/n} "I apologise, Rogue Trader. I was delighted to find such keen interest in my nature and... forgot myself."
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Manipulus}Manipulus{/g} sinks low.{/n} "Apologies, Rogue Trader. I forgot myself."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Attack him?" {n}Eogunn twists a bolt on his beard in confusion.{/n} "I merely used him as a visual aid for a harmless demonstration conducted under controlled conditions. Furthermore, in the process, I identified several faults in his augments and repaired them. I assure you that any effects on his organic components were negligible."
  - After: "Attack him?" {n}Eogunn twists a beard bolt.{/n} "A harmless demonstration. I even fixed his augments."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Manipulus}Manipulus{/g} turns to Nuncius and listens intently. After a few moments, he nods.{/n} "Yes, you're right, the Rogue Trader is concerned with the ethics of the matter." {n}Eogunn turns back to you, bowing his head.{/n} "I will endeavour to temper my enthusiasm in the future."
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Manipulus}Manipulus{/g} listens to Nuncius.{/n} "Yes, ethics." {n}He bows his head.{/n} "I'll temper my enthusiasm."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}The Seneschal clears his throat, looking bemused.{/n} "I... shall bear in mind Master Nuncius's eloquence."
  - After: {n}Abelard clears his throat.{/n} "Noted, Master Nuncius's eloquence."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I fear my rendering will lack the sophistication inherent in Nuncius's {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Lingua-Technis{/g}, but, to crudely summarise, he is honoured by your attention and records the moment as significant."
  - After: "Crudely, from his {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Lingua-Technis{/g}: he's honoured."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn nods with satisfaction.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn nods, satisfied.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}For an instant, crimson engulfs the blue of Pasqal's visors. A disgruntled rasp trickles from his vox:{/n} "Status confirmed. Rejection of request acknowledged as valid."
  - After: {n}Pasqal's visors flash crimson.{/n} "Rejection acknowledged."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "But of course, I did not come empty-handed. I would like to present you with this augment. Now that the machine spirit of the implantation throne is awake, I can bestow its blessing upon you or one of your retinue, should the Rogue Trader will it."
  - After: "A gift: this augment. With the implantation throne awake, I can grant it to you or your retinue."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}His unaugmented eye closes and his mouth relaxes into a serene smile. Crossing his arms over his augmented belly, the Tech-Priest inhales deeply of air infused with ozone and sacred unguents.{/n} "A wise man once said that a machine spirit cannot be looked upon. And he was right, for the {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g}, in His infinite wisdom, has concealed His creation even from the gaze of His most devoted servants. But can the believer come to know the nature of a machine only through an eye of organics or steel? No. For the vapour that brings forth the scent of sacred unguents is the spirit's breath, the rumbling of joints and rods is the beating of its heart, and the Motive Force is the current of its blood."
  - After: {n}He smiles serenely.{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g} hides the machine spirit, yet its breath is vapour, its blood the Motive Force."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I have already transferred the basic Rite of Operation to a qualified contingent in the Sector Bionica. If you refuse us, Nuncius and I will linger just long enough to pass on the rest of our knowledge, after which we will disembark. The augmentation procedures can be performed without my participation."
  - After: "If refused, we'll finish teaching the Sector Bionica, then leave. Augmentation works without me."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Nuncius expresses his sorrow. I share his sentiments, but since the Omnissiah has determined this path for me, so be it."
  - After: "Nuncius is saddened, as am I. The Omnissiah wills it."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest looks stunned.{/n} "Do you think I would dare walk about with an anathema, a profane parody of the human mind, the greatest heresy against the Omnissiah? What an absurd idea!"
  - After: {n}He looks stunned.{/n} "Carry the greatest heresy against the Omnissiah? Absurd!"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}After Eogunn regains his composure, he raises his finger.{/n} "I honour the Crimson Accord of Mars and swear before the all-knowing, all-seeing Machine God that Nuncius is no spawn of tech-heresy. If I lie, then let me be struck down by the electromagnetic pulse of His wrath, and let the Motive Force desert my limbs forever and ever!"
  - After: {n}He raises a finger.{/n} "By the Crimson Accord of Mars, Nuncius is no tech-heresy. May the Machine God strike me if I lie!"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Nuncius is an incredibly sophisticated creation of sacred algorithms, interlaced with my own. It is difficult for a layperson to grasp their inner workings, yet not a single one violates the commandments of the Omnissiah."
  - After: "Nuncius is sacred algorithms woven with mine. Complex, but none break the Omnissiah's laws."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "The sacrament of Ferrum Sanctum will be made available to you and your retinue. That, too, is an incontrovertible fact." {n}His spherical torso rolls forward again in a deferential bow.{/n}
  - After: "The sacrament of Ferrum Sanctum will be yours." {n}He bows.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He stabs a mechadendrite into the augmented arm of a nearby technomat: power snakes along the Manipulus's chrome claw into his cell; the technomat's vox stutters and rasps, and then his implant goes limp. Once certain that you have seen the effect, Eogunn sends the power back into the augment and it returns to life.{/n} "Questions?"
  - After: {n}He drains a technomat's augmented arm limp, then powers it back.{/n} "Questions?"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "In other words, allow Nuncius and I to remain on the ship and accompany you. We are well-versed in augmetics, genetics, alchemy, the anatomy of humans and abominable {g|Encyclopedia:XenosGlossary}xenos{/g} alike, and the mysteries of the Motive Force and of sacred engineering. These fields of knowledge may also be employed to eliminate units whose views are not conducive to productive debate."
  - After: "Let us stay. We know augmetics, genetics, alchemy, human and {g|Encyclopedia:XenosGlossary}xenos{/g} anatomy — useful against foes, too."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Junior Lexmechanic Carr-Ain, operator of auxiliary terminal 289-0 of the lower workshops of Altar-Templum-Calixis-Ext-17. A pragmatist and a bureaucrat who saw the world solely through the prism of statistics, endless parades of outflows and inflows — he had little interest in anything other than keeping track of valves and vents. But, now and then, he would drop pearls of wisdom such as these without even noticing it himself. I felt it was my duty to pick them up."
  - After: "Junior Lexmechanic Carr-Ain, a valve-counting bureaucrat who dropped pearls of wisdom unawares. I picked them up."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix frowns slightly and nods, making some sort of mental note.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix frowns, noting it.{/n}
- **Nuncius**
  - Before: {n}If the servo-skull has heard you, it makes no sign of it.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servo-skull gives no sign.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn pensively tightens a bolt on his beard and nods.{/n} "Amazing sincerity, Nuncius. It is gratifying to see that you have not lost your sense of tact over the years."
  - After: {n}Eogunn nods.{/n} "Such sincerity, Nuncius. Still tactful."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Companion/ManipulusSelfSurgery/ManipulusSelfsurgery_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I would like to hear Nuncius's position."
  - After: "I'd like Nuncius's position."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It's not worth it. You can try to prolong existence indefinitely, but after a certain point, such existence can scarcely be called life."
  - After: "Not worth it. Prolonged past a point, existence isn't life."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your methods are highly original, Eogunn. What experiment are you conducting?"
  - After: "Original methods, Eogunn. What's the experiment?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Step closer] "I did not grant you leave to kill yourself!"
  - After: [Step closer] "I didn't allow you to kill yourself!"

  - Before: "Determinacy in amalgam individuals? Wait, is this related to your previous experiment?"
  - After: "Determinacy in amalgams? Tied to your last experiment?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why are you torturing yourself? You could have dulled the pain with stimulants."
  - After: "Why torture yourself? Use stimulants for the pain."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What knowledge are you seeking this time? Does it warrant this... self-excavation?"
  - After: "What knowledge warrants this self-excavation?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Wait. You mentioned two attempts? There was another Triasomata?"
  - After: "Two attempts? There was another Triasomata?"

  - Before: "Elaborate on your thesis, Eogunn. Why is vanquishing death so important to you?"
  - After: "Elaborate. Why does vanquishing death matter so much?"

  - Before: "Incredible... How are you able to endure something like this?"
  - After: "Incredible... How do you endure this?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why would you reverse someone's augmentation?"
  - After: "Why reverse someone's augmentation?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are right. Vanquishing death will be the triumph of reason and the triumph of being, born not by the will of chance but by the will of humanity."
  - After: "You're right. Vanquishing death will be humanity's triumph of reason, not chance."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Well, I shall readily share my thoughts."
  - After: "I'll gladly share my thoughts."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Life is a duty, not merely a right. A person must live as long as they are able to bring benefit to the Imperium."
  - After: "Life is a duty. Live as long as you can serve the Imperium."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Is this some special kind of Tech-Priest self-torture?"
  - After: "Is this Tech-Priest self-torture?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Should you break yourself, I will not fix you."
  - After: "Break yourself, and I won't fix you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Fascinating. I have never seen such operations performed on oneself before."
  - After: "Fascinating. I've never seen self-surgery like this."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The implantation throne stands before you in all its glory, illuminated with discharges of the Motive Force. A massive body is laid out upon it, and it takes you a moment to recognise it as Eogunn.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Nuncius, I am in complete agreement that any interference with the function of the galvanic abdomen will lead to acute hypertension, but I have the situation perfectly under control. All his body cavities have been carefully opened — you watch the crimson-pink lump of his augmented heart as it beats in his chest, and you see the faint flickering of his galvanic cell through the whitish film of his peritoneum.{/n}
  - After: "Nuncius, the galvanic abdomen risks hypertension, but not death." {n}His body lies open, heart beating, cell flickering.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Risks of a fatal outcome? The risks are negligible when what is at stake is crossing the limit of death itself.   - After: "Risk is negligible when crossing death is at stake. Both my Triasomata attempts failed; I need a new method." {n}He looks at you.{/n} "Your thoughts?"
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: {n}Eogunn nods; mechadendrites stitch his wounds.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Eogunn's mechadendrites do not stop rooting in his insides even for a moment.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am currently engaged in a study of determinacy in the existence of amalgam individuals. Your presence will no doubt enliven the discussion my dearest colleague and I are having as I work. You have caught Nuncius and me about halfway through our disputation."
  - After: "I study determinacy in amalgam individuals. Join Nuncius's and my debate."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "By the Machine God, be careful, Rogue Trader!" {n}Grimacing with pain and exertion, Eogunn struggles to extend one of his manipulators to the numerous toggle switches on the apparatus.{/n} "The throne circuit is overloaded with galvanic energies and so the current is rampaging.   - After: "Careful!" {n}Eogunn strains toward the switches.{/n} "The circuit's overloaded. Interfere and results become unpredictable!"

Nuncius, this is, truly, fascinating. Blood flow has slowed, the load on the main arteries has fallen dramatically. I classify my current condition as pre-mortem. Viability minimal."
  - After: {n}Manipulators pull out a maroon lump. He goes white, kept awake by the Motive Force.{/n} "Splenic extraction... fascinating. Condition: pre-mortem."

  - Before: {n}A triumphant binharic hymn pouring out of the implantation throne's vox-transmitters interrupts the Manipulus's musings, signalling the completion of the procedure. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Pain is merely the instrument by which living flesh alerts us to deleterious effects upon it. I am using this tool to receive the most complete and, thus, the most valuable information about the consequences of my procedures."
  - After: "Pain is flesh's warning. It gives me the fullest data."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Naturally. This is part of my path on the Quest for Knowledge, just as the creation of Triasomata was, but I have taken a different approach in my current experiment."
  - After: "Naturally. Like the Triasomata, but a different approach."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The throne's machine spirits instantly erupt in a cacophony of alarms. You count no less than thirty beats of your own heart before the pulsing organ is returned to its owner's chest.   - After: {n}Alarms blare. Thirty heartbeats pass before his heart returns.{/n} "Praise the Omnissiah! Thirty seconds is the optimal removal interval!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Deftly deduced from my deliberate vagueness in my last thesis!" {n}Eogunn tries to smile, but winces in pain as the throne's manipulators, obeying the will of the ancient machine spirit, begin to return all the extracted implants to their previous positions.{/n} "You are correct — the one you and I created was the second attempt.   - After: {n}Eogunn sighs.{/n} "Too long a story, Nuncius. I've since grasped more of the {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g}; both failures are mere setbacks."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Because if a machine as functional and multifaceted as the human organism ceases to exist — all practical meaning of it is destroyed." {n}Eogunn's large hands grip the edges of the implantation throne, their knuckles white.{/n} "And I have dared to fathom ways of prolonging life precisely to preserve that meaning.   - After: "When the human machine dies, its meaning is lost." {n}He grips the throne.{/n} "I'd overcome flesh's limits. Death sustains the Imperium." {n}He glances at the skull.{/n} "But life propels it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The hairs on your body stand on end. A tingling, unbearably hot wave of voltage rushes through your nerves, and every muscle twists in a sharp spasm. A powerful pulse of energy propels you backward.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Eogunn smiles through the pain.{/n} "I must assume that you have never met a Genetor of my calibre, Rogue Trader. The procedure is utterly trivial, if one observes the rituals of vivisection and the operational covenants of the Omnissiah."

  - After: "Augments' machine spirits may reject the flesh, causing agony, and removal often risks death. I seek to mitigate this."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A highly unusual goal for a Tech-Priest — in the eyes of the servants of the Omnissiah, human life rarely outweighs the value of augments. Something must have propelled him down this path in the past.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**

Abdominal extraction is impossible — this is an incontrovertible fact."
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Genetor}Genetor{/g} gasps awake.{/n} "Twenty percent: blackout. You were right, Nuncius. Abdominal extraction is impossible."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is impossible to tell whether the servo-skull shares his colleague's excitement.{/n}
  - After: {n}The skull's feelings are unreadable.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servo-skull is silent as always.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servo-skull is silent.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn frowns, pensively tugging at a piston on his beard.{/n} "You differentiate between the concepts of 'life' and 'survival'? But where do you draw the line? Can anything outweigh the desire to live at all costs? I admit, I have not considered the question from such a perspective, but your strength of will impresses me. Perhaps I should show some fortitude as well, and consider my hypothesis from a different angle."
  - After: {n}Eogunn frowns.{/n} "'Life' versus 'survival'? Where's the line? Your will impresses me. I'll rethink my hypothesis."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is extremely gratifying that you share my position!" {n}Eogunn's sonorous, vibrating voice rings with enthusiasm. A discharge bursts from the galvanic cell in his abdomen, sending blue sparks scattering in every direction.{/n} "I hope you will share in this triumph with me, Rogue Trader. I will apply myself to my research with redoubled zeal."
  - After: "You agree!" {n}His cell sprays sparks.{/n} "Share this triumph. I'll redouble my zeal."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Looking at life through the prism of duty is wise. I must never forget the purpose of my ambitions. There is sound reasoning to that argument, more than a little." {n}The Tech-Priest watches with deliberate nonchalance as the tips of the injectors plunge into his pale flesh again and again.{/n} "After all, every organism is a machine of the Omnissiah, and its purpose is to serve humanity."
  - After: "Life as duty — wise." {n}Injectors plunge into him unheeded.{/n} "Every organism is the Omnissiah's machine, made to serve humanity."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes, dearest colleague, you are certainly correct in asserting that death is the natural and inevitable cessation of life processes." {n}The Genetor presses his lips together.{/n} "But is that not why the Omnissiah granted us the gift of reason and the ability to comprehend existence, so that we humans would submit to the natural way of things?   - After: "Yes, colleague, death is inevitable." {n}He presses his lips together.{/n} "But did the Omnissiah give us reason only to submit? Don't machines strive for eternity in His image?"

  - Before: {n}Genetor Ferrenz holds a {g|Encyclopedia:ServoSkulls}servo-skull{/g} in the grip of his steel fingers — Nuncius. A vox-grille has been wired to the skull, from which the binharic hiss of error testing litanies can be heard.{/n}

  - After: {n}Eogunn scowls.{/n} "Ferrenz, you can't fix him, so you claim he's fine—"

  - Before: {n}Angry veins swell on the {g|Encyclopedia:Manipulus}Manipulus{/g}'s forehead.{/n} "The only thing it will show is your unfitness for your post, Ferrenz. Your lies will not fool the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTraderGlossary}Rogue Trader{/g}."
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Manipulus}Manipulus{/g} fumes.{/n} "Your lies won't fool the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTraderGlossary}Rogue Trader{/g}."

  - Before: "No authorisation, access denied. Authorisation required by unit Eogunn Februs."
  - After: "Access denied. Eogunn Februs must authorise."

  - Before: {n}Nuncius sits docilely in your hands. His eye is producing a constant flicker, while a grunting sound crackles from the vox.{/n}

No member of the Adeptus Mechanicus has ever granted this servo-skull the sacred boon of personal authorisation, despite Eogunn Februs's claims to the contrary. To retain information, much less mimic personality characteristics, requires a far more sophisticated {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} and organic base. These are absent here. For the past several decades, this 17-401 model has been operating on basic settings."
  - After: "None, ever. That needs a better {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}. This 17-401 runs on basic settings."

  - After: "Fool! How dare—" {n}Eogunn stops, listening to where Nuncius usually hovers.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}After a few moments, the Tech-Priest nods at the empty air.{/n} "Quite right, Nuncius, I should not have entrusted just anyone with such a delicate matter. Yes, I should have immediately sought out your expert opinion — we should stop this farce and repair you ourselves."
  - After: {n}He nods at empty air.{/n} "Quite right, Nuncius. We'll repair you ourselves."

  - Before: "With my dearest colleague, Nuncius, who else would I...?"
  - After: "With Nuncius, who else...?"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn looks in confusion at the servo-skull in your hands, then over his shoulder{/n}. "But... How... No. It cannot be. Pressing his fingers to his temples, he squeezes his eyes shut, straining desperately to remember something. Suddenly, his eyes fly open and you hear a strangled moan. He looks at you, dumbfounded.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn looks at the skull, then over his shoulder{/n}. "But... I can hear him." {n}He clutches his temples, then stares at you, stunned.{/n}

The {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g} has granted me a revelation, but I feel no gratitude, only heaviness and pain. Would it be a heresy to beg the Machine God to take back this knowledge? Yes, perhaps it would. It is not Nuncius who needs repairing. No, not him at all..."
{n}He looks at the servo-skull as if for the first time.{/n} "I'll take him back, and afterward... Find me on the bridge — I'll share this revelation with you. But for now, I need time to gather my thoughts."
  - After: "Rogue Trader... I apologise to you and Ferrenz. I see now. The {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g}'s revelation brings only pain. It's not Nuncius who needs repair..."
{n}He looks at the skull anew.{/n} "Find me on the bridge later. I need time."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}After a moment's hesitation, Eogunn grumbles,{/n} "I am willing to suffer this gross violation of privacy if it will allow me to expose Genetor Ferrenz's lies. Access to the logs has been granted."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/BeastArena/BA_BothWentOnHelp/BA_BothWentOnHelp_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You are both courageous and irreplaceable. Stand together, shoulder to shoulder, and once again prove yourselves worthy of atonement."
  - After: "You're both brave and irreplaceable. Stand together and earn atonement."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are a disgrace to the Astra Militarum. When faced with a common enemy, you bicker and stall for time. Instead of uniting and fighting."
  - After: "You disgrace the Astra Militarum, bickering instead of uniting."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Headstrong, the both of you. How has your regiment not died out yet?"
  - After: "Headstrong, both of you. How is your regiment still alive?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Captain. Sergeant. Both of you get back to camp."
  - After: "Captain. Sergeant. Back to camp."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have no intention of fighting alongside you. What I want is glory and that monster's blood, and you two are delaying my triumph. Get out of my sight."
  - After: "I want glory and that monster's blood, not you two delaying me. Go."
- **Player**
  - Before: "According to the Astra Militarum Handbook, your defiance of a superior officer qualifies as treason. Are you quite certain you wish to be counted a traitor?"
  - After: "Per the Handbook, defying a superior is treason. Want to be a traitor?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Cage needs you both. What happened to you is the fault of my dynasty. It is time to atone for the wrongs committed against your ancestors."
  - After: "The Cage needs you. My dynasty wronged your ancestors; atone for it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Stop arguing and both of you help me."
  - After: "Stop arguing and help me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am a bearer of a Warrant of Trade, Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius. And here, in the wild reaches of the Koronus Expanse, I represent the might of the God-Emperor. And you shall carry out His will."
  - After: "I am Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius. Here I represent the God-Emperor. Obey His will."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "What a surprise, Captain-Quartermaster! I got orders from Colonel Batoshski to assist {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}. He didn't mention you."
  - After: "Captain? I'm ordered to help {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}, not you."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "Since you brought it up, Sergeant, the Handbook does not obligate me to report my actions to you. And as your direct superior, I did not give you leave to join {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}'s operation."
  - After: "I never let you join {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}, Sergeant."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "I knew you would wish to prove your valour by facing the Drover with only your retinue at your side! Bold, risky... Just like all the legends say Rogue Traders should act."
  - After: "Facing the Drover alone! Like the legends."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "You are right, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. No better way to atone for the deeds of our forebears than turning your weapons on a xenos. Janur?"
  - After: "Right, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Killing xenos atones. Janur?"
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "Yes, Captain! Apologies for this show of weakness. I overstepped."
  - After: "Yes, Captain! I overstepped."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "That's just pretty nonsense. Atonement is only for the one, see. If something happens to the captain-quartermaster and I survive, I'll wish I'd never been born."
  - After: "Nonsense. If the captain dies, I'm done."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "I agree. The Handbook dictates that we always leave some of our fighters in reserve."
  - After: "Agreed. Keep reserves."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "I assure you, Captain, I'm just as capable of doing that much."
  - After: "I can do that too, Captain."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "It is because of that very stubbornness, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We refuse to perish until our duty is done."
  - After: "Stubbornness, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We outlive our duty."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You see how stunned the Merovians are by your reprimand. As the realisation that they are considered an undisciplined rabble sinks in, they all avert their eyes in shame.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Merovians look away, shamed.{/n}
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "Never thought I'd... As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Atonement for the one. And today it's definitely not going to be me."
  - After: "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Atonement for the one. Not me."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: {n}Janur gives Dunawski a long look. Finally, the two of them nod to each other.{/n} "Atonement for the one, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We understand."
  - After: {n}They nod.{/n} "Atonement for the one, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Have you forgotten the meaning of discipline?" {n}The Arbitrator's voice is deceptively calm, but his tense jaw betrays his irritation.{/n} "Rogue Trader, these people are wasting their time arguing. Bring them to order, or let me." {n}Glaito lets out a soft affirmative growl, almost blending in with his master's words.{/n}
  - After: "Forgotten discipline?" {n}Solomorne seethes.{/n} "Order them, or I will." {n}Glaito growls.{/n}
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "You were just going on about the importance of discipline and hierarchy, and now you dare to oppose the Lord Captain's orders?"
  - After: "You defy the Lord Captain?"
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "As you say, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but we shouldn't stand around here for too long."
  - After: "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Let's not linger."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I don't understand. Do you doubt my loyalty? Or my prowess in battle?"
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you doubt my loyalty?"
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: {n}The sergeant watches Dunawski leave.{/n}{br}
"She's a stubborn one, that Dunawski..."
  - After: {n}Janur watches her go.{/n}{br}
"Stubborn, that one..."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: {n}Dunawski nods to herself and turns to you.{/n} "It's a good thing you sent him back. Janur is a good soldier, but he can be too hard-headed. I have faith that our victory is certain, but Zarkov teaches you to always have a backup plan."
  - After: {n}She nods.{/n} "Good. Zarkov says: always a backup plan."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "With all due respect, those same articles also state that cowardice and inaction when command is in peril also constitute treason. You may have us shot for insubordination, but we shall not abandon you."
  - After: "Abandoning command is treason too. Shoot us; we stay."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I have my orders, but Captain Dunawski's death would mean the end of the Cage as we know it! Please, by the God-Emperor, send her back."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Without her, the Cage falls!"
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, Janur is a fine soldier and commander. But his skills are indispensable to the entire regiment. Batoshski can find a new quartermaster, but not so skilled a scout and hunter. He must not risk himself."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, Janur the scout is irreplaceable."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/BeastArena/BA_InspectSarcophagus_dialogue/BA_InspectSarcophagus_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The air is suffocatingly thick with the spicy scent of spores. A modest-looking sarcophagus stands before you. At its base rests a desiccated corpse, clad in robes bearing an insignia.{/n}
  - After: {n}Spore-thick air. A plain sarcophagus; a dried corpse in insignia robes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A cluster of flowers has bloomed across the remains of the unfortunate {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}agent of the Golden Throne{/g}, having literally drained the last of his life-fluids. A miraculously unscathed vox-scribe rests within his inner pocket.{/n}
  - After: {n}Flowers drained the {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}agent of the Golden Throne{/g}. He carries a vox-scribe.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Most of the messages catalogued by the machine spirit have long since been erased from its memory — save for the last.{/n} "Acolyte Watcher, Temple Cell. Attention from the locals has been avoided. We lost Acolytes Keykeeper, Oculus, and Dusk. Bastion Cell has ceased all contact. Void Cell has gone in search of Bastion."
  - After: {n}One message remains.{/n} "Watcher, Temple Cell. Lost Keykeeper, Oculus, Dusk. Bastion silent; Void seeking them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A search of the subject's suspected burial site yielded no results — no body was found. It appears it was never buried. No traces of heresy requiring cleansing. We continue to search for traces of Seberian von Valancius and to purge possible new traces of his heresies. The next marker is the xenoruins at the coordinates recorded in the vox-scribe's memory. Seberian reportedly surveyed them shortly before his death."
  - After: "Burial site empty. Still hunting Seberian von Valancius. Next: xenoruins at stored coordinates, which he surveyed before dying."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your ancestor's final resting place is so simple it would be an affront to the tastes of any Rogue Trader.{/n}
  - After: {n}A tomb too plain for a Rogue Trader.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The small plants clinging to the sarcophagus snap with soft, wet squelches as you move a surprisingly light lid. Inside, you see nothing but a gaping hollow. Neither your ancestor's body nor his legendary sword lie in the sarcophagus.{/n}
  - After: {n}Inside: no body, no legendary sword.{/n}

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/BeastArena/BA_PlanFight/BA_PlanFight_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I order you to deal with the growth."
  - After: "Deal with the growth."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "There it is, Lord Captain... God-Emperor protect us, this is the first time I've ever seen it this close." {n}Captain Dunawski regards the monstrosity with mingled terror and fascination.{/n} "I see two lines of attack. One to the flower, the other to the growth. The flower sprays poisonous pollen, while the growth spews out flesh-eating flies. Which approach do you want me to take, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"
  - After: "There it is." {n}Dunawski stares.{/n} "The flower sprays poison pollen, the growth flesh-eating flies. Which is mine, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Aett-Vater, I know of such creatures. Hiding dishonourably until you lure it from its lair by blood and by force. I have not vanquished these monsters before, but we shall see — perhaps this Drover will prove worthy of a verse!"
  - After: "Aett-Vater, such beasts hide till lured by blood. Perhaps a verse!"
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}The Drukhari's thin lips stretch into a nasty smile.{/n} "Such a creature would be to the taste of any arena owner in Commorragh... but this particular 'drover' has no chance of winding up there — it will die much sooner than that."
  - After: {n}Marazhai smirks.{/n} "Commorragh's arenas would love it. It dies first."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "That abomination is a testament to how xenos influence twists and defiles the very nature of all things. In the light of the God-Emperor, thorns should serve only as protection for fragile blossoms. But, with xenos involved, these barbs pierce the earth and drink its vital humours. Not for the sake of life, but for the sake of desolation."
  - After: "Xenos defile nature. These thorns drink the earth for desolation."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/FlayerTemple/FT_DeadWithAugment_dialogue/FT_DeadWithAugment_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The roots that have broken through the walls are tightly entwined around a desiccated corpse. You can make out that the mummy is wearing rusted armour bearing the Von Valancius emblem and has an {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}augmentation{/g} in place of one arm. You have never seen an implant of this kind before, and it has been crafted with incredible skill.{/n}
  - After: {n}Roots grip a mummy in Von Valancius armour, one arm a masterful, unfamiliar {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}augmentation{/g}.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Yet more evidence of Seberian's expedition, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Another loyal servant of the dynasty who gave his life for his Lord Captain." {n}Abelard's voice resounds with pride at the sight of this deceased retinue member.{/n}
  - After: "Another of Seberian's loyal servants, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Abelard sounds proud.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Despite your best efforts, you fail to avoid the spikes. You can feel them finding gaps in your armour and hungrily digging into your flesh. The puncture wounds immediately start to burn — the plant seems to be poisonous.{/n}
  - After: {n}Poison spikes pierce your armour. The wounds burn.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your fingers close around the augment's metal and you tug it slightly toward you. The corpse's old bones break with a dry crack, and you gently pull the implant out of the tangle of roots.{/n}
  - After: {n}Bones crack; you pull the implant free.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You feel the poisonous spikes scratching at you. Like rooting creatures, they search for any gap in your armour — and fail to find one.{/n}
  - After: {n}Poison spikes find no gap in your armour.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Registering an augmetic of unknown construction, probably handmade. Probability of tech-heresy: 54.89355%. Recommending the release of the machine spirit from the torment of this corrupted abode."
  - After: "Unknown handmade augmetic. Tech-heresy probability: 54.89355%. Free its spirit."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Oh, shereen! What a gorgeous little toy. Not better than mine, of course, but still a hand to inspire envy in all the azhi."
  - After: "Oh, shereen! Gorgeous. Not better than mine, though."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "An interesting piece. It appears to have been made by someone more capable than a typical {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g} craftsman."
  - After: "Too fine for a {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g} craftsman."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "A remarkable specimen. I have never witnessed such bold engineering in sacred iron! An unknown model? A classified prototype? It must be restored and comprehensively studied!"
  - After: "Remarkable! A prototype? It must be restored and studied!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is a marvel that the augmetic survived at all, albeit in a sorry, unusable state. The staff on your flagship should be capable of restoring it.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ruined, but your flagship's staff could restore it.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g}'s twisted, tarnished remains with splayed {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g} make you think of a squashed metal spider.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You eagerly reread the entry. Seberian was persistent in his efforts to get past the closed door. Did he succeed, or did he turn back?{/n}
  - After: {n}Did Seberian get through the door?{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You pass over several corrupted entries, until one, titled "The Truth Prevails", freezes your data-slate.{/n} "For hours upon hours, I prayed to the Omnissiah while devising patterns of xenos glyphs on my mental map, until finally my processing nodes experienced an epiphany. Although the xenos language is untranslatable, a comparative analysis of the glyphs provided me with a coordinate system sufficient for the purpose, enabling me to progress. Using it helped me reduce the range of images to only three. Seberian tried each of them in turn, and one opened the desired door." {n}A description of the glyph follows. You memorise it.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You move the heavy frame aside and rummage through the tangled wires and dried tubes. As you brush decayed scraps of cloth off the body, they reveal a rusted memory module.{/n}
  - After: {n}Under the wires: a rusted memory module.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A powerful shot pulverised the head into a tangle of metal and cables. Your eyes linger on the sprawling metal tentacles. Never before have you seen mechadendrites so peculiarly modified. The killer must have thought the same: one of the limbs is missing, with only a dark and empty connection socket where it ought to be.{/n}
  - After: {n}Head shot to scrap. One odd mechadendrite was taken; its socket is empty.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The buzz inside the memory module grows louder.{/n}
  - After: {n}The module buzzes louder.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After a series of dry clicks, the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} awaken from their long slumber. A steady buzzing sound from within the memory module grows louder, and the data-slate screen produces a pale glow.{/n}
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} wake; the slate glows.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Years of hibernation have taken their toll on the machine spirits and a flood of errors turns the screen red. The long list of journal entries left by the owner is all but completely corrupted. With luck, you might piece together useful information from the surviving fragments.{/n}
  - After: {n}Errors flood the screen. Only fragments of the journal survive.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The memory module belonged to the {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magos{/g} Exalt-117, the {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} of the von Valancius flagship. It appears that your ancestor made the Enginseer part of his retinue for a landing on the planet. Exalt-117 proceeded to keep meticulous records of the expedition's progress. One can but hope that the surviving entries will lift the veil surrounding Seberian's fate.{/n}
  - After: {n}Owner: {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magos{/g} Exalt-117, {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} of the von Valancius flagship, who logged Seberian's landing.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Entry after entry is reported as destroyed by the machine spirits, until finally you chance upon an intact fragment.{/n} "Only the {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g}'s wisdom enables one to find the true path. But what is one to do if the calculation of that path's vector proves incorrect because of unaccounted-for variables? One such variable is Seberian's fixation on the mysteries of the {g|Encyclopedia:XenosGlossary}xenos{/g}. His drive to pass through the sealed temple door is driving the expedition off the path I calculated. Only..." {n}Corrupted and unreadable lines follow.{/n}
  - After: {n}A fragment:{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g} shows the path, but Seberian's {g|Encyclopedia:XenosGlossary}xenos{/g} obsession with the sealed door strays from it. Only..." {n}Corrupted.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The effort to recover Seberian has been postponed several times now. An unpleasant hypothesis has formed at the intersection of my mental paths: not all expedition members desire his return. If events continue along the present vector, I must go and retrieve him myself. The likelihood of losing my way is small, as Seberian was planning on leaving marks behind."
  - After: "Seberian's recovery keeps being delayed; some don't want him back. I'll fetch him myself, following his marks."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Whatever happened to Seberian's retinue, it is quite likely that your ancestor's trail lies behind that door. Now you have only to find the glyph that opens it.{/n}
  - After: {n}Seberian's trail lies past that door. Find its glyph.{/n}

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/FlayerTemple/FT_FalseDoor_dialogue/FT_FalseDoor_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}An enormous gate clearly wrought by inhuman hands. The doors are emblazoned with a multitude of shimmering sigils. The skill evident in the carved xenos inscriptions both awes and disgusts you.{/n}
  - After: {n}A huge xenos gate of shimmering sigils, awesome and disgusting.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You feel your gorge begin to rise as your eyes linger on the gate. The carvings seem otherworldly, and the shimmering is slightly hypnotic: you feel as though, were you to touch the gate with your hand, it would pass straight through.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nausea rises. Your hand might pass right through.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "What a curious find, shereen! My intuition tells me that behind great doors like these, great mysteries often lie... and great treasures... but, more likely, even greater troubles." {n}Jae gives you a grim smile.{/n}
  - After: "Great doors hide treasures, shereen... or troubles." {n}Jae smiles grimly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After a few seconds, you become aware of an interesting detail: the gate appears utterly untouched by time — unlike the ruins around it.{/n}
  - After: {n}Unlike the ruins, the gate is untouched by time.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}A low, threatening growl rolls out of Glaito's muzzle. Solomorne raises his hand in a warning gesture. {/n} "There is danger inside, Rogue Trader. Type of threat: unknown, the augur scan is inconclusive. Consequences of entry are at your own risk."
  - After: {n}Glaito growls.{/n} "Danger inside, Rogue Trader. Unknown type. Enter at your own risk."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix's eyes narrow as he stares at the gate in grim contemplation{/n}: "What lies beyond this gate is unlikely to please me... or you, for that matter."
  - After: {n}Heinrix scowls{/n}: "Nothing beyond will please us."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "{name}, they're giggling again behind my door. But it's... fearful, somehow. Uncertain. I don't know, but anything that makes my little whispers so cheerful rarely means anything good..."
  - After: "{name}, they're giggling, but fearfully. Never good..."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}The Drukhari noisily sniffs and makes a face, examining the door with distrust.{/n} "To fall into such an obvious Oghyr trap would be foolish. If you enter there, it must be when you are prepared and on your own terms."
  - After: {n}Marazhai sniffs.{/n} "An obvious Oghyr trap. Enter on your terms."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The sacred embedded auspexes are registering blasphemous irregularity and are confounded by the inability to satisfy the Quest for Knowledge imperative."
  - After: "Auspexes register blasphemous irregularity. Knowledge unattainable."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "No need to hesitate on the threshold when a battle with the enemies of Humanity awaits us. Let me enter first. Wherever these gates may lead, I will not stray from the path He has blessed!"
  - After: "Let me go first. I won't stray from His path!"

  - Before: {n}Your eyes catch the glint of Batoshski's knife, coated in something greenish. The colonel has used the moment you spent answering Dunawski to coat his knife in poison.{/n}

  - After: "Just spice, heir of Seberian."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Batoshski's attack, meant only to deliver the poison under your skin, nicks your shoulder, leaving a stinging itch. You feel a surge of nausea and a salty tang in your mouth, yet {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_VenomResistance}no further symptoms follow{/d}.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Merovians begin chanting your name. It is soft, the whisper of hunters accustomed to silence, yet it cuts to your core. Oddly, Vedka does not rush to join the collective surge.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_KnowAboutIzhdrigWeakness}Pain wracks{/d} Batoshski's body and, for the first time, he screams. Wildly, furiously, frantically. His grip loosens, and blood gushes from his wounds.{/n}
  - After: {n}{d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_KnowAboutIzhdrigWeakness}Pain wracks{/d} Batoshski. He screams, letting go.{/n}
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: {n}The colonel nods, then gives a familiar predatory grin.{/n} "I swear by the blood that has been spilled, the blood now being spilled, and the blood that I will spill, that my life, soul, and loyalty without reserve belong to you, {name} von Valancius."

  - Before: {n}Izdrig steps back, shaking his head as he struggles to recover. The wounds on his body would have killed any other man, yet Batoshski stands in spite of it all, simply refusing to stop. And yet... He raises his hands.{/n}

Unexpectedly, there is respect in his smile, but it is that of a beast that has met another predator.{/n} "Because I wish to hand over the regiment to you following every tradition. ## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/SurvivorCamp/ElevatorGuardsman/SC_ElevatorGuardsman_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal, I believe this is a task for you."
  - After: "Pasqal, this is for you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Wait. I will shut down something in the settlement and return."
  - After: "Wait. I'll shut something down in the settlement."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I must have misheard. Are you suggesting that I scurry about the settlement like some sort of servant?"
  - After: "You expect me to run errands like a servant?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Eogunn, can't you solve our little problem?"
  - After: "Eogunn, can you solve this?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A young man is leaning over the control panel, hurriedly pulling levers and pressing worn buttons. He glances at the elevator, then looks askance at you, a flush slowly rising in his pale cheeks. Giving up, he removes his trembling hands from the panel and turns to you.{/n} "Your {mf|Shordlip|Shadylip}— sorry! Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Th-the lift. Th-there's n-no... power." {n}The young man takes a breath.{/n} "The xenos — damaged the batteries. To restore the current — we have to turn something off. In the settlement. Anything. That's it."
  - After: {n}A flushed young soldier turns from the panel.{/n} "Your {mf|Shordlip|Shadylip}— Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! N-no power." {n}He breathes.{/n} "Xenos hit the batteries. Turn off anything in the settlement."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Judging by the marks on the soldier's uniform, he has survived an encounter with the metal xenos. Who is to say which he found more terrifying: the sight of their iron claws, or the prospect of being an obstacle in your path?{/n}
  - After: {n}He survived the metal xenos, yet fears blocking you more.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your L-{mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!" {n}The young man drops to his knees.{/n} "I w-would do it myself! I-I swear! But — they won't let me turn everything off. It'll take too long. They won't refuse you! Turn off the power to anything!"
  - After: "Your L-{mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!" {n}He kneels.{/n} "They won't let me. They won't refuse you!"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I do hope your question is rhetorical, Rogue Trader, or I will be most aggrieved. I am a conduit and a receptacle of the Motive Force, for so the Omnissiah has spoken." {n}His mechadendrites latch onto the panel, directing power, accompanied by reverberant words of the First Galvanic Hymn.{/n}
  - After: "Rhetorical, I hope. I am a conduit of the Motive Force." {n}He powers the panel, chanting.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest's visor flashes in the direction of the lift.{/n} "The assessment is flawed. The machine spirits are ravenous, and my functionality does not allow me to satiate them. The algorithm of action proposed by the layperson is correct: it is necessary to plunge the excess machines into a blissful slumber and redirect the currents of Motive Force to the repository circuit."
  - After: {n}Pasqal's visor flashes.{/n} "I cannot sate these spirits. The layperson is right: idle excess machines."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You see the sense in the young man's words. As much as you might dislike lording it over the common people, you alone have the right to disconnect any device inside the settlement. {/n}
  - After: {n}Only you can shut off devices here. {/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn smiles.{/n} "There is no need for that, esteemed colleague. Each of us sooner or later meets the limits of our functions, there is no shame in that. However, if the Rogue Trader will permit, I am willing to shoulder burdens that are beyond you."
  - After: {n}Eogunn smiles.{/n} "No shame in limits, colleague. I'll carry what you cannot."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's visor flashes scarlet, and a stricken binharic screech erupts from his vox. The Tech-Priest does not dignify the Manipulus with a reply.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal screeches binharic, ignoring him.{/n}

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/SurvivorCamp/FieldHospital/SC_FieldHospital_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Try to save the doomed man] "Sergeant-Chirurgeon, you will assist."
  - After: [Try to save him] "Sergeant-Chirurgeon, assist."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Eogunn, I order you to save this man."
  - After: "Eogunn, save this man."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Grant the Emperor's Mercy] "All we can do now is grant him an easy death."
  - After: [Grant the Emperor's Mercy] "Let's give him an easy death."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The makeshift hospital is a hive of activity. Here and there, the wounded moan through gritted teeth. A man wearing a chirurgeon's armband and a lieutenant's insignia stands at one bed examining a patient, while a young assistant with the rank of sergeant rushes about.{/n}
  - After: {n}A busy field hospital. A chirurgeon and his young assistant tend the wounded.{/n}
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "The Undying One had already whispered his name. And the Domin's hand bestowed upon him the greatest of all honours."
  - After: "The Undying One called him; the Domin honoured him."
- **Chirurgeon Lukha**
  - Before: "There is nothing we can do here now. I'm sorry, Jovakha, but your chances are slim."
  - After: "Nothing more to do. Sorry, Jovakha."
- **Lukha's Assistant**
  - Before: "Jovakha taught half the regiment how to shoot! He's got God-Emperor-given talent as an instructor!"
  - After: "Jovakha taught half the regiment to shoot!"
- **Chirurgeon Lukha**
  - Before: "Sergeant, this is part of our duty. If we make a futile attempt to save one doomed man, we will lose him and a dozen other soldiers we could have helped. Toughen up."
  - After: "Saving one doomed man costs a dozen. Toughen up."
- **Drill Sergeant Jovakha**
  - Before: "Lukha, I understand. Atonement for the one. Go and save some of the others... I'll just... manage... on my own. I don't want... to be... a burden."
  - After: "I understand. Atonement for the one. Save the others..."
- **Chirurgeon Lukha**
  - Before: "Drill Sergeant Ondzej Jovakha was struck by one of the Drover's maces. We sutured the wounds from the spikes, but he seems to have internal injuries. Given more time, we might find a way to help him."
  - After: "Drill Sergeant Ondzej Jovakha took a Drover mace. Internal injuries. With time, we might help."
- **Drill Sergeant Jovakha**
  - Before: "Please. I don't want to... suffer. It's time for atonement... for the one."
  - After: "Please. No suffering. Atonement... for the one."
- **Lukha's Assistant**
  - Before: "God-Emperor, it's getting worse by the hour..."
  - After: "God-Emperor, he's worsening..."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}You turn and walk away, hearing behind you the groans of pain and the lamentations of the young chirurgeon trying to do something, but to no avail. {/n}
  - After: {n}You leave amid groans. {/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Absent the requisite instruments and compounds, full restoration of the patient is beyond my current capabilities, however..." {n}He looks around.{/n} "However, I can unequivocally perform this operation better than any of these laypeople. I will do what I can, Rogue Trader. Initiating the application of sacred medicae protocols." {n}The alembic sprays a cloud of anaesthetic solution.{/n}
  - After: "I can't fully heal him..." {n}He looks around.{/n} "But I'll outdo laypeople." {n}Anaesthetic sprays.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}You step back and wipe the sweat from your brow with the back of your bloodied hand. The patient's chest rises and falls steadily, and though his life is not yet saved, he has at least some chance of surviving long enough to be operated on fully.{/n}
  - After: {n}He breathes steadily; he may survive until surgery.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your efforts have failed. You step away from the dead man in the bed and wipe the sweat from your brow with your bloodied hand.{/n}
  - After: {n}You failed. He's dead.{/n}
- **Lukha's Assistant**
  - Before: "Thank you, thank you! Jovakha... he's like a father to a lot of us, you know? We owe him. And you..." {n}The young sergeant falls into reflection.{/n}
  - After: "Thank you! He's like a father to us." {n}She falls quiet.{/n}
- **Chirurgeon Lukha**
  - Before: "My gran would tell me stories about the First Call-Up. It's believed that your ancestor used to say that even the doomed are worth saving, for their debt of gratitude leads to grand deeds. It's not our way to waste our efforts on lost causes, but now... Thank you once again. The regiment will not forget what you have done!"
  - After: "Gran said your ancestor saved even the doomed, for their gratitude breeds grand deeds. The regiment won't forget!"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Allow me." {n}The scanners in Eogunn's mechadendrites spring to life in a flurry of quick flashes.{/n} "The patient's condition is critical, unstable, with a pronounced tendency toward deterioration. Lethal outcome in one hour and twenty-three minutes, unless emergency wound debridement is performed. My capabilities should prove adequate to undertake the procedure without delay, improving the patient's condition to a moderate state."
  - After: {n}Eogunn scans him.{/n} "Critical. Dead in one hour twenty-three minutes without debridement. I can do it."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "This servant of the God-Emperor fought with valour and utter devotion. Do not prolong his suffering. He has earned the Emperor's Mercy for his loyalty."
  - After: "He served valiantly. Grant him the Emperor's Mercy."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/SurvivorCamp/GadmansSqueal/SC_GadmansSqueal_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Those standing before you look utterly spent. Dark circles ring their eyes and their movements are jittery and frantic. Every sign speaks of people pushed to the very brink.{/n}
  - After: {n}Exhausted people at breaking point.{/n}
- **Cage-Born Man**
  - Before: "What is there to celebrate? Batoshski speaks the truth. They'll take us all and toss us into the grinder as cannon fodder!"
  - After: "Batoshski's right: we'll be cannon fodder!"
- **Cage-Born Woman**
  - Before: "And what is there for us here? To chew on vine leaves and shake with fear? I would rather die for the glory of the God-Emperor among the stars!"
  - After: "Better to die for the God-Emperor among the stars!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A soundless shriek lances through everything around you, setting your very eyes vibrating within their sockets. Fury, terror, and revulsion surge upward in a boiling tide from the depths of your consciousness.{/n}
  - After: {n}A soundless shriek. Fury and terror surge.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira casts a wary glance at you.{/n} "Don't blame them. When that beast shrieks, it smothers even my whispers. What hope do mere mortals have..."
  - After: {n}Idira glances at you.{/n} "It drowns even my whispers. Don't blame them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}But the feelings break against the unyielding rock of your will.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your will holds.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The emotions engulf you and as if in a dream you watch the scene unfolding before your eyes.{/n}
  - After: {n}It engulfs you, dreamlike.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A woman with a bone plate over one eye draws a knife and moves to plunge it into the man standing opposite her.{/n}
  - After: {n}A bone-eyed woman knifes at a comrade.{/n}
- **Cage-Born Woman**
  - Before: "The Handbook states that cowardice is punishable by death!" {n}With a practised, fluid motion, the woman slits her comrade's throat, spits, and then stalks away.{/n}
  - After: "Cowardice means death!" {n}She slits his throat.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: {n}Batoshski turns, hand on weapon.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes. Only we didn't go into the roots. We settled it all right there in the Cage. Six of us went out to fight. I was the only one left. If they all hadn't swarmed me, I might have spared someone."
  - After: "Yes, in the Cage. Six fought; only I lived."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A lot's been forgotten. It's not like our regiment is mentioned somewhere in the Handbook, if you catch my meaning." {n}Izdrig digs a hand into his beard, abruptly yanking out a wriggling stalk.{/n} "We came from Merov. It's the kind of place where the Brother-Generals are constantly looking for an excuse to snatch you up and throw you into a penal legion. Breathe the wrong way or say the wrong thing? Welcome to the service."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There are virtually no animals, but every type of plant life imaginable. And all of them try to kill humans. The Drover is just another tree, or a flower, but the nastiest of them."
  - After: "Few animals; every plant kills. The Drover's the worst."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "An expedition." {n}Batoshski grins crookedly as he says it.{/n} "The First Call-Up was requisitioned by Seberian von Valancius. I don't think they complained — better than serving as human shields for other regiments."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "As I said, the Drover itself hides in a tangle of roots. It will only come out if you chop down a whole bunch of its shoots. But here's the thing... no one's ever been able to kill it. Usually, it just runs away. But we don't have weapons like yours."
  - After: "Chop enough shoots and it leaves the roots. No one's killed it; it flees."
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: {n}Batoshski barks orders.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Seconds before the disgusting swill arrives in your stomach, you feel something unimaginably nefarious, majestic as death, and as disgusting as a decomposing corpse turn its gaze upon you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Something nefarious, majestic as death, turns its gaze on you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The colonel raises an eyebrow and looks at you with grim amusement.{/n} "We prepare while we're still recruits, but you can try the rot extract. But it'll be really foul. Even if you don't give your soul to the God-Emperor, your body still might not adapt."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Batoshski gives a vicious grin.{/n} "Here in the Cage, we don't even have half a company, it's true, though you haven't seen the whole lot: some have been cut off by the Drover's siege, and others I've stashed away just in case. So even if we all die here by the God-Emperor's will, the rest of the regiment will live."
  - After: {n}A vicious grin.{/n} "Few here, but outposts dot the world. The regiment will live."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Huge creatures of some kind once inhabited this world, but they all died out. The roots shot up after that. We often find a skull right in the middle of a root, or a vertebra the size of three men. It's clear as day, the roots had grown right through them."
  - After: "Huge creatures died out here. The roots grew through their bones."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A long time ago. I'd just become colonel. Out it came — not very close, but still close enough to be a problem. It almost gobbled up one of the outposts.   - After: "Once. Our squad died; my father leapt into its maw with our last grenades. It fed and left. I should've found atonement there. Childhood exposure to its poison saved me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Almost instantly, liquid flame spreads throughout your body. Pain pierces every nerve... and begins to slowly recede as your body adapts. A large tremor hits you, and sweat instantly soaks through your clothes.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Almost instantly, liquid flame spreads through your body. Pain pierces every nerve. After a few seconds, it begins to subside... but it does not go away completely. The slightest movement sends a scream of agony through your brain.{/n}

  - Before: "Like a bunch of abscesses, they are. They ripen right on the roots, then a swarm of carnivorous midges bursts out. Smash the growth early, otherwise more of the bastards will hatch." {n}A web of small bites on the man's shoulders alludes to the size of the insects.{/n}

  - Before: {n}He simply grunts in response.{/n} "It costs me nothing to give it."

  - Before: {n}The colonel fixes you with a fierce glare, but nonetheless unclips a pair of hand flamers from his belt.{/n} "Here, weapons of the First Call-Up. Rare and precious. When your time comes, detonate them before you die."

  - Before: {n}Batoshski silently claps his hands twice, applauding your quick wit.{/n}
  - After: {n}Batoshski claps twice.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

After waiting for the colonel's nod, he pours the contents of the flask into the cup. The heavy odour of rot permeates the air.{/n} "Well, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, not having second thoughts, are you?"

  - Before: "Well, as we say in our regiment, to your good health." {n}Batoshski watches as you tip the contents of the cup down your throat.{/n}
  - After: "To your good health." {n}You drink.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Wasn't my intention, but what's done is done."
  - After: "Unintended, but done."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In the First Call-Up, the rank of colonel was a lifetime post — he granted all other promotions and demotions unilaterally. The rank passed to his son, then to his grandson, who turned out to be a weakling. The others slit his throat, and the strongest and most cunning of them took the colonel's position. He set the rule that if you want a promotion, you prove your worth. You fight the Trial Match against others with the same ambition. It's the same for every rank: if you're aiming to become sergeant, you head into the roots with the other candidates. If you make it back, you've earned the rank."

  - Before: "Huh? I don't know those fancy words. But I know this: the best killer, as you put it, is only on top as long as the troops respect them. Either that, or as long as they're feared."

- **(conversation owner)**

  - Before: {n}A rasping growl escapes Batoshski's lips, only to dissolve into laughter.{/n} "Ha! No, don't be foolish. Traditions are there to be honoured and upheld. I'll face you, heir of Seberian, and make no mistake, I'll be fighting for keeps."

  - Before: "There are also some ruins, not made by human hands. We rarely go there. A decent man has no business in such a place. Ask Dunawski. When she was up for her promotion to captain-quartermaster, she led an expedition to those ruins."

- **(conversation owner)**

  - Before: {n}Regardless of the changes to the Cage, Batoshski remains the same as ever: savage, spiteful, and unyielding.{/n}
