- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What exactly do you want to know?"
  - After: "What do you want to know?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Janur tells me you've seen them already. You'll recognise it at once, it's a long vine with thorns on the end." {n}The colonel bares several ugly scars on his arm.{/n} "It carves you up deep, you'll bleed to death before you can blink. The creature can also spit its sucker at you — one slip-up and you're a shrivelled husk. If you manage to hack it up good, it'll try to dive back into the roots to regrow elsewhere. But there's a trick to it. Catch it with a burst of fire, and the mace loses its nerve and stays put."
  - After: "A thorned vine." {n}He bares scars.{/n} "It cuts deep and spits a draining sucker. Hacked, it flees to regrow — fire makes it stay."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This is our home. Bitter, wild, and deadly. Just like us."
  - After: "Home. Bitter, wild, deadly. Like us."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Izdrig scratches his beard as he looks around the outpost.{/n} "Fresh supplies are helpful. New people coming to Zarkov not so much. I'll see plenty more danger in my lifetime, but our children will have it a lot easier."
  - After: {n}Izdrig looks around.{/n} "Supplies help; newcomers to Zarkov, less."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar's thunderous laugh makes Batoshski start.{/n} "I like this mortal, Aett-Vater! Had he been born on Fenris, a Wolf Priest would have chosen him. What a joy it would be to watch him take the Test of Morkai!"
  - After: {n}Ulfar laughs.{/n} "I like this mortal, Aett-Vater! Fit for the Test of Morkai!"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I characterise the described method of increasing resistance to toxic substances as deleterious and unsuitable for application. Recommendation: avoid profane methods of bodily fortification."
  - After: "Deleterious method. Avoid profane bodily fortification."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Descendants of deserters who slew their own commander. That is an exhaustive description of this scum."
  - After: "Deserters' spawn who slew their commander. Scum."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "I trust, {name}, you will not deny yourself the opportunity to savour this 'nectar.' From what I have heard of your people's living conditions, consuming the processed remains of your own kind should hardly be a novelty for you."
  - After: "Savour this 'nectar,' {name}. Eating your own kind can't be new to you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Now, then. Was there something you wanted to discuss?"
  - After: "Now. Something to discuss?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The sayings, you mean? Atonement for the one comes from an old tradition that, if the whole regiment perishes except for one, then all of that person's wrongdoings are forgiven and eternal and faithful service to the God-Emperor awaits them. But atonement takes many forms. Commissar claptrap means lies, because our forebears never got any good from those deceitful, tempting spirits. If you want to know the rest, you should ask Vedka."
  - After: "Atonement for the one: a regiment's sole survivor is forgiven all sins. Commissar claptrap means lies. Ask Vedka for more."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "What exceptional loyalty to a final order. Exceptional both in its persistence and in its futility." {n}Jae gives a humourless smile and looks away.{/n}
  - After: "Loyal to a final order. Persistent, and futile." {n}Jae smiles thinly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That thing is ancient and huge. My great-grandfather saw it in the roots way back. We've known about it for ages, but this is the first time it got this close."
  - After: "Ancient and huge. It's never come this close."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/SurvivorCamp/JanurAfterAttack/SC_JanurAfterAttack_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Where did these things come from?"
  - After: "Where did they come from?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I see. I will head there with my retinue."
  - After: "I'll go with my retinue."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Where is Colonel Batoshski?"
  - After: "Where's Batoshski?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Where were Dunawski and Batoshski while the Cage was under attack?"
  - After: "Where were Dunawski and Batoshski?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "And where is Captain-Quartermaster Dunawski?"
  - After: "Where's Dunawski?"
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: {n}Janur's burn-scarred face beams with a smile, though his armour is now riddled with a few more holes.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, the attack has been repelled."
  - After: {n}Janur beams.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, we held."
- **Drill Sergeant Jovakha**
  - Before: {n}The patient you rescued back on your first trip to Zarkov is in poor shape, yet he maintains a firm grip on his lasgun.{/n} "It seems you have saved me twice now, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}Jovakha, battered.{/n} "Saved twice, Lord Captain."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: {n}It seems to you that Vedka's dark eye gleams with inner light as she raises her fierce gaze toward you. Her voice rings out clearly over the battlefield.{/n} "Lord Captain! I knew you would come, that you would not leave us in our time of need."
  - After: {n}Vedka's eye gleams.{/n} "Lord Captain! I knew you'd come."
- **Quartermaster Kuravich**
  - Before: {n}A ragged man in his forties spits a mouthful of blood and scowls while fixing his mangled armour.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I didn't get the chance to thank you for saving me. Colonel-Governor Kuravich, ready to serve the dynasty."
  - After: {n}Kuravich spits blood.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Colonel-Governor Kuravich, at your service."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "The enemy's base is at the xenoruins where most holy Seberian von Valancius disappeared, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "The xenoruins where Seberian vanished, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Chirurgeon Lukha**
  - Before: {n}The lieutenant-chirurgeon is splattered with blood from head to toe — yet he himself appears to be uninjured.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I owe you my life. Thank you... and glory to House von Valancius."
  - After: {n}Blood-soaked, unhurt.{/n} "I owe you my life, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: "I'll see to the defences, appoint new sergeants, and then follow your trail. I'll catch up with you at the ruins."
  - After: "I'll fix the defences, then join you."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "It's a shame not all the commanders made it. But we will scribe their names and sing a song in their honour."
  - After: "We lost commanders. We'll sing their names."
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: "From the very xenoruins where your ancestor met his end. The same ones you had us dig up. Those who fled the site told us."
  - After: "The xenoruins you had us dig up."
- **Chirurgeon Lukha**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you've spared me a lot of work." {n}The chirurgeon gives a tired smile, wiping blood from his face with his sleeve.{/n} "A new augment arrived for one of our soldiers, but she has no more need for it. Please, do not hesitate to take it — it might suit someone in your retinue."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}A tired smile.{/n} "Take this spare augment."
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: {n}Izdrig Batoshski lets out a strained growl as blood bubbles in his pierced lungs. The old soldier catches your eye and smirks, then gives you a nod. With one final movement, the colonel salutes, and his eyes close forever.{/n}
  - After: {n}Dying, Izdrig salutes. His eyes close forever.{/n}
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: {n}Vedka gazes into the sky with a smile, her features illuminated by an inner radiance.{/n} "Here is my atonement for the one, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It... it was an honour to fight by your side. Vedka Dunawski stands relieved of her post..." {n}A hand tipped with bone-claws rises to salute you, but death claims Vedka faster.{/n}
  - After: {n}Vedka smiles.{/n} "My atonement for the one, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Vedka Dunawski stands relieved..." {n}She dies mid-salute.{/n}
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "I have been informed that the captain-quartermaster took a group of our finest scouts and headed toward the ruins, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "Took scouts to the ruins, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "The colonel has gone off to the xenoruins, where the beasts emerge. I sure don't envy them!"
  - After: "Gone to the xenoruins. Rather him than me!"
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "They took a group of scouts and headed for the xenoruins. I think they've decided to strike at their base."
  - After: "Took scouts to hit the xenoruins base."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "The actions of a true servant of the God-Emperor — to fall upon the enemy of Humanity without doubt or fear."
  - After: "A true servant, striking without fear."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "Yet another set of strange ruins turns out to be an Oghyr tomb. What a fascinating and unexpected coincidence, wouldn't you say?" {n}There is enough malice in Marazhai's smile to poison an entire compartment of a voidship.{/n}
  - After: "Another Oghyr tomb. Fancy that." {n}A venomous smile.{/n}
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "You really are courage, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... I'll gather the garrison. We'll check the defences and follow you shortly. Atonement for the one!"
  - After: "Brave, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We'll follow. Atonement for the one!"
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: {n}Batoshski radiates an almost tangible fury.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}? You're here. Truth be told, it's good to see you."
  - After: {n}Batoshski seethes.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}? Good to see you."
- **Drill Sergeant Dankosh**
  - Before: {n}Drill Sergeant Dankosh greets you with a nod.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! It was well worth starting a fight with those iron bastards, just to get a chance to fight by your side!"
  - After: {n}Dankosh nods.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Worth it to fight beside you!"
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "According to the reports received, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, they emerged at the dig site we started on your orders."
  - After: "From your dig site, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "May the God-Emperor protect you, Lord Captain. We'll see to the defences and start purging those iron beasts."
  - After: "Emperor protect you. We'll purge the iron beasts."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/SurvivorCamp/JanurMain/SC_JanurMain_dialogue

  - Before: "What does your platoon do?"

  - Before: "Can you tell me anything about Merov?"
  - After: "Anything about Merov?"

  - Before: "Tell me about Zarkov."

  - Before: "I'd like to know more about the Drover."
  - After: "More on the Drover."

  - Before: "I must take my leave."

  - Before: "Batoshski and Dunawski are the senior officers here?"

  - Before: "For the casings, you could use something that burns easily but holds its shape. I think I saw some kind of coarse paper around here."

  - Before: "You disagree with Captain Dunawski?"
  - After: "You disagree with Dunawski?"

  - After: "Tell me about your settlement?"

  - Before: "I found cocoons made out of leaves, and what appeared to be... human corpses inside."
  - After: "I found leaf cocoons with... human corpses inside."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A large collection of crude Aquilas made from bark, wood, and bone lie before the sergeant. Each varies slightly from the next, however — some clutch an Astra Militarum sigil in their talons, others have the number 32 carved into their wings, while another group have one head depicted as a mechanical bird skull.{/n} "Is there something you wanted, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"
  - After: {n}Crude Aquilas of bark and bone lie before the sergeant, each slightly different.{/n} "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Janur tears his attention away from his carving with a grunt and looks up at you expectantly, one eyebrow raised.{/n}
  - After: {n}Janur looks up from his carving, eyebrow raised.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Captain!" {n}Janur drops his carving, stands up straight, and makes the sign of the Aquila.{/n}
  - After: "Lord Captain!" {n}Janur stands and makes the Aquila.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That's right." {n}Noticing the confusion on your face, Janur continues.{/n} "That's our cemetery. Even a human corpse is a resource and object of value for us. We inject certain poisons and other extracts into the leaf shrouds to produce... something good. Nutrient paste, camouflage ointment, glue... lots of things."
  - After: "Our cemetery." {n}You look confused.{/n} "Treated corpses become paste, ointment, glue..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Maybe the captain-quartermaster was right — we should find new ways to serve the God-Emperor, instead of just clinging to the old ones..."
  - After: "Maybe the captain-quartermaster's right — new ways to serve the God-Emperor, not just the old..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "So, the people who serve in the funereal detachments are some of our most respected experts. They're even willing to risk their own hides to return a fallen soldier's body to the regiment. It's our means of survival."
  - After: "Funereal detachments are respected; they risk lives to recover bodies."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "They're commanders not officers. There's a difference. My uncle — I mean, the colonel — has been in charge of the regiment for over ten seasons. You won't find anyone on Zarkov who is more decent or tougher than him. I once saw him covering a retreat for the wounded. Three suckers from a mace latched onto him, but he didn't even blink until he got the wounded soldier to the Cage. They say the suckers just shrivelled up and died later."
  - After: "Commanders, not officers. My uncle, the colonel, is Zarkov's toughest. He once carried a wounded man home with three mace suckers on him. The suckers died."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Captain-Quartermaster Dunawski is the colonel's right hand. She's in charge of supplies, which makes her my immediate commander. She is a good sort, just a little bit... well... out there." {n}Janur makes a vague gesture near his head.{/n} "She believes that, now you've arrived, our lives will change overnight. Everything will get sorted and we'll head for the stars with you. That we'll get our atonement, even start eating off real plates. It used to sound like Commissar claptrap, but now... I don't know. I'd rather stick to my uncle's ways."
  - After: "Dunawski, his right hand, runs supplies — my commander. Good, but..." {n}He taps his head.{/n} "She thinks you'll take us to the stars. I'll stick with my uncle."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Atonement for the one is a complicated thing. I do what needs to be done. And I have no complaints about Vedka. Before your arrival, all this was just an excuse to babble. Besides, Izdrig's my uncle. He raised me after my parents died. Turning on him would be as bad as what the Brother-Generals did."
  - After: "Vedka's fine. But Izdrig raised me. Turning on him would be Brother-General treachery."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Only from the stories of the old Call-Ups. People there are nothing but property. And minor mistakes are grounds for imprisonment. Our regiment was once formed from such unfortunate souls. In short, it's a cursed place abandoned by the God-Emperor."
  - After: "From old stories: people are property, jailed for small mistakes. Cursed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It's our home, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Everything here is either poisonous, predatory, or fragile. In short, anything that isn't trying to kill you is only pretending to be safe. But you get used to it. And then you learn how to use it. Poisonous? Then you can use it for medicine. Predatory? Means it's edible. Hard to kill? You can probably use its skin for armour."
  - After: "Home, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Everything kills, but poison makes medicine, predators are food, hides are armour."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This is how we survive, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Die, or grow stronger and smarter."
  - After: "We die, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, or grow stronger."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There are these explosive flowers around here. Their pollen works as a substitute for... How do you call it... fyceline! You've got to recite a litany of fury over it and then mix it with some other things. We carve bullets out of bark and bones, either from our own dead or some huge creatures. It's trickier with shell casings, but sometimes you bore a hole through wood nice and clean — it depends on whether you recited the litany of fervent labour correctly or not. If you get it wrong, then the bullets tend to misfire, or even explode in the barrel."
  - After: "Explosive pollen, blessed with a litany of fury, replaces fyceline. Bullets are carved from bark and bone. Botch the litany of fervent labour on casings and they explode."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Well, maybe it's easy for you. You probably have some charging things back where you're from, but we don't have anything like that. But you can throw a battery on a fire. There's even a proper name for the ritual, but I can't remember it. The problem is that sometimes the battery just explodes. It's risky, and the rite ruins them eventually anyway. So, the ones who know exactly where to put it in the fire and how long to let it burn, they're valuable soldiers."
  - After: "No chargers, so we burn them in a fire, with a rite. Risky — they explode. The skilled are valuable."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Plenty of poisonous menaces growing around here. But, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, poisons can be used as softening agents, medicine, and all sorts of useful things. And if you mix it right, you can even make sleep-water. Sometimes we need it bad, especially after a rough few days in the roots."
  - After: "Poisons abound, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but make medicine, softeners — even sleep-water, needed after days in the roots."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Hmm... That's a great idea, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The casing will burn on its own as long as you clean the barrel once in a while. When we have time, we'll do some tests."
  - After: "Great idea, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We'll test it."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta pulls off her glove before picking up an unfinished wooden figurine of a soldier, as if afraid of damaging it. She turns the toy over in her hands, her brow furrowed in concentration, then suddenly grins.{/n} "Carve a smile upon his face, master craftsman. Let the children know that a soldier must be stern toward his enemies yet merciful toward those he protects. Just as you are toward these little ones."
  - After: {n}Argenta gently lifts a wooden soldier, then grins.{/n} "Carve him a smile, craftsman. Stern to foes, merciful to those he protects."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Squeezing the last juices from the dead..." {n}Cassia inhales sharply and covers her lips with her long fingers, as if stifling a surge of nausea.{/n}
  - After: "Squeezing the dead dry..." {n}Cassia stifles nausea.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I am registering sacrilegious interference in the rites of servicing the gifts of the Omnissiah by the laity. I insist upon the cautionary servitorisation of those responsible for the arsenal's upkeep."
  - After: "Lay sacrilege against the Omnissiah's gifts. I urge servitorising the armourers."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "How fascinating. Mon-keigh who could not subjugate a world have been forced to submit to the planet's laws instead. Your species is remarkably tenacious in its own survival."
  - After: "Mon-keigh who couldn't subjugate this world submitted to it instead. Tenacious."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's vox-emitter produces a barely audible sigh of sorrow, one that shifts into a quiet binharic litany.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal sighs, then murmurs a binharic litany.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Sleep-water? Hmm. You know, shereen, a draught that helps one forget one's terrors at night regardless of the horrors suffered during the day could have a grand future as an export to other worlds of the Imperium..."
  - After: "Sleep-water? A draught to forget one's terrors, shereen, could be a fine export..."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Even here, far from the filth of bureaucracy and ambition, blood ties are placed above lawful rank. It seems this particular heresy runs in Humanity's very blood."
  - After: "Even here, blood ties trump rank. Humanity's inborn heresy."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I carve things for myself and for the fellows, and sometimes I take commissions. Toys for volunteers, medals for awards, pieces to put on gun stocks. Sometimes I help with prosthetics. But I also do it for the pleasure of the thing."
  - After: "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Toys, medals, gunstock pieces, sometimes prosthetics. And for pleasure."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Well, officially we're a supply platoon. That is, we gather the resources that the Cage needs to survive. And each of us has to have some special skill. Like knowing about poisons, making ammo, or recharging power packs for las weapons. We're supply troops and that means we're the best of the best."
  - After: "Supply. Each of us has a skill: poisons, ammo, recharging power packs. The best."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm with Colonel Batoshski on this, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. There's nothing for us out there in the stars. We were born here, and we must die here. The songs say our regiment used to serve as cover for the cleaner regiments and rot in the mud for them too. Here on Zarkov, at least I know who and what I'm fighting for."
  - After: "I'm with Batoshski, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Born here, die here. Out there we were just cover for others."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Drover is an ancient creature. Maybe there's more than one. Every once in a while, the damn thing comes out and starts shrieking, making us deranged. Dunawski has ear protection, but they're the only pair, so they're no salvation."
  - After: "Ancient, maybe several. Its shriek slowly drives us mad. Dunawski has the only ear protection."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Of course. You'll be our commander soon enough, so it's only right that you should know."
  - After: "Of course. You'll command us soon."

  - After: "Our shared fight spares you, mortal!"
- **Merovian Guardsman**
  - Before: "Quite a show, wasn't it? The Drover's tendrils snatched your machine right out of the sky. The damn thing's been besieging us for two weeks now, we even—" {n}The soldier cuts himself off, seemingly before he says something he should not.{/n} "Doesn't matter. Not until we know who you are."
  - After: "The Drover snatched your machine from the sky. It's besieged us two weeks—" {n}He stops.{/n} "Who are you?"
- **Merovian Guardsman**
  - Before: "We'll go ahead to report your arrival. Just follow the trail, you can't miss it. You need to meet with the colonel."
  - After: "We'll report ahead. Follow the trail."
- **Merovian Guardsman**
  - Before: {n}The soldiers surrounding you visibly tense.{/n} "As per the tenets of the Holy Handbook, if you fail to identify yourselves, we open fire."
  - After: {n}They tense.{/n} "Identify yourselves or we fire."
- **Merovian Guardsman**
  - Before: {n}You see Janur's expression darken.{/n} "That's right, the 32nd Merov Penal Regiment."
  - After: {n}Janur darkens.{/n} "Yes. 32nd Merov Penal."
- **Merovian Guardsman**
  - Before: "Traverse what? We were born here. As for the details, you'd best take that up with the captain or the colonel."
  - After: "We were born here. Ask the colonel."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}The Seneschal clears his throat and adjusts his uniform.{/n} "You are in the presence of {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} {name} von Valancius, heir to the greatest protectorate in the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g} and bearer of the sacred {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant of Trade{/g}."
  - After: {n}Abelard clears his throat.{/n} "{mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} {name} von Valancius, of the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}, bearer of the {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant of Trade{/g}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The moment your name is spoken, a change ripples through the crowd. Some are struck with awe, others turn white as ghosts. The man in front of you makes the sign of the Aquila.{/n}
  - After: {n}The crowd is stunned. The man makes the Aquila.{/n}
- **Merovian Guardsman**
  - Before: "Sergeant Janur Batoshski, 3rd Supply Platoon, 32nd Merov Regiment. We are pleased to welcome you to Zarkov, Your... Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Janur stumbles slightly over these words, as if recalling their sound as he goes.{/n}
  - After: "Sergeant Janur Batoshski, 32nd Merov. Welcome to Zarkov, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}He stumbles on the words.{/n}
- **Merovian Guardsman**
  - Before: "I'm no help to you there. You need to head to the Cage. It's our camp and the biggest outpost on Zarkov. Our capital, I suppose, or whatever it is you call large settlements."
  - After: "Go to the Cage, our capital."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}The Drukhari eases his stance, resting his hand atop his weapon's hilt.{/n} "Go on, mon-keigh. Give me a reason."
  - After: {n}Marazhai touches his hilt.{/n} "Give me a reason."
- **Merovian Guardsman**
  - Before: "We just fought its tendrils, and those weren't even the largest. Can you imagine the size of the thing itself? Exactly." {n}The soldier wipes the sweat from his brow.{/n} "Anyway, let's hold off on any more idle talk for now. It's not safe here."
  - After: "Those were just tendrils. Imagine the rest." {n}He wipes sweat.{/n} "Not safe here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The last words sound rehearsed and unfamiliar, as if he's using them for the very first time. Yet, upon hearing them, the people around you grip their weapons tighter, and the blond man grows noticeably more confident.{/n}
  - After: {n}The rehearsed words embolden them.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "You call it 'penal.' I call it 'redemptive'! You surrendered to the basest impulses and stained your souls, yet you are permitted not to rot in chains but to burn away your transgressions in the heat of battle. So do not dishonour His gift of atonement with wretched shame!"
  - After: "Not 'penal' — 'redemptive'! Burn away your sins in battle, without shame!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You instantly {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}recognise the lines of the Handbook{/d}. It is the mandatory protocol for Astra Militarum sentries to challenge anyone approaching the perimeter of a secured site in exactly this manner.{/n}
  - After: {n}You {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}recognise the lines of the Handbook{/d}.{/n}
- **Merovian Guardsman**
  - Before: "I saw the markings on the fallen machine, Sergeant! It's {mf|him|her}, exactly as it has been foretold! Von Valancius has descended from the stars. Our service..."
  - After: "It's {mf|him|her}, Sergeant, as foretold! Von Valancius!"
- **Merovian Guardsman**
  - Before: "The Drover, obviously. Or its growths, if you want to be specific. But don't get distracted, go on."
  - After: "The Drover. Go on."
- **Merovian Guardsman**
  - Before: "It is both an honour and a joy, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We have waited so very long for your arrival. Truly, I never imagined I would see this day in my lifetime..."
  - After: "An honour, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We waited so long."
- **Merovian Guardsman**
  - Before: "About-turn! To the regiment's quarters, march!"
  - After: "About-turn! March!"

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/SurvivorCamp/JanurUnderAttack/SC_JanurUnderAttack_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Sergeant Batoshski, the God-Emperor protects you."
  - After: "Sergeant Batoshski, the Emperor protects."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Report the situation."
  - After: "Report."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do we know about our enemy?"
  - After: "What's our enemy?"
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you're here! I knew you wouldn't abandon us! Those iron creatures have been attacking us all over the planet. No one knows where they came from — or we haven't been able to find out in all the confusion, anyway."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Iron creatures attack everywhere, from nowhere."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "And Drill Sergeant Jovakha is leading a squad defending the path we've established to the xenoruins north-west of the landing pad. That's where the first wounded came in, and they were being chased by those cursed creatures."
  - After: "Drill Sergeant Jovakha holds the xenoruins path, north-west."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "And our new Drill Sergeant Dankosh has been pushed back to the road to the xenoruins, north-west of the landing pad."
  - After: "Drill Sergeant Dankosh fell back to the xenoruins road, north-west."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "For the von Valancius dynasty, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!"
  - After: "For von Valancius, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!"
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_VedkaGovernor}Governor Dunawski{/d}, according to the latest reports, is holding ground to the east, at the main gate. They say she's fighting as if the Drover itself is screaming right in her ear."
  - After: "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_VedkaGovernor}Governor Dunawski{/d} holds the east main gate like a fury."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "When those things appeared, {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_ZarkovNonameGovernor}Colonel-Governor Kuravich{/d} was personally handling the delivery of the sacred mechanisms to the red robes. Their machine spirit chapel is located in the north-east."
  - After: "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_ZarkovNonameGovernor}Colonel-Governor Kuravich{/d} was at the red robes' chapel, north-east."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "These iron creatures came out of thin air. They attack in waves, giving us hardly any break. It's a good thing we managed to get a message out in time. These things are not made of flesh and know no fear, and they're closing in on us on all fronts. So, your arrival is a blessing from the God-Emperor Himself."
  - After: "They attack in waves. Fearless, closing on all fronts."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "I left my post down in the roots to clear the landing pad. It's good that you're here. Now the creatures are as good as dead!"
  - After: "I left the roots to clear the pad. They're dead now!"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "It is true what they say: those who spurn fear are invincible beneath His shadow!" {n}Argenta salutes the somewhat flustered youth.{/n}
  - After: "Who spurns fear is invincible beneath His shadow!" {n}Argenta salutes.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's visors flare crimson and his voice rasps with a grating, plasteel edge:{/n} "I call for the activation of the algorithm for smiting tech-heretical filth! The Omnissiah demands the disposal of the unhallowed xenomechanisms!"
  - After: {n}Pasqal's visors flare.{/n} "Purge the unhallowed xenomechanisms!"
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_BatoshskiGovernor}Governor Batoshski{/d} is to the north-east, holding the red robes' chapel. They say he's run out of ammunition, but that hasn't stopped him from breaking those xenofiends with his bare hands."
  - After: "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_BatoshskiGovernor}Governor Batoshski{/d} holds the red robes' chapel, north-east, bare-handed."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "Lukha, our chirurgeon, went south to the gate. Right to the front, like a proper medicae. I think he's looking for anyone who can still be saved."
  - After: "Lukha, our chirurgeon, went south to the gate."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_ZarkovNonameGovernor}Colonel-Governor Kuravich{/d}, along with a detachment of soldiers, has secured the eastern main gates and is holding the line. He was right in the middle of receiving a supply drop when it all started."
  - After: "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_ZarkovNonameGovernor}Colonel-Governor Kuravich{/d} holds the eastern main gates."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: {n}Janur presses a portable vox to his mangled ear, his expression darkening.{/n} "Damn it... They've launched a fresh attack on all fronts. I have to get back to the other level of the roots. I'll hold back as many as I can."
  - After: {n}Janur hears his vox.{/n} "New attack on all fronts. Back to the roots!"
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "Lukha, our chirurgeon, is north-west of here, along the road to the ruins. That's where the first wounded came, with the creatures hot on their trail. So, he started administering first aid right on the spot..."
  - After: "Lukha, our chirurgeon, treats wounded on the ruins road."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "And Drill Sergeant Jovakha has advanced to protect the red robes in the north-east."
  - After: "Drill Sergeant Jovakha guards the red robes, north-east."
- **Sergeant Janur**
  - Before: "And our new Drill Sergeant Dankosh was just checking out the sentry recruits at the machine-spirit chapel in the north-east."
  - After: "Drill Sergeant Dankosh is at the machine-spirit chapel, north-east."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/SurvivorCamp/MerovPenalOath/SC_MerovPenalOath_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Activate vox] "Finally, time to get back to recaf, baths, and a hot meal! Vigdis, where is my shuttle?"
  - After: [Activate vox] "Time for recaf and a hot meal! Vigdis, my shuttle?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I shall need a commander for the Zarkovian troops. And the position of Arch-Militant also happens to be open."
  - After: "I need a commander for the Zarkovians. And an Arch-Militant."
- **Player**
  - Before: "From now on, Zarkov is a colony of the von Valancius protectorate. And it is time to appoint a governor."
  - After: "Zarkov is now a von Valancius colony. Time to appoint a governor."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Colonel Batoshski, you will be my new Arch-Militant."
  - After: "Colonel Batoshski, you're my new Arch-Militant."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Well, then, Dunawski, are you ready to go to the stars?"
  - After: "Dunawski, ready to go to the stars?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Then again, I don't think I'm quite willing to grant this position to anyone from Zarkov. My enforcers are dependable — the same cannot be said of you."
  - After: "No one from Zarkov gets this post. My enforcers are dependable; you aren't."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Colonel Batoshski, you are hereby appointed the Colonel-Governor of Zarkov."
  - After: "Colonel Batoshski, you're Colonel-Governor of Zarkov."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Who could make for a better colonel-governor than the captain-quartermaster?"
  - After: "Who better as colonel-governor than the captain-quartermaster?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Choose someone who did not wish to leave Zarkov — such a person would take care of their home better than anyone else, I am sure."
  - After: "Choose someone who wanted to stay. They'll care for their home best."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I shall appoint a representative from among those who yearn to return to the Imperium's embrace — a new era has dawned, and it is time for Zarkov to emerge from isolation."
  - After: "I'll appoint someone who yearns for the Imperium. Zarkov's isolation is over."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Turn on your vox] "All matters have been settled? Then this audience is over. Vigdis, send a shuttle."
  - After: [Turn on your vox] "All settled? Audience over. Vigdis, send a shuttle."
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: {n}Batoshski looks like a broken man, but at the same time, his face shows a strange relief.{/n} "Well, that's it. The oaths have been renewed. We've put our lives and fates in your hands, Lord Captain. We await your orders regarding Zarkov and the regiment."
  - After: {n}Batoshski, broken yet relieved:{/n} "Oaths renewed. Your orders, Lord Captain?"
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "So many Call-Ups later... And here it is: the oath, as written in the Handbook! Our regiment has found its purpose and returned to duty. All that remains is for you to decide, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, what to do with Zarkov and our regiment."
  - After: "The oath, per the Handbook! Decide our fate, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "The Undying One grants His servants the chances they deserve. Yours is still to come."
  - After: "Your chance is yet to come."
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: "I never dreamed of such a thing, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. But I took the oath and I accept the post."
  - After: "Unexpected, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I accept."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: {n}The captain's face beams with an inner light.{/n} "I've been preparing for this my whole life, Lord Captain!"
  - After: {n}She beams.{/n} "My life's dream!"
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: "Congratulations, Vedka. You got what you dreamed of."
  - After: "Congratulations, Vedka."
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: {n}Batoshski frowns and looks away.{/n}
  - After: {n}Batoshski looks away.{/n}
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: {n}Batoshski makes a sound of agreement and glances around the Cage.{/n} "I never really wanted to leave. So that suits me just fine. Don't worry, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I won't let anything happen to your new colony."
  - After: {n}Batoshski nods.{/n} "I wanted to stay. It's safe with me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "But... colonel-governor? Here? I mean... As you command, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "Governor? ...As you command, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: "Pull yourself together, Captain. What does the Handbook dictate? Endure hardships and execute the commander's orders exactly."
  - After: "Steady, Captain. The Handbook says obey."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vigdis's voice is interrupted by static, but you can still make it out.{/n} "Lord Captain, you're alive! An extraction team was already on its way to search for you. Transmitting your coordinates to their shuttles."
  - After: {n}Vigdis, through static:{/n} "Alive! Sending shuttles."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "I... I cannot, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Forgive me, I was wrong. You helped me see that I have no place in the world beyond the stars. I should stay... Someone has to uphold the Handbook, after all..." {n}Vedka lowers her head.{/n}
  - After: "I cannot, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I belong here, with the Handbook." {n}Vedka bows.{/n}
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "As you command, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Dunawski's chin trembles slightly, but she seems to be holding herself together.{/n}
  - After: "As you command, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Her chin trembles.{/n}

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/SurvivorCamp/PilotEmergencyLanding/SC_PilotEmergencyLanding_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Did you have a chance to see what attacked us?"
  - After: "What attacked us?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What of the shuttle? Can it be repaired?"
  - After: "Can the shuttle be fixed?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address your retinue] "Does anyone feel anything odd? As if something is pressing on your mind."
  - After: [Address your retinue] "Anyone feel pressure on your mind?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am heading to the settlement. Perhaps the vox-signal will break through to the flagship from there."
  - After: "To the settlement. The vox may work there."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your skull feels like it is about to split under the pressure. A heartbeat later, the agony ebbs, leaving behind only a haunting hum. It smothers your mind, stifling all reason and hindering your ability to think. Your gaze falls on the young pilot, who survived the crash and stumbled out of the wrecked shuttle after you. A wave of sickening fury suddenly swells within you — he is the one who lost control of the vessel!{/n}
  - After: {n}Pain, then a hum smothers thought. Fury rises at the pilot who crashed you!{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}By willpower alone, you pull yourself together. The fury fades, sinking into the depths of your mind, leaving a lingering terror, an urge to flee, and the knowledge that such escape is impossible.{/n}
  - After: {n}You master the fury. Dread remains.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The fury bursts out of you in a strangled roar. You feel you are watching a stranger as you step toward the pilot and strike him across his bloodied face. The servant of the dynasty meets your eyes with such fierce spite that it seems he might actually strike you back.{/n}
  - After: {n}Roaring, you strike the pilot. He glares back spitefully.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Research by the Magos Biologis has confirmed the existence of flora classified as Periculum Machine Majoris. Life forms of this category pose a serious threat to sacred transport vehicles and armoured units. There is a 96.543% probability that such a species inhabits this planet. In the observed case, the probability of more than one species of this threat category existing stands at 85.6789%."
  - After: "Periculum Machine Majoris flora threatens vehicles. 96.543% likely here; 85.6789% likely several species."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "A predatory tree? I have yet to slay such a monstrosity! We must find it and carry its durable timber back to Fenris. Let us carve it into the haft of a worthy weapon!"
  - After: "A predatory tree? Its timber will make a fine haft!"
- **Personal Pilot**
  - Before: {n}The pilot speaks through clenched teeth, fighting the urge to shout.{/n} "Movement on the port side, that's the last thing I saw, Lord Captain. Something massive, like a tree trunk. It was either thrown at the shuttle or... it attacked us itself, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: {n}Through clenched teeth:{/n} "Something huge, like a trunk, hit us. Thrown, or it attacked itself, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Personal Pilot**
  - Before: {n}He casts a bleak glance at the shuttle.{/n} "I'm afraid not, Lord Captain. The ship requires recovery and the application of Adeptus Mechanicus repair sacraments. And those can only be done aboard the flagship. We need an evacuation."
  - After: {n}He eyes it.{/n} "No. It needs Mechanicus repair on the flagship. We need evacuation."
- **Personal Pilot**
  - Before: {n}The rage on the pilot's face gives way to a look of panic as he realises how he has just behaved in the presence of the Rogue Trader. With a trembling hand, he reaches for the vox-augment on his head.{/n}
  - After: {n}Panicked, the pilot reaches for his vox.{/n}
- **Personal Pilot**
  - Before: "I thought it was a result of the impact... Like a hum or some kind of high-pitched screeching. It's a struggle to think straight, to keep from losing it. My apologies, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}..." {n}The pilot's face is sweating and shaking with tension.{/n}
  - After: "A high screeching. Hard to think. Forgive me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}He shakes.{/n}
- **Personal Pilot**
  - Before: {n}After a moment, the man looks at you with hollow eyes.{/n} "Lord Captain... All channels are nothing but static. I... I don't understand why, everything is functioning perfectly. It's as if something is jamming the frequency. We cannot contact the flagship. According to the charts, there is a settlement nearby. Perhaps the locals have a more powerful vox-unit?"
  - After: {n}Hollow-eyed:{/n} "Only static, as if jammed. The nearby settlement may have a stronger vox."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "A peculiar pattern of acoustic waves. I have never encountered anything like this before." {n}Eogunn appears utterly serene and even intrigued as he listens intently to something.{/n} "Infrasound alternating with ultrasound, and so naturally too... These frequencies are inaudible, Rogue Trader, yet they evoke a violent reaction from the deep-seated structures of the human brain. I would like to lay eyes on their source."
  - After: "Infra- and ultrasound, stirring the brain's depths." {n}Eogunn listens, intrigued.{/n} "I'd like to see the source."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "An indigenous organism of such formidable size that it can assault Imperial machinery? This world promises to be a true treasure trove of discoveries. A fine observation, Nuncius." {n}He turns toward his silent companion, whose servo-motors emit a phlegmatic buzz.{/n} "It could indeed be a specimen of either megafauna or megaflora."
  - After: "Something big enough to attack Imperial machines? Fine observation, Nuncius." {n}His companion buzzes.{/n} "Megafauna or megaflora."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn clicks his tongue in irritation, clearly displeased that his colleague was able to provide a more accurate answer.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn clicks his tongue, irritated.{/n}
- **Personal Pilot**
  - Before: "With your permission, Lord Captain, I'll remain here, in case the vox starts working or an evacuation team arrives from the flagship."
  - After: "I'll stay, Lord Captain, in case the vox works or evacuation comes."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta hurriedly whispers a litany, forming the Aquila over her chest.{/n} "The righteous mind cannot be broken by the machinations of His enemies."
  - After: {n}Argenta makes the Aquila.{/n} "His enemies cannot break a righteous mind."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I register both ultra- and infrasonic frequencies. Theoretically, such emissions are capable of inducing deleterious effects upon organic brains."
  - After: "Ultra- and infrasonic frequencies. They can harm organic brains."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "A strange semblance of a song, harsh and cruel to an unprotected mind — that is what I hear. For you, even perceiving its presence is likely a difficult task. For me, however..." {n}Yrliet grimaces, and it is clear that the mysterious phenomenon is causing her genuine pain.{/n}
  - After: "A cruel song. You barely sense it. For me..." {n}Yrliet winces.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "A peculiar noise, yet one that leaves no psychic trace. I suspect that prolonged exposure could lead to emotional volatility. It would be wise to monitor one's own state of mind and not give in to rash impulses."
  - After: "No psychic trace, but it breeds volatility. Avoid rash impulses."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "The sound seems barely audible, but also so loud that it drowns out even my whispers. I wonder how long we can endure this cacophony before we start slaughtering one another..."
  - After: "It drowns out even my whispers. How long until we slaughter each other?"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "A strange haze has enveloped me, and even the Undying One's whispers are hard to make out. In this land, I must rely solely upon your guidance, Domin."
  - After: "Even the Undying One's whispers are faint here. I rely on you, Domin."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Such a tormenting sensation. Something is conjuring painful, angry hues within me, as if splashing crimson and black across my canvas and ruining it. Is this how those I influence feel..." {n}Cassia looks more surprised than angered.{/n}
  - After: "Something splashes crimson on my canvas. Is this how my targets feel?" {n}Cassia looks surprised.{/n}

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Deathworld/SurvivorCamp/QuartermasterKuravich/SC_QuartermasterKuravich_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You could at least make yourself presentable."
  - After: "At least make yourself presentable."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Did I misspeak? Or do you only acknowledge an order after a Trial Match here?"
  - After: "Did I misspeak? Need a Trial Match first?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Look at you, you're held together by spit and prayers. Are you sure you don't need a visit to a chirurgeon?"
  - After: "You look half-dead. Need a chirurgeon?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do not even think about it, Governor. In the Imperium, we do not fashion blades from the xenos."
  - After: "Don't, Governor. No blades from xenos."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Aim these blades against the enemies of the dynasty."
  - After: "Turn these blades on the dynasty's enemies."
- **Player**
  - Before: "How has your life changed since your return to the fold of the Imperium?"
  - After: "How's life back in the Imperium?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What can you tell me about the iron creatures?"
  - After: "What about the iron creatures?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I wish to know how you are faring in your duties as governor."

  - Before: {n}You cannot miss the admiring gaze that glides over your augments. In this moment, Dunawski looks like a devout pilgrim who has suddenly found herself among saints' relics.{/n}

  - After: "I don't know, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The Handbook says trust your gear. They date from the First Call-Up."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Let me see if I understand this correctly.   - After: "Half heretics, half canonising everyone? Saints' blood, my report..." {n}Heinrix sounds grimly amused.{/n}
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "Our oath of loyalty, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. When you return victorious from the Drover's lair, Izdrig is going to challenge you... I wanted to warn you. Colonel Batoshski will fight bitterly, and you should prepare well. I once saw him drench himself in promethium and set himself on fire before fighting three of the Drover's shoots unarmed. He's a fearsome enemy."
  - After: "Our oath, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. After the Drover, Colonel Batoshski will challenge you. He once fought three Drover shoots unarmed, ablaze. Prepare."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The simplicity of the design borders upon the primitive, yet the device fulfils its intended function. I register a degree of interest in the material responsible for sound attenuation.   - After: "Primitive but functional. Local plant-based dampener. Study it before use."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "Lukha told me what you did for Jovakha. You cannot imagine how important a drill sergeant is to the 32nd Regiment. Thank you."
  - After: "Lukha told me what you did for Jovakha. Thank you."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "'Provide the commander with comprehensive intelligence appropriate to the situation.' So states the Handbook."
  - After: "'Provide the commander with intelligence,' says the Handbook."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "If you need anything else, I will be here."
  - After: "I'll be here."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: {n}Vedka draws herself up, clearly proud to share this with you.{/n} "That is our processing graveyard. A discovery of the Third Call-Up. The saps and poisons of various native plants can work wonders upon the bodies of the fallen, provided the right substances are injected into the cocoon and it is left for the proper time. The skin we use as material for grips or clothing. The sinews for bows or cords. The secreted compounds serve as poisons, medicines, or for tanning. Everything is put to use."
  - After: {n}Vedka beams proudly.{/n} "Our processing graveyard. Plant saps turn the fallen into skin, sinew, poisons and medicines. Everything is used."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: {n}The captain speaks with fervour, passion, a breathless intensity. Your eye, however, is involuntarily drawn to her leather satchel, upon which a crude tattoo is visible.{/n} "The funereal detachments are true geniuses, Lord Captain. I come from one myself, though now I serve as quartermaster. We honour our dead by sacrificing their bodies to the rest of the regiment. Every man and woman is prepared to give not only their life but their flesh after death, so that others might endure."
  - After: {n}A crude tattoo marks her satchel.{/n} "I came from a funereal detachment, Lord Captain. Our dead give their flesh so others endure."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "You mean the 'Hymn of the Lost,' Lord Captain. By it we live, and by it we die. If you want to learn anything about it, just ask. I know it by heart."
  - After: "The 'Hymn of the Lost.' We live and die by it. Ask; I know it by heart."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "It reminds us that our survival is built upon the bones of the Call-Ups that came before, and that upon our own bones will our children grow. It speaks of our duty and of atonement."
  - After: "We survive on our forebears' bones, as our children will on ours. Duty and atonement."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "Deep within the roots are xenos ruins. We do not venture there as a rule. It is a cursed place. A place of death." {n}Vedka's hand reflexively moves toward her missing eye, then she pulls it back.{/n}
  - After: "Xenos ruins in the roots. Cursed. We avoid them." {n}She nearly touches her missing eye.{/n}
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "Thus we honour our heroes. With each Call-Up, the song grows, line by line, name by name. It began with Sergeant Zarkov, the first commander to rise from the ranks of the common penal conscripts. We named this world in his honour. The greatest honour is to be enshrined in the lines of the Hymn after death."
  - After: "Our heroes, starting with Sergeant Zarkov, whose name this world bears. Joining the Hymn is our highest honour."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: {n}Dunawski's remaining eye widens, while a thin, translucent fluid trickles from the other, ruined socket.{/n} "That is against the Handbook, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! It states, 'One must never conspire against a commanding officer!' Your words are a trial I will pass with honour, by rejecting them."
  - After: {n}Fluid trickles from her ruined socket.{/n} "That's against the Handbook, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I refuse."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "Walk around the Cage, listen to the people. Work to understand us, and then you will know what to do in the Trial Match. I have faith in you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}A half-mad smile, that of a true fanatic, touches Vedka's lips.{/n}
  - After: "Walk the Cage, listen, understand us. Then you'll know what to do in the Trial Match, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}A fanatic's smile.{/n}
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "And why do we praise the God-Emperor even when all seems lost? Why do we struggle to survive even where we should surely perish? Because we have no choice but to fight against the inevitable. Izdrig will battle for the regiment even against the Emperor's Angels. As the Handbook states, 'The only thing a Guardsman should fear is the failure to do their duty.'"
  - After: "We fight the inevitable; we must. Izdrig would battle even the Emperor's Angels for the regiment."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: {n}Vedka pales, bringing her flesh-and-blood hand to her missing eye. The black stone within the socket seems to shift, ever so slightly.{/n} "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I was young and eager to prove my valour and fearlessness, during the Trial Match for the rank of captain-quartermaster. I took a large quantity of explosive pollen and went to those ruins. I intended to blow them up, to show my daring and that we feared no xenos."
  - After: {n}Vedka pales; the stone in her socket shifts.{/n} "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. For my Trial Match, I took explosive pollen to blow up those ruins."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "Your illustrious ancestor, Seberian von Valancius, saved us from the terrible fate of obscurity and took the First Call-Up into his own service. He gave us good uniforms and weapons, and then there were the von Valancius gifts. Stories passed down from our ancestors tell of how the Rogue Trader removed these gifts from his own body and offered them to soldiers who had proven themselves better than all the rest. These boons made them even stronger."
  - After: "Your ancestor, Seberian von Valancius, took the First Call-Up into service. He gave the best soldiers the von Valancius gifts — from his own body."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "I blew them up, all right... Only a shard of black stone took my eye in return. I tried to dig it out, but could not. Neither knife nor needle would do it. I grew used to it in time." {n}Dunawski speaks of it matter-of-factly, but you now understand that the scars around her eye socket were mostly self-inflicted.{/n} "Now the roots have grown over the whole thing. Whether the Drover worked its will, or Zarkov itself hungers to devour those cursed ruins..."
  - After: "I did. A black shard took my eye; I couldn't dig it out." {n}Her scars are self-inflicted.{/n} "Now roots cover the ruins."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Captain Dunawski salutes. The light that once shone in her surviving eye has dimmed and the solemn weight of responsibility has settled upon her features.{/n}
  - After: {n}Dunawski salutes, solemn.{/n}
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: {n}Vedka reaches out a hand, then sharply shakes her head and lets it fall.{/n} "As the God-Emperor is my witness, I very much wish to read those logs. But let us leave them with you until the oath-taking. I suspect they will serve you well during the swearing of the oaths."
  - After: {n}Vedka reaches out, then stops.{/n} "I long to read those logs. Keep them for the oath-taking; they'll serve you."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "We are making progress, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We are inviting new people, forging connections. We caught a pair of newly arrived scribes thieving, and granted one of them the chance for final atonement." {n}Vedka's gaze drifts meaningfully toward the leaves with the bodies within.{/n} "We labour for the glory of the dynasty and the God-Emperor."
  - After: "We're recruiting, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. One thieving scribe got final atonement." {n}She glances at the cocoons.{/n}
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "Augmetics, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. In our songs, it is said your ancestor possessed so many gifts that he could share them with others. I don't know if this is true. But that the Rogue Trader supplied the entire regiment with prosthetics is certain. We continue his work as best we can." {n}Vedka demonstratively clenches her metal hand, which is tipped with claws of bone.{/n}
  - After: "Augmetics, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Your ancestor gave the regiment prosthetics. We continue his work." {n}She flexes her bone-clawed hand.{/n}
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "But I shouldn't bore you with expressions of our gratitude. What do you wish to discuss, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"
  - After: "Enough gratitude. What shall we discuss, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "It is a world of terrors. Every living thing is trying to kill you, and if it doesn't succeed, it will certainly try again. The best thing we have here is our people. Zarkov has tempered us, prepared us for atonement and our oath, whereas the Final Order of your exalted ancestor gave us purpose."
  - After: "A world of terrors. It tempered us for the oath; your ancestor's Final Order gave us purpose."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "You jest, I'm sure, but... All of us here — it's us against the world, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. For hundreds of years, we learned to watch each other's backs and survive. If you kill our commander, you will become our enemy." {n}There is horror in Dunawski's eyes, but her voice is firm.{/n} "The Handbook states, 'A soldier who does not raise their weapon to save their commander is to be deemed complicit in their demise.'"
  - After: "You jest, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Kill our commander and you become our enemy." {n}Horrified, but firm.{/n}
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: {n}Dunawski raises her prosthetic clawed hand and examines it for a time.{/n} "Correct, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, they are. In remembrance of the von Valancius gifts. Seberian von Valancius used prosthetics to make the entire regiment stronger. When he died and we were trapped on Zarkov, it was only because of augments and prosthetics that our ancestors were able to survive. Without the maintenance of the esteemed Adeptus Mechanicus, our augments fell into disrepair. But we have learned, and now we do what we can to replace what is lost."
  - After: {n}She eyes her claw.{/n} "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, honouring the von Valancius gifts. Augments kept us alive here."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Your arrival is bound to bring change, and few people are fond of change. Some believe that rejoining the Imperium will lead to trouble because of the regiment's history. There are others, like myself, of course, who have no fear of meeting His servants, and we look forward to the day when we can return to serving Humanity. These disagreements have never been anything more than a reason to chew the fat on patrol, but now... Regardless, all of us will swear the oath, you can be sure of that! If anyone refuses, we'll grant them final atonement ourselves."
  - After: "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Some fear rejoining the Imperium; I don't. But all will swear, or get final atonement."

When he speaks again, his voice is almost calm.{/n} "We are simple people. We need to know how to survive an encounter with the Drover, not to understand where it came from."

But the Drover has entrenched itself right beside it, which means going there is certain death."
  - After: {n}He tilts his head.{/n} "His tomb lies below the outpost, beside the Drover. Going there is death."

  - Before: "That would be a deed worthy of the true heir of Seberian von Valancius"
  - After: "A deed worthy of Seberian von Valancius's true heir"
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: {n}Colonel Batoshski lets out a low, guttural growl to catch your attention.{/n} "When you return, we fight. That is the law of our regiment. There is no other way."
  - After: {n}He growls.{/n} "When you return, we fight. Regimental law."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "Regimental tradition, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. To take command, one must best the existing commander in combat. And that man is Izdrig."
  - After: "To take command, you must beat the commander, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Izdrig."
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: "Take the lift down. It'll put you right outside that thorny bastard's lair." {n}The colonel exhales heavily, the air hissing from his lungs. His green eyes, clouded by a veil of rage, rake over your face before suddenly softening.{/n} "If you want to throw your life away for nothing, I won't stop you, you can leave now. But if you have enough humility to take advice from a local, I'll be waiting for you at my quarters."
  - After: "The lift leads to its lair." {n}His eyes soften.{/n} "Or seek my advice at my quarters."

The message ends with the phrase: "Atonement for the one."{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Although the codes being transmitted are centuries out of date, you are able to make sense of them: an {g|Encyclopedia:AstraMilitarumGlossary}Astra Militarum{/g} regiment is requesting assistance and reporting that retreat from their present position is impossible.{/n}

Seberian von Valancius is dead. We have no means of comm... not found in orbit. We have been abandoned... {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g}, have mercy... Claim us... before the warp... finishes us off!"

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/ExplorationEvents/SuspiciousTunnels/SuspiciousTunnels_EPP

  - After: Send a new team after the missing group.

  - After: Send an armed squad after the missing group.

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Medbay/MB_AugmentationForAll/MB_AugmentationForAll_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I see you have lost your fear. Get out of my sight before I order the enforcers to disperse you by force!"
  - After: "You've lost your fear. Leave, or the enforcers will disperse you!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I want to hear your arguments. Why ought the workers be granted access to sacred implants?"
  - After: "Why should workers get sacred implants?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have come to a decision. I will allow augmentation."
  - After: "I've decided. I will allow augmentation."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have come to a decision. The workers will continue to make do with primitive prosthetics — the Omnissiah's gifts are intended for officers only."
  - After: "I've decided. Workers keep crude prosthetics; the Omnissiah's gifts are for officers."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do the experts from the Sector Bionica think?"
  - After: "What do the Sector Bionica experts think?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "It would be unfair if I allowed augmetics for one and denied the rest. From this day on, subjects from the lower decks will be granted access to augmentation!"
  - After: "Allowing augmetics for one but not the rest is unfair. The lower decks get augmentation!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The noisy procession, smelling of sacred unguents and sweat, falls silent as soon as you appear. Those at the head of the crowd step forward, one of them waving the wrapped stump of his right arm, while another gawps at you with his one eye. The medicae officers, shielded by a line of enforcers, also stare in your direction.{/n}
  - After: {n}The crowd hushes. A one-armed and a one-eyed man step forward.{/n}
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "May the Omnissiah bless the Rogue Trader's sound judgement." {n}The Genetor focuses his multiple visors on you and bows his head. Not one of his mechanical eyes dignifies the vivisector with even a glance.{/n}
  - After: "Omnissiah bless your judgement." {n}The Genetor bows, ignoring the vivisector.{/n}
- **Foreman**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, you... you came!" {n}The one-eyed man hesitates and bows awkwardly.{/n} "We have a request! A petition! To authorise the {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}augmentation{/g} of workers below the rank of junior officer in the Sector Bionica due to the need to increase the efficiency of the workforce." {n}He blurts out the obviously memorised words in a rapid stream, then adds peevishly:{/n} "The vermin don't want to give us iron arms and legs! But we just want to work, for the good of you and the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g}!"
  - After: "Lord Captain!" {n}The one-eyed man bows.{/n} "We petition for {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}augmentation{/g} for workers, for efficiency!" {n}He adds:{/n} "We just want iron limbs to work for you and the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g}!"
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "Of course, such privileges for the lower decks are unprecedented. Yet these people are the lifeblood of the ship, Lord Captain, however low their standing in the social hierarchy. Allowing augmentation in the lower decks will enable workers to toil longer and will help older crew members remain of sound mind and pass on their experience to younger generations. I advise you to grant the request — it will only strengthen your crew!"
  - After: "Unprecedented, but they're the ship's lifeblood. Augmetics mean longer work and sharp elders to teach the young. Grant it."
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "I insist upon rejection of the request. Augmentation is a sacred gift of the {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g} that requires careful monitoring and maintenance. The Sector Bionica's resources are finite and, as such, our focus must be on servicing the key life forms among the crew. Violating the established directive and wastefully distributing the gift of augmentations among the unworthy would be an outrage to the Omnissiah and barely tolerated by the Tech-Priests aboard this vessel."
  - After: "Reject it. Augmentation is the {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g}'s gift, needing upkeep, reserved for key crew. Wasting it on the unworthy would outrage the Tech-Priests."
- **Worker**
  - Before: {n}The faces of the crowd brighten: some begin to pray fervently, others to shout out their thanks. The one-eyed man wipes his nose, and the one-armed man makes the sign of the Aquila.{/n} "Long live Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius!" {n}The joyous cry is immediately echoed by dozens more voices.{/n}
  - After: {n}The crowd rejoices.{/n} "Long live Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius!" {n}Dozens echo it.{/n}
- **Foreman**
  - Before: {n}Your words cause the crowd to fall silent. The two crippled men who came forward look blankly at each other before beginning to back away warily.{/n}
  - After: {n}Silence. The two cripples back away.{/n}
- **Worker**
  - Before: {n}The one-armed worker steps forward, pushing the one-eyed man aside.{/n} "One of the lads, a voidsman soldier who got his skull crushed, came back to the lower decks after treatment not long ago. With his new {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FirstChoiceVivisector}metal head{/d}, he's working harder than ever! If they'd let us poor sods put some hardware in, we'd work even better than the healthy ones! We'd toil day and night for the good of the dynasty. The officers say it's not allowed, but you can do anything, even lift this ban! Be merciful, Lord Captain!"
  - After: {n}The one-armed worker pushes forward.{/n} "A voidsman got a {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FirstChoiceVivisector}metal head{/d} and works harder than ever! With hardware we'd outwork anyone. Lift the ban, Lord Captain!"
- **Worker**
  - Before: {n}The one-armed worker bows his head and steps forward.{/n} "One of the lads, a voidsman soldier who got his skull crushed, came back to us after treatment not long ago. His head's all bandaged and he's dosed up to the eyeballs on {g|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FirstChoiceAugmentator}stimulants{/g}. He can't live, can't work, he just raves and scares honest folk. And all because he wasn't given implants! At least let us put some hardware in, or sooner or later we'll all turn into madmen on these rotten stimulants!"
  - After: {n}The one-armed worker steps forward.{/n} "A voidsman denied implants just raves on {g|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FirstChoiceAugmentator}stimulants{/g} now. Give us hardware, or we'll all go mad."
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "I apologise if it seems like I am mistaken, but I think we are seeing a direct result of the decision to deny augmentation to ordinary workers. In the long run, restricting the use of implants seems... unwise." {n}The Vivisector's high, determined voice is audible even over the clamour of the crowd.{/n}
  - After: "Forgive me, but this is what denying implants causes. It seems... unwise." {n}Her voice carries.{/n}
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "The request is unacceptable. I predicted that augmenting the voidsman soldier life form above the established baseline would cause the utility life forms to develop a distorted perception of their individual value — that is, irrationally inflated." {n}The hiss of the {g|Encyclopedia:Genetor}Genetor{/g}'s vox can barely be heard over the murmuring of the crowd.{/n}
  - After: "Unacceptable. As predicted, augmenting the voidsman inflated their sense of worth." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Genetor}Genetor{/g}'s vox hisses.{/n}
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: {n}The Vivisector breathes a sigh.{/n} "I thank the God-Emperor every day for sending us such a merciful ruler." {n}There is no escaping the satisfied look the Vivisector gives the Genetor.{/n}
  - After: {n}She sighs.{/n} "Thank the God-Emperor for so merciful a ruler." {n}She eyes the Genetor smugly.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "To beg for respite from the fate chosen for them since birth? Perhaps we should hold up the sisters of the Order of the Valorous Heart as an example. They do not even permit the dulling of pain during treatment of their wounds, no matter how grievous..." {n}Argenta stops short, as if shamed by her own severity.{/n} "Yet... that comparison is unfair to common labourers. Perhaps they truly would benefit from some aid."
  - After: "Escape their fate? The Order of the Valorous Heart refuses even painkillers..." {n}She falters.{/n} "But labourers aren't sisters. Perhaps they need aid."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "A fairly standard start to a mutiny." {n}Solomorne appears bored, but the barrel of the shotgun resting on his forearm is casually pointed at the one-eyed man.{/n} "First they want to 'increase efficiency,' then those who disagree begin to disappear, and now the rampaging locals are already stringing up their own from the nearest girder."
  - After: "Standard start of a mutiny." {n}His shotgun points at the one-eyed man.{/n} "First 'efficiency', then dissenters vanish, then hangings."
