  - After: {n}He hides the find in his robe.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Do not forget to destroy the tech-heresy before you leave the compartment." {n}Every one of Ferrenz's visors is fixed unwaveringly on the mysterious technology in your hands.{/n}
  - After: "Destroy the tech-heresy before leaving." {n}His visors stay on it.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ferrenz wilts under the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}crushing weight of your gaze{/d}. Breaking eye contact with visible effort, the Genetor shakes his head convulsively, as if to dispel a haunting vision. When he speaks again, his voice sounds strangely humbled.{/n} "As you command, Lord Captain." {n}The Tech-Priest accepts the augment with trembling hands.{/n} "The technology will be refined to its maximum possible efficiency."
  - After: {n}Ferrenz wilts under {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}your crushing gaze{/d}.{/n} "As you command." {n}He takes it, trembling.{/n} "It will be perfected."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Flesh is weak. But its efficiency can be improved with blessed metal. According to the directives of the Omnissiah, pivotal life forms, like pivotal mechanisms, must withstand maximum stress and produce the best results — my duty lies in improving them."
  - After: "Flesh is weak; blessed metal improves it. Key crew must endure. I improve them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I maximised the efficiency of the life forms serving within the sacred manufactorum on Kiava Gamma. By the blessing of the Omnissiah, I ascended to Genetor rank and was deployed to this flagship. My proficiency in installing augmetics was appraised as exceptional by the previous {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTraderGlossary}Rogue Trader{/g}."
  - After: "I served the Kiava Gamma manufactorum, rose to Genetor, came here. The last {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTraderGlossary}Rogue Trader{/g} rated me exceptional."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The blow makes Ferrenz stagger. His visors refocus chaotically, as if overwhelmed by conflicting data streams. For a few moments, the Genetor freezes. Then, he slowly bows his head.{/n} "As you command, Lord Captain." {n}His trembling hands reach for the augment.{/n} "May the Omnissiah forgive me for this coming violation of the sacred machine rites."
  - After: {n}Ferrenz staggers, then bows.{/n} "As you command." {n}He takes the augment.{/n} "Omnissiah forgive me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Deep bass notes carrying genuine reverence rumble in Ferrenz's hiss.{/n} "I am inclined to conclude that the archeotech augmentation machine harbours a spirit that blesses all things around it with the grace of the Omnissiah." {n}The Genetor sweeps a mechadendrite over the space around him.{/n} "Its nodes and pistons are filled with the wisdom of the Machine God, unfathomable to humble adepts, and if entropy consumes the spirit entirely, such wisdom will be lost."
  - After: {n}Reverently:{/n} "The archeotech machine has a blessed spirit." {n}He gestures.{/n} "If entropy takes it, the Machine God's wisdom is lost."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I deem the results of your scan to be accurate. The Vivisector performs the functions of preparing the carrier for installation of the maximum-efficiency configuration."
  - After: "Accurate. The Vivisector prepares the patient."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "While the body of the machine remains in dysfunction, its spirit suffers from idleness. The Motive Force cannot nourish it, and its lenses remain blind. Litanies and rituals keep such an ancient creation of the Omnissiah from fading away completely, but these are only palliative measures. And if the spirit abandons its receptacle, the Sector Bionica will fall into decay, for this relic serves the same function as the heart does in human life forms."
  - After: "Broken, its spirit starves; litanies only delay it. It is the Sector Bionica's heart."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "With the highest priority, I notify the Lord Captain that the sacred archeotech is still in an agonal state caused by the malicious actions of the rebels. The functionality of the Sector Bionica is limited. The life form 'Genetor Majoris Ferrenz' humbly awaits your assistance in purifying the reliquary mechanism."
  - After: "Priority: the archeotech is still dying from rebel sabotage. I await your help purifying it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If it improves the efficiency of our interaction."
  - After: "If it improves our interaction."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Scanning... Analysis shows that the sacred machine of the implantation throne lacks the binharic litanies required to handle the highest grade of augmetics. In order to increase its performance, it is necessary to retrieve the litanies stored on the parent device — Altar-Templum-Calixis-Ext-17."
  - After: "The throne lacks binharic litanies for top-grade augmetics. Fetch them from Altar-Templum-Calixis-Ext-17."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Given your inability to conduct a scan... I will respond to a limited set of enquiries."
  - After: "You cannot scan... I'll answer a few enquiries."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The dry hiss that normally comes from the Genetor's vox suddenly becomes higher: {/n} "Registering an unprecedented increase in the functional efficiency of the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g}! Rivers of sacred unguents wash over their iron flesh, and the mechanisms sing the praises of the Omnissiah! Bless the decision that led to this miracle of rebirth!"
  - After: {n}His hiss rises:{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} sing! Bless this rebirth!"

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Medbay/MB_EliteAugmentation/MB_EliteAugmentation_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Where did you even find this old man?"
  - After: "Where did you find this old man?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is going on here?"
  - After: "What's going on?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Remove the augment. A sacred machine should be put to good use, not employed as a crutch."
  - After: "Remove the augment. Sacred machines aren't crutches."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Leave the old man alone. Let him live out his last years in peace."
  - After: "Let the old man live in peace."
- **Player**
  - Before: "His augmentation is truly that valuable?"
  - After: "Is his augmentation that valuable?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Sort it out among yourselves. And if you interrupt me again for such trivialities, I will have both of you strung up by your thumbs at the entrance to the Sector Bionica. Understood?"
  - After: "Sort it out yourselves, or I'll string you both up by your thumbs."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What are your expert opinions?"
  - After: "Your expert opinions?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The screaming is wearing on me. Get rid of the troublemaker and have his implant cut out and brought to my throne. The finest things on this vessel are mine alone."
  - After: "Get rid of him and bring his implant to my throne. The finest things here are mine."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The typical sounds of the medicae facility are cut off by a bone-chilling scream. It is coming from an old man, who has sprung from his bed and is now using it as a barricade against the medicae officers. He is partially disrobed and the scraps of the bed restraints hang from his wrists. From toe to hip, the old man's legs have been replaced with high-quality {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}augments{/g}.{/n}
  - After: {n}An old man with fine {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}augment{/g} legs screams, barricaded against the medicae.{/n}
- **Old Servant**
  - Before: "No! Don't touch my legs! They're all I have left!"
  - After: "Don't touch my legs! They're all I have!"
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "Request: cease the attempted sabotage of the operation! Protocol stipulates that augments must be removed from ineffective life forms!" {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} tries to reach the patient, but the old man evades his grasp with unexpected spryness.{/n}
  - After: "Cease! Protocol: ineffective life forms lose augments!" {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} grabs; the man dodges.{/n}
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "The patient disrupted the augment removal procedure and is resisting the accepted treatment protocols."
  - After: "The patient resists removal."
- **Old Servant**
  - Before: {n}The old man's frantic gaze latches on to you and he begins wailing piteously:{/n} "Lord Captain, please help me! These beasts want to cut off my legs! I was a senior gunner on a macro-cannon. I lost my legs in my youth — it was only thanks to my implant I was able to fulfil my duty, guiding teams of haulers! And now they say that that's it, I have to give my legs back, but how can I give them back? Butchers!"
  - After: {n}He wails:{/n} "Lord Captain, help! I was a macro-cannon gunner; these legs let me serve. Butchers!"
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "The service life of this life form lapsed long ago, but the installed augmentation is of rare quality — it will be functional for hundreds of cycles yet to come. The sacred machine's efficiency is seriously compromised by the substandard biological part." {n}The Genetor's visors are directed unmistakably at the old man's gaunt frame.{/n} "The principles of maximum-efficiency service require immediate replacement of the augmetic carrier."
  - After: "His service is over, but the rare augment will last centuries." {n}He eyes the old man.{/n} "It needs a new carrier."
- **Old Servant**
  - Before: {n}Upon hearing you, the old man seems to lose all will to resist. A moment ago he was ready to fight, but now he slumps onto the bed listlessly, and the surgical instruments are thrust into his body. Despite the pain, the man no longer screams, but stares at the ceiling with glistening eyes.{/n}
  - After: {n}The old man slumps and stares at the ceiling, silent under the knives.{/n}
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "This augmented life form arrived on board along with the rest of the replenishment from Rykad Minoris and has since dwelled in the ship's cannon bays. One of the servants of the Machine God noticed the incongruity of a high-performance sacred augmetic being worn by such a life form, and he was brought here."
  - After: "He came from Rykad Minoris, worked the cannon bays. A Tech-Priest noticed his augmetic."
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "Sacred machines of augmentation are blessed in their own right," {n}grumbles the {g|Encyclopedia:Genetor}Genetor{/g} jealously.{/n} "But this particular set is slightly rarer than others. With proper care, it can greatly increase the speed of a high-quality recipient."
  - After: "All augments are blessed," {n}the {g|Encyclopedia:Genetor}Genetor{/g} grumbles.{/n} "This rare set greatly boosts speed."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "Debating such a trivial matter..." {n}Marazhai arches an eyebrow.{/n} "It would be simpler and quicker if, instead of arguing, you let the implant owner assert his right to it in combat against the challenger."
  - After: "Trivial." {n}Marazhai arches an eyebrow.{/n} "Let them duel for it."
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "I apologise, Lord Captain! Genetor Ferrenz and I will endeavour not to trouble you again." {n}Martinax bows deeply before you, doubling over until he touches the floor, and Ferrenz follows suit, pitching his body as low as the mechadendrites at his back will allow.{/n}
  - After: "Forgive us, Lord Captain!" {n}Both bow low.{/n}
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "Thank you for your timely intervention, Lord Captain. Commencing the procedure."
  - After: "Thank you, Lord Captain. Commencing."
- **Old Servant**
  - Before: "G-{g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g} protect you!" {n}The old man sighs in relief.{/n}
  - After: "G-{g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g} protect you!" {n}He sighs in relief.{/n}
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "Thank you for talking some sense into my colleague, Lord Captain. We will send this man back to where the Tech-Priests found him and retrieve the augment when the time comes."
  - After: "Thank you. We'll take the augment when his time comes."
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "Leave him be, Ferrenz. Let the poor fellow live out his life with his own augmentation. You can still cut it off after he's dead."
  - After: "Leave him, Ferrenz. Take it after he's dead."
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "Thank you for your timely intervention, Lord Captain." {n}The Genetor focuses his visors on you.{/n} "The augment carrier's efficiency class will increase exponentially."
  - After: "Thank you, Lord Captain." {n}Visors on you.{/n} "Efficiency will soar."
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "This man does not have long to live — let him walk the rest of the way on his own two feet. He is unlikely to survive the augment removal procedure." {n}The Vivisector casts a sympathetic glance at the patient.{/n}
  - After: "He hasn't long, and wouldn't survive removal. Let him walk." {n}Martinax looks pitying.{/n}
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "It's hardly surprising, Ferrenz. You're trying to cut off the poor man's legs."
  - After: "No wonder. You're cutting off his legs."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Medbay/MB_FactotumThroneTragedy/FactotumThroneTragedy_dialogue 

- **Player**
  - Before: "What makes this machine so important?"
  - After: "Why is this machine important?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How were the relics damaged?"
  - After: "How was it damaged?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What sacraments can the throne perform?"
  - After: "What can the throne do?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "And how do we save the throne?"
  - After: "How do we save it?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Danrok, I'll rely on your connections."
  - After: "Danrok, use your connections."
- **Player**
  - Before: "In that case, time is of the essence."
  - After: "Then time is short."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I doubt this wreck can even be repaired, but since it's so important..."
  - After: "I doubt this wreck is fixable, but fine..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The implantation throne is majestic in its antiquity. The metal bench, surrounded by countless injectors, manipulators, and vidscreens, leaves no doubt as to its purpose. The very nature of this machine is designed to transform living bodies by fusing them with blessed iron. Even to the naked eye, it is clear that the machine is ailing, grievously so. The manipulators' segmented tubes hang limply, bleeding unguent, while the dusty lumens are only dimly illuminated. As the Tech-Priests try to revive the relic, each swing of their censer is like a pendulum ticking down the moments until the throne's untimely demise.{/n}
  - After: {n}The ancient implantation throne, built to fuse flesh with iron, is dying. Tech-Priests' censers tick down its last moments.{/n}
- **Zi-Ra Tallar**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest slowly extends her mechadendrites, twisting them in an intricate gesture of greeting.{/n} "Lord Captain. The blessed machine spirit that dwells within the throne is fading. I and many grieving Tech-Priests have been performing unending sacraments of tech-healing and prayers of operational benediction on this shrine, but even our devotions are merely staving off the inevitable."
  - After: {n}The Tech-Priest greets you with mechadendrites.{/n} "Lord Captain. The throne's spirit is fading. Our sacraments only delay it."
- **Zi-Ra Tallar**
  - Before: "Only a servant of the Machine God endowed with the high rank of Genetor Extremis, versed in all the necessary rituals, and learned in the mystical currents of the Motive Force, can perform the reparative sacraments and reanimate this mechanism. The only place where one might find such a servant is on the cloistered station of Altar-Templum-Calixis-Ext-17."
  - After: "Only a Genetor Extremis can revive it. Seek one at the cloister Altar-Templum-Calixis-Ext-17."
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: "To the best of my knowledge, the cloister Mistress Tallar is referring to is located in the Furibundus System. Its denizens are not well disposed to communicating with the laity, but I am willing to leverage every diplomatic connection I possess to gain an audience with the station's clergy."
  - After: "That cloister is in the Furibundus System. They shun outsiders, but I'll pull every string."
- **Zi-Ra Tallar**
  - Before: {n}The Drivesmaster's vox-grille emits a binharic aria of thanks.{/n}
  - After: {n}A binharic aria of thanks.{/n}
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: {n}The High Factotum adjusts his monocle with a satisfied look.{/n} "I thank you for your favour, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Before you depart the Sector Bionica, I would also like to present to you Genetor Majoris Ferrenz and Vivisector Jaze Martinax. They are currently performing an urgent procedure and therefore were unable to attend the inspection in person, but I am certain they will receive the Rogue Trader's visit as a great honour. If you will follow me."
  - After: {n}Danrok adjusts his monocle.{/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Now meet Genetor Majoris Ferrenz and Vivisector Jaze Martinax. Follow me."
- **Zi-Ra Tallar**
  - Before: "It is unique. One of a kind." {n}The Tech-Priest's optical augments flash, and surprising fervour creeps into her voice.{/n} "In the Logis Annals of the Adeptus Mechanicus, this throne is identified as a shrine capable of autonomous augmentation rituals. Its loss is unacceptable, and any condoning of it is sacrilege."
  - After: "It is unique." {n}Her optics flash.{/n} "A shrine of autonomous augmentation. Losing it is sacrilege."
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: {n}The High Factotum clears his throat and grimaces.{/n} "During the uprising instigated by the rebellious Master of Whispers, the Sector Bionica was besieged. The Genetors and medicae officers heroically defended the throne, but eventually the rebels broke through. Most of the defenders fell in the battle, and many machines were lost or damaged. Many were able to be restored, but the throne was particularly badly damaged."
  - After: {n}Danrok grimaces.{/n} "Rebels in the Master of Whispers' uprising stormed the Sector Bionica. The throne was worst damaged."
- **Zi-Ra Tallar**
  - Before: "The shrine is capable of autonomously healing flesh and blessing it with augmentations under the supervision of a knowledgeable Genetor. Complex procedures can be performed with unimaginable speed and precision, and stimulants administered in the required proportions and combinations. It is a true miracle of the Omnissiah!"
  - After: "With a Genetor overseeing, it heals flesh and installs augments with unmatched speed and precision. A miracle of the Omnissiah!"
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, thank you for gracing the Sector Bionica with your presence. You are already acquainted with Drivesmaster Zi-Ra Tallar — it is she who has been tending to the ancient relic. She is here to convey the wretchedness of our present position."
  - After: "Welcome, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Drivesmaster Zi-Ra Tallar tends the relic and will explain."
- **Zi-Ra Tallar**
  - Before: "This throne is a creation of the Omnissiah made centuries ago. Even before the unholy desecration of the relic, we were barely able to propitiate its ancient machine spirit to perform sacred augmentation procedures — many litanies and operating protocols did not survive through the ages. Now, with the demise of the keepers of the implantation throne during the mutiny, they have been lost forever. This sacred machine must be saved at all cost."
  - After: "Many of its litanies were already lost; its keepers died in the mutiny with the rest. It must be saved at all cost."
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: "In addition, only the Rogue Trader or persons authorised by the Rogue Trader may use it. It is an invaluable investment in your longevity and... bodily integrity."
  - After: "Only you or those you authorise may use it. An investment in your... bodily integrity."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Medbay/MB_FinalAugmentatorMedbay/MB_FinalAugmentatorMedbay_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal, what is this prayer about?"
  - After: "Pasqal, what's this prayer about?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Vigdis, can you translate this... speech... for me?"
  - After: "Vigdis, translate this... speech?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have more pressing matters to attend to. Get everyone off my bridge and back to their direct duties."
  - After: "I'm busy. Get everyone off my bridge and back to duty."
- **Zi-Ra Tallar**
  - Before: {n}The procession of {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} and augmented officers stops a dozen paces away from your throne. A female Tech-Priest, whose robe bears marks of high distinction, steps forward, and you recognise her instantly as the ship's Drivesmaster. Her vox-distorted voice rattles solemnly throughout the deck.{/n}
  - After: {n}A procession of {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} halts before your throne. The Drivesmaster steps forward.{/n}
- **Zi-Ra Tallar**
  - Before: "May the {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g} bless the Lord Captain for this sanctioned audience! This tech-procession has come reciting the canticles of gratitude. Let us sing of the Lord Captain's concern for those who have forsaken their flesh in the service of the machine spirit! The voices of metal will sing the praises of your piety throughout the decks of the ship. Give us leave to switch to the sacred {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Techna-Lingua{/g}, which will convey our admiration more accurately than limited words." {n}Binharic trills ring out across the deck, melding with the hum of the {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitators{/g}.{/n}
  - After: "{g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g} bless the Lord Captain! We sing thanks for your care of the augmented, in sacred {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Techna-Lingua{/g}." {n}Trills join the {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitators{/g}' hum.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "It is a ceremony of gratitude for a layperson who, by chance or insight, has aided in purging the frailties of the flesh."
  - After: "Gratitude to a layperson who helped purge the flesh's frailties."
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "The esteemed Tech-Priests are performing a ceremony of supreme praise for the layperson who divined the path of the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g}. The wearers of {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}augmentations{/g} are grateful to you for your rational decisions regarding the use of iron flesh. They... have even embedded your name in their Techna-Lingua. To my knowledge, the crimson priesthood rarely bestows such an honour on anyone."
  - After: "They praise you for divining the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g}'s path. The {g|Encyclopedia:AugmentationGlossary}augmented{/g} even wove your name into Techna-Lingua. A rare honour."
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "I would like to note that I share their sentiments. Thank you for your diligent attention to augment maintenance for the senior officers and my family personally. Machines replace our flesh in the name of our service to the dynasty, and your regard for us is of incomparable value."
  - After: "I agree. Thank you for caring for my family's augments. Your regard is priceless."
- **Zi-Ra Tallar**
  - Before: "As an engine generates motion in sacred mechanical nodes, so your instructions guide the servants of the Sector Bionica. The medicae officers share our gratitude. Know that if frail flesh should betray you, the iron shoulder of the ship's Tech-Priests will be here for you to lean on."
  - After: "Your orders drive the Sector Bionica like an engine. Should flesh fail you, lean on our iron shoulder."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The members of the procession bow to you, sending heady fumes of machine unguents wafting in your direction. From above, they resemble a rippling lake of metallic limbs and {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g}. At the very tail of the procession, you notice the familiar figures of the medicae officers.{/n}
  - After: {n}They bow, a lake of {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g}, the medicae officers at the rear.{/n}
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "I have taken over management of the sector, but I endeavour to adhere to the wisdom bestowed upon us by the Adeptus Mechanicus. Sacred augmentations are being installed in strict compliance with patient status and efficiency." {n}Martinax shudders and adds quietly,{/n} "I rather sound like Genetor Ferrenz, don't I?"
  - After: "I run the sector now, following Mechanicus wisdom: augments go by patient status and efficiency." {n}Martinax shudders.{/n} "I sound like Ferrenz, don't I?"
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "It was one of the most complex procedures I have ever performed! We replaced the majority of his head augments, but it was only thanks to the knowledge of the crimson priesthood that a neural implant capable of replacing the damaged parts of the brain was found in the repositories of the Sector Bionica. They had been keeping it in storage all this time, withholding it from the laity — and for good reason, as it turns out. Isn't that right, Ferrenz?"
  - After: "My hardest procedure! The priesthood's hidden neural implant saved his brain. Right, Ferrenz?"

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Medbay/MB_FinalVivisectorMedbay/MB_FinalVivisectorMedbay_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I have more important matters to attend to than accepting the gratitude of the rabble. Remove them immediately."
  - After: "I've more important matters than the rabble's gratitude. Remove them."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Is this the entire procession? I thought there would be more of them."
  - After: "Is this all of them? I expected more."
- **Foreman**
  - Before: {n}Under the astonished gazes of your senior officers, the augmented procession sweeps through the entire deck and stops a dozen paces away from your throne. The procession is hemmed in on all sides by enforcers, but that does not stop the people from shouting blessings in your honour. Most of the procession is made up of low-ranking officers and inhabitants from the lower decks, their scar-hatched faces blazing with unfeigned devotion. A bandaged man of uncertain age and bearing marks of distinction on his chest steps forward.{/n}
  - After: {n}An augmented procession, ringed by enforcers, stops before your throne. A bandaged, decorated man steps forward.{/n}
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "This is only a small part of the procession, Lord Captain. The Master-at-Arms personally selected and scrutinised the most stable and trustworthy. To allow the entire march from the other decks onto the bridge would be impossible — or at least highly unsafe."
  - After: "Only a few, Lord Captain. The Master-at-Arms picked the trustworthy. All of them would be unsafe."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}One after another, each face, disfigured by burdensome fate, eases. The head of the procession raises a metal arm above his head — and all those able to follow suit, until a sea of prosthetics are held aloft.{/n}
  - After: {n}The leader raises a metal arm; a sea of prosthetics follows.{/n}
- **Foreman**
  - Before: "Ordinary crew members have seldom been furnished with prosthetics before! A saw and a prayer to the God-Emperor — those were our two main treatments. But things have changed under your noble rule, and the people of the Sector Bionica agree with us!"
  - After: "Crew used to get a saw and a prayer. Under your rule, we get prosthetics!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The members of the motley procession bow deeply. Among them you see the familiar figures of the experts of the Sector Bionica.{/n}
  - After: {n}They bow. The Sector Bionica experts are among them.{/n}
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "I would like to note that, thanks to your adherence to your principles, the experts of the Sector Bionica have been able to perfect the process of installing basic implants. The operations can now be completed in the shortest time and without having to expend any pain-dulling supplies — and so, I ask you to accept something that should ensure that the resulting surplus instead finds good use in the battles you face."
  - After: "Your principles let us perfect basic implants without pain-dulling supplies. Accept the surplus for your battles."
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "Request accepted. The Sector Bionica is fully operational once more and under the oversight of this life form. Augmetics are being installed in accordance with approved protocols."
  - After: "Request accepted. The Sector Bionica is fully operational under this life form's oversight."
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "The functions of the life form 'Martinax' have been restored. Critical blood loss was quickly replenished by the multitude of lesser-status life forms from the lower decks who presented themselves for urgent blood-letting. Supposition: the rabble did this out of loyalty to that particular medicae officer. The life form 'Martinax' also wishes to thank you."
  - After: "Life form 'Martinax' is restored. Loyal lower-deck rabble gave blood for her. She thanks you."
- **Foreman**
  - Before: "We have come to bow before you, Lord Captain, to show our gratitude for your {mf|fatherly|motherly} heedfulness over each and every one of us! Now even the lowliest cripple knows that he can serve the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g} with a decent prosthetic. This bolsters our faith and spurs on our toil like never before. Thank you." {n}The man is clearly trying to maintain his lofty style of speech, but he still falters at the end and simply bows.{/n} "The light of your mercy leads even the most hopeless to righteousness."
  - After: "We thank you for your {mf|fatherly|motherly} care, Lord Captain! Even a cripple can now serve the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g} with a prosthetic." {n}He falters and bows.{/n} "Your mercy leads even the hopeless."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The assembled rows of people all look at you and make the sign of the Aquila over their chests. Some people clumsily render the Aquila because they do not possess hands — they have been replaced with crude metal hooks.{/n}
  - After: {n}They make the Aquila — some with metal hooks for hands.{/n}

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Medbay/MB_FirstVisit/MB_FirstVisit_dialogue

- **Player**

  - Before: "But that was all before I became a Rogue Trader..."

  - Before: "I believe he's deteriorating."

  - Before: [Continue to look at the patient]
  - After: [Keep looking at the patient]

  - Before: "I have made a decision."

  - Before: "I am the Rogue Trader, not a soul healer. How much longer do you expect me to entertain him?"
  - After: "I'm no soul healer. How much longer?"

  - Before: "What are your respective proposals?"
  - After: "Your proposals?"

  - Before: [Address the patient] "Do not forget to breathe. It will dull the pain."
  - After: [Address the patient] "Breathe. It dulls pain."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address the patient] "Your mother is here, Gnotec, and she is very worried about you. Hold on for her."
  - After: [Address the patient] "Gnotec, your mother's here. Hold on for her."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address the patient] "I have heard that a good story can dull the pain. Would you like me to tell you about my adventures? On one occasion..."
  - After: [Address the patient] "Want a story of my adventures? Once..."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The smell of medical supplies and weak cries of pain fill the cold air. Two figures stand over an operating table — the patient lying upon it is bound in place, and his head is soaked in blood. A woman in uniform is desperately trying to force her way to the table.{/n}
  - After: {n}Two figures over a bound, bloody patient. A uniformed woman pushes forward.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The man in the bed stares back at you through glassy eyes. His arms, held tightly to the bed by straps, shudder, his face contorting in a grimace.{/n}
  - After: {n}The strapped man stares glassily, grimacing.{/n}
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "I understand that my opinion may strike you as strange, for the mere fact that this poor soul has found his way to the Sector Bionica might itself be regarded as a blessing. Yet hear me out. The installation of a cortical augmentation will restore the patient to health, serving as an example for the rest of us through his heroism. This will inspire the people and strengthen their faith in the Lord Captain, and let them know that the Rogue Trader's mercy will not abandon them in their hour of need."
  - After: "A cortical augment would restore him as a heroic example, proving your mercy won't abandon the crew."
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "How curious... It seems the Rogue Trader's presence is indeed influencing the patient's state of mind." {n}Martinax looks back at you with interest.{/n} "Whether it is a manifestation of devout faith in His anointed, or a bizarre form of delusion, it can only be to our benefit. Whatever you are doing, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... please continue."
  - After: "Curious... Your presence helps him." {n}Martinax eyes you.{/n} "Faith or delusion — please continue, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The grimace fixed on the wounded man's pale face makes it impossible to tell how much attention he is paying to your story. It is not clear if he understands anything you are saying, but you do not hear any more moans.{/n}
  - After: {n}Whether he follows or not, the moaning stops.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}With each of his many ocular implants focused closely on the patient, Genetor Ferrenz is rooting around inside the man's open skull with a thin, sharp, probe-like instrument. Meanwhile, Chirurgeon Martinax's hands, clad in bloodstained gloves, are holding an injector of yellowish solution, which he administers into the patient's brain matter at regular intervals.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ferrenz probes the open skull; Martinax injects the brain.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Through the bloody foam on his lips, the prostrate man whispers,{/n} "God-Emperor bless you, Lord Captain!" {n}Barely exhaling the words, he takes a deep, pure breath.{/n}
  - After: {n}Through bloody foam:{/n} "God-Emperor bless you, Lord Captain!" {n}He breathes deeply.{/n}
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: {n}A moment later, the two people leaning over the patient simultaneously raise their instruments. In a colourless voice, the Tech-Priest proclaims,{/n} "Registering the complete stabilisation of the life form's condition. Internal cortical damage has been treated. Requesting closure of the calotte and transfer of the victim to B-class stimulants."
  - After: {n}Both raise their instruments.{/n} "Life form stabilised. Close skull; administer B-class stimulants."
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "He will live, but the stimulants won't replace that part of his brain. If we implant the sacred cortical augment in his skull, it will restore his lost ability to think and act. Lord Captain, please! Your subject has a genuine need for this augmentation!"
  - After: "He'll live, but stimulants can't replace lost brain. An augment would restore his mind. Please, Lord Captain!"
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}As soon as you avert your eyes, the man in the bed lets out a loud, anguished scream. The pair leaning over him flinch, but do not remove their hands from his sawn-open head.{/n}
  - After: {n}As you look away, he screams.{/n}
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "We hear and obey, Lord Captain." {n}Martinax offers you a graceful bow.{/n} "I will see to the implantation at once. And the esteemed servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g} will assist me in this procedure." {n}The Genetor Majoris's response in binharic carries a distinct tone of displeasure. Ignoring his colleague's reaction, the Vivisector begins inserting thin augmentation spikes into the patient's brain with uncanny precision. Before long, the iron plate of the cortical implant replaces the damaged bone with a resounding crunch.{/n}
  - After: "We obey." {n}Martinax bows.{/n} "I'll implant it, with the {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g}'s servant assisting." {n}The Genetor trills displeasure. The implant crunches into place.{/n}
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "Initiating expedited completion of the operation." {n}The upper, almost melted portion of the patient's skull closes over the brain matter with a crunch, and the drill at the end of the Tech-Priest's delicate {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrite{/g} emits a shrill whirring sound before digging into the bone and crudely putting it back into place.{/n} "Requesting assistance from the Vivisector life form by performing composite suturing of bone. No further operative intervention is required."
  - After: "Expediting." {n}A {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrite{/g} drill crudely refits the skull.{/n} "Vivisector, suture. Done."
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "We are almost finished, Lord Captain. I apologise for the inappropriate request, but we just need one more minute."
  - After: "One more minute, Lord Captain."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "True devotion is revealed not in a servant's life, but in their death. So teach the Tenets of the Web." {n}With a discreet motion, Kibellah touches the bloodstain on the wounded man's head and draws a crimson sign upon the metal of the cot.{/n}
  - After: "Devotion shows in death. So teach the Tenets of the Web." {n}Kibellah draws a blood sign.{/n}
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: {n}Still working the injector, Martinax turns his head to you.{/n} "This young man has suffered a serious head injury that requires immediate intervention. The Genetor Majoris and I are attempting to stop the flesh from dying off while simultaneously deciding on a strategy for further treatment."
  - After: {n}Martinax turns.{/n} "A severe head wound. We're keeping him alive while choosing treatment."
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "A soldier from a voidsman combat unit and a devoted servant of the Emperor. Lord Captain, this young man has been fighting for his life, even through horrendous pain. If you allow the augmentation to be installed, his perseverance will become an example for others to emulate."
  - After: "A devout voidsman soldier fighting through agony. Augmented, he'd inspire others."
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "In the last void battle, Lord Captain, where he barely survived his injuries. He has suffered a few healing attempts from charlatans on the lower decks and endured a long road to come here. However, no weapon can destroy the devotion and fortitude of a true servant of the God-Emperor."
  - After: "The last void battle. Charlatans botched him below; he came far. His devotion endures."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The medicae officer and the Tech-Priest exchange glances.{/n}
  - After: {n}They exchange glances.{/n}
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "The life form on the operating table is easily replaceable and does not possess any substantial functional value. Therefore, installation of the implant would be devoid of sense. Proposing replacement of lost function by means of class-B powder stimulants. The life form will have limited viability and will be gifted an optimal termination period with partial functionality."
  - After: "This life form is replaceable; an implant is senseless. Class-B stimulants: limited viability, then optimal termination."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}For a moment, you think there is a flicker of vivid emotion in the person's pain-ravaged eyes — something akin to extreme surprise.{/n}
  - After: {n}Surprise flickers in his eyes.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "The Throne of Terra, blazing in His light, turning aside every evil..." {n}A quiet chant emanates from off to your side. Turning your gaze from the patient, you see Sister Argenta, having made the sign of the Aquila, raising a prayer to the God-Emperor. Her melodic voice is soothing and instils confidence.{/n}
  - After: "The Throne of Terra, blazing in His light, turning aside every evil..." {n}Argenta prays softly.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: {n}A gasp of astonishment escapes Cassia's lips.{/n} "Lord Captain... the fading soul of this man has blossomed anew with colour, the very moment you drew near. The venerable medicae speak truly. Your mere presence instils in this wretch a will to cling to life."
  - After: {n}Cassia gasps.{/n} "His fading soul bloomed as you neared. You give him the will to live."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}Following {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Torture}your advice{/d}, the maimed man gasps for air — once, twice, thrice. His face regains a hint of colour, though his teeth are still clenched convulsively.{/n}
  - After: {n}Following {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Torture}your advice{/d}, he gasps thrice; colour returns.{/n}
- **Serenada Schwartz**
  - Before: "Please help my son, in the name of the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThroneGlossary}Golden Throne{/g}, I know you can! Gnotec has endured so much..." {n}The lined face of the middle-deck veteran is contorted with grief. Every word she speaks comes out in a long moan.{/n}
  - After: "Help my son, by the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThroneGlossary}Golden Throne{/g}! Gnotec has endured so much..." {n}She is grief-stricken.{/n}
- **Serenada Schwartz**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, our guiding light! My son, Gnotec, he's injured and dying. I carried him here in my arms, on my own, so the chirurgeons could pull him back from the brink, please don't leave us..." {n}The woman's gaze swings from you to the chirurgeons and back again — her mental state is obviously unstable.{/n}
  - After: "Lord Captain! My son Gnotec is dying. I carried him here — don't leave us..." {n}She is unstable.{/n}
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: {n}With a whirring sound, Ferrenz's optical augment focuses on you.{/n} "Scanning for the potential utility of the life form... Encephalic healing skill is lacking. At present, nothing can be done."
  - After: {n}Ferrenz's optic whirs.{/n} "You lack encephalic healing skill. Nothing can be done."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The patient's clouded gaze is locked on the woman's face, the corners of his parted lips stretching into the faint semblance of a smile. His mother stares back, almost without blinking.{/n}
  - After: {n}He faintly smiles at his mother.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The man chained to the bed is missing the top part of his skull: the moist pink contents glisten in the {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumen{/g} light. The patient is conscious — his eyes are open and his parched lips are constantly moving as he mumbles. The man's terrified gaze meets yours, and he falls silent.{/n}
  - After: {n}His skull is open, brain glistening in {g|Encyclopedia:Lumen}lumen{/g} light. Mumbling, he meets your gaze and goes silent.{/n}
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: {n}You do not need to finish the tale. A moment later, the two people leaning over the patient simultaneously raise their instruments and, in a colourless voice, the Tech-Priest proclaims,{/n} "Registering the complete stabilisation of the life form's condition. Internal cortical damage has been treated. Requesting closure of the calotte and transfer of the victim to B-class stimulants."
  - After: {n}Before your tale ends, both raise their instruments.{/n} "Life form stabilised. Close skull; administer B-class stimulants."
- **Serenada Schwartz**
  - Before: "My only son, he's serving in a void unit. I was the one who told him to go there... my poor Gnotec," {n}rasps the woman from behind the medicae officers.{/n}
  - After: "My only son. I told him to join the void unit... poor Gnotec," {n}she rasps.{/n}
- **Serenada Schwartz**
  - Before: {n}In the silence, you hear the soft sobs of a woman. Gnotec's mother is weeping helplessly, furiously wiping her eyes with her hand, but now a smile of relief lights up her face.{/n} "Thank you... Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I will remember your intercession for the rest of my life and pray for your good fortune."
  - After: {n}His mother weeps with relief.{/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I'll pray for you always."
- **Serenada Schwartz**
  - Before: {n}Gnotec's mother sucks in a breath and forcefully wipes away the tears. Her half-crazed eyes roam over her surroundings, and finally latch onto the Genetor Majoris. Animal rage simmers in her blown pupils, as if she were ready to lunge at the Tech-Priest, but the impulse dissipates after a moment. In a dull voice, she says,{/n} "Thank you for your mercy."
  - After: {n}His mother glares at the Genetor, then says dully,{/n} "Thank you for your mercy."
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "Do not be so hasty, colleague. Heal with the mind, not with medicaments — that's one of the key wisdoms of the Officio Medicae." {n}The Vivisector stares at the wounded man's face for a few seconds.{/n} "Perhaps Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s presence will lend strength to the patient. Try to support the patient while we attempt to stabilise his condition."
  - After: "Not so hasty. Heal with the mind, says the Officio Medicae." {n}He studies the patient.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, support him while we stabilise."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The patient's clouded gaze is locked on the woman's face, the corners of his parted lips stretching into the faint semblance of a smile. His mother stares back, almost without blinking.{/n}
  - After: {n}He faintly smiles at his mother.{/n}
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: {n}The hunched {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} on the opposite side of the table erupts in a furious binharic trill as he struggles to immobilise the thrashing and moaning patient. After a time, he likewise turns his metal-plated face to you.{/n} "The life form Genetor Majoris Ferrenz welcomes Lord Captain {name} von Valancius. I second my colleague's statement."
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} pins the thrashing patient, then turns.{/n} "Genetor Majoris Ferrenz welcomes Lord Captain {name} von Valancius. I concur."
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}The medicae officer dressed in protective attire briefly looks away from the table to welcome you with a solemn address.{/n} "Vivisector Jaze Martinax, at your service. The Rogue Trader's visit is a momentous event for the Sector Bionica. Will you grant us the honour of observing the operation?"
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}The medic glances up.{/n} "Vivisector Jaze Martinax. Will you observe?"
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "An expendable life form to be utilised in void battles, one of thousands."
  - After: "Expendable. One of thousands."
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "This constitutes a violation of the sacred directives. The value of an individual life form is incomparably less than the value of the sacred technology required. Augmetics of the specified class are rare and are restricted to senior officers. Thus dictate the regulations of the Sector Bionica."
  - After: "This violates sacred directives. Such rare augmetics are reserved for senior officers, per Sector Bionica regulations."
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "The scan results state the opposite. The heart rate of this life form is returning to normal."
  - After: "Scans disagree. Its heart rate is normalising."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Medbay/MB_GeneWarden/MB_GeneWarden_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I, Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, command you to open this door."
  - After: "I, Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, order this door open."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Answer me, machine spirit of the genetic guardian. Who is Seberian?"
  - After: "Machine spirit, who is Seberian?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Examine the coat of arms on the wall]
  - After: [Examine the coat of arms]
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The High Factotum, Chirurgeon Martinax and Genetor Ferrenz are already waiting for you by the mysterious door. The wall behind them looks perfectly flat. Only the metal coat of arms gleaming in the lumen light and the steady glow in the genetic guardian's impassive lenses reveal that one of the dynasty's secrets lies behind this wall.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your officers wait by a blank wall bearing a coat of arms and a genetic guardian.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The guardian of the secret room looks far less menacing than the gargoyle that guards the entrance to the Warrant Chamber — this is just a recess in the wall, framed in metal, with an analyser needle inside and a small vid-screen beside it. Lines of mechanically indifferent text appear on the screen:{/n} "Access is forbidden. Entry is authorised only for Seberian von Valancius or his direct descendants."
  - After: {n}A recess, a needle, a screen:{/n} "Access forbidden. Only Seberian von Valancius or his direct descendants may enter."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The analyser pierces your hand, wriggling repulsively beneath your skin. A split second later, the colour of the genetic guardian's vid-screen changes to a welcoming green.{/n} "Identification passed. Welcome, member of the von Valancius dynasty." {n}A tremor passes through the wall, accompanied by the deep groan of ancient locks releasing.{/n}
  - After: {n}The needle pierces your hand.{/n} "Identification passed. Welcome, von Valancius." {n}Locks groan open.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The guardian's vid-screen flickers just slightly.{/n} "Error. The request is invalid. Entry is authorised only for Seberian von Valancius or his direct descendants."
  - After: {n}It flickers.{/n} "Error. Only Seberian von Valancius or his direct descendants may enter."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The heraldic symbols cast in noble bronze are undoubtedly from the von Valancius dynasty. Only certain details draw your eye — some elements of the ornamentation and the archaic script. They indicate that the coat of arms, as well as the wall itself, is several centuries old.{/n}
  - After: {n}The von Valancius arms and wall are centuries old.{/n}
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: {n}Vivisector Martinax's pupils dilate. He takes a wary step forward and freezes.{/n} "Incredible! Generations of chirurgeons have toiled away here and were utterly unaware..."
  - After: {n}Martinax freezes.{/n} "Incredible! Generations never knew..."
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: {n}Ferrenz lets out a shocked exclamation in Lingua-Technis, which shifts to a sharp binharic screech. Then, embarrassed by his outburst, the Tech-Priest bashfully steps aside, respectfully making way for you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ferrenz screeches, then sheepishly steps aside.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Be careful, Lord Captain." {n}Abelard narrows his eyes at the outline of the coat of arms, his brows furrowed stubbornly.{/n} "Dynastic secrets can be more than a little dangerous. It is my righteous duty as Seneschal to escort you inside."
  - After: "Careful, Lord Captain." {n}Abelard frowns.{/n} "Dynastic secrets are dangerous. I'll escort you."
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: "I advise you to take every conceivable precaution, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Janris sighs heavily, steeling himself.{/n} "Dynastic secrets can be more than a little dangerous."
  - After: "Take precautions, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Janris sighs.{/n} "Dynastic secrets are dangerous."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The door slides to one side with a metallic thud. Stale air rushes out of the hidden room, carrying with it particles of centuries-old dust.{/n}
  - After: {n}The door opens; ancient dust rushes out.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The heraldic symbols cast in noble bronze are undoubtedly from the von Valancius dynasty. You struggle to discern anything unusual in them.{/n}
  - After: {n}Von Valancius arms. Nothing unusual.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Genetic confirmation of dynastic status required." {n}With an off-putting beep, the analyser needle lengthens slightly.{/n}
  - After: "Genetic confirmation required." {n}The needle extends.{/n}

  - After: {n}Instantly:{/n} "At once, Lord Captain!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your eye is drawn to the head of the predatory creature behind the man. Its beastly face, distorted in mortal rage, is vaguely familiar, and its gaze — too intelligent for a dead thing — is fixed on something very specific outside the painting.{/n}
  - After: {n}A vaguely familiar beast's head behind him, frozen in rage, seems to watch something outside the painting.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}There can be no doubt about the weapon's origins: the sword depicted by this unknown artist's brush was not forged by human hands. The fluid curves, the exceptional lustre of the blade, and the gem at the hilt show the weapon to be the work of an Aeldari artisan. The blade is also unusual for the runes engraved along its length — they are most ancient indeed. The inscription is in the Aeldari language, recounting the legend of an unholy god of war revered by the xenos.{/n}
  - After: {n}The sword is Aeldari-made, its ancient runes recounting the legend of an unholy xenos war god.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is hard to argue with the simple truth: the subject of the portrait was an extremely good-looking individual. Not one of his meticulously painted scars, which the Rogue Trader bore like medals for military valour, could spoil his noble beauty.{/n}
  - After: {n}He was strikingly handsome; even his scars look like medals.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Chiselled features, dark brows, and a gaze full of inner strength. You also notice the finely worked furrows of stubbornness on his forehead and at the corners of his mouth. The artist strove to capture the complex character of a strong-willed man, and seems to have done a superlative job.{/n}
  - After: {n}Chiselled, dark-browed, stubborn, strong-willed — masterfully captured.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}There can be no doubt about the weapon's origins: the sword depicted by this unknown artist's brush was not forged by human hands. The fluid curves, the exceptional lustre of the blade, and the gem at the hilt show the weapon to be the work of an Aeldari artisan.{/n}
  - After: {n}The sword is clearly Aeldari-made.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Only one thought occurs to you: the Rogue Trader in the portrait was no stranger to luxury or daring exploits.{/n}
  - After: {n}He knew luxury and daring.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You know you speak the truth. You begin to think that the man in the portrait is looking back at you with faith in his eyes.{/n}
  - After: {n}You mean it. His eyes seem to hold faith in you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The piercing stare from above seems to mock your self-assurance.{/n}
  - After: {n}His stare seems to mock you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The portrait remains silent. Perhaps because, despite the vividness of the person depicted, it is only an object that has been hanging on this wall for centuries.{/n}
  - After: {n}The portrait stays silent — just an old object.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The flames do not take hold immediately, as if the portrait were resisting its doom. The face of the ancient hero first becomes covered in a layer of melted paint, as if drenched in horror, and then curves in a malevolent snarl and collapses in on itself.{/n}
  - After: {n}It resists the flames, then the hero's face melts into a snarl and collapses.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Reflections of light play whimsically on the expensive oil with which the portrait is painted.{/n}
  - After: {n}Light plays on the expensive oil.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}With sudden clarity, you {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}realise{/d} that the image has been significantly embellished. What you have before you is a ceremonial portrait intended to cast its subject in the most favourable light possible. Either that, or... the artist whose brush produced this work truly did see your ancestor as some kind of idol.{/n}
  - After: {n}You {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}realise{/d} it's heavily flattering — or the artist idolised your ancestor.{/n}

  - Before: "What an intriguing blade. But to display it in a ceremonial portrait is a sign of either fantastic arrogance or self-indulgent stupidity."
  - After: "Intriguing blade. Flaunting it in a portrait is arrogance or stupidity."
- **Argenta**

Details are eroded by time, leaving only the essences crystallised within relics and images. We should preserve only that which fortifies us upon His path. The rest must be consigned to oblivion. Unfortunately... this portion of your legacy belongs to the latter."
  - After: {n}Argenta disapproves.{/n} "Keep only memories that fortify us on His path; forget the rest. Sadly, this legacy belongs to the latter."
- **Cassia**

The execution is so exquisite that glimpses of the model's own emotions flicker before my gaze. As if... As if the master has captured not only the man's likeness upon the canvas, but his very soul."
  - After: {n}Cassia touches the frame.{/n} "Masterful, Lord Captain. The artist captured not just his likeness, but his soul."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Medbay/MB_ServeAugmentation/MB_ServeAugmentation_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You belong to the Toliman dynasty? The same as my Vox Master, Vigdis?"
  - After: "You're Toliman dynasty? Like my Vox Master, Vigdis?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "So you want to be treated without waiting your turn?"
  - After: "You want to skip the queue?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "No officer on my ship will ever have to stand in a queue. Let them through."
  - After: "My officers never queue. Let them through."
- **Player**
  - Before: "There are no unimportant people on my ship. Everyone will be treated equally — and based on your place in the queue."
  - After: "Everyone on my ship matters. Wait your turn."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Take these upstarts out of here and have them flogged. That will teach them that, on this ship, the only person with preferential privileges is me."
  - After: "Flog these upstarts. Only I get privileges on this ship."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Explain what is going on here."
  - After: "Explain what's going on."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The two strangely dressed officers bow deferentially at the sight of you. The older one, a tall and wrinkled voidborn, steps forward. The tails of long neural cords embedded in his head dangle unpleasantly down his back like a ragged cloak.{/n}
  - After: {n}Two officers bow. The older, trailing neural cords, steps forward.{/n}
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "Request granted. Initiating the voiding of the medical equipment in accordance with the Lord Captain's decision." {n} The system mounted above the operating area springs into action, and, muffled under the rumbling of its mechanisms, Genetor Ferrenz lets out a binharic trill of satisfaction.{/n}
  - After: "Granted. Voiding equipment." {n}Ferrenz trills with satisfaction.{/n}
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "Lord Captain! I don't know how to thank you for your timely intervention. These people still don't understand that there are some things that can't be bought with a noble name or a lofty position."
  - After: "Thank you, Lord Captain! A noble name can't buy everything."
- **Augmented Aristocrat**
  - Before: {n}Kantus retreats a little to the side. The cables in his head jangle with the movement, and you notice that some of them have melted.{/n} "We are members of a noble clan that has spent years overseeing the sacred vox systems of this voidship. It is a job that requires frequent maintenance, for many machine sparks must pass through our augments. Recently, the frequency of their augment inspections has decreased as access to the Sector Bionica has become more fraught. Instead of esteemed officers, the local medicae officers prefer to cater to crippled vagrants..."
  - After: {n}Kantus's cables are partly melted.{/n} "Our clan tends the ship's vox systems; our augments need constant care. Yet the medicae favour crippled vagrants..."
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "I have already explained to you: we do not give preferential treatment to anyone. Your implants will be serviced according to your place in the queue, which is in turn based on the urgency of the required procedure. While you're too slothful to coat your own head in sacred coolants, someone else is dying for lack of a lung." {n}The Vivisector exhales heavily: judging by the dark circles under his eyes, fatigue is making it hard for him to maintain his usual cordiality.{/n}
  - After: "No favourites; urgency decides. While you idle, others die for want of a lung." {n}Martinax looks exhausted.{/n}
- **Augmented Aristocrat**
  - Before: "I find it fair to assume that those who belong to a high and esteemed clan have some privileges over those who can barely read. Our augments require careful maintenance as they are directly connected to the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g} of the ship's vox-stations."
  - After: "A high clan deserves privileges. Our augments serve the vox {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g}."
- **Augmented Aristocrat**
  - Before: {n}The old officer smiles and bows low to you. The young man behind him casts a sneering look at Martinax and walks to the vacated spaces with his nose in the air.{/n}
  - After: {n}The old officer bows. His son sneers at Martinax and struts to the beds.{/n}
- **Augmented Aristocrat**
  - Before: {n}The old man frowns, but still bows respectfully to you. The young man behind him looks outraged and tries to step forward, but the older officer deftly seizes his son by the long cable embedded in his head. A stifled splutter erupts from the vox-repeater replacing the young man's mouth, but it is drowned out by the father's booming voice:{/n} "We will accept your decision whatever it may be, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}The old man bows, yanking back his outraged son by a cable.{/n} "We accept your decision, Lord Captain."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "For once, an intelligent thought from the lips of your kind." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:DrukhariGlossary}Drukhari{/g}'s gaze rests intently on the young man, compelling him into sudden silence.{/n} "Then again, implanting such cattle with metal only increases the pain I can derive from them, so I must disagree in this instance."
  - After: "For once, a clever thought from your kind." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:DrukhariGlossary}Drukhari{/g} silences him.{/n} "Though metal makes cattle hurt more, so I disagree."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "I have witnessed the blood of a single martyr become a spark that ignites thousands of souls! His raiment was humble, but his word shone brighter than any fabric. Will you, then, presume to judge by mere uniform alone whether this broken wretch has fulfilled his duty to the Holy Throne?"
  - After: "One humble martyr's blood can ignite thousands! Will you judge his duty by his clothes?"
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}With a loud clang, the two beds tip over, sending their still living occupants hurtling into the corpse pit. One of them screams briefly before his body lands on the conveyor belt with a crunch.{/n}
  - After: {n}The beds tip their living occupants into the corpse pit. A scream, a crunch.{/n}
- **Augmented Aristocrat**
  - Before: "Allow us to introduce ourselves: Kantus Zehir Otto Toliman, officer of Vox-Repeater LMXIV on Upper Deck 6, Sector 2. And this young man is my eldest son. We are here on a serious matter, and we would be most grateful to Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} if you would lend your support to our fair petition for the staff of the Sector Bionica."
  - After: "Kantus Zehir Otto Toliman, officer of Vox-Repeater LMXIV, Upper Deck 6, Sector 2, and my son. Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, support our petition."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The young man, who has remained behind his father throughout the conversation, suddenly cannot restrain himself:{/n} "I saw an armless man being loaded onto an operating table! Why should he be treated at all? He should be disposed of, the ship is full of trash like him!"
  - After: {n}The son bursts out:{/n} "They're treating an armless man! Dispose of such trash!"
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "Master Toliman, as I have already told you both: you will be seen when you reach the front of the queue! Now I have work to do, please do not distract me, or, Throne forbid, the Lord Captain!"
  - After: "Master Toliman, wait your turn! Don't distract me — or the Lord Captain!"
- **Augmented Aristocrat**
  - Before: {n}The faces of both officers tense. The young man tries to step forward and block his father, but the older officer hurriedly speaks up:{/n} "We beg forgiveness for our insolence, Lord Captain, and will accept our punishment with humility!"
  - After: {n}The old man speaks quickly:{/n} "Forgive us, Lord Captain. We accept punishment."
- **Augmented Aristocrat**
  - Before: "Indeed. My son and I are distant relatives of Vox Master Toliman. Our family serves the ship faithfully, and sacred implants like ours are passed down from generation to generation along with our position." {n}The old man inclines his head in a bow.{/n}
  - After: "Yes, distant kin of Vox Master Toliman. Our implants pass down with our post." {n}He bows.{/n}
- **Genetor Ferrenz**
  - Before: "Scanning has revealed two lower-priority life forms in the operating area. Request: dispose of less effective crew members to make space for valuable officers." {n}Out of the corner of your eye, you notice that the Genetor is already standing near the cogitator that controls the mechanisms of the individual beds.{/n}
  - After: "Two lower-priority life forms present. Request: dispose of them for valuable officers." {n}Ferrenz is at the bed controls.{/n}
- **Vivisector Martinax**
  - Before: "Thank you for your intervention, Lord Captain! I always welcome your visits to the Sector Bionica — it brings blessed order to this place like nothing else."
  - After: "Thank you, Lord Captain! You bring order here."

It is too soft, too high, too sorrowful.{/n} "The grief of a beast whose cub has become a plaything in human hands is not easily softened, {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}.   - After: {n}Idira speaks in a sorrowful voice not her own:{/n} "A beast grieving her cub, {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}. Can you soothe her?" {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:PsykerGlossary}psyker{/g} coughs.{/n}
- **Vivisector Martinax**

Straightening up, he fixes his robe and bows deeply to you.{/n} "You are a blessing of the God-Emperor descended to us mere mortals. I would thank you more, but my presence is needed in the operating chamber. Genetor Ferrenz is in grave condition..."
  - After: "Thank you, Lord Captain," {n}Martinax bows deeply.{/n} "A blessing! Genetor Ferrenz needs surgery..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The weapon in the woman's hands noticeably trembles.{/n} "If anyone else had said this, I wouldn't listen. But you... and your achievements... You command reverence from so many throughout the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g}." {n}She falls silent for a time, consumed by her doubts.{/n}
  - After: {n}Her weapon trembles.{/n} "You're revered across the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g}..." {n}She wavers.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}Glaito seems to materialise out of thin air, like a ghost, and clamps his jaws down on her leg with a crunch. As she falls, she manages to point her autopistol at you and fire — before a round from Solomorne's weapon turns her head into a fountain of bloody shreds.{/n}

  - After: {n}She shakes her head.{/n} "They're one festering wound..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "People are replaceable, aren't they? You find yourself new butchers, and let these ones go to the void rats' table, the same place they send their patients, and where they sent my son."
  - After: "Find new butchers. Feed these to the void rats, like my son."

  - After: {n}A crazed smile.{/n} "I'm not here for mercy."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}An autopistol round lightly singes your hair, but misses you. The woman falls to the ground, hit by the return shot. As her body hits the deck, the figures around you move, Sauerback barking orders.{/n}

- **Serenada Schwartz**
  - Before: "The healers from the Sector Bionica killed my son. They promised me that Gnotec would come out of here good as new, but he didn't — he crawled out, {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FirstChoiceAugmentator}dosed up on chemicals{/d}, and died in my arms, foaming at the mouth like some void rat. Is this what we served for? Is this the thanks we get for putting ourselves in harm's way? I've come to collect my debt."
  - After: "Sector Bionica's healers killed my son. Gnotec crawled out {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FirstChoiceAugmentator}dosed up on chemicals{/d} and died foaming in my arms. Is this our thanks? I've come to collect."
- **Serenada Schwartz**
  - Before: {n}Your tone is cold enough the chill the bones: the woman flinches and looks at you, as if realising for the first time exactly who is talking to her.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your icy tone makes her flinch.{/n}
- **Serenada Schwartz**
  - Before: {n}The woman who has lost her child sits on the deck with her head hanging limply. She does not tremble or spit curses. She stares blankly at the floor — into the abyss that only she knows.{/n}
  - After: {n}The grieving mother sits limp, staring blankly.{/n}
- **Serenada Schwartz**

  - After: {n}She fires; you spoil her aim. The medicae falls, head bloody.{/n}

  - Before: [Knock the weapon out of the man's hands]

The weapon clenched in his hands is aimed directly at the head of the hostage, {g|Encyclopedia:Genetor}Genetor{/g} Ferrenz.{/n}

- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}A few seconds later, the criminal is disarmed and on his knees, pinned down by the guards. Sauerback snarls,{/n} "I will see to his punishment, Lord Captain, unless you would prefer to do it yourself!"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The criminal sneers, glaring at you. Another spasm contorts his face but does not reach his hands: the muzzle of the plasma pistol remains fixed on the Genetor's head. The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} emits a binharic trill.{/n}

- **Gnotec Schwartz**

- **Gnotec Schwartz**
  - Before: "I know the medicae officers are cutting you up too, piece after piece! They will drive you mad, Lord Captain, turn you into a machine. You will see! I have to stop this. Stop the pain." {n}The criminal's eyes lose their focus.{/n}

- **Gnotec Schwartz**

  - After: "These cranial shackles break me. I can't even pray!" {n}His gaze wanders.{/n}
- **Gnotec Schwartz**

  - After: "You're our guiding light..." {n}Pain jolts him.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You hide a hand behind your back and make a subtle movement with your fingers. A shot rings out, and the man in front of you collapses.{/n}
  - After: {n}You signal. A shot; he drops.{/n}
- **Gnotec Schwartz**
  - Before: "All these people are like rust eating away at the bowels of your ship. They must be scraped off, all of them, so they do not spread their iron shackles further. I will help you do this, Lord Captain."
  - After: "They're rust in your ship. Scrape them all off. I'll help."
- **Gnotec Schwartz**
  - Before: {n}The man looks up at you, and you catch a glimpse of surprise behind the grimace of suffering etched into his face. But it does not last. Moments later, the criminal's stare becomes empty once more, hollowed out by unrelenting pain.{/n}

- **Gnotec Schwartz**

But this ain't no saving, Captain, this is torture." {n}The man's face twitches uncontrollably again, and his eyelids flutter.{/n} "These {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FirstChoiceVivisector}cranial shackles{/d} keep me awake, muzzle my thoughts. I feel them tightening every waking moment. I cannot think, I cannot give orders. This dead metal makes me a dead shell, Lord Captain, I know this for sure. And so I have decided to share this death."
  - After: "They said they'd save me. This is torture." {n}He twitches.{/n} "These {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FirstChoiceVivisector}cranial shackles{/d} won't let me sleep or think. Dead metal made me a dead shell. So I'll share this death."

  - Before: "I did. The cranial shackles keep you from sleep, keep you from oblivion, but take a heavy toll. The one who put the iron in me has already gotten his due, though killing the crimson priest is harder. But don't worry, I've got a nice little gun ready for him."{n}The man eagerly points at the weapon with his chin.{/n}

- **Gnotec Schwartz**
  - Before: "Yes, yes, if I remember right — you were there, Lord Captain! You ordered the cranial shackles installed..." {n}The criminal's face twitches more violently than before, and you hear him grinding his teeth.{/n}
  - After: "Yes — you ordered the shackles..." {n}He grinds his teeth.{/n}

  - Before: "Lord Captain! You actually came. Just like you did for my surgery. You are here to relieve my pain." {n}The man's face twitches slightly, as if in a persistent tic, but he forces a smile nonetheless. The area where the implant connects to his head has turned red and oozes blood.{/n}

  - Before: {n}The man looks up at you with a clouded gaze.{/n} "Forgive me, Lord Captain. I cannot take it anymore. I must break free from these shackles."
  - After: {n}Clouded gaze.{/n} "Forgive me. I must break free."
- **Gnotec Schwartz**
  - Before: "I believe you, Lord Captain. You wouldn't allow it. You wouldn't hand your men over to the metal. I believe you." {n}The man's seizure-twisted face relaxes and the weapon slips from his grasp and falls to the floor.{/n}
  - After: "I believe you. You won't hand us to the metal." {n}The weapon drops.{/n}

The visors are the first to show signs of life, flickering erratically.{/n} "I need to go to the operating room immediately. The Martinax life form requires my expertise."

Clutching awkwardly at the floor with his {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g}, he turns to one side and wheezes.{/n} "I need to go... go to the operating room immediately. The Martinax life form requires my expertise."
  - After: "G-gratitude. Omnissiah bless you."{n}Ferrenz rises on his {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g}, wheezing.{/n} "The Martinax life form needs me. To surgery."

  - Before: {n}A glob of plasma misses you by inches, but still singes your hair. Struck by return fire, the man falls flat on his back. As soon as his body hits the floor, the figures around you spring into action, Sauerback barking out orders.{/n}

- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai licks his lips slowly, not moving an inch. He watches Gnotec's every movement and whispers so quietly that you can barely make out his words:{/n} "Pure, unadulterated suffering. Delectable. Give him to me, if you do not kill him first."

- **Gnotec Schwartz**

Augmentation makes Humanity stronger than any phenomenon in nature. Isn't that what the God-Emperor wants us to be?"

Forgive me, but I am not graced with such profound knowledge of the Omnissiah's sacred mechanisms... unlike Genetor Ferrenz." {n}For the first time, a spark of excitement flares in Martinax's voice at the mention of his colleague.{/n} "I am compelled to warn you, however — he may deem it beneath him to touch such dubious and heretical technology."

- **(conversation owner)**

Its loss would rob the Sector Bionica of its soul, Lord Captain. We cannot allow that to happen."
  - After: "No human can join flesh and metal so finely. Losing it would rob the Sector Bionica of its soul."
- **(conversation owner)**

Ferrenz believes that replacing flesh with iron, and receiving the blessing of the Omnissiah, is the privilege of the few. I, on the other hand, make no distinction between servants of the God-Emperor. Every faithful soul deserves a chance to continue working for the glory of Humanity. I'm afraid it's not always easy for Ferrenz and I to find a compromise."
  - After: {n}His tone cracks.{/n} "Yes, we disagree. Ferrenz reserves the Omnissiah's iron for the few. I say every faithful servant deserves it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Of course we get along! It would be unprofessional to involve my personal feelings in our work." {n}Martinax smiles thinly. You get the persistent feeling that he has not told you the whole truth.{/n}

Helping medicae officers with diagnostics, assisting with complex cases."

  - After: "Thank you!" {n}He takes the artefact.{/n}
