## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_DargonusLoop/BombsAlarm/DL_BombsAlarm_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}With a low roar, a wing of Valkyries emerges from over the horizon, hurtling toward the palace like raptors. The air raid siren sounds in time with their appearance. Within seconds, you hear the whistling of bombs as fire rains down from the sky.{/n}
  - After: {n}Valkyries swoop toward the palace as the air raid siren wails. Bombs whistle down.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The absence of an air raid siren suggests that you need not fear any {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g} bombardment of the command headquarters.{/n}
  - After: {n}No siren: no {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g} bombardment of headquarters.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The Valkyrie wing appears in the sky yet again, faultlessly obeying the laws of the time loop. A moment later, the bombardment begins.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Valkyries return, true to the loop. The bombing begins.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The chronometer stops just at the moment when the bombardment of the command headquarters ought to begin. You hear the usual sounds of battle, as well as sentries idly bickering about something or other... but the brass amplifiers of the public address system are silent. It seems there will be no air strike this time around.{/n}
  - After: {n}The chronometer reaches the bombing hour, but the address system stays silent. No air strike this time.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The air defence battery, now {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_DL_Exalt117RepairedTurrels}appeased by Exalt-117{/d}, stirs into action in perfect unison. Each gun fires several bursts, forcing the Valkyries to drop their shells early and retreat, so their strikes land only on the approach to the palace.{/n}
  - After: {n}The battery, {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_DL_Exalt117RepairedTurrels}appeased by Exalt-117{/d}, fires in unison, driving the Valkyries to drop early, short of the palace.{/n}

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_DargonusLoop/CatchJuvenna/DL_CatchJuvenna_dialogue

When he issues the order, his voice sounds calm:{/n} "Seneschal Voigtvir. Deal with this traitor."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_DargonusLoop/DiodasLastStand/DL_DiodasLastStand_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I have gone to great lengths to appear before you, Diodas af Irramon. May I ask you a few questions?"
  - After: "I came far to see you, Diodas af Irramon. May I ask questions?"

  - Before: "Why is the Inquisition moving against the dynasty?"
  - After: "Why is the Inquisition against the dynasty?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I hope, Inquisitor, that your sentence here will be final."
  - After: "I hope your sentence here is final, Inquisitor."

  - After: "We all serve the God-Emperor. Must we bleed senselessly?"

  - After: "Enough words. Let battle begin!"

  - After: "Pleased to serve you, Inquisitor."

- **Juvenna von Valancius**

  - After: "The von Valancius dynasty greets you, Diodas af Irramon, by the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g}'s will. Through {name}'s {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_DL_JuvennaSide}{mf|his|her} efforts{/d}, Seberian stands deposed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Are you trying to make me afraid? I am not permitted to fear. Whatever nets Seberian has set, I will break them. The God-Emperor leads me, and His will is stronger than any snare."
  - After: "I may not fear. His will breaks any snare."
- **Seberian**

I would not call making his acquaintance an honour, but you can decide that for yourself.   - After: {n}Seberian bows courteously.{/n} "Inquisitor. Meet {name}, a {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_DL_LariaSide}servant of my dynasty{/d}. {name}, he leads the enemy. I deny all and repent nothing."
- **Isimond Sauerback**
  - Before: "Today the name Sauerback will {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_DL_IzimondTraitor}ring out alongside{/d} that of von Valancius!"
  - After: "Today Sauerback will {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_DL_IzimondTraitor}ring out alongside{/d} von Valancius!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To refuse your request would show haste in delivering the sentence. But haste is a sign of weak faith.   - After: "Haste shows weak faith. Seberian was condemned when he thought xenos artefacts could serve the Imperium. Speak."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your attempt to delay the inevitable is as obvious as it is ridiculous. I will allow you to speak not because of your title: in the eyes of the God-Emperor, all heretics are equal. I am only giving you this chance so that you may realise for yourselves the futility of your intention."
  - After: "Stalling is futile; all heretics are equal. Speak, and see."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "A strong assertion, which just as strongly indicates one's fervent adherence to a puritan philosophy. This aligns with the limited data available to me regarding Inquisitor af Irramon."
  - After: "Fervent puritanism. Consistent with what I know of af Irramon."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "A prudent approach. The more bureaucratic procedures that precede an execution, the greater the latitude for manoeuvring afforded to the accused. Such efficiency is impressive."
  - After: "Prudent. Less bureaucracy, less room to manoeuvre."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}When you hand Seberian over to the {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g}, you notice that the Lord Captain never once lost his signature poise, even in the face of death. - **Sergeant Zarkov**
  - Before: "Soldiers, to me! Cover His Lordship's flank!"
  - After: "Soldiers! Cover His Lordship's flank!"
- **Exalt-117**

  - After: "Top priority: engaging enemy."
- **Exalt-117**

  - After: "Cannot engage: armament unready. Praying to Omnissiah."

- **Isimond Sauerback**

- **Seberian**

But you will hear no contrition from me, for the truth is on my side."
  - After: "Diodas, you poisoned my daughter! You defy Him, burning knowledge that could serve Humanity. My legacy is gone, but I won't repent. Truth is mine."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Inquisitor draws out a scroll bound with ribbon. The dark wax seal yields easily, and af Irramon unrolls the parchment. Until he arrives at the final lines:{/n} "...let this impious heretic, who bowed down before the xenos abomination, be consigned to the flames. The sentence is binding. The seal is set. For the glory of the God-Emperor."
  - After: {n}The Inquisitor calmly reads a sealed sentence:{/n} "...let this heretic, who bowed to xenos, burn. For the glory of the God-Emperor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You see, there is neither need nor use in repentance, for our faith grants no redemption. But by the grace of the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g}, Seberian will furnish the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanseGlossary}Koronus Expanse{/g} with one final gift. It will serve as a reminder that the more one earns of His blessings, the heavier the burden of responsibility becomes. And for those whose backbone of faith should break under that burden, there is no other way but cleansing with holy fire." {n}The Inquisitor's voice sounds muted and measured, lending weight to every word.{/n}
  - After: "Faith grants no redemption. By the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g}'s grace, Seberian gives the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanseGlossary}Koronus Expanse{/g} a lesson: greater blessings, heavier burdens. The broken burn." {n}Measured.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}You are interrupted by the sound of metallic laughter — erratic and jagged, like a weak vox-signal. And then, just as suddenly, it cuts off.{/n} "Bow my head? I, an anointed steward of the God-Emperor whose servants you proclaim yourselves to be? I, whom you are sworn to obey until your dying breath? When He bestowed upon my ancestors the Warrant of Trade, He distinguished the name of my dynasty and charged it with expanding the borders of His Imperium. Know this: today, you oppose the God-Emperor's will. Today, I name you traitors."
  - After: {n}Jagged metallic laughter.{/n} "Bow? I, His anointed steward? His Warrant of Trade charged my dynasty to expand His Imperium. You defy Him. I name you traitors."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man before you is immediately recognisable as a servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThroneGlossary}Golden Throne{/g}, thanks to his heavy insignia of dull gold. The man is swathed in dark fabric, with a cloak of rough cloth thrown over the top. His face, which is heavily lined but not by the ravages of time, is so unremarkable that it is as if it were a deliberate attempt to make himself forgettable. But his eyes — no one would soon forget those. They are the eyes of someone who stares when others look away. Only someone strong of will or a mindless monster could withstand that penetrating gaze.{/n}
  - After: {n}A servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThroneGlossary}Golden Throne{/g} in dull gold and dark cloth. Forgettable face; unforgettable, piercing eyes.{/n}

- **Player**

  - Before: "Your regiment's a little out of the ordinary, I see..."
  - After: "Unusual regiment..."

  - After: "News of Gaprak reinforcements?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Standing at attention before you — as clumsily as his gawky figure would suggest — is a gangling young fellow, with a neck so long, his head looks like a {g|Encyclopedia:ServoSkulls}servo-skull{/g} floating above his shoulders.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "Yes, {mf|sir|ma'am}. Useless on the ground."

How else would I have got into the {g|Encyclopedia:AstraMilitarumGlossary}Astra Militarum{/g}? My health's not good. But they're not picky in the penal legion. ## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_DargonusLoop/JarubInterrogation/DL_JarubInterrogation_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It all looks so real... but if you listen closely, you cannot hear the thrumming of the hive. Even in the thick of war, it should be audible. Such a masterful reproduction! A question arises unbidden in your mind: would it not be easier to live out these hours in blissful ignorance, just as the others do? After all, with each repetition, your actions would only become more familiar, more practised. As if you were slowly turning into a {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitor{/g}.{/n}
  - After: {n}It looks real, but the hive is silent. Why not live in ignorance like the others, repeating until you become a {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitor{/g}?{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The clerics of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorumGlossary}Adeptus Ministorum{/g} would deem such an act the heresy of oathbreaking, for you would be refusing to continue in the service of the God-Emperor. But in this case, duty does not end even in death.{/n}
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorumGlossary}Adeptus Ministorum{/g} would call it oathbreaking. But duty outlasts death here.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}When the shells fall, you will be the only one not surprised.{/n}
  - After: {n}Only you won't be surprised by the shells.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}Everything is taking place as it should: the attack by the combined forces of the {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g}, and the convening of the council. The pivotal moment approaches, and it will either set you free or condemn you to a new round of torture.{/n}
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g} attacks; the council convenes. Freedom or new torture awaits.{/n}

- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Astounding!" {n}Eogunn does not appear frightened or shocked, but rather utterly captivated. The {g|Encyclopedia:ServoSkulls}servo-skull{/g} Nuncius hovers sedately at his shoulder.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, this is a wholly extraordinary violation of the law of causality. Oh, if only I could discover a machine that could realise such effects!"
  - After: "Astounding!" {n}Eogunn is rapt; the {g|Encyclopedia:ServoSkulls}servo-skull{/g} Nuncius hovers.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, causality violated! If only I had such a machine!"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Hypothesis: the observed reality is a complex optical illusion constructed using perverse xeno knowledge." {n}Pasqal swings a {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrite{/g} at the nearest section of wall, leaving a deep scratch on the stone.{/n} "Replication level: extremely high. The hypothesis does not explain the observed effect of the space-time paradox."
  - After: "Hypothesis: xenos illusion." {n}Pasqal's {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrite{/g} scratches the wall.{/n} "Hypothesis fails to explain the time paradox."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira plunges both hands into her hair, violently tousling it.{/n} "Wrong, this is wrong!" {n}She wraps her arms around her head, swaying slightly.{/n} "They only seem real, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but when you look closer... half are ghosts, and the other half are walking around with their souls cut out. This is a deathtrap, a bad place. We need to get out of here, and take any still alive with us."
  - After: {n}Idira tugs her hair.{/n} "Wrong, this is wrong!" {n}She sways.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, they're ghosts or soulless. A deathtrap. We must leave."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "God-Emperor, fortify our courage against the delusions of the xenos, ignite within us a hatred strong enough to shatter their sorceries!" {n}Argenta prays without pause, shocked by what has occurred.{/n}
  - After: "God-Emperor, let our hatred shatter xenos sorcery!" {n}Argenta prays.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}The Interrogator takes to circling the members of your retinue, scrutinising each one in turn.{/n} "You are all real, there is no doubt. As are my memories of what just happened. Either the devious wretches are playing with our minds, or there is something else at work here that I cannot explain, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}The Interrogator studies the retinue.{/n} "We're real, as are my memories. Mind games, or something I can't explain."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar's thunderous roar shakes the surroundings, trailing off into a low, menacing rumble.{/n} "By the Allfather's steadfast hand, these xenos think to mock us, as if they count themselves the wisest of the wise! When I lay my hands upon them, their skulls shall crack beneath my boots!"
  - After: {n}Ulfar roars.{/n} "By the Allfather, these xenos mock us! I'll crush their skulls!"
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "How can this be...? " {n}The Lady Navigator blinks in puzzlement, her lashes fluttering as she stares dazedly ahead.{/n} "The Sea of Souls is placid, yet the very canvas of the {g|Encyclopedia:Realspace}Materium{/g} has disintegrated and reformed, filling up with other images. I... cannot describe it. It is something strange. Something other."
  - After: "How...?" {n}The Lady Navigator blinks.{/n} "The Sea of Souls is calm, yet the {g|Encyclopedia:Realspace}Materium{/g} broke and reformed. Something other."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "It is a mirage, Domin'{name}." {n}Kibellah digs a long fingernail into her forearm, leaving a bloody furrow in its wake.{/n} "Do not trust your eyes, do not heed your ears. Only will and faith in the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}Undying One{/g} will help you to distinguish what is true from the trickery of the enemies of Humanity."
  - After: "A mirage, Domin'{name}." {n}Kibellah cuts her arm with a nail.{/n} "Trust only faith in the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}Undying One{/g}."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}The Arbitrator freezes, looking around anxiously. His cyber-mastiff rushes forward and stands between you and the rest of the retinue, as if to shield you from a possible attack.{/n} "Xenos machinations, Rogue Trader. I insist on thoroughly scrutinising everyone present before we enter a second time. Anyone capable of such a thing is an incredibly dangerous enemy."
  - After: {n}The Arbitrator's cyber-mastiff guards you.{/n} "Xenos work, Rogue Trader. I'll check everyone before we re-enter."
- **Jae**
  - Before: {n}Jae's ringing laugh startles the rest of the retinue.{/n} "These xenos are right ashmags, aren't they? So, this is how they punish those who stick their noses where they don't belong!" {n}Once she is done laughing, she brushes her dishevelled hair.{/n} "They are in for a great disappointment. We will find a way to escape this place."
  - After: {n}Jae laughs.{/n} "Right ashmags, these xenos! Punishing nosy folk!" {n}She fixes her hair.{/n} "We'll escape anyway."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}One thing is clear: the lies that the devious xenos used to entangle existence must be sundered, and the time loop must be broken. The Lord Captain will not deign to spend any longer in this trap than {mf|he|she} wishes.{/n}
  - After: {n}The time loop must be broken. The Lord Captain leaves when {mf|he|she} chooses.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You and your retinue seem to be the only ones here still in possession of free will. The other captives of this mysterious trap are doomed to repeat the same actions over and over again, forever trapped in the day Dargonus was besieged by {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g} forces.{/n}
  - After: {n}Only your retinue has free will. Everyone else relives the {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g} siege of Dargonus forever.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Stunned, you return to reality. Something inexplicable just happened, and the echoes of it are still coursing through your blood, causing your heart to clench in convulsions. Nevertheless, you are unharmed, and you once again find yourself standing at the gates of your dynasty's palace on Dargonus. There is nothing around you to indicate that what happened to you was real. Nothing but your memories.{/n}
  - After: {n}Stunned but unharmed, you stand at your palace gates on Dargonus. Only memory says it happened.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}No matter how hard you try to dredge your memory for any facts about the siege of Dargonus — surely a major historical event — only the word "Senai" comes to the surface. It seems devoid of any meaning.{/n}
  - After: {n}Of the siege of Dargonus, only the word "Senai" surfaces, meaningless.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}When you share your conclusions with the Seneschal, he nods.{/n} "I agree, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I have had cause to read a good many scrolls from the dynastic archives in the course of my duties, and there was never any mention of Seberian's heretical tendencies."
  - After: {n}The Seneschal nods.{/n} "Agreed, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The archives never mention Seberian's heresy."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard shakes his head with a look of total astonishment.{/n} "It all looks like a grand hoax, Lord Captain. In the time of your glorious ancestor, Dargonus was besieged by the Saynay pirate clan, and he managed to repel their brazen attacks. I have never come across any mention of a conflict with the Inquisition."
  - After: {n}Abelard is astonished.{/n} "A hoax, Lord Captain. Your ancestor repelled the Saynay pirates. No conflict with the Inquisition."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}But of one thing you are certain: you were thrown back to your starting point at the precise moment that your distinguished ancestor, Seberian von Valancius, breathed his last.{/n}
  - After: {n}You were thrown back the moment Seberian von Valancius died.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sentence read out by the Inquisitor to your ancestor still rings in your ears. To find Seberian von Valancius alive mere moments before his execution — what a foul xenos joke. Everything you have seen here seems designed to mock you, including the fact that you are back where you started, as though a disgruntled host had tossed you out the door like unwanted guests.{/n}
  - After: {n}Seberian alive before his execution: a foul xenos joke. And you're tossed back like unwanted guests.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The path is blocked by a military cordon. You stop at a respectful distance, a reasonable response to the rifle muzzles pointed at your chest by way of welcome. Your gaze slides over the faces: their expressions are so eerily similar, they must have been issued along with the uniforms. Serving in the {g|Encyclopedia:AstraMilitarumGlossary}Astra Militarum{/g} brings with it insomnia, a stomach for slaughter, and a touch of hopelessness. You can tell who is in charge even before he speaks, and not by the big fellow's insignia, but by the crushing weight of his stare.{/n}
"Sergeant Branek Zarkov. Whoever you are, my {mf|lord|lady}, I advise you to recognise the present circumstances. And come to the only right decision. This is no place for a stroll."
  - After: {n}Rifles of a {g|Encyclopedia:AstraMilitarumGlossary}Astra Militarum{/g} cordon aim at you. Their leader's stare is crushing.{/n}
"Sergeant Branek Zarkov. My {mf|lord|lady}, this is no place for a stroll."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Did you crawl out of a cave or something? Dargonus is under attack. The enemy claims to be acting in the name of—" {n}The sergeant falters, beads of sweat gathering on his brow. After several painful seconds, he forces himself to continue:{/n} "In the name of the Inquisition. The 32nd has been guarding the gates here for days now." {n}He furrows his bushy eyebrows: your question has rubbed him the wrong way.{/n} "I don't give briefings — that's not why I was deployed here. Move along, before you're mistaken for spies. All expected reinforcements are in the cogitator log — there's nothing there about you." {n}The sergeant nods at a panel nearby.{/n}
  - After: "From a cave? Dargonus is attacked in the name of..." {n}He sweats.{/n} "The Inquisition. The 32nd guards these gates." {n}He frowns.{/n} "Move along. You're not in the reinforcements log." {n}He nods at a panel.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Zarkov nods, lowering his weapon.{/n} "The Seneschal is waiting for you."
  - After: {n}Zarkov lowers his weapon.{/n} "The Seneschal awaits."

  - Before: "Apologies, we didn't recognise you. We thought you weren't coming. I'll let them know you've arrived."
  - After: "Apologies, we didn't expect you. I'll report."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Listen well: shooting madmen is a wretched business, but if I have to do it, I will." {n}The sergeant makes a point of adjusting the heavy weapon on his shoulder, which clanks menacingly.{/n} "Spew your gibberish somewhere else."
  - After: "I'll shoot madmen." {n}His weapon clanks.{/n} "Go elsewhere."

  - Before: "Find me at the back of the inner courtyard. Immediately."
  - After: "Find me at the inner courtyard's back. Now."

  - Before: {n}The soldiers look at each other in confusion. Zarkov reaches for the vox-transmitter. You hear Laria's voice on the other end. Their conversation is short: the sergeant stands guard even over his words.{/n}
  - After: {n}Zarkov briefly voxes Laria.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

All our reinforcements are logged — what use is this {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} otherwise?" {n}The sergeant nods at a nearby panel and speaks into his vox. After a brief exchange of remarks, he barks to you,{/n} "Go on, then. Just don't forget to present yourself to Lady Juvenna, she's waiting to hear news about this Elana of yours."
  - After: "No warning? It's not in the {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}." {n}He voxes, then barks,{/n} "Go. Lady Juvenna awaits news of Elana."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Merovians grab their weapons. Before, their chances of defeating you were slim, but now that you know all their fighting techniques, this will be no more taxing than a genteel hunting party.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Merovians draw weapons. You know their every move.{/n}

  - After: {n}Juvenna listens, then:{/n} "Sergeant, get rid of them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In the name of von Valancius! Soldiers, to arms!"
  - After: "For von Valancius! To arms!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sergeant frowns, but picks up his {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} — and soon hands the transmitter to you. Your apparent knowledge has rattled Juvenna. Gaining her trust will be difficult.{/n}
  - After: {n}The sergeant hands you his {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}. Juvenna is rattled; trust will be hard.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

If something had happened to Lord Seberian or his daughter, I wouldn't be standing here talking to you. We're their shield. The first strike lands on us." {n}The sergeant squares his shoulders as if he is genuinely expecting an attack.{/n}
  - After: "Absurd! We'd never shed von Valancius blood. We're the shield of Seberian and his daughter." {n}He squares up.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sergeant freezes instinctively, as do the soldiers under his command. He stares at you, biting his lip. In the stretching silence, you can practically hear Zarkov's thoughts turning heavily in his head. At last, he breathes a loud sigh.{/n} "Trying to trick me, are you? You want to be taken to His Lordship? That can be arranged. In the proper fashion!"

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_DargonusLoop/NecronDevice/DL_NecronDevice_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Set a melta charge] "It's time to dispose of this xenos filth!"
  - After: [Set a melta charge] "Destroy this xenos filth!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address your companions] "Do you have any insights to offer?"
  - After: [To companions] "Any insights?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Leave the device alone] "We will find another way out."
  - After: [Leave it] "We'll find another way."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}In the crater left by the dropped shell, a sliver of some unknown mechanism peeks through the stone. Dark, solid metal carved with emerald glyphs glints beneath the debris like the exposed innards of a mortally wounded beast. Green shimmers streak ceaselessly across its surface in eerie, perfect sequence, as if every moment the unseen spirits of the xenos device are checking their receptacle and attempting to heal its grievous wounds.{/n}
  - After: {n}In the crater, glyph-carved dark metal pulses green, as if healing itself.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You realise that the fragment you discovered is only a small part of something immeasurably larger. The mechanism extends deep underground, beneath the flawless recreation of the palace bridge, entwined with its very foundations. If this device were disabled, the repercussions of the outage would reverberate throughout the entire structure.{/n}
  - After: {n}It's part of a vast mechanism under the bridge. Disabling it would shake everything.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}This mechanism reeks of antiquity, inhuman precision, and cold menace. Even momentary interference in its operation would seem to be not harmless exploration, but rather an outrage provoking immediate retribution.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ancient and menacing. Tampering invites retribution.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The melta charge adheres to the dark metal with a hollow click. For a moment, the mechanism seems to awaken: a tremor runs through the casing. You arm the charge and make a hasty retreat.{/n}
  - After: {n}The charge clicks on; the casing trembles. You arm it and retreat.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "If I were you, I would find a way to destroy or at least damage this mechanism. I have no desire to be stuck in this trap for the rest of my days."
  - After: "Destroy it. I won't be stuck here forever."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The processing capacity of this unit's cogitator is insufficient to produce a precise prognostic calculation of the consequences. Preliminary hypothesis: deactivation of the xenomechanism will precipitate a localised catastrophe, with zero survivability for all those situated at its epicentre."
  - After: "Hypothesis: deactivation causes local catastrophe. Zero survivability at the epicentre."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira's eyes dart around several times before she speaks:{/n} "A foul business, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, a risky one. They'll notice, they'll know... They will come." {n}A violent shudder runs through the psyker's body.{/n}
  - After: {n}Idira glances around.{/n} "Risky, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. They'll come." {n}She shudders.{/n}
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Why sow empty doubts, Aett-Vater? Burn that abomination and be done with it. And if it angers the xenos, so much the better."
  - After: "Burn it, Aett-Vater. If it angers the xenos, better."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Smashing a big sinister machine to pieces would be a fine bit of fun, shereen!" {n}The Cold Trader grins eagerly.{/n} "But truly, we cannot simply take it with us, can we? Then we can let it fall into no one's hands, including the masters of this place."
  - After: "Smashing it would be fun, shereen!" {n}She grins.{/n} "If we can't take it, no one gets it."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "You require the Ordos' expert assessment to determine the heretical nature of this mechanism?" {n}Heinrix pauses, then exhales and nods.{/n} "This is heresy. Destroy it."
  - After: "You need the Ordos to judge?" {n}Heinrix nods.{/n} "Heresy. Destroy it."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Do not touch that mechanism, elantach, until you grasp its nature and purpose..." {n}Yrliet casts an appraising glance at you.{/n} "...and accept the fact that perhaps that moment will never come."
  - After: "Don't touch it until you understand it, elantach..." {n}Yrliet eyes you.{/n} "...which may be never."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "This place... vexes me. It is long past time for us to tear all of it to pieces. I do not see why we shouldn't begin with that clumsily concealed device."
  - After: "This place vexes me. Tear it apart, starting here."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I believe, Rogue Trader, that in this case we can base our actions on empirical data alone. And also on an intuitive understanding of logical principles, which the laity call 'gut instinct.' This exemplar of xenomachinery is too large and complex to be comprehended in a moment."
  - After: "Trust gut instinct, Rogue Trader. This xenomachine is too complex."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Beneath the ruptured slab, something ancient, immaculate, and alien continues to work.{/n}
  - After: {n}Beneath the slab, something alien keeps working.{/n}

Let my Seneschal decide Camilla's fate — it will be a good lesson in political manoeuvring for Laria."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_DargonusLoop/SecretVox/DL_SecretVox_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I am not Elana. But I am willing to give you the information you need in the name of the God-Emperor."
  - After: "I'm not Elana, but I'll help, for the God-Emperor."

  - Before: "Elana here. Give me a status report."
  - After: "Elana here. Status report."

  - Before: "Why are the servants of the Golden Throne laying siege to Dargonus?"

  - After: "Did Inquisition agents kill Gaprak?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I think I have changed my mind about helping you."
  - After: "I won't help you after all."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}An entire vox-array has been cleverly concealed behind the outer portion of the ferrogranite slab. The level of delicacy required to place the device discreetly in such a place is difficult to fathom.{/n}
  - After: {n}A vox-array, hidden behind the slab.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Servants of the Golden Throne to Elana. Will you report on the movements of Heretic Coryphaeus?" {n}The deep, steady voice of the speaker is almost hypnotising.{/n}
  - After: "Golden Throne to Elana. Report on Heretic Coryphaeus." {n}A hypnotic voice.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A right-minded servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g} amid the xenoheresy flourishing on Dargonus — could it be?"
  - After: "A true servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g} on heretic Dargonus?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Truth is earned through devotion. Now that we are allies, be prepared to listen."
  - After: "Truth is earned. Listen."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}You hear nothing from the vox but white noise.{/n}
  - After: {n}Only white noise.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The vox-station apparatus has been expertly built into the wall, with slim cables and miniature levers that perfectly match the colour of the stone. You can only find it if you know exactly where to look.{/n}
  - After: {n}Built into the wall, matching the stone. Nearly invisible.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You will learn no secrets here. Only the pure truth."
  - After: "Only truth here."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The vox-station is well hidden from unsuspecting eyes, but someone has been using it regularly. The handle of the voice receiver still retains some warmth from whoever held it last.{/n}
  - After: {n}The receiver is still warm.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Servants of the Golden Throne to Elana. We are alarmed by your silence. What is happening in the camp of Heretic Coryphaeus? Report."
  - After: "Golden Throne to Elana. Your silence alarms us. Report."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Such is the fate of any who calls himself the servant of a heretic. His army fell to the onslaught of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptaSororitasGlossary}Sisters of Battle{/g}, guided by Elana's wisdom. It does not matter what house they belonged to. We do not fight against humans — we fight for humanity."
  - After: "A heretic's servant's fate. The {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptaSororitasGlossary}Sisters of Battle{/g}, guided by Elana, crushed his army. We fight for humanity."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: "Servants of the Golden Throne to Palatine. The battle is near. Gather your units at the traitor's gates."
  - After: "Golden Throne to Palatine. Gather at the traitor's gates."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: "Servants of the Golden Throne to Elana. Respond immediately. Lack of communication will be construed as aiding the Heretic Coryphaeus due to cowardice and a dereliction of your sacred duty to Humanity."
{n}The vox-frequency does not fully convey the tone of voice, but the speaker is definitely anxious.{/n}
  - After: "Golden Throne to Elana. Respond, or be deemed a heretic's accomplice."
{n}An anxious voice.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The vox-array is silent: the speaker grilles are tightly encased in noise-dampening material.{/n}
  - After: {n}The speakers are muffled.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The vox-station looks well-maintained: you do not see even a speck of dust on the surface.{/n}
  - After: {n}Spotless.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}This device was made by private commission, surely violating about a dozen tenets of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g}. Its owner is staggeringly rich and has one foot outside the law.{/n}
  - After: {n}Custom-made against {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} tenets, for someone rich and lawless.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}Whether such technology is the work of Humanity, you cannot say for certain.{/n}
  - After: {n}You can't tell if Humanity made this.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The device housing has been made with exquisite skill — it fits perfectly into the niche, leaving almost no gap between itself and the stone. The internal workings and cables are neatly tucked away, like snakes lurking in the dark.{/n}
  - After: {n}Exquisitely made, fitted flush.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}A familiar sequence of numbers draws your eye. Few in the Expanse would recognise this combination, but you are one of them: this frequency belongs to the band used by the {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g}.{/n}
  - After: {n}You recognise the {g|Encyclopedia:InquisitionGlossary}Inquisition{/g}'s frequency band.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Numbers and symbols dance before your eyes: someone was using this device to communicate on many different waves, but none of these frequencies is familiar to you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Many frequencies, none familiar.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The God-Emperor looks favourably on the submission of the doomed. But why should we believe you?"
  - After: "Why should we believe you?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "First, you dare to call yourself a Gaprak, and now you don the mask of righteousness? No matter how many you put on, He sees through you."
  - After: "A Gaprak, now righteous? He sees through every mask."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You have changed your mind? How ingenious and inconspicuous is heresy. Should you think to oppose the envoys of the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThroneGlossary}Golden Throne{/g}, even once, then there is no way back. You are already dead, my fickle interlocutor." {n}A click signals the disconnection of the vox-transmission.{/n}
  - After: "Oppose the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThroneGlossary}Golden Throne{/g} once and you're dead." {n}Click.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your interlocutor is silent for a long time, then sighs:{/n} "Poverty of intellect is one of the supreme virtues. However, it seems you cannot claim to possess it. Speak the truth."
  - After: {n}A sigh.{/n} "You're not that stupid. Speak the truth."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_DargonusLoop/SoBVox/DL_SoBVox_dialogue

  - After: "{name} to servants of the Golden Throne! I have a report too."

  - After: "You'll bring me in, Elana. Or should I say... Juvenna?"

  - After: "No forgiveness for those who betrayed the von Valancius dynasty."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have changed my mind."
  - After: "I've changed my mind."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Elana to servants of the Golden Throne. Coordinates to strike the command headquarters: Four-Xi, Rho-Sigma. Do not target the outpost again: it is not significant."
  - After: "Elana to Golden Throne. Hit headquarters: Four-Xi, Rho-Sigma."
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "...No reinforcements. Coryphaeus is in the courtyard."

It seems the Gaprak forces were eliminated by this "Elana," and now she is relaying coordinates for an orbital strike on the command headquarters.{/n}
  - After: {n}So "Elana" killed the Gaprak army and scion, and now targets headquarters.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Elana the Unshaken is a Calixian saint who died many hundreds of cycles ago. This call sign cannot have been chosen by chance.{/n}
  - After: {n}Elana the Unshaken: a Calixian saint.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You hear a male voice, but you detect no trace of human feeling in it.{/n}
"You are absolutely right, lost child. Seberian has betrayed his dynasty, and the God-Emperor has already passed judgement on him. He should expect no mercy, and neither should you."
  - After: {n}A cold voice.{/n}
"Seberian betrayed his dynasty. No mercy, for him or you."
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The hissing that reaches your ears coalesces into the barely discernible words of a vox-transmission. The source of the sound is a {g|Encyclopedia:CommBead}vox-bead{/g}, tucked behind the bloody ear of a fallen {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptaSororitas}Sister of Battle{/g}.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The God-Emperor punishes! End transmission."
  - After: "The God-Emperor punishes! End."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A deep and even voice answers you. The kind of voice that could calm even an angry {g|Encyclopedia:Grox}grox{/g}.{/n} "Tell me, servant of the Imperium, what drives your desire to help us?"

- **(conversation owner)**

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_DargonusLoop/TrazynFirstMeet/DL_TrazynFirstMeet_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Trazyn the Infinite, I am {name} von Valancius, and I have come for my ancestor."
  - After: "Trazyn the Infinite, I am {name} von Valancius. I've come for my ancestor."

  - Before: "I will not let you imprison us both!"
  - After: "You won't imprison us both!"

  - Before: "We have destroyed your foul trap, xenos!"
  - After: "We destroyed your foul trap, xenos!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "Death to the enemies of Humanity! Death to the enemies of von Valancius!"
  - After: [Attack] "Death to the enemies of Humanity and von Valancius!"

  - After: [Hold your weapon at the ready] "Kneel and beg, xenos!"

  - After: "Why imprison the von Valancius ancestor here?"

  - Before: "I seem to have spoiled your plans. What now?"
  - After: "I've spoiled your plans. What now?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The metal giant, draped in a weighty mantle and holding a sinister-looking staff, turns his head slowly, surveying the palace of Dargonus. You see no hint of emotion in the unmoving mask that rests in place of the {g|Encyclopedia:XenosGlossary}xenos{/g}'s face, but in his unnatural voice, however, there is a clear note of vexation.{/n}
  - After: {n}A metal giant with a sinister staff surveys the palace. His {g|Encyclopedia:XenosGlossary}xenos{/g} voice is vexed.{/n}

  - Before: "A clutch of vermin. Stowed away inside an exhibit, spoiling my masterpiece. And now I am compelled to appear here, on the half-forgotten fringes of the galaxy? Well done — you have succeeded in drawing upon yourselves the gaze of Trazyn the Infinite, master of the Museion you worthless pests invaded." {n}Caustic laughter scrapes its way out of the mask like metal against glass.{/n}
  - After: "Vermin in my exhibit, spoiling my masterpiece. You face Trazyn the Infinite, master of the Museion you invaded." {n}Grating laughter.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your emotions riot within you, only growing in strength as they fail to find an outlet — in a shout, a movement, even a grimace. All you can hope is that your ability to feel will be exhausted before you lose consciousness from the strain.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your emotions rage with no outlet, not even a grimace.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

Curious determination and lack of foresight... then again, perhaps you had no notion of what you were getting into."
  - After: {n}His ancient gaze weighs on you.{/n} "Reaching here sets you apart. Determined, yet foolish."
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "Not your decision. However..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Destroyed? Hardly. You have merely disrupted the hypergeometric logic of the labyrinth with your unruly antics, nothing more." {n}The xenos's voice acquires a sardonic note.{/n} "But don't let that detail spoil your little celebration — it is still a most impressive feat for a member of a primitive species."
  - After: "Destroyed? You merely disrupted the labyrinth's logic." {n}Sardonic.{/n} "Impressive, for a primitive."
- **(conversation owner)**

The path for those in this place is determined by me alone — all the more so now that your actions have forced me to come here in person."
  - After: "Primitives deny their powerlessness. I alone decide your path here, now that you've made me come."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The muscles in your eyes refuse to obey you, just like the rest of your body. However, there is little chance that anything in your surroundings could help you in your present predicament.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your eyes won't move.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The world around you is frozen — the people, mechanisms, even the very breeze, absolutely everything has stopped, transfixed in eerie poses. You blink — and a wave passes over the world like static on an ancient {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} screen. The only creatures spared this strange stasis are your retinue and Seberian.{/n}
  - After: {n}Everything is frozen, flickering like {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} static. Only your retinue and Seberian are spared.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian seems to jerk awake and draws himself up straight, the movement accompanied by the piercing sound of dozens of ancient implants. With a burst of florid profanity, the Rogue Trader draws his weapon and rushes forward. In response, the xenos raises his hand and, without looking, lazily snaps his fingers.{/n}
  - After: {n}Seberian charges, cursing. Without looking, the xenos snaps his fingers.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Seberian stares ahead, dumbstruck, helpless to fend off the realisation crashing over him. The light of his cybernetic eye stutters, as though even his augmetics are breaking under the weight bearing down upon them.{/n}
  - After: {n}Seberian stares, crushed by the realisation; his eye flickers.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your body is in some kind of trap, but like none you have ever experienced. There is nothing restraining you, nothing confining you — and yet you cannot move a muscle. When you realise that your heart and lungs are also frozen, animal terror seizes you. The xenos has not only paused your body, but your very life.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nothing binds you, yet you can't move — not even your heart or lungs. He has paused your life.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}As though woken by your shout, Seberian raises his weapon with the roar of a wounded beast and rushes forward. But your all-out charge provokes no fear or even disquiet in the xenos. With his attention elsewhere, he absent-mindedly raises his hand and snaps his fingers.{/n}
  - After: {n}Seberian charges, roaring. The xenos idly snaps his fingers.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian's face — the part of it that remains — is frozen in a grimace. You are not even sure that the Rogue Trader still breathes — it is as if the xenos has stopped time for him.{/n}
  - After: {n}Seberian is frozen mid-grimace, time stopped for him.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}This attempted display of your indomitable spirit is an instant failure — your eye muscles are completely immobile, just like the rest of your body.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your eyes won't move; the glare fails.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You cannot look sideways at Seberian — your eye muscles are frozen, as is the rest of your body. The fate of your ancestor remains a mystery to you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your eyes are frozen; you can't see Seberian.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I do appreciate a rapt audience. Yet it is time to bring this encounter to a close."
  - After: "I enjoy a rapt audience. But we're done."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Hmm..." {n}Trazyn gives you and your weapon a cursory look.{/n} "A typical specimen of your kind — your ability to draw even the simplest logical conclusions is limited. I will simplify the terms so that you might understand: do you wish for the same treatment your fellow received?"
  - After: "Hmm..." {n}Trazyn glances at your weapon.{/n} "Simply put: want your fellow's fate?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your will, forged in the countless trials of the Rogue Trader's path, remains utterly powerless against the xenos enchantments shackling your body.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your will is powerless against the xenos's hold.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your lungs refuse to obey, no matter how hard you try to bring them back under your control. Your lips remain frozen, sealed shut by an unknown force.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your lungs and lips won't obey.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The xenos's head turns slightly toward Seberian.{/n} "The little thief. Dared to steal from the Preserver of Histories, and now causing trouble again. What is this, some foolhardy rescue attempt? So, your worthless name is still recalled by one of your short-lived kind?"
  - After: {n}He turns to Seberian.{/n} "The little thief who robbed the Preserver of Histories. Someone still remembers your name?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "An interesting choice of words — 'death to the enemies of von Valancius.' So you are indeed of Seberian's bloodline. Whether it was a naive desire to save him or a similar propensity for avarice that led you to follow your ancestor's trail, I do not know, but I'm sure you won't object if I explain how he — and now you — came to be here."
  - After: "'Enemies of von Valancius' — so you're Seberian's blood. Rescue or greed, let me explain how he, and you, came here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Now..." {n}Trazyn raises his hand in an impassioned gesture and pauses theatrically.{/n} "...get out of my Museion."
  - After: "Now..." {n}Trazyn raises a hand theatrically.{/n} "...get out of my Museion."

  - Before: {n}Covered in dust and blood, the Zarkovian soldiers crowd around Seberian, quietly talking to each other.   - After: "Here we part. We may meet again, God-Emperor willing. If not," {n}he bows.{/n} "Farewell."

  - Before: "You are in no need of instruction from me, {name}. I've been observing you, and I have to admit that I have nothing to teach you. You have made mistakes — but so did I. My presence at your side would only stir up those who wish you ill, thus weakening the dynasty — and that's not what I want for the protectorate."
  - After: "I've nothing to teach you, {name}. Beside you, I'd only weaken the dynasty."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I do not share your views on ruling the protectorate, but history will sort everything out."
  - After: "I disagree with your rule, but history will judge."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Many years ago, when I took the Crimson Dance of Khaine out of that crypt, I attracted the attention of an abominable xenos. It's only fair that the sword that started this conflict should put a long-overdue end to it as well. There is a pattern to it, don't you think? As though this was destined to happen."
  - After: "Taking the Crimson Dance of Khaine drew this xenos upon us. So I will find the Crimson Dance of Khaine, {name}, and end it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Let us face the truth, {name}." {n}Seberian extends a hand and clenches and then unclenches his metal fist.{/n} "I'm no longer as agile as I was in the days of my youth — not that I avoided grievous wounds even then. Look around you: we are in enemy territory, and the enemy is laying wicked schemes against us. To believe ourselves invulnerable to their cunning would be an admission of our own foolishness. But I am no fool, {name}. And I do not think you are either."
  - After: "Face the truth, {name}." {n}He clenches his metal fist.{/n} "I'm old, deep in enemy land. I'm no fool, {name}. Nor are you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No, it does not." {n}Seberian shakes his head sadly, yet you read something that looks like warmth in his eyes.{/n} "But I am grateful for your words. Do not think it has escaped my notice how the Koronus Expanse has changed. All that I knew and valued has been lost."
  - After: "No, it does not." {n}Warmth shows in his eyes.{/n} "But thank you. All I knew is lost."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I do not belong in this time. I want but one final thing, and that is to discontinue this accursed cycle. It is my gift to the protectorate, {name}. The only one this decrepit body of mine can give."
  - After: "I am a relic of the past." {n}His voice turns sorrowful.{/n} "I want only to end this accursed cycle. My last gift to the protectorate, {name}."

  - Before: {n}The vox-synthesiser makes a mocking trill.{/n} "You are a dreamer, {name}, and that is what I like about you. Your aspirations know no limits. Carry it proudly, for you are a worthy heir of House von Valancius. Bring greatness to our protectorate — for us both."
  - After: {n}The vox-synthesiser trills.{/n} "A dreamer, {name}. You won't sway me. Take my dream of the stars instead, worthy heir of House von Valancius."
- **(conversation owner)**

I can never be like you and accept rule by bureaucrats."
  - After: "The world belongs to paper-pushers now." {n}He looks past you, tired.{/n} "You fit. I never will."

Only a single mistake stands between me and oblivion, and once I correct it, I may lay myself to rest.   - After: "One mistake remains. Once I correct it, I may rest, perhaps at the God-Emperor's side."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "So I will find the Crimson Dance of Khaine, and together we will vanquish the xenos." {n}Seberian raises a hand and clenches his fist, as though the detested blade were already in his grasp.{/n}
  - After: "I will find the Crimson Dance of Khaine, and together we will vanquish the xenos." {n}He clenches his fist.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My dream was to reach parts of the void yet unexplored by humanity, to know their terror — and their grandeur." {n}He pauses for a moment, fascinated by the image in his mind's eye.{/n} "But it is only a dream, one that may never be fulfilled."
  - After: "I dreamed of the unexplored void." {n}He pauses.{/n} "It may stay a dream."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You will understand someday, my heir. When centuries of your life have gone by, and every decision you ever made is a heavy burden upon your shoulders. When you begin to feel like a relic of the past, remember my words: sometimes a withered old branch should be pruned to keep the tree healthy. The dynasty before everything, {name}."
  - After: "You'll understand in centuries, my heir. A withered branch must be pruned. The dynasty before everything, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I will set out to search for the sword. In the meantime, you must find a way to get to Trazyn.   - After: "I'll find the sword; you reach Trazyn. The augurs have our meeting point. If I'm late, go on."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But, if my daughter is alive, in whatever state the abominable xenos's captivity may have left her, I will take her with me to the cold stars." {n}Seberian breaks off.{/n} "But hope is a foolish sentiment, {name}."
  - After: "If my daughter lives, I'll take her with me to the stars." {n}He stops.{/n} "But hope is foolish, {name}."

  - Before: "Good point." {n}Seberian turns to the soldiers.{/n} "Soldiers of Zarkov! I, Seberian von Valancius, call on you to follow me! Do your duty and crush every enemy in your path! For House von Valancius!"

  - After: My sight returned: we were in the bombed-out Museion, near the thief of the {g|Encyclopedia:WarrantGlossary}Sacred Warrant{/g}. My heir had reached it, {mf|himself|herself} unharmed.

  - Before: With a crash and a roar, the world fell back into place. There was no doubt we were in the Museion, and the sight of its solemn halls destroyed by orbital bombardment filled my heart with vengeful joy. That joy, it turned out, was somewhat premature.
No sooner did we stir from our spots than sinister glyphs began to glimmer along the entire perimeter of the hall. The xenos had obviously made thorough preparations for this meeting.
  - After: The world returned. We were in the bombed-out Museion. My joy was premature.
Glyphs glimmered around the hall. The xenos had prepared.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: At the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTraderGlossary}Rogue Trader{/g}'s command, the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} servants accompanying the squad released a swarm of servo-skulls into the air. Guided by binharic hymns, their {g|Encyclopedia:Auspex}auspexes{/g} unerringly detected usable points of entry.
  - After: At the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTraderGlossary}Rogue Trader{/g}'s command, the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicusGlossary}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} released servo-skulls whose {g|Encyclopedia:Auspex}auspexes{/g} found entry points.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: We were exhausted and wounded but not broken, not even by our encounter with the faceless horrors of the catacombs. We remained determined to exact vengeance on Trazyn for every outrage perpetrated against House von Valancius.
  - After: Wounded but unbroken, we would avenge every outrage against House von Valancius.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Zarkovian soldiers faced the enemy with grim and stoic determination, not even a muscle twitching on their faces. A barrage of shots rained down on the oncoming xenos swarm, but the squad's firepower was not enough. Finding no resistance worthy of the name, the Necrons charged silently forward, eliminating the defenders with merciless efficiency.
  - After: The Zarkovians fired stoically, but the Necrons cut them down with merciless efficiency.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The platforms that carried us upward had already drawn level with the gates leading into the galleries of the Museion's lower floors when a terrible blow shook the crypt to its foundation. Another of the flagship's artillery strikes had hit the planet's surface not far from us, and the accursed pyramid proved insufficiently sturdy to withstand it. The last thing I saw was cracks running along its surface, filling with a poisonous green glow. Then an unbearably bright light flooded everything, and I was temporarily blinded.
  - After: Near the galleries' gates, an orbital strike cracked the pyramid. Green light flared, and I was blinded.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Izdrig's guttural roar, full of fury and contempt for the enemy, thundered like an exploding krak grenade. Hearing it jolted the Zarkovians out of their stupor at once. One after another, the soldiers jumped to their feet, clenching their teeth and wiping off the blood that seeped from their ears. They picked up and carried those who could no longer walk. The stoicism of the generations who had survived in the badlands of a frontier world for centuries had imbued them with an unshakeable resistance to fear.
  - After: Izdrig's roar jolted the Zarkovians. They rose, bleeding, carrying the fallen. Frontier life had made them fearless.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Warrant was there, somewhere ahead, along with the one who'd had the audacity to steal it. And we, the Rogue Traders of House von Valancius, were prepared to do anything to reclaim what had been granted to us by the God-Emperor Himself.
  - After: The Warrant and its thief lay ahead. House von Valancius would reclaim the God-Emperor's gift.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: My heir gave the order just in time, and everyone froze in perfect obedience to {mf|his|her} will. Rapid signals in {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Lingua-Technis{/g} sounded as the Tech-Priests in the rearguard advanced slowly, raising their plasma guns.
  - After: Everyone froze at my heir's order, obeying {mf|his|her} will. The Tech-Priests signalled in {g|Encyclopedia:LinguaTechnis}Lingua-Technis{/g}, raising plasma guns.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The scout's death was but the first of many, as the soldiers following him did not fall back in time. Their blood turned the black stone under our feet a rusty scarlet. Only a salvo from the plasma guns of the flagship's Tech-Priests, who were marching in the rear, made everyone freeze in place.
  - After: More soldiers died before a plasma salvo from the Tech-Priests made everyone freeze.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The battle was long. The humans fought to the last, though exhausted by the enemy's incredible might. At the cost of their lives, the soldiers dealt with the vanguard, but countless more xenos were emerging from the corridors. My heir ordered a retreat, and the sappers collapsed the passage behind us with melta charges to hold back the enemy and win us time.
  - After: The soldiers died killing the vanguard, but more came. My heir ordered a retreat; sappers collapsed the passage behind us.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Through a glowing green haze, I saw {name} struggle to {mf|his|her} feet, forcing {mf|himself|herself} to resist the pressure of the monstrous sound with a superhuman effort of the will. Alas, only a few mustered the strength to follow {mf|him|her}, the rest still paralysed by the terror that had drained the last of their strength.
  - After: Through green haze, {name} forced {mf|himself|herself} to {mf|his|her} feet. Few followed {mf|him|her}.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: For a moment, the sheer desperation in Vedka's sonorous voice overcame even the crypt's deadly dirge. Hearing it jolted the Zarkovians out of their stupor at once. One after another, the soldiers jumped to their feet, clenching their teeth and wiping off the blood that seeped from their ears. They picked up and carried those who could no longer walk. The stoicism of the generations who had survived in the badlands of a frontier world for centuries had imbued them with an unshakeable resistance to fear.
  - After: Vedka's desperate voice cut through the dirge. The Zarkovians rose, bleeding, carrying the fallen. Frontier life had made them fearless.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: I said those words over and over, until it dawned on me with horrifying clarity that the Museion's cursed air was preventing the humans from hearing a single word as it sapped their will to live. Living flesh was no match for the ancient terror brought forth by the maddened dead creatures of metal.
  - After: I kept shouting until I realised the cursed air drowned my words and sapped their will.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The deathly cold that grew more intense as we delved deeper into the pit was a terrifying trial for every one of us. It felt like the bone-chilling breath of death itself. It was only thanks to the soldiers' brutal training and rigorous discipline that we avoided unnecessary casualties.
  - After: The cold deepened as we descended. Only discipline spared us losses.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Yet the wisdom of the God-Emperor was still with me. The vox-augment that had replaced my throat amplified my voice a hundredfold, letting it drown out the crypt's dirge. My heir was the first to hear my call — and {mf|he|she} found the strength to rise to it. Others followed, inspired by {mf|his|her} example.
  - After: My vox-augment drowned out the dirge. My heir heard and rose; others followed {mf|his|her} lead, and {mf|he|she} found strength.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Yet the wisdom of the God-Emperor was still with me. The vox-augment that had replaced my throat amplified my voice a hundredfold, letting it drown out the crypt's dirge — but it was not enough. Alas, only a few mustered the strength to rally, with the rest still paralysed by the terror that had drained the last of their strength and snuffed out all hope for salvation.
  - After: My vox-augment drowned out the dirge, but too few rallied; the rest stayed paralysed.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Electric flashes, like the wrath of the God-Emperor Himself, pierced the air, shielding the humans from the death-bringing xenos. One after another, the servants of the Omnissiah fell, spilling blood and sacred unguent, and reciting binharic litanies filled with righteous anger until their last moments. Their deaths granted us the precious seconds we needed to reach the soaring platforms.
  - After: Tech-Priests' electric flashes shielded us. They fell one by one, buying the seconds we needed to reach the platforms.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Electric flashes, like the wrath of the God-Emperor Himself, pierced the air, shielding the humans from the death-bringing xenos. One after another, the servants of the Omnissiah fell, spilling blood and sacred unguent, but they were too few. A number of the xenos were struck down, only for the rest to advance their onslaught, treading on the bodies of the dying Tech-Priests. Only a handful survived from the squad — yet, defying fate and thwarting our monstrously powerful enemy, my scion and I were unharmed.
  - After: Tech-Priests' electric flashes shielded us, but the xenos trampled them. A handful survived; my scion and I were unharmed.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Guardsmen charged at the enemy, the battle cry of "Atonement for the one!" on their lips. Distant descendants of the penal legionnaires of Merov, the Zarkovians fought with all the fervour and ferocity of their progenitors, consumed by a holy hatred of the xenos. They unleashed the fury of the doomed upon the Necrons, and were able to hold them off just long enough for my scion and I to reach the platforms.
  - After: Crying "Atonement for the one!", the Zarkovians, heirs of Merov's penal legions, held the Necrons until we reached the platforms.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The descent was long and arduous. Many of the soldiers succumbed to the icy darkness they faced in the bowels of this Tomb World. The unbearable cold, emanating from the very walls of the place, sapped them; their strength spent, they unclenched their fingers and plummeted. Dark oblivion claimed their bodies forever.
  - After: The Tomb World's cold sapped many soldiers until they let go and fell into the dark.

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Finally, one of the creature's limbs extends in a lofty gesture, after which perfectly intelligible words in Low Gothic pour forth from the narrow slit that crosses its face where its mouth is:{/n} "I offer my greetings to you in the galleries of the Great Museion, visitor." {n}The xenos's pronunciation and word stress are flawless, but the tone is devoid of humanity.{/n}

  - Before: "A pejorative definition is semantically inappropriate in your utterance, primitive creature." {n}The metal plate replacing the xenos's face shows no emotion, but you read displeasure in the movements of his many limbs.{/n} "You have indeed beheld the Warden to whom the Infinite has entrusted the protection of the outer gates of the Museion."
  - After: "'Thing' is inappropriate, primitive." {n}He bristles.{/n} "You saw the Warden of the outer gates."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am Chronomancer Amatekh the Faithful, vassal of the Nihilakh dynasty, one of the Wardens of the Museion." {n}He gives you an indifferent look, yet you can still feel the contempt it carries.{/n} "It is my duty to maintain the exhibits to the fullest extent possible, safeguarding them from encroachment."
  - After: "Chronomancer Amatekh the Faithful, of the Nihilakh dynasty, Warden of the Museion." {n}Contempt.{/n} "I guard the exhibits."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This vault of rarities belongs to Trazyn the Infinite, Preserver of Histories, Archeovist of the Solemnace Galleries. A multitude of historical artefacts that have been deemed worthy of the Overlord's attention are gathered here at his will. The hall you see now contains remarkable artefacts from the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanseGlossary}Koronus Expanse{/g}."
  - After: "The vault of Trazyn the Infinite, Preserver of Histories. This hall holds relics of the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanseGlossary}Koronus Expanse{/g}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Necron subtly steps back, holding out a skeletonised hand clutching a staff.{/n} "Visitor, you show a lack of reverence for Lord Trazyn and his collection... which is to be expected from a member of an inferior race. As Warden, it is my duty to block the path of anyone who might damage the exhibits."
  - After: {n}He raises his staff.{/n} "Inferiors lack reverence. I bar any who might harm the exhibits."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Necron says nothing, in no hurry to dignify you with further conversation.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Necron says nothing.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

There is nothing here that belongs to you or your {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g}, and that is an inviolable truth." {n}The tip of the Warden's staff points straight at your chest, casting a menacing glow.{/n} "Any attempts to dispute this truth will result in your annihilation."
  - After: "Nothing here is yours or your {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g}'s." {n}His staff glows.{/n} "Dispute it and die."

  - Before: {n}The Necron holds out a hand with a staff clutched in it in front of him, more warning than threatening.{/n} "Visitor, you are of an inferior race. As Warden, it is my duty to bar entry to any who might damage the exhibits."

'Ashes at the Feet of the Imperium,' 'Stripped of Trophies,' 'Cleansed by Fire'... and 'Witness to the Power of the Holy Throne'!" {n}The Sister of Battle grips her weapon with such force, as though she were holding back a ferocious dog lunging toward prey.{/n}

It is located just beyond the historical diorama in the centre of the room, the one dedicated to the primitive who once stole that same object." {n}The polyhedrons hovering above the Chronomancer's head shimmer and rotate to the rhythm of his measured speech.{/n}

  - After: "Curse Trazyn." {n}He straightens.{/n} "What do I do, {name}? I cannot leave my daughter. But..." {n}He falls silent.{/n}

  - Before: {n}It is astonishing that the grievous injuries inflicted by the tormentors did not kill Laria instantly. The cruelty with which her body has been mutilated is horrifying. Most of her bones are broken, her torso has been flayed alive, and each of her vital organs bears crudely inflicted lacerations. What was done to her was not torture but slow execution. Even the most skilled medicae could not save her here and now.{/n}
  - After: {n}Bones broken, torso flayed, organs slashed: a slow execution. No medicae could save her here.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}When you touch the endless bloody wound that the entirety of Laria's body below the neck has become, she makes a muffled groan through her teeth, and for a few seconds her breathing stops. It seems the pain from the torture alone is so intense that any examination could bring about instant death from shock. Yet life still flickers within her, which means a chance to save her remains, however faint.{/n}
  - After: {n}At your touch her breathing stops briefly. She could die of shock, yet a faint chance remains.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn sets to his examination with focused intensity. His {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g} rise into the air, bristling with countless {g|Encyclopedia:Auspex}auspexes{/g}, injectors, and vials. Injector needles plunge into Laria's gaping wounds, and her breathing eases slightly.{/n} "I regret to say this, Rogue Trader, but I am powerless here. All I can do is ease the patient's final moments before she passes into oblivion. My skills are sufficient to replace damaged organs with Ferrum Sanctum, but this is simply impossible in field conditions."
  - After: {n}Eogunn's {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:Auspex}auspexes{/g} set to work.{/n} "I am powerless, Rogue Trader. Replacing her organs with Ferrum Sanctum is impossible in the field. I can only ease her end."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Murmuring a short prayer under his breath, Abelard opens his chirurgeon's kit and bends over the prone figure, but after a minute he shakes his head sharply.{/n} "Forgive me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but all my experience is not enough to help with such wounds. A whole host of chirurgeons and their assistants would be needed to heal these injuries. All we can do is pray to the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g} that He grant Laria a dignified death."
  - After: {n}Abelard examines her, then shakes his head.{/n} "Forgive me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We can only pray the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g} grants her a dignified death."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Don't try to give me false hopes, my heir. Evacuation is impossible, you know this as well as I." {n}A surge of the Motive Force flashes in Seberian's bionic eye and a drop of machine oil seeps from the juncture where the Ferrum Sanctum meets living flesh.{/n} "Futile efforts only hasten the inevitable." {n}He steps toward Laria and gently lifts her.{/n}
  - After: "No false hopes, my heir. Evacuation is impossible." {n}Oil seeps from his bionics.{/n} {n}He lifts Laria.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Laria's voice grows weaker and quieter with each passing second.{/n} "I dreamed for so long of escaping the clutches of that filth. Five centuries... of captivity. And now, at last, that moment has come." {n}Her voice drops to a barely audible whisper.{/n} "I am journeying to the cold stars, Father. Together with you." {n}The last spark of life leaves the wounded woman's eyes. In complete silence, Seberian reaches out his hand and closes the eyelids on his daughter's still face.{/n}
  - After: {n}Laria weakens.{/n} "Five centuries of captivity... and at last I'm free." {n}A whisper.{/n} "I journey to the cold stars, Father. With you." {n}She dies. Seberian closes her eyes.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian gently lifts the wounded woman, gazing into the gaunt face of his daughter.{/n} "Then I wish to bid her farewell, {name}."
  - After: {n}Seberian lifts his daughter.{/n} "Then let me bid her farewell, {name}."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Wait!" {n}But contrary to his command, Seberian hesitates, gazing helplessly at his daughter.{/n} "Grant me a few moments to bid farewell, {name}! Oh, how cruel the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g} is in His mercy, and how negligent in His protection..."
  - After: "Wait!" {n}Seberian hesitates.{/n} "Let me say farewell, {name}! How cruel the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}God-Emperor{/g}'s mercy is..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Laria meets death with a smile of relief and gratitude. Seberian, standing beside you, turns away but does not hinder the Emperor's Mercy that you bestow.{/n}
  - After: {n}Laria dies smiling. Seberian turns away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I can't go on, Father." {n}Laria looks not at you, but at Seberian.{/n} "Allow me to die with dignity." {n}She extends her hand, positioning it beneath the injector, and closes her eyes.{/n}
  - After: "I can't go on, Father. Let me die with dignity." {n}She offers her arm{/n} {n}and closes her eyes.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian watches in silence as his daughter loses consciousness, stupefied by the potent medicaments. A surge of the Motive Force flashes in his bionic eye, and a drop of machine oil seeps from the juncture where the Ferrum Sanctum meets living flesh.{/n}
  - After: {n}Seberian silently watches her slip away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The blood instantly soaks through the bandages, staining them a deep crimson. Contrary to expectation, the bleeding does not stop — the viscous fluid continues to ooze from beneath the dressings. Laria pushes your hand aside.{/n} "Leave it. Save the medicae supplies for your people. Wasting them on me is... pointless."
  - After: {n}Blood soaks the bandages. Laria pushes your hand away.{/n} "Leave it. Save the supplies."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Long moments pass before Seberian moves again. A rough, almost growling, command issues from the vox-grille:{/n} "Arch-Militant, soldiers, remain here and secure our rear. Follow me, my heir. It is time for the foul xenos Trazyn to answer for the wicked schemes he has wrought against our house."
  - After: {n}Seberian growls through his vox-grille:{/n} "Arch-Militant, hold our rear. Follow me, my heir. Trazyn will answer for his schemes against our house."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_Exhibition/EldarExhibitionTrazynOverview/EX_EldarExhibitionTrazynOverview_dialogue

  - After: [Inspect the empty pedestal]

  - Before: {n}Cassia stares at the empty podium, struggling to see what the vision just described.{/n} "But..." {n}she trails off, lapsing into confused silence.{/n}

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_Exhibition/ImperiumExhibitionTrazynOverview/EX_ImperiumExhibitionTrazynOverview_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A young and primitive civilisation, diligently exploring the region for the past several centuries. Rarely do they achieve anything of substance, and yet even such unremarkable creatures can at times leave a mark on history."
  - After: "A young, primitive civilisation that sometimes leaves a mark on history."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...curious that this specimen was deemed precious enough to be encased in such a construct. {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptaSororitasGlossary}Sister Messima{/g}, as she was called, was completing some march of penance in the region, which ended with her entering my collection..."
  - After: "...{g|Encyclopedia:AdeptaSororitasGlossary}Sister Messima{/g}'s penance march ended in my collection..."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Foul xenos wretch!" {n}Abelard turns bright red at Trazyn's words. The Seneschal is clearly fighting the urge to get into an altercation with the projection, which is entirely indifferent to present events.{/n}
  - After: "Foul xenos wretch!" {n}Abelard flushes red.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...who led Humanity's campaign in the region this race calls the Calixis Sector. These remains of Drusus — unlike those held by others of his kind — are genuine. Had they been in Humanity's possession, they would have been lost after a scant few millennia..."
  - After: "...who led Humanity's Calixis campaign. These remains of Drusus are genuine..."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta gazes bitterly at her fellow Sister of Battle, frozen in eternal imprisonment.{/n} "We should have found a way to free this noble sister... but all these years in unholy captivity may have riddled her soul and body with corruption..." {n}She shakes her head and turns away.{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta looks bitterly at the Sister.{/n} "We should free her... but she may be corrupted." {n}She turns away.{/n}
