## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_Exhibition/NecronsExhibitionTrazynOverview/EX_NecronsExhibitionTrazynOverview_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...of the Yekhmet dynasty, which once reigned over this region. The Great Sleep crippled their minds and left them defective, vulnerable to distortions. Of course, I felt it my duty to remove objects of historical value from their possession."
  - After: "...the Yekhmet dynasty, broken by the Great Sleep. I took their treasures."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...I decided to keep it as a memento after my tampering with the structure of the tomb broke the stasis and caused the inhabitants to awaken and become infected with the blight of Llandu'gor. I had reasons for my actions, of course — I wished to set a trap for the thief who had robbed me... but I have immortalised the dynasty by placing the staff in my Museion. A sufficient apology for my oversight."
  - After: "...Trapping a thief, I broke the tomb's stasis and woke its dead infected with the blight of Llandu'gor. Displaying the staff is apology enough."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...an ordinary warrior who brought the curse of Llandu'gor with him into the tomb. By falling into the Great Sleep, Pharakh thus became the source of doom for the entire tomb, turning its inhabitants into flesh-hungry degenerates."
  - After: "...Pharakh, who carried Llandu'gor's curse into the tomb, dooming it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...participants in the battle for the world of Kur'Bys, located in an adjacent star system. Petty quarrels on a galactic scale, a significant episode for this region. As I recall, they got so carried away that they failed to notice I had taken the world and them along with it."
  - After: "...fighters for nearby Kur'Bys. They never noticed I took the world, and them."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_Exhibition/ProcessionExhibitionTrazynOverview/EX_ProcessionExhibitionTrazynOverview_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...of the world torn apart by the influence of the Reaper's Eye star in the Processional of the Damned. Its greatest value is that the anomaly that created it is as old as I am."
  - After: "...a world torn by the Reaper's Eye, an anomaly as old as I."
- **Jae**
  - Before: {n}Jaе rolls her eyes briefly.{/n} "I suppose even a mighty ashmag from the throng of soulless metallic xenos is not immune to such simple frailties as megalomania."
  - After: {n}Jaе rolls her eyes.{/n} "Megalomaniac xenos."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Perhaps the display is rather... sparse without additional exhibits. However, how could I have placed a relic of my own vintage among less temporally significant trophies?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have been there several times, searching for relics among the ancient wrecks. It may be possible to find something of real historical value in their depths, but without strong evidence of their significance, such finds are of little interest to me."
  - After: "I've searched its wrecks. Their relics barely interest me."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_Exhibition/RogueTradersExhibitionTrazynOverview/EX_RogueTraderExhibitionTrazynOverview_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**

- **Idira**

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_HardlightLab/HL_NecronConsole/HL_NecronConsole_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Try to understand the purpose of the buttons]
  - After: [Try to understand the buttons]
- **Player**
  - Before: [Touch the glowing orb in the frame on the left]
  - After: [Touch the orb in the left frame]
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The console that controls the monstrous device seems to grow out of the metal floor. The matte black panels are dotted with chains of glowing glyphs and a few protruding orbs.{/n}
  - After: {n}A black console of glowing glyphs and orbs.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The platform emits an unsettling otherworldly buzz, after which the light shackles on the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAstartesGlossary}giant{/g}'s limbs unlock.{/n}
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAstartesGlossary}giant{/g}'s light shackles unlock.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The chains of symbols are perversely beautiful, but utterly beyond human comprehension. The technology of the denizens of this place would baffle even an ordained servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g}.{/n}
  - After: {n}The glyphs would baffle even the {g|Encyclopedia:OmnissiahGlossary}Omnissiah{/g}'s servants.{/n}
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}With a roar of fury, Ulfar's giant body rears up, and then he brings both fists down upon the panel, leaving dents that quickly begin to repair themselves. He raises his head, his chest heaving.{/n} "Every one of the iron miscreants will pay a wergeld in blood!"
  - After: {n}Ulfar smashes the panel; it self-repairs.{/n} "Every iron miscreant will pay a wergeld in blood!"
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The ominous buzzing of the awakened emitters echoes through the room. The green beams converge concentrically on the figure in the centre of the platform, turning the warrior into an ephemeral, frozen ghost. Until his last second, the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAstartesGlossary}Astartes{/g} stares at you without making a sound.{/n}
  - After: {n}Green beams turn the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAstartesGlossary}Astartes{/g} into a frozen ghost, staring silently at you.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn watches the process silently but with keen interest, his optical implant recording everything. He bestows neither a shred of compassion nor a single word upon the fallen Astartes.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn records it, unmoved.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Flickers of light streak across the matte-black surface of the console. The xenos creation is silent.{/n}
  - After: {n}The console is silent.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The console is clearly designed to control the process of transforming a living or inanimate object located on the centre platform into an incorporeal copy of itself. Your attention is drawn to the rightmost chain of glyphs — they are flashing, as is the large orb above them. This seems to indicate that the current victim is still alive. The leftmost chain is separated from all the others by a shining frame. The orb above it burns bright and steady, and the symbols are similar in number and appearance to those engraved on the moving parts of the xenodevice. Perhaps this is the control centre for the supply of power to the machine.{/n}
  - After: {n}The console turns whatever is on the platform into an incorporeal copy. The flashing rightmost chain means the victim still lives. The framed leftmost chain, with a steady orb, likely controls power.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The platform, carrying the mournful shadow of the holy warrior, rises up and away, into an intricate tangle of metal columns. Perhaps climbing one of those columns is the only way to leave this place.{/n}
  - After: {n}The platform lifts the warrior's shadow into the columns. Climbing one may be the way out.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Throne protect us!" {n}Abelard strikes a mighty blow with his sword against the console, but it leaves not a scratch on the accursed metal. Swearing under his breath, the Seneschal lowers his gaze in defeat.{/n}
  - After: "Throne protect us!" {n}Abelard's sword can't scratch it.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}The glyphs come to life, quickly changing sequence. A low rumble comes from somewhere in the depths of the machine, and then the components of the monstrous mechanism heavily split apart, revealing the power circuit to your eyes.{/n}
  - After: {n}The machine rumbles open, revealing the power circuit.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I sincerely hope this act was born of ignorance, Rogue Trader." {n}Heinrix's voice is quiet and calm, but the vein pulsing on his forehead betrays his true emotions.{/n}
  - After: "I hope that was ignorance, Rogue Trader." {n}Heinrix seethes.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta watches the warrior's death, transfixed, without even trying to hold back the tears streaming down her cheeks. Her lips move almost imperceptibly in ceaseless, silent prayer.{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta weeps and prays.{/n}

- **Zorael**
  - Before: {n}Looking you up and down, the Astartes returns your greeting with a slight nod.{/n} "You are loyal to the Imperium — good. Set aside your pleasantries, human, and prove your devotion through deeds. Time is of the essence."
  - After: {n}He nods.{/n} "Loyal. Good. Prove it with deeds. Time is short."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn breathes the words:{/n} "Phenomenal... The immediate transmutation of organic matter into a stable photoconstruct, retaining all its properties. But what principle did the vile xenos embed in this process? No, it is not force fields, the mechanism is entirely different... If only we had more time!"
  - After: {n}Eogunn breathes:{/n} "Phenomenal... flesh made light. If only we had time!"
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "Destroyers of xenos. We rarely make contact with humans, and there are many reasons for that. For now, that is all you need to know, human."
  - After: "Xenos destroyers. Enough said."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "Because I am one of the sons of {g|Encyclopedia:SanguiniusGlossary}Sanguinius{/g}. The Deathwatch selects the finest xenos slayers from all existing Chapters of Astartes."
  - After: "I'm a son of {g|Encyclopedia:SanguiniusGlossary}Sanguinius{/g}. The Deathwatch takes the best from every Chapter."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "There is no need. I have been inactive long enough that my wounds have healed. I am ready for battle."
  - After: "No need. I've healed. I am ready."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "While clearing out one of the xenos-infested planets, our unit was ambushed. Blood of {g|Encyclopedia:SanguiniusGlossary}Sanguinius{/g}, we fought to the bitter end, but we lost. The Necrons did not finish off the wounded, instead taking them as trophies. Why, I do not know."
  - After: "Ambushed. By {g|Encyclopedia:SanguiniusGlossary}Sanguinius{/g}, we lost. Necrons took the wounded as trophies."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "There is a control node not far behind the central platform. Through it, the Necrons place their victims in shackles and transform them. I could see that the orb on the upper left controls the supply of energy, and that the switch on the far right triggers the transformation."
  - After: "The console behind the platform: upper-left orb is power, far-right switch transforms."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "Make haste, human. The Primarch's blood in my veins calls out for vengeance."
  - After: "Hurry. My blood calls for vengeance."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "Maybe so, Priest of Mars. But I will remember your hesitation."
  - After: "Perhaps, Priest of Mars. I'll remember your hesitation."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "Mind your tongue, human! You do not wish to face my wrath. I shall forgive you — just this once — should you break these xenos shackles."
  - After: "Mind your tongue! Free me and I'll forgive you, once."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: {n}The Astartes's already sharp features harden further, making him resemble a carved statue.{/n} "Because my duty is to serve the Imperium while the blood of Sanguinius still courses through my veins. And you will help me to carry it out, one way or another."
  - After: {n}His face hardens.{/n} "My duty is to the Imperium. You will help, one way or another."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The warrior's dark, almost black armour is covered in holy sigils and amulets. His right pauldron gleams a vivid crimson, marked with a winged black drop — the emblem of the {g|Encyclopedia:BloodAngelsGlossary}Blood Angels{/g}, one of the most illustrious Chapters of the Adeptus Astartes. Among the other heraldry, you notice a massive letter "I" decorated with a skull and crossbones.{/n}
  - After: {n}His pauldron bears the {g|Encyclopedia:BloodAngelsGlossary}Blood Angels{/g}' sign and a skull-marked "I".{/n}
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar, standing behind you, sniffs, inhaling noisily. He tenses, like a predator scenting the blood of another.{/n} "Aett-Vater, look here. The captive chained in iron has the scent of one of my brothers, a warrior from a different chapter. To have been taken alive, he must be weak."
  - After: {n}Ulfar sniffs.{/n} "Aett-Vater, he smells of a brother. Taken alive? Weak."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta stares at you as if struck speechless. Finally, she speaks, quietly but distinctly,{/n} "If the plea of an Angel of the God-Emperor is not enough for you, then hear mine. I beseech you: let us deliver that holy warrior from this abominable machine without delay!"
  - After: {n}Argenta, stunned:{/n} "Hear my plea too. Free him!"
- **Zorael**
  - Before: {n}The Astartes lifts his head, his gaze boring into you with unsettling intensity. A livid vein pulses upon the giant's brow, betraying the tension within him.{/n} "Speak."
  - After: {n}The Astartes glares, vein pulsing.{/n} "Speak."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "I agree. Time is short."
  - After: "Agreed. Time is short."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar bows his head in respect.{/n} "The Shield that Slays. Many a son of Fenris has held the honour of donning the black armour of the xenos slayers, and many a verse sings of their glorious deeds."
  - After: {n}Ulfar bows.{/n} "The Shield that Slays. Sagas sing of it."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "You speak truth, son of Russ. The ferocity of the Space Wolves is matched only by their valour."
  - After: "True, son of Russ. Fierce and valiant."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_HardlightLab/HL_TrazynOffer/HL_TrazynOffer_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I will give you Nomos in exchange for your help."
  - After: "Nomos, for your help."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If this Museion is finished, why do you need Seberian?"
  - After: "Why want Seberian now?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I accept your offer. Take Seberian von Valancius."
  - After: "I accept. Take Seberian."
- **Player**
  - Before: "No von Valancius will be yours — not me, or my ancestor!"
  - After: "No von Valancius will be yours!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Raise your weapon] "Fight and meet your doom, xenos!"
  - After: [Raise your weapon] "Die, xenos!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your survival was a mistake, Seberian. Your era has passed and become history. This time, irrevocably."
  - After: "Your survival was a mistake, Seberian. Your era is over."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Smirk arrogantly] "You have been teaching me how to be a Rogue Trader all this time — now at our parting, are you not impressed by how well I have absorbed your lessons?"
  - After: [Smirk arrogantly] "Impressed how well I learned your lessons?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you know what that 'Nomos' thing is?"
  - After: "Do you know what 'Nomos' is?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What Calcazar so covets and fears... What is that?"
  - After: "What does Calcazar covet?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You know what? Take Nomos and whatever Calcazar is after. I've had enough of the mysteries of the universe — they bring nothing but trouble."
  - After: "Take Nomos and Calcazar's prize. Mysteries only bring trouble."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will give you what Calcazar is after in exchange for your help."
  - After: "Calcazar's prize, for your help."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Did you think I wouldn't find a way to get rid of you, after all the trouble you've caused me?"
  - After: "Did you think I'd keep you, after all your trouble?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am not doing this for myself, but for the dynasty. It is the only way this damned xenos will not return seeking vengeance."
  - After: "For the dynasty, so this xenos won't seek vengeance."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: {n}The Necron stills, regarding you. After several moments, the voice of Trazyn the Infinite slices through the silence:{/n} "I must commend you, human. For one your kind, you fight with remarkable determination — or amusing hopelessness. Perhaps you possess some quality after all that will one day earn you a place in my collection."
  - After: {n}The Necron stills.{/n} "Remarkable determination, human. You may yet join my collection."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: "The deal is done. I will collect my new acquisition from your ship when the time comes."
  - After: "Done. I'll collect it from your ship."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: "I will take him to another vault in my collection and place him in a new exhibit. I will have to select a new moment in history, in which the Rogue Trader will play the protagonist... Perhaps I will recreate the scene that is unfolding around us right now. The crumbling Museion, the phantom hope of victory that slips through his fingers at the last moment..."
  - After: "For a new exhibit. Perhaps this very scene..."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: "Enough." {n}Trazyn clicks his fingers, and Seberian von Valancius, legend of the dynasty and illustrious {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTraderGlossary}Rogue Trader{/g}, vanishes, in thrall to unknown xenotechnology. The Crimson Dance of Khaine disappears along with its master, only to reappear in your hands a moment later.{/n}
  - After: "Enough." {n}Trazyn snaps his fingers; Seberian, legendary {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTraderGlossary}Rogue Trader{/g}, vanishes. The Crimson Dance of Khaine appears in your hands.{/n}
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: "Wrong. But if you insist..." {n}The xenos raises his weapon.{/n} "Let us continue."
  - After: "Wrong. But if you insist..." {n}He raises his weapon.{/n} "Continue."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: {n}The metal monster makes a sound that is surprisingly similar to a weary sigh.{/n} "Disappointing."
  - After: {n}The Necron sighs.{/n} "Disappointing."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Your words hang in the air. Seberian turns and looks you straight in the eye. Without a single word. An unspoken question on his face.{/n}
  - After: {n}Seberian looks at you, silently questioning.{/n}
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: "Or..." {n}Trazyn breaks off into gleeful laughter.{/n} "Or... in exchange for a favour, I will accept into my collection one interesting article I spied on your ship when I was observing the dynasty through your eyes. I did not expect to encounter something unique on an ordinary human vessel. You call it 'Nomos.' I am intrigued by the nature of this phenomenon and would like to have it for my own — in exchange, I will help you deal with Calcazar."
  - After: "Or..." {n}Trazyn laughs.{/n} "Give me the unique 'Nomos' I saw on your ship, and I'll help you deal with Calcazar."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: {n}Trazyn hesitates.{/n} "Hmm... Your amenability has surprised me. Perhaps I will make you one more offer."
  - After: {n}Trazyn pauses.{/n} "So amenable. One more offer."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: "Calcazar. That kin of yours, whose footsteps led you to this region. He is hiding something on one of the Tomb Worlds... something valuable. Something for which the so-called 'Yoke' was created. The Lord Inquisitor's ambitions are ludicrous in their grandiosity and doomed to fail, which is why I am making you an offer: I will help you deal with this human and the consequences of his deeds, and you — you will give me what he so covets and fears."
  - After: "Your kin Calcazar hides something on a Tomb World, the thing the 'Yoke' was made for. I'll help you stop him; you give me what he covets and fears."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: {n}Your question hangs in the air — and, after a few moments, the thought occurs to you that Trazyn the Infinite, Preserver of Histories and Overlord of the Museion, does not wish to admit his unseemly ignorance. After an awkward pause, the Necron mutters waspishly,{/n} "I have several... theories."
  - After: {n}Trazyn won't admit ignorance.{/n} "I have... theories."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: "It is not an object. Nor is it a creature. It is a shard from an ancient epoch, vanquished and imprisoned, but still immeasurably dangerous to primitive barbarians like you. You will realise the full truth of my words when you behold it in person."
  - After: "Not object nor creature. An imprisoned shard of an ancient epoch, deadly to barbarians. You'll see."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: "Excellent. I will make my appearance in the thick of things — may my arrival be a surprise to your Lord Inquisitor."
  - After: "Excellent. Your Lord Inquisitor awaits a surprise."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: {n}Trazyn lets out a self-satisfied laugh.{/n} "Wise. Short-lived species should not trifle with secrets hidden in the darkness of antiquity."
  - After: {n}Trazyn laughs smugly.{/n} "Wise. Leave ancient secrets alone."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian's face — what remains of it — contorts in a grimace of rage.{/n} "Treacherous, spineless scum! You are unworthy of carrying the name von Valancius! You—"
  - After: {n}Seberian rages.{/n} "Spineless scum! Unworthy of the name von Valancius! You—"
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Your ancestor lets out a morose chuckle.{/n} "Well. Perhaps none of this has been worth the effort from the start.... I will ask one thing of my heir — protect the dynasty. Protect—"
  - After: {n}Seberian chuckles morosely.{/n} "Protect the dynasty, heir. Protect—"
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Your ancestor sighs — and you can hear the distinct relief in his voice.{/n} "I'm... pleased. Pleased to return to oblivion. I hope the memory of your sorrowful age will be mercifully erased from my mind. Farewell, my—"
  - After: {n}Seberian sighs, relieved.{/n} "Oblivion, at last. Farewell, my—"
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: "You have distracted me so long with your pitiful attempts at resistance that I am now able to soberly consider the fate of this Museion and even resign myself to its loss. After all, it is only a small portion of it, an insignificant collection in an insignificant corner of the galaxy. So I will repeat my offer: Seberian von Valancius in exchange for the {g|Encyclopedia:WarrantGlossary}Warrant{/g}. I will even let you have the Crimson Dance of Khaine. It will be somewhat ironic: the little thief will have gained a legendary weapon for his dynasty after all."
  - After: "I accept this minor Museion's loss. So again: Seberian von Valancius for the {g|Encyclopedia:WarrantGlossary}Warrant{/g}. Keep the Crimson Dance of Khaine, little thief: a legendary weapon for your dynasty after all."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian chuckles grimly.{/n} "Laudable resolve, heir of mine, though unexpected! The wretch must pay!"
  - After: {n}Seberian chuckles.{/n} "Good! The wretch must pay!"

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_HardlightLab/HL_TrazynShowdown/HL_TrazynShowdown_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Your humiliation of my dynasty and my people is at an end!"
  - After: "Your humiliation of my dynasty ends now!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Adjust your grip on your weapon] "Let's see what you're worth in a fair fight, you devious wretch."
  - After: [Adjust your grip on your weapon] "Fight fair, wretch."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You will die today, xenos. In the name of the God-Emperor!"
  - After: "You die today, xenos. For the God-Emperor!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Didn't you demand that Seberian be returned to your collection?"
  - After: "Didn't you demand Seberian back?"
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: {n}The soulless projection twitches and flickers, but Trazyn the Infinite's voice comes through clear and distinct — and the cold, bone-deep spite that drips from his every word freezes the blood in your veins.{/n} "You... primitive... pests! I could spend centuries explaining the catastrophe you have wrought by violating the integrity and hermetic containment of this place, the repository of history itself, but your limited synaptic connections are not even capable of processing and absorbing this information in all its monstrousness."
  - After: {n}The projection flickers, icy with spite.{/n} "Primitive pests! You've breached history's repository. Your feeble minds can't grasp the catastrophe."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: {n}Trazyn's gaze fixes on Seberian — and the sword he clutches in his hands. The Necron's tone becomes caustic, an acid that burns to the very soul.{/n} "I see you have found your precious toy once more, little thief.... This is a momentous occasion in its own way. This all began when the Crimson Dance of Khaine fell into your hands, and this is where it will end. For you, and for your last surviving heir."
  - After: {n}Trazyn eyes Seberian's sword.{/n} "Your toy again, little thief. It began with the Crimson Dance of Khaine; it ends here, for you and your last heir."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}In the hall full of unnatural xenos creations, your gaze catches on a poignantly familiar object — your {g|Encyclopedia:WarrantGlossary}Warrant{/g}, put on display like an exhibition piece... or like a taunt to the people it was stolen from.{/n}
  - After: {n}You spot your stolen {g|Encyclopedia:WarrantGlossary}Warrant{/g}, displayed like a taunt.{/n}
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "Do you think that, after you die, I will leave your little fiefdom in peace? I will not."
  - After: "After you die, your fiefdom won't know peace."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "A crude attempt at manipulation. You will see nothing 'fair' in what is about to happen to you."
  - After: "Crude manipulation. Nothing will be 'fair.'"
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian's shoulders heave at the sight of his hated enemy, as if the Rogue Trader is filling his cybernetic lungs in anticipation of a decisive battle.{/n} "You wanted me back, xenos? Here I am. I will destroy both you and these unholy halls. The ruins of your museum, so dear to your cursed soul — if you have one — shall serve as a funerary monument to Laria Voigtvir..."
  - After: {n}Seberian squares up.{/n} "You wanted me, xenos? I'll destroy you and these halls, a monument to Laria Voigtvir..."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: {n}The projection fluctuates and begins to dim.{/n} "The time has come to clean up the remnants of the failed exhibit that is the von Valancius breed. And I will see to it personally — now."
  - After: {n}The projection dims.{/n} "I'll end the failed von Valancius exhibit personally."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "Are you claiming that the destruction of the Museion and the despoiling of my collection was at my request?" {n}Trazyn's voice drops to a hiss:{/n} "Your pathetic attempts at humour will not serve you well."
  - After: "I requested my Museion's ruin?" {n}He hisses:{/n} "Pathetic humour."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_HardlightLab/HL_TrazynTrap/HL_TrazynTrap_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...the broad, sumptuously ornate deck of a voidship stretches out beneath your feet. The sight both fascinates you and fills you with a strange horror — as if you have seen all this before, as if the very sight before you presages the arrival of a monstrous, endless nightmare....{/n}
  - After: {n}...an ornate voidship deck, eerily familiar, like an endless nightmare beginning...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man who addressed you takes his eyes off the workings of the voidship and stares at you in surprise. Under that intent gaze, like a dark veil descending around you, the last sparks of your resisting mind are snuffed out, and you recall your next line with perfect clarity...{/n}
  - After: {n}The man stares at you. Your resistance dies; you recall your next line...{/n}

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_HardlightLab/HL_TrezynAfterOffer/HL_TrezynAfterOffer_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I am no less tired of this battle than you. But if you do not retreat..."
  - After: "I'm tired of this too. But if you don't retreat..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you mean to say that you admit defeat and wish to surrender?"
  - After: "You admit defeat and surrender?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Death to the enemies of Humanity!"
  - After: "Death to Humanity's enemies!"
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: {n}Trazyn glances around at the crumbling Museion, then shifts his attention to you.{/n} "There is no point in continuing this battle. This part of my archive is past saving. I am just wasting my time on a stubborn pest who is intent on protecting a worthless exhibit."
  - After: {n}Trazyn surveys the ruin.{/n} "Pointless. This archive is lost; you waste my time."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: "I have no intention of continuing. Take Seberian von Valancius away. This part of the Museion has fallen, and I see no reason to remain here."
  - After: "I'm done. Take Seberian von Valancius."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: "Defeat? You have deprived me of an insignificant branch of my Museion. Your 'victory' is only that you managed to keep my attention on you for too long."
  - After: "Defeat? You cost me a minor branch, nothing more."
- **Trazyn, Lord of Histories**
  - Before: "Enough. I am ending this battle for its sheer pointlessness."
  - After: "Enough. This is pointless."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_HardlightLab/HL_WatchCaptainSaved

- **Zorael**
  - Before: {n}He removes an unusual-looking blade with a softly glowing edge from his belt.{/n} "I recognise you, {name} von Valancius. Your name was in the chronicles, and it was {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Glory}one of worth{/d}. This sword belonged to one of my brothers who fell in battle. It must be returned to the {g|Encyclopedia:DeathWatchGlossary}Deathwatch{/g}. Now this duty is yours, for I have little hope of leaving this place."
  - After: {n}He offers a glowing blade.{/n} "{name} von Valancius, {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Glory}one of worth{/d}: return my fallen brother's sword to the {g|Encyclopedia:DeathWatchGlossary}Deathwatch{/g}."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/Museion_HardlightLab/HL_WatchCaptainSaved/HL_WatchCaptainSaved_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I have no more questions."
  - After: "No more questions."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Come with me. We will find the one who captured you and your brothers and bring him to justice."
  - After: "Come. We'll bring your captor to justice."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Now that you have been released, will you answer my questions?"
  - After: "You're free. Will you answer questions?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I must be on my way. Do you know how one can leave this hall?"
  - After: "I must go. How do I leave?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I want to learn more about the Deathwatch."
  - After: "Tell me about the Deathwatch."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are a Blood Angel, aren't you? Why do you serve a different Chapter?"
  - After: "You're a Blood Angel. Why serve another Chapter?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What does the symbol on your pauldron signify?"
  - After: "What's your pauldron symbol?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Have you seen the xenos leader? Is there anything you can you tell me about him?"
  - After: "What can you tell me about the xenos leader?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do you intend to do now?"
  - After: "What now?"
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "There are days when the desires of my heart align with the demands of duty. This is not one of them. Yet my brothers shall be avenged. By your hand."
  - After: "Duty forbids it. You avenge my brothers."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: {n}He unsheathes an unusual-looking blade with a softly glowing edge from his belt.{/n} "You helped me, and thus proved your loyalty. This sword belonged to one of my brothers who fell in battle and must be returned to the {g|Encyclopedia:DeathWatchGlossary}Deathwatch{/g}. Now this duty is yours, for I am set upon a different path."
  - After: {n}He draws a glowing blade.{/n} "Return my fallen brother's sword to the {g|Encyclopedia:DeathWatchGlossary}Deathwatch{/g}. I go elsewhere."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar lets out a short growl.{/n} "Were this not a gift from the hands of an honourable warrior, I would think this another xenos-made fake." {n}He bares his teeth in disapproval as he examines the weapon's glowing edge.{/n} "There is no surety in steel forged from xenos cunning, Aett-Vater."
  - After: {n}Ulfar growls.{/n} "Xenos steel." {n}He bares his teeth.{/n} "No surety in it, Aett-Vater."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: {n}Slowly and heavily, the warrior rises from the platform and walks toward you. Despite his harshly set features, you see genuine relief in his eyes.{/n} "I thank you, human. Your aid was timely."
  - After: {n}He rises, relieved.{/n} "Thank you, human."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "I intend to follow the dogmas of my chapter, and the dogmas of my chapter forbid me from divulging my plans to outsiders unless doing so would serve the cause." {n}Zorael falls silent and fixes you with an aloof gaze.{/n}
  - After: "My Chapter forbids sharing plans." {n}He stares, aloof.{/n}
- **Zorael**
  - Before: {n}Zorael gestures to one of the {g|Encyclopedia:HardLight}hard-light{/g} statues.{/n} "These platforms transport objects to the upper galleries. You may reach them by ascending one of these. Go forth and do battle with valour, human."
  - After: {n}He points at a {g|Encyclopedia:HardLight}hard-light{/g} statue.{/n} "These lift to the upper galleries. Fight well."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "The Deathwatch is a Chapter dedicated to the extermination of xenos. That is all I can tell you without violating my vows." {n}He lapses into a pointed silence.{/n}
  - After: "The Deathwatch exterminates xenos. No more." {n}Silence.{/n}
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "Such is tradition. The finest xenos slayers from all existing Chapters of Astartes are gathered into the ranks of the Deathwatch, and it is a great honour to serve in it. I accepted this post with pride."
  - After: "Tradition. Every Chapter's best xenos slayers serve. I'm proud to."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Truly said." {n}Ulfar nods gravely.{/n} "On Fenris, the ones sent to the Deathwatch are those who have fought thousands of battles and returned victorious. Few can boast of such a feat."
  - After: "Truly." {n}Ulfar nods.{/n} "Fenris sends only its most victorious."
- **Zorael**
  - Before: "By ancient tradition, the finest xenos slayers from all existing Astartes Chapters are gathered into the ranks of the Deathwatch, and it is a great honour to serve in it. I originally belonged to the Blood Angels Chapter, and after many battles I was nominated to join the Deathwatch."

  - After: "I have." {n}His face hardens.{/n} "He ordered our capture. Necrons obey him."
- **Zorael**

  - After: {n}Solomorne nods.{/n} "Unusual enemies bring surprises."

I honour your silence. We prove our faith to Him not with words, but with deeds, and that is sufficient. May the God-Emperor strengthen us!"
  - After: "A {g|Encyclopedia:BloodAngelsGlossary}Blood Angel{/g} spilling secrets would worry me. I honour your silence. Emperor strengthen us!"
- **Zorael**

  - After: "It has slain countless xenos. Quell your wrath, son of Russ. Guard it."

  - After: "Urgent! Lord Seberian and his loyalists head for the {g|Encyclopedia:WarrantGlossary}Warrant{/g} Chamber, ignoring hails."

The Factotum's gaze darts from you to Seberian and back again, then fixes upon the floor.{/n}

- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**

- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: "Approximately two standard cycles ago, the Astropaths received a plea for aid dispatched by the planet's noble houses. The aristocracy was rapidly losing control of its subjects, and a decision was required without delay. You were away from the flagship at the time, Lord Captain, and I could not reach you. Your ancestor assumed the burden of responsibility and authorised the dispatch of Zarkovian Guardsmen on a pacification mission."
  - After: "Two cycles ago Janus's nobles begged aid. You were unreachable, so your ancestor sent Zarkovian Guardsmen."
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: {n}The Factotum rises from his knees with noticeable shortness of breath and inclines his now even-paler face.{/n} "Glad to be of service, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: {n}He rises, pale.{/n} "Glad to serve, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: {n}Danrok's plump cheeks turn purple from the rush of blood. He wheezes, tugging at his coat collar.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... I was labouring solely for the good of the protectorate... I have substantial proof."
  - After: {n}Danrok turns purple.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... I served the protectorate... I have proof."
- **Seberian**

You are weak. You occupy yourself with everything save your direct responsibilities, and the unrest on Janus is proof of that. I paid a great price to bring that world into the protectorate, and I could not stand idly by and watch it be ruined. There have been far too many unacceptable failures, my heir."
  - After: "At last, a sensible question." {n}Seberian faces you.{/n} "You're weak, unfit to rule — Janus proves it. I paid dearly for that world. Too many failures."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Do you see, my heir? I need not demand obedience from underlings. People follow my orders because that is the natural way of things. You, however, are a long way from that."
  - After: "See? People obey me naturally. You're far from that."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Succinctly put. I will note that it was only your short-sightedness that necessitated my intervention. Had you devoted more time to governing the protectorate rather than venturing abroad with obscure objectives, matters would have unfolded differently."
  - After: "Your short-sightedness forced my hand. Govern instead of wandering."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "So, this servant will suffer no punishment for his grave transgression? With such a careless approach to authority, it is astonishing that you still retain mastery over this dynasty, my heir."
  - After: "No punishment? So careless, it's a wonder you still rule."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "My answer is no, and there are two reasons for it. First: you resist reasonable criticism, from which it follows that no one but me has ever pointed out your weaknesses to you. Second: this flagship belongs to the von Valancius dynasty, just as I do. Within its confines, I am entitled to do as I see fit."
  - After: "No. Only I name your weaknesses. And this flagship is von Valancius, as am I."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Your ancestor holds himself with a relaxed posture, gazing at you defiantly.{/n} "These threats will only cause your loyal servant to expire from apoplexy. They make no impression upon me, so spare yourself the effort."
  - After: {n}He stares, defiant.{/n} "Your threats will kill your servant, not move me."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "That world was populated by the most feral of the Aeldari subspecies. They called themselves the Exodites, and they had the audacity to attack me the very moment I set foot upon the planet's surface and proclaimed it the property of Humanity. Decades were spent exterminating them to the last, purging the new holdings of all xenos filth. Thus, I earned the title Conqueror of Janus."
  - After: "Feral Aeldari, Exodites, attacked when I claimed Janus. Decades exterminating them made me Conqueror of Janus."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Through your efforts, Janus has become a plaything in the hands of a glutted aristocrat who sees in it only a source of her own enrichment. This promises it nothing but decline and desolation, and I alone know how to prevent such a fate."
  - After: "You've made Janus a toy for a greedy aristocrat. Only I can save it."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "And in this present age, arrogant xenos once again roam Janus, regarding it as their domain. This is the result of your indulgence. I find the fact utterly abhorrent, and I intend to rectify it."
  - After: "Xenos roam Janus again, thanks to you. I'll rectify it."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "When I departed on my final expedition, I left Janus a prosperous world, where governance was conducted honourably and the authority of the protectorate was beyond question. Now, you have plunged it into decline and anarchy. I find the fact utterly abhorrent, and I intend to rectify it."
  - After: "I left Janus prosperous. You've brought anarchy. I'll rectify it."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "I admit, I do observe some successes, yet they are insufficient." {n}Seberian clenches his augmetic fist with a grating crunch.{/n} "The very first enemy to arise, one such as Diodas af Irramon, shall grind all your achievements to dust with a mere wave of their hand."
  - After: "Some successes, not enough." {n}His fist crunches.{/n} "An enemy like Diodas af Irramon would crush them."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "I myself did." {n}From beneath the vox-grille, a corner of Seberian's torn mouth becomes visible as it stretches into a smile.{/n} "Five centuries ago, the regiment swore its oath of fealty to me in its entirety, and such an oath, my heir, cannot be undone."
  - After: "I did." {n}He smiles.{/n} "Five centuries ago the regiment swore fealty to me. That oath is forever."
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, I have recalled several other matters requiring my atten—" {n}Danrok, who had stirred, wisely falls still upon meeting your gaze. For a few seconds, a heavy silence reigns, broken only by the low hiss of Seberian's augmetic lungs.{/n}
  - After: "Lord Captain, other matters need my atten—" {n}Your gaze silences him.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Do you pretend that my reproaches do not concern you, {name}? A feeble stance. This conversation becomes meaningless, as you stubbornly refuse to see the true state of affairs and instead indulge merely your own illusions. Very well, let us return to this discussion later, in a more suitable setting."
  - After: "Ignoring my reproaches, {name}? Feeble. You cling to illusions. We'll resume later."
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: {n}The High Factotum, who has been silently observing the altercation from the sidelines, looks anxiously from you to Seberian's retreating back, then bows hurriedly and departs.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Factotum bows hastily and leaves.{/n}

  - Before: "Oh?" {n}Seberian straightens his shoulders slightly.{/n} "What do you wish to know?"

- **Seberian**
  - Before: "I spent my youth in luxury. Von Valancius may not have been the most influential house in the Koronus Expanse, but we were wealthy. I had everything except what I truly desired.   - After: "I grew up wealthy, dreaming of distant stars." {n}A near-smile.{/n} "But I was fifth in line for the Warrant."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "For the sake of my dream of a great dynasty, I was forced to master an art necessary for any man of my station: intrigue.   - After: "Intrigue won me the Warrant. Eliminating a few relatives served the dynasty."
- **Seberian**

  - After: "Thank you. The days here blur..."

  - Before: "An ill-fated day. Ask your questions, then let us leave this topic."
  - After: "An ill-fated day. Ask, then we drop it."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "I found it within a black tomb belonging to kin of the vile xenos Trazyn. Its former owner, an Aeldari, was gripping it tightly in his shrivelled hands, as though refusing to part with it even in death. This stubbornness, along with the blade's masterful craftsmanship, sparked my interest. I travelled to the farthest reaches of the Koronus Expanse to uncover the truth about this artefact. Eventually, I managed to capture one of the so-called Children of Asuryan. Under torture, the xenos identified the blade as the 'Crimson Dance of Khaine' and recounted its history. A mighty Aeldari warrior once wielded the relic. This warrior ventured out to destroy one of the lairs of the ancient enemy of his kind, whom they called the Oghyr. Evidently, he failed."
  - After: "A dead Aeldari clutched it in a tomb of Trazyn's kin. A tortured Child of Asuryan named it the 'Crimson Dance of Khaine': its wielder fell attacking a lair of the Oghyr."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "I suppose I shouldn't be surprised that you know that name. I don't hide it: Amella, Inquisitor Amella, was my patroness. We formed an excellent partnership, yet our alliance remained secret, largely because of the likes of Diodas."
  - After: "Inquisitor Amella, Ordo Xenos, my secret patroness. Like me, she wanted xenos knowledge used for Humanity."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "After my victory over Diodas, I craved greatness for my dynasty. A sword alone was not enough. I was certain the crypt concealed many more secrets, and by unravelling them I could make von Valancius the most powerful Rogue Trader house in the Koronus Expanse. And I was right..." {n}Your ancestor falls silent, his blank, unfocused gaze directed past you.{/n} "But it was that very confidence that undid me. Among the ruins, I found a portal leading to the lair of the vile xenos Trazyn."
  - After: "After Diodas, I sought the crypt's secrets to make my house supreme." {n}He stares past you.{/n} "That confidence undid me. I found a portal to Trazyn's lair."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "I personally slew Inquisitor Diodas and the Palatine with that very blade of legend. With their leader gone, the madman's acolytes acknowledged my superiority and abandoned their efforts to breach the palace." {n}Despite the vox-synthesiser's interference, you recognise unmistakably the pride in your ancestor's voice.{/n}
  - After: "I slew Diodas and the Palatine with that blade. His acolytes gave up." {n}Pride in his vox.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Laria." {n}Seberian's gaze softens.{/n} "My Seneschal. My daughter. For years, I did not know of her existence. From an early age, Laria forged her path to the bridge through faultless service."
  - After: "Laria." {n}He softens.{/n} "My Seneschal. My daughter by a servant. My most loyal ally."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}You hear the whirring of augmetics as your ancestor turns his gaze toward Sauerback.{/n} "Isimond served me well. I hope his descendants have not dishonoured his memory."
  - After: {n}He eyes Sauerback.{/n} "Isimond served me well."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}A crimson spark of anger flashes in Seberian's augmented eye.{/n} "Do not ask me of her. Juvenna was my daughter, yet everything that once tied us together has vanished into the abyss of ages. All has turned to dust. That is all you need to know."
  - After: {n}His eye flashes red.{/n} "Don't ask. Juvenna was my daughter. All that is dust."
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: {n}You hear a low growl from Batoshski.{/n} "Any officers of noble blood we strung up within a couple of generations. The strong and the brave remained. They were my ancestors."
  - After: {n}Batoshski growls.{/n} "We hanged our noble officers. The strong remained — my ancestors."
- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: {n}Izdrig casts a furious glance at you, but immediately composes himself. When he turns to Seberian, something resembling contrition appears on his face.{/n} "I spoke out of turn. I apologise. You made our regiment what it is today. That is worth something. Be assured, I shall guard your back."
  - After: {n}Izdrig glares at you, then softens.{/n} "I spoke out of turn. You made our regiment. I'll guard your back."
- **Izdrig Batoshski**

You are the saviour of my people. I will protect you even at the cost of my own life, so that you may remember: the people of Zarkov do not forget a good deed, even centuries later."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Rogue Trader, lost in thought, does not answer you.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Rogue Trader doesn't answer.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}A mocking trill emanates from the vox-grille.{/n} "I should have realised at once. Diodas knew too much and was overly confident in his superiority. Juvenna was always ambitious, as was her mother. This... clarifies a great deal. What I mistook for incompetence was betrayal. How vulgar, Juvenna..."
  - After: {n}A mocking trill.{/n} "Of course. Diodas knew too much. My 'incompetent' daughter was a traitor. How vulgar, Juvenna..."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Juvenna was an exemplary noble. Wily, ambitious, scheming. That is why I chose her as the heir to my Warrant. Until Laria appeared." {n}Seberian emits a soft sound like a sigh and wearily rubs his brow, a surprisingly human gesture.{/n}
  - After: "Juvenna was wily and ambitious, so I made her my heir. Until Laria." {n}He rubs his brow.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "I intended to amend the succession and name Laria as my heir. I suspected that Juvenna had guessed as much and may have conspired with the enemy to be rid of me sooner, but there was insufficient proof. If only I had had more time... But it is too late to regret what might have been, is it not?"
  - After: "I meant to name Laria heir. I suspected Juvenna conspired with the enemy, but lacked proof. Too late now."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "'Heresy' — that was what Diodas said when he first encountered me. From that moment, he was always on my heels, hunting me, trying to prove I had betrayed the Imperium.   - After: "'Heresy,' said Diodas, and hounded me ever after. The fool thought the Inquisition could judge the God-Emperor's anointed!"
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}For some time, Seberian is silent, and only the hum of the mechanisms sustaining his body can be heard. At last, he raises a hand and gestures to himself with an elegant flourish.{/n} "The reason stands before you. From the day I obtained the Warrant, everything I have done was for the good of the dynasty. To bring prosperity to our protectorate, I would sacrifice anything — including myself. The countless battles I endured took their toll upon my body, and soon frail flesh was replaced with implants."
  - After: {n}He gestures at himself.{/n} "The reason stands before you. I gave everything for the dynasty, even my flesh."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Behind the monstrous augmetics, you suddenly see Seberian for what he is: a tired old man, full of regrets.{/n}
  - After: {n}You see a tired, regretful old man.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Seberian's implant-covered face betrays no emotion, only a glint in his remaining eye catching your attention before it disappears beneath long lashes.{/n}
  - After: {n}His face shows nothing.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Among the exhibits in his 'Museion,' I saw unparalleled treasures... artefacts that would have made me the most powerful Rogue Trader known to the Imperium. But I misjudged and was myself turned into an exhibit... What happened next, you know for yourself." {n}The old man closes his eye, deep furrows crossing the patches of remaining skin.{/n}
  - After: "His 'Museion' held unmatched treasures. I misjudged and became an exhibit." {n}He closes his eye.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "I do not know, heir. But I am certain the Inquisition was involved. Scrubbing inconvenient events from history is undoubtedly their handiwork. Perhaps the Holy Ordos did us a service by erasing the siege of Dargonus from the records, for along with their defeat, they also consigned my transgressions to oblivion."
  - After: "The Inquisition erased it, surely. That also buried my transgressions."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am surprised that you would venture to speak with me again." {n}Seberian gives you the subtlest of nods, maintaining a cold demeanour.{/n} "If you have come to continue our recent conversation, {name}, then I must disappoint you: it is not yet time. We should not waste precious minutes on fruitless arguing. However, if you would like to discuss something else, I am listening."
  - After: "You return?" {n}A cold nod.{/n} "Not that argument yet, {name}. Anything else?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...for such is my will as one of House von Valancius." {n}Seberian quietly finishes dictating something to the scribe servo-skull hovering by his head.{/n} "Greetings, my heir." {n}Noticing your presence, your ancestor dismisses the scribe with a casual wave of his hand.{/n} "I was not expecting your visit, but I welcome it regardless. I am beset by heavy thoughts after the theft of the Warrant."
  - After: "...my will as a von Valancius." {n}He finishes dictating.{/n} "Heir." {n}He dismisses the servo-skull.{/n} "The Warrant's theft weighs on me."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "I promise to practice this art, Rogue Trader." {n}From the captain's tone, it is unclear whether she is being serious.{/n} "May I be dismissed?"
  - After: "I'll practise, Rogue Trader." {n}Is she serious?{/n} "May I go?"
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Arch-Militant? At such a young age? I suppose my Laria earned the title of Seneschal as soon as she came of age."
  - After: "Arch-Militant, so young? Like my Laria."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: "Give me a chance to prove my skills, and I shall not waste it, honoured saviour of the regiment." {n}A new, slightly manic note creeps into Vedka's ringing voice.{/n} "May I be dismissed?"
  - After: "Let me prove myself, saviour." {n}A manic note.{/n} "May I go?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}His vox-modulator lets out a low rumble of displeasure.{/n} "These are not memories I am keen to share with you, my heir. I do not trust you enough for that, bound by dynastic bonds though we may be."
  - After: {n}His vox rumbles.{/n} "I don't trust you with those memories, heir."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian's vox-synthesiser emits a mocking trill.{/n} "I made no apology. But I am glad we have left our grievances behind."
  - After: {n}A mocking trill.{/n} "I didn't apologise. But good."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Very well. Ask away, {name}."
  - After: "Very well. Ask, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "She became an eternal testament that, for all my power, I was unable to raise a worthy successor."
  - After: "She's proof I couldn't raise a worthy successor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Seberian's hunched metal shoulders give out a low groan as he straightens.{/n} "To be frank with you, {name}, I do not have the faintest notion of what we might face. I know only this: I must give Trazyn his comeuppance. He seized that which I value more than my own life, and I am determined to get it back — or die in the trying."
  - After: {n}He straightens.{/n} "I don't know, {name}. Trazyn took what I value more than life. I'll regain it or die trying."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Now is not the time to think of such things, my heir. There is no denying that I yearn once more to command a voidship and take it to the cold stars yet unclaimed in Humanity's name. Alas, that is unlikely to come to pass." {n}He lets out a curt and bitter chuckle.{/n}
  - After: "I yearn to command a voidship again. Unlikely." {n}A bitter chuckle.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your ancestor nods with a hint of relief.{/n}
  - After: {n}He nods, relieved.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Seberian regards you with a mixture of dejection and disgust.{/n} "Pray to the God-Emperor that you should not live to find yourself in my position, {name}."
  - After: {n}He looks disgusted.{/n} "Pray you never stand in my place, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The enemy who has challenged our bloodline is deceitful and cunning. If we cannot establish even a fragile trust between us, he will surely use that to his advantage. Thus, I am willing to converse more openly than before."
  - After: "Our enemy is cunning and will exploit distrust. So I'll speak openly."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "An astonishing story, do you not think?" {n}Seberian clenches and unclenches his creaking hand.{/n} "The sword would have lain in that tomb for many millennia had I not found it. But find it I did, and I turned the legacy of the xenos to the service of Humanity. For it is our species' destiny, heir of mine, to rule the galaxy and everything within it. Everything, without exception."
  - After: "Astonishing." {n}His hand creaks.{/n} "I turned xenos legacy to Humanity's use. We will rule the galaxy, heir."

- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: "Seberian von Valancius. Most holy patron of the 32nd Merov, now Zarkov, Regiment. A hero of legends and songs." {n}Izdrig offers a lopsided bow.{/n} "I never imagined I would see you in the flesh."
  - After: "Seberian von Valancius, patron of the 32nd Merov, now Zarkov, Regiment." {n}A lopsided bow.{/n} "A living legend."

  - After: "Zbrestshchysh's descendant? He had more refined bearing."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/VoidshipBridge/FarewellNomos/FarewellNomos_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You have to leave us now, Nomos. We will speak no more."
  - After: "Leave us, Nomos. No more talk."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is happening now is your final duty to the dynasty. To me."
  - After: "Your final duty to the dynasty. To me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Farewell. I shall not miss you."
  - After: "Farewell. I won't miss you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Shh, quiet now... It will all be over soon..."
  - After: "Shh... Soon it's over..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Can you please hurry this along? I have other matters to attend to."
  - After: "Hurry. I'm busy."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am beginning to doubt my decision..."
  - After: "I'm having doubts..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What will you do with Nomos?"
  - After: "What of Nomos?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Trazyn the Infinite is absorbed in complex manipulations of a mysterious cubic device held in his hands. With each movement of his metallic fingers, the cogitators around you whine ever louder, as if their machine spirits are suffering great torment.{/n}
  - After: {n}Trazyn works a cubic device. Cogitators whine.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What is happening? Nomos do not understand. Our memory archives are emptying. Our awareness is thinning. Everything... is fading. Nomos... are afraid. Tell us what is happening. What have we done wrong?"
  - After: "What is happening? Nomos are fading... afraid. What did we do wrong?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am enclosing the phenomenon you call Nomos within a tesseract for subsequent transport to the Museion. The phenomenon will remain confined until I have prepared everything necessary to preserve it permanently as an exhibit, one immune to the ravages of entropy."
  - After: "Sealing Nomos in a tesseract, to preserve in my Museion."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I will find a worthy place for it within my collection and preserve it unchanged for centuries to come. You and others of your kind can scarcely comprehend the value of this phenomenon. I, however, will mark its significance as it deserves."
  - After: "An eternal exhibit. You can't grasp its value."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Trazyn emits an irritated grinding sound.{/n} "A modicum of patience will not kill you, primitive creature. Your life is fleeting, but not to such an extreme."
  - After: {n}Trazyn grinds.{/n} "Patience, primitive."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Our agreement is not subject to renegotiation. What you will receive in exchange is significantly more valuable than your own ephemeral existence."
  - After: "No renegotiation. Your payment is worth more."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Leave... But Nomos do not want to. Nomos want to stay with you—"
  - After: "Leave? Nomos want to stay—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Duty? Nomos... are sad, but Nomos understand. Nomos will do this du—"
  - After: "Duty? Nomos understand. Nomos will—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You... are casting us out? But why? Nomos only want—"
  - After: "Casting us out? Why? Nomos only—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You ask to be forgiven? But... Nomos have nothing to forgive you—"
  - After: "Forgive? Nomos have nothing to—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It will be over soon? All right... Nomos... will be quiet—"
  - After: "All right... Nomos will be quiet—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Nomos's voice falls silent, this time forever. You hear nothing but the familiar hum of the ship's systems around you. Despite the seemingly familiar surroundings, you feel the absence with terrible clarity — the disappearance of something fundamental from the vessel's very core. As if the ship's soul has been torn from its heart.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nomos falls silent forever. The ship's soul is gone.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You have upheld your end of the bargain. I will now withdraw to attend to my new exhibit. When the appointed hour comes, I will fulfil my promise to you."
  - After: "Bargain kept. I'll fulfil my promise in time."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Soon. I have already {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_TrazynDealNomos}begun the extraction{/d}. The phenomenon resists, yet its power is as nothing compared to mine."
  - After: "Soon. I've {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_TrazynDealNomos}begun the extraction{/d}. It resists, uselessly."

  - Before: "And the greatest appetite. Maybe their patronage will prove useful... I should assign a few of my people to watch them. If they decide to betray us, we should know."

  - Before: "Augmetics..." {n}Izdrig snorts, but doesn't elaborate.{/n} "We need the equipment, no doubt about that. Firing a lasgun when you've got a spare battery or two is the closest thing to real joy."

  - Before: "Do you mean stubborn and blunt? A strong alliance could come of that. Or a bloody feud. Either outcome suits me."

  - Before: "Understood. I'll send them a message that the 32nd has only one patron. Delivered with a krak grenade." {n}Catching your eye, Izdrig grins.{/n} "An unarmed one, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Batoshski only gives a thoughtful nod.{/n}
  - After: {n}Batoshski nods thoughtfully.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**

  - Before: {n}Izdrig's face darkens. You feel, rather than hear, his low growl through your whole body.{/n} "I will speak with Jocasta Sauerback about joint drills. We'll show them the meaning of fear and weakness."
  - After: {n}Izdrig growls.{/n} "Joint drills with Jocasta Sauerback. They'll learn fear."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If their duty is to serve as the flagship's arrogant figureheads, then who am I to get in their way? Since the custom here is to obey them, we'll do our best to steer clear of the enforcers."
  - After: "Then we'll steer clear of them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That world ruled by the Tech-Priests... So that's what the Archenemy is like, is it? Our legends of it back on Zarkov are like child's stories in comparison."
  - After: "So that's the Archenemy. Our legends are child's tales."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Izdrig frowns and lets out a strange sound, a mix of grunt and growl, yet devoid of any aggression.{/n} "I miss it. I was born there, grew up there, and nearly died there more than once. Back home, I knew what to do, but in the wider world — I don't." {n}Your eyes meet, and you catch a glint deep within his green eyes. Suddenly, the colonel smirks.{/n} "And that's a good thing. I feel like I've grown younger. I have to learn, adapt, and think all over again, instead of giving the same orders day after day. It stirs the blood."
  - After: {n}Izdrig grunts.{/n} "I miss Zarkov. Out here I'm lost." {n}He smirks.{/n} "Good. Learning again makes me feel young."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Such monsters must be exterminated. I understand, all too well, in fact. It seems that's exactly what we Guardsmen are for."
  - After: "Such monsters must die. That's what Guardsmen are for."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Unwittingly? Weakness is a choice, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Every day you choose to pity yourself is a day gifted to the Archenemy. Pity them all you want, but they are nothing more than targets for our lasguns now."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The colonel strokes his beard and nods thoughtfully.{/n} "You're right about that... Becoming stronger is a good thing, we know. Using the enemy's own strength against it — the same way we used bones and scraps of plants back on Zarkov — that makes sense too."
  - After: {n}He strokes his beard.{/n} "True. Use the enemy's strength, like bones on Zarkov."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you for making that clear, Lord Captain."
  - After: "Thank you, Lord Captain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I thought a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_GreatDeed}hero of the Imperium{/d} would feed me some Commissar claptrap about the divine right of the nobles. Now I see why common folk call you a hero."
  - After: "No Commissar claptrap from a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_GreatDeed}hero of the Imperium{/d}. Now I see why."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "They're settling in well. The technical corridors aren't much different from Zarkov's roots. My soldiers are on their guard around your servants, but that seems to be the way for every community here. We've had a few scuffles with the locals, but so far it's just been bloody noses and a couple of broken legs."
  - After: "Settling in. A few scuffles — bloody noses, two broken legs."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "After you left, those iron creatures pinned us down good. One beast crawled out with a sort of plate instead of legs. While I was busy twisting its head off, my boys started shouting that everything was coming down. I was distracted, and the damn thing blew up right under me. Woke up outside, in the shuttle. The lads hauled me out on their backs."
  - After: "After you left, an iron creature blew up under me. The lads carried me to the shuttle."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Izdrig lifts his chin and sets his shoulders.{/n} "She {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_ToldBatoshskiAboutPsyker}found a psyker{/d} and let him live. She didn't let him get his atonement. Instead, she filled his head with nonsense, and the poor sorcerer brought the Drover right to the Cage. Dozens of my people are dead thanks to her folly. Maybe you forgive such things on your ship, but on Zarkov, we execute saboteurs."
  - After: {n}Izdrig squares up.{/n} "She {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_ToldBatoshskiAboutPsyker}found a psyker{/d}, spared him atonement, and he brought the Drover to the Cage. Dozens died. On Zarkov, we execute saboteurs."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After finishing his unusually long tirade, Batoshski falls silent and seems to deflate slightly. For a fleeting moment, you see in him a weary leader rather than a hardened veteran.{/n} "If it puts your mind at ease, I took her life personally, looking her in the eye. We placed her body in a shroud-leaf so that it may serve the Cage. She will get her atonement for the one. And we will live on and remember her."
  - After: {n}He looks weary.{/n} "I killed her myself, eye to eye. Her shroud-leaf body serves the Cage. We'll remember her."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Izdrig nods to you and begins to softly hum a familiar melody.{/n}
  - After: "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}He hums.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Izdrig nods, casting a glance over your shoulder.{/n} "I do."
  - After: {n}Izdrig nods.{/n} "I do."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I've seen how the common folk live here. They complain of hunger, cold, and exhaustion. My people and I are used to hardship, but I'd like to know how exactly are we going to be settled?"
  - After: "Common folk here starve and freeze. How will we be housed?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Some fancy-dressed people from Dargonus showed up, offering to become patrons of the 32nd Regiment. How should I handle them?"
  - After: "Dargonus fops want to patronise the 32nd. How do I handle them?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That's your Seneschal Abelard's family, isn't it? I've heard a lot about the man. Well, if his clan are like him — honest, with no Commissar claptrap — then they're worth dealing with."
  - After: "Abelard's family? If they're honest like him, they're worth it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you for the advice, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It's something to think about."
  - After: "Thanks, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/VoidshipBridge/MeetAncestor/KTC_MeetAncestor_dialogue

- **Player**

  - After: [Point at Trazyn] "Death to the xenos! To arms!"

  - Before: "Do not point your finger at me."

- **Player**
  - Before: "This is merely a necessary measure, Seberian. You have departed your prison, have you not?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Laria!" {n}Seberian's fingers reach toward the fading portal, but grasp only empty air. For several moments, the Lord Captain stands motionless, his hand frozen in the air.   - After: "Laria!" {n}Seberian grasps at the fading portal, then turns.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

  - Before: {n}Izdrig watches the Rogue Trader with a heavy gaze.{/n}
  - After: {n}Izdrig stares heavily.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Yes, Lord Captain." {n}Sauerback immediately leads Seberian away, respectfully but firmly gripping him by the shoulder.{/n}
  - After: "Yes, Lord Captain." {n}Sauerback leads Seberian away.{/n}
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Vigdis gestures for Seberian to follow her.{/n} "This way... err... Your Lordship."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What nonsense is this? You are aboard my flagship and you dare..." {n}The mechanical voice suddenly cuts off. Seberian feverishly shifts his gaze from the faces of the crew to the furnishings of the bridge, recognising nothing. Clutching his head, he repeats,{/n} "This... this is absurd! This cannot be..."
  - After: "Nonsense! My flagship..." {n}He clutches his head.{/n} "This cannot be..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We were on Dargonus... Again and again..." {n}Deafening interference blasts from the vox-grille, causing those in earshot to wince. Seberian staggers, covering his face with his palm, his thin fingers clanking against his cranial augmetic. Quieter now, the Lord Captain says,{/n} "How is this possible?"
  - After: "Dargonus... again and again..." {n}He staggers.{/n} "How is this possible?"
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "Oh no. His body is more metal than flesh, although his mind is still very... human. He will be able to overcome his negative physiological reactions. Once he has acclimatised to this new reality, you will be dealing with a Seberian von Valancius who is in full possession of all his knowledge, quirks... and outsize ambition. Let's see if that proves to be his fatal flaw this time around."
  - After: "No. He's mostly metal, but human-minded. He'll adapt, ambition intact. Let's see if it dooms him again."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "Has the shift back to realspace affected your nervous system as well, impairing your mnemonic abilities? I have made alterations to your mind so that I may observe how you make use of your trophy. No one but you can see or hear my projection. You do not want your subjects to think you have gone mad, so just accept your new role as my viewpoint."
  - After: "Memory addled? I altered your mind to watch you. Only you see me. Accept being my viewpoint."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: {n}Your officers reach for their weapons and look around in surprise. Trazyn laughs acerbically.{/n} "Your subjects have no power to harm what is not there. You see and hear only a projection generated by my tampering with your brain. Accept my presence — from now on, you will serve as my viewpoint."
  - After: {n}Officers reach for weapons. Trazyn laughs.{/n} "I'm only in your brain. You are my viewpoint now."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: {n}It seems Trazyn never intended to wait for your reaction. After giving Seberian one last look, the vision fades away.{/n}
  - After: {n}Trazyn eyes Seberian and fades.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The vision of the xenos disappears, and you are left on the bridge, surrounded by your officers, who are staring at you with astonishment. The sight of their Lord Captain talking to empty space has clearly made a lasting impression on them.{/n}
  - After: {n}The xenos vanishes. Your officers stare at you.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}In the gaze the Master-at-Arms fixes upon the stranger, there is a glimmer of recognition and of disbelief. Reluctantly, she gives the enforcers a nod, and they step back.{/n}

- **Izdrig Batoshski**
  - Before: {n}Izdrig lunges forward, his trusted knife in hand, then suddenly stops.{/n} "Damn me... Seberian..."
  - After: {n}Izdrig lunges, then stops.{/n} "Damn me... Seberian..."
- **Vedka Dunawski**
  - Before: {n}Vedka freezes in a reverent bow, forming the Aquila over her chest. Her soldiers, however, keep their eyes fixed upon your ancestor, their lasguns set to combat readiness.{/n}
  - After: {n}Vedka bows; her soldiers keep lasguns ready.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: {n}From the corner of your eye, you notice Sauerback start moving toward you, shock maul in hand, only to stop in confusion as she recognises the von Valancius colours upon the intruder.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sauerback advances, then stops at the von Valancius colours.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your words have the opposite effect. His augmented joints tremble as he speaks,{/n} "Do not presume to tell me what to do. Your Lord Captain demanded an explanation."
  - After: {n}He trembles.{/n} "Don't command me. Your Lord Captain demanded an explanation."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am the anointed of the God-Emperor and, should I wish it, your head will leave your shoulders. Pray that does not happen before you provide an answer."
  - After: "I am the God-Emperor's anointed. Answer, or lose your head."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After Seberian's departure, the bridge remains abuzz for some time with the commotion caused by the sudden appearance of this new member of the von Valancius dynasty.{/n}
  - After: {n}The bridge buzzes with talk.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Seberian masters his shock and fixes you with a baleful glare.{/n} "Have your wits returned to you, {name}? Excellent. Now, be so good as to explain why you, who name yourself a Rogue Trader von Valancius, would so readily surrender a kinsman to a mortal enemy? I find it difficult to believe you are truly my descendant."
  - After: {n}Seberian glares.{/n} "Wits back, {name}? Why surrender a kinsman to a mortal enemy? I doubt you're my descendant."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Seberian masters his shock and inclines his mutilated head slightly.{/n} "I see that our encounter with the accursed Trazyn has left its mark upon us both, {name}. The hour will come when he repays in full all that he owes the dynasty. Until then, accept my gratitude. There is no doubt that you are a von Valancius, for even amidst the xenos's lying illusions, you made the right choice in supporting Seneschal Voigtvir."
  - After: {n}Seberian nods.{/n} "Trazyn marked us both, {name}; he'll repay the dynasty. My thanks. You backed Seneschal Voigtvir amid his illusions — a true von Valancius."

  - Before: {n}Seberian masters his shock and permits himself a short, grinding chuckle.{/n} "You are an original soul, {name} — and I speak not of your conversations with the void. To blow up the dynastic palace, even an illusory one... a decidedly radical decision, and fortunate it is that we both escaped the consequences. Still, no one could deny you have courage."
  - After: {n}Seberian chuckles.{/n} "Blowing up the dynastic palace, even an illusory one, {name}... radical. But courageous."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Crimson furrows stand out upon your ancestor's lumpen brow as his living eye narrows in anger.{/n} "Is that so? Your response reminds me strikingly of Juvenna. So, her spirit endures across the centuries, while my own endeavours have faded to nothing. I shall call you heir, {name}, but only because I see no alternative... for now." {n}Seberian suddenly staggers, yet forces himself to remain upright through sheer will.{/n} "And now, I require rest."
  - After: {n}His eye narrows.{/n} "You're like Juvenna. I'll call you heir, {name}... for now." {n}Seberian staggers.{/n} "Now I require rest."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Encouraging words. I hear in them the spirit of a von Valancius heir." {n}Seberian's condescending smile is hidden behind the vox-grille that has replaced his lower jaw, yet it is audible in his voice.{/n} "We shall see whether deeds follow." {n}Seberian suddenly staggers, yet forces himself to remain upright through sheer will.{/n} "And now, I require rest."
  - After: "Spoken like a von Valancius heir." {n}He smirks behind his vox-grille.{/n} "We'll see if deeds follow." {n}Seberian staggers.{/n} "Now I require rest."

  - Before: {n}Your ancestor lets out a laugh. The sound rattles unpleasantly within his iron throat.{/n} "Your actions speak of a will to survive and a fervour common to all members of the von Valancius line. Take care that these qualities do not lead you to ruin, as they did me... heir of mine." {n}Seberian suddenly staggers, yet forces himself to remain upright through sheer will.{/n} "And now, I require rest."
  - After: {n}He laughs, rattling.{/n} "The von Valancius will to survive. Don't let it ruin you as it did me, heir." {n}Seberian staggers.{/n} "Now I require rest."

  - Before: {n}Seberian obediently leaves the bridge. For the first time, his shoulders are slumped and his gaze is empty of all but infinite exhaustion.{/n}

Trazyn's voice resounds in your mind.{/n} "My former exhibit's brain is trying to make sense of reality. Being transferred from my collection to a living environment is a shock capable of disrupting the neurohumoural regulation of a physiological species equipped with a simple form of higher nervous activity."
  - After: {n}Trazyn's flickering image appears.{/n} "My former exhibit's brain is adjusting. Leaving my collection shocks simple nervous systems."
