## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/VoidshipBridge/VedkaDunavskiArchmilitant/VB_VedkaDunavskiArchmilitant_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I must take my leave."
  - After: "I must go."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I see you have replaced your prosthetic."
  - After: "You replaced your prosthetic."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Seek out the servants of the Ecclesiarchy and do as they instruct."
  - After: "Do as the Ecclesiarchy instructs."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Faith in Him has a thousand faces. Yours is one. But not everyone believes that the God-Emperor can be worshipped in different ways."
  - After: "Faith in Him has a thousand faces; yours is one. Not everyone agrees."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do not listen to those blinkered fools. Continue to believe in that which grants strength to your body and soul. Do what is right for you."
  - After: "Ignore those blinkered fools. Keep the faith that strengthens you. Do what's right for you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Captain — now Arch-Militant — Dunawski does not immediately notice you. She is looking around the bridge in awe, wandering among the majestic statues and command alcoves.{/n}
  - After: {n}Dunawski gazes around the bridge in awe.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Upon seeing you, the Arch-Militant makes the sign of the Aquila and bows, waiting for permission to speak.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Arch-Militant bows, waiting.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Like on Zarkov, where a single mistake costs lives. Only here, it is souls. The Merciful God-Emperor, now I even feel pity for those who have fallen in thrall to the Archenemy. But I also know how important it is to protect people from their own mistakes."
  - After: "Like Zarkov, but mistakes cost souls. I even pity the Archenemy's thralls."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your words... It isn't just fear, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! It is an abomination in the eyes of the God-Emperor and all of Humanity!"
  - After: "Not fear, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Abomination!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The soldiers of the 32nd Regiment have occupied their assigned barracks in accordance with the Code and have commenced scheduled duties, Lord Captain!" {n}Vedka catches your eye and continues in a lower voice.{/n} "I mostly selected those who, like me, wanted to leave Zarkov. They are glad to serve you, glad to be among the stars. Everything here is still strange and frightening, but we will adapt. We always do."
  - After: "The 32nd Regiment is quartered and on duty, Lord Captain!" {n}Quietly:{/n} "We'll adapt."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A whirlwind of emotions flickers across Vedka's face for a moment before she composes herself.{/n} "During the journey, I familiarised myself with the Astra Militarum Handbook I found in the ship's library, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It's... It's significantly different from the Handbook on Zarkov. Over centuries of copying, we have unwittingly changed so much. It has unsettled many, but otherwise, we are well, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}Vedka steadies.{/n} "The ship's Handbook differs from Zarkov's, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It unsettled many, but we're well."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Dunawski's gaze wanders, scanning the bridge for a few seconds as if she searches for something.{/n} "Do what's right. I hear you, Lord Captain! We'll stand by our traditions, regardless of what anyone else has to say."
  - After: {n}Dunawski looks around.{/n} "Yes, Lord Captain! We'll keep our traditions."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Not at all, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Life here on your flagship is confusing and difficult, but we are not afraid of challenges. We're used to them. You have given us a chance to achieve atonement, and believe me, every one of us will fight for it until the end."
  - After: "Not at all, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! You gave us a chance at atonement. We'll fight for it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vedka smiles broadly as she raises her augmented arm, admiring her clenching and unclenching fingers. She has not relinquished her bone claws, however — the trophy is now mounted on the wrist of her new bionic.{/n}
  - After: {n}Vedka flexes her new bionic, bone claws on its wrist.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I've noticed that your common servants are fond of complaining about their lives. The filth, the hunger, sharing a single bunk between several people... My soldiers are asking if they can expect the same living conditions as the rest of the crew?"
  - After: "Your servants share bunks and starve. Will my soldiers too?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Dargonus was magnificent! Back there, all kinds of nobles approached me. I gather they're interested in becoming patrons of the Zarkov Regiment. I think it might be beneficial, since that seems to be the custom in your protectorate, but I know nothing about them. Please, what is your advice?"
  - After: "Dargonus nobles want to patronise the Zarkov Regiment. Your advice?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I've learned that they are the most recently ascended of the noble dynasties on Dargonus. We are newcomers as well. Perhaps we ought to stick together."
  - After: "They're Dargonus's newest dynasty. Newcomers, like us."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm still not sure what 'influence' is, nor how you get it. It seems only wise to learn from those who actually understand it."
  - After: "Best learn 'influence' from those who understand it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vedka looks thoughtfully at her prosthesis.{/n} "The von Valancius gift... Forgive me for wasting your time, Lord Captain. I should have made such an obvious choice right from the start."
  - After: {n}Vedka eyes her prosthesis.{/n} "The von Valancius gift... Of course."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "An alliance of the God-Emperor's faithful servants, blessed by His anointed one? We could ask for nothing greater."
  - After: "An alliance of His faithful? Nothing greater."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'll give the order to notify the noble houses immediately. Our loyalty belongs to you alone — we won't let anyone question that."
  - After: "I'll tell the houses: our loyalty is yours."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The priests in the flagship's chapel say that the God-Emperor Himself grants power to the nobility. And He cannot be wrong. If you suspect these noble families of heresy, you need only give the word."
  - After: "The priests say He empowers the nobility. But if you suspect heresy, say the word."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you for your guidance, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There have been a few run-ins between your soldiers and Jocasta Sauerback's enforcers. Now they're looking at the 32nd with suspicion. Your people want to know: how should they conduct themselves around the enforcers?"
  - After: "Sauerback's enforcers distrust the 32nd after clashes. How should we act?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your words are the will of the God-Emperor, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I'll have them conveyed to the troops. In His name and for the glory of the dynasty, we shall endure."
  - After: "His will, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We'll endure."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Dunawski frowns, causing the stone in her eye socket to shift slightly.{/n} "I thought things would be handled differently in the Imperium. But here, it seems, it's just like back on Zarkov. Well... at least we're used to it."
  - After: {n}Dunawski frowns.{/n} "Just like Zarkov. We're used to it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Those are the words of a true commander, Lord Captain. Not some Commissar claptrap, but genuine care for the soldiers. Right out of the Handbook. I'll be glad to tell the troops!"
  - After: "True care, right from the Handbook. I'll tell the troops!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And let their guard down? That's not the answer, Lord Captain. I'll talk to Jocasta. I'm sure we'll find a solution. Maybe joint patrols, or using the 32nd to bolster punitive operations."
  - After: "Lower their guard? No. I'll arrange joint patrols with Jocasta."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Right you are, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! As long as you are with us, we are safe, and we are with you forever. The matter is settled. I won't raise it again."
  - After: "Right, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! With you, we're safe."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "With your permission, I will not tell the soldiers that, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Back on Zarkov, we'd have paid the enforcers back in blood for an insult like that. But the rules are different here."
  - After: "I won't tell them that, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. On Zarkov we'd answer such insult in blood."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Then we should honour their service to Him and accept their suspicion as a given. I'll tell the soldiers, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We'll cause no more trouble."
  - After: "Then we'll accept their suspicion, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. No more trouble."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Archenemy on that metal planet... I can't stop thinking about what I saw. We had no idea of the horror it truly is."
  - After: "That metal planet... I can't forget the Archenemy's horror."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It turns out that some of our traditions disgust the other servants of the dynasty. Some are even whispering of heresy... People are especially unsettled by our funeral rites. We brought shroud-leaves with us and have already placed a few free-thinkers inside them, and your servants started an uproar."
  - After: "Your servants call our shroud-leaf funerals heresy. There was uproar."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... I beg your pardon, I was distracted and didn't see you right away." {n}Vedka snaps to attention and clicks her heels.{/n} "Arch-Militant Vedka Dunawski is ready to serve!"
  - After: "Pardon, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}She snaps to attention.{/n} "Arch-Militant Dunawski, ready!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "By the God-Emperor's grace, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. After you left, we repelled several waves of the enemy. Then the whole place started coming down, and the heretical iron things shut down. We gathered the wounded and ran. We made it out just as the place collapsed. A shuttle picked us up outside. I have already ordered the names of those who fell in that cursed place to be carved into the memorial wall."
  - After: "By His grace, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We held until the place collapsed. A shuttle took us out. The fallen go on the memorial wall."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Speaking with you is the greatest honour, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "Always an honour, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes, I have, Lord Captain. Genetor Majoris Ferrenz presented me with a true gift of von Valancius on your behalf. I suppose my status as Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s Arch-Militant had something to do with it. I feel like I've stepped right out of one of the songs!"
  - After: "Yes. Genetor Majoris Ferrenz gave Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s Arch-Militant a von Valancius gift!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "So I see. Many of the sermons and dogmas of the Ecclesiarchy and our Handbook have now taken on a new meaning for me. I will share it with the Zarkovians."
  - After: "The sermons mean more now. I'll tell the Zarkovians."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have already sought their counsel, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The priests told us to get rid of the shroud-leaves and bury our fallen according to shipboard tradition. They say, since we have your patronage, our struggle for survival is over. Perhaps they are right, and it is time for us to let go of the customs of our world..."
  - After: "The priests say bury the shipboard way, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Maybe it's time to let Zarkov go..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vedka frowns, her lips thinning into a tight line.{/n} "Then, with your permission, I will share our ways with those willing to listen — the Handbook, our songs, and the stories of Zarkov. Perhaps that will help them understand..."
  - After: {n}Vedka's lips thin.{/n} "Then I'll share our Handbook and songs with whoever listens."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you. I will do what is right."
  - After: "Thank you. I'll do what's right."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The words of a true {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_GreatDeed}hero of the Imperium{/d}! As long as you are with us, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, not even the slightest seed of fear or doubt will take root in our souls! I will remind the soldiers of this."
  - After: "A true {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_GreatDeed}hero of the Imperium{/d}! With you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, no doubt takes root!"

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/WarrantChamber/WC_AlertSquad/WC_AlertSquad_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "We have prevailed and retrieved the Warrant. The xenos capitulated and cast us back to the flagship."
  - After: "We won the Warrant back. The xenos sent us home."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Thank you. It took time, but we have come to an understanding."
  - After: "Thanks. We understand each other now."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It is high time we acknowledged that the dynasty has only one Rogue Trader, and that is me."
  - After: "The dynasty has one Rogue Trader: me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am going to give you a short head start before sending assassins after you — as payback for all you have done."
  - After: "Run. My assassins follow shortly — payback."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Make arrangements for the ceremony and return the Warrant of Trade to its proper place."
  - After: "Arrange the ceremony; restore the Warrant of Trade."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Nothing to report on board, I hope?"
  - After: "All quiet on board, I hope?"
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Lord Captain?" {n}Disbelief is written on Sauerback's face, as if she cannot believe what she's seeing.{/n} "But... you..." {n}Suddenly regaining her composure, the Master-at-Arms throws back her shoulders, standing at attention.{/n}
  - After: "Lord Captain?" {n}Sauerback stares.{/n} "But..." {n}She stands to attention.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you have returned... Thank the God-Emperor." {n}Your Seneschal puts his weapon back in its sheath, staring at you with naked relief.{/n}
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Thank the Emperor." {n}Abelard sheathes his blade.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} detected an anomalous surge of energy. We came here to investigate, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "{g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} saw an energy surge, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian lets out a bitter chuckle, the sound like the clanking of a broken mechanism.{/n} "Indeed. My time has passed, never to return."
  - After: {n}Seberian chuckles bitterly.{/n} "Indeed. My time has passed."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian ceremoniously bows his head as he hands the sword into your keeping.{/n}
  - After: {n}Seberian bows, handing over the sword.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian bows his head in thought.{/n} "Indeed. The God-Emperor knows I can hardly claim credit for bringing that about, but you found a way to impress an old man."
  - After: {n}Seberian nods.{/n} "Indeed. You impressed an old man."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "It will be done without delay, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I will summon the ship's chaplain to come and organise a cordon."
  - After: "At once, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "Correct, Lord Captain! Nothing worthy of your attention has happened since your landing. The ship is still orbiting the dead world."
  - After: "Correct! Still orbiting the dead world."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Once our ordeals in this dark sector are over and your ship returns home, I shall find a Chartist willing to take on board a reanimated dead man who still dreams of the stars, and set out toward the unknown. I have spent too long gathering dust. It is time to conquer new worlds for the dynasty... and leave the protectorate to its rightful owner."
  - After: "Once home, I'll find a Chartist to take me into the unknown, conquering worlds for the dynasty. The protectorate is yours."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Domin, you are here! As it was always meant to be, for His cards never lie, yet unworthy doubts have gnawed at my soul." {n}Two long, half-healed cuts bloom like a bright cross upon Kibellah's face.{/n}
  - After: "Domin! The cards never lie." {n}Cuts cross Kibellah's face.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "You defeated that unholy thief?" {n}Sauerback asks, as if unable to believe what she is hearing.{/n} "Well, I couldn't have hoped for anything better. Except for the death of that accursed {g|Encyclopedia:XenosGlossary}xenos{/g} as well."
  - After: "You beat that thief?" {n}Sauerback marvels.{/n} "Pity the {g|Encyclopedia:XenosGlossary}xenos{/g} lives."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Of course, Lord Captain. I will immediately make arrangements for the solemn ceremony and re-consecration."
  - After: "Of course. I'll arrange re-consecration."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian sighs heavily and turns to you.{/n} "I must give you credit where it is due, my heir... While there have been situations and problems we saw differently, and while I have noted mistakes and misjudgements in your actions... you are nevertheless a worthy holder of the Warrant, fit to carry forward the von Valancius legacy. For this, I thank you. Now I can find peace in the knowledge that our dynasty is in safe hands."
  - After: {n}Seberian sighs.{/n} "You've erred, heir, but you're worthy of the Warrant. Thank you. The dynasty is safe."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian raises his hand with the Crimson Dance of Khaine in his grasp and studies the blade for a while.{/n} "The origin of all my troubles, and a witness to my final victory... This weapon should belong to you, {name}. Accept it, for none are fit to possess it but a Rogue Trader of House von Valancius."
  - After: {n}Seberian raises the Crimson Dance of Khaine.{/n} "My ruin and my victory. Take it, {name}, von Valancius."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian nods slowly, not averting his gaze.{/n} "I thank you for the head start. When we return to the known reaches of the Koronus Expanse, I shall most certainly take advantage of it."
  - After: {n}Seberian nods.{/n} "Thanks. I'll use the head start."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/WarrantChamber/WC_SeberianDisappointed/WC_SeberianDisappointed_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Those are your reasons? I would call them a pretext!"
  - After: "Reasons? Pretexts, more like!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I demand an explanation. You are on my ship."
  - After: "Explain yourself. This is my ship."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Don't you dare touch the gene-lock! I forbid it under penalty of death!"
  - After: "Touch the gene-lock and you die!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What are you doing? What is this madness?"
  - After: "What is this madness?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address your ancestor's retinue] "I might spare Seberian himself, but you shall be executed as common rabble."
  - After: [Address your ancestor's retinue] "Seberian I may spare. You'll hang."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are right. I am not ready for the weight of this title."
  - After: "You're right. I'm not ready for this title."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Your swiftness is commendable, my heir. Which, alas, is more than I can say about your foresight or your readiness to bear the burden of power. But I will let you save face. Wait here and pretend you were a little late." {n}Under the vox-synthesiser distortion, Seberian's voice sounds sincere. How genuine those emotions truly are remains to be seen.{/n}
  - After: "Swift, heir, but unready for power. Wait here; pretend you were late." {n}He sounds sincere, perhaps.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "I know how unworthy leadership withers a dynasty. I know how the spirit of von Valancius has been dwindling over the generations, turning its leaders into common merchants. And I know how a dynasty can become a puppet. I will not let that happen."
  - After: "Weak leaders turned our dynasty into merchants and puppets. Never again."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "I only have one wish, and that is to preserve and bolster the greatness of our dynasty. We are Rogue Traders, and that is what we must remain. A rare few independent thinkers, unconstrained by Adeptus Terra dogma, inquisitive, and bold enough to oppose anyone save the God-Emperor. We are the crusaders of Him on Terra. That and nothing else. I cannot allow you to reduce the dynasty to a shadow of what it is meant to be! I simply cannot." {n}Toward the end of his impassioned speech, the modulated emotions in Seberian's voice sound almost real to you. You can almost hear the voice he spoke with before his terrible injuries.{/n}
  - After: "Rogue Traders are free, defying all but the God-Emperor — His crusaders. I won't let you make us a shadow!" {n}His old voice almost returns.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "I wished to do this swiftly and without bloodshed. But a civil war aboard the flagship? I shall not become like the accursed Goge Vandire..." {n}Seberian falls silent, lowering his head with the whirring of his mechanical spine, before mustering his resolve.{/n} "I withdraw my claim, {name}. We shall settle this matter later, once the crisis has passed. And on that, I shall swear an oath. Before the Warrant itself." {n}Yet he voices even his capitulation and request as both a verdict and a command.{/n}
  - After: "Civil war on the flagship? I won't become Goge Vandire..." {n}He bows his head.{/n} "I withdraw my claim, {name}, until the crisis passes. I swear it before the Warrant." {n}Even surrender sounds like command.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "That would have been the truth — if a sad one — were I not alive. But as things stand, your claim to my flagship is dubious at best, don't you think?"
  - After: "I'm alive. Your claim to my flagship is dubious."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "You have no authority to give me orders. The Warrant of Trade is rightfully mine, more so than it is yours."
  - After: "You can't order me. The Warrant of Trade is mine."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "I would have turned a blind eye to that, were it not for your woefully poor leadership. Under your rule, our dynasty is headed into decline — something that I once paid a high price to avert. You allowed yourself to become Calcazar's puppet when you handed him the Yoke. You are not prepared, my heir. Bow before a true Rogue Trader and join my retinue. Then, one day, when you are ready, you will rightfully inherit my Warrant. And by the Golden Throne, you will be worthy! I will do everything to see to that."
  - After: "Your leadership dooms the dynasty. Giving Calcazar the Yoke made you his puppet. Bow, join my retinue, and someday inherit my Warrant worthily."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You see Seberian's newfound followers exchange nervous glances and turn pale. Seberian himself stands motionless, proud and majestic in his absolute composure.{/n}
  - After: {n}His followers pale. Seberian stays composed.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Unless you are pretending, you can be proud of yourself, my heir. You have overcome the thirst for power and you have looked beyond the veil of pride. One day, when I have taught you everything I know, you will be a great Lord Captain."
  - After: "If sincere, be proud, heir. You've overcome pride. I'll make you a great Lord Captain."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Haven't you realised yet, my heir? I never give up. Rogue Traders fight to the end, always, until they perish amid stars unknown."
  - After: "Rogue Traders never give up, heir. We fight until we die."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Sometimes salvation requires we take desperate steps. This is the only way, heir. To venture into the darkness between the cold stars, to move away from the Astronomican, is, by the measure of many, an even greater madness."
  - After: "Salvation takes desperate steps, heir. Leaving the Astronomican is greater madness."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Seberian inserts his hand into the gene-lock you remember well from the time of the mutiny on the ship that claimed Theodora's life and laid Kunrad's treachery bare. You see the liquid coursing through your ancestor's plasteen veins change colour. The servitor's eyes come alive, and the doors of the Warrant Chamber begin to open.{/n}
  - After: {n}Seberian puts his hand in the gene-lock from the mutiny that killed Theodora. The Warrant Chamber opens.{/n}

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/WarrantChamber/WC_WarrantReturned/WC_WarrantReturned_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Seberian, are you all right?"
  - After: "Seberian, all right?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Carefully step off the Warrant, whispering prayers of repentance] "May the God-Emperor forgive us..."
  - After: [Step off, praying] "Emperor forgive us..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Trazyn let us go just like that?"
  - After: "Trazyn just let us go?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Carefully step off the Warrant, trying not to damage it]
  - After: [Carefully step off the Warrant]
- **Player**
  - Before: [Walk unceremoniously over the Warrant] "Enough quaking. It's just an old writ."
  - After: [Walk over the Warrant] "It's an old writ."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The icy cold shredding your body into hundreds of frozen particles recedes, and the green glow of Necron technology is replaced by trembling firelight. You are on the deck of your ship, and something soft, rustling and muffling your footsteps bunches beneath your feet. An expanse of thin, beautifully preserved paper, covered in neat {g|Encyclopedia:HighGothic}High Gothic{/g} lettering. A great artefact of antiquity, your dynasty's {g|Encyclopedia:WarrantGlossary}Warrant of Trade{/g}, is spread out beneath your feet.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Necron cold fades. You stand on your ship — on the dynasty's {g|Encyclopedia:WarrantGlossary}Warrant of Trade{/g}, its {g|Encyclopedia:HighGothic}High Gothic{/g} script underfoot.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "The whispers beyond the door are rolling with laughter right now, the little blighters..." {n}Idira says, barely concealing a crooked, but unmalicious grin herself.{/n}
  - After: "The whispers are laughing." {n}Idira grins.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Attention all! Remove yourselves from the sacred Warrant of Trade immediately! We are quite literally standing on the dynasty's pride and glory!" {n}The Seneschal's face reveals genuine horror.{/n}
  - After: "Everyone, off the sacred Warrant!" {n}Abelard is horrified.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Holy Throne! Forgive and save us... God-Emperor!" {n}Sister Argenta stands frozen in prayer, her hands forming the sign of the Aquila.{/n}
  - After: "Throne! Forgive us!" {n}Argenta makes the Aquila.{/n}
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Only with much blood of the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}Undying One{/g}'s enemies shall we be cleansed of the taint of this sacrilegious trampling of the relic."
  - After: "The blood of the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}Undying One{/g}'s enemies must cleanse this."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Registering a transgression of the fourth... fifth degree? The Warrant of Trade was returned with a serious error in its coordinates." {n}There is disapproval in Pasqal's voice, but it is unclear whether it is due to what happened to the Warrant or the inaccurate calculations for teleportation.{/n}
  - After: "A fifth-degree transgression? A coordinate error." {n}Pasqal disapproves.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "We should all be taken into custody and tried for such a crime against this sacred relic..." {n}Solomorne is completely still, not permitting any new movement to further damage the Warrant.{/n}
  - After: "We should be tried for this..." {n}Solomorne stands still.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian glances at the Warrant, but no angry outbursts, curses, or prayers erupt from his vox-synthesiser.{/n} "The dynasty is saved. Such an obscenity is a small price to pay for the fate of the von Valancius." {n}His voice sounds thin, almost mechanical.{/n}
  - After: {n}Seberian is unmoved.{/n} "The dynasty is saved. A small price." {n}His voice is thin.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your efforts to inflict as little damage as possible on the Imperial relic are paying off — not that you have left no marks at all, but, at the very least, you do not seem to have damaged the paper itself.{/n}
  - After: {n}The paper seems undamaged.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your intentions to inflict no damage on the Warrant of Trade are not panning out. However, given its size, it is unlikely that anyone will notice a few small holes, right...?{/n}
  - After: {n}A few small holes. No one will notice...?{/n}
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: {n}Calligos rushes about the Warrant in a rage, heedless of the paper ripping and being marred beneath his feet.{/n} "That cowardly, underhanded xenos! I have not finished with you! I have not finished with you! I'll have your iron skull yet, you dishonourable groxshit!"
  - After: {n}Calligos storms about, tearing it.{/n} "Coward xenos! I'm not finished with you! I'm not finished with you! Groxshit!"
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "This is but a reprieve. That decrepit xenos does not forget. He will come back for you. You have made a powerful enemy, {name}." {n}Seberian lets out a dry chuckle.{/n} "But by our enemies is the glory of our lives measured, at the end of it all."
  - After: "A reprieve. He'll return for you, {name}." {n}Seberian chuckles.{/n} "Enemies measure our glory."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "I must say, this piece of organic material looks better as a rug. It is quite pleasant to trample the relics of the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g}. I must do it again if I have the chance." {n}Marazhai utters these words with murderous seriousness — unsavoury pleasure glitters in the depths of his eyes.{/n}
  - After: "A better rug. Trampling {g|Encyclopedia:ImperiumGlossary}Imperium{/g} relics is pleasant." {n}Marazhai's eyes glitter.{/n}
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "We have allowed our feet to touch the Warrant. We must flay our feet, make purity seals from the skin, and wear them until our wounds heal!" {n}Fire blazes in Incendia's eyes and voice.{/n}
  - After: "We must flay our feet for purity seals!" {n}Incendia blazes.{/n}
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "That xenos still found a way to have the last laugh. Even after losing in battle. But I believe the God-Emperor will forgive us for treading on the sacred Warrant." {n}Incendia's voice is cold and quiet.{/n}
  - After: "The xenos had the last laugh. He will forgive us." {n}Incendia is cold.{/n}
- **Uralon the Cruel**
  - Before: "And so the document signed by the False Emperor, the basis of all your power, Champion, lies beneath your feet like a vanquished foe. What does this mean to you now, {name}? What does the symbol of the dynasty and the favour of the corpse on the throne awaken in your soul? Listen to yourself — and you will hear the whispers of the Pantheon."
  - After: "The False Emperor's writ lies underfoot like a vanquished foe, Champion. What is it to you now, {name}? Hear the Pantheon whisper."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As you step off the rustling parchment, the doors of the Chamber begin to slowly open.{/n}
  - After: {n}You step off; the doors open.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You are too exhausted to make speeches, nor worry about anything at all. The Warrant has been recovered, and that is what matters. You feel hollow. You simply. Need. To rest.{/n}
  - After: {n}Too exhausted to care. You need. To rest.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your boots inevitably soil the Warrant, yet each sacrilegious step only stokes righteous fury within you, strengthening your will and your faith, as if the God-Emperor Himself is sending forth His divine wrath.{/n}
  - After: {n}Each step stokes your righteous fury.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}In this moment, the last sacred thing within you crumbles. The others are too shocked to even notice where you tread. But here and now, you have committed the final blasphemy, this time not only against the God-Emperor but against the very order of the Imperium. Even the dynasty no longer means anything to you — it is no more than a tool for your own ambitions.{/n}
  - After: {n}The last sacred thing in you crumbles. Even the dynasty is just a tool for your ambitions.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "The sacred symbol of which the {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g} are so proud is wrought with very primitive technology. It is as if the fragility and ephemerality of your species is reflected in your culture as well." {n}Yrliet takes a few feather-light steps, scarcely creasing the paper beneath her feet.{/n}
  - After: "Primitive, like the {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}." {n}Yrliet steps lightly.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Don't despair, shereen! We'll clean it all up! Your Warrant will be as good as new — I know a couple of restorers... scribes? Archaeologists?" {n}Jae curses quietly as the edge of the sacred paper crunches under her boot.{/n}
  - After: "I know restorers, shereen!" {n}Jae curses as paper crunches.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Great Throne, preserve us against false steps!" {n}Cassia fearfully lifts one foot off the paper.{/n}
  - After: "Throne preserve us!" {n}Cassia lifts a foot.{/n}
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "We have restored your honour, Aett-Vater, and that is what matters most. The Allfather's blessing is stamped on your dynasty from on high, and you need not mourn this... paper." {n}Despite his bravado, Ulfar is still careful not to tread heavily on the Warrant of Trade.{/n}
  - After: "Your honour is restored, Aett-Vater. Don't mourn paper." {n}Yet Ulfar treads lightly.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "It would be strange to suppose that that... being would release us without a final parting blow. This is the least of the harms it could have inflicted."
  - After: "A parting blow. The least harm it could do."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "No. But I will be, {name}. You could have left me there, after all, but you chose to talk an old man round. Against all odds. You have the heart of a true Rogue Trader — bold, hungry, fair to a fault. I... misjudged you. But now I am proud of you. You are an heir worthy of the dynasty's crown."
  - After: "No. But I will be, {name}. You talked me round. You have a true Rogue Trader's heart. I misjudged you. I'm proud, heir."

## DLC/DLC3/Narrative/WarrantChamber/WC_WarrantStolen/WC_WarrantStolen_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "How did you manage to steal the Warrant?"
  - After: "How did you steal the Warrant?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "First and foremost, we must deal with the xenos and recover the Warrant."
  - After: "First, deal with the xenos and recover the Warrant."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I shall overlook your insolence. For now."
  - After: "I'll overlook your insolence. For now."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Keep your hands where I can see them, and perhaps you will live long enough to stand trial for your assault upon my title."
  - After: "Hands where I can see them, and you may live to stand trial."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will give you Seberian in exchange for the Warrant."
  - After: "Seberian for the Warrant."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You will not have Seberian. Together, we shall wrest the Warrant from your foul clutches, xenos!"
  - After: "You won't have Seberian. We'll take the Warrant back, xenos!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I received a message from Trazyn. He wants you in exchange for the Warrant."
  - After: "Trazyn wants you in exchange for the Warrant."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What of our current dispute? Shall we simply pretend nothing happened?"
  - After: "And our dispute? We pretend nothing happened?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Who or what is this 'Yekhmet?'"
  - After: "Who or what is 'Yekhmet?'"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Dealing with a xenos sits even worse with me than dealing with you."
  - After: "Dealing with a xenos is worse than dealing with you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have no intention of betraying you to an enemy of Humanity."
  - After: "I won't betray you to Humanity's enemy."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is this, Seberian? Do I hear fear in your voice?"
  - After: "Seberian, is that fear I hear?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "No one outside this Chamber must learn that the Warrant has vanished until I find a way to recover it."
  - After: "No one outside this Chamber learns the Warrant is gone."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The cursed xenos has sealed his own doom by insulting the von Valancius dynasty."
  - After: "The xenos doomed himself insulting the von Valancius."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will consider your proposal."
  - After: "I'll consider your proposal."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have not yet had the time to consider it."
  - After: "I haven't had time to consider it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Perhaps we should indeed restore everything to how it was. The Warrant returns to the Chamber, and you return to the Museion."
  - After: "Perhaps restore things: the Warrant here, you to the Museion."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why have you changed your mind? What do you want with Seberian?"
  - After: "Why the change? What do you want with Seberian?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What makes you think I am heading to some gate?"
  - After: "Why think I'm heading to a gate?"
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian stares, motionless, at the Warrant's empty resting place. His augmented lungs do not inhale once. It is as though he has turned into a statue. The sacred chamber is silent as a crypt, save for the hum of servo-motors in the ancient Lord Captain's augmetics.{/n}
  - After: {n}Seberian stares, statue-still, at the Warrant's empty place.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "...I shall become Thy Wrath, and Thy Fury, and Thy Flame. For from Thy right hand flows only Righteous Redemption against any who raise themselves against Thee and against Humanity..."
  - After: "...I shall become Thy Wrath and Thy Flame against Thy foes..."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "God-Emperor... have mercy." {n}The Seneschal's face is drained of all colour, and his gaze, fixed upon the empty resting place of the Warrant, holds a soul-crushing despair. In all the time Abelard has accompanied you, he has never seemed closer to his heart giving out than now.{/n}
  - After: "God-Emperor... have mercy." {n}Abelard is ashen with despair.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "The voices... The voices say the withered dead know no peace. They cannot sleep in their tombs. They suffer, these lost souls... Whatever that means, {name}."
  - After: "The voices say the withered dead suffer... Whatever that means, {name}."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "This is blasphemy against the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}Undying One{/g}. An insult to the Domin. And a dishonour to all of the Bloodspun Web." {n}Kibellah retrieves one of her many knives and slowly draws the blade across her face, leaving a crimson trail in its wake.{/n}
  - After: "Blasphemy against the {g|Encyclopedia:EmperorGlossary}Undying One{/g}." {n}Kibellah cuts her face with a knife.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}The Arbitrator frowns, then speaks in a calm, warning tone.{/n} "Rog— {name} von Valancius, from this moment forward, all your rights, freedoms, incomes, holdings, and status may be called into question at any time." {n}He is silent for a few seconds.{/n} "Not by me, but still... should someone wish to put an end to you..."
  - After: {n}The Arbitrator frowns.{/n} "Rog— {name} von Valancius, your rights are now contestable." {n}A pause.{/n} "Not by me, but..."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai sweeps his gaze across those assembled. His narrow, gaunt face is filled with barely restrained ecstasy and a hazy veil of euphoria creeps over his eyes.{/n} "If only you knew how sweet your terror and fury are... and how much of it there is... Exquisite!"
  - After: {n}Marazhai looks euphoric.{/n} "Your terror and fury... Exquisite!"
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Do not grieve, Aett-Vater! A great deed awaits you: the recovery of the ancient scroll of rights, inscribed by the Allfather's own hand! What a glorious saga, what a thundering legend it will be! And the feast that will follow! That is your wyrd, {name} — do not dream of any other."
  - After: "Do not grieve, Aett-Vater! Recover the Allfather's scroll — a glorious saga! That is your wyrd, {name}."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Gone. The Warrant is... gone." {n}Seberian's voice sounds lifeless as he looks back and forth between you and the empty pedestal, and you see the skin-scrap of your ancestor's face tighten in a futile bid to convey his anger.{/n} "My heir, of all the scum in the Koronus Expanse, only one is capable of such a sacrilege — Trazyn!"
  - After: "The Warrant is... gone." {n}Seberian's face tightens in anger.{/n} "My heir, only one could do this — Trazyn!"
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}The apparition of the xenos dissipates, leaving empty air where the flickering image once stood, and with it the voice of Seberian, who has clearly been speaking for some time now, can be heard.{/n} "...it is time to set aside our quarrels and turn our united strength against a common enemy. The dynasty's Warrant must be restored to its place. Without it, the von Valancius will perish in the darkness. Do you agree to stand together against the enemies of Humanity and the dynasty?"
  - After: {n}The image fades.{/n} "...we must unite. Without the Warrant, the dynasty perishes. Will you stand with me?"
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "Such fervour. If I had need of a second Rogue Trader for my exhibition instead of one, I might even welcome that. But one way or another, you will bring him to me."
  - After: "Such fervour. But you will bring him to me."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "So that's how it is..." {n}Seberian sighs, and his entire metal-threaded body rises and slumps like a giant wave.{/n} "And what do you think about his offer?"
  - After: "So that's how it is..." {n}Seberian sighs.{/n} "What do you think of his offer?"
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: {n}A dry chuckle scrapes like metal on glass.{/n} "It is past time you rid yourself of the illusion of choice."
  - After: {n}A dry chuckle.{/n} "Drop the illusion of choice."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I do not... I do not understand, elantach. Everyone knows who you are. The crew, the retinue. What tragedy is there in the loss of some piece of paper?"
  - After: "I do not understand, elantach. Why mourn some paper?"
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "I have grown bored of watching Seberian attempt to insert himself into an age to which he does not belong. I suspect you feel the same. It is time to set things right. The Warrant will return to your domain, and Seberian will return to the Museion's exhibition. All you need do is travel to the territory of the Yekhmet dynasty, which lies beyond the very spatial gate you are already heading toward. The system's coordinates are already within your mind."
  - After: "Seberian bores me. The Warrant returns to you, he to my Museion. Go to Yekhmet dynasty territory, beyond the gate you approach. The coordinates are in your mind."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "When the time comes, we shall resolve it as befits people of our status, with a duel, or else a game of regicide. Or perhaps you will succeed in convincing me that the dynasty and the protectorate are in safe hands... and I will abandon my claim."
  - After: "Later we'll settle it by duel or regicide. Or prove yourself, and I'll drop my claim."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "The dynasty comes first, my heir. I am glad you understand that."
  - After: "The dynasty comes first, heir. Good."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "Likewise, I shall turn a blind eye to the threats looming over the protectorate as a result of a lack of vigilant oversight."
  - After: "And I'll ignore your lax oversight of the protectorate."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "I had no intention of causing you harm, my heir, and still do not. The God-Emperor knows you might make a worthy vassal yet." {n}Seberian waves a hand casually.{/n} "But enough on that. We have other business."
  - After: "I meant no harm, heir. You may yet be a worthy vassal." {n}He waves.{/n} "Enough. We have business."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "Your Warrant is safe within my Museion, for now. It holds little value to me in itself, like most of your so-called relics. However, as a means to settle a score with a dynasty of thieves who have made a habit of crossing my path..." {n}The Necron lets out a low laugh.{/n} "But, very well. I would be glad to be rid of the Warrant and return it to you, were it not for one problem: its place must be taken by another exhibit. The one that was stolen from me."
  - After: "Your Warrant is safe in my Museion." {n}The Necron laughs.{/n} "I'd return it, but the exhibit stolen from me must take its place."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The moment you speak these words, a familiar figure coalesces from emerald-green light beside the Warrant's resting place, and a voice dripping with mockery sounds within your mind.{/n} "What a striking demonstration of the differences between us. To you, a centuries-old relic is nothing but a dust-covered scrap, left unattended in a pathetic, unsecured storeroom. To me, each of my exhibits is a precious witness to its era, carefully preserved in stasis for millennia to come."
  - After: {n}Trazyn appears in emerald light, mocking.{/n} "To you, a relic is a dusty scrap. To me, a treasure preserved for millennia."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "The way you marvel at my kind's superiority over your own, human, might almost inspire a measure of endearment. In theory. In someone else."
  - After: "Your awe at my superiority is almost endearing. In theory."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "The von Valancius dynasty once stole a relic from me — the Crimson Dance of Khaine. I deemed it only fitting to claim the head of the von Valancius dynasty in exchange. That very same individual whom you, a representative of said dynasty, have now, centuries later, stolen back from me. Are you even capable of appreciating the elegance of the temporal recursion that now endows this object with unique value? I doubt it. But. at the very least, I have attempted to convey the notion."
  - After: "Your dynasty stole the Crimson Dance of Khaine, so I took its head — whom you stole back. That recursion makes him unique. Lost on you, surely."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: {n}Trazyn's smug chuckle makes you flinch.{/n} "Ever since your little escapade in the Museion drew my attention, I have learned a great deal about the scurrying of humans in this region of space. Suffice it to say, a certain portion of that scurrying has piqued my interest. And what interests me is naturally of interest to you, my informant."
  - After: {n}Trazyn chuckles.{/n} "I've watched humans here since your Museion escapade. What interests me interests you, informant."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "A convenient landmark for me. For your own sake, you would do your best to understand what I am speaking of after you depart through the gate."
  - After: "A landmark. You'll understand beyond the gate."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I will... temporarily overlook the Rogue Trader's lack of a {g|Encyclopedia:WarrantGlossary}Warrant{/g}, which would, in essence, mean the revocation of {mf|his|her} high station and all attendant privileges. Let us just rectify this 'minor inconvenience' as swiftly as possible, {name}."
  - After: "I will temporarily overlook the missing {g|Encyclopedia:WarrantGlossary}Warrant{/g}, and {mf|his|her} lost station. Fix this, {name}."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian is silent for several seconds.{/n} "Regret for what has been done is a path to nowhere. Focus on the present, however grim it may appear at this moment."
  - After: {n}A pause.{/n} "Regret leads nowhere. Focus on the present."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian is silent for a long time, clearly deep in thought. When he speaks, his voice sounds quieter and deeper than usual.{/n} "If our expedition ends in failure, if the risk of the dynasty being left without the Warrant becomes too great, you will have to make that bargain. Not for your own sake. For the dynasty's sake. For those who will inherit the Warrant and the title of Rogue Trader after you."
  - After: {n}Seberian speaks quietly.{/n} "If we fail, you must make that bargain. For the dynasty and your heirs."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "The sentiment is mutual, heir."
  - After: "Mutual, heir."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: "A worthy answer. Truly, whatever differences may stand between us, we must not show weakness before the true enemy. Duty to Humanity and to the dynasty outweighs all else."
  - After: "Worthy. No weakness before the true enemy. Duty comes first."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian lets out a low, satisfied chuckle.{/n} "Do not delude yourself. You shall need to work much harder than that to instil fear in my heart."
  - After: {n}He chuckles.{/n} "You'll need more to scare me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Guilt and shame crash down upon you like an avalanche. Once before, you {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}endured a disgrace{/d} you'd long considered the greatest of your life. But the loss of the Warrant humiliates not only you, it humiliates the entire von Valancius dynasty, jeopardising its very existence. Your mouth goes dry, and your heart begins to beat twice as fast within your chest.{/n}
  - After: {n}Shame crushes you, worse than the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}disgrace you once endured{/d}. This endangers the whole dynasty.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The answer to the enigma before your eyes {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}comes to you immediately{/d}. The Warrant could not have vanished on its own. It could only have been stolen. By someone possessed of such staggering power that no amount of precautions could stop them. By someone who has already proven themselves a great thief, having stolen the Rogue Trader himself from the von Valancius dynasty. Trazyn the Infinite.{/n}
  - After: {n}It {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Mind}comes immediately{/d}: the thief who once stole the Rogue Trader himself. Trazyn the Infinite.{/n}
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian's gaze bores into yours and then, receiving no answer, he sighs.{/n} "When the time comes, we shall resume this interrupted conversation. Sooner or later."
  - After: {n}He sighs.{/n} "We'll resume this. Sooner or later."
- **Seberian**
  - Before: {n}Seberian lifts his head as if straining against the weight of his numerous implants, and fixes you with an eye burning with righteous fire.{/n} "Our purpose is clear. Let us find the enemy and repay them according to their misdeeds, heir."
  - After: {n}Seberian's eye burns.{/n} "Let us find the enemy and repay them, heir."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Ashmags! The filthy azhi! {name}, we'll get your Warrant back for you! Just don't forget, shereen: as long as no one knows the relic is missing, no one can use that knowledge against you. So everyone present had best keep their mouths shut."
  - After: "Filthy azhi! {name}, we'll get it back! Keep quiet, all — what no one knows can't be used."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Registering an increased risk of complications of legitimacy. Registering a change in status for the subject {name} von Valancius." {n}Pasqal gives you a long, weighty stare, then his vox rasps.{/n} "I assume this observation to be self-evident, yet protocol demands its utterance: the security classification of this facility is hereby revised to 'untrustworthy.'"
  - After: "Registering legitimacy risk for {name} von Valancius." {n}Pasqal stares.{/n} "Facility rated 'untrustworthy.'"
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Poison-yellow fear and dark-blue anger, they spill so thickly through the air... and these hues blind me to the empty dais. How grateful I am for this blindness, for I could not look upon such a loss without weeping."
  - After: "Fear and anger blind me to the empty dais. I'm grateful."

## GlobalMaps/Colonization/Colonization_Narrative/ColonyChronicles/Dargonus/Dargonus_Part_1/Dargonus_Part_1

- **Player**
  - Before: "What is the cause of the catastrophe?"
  - After: "What caused the catastrophe?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Signal the hives to open the gates — we will not abandon a single person in the wastelands."
  - After: "Open the hive gates — we abandon no one in the wastelands."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Establish labour settlements in the ruins of Scipione 84-249 and relocate the refugees there. They have much work ahead of them to restore their former home."
  - After: "Build labour settlements in Scipione 84-249's ruins and move the refugees there to rebuild."
- **Player**
  - Before: "These commoners think that I would be merciful to those who facilitated the hive's destruction? Eliminate any who would try to enter the cities!"
  - After: "Mercy for those who let the hive fall? Kill any who try to enter the cities!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Argenta, see to it that the Ecclesiarchy does not ignore the laments of the dispossessed."
  - After: "Argenta, make the Ecclesiarchy heed the dispossessed."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Heinrix, set up prohibitive cordons at the perimeter of the hives."
  - After: "Heinrix, set cordons around the hives."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Terrible news from Dargonus, Lord Captain. A subsidiary hive city, Scipione 84-249, has been destroyed in a series of cascading failures. Production has halted, and millions of people have broken their vows of obedience and are fleeing. Many of them are perishing in the wastelands and overloading the transport lines leading to neighbouring hives. The surrounding residential sectors are becoming increasingly agitated by the influx of refugees. What is your directive regarding the distribution of these refugees?"
  - After: "Lord Captain, hive Scipione 84-249 on Dargonus has collapsed. Millions of refugees are fleeing to other hives. Your orders?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is still unclear. The noble houses are casting blame on one another. Agents of the esteemed Achilleas Scalander stationed in Scipione 84-249 died heroically while trying to save the population from this disaster. Their final reports mentioned some vulnerabilities in the industrial sectors of the lower hive but did not go into further detail. All your servants are currently too busy dealing with the consequences of the crisis to investigate its causes."
  - After: "Unclear; the nobles blame each other. Achilleas Scalander's agents died there; their last reports noted lower-hive industrial weaknesses."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The death of Achilleas's agents troubles me — it may not be a coincidence. Until the causes of the disaster can be concretely established, I would avoid letting refugees into other hives — there may be saboteurs among them. I recommend setting up prohibitive cordons, where the refugees can be contained in the wastelands between the hives."
  - After: "Achilleas's agents' deaths may be no coincidence. Saboteurs could hide among refugees. Keep them cordoned in the wastelands."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Emperor bids us to face the often cruel strokes of fate with dignity. If the other hives do not wish to accept the unfortunate victims of this tragedy, then let the victims themselves teach those living in the hives a lesson in resilience and humility. I'm sure that the Ecclesiarchy will aid the refugees in constructing camps to survive out in the wastelands and establish a community of proud desert-dwelling martyrs. Such harsh conditions will be a crucible of fortitude and fearlessness, this tragedy a feat of spirit."
  - After: "If the hives refuse them, let the Ecclesiarchy help them build wasteland camps — a community of proud desert martyrs."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The noble houses are trying to wash their hands of this — how predictable. And yet, it is their duty to see to it that the planet meets its tithe obligation and brings glory and revenue to the treasury in your absence. Let the aristocrats see to the refugees and not stop until every last one of them has been put to work!"
  - After: "The nobles dodge, predictably. Yet the tithe is their duty. Let them put every refugee to work!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I will draft a few orders for my informants on Dargonus."
  - After: "I'll send orders to my Dargonus informants."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "He who dares to remain deaf to the pleas of the destitute shall be branded a traitor to the faith."
  - After: "Whoever ignores the destitute is a traitor to the faith."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Not a single miscreant responsible for failing the Rogue Trader shall ever find peace on Dargonus!"
  - After: "No miscreant who failed the Rogue Trader shall find peace!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your mercy truly knows no bounds, Lord Captain! They shall pray for you every watch!"
  - After: "Boundless mercy, Lord Captain! They'll pray for you every watch!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Dargonus's nobles took no pleasure in distributing the refugees. Some of them have found their way into the personal service of the nobles, thankful to receive a nutribar and a mat to rest on for four hours between shifts. Others could only attain the most gruelling jobs at the manufactorums and service stations. They may be oppressed, but they have survived, a diaspora scattered across the hives of Dargonus.{/n}
  - After: {n}The nobles grudgingly took the refugees as servants and labourers. Oppressed, but alive.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The refugees quickly realised that they would not find shelter in the hives and dispersed across the wastelands. A harsh lesson in discipline has been delivered to the capital.{/n}
  - After: {n}Denied shelter, the refugees scattered into the wastelands.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Many of the Ecclesiarchy's priests sought to share in this burden with the poor souls, coming to their villages and preaching to them about the righteousness of hard work. Some priests have even chosen to stay in the camps permanently, where the desert cults of Aconyte martyrs have begun to gather around them, glorifying the Lord Captain for granting them the right to suffer for the glory of the God-Emperor.{/n}
  - After: {n}Priests joined the camps. Aconyte martyr cults arose, praising the Lord Captain for the right to suffer for the God-Emperor.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Van Calox's agents have run a thorough investigation to identify many of the refugees who had managed to reach and hide in the hives. Remembering how the Rogue Trader had treated their relatives and neighbours, they could have plotted their revenge... if only they hadn't been expelled into the wastelands.{/n}
  - After: {n}Van Calox's agents expelled refugees hiding in the hives before they could plot revenge.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The local inhabitants of the arcologies were less than amenable to being deprived of their jobs and gave their desperate guests a rather hostile welcome. The Scipions were forced to fight back, rallying behind their leaders, the workers' foremen. The streets are awash with violence.{/n}
  - After: {n}Locals attacked the newcomers; Scipions fought back under their foremen.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Those Scipions who still managed to sneak into and hide in the hives harbour a strong resentment against the Rogue Trader who condemned their relatives and neighbours to death. They have vowed not to forget their dead.{/n}
  - After: {n}Scipions hiding in the hives vow never to forget the dead the Rogue Trader doomed.{/n}

## GlobalMaps/Colonization/Colonization_Narrative/ColonyChronicles/Dargonus/Dargonus_Part_2

- **Player**
  - Before: "How do they survive in the wastelands? And why do they reject my rule?"
  - After: "How do they survive out there? Why reject my rule?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "We will do as Kibellah says. Lay down bait and poison the Vandals."
  - After: "As Kibellah says: bait and poison the Vandals."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Let the foremen negotiate with the Vandals. We can spend some thrones and avoid these problems altogether."
  - After: "Let the foremen negotiate with the Vandals. Some thrones will avoid trouble."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If they are so tenacious and militant, let them guard the hives in exchange for a small tribute."
  - After: "If they're so militant, let them guard the hives for a small tribute."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Destroy these engine heretics and show them no mercy!"
  - After: "Destroy these engine heretics without mercy!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal, draft a message to the Omnissian renegades. Let them serve the acquisition of Knowledge."
  - After: "Pasqal, message the Omnissian renegades. Let them serve Knowledge."
- **Player**
  - Before: "We will follow Yrliet's advice. Spread rumours about a great prize of some sort among the Vandals. And when they are done fighting among themselves, conduct a raid and finish them off."
  - After: "Yrliet's way: rumour a prize among the Vandals, then raid the survivors."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Lady Cassia is right. We should help them and give the aristocrats a real threat that will keep them in their place."
  - After: "Lady Cassia is right. Help them, and give the aristocrats a real threat."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I wish to hear what my advisors have to say."
  - After: "What say my advisors?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is... strange to teach you the methods we employ to fight against you."
  - After: "Strange, teaching you how we fight you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am still naive of even the basics of these games played by the powerful. But my intuition tells me that this is a winning strategy."
  - After: "I'm naive in power games, but this feels right."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A meeting with the leaders of the Engine Vandals was organised through the mediation of the foreman clan. They have gladly accepted the dynasty's proposal to serve.{/n}
  - After: {n}Through the foremen, the Engine Vandals agreed to serve.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A rumour about a heavy weapon shipment getting lost somewhere between two hives was spread among the Engine Vandals clans. A fight over seven armoured trucks, rumoured to contain cargo that would provide enough firepower to breach the defences of any hive, broke out in the wastelands. When the depleted winners had finally cut open the trucks' lining, the only thing waiting there for them was a squad of enforcers, enraged by three cycles of sitting in tight, dark spaces.{/n}
  - After: {n}A rumour of lost weapon trucks set the Vandal clans fighting. The winners found only furious enforcers inside.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If the Engine Vandals have managed to tame the ancient machine spirits, then that means there are technomats or even Tech-Priests among their ranks. That renders them... negotiable. It would be efficient to utilise such renegades instead of disposing of them. A promise of reward for every piece of technology found in the wastelands of Dargonus and returned to the dynasty will ensure their obedience and tractability."
  - After: "Taming machine spirits implies Tech-Priests among them. Negotiable. Reward each relic recovered from the wastelands and they will obey."
- **(conversation owner)**

In this way, they would be of use for returning the lost relics, and the Order of the Hammer would be satisfied with a just verdict."
  - After: "Penance: send them to find Saint Cognatius's relics and learn Saint Keefe's ways."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There was a similar theological dispute at the Fifth Ophelian Council, and the conflict between the two cults was resolved in sacred duel. Twenty champions from each side came forward, both sides vowing to accept the victor's teachings if they lost. I propose to invoke the council's edict and settle the dispute in the same way."
  - After: "The Fifth Ophelian Council settled such disputes by sacred duel, losers converting. Let's do likewise."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Hmm... They believe that their faith is superior? Then let them prove it. Subject them to a severe test of faith. If they survive it, they will have proven their steadfastness. Even if the Order of the Hammer does not accept their arguments, it will be easier for them to recognise the newcomers' right to interpret the way of Saint Cognatius if they prove it with their own blood and pain."
  - After: "Superior faith? Let a severe trial prove it, in blood."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Order of the Hammer thanked the Lord Captain for {mf|his|her} protection and staying true to the agreements between them.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Order of the Hammer thanked the Lord Captain for keeping {mf|his|her} word.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}One hundred Malpians have volunteered to undergo the trial of faith. Sixty-two have survived, proving the steadfastness of their beliefs and earning the respect of the Order of the Hammer.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sixty-two of a hundred Malpians survived, earning the Order of the Hammer's respect.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Four dozen fighters clashed in a bitter struggle. The forces were an equal match, and thus the duel righteous. By the end, only the indomitable Hectarchius, the prelate of the Order of the Hammer, was left standing, and, honouring their vow, the Malpians bowed down to him and accepted the teachings of Saint Nicomedes.{/n}
  - After: {n}Only Hectarchius, the Order of the Hammer's prelate, stood at the end. The Malpians accepted Saint Nicomedes's teachings.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The indomitable teaching of Philopimenes of Malpi laid down deep roots upon the hard soil of Foulstone. The followers of his teachings were zealous and determined.{/n}
  - After: {n}Philopimenes of Malpi's teaching took zealous root on Foulstone.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Malpians have renounced the concept of possession. Their vows are true and similar to ours, but they lack humility and reverence for the dead. The Bloodspun Web could embrace their leaders. We could teach them. We could soothe the turmoil."
  - After: "The Malpians renounce possession, like us, but lack humility. The Bloodspun Web could take and teach their leaders."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "From this day forth, these people serve the Undying One."
  - After: "They now serve the Undying One."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A grim and solemn procession of preachers came aboard and made a vocal renunciation of their former lives. Disturbed by the loss of their spiritual leaders, the refugees quieted down and no longer defied the Order of the Hammer.{/n}
  - After: {n}The preachers came aboard. Leaderless, the refugees stopped defying the Order of the Hammer.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Let them show the weight of their words and teachings."
  - After: "Let them prove their words."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Putting forth two dozen wise men from each side, the two cults have sought to find a common interpretation of the way of Saint Cognatius. They may not have achieved dogmatic unity, but they have at least managed to find a way to coexist on the same world.{/n}
  - After: {n}Wise men from both cults met. No unity, but coexistence.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I will arrange for the duelling grounds to be prepared in the monastery."
  - After: "I'll prepare the duelling grounds."

This spiritual feat depleted Prelate Hectarchius's strength, and he peacefully departed for the Emperor's Throne shortly after the sermon's conclusion."
  - After: "After a vision on the vox-spire's throne, he preached for three days of Saint Cognatius reborn from relics, then died."

  - After: {n}The monks long lamented the Crucible's unjust handover to the Tech-Priests.{/n}

- **Player**

  - Before: "What think my officers and advisors?"
  - After: "What think my advisors?"

  - After: "Servitorise them all, as the Tech-Priests say."

- **Player**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, the Crucible's great sculpting is underway — Foulstone is being transformed right before our eyes into a fertile world with lush groves and clean water. However, there is evidence that the Crucible has also created... humans."
  - After: "Lord Captain, the Crucible is making Foulstone fertile. It has also created... humans."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There is a split among the faithful — though many call it a miracle sent by the Emperor Himself and want to quickly put the Touched to work, a part of the population is frightened by these soulless creatures born from the ancient machine. They demand that the planet's learned men intervene in the great sculpting and find a way to stop the production of the Touched."
  - After: "The faithful are split: some see the Touched as a miracle, others fear them and want the sculpting stopped."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "They do not appear to pose a threat — the autopsy of several specimens has shown that they are physiologically identical to ordinary humans. No traces of corruption or xeno-influence were found either. However, their obedience is a double-edged sword. They obey any orders without knowing or caring who gives them. And thus, nothing prevents a cunning intruder from bending them to their will, creating an army of obedient slaves or spies at their disposal."
  - After: "They're ordinary humans, uncorrupted. But they obey anyone; an enemy could make them slaves or spies."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The disciples of the Malpian teaching believe that the souls of the Touched are too pure to cause harm to anyone. Those adherents of simplicity and purity have taken a liking to these meek and open-hearted creatures."
  - After: "Malpian disciples think the Touched too pure to harm anyone."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I will draft a detailed plan of the ceremony and hand it over to the prelate."
  - After: "I'll draft the ceremony plan."
- **(conversation owner)**

Arrange a public ceremony of tonsure to initiate the Touched into the Order of the Hammer and a service dedicated to reading parables about the acts of Saint Cognatius and his followers."
  - After: "Saint Cognatius's relic begot them, so they please the Emperor! Tonsure them into the Order of the Hammer publicly."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Why don't you make the first move and assemble a mighty force from these Touched ones? If they are so obedient and diligent, then they will make fine troops. Assign a loyal commander to each squad to keep an eye on them, and these strange people will turn from a threat into defenders of the Imperium."
  - After: "Make an army of them. With loyal commanders, the threat becomes defenders of the Imperium."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lack of will? Registering a high probability of manufacturing failure within the Crucible's sacred processes. It is recommended to dispose of the finished batch of units and halt production of new ones. The algorithm of the great sculpting requires further examination."
  - After: "Lack of will? Probable manufacturing failure. Recommend disposing of the batch and halting production."
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "Pick commanders ready to die for you, Aett-Vater."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Touched did not resist their newfound fate — nor any other order, for that matter. They were not particularly skilled at warfare, but they were obedient, dutiful, and most importantly, indifferent to their own deaths. Soon, the first regiments were taken to orbit on voidships and dispatched to other areas of the protectorate, as well as to the Rogue Trader's own flagship.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Touched obeyed. Poor but fearless soldiers, they shipped out across the protectorate and to the flagship.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priests' investigation uncovered a number of defects in the operation of the birthing vats within the Crucible. It was these defects that caused such strange obedience within the Touched. The proposition of making improvements to a sacred relic filled the Tech-Priests with the most profound dread, and thus Foulstone was left without its taciturn workers. However, the priceless knowledge extracted by the servants of the Omnissiah was a great reward in and of itself.{/n}
  - After: {n}Birthing-vat defects caused the obedience. Fearing to alter a relic, the Tech-Priests halted it, gaining priceless knowledge.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The servants of the Omnissiah have proposed a pre-emptive measure against this threat: subject the Touched to Servitude Imperpituis and inhibit them with binharic vows of obedience."
  - After: "The Tech-Priests propose Servitude Imperpituis with binharic obedience vows."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Tech-Priests who serve the Crucible came upon birthing vats built into the relic. The machine is constantly growing new Touched within them."
  - After: "The relic has birthing vats. It keeps growing Touched."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The people's wariness of the Touched never went away. A number of reports have described cases of persecution and even violence toward the Crucible's creations — such was the rabble's fear of them.{/n}
  - After: {n}Fear lingered; some Touched were persecuted and attacked.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "From the mouth of the relic came several thousand people who, speaking an archaic form of Low Gothic, demanded to be given orders. They cultivate land, build houses and production facilities with obedience and, in general, have a remarkable range of skills and knowledge. However, it seems that these people completely lack their own free will, and for this, the monks have named them Touched."
  - After: "Thousands emerged from the relic in archaic Low Gothic, demanding orders. Skilled, obedient, will-less. The monks call them Touched."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The knowledge will be extracted by any means necessary."
  - After: "The knowledge will be extracted."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The heads of the Touched were opened, and inhibiting engrams were implanted within to ensure that these obedient creature would follow no malicious commands.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Touched were implanted with inhibiting engrams.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The spiritual tutelage of the people of Foulstone was entrusted to the quiet, compliant, and withdrawn creatures known as the Touched. They did not preach or root out impurity, and they even seemed to be unaware of their high status. They simply worked without saying a word, and thousands of believers took vows of silence and obedience to follow their example.{/n}
  - After: {n}The silent Touched became spiritual guides. Thousands took vows of silence to follow them.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The public induction of the Touched along with their diligent service eventually solidified their image in the minds of the people as the executors of Saint Cognatius's will sent to the faithful to ease their burdens during the great sculpting. Any concerns about the Touched possibly posing a danger were completely dispelled.{/n}
  - After: {n}The people came to see the Touched as Saint Cognatius's servants. All fears vanished.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Prelate Inocrant even suggested to elevate these... dimmer subjects of your dynasty to spiritual guides. Inocrant finds that an immaculate heart is a better shepherd than a sharp mind."
  - After: "Inocrant suggested making these... dimmer subjects spiritual guides. A pure heart shepherds better than a sharp mind."

## GlobalMaps/Colonization/Colonization_Narrative/ColonyChronicles/Foulstone/Foulstone_Part_5/Foulstone_Part_5_dialogue
