  - Before: "Lord Captain, the situation on Foulstone requires your attention. One of the servants tasked with the Crucible's maintenance has declared publicly that he has been liberated of all worldly concerns, for he is none other than the reincarnation of Saint Cognatius. There are some extremely questionable reports claiming that he has performed miracles. Supported by a congregation garnered by preaching, he has asked for Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s permission to depart from Foulstone with the Crucible in tow so that he may continue Saint Cognatius's work and use the relic to transform worlds, ones true to the faith of the Imperium, into lush, splendorous gardens."
  - After: "Lord Captain, a Foulstone Crucible servant claims to be Saint Cognatius reborn. He asks Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s leave to take the Crucible and make faithful worlds gardens."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Archenemy's lies take on many guises — but the Emperor's miracles are a hundredfold stronger. On more than a few occasions, He has bestowed epiphanies upon the faithful, even those of the humblest origin. I myself bear the name of a poor orphan who was granted miraculous powers by His grace. So, give me time, and I will find you the most loyal agents to escort Brother Pure-Voice on his travels. They will keep him safe if he is pure, or punish him should they sense deceit in his words. But I have a feeling that his rebirth is a true wonder!"
  - After: "The Emperor blesses the humble. My agents will escort Brother Pure-Voice — guarding him if pure, punishing him if false."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Pure-Voiced Prophet was mobbed by an entourage of professional beggars and cripples. Upon seeing how many people need him on Foulstone, the saint reincarnate gave up on his ambitions of spreading the faith to new worlds. He vowed not to leave the planet for as long as there remained even a single soul in need of his help. He only left Foulstone once — to bless the Lord Captain's ship and counsel {mf|him|her} to carry on Saint Cognatius's holy cause.{/n}
  - After: {n}Mobbed by beggars, the Prophet stayed on Foulstone, leaving once to bless the Lord Captain's ship and urge {mf|him|her} on.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "They'll make his disappearance look like ascension."
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "Gladly, shereen. Simpletons love feeling needed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'll get to it immediately! I will choose the best people for this task, the most devoted!"
  - After: "At once! Only the most devoted!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Tibor Hyke, a technomat from Footfall. He now prefers to be called 'Brother Pure-Voice.' An unremarkable commoner with no family. Gaunt, unkempt, covered in scabs from working the Crucible."
  - After: "Tibor Hyke, a Footfall technomat, now 'Brother Pure-Voice.' A gaunt, scabbed nobody."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have had ample experience with saintly saviours like him in the past. Whatever great cause they proclaim as their mission, they genuinely, naively believe that people really do need them. If we round up enough orphans and lepers who would trip over themselves to beg our prophet for salvation, he will soon forget all about the Crucible and his holy mission. I know a few guilds of professional beggars who would be delighted to offer their services to us."

- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Pure-Voiced Prophet was arrested and mercilessly executed in front of the people. The execution reminded the Rogue Trader's faithful subjects about the virtues of obedience but stoked anger among the rabble.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It goes without saying that such a generous gift to the Koronus Expanse could bring great renown to Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but at a heavy cost. Foulstone would turn back into a wasteland and you would lose the prestige that comes with having charge over such a valuable relic."
  - After: "Renown for Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but Foulstone would revert to wasteland and you'd lose the relic's prestige."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Undying One does not release the souls that have come to Him. This man is either lying or misguided. An experienced spinner will help him see the truth... or repent the deception."
  - After: "The Undying One releases no souls. He lies. A spinner will show him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Let our duty be done. The Undying One is duty. The Undying One is death."
  - After: "The Undying One is duty. The Undying One is death."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Pure-Voiced Prophet disappeared in a single night. They found only a strange image of a labyrinth inscribed in his blood on the floor of his chamber. His followers gladly believed that this mysterious sign marked the ascension of "Saint Cognatius" to the Emperor, and made the cell a place of worship.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Prophet vanished, leaving a blood-drawn labyrinth. His cell became a shrine to his ascension.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

He never left his maintenance post, never rested, barely ever slept, fasting and living off stimulants and condensate from the relic's cooling circuit. Then he started having 'revelations' and eventually 'saw the truth'... or he went completely insane. His sermons are directed at commoners, appealing to them for humility and mercy. He often speaks about his former life as a saint, and many of these tales match known legends about Saint Cognatius. No anarchical pronunciations or radical deviations from the Creed have been found in his words... yet."
  - After: "He fixated on the Crucible, sleepless, living on stimulants and coolant. Then 'revelations'... or madness. He preaches humility; his tales match Cognatius's legends. No heresy... yet."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Pure-Voiced Prophet mysteriously vanished. Rumours of his miraculous ascension immediately spread among the rabble, and soon there were those claiming to have witnessed the event.{/n}

  - Before: {n}The Order of the Hammer is pleased that the suspicious prophet troubles the faithful no longer.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Order of the Hammer is pleased.{/n}

He now studies the art of humility, and his words now show far greater obedience and spread fewer alleged revelations. The prelate permitted the preacher to lead a mission of pilgrimage to the Lord Captain's ship so he could offer prayers for {mf|his|her} health and bless {mf|his|her} ship.{/n}

## GlobalMaps/Colonization/Colonization_Narrative/ColonyChronicles/Janus/Janus_Part_1/Janus_Part_1_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "What do we know about these 'retches'?"
  - After: "What of these 'retches'?"

  - After: "Move the retches to separate agri-complexes. We'll study them."

  - Before: "I take these unfortunate souls under my protection. They are victims of a mutation, not villains."
  - After: "I protect them. Victims, not villains."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will suffer no mutant to live. Hunt them down to the last man."
  - After: "I suffer no mutant to live. Hunt them all."

  - Before: "Let them atone for their flaw with labour."
  - After: "Let them atone through labour."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Take the required number of these retches to be studied by the Adeptus Mechanicus. Destroy the rest."
  - After: "Give some to the Mechanicus for study. Destroy the rest."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Take the required number of these retches for study and let the others work. Cassia, please share your knowledge of the Genetors' craft with my servants."
  - After: "Study some; the rest work. Cassia, share your Genetor knowledge."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, there are alarming reports coming from Janus. A number of strange mutations have been spotted among the population in remote agri-complexes. Aside from the obvious disfigurement and the subsequent estrangement, these mutants — called 'retches' by the rest of the colonists — are coming together to practise a primitive form of religion involving ritual worship of the land. While they display no disobedience or hostility, their very existence is concerning."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, disfigured mutants called 'retches' have appeared on Janus. They worship the land. Not hostile, but concerning."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The mysterious xenos advisors you appointed to oversee the planet have shown unexpected interest in the mutants' vulgar religious practices. They advise against persecuting the retches, but instead they recommend segregating them in separate residential sectors and placing them under observation."
  - After: "Your xenos advisors are intrigued. They advise segregation and observation."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Governor Vyatt suggested the mutation may have been caused by one of her genetic experiments aimed to 'improve' the working populace. She notes the docility of the specimens and asks not to treat them as abominations that would otherwise be purged."
  - After: "Governor Vyatt blames her worker-'improving' experiments. She asks the docile mutants be spared."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Janus nobility humbly awaits your decision."
  - After: "The Janus nobility awaits your decision."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Having to live in proximity to the retches disturbs the good, honest serfs and leads to outbursts of aggression and violence.{/n}
  - After: {n}Living near retches stirs the serfs to violence.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Rogue Trader's servants graciously accepted information on the mysterious Genetor arts from Lady Navigator Cassia's own hands. They started an inquest to discover the nature of the mutant strain. The retches' twisted flesh revealed its secrets on the autopsy table.{/n}
  - After: {n}With Cassia's lore, autopsies revealed the strain's secrets.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The wise Magos Biologis proceeded to study the degenerative genetic branch. The fruits of their research will be presented to the von Valancius dynasty.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Magos Biologis studied the strain for the von Valancius dynasty.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Their mutations cause the loss of skin pigment and the shedding of hair. Some have started developing a translucent third eyelid similar to that of reptiles, others have succumbed to progressive atrophy of the larynx, causing the loss of human speech. At the same time their tendons become denser and more elastic, providing increased endurance and load resistance."
  - After: "They lose pigment and hair; some grow third eyelids or lose speech. Their tendons strengthen."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I feel these mon-keigh have been touched by something wondrous."
  - After: "These mon-keigh have been touched by something wondrous."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "May the cleansing be calculated and rationally executed."
  - After: "May the cleansing be rational."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I saw your agents' pict-recordings, the signs these mon-keigh leave behind, their idols. And I cannot deny a connection, though a pathetic and extremely abstract one, to... the symbols of my people. Their guttural prayers echo the sounds of the Children of Asuryan's speech. The probability of them having come into such close contact with our civilisation is non-existent, yet they are still somehow connected. Protect these people, resettle them to distant abodes where they will not be harmed for their peculiarities. And keep watch — someday the truth may be revealed."
  - After: "Their idols faintly echo... my people's symbols, their prayers the Children of Asuryan's speech. Impossible, yet connected. Protect them, resettle them, and watch."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This mutation has not been properly studied and is missing from the catalogue. I am not registering a basis for delaying the commencement of immediate genetic purification. I recommend launching a thorough investigation into the genetic make-up of this forbidden strain."
  - After: "Uncatalogued mutation. Purify immediately, after studying the strain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The blessed sanction of the Imperium does not grace these mutants, but nor does it declare their existence anathema. Should we sentence them without further study? There are mutants whose existence is fully sanctioned, such as Ogryns, Ratlings, Pariahs, Pelagers, Felinids, or Troths. Our library had many treatises on the Genetors' craft, and I could impart some of that knowledge to your servants... purely theoretical, of course."
  - After: "The Imperium neither sanctions nor condemns them; Ogryns and Ratlings are sanctioned mutants. I could share some Genetor theory... purely theoretical."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The members of the Magos Biologis you tasked with healing Janus have found the mutation to be missing from the catalogue and recommend studying it and eradicating it immediately afterward."
  - After: "The Magos Biologis say: study it, then eradicate it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "As for their barbaric religion, they are deifying both the soil and Janus itself. To them, working in agri-complexes is a form of worship, which has had a positive impact on productivity."
  - After: "They worship the soil; farming as prayer boosts productivity."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The retches are commonly ostracised due to their grotesque appearance. There haven't been too many cases of mob justice yet, but they will become commonplace after the mutation's deformities become more obvious. The retches tend to form groups with similarly afflicted people, their average level of intellect is low. They all belong to the labour caste and communicate among themselves using a primitive vernacular of their own invention."
  - After: "Shunned, they face growing mob violence. Dim labourers, they cluster and speak their own crude tongue."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I hope my House will not judge me for this."
  - After: "I hope my House won't judge me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The mutants were resettled to distant agri-complexes where their unorthodox appearance will not put them in danger of being massacred by the serfs.{/n}
  - After: {n}The mutants were moved to distant, safe agri-complexes.{/n}

  - After: "Isolate the region and research it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Troubling news has arrived from Janus, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. While digging an irrigation ditch, workers found a xeno-obelisk made of unknown material. It was delivered to a laboratorium and subjected to a number of tests, one of which caused... a reaction. The obelisk generated a low-frequency vibration, and the events that followed were catastrophic."
  - After: "Bad news from Janus, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. A dug-up xeno-obelisk vibrated under testing, with catastrophic results."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am sending specialists to Janus capable of forcing compliance."
  - After: "Sending specialists in compliance."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Chem-Princes are hastily summoning militias and getting ready to start a purifying crusade. They await Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s blessing."
  - After: "The Chem-Princes await Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s blessing to purge it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The esteemed Ultrequisitors are gathering outlaws and fortune-hunters for an expedition into the heart of the region. They assume a priceless trove of xenomechanisms is waiting for them inside."
  - After: "The Ultrequisitors plan an expedition for xenomechanisms."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Adeptus Mechanicus recommend we fence off the afflicted area. According to their hypothesis, this anomaly is the world's attempt at self-recovery and therefore should be studied, not interrupted."
  - After: "The Mechanicus say fence it off: the world is healing itself."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The tip of the spear was comprised of Skitarii maniples armed with radium carbines, phosphex bombs, and other equally fearsome weaponry. The land that they left in their wake resembled the scarlet wastes of sacred Mars.{/n}
  - After: {n}Skitarii with radium and phosphex left a Mars-like scarlet waste.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The retch was thoroughly interrogated, and so were dozens of other captive mutants. What little they were able to tell was of no significant value — most of it was nonsensical peasant superstition, although all the retches as one claimed that if the afflicted region was left alone, it would not expand. This assertion was soon confirmed, and the neighbouring agri-complexes soon resumed normal operation.{/n}
  - After: {n}The retches babbled superstition, but swore the region won't spread if left alone. It didn't.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The vegetation demonstrated a remarkable ability for wild growth — it took the plants only two days to overrun the agri-complexes in the region. Extinct species of local megafauna have been spotted in the newly formed jungle, aggressive and acting in unnatural cohesion."
  - After: "A jungle overran the agri-complexes in two days. Extinct megafauna roam it, unnaturally coordinated."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We purged most of the miscreants as per your orders. Only a few dozen at most managed to sneak into the region."
  - After: "We purged most. A few dozen slipped in."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In accordance with your decree protecting the retch populace, no one attempted to detain them. As a result, almost a thousand specimens flooded into the region."
  - After: "Per your decree, none were stopped. Nearly a thousand went in."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Some were stopped by the watchmen appointed by your order. Unfortunately, about a hundred still made their way into the region."
  - After: "About a hundred got past your watchmen."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Governor Vyatt relayed a message that neither she nor her retinue understand the nature of this anomaly but are deeply concerned and advise its immediate eradication."
  - After: "Governor Vyatt is baffled and urges eradication."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The xenos you allowed to stay on Janus advised your servants to abstain from visiting the region and then ceased virtually all communication."
  - After: "Your xenos guests warned us off, then went silent."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Janus's natural world is rising up? It is a lucky coincidence that the planet boasts experts who specialise in both controlling and destroying life. Reports from the Magos Biologis chapel make no mention of storing weapons of mass destruction, but I have no doubt they possess some. They always do. I see no reason not to let them use them against all this, whatever it is."
  - After: "Nature rising? The Magos Biologis surely hide weapons of mass destruction. Let them use them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Deployment of fortified research stations in the affected sectors is recommended. The benefit of gathering more information justifies the increased casualty rate among personnel."
  - After: "Fortified research stations. Knowledge justifies casualties."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The retches know more about this pestilent growth than we do, something we must quickly rectify. We should capture some of these mutants and force them to cooperate — that way we can learn what it is we are dealing with."
  - After: "The retches know more. Capture some and make them talk."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The scouts who ventured into the heart of the afflicted region discovered ancient xenos creations emerging from the ground. The jungle reacted to the incursion by expanding and swallowing up some of the neighbouring agri-complexes.{/n}
  - After: {n}Scouts found xenos ruins rising. The jungle grew, swallowing agri-complexes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Fortified observation stations were set up in the largest clusters of ruins. The priceless data and artefacts collected there were paid for with the lives of the many watchmen who fought against the onslaught of Janus's enraged wilds.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ruin stations yielded priceless finds, paid for in watchmen's lives.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To learn how the retches are connected to the phenomena occurring in the local biota, the only reliable method is to perform dissections on several specimens. To examine their brains in exhaustive detail, documenting every step, and to comprehend the effect the anomaly has on them. Such investigations shall bring us closer to the truth and to an understanding of Janus's true nature."
  - After: "Dissect some retches and study their brains. It will reveal Janus's true nature."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am confident that the laboratories of the Magos Biologis can provide all that is necessary for an empirical investigation."
  - After: "The Magos Biologis labs have all we need."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Before long, the Genetors reported their initial findings. In the very first retch examined and subjected to vivisection, they discovered modified regions of the brain that serve to establish an unidentified connection with the planet's flora and fauna.{/n}
  - After: {n}Vivisection revealed retch brain regions linked to the planet's life.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A series of anomalies were recorded in the Epsilon II Majoris region — it is almost like Janus itself is fighting us there. Many logistical chains have been disrupted. The only people who visit the uncontrolled territory are the retches fleeing deeper into the region in greater and greater numbers. The observers report strange fires in the sky at night, completely imperceptible to the augurs."
  - After: "In Epsilon II Majoris, Janus itself seems to fight us. Supplies are cut. Retches flock there; strange night fires evade the augurs."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We do not know. It is as if they all received a signal telling them to abandon their work and rush deep into the afflicted territory."
  - After: "Unknown. As if a signal called them all in."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The rebelling wilds will soon become a scorched wasteland. A job well done, I say."
  - After: "Scorched waste soon. Good work."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "May the Omnissiah be merciful to the souls of those who will give their lives in the name of obtaining Knowledge."
  - After: "Omnissiah, have mercy on those who die for Knowledge."

## GlobalMaps/Colonization/Colonization_Narrative/ColonyChronicles/Janus/Janus_Part_3/Janus_Part_3

- **Player**
  - Before: "Let Governor Vyatt deal with the problem"
  - After: "Let Governor Vyatt handle it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Idira, ensure the enactment of the Ritual of Silence."
  - After: "Idira, enact the Ritual of Silence."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Argenta, invite the esteemed specialists to Janus."
  - After: "Argenta, invite the specialists."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell Muaran that the limits of my hospitality are not boundless, and that he should seek to solve this problem post-haste."
  - After: "Tell Muaran my hospitality has limits. Solve this."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Jae, find your xenowhisperers and have them exorcise the spirits."
  - After: "Jae, send your xenowhisperers."
- **Player**
  - Before: "We will get by with our usual methods — by fire and sword!"
  - After: "Fire and sword, as usual!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is spawning these wraiths? Is it the corrupted sector?"
  - After: "Is the corrupted sector spawning them?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do we know about these wraiths?"
  - After: "What are these wraiths?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, Janus is reporting about a disaster — ghostly xenos figures that appear at dusk and go away at dawn. In a ravenous swarm, they attack one agricultural facility each night, freezing everything they touch. The attacks take place in the complexes closest to the uncontrolled sector of the planet, where nature itself has turned against us."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, xenos ghosts swarm Janus nightly, freezing agri-facilities near the corrupted sector."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Governor Vyatt claims that she is capable of dealing with this herself. Her servants are already getting ready to conduct... some sort of procedure that will pacify the spirits."
  - After: "Governor Vyatt will pacify the spirits herself. Some... procedure."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The moon above the corrupted sector of Janus turned red. Thousands of serfs, rounded up by Vistenza's servants, became part of her "procedure," their blood spilling onto the soil and mixing into the world's rivers.{/n}
  - After: {n}The moon turned red. Thousands of serfs bled for Vistenza's "procedure."{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}At the appointed time, dozens of psykers around Janus started a rite known as the Ritual of Silence. Surprisingly, no catastrophe followed... none visible to the naked eye, at least.{/n}
  - After: {n}Psykers performed the Ritual of Silence. No visible catastrophe followed.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A group of haggard priests, dressed in holy robes and accompanied by a retinue of repentant flagellants, arrived on Janus. Armed with scriptures and lasguns, they led their flock into battle against the inhuman wraiths.{/n}
  - After: {n}Priests and flagellants arrived and led the faithful against the wraiths.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Locals have called the obelisks installed in the agri-complexes a blessed miracle. The energy resonance of the obelisks has formed intangible domes providing shelter against the wraiths.{/n}
  - After: {n}The obelisks' resonance domes shelter the agri-complexes. Locals call it a miracle.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is likely. They gather at its borders at the break of dawn and whirl in a wild dance, howling and destroying all living things, then disperse into thousands of fading flashes. The agricultural facilities that happen to be in the way of their dance fall into disrepair."
  - After: "Likely. They dance at its borders, killing everything, ruining facilities in their path."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Not much. They are incorporeal and difficult to discern, but they happen to have Aeldari features. The spirits draw the warmth out of humans, plants, and inanimate objects, but it seems that they do not hunt consciously, but rather they simply do not notice anything in their way. At dawn, they dissolve into mist. The wraiths also differ among themselves — some are as dark as the void, and others shine like the stars in the night sky."
  - After: "Incorporeal, Aeldari-featured. They drain warmth mindlessly. Some void-dark, some starlit."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Instead of relying on wicked ways to solve these problems, it would be better to turn to our good priests. There are skilled exorcists in the Ecclesiarchy who know how to drive out dark spirits."
  - After: "Better our priests than wicked ways. The Ecclesiarchy has exorcists."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "When dealing with xenos, one should be prepared for the manifestation of all sorts of ominous mysteries. There is a whole caste of specialists among the Cold Traders who use rituals to expel spirits from xeno-artefacts. Perhaps we should ask these xenowhisperers?"
  - After: "Cold Trader xenowhisperers expel spirits from artefacts. Ask them?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "After... certain events on board, I became interested in ghosts. I bought a book on Footfall — an illegal one, of course — that describes a so-called Ritual of Silence. It's said to be able to pacify violent spirits on the scale of an entire world, but... I can't vouch for the safety of this ritual."
  - After: "An illegal book from Footfall describes a world-wide Ritual of Silence. It may not be safe."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Without a doubt, the things your subjects saw were daemons, whose twisted image drove their ignorant minds to insanity.{/n}
  - After: {n}Daemons, surely, driving your subjects mad.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A group of suspicious characters covered in talismans arrived on Janus. After seeing the dance of ghosts first-hand, they conferred, and then made a short trip into the jungle. They later returned, their numbers diminished, loaded with ancient Aeldari obelisks stolen from the ruins.{/n}
  - After: {n}Talismaned strangers entered the jungle. Fewer returned, carrying stolen Aeldari obelisks.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After arming themselves and rousing their spirits with rotgut, squads in the employ of the agricultural facilities' various rulers gathered to fight the incorporeal xenos. Alas, conventional weapons proved to be wholly powerless against spirits, but it seems that the sheer number of resulting deaths caused such a strong psychic resonance that many of the wraiths dissipated or retreated.{/n}
  - After: {n}Drunk militias fought the wraiths uselessly, but their mass deaths' psychic resonance dispersed many.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Muaran, in all his arrogance, did not condescend to answer. However, mysterious obelisks, apparently taken from the Aeldari ruins, were found inside the endangered agricultural facilities a few cycles later.{/n}
  - After: {n}Muaran didn't answer. Later, Aeldari obelisks appeared in the endangered facilities.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}An invisible force pushed the wraiths away from the structures, stopped their horrifying dance, and shielded the Lord Captain's subjects from the rampage of the xenos.{/n}
  - After: {n}An invisible force drove the wraiths away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Fortunately, not too many facilities were damaged — our irreconcilable struggle has moved the borders of the affected sector. The important production lines have survived."
  - After: "Few facilities were damaged. Key production survived."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The wraiths did not disappear completely after the battle, but they have started to appear less often and avoid human settlements.{/n}
  - After: {n}The wraiths now appear less and avoid settlements.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The xenos, Muaran, has sworn that his diaspora was not involved but refused to share any further information, alluding to the 'unreliability of the human mind.'"
  - After: "Muaran denies involvement, citing the 'unreliability of the human mind.'"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I shall relay to the Lady Governor just how much trust has been placed in her."
  - After: "I'll tell the Governor of your trust."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I hope this gamble doesn't cause even more serious problems."
  - After: "I hope this gamble doesn't backfire."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I shall draft the message using the utmost formal language that will brook no denial... I hope this xenos knows a thing or two about the art of diplomatic sophistry."
  - After: "I'll make it firmly formal. Hope the xenos grasps diplomacy."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The priests will not leave their children in a time of need."
  - After: "The priests won't abandon their children."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Something is not right. The wraiths appear on the planet's outskirts and rush toward the heart of the contaminated region instead of invading from within it. Furthermore, their differences may suggest that there are two groups of wraiths opposing each other.{/n}
  - After: {n}Odd. The wraiths rush inward from the outskirts. Perhaps two opposing groups.{/n}

## GlobalMaps/Colonization/Colonization_Narrative/ColonyChronicles/Janus/Janus_Part_4/Janus_Part_4

- **Player**
  - Before: "Let the Inquisition do their job."
  - After: "Let the Inquisition work."
- **Player**
  - Before: "How much did the Inquisition sniff out?"
  - After: "What have they found?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Have Vistenza surrender some of her people. I want the Inquisition gone from the planet immediately."
  - After: "Vistenza gives up some people. Get the Inquisition out."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Aeldari will have to sacrifice some of their kinsmen to sate the hunger of the Inquisition."
  - After: "The Aeldari must sacrifice kinsmen to the Inquisition."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Heinrix, tell Lady Xue that I consider them our allies."
  - After: "Heinrix, tell Lady Xue we're allies."
- **Player**
  - Before: "We shall trick them. Have my servants persuade the Inquisition that there is nothing of significance on the planet."
  - After: "Trick them: convince them nothing's here."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I order the expulsion of those impudent fools from my world!"
  - After: "Expel those impudent fools!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Marazhai, I'm sure you can devise a treacherous trap where our uninvited guests might perish."
  - After: "Marazhai, trap our uninvited guests."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Heinrix, why was I not notified of their arrival in advance?"
  - After: "Heinrix, why wasn't I warned?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "From this moment, the acolytes shall receive all possible assistance in their investigation."
  - After: "Give the acolytes full assistance."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, an Ordo Xenos punitive unit, led by acolyte Lynett Xue, has arrived on Janus. The Inquisition forces have already taken control of the governor's palace and intend to enquire into the recent anomalies on Janus."
  - After: "Lord Captain, Ordo Xenos acolyte Lynett Xue has seized Janus's palace to investigate the anomalies."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Governor Vyatt and her retinue have left the residence and fled to some secret shelter. Many of her servants and lesser followers have been executed. There's no doubt that Lady Xue knew what exactly she was looking for."
  - After: "Governor Vyatt fled. Her servants were executed. Xue knew what she sought."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The xeno-inhabitants of Janus have been quick to scatter into the impassable forests and lay low to avoid the attention of the Ordo Xenos. Lady Xue's people are already combing the thickets and questioning suspected xenos collaborators."
  - After: "Janus's xenos hid in the forests. Xue's people hunt collaborators."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}During her investigation, Lady Xue was able to establish that the genetic changes in the retches' bodies were caused by mysterious substances secreted into the water by xeno-obelisks. These substances did not contaminate the water until recently, as shown by the analysis of the Magos Biologis. The same xeno-obelisks appear to be linked by a chain of energy communications, also serving as sources of unknown radiation that seem to have caused the outbreak of contaminated growth in the currently uncontrolled sector of the planet. This also seems to be causing the appearance of the mysterious phantoms.{/n}
  - After: {n}Xue found xeno-obelisks poisoning the water, mutating the retches. Their radiation caused the corrupted sector and likely the phantoms.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After Lady Xue had set up her headquarters at the governor's palace, she began to investigate the situation on Janus. All those feeling guilt for their crimes before the Emperor could only stay silent and pray.{/n}
  - After: {n}Lady Xue began investigating. The guilty prayed.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh, I love coming up with cunning traps for mon-keigh!"
  - After: "Oh, I love trapping mon-keigh!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Cooperating with the Inquisition would do us more good than trying to hide the current misfortunes of the colony. I can send them a message to keep us informed about the interrogation... as a favour."
  - After: "Cooperation beats hiding. I'll ask them to keep us informed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If only we could throw them a bone, and let them find the evidence they want, one that we can get by without... The rest could be concealed away from their inquisitive eyes. Like a sand lizard shedding its tail, sometimes one must cede the battle to win the war."
  - After: "Give them evidence we can spare; hide the rest. Lizards shed tails."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If someone were to walk around my domain so brazenly, they would certainly regret it. Lay open the trap, lace it with poison, put down the bait, and wait for the enemy to end their own worthless life."
  - After: "Bait a poisoned trap and let them die."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A group of Aeldari warriors fought a hopeless battle against the Inquisition's forces in the jungle. All the xenos fell, but not without taking Lady Xue and her closest advisors down with them.{/n}
  - After: {n}Aeldari warriors died fighting the Inquisition, taking Lady Xue with them.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am surprised that they have informed us of their arrival at all. It demonstrates a semblance of trust."
  - After: "They told us at all. Some trust."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Following a fabricated trail of clues, Lady Xue and her party went deep into the jungle. After several cycles, agri-scouts found the group's dead bodies. The remains of the deceased acolytes were sent to the Inquisition with honours, and Lady Xue's notes found their way onto the Rogue Trader's flagship.{/n}
  - After: {n}A false trail led Xue's party to die in the jungle. Her notes reached the flagship.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Lord Captain's servants have taken great pains to conceal any and all evidence to create an information vacuum around the Inquisition squad. Alas, it is unlikely that Lady Xue, who has since left Janus, was taken in by this deception — her group will most likely land on the planet once again in secrecy, and the agents she recruited during her sojourn on the world will obtain the information she needs.{/n}
  - After: {n}Evidence was hidden. Xue left, likely undeceived; she'll return secretly, and her agents remain.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lady Xue is a prudent and cautious acolyte. She's not prone to rash and daring antics."
  - After: "Lady Xue is cautious, not rash."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Under the steady sights of lasguns, the Inquisition squad was escorted to the shuttles and sent on their way. There is no doubt that they will make new attempts to infiltrate Janus, and no one knows exactly how many newly recruited agents they left behind on the planet.{/n}
  - After: {n}The squad was expelled at lasgun-point. They'll be back, and agents remain hidden.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The elaborate trap designed by the xenos failed — as if Lady Xue had been warned about it in advance. She disappeared into the crowds of serfs along with her people, becoming an outlaw. There is no doubt that the surviving agents of the Inquisition will cause a good deal of trouble in the future.{/n}
  - After: {n}The trap failed, as if Xue was warned. She vanished among the serfs, an outlaw sure to cause trouble.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The initial interrogations have set Lynett Xue on the tracks of the retches, toward the anomalous region. But her people continue to... dig deeper, so to speak."
  - After: "Xue follows the retches' trail to the anomaly. Her people keep digging."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The depleted but victorious Inquisition squad left Janus with the bodies of their fallen comrades in tow. The enforcers who provided invaluable assistance to the Inquisition in battle were publicly commended and rewarded with generous gifts. Lady Xue's records mysteriously disappeared just before the squad's departure, finding their way onto the Rogue Trader's ship.{/n}
  - After: {n}The squad left with their dead; helpful enforcers were rewarded. Xue's records ended up on the Rogue Trader's ship.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}According to Lady Xue's theory, there may be some sort of ancient mechanical construction on Janus that has awakened from its slumber. It is possible that the anomalies occurring on the planet are merely the side effects of the blasphemous machine trying to start itself.{/n}
  - After: {n}Xue theorised an ancient machine is waking on Janus, causing the anomalies.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I see only one way to make the Inquisition's sojourn on Janus brief: be proactive and give the acolyte what she is looking for."
  - After: "To end their stay fast, give her what she seeks."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It's the best option: the Inquisition will be satisfied and Janus will return to normal all the sooner."
  - After: "Best for all. Janus recovers sooner."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Rogue Trader's servants eagerly set about finding the smallest trace of anything that might be useful to the agents of the Inquisition. Lady Xue's people were so inundated with denunciations and testimonies that the acolytes suspected sabotage disguised as aid. However, the zealous assistance bore fruit and put the Inquisition on the right track.{/n}
  - After: {n}Servants flooded Xue with denunciations, so many she suspected sabotage, but it set her on track.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The search of the governor's palace was interrupted by a fire, which, for better or worse, was extinguished before it could destroy the residence. Hundreds of servants perished in the flames. However, the Inquisition still managed to discover traces of heretical rituals and have started their search for the governor."
  - After: "A palace fire killed hundreds of servants. Still, heretical rituals were found. They hunt the governor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Several battle squads have moved out in the direction of the Webway Gate — how they came to learn its coordinates is unknown. So far the only things they have been able to find are xenos ruins."
  - After: "Squads somehow found the Webway Gate coordinates. They've found only xenos ruins."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Inquisition's raid on the heretics' lair was successful — dozens of high-ranking aristocrats who worshipped the Ruinous Powers were exterminated. Lady Xue and her allies fell in a battle against a daemon summoned by the cult as an act of vengeance.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Inquisition purged dozens of Chaos-worshipping aristocrats. Lady Xue fell to the cult's vengeful daemon.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To serve Janus and the von Valancius dynasty!"
  - After: "For Janus and the von Valancius dynasty!"

## GlobalMaps/Colonization/Colonization_Narrative/ColonyChronicles/Janus/Janus_Part_5/Janus_Part_5

  - Before: "Have this retch, Khegh, lead my soldiers into the forest. We are ready to cooperate."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Typical of contact with the Immaterium. It intercepts information from the warp, which puts the minds and souls of the staff serving the machine in jeopardy. The warp is treacherous."

This mechanism is capable of picking up the whispers of the warp.   - After: "Lord Captain, Tech-Priests found Cubis Delphim's blasphemous machine on Kiava Gamma. It hears warp whispers and emits a harmless binharic melody."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Despite the short shifts and meticulous control, many Transmechanics were disposed of after their contact with the monstrous machine. But the small scraps of information they obtained justified their sacrifice.{/n}
  - After: {n}Many Transmechanics were disposed of. Their intel justified it.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The invited preachers, strict and stern, started to take shifts reciting a formidable litany about the inevitable victory of the Emperor into the vox-caster.   - After: {n}Preachers took shifts roaring litanies into the warp. When one died, volunteers replaced them.{/n}

Normally that would be all, but I will explain further — out of respect for you. The Inquisition can... reap benefits from this heretical machine. Our trained acolytes are able to carry a vigil near it, carefully listening to the dark whispers of the spirits of the Immaterium without succumbing to their corruption. We could discover their plans... and warn the Rogue Trader whenever any threat would loom over {mf|his|her} domain."
  - After: "The Inquisition bans contact; give it to us. Our acolytes can listen safely and warn the Rogue Trader of threats to {mf|his|her} domain."

  - Before: "The daemons wanted us to hear their vile speeches? Let them hear our righteous cry! {name}, let me summon the most zealous preachers who would dedicate their lives and zeal to reading a litany of fury and rage to this machine. Let the inhabitants of the warp hear our voice and fear us!"
  - After: "Daemons want us to hear them? Let them hear us! {name}, let zealous preachers roar fury into it!"

  - Before: "May the wicked cower in fear!"
  - After: "May the wicked cower!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Our duty of total knowledge acquisition will be fulfilled. The Omnissiah knows all, comprehends all."
  - After: "Total knowledge will be acquired."

  - Before: "By defying the dictums of the Omnissiah and venturing into the perilous field of experimenting with warp technology.   - After: "Forbidden warp-tech. But its vox-core predates Delphim; he likely found it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Thanks to the information overheard in the whispers of the warp, many heretical plots and blasphemous messages sent by the Cult of the Final Dawn have been uncovered. The protectorate has gained a new line of defence.{/n}
  - After: {n}Warp whispers exposed Cult of the Final Dawn plots. A new defence.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sinister heretics under the protection of the Rogue Trader moved the machine to their wicked lair. Listening to the echoes of the Immaterium, they welcomed more corruption and dark knowledge into their souls.{/n}

## GlobalMaps/Colonization/Colonization_Narrative/ColonyChronicles/KiavaGamma/KiavaGamma_Part_2_true/KiavaGamma_Part_2_true

- **Player**
  - Before: "What is known about this disease?"

  - Before: "Lord Captain, after the unsealing of Lady Theodora's secret workshop on Kiava Gamma, an epidemic of mysterious tech-leprosy has broken out. The Omega-18 manufactorum, the epicentre of the epidemic, is cordoned off, but the disease will burst out of there sooner or later."
  - After: "Lord Captain, opening Lady Theodora's secret workshop on Kiava Gamma unleashed a tech-leprosy warping augments and machines. Omega-18 manufactorum, the epicentre, is cordoned, but it'll break out."

  - Before: "We have not faced anything like this before. The plague only affects mechanisms, forcing them to transform and lose all functionality.   - After: "Unprecedented. It only ruins mechanisms. Origin unknown — perhaps secret research."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh, you will not regret it, shereen!"
  - After: "Oh, you won't regret it, shereen!"

  - Before: {n}Many of the Tech-Priests who had once maintained this manufactorum were left without a function and transferred to serve aboard the Rogue Trader's ship.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Even metal dies eventually, scarred by corrosion. To combat those who have stripped away their flesh and replaced it with machinery, the Bloodspun Web has procured a remedy, an acidic compound that burns through steel. We stand ready to help. To burn out this tech-leprosy."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priests, armed with a mysterious device they assembled according to the instructions of Magos Haneumann, entered the bowels of the manufactorum. The distorted mechanisms were honourably melted down, and so were the bodies of the dead Tech-Priests who carried the machine of Magos Haneumann, as well as the burnt remains of the machine itself. Before his execution, the heretic gave up the coordinates of the recently cleared tunnels, from which he had cleverly diverted the enforcers' investigative efforts.{/n}

  - Before: "I am sure that these well-armed dogs of war will make quick work of the rabble."
  - After: "These dogs of war will crush the rabble."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Heretics seek out those who are weak of spirit and entice them with promises of salvation. But such spineless lot lacks the resolve to fight and will drop their weapons should someone give them reason to fear. The purpose of many tactics in warfare is to sow terror in the enemy ranks, and I know some of these tactics well. Make them quiver, Aett-Vater, and those weaklings will forget all about their heinous intentions."
  - After: "Heretics recruit the weak, who drop weapons when afraid. Make them quiver, Aett-Vater."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, your resources and status allow you to make use of one of the most blunt and affordable tools of all — mercenaries. These dogs of war will storm the warp itself for the right price. Provide the overseers with some hired backup, and you can consider the crisis resolved."
  - After: "Lord Captain, hire mercenaries. Back the overseers and it's done."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Unfortunately, we do not know the heretics' true objectives... but there is nary a doubt that they are pursuing a sinister and wicked goal, and therefore must be stopped!"
  - After: "Their aim is unknown, but surely wicked. Stop them!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After receiving orders from the Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself}, the overseers charged — perhaps out of fear, perhaps owing to some newfound courage — and, despite suffering heavy losses, managed to break the ranks of the insurgents. The people had once already ripped their homeworld from the claws of the enemies of Humanity, and soon the cultists would feel their unsated wrath crash down upon them.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ordered by the Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself}, the overseers charged and broke the insurgents at heavy cost.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The leaders of the conspiracy, the cultists of the Final Dawn, were confronted in the mines. They had surrounded a strange dark xeno-obelisk covered with glyphs, trying to awaken it from its slumber. The glyph patterns were similar to those that the mad convicts had drawn before. The monstrous construction contained enough energy to tear the planet apart. By heroically disrupting the cultists' plan, the guards caused a malfunction within the terrible machine: instead of exploding, the obelisk emitted a blistering heatwave, melting itself and turning those around it to ash. Vheabos VI had been saved.{/n}
  - After: {n}In the mines, Final Dawn cultists tried to wake a glyph-covered xeno-obelisk that could tear the planet apart. The guards disrupted it; it melted, burning them to ash. Vheabos VI was saved.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The few words passed on to the leaders of the convicts had an incredible effect. On an invisible signal, the convicts turned against the cultists — first the instigators, and then the rebels. The overseers, finally able to break out of the cordon, watched in astonishment as their "wards" compliantly surrendered their weapons after emerging victorious.{/n}
  - After: {n}At a signal, the convicts turned on cultists and rebels, then meekly surrendered.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The colony's security systems awakened, its powerful air blowers pumping toxic gas out of the bowels of the planet and into the ventilation systems of the mining facilities. The rebellion was quashed in mere minutes — thousands of convicts and overseers had suffocated.{/n}
  - After: {n}Toxic gas flooded the mines. Thousands of convicts and overseers suffocated.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Following the advice given by the formidable Space Wolf, the overseers carried out a series of reprisals and acts of intimidation. Leaving behind mutilated corpses and infiltrating the rebel camp under the cover of darkness, they crushed the rebels' morale and forced them to surrender their weapons.{/n}
  - After: {n}On the Space Wolf's advice, the overseers' terror raids broke the rebels.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After hearing the stern words of the Rogue Trader, most of the convicts lowered their weapons and surrendered in horror. The overseers finished off the most rebellious and relentless.{/n}
  - After: {n}Most convicts surrendered in horror. The rest were killed.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Grasping at the chance to leave the accursed mines, some of the convicts turned on the rebels and joined the overseers' side. Each of them dreamt of freedom or even the great fortune of serving aboard the Rogue Trader's ship.{/n}
  - After: {n}Some convicts, hoping for freedom, joined the overseers.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is enough to kill a few to make the many lose their footing. Let the spinners bring death to the prominent instigators, and the rest will be intimidated. They will open themselves to an attack."
  - After: "Let the spinners kill the instigators. The rest will falter."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The spinners come, for death has whispered the names of the wicked."
  - After: "The spinners come."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servants of the Bloodspun Web launched a series of lightning-fast and silent attacks, stacking the corpses as grim messages. Frightened by the elusive and shadowy assassins, the heretics abandoned their lairs and fled into distant tunnels. The rebellion was decapitated.{/n}
  - After: {n}Bloodspun Web assassins left corpses as messages. The leaderless heretics fled.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We lay our own siege to the planet, then seize its vox-frequencies and broadcast the plain truth: that the convicts are fighting for a barely habitable rock, and that without Imperium authorities in charge, they will die. We will drive the message home with quotations from the Lex Imperialis, declaring that any resistance only aggravates the transgression."
  - After: "Seize their vox: without the Imperium, they die on this rock. Quote the Lex Imperialis."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The criminal rabble's morale is low. They will surrender soon."
  - After: "They'll surrender soon."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Never pausing for a minute, planet-wide broadcasts described in vivid detail how Vheabos VI would prove to be a death trap for the rebels. That disheartened many of them, and they soon turned their weapons against the Rogue Trader's enemies in the hope of receiving a lighter punishment.{/n}
  - After: {n}Broadcasts called Vheabos VI a death trap. Many rebels switched sides for leniency.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Incidentally, during my time as a jailer, I successfully petitioned for air filter reserves to be slashed, making the world more dependent on outside supplies. Thus, every breath the rebels take edges them closer to death — literally."
  - After: "As jailer, I had air filter reserves cut. Every breath kills them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The overseers are trapped inside the guard facilities, but there are many among the convicts who are loyal to Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. They remember your charitable mercy and may yet switch sides."
  - After: "Many convicts remember Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s mercy and may switch sides."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The overseers were caught unawares, but, fortunately, they have already gathered their forces and taken up solid defensive positions. Those who serve on Vheabos VI are loyal and merciless, ready to face any number of foes in your name. I am confident victory will be theirs."
  - After: "The overseers hold firm. They'll win in your name."

## GlobalMaps/Colonization/Colonization_Narrative/ColonyChronicles/Veabos/Veabos_Part_4/Veabos_Part_4

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Corruption has infiltrated Vheabos VI, Lord Captain! The cultists of the Final Dawn have agitated the convicts into a full-blown uprising, promising them a chance at escape. The planet's cargo port and guard facilities are now under siege!"
  - After: "Lord Captain, Final Dawn cultists have Vheabos VI's convicts revolting! Port and guard posts besieged!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The overseers are reporting tremors — it seems that the heretics are trying to clear the cave-ins that we used to ward off the subterranean monsters."
  - After: "Tremors — they're clearing the monster-blocking cave-ins."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The security post that we set up in those mining drifts reported a skirmish and then went silent."
  - After: "Our mine post went silent."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The cultists themselves have not joined the assault. They have scurried into the mines, deep into the tunnels that were infected with xenos corruption not too long ago."
  - After: "The cultists fled into the mines."

## GlobalMaps/Colonization/Colonization_Narrative/ColonyChronicles/Veabos/Veabos_Part_5/Veabos_Part_5

- **Player**
  - Before: "What kind of 'accidents' are happening there?"
  - After: "What 'accidents'?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Ulfar's advice is sound. We will leave bait for our enemy."
  - After: "Ulfar is right. Leave bait."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Marazhai is right. Set a series of traps and provoke it to attack."
  - After: "Marazhai is right. Set traps, provoke it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Send out scouts. We need to find its lair."
  - After: "Send scouts to find its lair."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Yrliet makes a good point. Find some effective disguise against our foe and wait for it to strike."
  - After: "Yrliet is right. Disguise ourselves and wait."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Place all mining complexes on high alert. Stay vigilant, and sooner or later, we will spot it."
  - After: "Put all mines on high alert. We'll spot it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "No one can see it, but snares do not need eyes. Leave some gifts out for our unwanted guest."
  - After: "Snares need no eyes. Leave gifts for our guest."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Eogunn's methods sound effective. Dispatch soldiers trained in the use of arc weapons to conduct patrols."
  - After: "Eogunn is right. Send arc-armed patrols."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, Vheabos VI begs for help! Something terrible prowls the planet, searching for a way to wipe out the planet's inhabitants. Victims died in small groups at first, so they dismissed it as simple accidents — a poisoning, a crashed transport, a fire. But the death toll has started to rise, and explaining everything as mere coincidence is no longer an option. The enemy appears to be testing out different methods of killing your subjects, like it's looking for the most efficient way to murder as many of them at once as possible. Our pict-traps sometimes catch sight of a blurry dark shadow walking among the people, but no one has actually seen it with their own eyes."
  - After: "Lord Captain, Vheabos VI begs for help! Something is killing people, testing ways to kill more. Pict-traps glimpse a shadow; no one has seen it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A glorious hunt to the cunning hunters!"
  - After: "A glorious hunt!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I believe in you. Being irritating comes naturally to mon-keigh."
  - After: "Mon-keigh irritate naturally."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The art of hunting relies on the art of hiding. You cannot see your target... then make it so the target cannot see you. Deceive its senses and seize your advantage."
  - After: "Make it unable to see you. Deceive its senses."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A predator walks among your people? Well, then it's time we became predators ourselves! Your servants can't see it and don't know where its lair lies, but I will tell you how to find it: you need to spark the beast's curiosity. Leave something it craves out in the open and mark it so that you can track the beast as it's carrying the bait away in its jaws. That is how we hunt cunning prey on Fenris."
  - After: "Become predators! Leave marked bait and track it to its lair, as on Fenris."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Ha! You call it your enemy, but you are mere pests in its eyes. This isn't war, this is extermination. You are a nuisance, and that is your asset. Understand what it is you do that vexes it so much, and you will understand how to drive it mad. All that will be left then is to lay a trap."
  - After: "To it, you're pests. Learn what vexes it, then lay a trap."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The wardens were better suited for punishing convicts than lookout duty. At last, an alert came in: one of the inner gates that had previously been sealed was being opened. The guards who arrived on the scene saw a dark figure and opened fire. Wounded, the creature fled.{/n}
  - After: {n}A sealed gate opened. Guards shot a dark figure; it fled wounded.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}To attract the enemy's attention, a "lethal incident" was staged: a radiation leak caused by an open transuranium container. Shortly after, a handful of this hazardous material went missing, and the wise Tech-Priests used the radioactive trail to locate the monster's lair.{/n}
  - After: {n}A faked radiation leak lured it. Tech-Priests tracked stolen transuranium to its lair.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "May the hunters find patience."
  - After: "Patience, hunters."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The colony's wardens experimented with several means of disguise but did eventually succeed in hiding themselves from the eyes of their mysterious foe.{/n}
  - After: {n}The wardens hid themselves from their foe.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Alas, setting traps was not one of the wardens' talents, and for the longest time, the enemy managed to avoid them. Eventually, however, an explosion signalled that the beast had been caught. The wounded creature was then discovered and driven off.{/n}
  - After: {n}At last a trap exploded. The wounded beast was driven off.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Alas, it took some time for the colony's wardens to come up with an effective camouflage that could hide them from this mysterious foe.{/n}
  - After: {n}Camouflage took the wardens a while.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The warden whose unfortunate lot it was to keep watch inside of an air purifier spotted a strange shadow right between the working mechanisms and the lead cover. The enemy had grown careless and finally revealed itself. The brave warden raised the alarm, wounded the creature, and fell in battle, but his comrades managed to chase the beast away.{/n}
  - After: {n}A warden in an air purifier spotted it, wounded it and died. Comrades drove it off.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A series of tempting lures marked with radiation was left for the mysterious enemy to find, but the wardens' efforts were hardly inconspicuous, and for a while, they could not fool the beast.{/n}
  - After: {n}Clumsy radiation lures failed at first.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The vigilant wardens were up to the Rogue Trader's task: having placed the colony on high alert, they waited for the moment when the enemy would reveal itself.{/n}
  - After: {n}The colony went on high alert and waited.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Fortune soon smiled upon the diligent hunters when they discovered promising-looking tunnels beneath the surface.{/n}
  - After: {n}The hunters found promising tunnels.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Assuming that the creature had been angered by the mining efforts, the overseers increased work shifts in remote sectors. The assumption proved to be correct: the beast came to destroy those who had disturbed its rest and walked right into the traps laid out for it. Wounded, it fled.{/n}
  - After: {n}Mining in remote sectors drew the beast into traps. It fled wounded.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Soon enough, the mysterious shadow walked into one of the devious traps and, wounded by the powerful explosion, ran for its life.{/n}
  - After: {n}The shadow hit a trap and fled, wounded.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Cornered in its den, the monster fought its final battle and was slain. It was a terrifying xenos with a metallic skeletal body and a single emerald eye. Its lair turned out to be a crypt-like chamber, and beneath it was an entire fortress buried in stone. The walls were covered in glyphs similar to the mysterious patterns that the mad convicts had been drawing.{/n}
  - After: {n}Cornered, the monster died: a metal-skeletal xenos with one emerald eye. Beneath its crypt lay a buried fortress, its glyphs like the mad convicts' drawings.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The chamber also contained the dissected remains of the missing miners. The Omnissiah's servants studied the bodies, the crypt, and the xenos's corpse, hypothesising that the inhuman belonged to a caste of sages among its kind. It had remained in stasis for ages untold but had recently been awakened either by the mining efforts or the explosions caused by the Drukhari invaders. After killing everyone who had approached its lair, the creature tried to wake its brethren, but millennia of tectonic shifts had crushed the underground fortress. The creature was alone.{/n}
  - After: {n}The missing miners lay dissected there. Tech-Priests judged it a xenos sage, woken from stasis by mining or Drukhari blasts. It tried to wake its kin, but the fortress was long crushed. It was alone.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The hunters searched everywhere, but, given their lack of experience, their efforts remained unsuccessful for a long time. However, eventually, they discovered the enemy's lair.{/n}
  - After: {n}After a long search, they found the lair.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Regrettably, the wardens were not particularly skilled in deception or provocation. However, they did eventually lure the enemy out with large-scale underground blasting operations. The creature came to the mining site, walked into the traps, and retreated upon having suffered a painful injury.{/n}
  - After: {n}Big underground blasts finally lured it into the traps. It retreated, hurt.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The fearsome insects, the ones that assailed the colony, were the only tool the xenos had left, so it chose to lie in wait. But when the heretics of the Final Dawn sabotaged the fortress's reactor in their attempts to destroy the planet, the xenos grew restless and started searching for a way to exterminate the humans. Now the last xenos survivor was dead, and so was its entire race — or at least, so prayed every denizen of Vheabos VI.{/n}
  - After: {n}With only its insects left, the xenos waited, until the Final Dawn sabotaged its reactor and it set out to exterminate humans. Now its race was dead — or so Vheabos VI prayed.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Speaking as an expert, all evidence indicates that the unknown creature is an ancient xenos, cunning and dangerous. Conventional methods will be inadequate at overcoming it. Only the Motive Force, the blessed energy granted to us by the Omnissiah, can bypass this creature's defences. Equip a squad of the most effective fighters with arc rifles and shock grenades, and deploy them at locations where the xenos is most active."
  - After: "An ancient xenos. Only the Motive Force pierces its defences. Deploy arc rifles and shock grenades where it's active."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If it can be captured alive, it would be an invaluable specimen for study."
  - After: "Alive, it'd be invaluable for study."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Having miraculously discovered the creature within one of the maintenance chambers, the guards unleashed a withering barrage upon it. Arc weapons did indeed prove dangerous to the xenos — it fled, but its wounds meant it was no longer as swift and elusive as before.{/n}
  - After: {n}Guards found it and fired. Arc weapons hurt it; it fled, slowed.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The fate of the guards patrolling the complex's corridors proved grim indeed: the creature left them little more than a pulp of blood, flesh, and splintered bone. It dragged one of the guards away and, by following the blood trail, the other soldiers were able to trace it back to its lair.{/n}
  - After: {n}It pulped the patrols and dragged one off. The blood trail led to its lair.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Various sorts of mechanical failures. Ventilation systems emitting substances that have no business being there. Auspexes registering spikes of radiation. Maintenance systems shutting down for no apparent reason. It all resembles extermination experiments, with your servants playing the role of test subject."
  - After: "Failures. Gas in the vents. Radiation spikes. Like extermination tests on your people."

## GlobalMaps/StarSystemObjects/ExplorationPlanetPoints/AbandonedExtractor/AbandonedExtractor_EPP_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: Provide the technicians with scrap to repair the extractium.
  - After: Give technicians scrap to repair the extractium.
- **Player**
  - Before: Dismantle the surviving extractium for spare parts.
  - After: Dismantle the extractium for parts.
- **Player**
  - Before: Leave the world to face its end alone.
  - After: Leave the world to its end.
- **Player**
  - Before: Take the extractium machine on board. Its capabilities can be applied elsewhere.
  - After: Take the extractium aboard for use elsewhere.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The sight before you has excited the officer corps, who are delighted to witness the truly majestic end of this planet through the huge windows on the bridge, one of many nameless worlds throughout the Expanse. An unknown reason caused the planet to break into several uneven parts, but its strong magnetic field is still preventing them from drifting into the cold abyss of space. The planet's hard inner core has remained almost untouched as thousands of explosions taking place under its shell of hard metals light up the world's heart from the inside.
  - After: Officers watch, rapt, as this nameless world dies: split apart, held by its magnetic field, its core lit by explosions.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: A few dozen time bells later, the Lord Captain is informed that the repair crew is suffering from unrelenting headaches, most likely caused by the oppressive magnetic field of this world. However, the machines have been successfully repaired, and the extraction of adamantine may continue if the Lord Captain wishes. Of course, the mine needs to be staffed with a squad of working servitors and a maintenance brigade doomed to endure the endless pain caused by the magnetic storms.
  - After: Repaired, though the crew suffers magnetic headaches. Adamantine mining can continue, but servitors and a maintenance crew must stay, in endless pain.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: You leave a part of the crew to extract adamantine for the von Valancius protectorate. Those fortunate to escape such a fate fervently pray for the lives of their friends and family, hoping to find them in good health should they be reunited someday.
  - After: Part of the crew stays to mine adamantine for the protectorate. The rest pray for them.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The augur crew detects several ruined extractiums on the broken planet's surface. Their analysis shows somebody used to mine adamantine here but abandoned the deposit after the catastrophe. Most of the machines are damaged beyond repair, but the Tech-Adepts claim one of the complexes can be restored if the Rogue Trader has the required parts and equipment.
  - After: Augurs find ruined adamantine extractiums, abandoned after the catastrophe. Tech-Adepts can restore one, given parts.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: You decide not to spend the resources on fixing a mechanism on the surface of a world that may literally break apart at any moment. Over the course of several rotations, your people fully dismantle the extractium and evacuate the planet without incident.
  - After: Not worth fixing on a breaking world. Your people dismantle the extractium and leave safely.

  - After: The Rogue Trader's word is final. Ready weapons!

Countless primed mines are still scattered among the wreckage.
  - After: Augurs spot a crippled Aeldari ship amid a century-old, still-live Navy minefield.

With notes of sadness in her voice, carefully picking her words, she concedes that the elantach did all they could to save her kin... And yet it is the mon-keigh who are responsible for the loss of the Aeldari voidship. Saddened by the pain and hatred that humans have wrought upon her kind, Yrliet quietly leaves the bridge.

Then, she turns to the Lord Captain, powerless.

  - Before: But are the calculations correct? The Tech-Priests warn that in solving this kind of problem, it is impossible to account for every possibility — too many unknowns, too little time.

## GlobalMaps/StarSystemObjects/ExplorationPlanetPoints/BurningWorlds/BurningWorlds_EPP_dialog

- **Player**

Thousands of years ago, a single flash of lightning or some other spark launched a chain reaction that transformed the world into a blistering inferno.
  - After: Yet another: gas geysers feed an ancient planet-wide blaze.
- **(conversation owner)**

More evidence is required if the research is to continue.
  - After: These artefacts belong to an ancient heat-adapted xenos race, dubbed the Builders From the Flame. More evidence is needed.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: It looks like the Builders From the Flame used hereditary bacterial structures to record information. The artefacts you discovered on the burning worlds contained colonies of bacteria whose genes carried the message of these xenos across generations. Their language, however, bears a passing semblance to some of the ancient samples already available to your scientists. They managed to make a crude translation of some of these records.
  - After: The Builders stored records in hereditary bacteria. Their language resembles known ancient samples; a crude translation succeeds.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: They revealed that the Builders From the Flame were not originally colonising the burning worlds. Their homeland was not a planet but a star. It is hard to imagine what the creatures that evolved in the burning ocean of a faraway sun may have looked like, but one day their peaceful existence came to an end. The records contain a chilling legend about some cosmic horror that arrived and devoured the sun that the Builders called home. Fearing the monster, they fled and no longer dared to settle on stars.
  - After: The Builders evolved in a star until a cosmic horror devoured it. They fled, never again daring to settle on stars.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Builders considered burning worlds as the most fit for habitation, yet they went extinct shortly after the exodus, perhaps unable to adapt to the harsh realities of life outside their stellar home. Their civilisation left a wealth of unique technologies and heat-resistant materials, and now this treasure belongs to the von Valancius dynasty!
  - After: They settled burning worlds but soon died out. Their heat-resistant technologies now belong to the von Valancius dynasty!
- **(conversation owner)**

A number of constructions of artificial origin can be detected under the planet's surface. They are too vast and peculiar to have been created by humans, but their geometric shapes and other properties clearly indicate they were put together by sentient beings of some kind.
  - After: Tech-Priests detect vast subsurface structures, inhuman yet clearly built by sentient beings.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The augurs report nothing you don't know already. This world is hostile, inhospitable, and of little interest.
  - After: The augurs find nothing new. Hostile, and of little interest.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The operation is difficult but proceeds without a hitch. The machines make way to the unusual constructions and return carrying priceless samples. Seemingly uninteresting, these plates and weaves of heat-resistant material cause great excitement among the Tech-Priests.
  - After: The machines return with heat-resistant plates and weaves that thrill the Tech-Priests.
- **(conversation owner)**

A mistake in the Tech-Priests' calculations causes the machines to succumb to severe heat stress and malfunction, damaging the strange constructions beyond repair. This is not the end, however, as there are more burning worlds where this research can be carried out after the necessary modifications are made.

  - After: You lack the knowledge to solve this yet.

  - Before: The yellow-red glare of the burning world coming through the bridge windows hurts your eyes.
  - After: The burning world's glare stings your eyes.
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: Knowing what to seek, augurs easily find the hidden structures.

Attackers with emaciated bodies pounced from the darkness without warning.
  - After: A patched plasteel door blocks the cave. Inside, emaciated attackers ambush your team.

He and his brothers and sisters were tasked with guarding this strange cemetery and preventing anyone from entering. He equally could not hide that the unfortunate inhabitants of the cryo-vaults were killed by his people. Alas, that was his last confession as the harsh interrogation finally took its toll.
  - After: Under torture he admits his Cult of Saint Drusus guards this cemetery and killed the sleepers. Then he dies.

  - After: Scouts find a hall of cryo-vaults holding dead nobles. One stands open and empty.
