  - After: The captive learns how ruthless the Bloodspun Web can be.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The squad landed near a suspicious cave. The entrance to the cave was blocked by a massive plasteel door that had previously been pierced by a melta charge and then shoddily patched up. After receiving a signal from his faithful cyber-mastiff, Proctor Anthar warned the enforcers of the ambush ahead, and the attack was not long in coming — armed people with emaciated bodies charged out of the darkness.
  - After: A patched door blocks the cave. Anthar's cyber-mastiff warns of an ambush; emaciated attackers charge.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Despite the brutal torture and various persuasive, mind-altering solutions administered into the prisoner's bloodstream by a wise Tech-Priest, the bastard maintained his arrogant silence and perished before a single word escaped his lips.
  - After: Despite torture and a Tech-Priest's drugs, he dies silent.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Tech-Priests sent at your command have reported that the machine spirits of all cryo-vaults are healthy and obedient, excepting the one living within the opened sarcophagus. This machine spirit is in terrible condition and afflicted by great madness, muddying its algorithms.
  - After: All cryo-vault spirits are healthy except the opened one's, which is mad.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The enforcers of the von Valancius dynasty reacted with lightning speed. They walked away from the vicious battle not only victorious but having captured the enemy commander.
  - After: The von Valancius enforcers win fast and capture the enemy leader.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Offering up prayers to the Machine God, the augur operators turned their blessed optics toward the very epicentre of the raging magnetic storm. In spite of the thick haze of static covering the augurs' pict-visors, something unexpected appeared.
  - After: The augurs peer into the magnetic storm. Something appears.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The bastard did not appreciate your mercy. He threw himself at the guards as soon as he was unchained. In the resulting scuffle, both his brains and the secrets they concealed were splattered across a bulkhead.
  - After: Unchained, he attacks the guards and is killed, secrets and all.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: For the attempt on the lives of subjects of the von Valancius dynasty, the bastard was placed in the nozzle of a manoeuvring thruster, where the zealous machine spirit incinerated him with a jet of roaring flame.
  - After: For attacking your subjects, he is burned alive in a thruster nozzle.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: In addition, a curious machine was destroyed during the battle. As further inspection would show, this was the very contraption responsible for creating the magnetic storms blanketing the planet, concealing the cemetery from prying eyes. Its machine spirit extinguished forever, Tech-Priests still managed to extract those parts that still held value.
  - After: A wrecked machine had made the storms hiding the cemetery. Tech-Priests salvage its parts.

- **Player**
  - Before: The Rogue Trader orders to behead everyone on the illegal mining rig and send their heads to Incendia Chorda — with the very best of wishes.
  - After: Behead everyone on the illegal rig and send the heads to Incendia Chorda, with best wishes.

  - After: The Seneschal insists on confiscating and relocating this illegal extractium.
- **Player**

  - After: Pasqal notes Atle's core holds rare refractory metals. Keep the extractium for {mf|himself|herself}.
- **Player**
  - Before: The Rogue Trader graciously allows Incendia Chorda to feed on crumbs unworthy of the von Valancius dynasty's attention.
  - After: Let Incendia Chorda have crumbs unworthy of the von Valancius.
- **Player**
  - Before: The Rogue Trader decides to keep the extractium for {mf|himself|herself} with all the workers and servitors.
  - After: Keep the extractium for {mf|himself|herself}, workers and servitors included.
- **Player**
  - Before: The Rogue Trader commands that the machines be confiscated and put into the ship's cargo hold.
  - After: Confiscate the machines into the cargo hold.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: This dwarf planet is marked on the von Valancius protectorate charts as "Atle" and serves as a backup source of water for the habitable worlds of neighbouring systems. Due to the abundance of bacteria proliferating in the Atle hydrosphere, the extraction of ice was stopped half a century ago, but much to your officers' surprise, the augurs detected an unidentified mining rig deep underground. Presumably, the excavation is aimed at extracting clay minerals near the planet's core, enriched with iron and other metals.
  - After: Atle, your dwarf planet, was a backup water source until bacteria halted mining fifty years ago. Now augurs find an unknown rig deep below, digging for metal-rich clay.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: As soon as your people return to the flagship, you receive an Astropathic response from the Administratum ordinate: the governor of one of the nearest Chorda worlds has been implicated in the illegal mining. The perpetrator will be severely punished, and compensation will be sent to the Rogue Trader's treasury immediately.
  - After: The Administratum: a Chorda governor ran the mine. He'll be punished, you compensated.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The extractium turns out to be Incendia Chorda's latest investment, whose demesne is located just within a few jumps from the Cranach System. While this world is of little value to the von Valancius dynasty, your officers see this gesture as an attempt to test the boundaries of the newly minted Rogue Trader's leniency.
  - After: It's Incendia Chorda's extractium, a few jumps from Cranach. Your officers see a test of your leniency.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The transmission cuts off as soon as the scouting party reaches the extraction zone. All subsequent attempts to contact them fail, presumably because they were eliminated by the extractium's defence systems.
  - After: The scouts' signal dies at the site. Likely killed by its defences.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Vox Master reports that your message was sent and received. Several hours pass, but there is no reply.
  - After: Message received. Hours pass, no reply.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The crew carries out the order with grim determination. Not a hand trembled, each face focused without demur. The property of the von Valancius dynasty is yours alone, and the crew stands ready to prove this to any would-be challenger as often as is necessary.
  - After: The crew obeys without a tremor. Von Valancius property is yours.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The frightened workers and the token security crew do not even attempt to resist the superior forces. The machines are delivered to the flagship's cargo hold, and shortly after the officers plant the von Valancius banner on the spot where the extractium used to be.
  - After: No resistance. The machines go to your hold; your banner rises over the site.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Your people easily assume control as the frightened workers and the token security crew do not even attempt to resist. The extractium's machines are restarted shortly after, the amassed containers filled with precious ore are delivered to the flagship's cargo hold.
  - After: No resistance. The machines restart, and ore goes to your hold.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: All that remains of the extractium is a handful of craters. The augur crew scans the surface one more time and finds parts of the extractium machines scattered all over the area.
  - After: Only craters and machine scraps remain.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Vigdis reports that your order was being quite actively discussed on the crew's personal vox-casters until the lights-out bell. Some believe you lack the staunchness required of a Rogue Trader, but others are impressed by your clever response. Only the combat crews are bitterly disappointed, not having the pleasure of "teaching Chorda's space mongrels a lesson they won't soon forget."
  - After: Vigdis: the crew calls you soft or clever. Combat crews wanted to teach "Chorda's space mongrels a lesson."

  - After: Search the grass for more.

  - After: Keep exploring.

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Under thin clouds, as if shredded by a careless blade, sway vast steppes carpeted by pale gold deadwood. The Rogue Trader's attentive eye distinguishes a region among the endless grasses that does not fit into the general landscape.

- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: The xenos camp hides many dangers.

- **(conversation owner)**

Their bodies swell from the punctures, being filled with an unknown toxin. Their comrades above freeze from the screams then come to their senses and begin extracting the unfortunate explorers. In a niche sunk into the wall of the trap glitters a volumetric flask with an ugly creature that looks like several brains stuck together.
  - After: Some scouts fall into a toxic needle pit and are pulled out swollen. In a niche, a flask holds a creature like fused brains.

When the von Valancius scouts approach, they find a wax seal bearing the symbol of the Inquisition and a monogram formed from the letters XC. An officer voices the proposition that the initials correspond to the name of Lord Inquisitor Xavier Calcazar.
  - After: Behind the maze: shuttle prints and an Inquisition seal marked XC. Lord Inquisitor Xavier Calcazar, an officer guesses.

Among the chopped stems lies a piece of a Drukhari trophy — a flap of dark skin stretched out by thin chains. Most of it is covered by a tattoo: a silhouette of a storm or tornado and a black symbol composed of curved lines and sharp shapes.
  - After: In cut grass lies a Drukhari trophy: chained dark skin tattooed with a storm and a black symbol.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: There is nothing in the dry grass around the depressions in the ground that would merit the Rogue Trader's attention.
  - After: Nothing else of note in the grass.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Rogue Trader's people recognise the grotesque figure as a Drukhari medusa — a parasite capable of registering emotions and transferring them to its masters. This thing was left here as the equivalent of a pict-recorder, collecting the suffering of the Drukhari's victims.
  - After: A Drukhari medusa, a parasite recording victims' suffering for its masters.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The flask explodes into shrapnel fragments under a salvo from the scouts' rifles. The remaining liquid is collected into several test tubes to be examined in the ship's laboratorium and put to good use — or destroyed on the orders of the Rogue Trader.
  - After: Rifle fire shatters the flask. The liquid goes to the laboratorium.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The scouts from the shuttle see signs of intelligent life. Judging by the trampled soil and tent frames, someone made camp here. Distant silhouettes form a tangle of paths and obstacles — a maze. The outer walls are supplemented by a multitude of spikes and blades and decorated with scraps of leather and withered crucified prisoners. It does not take an expert in xenoculture to reason that Drukhari have been here.
  - After: The scouts find an empty camp and a maze of spikes, blades and crucified prisoners. Drukhari were here.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The servants of von Valancius find a rough illustration of the camp in the pocket of a filthy coat. On it are marked two locations. The first is shown with a sword and highlights the area where the items were found. The other is a skull and points to a patch of ground by the maze.
  - After: A coat holds a camp map: a sword where the items lay, a skull by the maze.

## GlobalMaps/StarSystemObjects/ExplorationPlanetPoints/DeepestCave/DeepestCave_EPP_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: Send an exploration team equipped with a drilling apparatus to the asteroid.
  - After: Send a team with a drill to the asteroid.
- **Player**
  - Before: The Lord Captain decides that the potential reward is not worth the team's labours and gives the order to leave the asteroid belt.
  - After: Not worth the labour. Leave the asteroid belt.
- **Player**
  - Before: Order the squad to ignore these paltry deposits and move on.
  - After: Ignore these paltry deposits and move on.
- **Player**
  - Before: Exploring these caves no longer seems like a good idea, and the Lord Captain commands the squad to return to the voidship.
  - After: This is a bad idea. Recall the squad to the voidship.
- **Player**
  - Before: Plasteel is an important resource. An opportunity to acquire some should not be disregarded.
  - After: Plasteel is important. Don't pass it up.
- **Player**
  - Before: There is not enough data on the substance. The Rogue Trader orders the team to circumvent the toxin-filled tunnels to avoid risking their health and equipment.
  - After: Too little is known. Bypass the toxic tunnels to protect the team and gear.
- **Player**
  - Before: There's no need for haste. The explorers are to gather as much material as possible and transfer the find to the Magi Alchemys for further processing.
  - After: No haste. Gather as much as possible for the Magi Alchemys.
- **Player**
  - Before: Order the collection of the xenos totems. Flogiston is too valuable to leave it here.
  - After: Collect the xenos totems. Flogiston is too valuable to leave.
- **Player**
  - Before: The flogiston is tainted by xenos filth and must be destroyed alongside the city.
  - After: The flogiston is xenos-tainted. Destroy it with the city.
- **Player**
  - Before: This city remained untouched for aeons. Let it remain so.
  - After: This city stood untouched for aeons. Leave it so.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The gigantic asteroid's surface is densely sown with craters and pits leading into deep caves. Augurs indicate that the asteroid consists of layers characterised by strange heterogeneity. There is a high probability of finding valuable resources inside the stone — they can be extracted by sending an exploration team deep into the tangled tunnels.
  - After: A huge, cave-riddled asteroid of odd layers. A team sent deep inside may find valuable resources.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Several caverns on the asteroid's surface release an unknown substance. Viscous and cloudy, it spreads over the stone's porous surface and expands into shapeless blots in the weightlessness of the void. The augur team warns that the substance is extremely toxic, and that the emanations are steadily eating away at the rock. Exploring the asteroid is impossible.
  - After: Caverns leak a cloudy, highly toxic substance that eats the rock. Exploration is impossible.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The tired squad begins the return journey up to the surface, forever leaving the pathways of the ancient city behind.
  - After: The tired squad climbs back up, leaving the ancient city forever.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The massive beasts turn out to be surprisingly agile — in a couple of jumps they reach the team of explorers and dig into the poor souls' bodies with powerful mandibles, mashing them into a bloody paste. Gorged on fresh meat, the monsters scurry away into the colossal cracks in the walls. Having neither the time nor the strength to bid a final farewell to the fallen, deprived of equipment and hope, the remnants of the expedition rush out of the accursed caverns... back, to the ship, as soon as possible!
  - After: The agile beasts catch the team and mash them with their mandibles. The survivors flee for the ship, leaving gear and dead.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: With the help of the massive drill, the exploration team penetrates into the cavernous depths. The squad reports that their auspexes have detected meagre reserves of a substance used in the synthesis of plasteel in the rock. Their excavation will take time and significant effort.
  - After: The drill breaks through. Auspexes find meagre plasteel ingredients, slow to extract.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The equipment struggles with the unexpected hardness of the rock, but after three watches the squad manages to set up enough mobile extractiums to gather the coveted material.
  - After: After three watches against hard rock, enough extractiums are set up to gather the material.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Cracking the unusual rock turns out to be impossible. Having encountered unexpected resistance, the equipment falls into disrepair. After several fruitless watches, the squad decides to continue moving deeper into the asteroid in the search of richer veins.
  - After: The rock won't crack and the gear breaks. The squad presses deeper for richer veins.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The noise and vibrations caused by the instruments have disturbed strange currents inside the asteroid. A transparent, viscous substance streams down from the porous walls of the caverns, slowly filling the caves. The squad's auspexes raise the alarm — a prolonged stay in these tunnels will undoubtedly result in the toxic liquid destroying the gear and equipment. Despite this, the explorers suggest blocking the livelier streams in order to leave them with enough time to fill several canisters with the strange substance. Later, the Magi Alchemys will no doubt be able to synthesise many useful chemicals from it.
  - After: The drilling stirs a toxic liquid that seeps from the walls, threatening the gear. The explorers suggest blocking the streams to fill canisters for the Magi Alchemys.
- **(conversation owner)**

With each occurrence, the devices look more and more distorted, bent, and sometimes even appear directly in the remnants of walls or overlap each other. The only stable thing in this structure is a deep hole with a melted rock at its centre. Whatever purpose this structure served for the xenos, the meteorite destroyed it long before the arrival of the Rogue Trader.

## GlobalMaps/StarSystemObjects/ExplorationPlanetPoints/FrozenColony/FrozenColony_EPP_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: Send out a scouting party.
  - After: Send a scouting party.
- **Player**
  - Before: Find out what happened to the world.
  - After: Learn what happened here.
- **Player**
  - Before: Leave the colony to its own devices.
  - After: Leave the colony be.
- **Player**
  - Before: Take any machinery from the colonists and abandon them on the freezing world.
  - After: Seize their machinery and abandon them.
- **Player**
  - Before: Give the unfortunate people a gift of promethium and send Tech-Priests to perform the rites of generator maintenance.
  - After: Gift promethium and send Tech-Priests to restore the generators.
- **Player**
  - Before: Abandon the freezing colony.
  - After: Abandon the colony.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: At first it looked like the snowy and desolate planet was devoid of surprises, but the yellow and orange flickering of the lumens and the notifications from the augur system informed the officers there was a small colony that survived in spite of the harsh climatic conditions. All attempts to hail the colony have failed.
  - After: The augurs find a small colony surviving on the frozen planet. It doesn't answer hails.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The explorers report the dismal condition of the settlement and its inhabitants. Their skin is translucent and pale, their icy-blue eyes see practically no colour, their language is rough and guttural and their stomachs cannot tolerate anything except a stew made from local roots and mosses. And yet they are subjects of the Imperium, still loyal to the Emperor — they have mistaken your people for His emissaries.
  - After: The colonists are pale, near colour-blind and live on root stew. Still loyal to the Emperor, they think your people are His emissaries.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The local elders woefully reminisced about times long gone. Most of them were still sheltered in their mothers' wombs when snow first settled on the verdant fields. Hail ruined the crops and frost hardened the soil. Plants and large beasts that could not sustain themselves were the first to go. They were soon followed by birds and other small animals. Most people in large cities perished, unable to warm themselves and their families.
  - After: The elders recall the snow coming when they were unborn. Crops, beasts and birds died; most city folk froze.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: They say the governor and his entourage left the world in the first days of winter, taking all the provisions and fuel with them. No one responded to the pleas from this dying world — the stars remained deaf to the messages transmitted by the planet's vox-stations. These abandoned subjects of the Imperium still managed to save the machines and other valuables, but they were of little use without a supply of promethium. And yet those who survived eventually adapted to the tribulations that the God-Emperor had bestowed upon them.
  - After: The governor fled with all the food and fuel. No one answered their pleas. They saved machines, useless without promethium, yet the survivors adapted.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Your people had little difficulty subduing the locals — nobody had the strength to resist. Gaunt and exhausted by their miserable lot, they dolefully watched on as the invaders carried away the wealth, machines, and possessions laboriously scrounged together by generations of their ancestors. The shuttles, glutted with their society's toil, soared high above the oppressive clouds, far out of reach. There was nothing left to help them survive, but who cares about other people's misery.
  - After: The starving locals can't resist as you strip generations of their toil. Your shuttles leave them nothing to survive on.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: When the maw of the first generator belched forth a furious roar and black ash started falling from the sky instead of snow, the locals laughed and danced, trying to warm their limbs after decades of cold. They called down blessings upon their unseen saviour, a Rogue Trader from the von Valancius dynasty, and thanked the God-Emperor for the fortuitous encounter.
  - After: As the first generator roars to life, the locals dance in the falling ash, blessing the von Valancius Rogue Trader and the God-Emperor.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The colony looks much better than the last time. The moribund machines have been set in motion — the locals use them to mine hard fossil fuels to be used when promethium runs out. The delegation members are welcomed as royalty — by local standards, of course. The great Rogue Trader, the saviour of the colony, Vonvalancius, as the locals now call it, is offered gilded statues from one of the abandoned cities as well as precious gems and documents of value.
  - After: The colony is thriving; its machines now mine fossil fuels. Hailing their saviour "Vonvalancius", the locals offer gilded statues, gems and valuable documents.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The explorers' departure was accompanied by shouts of grateful approval — not to mention their many parting gifts.
  - After: The explorers leave to grateful cheers and many gifts.

## GlobalMaps/StarSystemObjects/ExplorationPlanetPoints/GasGiantStorm/GasGiantStorm_EPP_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: We can only hope it is an omen of great things to come.
  - After: Let's hope it's an omen of great things.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The crew were treated to a truly impressive sight — a colossal storm on the gas giant's surface. The planet's dimensions in themselves were mind-boggling, and then it birthed a tempest, the storm to end all storms. As the Lord Captain and {mf|his|her} officers observed it from a safe distance through the bridge's huge viewing windows, someone suggested giving it a name, and "The Emperor's Wrath" garnered the most votes. Some in the crew believed the storm to be an omen.
  - After: A colossal storm rages on the gas giant. Watching with {mf|his|her} officers, the Lord Captain hears it named "The Emperor's Wrath". Some call it an omen.

## GlobalMaps/StarSystemObjects/ExplorationPlanetPoints/GaussAnomaly/GaussAnomaly_EPP

- **Player**
  - Before: Fire plasma torpedoes at the xenos monoliths.
  - After: Torpedo the xenos monoliths.
- **Player**
  - Before: It is rare to find such an ominous phenomenon in lifeless ice.
  - After: An ominous sight in lifeless ice.
- **Player**
  - Before: Recall the scouts to the ship.
  - After: Recall the scouts.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Most of the surface is covered in icy dunes with greenish highlights. At first, officers aboard the vessel decide that the unusual colour of the ice is due to a quirk of the atmosphere. Later, it becomes evident that the source of the highlights is a group of monstrous pyramidal structures wreathed in an emerald fire. Examining them in detail with magnoculars, it can be seen that one of the monoliths is damaged. A device on its wall emits an energy beam at a similar pyramid not far from itself.
  - After: The icy dunes glow green from pyramidal monoliths wreathed in emerald fire. One damaged monolith beams energy at another nearby.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The von Valancius scouts approach the monoliths with as much care as possible, fearing the appearance of an enemy. A small servitor, sent to gather data about the energy beam, clearly demonstrated the destructive power of this xenotechnology. After carelessly making contact with the beam, it instantaneously broke apart into minuscule pieces. It is curious that the second pyramid is still intact, and that only matter at the source of the beam is being destroyed.
  - After: A servitor touching the beam is instantly shredded. Oddly, the target pyramid is intact; only matter at the source is destroyed.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The energy beam barely reflects off the dark metal of the pyramid. Occasionally, a scarcely visible wave runs across the surface of the monolith's walls, after which the material appears to become even smoother. It's as if one monolith is feeding the other, not destroying it. A few scouts decide to come closer in order to better examine the phenomenon.
  - After: Waves ripple over the target pyramid, smoothing it — as if one monolith feeds the other. A few scouts move closer.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The squad returns aboard safe and sound.
  - After: The squad returns safely.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The soldiers of von Valancius notice a fragment of a metallic ribcage melted right into the material of one of the walls like a bizarre bas-relief. Between the rows of ribs, a talisman of black stone shimmers with coloured light after each wave of energy. The figure to which the talisman belonged shows no signs of life. After a quick debate, the officers decide to take the artefact on board.
  - After: A metal ribcage is melted into one wall. Between its ribs, a black stone talisman glimmers. The officers take the artefact aboard.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The scouts come too close to the monolith. Their presence seems to attract the beam, and their bodies quickly fall apart much like the servitor previously did. The monolith begins to crumble into blocks, and the remainder of the team has to swiftly leave the area.
  - After: The beam seeks out the scouts and disintegrates them. The monolith crumbles; the rest flee.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The phenomenon seems too dangerous to leave it as is, and the von Valancius flagship bombards the monoliths until the last fragments are turned to dust by torpedoes and flashes from the pyramids' own deadly weaponry.
  - After: Too dangerous to leave: your flagship bombards the monoliths to dust.

## GlobalMaps/StarSystemObjects/ExplorationPlanetPoints/GiantAnomaly/GiantAnomaly_EPP_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: Remain in and research the anomalous zone.
  - After: Stay and research the anomaly.
- **Player**
  - Before: Ignore the strange occurrence.
  - After: Ignore it.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Master Helmsman Ravor reports on the giant anomaly covering most of the system. Confusion is evident in his voice: the augurs are incapable of detecting the area itself and the objects within it, but it is obvious that they exist. The blurry blots of planets and space debris are visible from the bridge of the voidship. The area distorts even the faraway stars — dim sparks enclosed in thick, curved glass.
  - After: Master Helmsman Ravor is baffled: augurs can't detect the giant anomaly, yet blurred planets and warped stars are visible.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The ship's instruments are powerless before the aberration of the Raeth-Tawi system. Sister Argenta's face twists with chagrin and contempt. She sees the accursed hand of the Archenemy at play, reaching out to conceal this holy place from the faithful defenders of the Imperium. By her words, "in this the enemy failed," for the servants of the Emperor are already here.
  - After: Raeth-Tawi defeats the instruments. Sister Argenta sees the Archenemy hiding this holy place — and failing.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The ship's instruments are powerless before the aberration of the Raeth-Tawi system, but Lady Cassia is able to see much more. She describes this image as a purple veil of blind hopelessness, dotted with azure and crimson, in which the Navigator reads the imprint of anger and pain. However, not even her sight is capable of piercing this veil.
  - After: Raeth-Tawi defeats the instruments. Lady Cassia sees a purple veil of anger and pain she can't pierce.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The ship's instruments are as powerless before the aberration of the Raeth-Tawi system as the senses of Idira Tlass. Staring at the twisted, blurred cosmos, the psyker whispers of the past, which is erased, of a present, which wasted, and of the future, which is hidden. Her prophecies are bereft of herself and the other followers of the Rogue Trader — only the abyss rules this kingdom.
  - After: Raeth-Tawi defeats the instruments and Idira Tlass. She whispers of an erased past and hidden future — only abyss.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The ship's instruments are powerless before the aberration of the Raeth-Tawi system. Yrliet Lanaevyss says that Farseers once spoke about such a thing: the impenetrable canopy is an echo, wounds created by the warp, but nothing more is known. Where even the Aeldari could not find answers, human efforts are completely futile.
  - After: Raeth-Tawi defeats the instruments. Yrliet Lanaevyss calls it a warp wound; where Aeldari failed, humans cannot succeed.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The ship's instruments are powerless before the aberration of the Raeth-Tawi system. The Lord Captain is vexed by the lack of results but can do nothing besides accept the inscrutability of certain mysteries of the universe.
  - After: Raeth-Tawi defeats the instruments. The Lord Captain accepts the mystery.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The ship's instruments are powerless before the aberration of the Raeth-Tawi system, and so is Kibellah's divination. The reading of the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperialTarotGlossary}Emperor's Tarot{/g} provides no answer, for no card in His deck can relay the twisted and aberrant nature of the anomaly.
  - After: Raeth-Tawi defeats the instruments and Kibellah: no card in the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperialTarotGlossary}Emperor's Tarot{/g} fits it.

## GlobalMaps/StarSystemObjects/ExplorationPlanetPoints/HabitablePlanet/HabitablePlanet_EPP_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: Ask the governor what is going on.
  - After: Ask what's going on.
- **Player**
  - Before: Order your men to eliminate the mutants.
  - After: Eliminate the mutants.
- **Player**
  - Before: Execute the governor on the spot.
  - After: Execute the governor.
- **Player**
  - Before: Express the desire to become the herald to the King of Distortion.
  - After: Ask to become the King of Distortion's herald.
- **Player**
  - Before: Thank the governor and leave the planet.
  - After: Thank the governor and leave.
- **Player**
  - Before: Order that the crew chart a course to the anomaly known as the "King of Distortion."
  - After: Set course for the "King of Distortion" anomaly.
- **Player**
  - Before: This world could have suffered a much worse fate — its cleansing was an act of mercy.
  - After: Its cleansing was an act of mercy.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: A small planet gently wrapped in amber forests greets you with a ruby-coloured dawn. Basil von dem Clearch, the local governor, gives the Rogue Trader a warm welcome. After several glasses of damassine, the sweltering ruler asks if {name} von Valancius would like to keep him company during the upcoming hunt.
  - After: Governor Basil von dem Clearch welcomes you warmly and invites {name} von Valancius to join his hunt.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: A dozen containers stained with blood and marred with unusual substances make their way onto your ship's cargo hold. The King of Distortion favours you, and you can feel it.
  - After: Blood-stained containers fill your hold. The King of Distortion favours you.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: After several hours of riding the local peculiar animals, you make camp in the middle of a golden forest. Basil von dem Clearch points at the sky — a flat disc rises over the horizon, constantly morphing its colour and shape. The forest grows silent and empty, you can no longer hear the singing of birds or even the rustle of wind. The governor nods with satisfaction, and a few shapes step into the clearing. Their bodies are twisted by an unknown phenomenon, and you watch the freaks with astonishment as they begin to dance to the throaty cackling of their brethren, turning the bony growths and pulsating flesh of their scaly hands toward the unnatural thing in the sky.
  - After: At camp, Basil points to a shifting disc rising in the sky. The forest falls silent. Twisted mutants enter and dance toward it.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Basil von dem Clearch looks extremely upset, but gives Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} a few chests as a parting gift nevertheless.
  - After: Basil is upset but gives Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} a few chests anyway.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The governor smiles coyly. You are about to see with your own eyes what is happening here.
  - After: The governor smiles coyly. You'll soon see.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Having armed themselves with flamers and chainswords, your party cleared out several acres of nearby forest. The scouts report destroying several villages inhabited by heretical entities.
  - After: Your party burns the forest and several heretic villages.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The hypnotic dance seemed to continue forever. The unfortunate creatures howled, whined and convulsed, unable to tear their bleeding eyes from the celestial body. When the pavonine disk outshone even the light of the local star, the physical shells of the things that used to be men burst, releasing beasts onto this plane that not even the most fluent and capable pen could describe.
  - After: The mutants convulse until the disc outshines the sun, then burst, releasing indescribable beasts.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Basil von dem Clearch excitedly explains that the creatures you saw are the children of the great King of Distortion. It is he who is the true god and patron of these fertile grounds. Once every cycle his chariot shines its light upon the world and bestows transformations upon his most ardent followers. The Rogue Trader may become one of his heralds.
  - After: Basil explains: they're children of the King of Distortion, this world's true god, who transforms his faithful. You could be his herald.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The governor's head separates from his neck with a distinctive squelch. Black and brown blood seeps into the soil beneath his corpulent body and is immediately transformed into a writhing tangle of worms that burrow deep into the ground with unnatural speed. You return to the ship pondering what to do with the world and, more importantly, what to do with the King of Distortion.
  - After: The governor's head falls; his blood becomes burrowing worms. You return, pondering the King of Distortion.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The governor practically shrieks with delight, and more eyes open on his hands and neck to give you a closer look. You must speak with the God-in-the-Chariot himself and surrender to him whatever you value most in life.
  - After: The governor shrieks with joy, sprouting eyes. You must meet the God-in-the-Chariot and surrender what you value most.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The senior officers observe suspicious activity emanating from the twisted celestial body at the heart of the system. The chaplain advises you to get ready for a potential encounter with spawn of the Archenemy, so it may be wise to reconsider unless you have holy relics, sacred wards, or blessed effigies of the Emperor.
  - After: The chaplain warns of Archenemy spawn at the system's twisted heart — reconsider without holy relics, wards or blessed effigies.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The estates of Amberworld now belong to you alone. The blessings of the King of Distortion kept spreading over the world, no longer affecting just humans. Even the birds and beasts are now subject to its divine influence! Like a true herald, you must protect this promised garden from any dangers or outside threats.
  - After: Amberworld is yours, its beasts now blessed by the King of Distortion. As herald, guard this garden.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Crimson flame devours the golden woods and black smoke covers the sky as far as the eye can see. Amberworld dies at your feet, but you regret not. It has no place when dealing with the encroachments of the Archenemy on the holy lands of the Imperium of Man.
  - After: Flame devours the golden woods. Amberworld dies; you feel no regret.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: From that moment the world belonged to the Rogue Trader alone. Your people eradicated the settlements' housing and the unclean followers of the profane cult. The corruption instilled by the King of Distortion loosened its grip, and the estates of Amberworld can breathe a sigh of relief thanks to the efforts of their new ruler. Yet malicious servants of the Archenemy still lurk in the shadows, waiting for the right moment to wrap the planet in a web of heresy. Evil does not simply disappear without a trace.
  - After: The world is yours. The cult is purged and the King of Distortion's grip loosens — but Archenemy servants still lurk.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Where endless golden forests used to glimmer, now only scorched earth and the rare flashes of burning trees remain. The flames that erased this filth from the face of the planet also stripped it of its former charm. This is the price of purification.
  - After: Golden forests are now scorched earth. Purification's price.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Relieved to be free from the Archenemy's yoke, the planet's subjects gratefully send you their humble gifts.
  - After: The freed, grateful subjects send gifts.

## GlobalMaps/StarSystemObjects/ExplorationPlanetPoints/HaemonculusThing/HaemonculusThing_EPP_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: Order the scouts to bring the beacon to the ship.
  - After: Bring the beacon to the ship.
- **Player**
  - Before: Send a scout team to the beacon.
  - After: Send scouts to the beacon.
- **Player**
  - Before: Send an assault squad to the planet's surface.
  - After: Send an assault squad down.
- **Player**
  - Before: Send a scout team to the source of the signal.
  - After: Send scouts to the signal's source.
- **Player**
  - Before: The xeno-artefact does not belong on the Rogue Trader's voidship. Order the device's destruction.

- **Player**
  - Before: Order the team to activate the beacon.
  - After: Activate the beacon.
- **Player**
  - Before: All trace of the ungodly xenos in the Imperium must be destroyed! Burn the place with holy flame.
  - After: Destroy all xenos traces! Burn it with holy flame.
- **Player**
  - Before: Give the scout team the order to return to the ship, leaving the enclosure and the mutants within alone.
  - After: Recall the scouts, leaving the mutants alone.
- **Player**
  - Before: Send out a scout team to the beacon.
  - After: Send out scouts to the beacon.
- **Player**
  - Before: Order the scouts to bring the beacon to the ship.
  - After: Bring the beacon to the ship.
- **Player**
  - Before: Ready the ship's weapons and destroy the beacon and the enclosure from orbit.
  - After: Destroy the beacon and enclosure from orbit.
- **Player**
  - Before: Leave the planet's orbit.
  - After: Leave orbit.
- **Player**
  - Before: Order the scouts to bring the beacon to the ship.
  - After: Bring the beacon to the ship.
- **Player**
  - Before: Burn the ungodly place with holy flame alongside every mutant.
  - After: Burn the place and every mutant with holy flame.
- **Player**
  - Before: Remind the soldiers that Humankind is capable of fighting off even the most terrible xenos threat, provided they find the inner strength not to yield to it.
  - After: Remind them Humankind can beat any xenos threat if they don't yield.
- **Player**
  - Before: Order the soldiers to retreat.
  - After: Order a retreat.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The emissions of the beacon previously detected by augurs turn out to be a cruel trap for the assault squad — acting on the soldiers' minds, it sends them horrible visions of brutal deaths and excruciating torture, preventing them from coming closer to the beacon and the cargo. The images of such abominable fates appearing directly in the brain would have brought ecstatic pleasure to a Drukhari, but even those warriors tempered by battle can scarcely withstand them.
  - After: The beacon is a trap, flooding the squad's minds with visions of torture. Even hardened soldiers barely endure.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Immediately after the ship approaches close enough to the planet, the strange artefact from the Haemonculus's laboratory activates! Trying to receive the incoming signal from the planet's surface, the black faces of the prism have started to emit a pulsating lilac light. The augur team reports that the source of the signal is a small beacon which cannot be studied from orbit. A group of living organisms is detected around the beacon.
  - After: The Haemonculus's prism activates, pulsing lilac. Its signal comes from a surface beacon surrounded by living organisms.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Haemonculus's prism that had been kept aboard the ship has activated again! Augurs detect another Drukhari beacon, only this time the dark artefact from the Haemonculus's laboratory establishes connection with it as soon as the ship enters orbit. The prism shows the next set of coordinates, but the beacon on the planet's surface continues emitting its sinister signal.
  - After: The prism activates again, linking with another Drukhari beacon and showing new coordinates. The beacon keeps signalling.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Haemonculus's prism residing on the ship receives the incoming signal from the planet's surface and shows the next set of coordinates. Augurs determine that, as before, the beacon on this planet is set up in the middle of a fenced area with a multitude of living creatures within.
  - After: The prism shows new coordinates. Again, the beacon sits in a pen full of creatures.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Augurs have detected a container with unidentified cargo on the planet next to the Drukhari beacon. Many kilometres around this zone are filled with huge, likely dangerous xenos lifeforms. A very strong emission of unclear nature radiates from the beacon itself. The cargo can only be taken from the planet by force with the help of an assault squad.
  - After: Unidentified cargo lies by a Drukhari beacon amid huge xenos lifeforms. The beacon radiates a strong emission. Only an assault squad can take it.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: A disgusting sight unfolds before the scouts. In a sinister, high-fenced enclosure, hideous mutants crawl and writhe. Hundreds of ugly beasts, their shapes vaguely reminiscent of humans, squirm on several pairs of deformed arms and legs. Incapable of attacking or doing much of anything else beyond crawling in the dirt, the creatures are riven with endless pain which seems to feed the Drukhari beacon at the very centre of the pen. A pulsating lilac light flows from the beacon.
  - After: In a fenced pen, hundreds of many-limbed mutants writhe. Their pain seems to feed the Drukhari beacon.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The activated beacon on the planet emits a thin lilac beam, sending out a signal, which is promptly accepted by the artefact on board. The prism unfolds into many small petals and shows a holographic image of a certain planet and corresponding coordinates.
  - After: The beacon signals the prism, which projects a planet and its coordinates.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: In response to the beacon's attempted removal, the collars and chains binding the mutants together suddenly activate, emitting a series of destructive impulses that slowly inflate and explode the beasts one after the other. In nightmarish agony, writhing and shrieking from unbearable pain, the Haemonculus's victims are finally granted their deaths and long-awaited freedom.
  - After: As the beacon is removed, the mutants' collars explode them one by one. The Haemonculus's victims finally die.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: This time around, the scene the scouts face is no less loathsome than the last. Hundreds of those who were undoubtedly at some point humans are lined up in a chain of bizarre geometric shapes. Their bodies, fused with each other at the hands and the feet, swing steadily, unable to fall. Tortured wails break through sewn lips, and burned-out eye sockets gape outward from mutilated faces.
  - After: Hundreds of former humans are fused hand to foot into swaying chains, wailing through sewn lips.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The removal of the beacon from its platform leads to a grotesque spectacle. As if the beacon had sent a signal, unseen devices within the mutants activate sequentially, burning out each mutant's innards with a scarlet glow. One after the other, continuing down the chain, the poor souls' bodies slowly smoulder and turn to ash.
  - After: As the beacon is removed, devices burn the mutants to ash one by one.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Expecting resistance, the assault squad disembarks some distance away from the beacon. To the soldiers' surprise, the gigantic mutants surrounding the beacon turn out to be incapable of even moving. Like carpets of formless chunks of flesh, these groaning and bleeding creatures cover the earth for many kilometres around. Something unseen brings them unbearable suffering.
  - After: The squad lands warily, but the giant mutants can't move — carpets of groaning flesh, suffering from something unseen.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Lord Captain's order sent through vox-devices remains unheard by the soldiers — consumed by mind-destroying visions, they open fire in an attempt to preserve their souls. Their haphazard volley directed at the beacon and containers leads to a bright explosion, in which both the warriors and the Haemonculus's heinous works perish.
  - After: Maddened, the soldiers open fire. The beacon and containers explode, killing them and the Haemonculus's works.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Guided by the Lord Captain's word, the soldiers resolutely advance on the beacon. The Rogue Trader's speech helps them withstand the beacon's horrors and remain sane. By activating a switch on the beacon, the soldiers finally turn off the torturous emissions.
  - After: Your words keep the soldiers sane. They shut off the beacon's emissions.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Guided by the Lord Captain's word, the soldiers resolutely advance on the beacon. A few of them manage to withstand the nightmarish visions, remaining sane and not taking their lives before reaching the beacon. By activating a switch on the latter, the soldiers finally turn off the torturous emissions.
  - After: Only a few soldiers withstand the visions. They shut off the beacon's emissions.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The removal of the beacon from the platform proceeds as planned. Nothing happens afterward. The gigantic groaning carpet of mutants continues lying where they were — neither exploding nor burning up. The Vox Master reports that the prism from the Haemonculus's laboratory shattered into a myriad of needles. It flew apart in every direction with a loud snap, gravely wounding several crew members.
  - After: The beacon is removed; the mutants are unharmed. But the prism shattered into needles, gravely wounding several crew.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Once the beacon is torn off its platform, a scarlet-lilac impulse runs across the giant rods that pierce the statues of flesh. All the unholy figures are gripped at once by blinding blue flame as the air is filled with incoherent screams and the smell of burned meat.
  - After: As the beacon is removed, the flesh statues burst into blue flame amid screams.
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: Augurs spot a von Valancius shuttle, marked as from your own ship, beside a tunnel entrance.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: In the registry the expeditionary shuttle number 712 has been designated as "irretrievably lost" for many years. Information about the circumstances of its disappearance is suspiciously sparse, as if someone deliberately erased it. From the crumbs of information that remain, you gather that it was sent to explore some object on an unknown world on the order of Lord Captain Theodora and never returned.
  - After: Shuttle 712 is listed "irretrievably lost" years ago, its records suspiciously erased. Lord Captain Theodora sent it to explore an unknown world; it never returned.
- **(conversation owner)**

This shuttle has clearly been here for a very long time. Next to the shuttle you find crates of archaeological equipment, on which one can just barely make out the emblem of the Explorators. Most of these crates are lying next to massive black doors of xenos origin — the entrance to the tunnels.
  - After: The shuttle is half-buried, its crest worn away. Long here. Explorator crates lie by massive black xenos doors: the tunnel entrance.

You make your way through cramped corridors giving way to huge black halls, where a dim emerald glow from no discernible source brings forth the silhouettes of equipment abandoned by the Tech-Priests. The suffocating, oppressive silence that accompanies you during the descent is broken only by the echo of your footsteps — deafening and yet so insignificant against the background of the cyclopean arches.
  - After: Hours of descent through vast black halls, an emerald glow on abandoned Tech-Priest gear. Oppressive silence.

## GlobalMaps/StarSystemObjects/ExplorationPlanetPoints/TombSotto/TombSotto_EPP_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: This sordid place has neither life nor loot. But knowing the nasty tricks that life can pull is a treasure in its own right.
  - After: No life, no loot. But life's nasty tricks are a lesson worth having.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Imperium cartographers and chroniclers know this place well. Long ago the planet was a prosperous outpost capable of eclipsing even Footfall. There used to be a cyclopean tomb station on its orbit, the final resting place of Cornelius Sotto, one of the discoverers of the Koronus Expanse. The tomb gave its name to the entire system.
  - After: Once an outpost rivalling Footfall, orbited by the tomb of Cornelius Sotto, discoverer of the Expanse.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: However, about four hundred years ago, an unknown cosmic body rammed into the station, causing it to collapse onto the planet. Not only did the catastrophe kill the settlers, it also made the world uninhabitable for centuries. The crater formed by the station's impact can still be observed from orbit. Sotto's Tomb became a sepulchre for the entire planet.
  - After: Four centuries ago, a cosmic body smashed the tomb onto the planet, killing all. It became the world's sepulchre.

Should the Tech-Adepts of the Machine Cult manage to awaken its spirits, the Rogue Trader's crew may explore the depths of the sea at their leisure.

The officers on the bridge worriedly look up from their cogitators — the machines' screens turn on and off chaotically, not obeying any of their operators' commands.
  - After: A bottomless hole of total darkness. Augurs learn nothing, and the ship is slowly drawn in. Cogitators flicker, ignoring commands.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Rogue Trader's vessel slowly draws closer to the cosmic hole. The outlines of walls, equipment, and people inside the voidship are distorted as they flicker and stretch under the influence of an invisible force. The machine spirits are badly affected and start rampaging across the ship, disabling cogitators on every deck.
  - After: Walls and people stretch and flicker. Maddened machine spirits disable cogitators everywhere.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: A few operators manage to wring a minute amount of useful information out of the archives. Such anomalies are extremely rare, randomly appearing gravitational wells which connect different points in space. Where such a well leads is impossible to predict.
  - After: The archives say: a rare, random gravitational well linking points in space. Where it leads is unknowable.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The voidship's machines refuse to carry out their orders and shut off in response to every attempt to access a function. Terrified by the flickering distortions in their own bodies, the operators frantically try to find out at least some information about the phenomenon, but their attempts remain in vain.
  - After: The machines shut down; terrified operators learn nothing.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The closer the vessel gets to the hole, the faster it is pulled in. Thousands of people on every deck are gripped by panic — their bodies are turning into thin, twisting threads, fraying and tearing into pieces, exposing veins, bones, and internal organs. Falling apart into screws, plates, and bolts, Tech-Priests continue to offer relentless prayers to the machine spirits, but their binharic chants melt into the endless screams and cries for help. Finally, the voidship jumps into the cosmic tunnel with a torturous lurch.
  - After: The pull quickens. Bodies fray into threads, exposing bone and organs; Tech-Priests fall apart mid-prayer. The ship lurches into the tunnel.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Barely overcoming the anomaly's pull, the voidship crawls in the other direction. A nightmarish cacophony of moans, prayers, and the screeching of metal fills every deck. Thousands of people are gripped in panic — their bodies are turning into thin, twisting threads, fraying and tearing into pieces, exposing veins, bones, and internal organs.
  - After: The ship crawls away amid screams and screeching metal, bodies fraying into threads.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The walls of the bridge, the crew's silhouettes, and the ship's holy machines tremble and stretch out like rubber bands. Alerts of malfunctioning cogitators and maddened chronographs come in from every deck, as do reports of indescribable hallucinations gripping the crew. While the Tech-Priests are trying to placate the machine spirits, helmsman Ravor reports that the situation is bad. Navigational systems are barely functional, and the invisible force is getting stronger and accelerating, ceaselessly dragging the vessel into its dark bosom. There is little time, and the Lord Captain must decide — leave the dangerous place or give in to the force and study the anomaly from within.
  - After: The bridge stretches like rubber; the crew hallucinates. Helmsman Ravor: navigation barely works and the pull is growing. Escape, or yield and study it from within?
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: By chance or by the Emperor's grace, the voidship successfully clambers out of the tenacious grasp of the anomaly. Its influence dissipates — onboard systems return to normal one after another, and the deformed bodies of the crew take on their original shapes as if nothing had happened. Now, the only reminder of the event is a dull muscle pain.
  - After: By the Emperor's grace, the ship breaks free. Systems and bodies return to normal, leaving only dull muscle pain.

Raising his voice to a shout, the operator reports that his comrades are already dead, and soon it will be his turn! The augurs are telling a different story: all of the scouts are alive and still moving forward.

Worried murmurs sweep across the bridge — the officers are certain that this is the voidship of the old ghost stories. The Queen's Lament has appeared countless times in all corners of the Imperium. Like a ghost, it manifested out of nowhere and just as mysteriously vanished in the darkness of space, taking with it those who dared to board.
  - After: The vox works, but only silence comes. Officers murmur: it's the legendary ghost ship that takes those who board.

The soldiers confirm that they're not seeing ghosts but living people made of flesh and bone. The soldiers are begging the Rogue Trader to let them talk to their loved ones for a moment.
  - After: A child's cry. The operator stutters: the scouts' dead loved ones block the way, flesh and bone. The soldiers beg to speak with them.

  - Before: Queen's Lament — the Rogue Trader has heard that name before. This voidship was destroyed by xenos in one of the violent battles for the Expanse over three millennia ago. They say that its captain was a devout and vengeful man.
  - After: Queen's Lament: destroyed by xenos in the Expanse three millennia ago. Its captain was devout and vengeful.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: After fumbling with a few switches, the Vox Master says in a perplexed voice that the incoming signal should've been interrupted, but it's still being received by the Rogue Trader's vox.
  - After: The Vox Master is baffled: the signal should be cut, yet it continues.

The tormented cries of these souls drown out all thoughts, and visions of the past intertwine with those of the present. The dead see the living as treacherous xenos, attacking the crew with ghostly chainswords and bolters, knocking the wind out of the terrified officers. The apparition dissipates into thick blue mist just as suddenly as it appeared, leaving behind only several strands of grey hair among the most impressionable crew members.

The young man's hair has turned white after the time spent on the cursed vessel, and he has lost the ability to speak. His story and rumours of what happened to the other scouts will live on for many years in hushed whispers across every deck of the Rogue Trader's voidship.

  - After: The trip took sixteen hours and forty-one minutes; they need rest. Vigdis: only half an hour passed outside.

  - After: The ghost ship's tale will be whispered for years.

  - After: Check whether it's an illusion

However, the ship's air remains undefiled by the rank odour, and the maggots sometimes completely vanish from sight. Should we get rid of the affected stores?
  - After: The quartermaster reports food and water crawling with grey maggots, yet there's no stench, and the maggots sometimes vanish. Destroy the stores?
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The purifying flame consumed the provisions in an instant, much faster than anyone expected. The crew's ears rang with a pained shriek and the scorched stores vanished without so much as a trace of ash. The vessel's ecclesiarchs consecrated the compartment with holy signs, but the rest of the voidsmen decided that the contamination had been nothing more than an illusion.
  - After: The flame consumes them instantly, with a shriek and no ash. The crew calls it an illusion.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The officers ordered the men to unleash a salvo. Upon ignition, one of the flame throwers unleashed a blazing whirlwind, turning its owner into a wailing torch. The spill from the exploded fuel tank drenched the ship's bulkhead and severely damaged the adjacent hold, burning many of the resident voidsmen. The scorched stores vanished without so much as a trace of ash, as such most everyone decided the worms had been nothing more than an illusion.
  - After: A flamer explodes, burning its wielder and many voidsmen nearby. The stores vanish without ash; most call it an illusion.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: At first glance the provisions are hopelessly ruined by scabs and disgusting larvae, but looking away makes the squirming filth vanish into thin air. "Yet another deception of the warp," thought the Lord Captain, proved right when the vessel arrived in realspace.
  - After: The larvae vanish whenever you look away. A warp deception, as realspace confirms.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The disgusting larvae started to spread, ruining the provisions. No one dared to approach the crates, and the compartment remained sealed until the very end of the journey. Upon leaving the Sea of Souls, the quartermaster was in no hurry to inspect it. When he finally gathered the courage, it turned out the contamination had been an illusion and nothing more.
  - After: The larvae spread; the hold stays sealed until journey's end. It proves an illusion.

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Sister Argenta, one of the Lord Captain's personal retinue, was found in her cabin — pale, crying, and caught up in a waking dream. She didn't seem to notice anyone around her. Instead, she clutched a fragment of a burnt Aquila in her hand and kept calling for her mother. It took an hour to bring her round.
  - After: Sister Argenta was found weeping in a waking dream, clutching a burnt Aquila, calling for her mother.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Seneschal Abelard Werserian was found in his quarters in a trance-like state. He was pacing the room and talking to an unseen interlocutor, asking the same questions over and over: "Why won't the fever break?" and "Does the esteemed chirurgeon have the faintest idea what he is doing?" Then he sat by the bed for a long time, clutching the sleeve of a void suit, and repeating, "Everything will be all right, son." With great difficulty, the enforcers managed to return the Seneschal to his senses.
By the order of Seneschal Werserian, the report on this incident has been erased from the ship's logs.
  - After: Seneschal Abelard Werserian was found in a trance, cursing an unseen chirurgeon over a fever, then clutching a void suit sleeve: "Everything will be all right, son." He had the report erased.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The xenos Yrliet, one of the Lord Captain's personal retinue, was found delirious in one of the ship's bays. She was screaming in her unholy language, her arms raised high above her head, as if she was trying to keep the sky from falling. The enforcers were unable to free her from the trance. Two who attempted to move Yrliet were attacked and died instantly. The xenos regained awareness about ten hours later. She explained that she had seen her homeworld of Crudarach collapsing around her and she had been the only one able to hold up its walls. She added that no mon-keigh should ever touch her again without permission, and that, in the future, she would deal with the call of the warp on her own.
  - After: Yrliet was found screaming, arms raised as if holding up the sky. Two enforcers who touched her died. Waking, she said she'd held up collapsing Crudarach. No mon-keigh may touch her unbidden.

## GlobalMaps/WarpTravel/WarpEvents/Reactivity/WarpReactivityE_2/WarpReE_2

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The warp jump went smoothly enough, although many crew members reported strange incidents while they were asleep — they sensed someone approaching them and laying a hand on their forehead. Then the hand seemed to pass through their skin, through their skull, and with tender motions, sorted their jumbled thoughts into some sort of order.
  - After: Sleeping crew felt a hand pass into their skulls and tidy their thoughts.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Magos Pasqal noted that the mysterious incident had allowed him to "remember" a few highly obscure tech-rituals... which, it seemed, he had never studied in the first place.
  - After: Magos Pasqal now "remembers" tech-rituals he never studied.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Everyone affected by the incident was horrified for a long time afterward. Resident psyker Idira Tlass, however, remarked with a grin that the "tidying up" had allowed her to dredge up a vital memory and find the left sock that had long been missing from her favourite pair.
  - After: Most were horrified. Idira Tlass grinned: it found her long-lost left sock.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: After the strange incident, Jae Heydari was uncharacteristically sombre for almost two watches and spent several hours in the ship's chapel praying.
  - After: Jae Heydari turned sombre and prayed in the chapel.

## GlobalMaps/WarpTravel/WarpEvents/Reactivity/WarpReactivityE_3/WarpReE_4

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Strange phantoms drift through the crew's minds. The voidsmen discuss the fantastic visions that haunt their sleep and fill their dreams, the visions of a future that never was. A strange melancholy holds sway over the ship's company.
  - After: The crew dream of a future that never was. Melancholy grips the ship.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Interrogator Heinrix van Calox did not leave his cabin for 24 hours, after which he went to the medicae facility for help, weakened by blood loss and exhaustion. There were open and bleeding wounds at his nape, neck, and back. A chirurgeon remarked that the location of the stigmata resembled the placement of neural connectors on the bodies of Imperial Knight pilots, and van Calox forcefully and most indecorously suggested the man keep his idle fantasies to himself.
  - After: Heinrix van Calox emerged after 24 hours, bleeding where Imperial Knight pilots have neural connectors. He told the chirurgeon to keep his fantasies to himself.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Jae Heydari spent several days in feverish excitement, bothering the crew with stories of some "heroic exploit that would make her name famous for centuries" and persistent demands that they "raise a glass for her new promotion." Before the officers could discern the reason for such agitation, the obsession left her. According to reports, Mistress Heydari has come to her senses and is stubbornly pretending the episode never happened in the first place.
  - After: Jae Heydari spent days boasting of a "heroic exploit" and a "promotion." Now she pretends it never happened.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Tradition dictates that whatever happens in the Navigator's Sanctum during a warp jump remains a mystery, but the transmissions from the esteemed Lady Orsellio during the assault of the phantoms frightened vox operators. According to them, Cassia's voice became unrecognisably clear and cheerful. One of the radio operators reported strange conversations in the Sanctum where the Lady Navigator chattered happily, suggested they "play in the garden," and giggled. Several hours later another operator claimed he heard a woman weep bitterly over the vox-channel.
  - After: Over the vox, Cassia sounded cheerful, giggling, "Let's play in the garden." Hours later, a woman was heard weeping.

## World/Dialogs/Ch0_Prologue/BeforeFinalBattle/BeforeFinalBattle

- **Player**
  - Before: [Draw your weapon] "Voigtvir, you duplicitous cur! The Rogue Trader's death will be avenged!"
  - After: [Draw your weapon] "Voigtvir, you cur! The Rogue Trader will be avenged!"

  - Before: "Theodora von Valancius is dead. I found her and the Arch-Militant in her study."
  - After: "Theodora is dead. I found her and the Arch-Militant in her study."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The ship can still be steered out of the warp, but we must first restore communication between the bridge and the Navigator's Sanctum."
  - After: "We can leave the warp if the bridge reaches the Navigator's Sanctum."

  - After: "The Lord Captain won't be joining us."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Merely a trace of the corruption that is assailing this vessel."
  - After: "Just a trace of the ship's corruption."

  - Before: "I have a Sister of Battle at my side! What suspicions could you possibly have?"
  - After: "A Sister of Battle stands with me! What suspicions?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I forbid you the very thought of yielding! Only by resigning to your fate will you truly suffer defeat!"
  - After: "Don't you dare yield! Only resignation is defeat!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Perhaps the warp does not have to be the end..."
  - After: "Perhaps the warp needn't be the end..."
- **Player**

  - After: [To the party] "Weapons ready. Let us die with honour."

  - After: {n}Edelthrad glares.{/n} "Traitor! You ignored my {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox-casts{/g}!"
- **Edelthrad**

  - After: {n}Edelthrad, harrowed.{/n} "{name}! Where's the Lord Captain?"

But if there is any honour in you, we can at least die with dignity and give our lives for the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}."
  - After: {n}Edelthrad, bleeding.{/n} "{d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentBack}Too late{/d}. Let's die for the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Edelthrad winces, which only makes his grimace worse.{/n} "I am still standing. And I have enough strength in me for one more fight. All that truly concerns me is this: where is the Lord Captain?"
  - After: {n}Edelthrad winces.{/n} "I can fight. Where's the Lord Captain?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Edelthrad's eyes widen.{/n} "Shameless filth. How dare—"
  - After: {n}Edelthrad gapes.{/n} "Shameless filth. How dare—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What? You!" {n}Edelthrad looks at you.{/n} "This is your doing!"
  - After: "You!" {n}Edelthrad stares.{/n} "Your doing!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Edelthrad's eyes widen.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}God-Emperor{/g} preserve us, the Rogue Trader is dead? The ship has lost her Lord Captain, and the house its head..."
  - After: {n}Edelthrad pales.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}God-Emperor{/g} preserve us! The house is headless..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g} narrows his eyes.{/n} "I sense the mark of the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} on you... an {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentWithTheodora}echo of the powers{/d} that are ravaging this ship. What is it? The aftermath of the terrors that you had to face or an admission of guilt?"
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g} squints.{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} marks you, an {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentWithTheodora}echo of the powers{/d} here. Terror or guilt?"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Master Edelthrad... no. We have remained in each other's sight ever since {name} broke free from Kunrad's schemes. The Lord Captain was killed by another's hand... and, by the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g}, I can surmise whose hand it was!"
  - After: "No. {name} was with me. By the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g}, I know who killed the Lord Captain!"

  - After: "I can't vouch for you, {name}." {n}Argenta looks away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Edelthrad glares at you for a few moments longer.{/n} "Perhaps. The {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}God-Emperor{/g} knows this crew is infested with corruption as it is..."

- **Abelard**

  - Before: {n}Edelthrad shudders and grabs his shoulder. As you watch, the sleeve of his jacket bursts open, and two bone growths pierce through the fabric.{/n} "No matter what ritual Kunrad is performing there... the warp is too strong, I cannot withstand it. I feel my body changing with every second... The warp is ringing in the air... This is the end.   - After: {n}Bone bursts from Edelthrad's sleeve.{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} takes me. We die here with the {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} and heirs."
- **Edelthrad**
  - Before: "We are out of time!" {n}Edelthrad bites his knuckle, desperately thinking. You see a wave ripple across the whites of Edelthrad's eyes, and they begin to turn a sickly yellow.{/n}
  - After: "No time!" {n}Edelthrad's eyes yellow.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Edelthrad stares at you, and his eyes harden with cold resolve once more.{/n} "Then we have no right to bow our heads..."
  - After: {n}Edelthrad steels himself.{/n} "Then we won't bow..."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Enough talking rubbish! The {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g}'s alive and ready to take the ship out of the warp if he gets some help from the bridge!"
  - After: "Rubbish! The {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g} needs the bridge's help!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Save the lofty words for later, will you? The {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g}'s ready to take the ship out of the warp if he gets some help from the bridge!"
  - After: "Save it! The {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g} needs the bridge's help!"

  - Before: {n}Edelthrad gives you a confused look. Then, as realisation dawns on him, his eyes fill with disbelief.{/n} "No... The Rogue Trader... is dead?"
  - After: {n}Edelthrad, stunned.{/n} "The Rogue Trader... is dead?"
