## World/Dialogs/Ch0_Prologue/EdgeOfDaybreak/EdgeOfDaybreak

- **Player**
  - Before: "Are you the one behind all that is happening here? The one who addressed me and guided me out of the flames?"
  - After: "Are you behind this? Did you lead me from the flames?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am saving my people. Do your worst, but you cannot stop me."
  - After: "I'm saving my people. You can't stop me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have already resisted the temptation of the warp once. Whatever you are, you will not cloud my mind with a new illusion!"
  - After: "I've resisted the warp once. No more illusions!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You... You are to blame for Theodora's death?"
  - After: "You caused Theodora's death?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The vision lets out a cawing laugh.{/n} "I am the beginning and the end, and all that courses in between. I am the voice of the Truth that is destined to triumph, for this triumph is the terminal point of every twisted maze of fate."
  - After: {n}It caws with laughter.{/n} "I am beginning and end, the Truth destined to triumph."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Did you stand in the path of another's destiny only to steal it? You accepted the call of the Primordial Truth — and claimed that fate as your own. So be it. I wove the threads of destiny and {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentWithTheodora}held out my hand to you{/d} when the flame arose in your path. You took it and, in doing so, sealed your fate. In the future... in the future, you will repay me for this boon in full."
  - After: "You stole another's fate. I {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentWithTheodora}held out my hand to you{/d} in the flames; you took it. You will repay me in full."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Who are you to {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentBack}oppose destiny itself{/d} for the sake of lives that are not your own? So many threads stretch between you and other creatures of your world — pitiful, worthless links, ready to shatter at the slightest touch. A muddled, erratic, pointless tangle."
  - After: "Who are you to {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentBack}oppose destiny itself{/d} for others' lives? Your bonds are a pitiful tangle."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Mortal. Who are you to oppose the very flows of fate?" {n}The vision lowers its head, its harrowing gaze boring into you. For but a moment, something changes in Theodora's expression. It almost looks like a shadow of... {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentThroughFire}fear{/d}?{/n} "It matters not. Your footfalls are an echo of the sand pouring between the scales. Your hopes and faith are my mockery."
  - After: "Mortal, you oppose fate?" {n}A flicker of {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentThroughFire}fear{/d} crosses Theodora's face?{/n} "No matter. Your faith is my mockery."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Indeed, for the boundless Truth encompasses all. Merely one part of it reached out to you — and answer you did. You could become the new champion."
  - After: "Indeed. Part of the Truth called, and you answered. You could be the new champion."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Theodora lets out a long screech — a shrill, overwhelming sound that can only be interpreted as laughter.{/n} "Lead them, mortal. Guide them, persuade them, force them to walk your path. You will need followers, for destiny is preordained."
  - After: {n}Theodora screeches with laughter.{/n} "Lead them, mortal. You'll need followers. Destiny is preordained."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Theodora hisses almost painfully, as if wounded by your words.{/n} "Resisting the inevitable means only that realisation and submission will bring greater torment. There is no power that can hinder the flows of fate."
  - After: {n}Theodora hisses, wounded.{/n} "Resistance only deepens the torment. Nothing hinders fate."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your head begins to spin and viscous drops slither down your cheeks. You blink — and you are no longer looking at Theodora. It is the traitor Voigtvir, just as fluid and ephemeral as the previous apparition. The same terrifying voice seethes from his lips.{/n} "The aspirant vowed to return with a trophy — a relic that could serve the Edge of Daybreak. That fate was assured and the steps chosen. And yet... you broke the unbreakable when you took the aspirant's place. I see you — on the day when the final dawn rises over the iron world. I see you by my side on that day, the day of my resurrection."
  - After: {n}It becomes Voigtvir.{/n} "The aspirant was to bring a relic for the Edge of Daybreak. You took his place. I see you beside me at the final dawn over the iron world: my resurrection."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The image is scattered by invisible sorcerous winds — and you see Idira, her eyes aglow with the same sinister flame.{/n} "Your image is woven into the tapestry of things to come. I am the will of the Weaver of Destinies, and today, I will weave a new thread of elusive possibilities and fickle chances. The thread that will lead you out of the maw of irreversibility. The thread that will help you find the keys to salvation. The thread that will guide you and the weapon of our return to me."
  - After: {n}Now it is Idira, eyes burning.{/n} "I, the Weaver of Destinies, weave your thread: to salvation's keys, then back to me with the weapon of our return."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A cavalcade of hazy glimpses of a future yet unknown passes before your eyes. A flash of crimson... purple... The images replace one another in a violent kaleidoscope without ever letting you get a proper look at them. Through the rippling mirage, you see a twisted image of Abelard, the loyal Seneschal of the dynasty.{/n} "The path is set, Child of the Dawn. The thread is woven. Follow it... servant of mine."
  - After: {n}Future glimpses flash: crimson, purple. Then a twisted Abelard.{/n} "The thread is woven, Child of the Dawn. Follow it... servant of mine."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The image before you is hazy, swaying in sorcerous currents invisible to mortal eyes, as if whatever is beneath this thin shell is constantly changing while still remaining the same. It has taken on the guise of Theodora, but the false Rogue Trader's eyes reveal the entity's true, surreal nature. One of Theodora's eyes is engulfed in otherworldly fire, the other, a vessel of ancient evil, bores into you. A voice seeps directly into your brain without ever reaching your ears, and this voice booms with all the horrors of the warp.{/n}
  - After: {n}An apparition wearing Theodora's face, one eye ablaze, speaks inside your skull.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It resonates and merges with the voices that have {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}already dug their foul roots{/d} into your consciousness. A moment later, you realise that all these voices are the myriad manifestations of the same call that has finally invaded your mind.{/n}
  - After: {n}It merges with voices that {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}already dug their foul roots{/d} into you: one call.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch0_Prologue/EmperorProtects/EmperorProtects

- **Player**

  - After: "The Aquila was glowing!"

  - Before: "We're still alive! Fancy that!"
  - After: "We're alive! Fancy that!"

  - After: [Refuse help, stand] "I'm fine."

  - Before: [Rise and stand tall] "No element holds power over the righteous."
  - After: [Rise tall] "The righteous do not burn."

  - After: [Accept Abelard's help] "I've been better."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The blinding inferno, the harrowing pyre, the all-consuming storm releases you as you step out, barely able to stay on your feet. The blood is pounding in your ears, drowning out the world around you. Your eyes, caked in soot and burnt eyelashes, refuse to open. Free from the flames, you take two more steps before collapsing to your knees.{/n}

A new strength spreads throughout your veins, and despite the wounds, your body is once more ready for trials and struggle. You open your eyes and see, aglow with warm light before you, the {g|Encyclopedia:Aquila}Aquila{/g} — the sacred symbol of the Imperium.{/n}
  - After: {n}The pain suddenly retreats; new strength fills you. Before you glows the {g|Encyclopedia:Aquila}Aquila{/g}.{/n}
- **Abelard**

He notices your gaze and breathes a sigh of relief.{/n} "You are alive... which is more than I was expecting after what you just did!"
  - After: "—{mf|ster|stress} {name}! {mf|Master|Mistress} {name}, can you hear me?" {n}Abelard leans over you, relieved.{/n} "Alive... I didn't expect that!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Behind Argenta, you see Idira Tlass doubled over in a fit of nausea. The rest of the people who were following you have withered away in the fire that continues to rage mere two steps away from you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Idira retches. Everyone else who followed you burned.{/n}

  - Before: "Your attempts at humour are inappropriate." {n}Abelard frowns.{/n} "You nearly got us all killed..."
  - After: "Inappropriate." {n}Abelard frowns.{/n} "You nearly killed us all..."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira wipes her mouth and rasps,{/n} "What happened to Lady Theodora? Did she follow us?"
  - After: {n}Idira wipes her mouth.{/n} "Where's Lady Theodora?"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "There was no Theodora, witch." {n}Argenta is staring straight ahead, then crosses her arms over her chest with reverence.{/n} "There was an illusion, a temptation, a foul taint that tried to lead us astray. But {name} perceived its true nature!"
  - After: "There was no Theodora, witch." {n}Argenta, reverent.{/n} "Only an illusion. {name} saw through it!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Is that right, Adepta Sanctimonious? What, we'll just pretend like we didn't see the Lord Captain standing there in the fire? Abelard, you tell her!"
  - After: "Really, Adepta Sanctimonious? We didn't all see the Lord Captain? Abelard, tell her!"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Whatever it was... it matters no longer." {n}Abelard sighs.{/n} "Your conduct, {name}, is bordering on madness... or holiness. A path opened behind you. Truly, would you have received wounds like these if there had been no fire?"

- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard glances around, then looks back at you, his expression now twice as worried.{/n} "You are delirious, {name}. Whatever it is you think you are seeing..." {n}He seems perturbed by your words — he casts another, surreptitious glance at the Aquila you just pointed at.{/n}
  - After: {n}Abelard frowns.{/n} "You're delirious, {name}..." {n}He glances uneasily at the Aquila.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Even if you were anticipating another wave of pain, it does not come: your muscles feel strong, and your limbs obey you without fail. And yet, deep inside, somewhere next to your heart and stomach, you feel a certain tension akin to that of a taut string: you are at your limit. Be it adrenaline or the strength of your faith, it will not carry you much farther.{/n}
  - After: {n}No pain comes, but you feel taut as a string: you're at your limit.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Praise the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g}!" {n}Argenta kneels next to you, and for the first time you see her eyes radiate pure, unclouded joy.{/n} "We passed through the flames! Oh, how can this be anything but a portent? For so it is said that the Emperor will bless the worthiest and most steadfast in their faith!"
  - After: "Praise the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g}!" {n}Argenta kneels, joyful.{/n} "We passed through flame! He blesses the faithful!"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "The wounds are merely a sign of a trial laudably passed. It is something to be proud of, the same as decorations or badges of honour." {n}Argenta herself sounds proud, even fervid.{/n}
  - After: "Wounds are badges of honour for a trial passed." {n}Argenta, fervid.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}In the next moment, you are struck with another realisation: the {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}repulsive presence{/d}, the one that has plagued your mind since Voigtvir wounded you, is gone. The fire seems to have burned the entity away without a trace.{/n}
  - After: {n}The {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}repulsive presence{/d} from Voigtvir's wound is gone, burned away.{/n}

  - Before: {n}The woman bursts into guttural, drunken laughter.{/n} "Sorry, old man — the voices are so loud I can't even hear myself! They shriek, they sing, they— oh, Abelard, how they sing!"
  - After: {n}She laughs drunkenly.{/n} "Sorry, old man! The voices sing so loud!"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "{name}, this is Idira Tlass, personal psyker and diviner of Her Ladyship Theodora von Valancius." {n}Abelard looks her up and down.{/n} "Idira..."
  - After: "{name}, Idira Tlass, Lady Theodora's psyker." {n}Abelard eyes her.{/n} "Idira..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Dead. Without a doubt. And the voices wail, heralding countless nightmares, cackling at each soul among the hundreds that are now joining the warp. The shriek from the Navigator's Sanctum was louder than the rest — and it's better that we save the Navigator than some lever-puller from a cooling module or a cook from the middle decks!"
  - After: "Dead. Hundreds are joining the warp. The Navigator's Sanctum shrieked loudest; save him first!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Idira nods, yet her gaze is directed somewhere away from you.{/n} "The voices from beyond the threshold whisper to me. Sometimes their murmurs are clear, they grant insight. Sometimes they drive me mad... But I am patient. I know how to listen. And discern. But now, with this clamour around me... Too many voices. Too loud."
  - After: {n}Idira looks away.{/n} "The warp's voices bring insight, or madness. Now there are too many."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Idira turns her head to you, her vacant eyes flaring like embers.{/n} "And you... you, {name} von Valancius, are a sorcerer {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}too{/d}. Just like the other one. Lady Theodora must have grown so fond of psykers she wants one to replace her..."
  - After: {n}Idira's eyes flare.{/n} "You're a sorcerer {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}too{/d}, {name} von Valancius. Theodora wants a psyker successor..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The whispers called me — the ones I could make out among all the screams and screeches. Those who are rocking this boat hit us where it hurt — they went after the {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g}, our guide through the warp. Other whispers called me to the enginarium... but it was too late. I heard the cry of our master cog... and the silence that followed."
  - After: "The whispers called me. They struck the {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g}, our warp guide. The enginarium too; I heard our master cog cry, then silence."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh, no. No, no, no. Nothing is well about him. Can't you feel the chill crawling on your skin? The eyes watching you? The warp ice has already encased the bulkheads... What follows is calamity."
  - After: "No. Feel the chill? Warp ice covers the bulkheads. Calamity follows."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Idira freezes. Then she slaps her cheeks, rubs her face, and looks at you — the supernatural glow is gone from her eyes, and a smirk spreads across her lips.{/n} "But we're not just going to stand here and take it, are we? The state of things in here suggests there's a Navigator around — maybe one who's crippled or at death's door, but still kicking. And since our skin hasn't peeled off our faces just yet, his third eye must be closed — at worst, it's a little roughed up. So what are we moping around for? Let's go protect that noble mutant while we're still alive!"
  - After: {n}Idira slaps her cheeks and smirks.{/n} "But we won't take it lying down! The Navigator's alive, his third eye shut. Let's protect that noble mutant!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm not drunk, old man. I'm suffering the effects of the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} that is seeping through these walls. I see the ship's fate — to die in the waves of the Immaterium, fall under the burning rays of the final dawn... And in the roaring blaze, I see a figure standing... Who is it? I have no answer."
  - After: "Not drunk. It's the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g}. I see the ship dying under the final dawn, and someone in the blaze. Who? Unknown."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard spits out a florid curse.{/n} "Blast it! You're right — first we need to deal with what is happening here."
  - After: {n}Abelard curses.{/n} "Blast it! You're right."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}entity in your consciousness{/d} shrinks and crawls in deeper, its claws scraping against the walls of your mind, as if the presence is trying to hide from the seer standing before you.{/n}
  - After: {n}The {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}entity in your consciousness{/d} hides from her.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You flinch at the seer's words. No doubt she is referring to the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Torture}nightmares{/d} the torturers inflicted upon your body and mind. Your muscles contract involuntarily as if steeling themselves once more for the inevitable pain.{/n}
  - After: {n}You flinch, remembering the torturers' {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Torture}nightmares{/d}.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The seer's words dredge up {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}something dark and frightening{/d} from the depths of your memory. Your soul has been tainted by the influence of warp sorcery, and it seems you will never be rid of it.{/n}
  - After: {n}Her words stir {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}something dark and frightening{/d}: your soul's lasting warp-taint.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Idira turns her head to you, her vacant eyes flaring like embers.{/n} "And you... you are {name} von Valancius, one of Lady Theodora's heirs. Well, then. We finally meet."
  - After: {n}Idira's eyes flare.{/n} "{name} von Valancius, Theodora's heir. We finally meet."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The seer's words bring back a wave of memories of the bitter, humiliating moments of {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}your greatest shame{/d}. Something sour rushes to your tongue, and your head is clouded with a sickening sense of your own worthlessness.{/n}
  - After: {n}You recall {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}your greatest shame{/d}, sick and worthless.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What, you think Lady Theodora didn't ask me to peek into the darkness behind the backs of those she sees as her prospective heirs?" {n}Idira laughs in a deep voice.{/n} "I have seen you, {name}. I have seen the footsteps of your past and the wounds of your heart."
  - After: "Theodora had me scry her heirs." {n}Idira laughs.{/n} "I've seen your past, {name}, and your wounds."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "What? You don't mean the Enginseer Prime is..."
  - After: "The Enginseer Prime is..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You hear a few clicks from the relays on the servo-skull, which has followed you all the way here, and Theodora's scrambled words give way to a voice vaguely familiar to you:{/n} "...officers' frequency. To all who can hear me: those with a weapon in their hands are to gather on the officers' deck at once. I repeat... gather on the officers' deck at once and prepare to launch a counter-attack..."
  - After: {n}The servo-skull crackles with a familiar voice.{/n} "...officers' frequency. All armed, gather on the officers' deck for a counter-attack..."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "That's Edelthrad! Emperor's providence, the other heir lives as well! Quickly, we must head to—"
  - After: "Edelthrad! The other heir lives! Quickly—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Not so fast, old man! If we drown in the warp, Lady Theodora's heirs won't be any good to us! If Edelthrad's like me and hasn't yet surrendered his mind or body to the mercy of the warp, then he can still hold on a little longer without us!"
  - After: "Wait, old man! Heirs are useless if we drown in the warp! Edelthrad can hold on!"

  - After: "Regards, Commissar. Your {g|Encyclopedia:ScholaProgenium}Schola Progenium{/g} past made you hard to find. Providence." {n}Voigtvir smiles faintly.{/n}

  - After: "Regards, Lieutenant General. The {g|Encyclopedia:AstraMilitarum}Astra Militarum{/g} is the Emperor's hammer. You'll get to command." {n}Voigtvir smiles faintly.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man casts an intrigued eye over you.{/n} "An interesting perspective. - **(conversation owner)**

  - Before: "That is commendable, quite so. However, there are many, many who believe that toils in His name start with diligence in choosing one's own words. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man bows slightly.{/n} "I am glad to have pleased you, for that is my duty to the dynasty of His chosen."
  - After: {n}He bows.{/n} "My duty to the dynasty."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He studies your face with interest.{/n} "Your position won't protect you for long if you continue making such pronouncements. Know that a fate far more compelling and eventful awaits you than being executed as a heretic."

  - Before: "I will be frank with you: you may forget your past titles no matter who gave them to you or what their origins are.   - Before: "To put it plainly, I am the head of the network of spies and informers who serve the interests of House von Valancius. I uncover weak links both among Lady Theodora's retinue and in the ranks of her rivals. I eliminate our vulnerabilities and exploit those of others."

  - After: "The Lord Captain and Master Edelthrad von Valancius are on the observation platform. Come."

  - Before: {n}Voigtvir shrugs slightly.{/n} "There is. And you will meet him soon enough."

  - Before: "My regards, Your Reverence.   - Before: "Careful! Careful! Be gentle with our guest — {mf|he|she} has an important mission to complete during our visit to the {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} Chamber, and for that I need {mf|him|her} breathing." {n}Voigtvir looks down at you.{/n} "You are back with us, I see. Delightful."
  - After: "Gently! I need {mf|him|her} breathing; {mf|he|she} has work in the {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} Chamber." {n}Voigtvir looks down.{/n} "Awake. Delightful."

  - Before: {n}Voigtvir tilts his head.{/n} "Hmm... I may consider it. Once you have done what I need you to do."
  - After: {n}Voigtvir tilts his head.{/n} "Perhaps. Once you've done your part."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You must have hit your head harder than I thought... No matter — very little is required of you. Just your blood, which you can either share of your own volition, or I will spill it for you."
  - After: "I need your blood. Give it, or I'll spill it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "How perceptive of you, {name}. I'll help you with the next insight: I need you here for your blood. You have the option to share it voluntarily — or I will squeeze it out of you myself."
  - After: "Perceptive, {name}. I need your blood, given or squeezed out."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We are in the anteroom of the Warrant Chamber — this voidship's most hallowed vault. I expected to do this part myself, but... never mind. You will offer your blood to the Sentinel."
  - After: "Beyond those gates lies the {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant of Trade{/g}. The Sentinel opens them only for a true heir. Give it your blood."

  - Before: "On the contrary. The warp's blessing has raised me too much above your kind, von Valancius. The Sentinel refused to submit to me... but you can help — after all, isn't that what family is for?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There's a good {mf|boy|girl}. Then go to the Sentinel at the gates of the Warrant Chamber and fulfil your destiny. I had hoped to feed Edelthrad to the machine — he is the one who caught Theodora's eye, after all — but since procuring him has proved difficult, you will have to do."
  - After: "Good {mf|boy|girl}. Go to the Sentinel. I wanted Edelthrad for it, but you'll do."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am afraid that you, {name} von Valancius, have no choice in the matter." {n}Voigtvir produces a strange object — a blade without a handle that shimmers blue in the light.{/n} "Try to resist, and I will demonstrate the power that the warp holds over mortals. Come to think of it, I might even take some pleasure in doing so."
  - After: "You have no choice, {name} von Valancius." {n}He draws a handleless blue blade.{/n} "Resist, and I'll show you the warp's power."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The blade flashes in the dim light, and drops of blood appear on your palm. For a brief moment, you feel nauseous, your head is spinning... and then quiet whispers begin to flood your mind.   - After: {n}The blade cuts your palm. Whispers flood your mind... Go. To. The gate.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I doubt it, my dear {name}. But that's enough talk. Fulfil your destiny."
  - After: "I doubt it, {name}. Now go."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Something — either your tone or the venomous words — throws Kunrad off for a moment, as hateful fury blazes from beneath the mask of a cold professional.{/n} "Wretched? What do you know about wretchedness, Theodora's cur? Are you hoping to buy a grain of her indulgence with your blind loyalty? Oh, I know this delusion — but, thank the gods, it no longer has power over me. Humanity can rot — I no longer serve mortalkind."
  - After: {n}Kunrad's mask slips into fury.{/n} "What do you know of wretchedness, Theodora's cur? Humanity can rot. I serve it no longer."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Voigtvir hesitates for a second and then produces a strange weapon — a blade without a handle that shimmers blue in the light.{/n} "Once my work is done, I'll make that pompous wench von Valancius watch as I sacrifice her entire dynasty and commit their fate to the gods... and you, {name}, will be the instrument by which I will accomplish this righteous act."
  - After: {n}Voigtvir draws a handleless blue blade.{/n} "I'll sacrifice von Valancius's dynasty to the gods, and you, {name}, will be my instrument."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You close your eyes and try to {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}focus{/d}... and then you feel the touch of something sharp — Voigtvir has somehow sensed a shift in the warp and delivered a pre-emptive strike.{/n}

  - After: {n}The voices mock you. An {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}intruding influence{/d} drives you toward the gates.{/n}

  - After: "I'll do all I can."

Perhaps this is an organised mutiny."
  - After: "Comms are dead; the lower bays spew heresy." {n}Voigtvir pauses.{/n} "Reaching the officers' deck this fast? An organised mutiny."

  - After: {n}Mort looks back.{/n} "We're done." {n}He reports by vox.{/n}

  - After: "First, secure the bridge and Navigator's Sanctum. I can do both." {n}Her eyes flash.{/n}

  - After: "Blast! Master of Whispers, find Edelthrad. Seneschal, fetch Tlass and the Sister. Mort, with me. {name}..." {n}She eyes you.{/n}

- **Abelard**
  - Before: "A rite... A sacrifice offered... Oh, my heart tells me that Kunrad was not deterred by his defeat in the Warrant Chamber!"
  - After: "A rite... A sacrifice... Kunrad survived the Warrant Chamber!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: "What? Kunrad betrayed Lady Theodora?" {n}Idira clutches her head.{/n} "But how is that... How... He was as loyal as a dog! And I didn't hear a thing, I swear!"
  - After: "Kunrad betrayed Lady Theodora?" {n}Idira clutches her head.{/n} "He was loyal as a dog!"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}The Seneschal gazes at the figure in the chair.{/n} "The ship can only begin the translation with the assistance of the Master Helmsman... if he is still alive. It is worth a try. We must get to the bridge, but we will need support. Our only option is to fight our way to the officers' deck and join forces with Edelthrad and his people. I believe we will also find Lady Theodora there — she must have heard the call to arms that the servo-skull relayed to us earlier."
  - After: {n}The Seneschal studies him.{/n} "Translation needs the Master Helmsman. We fight to the officers' deck, join Edelthrad, then the bridge. Lady Theodora should be there."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira reaches her hand out toward the Navigator, but pulls it back at the last moment.{/n} "Vespiadas... good luck. And thank you."
  - After: {n}Idira reaches out, then pulls back.{/n} "Good luck, Vespiadas. Thank you."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "I believe Master Vespiadas still lives..." {n}Abelard flinches at the sight of the stretched skin and the dark marks on the face of the creature.{/n} "The servants are dead... but the chamber, thank the Emperor, is still sealed from the warp. Well, we have a chance of leaving this place alive..."
  - After: "He lives..." {n}Abelard flinches.{/n} "The chamber is still sealed. We have a chance."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "You can't! It's only thanks to Master Vespiadas that we're still alive. If he falls, this whole ship is doomed!" {n}She catches her breath.{/n} "Let him do his duty. You know it's the last thing he'll ever do... if he lasts that long..."
  - After: "No! He's why we live. If he falls, the ship is doomed!" {n}She breathes.{/n} "Let him do his last duty."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Idira's scream is echoed by the silent cries in your head — the {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}unseen creature{/d} triumphs at the sight of the Navigator succumbing to the paroxysms of corruption.{/n}
  - After: {n}The {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}unseen creature{/d} gloats as the Navigator succumbs.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch0_Prologue/NewRogueTrader/NewRogueTrader

- **Master Helmsman Ravor**
  - Before: {n}Ravor turns around and looks up at you. He hesitates for a few moments, then addresses Abelard, who is standing next to you.{/n} "Seneschal, the Navigator's Sanctum is silent. The vox-signal is stable, which means..."
  - After: {n}Ravor turns to Abelard.{/n} "Seneschal, the Navigator's Sanctum is silent..."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard nods absent-mindedly.{/n} "The Navigator gave his life battling the storm that nearly claimed the von Valancius flagship. We will honour his memory along with that of all who died this day."
  - After: {n}Abelard nods.{/n} "The Navigator died saving our flagship. We'll honour him."
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**
  - Before: {n}Ravor does not look away. He is giving you a hard stare, his white brows furrowed.{/n} "Seneschal... Will you tell us now? Who is that? Where's the Lord Captain?"
  - After: {n}Ravor stares at you.{/n} "Who is that? Where's the Lord Captain?"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}It takes time for Abelard to respond: you watch as he grits his teeth, unable to bring himself to say anything. Finally, he adjusts his blood-stained coat, straightens, and begins to speak,{/n} "As First Officer, it is my duty... to inform you, with the greatest regret and indelible sorrow, that Lord Captain Theodora von Valancius is dead. May her memory never fade from the annals of the dynasty."
  - After: {n}Abelard grits his teeth.{/n} "With deepest sorrow: Lord Captain Theodora von Valancius is dead."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}After waiting out the first wave of shocked cries, Abelard glances at you and continues,{/n} "By right of blood succession and with the absence of other kin who could challenge this decision..."
  - After: {n}Over the cries, Abelard glances at you.{/n} "By blood succession..."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}The Seneschal turns to you. He looks at least half a decade older.{/n} "The deed is done, {name}... My apologies. I meant to say, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}The Seneschal looks older.{/n} "It's done, {name}... Lord Captain."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "...it is hereby declared that the successor to Theodora von Valancius is {name}, the rightful inheritor of the Warrant of Trade and the title of Rogue Trader. The official ascension ceremony will be held at a later time. In the interim..." {n}Abelard stops short and glares fiercely at the confused officers.{/n} "Have you lost your tongues? Hail your {mf|lord|lady} — it is because of {mf|his|her} toils that we all still live!"
  - After: "...{name} inherits the Warrant of Trade as Rogue Trader." {n}Abelard glares.{/n} "Hail your {mf|lord|lady}! We live by {mf|his|her} toil!"

## World/Dialogs/Ch0_Prologue/OfficerReadyToTranslate/OfficerReadyToTranslate

- **Player**
  - Before: "I am ready. Begin the ritual."
  - After: "I'm ready. Begin the ritual."
- **Player**
  - Before: "We need to re-establish contact with the Navigator's Sanctum. It is our only chance of escaping from the warp."
  - After: "Restore contact with the Navigator's Sanctum. It's our only way out."
- **Player**
  - Before: "How did you people survive in here?"
  - After: "How did you survive in here?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "By the Emperor, it's the Seneschal! Living and breathing!" {n}The white-haired man with sickly-pale skin salutes you.{/n} "Well, there's a tricky question — the whole place is so overgrown with foul wickedry we'll be scrubbing it off the vid-screens for Throne knows how long..."
  - After: "The Seneschal, alive!" {n}A pale, white-haired man salutes.{/n} "Tricky question. Foul wickedry's everywhere..."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Restore the vox-channel to the Navigator's Sanctum. Ready the crew. Prepare for translation to realspace!" {n}Abelard pauses for a few seconds before turning to you.{/n} "{name}, you may call me superstitious, but translation is not a good time to disregard rules. You are the only one who speaks for House von Valancius. You may not be the Lord Captain, but you, more than anyone else, deserve to take her place in the ritual that is about to commence." {n}He directs your attention upward — to the throne that sits at the apex of the tall staircase.{/n}
  - After: "Restore the vox to the Navigator's Sanctum. Prepare for translation!" {n}He turns to you.{/n} "{name}, you speak for House von Valancius. Take her place." {n}He points to the throne.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Take the Lord Cap'n's seat. Order the final preparations. Wait for the officers to report... bah, blast it all to the void! Translation is a craft, not something to be explained in a tick! Just go up to the throne, {mf|Master|Mistress} {name} — these people are about to do the impossible, the least they deserve is the solace of seeing a figure sitting in the usual spot. Please hurry! Every second we waste is a terrible risk!"
  - After: "No time to explain! Sit the throne, {mf|Master|Mistress} {name}; the crew needs to see someone there. Hurry!"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Ravor! Master Helmsman! Systems status report!"
  - After: "Ravor! Master Helmsman! Status report!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your words seem to knock the officers out of their stupor, and the air around you fills with voices and commands being issued. You hear someone sobbing — one of the survivors buckling under the stress. Abelard cuffs the crying officer without even looking.{/n}
  - After: {n}Officers snap to. One sobs; Abelard cuffs him.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man glances around the bridge.{/n} "Musta been providence... it better have been the Emperor's, not someone else's. When they barged in here, the ones with the Master of Whispers, some officers charged them, but it wasn't even a fight... I grabbed whoever I could and dragged 'em behind the cogitators, then I prayed for our rescue."
  - After: {n}He glances around.{/n} "Providence. The Master of Whispers' lot slaughtered our officers. I hid who I could and prayed."

## World/Dialogs/Ch0_Prologue/TheodoraChoice/TheodoraChoice

- **Player**
  - Before: [Accept the offer of help] "Take my pain away. And give me power."
  - After: [Accept the offer of help] "Take my pain. Give me power."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Walk through the fire] "The Emperor will guide the righteous on their path."
  - After: [Walk through the fire] "The Emperor guides the righteous."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Get the people off the bridge] "I will not leave my people in harm's way!"
  - After: [Get the people off the bridge] "I won't leave my people in harm's way!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The roar of the flames rings in your ears, and the choking smoke makes you cough and gasp for air. You instinctively recoil from the scorching heat, wiping your face. A moment later, a hazy silhouette forms in the raging wall of fire. You are surrounded by ear-splitting noise and screaming, yet you distinctly hear the sound of footsteps — and then you see the figure walk out of the fire toward you. It is Theodora von Valancius.{/n}
  - After: {n}Roaring flames, choking smoke. Theodora von Valancius walks out of the fire.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your mouth begins to salivate — each word Theodora speaks is like music to your ears. The {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}entity{/d} that now dwells in the deepest recesses of your mind is pleading, begging, demanding that you give her an immediate answer — and that answer can be nothing other than acceptance.{/n}
  - After: {n}The {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}entity{/d} in your mind begs you to accept.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta goes as still as a statue, then slowly raises her weapon.{/n} "An apparition... A sorcerous apparition! Trickery of the warp!"
  - After: {n}Argenta raises her weapon.{/n} "A sorcerous apparition! Warp trickery!"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Sister, you will lower your weapon!" {n}Despite his commanding tone, Abelard does not sound too confident — he is staring at the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}, and you notice a muscle in his cheek twitching.{/n} "Threatening the Lord Captain is outrageous..."
  - After: "Sister, lower your weapon!" {n}Abelard stares at the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}, cheek twitching.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Pain is but a reflection of one's weakness, {name}. To renounce weakness of spirit in pursuit of greatness is the only path to heights worthy of a Rogue Trader."
  - After: "Pain is weakness, {name}. Renounce it."

  - Before: "I am a Rogue Trader, {name}. I am wherever my will demands me to be. Would you prefer to be elsewhere at this time? Indubitably. But are you ready?"
  - After: "I go where my will demands, {name}. But are you ready?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Theodora watches you without blinking. Her snake-like gaze almost makes you forget about the fire searing you, leaving burns on your skin.{/n} "I can lead you out of these flames, {name}. Show you a path. Rid you of pain. And give you a weapon so that you may defeat your enemies. Decide."
  - After: {n}Her snake-like gaze holds you.{/n} "I can lead you out, {name}. End your pain. Arm you. Decide."

The {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} protects. His faithful will not be deterred by either darkness or deceitful promises. Nor will the fire burn those who carry the torch of faith in their soul!"

  - After: "Follow Lady Theodora before we suffocate!"

We must help the crew... lead them out... find a way around..." {n}Over the roaring flames, you hear distant sounds... frightened voices, screams... muffled and distorted, as if there were a body of water between you and them.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch0_Prologue/TheodoraFirstConversation/TheodoraFirstConversation

- **Player**
  - Before: "My experience tells me that when wealth is involved, someone is trying to appropriate it. This looks like the actions of a criminal syndicate stealing extractors under the cover of barbaric rites. I am ready to land on the planet with an assault squad and pass judgement on the thieves."
  - After: "Where there is wealth, there are thieves. Likely a syndicate stealing extractors behind barbaric rites. I will land a squad and judge them."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am a former Commissar. I would continue sending in more people. One crew after another, until someone succeeded in their service to Humanity and the conquest of Aion VI."
  - After: "As a former Commissar, I would send crew after crew until one conquered Aion VI."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Seismic activity, you say? I wish I could look at some augur readings, but, theoretically, a couple of well-placed orbital strikes would drown Aion VI and all its terrors in an ocean of magma."
  - After: "Seismic activity? A few orbital strikes could drown Aion VI in magma."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have retained some connections in the Astra Militarum... A few Imperial Guard regiments would take care of the natives, their 'spirits,' and the magma — solid fortifications have never let me down."
  - After: "My Astra Militarum contacts could send Guard regiments. Solid fortifications would handle natives, 'spirits' and magma."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I believe I could use my personal abilities to ascertain whether there was sorcery on Aion VI. But it would require going down to the surface in person."
  - After: "My abilities could detect sorcery there, but I must go down in person."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why should I concern myself with making this decision? I always have servants on hand to whom I can delegate matters such as this — just as you have delegated it to me."
  - After: "Why decide myself? I would delegate it to servants — as you did to me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If my... particular life experiences are any indication, some of the natives would eagerly betray their chieftains in exchange for a quiet life serving on board my ship. I would then leave dealing with Aion VI to those who know it best."
  - After: "Some natives would betray their chieftains for a quiet life on my ship. I would let them handle Aion VI."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The natives of Aion VI are lost souls in need of a shepherd's crook... or a whip. I am a priest of the Ecclesiarchy. I know how to instil reverence for the Emperor. There are many ways."
  - After: "As an Ecclesiarchy priest, I would teach these lost souls reverence for the Emperor, by crook or whip."
- **Player**
  - Before: "These reports of spirits certainly sound like evidence of heresy... however, I would put my interests first. No matter what means I would have to use, the riches of Aion VI would be mine."
  - After: "Heresy, perhaps, but my interests come first. By any means, Aion VI's riches would be mine."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Aion VI must be purged. For the good of the Imperium, I shall exterminate the heretical beliefs and otherworldly powers that rule the native apostates."
  - After: "Aion VI must be purged. I would exterminate its heresy and the powers ruling it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "There are ways to confirm whether what is happening on Aion VI is witchcraft or not. It might cost several psykers to do so, but it will give us the answer."
  - After: "Several psykers could confirm if it is witchcraft. Costly, but conclusive."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Gracious Lord Captain! Surely there are ways I can prove myself a worthy heir?"
  - After: "Lord Captain! Surely I can prove myself a worthy heir?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Navigator? Translation? What are these things that you speak of?"
  - After: "Navigator? Translation? What are those?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have no more questions."
  - After: "No more questions."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I gave a straight answer to a simple question. Which, as I understand, was still more than you could do, Edelthrad."
  - After: "I gave a straight answer. More than you managed, Edelthrad."
- **Player**
  - Before: "We are both servants of the God-Emperor and Lady Theodora. Does it become anyone of our status to engage in petty feuds?"
  - After: "We both serve the God-Emperor and Lady Theodora. Why feud?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I find your tone most disagreeable, Edelthrad. You will kindly alter the manner in which you address me, or else you will live to regret the consequences."
  - After: "Mind your tone, Edelthrad, or you will regret it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Shut your mouth, Edelthrad, before I decide to shut it for you."
  - After: "Shut your mouth, Edelthrad, or I will."
- **Player**
  - Before: "'One of'? Does this mean there are other heirs?"
  - After: "'One of'? There are other heirs?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "If you are satisfied with Edelthrad, then what sense is there in having this conversation? Why are you wasting your time on me?"
  - After: "If Edelthrad satisfies you, why waste time on me?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Did I hear you correctly? The Master of Whispers is related to you?"
  - After: "The Master of Whispers is related to you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Thank you for clarifying. May I ask my questions now?"
  - After: "Thank you. May I ask my questions now?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "An incident took place on the officers' deck: some servitors went berserk and attacked the crew."
  - After: "Servitors went berserk on the officers' deck and attacked the crew."
- **Player**
  - Before: "There are questions that I wish to have answered."
  - After: "I have questions I want answered."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not know just yet. I hope you will clarify that."
  - After: "I do not know yet. I hope you will tell me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Those 'spirits' could well be the natives' name for dangerous aliens — I would first verify if that is indeed the case and if the population of Aion VI engages in xenoworship."
  - After: "Those 'spirits' may be xenos. I would first check whether the natives worship aliens."
- **Edelthrad**
  - Before: "That is simply irrational, Lady Theodora," {n}says the man dressed in peculiar garb, his voice tight with tension. His face, half of which is covered by synskin, is twisted in a grimace of displeasure and disbelief.{/n} "Assimilation into the trade structure would be political and economic suicide, practically an admission of heresy!"
  - After: "Irrational, Lady Theodora!" {n}A half-synskinned man grimaces.{/n} "Joining the trade structure is suicide, near heresy!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The tall, grey-haired woman pins him with her gaze, her cybernetic eye flashing crimson.{/n} "Then suggest an alternative that will satisfy me. I have described the situation — no worse than my Seneschal could have done. Make a decision: what will you do with Aion VI, Edelthrad?"
  - After: {n}The grey-haired woman's cybernetic eye flashes.{/n} "Then offer better. What will you do with Aion VI, Edelthrad?"
- **Edelthrad**
  - Before: "What is this?" {n}Edelthrad turns to you and regards you with indignation.{/n} "Is this someone from your retinue, Theodora? Do you permit your people to interrupt your conversations in such a fashion?"
  - After: "What is this?" {n}Edelthrad glares.{/n} "Your people interrupt you, Theodora?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I give that permission to those with something of substance to say. Let us see if it was worth it." {n}Theodora tilts her head. Her lips stretch into a cold smile.{/n} "This is {name}, the second candidate for the title of my successor." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} regards you with a look that is imperious, predatory, and oppressive.{/n} "Step forward, {name}."
  - After: "If it is worth it." {n}A cold smile.{/n} "This is {name}, my second candidate." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} looms.{/n} "Step forward, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh yes, you would be, wouldn't you? The question is, am I ready to choose you over the rest? You came aboard hours before the warp jump and have not yet distinguished yourself in any way. As things currently stand, I have doubts that you are suitable for the role of Rogue Trader."
  - After: "Would you? You arrived hours ago and have proven nothing."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Perhaps. Yesterday, you were just another servant of the Imperium, one of the faceless multitudes. Today, visitors in the von Valancius colours come to you without any explanation and escort you to a vessel that departs for the far-off {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}. But such is the nature of my position, {name}. My claim on you is sacred and non-negotiable. I require all those who possess even a drop of the von Valancius blood, no matter who they may be."
  - After: "Perhaps. Yesterday, a faceless servant; today, bound for the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}. My claim on you is sacred, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Naturally. Some have yet to arrive on board, but you have had the pleasure of meeting one of them. Edelthrad may be somewhat disconcerted by the scale of the responsibilities that may potentially fall upon his shoulders... However, I have a good feeling about him as a candidate."
  - After: "Naturally. You met Edelthrad. He is daunted, but I like him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Theodora scoffs.{/n} "You have ceded the opening that was offered to you in a woeful display of meekness. Admittedly, this tendency is equally strong in all who toil in the Emperor's service. Immutable hierarchy, absolute obedience, lickspittlery, compulsion to please... I value none of these things. From the moment my envoys came for you, the terms of your existence changed."{g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}{/g}
  - After: {n}Theodora scoffs.{/n} "Meek. I do not value obedience. Your life changed when my envoys came."{g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}{/g}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Theodora arches an eyebrow.{/n} "Reasonable and prudent. However, chasing after ethereal creatures may prove a rather long and fruitless endeavour."
  - After: {n}Theodora arches an eyebrow.{/n} "Prudent. But chasing phantoms may prove fruitless."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No doubt, inspiring each new departing crew with passionate speeches?" {n}Theodora sighs wearily.{/n} "I have never believed in the power of propaganda. It is only effective in the worst of circumstances — when you want people to die in someone's name, not prevail and achieve."
  - After: "With rousing speeches?" {n}Theodora sighs.{/n} "Propaganda helps people die, not succeed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Trying to apply familiar methods to a new problem?" {n}Theodora raises an eyebrow.{/n} "The criminal underworld of {g|Encyclopedia:Calixis}Calixis{/g} is a far cry from a savage borderland planet..."

  - Before: {n}The servitor on the gate begins to move. With the screeching and groaning of metal, it leans forward, closer to you. The vid-screen to the right of you lights up, showing strings of mysterious symbols on a green background.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servitor leans in, jaw gaping wide with metal fangs. A screen shows green symbols.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You hear the voice again, and this time you realise that it is coming from the two speakers built into the Sentinel's shoulders.{/n} "Genetic code identified. Child of House von Valancius, do you require assistance?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servo-skull's creaking gradually turns into comprehensible words:{/n} "...escort the child of the house to safety."
  - After: {n}The servo-skull's creaks become words:{/n} "...escort the child of the house to safety."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...mobile unit of the {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} Sentinel designed as a personal escort of the child of the house and a means of communicating with the Rogue Trader's subjects. Mobile unit standing by."
  - After: "...{g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} Sentinel mobile unit: escort and messenger. Standing by."
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "...stress-induced confusion. {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} Sentinel unit standing by."

  - Before: "...{g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox-cast{/g} frequencies disrupted. Initiating setup... Establishing connection..."
  - After: "...{g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox-cast{/g} disrupted. Connecting..."

## World/Dialogs/Ch1/BridgeAndCabinet/Briefing

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The medics only just saved you in time — luckily, one of the healers remembered the existence of a long-forgotten augment station in storage. The blessings of the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g} saved your life — some of your internal organs had to be replaced with {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g}. The good news is that now we have the capabilities to install augmentations of any complexity." {n}The Seneschal then mutters to himself,{/n} "I swear, sometimes it seems new compartments spring up on this ship of their own volition..."
  - After: "An augment station saved you; by the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}, some organs are now {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g}." {n}The Seneschal mutters,{/n} "This ship grows compartments."

## World/Dialogs/Ch1/BridgeAndCabinet/Briefing/Briefing_c1_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: "I wish to hear the Infernus Master's report."
  - After: "Infernus Master, report."

  - Before: "How did we come to lose so many officers?"
  - After: "How did we lose so many officers?"

  - After: "Introduce those present, Abelard?"

  - After: "I'd be honoured to fulfil the Inquisitor's commission. What did he ask of Theodora?"

  - After: "So: heavy crew losses, and we need a new Enginseer Prime and Navigator. Is that all that stops us?"

  - After: "Yes. I'll leave the ship at the first chance."
- **Player**
  - Before: "No. Forget this discussion."

  - Before: "Is that so? And what is the task with which she was entrusted?"

  - After: "Drivesmaster, report."

  - Before: "Stand down! Release him. I have no intention of punishing a man for a moment of weakness, not after the terrible attack we have endured."

  - After: "Wait, Abelard. I don't want to be the Rogue Trader."

  - After: "Master of Ordnance, anything to report?"

- **Abelard**

  - After: {n}Weary Abelard looks you over.{/n} "Well, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}..."

  - After: "Your first briefing as Lord Captain. We lost so many officers that some posts sit empty; the deck clans pick new leaders."

  - After: "Lastly, High Factotum Janris Danrok: supplies and procurement."

  - After: "I defer to the Vox Master. Mistress Toliman?"

  - Before: "We are in the Rykad star system, and our voyage here was undertaken on the orders of Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s predecessor. There are three inhabited bodies in this system, and our attempts to send {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox-messages{/g} have produced confounding results."
  - After: "Rykad system, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, by your predecessor's order. Three inhabited bodies; our {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox-messages{/g} get strange replies."

  - Before: "The Navis Nobilite station has not simply failed to answer — it seems to be maintaining total vox-silence.   - After: "The Navis Nobilite station is silent. The prison planetoid sent a distress call. Rykad Minoris won't answer; {g|Encyclopedia:Augur}augurs{/g} detect fighting there."

  - After: "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}He indicates an augmented woman.{/n} "Vigdis Surri Otta of the Toliman line, {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}Vox Master{/g}."

  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, there is one other thing. A confidential matter of the utmost importance.   - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, a secret." {n}Abelard hesitates.{/n} "Theodora came here on commission from the {g|Encyclopedia:Inquisition}Lord Inquisitor{/g}, Hand of the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} in the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Precisely, Lord Captain. But bear in mind that this will not be the end of our trials.   - After: "Yes. Then repairs at {g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g}'s dockyard — once these three are solved."

- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira's glazed eyes rove over those assembled. One word bursts from her lips:{/n} "Daybreak..."
  - After: {n}Idira's glazed eyes rove.{/n} "Daybreak..."

  - After: "Damn it!" {n}She clutches her temples.{/n} "Y-Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, something strange is coming. One word rings like a bell: 'daybreak.' But why so dark?"

  - After: "Silence!" {n}Abelard's roar shakes the glass.{/n} "Enforcers, seize this mutineer!"

  - After: "One word tells us nothing. Anything else, Mistress Tlass?"
- **Idira**

  - After: "Not yet. The voices all shout. I'll report later."

- **Abelard**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A dozen pairs of eyes bore into you, the expressions revealing restraint, joy, curiosity... and wariness.{/n}
  - After: {n}A dozen wary eyes watch you.{/n}
- **Abelard**

  - After: "Second row: Master of Ordnance, artillery; Infernus Master, fires; and the Drivesmaster, servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}."

  - After: {n}They salute — one confident, one nervous, the {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} waving {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g}.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You had us worried for a few hours there." {n}Abelard offers a thin smile.{/n} "But after witnessing you fearlessly {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentThroughFire}rush into the fray{/d} on deck, the only thing that surprises me is how long you stayed on your feet: your strength only left you once the fighting was all over.   - Before: {n}You cannot help but notice that the Seneschal does not know how to talk to you or where to begin.   - After: {n}Abelard falters; you smirk, as if {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}someone else{/d} gloats.{/n}

  - Before: {n}The {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_CutByKnife}alien entity{/d} coiled in the depths of your mind begins to shift restlessly. Its demand is clear: find. - **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: "We are toiling day and night to compile a full account of the losses. The task will require next to no involvement from Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} — I will personally ensure that all damaged components are given into the Tech-Priests' hands for attention and that all lost supplies are replaced. There is only one resource that I cannot replenish single-handedly, and that is people. We have lost more than two thousand crew members, and, unfortunately, this number is not confined to the scum from the lower decks, which are easily replaced, but also includes trained professionals."
  - After: "I'll handle repairs and supplies, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. But over two thousand crew are lost, professionals too — those I can't replace."
- **Ashar Naitallomo**
  - Before: {n}The Master of Ordnance gives you a gloomy look.{/n} "No. My job's simple — maintain the arsenal and fire where I'm told. But just ask anyone — we've got no able crew, no Lord Captain—"
  - After: {n}He glowers.{/n} "No. But we've no crew, no Lord Captain—"
- **Zi-Ra Tallar**
  - Before: "With great sorrow I must also report that the {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} Prime, overseer and spiritual authority of all Tech-Priests on board, fell in battle. The Magos was betrayed by the little flesh that remained part of him. A most terrible loss! There is no one among my comrades aboard whose experience and comprehension of the sacred protocols equals that of the fallen Magos. We require a replacement, and as soon as possible."
  - After: "Sadly, our {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} Prime, head of all Tech-Priests, fell — betrayed by his flesh. We need a replacement."
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "The ship's most senior Tech-Priest — most senior both in rank and in experience — is dead. If we do not find a replacement, we will be unable to resolve the problems with the warp engine," {n}answers the Vox Master instantly, without even thinking — this is not the first time she has acted as an interpreter between the ship's various inhabitants.{/n}
  - After: "Our senior Tech-Priest died. Without another, the warp engine stays broken," {n}the Vox Master interprets.{/n}
- **Zi-Ra Tallar**
  - Before: {n}A voice distorted by a vox-retranslator emerges from under the Tech-Priest's scarlet hood.{/n} "Lord Captain, the foes that set upon this noble voidship destroyed the repositories of hundreds of {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g}. The great {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp engine{/g} entrusted into my charge is unharmed, thank the Omnissiah, but its spirit mourns its dead brethren. We have not yet identified a prayer protocol capable of assuaging its sorrow and anger."
  - After: {n}A vox-distorted voice:{/n} "Lord Captain, hundreds of {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} died. The {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp engine{/g} is intact but grieves inconsolably."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The assembled officers salute you as one.{/n}
  - After: {n}The officers salute as one.{/n}
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: "We will be able to make up our losses on the nearest planet, Rykad Minoris. However, the planet — the whole system, in fact — belongs to the Winterscale {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} dynasty. We cannot simply begin recruiting on the planet without first coming to an understanding with the governor. In that respect, I am powerless — negotiations at this level are a matter for the Rogue Trader."
  - After: "Rykad Minoris has people, but it's Winterscale {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} territory. Recruiting needs its governor's consent — your task."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Especially true given Calligos Winterscale's penchant for attacking first and asking questions later, and the kind of thick-skulled thugs he usually installs as governors on his planets," {n}rumbles Abelard, frowning.{/n}
  - After: "And Calligos Winterscale attacks first and appoints thugs," {n}Abelard frowns.{/n}
- **Ashar Naitallomo**
  - Before: "So what?" {n}comes the officer's hostile and bitter reply. It is as if a dam has burst inside and all his pent-up emotions are rushing out of him.{/n} "The ship's in ruins! Every second officer's dead! And now we've got a green Lord Captain who's supposed to lead us to void knows where!"
  - After: "So what?" {n}he snaps.{/n} "The ship's wrecked! Officers dead! And a green Lord Captain!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The brittle laughter of the Master of Ordnance reverberates around the bridge as he is led to his fate.{/n}
  - After: {n}He laughs brittlely as he's led away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Abelard grunts.{/n} "If only one officer out of the whole lot has fallen to pieces, then that's not bad at all.   - After: {n}Abelard grunts.{/n} "Only one broke. Apologies, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. His fate? We have a replacement."

  - After: "Twenty lashes monthly for six months, no officer's rations or privileges. Record it!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The report will be far from cheering — we must find a replacement for the dead {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g}.   - After: "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. First, a {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g}. By divine luck, a {g|Encyclopedia:NavisNobilite}Navis Nobilite{/g} station is here. Visit it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You would cease to be a Rogue Trader. And perhaps cease to be altogether," {n}Abelard says gravely.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, it is your prerogative to disregard anyone you wish in the Koronus Expanse. But not the Inquisition. Never the Inquisition."
  - After: "You'd cease being Rogue Trader — perhaps cease altogether," {n}Abelard warns.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, ignore anyone but the Inquisition."
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**
  - Before: "Right you are, Lord Cap'n. To cut a long story short — the outlook is bleak. The ship's sound, more or less, but without our {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} Prime and {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g}, who fell in battle, we have no way out of the system. If we try to set so much as a toe inside the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g}, I don't know what'll happen first, our warp drive being torn to pieces or all of us melting into the bulkheads."
  - After: "Bleak, Lord Cap'n. Without {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} Prime and {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g} we're stuck; the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} would tear us apart."
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**
  - Before: "If I were you, I'd grab this chance with both hands, or else you'll soon be eyeing up asteroids to use as your new residence!   - After: "Grab this chance! Meanwhile, we can circle while {g|Encyclopedia:Promethium}promethium{/g} lasts and swat raiders."
- **Abelard**

  - After: "No mistake, Your Ladyship. The rank is fixed — Theodora was Lord Captain too. The {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} chose you as {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}; {g|Encyclopedia:HighGothic}High Gothic{/g} is rigid."
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, if you will allow me to interject — when we arrived in this system, my crew followed standard protocols and conducted a count of all the available communication channels in the region. To have located a Navigator in the very same system is an incredible stroke of luck, a true blessing from the God-Emperor."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, there's a silent {g|Encyclopedia:NavisNobilite}Navis Nobilite{/g} station here — a God-Emperor's blessing."
- **Master Helmsman Ravor**
  - Before: {n}The bearded man with pale, almost transparent skin, large dark circles under his eyes, and a dour expression that seems hardwired into his face, gives a sullen nod.{/n} "Hail, Lord Cap'n. This here ship's as good as home to me, so rest assured she's in safe hands. I'll die before I let her come to any grief!"
  - After: {n}A pale, dour man nods.{/n} "Hail, Lord Cap'n. I'll die before this ship comes to grief!"
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: {n}Dressed in an embroidered jacket, the heavyset man with oiled hair offers an obsequious smile and bows.{/n} "It is an honour, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. You may trust me with all matters concerning your comfort — everything will be done to the highest standard!"
  - After: {n}A heavyset man bows obsequiously.{/n} "An honour, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Trust me with your comfort!"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}The old officer gasps and looks at you oddly.{/n} "I... do agree that your elevation to your new status was rather precipitous. I assure you there are good reasons for it — not least the fact that without a Lord Captain, the ship would be destined for naught but disaster... but I digress."
  - After: {n}Abelard gasps.{/n} "Your rise was abrupt, yes. But a ship without a Lord Captain is doomed."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard's voice softens slightly.{/n} "You do not have a choice, {name}. You are the named heir of the Rogue Trader, and your fate is predetermined. Besides..." {n}The Seneschal lowers his voice.{/n} "If Kunrad is intent on eliminating all the candidates, then his assassins must still be out there... waiting. I doubt they are reckless enough to attack you if you are draped in the mantle of the Rogue Trader.   - After: {n}Softly:{/n} "You're the heir, {name}; no choice." {n}Quieter:{/n} "Kunrad's assassins may lurk. They'd fear a Rogue Trader — not a mere servant of the Emperor..."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard nods deferentially.{/n} "We all have burdens to carry in the name of the God-Emperor, {name}."
  - After: {n}Abelard nods.{/n} "We all bear burdens for the God-Emperor, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Item two on the bad news list — our {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} Prime fell in battle. Without his assistance, we cannot soothe the ship's {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g}. Finding a new {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g}, and a {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magos{/g} at that, will be far from easy. But there is some prospect of success."
  - After: "Second: the {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseer{/g} Prime fell; the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} need soothing. A new {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magos{/g} is hard to find."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}The Seneschal makes an approving sound.{/n} "A wise decision."
  - After: {n}The Seneschal approves.{/n} "Wise."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard looks at you in alarm.{/n} "I... can scarcely stop you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Are you certain of your decision?"
  - After: {n}Abelard is alarmed.{/n} "I can't stop you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Are you certain?"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard sighs heavily and seems to age another ten years before your eyes.{/n} "Very well, {name}. I shall relay all the necessary instructions for the landing. It was a pleasure to know you. Farewell."
  - After: {n}Abelard sighs, aging visibly.{/n} "Very well, {name}. I'll arrange your landing. Farewell."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "You have endured much in recent days... anyone in your position would lose their equilibrium." {n}Despite his relaxed tone, Abelard continues to scrutinise you.{/n}
  - After: "You've endured much; anyone would falter." {n}He keeps watching you.{/n}

  - Before: "Yes, quite right. X.C. — Xavier Calcazar."
  - After: "Yes. X.C. — Xavier Calcazar."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}For a brief moment, Sister Argenta's voice sounds hesitant.{/n} "I was also hoping to approach you with a personal request. But it can wait. Speak with me when you have time, Rogue Trader."

  - Before: {n}Abelard gives a reserved nod and glares at the speechless officers.{/n} "I certainly hope that all of us here have taken this lesson from the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}Officio Prefectus{/d} to heart."
  - After: {n}Abelard glares at the officers.{/n} "I trust we've all learned from the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}Officio Prefectus{/d}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The High Factotum breaks away from the rest and approaches you, bowing repeatedly.{/n} "Lord Captain, if I may steal just one more moment of your time...   - After: {n}The High Factotum bows.{/n} "Lord Captain, a delicate matter: a battle trophy."

  - Before: "And the third piece of bad news — the last one, fortunately. Crew losses have surpassed two thousand people. We will probably be able to find sufficient workers there, but there is a matter of some diplomatic delicacy — the planet is controlled by House Winterscale, the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} dynasty. We cannot simply recruit people from the planet without first coming to an agreement with the governor."
  - After: "Last: over two thousand crew lost — too few to fly. Rykad Minoris has workers, but House Winterscale, a {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} dynasty, rules it; its governor must agree."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Abelard grits his teeth.{/n} "No, Lord Captain. In all the commotion, his trail went cold. I am afraid that it will be some time before he answers for all that he has wrought."
  - After: {n}Abelard grits his teeth.{/n} "No. His trail's cold; perhaps he took a shuttle."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Tlass, cease your buffoonery immediately and report the reason for your intrusion!"
  - After: "Tlass, stop this buffoonery and explain your intrusion!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, if you want me to take a closer look into your future, find me on the bridge and we can talk. Lady Theodora was well served by my whispers on many occasions, and I'm sure you would benefit from them as well." {n}The psyker's bitten lips stretch into a wry smile.{/n}
  - After: "Lord Captain, want your future read? Find me on the bridge. Theodora valued my whispers." {n}A wry smile.{/n}
- **Ashar Naitallomo**
  - Before: {n}The Master of Ordnance chokes back the words he was obviously about to blurt out without thinking. He casts another look at you before turning away.{/n} "I apologise profusely, Lord Captain. Pardon the fool...   - After: {n}He bites his tongue.{/n} "Forgive me, Lord Captain. Fear took me."
- **Ashar Naitallomo**
  - Before: {n}He looks up at you.{/n} "But I've heard of you, oh yes! Your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Glory}fame{/d} has reached even as far as the Expanse. We are ready to fight, if that is the Lord Captain's will!"
  - After: {n}He looks up.{/n} "But your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Glory}fame{/d} precedes you!" {n}He straightens.{/n} "The arsenal is saved, the battery ready to fight!"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "It appears the heretics were deliberately targeting the vessel's command — they knew exactly whom they were looking for and where they could be found. Which is unsurprising, given that their informant on board was our own Master of Whispers..." {n}Abelard grimaces.{/n}
  - After: "The heretics targeted command — tipped off by our own Master of Whispers." {n}Abelard grimaces.{/n}
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: "It is equally regrettable that two more individuals worthy of mention could not join us at the briefing: the Master-at-Arms and Confessor Adalbert. And Mistress Sauerback, who has replaced her late predecessor as our Master-at-Arms, is currently leading the search for any surviving agents of Voigtvir."
  - After: "Also absent: Confessor Adalbert, holding funerals for the fallen, and Master-at-Arms Sauerback, hunting Voigtvir's agents."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Reports on the condition of the ship and crew. The Lord Captain is not usually drawn away from her important affairs to attend such routine briefings, but this is a unique situation. So prepare to hear a bevy of complaints and excuses, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Take this opportunity to get a good look at the officers who work six decks away from the bridge.   - After: "Ship and crew reports. Normally beneath a Lord Captain, but news is grim; flying again may need you to negotiate with this system's authorities. Expect complaints, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} — and let your officers see you."

  - Before: "The situation is not very encouraging. But without a Navigator, a Tech-Priest, and new crew members, we won't be able to travel anywhere — therefore, we must go to the planet and the Navis Nobilite station and find out what in the void is going on!"
  - After: "Grim. But without a Navigator, a Tech-Priest and crew, we're stuck — we must visit the planet and the Navis Nobilite station."

  - After: [Leave the Navigator undisturbed]

  - After: "Lord Captain, {g|Encyclopedia:Enginseer}Enginseers{/g} report agitated {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} shipwide. Damage unknown yet."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And here, beyond the wall of glass, a daughter forsaken by her father yearns for her brother. And the sun's pale disk goes in tireless pursuit... of her? No. Of me. Its frozen rays lie that spring is here. The light is deadened. The Great Ruler is... GONE!"

  - Before: "I... see... violet vortexes lashing an ocean with a million flails... and umber shadows spinning over the surface in a fiery dance... A storm rising above foaming waters. Armadas drowning in fog — the path from one end to another cannot be seen."

  - Before: "Rogue Trader, I fear I have unfortunate news. ## World/Dialogs/Ch1/BridgeAndCabinet/EvacuationFromRykad/EvacuationFromRykad_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Which of the planet's inhabitants can we evacuate?"
  - After: "Who can we evacuate?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "We will not waste any time on this world. Pull back and begin preparations for translation to the warp."
  - After: "No time for this world. Prepare for warp translation."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thanks to you, we have salvaged many shuttles from the starport that we can now use."

  - Before: "Thanks to you, we have at our disposal several shuttles rescued from the starport that we can now use in the evacuation effort."

- **(conversation owner)**

- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "We can rule out that possibility. The Drukhari would never ally themselves with the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Archenemy{/g}'s worshippers. If I had to name one thing that Humanity and these xenos have in common, it would be a shared loathing for {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} corruption."

  - Before: "I fear that Rykad Minoris is lost. The situation is deteriorating by the minute — we must leave this system as soon as possible."

- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Any delay caused by loading and transporting to the ship will cost us precious time. Do not deceive yourself, {name} — if you indulge your vanity, you will doom billions to eternal torment at the hands of the Archenemy."
  - After: "Indulge your vanity, {name}, and billions are doomed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I stand ready to fulfil the order, Lord Captain, but I must inform you that this course of action places the shuttles at great risk, and even if it is successful, the number of evacuees will be negligible. Do you still wish to begin the rescue operation?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "However, there are still people on the planet who have not succumbed to heresy and who are worthy of rescue. Besides the small number of our own shuttles, we also have the shuttles salvaged from the starport."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I concur with your decision, Lord Captain."
  - After: "I concur, Lord Captain."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix inclines his head.{/n} "The right choice, Lord Captain. May the sacred Exterminatus cleanse this vale of corruption."
  - After: {n}Heinrix nods.{/n} "Right choice. May the Exterminatus cleanse it."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}His face becomes impenetrable, but his voice burns cold.{/n} "I understand, {name}. With your decision, you are handing an entire planet over to the Archenemy, and I will be obliged to notify the Lord Inquisitor of what has happened."
  - After: {n}Coldly:{/n} "You hand a planet to the Archenemy, {name}. I must inform the Lord Inquisitor."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "You should have listened to me, Rogue Trader. We will all have to pay for this mistake."
  - After: "You should have listened. We'll all pay."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}You detect a flicker of something beneath Heinrix's sanguine mask. Whatever it may be, it does not seep into the Interrogator's dispassionate voice.{/n} "In that case, I consider it necessary to point out that the mark of the Archenemy could infiltrate the ship with the priests escorting the reactor.
