## World/Dialogs/Ch1/RaycadMinoris/ArcheotechReactor/Archeotech_Reactor_Mummy/Archeotech_Reactor_Mummy_Dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not know the words of that hymn, and so I will ask you to enlighten me."
  - After: "I don't know that hymn. Teach me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I may not be a member of your priesthood, but you and I are of the same faith!"
  - After: "I'm not a priest, but we share a faith!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Disconnect one of the wires from the body]
  - After: [Disconnect a wire]
- **Player**
  - Before: "Another attempt on my person and I will cut you into pieces!"
  - After: "Try that again and I'll cut you apart!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Let us praise the twin charges, the body electric, and the Omnissiah who lights the spark of reason within us. And let us carry His charge to those who have turned their minds toward His light."
  - After: "Praise the twin charges, the body electric, and the Omnissiah who sparks our reason. Let us carry His charge to the faithful."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Improvise] "Glory to the Holy Martyr Galvanica, and may a great... em... abundance of current persist in her induction coils! May electrons flow through thee as they flow through... errr... sacred copper!"
  - After: [Improvise] "Glory to Martyr Galvanica, may... em... current fill her coils! Flow, electrons, like... errr... sacred copper!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell me what your datadream is like."
  - After: "What's your datadream like?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Destroy the body] "The cultists might get to him. That is undesirable."
  - After: [Destroy the body] "Keep him from the cultists."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I shall trouble you no more."
  - After: "I'll trouble you no more."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Stick to ordering your monks about, corpse. I will not be chanting anything for you."
  - After: "Order your monks, corpse. I won't chant."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Kill the Tech-Priest] "Die a proper death!"
  - After: [Kill the Tech-Priest] "Die properly!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Would you prefer to wait until they get their dirty hands inside your sacred reactor? Do you have any idea what they will do to it?"
  - After: "Will you wait until their dirty hands are inside your sacred reactor?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The monastery is under attack by heretics. Can you help?"
  - After: "Heretics attack the monastery. Can you help?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Different though His names may be that we use to crown our prayers, all our thoughts and intents still stem from the one pillar of all that is holy and sacred. I was once one of the Adeptus Ministorum. I serve the God-Emperor, whom you call the Omnissiah, and thus we are of the same flock."
  - After: "Our names for Him differ, but our faith is one. I was Adeptus Ministorum. I serve the God-Emperor, your Omnissiah; we're one flock."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Bow] "Apologies for disturbing you, but I am in need of your wisdom."
  - After: [Bow] "Forgive me; I need your wisdom."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal, apologise to the esteemed Tech-Priest on my behalf."
  - After: "Pasqal, apologise for me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g}'s body rests on a metal table, surrounded by sparking spirals of copper coil. A patina of sacred unguents covers his withered flesh. His {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augmetics{/g} have been polished with great care. Intricate electoos cover the dead man's crossed arms and bare torso, and strands of wires envelop his head.{/n}
  - After: {n}A withered {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} lies amid sparking coils, {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augmetics{/g} polished, head wired.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The First Article of Faith says, 'The Motive Force is life.' Therefore, so long as it fills me, I am alive."
  - After: "'The Motive Force is life.' While it fills me, I live."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As soon as you touch the copper-coated wire, searing pain stabs through your fingers and wrist. The world becomes very bright for a second, and then darkness falls.{/n}
  - After: {n}Searing pain. A flash, then darkness.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A discharge runs through the wires that envelop the Tech-Priest's head, and a forbidding hiss comes from the vox-system on the ceiling. A soft voice, sounding as though it is struggling to overcome its dreamy torpor, addresses you sternly:{/n} "I shall fear no enemy, for the Motive Force is with me, and its discharge will smite any who lift their hands against the righteous."
  - After: {n}A stern voice from the vox:{/n} "The Motive Force smites any who strike the righteous."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In my datadream, I saw their unholy requests and rejected them angrily, for it is said in the Fourth Article of Security, 'No unbeliever's hand shall intrude upon the operation cycle.' They have seditious designs on the relic — but should I give you, who does not belong to our faith and fellowship, my blessing to stand up to the blasphemers?"
  - After: "I refused their unholy requests. They covet the relic. But should I bless you, an unbeliever, to oppose them?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The body seems motionless, but you notice a slight tremor in the fingertips. This ancient servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g} must be datadreaming. His mind, enveloped in digital reverie, can persist for hundreds or thousands of years while his frail body is decaying. This sacred state of trance is a great reward only earned by the wisest and most pious servants of the Machine God.{/n}
  - After: {n}His fingers tremble. This {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g} servant is datadreaming, his mind outliving his decaying body: a reward for the pious.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As you look closer, you note that small tremors run through the Tech-Priest's body every now and then. There must be a faulty wire in the tangle around the dead man, sending Motive Force shocks through his lifeless shell.{/n}
  - After: {n}Tremors run through him. A faulty wire.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The light in the crypt becomes a little brighter and sharper, and the smell of ozone fills the air.{/n}
  - After: {n}The light sharpens; ozone.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Sad binharic trills are heard from Pasqal's vox. His {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g} bend down to the floor in an apologetic gesture.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal's {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrites{/g} droop apologetically.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The vox's voice grows louder:{/n} "Praetor Electroid Dahr-Impulse II, by the will of the Omnissiah, the prior of this monastery and the guardian of the Miraculous Fusion Reactor, now and ever, world without end."
  - After: {n}The vox:{/n} "Praetor Electroid Dahr-Impulse II, prior and guardian of the Miraculous Fusion Reactor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Let it be so indeed."
  - After: "So be it."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal looks at you indignantly.{/n} "I am registering sacrilege! This devotee of the faith was posing no threat. Terminating his vital functions was unwarranted."
  - After: {n}Pasqal, indignant:{/n} "Sacrilege! He posed no threat."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This statement is true. The First Article of Security says, 'Fear above all evils the defilement of Knowledge,' and its command outweighs the prohibition contained in the Sixth Article of Security, 'Let Knowledge be locked away from the ignorant.'"
  - After: "True. Guarding Knowledge from defilement outweighs keeping it from the ignorant."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Next to the table the body is resting on, you see small amulets crafted from burned cogitator circuit boards. There is no dust on these small offerings. They were clearly left here recently.{/n}
  - After: {n}Fresh offerings, amulets of burned circuit boards, lie by the table.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Absolution granted. I sense no profanity in you, only a curtain of ignorance drawn over your mind."
  - After: "Absolution granted. You're ignorant, not profane."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I know not what your name is, nor what your faith is. I will not waste my blessing on a misbeliever."
  - After: "I know not your name or faith. No blessing for misbelievers."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The relic... The mere thought of its desecration is a blasphemy. The mere chance of it is a sacrilege."
  - After: "The relic... Its desecration is unthinkable."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "So be it. In the name of shaming the unbelievers, I grant you the blessing of special access and protection from the rage of the Motive Force." {n}Dry cracking sounds come from inside the crypt's walls as awakened cogitators process the ancient Tech-Priest's command.{/n}
  - After: "So be it. I grant you access and protection from the Motive Force." {n}Cogitators crackle.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The vox on the ceiling comes alive and lets forth a solemn binharic aria that turns into a crackling, somnolent voice:{/n} "In this dark hour, I am ready to bring you good tidings, tech-brethren! Now respond with the words of the Second Galvanic Hymn."
  - After: {n}The vox wakes:{/n} "Good tidings, tech-brethren! Respond with the Second Galvanic Hymn."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Absolution granted, tech-brother. May the charge of the Omnissiah's grace persist in the batteries of the faithful."
  - After: "Absolution granted, tech-brother."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The obstinate elder's vox hisses and rasps.{/n}
  - After: {n}The elder's vox rasps.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Second Galvanic Hymn is a revered and miraculous prayer of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g}. Naturally, you know it very well.{/n}
  - After: {n}You know this {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} hymn well.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You vaguely remember hearing about a Saint Galvanica, a martyr if you are not mistaken. She is probably who the hymn is dedicated to.{/n}
  - After: {n}It's probably for Saint Galvanica, a martyr.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Here, in this cell of mine, I have conquered death, and my mind has soared toward the Omnissiah in a blessed datadream. My body is decaying, but my spirit will remain by my master's side. For I am the sacred sentinel of the code, the guardian of the sacred relic, and the eye that watches over the Rite of Operation."
  - After: "Here I conquered death. My body decays, but my mind guards the code and the relic."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am one with the Motive Force, and it opens my mind to the sacred impulses of Knowledge. My reason has become as fast as the flying electron and the ray of light, and time is no more for me, for I am eternal. In my binharic reverie, I comprehend the wisdom of the Machine God and share it with the humble priests who come to my cell, thirsting for my Knowledge."
  - After: "One with the Motive Force, I am swift as light and eternal. I share the Machine God's wisdom with seekers."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My tech-brethren will suffer no sacrilege to be committed. I hear their prayers, and I trust in their fury."
  - After: "My tech-brethren will stop any sacrilege."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Such... purity of colour. I have never seen anything like it! Deep tranquillity shrouded in a cool-white cloud. Such unity of thought and spirit... The dead are incapable of exuding such hues."
  - After: "Such pure, calm colour! The dead don't glow like this."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Denied, for it is said in the Eighth Article of Diligence, 'He who seeks Knowledge, let him receive it in accordance with his rank and admission.' The prayer that is unknown to you was hidden from laypeople for a reason. But you will not be denied my wisdom, for the Omnissiah looks favourably upon those who are drawn to knowledge."
  - After: "Denied; that prayer is kept from laypeople. But the Omnissiah favours the curious, so ask."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal respectfully bows his head before the dead man and carefully touches the shrivelled body with the tip of his mechadendrite.{/n} "Honoured adherent, I thank you for showing us the truth of Fabricator General Pechrovahr's maxim: death does not end the service of a spirit driven."
  - After: {n}Pasqal bows to the body.{/n} "Honoured one, you prove Fabricator General Pechrovahr's maxim: death does not end service."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A single blow is more than enough to terminate the residual vital forces in the frail body. The {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} on the ceiling bursts into an indignant wail that becomes a thin, single-note squeak.{/n}
  - After: {n}One blow ends him. The {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} wails into a squeak.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch1/RaycadMinoris/ArcheotechReactor/Aurora/ArcheotechReactor_Aurora_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "So what is this Final Dawn? It is all your followers ever talk about."
  - After: "What is this Final Dawn?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Silence, heretic. Your crazed preaching will not touch my mind."
  - After: "Silence, heretic. Your preaching won't touch me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Step away from the sacred reactor and I might allow you to surrender."
  - After: "Leave the reactor and I may let you surrender."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal, announce my arrival."
  - After: "Pasqal, announce me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What a talented enemy! Can you do the governor's voice?"
  - After: "Talented! Do the governor's voice?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Whose servant are you? Is Uralon a daemon or just another heretic?"
  - After: "Whose servant are you? Is Uralon a daemon or a heretic?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Are you trying to blow up the reactor?"
  - After: "Are you blowing up the reactor?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I think that is enough heretical talk."
  - After: "Enough heresy."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Inspect the control panel damaged by Aurora]
  - After: [Inspect the panel Aurora damaged]
- **Player**
  - Before: "Let us finish cleansing the monastery, Pasqal."
  - After: "Let's finish cleansing the monastery, Pasqal."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Edge of Daybreak? Is that your unholy patron?"
  - After: "The Edge of Daybreak? Your unholy patron?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "Enough. I will rid Rykad Minoris of your tyranny."
  - After: [Attack] "I'll free Rykad Minoris of your tyranny."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "In the name of the God-Emperor — die, foul creature!"
  - After: [Attack] "For the God-Emperor, die, foul creature!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Take a good look at me, Aurora. Predestination has changed. Now I am your master's favourite. Will you dare to go against his will?"
  - After: "Look at me, Aurora. I'm your master's favourite now. Dare you defy him?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Will you be finished soon, Master van Calox? I cannot stand being made to wait."
  - After: "Done soon, Master van Calox? I hate waiting."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What servitude are you talking about? What predestination?"
  - After: "What servitude? What predestination?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Heinrix, take a look over here. Is this by any chance what you are looking for?"
  - After: "Heinrix, is this what you're after?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Toss the shard into the depths of the reactor]
  - After: [Toss the shard into the reactor]
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The face of the woman who stands before you is hidden behind a grotesque barred mask. Yet the voice pouring out beneath it belongs to someone else: it is the husky, sombre bass of a void wolf, a boarder of ships.{/n} "How predictable your path is. How static. All the possible deaths you have skirted, only to perish here, in the fiery tempest that will mark the Final Dawn."
  - After: {n}A masked woman speaks in a void wolf's bass.{/n} "So predictable. You dodged death only to burn here in the Final Dawn."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You cannot make out her blasphemous words, but the name the heretic keeps repeating — the Edge of Daybreak — digs into your hearing like a blade into defenceless flesh. Its sound is almost physically painful. It spawns strange and impossible phantoms in your mind.{/n}
  - After: {n}One name, the Edge of Daybreak, cuts into you like a blade, spawning phantoms.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I would take some time to wrest from you the details of the 'future' that the cult prophesies. Hopefully, when we're done, what's left of you will still be capable of coherent speech."
  - After: "I'll wrest the cult's 'future' from you."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "The motley hues have rejected her, leaving... only a greyish-green thread — the noose that the heretic put around her own neck. I have seen this many times before. No one can escape fear itself."
  - After: "Only a grey-green noose remains. Fear catches everyone."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The corruption that was born within you on the day of Theodora's death answers the call. Aurora's words seem to mesmerise you, conjuring visions in your mind's eye of a flame-engulfed world in which muttering eyeless ghosts wander about, untouched by fire, and the whispers of daemons resonate together to shake the scorched rock below.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your corruption from Theodora's death answers: visions of a burning world and daemon whispers.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix raises his head, gets up, and makes a wry face as he carefully examines Aurora's weapon.{/n} "This unholy object is the work of inhuman hands. And judging by the cold I am sensing, it is a tool of the Archenemy... I am most grateful for your vigilance, {name}."
  - After: {n}Heinrix studies it.{/n} "An Archenemy tool. Thank you, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Do you cling to your blindness so desperately? Do you think it will protect you from the blinding radiance of the truth?"
  - After: "Will blindness shield you from the truth?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Surrender? The gall of it. You are chained to the falsehood of a {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}dead god{/g}'s religion. Captives do not take captives."
  - After: "Surrender? You serve a {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}dead god{/g}. Captives don't take captives."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal lets out an intimidating binharic trill and announces grimly,{/n} "With the Omnissiah's blessing, the Rogue Trader von Valancius has come before the Miraculous Fusion Reactor, seeking to perform purification and eradicate the corruption. All unauthorised persons are hereby ordered to lay down their arms and humbly accept their punishment."
  - After: {n}Pasqal trills:{/n} "Von Valancius comes to purify the reactor. Disarm and accept punishment."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I cannot. Slaves such as you and he have no voice. You are mute."
  - After: "No. Slaves like you have no voice."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Humility is the lot of the meek. I am a harbinger of great changes, and visions of the great cataclysms to come have incinerated what humility I had in my heart."
  - After: "Humility is for the meek. My visions burned mine away."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman's voice breaks and shifts to a different pitch and timbre — a martyr's voice, young, fervent, and in pain:{/n} "Time has all but run out. I can hear the fist of the future knocking on the door of the present. Choose quickly what you want to be when it walks in: a blind slave to what is gone, a faithful servant of what is to come, or a corpse."
  - After: {n}A martyr's voice:{/n} "The future knocks. Choose: slave to the past, servant of the future, or corpse."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A blinding voltaic arc bursts forth from the broken control panel and strikes at Aurora's uncanny mask. Its metal heats up. Smoke billows through the bars. With a howl, the cultist collapses.{/n}
  - After: {n}An arc from the panel strikes Aurora's mask. She collapses, howling.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Conversations about truth always frighten ignorant minds."
  - After: "Truth frightens the ignorant."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}This is no human-made object. It was grown from {g|Encyclopedia:Wraithbone}wraithbone{/g}, a material favoured by the {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g}.{/n}
  - After: {n}It's {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Wraithbone}wraithbone{/g}.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Do you think they are blind? They see far more than you do. Through reflections in mirrors blessed by the energies of the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}Immaterium{/g}, the Edge of Daybreak reveals to them visions of true existence and gives them glimpses of what is to come. The eyes lie: our erstwhile masters have taught them to see only what is consistent with the lies they tell. The gift we give is that of true sight."
  - After: "They see more than you. In {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}Immaterium{/g} mirrors, the Edge of Daybreak shows them the future. We give true sight."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Our teacher. Our saviour. Our merciful god born in the Immaterium out of the woes of those labouring under a legacy of ignorance and servitude."
  - After: "Our merciful god, born in the Immaterium from the woes of the enslaved."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It does have a vile temper. But I have assistants who can help tame it." {n}The woman nods casually toward the maimed Electro-Priests whose hands are affixed to the control panels with steel stakes.{/n}
  - After: "My helpers tame it." {n}She nods at Electro-Priests staked to the panels.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Executing. Let the Omnissiah-given Motive Force flow and all obstacles in its path be eradicated."
  - After: "Executing. Let the Motive Force flow."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman's voice becomes thin and brittle like that of an innocent child:{/n} "Execute them in the name of the Edge of Daybreak!"
  - After: {n}A child's voice:{/n} "Execute them for the Edge of Daybreak!"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "What you'll be is a living torch blazing for His glory!" {n}Argenta's voice burns with pure hatred and trembles with impatience to make the promise come true.{/n}
  - After: "You'll be a living torch for His glory!" {n}Argenta seethes.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix grimaces in disgust.{/n} "The heretic took her secrets with her. Pity."
  - After: {n}Heinrix grimaces.{/n} "Her secrets died with her. Pity."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Ah!" {n}Cassia squints and looks away.{/n} "Yellows, reds, violets, oranges, blues... Wild colours that scorch the eyes. But where the motley masks end, nothing but a colourless void remains."
  - After: "Ah!" {n}Cassia looks away.{/n} "Scorching colours... then a colourless void."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Enough." {n}Now an aged, rattling voice speaks to you from behind the bloodstained mask.{/n} "You are powerless to halt the approach of what is to come. I see the glow of the Final Dawn, and that means existence has made its choice!" {n}A dagger flashes in Aurora's hand. She drives it into the control panel with all her strength.{/n} "Now you will see it too!"
  - After: "Enough." {n}An old voice.{/n} "A {g|Encyclopedia:CicatrixMaledictum}crimson trail{/g} leads Humanity to doom!" {n}She stabs the panel.{/n} "Now you'll see it too!"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}As you touch the handguard, an otherworldly cold envelops your hand — only for a mere instant, as in the very next second, you send the corrupted weapon flying into the shining abyss. The terrible wail of several dozen voices pierces your mind for a moment, only to turn into a deafening shriek and break off as a clap of electricity is heard somewhere beneath your feet.{/n}
  - After: {n}A flash of cold; you fling it in. Voices wail, then silence.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Everyone born in the Imperium has a predestination. The soldier, the commoner, the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratum}Administratum{/g} official, the technomat, the void rat — all are consigned to serving the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g} and then dying a grim death for its glory. The Imperium never thinks twice about treating people as exploitable and expendable. After all, they are the most easily replenished of all resources."
  - After: "All in the Imperium, soldier, {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratum}Administratum{/g} clerk or void rat, serve the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g}, then die for it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My name is known to you. I am Aurora, servant of Uralon the Cruel and the spark of the Final Dawn that is destined to set Rykad Minoris ablaze."
  - After: "I am Aurora, servant of Uralon the Cruel, spark of the Final Dawn that will burn Rykad Minoris."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Resounding laughter comes from behind the mask.{/n} "Your flippancy is so amusing. Why, you have no inkling of the chasm that separates us. He is a prophet who foresaw our impending doom and who graciously bestowed upon us the right to choose a different path. He is a shard of ancient wisdom from a time before we were slaves to our bitter predestination."
  - After: {n}She laughs.{/n} "He's a prophet who foresaw our doom and offered another path."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Even your path is predestined, {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}: you will inevitably perish on your quest to expand Humanity's domain, and your end will be particularly grim and ghastly.   - After: "You too, {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}, will die grimly while aristocrats on {g|Encyclopedia:Mars}Mars{/g} and {g|Encyclopedia:HolyTerra}Terra{/g} profit."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am lighting the spark of the Final Dawn. Sometimes the future revealed in the Edge of Daybreak's visions is fragmented between the facets of possibility, and the view is unclear. False believers will perish in the fire, whilst the faithful will find their salvation and their new form in it."
  - After: "I'm lighting the Final Dawn. It will drag this world into the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}Immaterium{/g} for rebirth. Unbelievers burn; the faithful are saved."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After Aurora finishes, she studies you silently for a while and says in a pleased voice,{/n} "You can sense the truth of my words, can you not? You have softened your soul enough for it to sense, almost as clearly as mine does, the coming changes."
  - After: {n}Aurora, pleased:{/n} "You sense it, don't you? Your soul feels the coming change."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Brother Twilight, known to you as Kunrad, marked you as a target. Your foiling of his plans sealed your death warrant. It is now a predestined certainty that changes can no longer affect."
  - After: "Brother Twilight, your Kunrad, marked you. Foiling him sealed your death."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A great path for one who was born into the Imperium's bondage but shunned her predestination in favour of the changes promised by the Edge of Daybreak."
  - After: "A great path for one who fled Imperial bondage for the Edge of Daybreak."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "They insist that it is the natural order of things, but that is a lie. It is an order that benefits them."
  - After: "Their 'natural order' is a lie that serves them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman turns her mask to Pasqal and gloats,{/n} "You have arrived just in time, little cog. The schismaticals use your regalia like a mask to subdue the reactor."
  - After: {n}To Pasqal:{/n} "Just in time, little cog. The schismaticals use your regalia to subdue the reactor."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's vox rasps musingly,{/n} "A cog. I cannot comprehend why apostates try to insult me by comparing me to the sacred symbol of our faith. From the dust, I will build order."
  - After: {n}Pasqal:{/n} "Insulting me with our sacred symbol is irrational." {n}His drill whirrs.{/n} "The cog grinds corruption to dust."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix gives you an appraising look, then shifts his gaze to the cogitator's control panel.{/n} "An impressive blow. I suppose whatever she used to breach the frame was melted by the impact of the Motive Force... Hmm."
  - After: {n}Heinrix eyes the panel.{/n} "Impressive. The Motive Force melted whatever she used... Hmm."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cogitator is probably well beyond repair, but your attention is drawn away from the sacred machine and toward the dagger sticking out of the control panel. On closer inspection, it turns out to be the lavishly decorated handguard of a sword whose blade has been pried out. Its pommel is decorated with a strange adornment resembling an eye covered by a scaled lid. What remains of the blade has a blue sheen to it — the same tint as Kunrad's weapon during the mutiny on your voidship.{/n}
  - After: {n}A sword hilt juts from the ruined panel, pommel a scaled eye. Its blue sheen matches Kunrad's weapon from the mutiny.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal examines the corpse with contempt, then concludes dryly,{/n} "Confirming purgation and termination."
  - After: {n}Pasqal:{/n} "Purgation confirmed."
- **Electro-Priest**
  - Before: {n}One of the servants of the Omnissiah casts a tortured glance at you, his voice trembling with horror:{/n} "Blasphemous spirits have crawled under our skin and into our sacred iron. Take the Motive Force of our bodies, I implore you. We do not wish to offend the Omnissiah with the sacrileges our hands are committing."
  - After: {n}A tortured Electro-Priest:{/n} "Spirits possess us. Take our Motive Force, I beg you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "They resisted for a long time, but now their bodies and souls belong to the schismaticals. Line after line, the scrap-code they produce will awaken the reactor's unyielding spirit as well. And it, too, will yearn for change and freedom."
  - After: "They're ours now. Their scrap-code will wake the reactor's spirit to crave freedom."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Salvation from a death whose name is yet unknown, but whose approach is sensed by many. Soon it will claim every inhabitant of the Koronus Expanse. Do you think anyone will come to our aid when cataclysms shake our homes and planet-wide genocides are unleashed? Will the Emperor help? Or the idol of iron they call the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}? No. We will die alone and abandoned. Only one deity is promising salvation: the Edge of Daybreak. Mercy and salvation will come to all who believe in him and purify their souls in the light of the Final Dawn."
  - After: "Salvation from a death coming for the Koronus Expanse. Neither Emperor nor {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g} will save us. Only the Edge of Daybreak will."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Electro-Priests rip their hands off the command panels, rending their flesh on the stakes that pierced them. As their schismatical-controlled bodies are imbued with the Motive Force's radiance, all the unfortunates can do is scream in horror and plead for a swift death. Aurora begins muttering an unholy litany in broken Gothic.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman takes a glass prism out of the folds of her clothes, and looks at you through it with a mocking chuckle. The prism's bluish-pink sheen imprints itself on your retinas as though it has been burned into them.{/n} "Guess what I see when I look at you."
  - After: {n}She eyes you through a searing prism.{/n} "Guess what I see."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman's face is hidden behind the mask, but there is a sharpness to her voice that convinces you that her face is contorted in a grimace.{/n} "And he remembers you, {name} von Valancius. Your little {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentThroughFire}purge by fire{/d} will not make you invisible to the Weaver of Destinies."
  - After: {n}Sharply:{/n} "He remembers you, {name} von Valancius. Your {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentThroughFire}purge by fire{/d} won't hide you from the Weaver of Destinies."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The iron helmet is firmly attached to the heretic's flesh. Her face is impossible to make out in the darkness behind the bars of her mask, but after peering at it for a little longer than necessary, you wonder if, for a moment... you saw something move.{/n}
  - After: {n}The helmet is fused to her flesh. Something moves behind the bars?{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "In that case you should consider losing the eyes too, sister, 'cause your visions are all wrong. My whispers are telling me something completely different about who dies here and how. I won't spoil the surprise, so let's just say it will come as quite a shock to you." {n}Idira grins maliciously.{/n}
  - After: "Your visions are wrong, sister. My whispers disagree about who dies here." {n}Idira grins.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "I said it would come as a shock to her, didn't I? They keep sneering and guffawing as if the joke's on us and not her."
  - After: "Told you it'd shock her!" {n}Idira frowns.{/n} "But my friends behind the door are still laughing at us."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You cannot see the woman's face behind her mask, but her voice is trembling with what could be anger or fear.{/n} "And he {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_EdgeHelp}spread the word about you{/d}, {name} von Valancius. The interloper who got in Brother Twilight's way... I will avenge him."
  - After: {n}Trembling:{/n} "He {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_EdgeHelp}spread the word about you{/d}, {name}, who crossed Brother Twilight. I'll avenge him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You cannot see the woman's face behind her mask, but judging by her tone of malicious triumph, you could swear she is smiling.{/n} "And he remembers you, {name} von Valancius. The silly {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentBack}saviour fantasy{/d} you have been acting out amuses the true masters of those people's fates."
  - After: {n}Smugly:{/n} "He remembers you, {name}. Your {d|Encyclopedia:Prologue_WentBack}saviour fantasy{/d} amuses their true masters."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Aurora hesitates. Then a madwoman's hoarse laughter comes from behind the mask.{/n} "You are no successor to Brother Twilight, oh no. You are a mere impostor believing {mf|him|her}self to be a decider of fates! I deny you! I deny you!"
  - After: {n}Mad laughter.{/n} "You're an impostor who thinks {mf|him|her}self a decider of fates! I deny you!"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "What is this poison you speak, Rogue Trader?"
  - After: "What poison is this, Rogue Trader?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The light... is gone. Was that it? The Final Dawn? But why was it so different from what our teacher promised?" {n}Aurora shakes her head blindly. Her iron mask hits the ground with a dull thud.{/n}
  - After: "The light is gone. Was that the Final Dawn?" {n}A frightened woman now.{/n} "You'll pay—" {n}She collapses.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix eyes you icily.{/n} "Interesting choice of words, {name}."
  - After: {n}Heinrix, icily:{/n} "Interesting words, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Aurora's entire body flinches as if she has been struck. A cough sends a scarlet spatter through the grille of her mask.{/n} "What— what is this? Punishment? But for what? I have not renounced the Edge— I— this cannot be— execute them at once!" {n}Aurora attempts to recite an unholy litany in broken Gothic, but her own voice fails her as she is shaken by a violent coughing fit until she can barely breathe.{/n}
  - After: {n}Aurora coughs blood.{/n} "Punishment? I never renounced the Edge— execute them!" {n}Coughing chokes her litany.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Electro-Priests rip their hands off the command panels, rending their flesh on the stakes that pierced them. As their schismatical-controlled bodies are imbued with the Motive Force's radiance, all the unfortunates can do is scream in horror and plead for a swift death.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Electro-Priests tear free of the stakes, screaming for death.{/n}
- **Heinrix**

  - After: {n}Heinrix kneels by the body.{/n} "Just a minute, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As you lean over the shard, you suddenly hear a multitude of voices. They blend together and individual words are distorted, as though they are mocking your attempts to grasp their meaning. The nagging whisper is like the burning red scratch of an unholy claw upon your mind.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Patience is one of the greatest strengths of a powerful dynasty, {mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius."
  - After: "Patience is a dynasty's strength, {mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix efficiently searches Aurora's corpse as if he is looking for something specific. After checking every belt and pouch, he straightens up with an annoyed sigh, glances at the mangled cogitator, and walks toward it with a resolute stride.{/n} "I've found what I've been looking for."
  - After: {n}Heinrix searches the corpse, then goes to the cogitator.{/n} "Found it."

  - Before: "Rogue Trader, on behalf of the Holy Ordos, I thank you for your cooperation and release you from requisition. From this moment on, I am at your service.   - After: "The Holy Ordos thank you and release you from requisition. I'm at your service, ready for Footfall when you are."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}No matter how hard you try, you cannot get it out of your head. Are you really going to carry it around in your mind... forever?{/n}
  - After: {n}It won't leave your head. Forever?{/n}
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Your own death. You just haven't recognised it yet." {n}Kibellah leans forward and whispers with a smile,{/n} "Remember its face."
  - After: "Your own death." {n}Kibellah smiles.{/n} "Remember its face."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}However, you manage to muster your strength and banish it from your mind.{/n}
  - After: {n}But you banish it.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Rogue Trader! I can't wait to close this creature's mouth with the seal of death. Or are you saving this glorious deed for yourself?"
  - After: "Rogue Trader! Let me silence this creature. Or is that yours?"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "You will never tame the spirit of this ancient and noble machine, ignorant layperson."
  - After: "You'll never tame this noble machine, layperson."

  - Before: {n}When you touch the abomination, the whispers in your ears become louder and more... bloodthirsty. You pocket the trophy surreptitiously, just before the Interrogator appears at your shoulder.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch1/RaycadMinoris/ArcheotechReactor/Avel/ArcheotechReactor_Avel_dialogue

  - Before: [Try to take down the Tech-Priest crucified on the machine]
