  - Before: "It is not common for the voidborn to settle on a planet."
  - After: "Voidborn rarely settle planetside."
- **Player**
  - Before: "And what about Naaki Erebis?"
  - After: "And Naaki Erebis?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You have a good heart, it seems. I am surprised."
  - After: "You have a good heart. Surprising."

  - After: "Give them little joys. Sweets, toys... They deserve it."

  - After: "Nothing extravagant. Only food, warm clothes and training."

  - Before: "Educate them so that they may grow up to be of greater use to the ship. Assign teachers, supply books, and commend the best students with gifts."
  - After: "Educate them to serve the ship: teachers, books, prizes for the best."

  - After: "I'll allocate extra for the orphans."

  - Before: "What do the followers of Saint Drusus acquire from us?"
  - After: "What do Saint Drusus's followers get from us?"

  - Before: "Contact the curiosity merchant from the Dargonus palace. A cyber-beast needs new equipment."
  - After: "Contact the Dargonus palace curiosity merchant. A cyber-beast needs new gear."

  - Before: "Tell me more about the Explorators."

  - Before: "I am interested in the Kasballica Mission."
  - After: "Tell me about the Kasballica Mission."

  - Before: "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Would you like the Enginseer Prime to accompany you?"

  - Before: "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. How else may I assist you?"
  - After: "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Anything else?"

  - Before: "As the High Factotum, my duties encompass anything that might enrich you and your protectorate.   - Before: "Chief Record Warden Meryt Sancvida, temporarily holding the position of the ship's High Factotum since the esteemed Master Danrok's... termination." {n}She gulps, and you notice that she is shaking violently.{/n} "I served as his bookkeeper and am well apprised of the Lord Captain's business dealings. I assure you that all your transactions are being completed without fault or delay — the late Master Danrok's subordinates toil day and night to ensure that they are!"
  - After: "Meryt Sancvida, Danrok's bookkeeper, acting since his... termination." {n}She trembles.{/n} "Your business runs flawlessly."

## World/Dialogs/Ch1/Voidship/VoidMaster/Voidmaster_Dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You are a voidborn, are you not?"
  - After: "You're voidborn, aren't you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Indeed, that will be enough."
  - After: "That will be enough."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I must take my leave."
  - After: "I must go."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Thank you for your answers. It was definitely not you."
  - After: "Thanks. It definitely wasn't you."

  - Before: "I can see you are not a gregarious sort."
  - After: "Not a gregarious sort, are you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What can you tell me about the other officers?"
  - After: "What about the other officers?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Did I mishear you, or are you giving the Rogue Trader cheek? Answer me, void rat!"
  - After: "Giving the Rogue Trader cheek? Answer me, void rat!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am merely sharing an observation."
  - After: "Just an observation."
- **Player**
  - Before: "On the contrary, you are the first person on the bridge who's not tripping over themselves to lick my boots."
  - After: "No, you're the first on the bridge not licking my boots."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Who are these idiots you are in charge of?"
  - After: "Who are these idiots you command?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you control the ship in realspace?"
  - After: "You steer in realspace?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You must have dealings with the Navigator as part of your duties..."
  - After: "You must deal with the Navigator..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "That's enough for now."
  - After: "Enough for now."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell me, do you like anyone at all?"
  - After: "Do you like anyone at all?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "An exhaustive answer."
  - After: "Exhaustive answer."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Ravor, it has come to my attention that a fuel lever on the bridge may be defective. Can you not be trusted to carry out your duties without my personal oversight?"
  - After: "A bridge fuel lever may be defective. Can't you work unsupervised?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Does the word 'Epitaph' mean anything to you? Or, perhaps, 'Incident N872-04' or 'tech-blight'? It all has something to do with Theodora's travels. Rather extraordinary travels at that."
  - After: "Do 'Epitaph', 'Incident N872-04' or 'tech-blight' mean anything? They tie to Theodora's travels."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I used to be an officer in the Imperial Navy, and I can say this with certainty: the best helmsmen come from the voidborn. I am glad to have you at the helm of my ship."
  - After: "As ex-Navy, I know the best helmsmen are voidborn. Glad you're at my helm."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you know anything about a ship named the Fiery Reckoning?"
  - After: "Know a ship called the Fiery Reckoning?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am prepared to discuss Proctor Anthar's actions against your voidsmen."
  - After: "Let's discuss Proctor Anthar's actions against your voidsmen."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The tall man before you appears to be woven from tendons and muscle. Blue veins snake under his white, almost dove-coloured skin, and his scalp and chin are covered in cropped white hair. His neck and shoulders are wrapped in wires that hint at the presence of neural connectors under his uniform. The officer's face seems to be twisted in a perpetual grimace of annoyance and anger, but he greets you with a respectful nod.{/n} "Lord Cap'n! Master Helmsman Ravor, at your service."
  - After: {n}A sinewy, pale, wired man with a permanent scowl nods.{/n} "Lord Cap'n! Master Helmsman Ravor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ravor greets you with a nod.{/n} "To what do I owe the honour, Lord Cap'n?"
  - After: {n}Ravor nods.{/n} "Lord Cap'n?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Through my implants, I feel at one with this ship. And I sense that — and I don't know when it happened exactly — it started behaving differently. Became more responsive. Livelier. Yes, 'livelier' is exactly the word... And when you said 'epitaph' and 'incident' it just dawned on me. Pardon my bungled report, Lord Cap'n, but that's all I've got to say on that front."
  - After: "Through my implants I feel the ship. She's grown livelier. Your 'epitaph' and 'incident' made it click. That's all."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ravor stays silent for a few seconds.{/n} "Not much to tell. I gutted everyone I could get to, and then I fled upward, to the middle decks. That's where the augur operators took me under their wing — they have apprentice helmsmen of their own up there, you see. Nobody asked me any questions, so I stayed. I grew up, trained, got smarter. Then ended up a junior helmsman. A dozen years later, Danrok spotted me and lured me away, the cheeky blighter."
  - After: {n}A pause.{/n} "I gutted who I could and fled up. Augur operators trained me. Later Danrok poached me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ravor winces and rubs his temple.{/n} "Lord Cap'n, I mean no disrespect... But you'd do better to find someone with a knack for conversation, like Toliman, the new Vox Master. I ain't the talkin' type, I just get the ship where she needs to go. Best let folk stick to what they do best."
  - After: {n}Ravor rubs his temple.{/n} "Ask Toliman. I ain't a talker."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm the Master Helmsman, Lord Cap'n. I stand at the wheel of this here tub... I mean, your vessel, and bark commands at the idiots who tend to its related systems. In layman's terms, I'm the one who stops us from running into an asteroid or a disruptive gravitational wave when we're travelling through the void."
  - After: "Master Helmsman. I steer and bark at idiots. I keep us off asteroids."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ravor winces and nods.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ravor nods.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Cap'n." {n}Ravor acknowledges you with a nod and turns away.{/n}
  - After: "Lord Cap'n." {n}Ravor turns away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That I am. Born into a helmsman clan in the bowels of a Chartist vessel. Studied the family trade until I was fifteen, then my entire clan was butchered in a mutiny by lower hold scum. They spared the young 'uns — of course they did, kids with implanted connectors make great navigational servitors. But I was having none of it — they weren't going to make a servitor out of me — so I escaped into the crawlways. And then I spent months picking them off, one after the other—" {n}Ravor stops abruptly.{/n} "You got me talking up a storm. Anyway, yes, I'm a voidborn."
  - After: "Helmsman clan, Chartist vessel. At fifteen, mutineers butchered my clan, keeping kids for servitors. I fled into the crawlways and hunted them—" {n}He stops.{/n} "Anyway. Voidborn."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ravor's eye twitches, which makes the grimace on his face even uglier.{/n} "'Ave... 'Ave I done something to displease the Lord Cap'n?"
  - After: {n}Ravor's eye twitches.{/n} "'Ave I displeased you?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}When you shout, Ravor winces as if the sound physically hurts.{/n} "Beg your pardon, beg your pardon, Lord Cap'n... I do apologise! But the blame for my ugly mug and foul temper can't be laid at my door only."
  - After: {n}Ravor winces.{/n} "Beg pardon! But my temper ain't all my fault."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Good-for-nothing wasters, that's what they are. Each and every one. Take Janris Danrok, that highborn weasel. He fawns over the officers, but some of the deals he makes would get him burned alive. He drags other people into his schemes so they can take the fall for him, too. One of my junior helmsmen was ferrying goods from Footfall for him, got caught by the Seneschal, and ended up in the void hatch. Danrok couldn't care less!"
  - After: "Wasters, all. Danrok makes burnable deals and lets others take the fall. My helmsman smuggled for him and went out the void hatch."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Vox Master — another Toliman like the last one, void rest him — is no better. She cut off half the vox-channels the day she took up her post. Said the vox-systems were damaged and the enginarium had no contact with other modules... But how am I supposed to steer the ship? Collect the cogs' reports with the power of my mind?"
  - After: "The new Vox Master Toliman cut half the vox-channels. How do I steer blind?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "First Officer Werserian... I can't stand him. Like every Navy officer I ever met, he doesn't know a thing about controlling a vessel in the void, but he puffs himself up all the same and throws his weight around. Me and him had to have words a few times before he left me alone. Thank the Emperor Lady Theodora trusted me more than the Seneschal when it came to helming a voidship!"
  - After: "First Officer Werserian — Navy, knows nothing of the void. Theodora trusted me over him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Then there's that woman, what's her name? Tlass? Lady Theodora brought her along wherever she went, and look what happened to her? I wouldn't be surprised if it turns out it was that witch that delivered her to an early grave, just like countless souls before. I don't see why anyone would want that walking calamity on their ship, but some would disagree... They say she's friends with young Toliman, you know. Or at least, she used to be."
  - After: "And Tlass. I bet that witch got Theodora killed. She was friends with young Toliman."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ravor looks perplexed.{/n} "What kind of a question is that? I like you. And Lady Theodora before you. Where would I be if I was making cracks about the Rogue Trader? Hah, I don't want to die just yet."
  - After: {n}Ravor looks puzzled.{/n} "I like you, and Theodora. I want to live."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ravor gives you a careful look and scoffs.{/n} "Right you are. It's not hard to see that I'm in a foul mood. I'm not the only one to blame for it, you know."
  - After: {n}Ravor scoffs.{/n} "Right. Foul mood, not all my fault."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Helmsman's perpetually twisted mouth twitches as if he's trying to smile. It looks sinister rather than friendly.{/n} "Oh yeah? Well, I'm pleasantly surprised myself that you aren't having me flogged for insubordination. Will wonders never cease?"
  - After: {n}A sinister half-smile.{/n} "And you ain't flogging me. Wonders."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ravor points at the cables around himself.{/n} "Connecting wires. Once they go into the control panel, I become one with the ship. Except the bloody cogs messed up the wires' stimulus injectors and connectors when they implanted them — they twisted the wires the wrong way or burned something in my noggin. Anyway, I can't sleep. It just doesn't happen anymore. It's been thirty years of non-stop stimulants and a splitting headache. So you'll forgive me if I'm not all smiles, Lord Cap'n."
  - After: {n}He points at his cables.{/n} "The cogs botched my ship-link implants. Thirty years without sleep, just stimulants and headaches. So no smiles."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I wish that was my only job. I have to steer her through the warp too, but most of the credit for that goes to the Navigator. The warp's a nightmare, always tossing up something new — all my years at the helm, they count for nothing in there. My part's small enough — I just monitor our systems, follow the charted route, and I don't kick up a fuss when new orders come in from the Navigator's Sanctum."
  - After: "And the warp, though that's mostly the Navigator. There I just watch systems and follow her route."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There are too many to list them all. Tech-Priests from the enginarium, voidsmen from the augur decks, the work-shy fools on the bridge. I'd have every last one of them flogged! They all need a wake-up call. They need to be whipped into shape or else this ship'll be going nowhere. Or even worse, it'll go somewhere we don't want it to."
  - After: "Tech-Priests, augur voidsmen, bridge loafers. Flog them all, or we go nowhere."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "{g|Encyclopedia:Realspace}Realspace{/g} — now that's where I keep my eyes peeled. Gravitational anomalies, void currents, hard radiation — that kind of shit shows up everywhere. Thank the Emperor, the augurs on this vessel are holding up, and so far we've been able to spot if something bad's coming our way."
  - After: "{g|Encyclopedia:Realspace}Realspace{/g} hazards are everywhere. Our augurs hold up."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ravor stares at you before blurting out,{/n} "Dammit, Lord Cap'n... To tell the truth, I've been asking myself... where'd the Lord Cap'n fish this Orsellio girl out of? Now, it's not like I've met many Navigators, but this one... I don't feel safe with that little princess pulling our voidship through the warp. She's done a decent job so far, though, so I guess she's managing."
  - After: {n}Ravor blurts,{/n} "Where'd you find this Orsellio girl? She makes me nervous, though she's managing."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'll be blasted if I understand a thing, but I'm here to serve. Something else you'd like to discuss?"
  - After: "Don't understand, but I serve. Anything else?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The officer's furrowed eyebrows draw even closer together. He speaks slowly, carefully picking his words:{/n} "I most definitely can, Lord Cap'n. The technomats will inspect the equipment immediately. I will also deal with those in charge without delay."
  - After: {n}Ravor frowns.{/n} "I can. Technomats will inspect it, and I'll punish those responsible."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Can't say they do, Lord Cap'n. Doesn't ring any bells. Then again, remembering all the places Lady Theodora went is..." {n}His brow furrows.{/n} "Epitaph, incident... We've always had heaps of incidents happening on board, but..."
  - After: "No bells, Lord Cap'n." {n}He frowns.{/n} "Epitaph, incident... Plenty of incidents, but..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ravor freezes, tensely staring you in the eye and clearly trying to discern if your words are meant as mockery. After a moment's pause, a muscle in his face twitches, then another. His cheeks spasm, his mouth twists... and you realise that Ravor is unsuccessfully trying to remember how to smile.{/n} "Th-thank you, Lord Cap'n. I won't let you down."
  - After: {n}Ravor's face spasms as he tries to smile.{/n} "Th-thank you, Lord Cap'n. I won't let you down."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ravor winces as if in pain.{/n} "I've heard the name, that much I'm sure of... but I can't recall the details. Ha... I wonder if it was part of that operation that the late Mort was put in charge of. If it was, then there's nothing I can tell you, Lord Cap'n. The whole thing was kept under wraps. Your best chance would be to ask the High Factotum — maybe some of his treasury records have mentions of this 'Fiery Reckoning.'"
  - After: {n}Ravor winces.{/n} "Heard of it. Maybe Mort's secret operation. Check the High Factotum's records."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No. I'm up to my connectors in work as it is."
  - After: "No. I'm up to my connectors in work."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The helmsman scratches the back of his head thoughtfully.{/n} "Damned if I know, Lord Captain. If you ask me, our orphans have it worlds better than they would on other ships."
  - After: {n}He scratches his head.{/n} "Dunno. Our orphans have it better than most."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Those some weren't trying hard enough or listening to their higher-ups, is all. Or has someone you know died on you and I'm supposed to offer my sympathies?" {n}Ravor grunts and looks away.{/n} "Odd choice of person to come to with something like that, Lord Captain."
  - After: "They didn't try hard enough. Want sympathy?" {n}Ravor grunts.{/n} "Wrong man, Lord Captain."

Moreover, scouting reports indicated that the instigators of the uprising were also hiding there — {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g}, the enemies of Humanity. Governor Vyatt suggested burning the worthless forests to the ground so the rebels could no longer hide, however, there were serious doubts about the competence of the officers she selected for the task. Locating the camps using the blessed Lord Captain's ship's technical equipment was a real challenge possible only for a highly sensitive and powerful augur.
  - After: The camps, and their {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g} instigators, hid in island forests. Vyatt urged burning them, with dubious officers. Ship augurs would struggle.

He proposed that members of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} who served such machines could contribute to intelligence gathering.
  - After: Magos Haneumann proposed using the islands' seismic machines and their {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} keepers.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The esteemed Idira Tlass put forth a suggestion of using psyker divination to try to discover the traitors' camp.
  - After: Idira Tlass suggested psyker divination.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The berries found by the Lord Captain among the rebels' belongings only grow in certain regions of the planet where the soil has a unique mineral composition.
  - After: The rebels' berries grow only on specific mineral soil.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: After sending scouts to that area, the Lord Captain quickly discovered the rebels' hideout. Sensing that the end was near, the rebels gathered in their camps and prepared to take a final stand.
  - After: Scouts found the hideout. The rebels prepared a last stand.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Unfortunately, the scouts sent to that area by the Lord Captain failed to locate the rebels' hideout — they could not penetrate the advanced camouflage provided to the rebels by their ungodly backers, the xenos.
  - After: Xenos camouflage hid the rebels from the scouts.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Armed with flamers, the soldiers of the planetary garrison began methodically burning the island forests. With no cover left to conceal them, the rebels gathered in their camps and manned the defences, sensing their imminent death.

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Unfortunately, few of the planetary garrison soldiers were skilled enough to wield these powerful tools of destruction without any adverse consequences. Numerous incidents related to the combustion of {g|Encyclopedia:Promethium}promethium{/g} tanks, made torching the forests a slower and more difficult process.
  - After: Unskilled soldiers caused {g|Encyclopedia:Promethium}promethium{/g} accidents, slowing the burning.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The ship's all-seeing augurs fixed their unblinking eye on the island forests, quickly flagging points where suspicious activity was detected. The rebels' camps were found, and within them the insurrectionists were taking one last, desperate stand.
  - After: The ship's augurs found the camps. The rebels made a last stand.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Unfortunately, even the all-seeing eye of the ship's augurs failed to quickly locate the rebels' camps in the island forests. The scant information supplied by the {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} only coalesced into a clear picture when it was too late.
  - After: The augurs were too slow; the {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g}' data came too late.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The wise ones of the Adeptus Mechanicus appealed to the sacred machines of geological monitoring with prayerful enquiries. After analysing the blessed rhythms of seismic activity, they gave the Lord Captain a report with the supposed coordinates of the rebels' camps. The rebels were locked inside their lairs, preparing to take one last, desperate stand.
  - After: The Mechanicus read the seismic rhythms and gave the camps' coordinates. The rebels prepared a last stand.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The wise ones of the Adeptus Mechanicus appealed to the sacred machines of geological monitoring with prayerful enquiries, but then they fell into a gruelling debate about whether it was permissible to reveal the blessed rhythms of seismic activity to laypersons. The debate was never-ending and delayed the conclusion of the operation.
  - After: The Mechanicus debated endlessly whether laypeople may know seismic data, delaying everything.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The psyker divination revealed the precise location of the traitors to the Imperium. Following the scent of their profane thoughts, the soldiers of the planetary garrison tracked down the rebels' bases and blockaded them.
  - After: Divination pinpointed the traitors; the garrison blockaded their bases.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The attempt at psyker divination proved unsuccessful — all that came of it were confused and contradictory predictions and strange, tall shadows hiding among the trees of Janus, anointing the planet's core with their tears. The conclusion of the operation was delayed as a result.
  - After: Divination failed: only contradictions and tall shadows weeping among the trees. The operation was delayed.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: As a result of the actions of the forces loyal to the Imperium, the rebels were driven into isolated regions, where their camps were then discovered and blockaded.
  - After: Rebels were driven to isolated regions and their camps blockaded.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The harsh reprisals carried out by the Lord Captain's servants in the struggle against the rebel underground considerably reduced the population of Janus and diminished its value as a colony.
  - After: Harsh reprisals depleted Janus's population and value.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: When the rebels were being driven out of the jungles, targeted orbital strikes were carried out that damaged the agricultural infrastructure of the agri-world and impaired the planet's production capacity.
  - After: Orbital strikes damaged agricultural infrastructure and output.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The planet's defence complexes were damaged in the course of the rebels' terrorist acts, which negatively affected its security.
  - After: Rebel terror damaged planetary defences.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The operation to combat the xenos-incited traitors to Humanity was a success. The wisdom and will of our illustrious Lord Captain made possible the ultimate eradication of that ungodly movement, and that process was personally overseen by the Rogue Trader — the sovereign of Janus and agent of His will.
  - After: Success. The Rogue Trader, sovereign of Janus, personally eradicated the xenos-incited traitors.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: On the Lord Captain's orders, thrice-daily planet-wide prayer services were held, in which the population of Janus prayed for the deliverance of His land from the clutches of the enemies of Humanity. The rituals and litanies had an effect on the agri-world's inhabitants — reports soon began to arrive that the members of the underground had lost the support of the peasantry and had been forced to abandon the world's major settlements.
  - After: Thrice-daily planet-wide prayers turned the peasants against the rebels, who abandoned the major settlements.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The campaign organised by the esteemed Lord Captain's people took effect. {mf|His|Her} address to {mf|his|her} subjects was broadcast by {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-systems throughout the colony, while workers in towns were granted a shift off work and given provisions, {g|Encyclopedia:Recaf}recaf{/g}, and personal fuel cells. Moved by the Lord Captain's kindness, the colony inhabitants rushed to the recently established confessional centres. The rebel underground was forced to hastily retreat from the major cities.
  - After: It worked. {mf|His|Her} {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-address and gifts of {g|Encyclopedia:Recaf}recaf{/g} won {mf|his|her} subjects; they confessed, and rebels fled the cities.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The campaign organised by the esteemed Lord Captain's people did not produce the expected result. The dissolute and brutish subjects of Janus did not respond with gratitude to the Lord Captain's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-address, which was broadcast throughout the colony, or to the distribution of provisions and {g|Encyclopedia:Recaf}recaf{/g}. Instead of accepting the Lord Captain's gifts with thanks, the people began to mutter that the authorities were trying to buy them off with surplus rations packs.
  - After: The campaign failed. The {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-address, provisions and {g|Encyclopedia:Recaf}recaf{/g} were scorned as bribes of surplus rations.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: With the support of resources from Governor Vyatt, the spy network of the esteemed Heinrix van Calox quickly established surveillance in the planet's major cities. No one escaped the attention of this unblinking eye, and the underground rebels were forced to retreat to more remote locations after the first wave of arrests.
  - After: Backed by Vyatt, van Calox's spies watched every city. After the first arrests, the rebels fled.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The faithful servants of the esteemed Governor Vyatt assured the Lord Captain of their complete and unquestioning devotion and readiness to serve {mf|him|her} to the best of their ability.
  - After: Vyatt's servants swore total devotion to {mf|him|her}.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Alas, the spy network of the esteemed Heinrix van Calox failed to capture all of the colony's subjects in its surveillance net. Its success was hampered by sabotage efforts by the rebels and the incompetence of Governor Vyatt's forces, who were assisting the operation. Agents on the ground were killed, surveillance reports went missing, and tracking devices were tampered with.
  - After: Rebel sabotage and Vyatt's incompetence foiled van Calox's network.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Lord Captain's agents managed to infiltrate the rebel underground via networks of contemptible thieves and smugglers and identify the main leaders. After the wave of arrests, the remaining rebels fled the major cities.
  - After: Agents infiltrated via smugglers and exposed the leaders. After arrests, the rebels fled the cities.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Unfortunately, the operation to plant agents in the rebel underground via the planet's criminal circles was a failure. All the spies were executed en masse by the paranoid insurrectionists, and this minor victory only served to raise their morale and harden their resolve.
  - After: The infiltration failed. All spies were executed, boosting rebel morale.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The voidship's medics who landed on the planet to support the offensive were prepared to render first aid to the wounded.
  - After: Ship's medics landed to aid the wounded.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: In choosing a strategy, the Lord Captain had to consider the limited trustworthiness of the world's population, which was uncovered by the ship's medics deployed on the planet to support the offensive. Their reports indicated widespread genetic anomalies in the colony's inhabitants for which there was no logical explanation.
  - After: The medics found widespread unexplained genetic anomalies, so the locals couldn't be trusted.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Using the rebels' transmitter captured by the Lord Captain, the officers of the planetary garrison engaged in an elaborate {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-game, interfering in the rebels' discussions, spreading disinformation, and sowing paranoia within their ranks.
  - After: With the captured transmitter, officers ran a {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-game of disinformation and paranoia.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: This cunning strategy allowed the wardens to quickly push the enemy out of the agricultural production areas into island regions of no economic value.
  - After: It pushed the enemy to worthless islands.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Unfortunately, the traitors to Humanity quickly realised the deception and changed their vox-frequency, stalling the large-scale jungle offensive.
  - After: The traitors caught on and switched frequency, stalling the offensive.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Strikes thundered down upon Janus with almighty force, hitting the island forests and turning the ancient wilds to ash. The terrified rebels fled for their camps, where they manned the defences, anticipating their imminent death.
  - After: Bombardment turned the island forests to ash. The rebels fled to their camps for a last stand.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: As expected, the brutal punitive raids, searches, and public punishments struck terror into the population and spurred them to unmask the traitors within their ranks. The rebel underground was quickly driven from the major cities.
  - After: Brutal raids terrified people into exposing traitors, and the rebels fled the cities.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The main rebel forces were hiding in the jungles that blanketed Janus. These sparsely populated regions were home to the colony's key agricultural facilities, which the fighters used as cover for their actions, allowing them to carry out incursions. Governor Vyatt's wardens lacked the training and skills to operate in such conditions.
  - After: Rebels hid in the jungles, using farm facilities as cover. Vyatt's wardens lacked jungle skills.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: In addition to this, the ship's medics' reports revealed a broad spectrum of genetic abnormalities among the governor's wardens, and among Janus's peasant population. Active sources of radiation or biological xenothreats were deemed unlikely, but the influence of the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Ruinous Powers{/g} on the bodies and souls of the planet's inhabitants could not be discounted. Given this information, it would have been unwise and dangerous to place any trust in the locals.
  - After: Medics found mutations in wardens and peasants, possibly the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Ruinous Powers{/g}. Locals weren't trustworthy.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The esteemed Abelard Werserian proposed using the rebels' own weapons against them. Their strength lay in the covert guerrilla tactics of their attacks. The esteemed Abelard expressed his conviction that he could teach the basics of these tactics to the soldiers of the planetary garrison, eliminating the rebels' advantage.
  - After: Abelard Werserian proposed teaching the garrison the rebels' guerrilla tactics.

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/AgriworldJungle/RebelLeadersDialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Yrliet, are you staying with us? I'll be departing this world soon and heading for the stars — perhaps you want to do that too?"
  - After: "Yrliet, will you come to the stars with me?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I must take my leave."
  - After: "I must go."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/AgriworldJungle/RebelLeadersDialogue/RebelLeadersDialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Address Yrliet] "I can't convince your kinsman, but I know you are on my side... Will you help me save the Lilaethan from the true enemy?"
  - After: [Address Yrliet] "You're on my side. Help me save the Lilaethan from the true enemy?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "I want to cleanse Janus of heresy — of you!"
  - After: [Attack] "I'll cleanse Janus of heresy — of you!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I'm sorry to hear that your home was destroyed. But I wasn't there and know nothing of this calamity."
  - After: "Sorry about your home. But I know nothing of it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "And your kin from Janus do not object to sending you Throne knows where to look for the survivors all on your own?"
  - After: "Your kin let you search for survivors all alone?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Perhaps Muaran would see a little more if he bothered to pull his head out of his arse."
  - After: "Muaran might see more with his head out of his arse."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Let's cool our tempers and try to speak calmly about this."
  - After: "Let's cool our tempers and talk calmly."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am willing to help the Aeldari defeat the Archenemy. But first we must deal with the rebellions you have been orchestrating..."
  - After: "I'll help fight the Archenemy. But first, your rebellions..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If I may, I would like to say something—"
  - After: "If I may say something—"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "Why listen to you talk when I can just kill you?"
  - After: [Attack] "Why listen when I can kill you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Xenos! Fall on your knees before the Rogue Trader, whose world you have plunged into anarchy, and beg for forgiveness!"
  - After: "Xenos! Kneel before the Rogue Trader whose world you wrecked, and beg forgiveness!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I've had enough of talking. If you xenos refuse to bow down before the Rogue Trader, you will leave me no choice but to kill you."
  - After: "Enough talk. Bow to the Rogue Trader, xenos, or die."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If this world is in serious danger, there is no sense in fighting each other — let us deal with our common enemy together!"
  - After: "If this world is in danger, let's face our common enemy together!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Putting a xenos at the head of an Imperial planet is suicide."
  - After: "A xenos ruling an Imperial planet is suicide."
- **Player**
  - Before: "And where's my guarantee that the planet and its inhabitants will be safe?"
  - After: "What guarantees the planet and its people stay safe?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address the rebel] "Come to your senses, servant of the God-Emperor! Throw off this cursed fog of sorcery and stand with me against the xenos, against these enemies of Humanity!"
  - After: [Address the rebel] "Wake up, servant of the God-Emperor! Throw off this sorcery and stand with me against the xenos!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am looking for whoever's behind the uprisings on Janus."
  - After: "I seek whoever's behind the Janus uprisings."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I learned there were xenos dwelling on the planet. And I wanted to meet you."
  - After: "I learned xenos lived here. I wanted to meet you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have learned a lot about Janus in my time here so far, and I see signs of another threat besides that of the 'mon-keigh.'"
  - After: "I see signs of a threat on Janus besides the 'mon-keigh.'"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why are you fighting against the governor?"
  - After: "Why fight the governor?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How did you come to be on Janus?"
  - After: "How did you come to Janus?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The people on the planet are afflicted with mutations whose origins remain unknown to us. As there are no major sources of radiation on the agri-world, we can discount a technological cause."
  - After: "The people suffer mutations of unknown origin. No radiation here, so it's not technological."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The forests are teeming with signs of blight — distorted plants, deranged animals. Go into the trees and you will see it for yourself."
  - After: "The forests teem with blight — twisted plants, deranged animals. See for yourself."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have heard more than a few rumours that the governor and her circle are engaging in some... reprehensible activities."
  - After: "I've heard the governor's circle does... reprehensible things."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I don't want any more blood — neither yours nor ours. You have my permission to take Janus and its inhabitants into your... charge."
  - After: "No more blood, yours or ours. Take Janus and its people into your... charge."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I cannot give Janus to the Aeldari — humans will only be ruled by humans. But I promise that no harm will come to you."
  - After: "Humans will only be ruled by humans; Janus isn't yours. But no harm will come to you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I'm not obliged to convince you of anything. Think what you like."
  - After: "I needn't convince you. Think what you like."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Even if Crudarach was destroyed by humans as you claim, I imagine you gave them a perfectly good reason to do so."
  - After: "If humans destroyed Crudarach, I bet you gave them good reason."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Watch your tongue, xenos. I'm doing you a favour just by listening to your vile words."
  - After: "Watch your tongue, xenos. I'm doing you a favour by listening."
- **Player**
  - Before: "My duty is to protect my worlds and my vassals. If Janus is being threatened by the Archenemy, I will fight to the end."
  - After: "I protect my worlds and vassals. If the Archenemy threatens Janus, I'll fight to the end."
- **Player**
  - Before: "An entire herd of xenos. The hunt will be good."
  - After: "A whole herd of xenos. Good hunting."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, the sovereign of Janus and {mf|master|mistress} over every living soul on this world! On your knees, foul heretics!"
  - After: "I am Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, sovereign of Janus and {mf|master|mistress} of every soul here! Kneel, heretics!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "We? Do you wish to join my entourage?"
  - After: "We? You want to join me?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Speak to the Rogue Trader like that again and it will be the last thing you say."
  - After: "Talk to me like that again and it'll be your last words."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I certainly will not be needing xenos' help in this affair."
  - After: "I won't need xenos help here."
- **Player**
  - Before: "We shall do things another way: I shall grant my protection to this form of alliance between xenos and representatives of Humanity. Together we shall destroy Vistenza and her associates, and then humans and Aeldari will flourish on Janus under my patronage!"
  - After: "Another way: I'll protect this xenos-human alliance. We'll destroy Vistenza and her associates, then humans and Aeldari will flourish on Janus under me!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "In the name of the Golden Throne, I will purge this Imperial world of the heresy that has tainted it!"
  - After: [Attack] "In the Golden Throne's name, I'll purge this world of heresy!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Yrliet, do I need to convince you? Maybe you can try trusting your own intuition instead of your overseer? You know, that thing that's telling you not to believe everything Muaran says?"
  - After: "Yrliet, trust your own intuition, not your overseer — the one telling you not to believe Muaran."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Stop pretending I am not here. I have come to discuss the situation on Janus."
  - After: "Stop ignoring me. I'm here to discuss Janus."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I took this skull from the governor's secretary. The secret of your presence on this planet is not as well-kept as you think — at least not among Vistenza's circle."
  - After: "I took this skull from the governor's secretary. Vistenza's circle knows about you."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address Yrliet] "Do you not see? Every breath your kinsman takes is riddled with corruption. He resorts to lies, obfuscations, and accusations — all to save his rotten little soul. Kill him. You want to save the Lilaethan, don't you?"
  - After: [Address Yrliet] "Your kinsman reeks of corruption — lies and accusations to save his rotten soul. Kill him. You want to save the Lilaethan, don't you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have already been patient with your kin. And now you are asking for more?"
  - After: "I've been patient with your kin. You want more?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Mon-keigh titles mean nothing to me. If you came here to make boasts in empty words, your journey has been for nothing."
  - After: "Mon-keigh titles mean nothing. You wasted your journey."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet seems to freeze for a moment, and then she turns sharply to Muaran.{/n} "Throughout all the cycles that I wandered amidst the stars, I was sure of one thing: fate can be changed. Cling to your faith, Farseer, but I refuse to follow a blind man who is dooming his kin to a false hunt. I am going off on my own Path — with the elantach."
  - After: {n}Yrliet turns to Muaran.{/n} "Fate can change. I won't follow a blind Farseer. I go my own Path — with the elantach."
- **Bogul**
  - Before: {n}The rebel looks at you with undisguised {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusViolent}contempt{/d}. He pointedly spits in your direction and turns away.{/n}
  - After: {n}The rebel spits with {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusViolent}contempt{/d}.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I am a {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Child of Asuryan{/g}, Muaran, not a plaything in the cold hands of fate, which you claim speaks through your mouth! My choice of Path is no worse than yours or any other Aeldari's — and my Path calls me to fight our true enemies, not eradicate the mon-keigh! If it comes to it, I will stand with them, for this elantach can see what you are blind to, Farseer!" {n}Yrliet's eyes are alight with fury. She pointedly lays her hand on her weapon, looking away from the Farseer.{/n}
  - After: "I'm a {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Child of Asuryan{/g}, not fate's plaything! My Path is fighting our true enemies, beside this elantach!" {n}She grips her weapon.{/n}
- **Bogul**
  - Before: {n}The rebel lets out a laugh that sounds more like a hoarse caw and wipes the corner of his mouth on his shoulder.{/n} "{mf|Master|Mistress}... Off that voidship the vox-ops are on about, I suppose? You're already working with the governor... There's no point talking to this one, Commander, just say the word and we'll—"
  - After: {n}The rebel caws a laugh.{/n} "{mf|Master|Mistress}? The governor's ally. Commander, say the word—"
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "The words of a creature whose will is ruled by momentary whims. There is nothing you can do to make me believe in the strength of your convictions."
  - After: "A creature of whims. I don't believe you."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "Yrliet the Outcast is as beholden to her emotions as you mon-keigh are. Isn't that why she abandoned her true path — and after years of wandering, her {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Asuryani{/g} blood has run dry and become more like yours. Speak then, if you have something to say."
  - After: "The Outcast is as emotional as you; her {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Asuryani{/g} blood runs thin. Speak."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Are you insane? You're condemning us all to death in Sai'lanthresh's maw!" {n}Yrliet grabs her weapon, her voice breaking into a desperate shout.{/n} "I won't let you kill the elantach, Muaran!"
  - After: "You'll doom us to Sai'lanthresh!" {n}Yrliet draws.{/n} "I won't let you kill the elantach!"
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "The name of that danger is mon-keigh, and I will see to it that the Lilaethan is purged of those defiling her face. Then again... there is one way to prove to me that the mon-keigh truly do care about the well-being of their captured world. Eliminate the ruler of the mon-keigh sojourning on the Lilaethan, and relinquish the governing of this world to me and my kin."
  - After: "The danger is mon-keigh. Prove otherwise: kill your ruler here and give this world to my kin."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "This elantach was the first person to discover the coming of Sai'lanthresh — one of those whom the mon-keigh call {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos Gods{/g}. Without {mf|him|her}, I would still be deceived by your words about destiny and the true future."
  - After: "This elantach found Sai'lanthresh's coming, one of the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos Gods{/g}. Without {mf|him|her}, I'd still believe your lies."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "Do not forget: the current ruler of the mon-keigh must die — by your hand or ours. And I will consider the conditions of our deal unmet until that happens."
  - After: "Your ruler must die, by your hand or ours. Until then, no deal."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "Mon-keigh revealing paths... it's ludicrous. Mon-keigh bring pain and strife — in our time, and for all time. How can you trust a mon-keigh after what we taught you? After hearing the sorrowful song of the dying world?" {n}Muaran turns his head toward you.{/n} "It was not chance that brought Crudarach down. Mon-keigh destroyed our ancient home. Stripped us of our defences. Doomed us to wander amidst the cold stars."
  - After: "Mon-keigh revealing paths? Ludicrous." {n}He turns to you.{/n} "Mon-keigh destroyed Crudarach, our home."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Muaran says nothing for a few moments, then adds mockingly,{/n} "I suppose my demands can be considered a gift for the likes of you. You could not wish for anything better than {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} stewards to rule over mon-keigh without bloodshed..."
  - After: {n}Mocking:{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} stewards, no bloodshed. A gift."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "You have the word of a {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Child of Asuryan{/g}, who venerates life far more than any of you. What is more, mon-keigh, I have not the slightest desire to inflict harm upon the Lilaethan, the land of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} ancestors."
  - After: "A {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Child of Asuryan{/g} gives his word. I won't harm this land of {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} ancestors."
- **Muaran**

- **Muaran**
  - Before: "Mon-keigh, state the reason for your coming. I hope it is convincing, or else you will be sent to meet your ancestors without delay."
  - After: "Why are you here, mon-keigh? Convince me, or die."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "Your kind is not amenable to talking — only to senseless destruction. The mon-keigh have corrupted and obliterated our home, the Lilaethan — all because of their primitive affinity for violence, no doubt. Your advances in this art surpass those of other more ancient civilisations of the universe."
  - After: "Your kind only destroys. You ruined our home, the Lilaethan."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet leans forward.{/n} "Of what do you speak, elantach?"
  - After: {n}Yrliet leans in.{/n} "Of what, elantach?"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "As I have told you, Muaran... even the mon-keigh recognise the threat that has veiled the Lilaethan in shadow! Why are you so insistent on hating the mon-keigh when our most ancient foe has raised its head?"
  - After: "Even mon-keigh see the threat, Muaran! Why hate them when our ancient foe rises?"
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "The Lilaethan herself will stand as surety for our agreement. As will your compatriots who live on it.   - After: "The Lilaethan is your surety." {n}He tilts his head.{/n} "Human puppets replace your leaders; we rule from shadow."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Muaran glares at you for a while, then nods.{/n} "So be it."
  - After: {n}Muaran nods.{/n} "So be it."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet pauses, and then looks at the other Aeldari.{/n} "I have seen it before on my wanderings.   - After: {n}Yrliet turns.{/n} "Muaran, are you blind? She Who Thirsts rises over the Lilaethan..."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "There are even signs of corruption among those who share our refuge. I thought it was the natural way of things for our kind — an early prime, accelerated ageing, and then rotting alive year after year."
  - After: "Even our refuge shows corruption — rotting alive. I thought it natural."
- **Yrliet**

  - After: "No blight — the Lilaethan's cry for help. The World Spirit fights back, harder by the hour."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Muaran makes a sharp gesture.{/n} "No. We will restore the Lilaethan to her rightful custodians, or our conversation is over."
  - After: {n}Muaran gestures.{/n} "No. The Lilaethan returns to us."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet goes still when she sees the skull — and then whips around to face Muaran.{/n} "How did our kin's remains end up in the hands of the mon-keigh? - **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet stares at you intently, and then turns away.{/n}
  - After: {n}Yrliet turns away.{/n}
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}A heavy silence falls between you and the assembled {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g}.{/n}
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} fall silent.{/n}
- **Bogul**
  - Before: "What?" {n}The man shudders, screws up his face, and after a second, stares around in bewilderment as if seeing everything for the first time.{/n} "By the God-Emperor! They're..."
  - After: "What?" {n}The man blinks, bewildered.{/n} "By the God-Emperor! They're..."

  - Before: {n}Muaran utters a florid curse and calls his kin to battle.{/n}
  - After: {n}Muaran calls his kin to battle.{/n}
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Muaran's voice rumbles like distant thunder.{/n} "You will not defy your masters and betray the customs of Crudarach again, Outcast..."
  - After: {n}Muaran rumbles.{/n} "You won't defy Crudarach again, Outcast..."

  - Before: {n}Muaran leans down over Yrliet, his tone menacing.{/n} "You left Crudarach in our darkest hour to gratify your ego.   - After: {n}Muaran looms.{/n} "You fled Crudarach in its darkest hour. I took you in, and you insult a Farseer? You've ruined us!"

  - Before: "The Lilaethan is struggling to expel the disease that has settled within her borders. And if the mon-keigh's efforts to destroy this planet are only increasing, isn't it right for the Maiden World to seek retribution?"
  - After: "The Lilaethan is expelling a disease. Isn't that just?"
- **Muaran**

  - After: "Your true face shows. Kin, kill the outsider."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I heard the ruler giving out orders... She called them the 'innovations of the finest minds on Janus.' What minds would condemn themselves to such a woeful fate?"
  - After: "The ruler called them 'innovations of the finest minds on Janus.' Who would choose that?"
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "If the Lilaethan remains in our charge, I am willing to come to an agreement. - **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Muaran says nothing for several moments.{/n} "The path I set for you had been travelled before, Outcast. Karantar was sent to the ruler of the mon-keigh before you came among us. His fate was hidden from my sight..."

- **Yrliet**

  - After: "My Path is no curse!" {n}Yrliet seethes.{/n} "It saved me from dying with Crudarach!"
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "You foolish wretch! You have exceeded my patience — your Path ends here and now!"
  - After: "Wretch! Your Path ends here!"
- **Bogul**
  - Before: {n}Muaran tries to say something, but the rebel interrupts him:{/n} "If this... offworlder keeps dictating terms, I won't be able to stop myself, Commander! - **Bogul**
  - Before: {n}The rebel looks at you with a hint of doubt.{/n} "We'll see. You may have {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusHarsh}stuck it{/d} to us... but, to be fair, we did break the law of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g} with all our riots. So let's try it this way."

- **Yrliet**

- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet speaks so quietly, you can barely make out her words:{/n} "We should have remained shadows to the mon-keigh — ghosts wandering amidst the ancient ruins. But you, elantach... whose hand led you to the Lilaethan? Destiny or damnation? Muaran, allow {mf|him|her} to speak."
  - After: {n}Yrliet whispers:{/n} "Destiny or damnation brought you, elantach? Muaran, let {mf|him|her} speak."
- **Yrliet**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After Yrliet's words, the two tall Aeldari behind Muaran start moving — one looks around at the leader, while the other lets out a cry, muffled under his visor. - **Yrliet**

  - After: "Their hearts hurt too. Fear? Despair? Ah!" {n}Cassia bleeds from her cheek.{/n}
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}The Aeldar chuckles, his voice turning venomous.{/n} "Or it could be that your uncontrollable hunger to destroy everything in your path reigns over your every thought and deed."
  - After: {n}He chuckles.{/n} "Or your hunger to destroy rules you."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "Rest assured, the very sound of your primitive tongue causes us as much suffering — even a translator cannot alleviate its crudeness."
  - After: "Your crude tongue pains us equally."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Muaran gazes at you intently.{/n} "If these words had come from an {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g}, I would have believed them. - **Muaran**

- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet shakes her head.{/n} "You are attempting to cloud my sight, mon-keigh."
  - After: {n}She shakes her head.{/n} "You cloud my sight."
- **Bogul**
  - Before: "You won't believe what they do to the people! You won't see much at the nobles' estates, but if you go out to the agri settlements... - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The warriors are the first to raise their weapons and charge into the fray. A moment later, the rebels follow suit.{/n}

  - After: {n}A trembling rebel, strange device at his neck, eyes you.{/n} "Who are you?"
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Muaran stares at you for several seconds. At last, he says,{/n} "An alliance? That is how you interpreted what I said? Then again, if you prefer that word, let us call it an alliance."
  - After: {n}He stares.{/n} "Alliance? Call it that."
- **Bogul**

  - After: {n}He nods.{/n} "Good... Our commanders know best..." {n}He winces.{/n}

  - After: "Ha! Humans and xenos allied? Joke, right, shereen?"

- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Finally, Muaran tilts his head.{/n} "I am not willing to risk my kin's lives, mon-keigh. I will steel my soul and try to believe your promise."
  - After: {n}He nods.{/n} "I won't risk my kin. I'll trust you."

  - After: "Then start with your kind, defilers of the Lilaethan."

  - Before: "You've found them. And what do you plan to do with us?"
  - After: "You've found us. Now what?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "This is a gross violation of every sacred covenant of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}. I do not know, {name}, what dictates this... this wilfulness... but I promise you: Janus will face the most serious consequences."

- **Bogul**

- **Bogul**

- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}The tall being in a fine long garment turns to you, their face hidden behind the blank visor of their helmet. When they begin to speak, even from a distance you feel the air around the figure grow cold.{/n} "Mon-keigh. You should not be here."
  - After: {n}A tall, visored, robed being turns; the air chills.{/n} "Mon-keigh. You should not be here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You see Yrliet among the beings clustered around the strange, tall structure. She watches you with complete indifference, the way one watches an insect crawling up a wall.{/n}
  - After: {n}Yrliet watches you indifferently.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet strides forward, her eyes flashing.{/n} "Muaran! I am calling you to account!   - After: {n}Yrliet strides forward.{/n} "Muaran! You blamed the mon-keigh, but Sai'lanthresh, She Who Thirsts, threatens this world — and you hid it! Did you lie to me?"
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}The robed figure inclines their head. And then they begin to speak.{/n} "Yrliet the Outcast. You left the path that was set out for you.   - After: {n}The figure speaks.{/n} "Outcast. You left your path, brought {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g} here, and rage at me. Wandering tainted you."
- **Argenta**

  - After: "At last!" {n}Argenta raises her weapon.{/n} "I am His wrath!"
- **Abelard**

  - After: "'Commander'?" {n}Abelard reddens.{/n} "Calling xenos leader? Disgraceful!"
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "Bring your entourage to heel, Yrliet the Outcast. Their mere presence offends my sensibilities — the least they can do is display the obedience we have impressed upon our mon-keigh servants."
  - After: "Bring your entourage to heel, Outcast."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "My wanderings are the Path I have chosen for myself. Far from the walls of Crudarach, I have seen and come to know things that no other {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} could hidden away in a craftworld their entire life. Why do you deny my words about Sai'lanthresh? Is it because you were lying to me and my kin when you showed us the true Path?"
  - After: "My wanderings taught me what no craftworld {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} knows. Why deny Sai'lanthresh? Did you lie about the Path?"

- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "You are playing with words and avoiding the question!" {n}Notes of desperation — and rage — are creeping into Yrliet's voice now.{/n} "The Lilaethan is under threat from our eternal foe — and yet you're more concerned about the presence of the elantach than the corruption that is flowing through the veins of this world!   - After: "You dodge the question!" {n}Yrliet grows desperate.{/n} "Our eternal foe corrupts this world! Your war may hasten Sai'lanthresh's triumph!"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet stands frozen like a statue, and then suddenly turns to face Muaran.{/n} "The elantach is right. I mistook the wicked intent in your heart for stubbornness and vanity.   - After: {n}Yrliet turns to Muaran.{/n} "The elantach is right. No Farseer would ignore Sai'lanthresh. You serve Her."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet gives you a long, studying look.{/n} "The tale of the Children of Asuryan on the Lilaethan is coming to an end, but somewhere out there, among the cold stars of the cosmos that your kind calls the Expanse, there are others.
