- **Muaran**
  - Before: "Look around you, mon-keigh. Your kind captured a world that did not belong to you. You broke open her heart, crushed her will, disfigured her face, trying to squeeze every drop of life out of the Lilaethan like a ripe fruit. I have seen the paths that lie before us — on each of them, the presence of the mon-keigh heralds the demise of the World Spirit. I will not allow it."
  - After: "Your kind is bleeding the Lilaethan dry. In every future, mon-keigh kill the World Spirit. I won't allow it."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "We came from the sky, just like you. If you want to know where our ships and our kin are, I will not tell you. The ones who brought us here mapped out the limits of this star long ago — in search of other kin lost in the darkness amidst the stars."
  - After: "From the sky, like you. I won't say where our ships are. We seek lost kin."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Accept your release from an unclean existence, and be grateful." {n}Kibellah assumes a stance, ready to begin a dance of blood.{/n}
  - After: "Accept release." {n}Kibellah readies a blood-dance.{/n}
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "Is that so? Is that why your servants have been {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusViolent}slaughtering their own kind{/d}? Is that why your weapons sought to disfigure the Lilaethan from orbit? Your words are nothing but lies and hypocrisy, mon-keigh."
  - After: "Then why do your servants {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusViolent}slaughter their own kind{/d}? Lies, mon-keigh."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "This will affect Janus's tithe assessment. There is less trust in produce from agri-worlds with pest problems."
  - After: "This hurts Janus's tithe. Pest-ridden agri-worlds are trusted less."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Muaran's voice rumbles like a distant storm.{/n} "You dare to accuse me of such a thing? You have lost your mind, Outcast..."
  - After: {n}Muaran rumbles.{/n} "You dare? You've lost your mind, Outcast..."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "A highly ambivalent decision, Rogue Trader. The sole benefit it may yield is facilitating access to xenos cadavers and technology. And rest assured, cadavers will by no means be in short supply on either side, no matter what promises the xenos have made."
  - After: "Ambivalent. The only gain: xenos cadavers and technology — which will be plentiful."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "Tread carefully, Outcast. Do not allow another's words to shake your faith in your chosen fate."
  - After: "Careful, Outcast. Keep faith in your fate."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/AgriworldJungle/RebelsWithoutEldar/RebelWithoutEldar_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "There is no excuse for rebelling against the Imperium's rightful authority. That the xenos manipulated you with such ease shows your weakness of faith and cowardice. The sentence for this crime is death."
  - After: [Attack] "Rebellion is inexcusable. Xenos swayed you through weak faith and cowardice. The sentence is death."
- **Player**
  - Before: "People of Janus, you have suffered enough! The xenos have been taken care of, now it is time to free yourselves from the Chaos-worshipping governor!"
  - After: "People of Janus, the xenos are gone! Now free yourselves from the Chaos-worshipping governor!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "By assisting me, you have earned your pardon... Go back to your homes, and I will forget I ever saw you here. Your uprising against the rightful authority on this world is over."
  - After: "You've earned a pardon. Go home and I'll forget you were here. Your uprising is over."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "Now it's going to be even easier to kill you all!"
  - After: [Attack] "Now killing you is even easier!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The surviving rebels are panting heavily, catching their breath after the battle. One by one, they look at you expectantly.{/n}
  - After: {n}The panting rebels look to you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The tricked rebels exchange a glance — and charge into battle with furious cries!{/n}
  - After: {n}The rebels charge, screaming!{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Well... what now? What are you going to do with these... these gullible idiots, Lord Captain?"
  - After: "What now, Lord Captain? These gullible idiots?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Jubilant cries shake the forest. The survivors shout out your name, praising the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} and gabbling promises of eternal loyalty. It seems that with the removal of the Aeldari, an unseen weight has been lifted from their shoulders.{/n}
  - After: {n}Freed of the Aeldari, the survivors cheer the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The tricked rebels raise their weapons and launch into a desperate attack.{/n}
  - After: {n}The rebels attack desperately.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The tricked rebels exchange glances, clearly not fully comprehending what exactly just happened. In the end, exhaustion and confusion do their work: slowly, with an odd glance over the shoulder, they all walk away from the battlefield, leaving behind the camp and the ravaged bodies of their erstwhile allies.{/n}
  - After: {n}Confused, the rebels slowly leave.{/n}
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "They have let themselves be turned into a weapon in the hands of xenos." {n}Kibellah enunciates every word as if announcing a verdict.{/n} "Their lack of spirit has opened the way for His enemies. Thus, they are poisoned — both by their own weakness and by inhuman sorcery."
  - After: "A xenos weapon." {n}Kibellah pronounces judgement.{/n} "Poisoned by weakness and sorcery."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/AgriworldJungle/YrlietAftermathDialogue/YrlietAftermathDialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You lot are still studying this gate, I take it..."
  - After: "Still studying this gate?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Where's your brother Muaran?"
  - After: "Where's Muaran?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How are things on Janus?"
  - After: "How is Janus?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I must take my leave."
  - After: "I must go."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What will happen if you succeed in opening it?"
  - After: "What if you open it?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What exactly are you doing to the gate?"
  - After: "What are you doing to it?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Have you ever been to the Webway? What does it look like?"
  - After: "What's the Webway like?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "If your offer of mutual cooperation still stands, I would like to have you in my entourage."
  - After: "If the offer stands, join me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet looks down at you from above. Her hands are resting on her weapon, and yet she appears completely relaxed.{/n} "You have returned, elantach."{g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}{/g}
  - After: {n}Yrliet looks down, relaxed.{/n} "You've returned, elantach."{g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}{/g}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I greet you, elantach. What brings you to our sanctuary?"
  - After: "Greetings, elantach. Why are you here?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Upon my return, he found it in himself to believe that I was capable of taking care of myself without him watching over me, so he chose to look after those of us who had not yet earned such a high degree of trust." {n}Yrliet's voice is almost impassive, but a half-smile plays at the corners of her mouth.{/n}
  - After: "He trusts me now, so he watches others." {n}She half-smiles.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The former rebels have returned to their homes. We continue to eradicate Sai'lanthresh's corruption that seeped into the Lilaethan's veins... but now the planet is at peace, and the World Spirit is safe from all harm."
  - After: "The rebels went home. We purge Sai'lanthresh's taint; the World Spirit is safe."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Our duty is keeping us on the Lilaethan, but I doubt that all my kin will remain on the Maiden World. Only those who are essential to guarding this planet against the machinations of Sai'lanthresh."
  - After: "Only those needed to guard against Sai'lanthresh will stay."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My kin labouring over the gate are better versed in the art of wraithbone creations... but even they cannot fathom every detail designed by the Worldsinger — the sacred keeper of the Lilaethan, who shared a rare bond with the World Spirit. Their spirit now rests among their kin — whilst we, blind in our insight, blunder into the intricate tangle of the gate, stumped by the mystery of its silence."
  - After: "Even our wraithbone experts can't fathom the late Worldsinger's design. The gate stays silent."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Imagine myriads of trails, intertwined by the will of the finest creators this universe has ever known... The Webway was created in a time of legend, back when the galaxy belonged to beings far more powerful than you or I."
  - After: "Myriad trails, woven by mighty creators in a legendary age."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The {g|Encyclopedia:Webway}Webway{/g} Gate is one of the surviving relics of the old world that was forever lost to us. Crudarach had its own gate, but it worked... differently. Not like the creations of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} who brought the Lilaethan into being."
  - After: "The {g|Encyclopedia:Webway}Webway{/g} Gate is a relic of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} who made the Lilaethan. Crudarach's worked differently."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We will leave this world. Was this not your wish when you refused my kin the right to be the guardians of the Lilaethan?"
  - After: "We'll leave. Wasn't that your wish?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Webway runs throughout the entire cosmos — by stepping through a gate on one planet, one can traverse millions of light years in but a few hours and emerge on the other side of the universe. My people have long used the Webway to travel between surviving worlds — both planets and crafts."
  - After: "It spans the cosmos — millions of light years in hours. We travel it between surviving worlds."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Sai'lanthresh's corruption is slowly being purged from the face of the Maiden World. The Lilaethan will never regain her former purity... but now the World Spirit has a faithful guardian."
  - After: "The taint fades. The Lilaethan won't be pure again, but has a guardian."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/AgriworldJungle/YrlietBetrayed

- **Player**
  - Before: "No one forced your kin to go against me and die. Their stones are my trophies now. I earned them."
  - After: "Your kin chose to fight me. Their stones are my earned trophies."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You may take the stones — I have no use for them."
  - After: "Take the stones. I've no use for them."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It seems these stones are extremely valuable... I think I'll keep them."
  - After: "These stones seem valuable. I'll keep them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Before we leave this place..." {n}Yrliet's voice trembles.{/n} "Allow me to search the bodies of the fallen, elantach. I wish to collect their spirit stones — the vessels that protect us from Sai'lanthresh's maw after our physical death. Muaran's foresight led these warriors against us — foresight that can be corrupted by ill intentions they were unaware of. Their souls are locked within these stones — don't let them perish here."
  - After: {n}Yrliet's voice trembles.{/n} "Elantach, let me gather the fallen's spirit stones, their shield from Sai'lanthresh. Don't let their souls perish."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your soul is full of wasted rage — and hunger for others' suffering. Perhaps Sai'lanthresh has already laid her touch upon you too."
  - After: "Your soul hungers for suffering. Perhaps Sai'lanthresh touched you too."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you, elantach. I will take care of my kin."
  - After: "Thank you, elantach. I will care for my kin."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "How can a mon-keigh know the value of another's soul? Foul, savage species..."
  - After: "What does a savage mon-keigh know of souls?"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I have come across references to xeno-artefacts of this type in archives. If Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship allows, I will examine these... trophies." {n}A velvety, curious voice pours from the vox-synth, not interrupted by a single hiss of static.{/n}
  - After: "With Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship's leave, I'll examine these xeno-artefacts." {n}His vox sounds curious.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/AgriworldJungle/YrlietBetrayed/YrlietBetrayed_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Enough talking — just lead me to wherever you were going."
  - After: "Enough talk. Lead on."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If Vistenza is to blame, then why haven't you gone to the palace and killed her already?"
  - After: "If Vistenza's guilty, why not kill her?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Calm down. It's already over."
  - After: "Calm down. It's over."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I don't know who you're talking about, but I promise I'll gladly help you pour the 'cup of suffering' down their throat."
  - After: "Whoever it is, I'll gladly help pour the 'cup of suffering' down their throat."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Get a grip. I doubt that will be the last battle we see today, and I need allies with all their wits about them."
  - After: "Get a grip. More battles are coming; I need clear-headed allies."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Well, well, who knew a tempest was raging beneath that unruffled surface!"
  - After: "Well, a tempest beneath that calm surface!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "If we want to meet with the leaders of the uprising, we better keep moving."
  - After: "To meet the uprising's leaders, keep moving."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Isn't it time you told me what's going on here?"
  - After: "Time you told me what's going on."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Who is Muaran? What treachery are you talking about?"
  - After: "Who is Muaran? What treachery?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why did your own kind attack you?"
  - After: "Why did your kind attack you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I trust your judgement, Yrliet. Vistenza will be punished for her betrayal."
  - After: "I trust you, Yrliet. Vistenza will be punished."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why would a handful of xenos go to war against a whole planet? You can't kill everyone!"
  - After: "A few xenos against a whole planet? You can't kill everyone!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I don't believe that Vistenza is guilty. You may not like mon-keigh, but we do not serve the Archenemy."
  - After: "Vistenza isn't guilty. We don't serve the Archenemy."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You came to Janus along with the rest of the Aeldari?"
  - After: "You came to Janus with the other Aeldari?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How are your kin connected to the uprising on the planet?"
  - After: "How are your kin tied to the uprising?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why are you telling me all this? What's brought on this candour?"
  - After: "Why tell me all this now?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Maybe Vistenza is tainted from consorting with the Archenemy. We will have to find out for ourselves."
  - After: "Maybe Vistenza is tainted. We'll find out ourselves."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Make another accusation against a servant of the Imperium and I will have you stuffed and put on display in my stateroom."
  - After: "Accuse an Imperial servant again and I'll have you stuffed for my stateroom."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet's usually dispassionate face is contorted in a grimace of pain and rage. Your {g|Encyclopedia:Elucidator}Elucidator{/g} activates when she begins speaking in her own language.{/n} "I swear on Khaine's riven heart, Muaran, you will pay for your treachery! May Morai-Heg sunder your fate and cast it away, may the blood of Eldanesh flood your throat—"
  - After: {n}Yrliet seethes. Your {g|Encyclopedia:Elucidator}Elucidator{/g} translates.{/n} "By Khaine's heart, Muaran, you will pay! May Morai-Heg sunder your fate, may Eldanesh's blood flood your throat—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet closes her eyes, sucks in a breath through her teeth, and quickly murmurs something. When she opens her eyes, her face is once again a mask of cool serenity. She looks at you and begins to speak, this time in Low Gothic.{/n}
  - After: {n}Yrliet murmurs, calm again, and speaks Low Gothic.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The signs that have been revealed to me — they all indicate the presence of corruption on this world. Tendrils of corruption may be threading through the World Spirit, poisoning it even as we speak. But for corruption to take hold of the planet so quickly requires effort — effort directed by the will of another." {n}Yrliet pauses.{/n} "I believe Vistenza Vyatt is in thrall to the will of Sai'lanthresh."
  - After: "The signs show corruption spreading fast, guided by a will." {n}She pauses.{/n} "Vistenza Vyatt serves Sai'lanthresh."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "After the calamity, the Lilaethan offered my kin a sanctuary — a place of respite in the ruins of our ancestors, under the canopy of the forests created by the wisdom of our Worldsingers... living alongside your kind, who reap the fruits of our labour with such vulgarity."
  - After: "After the calamity, the Lilaethan sheltered my kin in our ancestors' ruins... beside your vulgar kind."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Some evil transcends loyalty to one's own kind. What will become of the Lilaethan if you allow the enemy of all creation to live among your subjects? How long with this mutilated world remain loyal to your {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g} before she becomes a chasm bringing forth servants of Sai'lanthresh?"
  - After: "Some evil transcends kinship. Harbour it, and this world will leave your {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g} for Sai'lanthresh."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Please excuse me, elantach — I allowed the turmoil in my soul to win out over my reason. A slip like that could cost me more than you can even imagine — my very soul. I must be more careful... even in the face of treachery."
  - After: "Forgive me, elantach. Such a slip could cost my soul."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Over? Oh no, {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}, this path is far from its end!" {n}Yrliet is almost shouting, her voice ringing with fury.{/n} "But when we get to Muaran, I will make him reveal the full extent of his duplicity and tell me where the truth ends and the lies begin!"
  - After: "Over? No, {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}!" {n}Yrliet nearly shouts.{/n} "Muaran will confess all his lies!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The only punishment for such a crime is death, elantach. The one who steps onto the path of Sai'lanthresh forfeits the light forever."
  - After: "The punishment is death, elantach."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There is only one crime graver than serving Sai'lanthresh — it is betraying the Children of Asuryan for her benefit. Muaran saw the paths, he beheld the future... how could he not see the dark stain on its face? How could he fail to do everything in his power to rid the Lilaethan of this canker?" {n}Yrliet's voice grows angrier, more piercing.{/n} "Before I rip this poisoned seed from the Lilaethan's body, I will make Muaran answer me!"
  - After: "Worse is betraying the Children of Asuryan for Sai'lanthresh. Muaran saw the future — how did he miss this?" {n}Her voice sharpens.{/n} "He will answer me!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The mon-keigh are weak in spirit — they are susceptible to the propositions of She Who Thirsts, and in their drive to attain her poisoned gifts, they perform perverse rituals in her name... rituals that require sacrifices. Like the mon-keigh who were brought to the palace and never seen again."
  - After: "Weak mon-keigh court She Who Thirsts with sacrifices. Like those taken to the palace, never seen again."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Muaran is the one responsible for the rebellions against the ruler of Janus... but allow me to tell you everything from the beginning."
  - After: "Muaran leads the rebellions against Janus's ruler... let me start at the beginning."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My kin became military advisors to the mon-keigh who rose up against the ruler of this world. I had a different mission: to become Vistenza's handler, since the rebels would be unable to get to her until both sides were sufficiently weakened. The ruler of the humans had never seen a Child of Asuryan before, and so she accepted the lie about a degenerate branch of mon-keigh dwelling far from their own kind."
  - After: "My kin advised the rebels. I was Vistenza's handler; she thought me a degenerate mon-keigh."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No. My path brought me to the Lilaethan later..." {n}Yrliet hesitates.{/n} "...by another route."
  - After: "No. I came later..." {n}Yrliet hesitates.{/n} "...by another route."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It was Muaran who welcomed me here — he was one of the surviving Farseers of Crudarach. He was with a handful of {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Asuryani{/g} who had escaped death and found the path here, to the destroyed cradle of our kind. They were outraged when they saw how the mon-keigh had ravaged our flourishing garden!"
  - After: "Muaran, a surviving Farseer of Crudarach, welcomed me. His few {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Asuryani{/g} raged at how mon-keigh ravaged this world!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I know not the answer to that question." {n}Yrliet lowers her head.{/n} "Many cycles have passed since I departed these forests and my kin. They cannot... they cannot have forgotten me, can they?"
  - After: "I do not know." {n}She lowers her head.{/n} "Have they forgotten me?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You struggle to understand the Children of Asuryan, and I do not blame you for that — we are too different." {n}Yrliet says nothing for a few moments, choosing her words.{/n} "Mon-keigh walk blindly into the future. We choose the path, guided by our Farseers. Crudarach was the birthplace of the powerful watchers of things to come — our leaders were selected from among their ranks, and their word was set in stone, unshakeable like the universe itself."
  - After: {n}Yrliet pauses.{/n} "Mon-keigh walk blindly. Crudarach's Farseers chose our path, their word unshakeable."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Muaran, our leader here, is one of that group. The Children of Asuryan are subject to his will, and he is subject to the will of his visions. Muaran saw the Lilaethan in a vision, suffering and crying out to be cleansed, and we did everything we could to rid the Maiden World of the mon-keigh. Our lives, our desires — all that is dust compared to the light of the path Muaran has chosen for us. At least, that is what my kin believe. I used to believe it too... until recently."
  - After: "Muaran, our leader, saw the Lilaethan crying to be cleansed, so we fought to purge the mon-keigh. So my kin believe. I did too... until recently."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Lilaethan's World Spirit senses the threat — and resists as much as it is able. The living things that inhabit this world are becoming its weapons — weapons turned against the mon-keigh. Poisonous plants, rabid beasts — these are all like a blade in the Lilaethan's hand as she fights the coming of Sai'lanthresh."
  - After: "The Lilaethan resists. Poisonous plants, rabid beasts — her blades against the mon-keigh and Sai'lanthresh."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Sai'lanthresh is deceitful and cunning... She subtly penetrates the soul, offering false perfection, luring victims into her web with promises of a wicked ideal. The ruler of the mon-keigh perhaps does not even know that her soul has been corrupted."
  - After: "Sai'lanthresh lures with false perfection. The ruler may not know she is corrupted."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Asuryani{/g} do not enter battles they cannot win. However, it is in our power to direct the currents so that the elements themselves wash obstacles and enemies from our path. And so it was in this case — Muaran, the Farseer from Crudarach, saw a future without the {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}, and we followed his lead. We simply used the mon-keigh's passions against them. Their love of freedom and anarchy. Their love of domination and violence. Stoking enmity between servants and rulers is easier when your targets are governed by emotion rather than reason."
  - After: "The {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Asuryani{/g} steer currents rather than fight. Muaran, Farseer of Crudarach, saw a future without {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}, so we turned servants against rulers."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Perhaps the signs I uncovered have failed to convince you. I pray to the gods that other proof — something more comprehensible to you — will emerge to sway your opinion."
  - After: "I pray clearer proof convinces you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Who gave you the authority to vouch for every soul of your kind? There are those among you who are weak or perverted by passion — it is those mon-keigh Sai'lanthresh chooses to serve her."
  - After: "You cannot vouch for all your kind. Sai'lanthresh chooses your weak."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}His green visor flashing with interest, Pasqal carefully clarifies:{/n} "Which border exactly?"
  - After: {n}Pasqal's visor flashes.{/n} "Which border exactly?"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}An angry {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} crackle interrupts Jae. However, Pasqal confines himself to this threatening gesture, obviously not wanting to bicker in front of the Aeldari about who has the right to plunder the world of her kin.{/n}
  - After: {n}A {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} crackle cuts Jae off; Pasqal won't argue plunder now.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We call ourselves the {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Children of Asuryan{/g}. {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} is another name of ours. We are the echoes of the great empire that once ruled the galaxy and created new worlds. The planet that you call Janus is one such Maiden World, the Lilaethan. A haven that our ancestors made for their kin. For many millennia, only the shadows of our predecessors lived among the ruins... until you humans came here."
  - After: "We are the {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Children of Asuryan{/g}, or {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g}, heirs of a world-making empire. Janus is our Maiden World, the Lilaethan, empty... until humans came."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You don't need to know that, iron mon-keigh. I am aware of your looting practices."
  - After: "Not your concern, iron mon-keigh, looter."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}"Sai'lanthresh" and "She Who Thirsts" are the names the Aeldari give to the Chaos God Slaanesh, their ultimate enemy. Slaanesh is the god of passion, excess, and forbidden pleasures, and is known for his fickle and treacherous nature.{/n}
  - After: {n}"Sai'lanthresh" and "She Who Thirsts" are Aeldari names for Slaanesh, Chaos God of excess.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You have never heard of this entity before. It must be another Aeldari term for one of the beings from the pantheon of the Ruinous Powers known to Humanity.{/n}
  - After: {n}Likely an Aeldari name for a Ruinous Power.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "As lamentable as it may be, the Imperium's history knows many cases where even the most steadfast followers of the Creed would turn away from His light. Governor Vyatt had to tap into many founts of knowledge to turn Janus into a prosperous agri-world. Perhaps... one of those founts became her undoing."
  - After: "Even the faithful fall. Governor Vyatt drew on many founts of knowledge. Perhaps one undid her."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Ah, xenos... Such wonderful creatures, shereen! Just before we came, Pointy Ears spent her days serving the governor, but the moment the wind changed, she started regaling us with tragic tales about her people's dismal fate and the world's plights... and we humans are to blame for everything, naturally!" {n}Jae clicks her tongue and glances at Yrliet with suspicion.{/n} "Although there is a grain of sense to her words, I will give her that."
  - After: "Pointy Ears served the governor till the wind changed, shereen. Now humans are to blame!" {n}Jae eyes Yrliet.{/n} "She has a point, though."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Give just about any planetary governor a hard-enough shake, and a whole slew of heresies will come pouring out, so we are not as shocked as you might think, xenos. Regardless, if Vyatt is guilty of anything, she will not be judged based on your word."
  - After: "Shake any governor and heresy spills out. But Vyatt won't be judged on your word, xenos."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We are the heirs, and we are entirely within our rights to call the Maiden World our own. However, our arrival is a tragedy, not a homecoming." {n}Sorrow seeps into Yrliet's voice.{/n} "We belong... belonged to {g|Encyclopedia:Craftworld}Craftworld{/g} Crudarach, which fell on the border of this star region. Only the providence of the merciful gods allowed us to escape the fate that befell those whose souls perished amidst the stardust along with our abode."
  - After: "This world is ours by right, but we came in tragedy." {n}She sounds sorrowful.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:Craftworld}Craftworld{/g} Crudarach fell on this region's border. Only the gods spared us."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet hesitates for a moment, as though preparing to say something, before finally turning away.{/n}
  - After: {n}Yrliet hesitates, then turns away.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Destroying an Aeldari craftworld is a serious achievement. I'd like to shake the hand of whoever did it."
  - After: "Whoever destroyed a craftworld, I'd shake their hand."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "A destroyed craftw—" {n}Jae breaks off, and then hurriedly whispers to you,{/n} "Hey, {name}... If we get a chance, we should check this place out. Even if the craftworld was blasted to bits, anyone who finds a piece of it will make a fortune."
  - After: "A destroyed craftw—" {n}Jae whispers,{/n} "{name}, craftworld pieces are worth a fortune."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Disfigurements — it seems you call these 'mutations' — are the surest sign of this threat. By mutilating living forms, this malevolent power subjugates them and bends them to its will. You have seen the deformities in the faces of those who are closer to the Lilaethan's body than others — the rebels who hide under the canopy of these forests."
  - After: "Mutations are the surest sign. You've seen them on the forest rebels."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "What? Vistenza Vyatt? The governor who has duly served the dynasty and the Imperium for decades? {name}, I hope you will not stand for such scurrilous slander aimed at one of your finest servants!"
  - After: "Vistenza Vyatt? After decades of loyalty? {name}, don't stand for this slander!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Elantach, your arrival has thrown my paths into disarray — and lifted the veil on the truth that had been hidden from me. The threat should be familiar to you, as it is to other intelligent species in the galaxy. We call it Sai'lanthresh. She Who Thirsts. Goddess of Chaos."
  - After: "Elantach, you revealed another threat to the Lilaethan: Sai'lanthresh. She Who Thirsts. Goddess of Chaos."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/AgriworldJungle/YrlietKilledBrethren

- **Player**
  - Before: "No one forced your kin to go against me and die. Their stones are my trophies now. I earned them."
  - After: "Your kin chose to fight me. Their stones are my earned trophies."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It seems these stones are extremely valuable... I think I'll keep them."
  - After: "These stones seem valuable. I'll keep them."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You may take the stones — I have no use for them."
  - After: "Take the stones. I've no use for them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you, elantach. I will take care of my kin."
  - After: "Thank you, elantach. I will care for my kin."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "How can a mon-keigh know the value of another's soul? Foul, savage species..."
  - After: "What does a savage mon-keigh know of souls?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Before we leave this place..." {n}Yrliet's voice trembles.{/n} "Allow me to search the bodies of the fallen, elantach. I wish to collect their spirit stones — the vessels that protect us from Sai'lanthresh's maw after our physical death. Muaran's foresight led these warriors against us — foresight that can be corrupted by ill intentions they were unaware of. Their souls are locked within these stones — don't let them perish here."
  - After: {n}Yrliet's voice trembles.{/n} "Elantach, let me gather the fallen's spirit stones, their shield from Sai'lanthresh. Don't let their souls perish."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I have come across references to xeno-artefacts of this type in archives. If Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship allows, I will examine these... trophies." {n}A velvety, curious voice pours from the vox-synth, not interrupted by a single hiss of static.{/n}
  - After: "With Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship's leave, I'll examine these xeno-artefacts." {n}His vox sounds curious.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your soul is full of wasted rage — and hunger for others' suffering. Perhaps Sai'lanthresh has already laid her touch upon you too."
  - After: "Your soul hungers for suffering. Perhaps Sai'lanthresh touched you too."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/AgriworldJungle/YrlietKilledBrethren/YrlietKilledBrethren

- **Player**
  - Before: "You dispatched the enemies of Humanity admirably. You'll make an excellent sanctioned xenos."
  - After: "You killed Humanity's enemies well. A fine sanctioned xenos."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You just slaughtered your kin over a minor disagreement. You're in no place to talk about pride."
  - After: "You slaughtered your kin over a quarrel. Don't talk about pride."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Kill Yrliet] "Might as well send you off along with the rest."
  - After: [Kill Yrliet] "You can join the rest."
- **Player**
  - Before: "There is nothing more to be done here. Time to return to the shuttle."
  - After: "Nothing more here. Back to the shuttle."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Get out of my sight. I have no need for the company of a traitor."
  - After: "Get out of my sight, traitor."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet surveys the field of battle.{/n} "May the gods guard us against pride and wandering in the vagaries of fate..."
  - After: {n}Yrliet surveys the battlefield.{/n} "May the gods guard us against pride..."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet rewards you with a contemptuous look.{/n} "Muaran was right about one thing: your primitive consciousness prevents you from seeing anything that does not lie on the surface. My actions were not done out of a desire to gratify you."
  - After: {n}Yrliet sneers.{/n} "You see only surfaces. I did not act to please you."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "My kin have trusted in the visions of Farseers for millennia to show us our path amidst the stars. But throughout my life on Crudarach, I have too often seen knowledge of things to come — as changeable and capricious as deepwater currents — weave chains around the bodies of those who fear to enter murky waters. That is why I became an Outcast, renouncing the traditions of Crudarach and leaving its confines — to seek out my own Path."
  - After: "On Crudarach, I saw Farseers' visions chain the fearful. So I became an Outcast, seeking my own Path."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Your consciousness is incapable of grasping the full depth of the abyss into which Muaran lured my kin, and that is why my actions seem monstrous to you. Far from it — at least now their souls will not end up in Sai'lanthresh's maw."
  - After: "You cannot grasp Muaran's abyss. Now their souls escape Sai'lanthresh."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "All right? I am overcome with grief, and anger, and anguish. But if I give free rein to my emotions, I will be drawing the thirst of She who has already entangled the Lilaethan, and, it seems, befuddled the mind of the one who was called to lead my kin."
  - After: "I grieve and rage. But indulging that draws She who ensnared the Lilaethan, and Muaran."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Perhaps Crudarach's demise filled Muaran with so much sorrow that it poisoned his mind. Or perhaps it was hatred for the mon-keigh who desecrated the face of the Lilaethan that plunged his mind into darkness. Or perhaps... perhaps Sai'lanthresh herself was toying with the Farseer who had found himself amidst her poisoned gardens." {n}Yrliet begins speaking more quietly, though harshness breaks through in her voice at times.{/n} "I will never learn the answer to this question... but perhaps if I uncover the secret of Crudarach's demise, I might be able to lift the veil even a little on this mystery."
  - After: "Grief, hatred, or Sai'lanthresh darkened Muaran's mind." {n}Yrliet's voice hardens.{/n} "Learning how Crudarach fell may tell me more."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet drops to the ground like a severed vine.{/n}
  - After: {n}Yrliet drops like a severed vine.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet looks at you, tilting her head slightly.{/n} "Do not forget that the Lilaethan still needs help. Vistenza Vyatt must be slain so that the Maiden World can live."
  - After: {n}Yrliet tilts her head.{/n} "Vistenza Vyatt must die so the Lilaethan can live."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet flinches as though your words have wrenched her back to reality.{/n} "Very well. Then, farewell, elantach. May the stars guide each of us on our Path."
  - After: {n}Yrliet flinches.{/n} "Farewell, elantach. Stars guide our Paths."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Should you grow tired of this xenos, Domin, I could take her thin bones to the temple of the Bloodspun Web. They will serve as dust beneath the feet of the righteous."
  - After: "Tire of this xenos, Domin, and her bones can be dust at the Bloodspun Web's temple."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/AgriworldPalace/Governor_Dialogue/Governor_dialogue

  - Before: "Who is behind the assassination?"
  - After: "Who's behind the assassination?"

- **Player**
  - Before: "I'd like to get back to talking about foodstuff supplies from Janus."
  - After: "Back to food supplies from Janus."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Well, I'll track down these elusive fugitives myself. As for you, Vistenza, you will not be permitted to fail again. I am removing you from your post as governor of this planet and I am placing you under arrest. When I have finished with the rebels, I'll decide what to do with you."
  - After: "I'll hunt the fugitives myself. You're removed as governor and under arrest, Vistenza. I'll decide your fate later."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I've already heard enough, Vistenza. But if you wish me to repeat myself — we know that your loyalty lies with the Ruinous Powers."
  - After: "I've heard enough. We know your loyalty lies with the Ruinous Powers."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are not saving Janus or improving it, Vistenza. You are destroying this world with your own hands."
  - After: "You're not saving Janus, Vistenza. You're destroying it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I won't be able to change your mind, will I? Then I won't try."
  - After: "I can't change your mind, can I? Then I won't try."
- **Player**
  - Before: "This world possesses a soul. A soul that your 'patron' is trying to destroy, and without which Janus will become barren."

  - After: "Another xenos came before Yrliet. Your retinue hid him from you to sacrifice him."
- **Player**

  - Before: "You neglected to mention the strange changes in the planet's flora and fauna."
  - After: "You didn't mention the strange changes in flora and fauna."
- **Player**
  - Before: "How much more proof do you need, Vistenza? That's enough! Renounce that vile sorcery while there is still hope!"

  - Before: "I must take my leave."

- **Player**
  - Before: "Let's move on to business now."

  - Before: "You dare to lie to me, Vistenza?"

  - Before: "What is the situation on the planet?"

  - After: "I've heard rumours of oddities among Janus's people..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are forgiven. You may return to your duties."
  - After: "You're forgiven. Return to your duties."

  - Before: "Death, my dear. Did you really think there could be any other outcome?"

- **Player**
  - Before: "Let's not waste time on meaningless chatter, Vistenza. You are a servant of the Archenemy."

  - Before: "Even for an agri-world in the back of beyond, this place is a real dump. What do you all do here for fun — when you have free time, that is?"

  - Before: "Everything, Vistenza. I know everything. And now you have one chance to beg for mercy."
  - After: "I know everything, Vistenza. You have one chance to beg for mercy."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Then again... let's just leave things as they are."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/AgriworldPalace/SecretaryAfterKillingGovernor/SecretaryAfterKillingGovernor_Dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Vistenza Vyatt has tragically perished at the hands of perfidious traitors to the Imperium who infiltrated her inner circle. She must be avenged — hunt down and execute the conspirators."
  - After: "Traitors in her circle killed Vistenza Vyatt. Hunt down and execute them."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Lie] "Vistenza Vyatt has tragically perished at the hands of perfidious traitors to the Imperium who infiltrated her inner circle. She must be avenged — hunt down and execute the conspirators."
  - After: [Lie] "Traitors in her circle killed Vistenza Vyatt. Hunt down and execute them."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Vistenza Vyatt has been executed as a traitor to the Imperium. Her accomplices must be found and put to death immediately."
  - After: "Vistenza Vyatt was executed as a traitor. Find her accomplices and kill them."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Don't ask questions — the answers are no concern of yours. You will receive all future instructions from my authorised representatives."
  - After: "No questions. My representatives will instruct you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Out of the way! I don't have time for you!"
  - After: "Out of the way! No time for you!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Janus was under two distinct threats: the corruption of Chaos in the form of Vistenza Vyatt and her associates, and the xenos who had manipulated the servants of the Imperium. I dealt with both of them."
  - After: "Janus faced Chaos in Vistenza Vyatt and her circle, and xenos manipulating the Imperium. I dealt with both."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The secretary is shaking in terror, looking around at the devastation.{/n} "Y-Y-Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! What happened? Where is Lady Vyatt?"
  - After: {n}He trembles.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Where's Lady Vyatt?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Heresy? Xenos?" {n}The secretary makes a protective gesture in the air.{/n} "God-Emperor preserve us! Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you have surely saved us from our doom! We will immediately begin scouring the planet to root out any remaining conspirators and traitors!"
  - After: "Heresy? Xenos?" {n}He signs.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you saved us!"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}The secretary stares at Yrliet in horror. His face twists, but he cannot seem to get out a single word.{/n}
  - After: {n}He stares at Yrliet, speechless.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh no! Heresy! Heresy on Janus!" {n}The secretary makes a protective gesture over himself.{/n} "May the God-Emperor watch over us! Whatever... whatever the governor did, I had no knowledge of it! We will root out those who colluded with her right away!"
  - After: "Heresy!" {n}He signs.{/n} "I knew nothing! We'll root out her accomplices!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The secretary pauses, then bends into a deep bow.{/n} "Of course, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: {n}He bows deeply.{/n} "Of course, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The secretary begins to speak, but thinks better of it, instead choosing to step aside and bow his head as you pass.{/n}
  - After: {n}He bows and steps aside.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The governor... killed by heretics?" {n}The secretary makes a protective sign over himself.{/n} "God-Emperor protect us! We'll soon root out those responsible!"
  - After: "Heretics?" {n}He signs.{/n} "We'll find them!"

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/AgriworldPalace/YrlietAfterKillingGovernor/YrlietAfterKillingGovernor_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I hope that's the last I'll hear about cultists on Janus."
  - After: "I hope that's the end of Janus's cultists."
- **Player**
  - Before: "So, the heretic is dead. Now what?"
  - After: "The heretic is dead. Now what?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Are you trying to say that it's open season on humans for Aeldari now?"
  - After: "So Aeldari may hunt humans freely now?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will most likely return to Janus in the future. I must keep an eye on my worlds."
  - After: "I'll likely return to Janus to watch my worlds."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am leaving Janus. And I hope never to see you or your brethren ever again."
  - After: "I'm leaving Janus, and hope never to see your kind again."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet lowers her weapon, but her shoulders remain tense. She finally catches her breath, shaking her hair out of her face in a fluid motion, and looks at you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Yrliet lowers her weapon, looking at you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are hoping in vain. The seeds these spawn leave behind may sprout in a hundred years — in other people and other deeds. I pray that I am wrong."
  - After: "Vain hope. Their seeds may sprout in a century."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Only if you consider the servants of She Who Thirsts to be human... I hope not. The only thing those abominations deserve is death and burning."
  - After: "Servants of She Who Thirsts deserve only fire."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Yeah, yeah, tracking down your kin... and also, there'll be somebody on the ship who scares the crap out of everyone even more than I do."
  - After: "Sure, kin... and someone scarier than me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet's lips twist into a bitter smile.{/n} "I think that would be best. For you, mon-keigh. Farewell."
  - After: {n}A bitter smile.{/n} "Best for you, mon-keigh. Farewell."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "It is not your place to deem anyone in the Domin's retinue unworthy, Vil'Jae." {n}Kibellah turns to you and bows her head slightly.{/n} "Your decisions are inscrutable, Domin, but nevertheless, your shadow will keep a vigilant eye on the unclean xenos from now on."
  - After: "Not your place, Vil'Jae." {n}Kibellah bows.{/n} "I'll watch the xenos, Domin."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I doubt xenos are capable of eliminating heresy on the planet, {name}. But in a situation with limited resources... Throne preserve me if I ever repeat this sentiment, but... the Aeldari's assistance is the best we can hope for in the short term. Barring a radical solution to the problem."
  - After: "Xenos can't purge heresy, {name}. Throne help me, her aid is our best hope."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "The Warrant does permit taking xenos servants, but I had hoped never to witness anyone actually invoke this... unique right."
  - After: "The Warrant permits xenos servants. I'd hoped never to see it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You have done your duty, elantach. From now on, the Lilaethan has hope for the future — a future without Sai'lanthresh and her followers. This world has yet to be cleansed, but there is a time for everything. Now is the time to thank you." {n}Yrliet bows her head slightly.{/n}
  - After: "Duty done, elantach. The Lilaethan has hope beyond Sai'lanthresh. Thank you." {n}She bows.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Oh, shereen... I pray to the Exalted One that your good heart is not broken by the black ungratefulness of those you welcome into your retinue. My only consolation is that this xenos is still a little different from the damned scum that plague Humanity in the Koronus Expanse."
  - After: "Oh, shereen... at least this xenos isn't Expanse scum."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There's no doubt that our visit has... stirred up the inhabitants of this place. But it is unlikely that their devotion to She Who Thirsts will outweigh their fear of your authority — whatever it is based on in your society. You have nothing to fear."
  - After: "We stirred them, but they fear you more than She Who Thirsts."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Xenos in the retinue of a Rogue Trader is an acceptable precedent. Although highly undesirable and fraught with danger."
  - After: "A xenos retainer has precedent. Dangerous, though."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If you truly cared for the elantach, you wouldn't be following {mf|him|her}, you would have thrown yourself into the abyss long ago. You are a canker, and the jaws of Sai'lanthresh yawn wide within you. Don't talk to me about dangers, you, a mon-keigh who has no notion of what he is playing with!"
  - After: "If you cared for the elantach, you'd leave {mf|him|her}. Sai'lanthresh gapes in you, canker. Don't lecture me, mon-keigh!"

  - Before: "If things continue in this vein, I dare not even imagine what it could lead to! There are worlds that are ravaged by war for generations... generations, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!
