  - After: "Oh yes! Taken from {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g} in the Rifts of Hecaton. They nearly had my throat!" {n}He beams.{/n}
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "Well then, since you have turned out to be a pleasant surprise and stopped Incendia from snatching my possession, I should reward you. Take this grim weapon — it performed superbly in battles against xenos, and it helped me acquire the more substantial gift I have brought."
  - After: "You kept Incendia off my property, so take this grim xenos-killing weapon."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "Kill someone important with it. That would be the best show of gratitude."
  - After: "Kill someone important with it."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "Well, I, for one, liked Theodora. The stories they told of her travels to nameless stars! And — yes, there was no fear in her." {n}Winterscale sighs pensively, and his lively expression grows a little greyer.{/n}
  - After: "I liked Theodora. She feared nothing." {n}Winterscale sighs.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Undaunted, Winterscale chuckles.{/n} "Perhaps we will see for ourselves one day. It has been a long time since {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Traders{/g} last waged war in the Koronus Expanse."
  - After: {n}Winterscale chuckles.{/n} "Perhaps we'll see. {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Traders{/g} are overdue a war."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "The funny thing is, people still call me the foul-tempered tyrant in all this." {n}Calligos's amiable smile somehow resembles the bared teeth of a wild animal.{/n}
  - After: "And they call me the tyrant." {n}Calligos bares his teeth.{/n}
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "Thwarting Incendia Chorda's ambitions deserves a worthy trophy." {n}He snaps his fingers, and the armoured brute hands you an exotically adorned rifle, clearly not of human making.{/n}
  - After: "A trophy for thwarting Incendia." {n}Worten hands you an exotic xenos rifle.{/n}
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "When Saint Drusus missionaries discovered her secret repository, all of my kin had already died excruciating deaths due to equipment failures, and I was dying. It was a miracle that they pulled me out of my slumber. For three years I had lain within the cryo-vault, paralysed, blind, alone with the darkness, the cold, and my hope for His mercy. Three years of imprisonment in a frozen nightmare. Only the prayers of the blessed priests had kept me from losing my mind."
  - After: "Saint Drusus missionaries found me dying, my kin dead. Three years blind and paralysed in the cold. Prayer kept me sane."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "You may rest assured that I will not linger in your domain a minute longer than etiquette dictates."
  - After: "I'll leave as soon as etiquette allows."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "I see that you have picked up some of Theodora's habits. What blasphemous idea is this — to accept an ungodly xenos slave into your entourage? And to have her as your confidante during the ceremony, signalling that you intend to have dealings with inhumans?"
  - After: "Theodora's habits already? A xenos slave at your side? You'd deal with inhumans?"
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: {n}Calligos's face turns into a grimace of hatred... but then he catches Incendia looking at him and breaks into a sly smile.{/n} "I ought to make your protectorate bleed as compensation. But you have spited both myself and Incendia, and it is high time our dear sister curbed her appetites. For this, I forgive you. But do not test my mercy again — it is not my strong suit."
  - After: {n}Calligos scowls, then glances at Incendia, smiling.{/n} "You spited her too. Forgiven. Don't test me again."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "It's a trophy from a good hunt. You and I should hunt together sometime — so you can show yourself in action, new blood." {n}Calligos exuberantly punches you in the shoulder.{/n}
  - After: "A hunting trophy. Let's hunt together sometime, new blood." {n}He punches your shoulder.{/n}
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "When I beheld light again, I swore an oath to Him — to pursue Aspyce and other miscreants like her till my last breath. To castigate heretics and offenders of faith — such is my path now."
  - After: "Freed, I swore to Him to hunt Aspyce and every heretic till death."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "Only one in ten made it out of Hecaton, and now it's only me and Worten here. We returned without any loot and virtually without a ship. All I got from that trip was a hold full of dead xenos and this deadly beauty, which their leader used to put two holes in my hide."
  - After: "One in ten survived Hecaton. No loot, barely a ship. Just this, which shot me twice."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: {n}Calligos gives you a cheerful and somewhat feral smile.{/n} "I should be thanking you. I was almost certain that you would use my difficulties on Footfall as a means to bring that devious weasel Vladaym to heel and take the station for your own. It's what any Rogue Trader would have done. But you have proved yourself to be less predictable than that!"
  - After: {n}Calligos grins.{/n} "Thanks. Any Rogue Trader would've taken Footfall from Vladaym. You surprised me."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: {n}Calligos watches Incendia with a smile, broad and filled with anticipation, as if expecting her to scratch your eyes out.{/n}
  - After: {n}Calligos grins, hoping Incendia claws your eyes out.{/n}
- **Hieronymus Doloroso**
  - Before: "I saw Sister Argenta at your side during the ceremony and rejoiced. For this is a clear sign that the von Valancius dynasty honours the virtuous."
  - After: "Sister Argenta at your side gladdened me. Your dynasty honours the virtuous."
- **Hieronymus Doloroso**
  - Before: "An impressive victory. But do you truly believe a creation of the ungodly xenos to be a good gift, Calligos?"
  - After: "Impressive. But a xenos gift, Calligos?"
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: {n}Winterscale's whisper is as audible as yours:{/n} "What can you mean? Today she is in remarkably good form."
  - After: {n}Winterscale whispers back:{/n} "She's in fine form today."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "While Footfall was in my charge, I graciously guarded its trade routes. But now their safety is no longer my concern. In accordance with my privileges, I hereby declare Furibundus and the neighbouring systems to be a free hunting zone. Any item of cargo procured in it by a subject of mine will be considered a fair trophy rather than the proceeds of piracy."
  - After: "Then Furibundus and nearby systems are now my free hunting zone. Cargo taken there is a trophy, not piracy."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "Threaten the esteemed Hieronymus one more time, Calligos, and the war that you love to prattle on about will commence. I swear it — one drop of holy blood spilt by you will send the remains of your realm up in flames better than any tanker of {g|Encyclopedia:Promethium}promethium{/g}." {n}Incendia and Calligos exchange looks of fury. The latter, snarling like a wolf, is clearly ready to start said war here and now.{/n}
  - After: "Threaten Hieronymus again, Calligos, and your realm burns like {g|Encyclopedia:Promethium}promethium{/g}." {n}Calligos snarls, ready for war.{/n}
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "I believe you understand me. After all, on this glorious day, you saw fit to cleanse your capital of thieves and criminals."
  - After: "You understand. You purged your capital's criminals today."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "I believe you understand me. After all, your ascension was accompanied by the sounds of holy hymns all over the planet. With this song of righteousness on their lips, your subjects walk toward a dark future filled with blood and trials."
  - After: "You understand. Hymns sang your ascension; your subjects march toward blood."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Next to him is an unmoving hulk of a man clad in armour. His low forehead and gloomy face bear signs of degradation, and his bloodshot eyes are expressionless, like a pair of glass buttons.{/n}
  - After: {n}Beside him stands a dull-eyed armoured hulk.{/n}
- **Hieronymus Doloroso**
  - Before: {n}Hieronymus's dry voice hits your ears like the crack of a whip.{/n} "Quell your pride, both of you. I do not wish to fight you, Calligos, but I fear not your threats. Death does not frighten me, for it is inevitable. It is as true as the senselessness and pointlessness of a war between us."
  - After: {n}Hieronymus snaps,{/n} "Enough. I fear not death, Calligos. War between us is pointless."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "Theodora taught you only too well, it seems — she too was far less concerned with her duty to the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Expanse{/g} than her own personal interests. But you can be sure that I will not cease cleansing the Furibundus System of the pirate scourge. And if your trade prospects are damaged in the process, you will have only yourself to blame."
  - After: "Like Theodora, you put profit before the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Expanse{/g}. I will still purge Furibundus of pirates, whatever it costs your trade."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: {n}Winterscale remarks, taking an obvious jab,{/n} "I've heard that you, {name}, are decent in a fight. What do you think — could you gut Worten if it came down to it? Or would he be the one gutting you?"
  - After: {n}Winterscale jabs,{/n} "Could you gut Worten, {name}? Or would he gut you?"
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: {n}Winterscale smirks acidly.{/n} "Did my Arch-Militant scare you? Reverend, pray to the Emperor that {name} never meets Worten in battle."
  - After: {n}Winterscale smirks.{/n} "Scared? Pray, Reverend, {name} never fights Worten."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "You would call into question the privileges bestowed upon me by the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g}? You can try. Let the {g|Encyclopedia:Drusians}Saint Drusus mission{/g} put forth their champion, and I will slay him in a trial by combat."
  - After: "Question my {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g}-given rights? Let the {g|Encyclopedia:Drusians}Saint Drusus mission{/g} send a champion. I'll slay him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The grey spots on Worten's face are what catch your attention. Marks like these can be seen on fighters who are too fond of combat stimulants. A small price to pay for the increased speed and reaction that could save your life in a fight. Although those spots are usually tiny pockmarks, not whole islands of grey on the skin.{/n}
  - After: {n}Grey patches mar Worten's face — stimulant marks, but far too large.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He is strong, but hardly quick. Dodging his blows would be easy, as would striking him square in his massive chest.{/n}
  - After: {n}Strong but slow. Easy to dodge.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ignoring the fearsome-looking broadsword and pistol, which hang from his belt rather ostentatiously, you notice a great number of thin blades with curved edges skilfully concealed within Worten's armour. These toys are deadly in the hands of a quick fighter — it appears that Winterscale's Arch-Militant likes to surprise his opponent with unexpected speed.{/n}
  - After: {n}Curved blades hide in Worten's armour. He relies on surprising speed.{/n}
- **Worten the Grey**
  - Before: {n}A new glint appears in the bloodshot eyes. A glint of appraisal, intelligent and cunning. No, Worten is not the thick, bloodthirsty beast he wants to be seen as. Behind this mask is a careful and keen mind.{/n}
  - After: {n}Worten's eyes glint, cunning. The brute is a mask.{/n}
- **Worten the Grey**
  - Before: "Many have said that." {n}Worten boldly bares his crooked teeth, which somehow all fit in his mouth. His dull face shows nothing but the desire to fight someone, anyone.{/n}
  - After: "Many have said that." {n}Worten grins, eager to fight.{/n}
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "I can assure you that this is false. She will unleash upon you a thousand sermons, reprimanding you for your wicked conduct, and only then will she deign to take her leave."
  - After: "False. She'll deliver a thousand sermons first."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "It will not be a long one, I assure you."
  - After: "It will be brief."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You notice a peculiar wrongness about Incendia's movements. A barely perceptible fugue that makes her body try to repeat the movements it has just performed. Her chin jerks spasmodically when she turns her head, and the gestures of her fingers are slightly more chaotic and loose than they should be.{/n}
  - After: {n}Incendia's movements stutter, repeating; her chin jerks, fingers twitch.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Something strikes you as strange. Calligos Winterscale wasn't always this... nonchalant about his protectorate. He used to be known as shrewd and business-minded, even concerned for his subjects. But it seems he has grown bored of ruling.{/n}
  - After: {n}Odd. Calligos was once shrewd and cared for his subjects. Now he seems bored of ruling.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Calligos Winterscale is acting like a true Rogue Trader. Capricious, unaware of the value of money, and never a cloud on his countenance.{/n}
  - After: {n}Calligos acts a true Rogue Trader: careless, carefree.{/n}
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "Oh, believe me, I intend to enjoy myself to the full. To justify so long a voyage, if nothing else."
  - After: "I'll enjoy it fully. To justify the voyage."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}"Asp—" That must be Aspyce. Aspyce Chorda. You remember the name. From what you recall, she was a Rogue Trader too, and a renowned one at that.{/n}
  - After: {n}"Asp—" Aspyce Chorda, a renowned Rogue Trader.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You didn't quite catch what word Incendia was about to say.{/n}
  - After: {n}You missed Incendia's word.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You know whose name Incendia almost uttered — you have heard it in your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}former life{/d} more than once. Aspyce Chorda, a Rogue Trader of the Koronus Expanse. An infamously merciless and avaricious pillager who was scarcely different from a common pirate and heretic. One would never think so by looking at Incendia Bastaal-Chorda, but it appears that she and Aspyce are related.{/n}
  - After: {n}From your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Criminal}former life{/d}: Aspyce Chorda, a merciless Expanse raider, near-pirate. Incendia seems her kin.{/n}
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: {n}Incendia's gaze turns to you.{/n} "My servants have brought... certain facts of the new Rogue Trader's {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}biography{/d} to my attention. It may be wise of you to do the same, Calligos, unless you wish to face disappointment in the future." {n}There is a hint of superiority in her eyes. Your ears are burning, and your mouth is dry. She knows of the shame of your past. It would seem that the meticulous archivists of House Chorda have performed regrettably well.{/n}
  - After: {n}Incendia eyes you.{/n} "I've learned of the new Rogue Trader's {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}biography{/d}. Look into it, Calligos." {n}She smirks. She knows your shameful past.{/n}
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "What is more, ever since you gave them {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusChaosFood}provisions{/d}, heresy on Footfall has only increased! Fanatics calling themselves 'harvesters' are spreading their blasphemous doctrines in the Shadow Quarters. Grain is not enough for those madmen — no, they devour their brothers and sisters at secret heretical feasts! The well-fed rabble have surely sensed they are free to act with impunity and have forgotten their duty to the Emperor."
  - After: "Since your {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusChaosFood}provisions{/d}, Footfall heresy grows! Cannibal 'harvesters' feast in the Shadow Quarters."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: {n}You notice Incendia seemingly freeze and choke up at the mention of Aspyce. But the priest's condemning words cause her icy rigidness to evaporate, and her dark eyes fill with righteous fury.{/n}
  - After: {n}Incendia freezes at Aspyce's name, then the priest's words stoke her fury.{/n}
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "Simply colluding with that two-faced snake Vladaym would have been bad enough. But that your conniving has destroyed any pathetic excuse for order that was on that station is pure insolence! I don't know what you did, but now, on top of every other mangy dog that lives on Footfall, there is this new cult of 'harvesters.' What good is your {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusChaosFood}grain{/d} if the station is now crawling with flesh-eating lunatics?"
  - After: "Colluding with Vladaym was bad enough. Now Footfall has a flesh-eating 'harvesters' cult. What good is your {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusChaosFood}grain{/d} now?"
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "A true Rogue Trader always keeps a living weapon close at hand. But you don't need me to tell you that — you have a Death Cult assassin in your employ! Not bad, new blood, but I would wager my Worten has a meaner bite than that zealot of yours."
  - After: "A Rogue Trader keeps a living weapon. You have a Death Cult assassin, but my Worten bites harder."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "And since you asked... A psyker in the service of the governor of my world has recently swapped a luxurious bedchamber in the palace for the cramped confines of a ship's cabin. His escape was so skilfully orchestrated that I couldn't help but look into it further. And what I discovered broke my heart, new blood." {n}Behind Winterscale's sly, narrowed gaze, you see icy rage. But a moment later, the cordial grin is back on his lips.{/n} "However, would I quarrel over such a trifle as a runaway servant? Consider Herimon a gift to you."
  - After: "My governor's psyker fled to your ship — too skilfully. I looked into it, new blood." {n}Icy rage, then a grin.{/n} "But keep Herimon. A gift."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: {n}Calligos bursts into laughter.{/n} "Of course, a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Arbitrator}{mf|lawman|lawwoman}{/d}'s sole topic of conversation is the tithe! I'll have you know, new blood, that my worlds still bring in more tithes than you have seen in your whole life. So I can do as I well please — and so I will."
  - After: {n}Calligos laughs.{/n} "A {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Arbitrator}{mf|lawman|lawwoman}{/d}, all tithe! My worlds still out-tithe your lifetime. I'll do as I please."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "Hieronymus Doloroso, head of the {g|Encyclopedia:Drusians}Saint Drusus mission{/g} and my confessor. An advocate of faith."
  - After: "Hieronymus Doloroso, head of the {g|Encyclopedia:Drusians}Saint Drusus mission{/g}, my confessor."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "This is Worten the Grey, my Arch-Militant. A fierce warrior, and as loyal to me as an obedient beast to its master. I bought him in a miserable colony back when he was a runt on his last legs, and now he is practically a part of my dynasty."
  - After: "Worten the Grey, my loyal Arch-Militant. Bought as a dying runt; now nearly family."
- **Worten the Grey**
  - Before: {n}Worten the Grey, whose skin really is dotted with grey spots, looks at Calligos with purest devotion. Indeed, he is akin to an animal — one that is bloodthirsty and mindless.{/n}
  - After: {n}Grey-spotted Worten gazes at Calligos with mindless devotion.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/Dargonus/RogueTraderPalace/Achilleas/Achilleas_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I'm not so foolish as to fail to notice a conversation in code."
  - After: "I can tell a conversation in code."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I would like to know that myself. Van Calox left my retinue on Kiava Gamma, but not before stealing one of the ship's shuttles."
  - After: "Me too. Van Calox left at Kiava Gamma, stealing a shuttle."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Van Calox attacked a Rogue Trader and was executed for his crime."
  - After: "Van Calox attacked a Rogue Trader and was executed."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Heinrix died doing his duty to the Golden Throne."
  - After: "Heinrix died doing his duty."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Interrogator is well and currently aboard my ship."
  - After: "The Interrogator is well, aboard my ship."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I know nothing of the Interrogator's fate."
  - After: "I don't know his fate."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Is there a reason for this ill-mannered behaviour, Heinrix? Perhaps you two could find another time to discuss personal matters?"
  - After: "Why so rude, Heinrix? Talk later."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What are your responsibilities here on Dargonus?"
  - After: "What are your duties here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you know anything about the Cult of the Final Dawn?"
  - After: "What of the Cult of the Final Dawn?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You promised me a report on the present state of affairs in the protectorate."
  - After: "You promised a report on the protectorate."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What can you tell me about House Sauerback?"
  - After: "And House Sauerback?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I would like to know more about the Werserians."
  - After: "Tell me about the Werserians."
- **Player**
  - Before: "After hearing all that, I now feel the urge to have every one of those sycophants executed at once."
  - After: "I want those sycophants all executed."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Enough about the nobles. Was there anything else you wanted to report?"
  - After: "Enough of nobles. Anything else?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I've been to Kiava Gamma already. The planet was tainted by the Cult of the Final Dawn."
  - After: "Kiava Gamma was tainted by the Cult of the Final Dawn."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Whom do you truly serve — the Rogue Trader or the Interrogator of the Inquisition?"
  - After: "Whom do you serve — me or the Inquisition?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Dargonus has no need for spies from the Inquisition. Begone!"
  - After: "No Inquisition spies on Dargonus. Begone!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have other questions to ask."
  - After: "I have other questions."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I must take my leave."
  - After: "I must go."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I want a list of all your agents and the means to contact them."
  - After: "I want a list of your agents and contacts."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell me about the noble houses of Dargonus."
  - After: "Tell me about the noble houses."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have learned all I wanted to."
  - After: "I've learned enough."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The scars on your face... What happened?"
  - After: "Your scars... What happened?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you know anything about what has become of Kunrad Voigtvir? The former Master of Whispers is a heretic and a traitor to the dynasty."
  - After: "What became of Kunrad Voigtvir, the traitor Master of Whispers?"
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "{name} von Valancius, I greatly appreciate that you've found the time to see me before meeting with the governor. But before we get wrapped up in important matters, allow me to enquire — where is Master van Calox? I thought he accompanied you on the journey."
  - After: "{name} von Valancius, thank you. But where is Master van Calox?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix frowns.{/n} "For as long as the stars shine in the sky, my vigil continues."
  - After: {n}Heinrix frowns.{/n} "My vigil continues."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Achilleas, it's been many moons. I hope your cousin is feeling well."
  - After: "Achilleas. Is your cousin well?"
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "That is... a terrible loss. For the Inquisition and for the Imperium." {n}Achilleas clasps his hands, his burnt lips mouthing words of prayer.{/n}
  - After: "A terrible loss." {n}Achilleas prays.{/n}
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "I'm glad to hear it. But still, I was hoping that Master van Calox would introduce us personally."
  - After: "Good. I'd hoped he'd introduce us."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix looks at Achilleas.{/n} "Allow me to introduce Achilleas Scalander properly. In addition to his duties as secretary of the Administratum, he acts as an agent of the Golden Throne under my aegis. Master Scalander was transferred into my remit by a colleague who is engaged in other matters in the Koronus Expanse. I'm sure you will find Achilleas's service useful — especially when dealing with the schemes of Humanity's foes within the borders of your protectorate."
  - After: {n}Heinrix looks at Achilleas.{/n} "Achilleas Scalander: Administratum secretary, and my agent. He'll help against Humanity's foes in your protectorate."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "Officially, I'm a secretary at this world's Administratum department. Less officially... I'm afraid I can't disclose that even to you. In short, I collect and investigate reports of heresy taking root on upstanding planets of Humanity. Above all else, I am concerned about the xenos threat that hangs over the entire Koronus Expanse, including your protectorate. Sadly, my mission was complicated by the recent warp disturbances — I am still trying to re-establish contact with many of my agents."
  - After: "Officially, a secretary. Unofficially, I hunt heresy and, above all, xenos. The warp storms cut me off from many agents."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "The residents of the local systems are no strangers to skirmishes with enemies of Humanity. But recently the loathsome beasts seem to have completely flown off the handle. We're receiving reports from ships that made it through the warp to Dargonus — both they and the colonies that they departed from are being attacked. We have identified the breed of xenos that pose this threat — the {g|Encyclopedia:Drukhari}Drukhari{/g}, Humanity's ancient and insidious foes. Be vigilant on your travels — the xenos will undoubtedly attack a Rogue Trader's ship should they find the circumstances to be in their favour."
  - After: "Xenos raids have surged on ships and colonies. The culprits are the {g|Encyclopedia:Drukhari}Drukhari{/g}. Beware — they'll strike your ship if they can."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "My knowledge is deplorably limited, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} — all my attention has been focused on tracking xenos activity. I'm certain that Master van Calox can tell you much more about those heretics than I."
  - After: "I know little, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Master van Calox knows more."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas catches himself.{/n} "That is to say, he could tell you if he were alive."
  - After: {n}Achilleas catches himself.{/n} "Knew, rather."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "The nobles of Dargonus are well-respected, rich, and powerful individuals who held Lady Theodora's favour for many years and found ways to rise above the rest by diligently serving the Rogue Trader. Every family pursues its own selfish interests, and each one expects that with the transition of power, they will retain and even add to their lands and wealth. The families I would recommend giving particular attention to are the Drivestems, the Gapraks, and the Sauerbacks. I should also mention the Werserians — not a noble house per se, but a family that was part of Lady Theodora's inner circle, to the blue bloods' great displeasure."
  - After: "Each house expects to gain from the transition. Watch the Drivestems, Gapraks and Sauerbacks — and the Werserians, Theodora's untitled favourites."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "I have already forwarded all official reports to your Seneschal. As for the conversation we're having right now, I wouldn't trust any paper or data-slate with its contents. You see, Lady Theodora, may the Emperor have mercy on her soul, was perfectly aware of Dargonus's political environment. You, however, have only just arrived on the capital world, and I thought it would be best to bring you up to speed. Frankly, the nobles of Dargonus, much like nobles on most worlds, are akin to spiders in a jar, ready to pounce on whoever is the weakest... or whomever they deem to be the weakest."
  - After: "Your Seneschal has the official reports. This I trust to no data-slate: the nobles are spiders in a jar, ready to pounce on the weakest."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "The Drivestems are the ancient governor house of Dargonus. Predictably, the greater the wealth of the von Valancius protectorate, the fuller their coffers grow. Their reputation is flawless except for one detail — we have evidence that Urbend Drivestem's rivals seem to have the misfortune of regularly falling victim to xenos raids. I find that these attacks are always a little too advantageous for the Drivestems, but we lack solid proof — and it might never surface."
  - After: "The Drivestems, Dargonus's ancient governor house, profit as the protectorate does. Urbend's rivals keep falling to xenos raids — convenient, but unproven."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "The Gapraks hail from a remote forge world, and among their distant relatives, there are many servants of the Omnissiah, and the house itself is close to the cult of the Adeptus Mechanicus, both in spirit and in their business connections. The Gapraks oversaw the industrial shipments within your protectorate — until recently. Ever since the Astropathic communication with Kiava Gamma was severed, they've been quite concerned about the security of the planet placed in their care."
  - After: "The Gapraks are forge-worlders, close to the Mechanicus. They ran industrial shipments until Kiava Gamma, their charge, went silent."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "Religious and hardworking... The Sauerbacks own many enterprises, including distillation manufactorums that produce promethium. I must note that lately members of the Sauerback family have been prone to overly liberal statements about the von Valancius dynasty — they believe that Lady Theodora was a bit too keen to leave her worlds without proper oversight."
  - After: "Pious Sauerbacks own promethium manufactorums. Lately they say Lady Theodora neglected her worlds."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "The Werserians are a line founded by Lady Theodora's Seneschal and as such are nominally considered nobility — at least from the standpoint of the Imperial Navy, from which Lord Abelard hails. On Dargonus, however, their position is precarious — firstly, they never were granted an official title, a process which has been impeded for decades by the old houses of Dargonus, and secondly, the other families do not see them as equals, but more as upstarts clinging to the Rogue Trader's favour. The Werserians are responsible for the capital world's fleet and the majority of the cargo shipments on domestic routes."
  - After: "The Werserians descend from Theodora's Seneschal, Lord Abelard. The old houses deny them a title. They run the capital's fleet and domestic cargo."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas shrugs.{/n} "You are, naturally, well within your right, Rogue Trader. But remember that this will cause the multilayered bureaucratic system of Dargonus — of your entire protectorate, in fact — to come apart at the seams. And that's not even considering the likelihood of attempted reprisals from their families and allies."
  - After: {n}Achilleas shrugs.{/n} "Your right. But the bureaucracy would collapse, and their families would retaliate."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "There was, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. And this time, it concerns the main reason for my presence on this planet — xenos and the threat they pose both to you and to Humanity as a whole."
  - After: "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} — the xenos threat."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas shakes his head.{/n} "These are grim tidings... It's a tragedy that an {g|Encyclopedia:IndustrialWorld}industrial world{/g} of such tremendous capacity was brought down by the pernicious influence of the Archenemy. Perhaps my... colleagues can pick up the cultists' trail in the cold void. Of course, it would be a small consolation to all of us."
  - After: {n}Achilleas shakes his head.{/n} "A great {g|Encyclopedia:IndustrialWorld}industrial world{/g}, lost to the Archenemy. My colleagues may track the cultists."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "And whom does the Rogue Trader serve? The Golden Throne? The protectorate? Could it be that one stems from the other? And if so, is there any sense in discussing it?"
  - After: "And whom does the Rogue Trader serve? Throne or protectorate? Is there a difference?"
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "I would never defy a Rogue Trader on {mf|his|her} capital world. However, I am here on direct orders from the Lord Inquisitor, whose authority, pardon my brazenness, supersedes yours. I cannot leave my post — at least not until he recalls me personally. Please, stay your anger, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. For I am doing everything I can to rid the von Valancius worlds of the threat of burgeoning heresy."
  - After: "I'd never defy a Rogue Trader on {mf|his|her} own world. But the Lord Inquisitor posted me here; only he can recall me. I fight heresy for you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "I sincerely hope that I can answer every one of them."
  - After: "I hope I can answer."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "Thank you for your time, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}With a formal bow, Achilleas takes his leave.{/n}
  - After: "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Achilleas bows and leaves.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "The closer an official is to a Rogue Trader, the braver and safer they feel. I would just like to remind everyone that rubbing shoulders with xenos is a heresy that can be overlooked only in the case of the von Valancius heir, not {mf|his|her} servant."
  - After: "Consorting with xenos is heresy — forgivable in the von Valancius heir, not in {mf|his|her} servant."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "I can understand your desire as a Rogue Trader to have everything under your control. And yet I am not at liberty to make use of classified information related to the Interrogator's agents in whatever way I see fit." {n}Achilleas lowers his gaze and nods politely.{/n}
  - After: "I can't share the Interrogator's classified agents." {n}Achilleas nods politely.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The last few months have been difficult for the people who report to me — my eyes and ears scattered throughout the Koronus Expanse. Warp disturbances, Astropaths overcome with madness, ships disappearing in the Immaterium... many of my observers and contacts have gone dark or have been killed by some calamity or other. Still, I managed to establish communication with some key... individuals who were able to warn me about incoming threats, including xenos raids."
  - After: "Warp storms have silenced many of my contacts. A few still warn me of xenos raids."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}The slender figure, clad in robes made from expensive fabric, shudders from violent coughing. Pressing a gilded respirator to his face, the man takes several deep breaths.{/n}
  - After: {n}A slender, richly robed man coughs into a gilded respirator.{/n}
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas nods to you pensively.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, how may I be of service?"
  - After: {n}Achilleas nods.{/n} "How may I serve, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?"
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas's genial expression is instantly drained of all emotion. He looks at you for a few moments, then nods, as if to himself.{/n} "I thank you for your candour. I hope that the Lord Inquisitor investigates the matter thoroughly."
  - After: {n}Achilleas's face goes blank.{/n} "Thank you for your candour. I hope the Lord Inquisitor investigates."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "Truly? That is regrettable."
  - After: "That is regrettable."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "I will gladly refresh your memory, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "Gladly, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "I would hold off on the death sentences. Act with restraint and wisdom, present for all to see sufficient proof of the unwanted house's guilt. Do not mistake me — mass executions are one way to solve your problems — but in that case, you should weigh up every possible scenario before you act."
  - After: "Hold off. Prove a house's guilt first, and weigh every outcome before mass executions."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas looks you in the eye without blinking.{/n} "It is within my power to supply you with intelligence on where and when the xenos will strike next. I do not doubt that Governor Drivestem will beg you for protection against the xenos, and in this fight, the information from my contacts will serve you well. I beseech you, {name} — if I ever report a threat looming over a ship or a planet, do not dismiss it. Sometimes it takes an intervention from the Rogue Trader and {mf|his|her} mighty voidship to avert a disaster."
  - After: {n}Achilleas stares.{/n} "I can tell you where xenos will strike next. {name}, heed my warnings — sometimes only a Rogue Trader and {mf|his|her} voidship can avert disaster."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas's amber eyes flash with interest.{/n} "Yes?"
  - After: {n}Achilleas's eyes flash.{/n} "Yes?"
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas covers his burnt lips, trying and failing to suppress a coughing fit.{/n} "She... she is in good health... She sends her regards to you, as well as her wishes for your swift return."
  - After: {n}Achilleas coughs.{/n} "She is well... and hopes you return soon."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas bows and brings the respirator to his burnt lips.{/n}
  - After: {n}Achilleas bows.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas nods grimly.{/n} "Word of his treason reached Dargonus too late. Kunrad came to the planet and left it almost immediately, once he had sown discord in the minds of the gullible and naive. The worst of the rumours he started was that you were the one responsible for Lady Theodora's sudden demise. Of course, your loyal subjects did their best to skin alive any who showed signs of doubt. But it seems unlikely that the wardens got to everyone who has allowed doubt into their heart and now nurtures it in secret."
  - After: {n}Achilleas nods grimly.{/n} "Kunrad passed through, spreading rumours that you killed Lady Theodora. Doubters were punished, but some still doubt in secret."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas quickly glances at Heinrix.{/n}
  - After: {n}Achilleas glances at Heinrix.{/n}
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "About..." {n}He coughs.{/n} "...five years ago, there was an accident. Several tanks of promethium exploded in the storehouse at my estate, and I was buried alive under the rubble. The Emperor preserved my soul, and the skilled physicians of Dargonus saved my body — except for my lungs, with which I had to part. I presume the incident was an attempt on my life, but the identity of whoever was behind it remains a mystery."
  - After: "Five years ago..." {n}He coughs.{/n} "...promethium tanks exploded at my estate. I lost my lungs. An assassination attempt, I suspect."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Unfortunately, in the host of Humanity there are those who are willing to grovel before our enemies in the hopes of a valuable reward. You may be interested to know that we are on the trail of such heretics..." {n}Achilleas glances at a data-slate.{/n} "Overwhelming evidence indicates that a plundered void station in Langrenn's Belt is being used as a base by a band of pirates who are not above dealing with xenos. I was unable to persuade the chancellor of the need to dispatch a ship there, but... perhaps you would like to pay a courtesy call to these scoundrels yourself?"
  - After: "Some humans serve xenos for reward." {n}He checks a data-slate.{/n} "Xenos-trading pirates hold a void station in Langrenn's Belt. The chancellor won't send a ship... will you?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Achilleas is the critical link in a long chain of people who toil day and night, putting their lives and souls at risk, to protect Humanity from its many enemies — your enemies. To send Scalander away is to blind both your eyes and be left ignorant about those who are seeking to stab you in the back."
  - After: "Achilleas is a vital link protecting Humanity — and you. Send him away and you blind yourself to backstabbers."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix lets out a sigh of disappointment.{/n} "There's no point in pressing my agents — none of them would ever reveal such vital information. Especially not in my presence."
  - After: {n}Heinrix sighs.{/n} "My agents would never reveal that. Especially not before me."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "My apologies, {name}. Given the break in the communications between systems in the Expanse, it has become difficult to maintain contact with agents. Receiving this report and assessing the situation is my primary responsibility."
  - After: "My apologies, {name}. With communications broken, this report is my priority."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "So it does." {n}Achilleas thumps himself on the chest with his augmented hand. You hear the clanging of metal against metal.{/n}
  - After: "So it does." {n}Achilleas thumps his metal chest.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Your insight deserves credit, Rogue Trader — then again, I expected nothing less from Theodora von Valancius's successor."
  - After: "Insightful, Rogue Trader — as expected of Theodora's successor."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "My apologies, {name}. Now, to the reason why I asked to be present during the landing on Dargonus."
  - After: "My apologies, {name}. Now, to business."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas blinks in surprise.{/n} "I'm sure that such actions must have had valid reasons. I hope your property is returned to you eventually."
  - After: {n}Achilleas blinks.{/n} "He must have had reasons. I hope you recover the shuttle."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas bows.{/n} "According to the message I received a few minutes ago, Governor Drivestem has arrived at court. I imagine that the chancellor is already prepared to arrange the meeting — all that's left is to notify her that you are ready to see Urbend."
  - After: {n}Achilleas bows.{/n} "Governor Drivestem has arrived. Tell the chancellor when you're ready to see Urbend."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "Greetings, {mf|Lord|Lady} {name} von Valancius. Allow me once again to express my deepest condolences on the loss of Lady Theodora. I will do everything I can to track down and destroy all of Kunrad Voigtvir's accomplices on the capital world."
  - After: "Greetings, {mf|Lord|Lady} {name} von Valancius. My condolences. I'll hunt down Kunrad Voigtvir's accomplices here."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/Dargonus/RogueTraderPalace/DargonusFirstArrival/DargonusFirstArrival_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "The Emperor protected us on our journey through the stars."
  - After: "The Emperor protected our journey."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It was uneventful, thank you."
  - After: "Uneventful, thank you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Emperor blesses those who strengthen Humanity's domain through their deeds. You have reason to be proud of your progeny."
  - After: "The Emperor blesses those who strengthen Humanity. Be proud of your progeny."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It was terrible! I did not realise my demesne's security was so illusory."
  - After: "Terrible! My demesne's security is an illusion."
- **Player**
  - Before: "We had some incidents, but those are irrelevant at this moment."
  - After: "We had incidents, but they're irrelevant now."
- **Player**
  - Before: "All that concerns me is the prosperity of my protectorate."
  - After: "I care only for my protectorate's prosperity."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why isn't the governor here with you to greet me?"
  - After: "Why isn't the governor here to greet me?"

  - Before: "I would like to rest before the meeting. Where are my chambers?"
  - After: "I'd like to rest first. Where are my chambers?"

  - Before: "Hold on a moment, Clementia. What did you say your last name was?"

  - Before: "Easy, Abelard. I was simply asking."

  - After: "The Emperor protects! Welcome home, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}A stern, grey-haired woman curtsies.{/n}

  - Before: "I'm glad to hear it, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "Glad to hear it, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "It saddens me to hear this, Rogue Trader. I hope that here, within the walls of your family estate, you can rest and regather your strength."
  - After: "I'm sorry. Rest here, Rogue Trader."

  - After: "Questions, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}? Governor Urbend Drivestem is coming, but Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} has time."

  - Before: {n}Abelard huffs with feigned indifference.{/n}
  - After: {n}Abelard huffs.{/n}
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Apologies, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Governor Drivestem's residence is on the other side of the world — by the Administratum Palace of Dargonus. We sent word as soon as you entered the system. But it takes time to travel the great distances of your domain."
  - After: "Apologies, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The governor lives across the world, by the Administratum Palace."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "For House Werserian, your dynasty's well-being is of paramount importance."
  - After: "House Werserian lives for your dynasty."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "They are very close, just down the hall. That is also where the study and the audience chamber are." {n}Achilleas's face brightens with a pearly-white smile, restoring some of his former good looks.{/n} "Lady Theodora's study has remained locked since her last departure, but, on account of your arrival, we've arranged for it to be tidied up — it is ready whenever you may need it."
  - After: "Just down the hall, by the study." {n}Achilleas smiles.{/n} "Lady Theodora's study is ready for you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Clementia nods politely.{/n} "You heard correctly, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I am of House Werserian — Lord Abelard's granddaughter and direct descendant."
  - After: {n}Clementia nods.{/n} "Yes, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Werserian — Lord Abelard's granddaughter."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "I apologise for my bluntness, but I have a request to make. Perhaps, before the meeting takes place, the illustrious Lord Captain could spare a few minutes for a conversation with me?" {n}Achilleas bows his head.{/n} "I'm certain that you will find my report on the state of affairs in the von Valancius protectorate most useful."
  - After: "Might I have a few minutes before the meeting?" {n}Achilleas bows.{/n} "My report on the protectorate will help."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Your yellow words becloud the Rogue Trader... yet I can see the swampy muck behind the veneer. You are trying to shield the Lord Captain from the unseemly truth, but it is a servant's duty to share every truth with their master."
  - After: "Your yellow words hide muck. A servant owes the master every truth."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}Clementia flinches and nods uncertainly.{/n} "Of course... You are right, Lady Navigator. I believe that the governor is testing the limits of what is allowed. An audacious move on his part, but Her Ladyship always favoured audacity."
  - After: {n}Clementia flinches.{/n} "True, Lady Navigator. The governor is testing limits. Her Ladyship liked boldness."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}Chancellor Werserian appears unruffled, but you cannot shake the thought that the governor's lateness is a subtle political gesture designed to test the limits of what is acceptable when it comes to interacting with the new Rogue Trader.{/n}
  - After: {n}The governor's lateness feels like a political test of you.{/n}
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}She has a point. Dargonus is a vast world, and a trip from one pole to another must take a considerable amount of time.{/n}
  - After: {n}Fair. Dargonus is vast.{/n}
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}The young man quickly brings a respirator to his burnt face and bows his head courteously. His raven black hair veils his burns and skull implants, and his thin metal fingers creak quietly as he offers a welcoming gesture.{/n} "Achilleas Scalander, secretary at the Administratum department. I hope your journey to Dargonus was not darkened by unwanted troubles?"
  - After: {n}A burnt young man with metal fingers bows behind a respirator.{/n} "Achilleas Scalander, Administratum secretary. Was your journey untroubled?"
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "I am Clementia Werserian, court chancellor of the von Valancius dynasty. On behalf of all of Dargonus, please accept my deepest condolences on the untimely passing of Theodora von Valancius. Her departure is a terrible blow to us all. But as one star expires, another always flares to life. And, although still overcome with bitterness and grief, your subjects hope that you will become the trade dynasty's guiding light in these trying times."
  - After: "Clementia Werserian, court chancellor. We mourn Theodora, but as one star dies, another flares."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Clementia." {n}Abelard offers a reserved nod. She nods in return, and the lines on his brow soften ever so slightly.{/n}
  - After: "Clementia." {n}They exchange nods.{/n}
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "Quite right, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. What happened cannot be changed, but you still have great deeds ahead of you. So let us look to the future with hope in our hearts."
  - After: "Quite right, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Let us look ahead."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Chancellor Werserian has held her position at the von Valancius court for many years. She earned Lord Captain Theodora's respect through acts of great perseverance. There's no room for doubt — blood had nothing to do with it."
  - After: "Clementia earned Theodora's respect through perseverance, not blood."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas makes the sign of the Aquila.{/n} "And may He remain merciful to us till the end of time."
  - After: {n}Achilleas makes the Aquila.{/n} "May He stay merciful."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard looks at you in surprise, but then immediately puts on an air of indifference.{/n} "Thank you, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}Abelard looks surprised.{/n} "Thank you, Lord Captain."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The succession of service is an effective good. It grants new generations understanding of their function within the mechanism."
  - After: "Inherited service is efficient. Each generation learns its function."

  - Before: {n}The governor hurriedly lowers his head in an obliging bow, but you catch a glimpse of the grimace on his face. He is clearly displeased by your words.{/n} "In that case, I think it's appropriate not to change the established order of things — you will be represented by the governor house of Drivestem."
  - After: {n}He bows, hiding a grimace.{/n} "Then the governor's House Drivestem will represent you, as tradition holds."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard turns to you and bows respectfully.{/n} "Lord Captain! To accompany you at such a critical hour is the greatest honour for the Werserian bloodline! Have no fear — we will not fail you."
  - After: {n}Abelard bows.{/n} "Lord Captain! The greatest honour for the Werserians! We won't fail you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Drivestem pales in terror. It is clear from the unseemly grimace on his aristocratic countenance that his fear is not feigned.{/n} "R-Ruinous Powers? Truly horrifying news. I commend your resolve and unwavering severity! Death to the enemies of Humanity!"
  - After: {n}Drivestem pales in genuine terror.{/n} "R-Ruinous Powers? Horrifying! Death to the enemies of Humanity!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Drivestem gives you a look of admiration. It seems that he is quite aware of your fame, and this opportunity to curry favour with such an {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Glory}eminent figure{/d} is one he does not wish to miss.{/n}
  - After: {n}Drivestem eyes the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_Glory}eminent figure{/d} admiringly, eager to curry favour.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As much as the governor is trying to appear sincere, there is something in the curve of his nervous half-smile that you find troubling. Is it a hint of reproach? Mockery? Condemnation? Or is it merely your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}guilty conscience{/d} playing tricks on you under the governor's keen gaze, stirring up memories of your past?{/n}
  - After: {n}His half-smile troubles you. Reproach, or your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Shame}guilty conscience{/d}?{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Urbend Drivestem, governor of this great world. First and foremost, please accept my deepest condolences. It will be difficult to recover from the loss of a woman as great as Theodora von Valancius. It pains me to think that she is no longer with us. The citizens of Dargonus and of the entire protectorate grieve alongside you. Please allow us to declare half a year of mourning so that we can honour the memory of our beloved lady."
  - After: "Urbend Drivestem, governor. My condolences for Theodora. Allow us half a year of mourning."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Alas, it won't be an easy task to accomplish. Some time ago, the {g|Encyclopedia:Astropath}Astropaths{/g} of Dargonus flew into a rage, and they had to be... subdued. We are gradually restoring our ability to speak with neighbouring worlds, but the contacts are still weak, and the routes are tangled and no longer lead to the systems that the captains expect them to. Given that the vast majority of ships in the Dargonus navy travel without relying on the services of {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigators{/g} — without your engagement, the well-being of the von Valancius dynasty and billions of its subjects is presently at risk."
  - After: "Hard. Our {g|Encyclopedia:Astropath}Astropaths{/g} went mad. Routes are tangled, and our ships lack {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigators{/g}. Without you, billions suffer."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And yet you are still a descendant of a great dynasty. But I shan't tire you further with my humble opinion."
  - After: "Yet you descend from a great dynasty. But I'll say no more."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "As you will, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Drivestem bows his head.{/n}
  - After: "As you will, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}He bows.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you for your time, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Since duty calls, I shall take my leave. May the Emperor's grace be with you!"
  - After: "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The Emperor's grace be with you!"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Command the spinners of the Bloodspun Web — and they will set a fine snare of retribution, Domin'{name}. We will whisper names, and that whisper will drown out insolent voices."
  - After: "Command the Bloodspun Web, Domin'{name}. Our whispers will drown out insolent voices."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Hmm... Well, I'll be sure to notify the Gapraks of Kiava Gamma's current situation. Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "Hmm... I'll inform the Gapraks. Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A cold sweat breaks out on Drivestem's face. He forces a subservient smile on his face.{/n} "This will bring the noble houses into line for years to come, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It will make them fear not only blasphemous words, but also their own shadows."
  - After: {n}Drivestem sweats, smiling servilely.{/n} "The houses will fear their own shadows, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The governor stares at you with a mixture of worry and incredulity. Nevertheless, after hearing your words, he bows his head in obedience.{/n}
  - After: {n}Worried, the governor bows.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Drivestem humbly bows his head.{/n}
  - After: {n}Drivestem bows.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Drivestem tosses Abelard a look that lacks even the smallest shred of respect.{/n} "Forgive my boldness, but I must remind you that the Werserians, whose lineage traces back to a Navy officer, are not of the Dargonus nobility. Such decisions may have adverse effects on your subjects' loyalty, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: {n}Drivestem sneers at Abelard.{/n} "The Werserians aren't nobility. This may cost loyalty, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "It will be done, Domin'{name}. Let the sacrament of the hunt commence."
  - After: "It will be done, Domin'{name}. Let the hunt begin."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, it would seem that Kunrad somehow got his hands on a copy of your authorisation — or perhaps even the original! A tool like that in the hands of a traitor does not bode well!"
  - After: "Lord Captain, Kunrad must have your authorisation — a copy or the original!"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}At Urbend's last words, Abelard lets out a sound that could be interpreted as either a snort or a cough. Urbend gives him a look, which Abelard meets with an expression of utter nonchalance.{/n}
  - After: {n}Abelard snorts. Urbend glares; Abelard shrugs it off.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Hmm... This is a truly regrettable bit of news. What's more — leaving Dargonus has been forbidden for several cycles now! It seems the Werserian family has once again failed in their primary responsibilities." {n}He shoots Abelard a condescending look.{/n}
  - After: "Leaving Dargonus is forbidden! The Werserians failed again." {n}He eyes Abelard.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "{g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}Xenos{/g}, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I don't rightly know where to begin..." {n}He rubs the bridge of his nose wearily.{/n} "Otherworldly beasts are not an uncommon sight in the Koronus Expanse — they have been a menace to the worlds this side of the Maw for decades. But now... now those abominations are on the rampage. They show no signs of fear as they attack ships, either damaging them to the point where they become unfit for transport duty or outright gutting them!"
  - After: "{g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}Xenos{/g}, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}He sighs.{/n} "They've long plagued us, but now they rampage, gutting our ships!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Only you have the power to stop this madness! We are in the process of restoring the Astropathic Choir of Dargonus. Luckily, we were forced to slay only some of the deranged psykers, although those that remain are as yet unable to transmit messages. I hope Master Scalander will keep his word and offer you his support in the war against the xenos. According to his reports, the region of Vheabos VI has been of particular concern in the last few cycles... which is all the more reason to discover the colony's fate as soon as possible."
  - After: "Only you can stop this! Our Astropaths can't transmit yet. Master Scalander may help; he reports trouble near Vheabos VI. Learn its fate soon."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "An elegant solution, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Other families will assume that your relationships with the defiant houses are more complicated than one might think, and the agitators will receive the message that they are being watched."
  - After: "Elegant, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The agitators will know they're watched."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/Dargonus/RogueTraderPalace/TradeRepresentative/TradeRepresentative_dialogue

- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Clementia bows her head politely. For a chancellor to a Rogue Trader, she is dressed rather simply — a parade doublet, polished boots, and a comfortable cloak. She bears a sabre in a gilded scabbard — whether for show or protection, one could not say. Only her ring with the Werserian coat of arms indicates that she is of the highest social stratum.{/n} "The governor is waiting on the periphery of the palace. Please let me know when you would like to see him."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Clementia bows, plainly dressed, a gilded sabre at her side.{/n} "The governor awaits your word."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "No... no, I don't believe I feel either, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Clementia's steely eyes stare into the distance, her jaw clenching visibly. She speaks in a polite but clipped manner, clearly flustered by your insight.{/n} "We have different views on how to run a world. We sometimes have discussions over the laws that are enacted. But we both work for the good of the von Valancius protectorate, that much can be said without a doubt."
  - After: "No, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Her jaw clenches.{/n} "We differ, but both serve the protectorate."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}She looks surprised.{/n} "Why, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I would never! Of course, the governor and I are not exactly close friends, but I respect his contribution to the protectorate's development, and I'm thankful for his concern for Dargonus."
  - After: {n}Surprised.{/n} "Never, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! I respect his work."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "I serve the von Valancius protectorate, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "I serve the protectorate, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "To put it simply, I am your trade representative. Any and all decrees, deals, official communication, and meetings are first reviewed by me and then forwarded to you and from you down the hierarchy."
  - After: "I'm your trade representative. All decrees, deals and meetings pass through me."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "All deals and important decisions are made here in the capital. Many years ago, an ancestor of Lady Theodora signed an agreement with the Adeptus Administratum which allowed for efficient management of the world and the neighbouring systems. In accordance with the decree, a share of the planet's population was assigned to the Administratum and converted into servitor scribes. They now toil across the entire world."
  - After: "Decisions happen here. Theodora's ancestor let the Administratum run this region; many citizens became servitor scribes."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Unfortunately, not at this time, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. After the few representatives of the Adeptus Astra Telepathica on Dargonus went into a frenzy, some of the psykers were tragically pacified by the respective authorities. Since then, communication with the neighbouring systems has been unreliable at best. Thanks be to the Master of Mankind that you managed to find your way to the capital!"
  - After: "No, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Our psykers went mad and some were pacified. Contact is unreliable."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}Clementia is different from most nobles — not just in the way she's dressed, but in her bearing too. Although, judging by the scars visible on her skin, at least some part of her education took place on a battlefield, rather than within the secure confines of a lyceum.{/n}
  - After: {n}Her scars suggest a battlefield education.{/n}
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Apart from the disrupted communications, Dargonus was recently raided by enemies of Humanity. However, the fleet, under the command of Captain Marthius Werserian, triumphed over the accursed xenos. If you ask for my opinion on this matter — we have the situation completely under control."
  - After: "Xenos raided us, but Captain Marthius Werserian's fleet won."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Is that truly all that concerns you, peddler of xenoheresy?" {n}Clementia's words cut Jae off like the swing of a sabre. Then Clementia turns to you, her head lowered in shame.{/n}
  - After: "Is that all you care about, peddler of xenoheresy?" {n}Clementia turns to you, ashamed.{/n}
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Urbend Drivestem is a well-respected man — and not just on Dargonus but throughout the protectorate. For many centuries, his house has supported the capital's administration and the logistics between the von Valancius systems. The Drivestems' efforts secured years of order and prosperity for Dargonus. What's more, Lady Theodora personally insisted that Lord Urbend specifically be made the next governor."
  - After: "Urbend Drivestem is respected. His house has run our logistics for centuries. Theodora chose him."

  - Before: "They lost your seal, shereen. They lost it and tried to hide the fact from both me and you."
  - After: "They lost your seal, shereen, and hid it."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}Clementia bows before leaving.{/n} "I shall arrange for him to be escorted to your study."
  - After: {n}Clementia bows.{/n} "I'll have him escorted to your study."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Certainly, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. However..." {n}Her thin lips twist slightly.{/n} "I do not concern myself with the governor's feelings, but I must warn you — your action or inaction may be interpreted in a certain way. Now, if Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} will excuse me."
  - After: "Certainly, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Her lips twist.{/n} "But the court reads meaning into every choice, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

  - Before: "My purview also includes overseeing Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s property — the palace, the estates, the many gardens, and other demesnes on Dargonus that you have inherited from Lady Theodora. And whenever you are present on Dargonus, consider me your personal secretary."
  - After: "I also manage your inherited estates, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, and act as your secretary here."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "I am at your service at any time, day or night, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "At your service, day or night, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}You catch her avoiding your gaze for just a moment — for the first time. It's obvious that Clementia is looking out for her house's good name. But despite the confidence in her tone, you can tell that she does not entirely believe her own words.{/n}
  - After: {n}She briefly avoids your gaze, not quite believing herself.{/n}
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}Clementia raises her head proudly — she is obviously pleased with her house's accomplishments.{/n}
  - After: {n}Clementia raises her head proudly.{/n}
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Understood, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Clementia promptly makes a note on her data-slate.{/n} "Would you like to hold this meeting shortly?"
  - After: "Understood, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}She notes it.{/n} "Meet them soon?"
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Over the many centuries, an intricate hierarchy has formed within the ruling elite of Dargonus. The great houses do more than plunder your treasury — it is replenished, to a large degree, thanks to their administrative work and their lands. Naturally, you can get rid of anyone whom you consider surplus to requirements, but right now, it could threaten the fragile stability that is currently holding the protectorate together."
  - After: "The great houses fill your treasury. Removing them now risks the protectorate's fragile stability."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}Clementia immediately focuses on the data-slate in her hands.{/n} "Allow me to report — the esteemed Navigators of House Orsellio have taken residence in the guest estate and await a meeting with you. How would you like to receive them?"
  - After: {n}She checks her data-slate.{/n} "House Orsellio's Navigators await at the guest estate. How will you receive them?"
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?" {n}Clementia looks away from her data-slate.{/n} "I hope your stay on Dargonus will be beneficial to your physical and mental state. I understand that the heir to a protectorate must have {mf|his|her} hands full, but one shouldn't forget about rest."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?" {n}She looks up.{/n} "An heir has {mf|his|her} hands full, but must rest."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Then I'll have messengers sent to retrieve the esteemed guests."
  - After: "I'll send for the guests."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Members of the Navis Nobilite have little patience for long waits, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. But I'll think of something."
  - After: "The Navis Nobilite hate waiting, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I'll manage."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "I am afraid that my words may anger Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Clementia lowers her head in shame as if offering it up to be removed from her shoulders.{/n} "The seal you are looking for was lost over a quarter of a century ago. Her Ladyship Theodora von Valancius ordered a new one to be delivered from the Imperium, but... as you well know, we are a long way away from Holy Terra. And with warp storms ravaging the Koronus Expanse, we have been unable to receive a replacement to this day."
  - After: "This may anger Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}She bows her head.{/n} "The seal was lost over twenty-five years ago. Theodora ordered another, but warp storms block its delivery."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "However..." {n}She refers to her data-slate.{/n} "One of the worlds under Calligos Winterscale's rule, like Dargonus, was granted the honour of keeping the sacred sigils of the Administratum. The archives of House von Valancius mention three systems that are presently under the control of House Winterscale. Those would be the Forgotten Twins, Langrenn's Belt, and the Nameless Star. I am confident that the Administratum Palace is located on one of the planets there."
  - After: "However..." {n}She checks her data-slate.{/n} "A Winterscale world also keeps Administratum sigils, in the Forgotten Twins, Langrenn's Belt or the Nameless Star."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "The loss of the seal is certainly a great tragedy, but... self-flagellation?" {n}Jae clicks her tongue disapprovingly.{/n} "Admit it, Chancellor, you simply enjoy wallowing in pain while praising the Emperor's name.   - After: "Self-flagellation?" {n}Jae tuts.{/n} "The Exalted One wants faith, not torment, Chancellor. You follow the Ecclesiarchy like a sheep."

- **Clementia Werserian**

  - After: "Always at your service."
- **Clementia Werserian**

- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}Clementia purses her lips and glowers at Jae.{/n}
  - After: {n}Clementia glowers at Jae.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And lastly, Dargonus has its own fleet — a luxury unavailable to the vast majority of other worlds in your realm. In addition to warships, the protectorate also employs privateer ships which are used to transport cargo between worlds."
  - After: "Dargonus also has its own fleet, rare in your realm — warships and cargo privateers."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Oh no, this isn't about me at all." {n}Jae narrows her eyes as she peers into Clementia's face until the latter finally looks away.{/n} "I see. Well, Chancellor? Will you tell us yourself, or should I help you?"
  - After: "It's not about me." {n}Jae stares Clementia down.{/n} "Will you tell, Chancellor, or shall I?"
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Ah, but, shereen! What about the Mercatum Tabula Offici—"
  - After: "But, shereen! The Mercatum Tabula Offici—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I beg your forgiveness, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I should have reported this earlier, but there was never a good time. The seal Mistress Heydari is looking for was lost over a quarter of a century ago. Her Ladyship Theodora von Valancius ordered a new one to be delivered from the Imperium, but... as you well know, we are a long way away from Holy Terra. And with warp storms ravaging the Koronus Expanse, we have been unable to receive a replacement to this day."
  - After: "Forgive me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I should have said. The seal was lost over twenty-five years ago. Theodora ordered another, but warp storms block its delivery."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Hold your tongue, peddler of xenoheresy, and speak not of things you know nothing about!" {n}Clementia's words cut Jae off like the swing of a sabre. Then Clementia turns to you, her head lowered in shame.{/n}
  - After: "Silence, peddler of xenoheresy!" {n}Clementia turns to you, ashamed.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Oh, by all means, shereen! I dare not waste any more of the precious balm that is your time on matters related to me. If I may excuse myself."
  - After: "Of course, shereen! Excuse me."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Unquestionably, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Clementia accepts your words with ice-cold calmness.{/n} "At day's end, I will submit myself to self-flagellation at the Werserian family chapel. A hundred lashes — and if that won't be sufficient, I will add five dozen more."
  - After: "Unquestionably, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Ice-calm.{/n} "Tonight I'll take a hundred lashes in our chapel — sixty more if needed."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "I do not fear pain, for it offers redemption. It would benefit you to learn this lesson one day, Mistress Heydari."
  - After: "Pain redeems. Learn that, Mistress Heydari."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "I'm afraid I have to refuse, thank you."
  - After: "I'll pass, thanks."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "I shall humbly await the day when Dargonus has its seal once again."
  - After: "I'll await Dargonus's new seal."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Why, none at all, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Secretary Scalander is an outstanding individual and a loyal servant of the von Valancius dynasty. In Lady Theodora's absence, we collaborated on a number of issues related to the well-being of your domain, and he has proven himself quite capable. And, I don't know why, but even the governor trembles before Achilleas. Which is... unusual for a man of his, shall we say, standing." {n}The last word brings a slight smile to her lips.{/n}
  - After: "None, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Secretary Scalander is loyal and capable. Oddly, even the governor fears him." {n}She smiles slightly.{/n}
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, Governor Drivestem is waiting in the audience hall. I advise you to respond to his lateness in kind — that way you can let Urbend know that his behaviour has not gone unremarked. But I would not delay too long — right now, the court is closely observing your every step."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, Governor Drivestem came late; he waits in the audience hall. Make him wait too, briefly. The court watches."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}The sharp gaze, the impeccably straight back, the composure — for a moment, you feel like you're looking at a younger version of Abelard himself, not his heir. Judging by the scars on the exposed parts of her body, Clementia saw her fair share of combat prior to assuming the position of chancellor.{/n}
  - After: {n}Her bearing recalls a young Abelard; her scars show past combat.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/Dargonus/Siege/AchilleasWounded

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Hah, so that's what distracted the xenos... your appearance at the palace. I was only able to break free from their clutches because the void-damned Drukhari suddenly dropped what they were doing and ran off." {n}Achilleas's amber eyes glitter viciously as he nods at the corpses at his feet.{/n} "It was a mistake on their part to turn their backs to me."
  - After: "You distracted the Drukhari, so I broke free." {n}Achilleas eyes the corpses.{/n} "Their mistake."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/Dargonus/Siege/AchilleasWounded/AchilleasWounded_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Heinrix, help him. Use your abilities."
  - After: "Heinrix, heal him."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What happened here?"
  - After: "What happened?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Praise be to the Golden Throne and the God-Emperor, you're alive!"
  - After: "Praise the Emperor, you're alive!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "By the yawn of the darkest abyss, Achilleas, why did my expert on xenos fail to prevent the Drukhari assault?"
  - After: "Achilleas, why did my xenos expert miss this?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "They tortured you? Why?"
  - After: "Why torture you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Were you able to glean anything from your attackers?"
  - After: "Did you learn anything?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "That's enough talking, Achilleas. I will contact Clementia and have her summon a medicae. Get out of the palace while you can!"
  - After: "Enough. Clementia will summon a medicae. Go!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Strike him] "You have failed me and all of Dargonus!"
  - After: [Strike him] "You failed me and Dargonus!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Covered in Drukhari blood and his own, Achilleas Scalander looks around with a haunted expression on his face. He finally manages to focus his gaze on you and lets out a barely audible gasp.{/n} "God-Emperor preserve me... Could it be... Is it truly you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?" {n}He is struck by an excruciating coughing fit, his hand grasping for his respirator on its golden chain, but it is missing.{/n}
  - After: {n}Bloodied, Achilleas gasps.{/n} "Is it you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}?" {n}He coughs.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Rough}impassively observes{/d} Achilleas's torment. Then his lip curls as he shakes his head.{/n} "Poor show, Scalander. How could you fail to notice the impending danger? Perhaps I was wrong to have had such high hopes for you?"
  - After: {n}Heinrix {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Rough}scoffs{/d}.{/n} "Poor show, Scalander. I expected better."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "When the report came from orbit about the xenos attack, I was in the Administratum halls, resolving the matter of your succession. I rushed to my shuttle and prayed to the God-Emperor that I would reach the palace before they struck.
