  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} sent you to stop an injustice!" {n}He grimaces at his fawning.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Good {mf|sir|lady} of House von Valancius! I'm ever so glad to see at least one decent person in this crowd..." {n}His eyes narrow.{/n} "Can we talk? Support from an envoy of an esteemed dynasty could very much help... to prevent a terrible injustice from happening."
  - After: "Good {mf|sir|lady} von Valancius!" {n}His eyes narrow.{/n} "A word? You could prevent a terrible injustice."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If I was the one lying in that box, he wouldn't be crying his eyes out either," {n}Kas bites out with sudden acidity. He takes a moment to calm himself.{/n} "A son's feelings are complicated. I wasn't a good son; old Denz wasn't a good father. But I do miss him in my own way, yes. He always seemed timeless to me, not just a bag of meat and ugly ambitions like the rest of us are."
  - After: "He wouldn't cry for me either," {n}Kas snaps.{/n} "We were bad to each other. But I miss him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Well..." {n}He grimaces.{/n} "The lawful heir is being robbed of his inheritance. My dear father left his entire fortune, down to the last coin, to some nobody — a certain Fidelio, who hasn't even bothered to come to his funeral. And I'm left with nothing. Do you think it's fair?"
  - After: {n}He grimaces.{/n} "Father left everything to some Fidelio, who skipped the funeral. I get nothing. Fair?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You're nobility — you, of all people, must realise just how wrong and unacceptable this situation is. So I thought — maybe you could lend me a hand somehow? For the sake of friendship with the future keeper of the Bellardo fortune — me. And for the sake of justice, of course!"
  - After: "Help me, noble. For friendship with the future Bellardo heir. And justice!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "As if I know! The old man wasn't a heart-to-heart sort of person. Right up until the announcement of his last will and testament, I had no idea he'd put me in the doghouse."
  - After: "No idea! I learned at the will's reading."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have absolutely no idea. Zero. There's a will, there's a name — that's it. Maybe they're my father's by-blow, some brother or sister I never knew I had? Maybe they're a whore who brightened his final days? I get the feeling that old louse Chaplain knows, he's always known more about Father's business than any of us. But he's keeping quiet."
  - After: "No idea. A by-blow sibling? A whore? Old Chaplain knows, I bet, but he's silent."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I've never even been in the presence of a person of your status, let alone talked to one! But I just thought — maybe you can impose your will on the matter of the inheritance? It would be great to find out who this Fidelio is too, true, but that's nothing, that's just my curiosity..."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, could you sway the inheritance? And learn who Fidelio is?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Put a word in for me, suggest that they go over the will one more time... You're an envoy of House von Valancius, after all, and Footfall respects that name. And, well, it would be nice to find out who this Fidelio is too."
  - After: "Have them review the will. Footfall respects House von Valancius. And find Fidelio."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He bows.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, thank you! I don't know how to thank you for your kindness — but I'll definitely try if it all works out!"
  - After: {n}He bows.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, thank you! I'll repay you!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Much obliged! And know that I'll make it worth your while. If I get the inheritance, I'll express my gratitude in whatever way I can."
  - After: "Much obliged! If I inherit, I'll show my gratitude."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He slumps a little.{/n} "That's that, then... It's just not my day. When is it ever?"
  - After: {n}He slumps.{/n} "Not my day. As ever."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "To turn a funeral rite into a stepping stone for one's covetous desires is blasphemy. To dispute the will of the dead is doubly blasphemous." {n}Kibellah's dark eyes seem to burn right through the man, making him swallow nervously and avert his gaze.{/n}
  - After: "Greed at a funeral is blasphemy. Disputing the dead's will, doubly so." {n}Kibellah's stare cows him.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My dear Fidelio, leaving already? And you won't even stay to see the old man burn — I mean, laid to rest?"
  - After: "Fidelio, leaving before the old man burns, I mean, rests?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Pardon me. Kas Bellardo. I have the honour of being the only child of the deceased." {n}He sends a mocking salute in the direction of the coffin.{/n}
  - After: "Kas Bellardo, the only child." {n}He mock-salutes the coffin.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Ha ha, ha ha ha, that's hilarious. Even good old Chaplain doesn't tell me to repent — he gave up on me long ago. And my old dad, he gave up on me long before that!" {n}He laughs nervously.{/n} "Wait... you mean that 'repentance'? Those stupid ghosts or whatever it was? I'm pretty sure my father did it himself, the senile old kook, or maybe it was my daughter messing around. Where else could those words have come from?"
  - After: "Ha! Everyone gave up on my repenting." {n}He laughs nervously.{/n} "Oh, the 'Repentance' ghosts? Father did it himself, or my daughter."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He forces a smile.{/n} "That you were... very close with... ah, forget it! I didn't mean anything by it. Just making conversation."
  - After: {n}He forces a smile.{/n} "That you were close with... forget it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh, you don't know? Out of the blue, writing started appearing on a wall in our house, just one word — 'Repentance.' Big, sprawling scribbles, like a child's handwriting. The first one appeared about ten or so years back. The help kept whispering about it being the work of ghosts, woooh! But for some reason the old man didn't want to do anything about it, and he told me not to. The writing amused him somehow. Whenever he'd see 'Repentance' scratched on the wall, he'd just grin."
  - After: "'Repentance' began appearing on our wall in childlike scrawl ten years back. The old man let it stay. It made him grin."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Age. Debauchery. Old wounds. By the end, my old dad was more {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implant{/g} than man. Especially after the assassination attempt — people tried to kill him, you see, about twelve years ago."
  - After: "Age, debauchery, old wounds. More {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implant{/g} than man after the assassination attempt twelve years ago."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What, am I supposed to die... at my own father's funeral? Ha ha. No, I don't think I will!"
  - After: "Die at my father's funeral? I think not!"

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/Footfall/Atrium/UnderworldQuest/RealFidelio/RealFidelio_Footfall_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: "Chaplain? Is everything clear to you now?"
  - After: "Chaplain? Is it clear now?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Can a servitor even inherit?"
  - After: "Can a servitor inherit?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Summon everyone. It is time to decide the fate of Bellardo's estate — and that of the heirs."
  - After: "Summon everyone. Time to decide the estate and the heirs."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}If you didn't know what to look for, it would be easy to overlook this {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitor{/g}, which may have once been a woman. The servitor's implants, the mechanical nature of its movements, the empty gaze — it's all there. But...{/n}
  - After: {n}A {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitor{/g}, once a woman. Empty gaze. But...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}That single word causes the servitor's body to twist in a violent spasm. Something akin to a sob or a growl builds in its throat, and its mechanical appendages jerk convulsively.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servitor spasms, half sob, half growl.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Servitors are the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}'s stepchildren. That's what they say in my homeland. Shouldn't the inheritance go to the parent? Their representative, to be specific." {n}Jae somehow manages to cast Pasqal a glance that is both conspiratorial and pleading.{/n}
  - After: "Servitors are the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}'s stepchildren. So His representative inherits?" {n}Jae eyes Pasqal.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I have not encountered this statement before and I am unwilling to endorse it. Poetic platitudes, though they may seem innocuous, can be a false visage for perverse interpretations of His tenets." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-synthesiser suddenly starts malfunctioning, causing Pasqal's timbre to jump like a fooling jester.{/n}
  - After: "I will not endorse that. Platitudes mask heresy." {n}His {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} glitches.{/n}
- **Chaplain**
  - Before: {n}Chaplain's tall figure appears next to you.{/n} "So this is our heir! Right?" {n}He pauses, mulling it over, then gestures for the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratum}Administratum{/g} clerk who gave the opening speech to approach.{/n} "The inventory of Denz's possessions, what does it say about this servitor?"
  - After: {n}Chaplain appears.{/n} "Our heir?" {n}He calls the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratum}Administratum{/g} clerk.{/n} "What does Denz's inventory say?"
- **Clerk**
  - Before: "Let's see here, let's see... one moment... mmhmm, mmhmm... Section B17/40, 'Personal Effects of the Deceased,' subsection 'Servitors'... Here it is!"
  - After: "One moment... Here!"
- **Chaplain**
  - Before: "I believe so. Didn't I tell you that Denz, after he survived the assassination attempt, sent a whole squad of mercenaries to hunt down the woman who tried to kill him? Looks like he found her." {n}Chaplain nods at the servitor.{/n}
  - After: "Yes. Denz hunted down his would-be assassin. He found her." {n}He nods at the servitor.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Silence. The servitor's eyelids flutter slightly, its gaze staring off into space. Deep inside its single human eye, dark as a well, a spark seems to flicker... or is it just your imagination?{/n}
  - After: {n}Silence. A spark in its eye?{/n}
- **Chaplain**
  - Before: "She was allowed to keep her memory and some semblance of awareness, so I suppose the mysterious writing of 'Repentance' both here in the book and back at Denz's home was done by her. The question that remains, of course, is why would Denz decide to make a servitor his heir? This is either his last and cruellest joke — or an incredibly ham-fisted attempt to make amends on his deathbed. I'd like to believe that it's the former."
  - After: "She kept her memory and wrote 'Repentance,' here and at Denz's home. Why make her heir? A cruel joke, or clumsy amends?"
- **Chaplain**
  - Before: "Or — we could ask {mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius to settle the matter in the name of {mf|his|her} dynasty. This is Footfall, after all. If a {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} says that a servitor can inherit — then that's how it's going to be."
  - After: "Or {mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius decides for {mf|his|her} dynasty. On Footfall, a {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}'s word is law."
- **Clerk**
  - Before: "Oh, this is a rare, one-of-a-kind unit! Commissioned personally by Master Bellardo twelve years ago! The main function of this servitor is cleaning the house, bedrooms, vestibules, bathrooms... In accordance with Master Bellardo's wishes, its free will was completely eradicated, and the parts of its brain that regulated pleasure responses were destroyed... but to a large extent, its memory and awareness were preserved!"
  - After: "A unique cleaning unit Bellardo commissioned twelve years ago! Free will and pleasure destroyed, memory and awareness kept!"
- **Clerk**
  - Before: "Th-this matter requires further investigation... We will have to go over the codices, bylaws, statutes, regulations... from the last four hundred years or so." {n}The clerk pales a little.{/n} "But we'll find the answer sooner or later!"
  - After: "Th-that means centuries of statutes." {n}The clerk pales.{/n} "We'll find out!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Were this not a gathering of criminal rabble, maybe I'd make an effort to recall the inheritance laws in effect on Footfall. But seeing as that is what you are..." {n}Solomorne cracks his neck.{/n} "...you're fresh out of luck."
  - After: "No inheritance law for criminals." {n}Solomorne cracks his neck.{/n} "Tough luck."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Drifting toward the servitor, Eogunn runs his auspex across the servitor's entire frame with surprising meticulousness, staring closely at the readouts.{/n} "That is indeed true. The behavioural patterns of this servitor have severely degraded due to an irreconcilable conflict between consciousness and augmetics. It is imprudent to leave a personality within a vessel whose volition is entirely supplanted by the imperatives of the sacred iron."
  - After: {n}Eogunn scans it with his auspex.{/n} "Confirmed. Mind and augmetics conflict. Cruel to leave a personality inside."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Yet, a narrow mind frequently bars the path to knowledge. Reflect upon this, esteemed colleague." {n}Jae flashes the Manipulus a grateful smile.{/n}
  - After: "Yet a narrow mind bars knowledge." {n}Jae smiles gratefully.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/Footfall/Atrium/UnderworldQuest/ScionDaughter/ScionDaughter_Footfall_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: "Have you ever heard the name Fidelio?"
  - After: "Heard the name Fidelio?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Who are you and what are you doing here?"
  - After: "Who are you? Why are you here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Someone left some strange words in the book of remembrance, as if they were from Fidelio. That wasn't your doing by any chance?"
  - After: "Did you write Fidelio's words in the remembrance book?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I must take my leave. Goodbye."
  - After: "I must go. Goodbye."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Did your grandfather ever mention the word repentance to you?"
  - After: "Did your grandfather mention repentance?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The girl dressed in expensive clothes raises her sad little face to you and says in a serious voice,{/n} "Hello."
  - After: {n}A finely dressed girl looks up sadly.{/n} "Hello."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "He did. That word kept appearing in our house, and nobody knew who wrote it. It used to make Grandpa happy when I was little. He always smiled when he saw it! But then... later, when I was a little bigger and Grandpa was already old... it stopped making him happy. He was sad. He would just sit there and stare at nothing. And after that, when he got sick..." {n}She stops, her big eyes glistening with tears.{/n}
  - After: "It kept appearing at home. Grandpa smiled at it, later grew sad. Then sick..." {n}Her eyes glisten.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "When he got sick, the writing started to scare him. More and more of it appeared. 'Repentance, repentance, repentance.' Even in his bedroom! One time, he pointed at that word... and said something... something very weird... About dead eyes. And about cobras going to class."
  - After: "Then it scared him. Once he pointed at it and spoke of dead eyes. And cobras going to class."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Adelia tries to smile, then just nods seriously.{/n}
  - After: {n}Adelia nods seriously.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Hiding." {n}She hesitates for a moment.{/n} "I thought I was going to cry, and I didn't want anyone to see. I... my name is Adelia Bellardo. It's my grandpa in there, in the box."
  - After: "Hiding my tears." {n}She hesitates.{/n} "I'm Adelia Bellardo. That's Grandpa in the box."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard, who was looking at her with sympathy, narrows his eyes.{/n} "What did you say? Cobras going to class? Are you sure this is what your grandfather said?"
  - After: {n}Abelard narrows his eyes.{/n} "Cobras going to class? Sure?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The girl raises her serious and sad eyes to you.{/n}
  - After: {n}She looks up sadly.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard strokes his beard.{/n} "Perhaps this is the old {g|Encyclopedia:ImperialNavy}Navy{/g} officer in me talking, but I am almost certain he wasn't talking about a snake, but a Cobra-class destroyer. 'Cobra' going to 'class,' you see?"
  - After: {n}Abelard strokes his beard.{/n} "Spoken like an old {g|Encyclopedia:ImperialNavy}Navy{/g} man: a Cobra-class destroyer."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It's someone my dad is very mad at. But Dad is always mad at everyone — at Grandpa, Mum, Daggen, Chaplain..."
  - After: "Someone Dad hates. Dad hates everyone."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Ha. That would've been a funny prank!" {n}Her eyes light up a little.{/n} "But I don't play pranks. It was someone else. Maybe Fidelio did it, very quietly? Or maybe it was someone who's not on the list, but also someone nobody would suspect?"
  - After: "Ha!" {n}Her eyes light up.{/n} "Not me. Fidelio? Someone unsuspected?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My dad is Kas Bellardo. He's with the guests. And my mum ran away, they told me she hates Dad and Grandpa. I guess she hates me too, I don't know. It was a long time ago, I don't even miss her anymore. I miss Grandpa... He was the nicest." {n}She presses her lips together and lets out a quiet, very unchildlike sigh.{/n}
  - After: "Dad's Kas Bellardo. Mum ran off. I miss Grandpa most." {n}She sighs.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Her last phrase stirs your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Navy}memories{/d}. No, this naive child's tale has nothing to do with reptiles... "Class," "cobras"... It seems her mind has distorted her late grandfather's words — he must have been talking about a voidship. More specifically, about a Cobra-class destroyer.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Navy}memories{/d} stir: he meant a Cobra-class destroyer.{/n}
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "If you do not wish to be parted from your forefather, then sever his head, embalm it, and put it in your bed." {n}Kibellah's voice sounds mundane, like she is explaining the most basic things.{/n} "Speak to him before you go to sleep and after you wake up, and that way he will stay with you."
  - After: "Embalm his severed head and keep it in bed." {n}Kibellah is matter-of-fact.{/n} "Talk to it."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta's face softens. She reaches out and gently strokes Adelia's head.{/n} "The tears will pass, Adelia. The tears will pass, the strength will return, and your courage will never leave you."
  - After: {n}Argenta strokes Adelia's head.{/n} "The tears will pass. Your courage won't."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Wh-what?" {n}Adelia shrinks away fearfully, looking to you for protection.{/n}
  - After: "Wh-what?" {n}Adelia shrinks toward you.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Don't listen to the lady. The lady is nuts. Like, properly off her rocker. Listen to your elders, eat your breakfast, and don't cut off your grandpa's head."
  - After: "Ignore the nutty lady. Eat breakfast, keep grandpa's head on."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Of course I'm sure. When Grandpa was ill, I sat with him, and this one time he just started talking about cobras. I was sad, but it was also a little funny. 'Cobra, get to class!' he said."
  - After: "Sure. He said, 'Cobra, get to class!'"

  - After: {n}Pasqal studies it.{/n} "Denied. It defiles Ferrum Sanctum."

  - Before: "It doesn't take a fortune-teller to figure out the specifics of that mission..."
  - After: "Easy guess, that mission..."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Hang on, you can just say no?"
  - After: "You can say no?"

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/Footfall/Atrium/UnderworldQuest/Slyboots/Slyboots_Footfall_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: "Wait, so you hid valuables in the crematorium's furnace?"
  - After: "You hid valuables in the crematorium furnace?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I refuse to have any part in this."
  - After: "I'll have no part in this."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will help you on the following condition. You see, I am — most definitely — {mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio. I'm afraid I've misplaced some of my documents. If you make me a copy of everything you can find in the archives that has my name on it — you'll get your contraband."
  - After: "One condition. I am, most definitely, {mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio, and I've lost my papers. Copy everything in the archives with my name, and you'll get your contraband."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why did you decide to ask me specifically for help?"
  - After: "Why ask me?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do you need from me and what are you offering in return?"
  - After: "What do you need, and what do you offer?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You hear someone delicately clearing their throat. The source of this sound turns out to be the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratum}Administratum{/g} clerk you saw next to Chaplain. His clothes are neat and impeccably pressed. His face, however, reveals extreme nervousness bordering on fear.{/n} "My good {mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio! I do hope you're satisfied with the services provided by our establishment?"
  - After: {n}Chaplain's {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusAdministratum}Administratum{/g} clerk coughs, neat but terrified.{/n} "{mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio! Satisfied with our services?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I had just prepared the newest batch of superb, unique implants of the highest quality. But I got careless! I used my first sick leave in four standard years! And it was on that very day that Master Bellardo passed away, and his family was quick to organise a ceremony in our crematorium... I simply didn't have time to prepare. And now my container full of goods — it's in the furnace, and if you don't help me, they're going to burn it any minute!"
  - After: "I took my first sick day in four years, and Bellardo died that day. My new batch is still in the furnace, and they'll burn it any minute!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Therefore, I am forced — practically forced! — to look for other sources of income that allow me to stay within the walls of this here establishment. I've set up a little, shall we say, enterprise — I replace the {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g} of the deceased with identical replicas and sell them to the right people when I have a shipment ready."
  - After: "So I swap the dead's {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g} for replicas and sell the originals."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "While there's still time, could you please get to the furnace and pull the container with implants out of there? We'll split the goods fifty-fifty, you can even have first pick! Just please, hurry! They'll soon be putting the coffin with old Bellardo where it belongs, and then... poof! It will be reduced to ash, and my priceless augmetics along with it!"
  - After: "Pull my implant container from the furnace before Bellardo's coffin goes in! Fifty-fifty, you pick first. Hurry!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Such a shame, such a terrible shame... but if you change your mind — just pop into the furnace and get the container out. It's in the far corner, you can't miss it!"
  - After: "A shame... It's in the furnace's far corner, if you change your mind."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "{g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Throne{/g} preserve you! Make it look like you're just having a look around — it's a lot easier for you to wander into a restricted area without arousing suspicion than it is for me. Find the container — it's in the far corner — get out and come back to me! I'll be waiting!"
  - After: "{g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Throne{/g} preserve you! Act like you're browsing. Far corner. I'll wait!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He leans in a little closer and whispers,{/n} "I beg of you... help me! But please keep your voice down, we can't let anyone hear us... It's a matter of life and death!"
  - After: {n}He whispers,{/n} "Help me! Quietly. It's life and death!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The clerk wipes the sweat from his brow nervously.{/n} "Please understand, it's very difficult to get by on Footfall with my wages! And Imperial regulation 4030/8L 'On Postmortal Service Workers on Peripheral Worlds' directly prohibits the chief operator of the crematorium from leaving their workplace for any reason other than sleep, food, severe illness, and ministration of sacraments."
  - After: {n}He wipes sweat away.{/n} "My wages are meagre, and regulation 4030/8L forbids me to leave the crematorium except to sleep, eat, for illness or sacraments."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I've been hiding them there for ten years now, and quite successfully, I might add! Only the richest citizens can afford the services of a crematorium, and, sadly, they don't die all that often. Usually I sell the goods before the next body arrives. But I got unlucky this time. Help me, I beg of you!"
  - After: "For ten years! Only the rich get cremated, and they rarely die. Not lucky this time. Please!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Of course... of course, will do! You'll be most pleased with the results! Just help me, for {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Throne{/g}'s sake..."
  - After: "Of course! Just help me, for {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Throne{/g}'s sake..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There's no one else to turn to!" {n}The clerk exclaims in dismay.{/n} "All the guests here are scoundrels, murderers, or crooks — or all three at once! I was going to send in a {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitor{/g}, but only personal servitors of House Bellardo are allowed into the courtyard today, and I don't have their access codes. You're all I have left! And I can tell you're an upstanding individual... with a most noble countenance, too! The moment I saw you, I knew — {mf|he|she} is the one who will save me!"
  - After: "Who else?" {n}He's dismayed.{/n} "The guests are all crooks! Only Bellardo {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitor{/g}s may enter. I knew {mf|he|she} would save me!"

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/Footfall/Atrium/UnderworldQuest/Squatters/Squatters_Footfall_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "Die, human refuse!"
  - After: [Attack] "Die, refuse!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Give alms] "I'm feeling kind today. Here, for your help with the fire."
  - After: [Give alms] "Here, for putting out the fire."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Who are you and what are you doing down here?"
  - After: "Who are you? Why are you here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you happen to know who Fidelio is?"
  - After: "Do you know Fidelio?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How do I get out of here?"
  - After: "How do I get out?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I must take my leave."
  - After: "I must go."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "They're on fire! On fire! Put them out, put them out, quick!" {n}The voices come to you through streams of something thick and foul — your eyes are covered with whatever your unbidden saviours saw fit to splash over your head.{/n}
  - After: "On fire! Put them out!" {n}Something foul splashes your face.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}At last, you can make out the silhouette of a vagrant dressed in rags leaning over you. He throws up his hands.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordiness|Ladyness}, are you all right? Did you hit anything? Any bad burns? You fell right through that there ceiling, and it's mighty high up!"
  - After: {n}A ragged vagrant leans over you.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordiness|Ladyness}, hurt? You fell through the ceiling!"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The fact that the incompetence of the crematorium's maintenance staff saved our lives does not make their negligence any less egregious. I will register a complaint."
  - After: "Their negligence saved us, but I will complain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The vagrants' faces brighten, and they accept your handout with a bow.{/n} "Oh, thank you, thank you kindly! Something to buy a bit of food with. 'Cause, well, we used our soup to put you out, you see. And it was only two days old!"
  - After: {n}The vagrants bow.{/n} "Thank you! We used our soup on you!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We live here, is all... Your {mf|Lordiness|Ladyness}. You see, these are old tunnels, they dug 'em back in Parsimus Dewain's times, right through the asteroid. It's a little stuffy down here, but it's warmer than up in the big palaces on the surface."
  - After: "We live here, Your {mf|Lordiness|Ladyness}. Old tunnels from Parsimus Dewain's day. Warmer than the palaces."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And it sure is warm under the crematorium's furnace! They barely burn anyone up there, but they do fire it up often enough — and that's good for us... sure, sometimes an odd smell makes it through the vents, like they're making roast — makes yer mouth water! But what can you do... that's the cost of comfort for ya!"
  - After: "Warmest under the furnace! Smells like roast sometimes."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The vagrants look at each other in surprise.{/n} "I mean, wasn't there that Fid lad, used to live under the Fifth Void? And his hussy kept yellin' all like, 'My Fiiido!'? Fidelio, Fid — same deal, right?"
  - After: {n}They exchange looks.{/n} "There was a Fid under the Fifth Void. Same thing?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Well, there's no climbing back into the crematorium for ya — look for yourself, it's all burnt and collapsed. But it's no biggie! There's only one way up there, so you won't get lost. First you'll need to pull this big old lever to open the doors. It's by the busted pipe — that's where the lever is. After that, you just walk. Through the corridors, the shaft, the old warehouse. And there you are, on the surface."
  - After: "The crematorium way's collapsed. Pull the lever by the busted pipe, then go through the corridors, shaft and old warehouse to the surface."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "All the best on your journey and all! May the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} help ya and guide you out!"
  - After: "Good luck! {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} guide you!"

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/Footfall/Atrium/UnderworldQuest/SwindlerClerks/SwindlerClerks_Footfall_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: "Honourless, spineless, godless whelps! And you have the gall to call yourselves Imperium subjects? You scoundrels aren't even worthy of a bolt to the head from me — which is a privilege granted to any cowardly weasel on the front lines!"
  - After: "Honourless, godless whelps! Imperium subjects? You aren't even worthy of a bolt to the head, a privilege any front-line coward gets!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "And just who are you and what are you doing in here?"
  - After: "Who are you, and what are you doing here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Look, all I did was stop by a funeral and introduce myself as Fidelio. Because of this, some people have attempted to burn me alive, others have drenched me in swill, and now thieving utility workers want to murder me. This is starting to feel like a bad joke. How about I just go on my merry way?"
  - After: "I said I was Fidelio at a funeral. Since then I've been nearly burned alive, drenched in swill, and now threatened by thieving utility workers. A bad joke. How about I just leave?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "You dare threaten one of the von Valancius dynasty. You will pay for this."
  - After: [Attack] "You threaten a von Valancius? You'll pay."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Move it, I said move it! If the inspection gets to the circuit station before we do — I'll have all of you recycled!"
  - After: "Move! Beat the inspection to the circuit station!"
- **Clerk**
  - Before: "Yelling your brains out at {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitors{/g} won't make them work faster."
  - After: "Yelling won't speed {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitors{/g}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You know another way to get the lazy brutes to shift themselves? Well, I'm all ears! If the inspection sees a circuit station without a unit, they'll go to Vladaym with this. And if Vladaym finds out, he won't mince words. He'll give us the old 'Kasballican severance.' As in, kick us out the trash chute without a void suit!"
  - After: "If inspectors find a station without a unit, Vladaym spaces us!"
- **Clerk**
  - Before: "Simmer down, we'll be fine. Back in my transport days, I'd show the inspection the same protection screen on eight different sites — and I never got busted once. I seriously doubt that Vladaym's inspectors are any more diligent. They'll fall for our one support unit on three circuit stations, they won't notice a thing. Better worry about selling the two units that we borr— who the Throne is that?"
  - After: "Relax. One unit for three stations fools them. Sell the two we borr— Throne, who's that?"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah turns to Pasqal and smiles faintly.{/n} "Now I can take them. Now I hear their names."
  - After: {n}Kibellah smiles at Pasqal.{/n} "Now I hear their names."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Fidelio? I've no idea who that is..."
  - After: "Fidelio? No idea..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The two strangers glance at each other in disbelief and reach for their weapons.{/n}
  - After: {n}They reach for weapons.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We're from Footfall Station Services, carrying out scheduled maintenance... but you're not gonna believe that, are you? You heard everything."
  - After: "Station Services... but you heard everything."
- **Clerk**
  - Before: {n}After glancing briefly at his partner, the man lays a hand on his weapon.{/n} "I promised my wife I could go a month without murder... too bad. I'd rather break my word than get on the Liege's bad side."
  - After: {n}He draws.{/n} "Sorry, wife. No crossing the Liege."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The two of them look at each other.{/n} "Hmph. Sure, by all means, go right ahead."
  - After: {n}They exchange looks.{/n} "Sure, go ahead."
- **Clerk**
  - Before: {n}Then they immediately point their guns at you.{/n} "Just kidding. Ha ha ha! Sorry, but it's the trash chute for you!"
  - After: {n}They aim.{/n} "Kidding! Trash chute!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Course you won't — dead men tell no tales."
  - After: "Dead men tell no tales."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Von V— bah, whatever! We'll worry about that later!"
  - After: "Von V— bah, later!"
- **Pasqal**

  - After: {n}Pasqal turns to Kibellah.{/n} "The Undying One has catalogued them. Kill them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Hey! That... That's not true, I am worthy!"
  - After: "Hey! I am worthy!"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "This goes beyond a violation of the Rite of Operation. It downright stinks."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/Footfall/Atrium/UnderworldQuest/YouDeadFidelio/YouDeadFidelio_Footfall_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: [Point at the servitor] "Who among you knows this woman? What about the story of the ship named Repentance? I wish to hear it all."
  - After: [Point at the servitor] "Who knows this woman? And the ship Repentance?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have no use for this wealth. Do with it as you see fit, Chaplain."
  - After: "I don't need this wealth. Use it, Chaplain."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Again people want to kill me without saying why."
  - After: "Killing me again without saying why."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I don't quite know how to explain it to you all, but I'm not actually Fidelio."
  - After: "I'm not actually Fidelio."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I find that Kas Bellardo should inherit the fortune by right of blood."
  - After: "Kas Bellardo inherits by right of blood."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "Oh well. Let's get this over with, I suppose."
  - After: [Attack] "Oh well. Let's get this over with."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "I'll take my chances with the gun!"
  - After: [Attack] "I'll risk the gun!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address Fidelio the Servitor] "Today you will watch your enemies die."
  - After: [Address Fidelio the Servitor] "Watch your enemies die."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Daggen, Denz's mate, deserves to be the heir."
  - After: "Daggen, Denz's mate, deserves it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am Fidelio, and I wish to claim my inheritance."
  - After: "I am Fidelio. I claim my inheritance."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Kas, get out of my sight. The rest of you — prepare to die. It is time to purge this world of some of its pirate scum."
  - After: "Kas, get lost. The rest of you pirate scum — die."
- **Player**
  - Before: "None among you deserve pity. You will die. All of you."
  - After: "No pity. You all die."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Treat their wounds. I'm not in a killing mood."
  - After: "Treat their wounds. No more killing."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I still have a question. Who — in the name of the Golden Throne — is Fidelio?"
  - After: "Who — by the Golden Throne — is Fidelio?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Take care of her, Chaplain. Let her live the rest of her life as peacefully as possible."
  - After: "Care for her, Chaplain. Let her live in peace."
- **Player**
  - Before: [End her] "Farewell, Fidelio. Both you and the Repentance have been avenged."
  - After: [End her] "Farewell, Fidelio. You and the Repentance are avenged."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have other business to attend to."
  - After: "I have other business."
- **Player**
  - Before: "That pirate scum doesn't deserve the honour of my attendance. I'm leaving."
  - After: "Pirate scum doesn't deserve my attendance. I'm leaving."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Master or Mistress Fidelio! If you are here now — come forth and lay your claim to the inheritance!"
  - After: "Fidelio! If you're here, claim your inheritance!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What happens to the girl now?"
  - After: "What happens to the girl?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "That takes care of the inheritance. What do we do next?"
  - After: "Inheritance settled. What next?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "There is still the unresolved matter of Denz's inheritance."
  - After: "Denz's inheritance is still unresolved."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Then so be it! I am Fidelio, and the inheritance is mine!"
  - After: "So be it! I am Fidelio — the inheritance is mine!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The only one here who truly loved Denz is his granddaughter, Adelia Bellardo. She inherits his fortune."
  - After: "Only Adelia Bellardo, his granddaughter, loved Denz. She inherits."
- **Player**
  - Before: "That was a good shot."
  - After: "Good shot."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am the Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, and as such, I am vested with complete authority on Footfall. I hereby exercise that authority by voiding the will of the pirate Denz Bellardo and confiscating his fortune in its entirety."
  - After: "As Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, with full authority on Footfall, I void pirate Denz Bellardo's will and confiscate his fortune."
- **Player**
  - Before: "A fascinating tale. That is all I have to say."
  - After: "Fascinating tale. That's all."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It's all in the past, let us not spill any more blood. Chaplain, take care of this poor soul. May she live out her days in peace."
  - After: "No more blood. Chaplain, care for her; let her live in peace."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As soon as you appear, a dozen eyes — and guns — shift in your direction. The guests of the ceremony no longer pretend to be peaceful mourners. They are, however, stunned to see you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eyes and guns turn to you. The mourners are stunned.{/n}
- **First Mate Daggen**
  - Before: "I don't believe it... You had the nerve to come back? After your tumble through the flames?"
  - After: "You came back? After the flames?"
- **Kas Bellardo**
  - Before: "Listen, Daggen. I hate you, you hate me. But maybe we can set aside our differences? For the sake of our mutual... target, so to speak." {n}The man nods at you and narrows his eyes ominously.{/n}
  - After: "Daggen, truce? For our mutual target." {n}He eyes you.{/n}
- **First Mate Daggen**
  - Before: "Finally, boy, you're showing some signs of being your father's son. Denz would never beat around the bush with rivals. Shoot their head off and be done with it! Anyway, I accept your proposal." {n}He aims his weapon at you.{/n} "We've tried killing you quietly, that didn't work out, so we'll just kill you, plain and simple like. This is Footfall, for Throne's sake! Bye-bye, Fidelio."
  - After: "Like your father at last, boy. Deal." {n}He aims.{/n} "Bye-bye, Fidelio."
- **Chaplain**
  - Before: "And so, according to the deceased's will, all of Bellardo's fortune goes... not to his worthless son Kas. Not to his brainless mate Daggen. But to Fidelio — a mysterious new heir. However, I believe a certain party would like to intervene in this process." {n}Chaplain looks straight at you and chuckles.{/n}
  - After: "The will leaves everything not to Kas or Daggen, but to Fidelio, a mystery heir. Someone objects, though." {n}He chuckles at you.{/n}
- **First Mate Daggen**
  - Before: "Don't play dumb. Denz, the weasel, left all his money to you — a whole lotta money! I don't know why and I don't want to know, but I think it was very, very wrong of him to forget his old friend. I've got no choice but to fight for justice! So you're going to sit quietly under lock and key while I discuss my share of the inheritance. Isn't that right?"
  - After: "Don't play dumb. Denz left you everything. You'll sit locked up while I take my share."
- **First Mate Daggen**
  - Before: "Anyway, the three of us sat there — me, Denz, and the captain of the Repentance — as the boys brought whoever was left of their crew, one by one — and we popped them. I bet Cockeye over there remembers, he was there too, and so were the Twins." {n}Daggen nods at a few of the guests.{/n}
  - After: "Me, Denz and their captain sat while the boys brought his crew one by one, and we popped them. Cockeye and the Twins saw." {n}He nods at guests.{/n}
- **Kas Bellardo**
  - Before: "Anyone would say that looking down the barrels of a dozen guns."
  - After: "Anyone would say that at gunpoint."
- **Servitor**
  - Before: {n}Fidelio is standing in a typical servitor pose, eyes staring into space. Only the grips of its metallic appendage are trembling slightly — perhaps caused by a malfunction, or perhaps by suppressed emotions looking for release.{/n}
  - After: {n}Fidelio stands blankly, grips trembling.{/n}
- **Kas Bellardo**
  - Before: "Come now, Daggen, let's give the {mf|man|lady} an explanation before {mf|his|her} death. You see, {mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio, my late father — Denz, daemons take him, Bellardo — has bequeathed his entire fortune to you. Not to me, his only son, not to his first mate — you. So where does that leave us? You must die."
  - After: "Explain before {mf|his|her} death, Daggen — the {mf|man|lady} deserves it. {mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio, Denz left you everything. So you die."
- **Chaplain**
  - Before: {n}Chaplain looks at the carnage around him matter-of-factly.{/n} "Wonderful. This is a funeral Denz would be proud of!"
  - After: {n}Chaplain, unmoved.{/n} "Wonderful. Denz would be proud!"
- **Kas Bellardo**
  - Before: {n}Kas Bellardo clutches his wounded body.{/n} "The crematorium's going to have its hands full today..."
  - After: {n}Kas clutches his wounds.{/n} "Busy crematorium today..."
- **First Mate Daggen**
  - Before: {n}Daggen lifts his bloodied face.{/n} "Agh... It hurts..."
  - After: {n}Daggen, bloodied.{/n} "Agh... It hurts..."
- **Chaplain**
  - Before: "As it is written in the will. So be it! I will see to all the formalities and make sure you receive all the deeds to the property."
  - After: "As the will says. I'll handle the deeds."
- **Chaplain**
  - Before: {n}Chaplain looks at the coffin.{/n} "I would like to say goodbye to my old friend."
  - After: {n}He eyes the coffin.{/n} "Goodbye, old friend."
- **Chaplain**
  - Before: {n}Chaplain is observing the carnage, unfazed.{/n} "Denz would approve of a funeral like this. Now what? What are we going to do with Fidelio?"
  - After: {n}Chaplain, unfazed.{/n} "Denz would approve. Now, what about Fidelio?"
- **Chaplain**
  - Before: "If Fidelio were here, if they were to know about their status as the heir — they would have made themselves known by now. And if it's not you, {mf|sir|ma'am}, then I suppose we'll never know the truth. But we can make our own truth, can't we? We're on Footfall, names and ideas are traded and used here in every way imaginable. And so all that remains is to recognise you as Fidelio."

  - Before: {n}The servitor that was once a woman is kneeling, motionless, and showing no signs of life. There are two charred holes where the eyes once were — some malfunction must have burned its brain from the inside. Its face bears a peaceful smile.{/n}

  - Before: "I don't know about the servitor — I've got better things to do in life than look at furniture. And the ship... hmm... I think there was one Cobra by that name or something similar. - **First Mate Daggen**
  - Before: "Planning to leave us after all, {mf|Master|Mistress} Fidelio?" {n}His voice is quiet, but any hint of courtesy is gone. Once more, everyone's eyes focus on you — as their hands reach for their weapons.{/n}

If you don't want to go boom — my boys will escort you to a small, cosy room nearby where you'll stay for the next hour or two while I say my goodbyes to my pal Denz... and claim my share of the inheritance, everything I deserve for our years of friendship."
  - After: "My boys' gun will blast you to the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g}." {n}He smirks.{/n} "Or they lock you up an hour while I bury Denz and claim my share."

  - After: "Then we torched the captain alive on his crew's bodies. Good times... Shame Denz went 'peaceful'. Might've lived twenty more years."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/Footfall/Cantina/DepressedHistorian/DepressedHistorian_Footfall_dialog

  - After: "Tragic. I wish I could see Footfall as its creator envisioned."

  - Before: "But you're an architectural historian. Is what happened to Footfall not part of its history?"
  - After: "You're an architectural historian. Isn't Footfall's fate part of its history?"

  - Before: "You look deeply despondent over something. What happened?"
  - After: "You look despondent. What happened?"

  - Before: "I must take my leave. Good luck to you!"
  - After: "I must go. Good luck!"

  - After: "I found a nook in the lantern, with clues to other caches."

  - After: "Puzzle solved — how about becoming my resident architecture expert? See dozens of worlds aboard my ship!"

  - Before: "Tell me about the places these riddles lead to."
  - After: "Where do the riddles lead?"

  - Before: "A compelling cautionary tale! If there was a book on the folly of chasing wild fantasies, you would take up a whole chapter."
  - After: "A fine cautionary tale! You'd fill a chapter on the folly of chasing fantasies."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Have you not tried to make this wondrous discovery for yourself?"
  - After: "Haven't you searched yourself?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The flabby man in worn clothes is sighing sadly over a glass of murky booze. Only when he looks up at you do you notice his eyes — large, piercing, and full of sorrow, a stark contrast to his unkempt appearance.{/n} "Could it be that someone actually wishes to keep me company?"
  - After: {n}A shabby man with sorrowful, piercing eyes sighs over his drink.{/n} "Company? For me?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Allow me to introduce myself. Gordei Skatov, architectural historian."
  - After: "Gordei Skatov, architectural historian."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Most certainly. Footfall and I, we both serve as excellent warnings to those who would indulge their flights of fancy."
  - After: "Indeed. Footfall and I both warn dreamers."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Be that as it may, I just wanted to say... Thank you for hearing me out! Over the dozen years I have spent on Footfall, not one person has hung around long enough to listen to my story to the end. It's such a delight to have shared everything that's been weighing on my mind!"
  - After: "Thank you! In twelve years, no one heard me out."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm poor as a church mouse, but I still have something to offer you as a token of my appreciation! After studying the booklet thoroughly, I discovered something interesting — a ciphered message scattered throughout its pages. Taking the form of a riddle, it described certain places of interest on Footfall. I believe it is the work of the booklet's creators. What if these riddles lead to something? A wondrous discovery? I will gladly share what I've been able to learn with you!"
  - After: "I can repay you. The booklet hides a ciphered riddle pointing to places on Footfall. Maybe a discovery? I'll share!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Gordei sighs heavily.{/n} "Here I go again, pouring my heart out to have you disappear in ten minutes just like everyone else before you. But all right. Here is the story of Gordei Skatov, the unluckiest historian in the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}."
  - After: {n}Gordei sighs.{/n} "You'll vanish like everyone. Fine. The tale of Gordei Skatov, unluckiest historian in the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I was born two sectors away from here. My family was quite influential, which allowed me to dedicate myself to my great passion — the history of Imperium architecture. I spent a number of years studying every scholarly work there was to find on this art, and then, once I had inherited my family's fortune, I travelled and documented the development of architectural thought on different worlds. Until one day — oh, that accursed and blessed day! — until one day I came into possession of something quite special."
  - After: "Born to wealth two sectors away, I spent my inheritance documenting Imperium architecture. Then one accursed, blessed day, I found something."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Gordei pulls what looks like a book or an album with a home-made leather cover out of his bag. Both the pages and the binding look well-worn.{/n} "Here it is. My undoing.   - After: {n}He pulls out a worn booklet.{/n} "My undoing. Dewain's Design, printed centuries ago when Footfall was built."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh, it's you again! Not many people bother to talk to me in the first place, let alone twice. Do you want to hear the rest of my story?"
  - After: "You again! Want the rest of my story?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is no easy feat to cross two sectors, especially for a common citizen, albeit one who has some resources at his disposal... I had to change one ship after another, at times being forced to stay on transfer worlds waiting for a vessel headed in the right direction or for {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} disturbances to subside. The voyage took me a total of one hundred and seven years. In {g|Encyclopedia:Realspace}realspace{/g} time, of course. For me it was much less than that, somewhere in the neighbourhood of thirty or thirty-five. And then, after all those years, having spent all of my savings, I reached my dream..."
  - After: "Ship after ship, waiting out {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} storms. A hundred and seven years in {g|Encyclopedia:Realspace}realspace{/g}, thirty for me. My savings spent, I arrived..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That is incredible news! This is the first inspiring thing that has happened to me since the day I came to Footfall. Please, do not stop searching! I'm dying to know what this puzzle from the days of the station's youth is about."
  - After: "Incredible! The first good news in years. Keep searching!"
- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And all the very best to you too!"
  - After: "All the best to you too!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Gordei continues to talk and gesticulate passionately.{/n}
  - After: {n}Gordei talks on.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The first location from the riddles isn't far from here — it's a bridge that was supposed to go through the centre of this district and into the void toward the neighbouring asteroid.   - After: "First, the nearby bridge meant to cross the void to the next asteroid. Only ruined spans remain. If the cache survived, it's there."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The second location is the lantern of the Great Cathedral. A lantern is a small tower on top of a dome. You've seen Footfall's Atrium, haven't you? The Great Cathedral, had it been built, would have been even bigger. But, alas, its construction was just getting underway when Dewain died and the work stopped. The lantern from its dome, however, had already been built and survived. It was brought inside the Atrium and dubbed the Chapel of Saint Drusus the Warrior."
  - After: "Second, the lantern of the Great Cathedral, unfinished when Dewain died. The lantern survived — now the Atrium's Chapel of Saint Drusus the Warrior."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And what did I see? A dump in place of the exquisite portico! Metal anthills clinging to the columns! The marble tiles pilfered by paupers to use as cladding for their hovels!" {n}Gordei hangs his head.{/n} "It's been a dozen years since I came here, and I still haven't recovered from the shock. I had suspected that not everything from the booklet would exist in reality, but I never expected to see Footfall in such a sorry state.   - Before: "It was to be expected. The puzzle is several centuries old, and the locals are quite adept at gutting, dismantling, and breaking anything that catches their eye. But the very fact that the cache ever existed gives me hope! It means that there could be others."

  - Before: "A message from Dewain himself!" {n}His eyes light up.{/n} "The great dreamer and visionary! I should have guessed. - **(conversation owner)**

  - After: {n}Abelard, impressed.{/n} "I'll be! Even I didn't know that!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira blinks sleepily, barely suppresses a yawn, and starts looking around with a bored expression.{/n}
  - After: {n}Idira yawns.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He takes a closer look at you.{/n} "Not just someone — it's {mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius {mf|himself|herself}! Yours is an ancient and glorious line, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. A number of magnificent structures built on your ancestors' orders — both for defensive and decorative purposes — remain in the Scarus Sector. They keep your dynasty's memory alive despite the fact that it has long since focused its endeavours in a different sector."
  - After: {n}He peers at you.{/n} "{mf|Lord|Lady} von Valancius {mf|himself|herself}! Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s line built great structures in the Scarus Sector."
- **Jae**
  - Before: {n}Jae, who looks just as unimpressed with Gordei's lengthy tale, catches Idira's gaze and rolls her eyes theatrically, making Idira snicker.{/n}
  - After: {n}Jae rolls her eyes; Idira snickers.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: {n}Cassia, who has been listening to the historian's every word with bated breath, shushes Idira indignantly.{/n}
  - After: {n}Rapt, Cassia shushes Idira.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta's gaze darkens.{/n} "The warp, like a shameless thief, is guilty of stealing the short span allotted to His servants... but what sense is there in spending half your life on such an enterprise, only to then lose your spirit and waste the remaining half on nothing at all?"
  - After: {n}Argenta frowns.{/n} "The warp steals our time... why spend half a life on this, then waste the rest?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Your perseverance, Master Skatov, should have been applied elsewhere. However, the fact that you succumbed to indolence after your journey is far more deserving of reproach than your questionable choice of life goals."
  - After: "Misapplied perseverance, Master Skatov. Your idleness since is worse."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "What a curious read. Please, tell us more!" {n}As Cassia takes a shy step forward, Gordei smiles and shows her some of the faded pages.{/n}
  - After: "Tell us more!" {n}Gordei shows Cassia the pages.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "So then ink and paper too can lie and cause pain." {n}Cassia sighs sadly.{/n} "Does this mean that all I have ever read about will one day disappoint me with the ugliness of reality?"
  - After: "So books can lie and hurt." {n}Cassia sighs.{/n} "Will all I've read disappoint me?"
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Riddles?" {n}A flash of burning, almost childish curiosity brightens Cassia's austere countenance.{/n}
  - After: "Riddles?" {n}Cassia lights up.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Footfall's founder, Lord Parsimus, was obsessed with his creation's grand future. This booklet describes in detail what Footfall was meant to become upon its completion. Dozens of asteroids turned into glorious palaces and temples! Massive bridges spanning the void itself! And the marvellous flying buttresses! The archivolts of the exterior arches, the elegant arrangement of balusters!"
  - After: "Founder Lord Parsimus was obsessed with Footfall's future. This shows it finished: asteroid palaces and temples, void-spanning bridges, flying buttresses!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Now that we can only dream of. Dream of and yearn for..."
  - After: "Now we can only dream and yearn..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Gordei strokes his goatee in thought.{/n} "Yes, Footfall's current appearance — slums fused together with the remains of majestic palaces — is a unique phenomenon. It would be curious to observe if other places have taken after it, thereby solidifying it as a new style of architecture, or if it still remains a local oddity. My word, you certainly know how to provide an unexpected perspective on things!"
  - After: {n}He strokes his goatee.{/n} "True — slums fused with palaces is unique. A new style, or a local oddity? What a perspective!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have, of course. But I'm an old man who is blind in one eye and can barely move his legs. I never found anything, but that doesn't mean there's nothing to find!"
  - After: "I tried, but I'm old, half-blind and lame. I found nothing — but something may be there!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Absorbed in reminiscing, Gordei doesn't notice your gesture. He is looking at the booklet in his hands with indescribable tenderness and longing.{/n}
  - After: {n}Gordei gazes tenderly at the booklet.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And the interior! Poliforas ten stories tall and more than a kilometre long! Cyclopean light tubes that catch the light of Furibundus and use it to brighten the halls in the hearts of the asteroids! Stained glass windows and mosaics, bas-reliefs and statues!" {n}Engrossed in his own description, Gordei stands up and starts tracing the outlines of arches and galleries with his hand.{/n}
  - After: "Inside, kilometre-long poliforas! Light tubes channelling Furibundus! Stained glass, statues!" {n}He traces arches in the air.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Emerging from his reverie, he catches himself, blushes slightly, and loudly flops back onto his seat.{/n} "I apologise, I... I got carried away. But you must understand how deep an impression this booklet left on me when my young self picked it up! I simply couldn't think about anything other than Footfall. I was ready to give my life just to see this incredible station! And of course, no matter how hard my friends and loved ones tried to dissuade me, I still gathered all my savings and set out on a journey."
  - After: {n}He blushes, sits.{/n} "Sorry, carried away. The booklet gripped me young. Despite everyone's pleas, I took my savings and set out."

  - Before: {n}The burly woman with a wealth of fiery hair is in the process of tinkering with some unknown device that is clinking melodiously. I don't know what sort of cargo it was, but the ship he served on usually goes between Footfall and Winterscale's Realm. She passes the Hundred Dreams Crossroads and Langrenn's Belt. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The glass contains a liquid that is clearly made from spent promethium. This is moonshine, virtually unfiltered, that quickly blows the drinker off their feet and, when imbibed regularly, turns their liver into a bubbling sponge.{/n}
