  - Before: {n}His expression twists in pain as he stares at you in rage and bafflement.{/n} "Pitiful insect. You dare—"
  - After: {n}He glares in pained rage.{/n} "Insect. You dare—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "They call you a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_GreatDeed}hero{/d}. An empty word, a worthless pedestal among hundreds like it, all built by the lackeys of the false god in their hubris and ignorance. This pedestal will soon become a sacrificial altar, and you will become yet another reminder to the Expanse that no 'hero' can save it from the Truth."
  - After: "They call you a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_GreatDeed}hero{/d}. Your pedestal will become an altar."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Especially since..." {n}He bares his teeth and chuckles.{/n} "Especially since the soul of your leashed sorcerer has already been marked by my lord."
  - After: "Besides..." {n}He chuckles.{/n} "your leashed sorcerer's soul is already marked by my lord."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The warrior's inhuman eyes bore into you.{/n} "I am the master of those who have been felled by your hand in the halls of the Primordial Truth. I am Uralon the Cruel. The souls of my followers returned to the fount of power they served, crying out for me to cast my gaze toward this sacrilege. And what do I see? Yet another lackey of the corpse emperor."
  - After: {n}Inhuman eyes bore into you.{/n} "I am Uralon the Cruel, master of those you slew in the halls of the Primordial Truth. Their souls called me. I see another lackey of the corpse emperor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You squint and wipe away the tears — and for the moment, your vision clears. Before you stands a mighty giant clad in dark power armour lavishly adorned with bas-reliefs of snarling daemonic silhouettes and punctured with prayer scrolls. Two braziers are mounted behind his shoulders, burning with unnatural blue flames and emitting thick black smoke that curls and twists upward like a funnel. Behind the giant, you catch a brief glimpse of a crumpled figure bound in chains.{/n}
  - After: {n}A giant in daemon-carved armour, blue flames at his shoulders. Behind him, a chained figure.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Through the howling of the storm, you hear a new, chilling sound — roaring, cruel laughter. The figure advances toward you, and you feel that if it takes just one more step, it will step on you and crush you like a bug.{/n}
  - After: {n}Cruel laughter. The figure looms, ready to crush you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Writhing in pain, you raise your head and peer into the roiling darkness. You make out the figure's features — it is a huge man clad in dark power armour, from which daemonic silhouettes snarl at you. The wind picks up, and you close your eyes, unable to stare into the face of this raging tempest.{/n}
  - After: {n}A huge man in daemonic armour. The wind forces your eyes shut.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The giant's voice causes the storm raging around you to die down somewhat, as if the very sound of his voice is enough to make the whirlwind subside. You glance at the huge warrior, and notice on his chest a winding azure symbol — the shades of blue seem to glimmer and mingle together.{/n}
  - After: {n}His voice calms the storm. An azure symbol glimmers on his chest.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I want to look upon the one who has disrupted my flock's duties and my master's plans. That warrior from my Legion... the Fabricator-Censor... You think of their deaths as a triumph; however, it is but a minor hindrance on our path. There are other worlds that serve our goals. There are other sources of plasteel and adamantine. Revel in your victory — it will change nothing."
  - After: "I came to see who disrupted my master's plans. My Legion brother, the Fabricator-Censor — mere hindrances. Your victory changes nothing."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "All things in this world are subservient to change, Rogue Trader. Your predecessor thought herself immortal — and where is she now? What makes you think you won't be joining her shortly?"
  - After: "All things change. Your predecessor thought herself immortal. You'll join her soon."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Nevertheless, the blood in your veins whispers to the spirits that you warrant a closer look. Hmm... Yes... You are a descendant of the Rogue Trader whose {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} Kunrad Voigtvir sought to obtain. By defiling the relic and binding it to himself with the tethers of the Empyrean, he was meant to become my servant, a Rogue Trader who would do the work of the Truth... but then you interfered. Could it be that you wish to gain the true gods' favour instead? Do you wish to present the corpse's relic to me and serve the Truth? Hear your very blood calling, begging you to submit to me — what would be the point of futile defiance?"
  - After: "Your blood marks you: heir of the {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} Kunrad Voigtvir defiled to serve me — until you interfered. Give me the corpse's relic and serve the Truth. Your blood begs it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Conquering the weakness and pain, straining every muscle in your body, you slowly rise to your feet, straighten, and stare Uralon straight in the eye. He smiles, but there is no mirth in his eyes — only malicious curiosity, the kind with which one looks at an insect with its wings torn off.{/n}
  - After: {n}You rise and meet Uralon's eye. He smiles coldly, as at a maimed insect.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You strain every muscle in your body but cannot move an inch — the dark will presses down upon your shoulders, forbidding you even from straightening your back.{/n}
  - After: {n}The dark will pins you down.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This is the bridge that connects our minds, created by the will of my slave — whose fate you should be envying. The {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g} is useful enough to me to be left alive. You... less so."
  - After: "A bridge between our minds, made by my slave. That {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g} is useful. You aren't."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A gust of wind sweeps Uralon's figure away without a trace. The mist around you begins to dissipate, revealing the dark halls of the manufactorum and leaving behind an oppressive sense of powerlessness.{/n}
  - After: {n}Uralon vanishes. The mist lifts, leaving the dark manufactorum and a sense of powerlessness.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The manufactorum around you looks the same as before the vision — maybe the shadows have grown a little deeper and darker. You dust yourself off and continue on your journey through the darkness.{/n}
  - After: {n}The manufactorum looks unchanged. You press on.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix is standing beside you, white as a sheet, eyes wide, grimacing. The air around him seems to roil — though the phenomenon passes almost immediately. As he begins to speak, his voice sounds hoarse and cracked:{/n} "That... was not easy."
  - After: {n}Heinrix stands beside you, pale and hoarse.{/n} "That... was not easy."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "One of the traitors to the Imperium? I don't think it was he who touched your mind — I wouldn't have had the strength to go up against a psyker from the ranks of those monsters. He might have forced some mortal to do his bidding. Perhaps it was through the same hapless medium that he sensed the deaths of his henchmen." {n}Heinrix looks away and frowns.{/n} "Such indescribable power... to have reached out to your mind at such a distance..."
  - After: "He likely used a mortal psyker as medium — else I couldn't have resisted." {n}He frowns.{/n} "Such power, at such distance..."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix stares at you — whether in surprise or anger, you do not know. Then he gives a curt nod.{/n} "I see. We can theorise later — although I will say, {name}, that his words do not leave much room for interpretation."
  - After: {n}Heinrix nods curtly.{/n} "Later. Though his words leave little doubt, {name}."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix eyes you suspiciously, then reluctantly nods.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix nods, suspicious.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Chaos Space Marine's laughter is akin to the roll of distant thunder.{/n} "Words of a wretch who wanders through the darkness of ignorance. We were the first among our brothers to discern the great lie and forge the path to divinity. Our Primarch went on a pilgrimage to find the Truth — a path that is still open to the sighted. Your accusations are the words of a blind servant in thrall to an ancient lie."
  - After: {n}He laughs like thunder.{/n} "We were first to see the great lie. You serve an ancient lie, blind."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He chuckles and inclines his head.{/n} "When the time comes, I will remind you of this promise. The sinews of fate have yet to be bound... I will not stop my servants from hunting for that which I require. If you survive, you will have earned the right to serve the Truth."
  - After: {n}He chuckles.{/n} "I'll remember this promise. Survive my servants, and you may serve the Truth."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That outcome is acceptable. Once the servants of the Primordial Truth are done with you, they will see to it that the treasures of the Imperial ship are extracted and brought into the service of the true gods."
  - After: "Acceptable. My servants will claim your ship's treasures for the true gods."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "'Never'... do you know how many mortals uttered this word to me? And how many of them, just minutes later, were willing to give up all that was precious to them to make the torment stop?"
  - After: "'Never'... Many said that, then gave up everything to end the torment."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The blood starts pumping frenetically in your temples as a tell-tale sign of danger. You close your eyes and focus all your efforts on resisting the sorcerous attack. After a few moments, your heart slows down, and your blood vessels are no longer trying to burst from the pressure. The fear that washed over you, spurred on by another's ill will, ebbs away powerlessly.{/n}
  - After: {n}Blood pounds in your temples. You resist, and the sorcerous fear ebbs.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You feel blood rushing to your face, drumming in your temples, coating your tongue and lips in a viscous membrane. You no longer feel your arms and legs — as if your entire life force is trying to leave your body, pouring out of your mouth along with globs of crimson. The giant Chaos Space Marine is asking you questions, which you are answering obediently and hurriedly, not even comprehending what you are talking about.{/n}
  - After: {n}Blood fills your mouth. You answer the giant's questions without knowing what you say.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh, clinging to illusions will do you no good. The rituals have already been performed. The mortals are already singing the litanies of the Primordial Truth or decorating the sacrificial altars with their flesh. Kiava Gamma, as you call it, is already saturated in the nectar of the Truth — a fate that awaits all worlds that would stand in our way."
  - After: "The rituals are done. Kiava Gamma is already steeped in the Truth, as all worlds in our way will be."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This isn't your first time meddling in the deeds of the Word Bearers. You were there on Rykad Minoris, and so I want to know if you hold in your hands that which is not yours to hold. And you will tell me yourself." {n}He utters a few words in an unknown tongue over his shoulder — and you feel your head being clamped by an unseen vice.{/n}
  - After: "You meddled with us on Rykad Minoris. Do you hold what isn't yours? Tell me." {n}A vice clamps your head.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You feel your blood start pumping alarmingly in your temples at an increasing pace as the wind is knocked out of you... but then the drumming in your ears quiets, and your heart, which was about to leap out of your chest, slows its rhythm.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your blood pounds... then quiets.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Uralon chuckles.{/n} "Hmm... It appears I am not the only one who appreciates the value of a pet psyker. I will make good use of your watchdog when my servants get to you."
  - After: {n}Uralon chuckles.{/n} "A pet psyker. I'll make good use of your watchdog."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I sensed the presence of another psyker — someone made contact with you mentally, then tried to harm you with sorcery. I did what I could... you at least appear unharmed. Can you remember what you saw?"
  - After: "A psyker reached your mind and attacked with sorcery. I did what I could. What did you see?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Another's will bears down on you, but as soon as you awaken {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}your own powers{/d}, your soul fills with defiant resolve.{/n}
  - After: {n}{d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}Your own powers{/d} wake in defiance.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Through the thunder and wind, you hear the giant's disdainful laughter:{/n} "You carry merely one part of the whole... Keep it, then, until the hour of our meeting. I will pluck this boon from your dead hands and use it for the glory of the Truth."
  - After: {n}The giant laughs:{/n} "You carry only one part. Keep it. I'll take it from your corpse."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The giant's voice rises over the howling winds — and it is heavy with fury and tinged with disbelief:{/n} "You... You, a mere insect, have obtained both shards! Do you truly think yourself a new aspirant vying for the favour of the Edge? So be it... Fate shall execute the will of the Weaver. Follow the pattern, then, Rogue Trader... March on."
  - After: {n}He roars in disbelief:{/n} "You have both shards! So be it — fate serves the Weaver. March on, Rogue Trader."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sensation is familiar, for this is not the first time the {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}shadow of warp sorcery{/d} has fallen heavily upon you. You close your eyes and cast aside all thought — and your inner horrors cry out and rise against the will of another.{/n}
  - After: {n}The {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_DH_Signs}shadow of warp sorcery{/d} is familiar. Your inner horrors rise against it.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Struggling against the elements, you can barely raise your head to look. Your eyes sting and burn, but through the tears, you see it — a colossal silhouette rising above you. The roaring tempest is unable to shake the mighty figure.{/n}
  - After: {n}Through tears, you see a colossal silhouette above you.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard looks you over worriedly, then sighs in cantankerous relief.{/n} "That was a close call! For the sake of Holy Terra, if I had lost a second Rogue Trader in such a paltry span of time — my only option would have been to shoot myself out of unending shame..."
  - After: {n}Abelard sighs in relief.{/n} "Close call! Lose a second Rogue Trader so soon? I'd shoot myself for shame."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Quit dawdling, Heinrix!" {n}Abelard peers over Heinrix's shoulder, looking agitated.{/n} "I can't lose a second Rogue Trader in such a ridiculous span of time! Oh, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you've come to! Thank the Throne!"
  - After: "Hurry, Heinrix!" {n}Abelard peers over.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, you're awake! Thank the Throne!"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Sister Argenta, who has been watching all of this intently, grows pale and makes the sign of the Aquila to ward off evil.{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta pales and makes the sign of the Aquila.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Worthless rat... Still, I will rip the answers out of you personally. When the time comes."
  - After: "Worthless rat. I'll rip the answers out of you myself."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After swallowing down your blood and barely catching your breath, you regain the ability to hear. The giant's voice roars over the howling of the whirlwind,{/n} "Enough. Even if you have touched my master's relic, it is not with you now. Very well, servants of the Truth will seek it out and bring it back into the fold. As for you... other servants of the Truth will deal with you."
  - After: {n}The giant roars:{/n} "Enough. You've touched my master's relic but lack it now. My servants will find it — and you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your soul, {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}tempered by the curse of sorcery{/d}, stands strong against the psychic onslaught, and you direct your gaze forward.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your soul, {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Psyker}tempered by the curse of sorcery{/d}, holds firm.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}A shadow passes over Heinrix's face — astonishment, anger, and, finally, alarm.{/n} "Most likely, our enemy wanted to sow doubt among your allies. If I were a follower of the Archenemy, would I have fought for your soul? Don't trust a word the enemies of the Imperium say, {name}, lest you put your own soul at risk."
  - After: {n}Heinrix looks alarmed.{/n} "He wants to sow doubt. Would an Archenemy follower fight for your soul? Trust nothing they say, {name}."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/ForgeWorld/ChaosEngineTamed

- **Player**
  - Before: "I intend to use this weapon against Chaos itself."
  - After: "I'll use this weapon against Chaos itself."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Lie] "Just look at this thing. It must be defective if it fights its own!"
  - After: [Lie] "It fights its own — must be defective!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Blast it... I was looking forward to enjoying my new toy."
  - After: "Blast it... I wanted my new toy."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Disobeying the Rogue Trader's will is a crime against the Imperium! I am removing you from my retinue! Away with you!"
  - After: "Defying the Rogue Trader is a crime against the Imperium! You're out of my retinue!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "We are done here. It is time we pressed on."
  - After: "We're done here. Let's press on."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}The Interrogator looks at the Daemon Engine for a few moments.{/n} "You have stepped dangerously close to the line that separates radical thinking from indisputable heresy. Be more prudent in your experiments, {name}."
  - After: {n}Heinrix eyes it.{/n} "Near heresy, {name}. Be prudent."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira bites her lip to conceal a smile. She casts a mocking glance at the unsuspecting Interrogator.{/n}
  - After: {n}Idira hides a smile.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The monster's hulking frame, a moment ago brimming with ruinous energy, now lies at your feet.{/n}
  - After: {n}The monster lies spent at your feet.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Which is why I had to act of my own accord to shield you from unspeakable heresy, Rogue Trader! If I hadn't..." {n}Argenta pointedly adjusts her grip on her weapon, her burning gaze trained on you.{/n}
  - After: "I acted to save you from heresy!" {n}Argenta glares.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix's voice drops to a hiss:{/n} "A Rogue Trader's privileges have their limits, {name}. I have the right to punish heresy, and you should be thankful that I disposed of the Engine and only the Engine!"
  - After: {n}Heinrix hisses:{/n} "Your privileges have limits, {name}. Be glad I spared you!"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard silently makes the sign of the Aquila.{/n}
  - After: {n}Abelard makes the sign of the Aquila.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Exalted One protect us and Humanity's guardians..."
  - After: "Exalted One protect us..."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Your 'toy'? It was built by heretics to become a vessel for an abomination of the warp, an instrument of destruction and corruption! {name}..." {n}Heinrix is briefly choked with fury.{/n}
  - After: "'Toy'? It's a vessel for a warp abomination! {name}..." {n}Heinrix seethes.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Should the hour ever come when you indeed employ an abominable weapon of the Archenemy, it will be the hour when my weapon turns against you — and then, trust my word on it, nothing will save you from righteous judgement!"
  - After: "Wield the Archenemy's weapon, and mine turns on you!"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet throws out her arm as if in an attempt to halt your words.{/n} "Enough! Your obliviousness to the true atrocious nature of this creation is staggering, elantach. Stop, for I wish not to hear another word of this madness!"
  - After: {n}Yrliet raises a hand.{/n} "Enough, elantach! I'll hear no more madness!"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta raises her chin.{/n} "So those are the words you've chosen? Very well. Knowing how mild your convictions are when it comes to dealing with heresy... when next we meet, do not count on me to be merciful and let you leave unscathed. May the God-Emperor's grace guide you onto the one true path!"
  - After: {n}Argenta lifts her chin.{/n} "So be it. Expect no mercy next time."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix scoffs coldly.{/n} "It is not for the Rogue Trader to gainsay the will of the Lord Inquisitor. I am in this retinue at his behest, not yours."
  - After: {n}Heinrix scoffs.{/n} "I serve the Lord Inquisitor, not you."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "If the anathema demonstrates the slightest disobedience, this unit will open its armour plating, pulverise its hydraulic pistons, and start cutting its contact wires one after another to see which cogitation groups shut down first." {n}As Pasqal whispers his threats, the monstrosity's plated form shrinks and lets out a vicious but somewhat wary growl.{/n}
  - After: "If it disobeys, this unit will dismantle it." {n}It growls warily.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/ForgeWorld/ChaosEngineTamed/ChaosEngineTamed_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal, don't you want to see what this creature is made of and learn about any weaknesses that we could use in the fight against heresy?"
  - After: "Pasqal, don't you want to study it for weaknesses against heresy?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Argenta, this is our chance to turn a creation of Chaos against the Archenemy!"
  - After: "Argenta, let's turn Chaos's creation on the Archenemy!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am taking it to my ship. I will make it serve me."
  - After: "It's coming to my ship. It will serve me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Heinrix, you were just investigating a corrupted cogitator — and now you would fault me?"
  - After: "Heinrix, you studied a corrupted cogitator — and you fault me?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Yrliet, you have my word that I will keep this thing under control."
  - After: "Yrliet, I promise I'll keep it under control."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Abelard? Rest assured, my new pet will give us little trouble. I am confident that you will manage perfectly well."
  - After: "Abelard, my new pet will be little trouble. You'll manage."
- **Player**
  - Before: "My decision is final. We are taking the machine on board."
  - After: "My decision is final. The machine comes aboard."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The steel behemoth standing before you twitches every so often. Its frame emanates tainted miasmas, as if its metal plates can barely hold the endless anathema contained within this fabricated cage.{/n}
  - After: {n}The steel behemoth twitches, leaking miasma.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira shakes her head, tilts it to one side as if listening to something, then shoots you a wary glance. As she meets your gaze, her expression hardens and she gives you a slight nod.{/n}
  - After: {n}Idira gives you a wary nod.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Your words are tainted by the Archenemy's lies, Rogue Trader! Such promises of power are what pave the road to heresy and ruin. You will not lead me astray!"
  - After: "The Archenemy's lies! You won't lead me astray!"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Sister Argenta readies her weapon.{/n} "Let fall the Archenemy's weapon that has turned on itself in a fit of madness!"
  - After: {n}Argenta readies her weapon.{/n} "Destroy the Archenemy's weapon!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The beast turns its monstrous head from side to side as if trying to catch someone's scent.{/n}
  - After: {n}The beast sniffs the air.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "What?" {n}The Interrogator stares at you in fury.{/n} "What lunacy has gotten into your head?"
  - After: "What?" {n}Heinrix glares.{/n} "What lunacy is this?"
- **Jae**
  - Before: "What a hypocritical ashmag you are, cog." {n}Jae meets Pasqal's glare and smirks.{/n} "Go ahead, look me in the eye and tell me again that I'm the one who wants to get my hands on things no one should ever touch."
  - After: "Hypocrite." {n}Jae smirks at Pasqal.{/n} "And I'm the one grabbing forbidden things?"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet lowers her head and steps back, her expression darkening.{/n} "Isha, bless the elantach with but a shred of reason, for {mf|his|her} own has abandoned {mf|him|her}..."
  - After: {n}Yrliet steps back.{/n} "Isha, grant the elantach reason, for {mf|his|her} own has left {mf|him|her}..."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Even Rogue Traders should not dabble in what we are dealing with now!" {n}His voice turns into a growl.{/n} "You are putting every soul aboard your ship in grave peril!"
  - After: "Even Rogue Traders mustn't dabble in this!" {n}He growls.{/n} "You endanger us all!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The monstrosity does not fight back when buffeted by a hail of attacks. The steel tears and comes apart, the heat radiating from the construct's bowels instantly becomes unbearable — and then dissipates completely. At last, the empty shell crumbles to the floor with a thundering crash.{/n}
  - After: {n}It doesn't resist. Its empty shell crashes down.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The abomination, seething with heat and malice, digs at the metal floor with its foot and lets out a stifled howl, as if in anticipation of new massacres and victims to come.{/n}
  - After: {n}The abomination howls, eager for victims.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet shoots you a gloomy look.{/n} "You, who cannot control {mf|his|her} own mad ambitions, frighten me far more than this monster."
  - After: {n}Yrliet looks grim.{/n} "One who can't rule {mf|his|her} own ambition scares me more than this monster."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As soon as you say the words, Argenta and Heinrix leap up as if on command...{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta and Heinrix leap up...{/n}
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah glowers at the metal creature.{/n} "If the unclean beast dares to defy your command, Domin, I will cast it into oblivion. And I will swiftly sever the thread of any of your subjects who may become sullied by its corruption."
  - After: {n}Kibellah glowers.{/n} "If it defies you, Domin, I'll destroy it."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne gives you a hard look.{/n} "Just because the Warrant allows you many things does not obligate you to exercise every right you have. Not all tools are fit for the service of the God-Emperor. Think on it."
  - After: {n}Solomorne frowns.{/n} "Not every tool serves the God-Emperor."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Sparks crackle from the pistons on Eogunn's chin, as his batteries emit a warning growl. The Manipulus stares in fascination at the mechanical monster.{/n} "This construct is extremely dangerous, yet how unfathomable its nature is! If you truly intend to claim it, Rogue Trader, I assert my priority right to study it."
  - After: {n}Eogunn stares, fascinated.{/n} "Fascinating! I claim first right to study it."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix raises a hand, and an unseen shroud of cold instantly falls upon him.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix raises a hand; cold falls.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Without saying a word, Argenta aims her weapon.{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta silently aims her weapon.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}The Seneschal lets out a strange, pained sound.{/n} "Of course, Lord Captain. After all, my options are rather limited."
  - After: {n}Abelard winces.{/n} "Of course, Lord Captain."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix raises a hand, and the temperature around him begins to plummet.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix raises a hand; the air chills.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal, even paler than normal, is staring at the creature with a mixture of rage and disgust, his visor flashing blue and green. A few sparks fly out of the burnt circuitry beneath the monster's armour, as if Pasqal's anger is setting its insides on fire.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal glares; sparks burst from the monster.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's voice clangs like military-grade plasteel:{/n} "Unacceptable sacrilege! The abomination must be eradicated!"
  - After: {n}Pasqal clangs:{/n} "Sacrilege! Eradicate it!"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal freezes while his mechadendrites flail back and forth. After a long pause, he utters quietly,{/n} "The anathema must be equipped with a mechanism for cessation of vital functions, which is to be put under my supervision. Then its existence can be prolonged for the duration justifiable by the sacred mission of Comprehension."
  - After: {n}Pasqal pauses.{/n} "Fit it with a kill switch under my control. Then it may exist."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}The Sister of Battle raises her weapon.{/n} "Halt in His name! Do you even comprehend what heresy you intend to wreak?"
  - After: {n}Argenta raises her weapon.{/n} "Halt! Do you grasp this heresy?"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard turns white as a sheet.{/n} "Begging your pardon, Lord Captain... Where would we even... We would have to keep it locked up... It will demolish half the deck!"
  - After: {n}Abelard pales.{/n} "It'll wreck half the deck!"
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Shereen, your triumph over the Archenemy's knaves must have obscured your mind, for what other explanation can I find for what I'm hearing? To bring a weapon of Humanity's bane on board the ship of the Exalted One's chosen? I mean..."
  - After: "Shereen, has victory clouded your mind? Bring Humanity's bane aboard?"

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/ForgeWorld/Cogitator_Dialogue1/Cogitator_Dialogue1

The {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g} once operated like one gargantuan well-oiled mechanism. The last record is from two months ago.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/ForgeWorld/Cogitator_Dialogue2/Cogitator_Dialogue2

- **Player**
  - Before: [View the third log data, which is hidden by the protection of the machine spirit]
  - After: [View the third log, protected by the machine spirit]
- **(conversation owner)**

The new protocols received at the synod from the great {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} have been executed, despite those who shuddered at the thought of changing a Standard Procedure. Embolden your hearts, those whose inner weakness breeds errors in personal calculations, for the Fabricator-Censor is the conductor of the higher will and the wisest among us..."
  - After: "...praise the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}! The {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g}'s new protocols are executed, despite doubters. Take heart: he conducts the higher will..."
- **(conversation owner)**

Today, dozens of Standard Procedures were lost, to be replaced by new ones, which the Fabricator-Censor will deliver to those who demonstrate the greatest devotion to serving the truth... but the data-banks contain no notion of 'Truth' — could there have been, may the All-Knowing One, the Gracious Keeper, forgive me, an error in the Fabricator-Censor's calculations, and he meant to say, 'serving the Quest for Knowledge'?"

And there are some who are not susceptible to the Enhancement Protocol that carries our tech-comrades to enlightenment — may the deliverers of fate be merciful to them. ## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/ForgeWorld/Cogitator_Dialogue3/Cogitator_Dialogue3

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/ForgeWorld/Cogitator_Dialogue5/Cogitator_Dialogue5

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}At first glance, the records look like a typical shipping report, but after further reading, it becomes apparent that the focus here is not ore or assembly parts, but {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augments{/g} extracted from living {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g}, and "spent mass" — the flesh of the victims killed either during or for the sake of machine rituals.{/n}
  - After: {n}A shipping log of {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augments{/g} torn from living {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g}, and victims' "spent mass."{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The log looks damaged — the lines are uneven, and some of the values seem impossible. After a few minutes of studying the records, you feel your head begin to swim — the stored data can only be comprehended by a twisted mind touched by {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} corruption.{/n}
  - After: {n}Garbled data only a {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g}-twisted mind could read.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}This record looks like a sermon of some mad {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} worshipper. The log, clearly written from someone else's words, mentions "the heart that exudes virtue" and "the cradle that rocks the child of Truth."{/n}
  - After: {n}A mad {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} sermon: "the heart that exudes virtue," "the cradle that rocks the child of Truth."{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/ForgeWorld/Cogitator_Dialogue6/Cogitator_Dialogue6

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Several lumens light up on the panel. You hear distinct clicks — and the cogitator goes quiet, clearly having fulfilled its purpose.{/n}
  - After: {n}Lumens flash. The cogitator goes quiet.{/n}

  - After: "It's inhumane. I'd end it, but I can't."

  - Before: "What do you find so appalling about this custom?"
  - After: "What appalls you about this custom?"

  - Before: [Cut away the tumour forming on the spinal cogitator]
  - After: [Cut away the tumour on the spinal cogitator]
- **Player**
  - Before: [Find the malfunctioning augment and disable it]
  - After: [Find and disable the faulty augment]
- **Player**
  - Before: [Observe the servitor closest to you]
  - After: [Observe the nearest servitor]

  - Before: "It is a necessary sacrifice for the survival of our entire civilisation."
  - After: "A necessary sacrifice for our civilisation's survival."

  - After: "Servitors are useful — unlike two-thirds of Humanity."

  - After: [Find the source of the clicking]

  - After: "Servitude is an honour, xenos. You wouldn't understand."

Upon your approach, one of the servitors jerks and tries to turn in your direction. The rest immediately repeat the motion.{/n}

  - After: "Nor do I wish to. Understanding can be a burden."

  - Before: {n}The servitor touches you. Something in the depths of the man-machine crackles — and you are hit by an electrical discharge. The sound causes the other servitors to flinch but they otherwise remain motionless.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Gently and swiftly, you step away from the servitor. It stretches out its hand, as if trying blindly to touch you in the space that you have already left, and stills once more — it seems its brain is incapable of quickly processing changes in its surroundings.{/n}
  - After: {n}You slip aside. It gropes at air, then stills.{/n}

  - Before: "It appears, then, that you do not hold your kin in high regard either. Yet you fail to see defects where you should."
  - After: "You scorn your kin too, yet miss the real defects."

  - Before: "Your kind is adept at surviving, that much is certain. But I do not believe that what I am seeing was done purely for the sake of survival..."
  - After: "This wasn't done just to survive..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The strange scene is complemented by a grating sound — dull clicks just at the edge of your hearing, coming from an unknown source.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The closest servitor twitches — and the others follow suit. It is clear that the entire group is connected by a single machine spirit, and something caused it to stop working. One of the servitors must have a fault in its cogitator or some other augment — and that fault then ended up affecting the whole group.{/n}
  - After: {n}They twitch as one. One machine spirit links them; a single faulty augment stalled them all.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Based on a cursory inspection, you conclude that the servitors were designed for precision work on an assembly line — possibly circuit production. The number of high-quality, expensive {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augments{/g} in their bodies greatly exceeds basic standards.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Soon enough, you locate the source of the clicking. On the back of one of the servitors, a tumour, oozing with murky ichor, is growing straight through the augments. The relays, coated in inflamed tissue, are blocked, hence the reason for the persistent clicking.{/n}
  - After: {n}A tumour on one servitor's back has grown through its relays — hence the clicking.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You carefully examine the servitor until you eventually spot the cover on its chest. After unscrewing and removing the plate, you discover the wires for the failed {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augmetic{/g} parts and cut them.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After failing to fully understand the servitor's design, you pick a {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} pretty much at random, one that looks busted, and cut it off from the rest of the system. Immediately, you hear hissing coming from deep inside the servitor's flesh. You catch a whiff of charred meat and burnt wiring.{/n}
  - After: {n}You cut a random {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}. It hisses; charred meat smell.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Without much difficulty, you cut the excess flesh from the mechanisms. The liberated relay lets out a rapid burst of clicks, then a spark flashes before your eyes, and something begins to hum deep inside the servitor's flesh.{/n}
  - After: {n}You cut the flesh away. The relay sparks; something hums.{/n}

  - After: {n}The servitors turn.{/n} "Crew 24, second lane of the {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g}. State your request." {n}Its {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} speaks.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You back away awkwardly, trip over your own feet, and flap your arms in an attempt to keep your balance. The servitors react to the movement — with deafening shrieks from their joints, they straighten and lunge forward!{/n}

  - After: "A mutated servitor? {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} reject flawed tissue. Something caused this — recently."

  - After: {n}Yrliet looks away.{/n} "Mon-keigh customs are terrible. Some, worse."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servitor's hand moves — it is slowly reaching toward you...{/n}
  - After: {n}The servitor reaches for you...{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet stares at you in amazement, tilting her head to the side like a bird.{/n} "I did not expect such words from you. You are... interesting, {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}."
  - After: {n}Yrliet tilts her head.{/n} "You are... interesting, {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}."

Mere coincidence, or malevolent intent?"
  - After: "Look, Nuncius." {n}Eogunn inspects the growth.{/n} "A fresh teratoma, already choking the machine spirit's nodes. Coincidence, or malice?"

A moment later, you recognise the dominant smell in the bouquet of scents permeating the air around the Tech-Priest — the stench of rotten meat.{/n}

The air on the {g|Encyclopedia:IndustrialWorld}industrial world{/g} is thick with the smell of fumes and molten plasteel, but standing close to the Tech-Priest, you can clearly smell the stench coming off him — a staggering mixture of machine lubricants, old sweat, and something even more revolting.{/n}

I..." {n}A click, a clank, a barely audible hiss — and only then the Tech-Priest's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} finishes the word,{/n} "Identification."

  - Before: "Who did this to you?"

  - After: [End his suffering] "Go to the Omnissiah."

  - Before: "Brace yourself. I shall help you."

  - Before: [End the man's suffering] "Go to the Omnissiah."

  - Before: {n}This pile of human remains, carelessly tossed together, emits a suffocating stench. The torn, gutted bodies once belonged to {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g}, but you cannot spot even a glint of metal anywhere — all their {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g} are gone. Suddenly, one of the ravaged bodies makes the tiniest movement. The tortured man's lips move ever so slightly, his half-closed eyelids twitching.{/n}
  - After: {n}Reeking, gutted {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g}, every {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implant{/g} gone. One twitches.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Without uttering a single word, Eogunn extends a mechadendrite, injector bared, toward the poor wretch, administering an unknown golden liquid into his neck. The Manipulus's face is set in a mask of deepest sorrow.{/n}
  - After: {n}Grieving, Eogunn injects a golden liquid.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet's alien, harsh features are graced with something strikingly similar to grief and compassion.{/n} "Such senseless savagery."
  - After: {n}Yrliet looks grieved.{/n} "Senseless savagery."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "What a horrible fate... to be betrayed by one's own."
  - After: "Betrayed by his own..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man, who is minutes from death, wheezes weakly,{/n} "It's an honour... I am thankful... for the right to serve..."
  - After: {n}He wheezes,{/n} "An honour... to serve..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man can barely breathe without his respirator implant. It is a miracle he survived the horrific vivisection. But it takes you a single look at the gaping wounds where the {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augment{/g} was ripped out to realise — death is only a matter of time. As if having sensed your presence, the half-dead man looks at you and sharply inhales the hot air.{/n} "Machine spirit... deliver me..."
  - After: {n}His {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}augment{/g} ripped out, he is dying.{/n} "Machine spirit... deliver me..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You walk away from the bodies, struggling to wipe the images from your memory — the mangled flesh and death masks forever imprinted on the bloodless faces.{/n}
  - After: {n}You walk away, haunted.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}In a single motion, you bring an end to his long torment. After checking that there are no more survivors in this pile of human remains, you step away from the nightmarish sight.{/n}
  - After: {n}You end his torment. No other survivors.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My... comrades..." {n}His voice is barely audible. It seems each word takes the man a great deal of effort.{/n} "Machine spirit... has the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g} truly... abandoned us? Kiava Gamma has fallen... into the maw of the Eternal Enemy..."
  - After: "My comrades..." {n}He struggles.{/n} "Has the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g} abandoned us? Kiava Gamma has fallen... to the Eternal Enemy..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The holy {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magi{/g}... they succumbed to heresy... the rest... were stripped of their True Flesh... to feed the heresy... Preserve us... deliver us... deliver me from erring..."
  - After: "The {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magi{/g} turned heretic... the rest, stripped of True Flesh... to feed heresy..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Sacrifice... living blood... from vessels of the True Flesh... while their heart is... still beating. After that... oblivion." {n}His eyes grow glassy.{/n} "I... knew... you would come... I've waited... so very long. Deliver me from my torment..."
  - After: "Living blood... from beating hearts... then oblivion." {n}His eyes glaze.{/n} "I knew you'd come... Deliver me..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}No treatment can preserve the life in this fading body, but for the moment, you are able to stabilise him. He groans weakly.{/n} "Why... why do you prolong... my cycle? Are you waiting... for my repentance? Have I not yet purged... my soul... through my torment..." {n}He breaks into a coughing fit.{/n} "Or must I... repent for the others..."
  - After: {n}You stabilise him.{/n} "Why prolong... my cycle?" {n}He coughs.{/n} "Must I repent... for others..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Despite all your efforts, the man breathes his last in your arms. You walk away from the pile of corpses with a feeling that your interference only added to the dying man's suffering.{/n}
  - After: {n}He dies in your arms, your help only prolonging his pain.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Something flashes in the man's eyes, as if your words have allowed him to gather what remains of his strength. Gritting his teeth, he barely raises his head and fastens his mad gaze on you.{/n} "May the Omnissiah strengthen my will... may I renounce the dissonance of variation..."
  - After: {n}Your words rally him.{/n} "Omnissiah... strengthen my will..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Without the True Flesh... I am weak, machine spirit... too... weak..." {n}The man dies in your arms. You let go of the deceased, stand up straight, and walk away from the pile of bodies.{/n}
  - After: "Too... weak..." {n}He dies in your arms.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Know, machine spirit, angel of the Deus Mechanicus... that I saw... the {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} himself... ripping the Flesh out of our tech-comrades... and chanting a litany over vessels of corruption... sarcophagi forged from corrupted metal... unholy shells designed to house evil!" {n}He lets out a weak howl.{/n}
  - After: "I saw the {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} rip Flesh from our comrades... and bless sarcophagi of corrupted metal... shells for evil!" {n}He howls.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Fabricator-Censor does not serve the Omnissiah... he obeys a different power... the one whose herald... came to Kiava Gamma at the onset of the insurgency... his mouth spewing lies and corruption... Fear him, for he is... he is..." {n}The words escape the man's mouth along with his last breath. Having spent the last bit of strength on his confession, he goes limp in your arms — forever this time.{/n}
  - After: "The Fabricator-Censor serves another power... whose herald came when the insurgency began... Fear him, for he is..." {n}He dies.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Behind you, you hear ragged wheezing that vaguely resembles fervent words of prayer.{/n}
  - After: {n}Behind you, wheezing prayer.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man gasps violently, as if the very thought terrifies him.{/n} "No! I was robbed... of the grace of the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Deus Mechanicus{/g}... waste not your efforts... and hear my confession..."
  - After: {n}He gasps.{/n} "No! The {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Deus Mechanicus{/g} forsook me... hear my confession..."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Heresy. To dare sever sacred metal from the flesh of the Machine God's servant... Damnation upon those who committed this deed. I will purge the Motive Force from their bodies and grind their flesh into disposable biomatter." {n}With anguish in his eyes, Eogunn levitates beside the poor soul. A gentle mist starts pouring from his alembic, carrying the sweet scent of an anaesthetic.{/n}
  - After: "Heresy. I will grind those who did this into biomatter." {n}Eogunn mists him with anaesthetic.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}The binharic requiem coming from Pasqal's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} sounds solemn and grim. Upon hearing it, the man's mutilated face twists into a weak semblance of a smile.{/n}

Requesting the right to extract the subject's organic matter for it to be used in the creation of an honourable servo-skull."
  - After: "He meets all three criteria for martyrdom. Requesting his organic matter for an honourable servo-skull."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The maimed man flinches only slightly at the injection, but his breathing starts to even out. Despite the oily film clouding his eyes, the faint ghost of gratitude shines through.{/n}
  - After: {n}His breathing evens, grateful.{/n}
- **Pasqal**

Wielding a long scalpel, it takes him mere moments to release the cervical vertebrae from the hold of muscles and sinew and to cut the vertebrae, severing the head from the body.{/n}

- **Pasqal**
