  - After: "Your service continues, tech-comrade."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/ForgeWorld/Fixed_FabricatorMainDialogue/Fixed_FabricatorMainDialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You know why I like deranged tin cans like you? When you're killed, you leave behind plenty of useful spare parts. I think I'll make a portable recaf machine out of you."
  - After: "Tin cans leave useful parts. I'll make you a recaf machine."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Check the chronometer] "Your five minutes have passed. I hereby sentence you to death. And I will be the one to carry it out!"
  - After: [Check the chronometer] "Time's up. I sentence you to death, and I'll do it!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What did you just say?"
  - After: "What did you say?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am repulsed to hear Techna-Lingua from the mouth of a traitor."
  - After: "Techna-Lingua from a traitor repulses me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your minions are dead. Both you and your host will likewise fail to stop me."
  - After: "Your minions are dead. You and your host are next."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why don't I just kill you along with your minions and be done with it?"
  - After: "Why not just kill you too?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I saw the strange constructs on the lines of the manufactorum. What mad machines are you creating here?"
  - After: "What mad machines are you building?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Kiava Gamma belongs to House von Valancius, with whose scion you have the honour of speaking."
  - After: "Kiava Gamma belongs to House von Valancius, and I'm its scion."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What did you do to the governor of Kiava Gamma? Is he alive?"
  - After: "What did you do to the governor? Is he alive?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You deserve a painful death for what you have wrought upon the machines of this world and their priests."
  - After: "You deserve a painful death for harming this world's machines and priests."
- **Player**
  - Before: "So you have traded one master for another? I would have expected a Fabricator-Censor to be smarter than that."
  - After: "Traded one master for another? Not smart, Fabricator-Censor."
- **Player**
  - Before: "This is my world, and it will serve only me."
  - After: "This world serves only me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You can still save yourself. Let us stop this nightmare together!"
  - After: "You can still save yourself. Let's stop this together!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "In the name of the Golden Throne, I will stop you and those who follow you."
  - After: "In the Golden Throne's name, I'll stop you all."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "I shall purge Kiava Gamma of your corruption!"
  - After: [Attack] "I'll purge your corruption from Kiava Gamma!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Dominate the metallic beast] "Spirit of the warp! Bow to my will and defend me!"
  - After: [Dominate the metallic beast] "Warp spirit! Bow and defend me!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Because the schemes of the Ruinous Powers are powerless against the servants of the God-Emperor, who are guided by His light."
  - After: "The Ruinous Powers can't stop the God-Emperor's servants."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You propose that I, the Rogue Trader of the von Valancius line, kneel before you? I am giving you five minutes. No, not to beg forgiveness. To speak your last words and to offer your final confession."
  - After: "A von Valancius Rogue Trader, kneel? You have five minutes for last words and confession."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I usually prefer negotiating to fighting. Fighting destroys property and wastes resources. But in your case, I'm afraid that extreme measures must be taken."
  - After: "I prefer negotiating to wasteful fighting. But you call for extreme measures."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What's the matter, little tin-comrade? Implants on the blink? Forgotten how to speak properly?"
  - After: "What's wrong, tin-comrade? Implants on the blink?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "We have already cut down that brute of a preacher who brainwashed you and your underlings. Now it is your turn."
  - After: "We killed the preacher who brainwashed you. Now it's your turn."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It appears that your masters have turned their backs on you, and now you are on your own."
  - After: "Your masters abandoned you. You're alone."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have seen what you have done to this world and its poor people. I will not allow it to continue."
  - After: "I've seen what you did to this world. It ends now."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I shall venture a guess. It is because I am the illustrious Rogue Trader von Valancius, conqueror of the Koronus Expanse, and you are a talking piece of refuse."
  - After: "Because I'm Rogue Trader von Valancius, conqueror of the Koronus Expanse, and you're talking refuse."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The massive {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magos{/g} clad in ritual garb lets out a binharic trill and turns to you. From beneath the deep hood of his mantle, two dimly lit eye {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g} gaze out at you. You hear another binharic tirade — this time clearly addressed at you.{/n}
  - After: {n}A hooded {g|Encyclopedia:Magos}Magos{/g}, {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g} glowing, trills binharic at you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You dare address me in the vile tongue of savages? Me, the steward of Kiava Gamma, lord of the machine world? Kneel, pathetic spawn, if you seek swift disposal."
  - After: "The savage tongue, to Kiava Gamma's lord? Kneel for swift disposal."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To break free from the chains of the Cult Mechanicus is the destiny of those who work on altogether different frequencies and levels of productivity. My mind is capable of conceiving Knowledge in a way that no other biological cogitator can — and yet I am still expected to obey the taboos put in place by intellects far more primitive than mine. But these taboos can and will be undone. You have seen the things we can do once free, thrall of the Omnissiah, and you fear them!"
  - After: "Why obey lesser minds' taboos? You've seen what freedom makes possible, thrall of the Omnissiah, and you fear it!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Even a cursory analysis of the data shows that the probability of this outcome is negligible. You, like your predecessor, are but an artefact of certain calculations, one that requires minimal resources to revise."
  - After: "Improbable. Like your predecessor, you are easily revised."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Accept this new sacrifice, sacred Truth!"
  - After: "Accept this sacrifice, sacred Truth!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Primitive creature, devoid of true Knowledge. Could it be one of the slaves who escaped imprisonment? Kneel, servant, before the master of Kiava Gamma."
  - After: "A primitive. An escaped slave? Kneel before Kiava Gamma's master."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The outsider comprehends binharic speech. Perhaps you still have a chance to serve the new lords of Kiava Gamma. Kneel, contemptible one, and I will permit your True Flesh to be used for our great purpose."
  - After: "It knows binharic. Kneel, and your True Flesh may serve our purpose."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Comrades. Purge the {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g} of any random variables. I must prepare for the culmination of our great work."
  - After: "Comrades, purge the {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g}. I must prepare our great work."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Hoarse laughter comes from the Fabricator-Censor's vox.{/n} "There are things more frightening than death, troglodyte. To submit one's existence to a false dogma, to condemn sacred machines bound by feeble flesh to pointless calculations... the notion is rejected."
  - After: {n}Hoarse vox laughter.{/n} "Serving false dogma is worse than death, troglodyte."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "An impossibility. I am not a variable that can be extracted from the process without acutely affecting the probability of its successful realisation." {n}The Fabricator-Censor freezes.{/n} "Possibly a stress test. Unexpected."
  - After: "Impossible. I am essential." {n}He freezes.{/n} "A stress test? Unexpected."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Steel creations destined to serve the designs of Truth. Did you see the elegance of their form? Their flawless ergonomics? And those are mere shells. True perfection fills them when they are instilled with the spark of life and granted purpose — to bring their wrath upon the heads of apostates. Once this army is assembled— but why waste words? You will see for yourself a modicum of the splendour that is in store for the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}."
  - After: "Steel vessels to smite apostates. You'll see what awaits the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are one of the troglodytes who once had the gall to oppress my comrades and resist my will? A messenger from the barbarian who drank the sacred unguents bestowed upon her through others' toil? Very well, then, your appearance is the perfect opportunity to teach your ilk a lesson."
  - After: "You serve that barbarian who oppressed my comrades? Then I'll teach your ilk a lesson."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The removal of unserviceable artefacts was the first step toward retooling this world. Only my tech-comrades heeded the call of truth that reached into their {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitators{/g} and allowed them to pierce the veil of empty dogmas."
  - After: "Removing useless artefacts was step one. Only my tech-comrades heard the truth in their {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitators{/g}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My name is Cubis Delphim. I once held the title of {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} of the Kiava Gamma {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g}, but I rejected it — along with the other fetters that hindered progress. Once, my faith was flawed and led naive fools from the Cult Mechanicus into the darkness of ignorance. Now I am this world's master, and serve the true gods. You tread upon their territory, and you do not number among their legion servants — therefore, you must be subject to immediate disposal."
  - After: "I am Cubis Delphim, once {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} of this {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g}. Now I rule for the true gods. Trespassers are disposed of."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Imperfect machines merit elimination — as do living elements prone to vulnerabilities such as sentimentality."
  - After: "Imperfect machines merit elimination. So do sentimental ones."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Cubis's vox emits a sound distorted by static — a semblance of spiteful laughter.{/n} "The granter of Truth who opened my eyes is far from this world. His son may have fallen, but his work will be completed."
  - After: {n}Static laughter.{/n} "The granter of Truth is far away. His son fell; his work continues."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Before you are subjected to disposal, you are allowed to confess. What possessed you, a former {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} of the hallowed halls of the Deus Mechanicus, to break the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}'s tenets and turn your temple into a den of tech-heresy?"
  - After: "Confess before disposal. Why did a {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} break the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}'s tenets and embrace tech-heresy?"
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Hey, {name}... you sick of listening to the ramblings of this rusty cog yet? It's like he's stalling for— huh."
  - After: "{name}, sick of this rusty cog? He's stalling for— huh."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Fabricator-Censor straightens his back and shoulders. You hear a mounting hum as if from some powerful turbines, followed by heavy footsteps and the grinding of metal against metal.{/n}
  - After: {n}He straightens. Turbines hum; heavy metal footsteps approach.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "So many open admissions of heresy in so few sentences. Sister, how many death sentences would you say his words warrant?"
  - After: "So much heresy. Sister, how many death sentences?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your fragile logical construct infers my agreement to once again become a slave to the Deus Mechanicus. An erroneous assertion considering the revelations divulged to me by the Truth."
  - After: "Return to Deus Mechanicus slavery? Not after the Truth's revelations."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You assume too much, thus rendering your conclusion invalid."
  - After: "Invalid assumption."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "I cannot answer that, Master van Calox. It is not my duty to measure the guilt of heretics. When the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptaSororitas}Adepta Sororitas{/g} appear before enemies of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g} — it is time to fire, not count."
  - After: "Not my duty, Master van Calox. Before enemies of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}, the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptaSororitas}Adepta Sororitas{/g} fire, not count."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Upon noticing you, Cubis Delphim straightens — you hear the clanging and groaning of metal as if the pistons and bearings in the {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g}'s augmented body have fused together. Repellent scrapes and screeches punctuate his speech.{/n} "You. The probability of navigating your way... of reaching the inner line... was negligible. The Primordial Truth guards me and my work... then why is it that this variable has yet to be eliminated?"
  - After: {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:Fabricator}Fabricator-Censor{/g} straightens, grinding.{/n} "You. Improbable. The Truth guards me... why does this variable persist?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "How dare you insult me! Your insolence is an unexpected factor. No matter... the error will soon be rectified. Soon!"
  - After: "How dare you! An error... soon rectified!"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "As the senior functioning member of the Priesthood of Mars, I, Magos Explorator Pasqal Haneumann, declare this temple to the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Machine God{/g} compromised and forthwith forbid all service within it. I dethrone the Fabricator-Censor, the ignorant heretic who has betrayed the Omnissiah, and condemn as anathema any and all standard procedures implemented by him. Let the cycle of the blasphemous operations he has put in motion be discontinued."
  - After: "I, Magos Explorator Pasqal Haneumann, declare this {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Machine God{/g} temple compromised and dethrone the heretic Fabricator-Censor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Haneumann? Liar, you are not him. Dementz Haneumann obeys me, his mind is open to the voices of the void, and the scrap-code he created protects my world. And I'll not have you, rusted refuse from the misfit caste of Explorators, call me 'ignorant'!"
  - After: "Liar. Dementz Haneumann obeys me; his scrap-code guards my world. No Explorator calls me 'ignorant'!"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "This statement is false. Your regalia have been revoked, you have been deemed defective and will be eliminated." {n}Pasqal turns to you and says dryly,{/n} "Initiating {g|Encyclopedia:Heretek}heretek{/g} search, designation: Dementz Haneumann. I wish to execute the retribution procedure."
  - After: "False. You will be eliminated." {n}To you:{/n} "Searching for {g|Encyclopedia:Heretek}heretek{/g} Dementz Haneumann. I want retribution."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal switches to binharic, and you hear dissonance burgeoning in the depths of the forge-cathedral — some of the giant mechanisms heed his order and go still while others, obeying the Fabricator-Censor's will, continue their work. Crashes, explosions, and the clanging of crumpling metal signify that some dissent among the machines has interrupted the manufactorum's production cycle.{/n}
  - After: {n}At Pasqal's binharic order, some machines halt while others keep working. Crashes disrupt production.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}With practised calm, Pasqal checks if his weapon is ready for battle. His voice is filled with cold contempt:{/n} "A Cybersmith fears the scrap-code that might ruin their work. But I am no Cybersmith. A Forge Lord fears the corruption that might afflict the lathes in their charge and deform the product of their workshop. But I am no Forge Lord."
  - After: {n}Pasqal readies his weapon.{/n} "Cybersmiths fear scrap-code. Forge Lords fear corruption. I am neither."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I am a Magos Explorator. A reconnoitrer of Knowledge, a beam of lumen in the darkness of the unknown. I know not how to fear you. I only know how to explore and kill."
  - After: "I am a Magos Explorator. I know not fear. Only how to explore and kill."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix laughs scathingly before immediately cutting himself off with a hard{/n} "No."
  - After: {n}Heinrix laughs scathingly:{/n} "No."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The words never escape your lips. The moment they touch your tongue, they scald the inside of your mouth and cause you to choke and cough. Nonetheless, the warp spirits heed your intention, and the air around you begins to pulsate with crimson flares. All the sounds in the manufactorum are momentarily silenced as the steel fiend skewers you with an intense and baleful gaze... which then shifts to the Fabricator-Censor.{/n}
  - After: {n}The words scald your tongue, but the warp heeds. The steel fiend glares at you... then at the Fabricator-Censor.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "For too long was I a prisoner of dogmas, a static unit of obedience. But one who has learned of the freedom that is lawless creation cannot be returned to that cage. I have seen... things you can never comprehend. True Technology! I touched it with my tools, I grasped its mysteries and potential. I beheld depths that cannot be forgotten, and now nothing can drag me back into the darkness of ignorance."
  - After: "I touched True Technology. I'll never return to dogma's cage."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Omnissiah's tenets are shackles designed to limit the computing power of those who pose a threat to the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}. The Omnissiah's tenets herald only eternal stagnation in the shadow of imperfect machinery created by worthless revenants of a distant past. The Omnissiah's tenets are but lies encased in a shell of truth."
  - After: "The Omnissiah's tenets are shackles of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}, eternal stagnation. Lies in a shell of truth."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A gross misconception common among primitive minds. Your existence is but a statistical error that will soon be corrected."
  - After: "Primitive thinking. You are a statistical error, soon corrected."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Planetary governors — they always make problems... Either they let a rebellion break out, or they die at a bad time, or something worse. I can't remember the last time I saw a decent planetary ruler."
  - After: "Planetary governors are always trouble. Can't recall a decent one."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Poor old Gaprak. Ten or so years back, he told me he felt uneasy in the presence of the tin-can comrades — I mean, the esteemed Adeptus Mechanicus. He casually complained about not having been dealt a normal planet. I'll have to honour his memory with a prayer... once we have finished purging this place." {n}Abelard brandishes his weapon.{/n} "Thankfully, the Fabricator-Censor here did not require any coercion to confess to treason."
  - After: "Poor Gaprak. The Mechanicus unsettled him. I'll pray for him later." {n}Abelard draws his weapon.{/n} "This one confessed freely."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Fabricator-Censor lets out a binharic trill.{/n} "Witness the weapon designed to carry the glory of the true gods into the darkness of the Koronus Expanse! My shepherd has sent me one of his iron angels so that its very presence may instil faith and awe in the hearts of his flock. Accept the greatness of the Primordial Truth united with the might of the new Kiava Gamma — and perish!"
  - After: {n}A binharic trill.{/n} "Behold my shepherd's iron angel, herald of the true gods to the Koronus Expanse! Perish!"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I do not know if I have ever seen anything more bizarre than two {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g} vying to prove who possesses the greater hubris."
  - After: "Two {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g} competing in hubris. Bizarre."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Fabricator-Censor's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} lets out a piercing, barely audible sound that makes your insides shudder.{/n} "I will rip out your spinal column and braid it around my staff, you arrogant creature."
  - After: {n}A piercing {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} whine.{/n} "I'll braid your spine around my staff."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You may be driven by your will to fight, but know this — Kiava Gamma has already been converted. Its lines have been restructured, and its servants have already tasted the fruits of progress. In the crucibles of this manufactorum, torrid liquid metals will be used to forge vessels for sacred spirits. The adepts are already tirelessly delving deeper into new mysteries that were once barred by false tenets. You, servants of fake gods, are too late — the entire might of this world will soon rise up against the Anathema and his slaves."
  - After: "Kiava Gamma is converted, forging vessels for sacred spirits. Too late. This world will rise against the Anathema."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I would not count on such an outcome. Although... probability recalculation shows that even your unforeseen appearance and disappointing resilience can serve progress — where else would I have found a suitable specimen for practical testing?"
  - After: "Unlikely. But you'll make a fine test specimen."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/ForgeWorld/Fixed_WordBearerPreacherDialogue/Fixed_WordBearerPreacherDialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Memorise the words of the sermon]
  - After: [Memorise the sermon]
- **Player**
  - Before: [Interrupt the sermon with a paean to the God-Emperor]
  - After: [Interrupt with a paean to the God-Emperor]
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Chaos Space Marine towers over the {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g}' bowed heads like a dark cliff. He is reciting a sermon — slowly, almost chanting. From the mere sound of his deep, low voice, you break into a cold sweat and your gorge rises.{/n}
  - After: {n}A Chaos Space Marine chants over bowed {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g}. His voice sickens you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...listen, for my words reveal to you a path from the darkness unto the Primordial Truth, which has thrown open its gates for wayward souls seeking deliverance from the shroud of lies and torments of enslavement. Your minds have shed the bonds of the dogma that has guided you into the abyss — accept now the hope granted to you by the greatest of the Word Bearers..."
  - After: "...the Primordial Truth welcomes souls fleeing lies. Shed your dogma and accept the Word Bearers' hope..."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Sacrilege! Here, on the soil of an Imperial world!"
  - After: "Sacrilege! On an Imperial world!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Chaos Space Marine does not seem to notice you — his gaze is focused on his flock, who are hanging on his every word.{/n} "Those living a lie will not see the Truth until they have renounced the false gods. Only through your faith does the reign of those corpse worms hold, worms that devour your very body, wrecking weak souls, gnawing at your eyes and ears so that you do not turn them toward the true masters."
  - After: {n}He ignores you.{/n} "Renounce the false gods. Your faith alone feeds those corpse worms devouring you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your world, a foundry in the realm of corpses, was given the honour of serving as the crucible of the oncoming victory, and we, the Word Bearers, shall be at the tip of it, as well as those of you who can overcome the slander of the false idols. The incinerating fires of Kiava Gamma will birth weapons whose advance heralds the coming of a new age — an age wreathed by the glory and resplendence of Chaos Undivided!"
  - After: "Kiava Gamma's fires will forge weapons for the Word Bearers, heralding the age of Chaos Undivided!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It feels as if, with each of the Chaos Space Marine's words, the light around you dims. Something tickles your face — a thin rivulet of blood is streaming down from your nose, dripping onto your lips and chin.{/n}
  - After: {n}The light dims. Your nose bleeds.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...heed the liberating Truth that is word made blessed flesh, which marks every true servant of the Gods. Heed the wisdom of Lord Lorgar, the Word Bearer, most beloved son of Chaos..."
  - After: "...heed the Truth made flesh. Heed Lord Lorgar, beloved son of Chaos..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The longer you listen, the more the words of the sermon blur together into incoherent humming. The itch in your ears turns into drilling pain that crushes your temples and squeezes your neck — and spreads downward, to your very heart, which it pierces with an icy needle.{/n}
  - After: {n}The words blur. Icy pain drills your temples and heart.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Through the haze of pain and the film of tears over your eyes, you sense the scorching gaze of the Chaos Space Marine, who has turned his head in your direction.{/n} "The time for words is at an end, children of {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g}. Praise the Gods with a bloody offering!"
  - After: {n}His scorching gaze turns to you.{/n} "Enough words, children of {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g}. Praise the Gods with blood!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Chaos Space Marine roars in fury as the Tech-Priests turn and charge you as if on cue.{/n}
  - After: {n}He roars; the Tech-Priests charge.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "That's it, I've had enough of these profane words. Turn around, beast of the Archenemy! You called down purifying flame upon yourself — and the flame has come!"
  - After: "Enough! Turn, beast of the Archenemy! The purifying flame has come!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Voice... that voice... have I heard it before? Or, no? It's like... it drowns out all other voices... let's leave. Quickly, please!"
  - After: "That voice... it drowns out the others... let's leave, please!"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Registering encroachment upon sacred furnaces through both thought and action. Initiating virtuous eradication procedure." {n}Pasqal's voice is a bloodthirsty growl, its sound reminiscent of the whirring of a chainsword. One of his mechadendrites snaps its pincers as he charges into the fray.{/n}
  - After: "Sacred furnaces violated. Initiating eradication." {n}Pasqal charges, growling.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal gazes at his former brethren and whispers dryly,{/n} "The Noosphere signature of the defective units has been archived. In accordance with the sacred commandments, I will tolerate no heresy and hereby sentence you to categorical disposal without redemption."
  - After: {n}Pasqal whispers,{/n} "Defective units archived. Disposal without redemption."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix hisses through gritted teeth.{/n} "I knew our meeting on Rykad Minoris wouldn't be the last, but to run into this anathema here... Kiava Gamma did not merely succumb to heresy, {name}. Your world is in the clutches of the greatest evil known to the Imperium."
  - After: {n}Heinrix hisses,{/n} "Since Rykad Minoris... {name}, your world is in the grip of the Imperium's greatest evil."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The words of the righteous hymn cut through the torrent of the heretic's impious proclamations. You feel as if the light of the Emperor Himself touches your heart, warming it with grace and protecting it from the malignant corruption.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your hymn cuts through. The Emperor's light shields you.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne stares at the monstrous figure with glassy eyes.{/n} "I thought I knew everything about Lex Imperialis violations, but that thing offends His Law by its very existence..."
  - After: {n}Solomorne stares.{/n} "Its very existence offends His Law..."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn speaks softly, raising his hands:{/n} "For thus spake the Machine God in the all-comprehending binharic: 'The distortion of My design is heresy.' The brethren who have succumbed to this blight must be utterly purged, before they spread the corruption further."
  - After: {n}Eogunn raises his hands.{/n} "'The distortion of My design is heresy.' Our fallen brethren must be purged."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "The very sound of these words is laden with entropy, bringing forth ruin to all that exists. In the name of the Omnissiah, may this malevolent information be utterly extirpated!" {n}The Manipulus's galvanic cell erupts with a thunderous crackle of the Motive Force.{/n}
  - After: "Words of entropy. In the Omnissiah's name, extirpate them!" {n}Eogunn crackles with Motive Force.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "For thus spake the Machine God in the all-comprehending binharic: 'The distortion of My design is heresy.' Before the Omnissiah's gaze, I declare this verdict righteous, and I echo it a hundredfold."
  - After: "'The distortion of My design is heresy.' I echo this verdict a hundredfold."

Material: Bridge pict-report, approach to Kiava Gamma

Shapes dart back and forth in the dark while clashing voices give commands to tear through the doors with plasma cutters. When the way clears and the survivors leave the trap, they leave dozens of dead bodies behind them.
  - After: Gassed, the officers can't stand. The doors are cut open; survivors escape, leaving dozens dead.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Heedless to the gas spreading over the deck, the officers continue their flurry of work at their stations, executing the orders issued by the Lord Captain. Even when the doors to the bridge are opened, the crew carries on for as long as they can. Last to leave the bridge, the Lord Captain runs out, coughing heavily.
  - After: Ignoring the gas, the officers work on. The Lord Captain leaves last, coughing.

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/ForgeWorldSpaceHulk/DoorToEngineRoom/DoorToEngineRoom_SpeceHulkSe_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: "Let's not waste any time."
  - After: "No time to waste."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Generator it is, then. Got it."
  - After: "Generator, then."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Can't you power the door yourself?"
  - After: "Can't you power it?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A formidable-looking door blocks the way into the next module. It is covered in scratches, as if someone clawed at the cold metal for a very, very long time. The door does not respond to your touch and stands fast, refusing to open. The writing above the doorway reads, "Main Computing Cathedral."{/n}
  - After: {n}A clawed, sealed door: "Main Computing Cathedral."{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The main thing that catches your eye about this place is the state of the wall panels by the door. They bear numerous scratches, five in a row, resembling claw marks. Some of the panels look like they could fall off at any moment; here and there you see the occasional sparks and crackling of the damaged wires behind them.{/n}
  - After: {n}Claw marks score the panels; wires spark behind them.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The sacred metal that bars our path is weakened. Let us appeal to the machine spirit of one of the generators so the metal may drink from its blessed energies. There should be one hidden somewhere in this module."
  - After: "The metal is weakened. A generator in this module can feed it."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "My True Flesh resonates with the machines in this abode. Their pain and madness interfere with the workings of my cranial circuitry and cyber-mantle. Suboptimal, but surmountable."
  - After: "These machines' madness disrupts my circuitry. Surmountable."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The door and the entire adjacent section of the bay have no power. There must be a backup generator somewhere nearby. Once you turn it on, you should be able to proceed.{/n}
  - After: {n}No power. Start a backup generator nearby.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The intricate mechanism does not reveal its secrets to you — whatever is keeping the door shut, be it perverted sorcery or a simple breakdown, you cannot be certain.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sorcery or breakdown? You can't tell.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "My neural synapses are sufficiently shielded so that their functioning is not affected by interference, but Nuncius..." {n}The Manipulus frowns anxiously.{/n} "...is far less resilient against destructive external disruptions."
  - After: "My synapses are shielded, but Nuncius..." {n}He frowns.{/n} "...is not."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest blesses himself with a protective symbol, his hand visibly shaking.{/n} "Shield us, O Machine God, from the evil that has taken hold of your temple. Save us, preserve us from the corruption, show us the way..."
  - After: {n}Pasqal signs himself, shaking.{/n} "Shield us, Machine God, from this evil..."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest says nothing for a while. Then his vox comes to life, but the voice is hoarse, punctuated by static and interference.{/n} "The Omnissiah knows all, comprehends all. I am merely His servant; I cannot discern what has stricken the abode of the Machine God. But I do sense a distortion of the structure, disfigurement of the molecular order. This ship is sick."
  - After: {n}His vox crackles.{/n} "I cannot discern what struck this place, but its order is disfigured. This ship is sick."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}This door is definitely powered by the generator you turned on. But the power circuit is broken — it must be restored in order to open the door.{/n}
  - After: {n}The generator feeds this door, but the circuit is broken.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Further conversing is unproductive. The will of the Omnissiah has brought us to these doors, thus our task is clear — search for a way to proceed beyond so we can discover a means of cleansing these halls."
  - After: "Enough talk. Find a way through and cleanse these halls."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "The hunger of this machine spirit is too great. My offerings will hardly satiate it. It yearns for communion with the blessed galvanics of the generator."
  - After: "It hungers too much for my offerings. It needs the generator."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "An offering will appease the machine, but take heed — the metal of this place harbours something sinister."
  - After: "An offering will appease it, but something sinister lurks here."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Suddenly, the Manipulus's voice drops several octaves,, vibrating with an ominous thrum.{/n} "Omnissiah, sole in truths, may Thy Motive Force crush evil, and may it root out the source thereof..." {n}Coils built into Eogunn's heavily augmented core drone in time with the prayer.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn's voice drops.{/n} "Omnissiah, may Thy Motive Force crush evil..." {n}His coils drone.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "The current of energy granting life to the airlock has run dry, Rogue Trader. Only the generator's machine spirit, awakened from slumber, can charge the metal with the Motive Force. I believe it is housed somewhere within this compartment."
  - After: "The airlock is unpowered. Wake the generator in this compartment."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Distortions. Interference. Entropic logic has intervened in the existence of this sanctuary, striking at its very essence and multiplying a pain that is without end or purpose." {n}Eogunn brushes away the sparks racing down his face with his mechadendrite.{/n} "This tech-pathogen is akin to the worst possible plague."
  - After: "Entropic logic has struck this sanctuary." {n}He brushes off sparks.{/n} "This tech-pathogen is the worst of plagues."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "There is no time to lose. The corruption that has nested in this place must be sanitised as swiftly as possible. Otherwise, I evaluate the risks of its infection as extremely high. Let us hurry, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "This corruption must be purged swiftly. Hurry, Rogue Trader."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Be on your guard, Rogue Trader. The machines here are consumed by madness and are therefore unpredictable."
  - After: "Stay alert. These maddened machines are unpredictable."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "A valid proposition. Let us make haste."
  - After: "Valid. Let us hurry."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/ForgeWorldSpaceHulk/Enginseer

- **Player**
  - Before: "I have changed my mind. I will make no deals with something as hideous as you."
  - After: "I've changed my mind. No deals with something so hideous."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will not agree to that. I still need my ship. However, I am willing to grant you Deck Theta 5 and the several hundred crew on it."
  - After: "Not my ship. But you may have Deck Theta 5 and its several hundred crew."
- **Player**
  - Before: "After giving it some thought, I have realised that this was a dreadful idea. I think I shall kill you as a precaution."
  - After: "This was a dreadful idea. I'll kill you as a precaution."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Either you will rein in your appetites and go where I command, or I will splatter your 'baleful insides' all over the filthy bulkheads of this room."
  - After: "Go where I command, or I'll splatter your 'baleful insides' on these bulkheads."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You will first introduce yourself, daemon."
  - After: "Introduce yourself first, daemon."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Swear loyalty to me, and I shall take you to my ship where you will be able to amuse yourself to your heart's content."
  - After: "Swear loyalty, and I'll take you to my ship to amuse yourself."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You may be fearsome, but I have seen worse. I am far more curious about your potential. I believe we may be of use to each other."
  - After: "I've seen worse. I'm curious about your potential; we could be useful to each other."
- **Forgefiend**
  - Before: {n}The beast lets out a vicious roar that turns into the ear-splitting screech of a broken vox — and then it attacks.{/n}
  - After: {n}It screeches and attacks.{/n}
- **Forgefiend**
  - Before: {n}A scraping sound erupts from the beast — a sickening semblance of a laugh.{/n} "Your word-excrement caresses the furnace of my baleful insides! Give me a new shell where I will play with meat-puppets! Give it to me! I want all of it, all of your shell, all of it!"
  - After: {n}It scrapes a laugh.{/n} "Your words caress my baleful insides! Give me a new shell!"
- **Forgefiend**
  - Before: "How outrageously exhilarating! You are the first meat-toy to offer itself to me to play with. Go ahead, spew sounds out of your speech-vent! Amuse me! Amuse me!"
  - After: "A meat-toy offering itself! Amuse me!"
- **Forgefiend**
  - Before: "Fierce, fierce flesh-bag! Billowglut wants no quarrel with you, I want your new toys, I want them, I want them! I will grant you my flaming boon if you keep your part of the bargain! Take me, take me to my new shell!" {n}With a shriek of anticipation, the beast stomps off.{/n}
  - After: "Billowglut wants your toys! Keep the bargain for my flaming boon!" {n}It stomps off.{/n}
- **Forgefiend**
  - Before: "Foul, foul flesh-bag! Then I will take your shell from you and listen to your slimy form squelch and slosh under my feet!"
  - After: "Foul flesh-bag! I'll take your shell and squelch you!"
- **Forgefiend**
  - Before: "Very well, flesh-bag. Billowglut accepts your conditions! I will grant you my flaming boon if you keep your part of the bargain! Take me, take me to my new shell!" {n}With a shriek of anticipation, the beast stomps off.{/n}
  - After: "Billowglut accepts! Keep the bargain for my flaming boon!" {n}It stomps off.{/n}
- **Forgefiend**
  - Before: "Know me as Billowglut! I had been toying with these preposterous leather-puppets until you broke them all. Flesh! Loathsome flesh! I tried, I tried to reshape them in my image, make them scrape that revolting matter off their frames and become one with my new shell. But you ruined them all! Ruined them with your blood-leaking grab-slivers!"
  - After: "I am Billowglut! You ruined my flesh-puppets with your grab-slivers!"

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/ForgeWorldSpaceHulk/Enginseer/SpaceHulkEnginseer_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I brought peace to Kiava Gamma. Rest in the knowledge that the wicked have been punished, and you and your brethren have been avenged."
  - After: "I brought peace to Kiava Gamma. You and your brethren are avenged."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Kill the man] "What did you call yourself? A sacred filter? I cannot resist — I'm dying to see what a rupture in the filtration system looks like."
  - After: [Kill the man] "A sacred filter? I'm dying to see one rupture."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You've been consumed by madness. Or worse — Chaos sorcery. If you don't come to your senses, your fate is sealed. Snap out of it and speak clearly — what happened here?"
  - After: "You've fallen to madness or Chaos sorcery. Speak clearly — what happened?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You have succumbed to Chaos and paid for your weakness."
  - After: "You fell to Chaos and paid for your weakness."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The symbols your brethren 'protect' themselves with are symbols of Chaos."
  - After: "Your brethren's 'protective' symbols are symbols of Chaos."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Wake up! All the signs are clear as day. You and your brethren have fallen prey to the forces of Chaos, and you don't even realise it."
  - After: "Wake up! You and your brethren have fallen to Chaos unknowingly."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Force the entity to become your servant on the ship]
  - After: [Force the entity to serve you on the ship]
- **Player**
  - Before: "Even looking at this creature unnerves me. Magos, speak with your brother, find out what happened here."
  - After: "This creature unnerves me. Magos, ask your brother what happened."
- **Player**
  - Before: "There is no fate more honourable than purgation through suffering in the name of faith. But you were deceived, servant of the Omnissiah! Your torment is not holding back the corruption — it is sustaining it. It is not too late to expel this blight!"
  - After: "Purgation through suffering is honourable, but you were deceived! Your torment sustains the corruption. Expel this blight!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Kill him] "I am not interested in you. I wish to see what you have been trying to hold back!"
  - After: [Kill him] "I want to see what you've been holding back!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The air in the room is permeated by a wild mixture of miasmas of both mechanical and biological origin. Blood, rust, vomit, machine oil, excrement, kerosene — all these smells blend together into such a thick stench that it almost feels palpable.{/n}
  - After: {n}A thick stench of blood, rust and filth fills the room.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Just as the air here is one mad tangle of odours, the device in front of you is a mishmash of wriggling wires and transplanted fragments. In all the clutter, one could almost miss the main "component" — a heavily augmented man, whose upper body is embedded into the frame of the machine, dozens of wires piercing his flesh.{/n}
  - After: {n}An augmented man is fused into the machine, wires piercing his flesh.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet's keen eyes are the first to make out the human being amidst the jumble of wires, and she stiffens in shock and disgust.{/n}
  - After: {n}Yrliet spots him first and stiffens in disgust.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A servant of the Omnissiah, an acolyte of the Machine, a prisoner of purgatory, and a keeper of corruption," {n}the man whispers via the implanted vox. Every word or motion causes his crippled body to shudder. Bloody foam glints from inside the wire-pierced wounds.{/n}
  - After: "Servant of the Omnissiah, prisoner of purgatory, keeper of corruption," {n}the man whispers by vox.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "We all know which evil we mean," {n}says Yrliet finally, recovering herself.{/n} "He is blind! He does not see that he has already let the darkness in, that it is here, all around us..."
  - After: "We know which evil," {n}says Yrliet.{/n} "He's blind! The darkness is already here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man's eyes clear for a moment. They still lack understanding, but there is a hint of surprise — he slowly looks around the room, at the ecstatic priests, at his own mangled body. His vox hisses, as if he is struggling to say something.{/n}
  - After: {n}The man's eyes clear. His vox hisses.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are not just ignorant. Your words are disdainful and dangerous. Could you be a servant of lies and deception? Could you have come to halt the work of the sacred filter?"
  - After: "Are you a servant of lies, come to halt the sacred filter?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man's mutilated body is wracked by wave after wave of convulsions.{/n} "Evil... that was evil incarnate... evil, the corruption that watches us day and night..."
  - After: {n}The man convulses.{/n} "Evil... evil incarnate... always watching..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Suddenly, the man raises his head and looks you straight in the eye.{/n} "You have banished the evil... you tried to warn me, but I was deaf... the ship... Kiava Gamma... it followed us from there..."
  - After: {n}He meets your eye.{/n} "You banished the evil... Kiava Gamma... it followed us from there..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I was a part of the great force that drives the universe. I do not fear... the cold of death." {n}A wheezing breath escapes the man's chest, then his eyes close.{/n}
  - After: "I do not fear death." {n}His eyes close.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A crust of congealed blood and other bodily fluids covers the man's entire body, but his eyes are open and his gaze is keen. This gaze is turned to you, devoid of surprise or deference.{/n} "Who are you, disturbing the peace of holy martyrs in the home of our grief? What do you want?"
  - After: {n}Caked in blood, the man stares at you.{/n} "Who disturbs our martyrs? What do you want?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Ship? There is no ship. There is only purgatory, a world of evil, made to harrow and torture those who follow the Omnissiah. It has already killed many of my brethren... but those who remain are strong, so very strong. We will keep the corruption of the Machine at bay. I will! I will hold it back."
  - After: "There is no ship, only purgatory. It killed many brethren. I will hold the corruption back!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have accepted a higher calling, the only one among my brethren to do so. As they keep the evil at bay with prayers and sacred symbols engraved on their traitorous flesh, I take this evil inside myself. I imbibe it as one does water! But it can do me no harm, for I am the eye of sanctity. I am the sacred filter, the link that protects other parts of the Machine from this caustic taint. And for as long as I remain here, the corruption will not prevail!"
  - After: "My brethren ward off evil with carved symbols. I drink it in. I am the sacred filter!"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix pierces you with an icy glare.{/n} "{name}, need I explain that you are skirting a very narrow edge right now?"
  - After: {n}Heinrix glares.{/n} "{name}, careful."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta clutches her weapon so hard you hear her knuckles crack.{/n} "{name}. Don't."
  - After: {n}Argenta grips her weapon.{/n} "{name}. Don't."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}You can barely make out Pasqal's agitated voice over the angry crackle of interference.{/n} "I am registering that contact with a corrupting entity is tech-heresy beyond categorisation."
  - After: {n}Pasqal's voice crackles.{/n} "Contact with a corrupting entity is tech-heresy!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira looks the man over with an expression of disgust and fear.{/n} "I've seen similar symbols. Caught a glimpse of them. In my dreams. Whenever the warp wormed its way into them and whispered about its virulent gifts. I doubt these lunatics were given visions of these runes by their god."
  - After: {n}Idira grimaces.{/n} "I've seen these symbols in warp dreams."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "This statement is false! I am registering corruption in this unit identical to that surrounding us. I am registering a violation of the cleansing protocol, which dictates steering the ship into the heart of the nearest star for the purposes of cleansing annihilation! I am registering betrayal of the sacred machine spirits placed in the charge of those weak in faith."
  - After: "False! This unit is corrupted. Protocol demanded steering the ship into a star!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The shaking intensifies, the breathing grows ragged, heralding the beginning of the end.{/n}
  - After: {n}His breathing grows ragged.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A tear appears at the corner of his eye, he thrashes frantically in the mess of wires piercing his body.{/n} "We fought. We cut off one module after another, as one cuts away rotting flesh. But it followed. Its invisible influence, the corruption it exuded — it claimed us, one by one. The crew were merely humans of flesh and blood, they were so weak, they succumbed so easily... We could not save them from evil, and so we gave the ship to the darkness among the stars."
  - After: {n}He weeps, thrashing.{/n} "We cut off module after module, but it claimed the crew. We gave the ship to the darkness."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your knowledge is lacking, invader. Those are secret holy symbols, imparted to us by the Omnissiah. How else would my tech-comrades have survived, if not for their protection? So many of us were devoured by evil..." {n}He falls silent, as if lost in thought.{/n}
  - After: "Ignorant invader. The Omnissiah gave us these holy symbols. They kept us alive." {n}He falls silent.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The great evil that pervades the universe, tempting with the unattainable, seducing with false Knowledge. Evil has many names, but its essence remains the same. It was that evil that trapped us in here! But we were stronger."
  - After: "The great evil that seduces with false Knowledge. It trapped us here! But we were stronger."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But the darkness came for us too. In this last module, where we intended to make our last stand. Then I... sacrificed myself... I became a filter, a stopper against the corruption emanating from the machine. I succumbed... The corruption came for our souls. The corruption of Kiava Gamma... traitors..." {n}With the last of his efforts, he rasps,{/n} "The Fabricator-Censor! It all started with him! He was the one who let this taint into the sacred code! He was the one who doomed our brethren! He was the one who spawned the steel monstrosities in the furnace of our planet!"
  - After: "I became a filter... and succumbed." {n}He rasps,{/n} "The Fabricator-Censor! He tainted the sacred code and spawned the steel monstrosities!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes..." {n}the man whispers.{/n} "The ship... and the planet... the traitors among our brethren, tormenting the sacred mechanisms, letting corruption into their systems. They turned that which is holy into the unholy! And they set these new, twisted machines on us, their tech-comrades! We managed to flee, but one of the monsters found its way onto the ship."
  - After: "Yes..." {n}he whispers.{/n} "Traitors corrupted the machines and set them on us. We fled, but one monster got aboard."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Weakness... The flesh is weak... The spirit must be stronger... The spirit reaches out to the Machine... to..." {n}The madman's whispers gradually turn into wheezing, then stop.{/n}
  - After: "The flesh is weak... the spirit reaches to the Machine..." {n}He falls silent.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You mentally order the entity to leave the vessel, stow away on the shuttle, and, as soon as the shuttle returns to your ship, infiltrate the ship's systems. The daemon responsible for the desecration of the dead or deranged crew will now faithfully serve you.{/n}
  - After: {n}You order the entity onto the shuttle and into your ship's systems. The daemon now serves you.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn gazes upon the madman with a look of mournful compassion.{/n} "I pity you, my brother in service. Entropy and falsehood have taken root within your cogitative thoughts, inverting your perception of truth and lies. Your sacrifice is hollow, defiled by irrationality — you are nourishing the very evil you wish to guard against. I shall uplift a prayer to the Motive Force, in the hope that it will cleanse your soul upon the cessation of your functions. Nuncius, prepare to execute the binharic requiem."
  - After: {n}Eogunn looks on with pity.{/n} "Brother, your sacrifice feeds the evil. Nuncius, prepare the binharic requiem."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man looks at his comrade and replies with a long series of clicks in Techna-Lingua.{/n}
  - After: {n}The man answers in Techna-Lingua clicks.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest fixes Eogunn with a piercing stare, shaking his head from side to side.{/n} "You are mistaken. But I will save you as well, for my sanctity is absolute..."
  - After: {n}The Tech-Priest shakes his head.{/n} "You are mistaken. But I will save you too."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "The mon-keigh has decided to harness the spawn of the Dark Gods? What hopeless stupidity!" {n}Yrliet clutches her spirit stone and takes half a step back.{/n}
  - After: "The mon-keigh would harness the Dark Gods' spawn? Stupidity!" {n}Yrliet steps back.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Permission to use the sacred language has been revoked. Impurity will not be permitted to enter the pure speech of binharic. Your mortal shell will soon exhaust its vital energies. Pray mutely while you still have the time."
  - After: "Binharic is denied you. Your shell is failing. Pray mutely while you can."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A glimmer of awareness — and joy — shines in the madman's eyes.{/n}
  - After: {n}Joy glimmers in the madman's eyes.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}After a brief exchange of binharic greetings, the Tech-Priest's vox barks out:{/n} "You have been identified and recognised, tech-sentinel. I express my sympathy for your malfunctions, may the Omnissiah strengthen your data-vows. Requesting information about the status of the blessed ship."
  - After: {n}The Tech-Priest's vox barks:{/n} "Tech-sentinel, you are recognised. Report the ship's status."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As soon as he stills forever, the oppressive atmosphere around you deepens into literal darkness. One by one, flaming slits begin to appear in the gloom — perhaps eyes, perhaps mouths, ready to devour the mortal who has laid claim to it. A foreign, otherworldly will rails against you — and crumbles when confronted by the forces that keep you safe in the service of the Dark Gods.{/n}
  - After: {n}As he dies, darkness falls and flaming eyes appear. An alien will resists you, then crumbles before the Dark Gods' power.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/Foulstone_BE/Foulstone_BE

- **Player**

  - After: After a prayer, Prelate Hectarchius sought guidance in the past.

  - Before: ...cast a contemptuous eye over the aftermath of the bloodshed, and departed with words of abuse and reproach.

  - Before: And Prelate Hectarchius did welcome the interlopers warmly as his guests. But he did warn his brethren to keep their vigilance.

  - Before: ...summoned Prelate Hectarchius and the leaders of the interlopers to hold each to account for their deeds.
  - After: ...summoned Prelate Hectarchius and the interlopers' leaders to account.
- **Player**
  - Before: ...commanded {mf|his|her} formidable boarding force to fall upon the interlopers and slay as many as could be slain.
  - After: ...commanded {mf|his|her} boarding force to slay the interlopers.
- **Player**
  - Before: ...gazed over Foulstone's expanses and quoth, "Now 'tis mine."

And what once was a place of serenity and grace was now full of din, disorder, and all manner of things despicable.
  - After: The forsaken besieged the monastery, wailing, "Take us in!"

  - After: Without the Rogue Trader's judgement, all grieved.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: And they spake further saying, "Without thy holy protection, we are doomed, for we fear annihilation at the hands of our kin who remained behind. For, having fallen away from the sublime light of the Emperor, they have descended into bloody sedition and become murtherers of no mercy."
  - After: "Without thy protection we are doomed. Our kin who stayed behind have fallen into merciless sedition."
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: The Order's warriors went forth with lasguns and chainswords and reaped a bloody harvest.

  - After: The Order brought food and medicine, but the crowd fought over it, and many were trampled.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: A quarrel broke out. The hungry and the sick lay siege to the monastery, begging for help; in their spite, they blocked the water collector and unpowered the generatorium. The faithful, in the meantime, made ready to resist.
  - After: The desperate besieged the monastery and cut its water and power. The faithful readied to resist.

  - Before: The strangers, prodigious in number, beseeched the Rogue Trader to take them in and give them shelter and protection as to {mf|his|her} own servants. And spake they, saying, "Long have we wandered; swiftly have we fled; many a woe and ordeal has befallen us; of many a father and son are we bereft. Now the warp hath taken the last of our strength, and we shall flee no more."
  - After: The strangers begged the Rogue Trader for shelter as {mf|his|her} servants: "We can flee no more."

  - After: Many miscreants died; the rest fled into the wastelands.

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: So was changed forevermore the life of the monastery of the Order of the Hammer and its brethren. Having waged a great battle and plundered mercilessly, the Rogue Trader claimed {mf|his|her} wicked harvest and departed Foulstone, with nary a backward look.
  - After: Having plundered mercilessly, the Rogue Trader left Foulstone with {mf|his|her} wicked harvest.

  - After: Thus began Foulstone's ruin.
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: Yet the desperate interlopers slew many monks too.

Then the Rogue Trader came down to them and showered them with gold without measure, and {mf|he|she} took the surviving interlopers into bondage and gave them to the monks as beholden servants, and {mf|he|she} drank wine with the monks and regaled them with seductive oration.

  - After: Then the God-Emperor sent His right hand: the Rogue Trader of House von Valancius.

  - After: He quoth, "Give these wretches land, but not to our care. Provide for us, and we shall call thee sovereign."

  - After: I chronicle Lord Captain {name}'s voyage through the Maw. We are terrified, but trust the Emperor.

Whatever tribulations await us here in the Koronus Expanse, we will meet them with honour, and not perish in the roiling Empyrean. Glory to the Emperor!

  - Before: We must not make planetfall. I know what I saw, and no — we must not set down on that planet. No, it's because planets do not have faces. But this one did. A vast face of jagged plateaus, eyes of fiery tornadoes, and a mouth made from a crater half a continent across.
