  - Before: The rousing speech from the Lord Captain, which was broadcast over the {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-system, inspired the crew, who promptly broke into teams to repair the primary systems. The volunteers, all departed, were later lauded in prayer.
  - After: The Lord Captain's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} speech inspired repairs. The dead volunteers were honoured in prayer.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The rousing speech from the Lord Captain, which was broadcast over the {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-system, failed to have the desired effect on the corruption-afflicted crew. After the execution of every tenth crew member, those who remained promptly formed teams to repair the primary systems.
  - After: The Lord Captain's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} speech failed. After every tenth man was shot, the rest began repairs.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Huddled next to the vox-caster, I, First Deputy Carto-Artifex Sebullon Primix, scream into it, hoping that my voice will by some miracle break through the turbulent abyss of the Immaterium into the real world. The Vox Master is dead, virtually everyone is dead, and I, disregarding the sacred vox-system protocol, scream my dispatch over and over: "All Imperial vessels! Help! We are dying! Dying! We're dyyyySTOPITSTOPITIMAFRAIDAFRAIDAFRAIDAFRAID..."
  - After: I, Deputy Carto-Artifex Sebullon Primix, scream into the vox: "All Imperial vessels! Help! We're dyyyySTOPITIMAFRAIDAFRAID..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The warp is a sly and insidious beast, Lord Captain. We are ready to acknowledge that now. It was pleased that we admitted our defeat. That is why it let us come back. And we believe there can be only one reason for that — an even worse fate awaits us here.
  - After: The warp let us return because we admitted defeat, Lord Captain. Something worse awaits us here.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: We are voidsmen, sir. We know we will die long before we ever get the chance to soil ourselves in our sickbed. We know our trade — we conquer the void, discover stars, ship freight, and plunder forgotten planets. And we die — we die in ways so horrible that most people can't even imagine such a death. Well, we've gone to a place others fear to even think about. And we've come back from there along with our Lord Captain. Next time the warp tries to play its games, we'll tell it, "What else do you have to throw at us?"
  - After: We're voidsmen, sir. We die young and horribly. We went where others fear to, and came back. Warp, what else you got?
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: I would be willing to swear that generator 6's power circuit unit was switched off when we began the warp jump. There were cracks in the casing, the enclosure was damaged. We would never start up that piece of junk, it would have blown in seconds. And I have no idea how it switched itself on. No one from the crew touched it. When the last generator failed, the energy supply should have been cut off, but... number 6 continued to run. It dragged us along for 18 minutes. Even though it should have exploded after 18 milliseconds. I don't know how that happened. The Emperor protects.
  - After: Generator 6 was cracked and off, yet it ran 18 minutes after the others failed. It should've blown in milliseconds. The Emperor protects.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Report from Enginseer deck.
All internal and external systems are damaged, but we have detected no critical failures. Emergency repairs are underway.
  - After: Enginseer deck report.
All systems damaged, none critically. Repairing.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: After offering up the requisite prayers, the crew received a {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-address from the blessed Lord Captain, in which our commander...
  - After: After prayers, the Lord Captain's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-address...
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: When the message came through the {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-net, I struggled to hear it over the whispering of the angel in my ears. My honourable {mf|lord|lady} gave the order to...
  - After: Over the angel's whispers on the {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}, my {mf|lord|lady} ordered us to...
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Over the static and the howling of the unholy warp spirits that had infiltrated our {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}-system, we heard the voice of our Lord Captain, who ordered us to...
  - After: Through warp howls on the {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}, the Lord Captain ordered us to...
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: We were all prepared to die that very hour, and then the Lord Captain bade us...
  - After: Ready to die, we heard the Lord Captain bid us...
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Lord Captain, a warp jump to the Hermitage cannot be calculated. We cannot detect its shadow within the sacred radiance of the {g|Encyclopedia:Astronomican}Astronomican{/g} — the warp's storms are obstructing everything. We think our only chance is to make a longer jump to Footfall. Our chances of survival are low, but not non-existent. Emperor preserve us.
  - After: Lord Captain, storms hide the Hermitage from the {g|Encyclopedia:Astronomican}Astronomican{/g}. Our only chance is a longer jump to Footfall.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: After tossing aside his discharged lasgun, a priest brought his fingers to his bleeding ears and then daubed these crimson words on the bulkhead: "Don't listen to him. He is no angel!" Who was he talking to? Me?
  - After: A priest wrote in blood: "Don't listen to him. He is no angel!" Was that for me?
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: I left the Astropathic Choir bay and spent this jump in the Navigator's Sanctum. Though the number of casualties was high there, many managed to survive, including me.
  - After: I spent this jump in the Navigator's Sanctum. Many died; I survived.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: I left the Astropathic Choir bay and spent this jump in the Navigator's Sanctum. I do not dare describe the horrors I witnessed there, or how my heart grieves for every one of the dozens who perished on this journey. The warp was merciless toward us, and only luck allowed me to escape the bloody harvest it reaped there.
  - After: I spent this jump in the Navigator's Sanctum. Dozens died horribly; only luck saved me.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: As soon as the ship exited the warp, thousands of crew members, assembled into teams, launched into repairing the major areas of damage. The will of our fearless Lord Captain drove them, and in that moment, I deeply envied their resolve.
  - After: Out of the warp, thousands of crew began repairs, driven by the Lord Captain's will. I envied them.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: As soon as the ship exited the warp, the voice of our fearless Lord Captain ordered the crew to begin repairs. But not all of them, far from all of them, heeded this order, gripped as they were by terror and despair, just as I was.
  - After: Out of the warp, the Lord Captain ordered repairs. Many, terrified like me, did not obey.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Halting their vigil over the sacred machines, the Enginseers left the majestic vaults of the enginarium. With prayers in Lingua-Technis, the warriors of technology sanctified the decks of humble mortals.
  - After: The Enginseers left the enginarium to bless the lower decks.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: To suppress the fire and give the damaged primary systems the proper level of care, each Tech-Priest was accompanied by a flock of rapidly servitorised crew members, whose brains had been loaded with the Mysteries of the Adeptus Mechanicus.
  - After: Each Tech-Priest led freshly servitorised crew to fight fires and tend systems.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Furthermore, when the malevolent tentacles of the warp reached into our souls, and a bloody inscription in an unholy language began to appear on the bulkhead, the Emperor granted me the blessing of bearing witness to a miracle. Sister Argenta, entirely undaunted, marched up to the bulkhead and erased the words with a fearless swipe of her hand. She turned to us with a smile and said, "It is only blood. Do not fear the Immaterium, for its nightmares are nothing before the Emperor's light." In that moment, I had faith that all was not yet lost. Today I believe I was mistaken.
  - After: Sister Argenta wiped blood-script off the wall: "It is only blood. Do not fear the Immaterium." I had faith then. Now I doubt.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: My {mf|lord|lady}, it grieves me to report the demise of 27.61% of the blessed machine spirits entrusted to my care. Reactors 2 and 3 required expedited burials, and the deck's crew held a vigil in their memory. The {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}servitors{/g} have logged at least eleven breaches in the hull exterior, and at least three in the hull interior. With my {mf|lord|lady}'s gracious permission, I will endeavour to save what can still be saved. The {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g} knows all, comprehends all.
  - After: My {mf|lord|lady}, 27.61% of my machine spirits are dead, Reactors 2 and 3 among them. {g|Encyclopedia:Servitor}Servitors{/g} logged eleven outer and three inner hull breaches. With my {mf|lord|lady}'s leave, I'll save what I can. The {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g} knows all.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: I cried out as I watched Enginseers burning holy incense and chanting the prayer to waken the plasma generator's machine spirit. A young acolyte, his heart wavering, accidentally disrupted the liturgy, releasing the Motive Force into the power circuit before it was time, and my poor eyes were blinded by the white light of the explosion.
  - After: An acolyte released the Motive Force too soon, and the plasma generator's blast blinded me.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: I don't know how they haven't gone crazy yet, sitting in the middle of this warp storm. There are around a thousand people there — a few hundred outcasts and anchorites living permanently on the station, and the crew of a trading vessel that barely made it as far as the Hermitage and won't be departing ever again. It seems they spend whole days sitting under their crystal dome praying, eating ration packs, and watching as reality loses its mind. They say the Emperor will protect them against the coming tempest... Of course they do. He is the only thing they can trust in now. For them, there is nowhere else to turn. We offered them passage on our ship — not one said yes. Mad, all of them.
  - After: A thousand outcasts and stranded traders pray under their dome as reality goes mad. We offered passage. None accepted. Mad.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Halting their vigil over the sacred machines, the Enginseers left the majestic vaults of the enginarium.
  - After: The Enginseers left the enginarium.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: To send repair teams to put out the fire, the officers had to drive the voidsmen away from the rescue shuttles with weapons in their hands. The instigators of the shameful attempt to escape were shot on the spot.
  - After: Officers drove voidsmen from the shuttles at gunpoint and shot the ringleaders.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Lord Captain, we report that, to our disgrace, we failed to safeguard the crew of the Navigator's Sanctum. During the warp jump, virtually the entire crew was afflicted with monstrous deformations, which we cannot bring ourselves to recount. The senior officers began the last watch, we were here al000ne, we gave all the junior crew the mercy of dFeaRth. We sealed the airlocks, as the echoes of our pain were great enough to drive the uninitiated to madness. Lead us where you will — onward to Port WanDONTer, or back. We will serve and steer the ship as long as we can.
  - After: Lord Captain, deformations took the Sanctum crew. We gave the juniors the mercy of dFeaRth and sealed the airlocks. Port WanDONTer or back, we'll steer.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The pict chronicle recorded by the eyes of the servo-skulls made my heart stutter. In horror, I watched as a crewman, who seemed perfectly healthy, struggled against the shackles pinning him to an operating table, and a group of doctors, whispering excitedly among themselves, drew out their steel surgical instruments and eagerly began cutting into his flesh.
  - After: The servo-skull picts showed eager doctors cutting into a healthy, shackled crewman.

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/PenalWorld/Survivors/Survivors_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "Why have you stopped? We aren't done with you yet!"
  - After: [Attack] "Why stop? We're not done with you!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Those who fought with me, get to the shuttle. As soon as we are away from here, I will give orders for the immediate evacuation of the remaining survivors."
  - After: "Fighters, to the shuttle. Once we're away, I'll order the other survivors evacuated."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Stay on the planet with everyone else and wait until I decide what to do with you. I do not have time for this now."
  - After: "Stay here with the rest until I decide your fate. No time now."
- **Player**
  - Before: "By destroying these foul xenos, you have atoned for your transgressions against the Emperor — get to the shuttle. The rest of you will be subject to selective punitive servitorisation so that you may further toil for the good of the Imperium."
  - After: "Killing these xenos atoned for your sins. To the shuttle. The rest face punitive servitorisation for the Imperium."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The surviving fighters turn their heads toward you one after another. All eyes on the battlefield are glued to you.{/n}
  - After: {n}The survivors all turn to you.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/PenalWorld/TazarraFirstEncounter/TazarraFirstEncounter_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell your Myrmyriss she's not going to like what she's about to see."
  - After: "Tell your Myrmyriss she'll hate what's coming."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It seems it is I who is in for a treat. I cannot even begin to fathom where my subjects found such an exotic beast — and a talking one at that!"
  - After: "My treat, rather. Where did my subjects find such an exotic talking beast?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Raise your weapon] "How about we skip the small talk and get down to business?"
  - After: [Raise your weapon] "Skip the small talk."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am a Rogue Trader, the Emperor's anointed, Guardian of Humanity — and your doom, xenos scum!"
  - After: "I am a Rogue Trader, the Emperor's anointed, and your doom, xenos!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You ravaged the planet. Wiped out millions of people. Made those who survived bend the knee... You will pay for this."
  - After: "You ravaged this world and killed millions. You will pay."
- **Player**
  - Before: "A small group of xenos who neutralised the planetary defences and managed to ruin an entire world... Impressive! How much would it cost to hire you?"
  - After: "A few xenos ruined a world. Impressive! Your price?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I presume the toxic atmosphere is your doing?"
  - After: "The toxic air is your doing?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address the fighters in the arena] "Dying to entertain xenos is a path to eternal shame and condemnation of souls touched by the Emperor's undying glory! Let us join our blades — we will destroy those who sought to kill you!"
  - After: [Address the fighters in the arena] "Dying for xenos amusement damns you! Join me and destroy them!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address the fighters in the arena] "How could you stoop to this? To killing one another for the amusement of the enemies of Humanity?"
  - After: [Address the fighters in the arena] "You kill each other for xenos amusement?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Turn to the fighters in the arena] "Do you truly wish to die at the xenos' behest? If we join forces now, we can end this senseless carnage once and for all."
  - After: [Turn to the fighters in the arena] "Die at xenos whim? Join me and end this."
- **Player**
  - Before: "By whose leave are you playing lord on my world?"
  - After: "Who let you play lord on my world?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Kneel, xenos, or I shall have you flogged."
  - After: "Kneel, xenos, or be flogged."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Beckon your cyber-eagle] "{petname}, take a look at these traitors. Let the Emperor see their erring souls through your eyes."
  - After: [Beckon your cyber-eagle] "{petname}, let the Emperor see these traitors through your eyes."
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: {n}The tall, lithe xenos moves with the grace of an otherworldly predator. The creature gives you a dispassionate glance and casually speaks a few words that are immediately picked up by your {g|Encyclopedia:Elucidator}Elucidator{/g}.{/n} "Mecandis, Aelith, what is this? Has one of the sisters found an amusing trinket in the ruins and saved it as a special treat for the Archon?" {n}The xenos takes a quick look over her shoulder toward the platform where a few more silhouettes in tar-black armour can be seen.{/n}
  - After: {n}A lithe xenos glances at you; your {g|Encyclopedia:Elucidator}Elucidator{/g} translates.{/n} "Mecandis, Aelith, a trinket for the Archon?" {n}She glances at armoured figures above.{/n}
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: {n}The xenos's eyes light up with interest.{/n} "The mon-keigh understands my speech! Where did you come by a device that can translate our language? Are you trying to impress me by appearing useful? Such words will earn you a bout in the ring at most. Without weapons, and, soon, without your skin."
  - After: {n}Her eyes light up.{/n} "The mon-keigh understands me! That earns you a bout in the ring. Unarmed, soon skinless."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I hereby declare you a Category Three blasphemer for tampering with the sacred production cycle of this world's extractiums." {n}The drill on Pasqal's mechadendrite springs to life with a howling screech.{/n}
  - After: "Category Three blasphemer, for tampering with this world's extractiums." {n}Pasqal's drill screeches.{/n}
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: {n}Tazarra takes a step back just as the other fighters charge with furious howls.{/n}
  - After: {n}Tazarra steps back as the fighters charge.{/n}
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: {n}Tazarra emits a furious scream and takes a step back, signalling to her companions.{/n}
  - After: {n}Tazarra screams and retreats, signalling her companions.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The humans scattered around you on the platform stare as if they've seen a ghost. The eyes of some betray their fear, others glare with bestial hatred, and yet more look upon you with hope.{/n}
  - After: {n}The humans stare: afraid, hateful, hopeful.{/n}
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: "My name is known to everyone on this planet, mon-keigh. I am Tazarra the Deliverer, Tazarra the Benevolent, the one who grants respite from the choking grasp of this world. I decide who lives, who dies, and who finds new purpose for their existence in Commorragh's many arenas. Surely this is why you have come here? To fight for my ever-changing favour and for the privilege of being the first to be chained?"
  - After: "I am Tazarra the Deliverer. I decide who lives, dies, or fights in Commorragh's arenas. Here for my favour, and chains?"
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: "Cousin, what are you doing among this rabble? What an unexpected and tantalising surprise." {n}Tazarra licks her lips hungrily.{/n} "I cannot wait to take you in my arms and clasp you tightly to me!"
  - After: "Cousin! How tantalising." {n}Tazarra licks her lips.{/n} "Let me hold you tight!"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Do not waste breath on your lies. Only the faint vestiges of blood connect the Asuryani and Dark Ones such as yourself."
  - After: "Spare your lies. Only faint blood ties Asuryani to Dark Ones."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "To be reduced to a xenos's plaything... A shameful fate for the scions of Humankind." {n}Abelard falls silent, shaking his head in dismay.{/n}
  - After: "A xenos's plaything. Shameful." {n}Abelard shakes his head.{/n}
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: "It could be. Or perhaps my mere presence is enough to make base creatures like yourselves forget how to breathe?" {n}Tazarra lets out a nasty chuckle.{/n} "Are you really surprised at what happened? You wove the net right under your own feet — we merely knocked out the pin that drew it closed tight around you. A couple of volleys at the seals on the underground well, and the planet, the one you had turned inside out, did the rest."
  - After: "Maybe." {n}She chuckles.{/n} "You wove the net. We shot the underground well's seals; your gutted planet did the rest."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Looks like the spectators grew bored when the performance hit a snag." {n}Heinrix reaches for his weapon.{/n}
  - After: "The audience is bored." {n}Heinrix reaches for his weapon.{/n}
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: "Oh, what passion! What naive arrogance! When all this turns into boundless despair and clinging terror, my guests and I will savour such exquisite pleasure. I would play with you myself, mon-keigh, but then the performance would be brief — and we don't want to upset my guests, now do we?"
  - After: "Naive arrogance! Your despair will delight my guests."
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: "Am I not paying for our mischief already? Am I not saving the worthiest among your kin, gifting them the right to die for the delight of my brothers and sisters? What kind of abhorrent ingratitude is this?"
  - After: "I'm saving your worthiest to die for our delight. Such ingratitude!"
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: "The presumption. The stupidity. You have nothing that could satisfy me, mon-keigh."
  - After: "Stupid. You have nothing I want."
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: {n}Tazarra raises her blade and points at you.{/n} "Tell the other mon-keigh that whoever slits your throat will depart for their new home ahead of schedule. And tell them to hold nothing back: tonight they dance for Yremeryss herself, the great Archon of the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest!"
  - After: {n}Tazarra points her blade at you.{/n} "Whoever kills this one leaves early. Dance for Yremeryss, Archon of the Kabal of the Reaving Tempest!"
- **Scarred Gladiator**
  - Before: {n}Exhausted and defeated faces trade worried glances. The hulking brute next to you hesitates, then spits and breaks into a grin.{/n} "We're going to die anyway, might as well do it without the heretic's brand! Slay the beasts!"
  - After: {n}A brute spits and grins.{/n} "We're dying anyway, might as well die clean! Slay the beasts!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Exhausted and defeated faces trade worried glances — and tighten their grip on their weapons.{/n}
  - After: {n}The fighters grip their weapons.{/n}
- **Scarred Gladiator**
  - Before: {n}A hulking brute who can barely stand coughs up blood and wipes his lips.{/n} "What, was I supposed to lie down and die? The ones who survive the arena, the xenos take them away — I saw humans boarding shuttles with my own eyes! They're going to take us away from here, you hear?"
  - After: {n}A brute coughs blood.{/n} "Arena survivors get shipped off. I saw shuttles!"
- **Scarred Gladiator**
  - Before: "Yeah! Who gives a shit about us convicts? The lanky buggers may keep me on a leash, but at least I'll be alive, not coughing up my lungs!"
  - After: "Better alive on a leash than coughing up my lungs!"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet chuckles haughtily.{/n} "Such grandiose names for a soulless wretch who tortures the breathless and torments the powerless. Your words hint at a nobility you have never possessed."
  - After: {n}Yrliet laughs.{/n} "Grand names for a soulless torturer."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You do not even notice the moment when you switch to the voice you used in your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}former life{/d} — the firm, uncompromising tone of a Commissar.{/n}
  - After: {n}You slip into your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Commissar}former life{/d}'s Commissar voice.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}The Proctor's voice booms with denunciation:{/n} "Now you see why Arbitrators prefer to execute criminals immediately — because this is what they will do otherwise with the life they are offered. From the moment they fall into heresy, they hardly have the right to be called human anymore — all they can do from then on is sink deeper."
  - After: {n}Solomorne booms:{/n} "This is why Arbitrators execute criminals at once. Heretics only sink deeper."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A loud bird call deafens everyone present. Like a living embodiment of the Imperium's Aquila, a two-headed eagle, its wings spread wide, swoops down on the fighters' heads. They recoil as the screeching bird sinks its talons into Tazarra's astounded face. With a furious scream, the xenos shakes the eagle off. Its claws have torn the skin of her face and damaged her eye.{/n}
  - After: {n}The two-headed eagle dives and claws Tazarra's face and eye before she flings it off.{/n}
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: "How cruel you are to your unfortunate kin! These mon-keigh have worked hard to entertain their elite audience. Each of them fights with a strength born of desperation, seeking to earn their place in my box of toys. There is always room for more — my toys do break so very easily."
  - After: "How cruel! They fight for a place in my toy box. My toys break so easily."
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: "And your brethren finished what the planet had started. Oh, how they strived to please me and my entourage! How they slaughtered and tortured their own kin for mine and my sisters' delight! How they decorated this little arena with still living mon-keigh! Did you think all that you see before you is the work of our hands? Think again."
  - After: "Your kind tortured their own to please us. You think this is all our work? Think again."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "This statement is false. You were supposed to furnish yourself with a means of respiratory protection and inflict maximum damage on the perpetrators before ceasing your vital functions."
  - After: "False. You should have damaged the perpetrators before expiring."
- **Tazarra**
  - Before: {n}From the dusk behind Tazarra comes a cry. The distance between you and the xenos is too great for the Elucidator to interpret the words, but the tone alone speaks of irritation and impatience.{/n}
  - After: {n}Someone behind Tazarra shouts impatiently.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix narrows his eyes and gives the xenos an appraising look.{/n} "The Drukhari of this breed are known as Wyches, {name}. They are experts at bloodletting in the arenas and on the battlefield. However, I am more interested in the ones skulking in shadows — judging by their armour, they are high-ranking representatives of a Kabal, a military clique from the Drukhari demesne. It seems we have disrupted a vile performance for their distinguished guests."
  - After: {n}Heinrix eyes her.{/n} "A Drukhari Wych, {name}. Those in the shadows are high-ranking Kabal. We've spoiled their show."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira spits on the ground.{/n} "If I'd been the one holding the device, she and I would have had words... I'd make sure the stuck-up bitch knew exactly what I think of her."
  - After: {n}Idira spits.{/n} "Give me the device. I'd tell that bitch off."
- **Jae**
  - Before: {n}Jae opens her mouth and then freezes, clenching the Aquila on her chest until her knuckles turn white.{/n} "If... I were faced with such a choice... the Exalted One would guide me on the right path."
  - After: {n}Jae clutches her Aquila.{/n} "The Exalted One would guide me..."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Stupid ashmags! Do you really think the Drukhari will whisk you away to a far-off wonderland? At best they'll put you in chains. At worst..."
  - After: "Stupid ashmags! At best, Drukhari chains. At worst..."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/SantielsPrideSurface/AliveScoutDialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You mentioned some crimson degenerates..."
  - After: "Crimson degenerates?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vir scratches his head in confusion.{/n} "That's us. The ones who remain. Those who survived to atone for the faults of our world before His all-seeing eyes!"
  - After: {n}Vir frowns.{/n} "Us. Survivors, atoning before Him!"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "We land on a world that is frozen to the bone, and the next moment an obliging stranger appears who is only too eager to lead us to the so-called survivors? How convenient. And suspicious."
  - After: "An eager stranger instantly leads us to survivors? Suspicious."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Say what you wish, but he harbours no secrets from us in his heart, while the path ahead is full of danger. Trust this poor man, Lord Captain — I do not hear any warning whispers."
  - After: "He hides nothing, Lord Captain. Trust him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The elders waited so long for a sign from heaven... They died waiting, in fact. May He smite me where I stand if they weren't talking about you! Y-you will help us unfortunates, won't you? I must go, take you to the others. It is not safe here — the bloody crimson degenerates are always skulking in search of prey, the ones you killed were hardly the last. I will show you the hidden chute. Come, come!" {n}Vir hesitates, awkwardly shuffling his feet.{/n} "And yeah... Thank you for saving my skin."
  - After: "The elders awaited a sign. You! Help us? Crimson degenerates hunt here. Follow me to the hidden chute." {n}Vir shuffles.{/n} "Thanks for saving me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Crimson Hand. Marauders, heretics and madmen... The apostates who stole the gifts prepared for God-Emperor — the bodies of those who finished their lifelong labour. And when they cannot find frozen corpses, it is us they come for!"
  - After: "The Crimson Hand. Heretics who steal the dead meant for the Emperor, then take us!"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Not everyone can face death with honour. Weakness begets heresy, and then the others must lay the corrupt souls to rest if they are still clinging to this world!"
  - After: "Weakness breeds heresy. Such souls must be put down!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vir delivers a fawning bow.{/n} "It will be as you say, {mf|master|mistress}... But I am begging you to exercise caution: the Nightmares found our old passageway and are now grabbing everyone they see. It would be better to go via my chute — I'll mark it on your map and will be waiting there just in case. May the Emperor protect you!"
  - After: {n}Vir bows.{/n} "Yes, {mf|master|mistress}. Nightmares found our old passage. I'll mark my chute on your map and wait there."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/SantielsPrideSurface/AliveScoutDialogue/AliveScout_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Calm down. My name is {name}."
  - After: "Calm down. I'm {name}."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will help your friends. Lead on."
  - After: "I'll help your friends. Lead on."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Mark the place where your companions are being held on the map. I shall find the way there on my own."
  - After: "Mark your companions on the map. I'll go alone."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Wait, I still have more questions."
  - After: "Wait, more questions."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Hit him] "Damn peasant! I am a Rogue Trader, appointed by the will of the Emperor Himself. I am the rightful ruler of this world!"
  - After: [Hit him] "Peasant! I'm a Rogue Trader, by the Emperor's will. I rule this world!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Never mind. Just tell me what happened here."
  - After: "Never mind. What happened here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You think it was the Emperor who brought punishment upon Santiel's Pride?"
  - After: "The Emperor punished Santiel's Pride?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why did House Chorda fail to dispatch a fleet to assist you?"
  - After: "Why didn't House Chorda send a fleet?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What are the xenos doing here?"
  - After: "Why are the xenos here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have learned everything I wanted to know."
  - After: "I've learned enough."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Helping the rabble is beneath the dignity of a Rogue Trader. Out of my way!"
  - After: "Helping rabble is beneath a Rogue Trader. Move!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You abandoned your friends and fled like a coward!"
  - After: "You fled and abandoned your friends, coward!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Execute him] "You were too afraid to fight the xenos and left your friends in their hour of need, traitorous vermin!"
  - After: [Execute him] "You left your friends to the xenos, traitorous vermin!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Did anyone else manage to survive aside from you? Deep in the bunkers, perhaps?"
  - After: "Did anyone else survive? In the bunkers?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The quivering figure wrapped in several layers of tattered clothes is pointing an old lasgun at you:{/n} "W-who are you? In the name of the God-Emperor, k-keep away from me!"
  - After: {n}A ragged man aims a lasgun at you:{/n} "W-who are you? Keep away!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vir eagerly gives you a servile bow, but his eyes are full of despair.{/n} "The will of the Heavenly Envoy is His will."
  - After: {n}Vir bows despairingly.{/n} "The Envoy's will is His will."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Have mercy, O Heavenly Envoy! Don't—"
  - After: "Mercy, Heavenly Envoy! Don't—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It takes the man several seconds to digest your answer.{/n} "May you be blessed by the Throne, {name}. And I am Vir... just Vir."
  - After: {n}He pauses.{/n} "Throne bless you, {name}. I'm Vir."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Who? You... You are one of the star children, right? I knew the Emperor could not have abandoned us! You have come to save us, have you not? May the Throne bless your radiant souls! I am Vir, one of the few survivors on this dispossessed world."
  - After: "A star child? The Emperor hasn't abandoned us! I'm Vir, a survivor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Have mercy, {mf|master|mistress}! In these dire times you cannot expect to meet anyone but the apostates! I humbly kneel, and may the radiance of the Throne bless your souls! I am Vir, wretched Vir!"
  - After: "Mercy, {mf|master|mistress}! I'm Vir, wretched Vir!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A-all right, I suppose you would've attacked by now if you were going to... I'm Vir, former scout and now doomed man."
  - After: "I'm Vir. Ex-scout, doomed man."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "R-really?" {n}The wretch cannot believe his ears.{/n} "Right away! Follow me and don't lag behind. And be very, very quiet! The Nightmares roam the streets, trust me, I know! They will be lying in wait up ahead, so tread carefully."
  - After: "R-really? {n}He can't believe it.{/n} Follow me quietly! Nightmares lurk ahead."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "R-really? If you say so... Be careful, the Nightmares will be lying in wait up ahead! And I will be waiting for you nearby, in case you need any help. But, I beg you, please hurry, Heavenly Envoy! They could be killing Albris as we speak..."
  - After: "Beware the Nightmares! I'll wait nearby. Hurry, they could be killing Albris..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes?.. Yes, of course! But please be quick." {n}The shaking man keeps glancing around nervously.{/n}
  - After: "Yes, but be quick." {n}He glances around.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Who? Oh, you must be taken about the Nightmares... God-Emperor preserve us! These beasts are prowling both in the depths and on the surface, they are the scourge for our transgressions before the Holiest One! Nobody ever returns from their clutches, for such is the will of the Divine. There are some who kill quickly, while others drag people into the dark, screaming. And some have turned into walking nightmares that feed on people's souls..."
  - After: "The Nightmares? Beasts punishing our sins! Some kill, some drag people off, some feed on souls..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If only someone knew! I've spent my entire life in the underhive — I only ever saw daylight once, so I'm not missing it much now. But the cold... It's the cold that was our undoing. The heat still lingers in the depths of the hive — that's where we are sheltering... Well, we were until recently. Until all the heat escaped the central pillar. When it did, myself and the others came up to get help and bring back supplies... and found you!"
  - After: "Who knows? The cold undid us. When the central pillar lost its heat, we came up for supplies... and found you!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vir gives you a frightened look.{/n} "The bunkers were the first to fall, my saviour. Starvation finished what the Nightmares started. It was easier to survive in small groups, but they too perished one after the other. The three of us... have not seen anyone else alive for a while now, only the corpses and His scourges."
  - After: {n}Vir looks frightened.{/n} "The bunkers fell first, then starvation. We three have seen only corpses since."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Who else but He?" {n}Vir blinks in confusion.{/n} "Only He has the strength to drive the shining Messenger from the sky and shroud the world in eternal darkness, making it tremble! And fill the night to the brim with Nightmares."
  - After: "Who else?" {n}Vir blinks.{/n} "Only He could drive the Messenger from the sky and fill the dark with Nightmares!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I know not why the Immortal One punished us, but who am I to deny His will?"
  - After: "Who am I to deny His will?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The poor man's eyes grow round and wide with terror.{/n} "Had the mistress of this world learned we lost Santiel's Pride... The punishment would be more dire than any Nightmare can inflict."
  - After: {n}He's terrified.{/n} "If this world's mistress learned we lost Santiel's Pride... worse than Nightmares."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vir stops talking abruptly and hesitates for a few seconds, straining to hear something in the howling wind.{/n} "Can we go already?"
  - After: {n}Vir listens to the wind.{/n} "Can we go?"
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "In another time and place I would immediately demand you cut the peasant down for such an outburst. And yet... It pains me to see his mind is so tightly constricted by greenish black thorns. Never have I seen such a frightening colour. This person, this hive... Everything here is drenched with despair."
  - After: "I'd normally demand his death. But greenish black thorns bind his mind. This hive is drenched in despair."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Elders have been waiting for a sign from the heavens for so long... Too much time has passed, so they died. But may He smite me if you are not the one! Y-you will help the ones in need of salvation, w-won't you?" {n}Vir freezes for a second, looking at you reverently and awkwardly shuffling his feet.{/n}
  - After: "The Elders died awaiting a sign. But you're the one! Y-you'll help us?" {n}Vir shuffles reverently.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You have saved my skin, holiest one, but my brothers in faith and misery were not as lucky! The living nightmares grabbed us the moment we stuck our noses out to the surface, trying to survive. I managed to break free and escaped, leaving my friends behind... Woe, woe is me! I am beside myself with shame. I am begging you, child of the stars, please save my comrades, save..." {n}Vir falters, gulps and whispers almost breathlessly:{/n} "Save Albris. I will take you there even if costs me my life!"
  - After: "Nightmares took my brothers. I fled... the shame! Please save them..." {n}Vir whispers:{/n} "Save Albris. I'll take you there!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Spare my worthless cowardly soul, Heavenly Envoy! I was a regular machinist, I prayed every day, I saw weapons only from afar and tried my best to avoid them! How could I tackle the Nightmares with a malfunctioning lasgun? But I had to. Yes, I had to, but I couldn't!" {n}The man covers his eyes with his frostbitten fingers and wails.{/n}
  - After: "Spare me! I'm a machinist, not a fighter! With a broken lasgun? I couldn't!" {n}He wails.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/SantielsPrideSurface/MedusaeDialogue/Medusae_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "A human? How is this possible?"
  - After: "A human? How?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Step away from the strange creature]
  - After: [Step away from the creature]
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A strange meaty growth the size of a human head is clinging to the skull and neck of... a man? The emaciated face — at least, the part of it you can see from under the pulsating alien flesh — bears no emotion, and the cracked lips hang slackly open.{/n}
  - After: {n}A fleshy growth clings to a blank-faced man's skull.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "This xenoform is classified in the Magos Biologis catalogues as Medusa Malifica. It is an empathic parasite."
  - After: "Medusa Malifica. An empathic parasite."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Pain. Fury. Sadness. Despair. Pleasure. Fury. Sadness. Pain. Despair. Pleasure. Pain. Despair. Fury. Sadness. Pleasure... The feelings wash over you, making your heart beat a mad tattoo, choking your breath, and turning your vision black... Scalding tears streak down your cheeks, crystallising in the frosty air. You can't take it anymore. You are exhausted. Home. You want to go home.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pain. Fury. Despair... Your vision blackens, tears freeze. You want to go home.{/n}
- **Scout**
  - Before: "Heavenly Envoy, today you saved the lives of the damned who even their own star and the Immortal One chose to rebuke! How is this not a miracle? May fortune always be as gracious to you as you have been to His lowly servants."
  - After: "Heavenly Envoy, you saved the damned! A miracle! Fortune favour you."
- **Scout**
  - Before: {n}Vir mumbles something unintelligible, wiping the instantly freezing tears from his weathered cheeks.{/n} "—give...Forgive me, Albris..."
  - After: {n}Vir weeps.{/n} "—give...Forgive me, Albris..."
- **Scout**
  - Before: "Spare him, I am begging you with all that is still left — spare my friend!"
  - After: "Spare my friend, I beg you!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The thing before you is a xenoparasite that Magi Biologis call medusae. These creatures latch onto the brain and nervous system of their victim with dozens of tendrils and assume control over the body of the host. Their nature is yet to be fully studied, but the prevailing hypothesis claims that medusae are capable of absorbing strong feelings and emotions from their environment, although the questions of how and why are still a matter of debate.{/n}
  - After: {n}A medusae: a xenoparasite that seizes its host's nerves and body, likely to absorb strong emotions. Why is unknown.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The disgusting, turgid body is clinging to its host with dozens of tendrils. The man is motionless — you are not even sure he is alive in the true sense of the word — and the creature likewise shows no interest either in you or its surroundings.{/n}
  - After: {n}Tendrils grip the host. Neither reacts to you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The parasite appears to be tightly and permanently attached to the victim's head... or so it seems. You spot a certain pattern in the location of the tendrils on the host's body. Making a few incisions here... and there... would probably allow you to separate the creature from its unfortunate bearer.{/n}
  - After: {n}The tendrils follow a pattern. Precise cuts could free the host.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A thickset man of average height is standing before you. His head, some of his face, and the back of his neck are hidden under the meaty flesh of the parasite, whose pulsing tendrils have grown into the victim's body.{/n}
  - After: {n}A thickset man, head buried under the parasite.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After a few well-placed cuts, the parasite's meaty body convulses, making the thin tendrils go soft and unable to maintain their grasp. You dislodge them one after the other, and soon the parasite releases its host of its own volition. The creature twitches its appendages in its death throes and goes limp in your hands. The man's body collapses onto the snow.{/n}
  - After: {n}A few cuts and the parasite lets go, dying. The man collapses onto the snow.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You circle the parasite for a few long minutes, trying to detach the rooted tendrils. You are trying to be careful, but at some point the host twitches and starts struggling violently. Your hand slips... The parasite releases the man's body, but both fall over dead.{/n}
  - After: {n}The host thrashes; your hand slips. Both fall dead.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The parasite is dead and is of no further interest — you let go, and the small body hits the ice with a sickly squelch.{/n}
  - After: {n}You drop the dead parasite. Squelch.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You contact the shuttle crew and give the order to transport the survivor to the voidship.{/n}
  - After: {n}You order the shuttle to take the survivor to the voidship.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Even dead, the parasite is too valuable to leave on the dying world. The small lifeless body will be delivered to your ship, where it will serve as a specimen for experiments or a trophy.{/n}
  - After: {n}The dead parasite goes to your ship as specimen or trophy.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The long silence is interrupted by the groans of the rescued man at your feet. He is still alive.{/n}
  - After: {n}The rescued man groans. Alive.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "In all that is holy on Terra... You von Valancius poke your noses into every mysterious abomination you encounter — it must run in the blood! Why didn't I choose a quiet post away from the front lines, quartermaster of a magnetic coil warehouse or some such thing?" {n}Abelard, who has been agitatedly rifling through equipment, looks up with a start.{/n} "Lord Captain, you have returned to us! And without the need for a medikit. A lucky escape!"
  - After: "You von Valancius poke every abomination! I should've taken a warehouse post." {n}Abelard looks up.{/n} "Lord Captain, you're back! Lucky!"
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "It feeds on human victims, which makes it a predator. I suggest that this is all we need to know to make the rational decision to destroy the creature."
  - After: "It feeds on humans. Destroy it."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Shereen, are you still with us?" {n}Jae anxiously waves her augmented hand in front of your face, then lets out a breath when she sees the awareness return to your eyes.{/n} "One of those things turned a whole squad of my guys mad once. Good lads they were too, loyal. Thanks be to the Exalted One for protecting you from the same fate!"
  - After: "Shereen, still with us?" {n}Jae is relieved.{/n} "One drove a whole squad of mine mad. Thank the Exalted One!"
- **Jae**
  - Before: "A little Drukhari beast coveted by a select circle of people. You should see how sophisticated folks fight to win these things at secret auctions — they'll use anything to get one: gold, bribes, swords. And I suppose it is funny when the proud new owner of the creature isn't usually seen again after the auction. But just think of all the gold and securities you could squeeze out of someone for one of these things..."
  - After: "A Drukhari pet. Rich folk kill for them at auctions, then vanish. But think what it'd fetch..."
- **Scout**
  - Before: "A-albris... Can you hear me? ALBRIS!" {n}Vir grabs his sagging shoulders with the stubs of his fingers, but the creature does not move.{/n} "I am begging you, Heavenly Envoy, do not kill him! Have mercy! This is Albris, just Albris..."
  - After: "ALBRIS!" {n}Vir shakes him; nothing.{/n} "Don't kill him, Heavenly Envoy!"
- **Scout**
  - Before: "I do not know... I don't know! This thing is a Nightmare, I have seen the likes of it before! Bound in chains, listlessly watching... They always accompanied their masters during the gory executions. They just stood there and stared... Always stared. But why is this creature riding Albris now? How... how do we take it off?"
  - After: "I don't know! It's a Nightmare. They watched their masters' executions. How do we get it off Albris?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The creature stands motionless as if you are not even there.{/n}
  - After: {n}The creature ignores you.{/n}
- **Scout**
  - Before: {n}Frantic with grief, the man pulls out a barely sharpened piece of rusty pipe and pleadingly offers it to you.{/n} "I... c-cannot do it. I do not have either the strength or the fingers. But you are blessed by Him, the sovereign of all the stars in the sky. So you can do it for me."
  - After: {n}Vir offers you a sharpened pipe.{/n} "I c-can't, no fingers. You're blessed by Him. You do it."
- **Scout**
  - Before: "Albris, you are saved, you are saved..." {n}The man kneels next to the limp body, clutching the man's motionless hand with his finger stubs.{/n} "Still warm..."
  - After: "Albris, you're saved..." {n}Vir clutches his hand.{/n} "Still warm..."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's voice synthesiser crackles in agitation, and a needle glints on a mechadendrite.{/n} "Neural overload detected. Protocol to render emergency aid activated."
  - After: {n}A needle glints.{/n} "Neural overload. Emergency aid protocol active."
- **Scout**
  - Before: "Anything but this! I am begging you, no!"
  - After: "Anything but this! No!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The unusual pair — a man with an ugly parasite clinging to his head — remain where you left them.{/n}
  - After: {n}The man and parasite remain.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The medusae is obediently hovering in the air. It is entirely unclear whether the creature realises its predicament. You decide to...{/n}
  - After: {n}The medusae hovers, unaware. You decide to...{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "L-Lord Captain? Are you all right? Forgive me... I didn't even have the chance to warn you..." {n}Idira looks frightened.{/n} "There was a bang, a howl, a blur of colour... a second before that creature... Oh, let's just get rid of it!"
  - After: "L-Lord Captain? Are you all right? I couldn't warn you..." {n}Idira is scared.{/n} "Let's get rid of it!"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "{name}, do not look!" {n}Yrliet's shout is the last thing you hear before darkness flows into your mind.{/n}
  - After: "{name}, don't look!" {n}Darkness floods your mind.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your vision grows dim and you have a sinking feeling in your chest. But you are still alive and are trying to open your eyes. Dark figures dash about in the twisting shadows cast by the fire. One of them is standing in front of you, casually tossing something from one hand to the other... You slowly turn your stiff neck and dumbly stare at the stump where your right arm used to be. The figure comes closer, tosses a frozen hand onto the ground, and breaks off the tip of your nose with a little crunch. Why haven't you died with the others? Why are you still alive?{/n}
  - After: {n}Firelit shadows. Your right arm is a stump. A figure drops your frozen hand and snaps off your nose. Why are you still alive?{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "This creature is not bound by any natural law. Its origins lie outside {g|Encyclopedia:Realspace}realspace{/g}. However..." {n}The sampling tool on one of Pasqal's mechadendrites jolts to life.{/n} "It can be studied using the methods of realspace."
  - After: "It comes from outside {g|Encyclopedia:Realspace}realspace{/g}. However..." {n}A sampler whirs.{/n} "It can be studied."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Frightened, cold, hurt... and aching to flee. But these feelings are not yours. You concentrate your will to shrug off the unbidden emotions, and the compulsion recedes — you once again see a man caught in the clutches of a disgusting parasite. The illusion is gone, but inexplicable anxiety still lingers in your soul like the aftermath of a particularly bad nightmare.{/n}
  - After: {n}Fear, cold, pain... not yours. You shake them off. Unease lingers.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I once was witness to the vivisection of such a creature. These parasites are called Drukhari medusae. As long as its current host lives, a medusae has no need to attack and dominate your mind. If its host dies, be careful not to let it latch onto your head."
  - After: "A Drukhari medusae. While its host lives, it won't attack you. If the host dies, keep it off your head."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "A medusae... The driver of nightmares and torment. My dark cousins use these creatures to amass emotions and experiences, which they then feed on."
  - After: "A medusae. My dark cousins use them to harvest emotions to feed on."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/SantielsPrideUnderhive/Captives/Captives_dialogue

  - After: "Can you reach the shelter alone?"

  - After: "Glad I came in time."

  - Before: "Oh, survivors! I did not even notice you were here."
  - After: "Oh, survivors! I didn't notice you."

  - Before: "Get away from me, vermin! It was not my intention to rescue you, it just so happened I was nearby."

  - Before: "Yes, yes. Now go away."

  - Before: "That will be all for now."
  - After: "That's all for now."

  - Before: "Abelard, under no circumstances will I speak to this rabble."
