  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, please forgive this oaf! Had it not been for you, these madmen would have eaten us alive! Or used us as parts for their monstrous statue! Or..." {n}The red-haired woman stops chattering and lets out a loud sigh.{/n}
  - After: "Forgive this oaf, your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Those madmen would've eaten us!" {n}A woman sighs.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The h-hive's passageways are like a maze. Some paths will lead you nowhere, while others might offer a shortcut if you restore the power and open the right doors."
  - After: "The hive's a maze. Restored power opens shortcuts."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And remember — it isn't just the Nightmares prowling in the dark that makes the passageways dangerous, they are also full of insidious traps! So many good men and women have died solely because they didn't keep their eyes peeled... May the Emperor's light welcome their souls."
  - After: "Beware traps too! Many died careless."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And... and... keep away from the feeding bay! They say a furious Nightmare is roaming the area. Many of us have died trying to stop it — not one of them came back! Not a single soul did, you h-hear?"
  - After: "Avoid the feeding bay! A furious Nightmare there kills everyone!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There are a couple in the section that's frozen over, but I'm afraid there is nothing useful left. Personal caches, though? You'll find them all over the place, and most of their owners are long gone."
  - After: "In the frozen section, picked clean. Personal caches abound, though."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And so are we! We are so very, very glad, {mf|master|mistress}!"
  - After: "So are we, {mf|master|mistress}!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Uh..." {n}The woman awkwardly scratches the back of her head.{/n} "Yes, of course. Forgive my stupidity, {mf|master|mistress}."
  - After: {n}She scratches her head.{/n} "Forgive me, {mf|master|mistress}."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Collect yourselves, commoners! {name} von Valancius, the Rogue Trader {mf|himself|herself} is standing before you! Now prove that your lives were worth saving."
  - After: "This is {name} von Valancius, the Rogue Trader {mf|himself|herself}! Speak!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "O-of course, of course! We are already leaving. May the Emperor light your path, {mf|master|mistress}!"
  - After: "We're leaving! Emperor light your path, {mf|master|mistress}!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Back into the dark corridors, to the Nightmares and lurking crimson beasts?" {n}The woman gazes hesitantly at the exit.{/n} "Of course, it will be as you say. We'll leave as soon as we catch our breath."
  - After: "Back to the Nightmares?" {n}She eyes the exit.{/n} "As you say."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The survivors listen to you, gaping in admiration.{/n}
  - After: {n}The survivors gape admiringly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You k-know, I just remembered something! The mad geezer, that false prophet of theirs, kept disappearing into the small chamber behind the statue. I have no idea what they keep inside, but nobody other than him dared to go in there!"
  - After: "Their false prophet kept entering the chamber behind the statue."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "W-wait, {mf|master|mistress}, I just remembered something! The mad geezer, that false prophet of theirs, kept disappearing into the small chamber behind the statue. I have no idea what they keep inside, but nobody other than him dared to peek in there!"
  - After: "W-wait, {mf|master|mistress}! Their false prophet kept entering the chamber behind the statue."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I do not know how lowborn commoners such as ourselves can possibly thank you. We scouts are simple people... Our possessions are long gone, but we know the bowels of the hive like the back of our hand. Maybe we could share some useful information?"
  - After: "We scouts know the hive. Advice?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "After you leave this vile lair, try to reach the geothermal node. It will be hard to miss — there are four massive pistons pumping what's left of the hot air from the planet's core. From there, keep moving toward the icebound area of the hive. After you hit the wall, turn left and go up the stairs. The Children of Redemption are huddling behind a secluded door, they are the few survivors who have not yet lost their minds in this forsaken place."
  - After: "Go to the geothermal node with four huge pistons, then the icebound area. At the wall, go left and upstairs. The Children of Redemption hide behind a door."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That's it! We can tell where you definitely mustn't go. Or we can explain how to get to our shelter."
  - After: "We can say where not to go, or how to reach our shelter."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It would be a good idea to loot these cadavers, too. The crimson degenerates hoard stuff, precious and useless alike. Now that you've killed them, it would be a shame to let all those things go to waste."
  - After: "Loot those corpses. The crimson degenerates hoard everything."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you again for delivering us from harm, your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We will forever remember your kindness! Or, well, until we die, anyway. Safe travels!"
  - After: "Thanks again, your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Safe travels!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Shut up, you lout! It was this highborn {mf|lord|lady} who saved you, not the Emperor!"
  - After: "Shut up! This {mf|lord|lady} saved you, not the Emperor!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There's also a shortcut. Leave the lair and go straight. There will be a ruined bridge on the left-hand side, jump onto it and you will find yourself near the hidden entrance to the shelter."
  - After: "Shortcut: leave the lair, go straight, jump onto the ruined bridge on the left to the shelter's hidden entrance."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Nightmares drag their victims deeper into the hive, but we are not desperate or crazy enough to risk following them all the way in... I don't know where exactly their lair is, but if you leave this place and keep going right, skipping all turns, you are bound to run into one of their patrols. As for what happens next... Only the Emperor can help you."
  - After: "Leave and keep right, skipping turns, to meet a Nightmare patrol. Then Emperor help you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "D-don't you worry about us, {mf|master|mistress}. We'll just catch our breath and move on. The shadows will hide us from the Nightmares. The shadows and... just a tiny bit of luck."
  - After: "Don't worry, {mf|master|mistress}. Shadows will hide us."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/SantielsPrideUnderhive/DeadPainEngine/DeadPainEngine_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Take a risk and proceed with the examination of the xenoconstruct]
  - After: [Risk it and keep examining the xenoconstruct]
- **Player**
  - Before: [Examine the signs of damage on the frame]
  - After: [Examine the frame's damage]
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Before you is a disgusting construct, a twisted nightmare made real by a fevered genius. An amalgam of rotting flesh and corroded metal is halfway buried under the rubble. The thing is motionless, but a dull green pus is still oozing from its swollen wounds.{/n}
  - After: {n}A construct of rotting flesh and corroded metal lies half-buried in rubble, oozing green pus.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You notice a spasm in the construct's organic limb just in time to dodge its lighting fast blow. The serrated blade whooshes less than an inch from your neck and drops to the floor with a heavy clang. The manipulators in the machine's underbelly give a furious screech, its frame twitches convulsively — and the construct becomes dormant once more.{/n}
  - After: {n}A limb spasms; you dodge its blade by an inch. The machine screeches, twitches, and goes still.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The terrifying construct is motionless — the heavy debris has firmly pinned the machine to a cold floor. And yet a single look at the disgusting thing is enough to make your skin crawl.{/n}
  - After: {n}Debris pins the motionless construct. It makes your skin crawl.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The massive ceiling beams and slabs are firmly pressing the machine to the ground, having crushed most of the antennae, hoses and reservoirs covering its frame. The marks left by bullets and chainswords are obvious on its armour plates — it does not look like these shots and blows inflicted much damage. However, the construct's tail and underbelly are in considerably worse shape after the explosion tore the armour away and exposed them to the elements.{/n}
  - After: {n}Beams crushed its hoses and reservoirs. Gunfire barely scratched it, but a blast tore open its tail and underbelly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The unfamiliar xenomaterial glistens with a metallic sheen. The construct's body and limbs are a patchwork of stitched flesh that inconceivably transitions to mechanical components, as if organic tissue and metal were somehow fused to make one whole.{/n}
  - After: {n}Stitched flesh fuses seamlessly into gleaming xenometal.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The construct's front manipulators were replaced with a massive sword and a mechanic palm. Both limbs are embellished with hooked barbs — doubtlessly to inflict additional suffering to the victim. The machine's armoured plates at the other join to create a prehensile scorpion-like tail with a pair of unknown projectile weapons where one would expect to find a stinger.{/n}
  - After: {n}Its forelimbs are a barbed sword and a mechanical palm. A scorpion-like tail ends in two unknown projectile weapons.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You discover the construct's weak spot and carefully cult away pieces of flesh melded with metal. it takes you a while to deposit the samples into secure containers with separated bunches of cable, manipulators and certain gadgets of particular interest.{/n}
  - After: {n}You find a weak spot and carefully seal flesh, cables, manipulators and gadgets into containers.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The gruesome tool of the enemies of Mankind remains dangerous even in this condition, so you decide to take no chances. A good charge of promethium explosives won't leave a single trace of this heresy.{/n}
  - After: {n}Too dangerous to keep. Promethium explosives erase this heresy.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You barely notice a flash of metal before the terrible impact comes. The massive limb that lunged at you drops to the floor with a heavy clang. The manipulators in the machine's underbelly give a furious screech, its frame twitches convulsively — and the construct becomes dormant once more.{/n}
  - After: {n}A flash of metal, then a terrible impact. The machine screeches, twitches, and goes still.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Anxiety makes you feel hot, with acrid sweat eating away at your eyes. When the plasma cutter gets to the place where metal fuses with living flesh, your hand slips, crudely severing the accessible part of the construct and a few reservoirs with oily liquid that immediately splashes everywhere. You gather the intact samples, tear away several manipulators and put everything into a container, hoping these research materials will be enough.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your plasma cutter slips, spilling oily reservoirs. You salvage some samples, hoping it's enough.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your attempts to separate the reservoirs from the frame remain futile until you push a lever under the armour plates. The vessels empty themselves with a loud click, letting the murky ooze drain into the construct via a series of pipes.{/n}
  - After: {n}A lever under the plates clicks; the reservoirs drain their ooze back into the construct.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The machine's armoured frame is covered with spikes and reservoirs — some of them are broken, and you see suspicious sanguineous liquid frozen between shards. The armour plates hide several rows of manipulators, razor-sharp scalpels and anti-gravity generators. The latter have fused into the engine's flesh and allow the construct to eerily hover above ground in search of victims.{/n}
  - After: {n}Cracked reservoirs of frozen blood. Under the plates: scalpels, manipulators and fused anti-grav generators that let it hover, hunting.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The nightmarish construct remains motionless in the dim light of the corridor.{/n}
  - After: {n}The construct lies motionless in the dim corridor.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Hoping the last blow was just the thing lashing out in its death throes, you resume studying the construct.{/n}
  - After: {n}Hoping that was a death throe, you continue.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal is looking at the abominable tech with a mixture of disgust and... greedy curiosity. Without tearing his eyes away from the beast, he produces devices with narrow saws, test probes and analysers from under his robe and carefully inserts them into the claws of his mechadendrites. The last thing to emerge is a small melta charge.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal eyes it with disgust and greedy curiosity, readying saws, probes, analysers... and a small melta charge.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Planting the explosives takes some time. Eventually your hand slips, and the timer goes off before you are ready for the explosion...{/n}
  - After: {n}Your hand slips; the timer fires early...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You find several loose holds and joints. A little effort, and the reservoirs with suspicious grim murky liquid give way with a click, easily separating from the frame.{/n}
  - After: {n}You find loose joints; the murky reservoirs click free.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/SantielsPrideUnderhive/EatMedusaeFruit/EatMedusaeFruit_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Give up on the endeavour]
  - After: [Give up]
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You forcefully squeeze your hand and the appendage busts with a squelching sound, splattering reddish and yellow liquid everywhere. A pungent sickly sweet stench permeates the air, and all of your attempts to wash it off remain futile.{/n}
  - After: {n}It bursts. The sickly sweet stench won't wash off.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You carefully place the appendage into a reinforced container, trying not to damage its organic surface. The fruit continues to pulsate softly — it looks like it may be stored in such matter a bit longer.{/n}
  - After: {n}You seal the pulsing fruit in a container.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: {n}Cassia's frail body is shivering with exertion:{/n} "{name}, you are awake! Praise the Emperor! You have been swept up by a tempest of colours and nightmares, a maelstrom of emotions plunging toward abyss... But I showed you the way upward, toward us all." {n}Cassia takes a shuddering breath, her gaze drifting out of focus.{/n} "The effort cost me dearly, {name}. Please do not subject yourself to such danger ever again."
  - After: {n}Cassia trembles:{/n} "{name}, you're awake! I guided you back from the maelstrom." {n}Her gaze drifts.{/n} "It cost me dearly, {name}. Never again."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You come closer and reach to separate the parasite from the body of its host, but the creature feels something is wrong...{/n}
  - After: {n}You reach; the parasite senses danger...{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Sister Argenta rushes forward.{/n} "You will thank me later!"
  - After: {n}Argenta rushes in.{/n} "You'll thank me later!"
- **Jae**
  - Before: "O-o-oh, shereen, no-no-no, I know this look and it seldom bodes well! Just toss away this rubbish and let's scram. Sounds like a plan, hm?"
  - After: "Shereen, no! Toss it and let's scram."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "The Dark Ones partake of such fruit to revel in the pleasure from pain and suffering it contains. Mon-keigh minds are not open and flexible enough to survive such an experience, however."
  - After: "The Dark Ones eat these to savour pain. Mon-keigh minds can't survive it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You bring the parasite's appendage close to your face and sense an unusual smell, attractive and repulsive at the same time. The fruit feels ripe under your fingers...{/n}
  - After: {n}It smells alluring and repulsive. Ripe...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You shake off the compulsion and push the object away from your face.{/n}
  - After: {n}You push it away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "{name}!" {n}How many infinities had passed before you heard this voice? It rings louder and louder in your head, growing ever more urgent.{/n} "{name}!" {n}But what is... a head? And what is a {name}? Colourful shadows slip into the void and drive back the darkness. The yellow ones fill you with warmth, the blue ones grant tranquillity, the red ones give life to a strange feeling in your chest... And you open your eyes.{/n}
  - After: "{name}!" {n}A distant voice.{/n} "{name}!" {n}What is a {name}? Colours drive back the dark... You open your eyes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The parasite's slimy flesh melts on your tongue... The taste buds start going insane — a thousand of tastes merge into one that no human language can describe. You salivate, yearning for more... Another piece! A pleasant warmth spreads through your body, making your limbs comfortably numb. The entire world shrivels into a single grain of sand, and then... Bursts into a maelstrom of colours you have never seen before!{/n}
  - After: {n}An indescribable taste. You crave more. The world shrinks, then bursts into unseen colours!{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The dead body of the host is twitching convulsively, but the creature does not seem to be in a hurry to let it go. The parasite's meaty body is covered with strange swollen growths that vaguely resemble succulent fruit. You haven't noticed them before.{/n}
  - After: {n}The parasite clings to the twitching corpse. Fruit-like growths swell on it.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Ber-taa-shal, stupid mon-keigh!" {n}Yrliet rushes to you and knocks the xenofruit out of your hand.{/n}
  - After: "Ber-taa-shal, stupid mon-keigh!" {n}Yrliet knocks it away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The creature stays affixed to its host, wrapping its vile tendrils around his brain and vertebrae. The parasite's meaty body is covered with strange swollen growths that vaguely resemble succulent fruit. You haven't noticed them before.{/n}
  - After: {n}The parasite grips its host. Fruit-like growths swell on it.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The growth makes a squelching sound as it separates from the creature's little body. The place where it used to be quickly fills with new flesh as if the tuber wasn't there. The fruit pulses in your hands like a small bearing heart.{/n}
  - After: {n}It squelches free, pulsing like a tiny heart.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, what are you even thinking!?"
  - After: "Lord Captain, what are you thinking!?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Rogue Trader, by the Emperor... What are you doing? Take this filth away from your face."
  - After: "By the Emperor... Get that filth away from your face."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You retreat to a respectable distance, the creature hesitates for a few seconds and shuffles away into the lightless corridors.{/n}
  - After: {n}You step back; it shuffles into the dark.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/SantielsPrideUnderhive/Haemonculus/Haemonculus_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I have no idea who you are, but it looks like you need this planet more than I do. Let us negotiate a compensation."
  - After: "You need this planet more than I do. Let us negotiate compensation."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, {mf|master|mistress} of Santiel's Pride and the sovereign of all souls that are bound to this world. Identify yourself!"
  - After: "I am Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, {mf|master|mistress} of Santiel's Pride. Identify yourself!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What breeding program are you talking about?"
  - After: "What breeding program?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Whoever you are and wherever you may be... I swear by the Throne, xenofilth, I will find you. I will make you rue what happened on Santiel's Pride!"
  - After: "By the Throne, xenofilth, I will find you and make you rue Santiel's Pride!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "If 'Farkir' was the freak I recently dispatched, I am afraid you will not be able to talk to him."
  - After: "If Farkir was the freak I killed, you can't talk to him."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am here to put an end to this madness and to redeem the survivors."
  - After: "I am here to end this madness and save the survivors."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have grown tired of you. I am taking my leave."
  - After: "I tire of you. I am leaving."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why steal the star? Was it for some sick experiment you have been conducting here?!"
  - After: "Why steal the star? For some sick experiment?!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Was it you who stole the local sun?"
  - After: "Did you steal the local sun?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How are you doing this? How are you making this corpse speak with your voice?"
  - After: "How does this corpse speak with your voice?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am not going to explain myself to a corpse!"
  - After: "I won't explain myself to a corpse!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man appears fused to the machine behind his back: the edges of his skin have turned blue where it seamlessly melds into a metal unlike anything you have seen before, and his flesh is pierced with dozens of needles, pipes and tubes of bubbling liquid. When you approach, the emaciated human body jerks into motion: the head rises as if attached to an invisible puppeteer's string. Grey skin, lifeless sunken eyes, flesh barely clinging to the protruding bones — before you is a dead man who nevertheless continues to move.{/n}
  - After: {n}A dead man, fused to a machine, pierced with tubes. His head jerks up like a puppet's.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Maintaining routine communication is a mundane task that even Farkir-level servants are capable of, and yet it fascinates one of your kind? A pitiful testament to your primitivism, mon-keigh."
  - After: "Even Farkir could talk. This fascinates you? Primitive, mon-keigh."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "This statement is false. The subject is clearly categorised as blasphemous, but the Explorator's creed demands I reject the commandment "know no evil, see no corruption". Unless the subject exhibits dangerous behaviour, it is to be studied."
  - After: "False. Blasphemous, yes, but my creed says study it unless dangerous."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's mechadendrites reach toward the strange corpse as if by themselves.{/n} "Identify yourself. Are you an operator or an interface?"
  - After: {n}Pasqal's mechadendrites reach out.{/n} "Identify yourself. Operator or interface?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The dead man cocks his head as if he heard something unusual.{/n} "You are a deviation from the norm — the assembled data reveals your kind is not simply prone to venerating deceased individuals, it built an entire social construct based on this particular belief."
  - After: {n}He cocks his head.{/n} "Curious. Your kind built a society on venerating the dead."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The dead man is snapping his jaw with the methodicalness of jammed mechanism. When he speaks again, his voice drops to a contented whisper.{/n} "Excellent, excellent... The next stage. The experiment may be continued, if only partially."
  - After: {n}The jaw snaps.{/n} "Excellent... The experiment may partially continue."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The dead man's face twists — not in a grimace but in a painful muscle spasm.{/n} "Hmm. A claim for property fights. It matches the expectations of a species at the lower stages of development."
  - After: {n}The face spasms.{/n} "A property claim. How primitive."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The dead man remains silent for a few seconds — and then continues in the same measured tone, obviously not paying attention to your reaction.{/n} "I suppose Farkir is dead. A regrettable loss of tools and, most likely, collected samples. Having said that... Tell me, specimen — what is your designated function?"
  - After: {n}He ignores you.{/n} "Farkir is dead, then. Regrettable. Specimen — what is your function?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The head drops to the floor and body twitches convulsively. The severed trachea reveals wires and pipes, one of them spewing black tar-like liquid. After a moment the corpse's seizures stop and he lies still, this time dead for good.{/n}
  - After: {n}The head drops, the neck spewing black tar. The corpse stills for good.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I can see you, specimen. Farkir preserved Subject Eighty Six's retinas just for this occasion". {n}Despite these words, the dead man is not looking at you — he is staring blankly into space right in front of him.{/n}
  - After: "I see you through Subject Eighty Six's retinas." {n}He stares past you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The corpse hesitates, and then his face twists into the mockery of a monstrous smile. The long dead man emits a hissing giggle.{/n} "This is precious! What an entertaining example of a primitive hierarchical system!"
  - After: {n}A hissing giggle.{/n} "Precious! What a primitive hierarchy!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The dead man remains silent for a while.{/n} "This is not what I asked you, specimen. A diminished intelligence, even for your species... Concentrate."
  - After: {n}A pause.{/n} "Not what I asked, specimen. Concentrate."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Knowing this will impede your designated function, needlessly complicating a simple mind's system of motivation. Execute your program, Subject Eighty Seven."
  - After: "Knowing would confuse you. Execute your program, Subject Eighty Seven."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The dead man's throat produces several clicks.{/n} "The injection process was terminated prematurely, thus interrupting the procedure." {n}The corpse falls silent for a few moments.{/n} "However, this is not the end just yet. Tell me your designated function, specimen."
  - After: {n}Clicks.{/n} "The injection was interrupted." {n}Silence.{/n} "But not ended. Your function?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Collectivity. Following hierarchy. Correcting behaviour in accordance with contributed notions of 'common good'. I expect the standard cognitive pattern of your species will manifest in the total sum of your upcoming actions."
  - After: "Collectivity. Hierarchy. 'Common good'. Your actions will show it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "'We' are a concept prevalent among species lacking higher cognitive function and compensating for its absence with pack behaviour. If using the word 'you' was an attempt to determine whether this action was performed by members of a single species... Then the answer is positive. Execute the program now that I have satisfied your curiosity."
  - After: "'We' is a pack concept. But yes, one species. Now execute the program."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The logic is flawed. I took advantage of a convenient opportunity that arose from the extraction of the star." {n}The dead man hisses and crunches his face in a grotesque parody of displeasure.{/n} "Are you satisfied with the answer, Subject Eighty Seven? Then proceed with the program. I have nearly exhausted my repertoire of subject encouragement that does not involve chemical stimuli."
  - After: "Flawed. I merely exploited the star's extraction." {n}He hisses.{/n} "Now proceed, before I use chemical stimuli."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Specimen... I will call you Subject Eighty Seven... You have interfered with a process the purpose of which you cannot understand. My means of restoring control and maintaining the rate of subject injection are limited. However, the setback at the current stage is insignificant. You may proceed in accordance with your natural breeding program. What matters is that your further actions produce practical result."
  - After: "Subject Eighty Seven, your interference is a minor setback. Follow your natural breeding program; only results matter."
- **(conversation owner)**

If aggression provides a sufficient motivation toward this goal, then I welcome it."

Upon hearing the low eldritch voice your Elucidator wakes up.{/n} "Kardha ma nae... You are not Farkir."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/SantielsPrideUnderhive/LostSurvivor/LostSurvivor_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Did this man die by your hand?"
  - After: "Did you kill this man?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What an atrocious way to greet your {mf|lord|lady} and {mf|master|mistress}! Seneschal, deal with this rabble!"
  - After: "Greet your {mf|lord|lady} and {mf|master|mistress} properly! Seneschal, deal with her!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I don't believe a single word that comes out of your mouth."
  - After: "I don't believe you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Who is here?" {n}A thin woman turns to the sound of your footsteps. Her lips are quivering and her gaze wanders. She is tightly clutching a bloody knife in a three-fingered hand.{/n}
  - After: "Who is here?" {n}A twitchy woman clutches a bloody knife.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman nervously twitches her head, trying to keep her face away from you. Her clothes, shoes and weapon are covered in fresh blood.{/n}
  - After: {n}She hides her face. She is bloodied.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A hoarse, sickly voice spits out one word after another:{/n} "Ingrid... An unworthy servant of His, born and raised in the deep bowels of this hive."
  - After: {n}Hoarsely:{/n} "Ingrid... His servant, hive-born."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I drew the short straw. Went to look for water and medicine for brothers and sisters of mine, but found more — found you! Perhaps..." {n}The woman turns pensive and starts uncomfortably swaying from side to side.{/n} "...such was His divine will? I must take you, yes... Take you to the shelter! The elders. They will explain everything. I just have to show you the way..."
  - After: "I sought medicine, and found you!" {n}She sways.{/n} "His will! The elders at the shelter will explain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman's wandering gaze suddenly fixes on you.{/n} "Perish in His crimson flame!"
  - After: {n}She stares.{/n} "Perish in His crimson flame!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman turns her head but doesn't even look at the body.{/n} "He did not. The corridors of our blessed polis are overflowing with danger. People die. The dead should rest in peace. This one does not. Which is why I wanted to take him to the shelter."
  - After: {n}She looks away.{/n} "No. He wasn't resting, so I took him to the shelter."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman smiles dryly.{/n} "Of course. Praise to the Emperor of all things — and his crimson light!"
  - After: {n}A dry smile.{/n} "Praise the Emperor's crimson light!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}She shrugs.{/n} "May He be merciful to you, and light the path in the darkness with his crimson light..."
  - After: {n}She shrugs.{/n} "May His crimson light guide you..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The scout nods in agreement.{/n} "In a world ravaged by darkness and shackled by ice, you can trust only yourself and the Emperor. And if the Emperor wanted him to die, who am I to defy the Exalted One?"
  - After: {n}She nods.{/n} "Trust only yourself and the Emperor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman's gaze is wandering about your figure but cannot focus. Her clothes are stained by dark red blotches, both old and recent, and the frostbitten hands are covered with rags and bandages. The bag at her feet is bulging with supplies and a stubber barrel is sticking out of it at an awkward angle.{/n}
  - After: {n}Unfocused eyes, bloodstained, frostbitten; a stubber in her supply bag.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "It will be done, Lord Captain... Hey!" {n}Abelard takes a step toward the woman.{/n} "Who are you and where are the rest of the survivors? Your planet has been visited by a Rogue Trader, the true owner of this world — who among you shall answer before {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}?"
  - After: "At once... Hey!" {n}Abelard steps up.{/n} "Where are the survivors? Who answers to {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}, this world's Rogue Trader?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Rogue... Trader? Could you be the ones who wander among the lights in the sky? If so, the elders... The elders will answer. I could take you to them. Past the horrors that lurk in the shadows of this place."
  - After: "Rogue... Trader? Sky-wanderers? The elders will answer. I'll lead you past the horrors."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard nods pensively.{/n} "Lord Captain, did you hear that? The poor woman mentioned elders. This is a good sign. Perhaps the survivors managed to preserve at least some resemblance of hierarchy. All that remains is to find them among the rubble."
  - After: {n}Abelard nods.{/n} "Elders. Some hierarchy survives. Good."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is difficult to say whether the survivor lies or is telling the truth. The corpse at her feet is relatively fresh, and the traces on the body could be caused not just by a knife but by any slashing weapon.{/n}
  - After: {n}Lie or truth? The wounds could be from any blade.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Your words fill the hive's hallways with slate-grey smoke. I cannot see the truth through it — only the dark intentions of your soul."
  - After: "Your words are slate-grey smoke. I see only dark intentions."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/SantielsPrideUnderhive/ScarletProphet/ScarletProphet_dialogue

  - After: "What is going on? What feast?"

  - Before: "Woah, the Emperor on a spit! That's not something you see every day."
  - After: "Woah, the Emperor on a spit! Not an everyday sight."

  - Before: "First, you shall kneel, for you are speaking to a Rogue Trader and the {mf|master|mistress} of this world!"

  - After: "The Children of Redemption warned me you were cultists and heretics."

The Crimson Hand welcomes all seekers of salvation!"

  - After: "I saw her die: a dark green flash at sunset, eclipsing her forever."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Did you think I would simply ramble on about divine retribution and the Nightmares the Emperor set loose on our world to punish our hubris?" {n}The old man smiles serenely.{/n} "I have seen many things in my lifetime, including the enemies of Humanity.   - After: "Expected divine Nightmares?" {n}He smiles.{/n} "I know Humanity's enemies. The Emperor wouldn't punish us so. The xenos came after the star died."

He will smite you in His fury!" {n}Suddenly, the old man stops shrieking and continues in a serene and blissful voice,{/n} "You must show greater reverence."
  - After: {n}Eyes bulging:{/n} "Heresy! He will smite you!" {n}Serenely:{/n} "Show reverence."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A Rogue Trader?" {n}The old man regards you with interest.{/n} "Oh, if only I had foreseen our meeting! I would have prepared a proper welcome."
  - After: "A Rogue Trader?" {n}Interested.{/n} "Had I known, I'd have prepared a welcome."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Like locusts that destroy everything in their path, they vanished just as suddenly, but not before taking countless lives. I was fortunate to have preserved my flock, for the blood tithe we pay to the Immortal One had imbued us with strength that was denied to the others. Not all the xenos left the planet, however. Some of them keep hunting us, but so far I have failed to divine their darker purpose."
  - After: "Like locusts, they killed countless and vanished. Our blood tithe saved my flock. Some xenos still hunt us, purpose unknown."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Children of Redemption are but a remnant of the past, the victims of centuries of misguided faith. Who are the mad ones, I ask you — the fanatics who revere a star and conflate it with a saint, or the loyal servants of the Emperor who have done everything they can to survive and to keep honouring the Immortal One? And besides... the elders are not so different from us, after all."
  - After: "The Children of Redemption worship a star as a saint. Who is mad? And the elders are not so different from us."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Global disasters often produce necrophage cults such as this. It is unfortunate what a desperate man can be reduced to after being cut off from the Imperium... But it would be best to set the anthropological observations aside in favour of practical considerations, such as ridding your world of this filth."
  - After: "A typical necrophage cult. Let us purge this filth."
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "Good. Fearless sacrifices stay tender."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Indeed. The patience of my brothers and sisters is running thin."
  - After: "Indeed. My flock grows impatient."
