  - Before: "What does the Heavenly Envoy wish to know?"
  - After: "What do you wish to know, Envoy?"
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "What knowledge does your heart desire?"
  - After: "What would you know?"
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "But the Messenger did not return, no matter how many fervent prayers we addressed to her. Without Nolla's scorching embrace, Santiel's Pride plunged into cold and darkness, and then... His Scourges ravaged our world."
  - After: "Nolla never returned. We froze. Then His Scourges came."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: {n}An-Vido does not sound nearly as excited:{/n} "If... If such is your will, we dare not refuse your mercy. But how do we get all Children to the surface? ? The Nightmare Driver is eagerly waiting to punish what remains of us all..."
  - After: {n}An-Vido, less eager:{/n} "But how do we reach the surface past the Nightmare Driver?"
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "The times are harsh, o Heavenly Envoy. Not only do people succumb to hunger and depredations of the enemies of Mankind, the frost is alien to the denizens of Santiel's Pride and has claimed just as many lives if not more. Which is why we cut away the garments of the deceased so that later we could cleanse them and process in accordance with the needs of the Children of Redemption."
  - After: "Frost kills as many as hunger. We strip the dead to cleanse them for our needs."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "We fled as far as we could, trying to keep close to the geothermal hubs. But the Scourges are treacherous and show no mercy — they stayed at our heels, tormenting us with their hounds that are still lurking in the lightless passages. Beware, o Heavenly Envoy! The few who survived an encounter with them swear these things can suck a soul straight out of a person's body!"
  - After: "We fled to the geothermal hubs. The Scourges' hounds lurk there. Beware — they suck out souls!"
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "We... Let corruption seep into the hearts of the citizens of Santiel's Pride..." {n}The young man shudders and looks away despite his face being covered by the mask.{/n} "It overtook our brothers and sisters, clouded their mind, twisted the true faith in God-Emperor... And made him punish our world by taking the Fiery Messenger away and dooming the infidels to perish in the icy embrace of the endless night..."
  - After: "We let corruption twist our faith." {n}He shudders.{/n} "So He took Nolla and left us to freeze."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: {n}Vego-An wants to object, but freezes in indecision. He turns to you, clutching his hands in a begging gesture.{/n}
  - After: {n}Vego-An hesitates, then begs you.{/n}
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "This is..." {n}Overcome by emotion, the woman grasps the Aquila on her chest.{/n} "We are deeply grateful, o Heavenly Envoy!"
  - After: "This is..." {n}She grasps her Aquila.{/n} "Thank you, Envoy!"
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "Please forgive my insolence, but what is going to happen to us now?"
  - After: "Forgive me, but what happens to us now?"
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "So now... You will take us away from here, won't you?"
  - After: "So... you'll take us away?"
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "From now and till the end of our days, we will pray even more fervently to redeem ourselves before Him... And beg Him to grant you a long life and prosperity."
  - After: "We'll pray harder to redeem ourselves, and for your long life."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "On the day of the Celestial Burial Nolla, Emperor's Fiery Messenger, was to ascend to its celestial throne and carry the deceased to the holy chambers of Terra where they would serve the Immortal. But on that rueful morning the Messenger abandoned us! She vanished from the planet's augurs! And so the preachers proclaimed we have displeased the Emperor and commanded the world to unite in prayer!"
  - After: "On Celestial Burial day, Nolla should have risen to carry the dead to Terra. She vanished! Preachers said we displeased the Emperor."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "How dares he compare our pure faith to his twisted heresy?! We may be are equally helpless before the Nightmares and we use to share the same world... But it does not make us equal! I would sooner find my end in a monster's clutches than call him a brother!"
  - After: "He compares our pure faith to his heresy?! I'd die before calling him brother!"
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "To die now or to perish in an icy blizzard some time later? You present us with a choice that matches our faults, o Heavenly Envoy. We will serve the Emperor one last time and redeem the transgressions of this world with our hard labour. We were born on this world and we will die here along with it."
  - After: "Die now or freeze later? Fitting. We'll labour for the Emperor one last time, and die with our world."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "We have nothing to say, Heavenly Envoy. We are His loyal children, the followers of light. Such is the truth, immutable and absolute."
  - After: "We are His loyal children, Envoy. That is the truth."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "N-no... No, don't!" {n}Vego-An buries his face in his hands, clawing at the golden mask. The sobs and moans grow louder until the young man is openly weeping.{/n}
  - After: "N-no, don't!" {n}Vego-An weeps, clawing his mask.{/n}
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "Such is the way, child. We are impure, so there is a price we must pay." {n}The woman gently pats the young man on the shoulder.{/n} "Come. Children of Redemption deserve to know what the fate has in store for them."
  - After: "We are impure, child. We must pay." {n}She pats his shoulder.{/n} "Come. Tell the Children."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "Horrible Nightmares sent by the Emperor to punish us... A-are you saying one of them is... gone?" {n}The fragile-looking young man shudders.{/n}
  - After: "One of the Nightmares... gone?" {n}He shudders.{/n}
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "Your generosity is boundless, Heavenly Envoy. We rejoice that by the Emperor's divine will and your mighty efforts another child of His was safely returned home."
  - After: "Thank you, Envoy. Another child of His is home."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "A funeral procession marches through the hive streets chanting prayers that resonate through the entire world as a hymn of mourning. The deceased are brought out to the surface, many of them for the first time in their entire lives. The departed take their places on the ritual slabs where they wait for Fiery Messenger's ascension, Nolla's blessed star that showers the deceased with its fiery kisses and delivers their souls to the Immortal, so they can serve him forevermore."
  - After: "The dead are carried to surface slabs to await Nolla, whose fiery kisses deliver their souls to the Immortal."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "Each turn the Fiery Messenger would depart her celestial halls. It was under her gaze that we brewed blessed promethium, extracted it from acid and thunder, and let it simmer in titanic vats. Patiently waiting for Nolla to retire, we departed for the manufactorums outside the hive to empty the boiling vats and refine the promethium for the von Valancius protectorate."
  - After: "By Nolla's light we brewed promethium in huge vats, then refined it for the von Valancius protectorate."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "The heretic believes that since we were born on one world, breathe the same air and look like one another, our minds must be tainted with dark thoughts just like his own. May the Emperor strike me down where I stand if he is speaking the truth!" {n}The young man is brimming with righteous anger, disgust... You sense no deception. And yet you cannot get rid of an vague feeling the kid is not telling you the entire story.{/n}
  - After: "The heretic thinks sharing a world taints us. Strike me down if it's true!" {n}No lie, yet something's hidden.{/n}
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "A great and holy festival! Each cycle during the turn announced by the prophets all Santiel's Pride subjects prepare their departed for the ceremony. Sometimes a spouse, friend or a parent of the deceased decides to accompany one to the Holy Terra — and if they are judged to be feeble, weak or body or unable to work for the good of the Immortal, they are permitted to take their leave along with the dead."
  - After: "A holy festival! Loved ones too weak to work may join the dead on the trip to Holy Terra."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "...extract and refine promethium. Build manufactories. Repair ships. Kill. Do whatever you say." {n}The elder's words ring with tempered steel.{/n}
  - After: "...refine promethium. Build. Repair ships. Kill. Whatever you say." {n}Steel in her voice.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The elders of Children of Redemption are whispering among themselves, but as you approach, they quickly fall silent and greet you with a deep bow.{/n}
  - After: {n}The whispering elders fall silent and bow.{/n}
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: {n}Vego-An shakes his head in dismay.{/n} "Danger besets Children of Redemption on every corner. The wandering Nightmares hunt us to wither our bodies and souls, and the thrice-cursed cultists butcher us to stuff their distended stomachs! Thirst, cold and starvation are our constant companions, but we never gave up hope of reaching out to the Imperium. Of contacting at least someone... Which is why we kept sending people to look for working vox-casters and communication centres."
  - After: {n}Vego-An shakes his head.{/n} "Danger is everywhere. But we keep seeking working vox-casters to reach the Imperium."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "We are the denizens of the hive, from its tallest spires to the very lowest maintenance tunnels. You will find all kinds of skilled people among Children of Redemption: actors and medics, solders and manufactory workers... Most of the survivors huddle behind the secure doors of the shelter's workshops and living quarters."
  - After: "Hive folk of every trade. Most hide in the shelter's workshops and quarters."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "Spare us, Heavenly Envoy! We are loyal servants of the Imperium and the von Valancius dynasty! We... How could be admit to such a disgusting heresy? We dreaded your wrath, for we are His most devoted servants and realise the terrible price of our downfall!"
  - After: "Spare us, Envoy! We're loyal! We feared your wrath too much to admit such heresy!"
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "We do not know where the creature made its lair. But unless you rid Santiel's Pride of this horror..." {n}The breath that is coming from the young man's mask is chocking and ragged.{/n} "Children of Redemption will never atone and abandon the hive — the Nightmares led by the spawn will wither our bodies and souls..."
  - After: "We don't know its lair." {n}Ragged breath.{/n} "Unless you kill it, its Nightmares will consume us."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "What?.." {n}The young man shudders and covers his face already hidden behind the mask.{/n} "Are they... desecrating the bodies of the Emperor's fallen children? But why?"
  - After: "What?" {n}He shudders.{/n} "Desecrating the Emperor's fallen? Why?"
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "W-we have thousands of people who can... who can..."
  - After: "W-we have thousands who can..."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: {n}The young man shoots An-Vido a nervous glance, then turns to you and starts talking so quickly he is almost jabbering:{/n} "O Heavenly Envoy, we will answer any question, but first I... I am begging... help us! Take us away from this doomed planet!"
  - After: {n}He jabbers:{/n} "We'll answer anything, Envoy, but please — take us off this doomed planet!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The shadows of this world's former splendour — two figures in dirty, once opulent mantles bow before you. They both carry heavy Imperial Aquilas on their chests, their faces hidden by smooth expressionless masks whose faded gold is covered in dents, soot and dried blood.{/n}
  - After: {n}Two elders bow in filthy mantles and dented gold masks.{/n}
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "Vego-An, have you gone mad? Our repentance is to live in this dark tunnels, among visions and nightmares! Our lot is to suffer, how else can we purge ourselves?"
  - After: "Vego-An, are you mad? Our penance is to suffer here!"
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "We do not have anything to thank such a powerful patron with. But still we hope you can make use of our meagre belongings. The scouts keep their most vital possessions in this crate."
  - After: "We have little, but take what's in the scouts' crate."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "We ordered the scouts to look for corpses... Frozen, not too badly decomposed..." {n}The woman meekly lowers her head as if facing a guillotine.{/n} "Cut away their clothes, washed them, prayed for their souls... And then made a stew out of the bones. At some point we did run into a supply warehouse, except... Our bodies rejected proper food. And so we realised we had been cursed — for now we can only draw nourishment from human flesh."
  - After: "Our scouts found frozen corpses." {n}She bows her head.{/n} "We made stew from the bones. Now our bodies reject real food. We can eat only human flesh."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "I... I... hope you will be lenient, o Heavenly Envoy!" {n}The young man's face is hidden by a mask, but the quavering shoulders and stifled voice give away his despair.{/n}
  - After: "Please be lenient, Envoy!" {n}He quavers.{/n}
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "As long as Nightmare Driver leaves, there is no hope for the Children of Redemption." {n}The woman nods to herself, but remembers who is standing before her and continues,{/n} "O Heavenly Envoy, I see that my words are unclear. Allow me to explain, the Divine Scourges brought along Visions and Nightmares — terrible creatures, monsters from prophecy and legend. They take commands from an abomination no less cunning and gruesome... We call it the Driver."
  - After: "While Nightmare Driver lives, we have no hope." {n}She explains:{/n} "The Divine Scourges brought Nightmares, led by a cunning abomination: the Driver."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "The Emperor favours us despite all our faults! When we discovered this shelter, its shelves were creaking from the weight of provisions. Water, medicine, devices, tools and weapons are what we are mostly looking for. And besides, scourges and heretics are clever enough to poison the supplies. We prefer to avoid risks as long as there is another way..."
  - After: "This shelter was full of provisions! We seek water, medicine, tools and weapons. Other food may be poisoned."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: {n}The elder takes a step back, covering the young man with her body.{/n} "Fear is nothing, for our faith strong. Death is nothing, for the Emperor shall deliver us..."
  - After: {n}She shields him.{/n} "The Emperor shall deliver us."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "In return? Perhaps... We might extract the remaining promethium from the outside vats so it could be lifted into orbit. But I must say... This will not lighten the burden of our misdeeds! Our lot is to suffer and repent. And even... Even if we wanted to leave the hive, there is no way we could reach the promethium vats. A sword is hanging over Children of Redemption, and Nightmare Driver is its name."
  - After: "We could extract the vats' remaining promethium for orbit. But not while Nightmare Driver hunts us."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "May the golden glow of the Throne shine on you forevermore, o Heavenly Envoy! We will overcome all of our vileness so we do not let you down!"
  - After: "Throne bless you, Envoy! We won't fail you!"
- **Cassia**
  - Before: {n}Cassia scrunches up her face as if she has just bitten into a bitter fruit.{/n} "Your subjects are skillfully dyeing their carmine burden of secrets into a golden glow of supplication. An answer without question, a question without answer."
  - After: {n}Cassia grimaces.{/n} "They gild their carmine secrets. An answer without question."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Danax Alaxius, a cardinal from the shrine world Vinibos, described in his works the tendency of illiterate plebeians to twist the teachings of God-Emperor from one world to another. And yet I remember regent Aaronto telling me that Santiel's Pride is one of the most pious planets in the Koronus Expanse. How could your subjects believe in such a gruesome fable, Rogue Trader?"
  - After: "Cardinal Danax Alaxius wrote that plebeians twist the faith. Yet regent Aaronto called this world most pious. How, Rogue Trader?"
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: {n}An-Vido puts a hand on the boy's shoulder and gives an encouraging nod.{/n} "When the darkness came, Nightmares overran our city. They slashed, ripped, tore at our flesh and sucked out our souls... Hundreds of our people perished trying to push back against the monsters. And yet... We managed to destroy at least one of the vile creatures! I will sleep more soundly tonight thanks to our scout's sacrifice."
  - After: {n}She nods to the boy.{/n} "Nightmares killed hundreds. But our scout's sacrifice destroyed one!"
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "The scouts saw him only once — a lumbering giant stitched together from mismatched pieces of flesh, with three twisted limbs, each ending in a tool so unspeakably vile words cannot describe it. There are bone growths bulging from his spine, and profane liquids pump his innards with greenish ooze."
  - After: "A stitched flesh giant: three limbs ending in vile tools, bone spines, green ooze."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "How can you turn an entire world into a concrete hive with combs of iron and then marvel at its lifeless splendour? Poisonous skies, toxic flesh of the ground — indeed, your species can only take, wither and destroy."
  - After: "You make your worlds iron hives, then admire them. Your species only takes and destroys."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Cast off your doubt. The mon-keigh is clearly describing the antics of my dark kin."
  - After: "That's my dark kin."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: {n}The young man nods thoughtfully.{/n} "I think... I think they are. Even after Santiel's Pride was plunged into darkness, we kept hearing the groans of the blessed mechanisms and the gurgling of cherished fuel from the open plains near the Hive."
  - After: {n}He nods.{/n} "I think so. We still hear machines near the Hive."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "But why?" {n}Vedo-An cocks his head in genuine surprise.{/n} "Does our beloved Emperor, Guardian of Humanity and Sovereign, not sit in the divine hall of the Holy Terra among the Saints? Do the souls of our departed not serve the Immortal, basking in the golden rays of His unearthly splendour?"
  - After: "Why?" {n}Vedo-An is surprised.{/n} "Don't our departed serve the Emperor on Holy Terra?"
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "But the extracting machines are bound by ice, o Heavenly Envoy. I mean no disrespect, but I am afraid this world is no longer capable of granting you its bounty. Only the promethium that had been refined before the judgement day can be saved. I mean... could be, had the manufactorums not been frozen and the streets were not beset by nightmares."
  - After: "The extractors are frozen, Envoy. Only already-refined promethium remains, in frozen manufactorums past nightmare-filled streets."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "Y-yes, of course. We understand, o Heavenly Envoy. And will carry our burden to the bitter end."
  - After: "Y-yes, Envoy. We'll bear our burden."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: {n}The elder lowers his head in confusion.{/n} "Divine Scourges, o Heavenly Envoy. The nightmares and visions that descended upon the world after Nolla abandoned us. They killed us, and chained us like cattle, and dragged us into darkness... The ones they did not take, they tortured, revived and tortured again. M-my mother..." {n}The boy's voice breaks, and you hear a shuddering sigh from behind the mask.{/n}
  - After: "Divine Scourges, Envoy. Nightmares that came when Nolla left. They killed, enslaved, tortured." {n}He lowers his head.{/n} "M-my mother..." {n}His voice breaks.{/n}
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: {n}A quiet moan echoes from under the young man's golden mask.{/n} "I hope... perhaps... you will change your mind."
  - After: {n}He moans.{/n} "Perhaps you'll change your mind."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "It is not clear? His divine wrath is so powerful He had condemned us to suffer even in death! We did not know this, o Heavenly Envoy. But now... All we can do is beg Him for forgiveness. And repent harder."
  - After: "His wrath condemns us even in death! We must repent harder."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "May your every step be blessed, o Heavenly Envoy! We will begin preparations immediately and ascend to the surface in one rotation so that we can welcome our new home!"
  - After: "Bless you, Envoy! We'll reach the surface in one rotation!"
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "It will be as you say, o Heavenly Envoy."
  - After: "As you say, Envoy."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "But what about..." {n}The young man turns to An-Vido and throws up his hands in desperation.{/n}
  - After: "But what about..." {n}He looks to An-Vido.{/n}
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "I hope... We will manage to solve the issue of our peculiar dietary requirement. We will take some, ahem, rations from Santiel's Pride, but it will not last long."
  - After: "Our... diet. We'll take some 'rations', but they won't last."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: {n}An-Vido tensely observes the jubilant young man. You can barely hear her stifled words:{/n} "May the Emperor protect us and forgive us..."
  - After: {n}An-Vido whispers:{/n} "Emperor forgive us..."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "O Lord of the Galaxy, Warden of Light and of all that there is, do your loyal servant's eyes deceive her? A stranger walks among Children of Redemption." {n}The tall figure speaks in a tired female voice.{/n} "We dared not hope for His mercy, and yet... Who are you? Did you really come to save us and to absolve us of all wrongs?"
  - After: "Lord of the Galaxy, a stranger here?" {n}A tired woman's voice.{/n} "Who are you? Have you come to save us?"
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "Do not lose faith, Vego-An. The Heavenly Envoy has already done too much. We will be able to take care of ourselves in the new land."
  - After: "Keep faith, Vego-An. We'll manage in the new land."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "You rid us of the Nightmares and were kind even though we did not deserve it. As for the Emperor... He abandoned us and doomed us to suffering. Never again will His light grace the sky of our dying world. So be it. We will repay you with our last act of servitude."
  - After: "You freed us. The Emperor abandoned us. So be it. We'll serve you one last time."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "To fade away in the cold dark or to slowly dissolve in your vessel's maw... We will accept our fate with dignity, o Heavenly Envoy. However sad it may be."
  - After: "Freeze or be devoured... We'll accept our fate with dignity."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "Unthinkable! Children of Redemption will never turn away from the God-Emperor, even though he doomed us to eternal suffering!"
  - After: "Never! We'll never turn from the God-Emperor!"
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "We will pray day and night for this mercy, oHeavenly Envoy!"
  - After: "We'll pray for it, Envoy!"
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "Send your cargo ships once every cycle — we will extract as much promethium from the vats as humanly possible, until the world perishes or we do."
  - After: "Send cargo ships every cycle. We'll extract promethium until we die."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "Back in the old days the Emperor's followers were forbidden from picking up a weapon, working for less than twenty klaxons, and most certainly from fighting the others to the death over a loaf of mouldy bread. These crimes had to be atoned for with lengthy prayers. This new world that the Children of Redemption now inhabit... is not fit for every soul. I pray that the Emperor forgives those who fled, for I forgave them a long time ago."
  - After: "Our faith forbade killing over bread. Not all could bear this. I forgave those who fled."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "And the Lord of the Galaxy heard us and showed mercy! And he led the scouts straight into an abandoned chamber, full of supplies. Blessed are those who are strong in faith and stalwart in patience!"
  - After: "And He led the scouts to a stocked chamber!"
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "We spent time praying to the Immortal, depriving shunning both food and sleep, sustaining ourselves with nothing but ice crystals..."
  - After: "We prayed, fasting, living on ice..."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "W-we... Have mercy, Heavenly Envoy, w-we are loyal..."
  - After: "Mercy, Envoy, w-we're loyal..."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "Is it... Is it the Heavenly Envoy {mf|himself|herself}, {mf|he|she} who would come as the legends foretold, following the Emperor's will on darkest day to rescue His wayward children?" {n}The young man's voice under the mask is both meek and quavering.{/n}
  - After: "The Heavenly Envoy {mf|himself|herself}? {mf|he|she} of legend?" {n}A quavering voice.{/n}
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "When darkness fell upon our world and Nolla, the Emperor's Fiery Messenger, fled her celestial palace, almost all venerable clans boarded ark ships to bring help from the void between the stars."
  - After: "When Nolla fled, nearly all clans took ark ships to seek help."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "Few left to witness the last few cycles of the dying world. My mother, Vego-An, was among them. It was her who gathered these people and named the most worthy among them the Elders, thus giving Children of Redemption one final chance for salvation. I took her name and her mask after she died — for such is the law of blood."
  - After: "My mother, Vego-An, stayed and named the Elders. I took her name and mask when she died."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "Everyone is equal before His face — and so every Child atones for their faults before the Emperor. We cast lots, and the ones chosen by Him venture into the labyrinths above to look for supplies... nourishment... and hope. It is in seeking to atone that we find purpose."
  - After: "We cast lots; His chosen search above for supplies."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "Each cycle we devoted ourselves to Fiery Messenger, begging her to guide the souls of the departed through void to the Golden Throne. Which is why we, Children of Redemption, mourn our final turns on this dying world. We are doomed to wander the void for eternity, unable to reach the Immortal without His guide. And though we commit the bodies of our dead to flame... The fire's heat cannot compare to Nolla's kisses."
  - After: "Without Nolla, our dead wander the void forever. Our pyres can't replace her."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "I am Vego-An, and this is An-Vido. We are the elders of Children of Redemption, the last sons and daughters of Santiel's Pride. The Lord punished our world by destroying—" {n}The young man chokes on these words.{/n} "—the blasphemers for their transgressions. All we can do is repent and beg Him for lenience..."
  - After: "I'm Vego-An; this is An-Vido, elders of the Children of Redemption. The Lord destroyed—" {n}He chokes.{/n} "—the blasphemers. We repent."
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: {n}The female figure twitches slightly and shoots a glance at the other Elder.{/n}
  - After: {n}She glances at the other Elder.{/n}
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "Silence, fool! You will doom us all!"
  - After: "Silence, fool! You'll doom us!"
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: {n}The young man's pitiful voice rises to a scream, and Vego-An turns to you.{/n} "They made us! They drove us over the bodies of our loved ones, over the ice, over the shards of our former lives... They locked us up, broke us, starved! An-Vido's children perished in her embrace, and my mother was torn apart by Nightmares! We only wanted to survive! Survived at any cost! And when the food ran out... I swear by His name, we never killed for sustenance!"
  - After: {n}Vego-An screams.{/n} "They made us! Starved us! An-Vido's children died in her arms; Nightmares tore my mother apart! We only wanted to survive! We never killed for food!"
- **The Elder An-Vido**
  - Before: "The... The answer remains shrouded in mystery. We tried everything — but since we started feasting upon our own kind, nothing but human flesh satiates our hunger."
  - After: "We don't know. Now only human flesh satisfies."
- **The Elder Vego-An**
  - Before: "And then... And we... We are your loyal subjects, o Heavenly Envoy!"
  - After: "We... We're your loyal subjects, Envoy!"

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/TheLure_Lair4/ExplorationPoint_Lure/EP_Lure_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: Land at the source of the transmission.
  - After: Land at the transmission source.
- **Player**
  - Before: Scan the ark ship using the augurs.
  - After: Scan the ark ship with augurs.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The vox operator has intercepted a transmission coming from the planet. The message runs, "With faith in our Emperor-Progenitor, we are broadcasting this to any who may hear. This is Jesevon, an abode of true-believing pilgrims, colonial designation AIII-649-Minoris. As commanded by our Emperor-Progenitor, we, the Church Nourishing, invite any who need help or are in distress to take shelter with us. It matters not whether you are pious people or apostates. Here in Jesevon, we help everyone."
  - After: A planetary vox message: "This is Jesevon, pilgrim abode AIII-649-Minoris. The Church Nourishing shelters all in distress, pious or apostate."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The pre-recorded message is replayed in the vox-frequency range every one-sixteenth of the planet's axial rotation. The source of the transmission is an ark ship, the Wasteland Wayfarer, which landed on the planet's surface.
  - After: It loops. Source: the landed ark ship Wasteland Wayfarer.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Towering motionless on the planet's surface is a majestic Jericho-class ship, the type that transports pilgrim settlers to new planets. This converted promethium refinery vessel can transport tens of thousands of colonists to their new homeworld. The landing was smooth, judging by the hull integrity. The Wasteland Wayfarer is listed on the register of ships belonging to the Cult of Saint Drusus. Its description, make, and vox-transmitter signature match the register record.
  - After: An intact Jericho-class pilgrim ship, built to carry tens of thousands of colonists. Registered to the Cult of Saint Drusus.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: A settlement has been spotted in the vicinity of the derelict ship. Its architectural and functional design is consistent with the Cult of Saint Drusus's standard templates for founding colonies. No lifeforms were detected. The condition of the structures indicates that the settlement has been abandoned for at least a hundred years.
  - After: A nearby Cult of Saint Drusus settlement. No life signs; abandoned a century or more.

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/TheLure_Lair4/LureDoor/LureDoor_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Contact the ship] "This is the Rogue Trader speaking. We're having difficulties here."
  - After: [Contact the ship] "Rogue Trader here. We have trouble."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Try to force the airlock open]
  - After: [Force the airlock open]
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The airlock is sealed. This isn't right: you distinctly remember never activating the seal on your way through.{/n}
  - After: {n}The airlock is sealed. You never sealed it.{/n}
- **Narrator**
  - Before: {n}Nuncius's empty eye sockets stare indifferently at his colleague's frustration.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nuncius stares on, indifferent.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "I know I am about to state the obvious, but I will state it anyway! There's something off about this. Something very off."
  - After: "Stating the obvious: something's very off."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The control panel refuses to heed any of your commands. The mischievous machine spirits are much too lively and unruly.{/n}
  - After: {n}The unruly machine spirits ignore you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The control panel is being uncooperative. You know enough about machine spirit behaviour to conclude it is not malice that is making them refuse to comply, but a higher-priority order they are executing.{/n}
  - After: {n}No malice; the spirits obey a higher order.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The white noise of static is all you hear in response. Either the Vox Master cannot reply, or she is brazenly ignoring you, or comms are being jammed. None of these possibilities bode well.{/n}
  - After: {n}Only static. Ignored, or jammed. Bad either way.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The plasteel, durable enough to withstand the pressure of the interplanetary void, absorbs your hits with supreme indifference. It will take more than that to break through.{/n}
  - After: {n}The void-proof plasteel shrugs off your blows.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}After repeating the command input sequence thrice, Eogunn huffs in disappointment.{/n} "No, Nuncius, I am certain that I interpreted the machine spirit's response correctly. It is guided by the simplest binharic logic, as well as a strict hierarchy of protocols. And right now, it would sooner die than open the way for us."
  - After: {n}Eogunn huffs.{/n} "No, Nuncius, I read it right. Its protocols forbid letting us through."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Allow me, esteemed colleague. Perhaps you have erred within the sacred rites of decryption." {n}Smiling, Eogunn nudges Pasqal aside to repeat the rites of unsealing. The door remains shut. The Manipulus huffs with irritation.{/n}
  - After: "Allow me, colleague." {n}Eogunn tries. The door stays shut. He huffs.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Emitting a snide binharic hiss, Pasqal declares,{/n} "The attempted re-evaluation of the Machine Spirit by Genetor Februs has been logged. The outcome has been flagged in his efficiency metrics, pending a formal review of his competence."
  - After: {n}Pasqal hisses:{/n} "Genetor Februs's failure is logged for review."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}After repeating the command entry protocol three times, with all the appropriate prayers, the Tech-Priest says in a gloomy, raspy voice,{/n} "The machine spirit controlling this airlock is too simple and guileless to be tricked. It would be easier to deconstruct this airlock than to compel it to open."
  - After: {n}After three tries, the Tech-Priest rasps:{/n} "Too simple to trick. Easier to dismantle it."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/TheLure_Lair4/LureVoxOperator/LureVoxOperator_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Excellent, a vox-caster that works. Now we can let the planet know I have graced it with my presence."
  - After: "A working vox. Let the planet know I'm here."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I'd kill you, but I don't want to get my hands dirty. Flee, freak."
  - After: "Not worth dirtying my hands. Flee, freak."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Make a dash for the vox-caster and try to contact the ship]
  - After: [Dash to the vox and contact the ship]
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you mean our God, the Master of Terra who sits atop the Golden Throne? Or the blasphemous petty deity of whatever cult you're in?"
  - After: "Our God on Terra, or your cult's petty deity?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "It was you or your accomplices who sealed the airlock, was it not?"
  - After: "You sealed the airlock, didn't you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I understand this to be a trap. Am I correct?"
  - After: "This is a trap, isn't it?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What was that you were muttering? A prayer?"
  - After: "What were you muttering? A prayer?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Is there anybody else here? Your brothers and sisters?"
  - After: "Is anyone else here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your words are blasphemous lies. Do not sully His name with your tongue!"
  - After: "Blasphemy. Don't sully His name!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Put your hands up, take off your hood, and don't make any sudden movements. Or else you'll be dead before we're properly acquainted.
  - After: "Hands up, hood off, no sudden moves. Or you're dead.
- **Player**
  - Before: "Abominations that looked exactly like you tried to take over my ship. I killed them all."
  - After: "Your kind tried to take my ship. I killed them all."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Hunched over the vox-caster, the hooded man mutters monotonously but emphatically into the machine as he rocks slightly to and fro,{/n} "In the light of distant stars our Emperor-Progenitor wanders wearily. With thoughts and visions of us, He sends us particles of His light. Though His body suffers, His mind lingers on us. Let us therefore nourish Him with the light of our souls, with our prayers, with our faith."
  - After: {n}A hooded man mutters into the vox,{/n} "Nourish our weary Emperor-Progenitor with prayer."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man falls silent. After a pause he says,{/n} "We know you have come, afflicted ones."
  - After: {n}He pauses.{/n} "We know you have come, afflicted ones."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta's expression brightens.{/n} "Countless foes and a cumbersome position. O Emperor, I thank Thee for giving us another chance to taste the sweetness of battle and the solemn joy of courageous deeds!"
  - After: {n}Argenta brightens.{/n} "Countless foes! Thank the Emperor for this battle!"
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Shereen, I hate to ruin a dramatic moment, but I do feel it's time for us to... run!"
  - After: "Shereen, sorry, but... run!"
- **Cassia**
  - Before: {n}Cassia looks around anxiously.{/n} "They can smell our thoughts, they can see their colour... just like I can! There's no hiding from them."
  - After: {n}Cassia looks around.{/n} "They see our thoughts, like I can! No hiding."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The mutant shrieks, grinning,{/n} "May the grace of our Progenitor be upon you!" {n}His words are piercing, becoming a shrill echo of a hundred... voices? Minds? Growing ever louder, it torments your mind, and before you know it, you reach for your weapon.{/n}
  - After: {n}The mutant shrieks,{/n} "May the Progenitor's grace be upon you!" {n}A hundred minds echo. You draw your weapon.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man smiles the broadest smile his abominable mouth can produce.{/n} "I am Lecocte, Clamavus of the Nourishers of the Afflicted. I am He-Who-Speaks-to-Our-Progenitor. This ship belongs to me."
  - After: {n}He grins.{/n} "I am Lecocte, Clamavus of the Nourishers of the Afflicted. This ship is mine."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man falls abruptly silent, as though sensing your presence. Then he says,{/n} "And here come the afflicted."
  - After: {n}He senses you.{/n} "Here come the afflicted."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}With a pale hand, he throws back his hood. You see an ugly face, with a flat, wide nose, disproportionately large brow ridges, irisless eyes with enormous pupils, a wide toadlike mouth, and skin that transitions to purple scales at the cheekbones. Standing before you is an abominable subhuman, a mutant.{/n} "Welcome to the abode of the Nourishers."
  - After: {n}He lowers his hood: a scaled, toadlike mutant.{/n} "Welcome to the abode of the Nourishers."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}This being's nature has strayed too far from Mankind's blessed genome. The Creed sees no humanity in deviations like these, and so it commands that such creatures be exterminated without mercy.{/n}
  - After: {n}Too far from Mankind's genome. The Creed demands extermination.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Now you know that even mutants can be pleasant looking, while others are downright freakish in appearance. The man talking to you is of the latter kind.{/n}
  - After: {n}As mutants go, he's downright freakish.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}One look tells you that there is nowhere to hide in this place. Well, at least you haven't wasted too much time.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nowhere to hide here.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I know no god but the Emperor-Progenitor. Others are either figments or ephemeral fleshless spirits."
  - After: "I know no god but the Emperor-Progenitor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My brethren have sealed the entrance. But you will be able to leave... later. With us. We are all going to leave this place."
  - After: "My brethren sealed it. You'll leave later... with us."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta frowns.{/n} "The faithful worship the Emperor under a great many names and after a great many fashions. And yet... I do not like this prayer."
  - After: {n}Argenta frowns.{/n} "I dislike this prayer."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Indeed, afflicted one. You have nowhere to run."
  - After: "Indeed. You have nowhere to run."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I was praising the Emperor-Progenitor so that my brothers and sisters might repeat the sacred words with me. Under stars unknown, He keeps His vigil, and sends us His light. He is exhausted and maimed, but in His graciousness, He does not allow Himself to forget us. And we are grateful. We know that our prayers will quell His agonising hunger, and therefore we speak to Him. We beckon Him so that one day, He and His faithful may come to take us under His care." {n}The man rocks gently in place as he makes his speech.{/n}
  - After: "Our prayers ease our maimed Progenitor's hunger. One day He will come for us." {n}He rocks.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man responds with joyful laughter.{/n} "They are here. They are hiding. Waiting. Once we were many; now we are but few. Our blood degenerated. Our flesh grew weak. We were on the verge of death. But you have come, and that is good. You and your people will infuse our blood with a new power. Your ship will take the Nourishers to new worlds. We will rise again."
  - After: {n}He laughs.{/n} "They hide. Your blood will renew ours; your ship will carry us to new worlds."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix recoils, then grimaces and touches his temple as if pained by a headache.{/n} "This is bad. This is very, very bad... Ready your weapon, {name}."
  - After: {n}Heinrix winces.{/n} "Very bad... Ready your weapon, {name}."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Do you believe in the God-Emperor, the Protector of Mankind, who dwells on Holy Terra? Make your answer forthright and clear, for I stand before you as His chosen servant, and this Rogue Trader has been anointed by Him!"
  - After: "Do you believe in the God-Emperor of Terra? Answer plainly!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira clutches her head.{/n} "Blast it! The pressure... What is this... thundering whisper that drowns out the voices!"
  - After: {n}Idira clutches her head.{/n} "This whisper drowns out the voices!"
- **Cassia**
  - Before: {n}Cassia begins to rock to and fro ever so slightly, in sync with the man.{/n} "Purple. Everything is purple. I can see..."
  - After: {n}Cassia rocks with him.{/n} "Everything is purple..."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Rogue Trader, I'm unsure if you have time for such things right now, but as a representative of the Inquisition, I can tell you that a retreat will not be judged as indicating a lack of faith in these circumstances."
  - After: "Rogue Trader, the Inquisition won't call retreat faithless here."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Optimal retreat route calculated. Delaying is not advised."
  - After: "Retreat route calculated. Do not delay."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Wherever the dead man's insane sermons are being broadcast to, static is all that fills the air. For a moment you think you hear Vigdis's voice, only for it to dissolve immediately in the static.{/n}
  - After: {n}Static. Vigdis's voice, briefly, then gone.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The clanging is getting closer. It's coming from the ventilation shafts and dried-up fuel ducts. The deck under your feet vibrates. They're closing in! The psychic din grows more and more distinct as the abominations rush toward you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Clanging through the vents. They're closing in!{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Sister, I fear we are about to partake of something quite different. Or, more likely, someone is about to partake of us."
  - After: "Sister, someone's about to partake of us."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The vox spits out a torrent of static, through which you nonetheless manage to catch fragments of words spoken by a voice not unlike that of your Vox Master:{/n} "...von Valanc— command— rlock..." {n}The signal is lost before you manage to say anything.{/n}
  - After: {n}Through static, your Vox Master:{/n} "...von Valanc— command— rlock..." {n}Lost.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix, evidently at the end of his patience, growls through gritted teeth,{/n} "We must... get out... of this trap!"
  - After: {n}Heinrix growls,{/n} "We must... get out... of this trap!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}If you had had a few hours to explore the ship, you surely would have found any number of discrete shafts and unlocked modules you could use to leave the ship. As it is, you're only aware of a single possible escape route: through the airlock, back the way you came. Any other path may lead to a dead end.{/n}
  - After: {n}The only known way out is back through the airlock.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your heart fills with unease and anger. You have heard thousands upon thousands of prayers over your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Ministorum}many years of service as a member of the Ecclesiarchy{/d}, and what this stranger is saying is a far cry from any holy text you know.{/n}
  - After: {n}In your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_Ministorum}years in the Ecclesiarchy{/d}, you've heard no prayer like this.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your gaze falls on a rune-covered control panel near the vox-receiver. A green lumen burns beneath the "Engage airlock seals" switch. The switch socket is corroded and does not immediately yield to your touch, but the lumen changes colour to blood red, and the whirring of deactivated airlocks rises up from the depths of the ship.{/n}
  - After: {n}You flip the "Engage airlock seals" switch. Airlocks whir open.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man's only response is a mocking grin.{/n}
  - After: {n}He grins mockingly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}His features are strikingly similar to those of the mutant scum you destroyed in the dynastic crypt.{/n}
  - After: {n}He resembles the mutants from the dynastic crypt.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man before you is undoubtedly a Genestealer cultist, a servant of the abominable xenos like the ones who almost took over your ship.{/n}
  - After: {n}A Genestealer cultist, like those who nearly took your ship.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man does not look surprised.{/n} "Though I had not known them before, the Emperor-Progenitor brought me the echo of their deaths, and an image — your image. But their deaths matter not, for you have answered the call. I am elated."
  - After: {n}Unsurprised:{/n} "The Progenitor showed me their deaths. No matter. You came."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Three sorrowful phalanges point the way to the Emperor-Progenitor. I am glad you have chosen ours."
  - After: "Three phalanges lead to the Progenitor. Glad you chose ours."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You hear a clanging echo growing louder in the empty modules: like hundreds of clawed limbs striking bulkheads and grabbing onto bars. Whoever is advancing upon you, there are a lot of them. You ought to run for your life before they trap you in this crammed vox-cabin.{/n}
  - After: {n}Hundreds of claws clang nearer. Run!{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "There's an old military adage that says: when you're already in deep... trouble, don't poke around anywhere unless you know what you'll find there. I propose we get out the same way we came in."
  - After: "When in deep trouble, don't poke around. Leave the way we came."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira touches her temples and says, in a hoarse voice,{/n} "They're flooding the air with their psychic whispers. There's... so many of them!"
  - After: {n}Idira touches her temples.{/n} "So many of them!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The man falls silent. A satisfied chuckle, without a hint of fear, comes from under his hood.{/n} "As long as our Father-Progenitor thinks of me, I am eternal."
  - After: {n}He chuckles.{/n} "While our Father-Progenitor thinks of me, I am eternal."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "If these beings are who I think, they will find us. And they will not lose our scent. Run, elantach!"
  - After: "They won't lose our scent. Run, elantach!"
