The Tech-Priest said the prayer, lamenting the dead ship and beseeching the Omnissiah not to turn His back on Humankind, though they sometimes failed to safeguard His wondrous gifts.
  - After: The Tech-Priest mourned the Fireborn more than its dead, begging the Omnissiah not to abandon Humankind.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: ...after returning to the bridge of {mf|his|her} ship, the Rogue Trader cast a final glance at the endless blackness and the shell of the Fireborn that lurked within it. In that moment, the ship's weapons batteries roared into life, lighting up the darkness with a barrage of fire. And the sad cursed vessel was soon turned into a brilliant mass of molten metal and plasma. For that which was born in fire should also perish in fire...
  - After: ...from {mf|his|her} bridge, the Rogue Trader ordered the batteries to fire. Born in fire, the Fireborn perished in fire...
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Time was up. The scouting party returned to their ship. With one last look at the Fireborn, the Rogue Trader...
  - After: Time was up. With a last look, the Rogue Trader...
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: ...we who walk down the same passageways in the same bays day after day, we who are born, live, and die to the hum of the ship's machines, we forever hunger for the smallest glimpse of another life... and for a chance to see the heroes who tirelessly fight for us and for the glory of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}.
  - After: ...we who live and die to the ship's hum hunger to glimpse the heroes of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Emperor's mercy, do not forsake your loyal servants now!" Van Calox's voice cut sharply through the panic that had descended upon the brave scouts like a net cast by an unseen hand. The psyker's eyes gleamed softly in the gloom — the touch of his sorcery drove the taint of weakness from the scouts' souls, and the sinister voice vanished as if it had never been there. After regrouping, the team retreated to the shuttle.
  - After: "Emperor's mercy!" cried Van Calox. His power drove the fear and voice away. They retreated.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The human mind is helpless in the face of horrors beyond comprehension. A many-voiced moan of despair rippled through the team, which was now in full thrall to the otherworldly terror...
  - After: Incomprehensible horror took the team...
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The units assembled at the shuttles and the Lord Captain gave the final order of this grim expedition:
  - After: At the shuttles, the Lord Captain gave the final order:
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Captain Vesti reported that his unit's foray had so far proceeded without incident, mystical or otherwise. They had found no survivors from the ship's crew. Or bodies, for that matter. However, the unit had encountered a problem — the passage leading to the deck section with the arsenal and storage depot was seriously damaged, especially the power cables. Proceeding further could be dangerous.
  - After: Vesti: no incidents or bodies, but damaged power cables block the way to the arsenal and depot.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The irrepressible Captain Vesti offered up a brief prayer for a favourable outcome to the expedition: "May we leave this place a little richer than when we arrived! For rich men are joyous men, and an honest man's joy makes heretics and Chaos cultists weep!"
  - After: Vesti prayed: "May we leave richer! Rich men's joy makes heretics weep!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: With the assistance of Abelard Werserian, who was familiar with the configuration of many Imperial ships, the Lord Captain devised a route around the dangerous section. The detour added two hours to their journey, but it was worth the effort — the storage depot, when the scouts finally reached it, was full of intact cargo.
  - After: Abelard Werserian plotted a two-hour detour. The depot was full of intact cargo.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Vesti's unit headed off to carry out their orders, while the Rogue Trader and {mf|his|her} team continued on...
  - After: Vesti's unit set off; the Rogue Trader and {mf|his|her} team continued...

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/VoidEvents/PiratesOfFuribundus/PiratesOfFuribundus_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Where did they come from? Why haven't you noticed them before?"
  - After: "Where from? Why unnoticed?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Could this be the work of Kunrad Voigtvir?"
  - After: "Is this Kunrad Voigtvir's work?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "On my order, all stations get ready for void combat!"
  - After: "All stations, void combat ready!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Can we evade this combat?"
  - After: "Can we evade?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Cap'n..." {n}Ravor's voice over the vox sounds weary rather than annoyed.{/n} "I'm getting reports of several ships moving toward us. Judging by the fact that they're not responding to our hails and the telemetry shows a trail of macro batteries, they're not here for a chinwag. Ready to issue orders to prepare for battle at your command."
  - After: "Lord Cap'n..." {n}Ravor sounds weary.{/n} "Hostile ships closing, silent, guns hot. Awaiting battle orders."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The rubbish of Furibundus. And I'm not talking about these wrecks that are about to open fire, I mean the remains of meteorites, gas clouds, refuse from the shipyards... It all bunches together, and the smaller ships hide behind it to harass ships as they emerge from the warp."
  - After: "Furibundus junk. Small ships hide in the debris to ambush ships leaving the warp."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The silence over the vox lasts for several seconds.{/n} "It's possible. He could have hired some scum... or maybe it's just a pirate who saw the state of our ship and decided to push his luck."
  - After: {n}Silence.{/n} "Possibly. Hired scum... or an opportunistic pirate."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ravor snorts, or perhaps chuckles.{/n} "I don't think so, Lord Cap'n. There'd be no reason to — it'll be easier to blast these scum to smithereens than to evade them. We'll warn Footfall we're coming with a few macro salvos!"
  - After: {n}Ravor snorts.{/n} "No, Lord Cap'n. Easier to blast them. We'll greet Footfall with macro salvos!"

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/VoidshipBridge/Furibundus_FirstArrival

- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "But before I leave you, {name}..." {n}Heinrix produces a small device wrapped in velvet.{/n} "I was supposed to deliver this to Lady Theodora, but considering the circumstances, I am giving it to you. This is an Elucidator — a sacred machine that can translate the languages of distant and lost worlds to Imperial Gothic. It is even capable of handling xenos languages, up to a point — there may be flaws in translation, but the overall meaning should be clear."
  - After: "One more thing, {name}." {n}Heinrix offers a device.{/n} "Meant for Lady Theodora. An Elucidator: it translates lost and xenos tongues into Imperial Gothic."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/VoidshipBridge/Furibundus_FirstArrival/Furibindus_FirstArrival_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: "Argenta, who is this Reverend Hieronymus who wants to talk to me?"
  - After: "Argenta, who is Reverend Hieronymus?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Are you leaving us, Heinrix?"
  - After: "Leaving us, Heinrix?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are a skilled fighter, I could use people like you. What do you say we extend your stay in my retinue?"
  - After: "You're a skilled fighter. Stay in my retinue?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Vigdis, tell me about the system we are arriving in."
  - After: "Vigdis, tell me about this system."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do I need to know about Footfall?"
  - After: "What about Footfall?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell the Lady Navigator I give her leave to make the translation from the warp into realspace."
  - After: "The Navigator may translate to realspace."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell me in detail how these choices will benefit me."
  - After: "How does each choice benefit me?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have decided. Tell the Liege I will arrive incognito."
  - After: "Tell the Liege I arrive incognito."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have decided. Tell the Liege I will arrive officially, as the Rogue Trader."
  - After: "Tell the Liege I arrive officially, as Rogue Trader."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why does the Liege want to see me so badly?"
  - After: "Why is the Liege so eager to see me?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Abelard, do you know anything about the Liege of Footfall?"
  - After: "Abelard, what of Footfall's Liege?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Footfall is just a brief stop. What next?"
  - After: "Footfall's a brief stop. Then what?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I hope we meet again. True servants of the Emperor are always welcome aboard my ship."
  - After: "I hope we meet again. Emperor's servants are always welcome aboard."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Finally. My benevolence and patience were both about to run out!"
  - After: "Finally. My patience was running out!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Solomorne, is there any assistance I can provide in your investigation?"
  - After: "Solomorne, can I help your investigation?"
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, allow me to report: our journey through the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} is coming to an end. Lady {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g} Orsellio informs me that we have reached the point where we can translate to {g|Encyclopedia:Realspace}realspace{/g} in the Furibundus System. The Lady Navigator and her pilots are awaiting your permission to begin the process."
  - After: "Lord Captain, the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} journey ends. {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g} Orsellio awaits leave to enter {g|Encyclopedia:Realspace}realspace{/g} at Furibundus."
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "As soon as we solve the issues plaguing the ship and establish contact with the key worlds of your protectorate, the time will come for your Magnae Accessio, the official ceremony of donning the mantle of the Rogue Trader. It is mostly a formality at this point — you already possess all the privileges granted by the Warrant. And yet it is a major milestone in your personal history, the moment your name graces the list of heads of the von Valancius dynasty. We are all looking forward to that day, Lord Captain."
  - After: "After repairs comes your Magnae Accessio, the formal taking of the Rogue Trader's mantle. A formality, but a milestone."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Not to mention pirate hideouts, smuggler caches, and forts belonging to a dozen gangs, groups, and factions. In the Koronus Expanse, the Imperium relies on this as its outpost. The fringes of Humanity's domain rarely resemble its central worlds, but so long as Footfall serves the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}God-Emperor{/g} — insofar as it can — it will be considered a citadel of the Imperium. Although, I have heard that the tithes it sends are... underwhelming, to say the least."
  - After: "And pirate dens. It's the Imperium's Expanse outpost, loyal to the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}God-Emperor{/g}, more or less. Its tithes are... underwhelming."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I will be leaving your voidship when we arrive on Footfall, {name}. Once that is done, consider the Lord Inquisitor's task complete."
  - After: "I leave at Footfall, {name}. That completes the Lord Inquisitor's task."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix replies with a respectful nod.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix nods.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The Kasballica. Vile tech-thieves." {n}Pasqal's vox barks out the last word like a profanity.{/n}
  - After: "The Kasballica. Vile tech-thieves." {n}Pasqal spits it.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix regards you with a curious look and a polite smile.{/n} "An Interrogator of the Inquisition seldom gets to hear such words. Thank you for your hospitality, {name} — I will not forget it."
  - After: {n}Heinrix smiles.{/n} "Interrogators rarely hear that. Thank you, {name}."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix's cold and piercing gaze does not betray any emotion, and neither does his dry smile.{/n} "In that case, I hope they last long enough to get me to Footfall."
  - After: {n}Heinrix smiles dryly.{/n} "Then I hope they last until Footfall."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vigdis begins issuing instructions. The massive ship appears to change with her every word — the bridge is set in motion as hundreds of people start to prepare for the shift to realspace and measured chanting fills the corridors to safeguard the vessel and its crew.{/n}
  - After: {n}Vigdis gives orders; the ship prepares for realspace amid chanting.{/n}
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: {n}Vigdis turns to you again.{/n} "One more thing, Lord Captain. No one at the station knows about Lady Theodora's demise and you inheriting the title. Liege Tocara will be informed — it is required so we can use the dock, and besides, he is expecting a personal audience with the Rogue Trader — he will not meet with an unknown person of unclear standing. However, there is still the matter of announcing your arrival. You can either arrive on the station with the proper pomp and ceremony — or choose to visit it incognito."
  - After: {n}Vigdis turns.{/n} "No one there knows Lady Theodora died. Liege Tocara must be told. Arrive with ceremony, or incognito?"
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "According to Footfall's unwritten laws, Rogue Traders enjoy special privileges that exceed even the power of the Liege. However, they may choose not to exercise those privileges in certain situations — arriving incognito will give you more room for manoeuvre, while an official visit will allow you to directly intervene in local affairs."
  - After: "There, Rogue Traders outrank even the Liege. Incognito gives you freedom; an official visit lets you intervene directly."
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "It is the largest port and the trading capital of the Koronus Expanse. It has a dockyard that will allow us to inspect and repair the voidship, and it boasts its own Astropathic Choir — the Koronus Expanse communications nexus."
  - After: "The Expanse's largest port, with a repair dock and the Expanse's Astropathic Choir."
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "Furibundus is valuable due to its close proximity to the Maw — the gateway to the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}. The system is mostly known for Footfall — the main base for merchants, privateers, and Rogue Traders traversing the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g}. Additionally, the star itself is orbited by an {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} station, which is off-limits to outsiders."
  - After: "Furibundus guards the Maw into the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}. It holds Footfall, hub of the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Koronus Expanse{/g} traders, and a closed {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} station."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Vladaym Tocara is a very peculiar young man. Consider your upcoming conversation a baptism of fire in Footfall's political arena. Such things are not spoken out loud, but Liege Tocara is the appointee of the {g|Encyclopedia:KasballicaMission}Kasballica Mission{/g}, the largest robber baron crime syndicate in the Calixis Sector. They specialise in the {g|Encyclopedia:ColdTrade}Cold Trade{/g} — the buying and selling of all kinds of {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g} rubbish."
  - After: "Vladaym Tocara: your baptism of fire. Quietly, he serves the {g|Encyclopedia:KasballicaMission}Kasballica Mission{/g}, a crime syndicate in the {g|Encyclopedia:ColdTrade}Cold Trade{/g} of {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g} goods."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Footfall was previously run by a Liege who did business with several criminal factions at once, but he suffered an 'accident.' The reins of power were picked up by Vladaym Tocara, whose appointment benefits not only the Kasballica but also their most powerful ally in the Koronus Expanse — Rogue Trader Calligos Winterscale."
  - After: "His predecessor had an 'accident.' Tocara serves the Kasballica and their ally, Calligos Winterscale."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Vladaym is a slippery yet very cautious fellow. He does not usually beat around the bush and does not play mind games. Perhaps more importantly, he is no fool — fools do not rise this high in the Kasballican hierarchy. Keep all this in mind. You are a Rogue Trader, you stand above him in status and wield considerable power. Having said that, history has seen cases where the Kasballican barons crossed swords with Rogue Traders and emerged victorious. Do not forget that, and remain vigilant."
  - After: "He's slippery, cautious, and no fool. You outrank him, but Kasballican barons have beaten Rogue Traders. Stay vigilant."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Not you personally — he wishes to meet with the Rogue Trader of the von Valancius dynasty. Tocara does not know about Lady Theodora's death and is simply seeking an audience with the powers that be. My gut is telling me that something must be very wrong on Footfall if our Astropath managed to read such strong emotion in such an anodyne message."
  - After: "He wants the Rogue Trader, unaware Theodora died. Our Astropath sensed strong emotion. Something's very wrong there."
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "We have no information, Lord Captain. The broadcast from the Footfall Astropathic Choir was the only missive Master Zacchary has received lately."
  - After: "No information, Lord Captain. Master Zacchary received only that message."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "I shall explain, if you do not mind. As per this unwritten rule, every Rogue Trader arriving at the station has the right to veto any of the Liege's decisions. But there is a catch — the Koronus Expanse is home to several influential Rogue Trader dynasties, and Footfall is where their interests intersect."
  - After: "By custom, any Rogue Trader there can veto the Liege. But many dynasties' interests meet on Footfall."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Of course, that does not prevent certain persons, namely Calligos Winterscale, from subtly pulling the strings on Footfall. If you, as a new Rogue Trader, start your career with an official landing and a parade in your honour, the other dynasties may see this gesture as the newcomer challenging their spheres of influence."
  - After: "Winterscale pulls its strings. A newcomer's parade may seem a challenge to the others."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "I do not see that as a bad thing, necessarily. Old man Winterscale may take slight offence. Chorda will be put on her guard. But you have just risen to prominence and most people in the Koronus Expanse have not even heard about Lady Theodora's departure yet. It must be made clear that the banner of von Valancius soars as high as ever."
  - After: "Not bad, though. Winterscale may sulk, Chorda grow wary. Show the von Valancius banner still soars."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "If I may, I would recommend arriving incognito. You will have plenty of opportunities to savour the sweetness and the burden of power, but right now is the last time you can take refuge in obscurity. This way, your arrival will not draw much attention, and the people will treat you as a person and not the almighty sovereign anointed by the Emperor — it could turn some situations to your advantage."
  - After: "Go incognito. It's your last chance at obscurity; people will treat you as a person, not a sovereign."
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "It will be done, Lord Captain." {n}Vigdis bows again.{/n} "With your gracious permission, I will return to my duties."
  - After: "It will be done." {n}Vigdis bows.{/n} "By your leave."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Thank you for your offer, but I must decline. I am afraid my duty to the Golden Throne comes before everything else."
  - After: "Thank you, but no. My duty to the Golden Throne comes first."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I hereby inform the Rogue Trader that during a comprehensive system inspection rite, this unit discovered data clusters within the captain's cogitator that are concealed from prying eyes by means of a personal cipher and a sacrament of algorithmic authorisation."
  - After: "This unit found ciphered, locked data clusters in the captain's cogitator."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Unit {name} von Valancius has been added to the access list and assigned the identifier 'Keeper 2.' The unit can access the data from the captain's cogitator provided that {mf|he|she} possesses the decryption key." {n}You detect a hint of something resembling curiosity in Pasqal's mechanical voice.{/n}
  - After: "Unit {name} von Valancius is now 'Keeper 2,' with access if {mf|he|she} has the key." {n}Pasqal sounds curious.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, young Evayne Winterscale has asked me to convey his gratitude for your hospitality and for saving him from certain death. Not wishing to outstay his welcome, he plans to disembark at Footfall. Lord Evayne swears he will not forget his debt to you."
  - After: "{mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, Evayne Winterscale thanks you for his life and disembarks at Footfall. He won't forget his debt."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "On a personal note, young Winterscale is almost as good as new. Thanks to the efforts of our chirurgeons and the talents of Master van Calox, he has made a speedy recovery, except for the gouged eye, which we were unable to save. But I am sure Lord Evayne will be able to afford a decent implant to replace it."
  - After: "Our chirurgeons and Master van Calox healed him, save one eye."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "The shed blood has washed away the taint from our bodies — it is only right that we now wash our souls with the blessings of the servant of the Undying One. The Drusians, like the Bloodspun Web, are devoted to asceticism, rejecting wealth and luxury and surrendering themselves to His service. Though their thread is different from ours, the First Spinner spoke of them with respect."
  - After: "Blood cleansed our bodies; now let the Undying One's servant bless our souls. The First Spinner respected the ascetic Drusians."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Thank you once again for rescuing my squad, Rogue Trader. We will disembark on Footfall — the trail of evidence leads to the docks, and it wouldn't hurt to pay the Liege a visit. I am sure he will graciously extend his cooperation to the Arbites."
  - After: "Thanks again for saving my squad. The trail leads to Footfall's docks, and to the Liege."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "Right at this moment, unlikely. We have a considerable amount of dirty and routine work ahead of us, such as checking cogitator logs and questioning the station's residents, including its less palatable individuals. None of that is worth the Rogue Trader's time, I assure you. Still, should circumstances change, I will absolutely welcome the aid of such a dependable ally as yourself."
  - After: "Not now; just routine logs and questioning. If that changes, I'll welcome your help."
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "Master Zacchary Weisz has recovered an invitation previously adrift in the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}Immaterium{/g} — the Liege of Footfall has humbly requested an audience with the Rogue Trader of the von Valancius dynasty. According to Master Zacchary, the message was 'tinted with shades of pleading.' I quote: 'Apparently the Liege is anxious to meet as soon as possible.'"
  - After: "Master Zacchary Weisz caught a message in the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}Immaterium{/g}: Footfall's Liege urgently, almost pleadingly, requests an audience with the von Valancius Rogue Trader."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Footfall... The place where filth and sanctity go hand in hand. Reverend Hieronymus Doloroso will most likely expect a visit from me. I imagine he will be interested in talking to you as well, {name}."
  - After: "Footfall... filth and sanctity together. Reverend Hieronymus Doloroso will expect me, and you, {name}."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "The arrangement between the Lord Inquisitor and your predecessor was that I be transported to Footfall and no farther. I dare not take advantage of your generosity and patience any more than I already have, {name}."
  - After: "The deal was passage to Footfall. I won't presume further, {name}."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "He is the head of the {g|Encyclopedia:Drusians}Drusian{/g} mission on Footfall and one of the most prominent clergymen in the sector. Paying him a visit is a good thing for any loyal servant of the Emperor to do. I assisted his mission before I joined Lady Theodora on her voyage. I need his blessing to accompany the new Rogue Trader of the von Valancius dynasty. If you wish to have me aboard your voidship, I request that we meet with Reverend Hieronymus."
  - After: "He leads the {g|Encyclopedia:Drusians}Drusian{/g} mission on Footfall. I served it before Theodora. I need his blessing to serve you, so we must meet him."
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "Due to Footfall's remoteness, it has developed its own rules and customs. Many of the goods that can be procured there would be considered heresy in the heart of the Imperium, enough to warrant summary execution. Moreover, Footfall is the domain of the Rogue Traders, who transcend certain Imperial laws by virtue of the Warrant they bear."
  - After: "Remote Footfall makes its own rules; its goods are heresy elsewhere. Rogue Traders' Warrants place them above some laws."
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: "The Furibundus System is home to {g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g} — the only Imperium outpost with a functioning wharf in the Koronus Expanse. The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} are begging you to have mercy on the machines worn down by the warp and to allow the servants of the Omnissiah to inspect and heal the voidship's wounds in the dock. The prayers and rituals will take some time, which our {g|Encyclopedia:Astropath}Astropathic{/g} Choir will use to establish a connection with the prime worlds of your protectorate — Dargonus, Janus, and Kiava Gamma."
  - After: "Furibundus holds {g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g}, the Expanse's only Imperial wharf. The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} beg to repair the ship there, while our {g|Encyclopedia:Astropath}Astropathic{/g} Choir contacts Dargonus, Janus, and Kiava Gamma."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Altar-Templum-Calixis-Ext-17. I had the honour of tending to this shrine for a few thousand cycles. I suggest you abstain from visiting it as most tech-comrades at the station are engaged in meditative calculations that should not be interrupted."
  - After: "Altar-Templum-Calixis-Ext-17. I tended it for thousands of cycles. Don't disturb its meditations."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/VoidshipBridge/InterrogatorBriefing_dialogue/InterrogatorBriefing_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Why did your suspicion fall on Kiava Gamma?"
  - After: "Why suspect Kiava Gamma?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I welcome the chance to assist the Inquisition with its enquiries, van Calox."
  - After: "Glad to assist the Inquisition, van Calox."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not object to you personally, but I find the continuous presence of an Inquisition agent at my side slightly unnerving."
  - After: "Nothing personal, but an Inquisition agent at my side is unnerving."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You wouldn't be on my ship if I had any say in the matter."
  - After: "If I had a say, you wouldn't be aboard."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Lord Inquisitor mentioned in his letter that he is willing to show lenience toward my actions that would otherwise be interpreted as radical."
  - After: "The Lord Inquisitor promised lenience for my radical actions."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I won't let anyone throw their weight around on my worlds, be they servants of Chaos, xenos, or heretics."
  - After: "No Chaos, xenos, or heretics will rule my worlds."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I want to know more about this Cult of the Final Dawn."
  - After: "Tell me about the Cult of the Final Dawn."
- **Player**
  - Before: "A Chaos cult in my protectorate... Heinrix, are you laying an accusation against my dynasty?"
  - After: "A Chaos cult in my protectorate... Accusing my dynasty, Heinrix?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have already agreed to give you a place aboard my ship. What else?"
  - After: "You already have a place aboard. What else?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You have spies on the von Valancius worlds?"
  - After: "You have spies on von Valancius worlds?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I must go about my business. Is there anything else I need to know?"
  - After: "I must go. Anything else?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why would Ordo Xenos agents investigate a Chaos cult?"
  - After: "Why would Ordo Xenos chase a Chaos cult?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not believe you lack compassion. You did not stop me after all, although you certainly could have tried to."
  - After: "You're not heartless. You didn't try to stop me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I guess sometimes the good of the Imperium demands we turn a blind eye to the fate of its individual servants."
  - After: "Sometimes the Imperium's good outweighs individual servants."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Let us assume Kiava Gamma has fallen to heresy. What then? Will you again propose we destroy an entire planet?"
  - After: "If Kiava Gamma is heretical, will you again propose destroying a planet?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "We met a Chaos Space Marine on Rykad Minoris — do we risk running into his brothers?"
  - After: "Will we meet more Chaos Space Marines like on Rykad Minoris?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Let us depart from business matters, Heinrix. You once promised to entertain me with a compelling conversation — surely, this is not what you had in mind."
  - After: "Enough business, Heinrix. You promised compelling conversation."
- **Player**
  - Before: "That is enough discussion about the Archenemy's servants. Tell me about the Drukhari who stole Rykad's sun."
  - After: "Enough of the Archenemy. Tell me about the Drukhari who stole Rykad's sun."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix nods slightly.{/n} "Thank you for finding an opportunity to talk. I trust now would be a good time to explain the reason for my return aboard your ship."
  - After: {n}Heinrix nods.{/n} "Thank you. Let me explain why I'm back aboard."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The person I mentioned is not a spy but a secretary in the Administratum department on Dargonus. The planet's governor and Theodora were fully aware of his status. His duty is to fulfil the sacred oath to the Golden Throne and eliminate threats to the Imperium, which the Koronus Expanse has in abundance."
  - After: "Not a spy: an Administratum secretary on Dargonus, known to its governor and Theodora."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "His name is Achilleas Scalander. As soon as we contact Dargonus I will introduce you as the new head of the dynasty. I am sure you will appreciate the presence of such an advisor among your subjects, and I suggest you heed his words at least occasionally."
  - After: "Achilleas Scalander. I'll introduce you once we contact Dargonus. Heed him sometimes."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Rogue Trader should deliver me to the system that contains the {g|Encyclopedia:IndustrialWorld}industrial world{/g} of Kiava Gamma. I will then accompany you to the surface and determine what the cult is planning and how it intends to use the resources that have fallen into their clutches — which may very well include the blessed engines of the Adeptus Mechanicus and even the followers of the Omnissiah themselves."
  - After: "Take me to the {g|Encyclopedia:IndustrialWorld}industrial world{/g} Kiava Gamma. I'll learn what the cult plans with what it seized, maybe Mechanicus engines."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I often encounter such reactions. As long as the Lord Captain and {mf|his|her} subjects do not interfere with my work or attract my professional interest, I will not interfere in the Rogue Trader's affairs or distract you with my presence more than is strictly necessary."
  - After: "Common reaction. If the Lord Captain and {mf|his|her} people don't obstruct me, I won't interfere."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your concern is unfounded... As long as there is no substantial reason for it. I hope there will not be one."
  - After: "Unfounded... unless given reason. I hope not."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, your enthusiasm is commendable." {n}The Interrogator smiles but his eyes remain cold.{/n}
  - After: "Commendable enthusiasm." {n}His eyes stay cold.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To business, then. The Cult of the Final Dawn. The madmen preach their heretical doctrine among the denizens of the Koronus Expanse and instigate crimes against the Throne and Humanity. One such crime took place in your protectorate. The Lord Inquisitor considered it necessary to have one of his acolytes accompany the Rogue Trader on the voyage into the corrupted region. I also need to meet with one of my observers on the capital world of your domain."
  - After: "To business. The Cult of the Final Dawn spreads heresy across the Expanse, including a crime in your protectorate. So I sail with you, and must meet an observer on your capital."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix nods.{/n} "That is correct. I should show greater tolerance for the mistakes of a newly appointed Rogue Trader. To be frank, I am surprised: the Lord Inquisitor is not the type to indulge the weakness of soul and mind — even in someone who only recently accepted the burden of a lofty title."
  - After: {n}He nods.{/n} "Yes, I'm to tolerate a new Rogue Trader's mistakes. Surprising; he rarely indulges weakness."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A commendable aspiration for a person who holds the fates of billions of people and dozens of Imperial worlds in {mf|his|her} hands. Which is why you need to be ever more vigilant when looking for seeds of corruption on your planets — lest they sprout someday and spell doom for whatever is tangled up in their roots."
  - After: "Commendable, with billions in {mf|his|her} hands. So watch your planets for seeds of corruption."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix stares you down.{/n} "On Rykad Minoris, you made a decision that sent billions of souls into the grasp of the Archenemy. An unreasonable and unforgettably high price for a small handful of people saved by your mercy. Do I consider it a worthy exchange? I most certainly do not. Will I make every effort to make sure such an exchange does not happen again? Of course I will. Sentimentality is a luxury I cannot afford."
  - After: {n}Heinrix stares.{/n} "On Rykad Minoris, you traded billions of souls to the Archenemy for a handful. Never again. Sentimentality is a luxury I cannot afford."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Chaos worshippers. Most often agents of the Throne run into lone renegades stirring up the rabble. Insane prophets and hysteric visionaries preaching the end of days. A passing comet, a mutant rebellion, an onslaught of monsters... Each time they come up with a new reason why people should prostrate themselves and quiver in fear. Much effort and the blood of those loyal to the Golden Throne were spent before we established the connection between those heretics."
  - After: "Chaos worshippers. Usually lone doom-prophets. Linking them cost much loyal blood."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are well versed in how the Inquisition is organised, {name}. Yes, initially our arrival in the Koronus Expanse was dictated by the need to fight xenos. But there is more — the cult is tangentially related to my main specialisation. Perhaps I will be able to reveal the full truth someday, but right now I ask you to display humility and patience."
  - After: "You know the Inquisition, {name}. We came for xenos, but the cult touches my specialty. Be patient; I may tell all someday."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "However, the Cult of the Final Dawn is something greater than a gaggle of misguided seers and fortune-tellers. They cleverly spread their agents all over the Koronus Expanse, disseminating heresy among honest people on the Imperial worlds. There is a certain strategy to their actions that changes whenever we get too close. And finally, they have enough military power to have had the two ships that we had sent after them later discovered as wreckage."
  - After: "But this cult is organised: agents across the Expanse, shifting tactics, and two of our ships destroyed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You needn't have used the word 'sometimes.' The good of the Imperium always prevails over the lives of its individual servants. I may sometimes falter, but that speaks of my weakness, not the generosity of my soul. Much hinges on the decisions made by the Inquisition, sometimes far more than an ordinary servant of the Throne can see."
  - After: "Not 'sometimes.' Always. If I falter, that's weakness, not generosity."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Interrogator's eyes narrow.{/n} "I haven't said I would not like to be able to afford such luxury. In fact, deep down I understand why you acted that way... I have yet to eliminate the understanding and acceptance within myself, but I will."
  - After: {n}His eyes narrow.{/n} "I wish I could afford it. I understand you... but I'll purge that."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Let me put it this way: you may think whatever you want of me, but my goal is not to hinder you. I am here to help you in the fight against foes you may not even be aware of. You have my word that I will provide every assistance in uprooting the heresy that has sprouted on the von Valancius worlds while their {mf|master|mistress} was away — and that I will try to be more patient with the less grievous flaws the bearers of the {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} are sometimes known to have."
  - After: "I'm here to help against foes you can't see. I'll help uproot the heresy on your worlds from their {mf|master|mistress}'s absence, and tolerate lesser flaws of {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} bearers."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Interrogator pauses. He then faintly smiles and adds in a slightly different tone,{/n} "Might I add that we still haven't had a chance to speak under less demanding circumstances? I hope we can revisit that once I have completed my mission."
  - After: {n}He smiles faintly.{/n} "We should talk at ease sometime. After my mission."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix inclines his head.{/n} "Thank you for sparing the time, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}Heinrix bows.{/n} "Thank you, Lord Captain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix winces.{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:Drukhari}Drukhari{/g}... One of the branches of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g}, an ancient and vicious {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g} race. Those creatures are a living terror to ordinary people who fall prey to their raids, for the simple reason that the victims are not killed outright but instead become their... 'playthings.' Just as you and I need air to survive, the Drukhari require psychic energy born from torment and pain, which they extract from their captives with uncanny expertise."
  - After: {n}Heinrix winces.{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:Drukhari}Drukhari{/g}, kin of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g}, vicious {g|Encyclopedia:Xenos}xenos{/g}. They take captives as 'playthings,' feeding on their torment."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Their ships, which are difficult to mistake for any other, arrive suddenly and undetected — their stealth technologies greatly surpass the capabilities of standard Imperium augur arrays. The objective of their raids is never to capture a world or a ship — no, they are only interested in fresh victims. After filling their holds with living captives, they disappear into the {g|Encyclopedia:Webway}Webway{/g} — a different dimension, which conceals their greatest stronghold. Commorragh. The Dark City of the Drukhari, from which none can hope to escape."
  - After: "Their ships evade our augurs. They raid for captives, then vanish into the {g|Encyclopedia:Webway}Webway{/g} to Commorragh, the Dark City. None escape."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix studies your expression.{/n} "I do not know why the Drukhari stole Rykad's sun and brought about the fulfilment of the cult's prophecies. Perhaps the xenos themselves have played into the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Archenemy{/g}'s designs. Or perhaps Aurora's divinations, in fact, described the Drukhari's actions... There is only one thing I can say with absolute certainty: there is no alliance between the Cult of the Final Dawn and the xenos. It is simply impossible."
  - After: {n}He studies you.{/n} "Why they stole Rykad's sun, I don't know. Perhaps they served the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Archenemy{/g}, or Aurora foresaw them. But cult and xenos allied? Impossible."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The growing difficulty in making warp jumps is detrimental to us but is unlikely to inconvenience those who engage in vile sorcery day in, day out." {n}Heinrix sighs.{/n} "After the events on Rykad Minoris, I suspected the cult might have built its nest inside Winterscale's domain, but the latest reports indicate it is your protectorate that is harbouring heretics. Being in your entourage improves my chances of getting closer to their secrets."
  - After: "Warp jumps grow harder, but not for sorcerers." {n}He sighs.{/n} "I suspected Winterscale's domain, but reports point to yours. With you, I'll get closer."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Disjointed pieces of data that finally merged into a single picture. Additionally, not long ago a vessel from that world arrived on Footfall. The reports from the crew were confused and alarming, making me fear a planet-wide rebellion."
  - After: "Scattered data formed a picture. And a ship from there brought alarming reports. I fear planet-wide rebellion."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have no doubt it will happen sooner or later, {name}. Chaos Marines siding with the cult is... very, very bad news: most likely they kept away until recently, pulling their puppets' strings from a respectable distance. These traitors seldom show up alone. The best we can count on is having to deal with just a squad of Chaos Space Marines in the Koronus Expanse and not an entire company."
  - After: "Surely, {name}. Chaos Marines with the cult is very bad news. At best, a squad, not a company."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I do remember our exchange. For the time being, however, I would prefer to focus on my direct responsibilities." {n}You hear a note of regret in Heinrix's voice as he shakes his head.{/n} "Perhaps, later. After Kiava Gamma."
  - After: "I remember. But duty first." {n}He sounds regretful.{/n} "After Kiava Gamma."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I will be frank: the answer to this question is unlikely to please either of us. The machinations of Chaos usually go beyond solely inflicting countless deaths and destruction. Having their plans come to fruition would lead to far more terrible consequences. One of the systems in the Koronus Expanse is already lost... May the Emperor protect us from watching this tragedy play out again."
  - After: "You won't like it. Chaos seeks worse than death. One Expanse system is already lost."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Chaos treads softly, {name}. The main danger of secret cults and sects is that they are like seeds. They can remain in the ground for decades, safe from all scrutiny — until an opportunity to sprout, grow, and bear monstrous fruit presents itself. The emergence of a cult on one of the Rogue Trader's planets does not mean the dynasty head {mf|himself|herself} is a Chaos worshipper. Having said that, it should be noted that Theodora von Valancius was famous for her loose interpretation of the freedoms granted by the {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g}."
  - After: "Chaos treads softly, {name}. Cults lie dormant for decades. One on your world doesn't make you {mf|himself|herself} a heretic. Yet Theodora read her {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} loosely."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix regards you with a probing look.{/n} "A bloodline can be stained by ancestral transgressions. If it is indeed so, it is in your best interests to do whatever necessary to redeem yourself — and then, perhaps, you will get a chance to salvage your dynasty's reputation."
  - After: {n}A probing look.{/n} "If ancestral sins stain your blood, redeem yourself, and perhaps your dynasty."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix looks at you closely.{/n} "It is known that corruption runs in the blood. Your propensity for heretical deeds is yet to be determined — perhaps by the Lord Inquisitor himself."
  - After: {n}He looks closely.{/n} "Corruption runs in the blood. Yours is for the Lord Inquisitor to judge."

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/VoidshipBridge/OfficersMeeting_dialogue/OfficersMeeting_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Very well, our course is clear. Do my officers have any other issues that require immediate attention?"
  - After: "Our course is clear. Any other urgent issues?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Abelard, what is your opinion? Which world should we deal with first?"
  - After: "Abelard, which world first?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do I need to know about Dargonus?"
  - After: "What about Dargonus?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What would the consequences of losing contact with these worlds be?"
  - After: "What if we lose contact with these worlds?"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I testify that Kiava Gamma is a world marked by the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}'s patronage. By His grace, the manufactorums of the colony are inhabited by committed and industrious machine spirits."
  - After: "Kiava Gamma bears the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}'s favour. Its machine spirits are industrious."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Now we can be certain that problems with {g|Encyclopedia:Astropath}Astropathic{/g} communication in the Koronus Expanse are no coincidence. There is a warp disturbance in your way, Lord Captain — it is swallowing messages and disrupting familiar routes. This means you need to locate the key worlds of the von Valancius protectorate as soon as possible — I am talking about Janus, Dargonus, and Kiava Gamma. Charting new routes so they can be reached and restoring control will be the necessary next step."
  - After: "{g|Encyclopedia:Astropath}Astropathic{/g} failures are no coincidence; a warp disturbance swallows messages and routes. Find routes to Janus, Dargonus, and Kiava Gamma and restore control."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Dargonus is the heart and soul of your protectorate. It is where the main administrative resources and storage facilities are, and so is the von Valancius palace. If you would like to know, this is where you will publicly accept the title of Rogue Trader. Dargonus is a major administrative hub that runs the cargo fleet and keeps track of finances."
  - After: "Your protectorate's heart: administration, finances, the cargo fleet, and the palace where you'll take your title."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That is all, Lord Captain. The vessel and the crew await your instructions and are ready to depart Footfall immediately, should you so desire."
  - After: "That's all. We can leave Footfall on your order."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: {n}Cassia makes a quick nervous gesture, adjusting the adornment over her third eye.{/n} "I have been studying the records left by the vessel's previous {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g}. I wanted to double-check the route to Dargonus and discovered that... it does not match the one recorded in the Atlas. It is more than a minor {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} fluctuation — the route has been wiped out, it can no longer be used for travelling. To make matters worse, I started checking the paths from the Atlas, one after the other, and saw the same thing everywhere. The warp is roiling with an {g|Encyclopedia:CicatrixMaledictum}ominous storm{/g}, bursting with vivid and screaming colours. It will not hinder our movement... But all previous knowledge is now utterly useless."
  - After: {n}Cassia fidgets.{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g}'s route to Dargonus is wiped out, like every Atlas path. An {g|Encyclopedia:CicatrixMaledictum}ominous storm{/g} roils the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g}. We can travel, but our charts are useless."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A world deprived of connection to its neighbouring systems and the Koronus Expanse's infrastructure can only rely on itself — and their capabilities are often limited. For example, Janus does not have a fleet of its own. Pirates, cultists, heretics, xenos — anyone could prey on the helpless planet. The loss of communication is a threat to your position. A {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} with no protectorate to back them is one that grows weaker by the day."
  - After: "A cut-off world stands alone. Janus has no fleet; raiders could prey on it. And a {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} without a protectorate weakens."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "On the other hand, I am concerned by the rumours concerning Kiava Gamma. There have been no problems on Janus for many years, but something is very wrong with the {g|Encyclopedia:IndustrialWorld}industrial world{/g} right now. Delay may cost us the entire planet."
  - After: "But Kiava Gamma worries me. The {g|Encyclopedia:IndustrialWorld}industrial world{/g} is in trouble; delay may cost it."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix coughs quietly.{/n} "Mistress Toliman neglected to mention that the Kiava Gamma manufactorum also supplies heavy machinery, from forage harvesters to vessel systems and components."
  - After: {n}Heinrix coughs.{/n} "Kiava Gamma's manufactorum also makes heavy machinery and ship components."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "I trust I do not have to explain the capital world? Losing it would make us the laughing stock of the other dynasties. Besides, the loss of chronicles and ledgers would spell a bureaucratic catastrophe... So all three systems are equally vital to the protectorate. It falls to you to decide which should be brought into the fold before the rest, Lord Captain."
  - After: "Losing the capital would shame us. All three are vital. You choose."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard turns his hard eyes on Heinrix.{/n} "You display commendable knowledge of our worlds' manufacturing capability, van Calox."
  - After: {n}Abelard glares.{/n} "You know our industry well, van Calox."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta angrily chops the air with a side of her palm.{/n} "Warp storms are our enemies, just like heretics and daemons. It is a shame they can't be dispersed with a flamer or a bolter!"
  - After: {n}Argenta chops the air.{/n} "Shame a flamer can't disperse warp storms!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, the inspection of the ship's systems is complete. The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} are reporting the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} are calm and satisfied. Everything is ready for onward travel... Except there is an issue you must be made aware of."
  - After: "Lord Captain, the {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priests{/g} report the {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirits{/g} content. We're ready... but there's an issue."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The surface of Janus was altered extensively so the planet could be designated an {g|Encyclopedia:AgriWorld}agri-world{/g}. It is a powerful food base, capable of supplying the burgeoning protectorate and exporting provisions to the outer worlds at the same time. Janus owes much of its prosperity to the Governor House of Vyatt. Under its leadership, the world has grown ever more prosperous year after year, securing shipments and taxes while keeping the workforce tightly controlled."
  - After: "Janus is an {g|Encyclopedia:AgriWorld}agri-world{/g} feeding your protectorate and exporting food, thriving under Governor House Vyatt's tight control."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "{g|Encyclopedia:IndustrialWorld}Industrial world{/g} Kiava Gamma is being managed by the Governor House of Gaprak and supplies your protectorate with rare mineral resources. Additionally, the planet features an {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g} that processes materials and prepares them for shipment."
  - After: "{g|Encyclopedia:IndustrialWorld}Industrial world{/g} Kiava Gamma, ruled by House Gaprak, supplies rare minerals, processed in an {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g}."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}A faint smile appears on Kibellah's lips.{/n} "If the faithless decide that your worlds are easy prey, that is good. We will find enough enemies in your domain, then. And we will kill them. The Undying One will look upon us with approval."
  - After: {n}Kibellah smiles.{/n} "Let the faithless come. We will kill them, and the Undying One will approve."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard strokes his beard for a few seconds before giving a hesitant reply:{/n} "Rediscovering the {g|Encyclopedia:AgriWorld}agri-world{/g} will supply your protectorate with something none of your servants can do without — sustenance. The importance of basic supplies should not be underestimated. Just look at {g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g} in its current pitiful state."
  - After: {n}Abelard muses.{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:AgriWorld}agri-world{/g} means food. Look at {g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g}'s sorry state."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "The Vox Master is entirely correct. You are Rogue Trader {name} von Valancius, the successor to Theodora von Valancius, one of the most influential women this side of the {g|Encyclopedia:Maw}Maw{/g}. But you are also new to the business of governing. Many will doubt your competence and try to carve up your protectorate so they can snatch a piece for themselves. It is important to show your potential allies and foes that you are in control of the situation. Which is why the sooner we reclaim these lost worlds, the better!"
  - After: "True. {name} von Valancius, Theodora's heir this side of the {g|Encyclopedia:Maw}Maw{/g}, is new. Rivals will circle. Reclaim these worlds soon!"

## World/Dialogs/Ch2_VS/VoidshipBridge/VoxMaster_dialogue/VoxMaster_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "How do you find life on the ship?"
  - After: "How is ship life?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell me about the lives of the voidborn in my crew."
  - After: "Tell me about my voidborn crew."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Thank you for your service, Mistress Toliman."
  - After: "Thank you, Mistress Toliman."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your appearance is unique. You are a voidborn, are you not?"
  - After: "You look unique. Voidborn?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Is this some kind of bad joke?"
  - After: "Is this a bad joke?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Connect me to the vessel's main channel. I wish to bolster the morale of my crew."
  - After: "Open the main channel. I'll rally the crew."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Bring me Jae Heydari. I have a question for her."
  - After: "Bring me Jae Heydari."
- **Player**
  - Before: "So... what did you make of the broadcast?"
  - After: "So... thoughts on the broadcast?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "There will be no further discussion of this incident. Forget everything you heard. I will receive the report and exile myself to Deck 18-Est. It seems to be the only place where I can find peace now."
  - After: "Forget this. Give me the report; I'll exile myself to Deck 18-Est."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Please tell me, why?"
  - After: "Why?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You crossed a dangerous line, Jae."
  - After: "You crossed a line, Jae."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Smile] "Jae, you... minx. You could have warned me."
  - After: [Smile] "You minx. You could've warned me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You do realise that this is not how we do things on my ship?"
  - After: "That's not how we do things here."

They won't need to whisper behind our backs once they know the truth. I enjoy being your companion and your lover, but I am not some embarrassing secret to be hidden away from so-called 'decent' people. I hope you take no issue with it, shereen."
  - After: {n}Jae turns serious.{/n} "Let them know their {mf|master|mistress} beds a smuggler and thief. I'm your lover, not a shameful secret, shereen."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A multitude of scout ships tirelessly explore the Expanse in search of new resource deposits, but unfortunately not all of them represent the interests of the von Valancius dynasty. I occasionally intercept vox-transmissions from ships prowling in your domain in search of easy loot. An asteroid the size of a small planet has been discovered in the Sotto's Tomb System, and the prospectors believe there may be a wealth of resources hidden under the crust."
  - After: "Raiders prowl your domain. In the Sotto's Tomb System, prospectors found a planet-sized asteroid likely rich in resources."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Vox Master's thin fingers dart between hundreds of wires and cables on the control panel. Flipping switches and turning dials, she issues commands and methodically checks the lines of communication with the crew on every deck. At last, accompanied by the sound of static, the crackling of the vox, and the flickering of signalling lights, the dance of her hands concludes.{/n}
  - After: {n}Her fingers dance over switches, testing every deck's vox-line.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And... the last item for today: a few pilgrims from Footfall who were graciously welcomed aboard have been filling the crew's minds with tales of a world of the ascended. They say that prayers on a world near the cold star Cinerus Maleficum have not ceased for several hundred years. They claim that the God-Emperor Himself chose this planet and raised all its people to His halls." {n}Vigdis coughs over the vox system's grinding.{/n} "We have suppressed these rumours to ensure that the crew are not distracted from their vital tasks. But perhaps you might decide to visit this planet, given its unusual reputation."
  - After: "Pilgrims aboard tell of a world near the cold star Cinerus Maleficum whose people the God-Emperor raised to His halls." {n}Vigdis coughs.{/n} "We've hushed it. You might visit."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I assume you heard my confessional message," {n}Vigdis replies, without a hint of awkwardness.{/n} "Do you wish to talk about it?"
  - After: "You heard my confession," {n}Vigdis says, unembarrassed.{/n} "Discuss it?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I was fault-checking the vox-devices in the ship's reliquary. Message recording works but deletion does not. You have helped me establish that. Thank you."
  - After: "Testing the reliquary's vox. Recording works; deletion doesn't. Thank you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "At that time, I had nothing to repent of, so I dictated an excerpt from an old letter to my mother. As you heard, it contained arguments in favour of keeping lop-eared kleppas on the ship. I can still recite it from memory."
  - After: "I read an old letter to my mother pleading for lop-eared kleppas."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am going to quote my mother's response: that is impossible. You see, the species went extinct several centuries ago." {n}Vigdis's voice grows ever so slightly warmer.{/n} "I am very sorry, Lord Captain. There aren't any kleppas to be had."
  - After: "As Mother replied: impossible. They're extinct." {n}Her voice warms.{/n} "Sorry, Lord Captain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am the ears and the voice of this voidship. I supervise several dozen officers and three times that number of support personnel. We receive, send, encrypt, and decode all incoming and outgoing messages through the ship's internal and external channels, and we also ensure clean communications and the optimal efficiency of the crew's vox-casters."
  - After: "I'm the ship's ears and voice. My staff handle all messages, encryption and the crew's vox-casters."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Will do, Lord Captain! Would you like to discuss other matters?"
  - After: "Will do! Anything else?"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Wait." {n}Kibellah's gaze, thoughtful until now, suddenly clears.{/n} "So it wasn't a common practice? I assumed it was a traditional ritual of the upper decks. Although I had my doubts."
  - After: "Wait." {n}Kibellah blinks.{/n} "That's not an upper-deck ritual?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Perhaps these are matters of long ago, of which only my predecessor or a past Seneschal could have known apart from Lady Theodora herself. But my grandfather never mentioned any such thing, and I never met the old Seneschal."
  - After: "Only my predecessor or the old Seneschal might know. My grandfather never said, and I never met that Seneschal."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I will relay your orders immediately, Lord Captain."
  - After: "Relaying your orders now."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "All finished, Lord Captain. No issues detected. The system is working as expected." {n}She studies your face as she awaits your response.{/n}
  - After: "Done. System works." {n}She watches your face.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I live to serve, Lord Captain."
  - After: "I live to serve."

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/Arena/Argenta_AfterFirstFight/Argenta_AfterFirstFight_dialogue

  - After: "Control yourself! Avenge him another day!"

  - After: [Look for a long-range weapon]
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}You follow Argenta's gaze to the soaring Drukhari craft and the squirming bodies nailed to its side.{/n} "That's... That's Sergeant Vigastes! I recognise him, I know his voice! {name}, help me! We have to save these people from this torture!"
  - After: {n}Bodies are nailed to a Drukhari craft.{/n} "That's Sergeant Vigastes! {name}, help me save them!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}By some miracle, Sergeant Vigastes is still alive. His sides and forearms are impaled on the crooked spikes that cover the side of the craft but his vital organs are intact: the Drukhari know how to prolong their victims' suffering. The rest of these people are not as fortunate. Some have nearly bled out, while others succumbed to the rough impact.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sergeant Vigastes lives, impaled. The others are dead.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Those are the words of the powerless! I must... I have to free him from this torment! There has to be a way!"
  - After: "Powerless words! I must free him!"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta does not hesitate for longer than a second before she raises her weapon and fires. The figure flinches and goes limp.{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta fires. The figure goes limp.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "There has to be a way! We can't... I can't simply stand here and watch!"
  - After: "There must be a way! I can't watch!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A shot rings out — and the figure pinned to the side of the ship flinches and stills.{/n}
  - After: {n}A shot. The figure stills.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A shot rings out but your target is still alive, his cries drowning in the roar of the ship's engines.{/n}
  - After: {n}You miss. He keeps screaming.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta freezes and then turns to face you. Her eyes are brimming with rage, astonishment, and unending sorrow. Her face momentarily twists into a grimace but then she drops her head and begins whispering words of prayer.{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta glares in grief and rage, then prays.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "No!" {n}Her voice becomes a piercing cry.{/n} "Not like this!"
  - After: "No!" {n}She screams.{/n} "Not like this!"
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Exalted be His name, hallowed be His sacrifice, honoured be His teachings..." {n}Argenta mutters the prayer through gritted teeth, her fists clenched in anger.{/n} "Commorragh will drown in blood... I swear it..."
  - After: "Exalted be His name..." {n}She seethes.{/n} "Commorragh will drown in blood. I swear it."
- **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "Groxshit!" {n}Jae chokes.{/n} "They nearly grabbed me too. Would I have...?"

  - After: {n}Argenta frees the sergeant, pressing his wounds.{/n} "Thank you, {name}."

  - Before: {n}Among the ravaged remains strewn all over the arena, you notice a severed arm lying not far from you. Its stiff fingers are clutching a pistol. With a crunch, you release the weapon from the death grip and claim it for yourself.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/Arena/ComissarFaith/ComissarFaith_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "With me, quickly! Into the portal!"
  - After: "With me! Into the portal!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Emperor will acknowledge your sacrifice, Commissar."
  - After: "The Emperor will honour your sacrifice."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I said fall back! That's an order!"
  - After: "Fall back! That's an order!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Commissar, towering fearlessly over the carnage, is barking orders to the fighters while simultaneously raining fire with his pistol. He sees you, turns his head, and shouts, still firing,{/n} "Not a good time, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Go, we'll cover you!"
  - After: {n}The Commissar fires, barking orders.{/n} "Not now, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Go, we'll cover you!"
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "So... much... gold..." {n}Cassia stares admiringly at the fighters, as if she is not looking at a massacre but at a liturgy.{/n} "It is as if His light had broken through the darkness of this place, dispelling the gloom in the hearts of these men. Oh, how I have missed the steadfastness of these colours."
  - After: "So much gold..." {n}Cassia gazes, rapt.{/n} "His light in this darkness. How I've missed it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Out of the question. We must hold our ground. It is an order we have given to ourselves. Everyone wants to make those scum pay for all the loss and pain they've suffered. And I'm making myself pay for being the scum that I was. Maybe the Emperor will take pity on me if I at least die a decent man. And you should get out of here, or our heroism will be for nothing! At least one person should truly escape from this pit of despair."
  - After: "No. We hold to make the scum pay, and I pay for the scum I was. Go, or this is for nothing!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thanks, but you can keep that luck to yourself. After all, we have the Emperor with us!" {n}With a parting wink, the Commissar turns back to his troops and bellows,{/n} "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ArenaFaithEnding}For the Emperor{/d}!"
  - After: "Keep your luck. We have the Emperor!" {n}He winks and bellows,{/n} "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ArenaFaithEnding}For the Emperor{/d}!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Just doing my duty as a disciplinary officer of the Imperium. Save yourself!" {n}With a parting wink, the Commissar turns back to his troops and bellows,{/n} "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ArenaFaithEnding}For the Emperor{/d}!"
  - After: "Just my duty, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Go!" {n}He winks and bellows,{/n} "{d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ArenaFaithEnding}For the Emperor{/d}!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It's too bad I'm not a real Commissar who would comply! No. We're staying. The Emperor has no love for cowards. If it makes it easier for you, consider it just another one of my lies, out of force of habit. That's me, a scoundrel to the end."
  - After: "A real Commissar might obey. We stay; the Emperor hates cowards. Call it my last lie."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah stares at the Commissar, her eyes wide with surprise.{/n} "You have returned to the faith, ready to welcome death... For such a thing to happen... in such a damned place..." {n}She grits her teeth and raises her chin.{/n} "Go and bathe in the blood of the Undying One's foes. May He accept your reborn soul into His hands."
  - After: {n}Kibellah stares.{/n} "Faith reborn, here..." {n}She lifts her chin.{/n} "Bathe in His foes' blood."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Lingering for a moment, Ulfar winks at the Commissar.{/n} "You are a fearless scoundrel. All right, you can have a line in my saga. Farewell and fight valiantly, so that the Allfather may hear the screams of your enemies."
  - After: {n}Ulfar winks.{/n} "Fearless scoundrel. You've earned a line in my saga."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}A furious line cuts across Solomorne's brow, but the wave of anger recedes before it can rise.{/n} "Whatever your past deeds, I admit that you are making an honourable choice now. I recognise your right to choose your own sentence — by the Lex Imperialis, may this act be taken into account when you face your final judgement."
  - After: {n}Solomorne's anger fades.{/n} "An honourable choice. May the Lex Imperialis weigh it at your judgement."
