  - After: "Careful, Marazhai, or Sinisthoria sends you against Khymerae again. Skinless."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The motionless Marazhai turns his head toward his kin, and you notice a thin red stripe on his neck below his ear, like a fresh stitch. Shaking with barely contained rage, the former Dracon stares at you with dark eyes.{/n}
  - After: {n}Marazhai, freshly stitched, glares, shaking with rage.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your unassailable arrogance makes the xenos's jaw drop for a moment. After a second, his expression changes to one of rage.{/n} "I will cut your smug throat and make you—"
  - After: {n}He gapes, then rages.{/n} "I'll cut your smug throat—"
- **Aebys**
  - Before: {n}Aebys frowns at the sound of the Elucidator and turns away from you dismissively, exchanging a few words with the Wych standing next to him. The mocking laughter and haughty looks in your direction leave no doubt about the subject of their conversation.{/n}
  - After: {n}Aebys turns away, mocking you to a Wych.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Despite the impotent rage on his face, Marazhai manages a sarcastic chuckle.{/n} "Something wriggling in your eye? I see Tervantias has not changed his methods for handling specimens."
  - After: {n}Marazhai chuckles.{/n} "Something in your eye? Tervantias hasn't changed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai gives you a predatory grin.{/n} "You think too highly of yourself, little beast. Pray you are killed in the arena before you know the caress of my blades."
  - After: {n}He grins.{/n} "Pray the arena kills you before my blades, little beast."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai looks at you again, now more surprised than enraged. Glancing at the Wyches, he switches to Low Gothic:{/n} "What, mon-keigh?"
  - After: {n}Surprised, he switches to Low Gothic:{/n} "What, mon-keigh?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Drukhari narrows his eyes.{/n} "Tervantias's creation must have been a low-grade imitation if the mirage did not completely overwhelm you... Even if what you say is true — what is it to you?"
  - After: {n}He squints.{/n} "A cheap mirage, then. What is it to you?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You? Help me?" {n}The Drukhari snorts disdainfully.{/n} "Why would the quarry help the hunter? If you expect me to believe that..."
  - After: "You? Help me?" {n}He snorts.{/n} "Quarry helping hunter?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai casts a contemptuous glance at the Wyches and without hesitation switches to Low Gothic:{/n} "This Wych Cult scum is not my kin. Half-borns like Aebys belong here in the filth of the Chasm—" {n}He cuts himself off, his gloves squeaking in protest as he clenches his fists.{/n}
  - After: {n}In Low Gothic:{/n} "Wych scum aren't kin. Half-borns like Aebys belong here—" {n}He clenches his fists.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Allies..." {n}Marazhai huffs a laugh.{/n} "Are you trying to convince me that you seek an alliance... with me?"
  - After: "Allies..." {n}He laughs.{/n} "With me?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai lifts his chin and lets out a hiss, more pensive than angry.{/n} "I—"
  - After: {n}Marazhai hisses, pensive.{/n} "I—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Mercy?" {n}Marazhai snorts, but a shadow of doubt flickers in his eyes.{/n} "How strange—"
  - After: "Mercy?" {n}He snorts, but doubt flickers.{/n} "How strange—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai allows himself a mocking chuckle, but you hear the ring of doubt in it.{/n} "What makes you think I intend to—"
  - After: {n}A doubtful chuckle.{/n} "What makes you think—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai clicks his tongue in irritation and rears back, but before he can respond, Aebys makes an impatient gesture.{/n}
  - After: {n}Marazhai bristles, but Aebys cuts in.{/n}
- **Aebys**
  - Before: {n}Aebys makes an impatient gesture.{/n} "I am tired of listening to you and your old friend whispering in that primitive babble. Enough. We must go."
  - After: {n}Aebys gestures impatiently.{/n} "Enough babble. We go."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai grudgingly obeys the order, but as he walks away, he cannot resist tossing another unreadable look in your direction.{/n}
  - After: {n}Marazhai obeys, glancing back.{/n}
- **Aebys**
  - Before: {n}The tall Drukhari, whose body is riddled with painful-looking puncture wounds and dotted with metal rings and clamps, lets out a chuckle as you approach and begins speaking in his own language. Your Elucidator hisses to life, translating the words:{/n} "Look, carrion... is this the mon-keigh that cost you your place at the Archon's side?"
  - After: {n}A pierced Drukhari chuckles. Your Elucidator translates:{/n} "Carrion, the mon-keigh who cost you the Archon's favour?"
- **Aebys**

  - After: {n}Aebys sours.{/n} "Come, proselytes. Training."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai's voice fills with venom:{/n} "Oh no, mon-keigh. I will live long enough to ensure such a death for you."
  - After: {n}Venomously:{/n} "No, mon-keigh. I'll live to give you that death."

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/Chasm/PitMeeting/PitMeeting_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "All I did was win another fight. What makes it so significant?"
  - After: "I just won another fight. Why does it matter?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have no orders to give. If you are true sons and daughters of Humanity, the Emperor will show you the way, not I."
  - After: "I have no orders. If you're true children of Humanity, the Emperor will guide you, not I."

  - Before: "Here are your orders: wait. I do not intend to die at the hands of xenos. Once I have destroyed them and found a way to escape, I shall return to take you with me."
  - After: "Your orders: wait. I won't die to xenos. Once I've destroyed them and found an escape, I'll return for you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Warriors of the Imperium! The God-Emperor's gaze is upon us, here and now. I am ready to meet my death face to face, for I know that He watches over me. What about you? Will you disgrace yourselves in His eyes? Or will you fight and prevail?"
  - After: "Warriors of the Imperium! The God-Emperor watches us now. I'll face death, knowing He watches over me. Will you disgrace yourselves before Him, or fight and prevail?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As soon as you walk in, the eyes of everyone in the room turn to you. The Commissar barks a command and the fighters salute you in perfect unison.{/n} "Glory to House von Valancius!"
  - After: {n}The fighters salute at the Commissar's bark.{/n} "Glory to House von Valancius!"

The Wyches won't let you emerge from your next fight alive. As true servants of the Imperium, we cannot let that happen. Awaiting your orders!" {n}His peaked cap gleaming, the Commissar clicks his boots loudly. The only sign that betrays his trepidation is the faint trembling of his hands.{/n}
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, your arena wins enraged the xenos. The Wyches will kill you next fight. Awaiting orders!" {n}The Commissar's hands tremble faintly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You hear confused exclamations, heavy sighs, and loud sobs. A dark wave of despair, powerlessness, and disappointment sweeps across the ranks of the resistance.{/n}
  - After: {n}Despair sweeps the resistance.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Commissar says in a lowered voice,{/n} "You wiped the floor with the Bloodstained Proselytes, the elite of the elite, in front of all of Commorragh. You didn't just spit in the faces of Keykeross and her chums, you publicly wounded the pride of every Drukhari who saw it happen. Pissing on a statue of Vect with everyone watching would've caused less of a stink. That's the Drukhari for you — they love their arenas." {n}The Commissar shrugs apologetically.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Commissar, quietly:{/n} "You crushed the Bloodstained Proselytes before all Commorragh, shaming Keykeross and every Drukhari. Pissing on Vect's statue would've stunk less." {n}He shrugs.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The people's expressions show different emotions: relief, doubt, disappointment. The members of the resistance start exchanging glances and whispering, until the Commissar silences them with a sharp command.{/n}
  - After: {n}Doubtful whispers, until the Commissar silences them.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The crowd's fierce and inspired roar deafens you. You see the glowing eyes of the people who have gathered here. This fire craves to be released so that it may consume any and all enemies of Humanity who dare to stand in the way of the Emperor's devout servants. As you observe the crowd, the Commissar's gaze jumps out at you. For the first time since you met him, his eyes are filled with {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ComissarRedeemed}genuine righteous fury, without a trace of falsehood or mockery{/d}.{/n}
  - After: {n}The crowd roars, eyes ablaze. The Commissar's eyes hold {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ComissarRedeemed}genuine righteous fury{/d}.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You can count on us, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Our best chance of gaining the upper hand is to hit them with a surprise attack. You are the {mf|man|woman} who triumphed over the Bloodstained Proselytes — it shouldn't be much of a challenge for you to last long enough in the arena until we can strike our enemy when they least expect it. Good luck to you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The Emperor protects!"
  - After: "Count on us, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Survive the arena, {mf|man|woman}, and we'll strike by surprise. Good luck, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The Emperor protects!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You dare doubt the words of a Rogue Trader, one anointed by the Emperor Himself? The {mf|man|woman} standing before you is willing to risk {mf|his|her} life against the superior forces of the detestable xenos so that we may have our long-awaited freedom! Pray to the Emperor that {mf|he|she} succeeds, for He protects the righteous!" {n}A deafening "The Emperor protects!" erupts in response, then the Commissar winks at you.{/n}
  - After: "You doubt the Emperor's anointed? This {mf|man|woman} risks {mf|his|her} life for our freedom! Pray {mf|he|she} succeeds!" {n}"The Emperor protects!" The Commissar winks.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He lowers his voice and says to you,{/n} "I'm going to put my faith in you too, you know. I have no idea how you plan on escaping or even surviving, but you've surprised me before on several occasions. I do hope this isn't some cruel joke to pay me back for my past... transgressions. It'd be a shame to have {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ComissarRedeemed}rediscovered my faith in the Emperor{/d} only to die in Commorragh. I mean, it would certainly be ironic: the old me would have loved it. Good luck!"
  - After: {n}He whispers,{/n} "I'm trusting you. Dying here after I {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ComissarRedeemed}rediscovered my faith in the Emperor{/d}? The old me would love the irony. Good luck!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Commissar uses just the right tone to stop the spreading chatter.{/n} "Fighters! Do not lose hope! Can't you see that the Rogue Trader's selfless sacrifice has spared our souls and given us more precious time to plan our escape? Or do you doubt the might of the Immortal Emperor? He won't forsake us! And neither will I forsake you! Take heart, for it is heresy to succumb to doubt. Dismissed!"
  - After: {n}The Commissar cuts in.{/n} "Fighters! The Rogue Trader's sacrifice buys us time! The Emperor won't forsake us, nor will I! Doubt is heresy. Dismissed!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He lowers his voice and says to you,{/n} "I see how it is. First you {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ComissarRedeemed}give me that inspirational crap{/d} about being a 'true leader' and escaping, and now it's everyone for themselves? I believed you, you know. Well, I won't hold it against you. I only have myself to blame for forgetting where I am. Say hello to the Emperor for me."
  - After: {n}He whispers,{/n} "So after {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ComissarRedeemed}that inspirational crap{/d}, it's everyone for themselves? I believed you. Say hello to the Emperor."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "I've seen you, you poisonous gnat, leading your comrades to their deaths in the arena. But now you are willing to stand with the Aett-Vater against all of Commorragh, to suffer what is certain to be a gruesome and agonising death? You are still an unworthy scoundrel, of course, but... you have chosen an honourable way out."
  - After: "I saw you, poisonous gnat, lead comrades to die in the arena. Now you'll stand with the Aett-Vater against all Commorragh? Still a scoundrel, but an honourable end."

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/Chasm/PitPascal/PitPascal_dialogue

- **Player**

  - Before: [Kill Pasqal] "You should have done this yourself."

  - Before: "That is no reason to back down. Do it!"

  - Before: "Then we must look for other options."
  - After: "Then we find other options."

  - Before: "You are a warrior of comprehension. Survive, then, and comprehend!"

  - After: "What happened after our capture?"

  - After: "If not lethal, leave the xenometal in for now."

  - Before: "You must be the one who decides what to do about the abhorrence inside you."

  - Before: "Now it is time to focus on regaining our freedom."

- **Player**
  - Before: "Is your faith in the Machine God so feeble that you would allow your body to harbour the taint of xenotech alongside the True Flesh?"
  - After: "Is your faith so feeble you'd let xenotech taint your True Flesh?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Would you reject knowledge simply because the thought of breaking one pathetic rule frightened you? Think of the possibilities: you could comprehend the technology of the xenos and use it against its creators!"
  - After: "Fear one rule? Comprehend xenos tech and turn it on its makers!"

- **Player**
  - Before: "Why did they remould you like that?"
  - After: "Why remould you?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The crooked figure wrapped in crimson looks nothing like the Pasqal Haneumann you know. Before, his silhouette, hunched though it may have been under the weight of his potentia coil, used to radiate authority and the power of restricted knowledge. Now he simply looks broken. His raiment is soiled with dark red bloodstains and black blotches of sacred unguents. His mechadendrites wriggle sluggishly like dying snakes.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal Haneumann, once authoritative, now looks broken and bloodied.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}At your command, Pasqal sinks his metal hand deep into the wound in his chest and clutches something. You hear a metallic creak... and then his fingers loosen powerlessly.{/n} "Request denied. This unit's motivational complex is weakened."
  - After: {n}Pasqal grips something in his chest wound, then goes limp.{/n} "Request denied. Motivation weakened."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal shakes his head in a surprisingly animated and human gesture for a servant of the Omnissiah who prefers pure Techna-Lingua to primitive body language.{/n} "Request denied. This unit is identified as an anathema. The situation requires... requires... resolution."
  - After: {n}Pasqal shakes his head.{/n} "Denied. This unit is anathema. It requires... resolution."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal does not look at you, for his gaze is focused inside his own body — there is a horrible gaping wound in his chest, and you see glinting, clanging mechanisms squirming within. Pasqal has plunged his fingers into the wide, dripping maw of the wound and is in the process of palpating his metal innards with great care.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal ignores you, probing the metal inside his gaping chest wound.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is difficult to say if the procedure that Pasqal has undergone was torture, sacred augmentation, or vivisection. His flesh is covered in fresh sutures interspersed with wounds that no one has taken the trouble to stitch up. An ordinary human would have long since bled out, but the Ferrum Sanctum sustains the bodies of the adepts of the Machine God. His metallic insides are exposed to the eye in all their vulgar and bloody nakedness.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sutures and open wounds cover him; only the Ferrum Sanctum keeps him alive.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Pasqal forces himself upright and says in a faltering voice,{/n} "This unit is ready to serve. Omnissiah have mercy on me."
  - After: {n}Pasqal forces himself up.{/n} "Ready to serve. Omnissiah have mercy."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal looks up at you. His skin has gone yellowish and clammy from the lubricant-like sweat, and there is something strange about the pupil of his left eye. You look closer and realise that its shape is no longer round — it is a tridecagon.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal looks up. His left pupil is now a tridecagon.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's knees buckle but there is steel ringing in his voice:{/n} "Cleansing process initiated. The process will be completed. This unit is ready to serve. Praise the Omnissiah!"
  - After: {n}His knees buckle.{/n} "Cleansing initiated. Ready to serve. Praise the Omnissiah!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Stubborn fury flares in Pasqal's gaze.{/n} "I am a warrior of Comprehension. And I will comprehend, whether I survive or not!"
  - After: {n}Fury flares.{/n} "I am a warrior of Comprehension. I will comprehend, survive or not!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The probability of total success is low due to expected premature cessation of vital functions." {n}There is no fear in Pasqal's voice. He is not trying to dissuade you, merely... informing you.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/Chasm/VigastisPit/VigastisPit_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I wish you luck, Sergeant."
  - After: "Good luck, Sergeant."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What matters is that you are alive and safe."
  - After: "You're alive and safe. That matters."
- **Player**
  - Before: "How did you end up in Commorragh?"
  - After: "How did you reach Commorragh?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "If you are nursing such a grudge against xenos, you are free to leave whenever you wish."
  - After: "Hate xenos? Leave whenever you wish."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Fear not, I will not allow what befell you and your people to ever happen again."
  - After: "I won't let this happen again."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Who tended to your injuries?"
  - After: "Who tended your injuries?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You survived. In Commorragh, that is no small feat. You should take some solace in that."
  - After: "You survived Commorragh. Take solace in that."
- **Player**
  - Before: "He will receive his due punishment, Sergeant. You can be certain of that."
  - After: "He will be punished, Sergeant."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why don't you kill the Commissar yourself? Lasguns can be used for purposes other than a makeshift crutch."
  - After: "Why not shoot the Commissar yourself? A lasgun isn't a crutch."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You have been avenged. The Commissar will not harm another soul ever again."
  - After: "You're avenged. The Commissar harms no one now."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell me about the Commissar's betrayal. How did you end up in the arena?"
  - After: "How did the Commissar betray you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "We are not in a position to pick our allies."
  - After: "We can't pick our allies."
- **Player**
  - Before: "When we get out of here, we will dress your wounds properly. The medicae facility on my ship is second to none."
  - After: "Once out, my ship's medicae will treat you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Leaning heavily on an astonishingly battered lasgun held together by a long history of field repairs and providence, Sergeant Vigastes glares daggers at the Commissar with clenched teeth. The sergeant himself looks much like his weapon: the horrible wounds on his arms and chest have been hastily stitched up and tightly wrapped in bandages soaked through with now dried blood.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sergeant Vigastes, bandaged and leaning on a battered lasgun, glares at the Commissar.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That bloody rotter. Now he's using me as a new symbol for his sham tales — a brave sergeant who escaped the xenos' clutches. The new guys stand there gawking, eating up every word, and all I can do is grit my teeth and think about how many people just like them... just like us... did the same and wound up butchered. I'll take {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_VigastisSaved}being impaled on stakes{/d} over this torture any day."
  - After: "That rotter parades me as his brave escapee, while new recruits march to slaughter. I'd take {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_VigastisSaved}the stakes{/d} over this."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "I swear to you, I knew not what I was condemning you to..."
  - After: "I swear, I didn't know..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}With a creak of his battered lasgun, Vigastes struggles to salute you.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: {n}Vigastes struggles to salute.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Sister, I'll be honest with you. When I was there, being skewered on spikes like a bug, I cursed your name too. More than once. But when you were pulling me off those spikes, one look at your face was enough to know that you'd been just as much a victim of that sick man's lies as the rest of us. I do not blame you."
  - After: "I cursed you on those spikes, Sister. But he lied to you too. I don't blame you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I served on a frigate, the Watchman of the Abyss. I got captured by a Drukhari boarding party. They took me to Commorragh and threw me aboard one of their gondolas bound for who knows where. With the last of my strength, I grabbed the pilot and jumped down into the Chasm. The xenos's body cushioned my fall, so, somehow, I survived. That's where the Commissar found me, before betraying me and sending me to die in the arena."
  - After: "Drukhari took me off the frigate Watchman of the Abyss. I leapt from their gondola into the Chasm, pilot and all. The Commissar found me, then sent me to the arena."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "'Allies' would be a generous choice of words, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. 'Enemies who haven't killed us yet' is a more fitting term in the world of Commorragh."
  - After: "Here, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, allies are just enemies who haven't killed you yet."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The only way to stop it from happening again is to destroy that traitor. He must answer for everything he has done."
  - After: "Then destroy that traitor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Sister Argenta offered me first aid, the rest was done by some rookie who barely knew how to stitch. The Commissar turned it into a show of him giving his last stimulant to save a hero of the Imperium. The scumbag." {n}Vigastes spits on the floor and immediately lets out a wet cough.{/n}
  - After: "Argenta and a rookie patched me up. The Commissar claimed he saved me. Scumbag." {n}Vigastes spits and coughs.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You and I must be very different people if you find solace in watching a scoundrel massacre desperate people in your stead."
  - After: "You find solace in a scoundrel massacring people? We differ."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vigastes summons all his strength to salute you with his hand before slumping back onto the support of his ramshackle lasgun.{/n} "I will scorn all my wounds just to give him what he deserves, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Just give the order. I beg of you."
  - After: {n}Vigastes salutes, swaying.{/n} "Give the order, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I beg you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In any case, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I'm grateful to you and Sister Argenta for saving my life. I hope one day to repay you for taking pity on a man who was as good as dead."
  - After: "Thank you and Sister Argenta for saving me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Just look at me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I have holes in my arms. My legs can't support my weight. If not for these wounds, that freak would already have a pretty new hole in his head. It's not the dying I'm afraid of, mind you — it's missing the mark."
  - After: "My arms are holed, my legs fail, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I don't fear dying, only missing."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A lone cripple won't last long in the Chasm. I don't intend to throw my life away after you have just saved it, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. At least here no one is trying to impale me on a stake or pour acid down my throat... yet."
  - After: "A cripple won't last alone in the Chasm, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Here nobody's impaling me. Yet."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Sister Argenta offered me first aid, and the rest was stitched up by one of these unholy maniacs. I suppose I should be glad he wasn't so hopped up on stimulants that he accidentally killed me in the process. That many-armed snake couldn't stop laughing. Whenever I screamed in pain, he told my 'chirurgeon' to slow down to prolong my suffering." {n}Vigastes spits on the floor and immediately lets out a wet cough.{/n}
  - After: "Argenta gave first aid, a maniac stitched me. That many-armed snake laughed at my screams." {n}Vigastes spits and coughs.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He chuckles mirthlessly.{/n} "When we get out, you say? I've heard that one before. That it's possible to escape this place. I believed it, and this is the result. Forgive me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but I can't seem to muster enough optimism right now."
  - After: {n}He chuckles mirthlessly.{/n} "I believed in escape once, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Look at me now."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Once he had found enough 'volunteers,' the Commissar sent me and the others on a special mission: to capture a ship for our escape. By an incredible stroke of luck, he got a hold of a portal that conveniently led straight to the docks. That creep. I still remember seeing the smug smile on his face as I entered the portal. As you may have figured, the portal didn't exactly lead to the vessel of our salvation. We were just cattle for his Drukhari cronies, and our misery and shock at having been betrayed was like a tasty snack for them. We fought back as best we could, but..." {n}The sergeant falls silent.{/n}
  - After: "He sent us through a portal to seize an escape ship. It led to his Drukhari cronies instead. We fought, but..." {n}He falls silent.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vigastes nods, leans on his battered lasgun, and goes back to glaring in the Commissar's direction.{/n}
  - After: {n}Vigastes nods and glares at the Commissar again.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Now I can die in peace. Except..." {n}Vigastes frowns as he looks at the caged Commissar.{/n} "If I may speak freely... Keeping him in a cage, like a xenos... Even a monster like him doesn't deserve to rot in this thrice-damned place. If it were up to me, I would execute him as a traitor and be done with it."
  - After: "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Except..." {n}He eyes the caged Commissar.{/n} "Caged like a xenos? I'd just execute the traitor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Leaning heavily on an astonishingly battered lasgun held together by a long history of field repairs and providence, Sergeant Vigastes stares in bewilderment at the Shriekers and Malice. The sergeant himself looks much like his weapon: the horrible wounds on his arms and chest have been hastily stitched up and tightly wrapped in bandages soaked through with now dried blood.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sergeant Vigastes, bandaged and leaning on a battered lasgun, stares at the Shriekers and Malice.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I never would've imagined that I'd {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_VigastisSaved}escape from the xenos{/d} who nearly disembowelled me only to take refuge in the den of different xenos who rub shoulders with heretics."
  - After: "I {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_VigastisSaved}escaped the xenos{/d} only to shelter with other xenos and heretics."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In any case, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I'm grateful to you and Sister Argenta for saving my life. I hope one day to repay you for taking pity on a man who was as good as dead. What warms my heart the most, though, is that the Commissar, that traitor, {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ComissarDead}got what he deserved{/d} and will not be sending any more desperate people to their deaths."
  - After: "Thank you and Sister Argenta, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. And that traitor {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ComissarDead}got what he deserved{/d}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Safe may be too strong a word, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, but it certainly feels good not to be dangling from stakes and hooks like a grox carcass. It looks like I'll get to serve the Emperor for another day or two." {n}Vigastes tries to chuckle, which makes him cough up blood instead.{/n}
  - After: "Better than hanging like a grox carcass, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}He laughs, coughing blood.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I don't know if he's a real Commissar or not, but he's an exceptional liar and sadist. His method was simple: find people on the streets of the Chasm, give them hope that there was a way out of this place, then recruit them to his 'resistance.' A few stirring speeches, food, shelter, a beat-up lasgun — that's all it took for us gullible simpletons to believe we could escape Commorragh."
  - After: "He's a liar and sadist. He promised Chasm strays escape and recruited them to his 'resistance.' We believed."

- **Jae**
  - Before: "Crude shmude!" {n}Jae casts you a desperate look.{/n} "{name}, it's not about how I look and talk right now. I need to see the Haemonculus! I absolutely must, got it? If you're so offended, I'll wash my mouth with soap, but later, shereen! Later!"
  - After: "Crude shmude!" {n}Jae is desperate.{/n} "{name}, I must see the Haemonculus! Later, shereen!"
- **Jae**
  - Before: "I... was in there, you understand?" {n}Jae breaks off and helplessly points at the entrance to the Haemonculus's chamber.{/n} "That's where he... cut me. The many-armed ashmag took away my breath! He started by cutting off my head, but I was alive and conscious. I hung from the wires and watched what he did to my body! He took out the implant, the throat, and the lungs, the whole thing! Then he grabbed a chunk of flesh, messed with it, sewed it into place... And everything came back!" {n}Jae is overcome by a hacking cough, flecks of blood on her hands when she draws them away from her mouth.{/n} "I'm dying, {name}! Dying again!"
  - After: {n}Jae points at the chamber.{/n} "He beheaded me, conscious, replaced my implant and lungs with grown flesh. It all came back!" {n}She coughs blood.{/n} "I'm dying again, {name}!"

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/Chasm/Wrack_ArenaFirstVisit/Wrack_ArenaFirstVisit_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Malice, what does it want and why is it calling the shots here?"
  - After: "Malice, why is it in charge?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What does this have to do with me?"
  - After: "How does this concern me?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "We didn't agree to this, Malice!"
  - After: "We didn't agree to this!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Nod] "I am ready."
  - After: [Nod] "Ready."
- **Player**
  - Before: "To the warp with you both! I am not going anywhere."
  - After: "To the warp with you! I stay."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Reach for your weapon] "Don't you even try forcing me, you scum!"
  - After: [Reach for your weapon] "Try forcing me, scum!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I came for the meat, Malice. Meat for the arena." {n}The rumbling voice of the creature stitched from flesh, pain, and fury echoes inside the black helmet.{/n}
  - After: "I came for arena meat, Malice." {n}The helmeted creature rumbles.{/n}
- **Malice**
  - Before: "And it is waiting for you. Shriekers, the sand is once again thirsting for your blood! Those of you who will give their lives to entertain our masters, know that I never cared. Those who will come back alive and in one piece will have as many stimulants as your pathetic bodies can handle." {n}Malice shifts his gaze to you and grins wickedly.{/n} "Give my best regards to the arena, fresh meat."
  - After: "Shriekers, to the sand! Survivors get stimulants." {n}Malice grins.{/n} "Enjoy it, fresh meat."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The booming voice that erupts from under the helmet is full of scorn and barely contained fury.{/n} "Bring your untransformed meat to heel, Malice, or it will not even make it to the pit."
  - After: {n}It booms.{/n} "Leash your meat, Malice."
- **Malice**
  - Before: "This is a servant of our lord Tervantias, the Haemonculus allied with the Reaving Tempest. This entire sector of the spire, the Chasm, is the domain bestowed upon him by the Kabal. This is where he harvests materials for his art... Screaming, pleading, panicked materials. And this is where he recruits gladiators for the arena."
  - After: "It serves Haemonculus Tervantias, Reaving Tempest's ally. The Chasm is his: he harvests screaming flesh and recruits gladiators here."
- **Malice**
  - Before: "Don't irk the servant of the esteemed Haemonculus, humanling. Follow him, do as he says, and once you find yourself in the pit, try to survive and entertain the masters."
  - After: "Don't irk it, humanling. Follow, survive, entertain."
- **Malice**
  - Before: {n}Malice looks visibly pleased when he says:{/n} "Now you are a Shrieker. Meat."
  - After: {n}Malice smiles.{/n} "You're a Shrieker now. Meat."
- **Malice**
  - Before: {n}Malice shrugs indifferently.{/n} "You don't say. Does that make me a scoundrel, then? A liar? I stand in awe of your perceptiveness."
  - After: {n}Malice shrugs.{/n} "A liar? How perceptive."
- **Malice**
  - Before: "How smart of you not to resist, humanling. Save your strength for the battle."
  - After: "Smart. Save your strength."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The monster points the muzzle of a device sticking straight out of the folds of its greyish flesh at your forehead. Its angry voice becomes uncharacteristically serene, almost normal.{/n} "Do not resist. It will only make things worse."
  - After: {n}It aims a flesh-grown muzzle at you, oddly calm.{/n} "Don't resist."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Move it. The masters wish to drink of your suffering."
  - After: "Move. The masters crave your suffering."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The monster snarls in frustration and points the muzzle of a device sticking straight out of the folds of its greyish flesh at your forehead.{/n} "I don't have time, meat."
  - After: {n}It snarls, aiming a flesh-grown muzzle at you.{/n} "No time, meat."

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/Chasm/ZanniAboutShow_dialogue/ZanniAboutShow_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "Yet another accursed xenos concealing its lies and treachery in florid riddles. Enough!"
  - After: [Attack] "Another xenos hiding treachery in riddles. Enough!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not understand what you want from me, xenos."
  - After: "What do you want from me, xenos?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Yrliet, one of your kind, lured me here. I wish to find her."
  - After: "Yrliet, an Aeldari, lured me here. I seek her."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you know where the Drukhari are holding the psyker Idira?"
  - After: "Where do the Drukhari hold the psyker Idira?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "My Navigator, Cassia, is missing. I doubt she will last very long here on her own."
  - After: "My Navigator, Cassia, is missing and won't last alone."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I wish to find my companion, Heinrix."
  - After: "I seek my companion, Heinrix."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I had a mercenary in my retinue. A bodyguard would be useful to me here."
  - After: "I need my mercenary bodyguard."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Before beginning a conversation with a Rogue Trader, xenos, it is customary to bow. I am waiting."
  - After: "Bow before a Rogue Trader, xenos. I'm waiting."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is this dance you are so intent on drawing me into?"
  - After: "What dance are you drawing me into?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have no intention of dancing to your tune or listening to this raving. Find yourself another toy."
  - After: "I won't dance to your raving. Find another toy."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am seeking a Genetor from my retinue, Eogunn Februs."
  - After: "I seek my Genetor, Eogunn Februs."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Forget your riddles for a moment. I am looking for my missing companions — do you know anything about their whereabouts?"
  - After: "Enough riddles. Where are my companions?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Everything is perfectly clear. There is a certain 'maestro of flesh' who conducts experiments on the bodies of others. He has a laboratory that can only be accessed by fighting in the arena to draw his attention. With his assistance, I will be able to escape the Chasm. Oh yes, and your name is Nocturne of Oblivion. Have I missed anything?"
  - After: "Clear enough. A 'maestro of flesh' experiments on bodies. Arena fights draw his notice and get me into his lab; he can get me out of the Chasm. And you're Nocturne of Oblivion. Anything missed?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am looking for my bodyguard, Kibellah."
  - After: "I seek my bodyguard, Kibellah."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I wish to find Pasqal, my Tech-Priest."
  - After: "I seek Pasqal, my Tech-Priest."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I shall endeavour to find the person of whom you speak."
  - After: "I'll find this person."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If you are unwilling to relieve me of your presence, at least spare me your senseless verbiage."
  - After: "If you won't leave, spare me the verbiage."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Let's go. We should not linger here."
  - After: "Let's go. We shouldn't linger."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The stranger standing before you brings to mind a motley-coloured, long-limbed doll abandoned amid carnage and detritus. The bright colours of his sleek costume seem comical against the unremitting gloom and hostility of this place. Only the sorrowful horned mask that hides his face and the dark hooded cloak he wears pay tribute to the overwhelming air of hopelessness. Every move the xenos makes sings with theatrical precision and a predator's grace. You cannot decide if this person is an accomplished dancer or a master assassin.{/n}
  - After: {n}A masked stranger in motley, graceful as a dancer or assassin.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This crib of putrid flesh offends your taste?
Oblivion comes now. Here its Nocturne plays.
I am that starlit strain that chills the soul,
The piece that doomed throngs pitches into dance.
You are among them, Merchant Vagabond.
So tread the steps I say, escape fate's grasp."
  - After: "Oblivion's Nocturne plays; the doomed dance.
Tread my steps, Merchant Vagabond."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You have never heard of such xenos before. What is he doing in the Chasm, and why is he standing before you now?{/n}
  - After: {n}You don't know this xenos. Why is he here?{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A melody of snarling agony,
Beguiling now, by rending flesh bewyched,
Through sinew, bone, and grisly pageantry,
It calls the blood-soaked drape to come unstitched.
A haggard chorus in the hall behind,
Their flesh employed to serve the maestro's art.
No prayer for mercy slips from throats confined,
The baton sets the beat of every heart."
  - After: "A chorus of agony in the hall behind,
Flesh serving the maestro's art."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Amidst the shadows dancing round us here
A crimson streak I spied by flesh consumed,
Malevolent, but not his own, I fear,
A vagrant languishing, alone and doomed."
  - After: "A crimson vagrant, flesh-consumed,
Lone and doomed."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet takes an involuntary step back, her face filled with fear.{/n} "Arebennian! Doom incarnate! Of all the places in the galaxy... you show yourself here!"
  - After: {n}Yrliet recoils.{/n} "Arebennian! Doom incarnate! Here!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Alas, my wants are neither here nor there...
But turn the question on yourself instead.
Pursue the melody, and find the key."
  - After: "Ask yourself instead.
Follow the melody; find the key."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Of glimpse and whisper dream the blind and deaf,
But you eschew them both for darkness mute.
I will not be a pest — I've said my piece."
  - After: "You choose darkness. I've said my piece."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To lose the Path, and then by touch again
Discover it — such is the Outcast's lot.
On parlous streets she treads a bloody trail
That leads her on through pain and wickedness."
  - After: "The Outcast gropes back to the Path,
Through blood and wickedness."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The one who mastered flesh's mysteries,
The soul's enigma is what plagues his mind.
All those who glint unnoticed by the rest
He now holds prisoner within his hall."
  - After: "The flesh-master craves the soul's enigma;
Those who glint unseen, he holds."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A dream to play, the maestro does declare,
His flesh now sings in chorus with the rest."
  - After: "The maestro's flesh now sings in his chorus."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your wait will test your patience and my own.
To pass the time, a sonnet I'll intone."
  - After: "Wait, then. I'll recite a sonnet."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The steps you know already, Vagabond.
A knife-edge minuet you must perform,
Between oblivion, foes, and your own friends.
So heed my sonnet well — it holds the key."
  - After: "A knife-edge dance, Vagabond,
Between oblivion, foes and friends.
My sonnet holds the key."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Merchant Vagabond rejects {mf|his|her} role?
But only curtain's fall will smash the chains
And fully break Commorragh's iron grip.
So heed my sonnet well — it holds the key."
  - After: "Reject {mf|his|her} role? Only curtain's fall
Breaks Commorragh's grip. My sonnet holds the key."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And entrails are for him an instrument,
And veins a living stave sans parallel,
Yet death to him is no impediment,
For corpses tunes do carry just as well.
Through spectacles of blood and gore forge past,
Should crave your eyes to glimpse sun's light at last."
  - After: "Entrails are his instruments.
Forge through gore to see the sun."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Perhaps when we stop to rest in a place of quiet, you will find time to hear me. But for now, we must go."
  - After: "Hear me later, somewhere quiet. Now, go."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You had already recognised this creature during the trial, but now, with the Drukhari poison purged from your body, your mind is clear.{/n}
  - After: {n}Poison purged, you recognise him from the trial.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The sage who dared to conquer death and time,
Now stands before its threshold, past his prime.
Within the halls of flesh, both crushed and spent,
Yet proud. Defeat he never shall consent."
  - After: "The sage who fought death nears its threshold,
Crushed, but too proud to yield."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Forge our path, elantach."
  - After: "Lead on, elantach."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Outcast and the Merchant — what a pair.
Bereft of blood and hope, without a path...
The parent cloaks the cradle once again,
And babe is doused in darkness as before.
But death is near, Asuryan's child — make haste."
  - After: "Outcast and Merchant, hopeless, pathless.
Death nears, Asuryan's child. Make haste."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A shiver runs down your spine. This is a Harlequin — the deadliest of all Aeldari warriors. You have heard of small Harlequin Troupes taking out entire armies of enemies, whirling in their mesmerising and terrifying dance of death.{/n}
  - After: {n}A Harlequin, deadliest of Aeldari, slayer of armies.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The xenos stills and looks at you intently. He is not accustomed to anyone so adroitly and quickly navigating his verbal labyrinths, that much is clear. At last, you hear a low chuckle behind his mask and the xenos claps his hands slowly, saying only one word:{/n} "Brav{mf|o|a}."
  - After: {n}Surprised, he claps slowly.{/n} "Brav{mf|o|a}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Whose life so dearly does the Merchant prize
To boldly now disrupt night's melody?"
  - After: "Whose life breaks night's melody?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Before you even finish speaking, the xenos is gone from view and you feel something cold and sharp pressed against the nape of your neck. The familiar lugubrious baritone sounds directly above your ear:{/n}
"You make yourself a fool by baiting me,
The one who knows ahead the players' moves.
Locate your wits, I say, and listen well."
{n}You blink, and the xenos is once again standing before you.{/n}
  - After: {n}He vanishes; a blade touches your nape.{/n}
"Bait one who knows every move? Listen well."
{n}He stands before you again.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}An indigo ripple passes over the xenos's body and he dissipates like a bad dream.{/n}
  - After: {n}An indigo ripple; he vanishes.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "{name}." {n}Normally unwavering, Yrliet stops in hesitation.{/n} "I promised that I would never again hide my soul behind a frozen wall of hubris and doubt. But this place... has too many eyes and ears to be sharing such thoughts."
  - After: "{name}." {n}Yrliet hesitates.{/n} "I vowed not to hide my soul. But too many ears listen."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Then go and dance. Do not forget the key."
  - After: "Then dance. Remember the key."

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/Chasm/ZanniBeforeThirdBattle_dialogue/ZanniBeforeThirdBattle_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Look at the chronometer] "Your timing is impeccable. You may leave now."
  - After: [Look at the chronometer] "Impeccable timing. Go."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Wait for a sign and run into the portal. Understood."
  - After: "Wait for a sign, run into the portal."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You have helped me more than once already. I am listening."
  - After: "You've helped before. I'm listening."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I shall deign to spare you one whole minute of my extremely valuable time. Do not waste it."
  - After: "You have one minute. Don't waste it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "One more word about roles, dances, or keys, and I will shoot you myself. Begone!"
  - After: "One more word of roles or keys and I'll shoot you. Begone!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What sign do you mean?"
  - After: "What sign?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "A mouth? What are you talking about?"
  - After: "A mouth? Meaning what?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "If I will be walking into a trap, why do you not simply extract me now?"
  - After: "If it's a trap, why not extract me now?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "If you wish to help me, why don't you finally demonstrate these exceptional skills of yours and aid me in battle?"
  - After: "Then show your skills and fight beside me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Wait for a sign and run into some kind of 'mouth.' Understood."
  - After: "Wait for a sign, run into some 'mouth.' Understood."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not know what I expected when I agreed to accept your help. You are talking in riddles. Again."
  - After: "Riddles again. Why did I accept your help?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "So, Keykeross is planning to kill me in the next fight, but you are ready to effect my escape. All I must do is survive the arena, wait for your sign, then run. You cannot possibly mean into a literal mouth, so you must mean for me to leap into a portal of some kind. Do I have that right?"
  - After: "So Keykeross plans to kill me, and you'll get me out. I survive the arena, await your sign, then leap into a portal. Right?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The already familiar baritone calls out to you from the shadows.{/n}
"The key unlocks a door that then will lead,
To one that only happenstance will free.
Your chance I'll be, to me the bolts will cede,
Your part comes next — to break the bonds and flee."
  - After: {n}The familiar baritone calls from the shadows.{/n}
"A key, a chance. Then break free and flee."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To you, the Merchant Vagabond, I bring
The gift of providence, but will you look?"
  - After: "Vagabond, I bring providence. Will you look?"
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "The portal. He means the portal to the arena."
  - After: "He means the arena portal."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I think the Arebennian is referring to the portal that takes us to the arena. Is he planning to do something to it?"
  - After: "He means the arena portal. Will he tamper with it?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The xenos's colours are like those of a broken kaleidoscope — your eyes water at the mere attempt to pick any one thing out, and your head is splitting more than ever. Yet despite this, you are subconsciously aware that the dark lilac cloud surrounding the slender figure poses unspeakable danger. And that the bright sparkles of silver indicate that this danger — at least, for now — is directed at you. When you avert your gaze and slowly exhale, the vision falls away as if it was never there.{/n}
  - After: {n}His colours hurt. A lilac cloud of danger surrounds him, aimed at you — for now.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Well, as you wish, this gift is not for all."
{n}The Harlequin vanishes in a cloud of blue smoke, leaving you with nothing but the feeling of unease before the coming battle.{/n}
  - After: "As you wish. This gift is not for all."
{n}He vanishes in blue smoke.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Both opening and warning is my boon,
Your fate hangs by a thread drawn breaking tight,
But with a show of patience opportune,
The Merchant certain death will turn to flight."
  - After: "Your fate hangs by a thread, but patience saves you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "'Tis wise indeed to count each moment past,
To nothingness they stream like grains of sand,
They steal your hours and days until at last
They turn to dust in reaper's wasted hand."
  - After: "Count your moments. They run like sand."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You stride not into battle but a snare,
Of guile and strife a neatly woven net,
Lust's mistress lifts her sword into the air
And baying for your blood her pack does set.
So dance a ring around oblivion,
Await a sign from night's own melody.
Catch sight of it, and then, make haste, begone!
One yawning mouth, one leap, to set you free."
  - After: "It's a snare; Lust's mistress hunts you.
Survive, await my sign, then leap into the mouth."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Poor show! The spice of life is mystery,
Too bland a spread would sour your appetite,
The sign of mine, fear not, you'll clearly see."
  - After: "Mystery is life's spice! You'll see my sign."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The greedy mouth that swallows brave and bold,
And after few releases from its hold,
The Vagabond this maw already knows,
Why, to your fights it marks the start and close."
  - After: "You know that mouth — it starts and ends your fights."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A lock that is not there cannot be picked,
And time alone will forge the key to it."
{n}The Harlequin shrugs as if his pronouncement makes perfect sense.{/n}
  - After: "No lock yet; time forges the key."
{n}He shrugs.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Harlequin laughs darkly as if you have uttered some naive inanity.{/n}
"In vain you grant compassion to the mask,
Though you and I play roles, desire has none.
Your part on stage — to break through barricades,
While mine's to chalk in darkness players' marks,
And lead the company to its finale."
  - After: {n}He laughs darkly.{/n}
"Your role: break barricades. Mine: lead the finale."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The xenos lays a finger over the mute lips of his mask and vanishes, as if to convey that your conversation is a great secret known only to the two of you.{/n}
  - After: {n}He hushes his mask's lips and vanishes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A wait, a sign, a mouth. Remember this."
  - After: "A wait, a sign, a mouth. Remember."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai is squirming with rage he does not dare to unleash on the Harlequin here and now. He hisses through clenched teeth,{/n} "All who have taken part in my downfall will be exterminated..."
  - After: {n}Marazhai hisses with suppressed rage,{/n} "All who ruined me will die..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "...and sooner than you thought, my Merchant thief!
Just like a drop of ink you fell upon
The page before this play's dramatic end,
Wherein your own kin's blood you will see shed.
Perform the lines required and vengeance will
Descend upon the stage and play its part.
And then away from spires on Merchant's trail,
Across the worlds a parlous road you'll tread,
And death you will find there, or else a path
To remedy your second enemy."
  - After: "...sooner than you think, thief!
Avenge yourself, then chase the Merchant across worlds
To death, or a cure for your second enemy."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai digests the Harlequin's words in silence. At last, a shadow of the usual smirk flashes on his face.{/n} "I... I hear you, Arebennian."
  - After: {n}Marazhai half-smirks.{/n} "I hear you, Arebennian."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "When the cursed jester says 'mouth,' he means the portal at the stadium. But where is the sense in that? It will just take us back to the Chasm!"
  - After: "His 'mouth' is the stadium portal. But that leads back to the Chasm!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Harlequin sweeps into a low bow, like an actor who has performed before a true lover of high art. He seems satisfied with your answer.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Harlequin bows low, satisfied.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The xenos means the portal that leads to and from the arena. But why would you return to the Chasm?{/n}
  - After: {n}He means the arena portal. But why return to the Chasm?{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The xenos's clarification is as vague as the rest of what he says.{/n}
  - After: {n}Still vague.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Sudden pain grips your skull and your vision clouds over. But as soon as you resurface, a dramatic scene appears before you — the streets of the Dark City are teeming with hundreds of colours, from grimy grey shades to extravagantly bold hues. At first they blend together in your vision, but soon you are able to distinguish their sources. People, xenos, animals, you... and, of course, the Harlequin standing in front of you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pain grips your skull. Then everyone blazes with colours — you, and the Harlequin.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Harlequin observes you with interest, his silence speaking volumes.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Harlequin watches silently.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "{name}, your colours! What... what have you done to {mf|him|her}, xenos?" {n}Cassia lifts her chin and the third eye on her forehead flutters threateningly behind the eyelid.{/n}
  - After: "{name}, your colours! What did you do to {mf|him|her}, xenos?" {n}Cassia's third eye flutters.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}At the sight of Marazhai, the Harlequin lets out a nasty chuckle:{/n}
"The trapper caught in snares of his own make!
The plotting of your play was up to snuff,
But Nazrakhei rewrote the denouement
Decided in the darkness of the wings.
Amidst the sombre spires and hunter's game,
'Tis wise to stop and once more check your knives—
For that which glittered in your hand before
You may now find a-twinkling in your back."

"The trapper trapped!
Nazrakhei rewrote your ending.
Check your knives — yours may be in your back."

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/CommorraghStreets/DrukhariPartyHosts

- **Player**
  - Before: [Turn to the growling giant] "And just who are you?"
  - After: [Turn to the growling giant] "Who are you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Enough of this nonsense. I came here for a purpose, not to give myself over to your deplorable delights."
  - After: "Enough. I'm here on business, not for your delights."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Wink] "Oh, yes, that is exactly why I am here. For enjoyment."
  - After: [Wink] "Yes, I'm here for fun."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Why?" {n}The fangs in Ulfar's mouth — or rather, his muzzle — appear to have grown larger. His distorted expression strikes you as odd: all his emotions have melted away, leaving behind nothing but predatory indifference.{/n}
  - After: "Why?" {n}Ulfar's fangs have grown; his face is predatory and blank.{/n}
- **Ulfar**

  - After: "A mocking xenos fled into a portal. Where is he? I'll eat his liver!"
- **Envoy of the Wounded Skies**
  - Before: "Let us feast, then. Don't be scared, mon-keigh, you won't die too soon. I intend to savour every moment."
  - After: "Let us feast, mon-keigh. I'll savour every moment."

  - After: "Sing your tale while I pull your nerves out. Slowly."
- **Ulfar**

  - After: {n}He looks down.{/n} "I am Ulfar, Space Wolf of the Allfather."

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/CommorraghStreets/DrukhariPartyHosts/DrukhariPartyHosts

- **Player**
  - Before: [Make an imperious gesture] "Now, to the purpose of my visit. The Reaving Tempest has decided that the Kabal that survives the celebration will be allowed to become their ally. One Kabal. Not two."
  - After: [Gesture imperiously] "The Reaving Tempest will ally with whichever Kabal survives. One, not two."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Ulfar, I wish to speak to them before you... do what you intend to do."
  - After: "Ulfar, let me talk to them first."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Smile] "So, which one of you is worthy of getting the first taste of my pain and which one will have to settle for scraps?"
  - After: [Smile] "Which of you gets first taste of my pain?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not wish to ruin your celebration with bloodshed, nor do I have any interest in you. Let us part in peace."
  - After: "I want no bloodshed. Let us part in peace."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Shut up, you inhuman degenerates!"
  - After: "Shut up, degenerates!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do either of you know what I am doing here?"
  - After: "Do you know why I'm here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address Ulfar in a silken voice] "Even if you are being manipulated wherever you go, is slaying xenos truly such a terrible fate? An eternity of killing them, one after another, and another, and another..."
  - After: [Silkily, to Ulfar] "Even manipulated, is slaying xenos forever so terrible? One after another..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "And who is your 'old plaything'?"
  - After: "Who is your 'old plaything'?"
- **Envoy of the Poisonous Whisper**
  - Before: {n}The elegant red-haired xenos takes a sip of her wine-like liquid and gives you an appraising and somewhat surprised look, then smiles and says to the xenos standing next to her,{/n} "What's this? New playthings, no doubt. And here I thought the Reaving Tempest was intending to offer up your paltry Kabal for our entertainment."
  - After: {n}The red-haired xenos smiles.{/n} "New playthings? I thought they'd offer up your paltry Kabal."
- **Envoy of the Wounded Skies**
  - Before: {n}The tattoo-covered Drukhari she is addressing, who is absent-mindedly sticking serrated needles into his own gums, scoffs in response.{/n} "The Poisonous Whisper should learn to live up to their name. Lest the Kabal of the Wounded Skies live up to theirs and make you bleed upon the Dark City, you sharp-tongued pest."
  - After: {n}The tattooed Drukhari scoffs.{/n} "Careful, Poisonous Whisper, or the Wounded Skies will bleed you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The symbols on their armour are different, indicating that these two belong to two different Kabals. If their venomous glares and thin smiles are anything to go by, they are ready to go for each other's throats at any moment.{/n}
  - After: {n}Two rival Kabals, ready to kill each other.{/n}
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai turns his head, looking around the room and grinning in fiendish delight.{/n} "This is one of the satellite towers of the main spire of the Reaving Tempest... What luck! Yremeryss's throat is now that much closer to my claws... But first I have to deal with my sister's pathetic guests."
  - After: {n}Marazhai grins.{/n} "A Reaving Tempest tower! Yremeryss is close. But first, my sister's guests."
- **Envoy of the Poisonous Whisper**
  - Before: {n}The red-haired xenos licks her lips.{/n} "There is enough suffering in you to satisfy everyone. All it takes is the right approach."
  - After: {n}She licks her lips.{/n} "Pain enough for all."
- **Envoy of the Wounded Skies**
  - Before: "The Kabal of the Poisonous Whisper may be feeble and few in number but inflicting pain is a talent you possess. I will allow you to make the first cut."
  - After: "Feeble Kabal, but skilled torturers. Cut first."
- **Envoy of the Wounded Skies**
  - Before: "You belong to the Wounded Skies. I will help you remember the name by burning it into your eyeballs."
  - After: "You belong to the Wounded Skies. I'll burn it into your eyes."
- **Envoy of the Poisonous Whisper**
  - Before: "The Wounded Skies are always so hasty and so eager to rush ahead, they fail to notice the daggers being shoved into their backs by more worthy aspirants who are offended by their witlessness." {n}The red-haired xenos gracefully places a hand on her weapon and the male Drukhari mirrors her gesture.{/n}
  - After: "The hasty Skies never notice daggers in their backs." {n}Both reach for weapons.{/n}
- **Envoy of the Poisonous Whisper**
  - Before: "I will give you no explanation, mon-keigh. Perhaps you have angered fate and the gods for them to have pushed you to such a miserable end."
  - After: "No explanations, mon-keigh. Fate must hate you."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "I've had enough talking with xenos. Their words are thick with lies. Once you let them touch your ears, you become a puppet pulled by their strings! We will put them all to death in a whirling bloodstorm — that will be a deed to honour the Allfather!"
  - After: "Enough talk! Xenos words make puppets. Kill them all, for the Allfather!"
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Words, words, poisoned words everywhere!" {n}Ulfar bares his teeth and his expression darkens.{/n} "I am so sick of you puny inhumans who know not of honest battle, steeped in the mire of your own intrigue. You have dragged me into that same mire with you. Is this proud warrior destined to wander your wretched lair forevermore, slaying xenos for other xenos' amusement?" {n}His voice changes, taking on guttural notes and sounding far from human. There is no sign of jovial rage left — only a grim thirst for blood.{/n}
  - After: "Poisoned words everywhere!" {n}Ulfar bares his teeth.{/n} "Must I slay xenos forever for xenos' amusement?" {n}His voice turns bestial, bloodthirsty.{/n}
- **Envoy of the Wounded Skies**
  - Before: "Ooh, I like this one. I want to cut the tendons in his every limb and watch him burn in the fires of his powerless frenzy."
  - After: "Ooh, I'll cut his tendons and watch him rage."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I expected something like this. At least we are no longer in the arena — there are far fewer xenos here capable of opposing us."
  - After: "Expected. Fewer foes than the arena, at least."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "A Farseer... Yremeryss had the temerity to bring a Farseer to Commorragh, only to feed it to some scum from the Dark City's gutters?"
  - After: "Yremeryss fed a Farseer to gutter scum?"
- **Envoy of the Poisonous Whisper**
  - Before: "A mon-keigh serving as a messenger of the Reaving Tempest? Preposterous!"
  - After: "A mon-keigh messenger? Preposterous!"
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "I see you have not wasted your time in the Dark City, and you have properly studied our... way of thinking." {n}Smirking contentedly, Marazhai places his hands on his blade grips.{/n}
  - After: "You've learned our ways." {n}Marazhai smirks, gripping his blades.{/n}
- **Envoy of the Wounded Skies**
  - Before: "It would be an outrageous stunt... An extravagant one... But not impossible. Whether or not the mon-keigh lies, the Wounded Skies desire to ally themselves with the Reaving Tempest. And achieving it will be easier if the Poisonous Whisper dies here!" {n}The two xenos simultaneously go for their weapons.{/n}
  - After: "Possible. Either way, the Skies want that alliance — so the Whisper dies!" {n}Both draw.{/n}
- **Envoy of the Poisonous Whisper**
  - Before: "You are most entertaining, mon-keigh. How can bloodshed ruin a celebration?"
  - After: "How can bloodshed ruin a celebration?"
- **Envoy of the Wounded Skies**
  - Before: "Step aside, Poisonous Whisper! I will have the first meal!"
  - After: "Step aside, Whisper! First meal is mine!"
- **Envoy of the Poisonous Whisper**
  - Before: "The outer halls of the Spire of the Reaving Tempest. The esteemed Kabal invited us to indulge in a small celebration. The Poisonous Whisper came as their desired allies. As for the Wounded Skies... I have no clue why one would invite them."
  - After: "The Reaving Tempest's Spire. They invited us, the Poisonous Whisper, as allies. Not sure why the Skies came."
- **Envoy of the Wounded Skies**
  - Before: "It fascinates me how pathetic and transparent the intrigue of their lesser kind can be. However, I have grown weary of this one's tales. I wish to taste {mf|his|her} anguish."
  - After: "Transparent intrigue. I want {mf|his|her} anguish."
- **Envoy of the Wounded Skies**
  - Before: {n}The xenos casually points at the writhing figure.{/n} "This knowledge is far beyond you, but I see no harm in humouring a soon-to-be corpse. This one is an exquisite delight: a Farseer. Nothing can compare to their heightened psychic emanations. Most delectable."
  - After: {n}He points at the writhing figure.{/n} "A Farseer. Their psychic pain is delectable."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}A bestial growl comes from behind you.{/n} "Did the jester bring me here to listen to these dung-ridden beasts practise their meagre wits? These blathering xenos are making me angrrry... I'll kill them."
  - After: {n}A growl behind you.{/n} "Prattling beasts! Angrrry... I'll kill them."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar lets out a ferocious roar and his eyes become bloodshot. Spraying spittle like a raging beast, he bellows mournfully,{/n} "I don't want your eternity! How can I claim the glory of a warrior's death if I am forever to trudge through honourless battles, to know of no taste but that of the putrid blood of inhumans spilt at their own behest?"
  - After: {n}Ulfar roars, bloodshot.{/n} "I don't want your eternity! Where's a warrior's death in honourless fights?"
- **Idira**
  - Before: "No... no no no... we were supposed to escape! What is this place? Are we the main course at this shindig?"
  - After: "No no no... we escaped! Are we the main course?"
- **Envoy of the Wounded Skies**
  - Before: "You insolent mon-keigh! I will cut pieces out of your liver one by one and feed them to you as I relish your screams. Believe me, I intend to savour every moment!"
  - After: "Insolent mon-keigh! I'll feed you your liver!"
- **Envoy of the Poisonous Whisper**
  - Before: {n}The red-haired Drukhari smiles faintly.{/n} "Let's see if you can make the savouring last longer than a handful of moments this time..."
  - After: {n}She smiles faintly.{/n} "Make it last this time..."
- **Envoy of the Wounded Skies**
  - Before: "That's enough out of you. This habit of talking to pets is ridiculous. It is time we toyed with {mf|him|her} instead: the old plaything is nearly spent and its pain has grown stale."
  - After: "Enough chat. Let's play with {mf|him|her} — the old plaything is spent."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You can sense the despair and the blind rage boiling inside Ulfar's chest. They are trying to gnaw their way out and you know the exact words that will drive them down the shortest path. This knowledge delights you.{/n}
  - After: {n}You sense Ulfar's rage, and the words to unleash it. This delights you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is hard to tell whether these two xenos are trading insults out of genuine enmity or merely as a result of their foul temperament so typical of inhumans.{/n}
  - After: {n}Real enmity or xenos spite? Hard to say.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/CommorraghStreets/DrukhariRaiders/DrukhariRaiders

  - After: "Take me to the top of the Reaving Tempest's Spire."

  - Before: [Shoot one pilot and address the other] "Is your answer the same?"

  - Before: "I killed all of your little friends inside. Would you like to join them?"

  - Before: "Everyone inside is dead. If you take me where I need to go quickly, you will make it back in time to loot the bodies."
  - After: "They're all dead. Take me fast and loot the bodies."

  - After: [Kill them both] "You're surplus."

They could have taken us with them, but no, they had to make us play guards instead. Greedy filthspawn... Look at this! I think a few playthings have slipped away from the festivities!"

A lobotomy to excise certain parts of the temporal lobes, cauterise the prefrontal cortex, and extend a direct electrode bridge to their somatosensory cortex... A surgery of this kind, if performed without the necessary equipment, will be excruciating, but useful and informative."

  - Before: {n}You take a glance at the xenos boat. Sure, its design and certain parts appear bizarre but you can still guess their purpose. You could probably steer it.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You take a glance at the xenos boat. The design looks utterly foreign to you. You have a vague idea what some of its parts might do but you do not even want to attempt to guess at the intended purpose of the rest. You need a pilot.{/n}
