## World/Dialogs/Ch3/CommorraghStreets/UlfarWhatTheHell

- **Player**
  - Before: "The Harlequin brought me here. Do you have any idea why he did that?"
  - After: "The Harlequin brought me here. Any idea why?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Surely you won't say no to an opportunity to kill a few xenos together, will you?"
  - After: "Surely you'd like to kill some xenos together?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I intend to get out of this place. And I can take you with me."
  - After: "I'm getting out of here. Come with me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "From what I understand, you have been surviving on your own for a terribly long time. Aren't you tired of being alone?"
  - After: "You've survived alone so long. Aren't you tired of it?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Forget what I said. It was a pleasure to make your acquaintance."
  - After: "Forget it. A pleasure to meet you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar gives you a doubtful look but says nothing.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ulfar looks doubtful.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}With a growl instead of a farewell, Ulfar turns around and walks off in search of new prey.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ulfar growls and leaves.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A faint but mirthful smile appears on his gloomy face.{/n} "Kill a few xenos? I would never say no to that."
  - After: {n}He smiles.{/n} "Never say no to that."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Maybe you will succeed. Or maybe you will meet a glorious end. Whatever happens, I want to be at your side at that moment. I'm in."
  - After: "Win or die gloriously, I'm with you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He gives you a long, pensive look before he says,{/n} "You do not even know what it is you speak of, mortal. I will tell you about being alone sometime. Once we are out of here."
  - After: {n}A long look.{/n} "You know nothing of it. I'll tell you once we're out."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I know nothing of his reasons. Here is my advice to you: do not try to peer into a xenos's thoughts. They are too perverse for a sound mind to comprehend. You would only risk catching that blight of degeneracy yourself."
  - After: "No idea. Don't read xenos minds — their perversion spreads."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai stares at him in disgust.{/n} "Blight of degeneracy, you say? Those words aptly encompass both the tragedy and the comedy of your kind's existence."
  - After: {n}Marazhai sneers.{/n} "Degeneracy? Your kind's tragicomedy exactly."

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/CommorraghStreets/UlfarWhatTheHell/UlfarWhatTheHell_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Stop. All your foes are dead. I am your comrade."
  - After: "Stop. Foes are dead. I'm your comrade."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What just happened to you?"
  - After: "What happened to you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What kind of grief must it be, to have nearly cost you your sanity?"
  - After: "What grief nearly broke your mind?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You have people to fight for. People who need you as you are: a warrior, not a beast."
  - After: "People need a warrior, not a beast."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You have a duty to kill the Emperor's enemies, not whomever you please."
  - After: "Kill the Emperor's enemies, not whoever you please."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If that is your nature, you should embrace it. Even blind destruction can serve a purpose, can't it?"
  - After: "Embrace your nature. Destruction has uses."
- **Player**
  - Before: "We are no longer on the same path. I do not trust you."
  - After: "Our paths part. I don't trust you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I suggest we go and see why Nocturne of Oblivion has dragged us to this place."
  - After: "Let's see why Nocturne of Oblivion brought us here."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You mad beast! You have killed everyone who could have told us anything!"
  - After: "Mad beast! You killed every witness!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Aim your weapon] "Stand down! Or you will fall right next to this scum."
  - After: [Aim your weapon] "Stand down, or fall with them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You are staring into the eyes of an animal that enjoys killing. No, it does not enjoy it. It just kills, finding no joy or delight in doing so. It kills because that is its nature.{/n}
  - After: {n}An animal that kills joylessly, by nature.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar shakes his head morosely.{/n} "It was not devotion to the Allfather that guided my hand. Only the black malice of Wulfen."
  - After: {n}Ulfar shakes his head.{/n} "Not the Allfather. Wulfen's malice."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar rumbles grimly,{/n} "Mortal, if you were to know of the bitter taste of Wulfen's malice, you would learn that grief takes no prisoners. Grief claims lives."
  - After: {n}Ulfar rumbles,{/n} "Wulfen's malice is grief. It claims lives."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Comrade..." {n}This word has a miraculous effect on the bloodthirsty warrior.{/n}
  - After: "Comrade..." {n}The word calms him.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Like a bolter shot, your commanding cry pierces the shield of bloodthirsty indifference on the giant's face.{/n} "I hear... and... obey..."
  - After: {n}Your command pierces his bloodlust.{/n} "I hear... and... obey..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is the breath of the frost that chills the bones. It is lightless malice born of despair. The curse that preys upon them who have seen too many things and hate with too much heart."
  - After: "Frost in the bones. Despair's malice, cursing the hateful."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Too long have I been here. Too long have I served as a tool of unrighteous wretches — a shameful fate for the Allfather's warrior, and shame is what scorches my soul. When I saw that I had once again become their plaything, that yet another xenos had set me upon his foes... I thought it would go on forever. My mind could not accept the indignity of it, so my mind hid like a coward would. Only thirst remained."
  - After: "Too long a xenos tool — it shames me. Set upon yet another's foes, I thought it endless. My mind fled. Only thirst remained."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Allfather. Russ. My brothers. I belong to them. I am their blade. And this blade will never break."
  - After: "The Allfather. Russ. My brothers. I am their unbreakable blade."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And so I will. No one will say that Ulfar was a craven who could not walk the bloody path laid out for him. That a single foe meant to fall at Ulfar's hand escaped their doom because Ulfar wavered."
  - After: "I will. Ulfar is no craven who lets doomed foes escape."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The hour will come, and the Curse of the Wulfen will have me. And that hour approaches. I can hear the crunch of snow beneath claws. But it has not arrived yet."
  - After: "The Wulfen Curse approaches. Not yet."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I... understand. Farewell, {name}. May you find your escape from this poisonous nest. But my soul has been trapped here for so long it has put down roots. I will go and kill someone who deserves it."
  - After: "Farewell, {name}. Escape this nest; I'm rooted here. I'll kill someone deserving."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes. Where is that slippery wretch? Let me have a word with him."
  - After: "Yes. Where's that wretch?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}From beneath the veneer of bloodthirsty indifference, something resembling a living emotion surfaces on the giant's face. You hear words breaking through the wall of bared teeth:{/n} "For... the... Allfather..."
  - After: {n}Emotion surfaces.{/n} "For... the... Allfather..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The malice of Wulfen beset my heart. And nearly consumed it forevermore."
  - After: "Wulfen's malice nearly consumed me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar's bristling fiery hair lies flat once more and the imprint of death vanishes from his gaze. The face of a wild beast gives way to a grimace of weariness, grief, and... shame.{/n}
  - After: {n}His fury fades into weariness, grief, shame.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Blind destruction. No thoughts. No regrets. No purpose. To be a beast, not a human. A sweet temptation for a lone wolf."
  - After: "No thought, no regret. A beast's sweet temptation."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The giant shows no fear as his body shifts forward with the promise of death... and stops. His lips barely move as he musters the words:{/n} "I won't kill... my own..."
  - After: {n}He lunges... and stops.{/n} "I won't kill... my own..."

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/CommorraghStreets/ZanniComplete/ZanniComplete

- **Player**

- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: {n}The slender figure of the Harlequin emerges from the shimmering haze. With the grace of one performing a sorrowful dance, he approaches the dying Aeldari nearby.{/n}
"Your dance is now tableau, and I lament,
The darkness in the eyes that saw the Path,
I peer into those tunnels black and bleak,
A gleam I seek, the one that points the way
To your imprisoned kin in tempest's cage."
  - After: {n}The Harlequin glides to the dying Aeldari.{/n}
"I mourn you. Where are your kin caged?"
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "Disdain you not will I with a refusal,
Your soul's refrain will I keep safe as well,
But leave to me reality, Farseer,
And dreams I'll give into your worthy hands."
{n}With a solemn strike, the Harlequin ends his kinsman's torment and carefully takes the spirit stone from his body. When the xenos turns to you, his hands are already empty — the stone is gone.{/n}
  - After: "I'll keep your soul safe, Farseer."
{n}He ends his kinsman's torment; the spirit stone vanishes in his hands.{/n}
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "The Merchant wishes them another fate?
A sudden turnabout, and curious.
What path ought they to take? All ears am I."
  - After: "Another fate for them? Curious.
Which path? Speak."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, beware, the colours of this xenos are constantly changing. Where there was clarity one moment, there is mystery and darkness the next. Foulness sprouts where there was goodness and then everything is stirred up and turned upside down. I cannot bear to look at it. It is making me feel dizzy..."
  - After: "Beware, Lord Captain. This xenos's colours keep shifting. It makes me dizzy..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It seems the xenos is trying to save the Farseers and their spirit stones at the behest of another, whose reasons are known only to them. All you have to guess now is if the "laugh of jest unending" that gave the Harlequin this mission is a living creature, a philosophical principle, or the figment of his deranged mind.{/n}
  - After: {n}He saves the Farseers for another. Is the "laugh of jest unending" a being, an idea, or madness?{/n}
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: {n}The Harlequin makes an exaggerated show of drawing back an imaginary curtain. The shadows beneath the black eye holes in his horned mask once again form a mocking smile.{/n}
"The grand finale of this gory piece,
Where perfidy and cunning reign supreme,
Shall now unfold, my Merchant Vagabond."
  - After: {n}The Harlequin mimes opening a curtain.{/n}
"Now the bloody finale, my Merchant Vagabond."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "You listen well, oh pathless wanderer,
Night music's leitmotif you have discerned,
And title virtuoso you have earned."
  - After: "You listen well; virtuoso indeed."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}After a blurred flash of movement, Yrliet appears between the feuding Heinrix and Marazhai, pale with fear and anger.{/n} "Enough! Hate has blinded you when Commorragh is about to let us out of its clutches. Marazhai, still your intractable tongue and stand down. And you..." {n}She looks at Heinrix in apparent bewilderment.{/n} "Do you really want to deny the one who makes your heart beat faster a chance at survival by dying or killing her allies as she escapes? Is that what you want?"
  - After: {n}Yrliet darts between them.{/n} "Enough! We're nearly free. Marazhai, stand down." {n}To Heinrix:{/n} "Would you doom the one your heart beats for?"
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai gives you a mocking look and turns back to Heinrix expectantly.{/n}
  - After: {n}Marazhai smirks at Heinrix.{/n}
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: {n}The horned mask tilts, as the Harlequin observes the mon-keigh and the Outcast's conversation with interest, but he does not make a sound.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Harlequin watches silently, head tilted.{/n}
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "A drum or harp, or any instrument,
Of maestro's eye it is the apple prized.
I will ensure that yours sounds once again,
From death I'll save your precious property."
  - After: "A maestro prizes his instrument.
I'll save yours from death."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet laughs bitterly.{/n} "You can kill me. Torture me. Grind to dust the very memory of my existence... But you cannot change what has transpired. The burnt mon-keigh made a misstep. I killed the traitor."
  - After: {n}Yrliet laughs bitterly.{/n} "Kill me; it changes nothing. The burnt mon-keigh erred. I killed the traitor."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "You blame the music for your graceless dance,
But who here is the means, and who the goal?
Of both together are sensations made.
You'll have the outcome, I the path thereto."
  - After: "Blame not the music.
You get the outcome, I the path."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}After delivering his speech, Heinrix seems to snap out of his haze of undiluted hatred. He takes a breath and glances at you, now looking weary beyond words.{/n} "Come on. Every minute in this cursed place brings us all closer to madness."
  - After: {n}Heinrix looks weary.{/n} "Come. This place breeds madness."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix freezes.{/n} "What..." {n}He slowly turns around and raises his gaze to the Drukhari.{/n} "...did you say?"
  - After: {n}Heinrix freezes.{/n} "What..." {n}He turns.{/n} "...did you say?"
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "No, he was squealing, like all cattle do at a slaughterhouse. Back on the ravaged world where I spent hours twisting his mind and spirit." {n}Marazhai draws out the words, slowly advancing toward the Interrogator.{/n} "Your servant traded away the most terrible secrets for a reprieve from pain. Yours, Heinrix van Calox, and those of your little mon-keigh Inquisition. Did I need them? No. What I wanted to know was beyond your servant's knowledge but he still would not settle down, desperate to purchase my mercy. He kept mumbling incessantly, both about you, whom he feared so much, and his beloved mistress... Lichtenhart, wasn't it?"
  - After: "He squealed like cattle." {n}Marazhai advances.{/n} "He sold your secrets for relief, Heinrix van Calox. He babbled of his mistress... Lichtenhart, wasn't it?"
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "Commorragh's ancient law was boldly spurned,
And too despoiled were Crudarach's remains,
The Tempest's mistress, spurred by avarice,
Forbidden plunder brought to her dark nest.
And though the City shrinks from those whose souls
In darkness gleam with coruscating flame,
The interdict is scorned, the pact ignored,
Commorragh waits, Commorragh tastes its doom.
To make of drama farce beyond belief,
A pair uncredited assume the stage:
A cutthroat mon-keigh, captive of a thief;
A dancer, makestrife poet, guileful knave."
  - After: "The Tempest's mistress broke Commorragh's law, bringing Crudarach's psykers home.
Two unbilled players enter: a mon-keigh captive and a guileful dancer."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: {n}With a weary sigh, the Harlequin concludes,{/n}
"When coda's note falls silent ever more,
The last a duty will perform, and then,
The first will move, {mf|his|her} exodus enact."
  - After: {n}He sighs.{/n}
"At the coda, one does his duty; then {mf|his|her} exodus."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}The xenos scoffs.{/n} "With pleasure. Especially now that we have both got what we wanted."
  - After: {n}He scoffs.{/n} "Gladly. We both won."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix looks at you with dead eyes, struggling to say something.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix stares at you, speechless.{/n}
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai does not hide the contempt in his look aimed at the Interrogator.{/n} "You should have killed the burnt mon-keigh immediately and not deluded yourself by putting faith in his strength and resilience. You mon-keigh are clueless when it comes to the art of espionage and treason. I could teach you a thing or two... If you ask nicely enough." {n}He turns his gaze toward you.{/n} "I am finished here. We may go."
  - After: {n}Marazhai sneers.{/n} "You should have killed the burnt mon-keigh at once." {n}To you:{/n} "I am finished. We may go."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "The starved ones' fate to shelter from the storm,
Enlisted me the laugh of jest unending,
The soul is not at home amidst dark walls,
It yearns to sing, and I to hearken long
Its elegy, by name oblivion.
A cradle I'll bestow, where may this song
Forevermore resound in endless echo."
  - After: "The laugh of jest unending bid me shelter these souls in an eternal cradle."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "The Executioner lost interest,
And blithely tossed the toy despised aside.
Proclaiming it a gift to empty bellies,
He let the rabble tear it into scraps,
And tooth and claw they fought to claim a share,
With every one extolling his largesse."
  - After: "Bored, the Executioner threw his toy
to the rabble, who tore it apart."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "A fitting end." {n}Marazhai snorts contemptuously and looks at you.{/n} "I am finished here. I trust we can move on to important matters: finding that ship the Arebennian kept babbling about and dealing with Yremeryss."
  - After: "A fitting end." {n}Marazhai snorts.{/n} "Done. Now the Arebennian's ship, and Yremeryss."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix and Marazhai give each other one last look — a hateful human glare and a disdainful Drukhari sneer — and silently follow.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix and Marazhai glare, then follow.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yremeryss acted recklessly when she decided to bring captive psykers back to Commorragh. The Webway is extremely sensitive to psychic powers and the psykers' presence could force the Dark City apart at the seams, opening gaping chasms to the warp. If the other Kabals knew about this audacious stunt...{/n}
  - After: {n}Yremeryss's psykers could rip the Dark City open to the warp. If the Kabals knew...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is clear that Yremeryss acted recklessly by taking such valuable prisoners and she risked starting a war with her xenos cousins.{/n}
  - After: {n}Yremeryss's captives risked war with her xenos cousins.{/n}
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "As surety this feral brute has served,
That to my plan there would be blood released,
Without remorse fate's course I've whipped and spurred,
A cruel hand on old, unruly beast."
  - After: "This brute assured bloodshed; I spurred fate without remorse."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Agh, you rotten-gutted swine! Used me as a war beast, did you? Set me on your enemies?" {n}Ulfar's face darkens in fury, but with gargantuan effort he forces it down and manages to prevent a fit of blood rage from taking hold.{/n}
  - After: "Used me as a war beast, you rotten swine?" {n}Ulfar holds back his rage.{/n}
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "A fragment's all that's left of what was whole,
The rest now worn away by treachery.
But if you prize this repercussion so,
This gesture I'll perform, and in return,
The laugh with no beginning you will serve."
  - After: "Only a fragment remains. I'll save it; you'll serve the laugh with no beginning."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Be careful, elantach. Arebennian weigh each word with meticulous pedantry. If you do not take care, you will receive what you want, only turned inside out, like the fabric of the void without any stars."
  - After: "Careful, elantach. Arebennian twist words inside out."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "Watch your words. Arebennian love nothing more than interpreting words superficially, and not how they were intended."
  - After: "Careful. Arebennian take words literally."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "The picture of compassion, so you are,
Remembering the weak and bare this way,
Why not? I'll show my care for them as well,
And guard them from Commorragh's horrors all."
  - After: "How compassionate.
Why not? I'll guard them from Commorragh too."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "No sooner said than done, offstage they go,
Their fates do matter little to our show."
  - After: "Done. Offstage they go."
- **Achilleas the Wrack**
  - Before: {n}Through his overwhelming rage, Achilleas chokes out a farewell:{/n} "I leave you... here... Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... I am a danger to you."
  - After: {n}Achilleas chokes:{/n} "Leaving... Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... I'm dangerous."
- **Achilleas the Wrack**
  - Before: "I was made for... fighting. My body is excited by the smell of blood... It wants more. If I lose control... during the voyage... the best case is that I destroy the gondola... and we all die..."
  - After: "Blood... excites me. If I lose control... aboard... we all die."
- **Achilleas the Wrack**
  - Before: "I betrayed you... once. And I swore... never again."
  - After: "I betrayed you... once. Never again."
- **Achilleas the Wrack**
  - Before: {n}His weakening human voice collapses into roars of rage and bloodthirst cloaked in flesh.{/n}
  - After: {n}His voice becomes roars.{/n}
- **Farseer**
  - Before: {n}The Farseer's voice is weak and tremulous from pain. It is strange that he is still capable of speech — his body has been horrifically maimed. The colours of his garb are familiar — the group of xenos you met on Janus wore the same.{/n} "At the top of the spire. They are all there. Help them, Arebennian. And help... me. Take me away from here, when it is all over... Soon."
  - After: {n}The maimed Farseer wears the colours of the Janus xenos.{/n} "Atop the spire. Help them, Arebennian. Then take me away."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: {n}The Harlequin's mournful mask gives no sign of his intentions. Who knows what goes on in his head?{/n}
  - After: {n}The Harlequin's mask reveals nothing.{/n}
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: {n}The xenos tilts his head, staring at Yrliet.{/n}
"The cradle's fragments smoulder dimly there,
Where tight has drawn the Tempest all together.
Dare you plunge your hand into the flame,
And drag truth's embers out into the light?"
  - After: {n}He eyes Yrliet.{/n}
"Your cradle's embers smoulder in the Tempest's nest. Dare you?"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Oh Arebennian, you ask if I am too afraid to try to save the little that remains of my home? Now that the wind of hope fans the flame of the coming truth?" {n}The stone on Yrliet's chest flares crimson — a timid glow that goes out as soon as the Aeldari touches her chestplate.{/n} "Even if the fire of truth burns me from within, I will follow this Path to the end."
  - After: "Afraid to save my home? Never." {n}Her stone flares crimson.{/n} "Even if truth burns me, I'll walk this Path."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Do you... truly not understand, elantach? It pains me to recall how I was willing to exchange your life for the pathetic scraps of information Marazhai scattered at my feet. But the Farseers... with those scraps, they have the ability to grow an entire forest of truth."
  - After: "I nearly traded your life for Marazhai's scraps. From scraps, Farseers grow forests of truth."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet tenses her lithe frame in an attempt to hold back the shudder of despair that rocks through her.{/n} "I understand your doubts, elantach. I but ask you to consider my request... and to do it not for my kin, for the Arebennian, or for anyone else. But for me."
  - After: {n}Yrliet fights despair.{/n} "I understand, elantach. Do it not for my kin, but for me."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Elantach, the Arebennian love jests, but this is not one. Please, before it is too late, I... we must save the Farseers! Allow me to go with you to the spire — to that nest of depravity, to that haven of pain, anger, and betrayal of my kind." {n}Yrliet's voice wavers like a taught string, and her eyes are veiled with darkness.{/n}
  - After: "No jest, elantach. We must save the Farseers! Take me to the spire." {n}Her voice wavers.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Harlequin said the words "laugh of jest unending" with reverence, as if it were a title or rank. You recall that Harlequins serve the Laughing God Cegorach. It seems the xenos is saying that it is at Cegorach's behest that he is attempting to save the Farseers.{/n}
  - After: {n}Harlequins serve Cegorach, the Laughing God; he must be the "laugh of jest unending" behind this.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet half closes her eyes, her lids fluttering from suppressed emotion.{/n} "A very long time ago, an old friend once told me, 'A bird does not know its feathers' worth until it loses the gift of harnessing the wind.' I think I understand now."
  - After: {n}Yrliet closes her eyes.{/n} "'A bird knows its feathers' worth only once grounded.' Now I understand."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet shudders as if she cannot believe your words, and her expression shifts subtly.{/n} "I... am grateful."
  - After: {n}Yrliet shudders, disbelieving.{/n} "I... am grateful."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "My Merchant Vagabond, their {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ArenaFaithEnding}part is played{/d},
It's not for you or me to denigrate
The artful script directing this charade
That writes them out — cast off to stormy fate."
  - After: "Their {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ArenaFaithEnding}part is played{/d}, Merchant Vagabond; stormy fate awaits."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Several encounters with the Harlequin have been enough to teach you that everything that is happening is merely one grand show or dance for him. It is pointless to converse with him like a typical xenos — he is a director, playwright, and actor all in one. All that interests him is that the performance comes off successfully.{/n}
  - After: {n}To the Harlequin, it's all a show; only the performance matters.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Cantraetal, who chose the Path of the Seer... Muaran told me he disappeared as soon as the cataclysm befell Crudarach. Does this mean my kin are being held captive at the top of the Reaving Tempest's spire? The truth is ready to reveal itself to me if I but stretch out my hand..." {n}Sparks of impatience flicker in Yrliet's gaze. She wants to talk to you, but she will not interrupt your exchange with the Harlequin.{/n}
  - After: "Muaran said Cantraetal the Seer vanished when Crudarach fell. Are my kin atop the Reaving Tempest's spire?" {n}Yrliet waits to speak.{/n}
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "The accursed jester, back again. If you start weaving your webs of rotten claptrap again, I'll rip out your useless tongue!"
  - After: "That jester again. More claptrap and I'll rip your tongue out!"
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "And yet the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_DaemonicBreach}feast of waking nightmares{/d} draws
Another pen into this narrative.
The playwright's face remains a mystery,
But message mine I hope will reach those ears:
That nightmares suffer nightmares of their own,
Where Nocturne of Oblivion resounds."
{n}The black gaze of the horned mask's eye hollows lingers on your face before the Harlequin continues his speech.{/n}
  - After: "The {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_DaemonicBreach}feast of waking nightmares{/d} draws in another author.
Let them hear Nocturne of Oblivion."
{n}The mask watches you.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Here we go again! Trusting the pointy-eared ones and saving xenos! We don't learn from our mistakes, do we? Nah, of course not!" {n}Jae's plaintive groan is directed more at herself than you.{/n}
  - After: "Trusting pointy-ears, saving xenos again! We never learn." {n}Jae groans at herself.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Ah, a ship! We will finally leave this horrible place flooded with scarlet hues of agony and washed-out tinges of despair."
  - After: "A ship! At last, out of this agony."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "Strive up to where the thieving storm has built
Its squalid nest among the darkened sky,
The tempest's plunder hoards are buried there,
And captives, riches, trophies all within.
Amidst this cache a gate to realspace find,
Pass through to freedom tempting and so craved,
Companions have I brought, and steps revealed,
My lines run out, I have no more to give.
The stage is yours, my Merchant Vagabond,
Go fetch a vessel swift — and get you gone!"
  - After: "Climb to the storm's nest; its plunder hides a gate to realspace.
The stage is yours, Merchant Vagabond. Be gone!"
- **Achilleas the Wrack**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas's growling becomes louder and louder. Through the rasping and gurgling, a tortured voice breaks through:{/n} "Combat... stimulants... Too many... I need... slaughter... Slaughter. Slaughter!" {n}Your former servant is teetering on a knife edge, threatening to tumble into bloodthirsty madness at any moment.{/n}
  - After: {n}Achilleas growls.{/n} "Stimulants... Too many... Slaughter!" {n}He teeters on madness.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "I don't know what's doing my head in more — my whispers or his damned metaphors. Why can't he just say, 'I saved your asses, now do this for me — whack these upstarts and get out while you can'?"
  - After: "Worse than my whispers. Just say 'I saved you, now whack these upstarts'!"
- **Achilleas the Wrack**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas's rasping snarl drowns out the Harlequin's last words. The beast looks around bloodthirstily, but there are no enemies left, and its interest in the xenos becomes more and more pronounced.{/n}
  - After: {n}Achilleas snarls, finds no enemies, and eyes the xenos hungrily.{/n}
- **Achilleas the Wrack**
  - Before: {n}Through his overwhelming rage, Achilleas chokes out a farewell:{/n} "Good luck... Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... Until we meet... on the other side."
  - After: {n}Achilleas chokes:{/n} "Good luck... Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... Farewell."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix stares for a few more moments at the spot where Nocturne just stood.{/n} "How much longer will we be playthings in the hands of damned xenos? The torture... the arena... even this effortless 'escape'... And the source of all these degrading ordeals is still alive." {n}His eyes, burning with hate, shift to Yrliet.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix scowls.{/n} "How long will we be xenos playthings? The cause still lives." {n}He glares at Yrliet.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet looks at Heinrix with empty eyes and shivers slightly.{/n} "The deluge of misfortune did not start with me, mon-keigh. It was your charge, Achilleas..."
  - After: {n}Yrliet shivers.{/n} "It began with Achilleas, mon-keigh, not me."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Do not speak his name! You sully the name of a servant of the Throne by uttering it." {n}Heinrix's voice has dropped to a rasping hiss.{/n} "And stop trying my patience with your lies."
  - After: "Don't sully his name! Enough lies." {n}Heinrix hisses.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "An Arebennian would not lie about this! Or did you not hear the words of the dying Farseer?" {n}Impatience burns in Yrliet's emerald eyes.{/n} "I hope your soul's doubts will be dispelled before we reach the spire. I am not asking you to rise to Nocturne's words, but to my request."
  - After: "Arebennian don't lie about this! Heed my request, not Nocturne." {n}Yrliet's eyes burn.{/n}
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai, who had been engrossed in his own thoughts, springs to life at the Interrogator's frenzied words. He turns his head with snake-like grace and stares unblinkingly at Heinrix.{/n}
  - After: {n}Marazhai turns with snake-like grace and stares at Heinrix.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix's gaze turns on you — and you are suddenly trembling, enveloped in an icy fog.{/n} "Because it is a hastily concocted tale that would fool only a naive simpleton. If you wish to trust the word of an enemy of Humanity, that is your unfortunate choice to make. But until I have better proof of Achilleas Scalander's treason than this pathetic prattle, I will not change my mind. Not now, not ever."
  - After: {n}Heinrix's gaze chills you.{/n} "A tale for simpletons. Without proof of Achilleas Scalander's treason, I won't relent."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai's scathing laugh seems to cut through the air.{/n} "He was weeping when he begged me for death."
  - After: {n}Marazhai laughs.{/n} "He wept, begging me for death."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Enough, xenos! Repeating the same thing over and over will not convince me of your ridiculous lies. The Rogue Trader takes you at your word — that is {mf|his|her} vice and heresy, not mine. And until I have more solid proof of Achilleas Scalander's treason than your prattle, I will not change my mind. Not now, not ever."
  - After: "Enough, xenos! Believing you is {mf|his|her} heresy, not mine. Without proof of Achilleas Scalander's treason, I won't relent."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix's face, twisted with hatred, turns whiter than snow.{/n} "No..."
  - After: {n}Heinrix goes white.{/n} "No..."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai's eyes flash with pleasure at the look of horror on Heinrix's face.{/n} "Yes, mon-keigh. You wanted proof of how weak your kind is and how insignificant your servants are, didn't you? The name of Emelina Lichtenhart. The poor singed beast... He tried so hard, he was so eager to please his new master that he sold out every one of you..." {n}Marazhai cocks his head as if straining to hear a distant sound, then grins carnivorously.{/n} "Oh, Heinrix van Calox. The shards of your naive illusions are slicing your soul so sweetly..."
  - After: {n}Marazhai savours Heinrix's horror.{/n} "Yes. Emelina Lichtenhart. The singed beast sold you all..." {n}He grins.{/n} "Your illusions cut so sweetly, Heinrix van Calox."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Interrogator remains still for another second, then his eyes glaze over, his face twists, and the air around him turns icy cold. Marazhai twitches and coughs strangely, his pale face turning purple. He staggers and reaches for his blade...{/n}
  - After: {n}The air turns icy. Marazhai chokes, purpling, and reaches for his blade...{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix takes a step back and looks at you in shock. After a moment, his face regains its usual stoic expression.{/n} "That is enough. You are right, xenos. About this..." {n}Heinrix hesitates, struggling to say the next words.{/n} "...and about other things too." {n}As if drained of the last of his strength, Heinrix turns away from you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix steps back, stunned.{/n} "You are right, xenos. About this..." {n}He hesitates.{/n} "...and more." {n}He turns away.{/n}
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai rubs his face, bruised from the ruptured blood vessels under the skin. His voice oozes contempt.{/n} "Keep your broodmale on a shorter leash, {name}. I might break your little plaything next time."
  - After: {n}Marazhai rubs his bruised face.{/n} "Leash your broodmale, {name}, or I'll break your plaything."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "A fragment's all that's left of what was whole,
The rest now worn away by treachery.
Reality for him is out of bounds,
But nightmares in Commorragh find a home,
Depart. Forget. And leave the past alone."
  - After: "Only a fragment remains.
He belongs to Commorragh's nightmares now.
Go. Forget."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai nimbly evades your blow and, having lost precious time, drops to his knees with a wheeze. The next moment his eyes burst, a fountain of blood gushes from his mouth, and the xenos's dead body slumps to the ground.{/n}
  - After: {n}Marazhai dodges, then collapses; his eyes burst and he dies.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix sighs heavily and stares down at the corpse at his feet. He looks suddenly forlorn.{/n} "Foolish... So foolish... I could have interrogated him... extracted every bit of information he managed to get from Achilleas..." {n}He looks up at you, his gaze filled with pain.{/n} "I'm sorry. I... lost my head for a moment. I will not let it happen again. No, I won't." {n}Casting one last hateful glance at the dead Marazhai, Heinrix turns away.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix stares at the corpse.{/n} "Foolish... I could have interrogated him." {n}He looks at you.{/n} "Sorry. I lost my head." {n}He turns away.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}The blow catches Heinrix off guard, and he gives you a stunned look before a razor-sharp blade slices through his face, cleaving his skull in two and severing the rest of his head. His decapitated body falls heavily at Marazhai's feet.{/n}
  - After: {n}Stunned, Heinrix falls to Marazhai's blade, his skull cleaved.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix flinches when you appear before him. He hesitates for another moment, and then, clenching his fists impotently, he looks away.{/n} "I am sorry, {name}. I... lost my head for a moment."
  - After: {n}Heinrix flinches and looks away.{/n} "Sorry, {name}. I lost my head."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "{name}..." {n}Heinrix's voice is barely audible.{/n} "I have detained us. I beg you to forgive my outburst. Please lead on."
  - After: "{name}..." {n}Heinrix whispers.{/n} "Forgive my outburst. Please lead on."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}At the Farseer's words, Marazhai's face stiffens and he opens his mouth, but to no avail. The Drukhari appears to have lost the power of speech.{/n}
  - After: {n}Marazhai tries to speak at the Farseer's words, but cannot.{/n}
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}When Harlequin's voice fades, the silence is broken by a torrent of untranslatable but highly expressive xenos profanities — Marazhai has regained the power of speech and is using it to curse someone's kin and progeny.{/n} "Farseers! Yremeryss brought Asuryani Farseers to the Dark City! You stupid, desperate shrew! If this news reaches the— oh, but of course it has reached him already! You, Arebennian! You came to Commorragh to inform Vect of my sister's crimes and rescue her prisoners!"
  - After: {n}Marazhai curses furiously.{/n} "Yremeryss brought Asuryani Farseers here! And you, Arebennian, came to tell Vect of my sister's crimes and free her prisoners!"
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: {n}The Harlequin makes a jester's bow.{/n}
"I am revealed and intrigue's curtain torn!
The Puppet Master deigned to briefly let
Me be the crosspiece of his artistry,
That tweaks and tugs the strings for dance and death.
To tempest's mistress, 'Vanish!' I do say,
I've fashioned from your shackles a garrotte.
Your burning wrath, my thief, direct her way,
And forth you'll see the fruits of vengeance brought."
  - After: {n}The Harlequin bows.{/n}
"Unmasked! Turn your wrath on the Tempest's mistress, thief, and taste vengeance."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "The accusations of consorting with mon-keigh are such a trifle compared to an attempt to bring about a dysjunction... If only I had known it! Had Yremeryss not managed to keep it secret from me..." {n}Marazhai shields his eyes, contemplating something.{/n} "I wonder how many times Nazrakhei cursed himself for not overthrowing Yremeryss at the Obsidian Court when he had the chance? He had unknowingly spared the one his ruler had condemned. Hardly an excuse that will help him at his next meeting with Vect."
  - After: "Mon-keigh dealings are nothing beside a dysjunction!" {n}Marazhai muses.{/n} "Nazrakhei spared Yremeryss at the Obsidian Court. Vect won't forgive that."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "You may applaud my disappearing act
The reaper's fatal steps I did conceal
From eyes that dreams of blood so wildly craved.
For unbeknownst to them, death merely moved
Into another hall, in harmony
With inmate's steps and night's own melody."
  - After: "Applaud my vanishing act:
I moved death to another hall, unseen."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "The Webway in which Commorragh resides is fragile. A ripple of the veil can breach its boundaries and cause a dysjunction, an incursion of Sai'lanthresh into the streets. Each such occasion is an ordeal that weakens the Dark City, and so those capable of piercing the veil are banned from the spires. Of course, there are madmen who try to exploit any dysjunction and the ensuing chaos to take down competitors and move up the food chain... It appears that Yremeryss decided not to wait for an opportunity, but to make it happen herself!"
  - After: "Commorragh's Webway is fragile. Psykers can trigger a dysjunction, a Sai'lanthresh incursion, so they're banned from the spires. Yremeryss meant to cause one!"
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "I did, because such was the deal with Tervantias. In exchange for his help, I was not to kill the veil-linked mon-keigh, but to sedate and hand them over to him, a degenerate obsessed with studying the forbidden. I expected them to vanish without a trace into the shadows of the Anatomical Opera... and believe me, the damned of your kind are far less dangerous to the Webway than the Farseers of the Asuryani!"
  - After: "Per my deal, Tervantias got the sedated mon-keigh psykers for the Anatomical Opera. They're far less dangerous than Asuryani Farseers!"
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "I had enough reasons even without this revelation! Kae-morag, I am half a step away from starting to see my expulsion from the Kabal as a blessing and not a punishment!"
  - After: "Reasons enough already! Kae-morag, exile starts to feel like a blessing!"
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: {n}Nocturne of Oblivion watches the raging Drukhari with obvious amusement, but his interest barely lasts a moment.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nocturne of Oblivion is briefly amused by the raging Drukhari.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "A bizarre tapestry of metaphors, yet containing a surprisingly deep meaning." {n}Eogunn listens closely to the Harlequin's recital, counting off on his fingers in rhythm with the stressed syllables of the poem.{/n} "Iambic pentameter. An unexpected choice, yet pleasing to my auditory receptors."
  - After: {n}Eogunn counts syllables on his fingers.{/n} "Iambic pentameter. Pleasing."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: {n}Although the Harlequin's mournful mask is absolutely still, you cannot shake the feeling that a nasty grin lurks behind it. This is a game, a test. You must choose your words carefully.{/n}
  - After: {n}The still mask hides a grin. A test: choose your words carefully.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Even flesh-speak is more efficient than the speech patterns of this xenos. Hypothesis: the elucidator machine spirit has been affected by the pernicious influence of this place and is producing distorted output. I seek permission to conduct a technical survey."
  - After: "Hypothesis: the elucidator spirit is corrupted. Permission to survey it?"

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/Dargonus_ChapterBeginning/AchilleasFoundTrace/AchilleasFoundTrace

- **Player**
  - Before: "I shall deal with this later."
  - After: "I'll deal with this later."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Hundred Dreams Crossroads, was it? Send the word: we are heading out at once."
  - After: "The Hundred Dreams Crossroads? We leave at once."
- **Player**
  - Before: "So Voigtvir had a hand in this as well?"
  - After: "Voigtvir was involved too?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "It has only been three cycles since the attack. How are your wounds?"
  - After: "Only three cycles since the attack. Your wounds?"
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "Ah, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Achilleas appears uncharacteristically pensive.{/n} "Might I ask for a few precious moments of your time? Critical information has come to my attention, however... Please let us first proceed to your study lest we be overheard."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Achilleas looks pensive.{/n} "Critical news. To your study, lest we be overheard?"
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "I implore you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It brooks no delay. We have the element of surprise on our side and an opportunity to lay a trap for Kunrad Voigtvir. If that opportunity slips away... we cannot be certain if we have caught every one of his spies on Dargonus and your voidship."
  - After: "It cannot wait, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Trap Kunrad Voigtvir now, or his spies may escape us."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "Your former Master of Whispers, Kunrad Voigtvir. Now we know how he's been able to dodge our spies time and time and again: he has the technology of enemies of Humanity on his side. Vile traitor! My agents ascertained the location of the base where Voigtvir has been meeting with xenos in secret, a station in the system of the Hundred Dreams Crossroads. The station is allegedly out of commission, abandoned some time ago. That plays into our hands: it is an excellent place to set up an ambush and strike where they least expect it."
  - After: "Kunrad Voigtvir, your former Master of Whispers, meets xenos at an abandoned station in the Hundred Dreams Crossroads system. Traitor! Ideal for an ambush."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "Consider it done. I will go with Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, for my investigation into this matter has only just commenced."
  - After: "Done. I'll come with Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: {n}Achilleas presses his lips into a line.{/n} "Since the xenos attack, I have been working relentlessly to follow their cold trail. I have had no time for rest but... My body is functional. Its condition is beneath Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s notice."
  - After: {n}Achilleas's lips tighten.{/n} "I haven't rested. My body functions; beneath Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s notice."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "That is hardly surprising. His connection to cultists has already been established. He is to blame for the death of Her Ladyship Theodora von Valancius and he came close to taking your life as well. Another betrayal of the Imperium, this time fraternising with xenos — although such crimes must come as easy to him as getting up in the morning."
  - After: "Unsurprising. He served cultists and caused Her Ladyship Theodora von Valancius's death. Now xenos too."
- **Achilleas Scalander**
  - Before: "If I may, I will get right to the point. After the attack on Dargonus, I focused my efforts on trying to discover how the xenos were able to launch that devastating raid. According to my findings, the enemies of Humanity received assistance from a hidden cell of conspirators. My agents spent a great deal of time tracking and interrogating infiltrators on Dargonus and other von Valancius colonies. The results... surprised me, to say the least." {n}Achilleas pauses to press his respirator against his burnt lips.{/n}
  - After: "After the Dargonus attack, I found a hidden cell of conspirators helped the xenos. Interrogating infiltrators across your colonies, I found... a surprise." {n}He breathes from his respirator.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/Dargonus_ChapterBeginning/FactotumChancellorReport/FactotumChancellorReport

- **Player**
  - Before: [Say nothing while maintaining a bored expression]
  - After: [Say nothing, looking bored]
- **Player**
  - Before: "Truly, the God-Emperor has blessed me with diligent subjects! Speak."
  - After: "The God-Emperor blessed me with diligent subjects! Speak."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Did I hear you quite right? Macharius Sauerback is sending me gifts, correct?"
  - After: "Macharius Sauerback is sending me gifts?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have lost track of how long I have been trapped on Dargonus for the good of the protectorate. Hurry up. I better hear some good news today."
  - After: "I've been stuck on Dargonus for ages. Hurry. I want good news."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}Clementia barely contains a yawn. Once Janris Danrok has finished, she pulls out her data-slate.{/n} "Thank you for your report, High Factotum. Your work is highly appreciated, both by everyone here and the Adeptus Administratum. Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, we are almost done here. We just need to go over the final items on today's agenda that I would like to report to you personally."
  - After: {n}Clementia stifles a yawn as Janris Danrok finishes.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, a few final items."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Your pet xenos... Yrliet, I believe, is seeking a meeting with you. She had the audacity to defile the Rogue Trader's palace with her profane presence and refuses to leave until she has spoken with you. I would never presume to be able to read the emotions of xenos, but the Aeldari appeared perturbed. I believe she mentioned a voidship of some sort. It may be best if she told you everything directly."
  - After: "Your pet xenos, Yrliet, won't leave the palace until she sees you. Something about a voidship."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Especially since His Lordship Winterscale's luck seems to be running out. Riots have broken out on several of his worlds, and yet, he has shown no intention of quelling them. Instead, the Rogue Trader inflicted brutal punishment upon one of his oldest colonies, Vesuvia Secundus, based on allegations of seditious sentiment. Oddly enough, our agents were unable to find any proof of sedition among the populace there. As soon as we have any updates, you will be the first to know, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Clementia glances down at her data-slate.{/n} "Lastly..."
  - After: "Winterscale ignores riots on his worlds, yet crushed Vesuvia Secundus for unproven sedition. More soon, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}She checks her data-slate.{/n} "Lastly..."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}The chancellor coughs in an attempt to break up the awkward pause.{/n} "Right, so..."
  - After: {n}The chancellor coughs awkwardly.{/n} "Right, so..."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Allow me to pass on gifts from your loyal subjects, the high nobility of Dargonus. It goes without saying that every living soul in your protectorate is blessed to serve Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} faithfully and wholeheartedly. However, this humble gesture is meant as a token of deepest appreciation of your magnanimity toward their esteemed families."
  - After: "Gifts from Dargonus's high nobility, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, in gratitude for your magnanimity to their families."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "House Werserian made arrangements for the delivery of several tonnes of supplies for your future journeys. The house is also transferring a regiment of its finest into your personal charge. Each of these brave troopers has undergone rigorous voidfarer training and will be humbled to lay down their life for you, Lord Captain." {n}Clementia is trying to maintain a neutral expression but you can see her face is beaming with pride.{/n} "Please command them as you see fit."
  - After: "House Werserian sends tonnes of supplies and a regiment of its finest troopers, Lord Captain." {n}Clementia beams with pride.{/n} "Command them as you wish."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "In the past cycle, House Drivestem tripled the tithes collected from the house's subjects. Your coffers are overflowing, and the governor has expressed hope that this modest gift will become a symbol of your present and future successes in your new status."
  - After: "House Drivestem tripled its tithes last cycle. Your coffers overflow with their gift."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "House Gaprak has sent shuttles carrying sacred technology and manufactured parts that can be used to replace old joints and connections within mechanisms. The machine spirits of these devices have been pacified. They are slumbering peacefully as they await your decision on how to employ their capabilities."
  - After: "House Gaprak sends sacred technology and spare parts, their machine spirits pacified and awaiting your use."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "House Sauerback has arranged for several regiments of expertly trained servants of the Emperor to be transferred to your personal command. Each of them will also serve as an honour guard for the holy relics that are to find their rightful place in the hold of your personal voidship..." {n}She stops, staring at her data-slate in surprise.{/n}
  - After: "House Sauerback sends regiments of trained soldiers to guard holy relics for your voidship..." {n}She stares at her data-slate.{/n}
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "No, not at all, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! The people and the cargo have indeed reached the port services, so there is no reason to doubt the sincerity of the house's intentions. It's just... such substantial and valuable gifts coming from Lord Sauerback..." {n}Clementia trails off.{/n}
  - After: "No, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! It all arrived. It's just... such gifts, from Lord Sauerback..." {n}She trails off.{/n}
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "That is exactly correct, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The port services have already received the aforementioned resources and are now in the process of accommodating them aboard your ship. It's just... Lord Sauerback..."
  - After: "Correct, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. It's being loaded aboard your ship. It's just... Lord Sauerback..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You have spent the first few hours of your morning listening to the High Factotum's lengthy report on the latest trade exchanges, arrangements, disputes, and countless bureaucratic procedures. From outside the illuminated, tightly closed windows, you can hear the muffled sounds of Dargonus and its everyday life — the life that has been passing you by lately, as you have been preoccupied with the affairs of your protectorate from dawn till dusk.{/n}
  - After: {n}You've spent the morning hearing the High Factotum's long report. Outside, Dargonus's daily life passes you by.{/n}
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "And with that, please allow me and Master Danrok to take our leave." {n}The chancellor and the High Factotum offer you their bows.{/n} "Perhaps that last request will serve as a welcome distraction? Indeed, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s stay on Dargonus has been rather long. However, your protectorate is now enjoying a period of relative stability that, for the time being, no longer demands Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}'s personal involvement in its affairs. Glory to the Rogue Trader!"
  - After: "We take our leave, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}They bow.{/n} "The protectorate can spare Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} now. Glory to the Rogue Trader!"
- **High Factotum Janris Danrok**
  - Before: {n}Danrok lets out an amused chuckle.{/n} "If I am to venture a guess, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, I believe the esteemed chancellor was staggered by such an irregular display of generosity from a man who is rather known for voicing his... doubts in Rogue Traders as a class. It would seem you have made quite an impression on Macharius, the old miser."
  - After: {n}Danrok chuckles.{/n} "The chancellor is staggered, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Macharius, the old miser, doubts Rogue Traders. You've impressed him."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, news of particular import has come from the house's intelligence network. Lord Inquisitor Calcazar is rumoured to be planning a visit to Footfall. A number of Imperial Navy ships were commandeered by Lord Calcazar and they are also being scrambled to Footfall. Furthermore, we have received reports claiming that secret messages were delivered to the capital worlds of Houses Chorda and Winterscale. It is possible that the Lord Inquisitor's call to arms may smother the conflict that is brewing between the two dynasties. We are seeing an increasing number of skirmishes between their ships in neutral systems. I do not doubt that Her Ladyship Chorda will attempt to sway the Lord Inquisitor to her side."
  - After: "Lord Captain: Lord Inquisitor Calcazar may visit Footfall with commandeered Imperial Navy ships. He sent secret messages to Houses Chorda and Winterscale, whose ships keep clashing. Her Ladyship Chorda will court him."
- **Clementia Werserian**
  - Before: {n}The chancellor and the High Factotum exchange nervous glances.{/n} "I will strive my best to live up to your expectations, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: {n}The two exchange nervous glances.{/n} "I'll strive to meet your expectations, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/Dargonus_ChapterBeginning/JaeReminder/JaeReminder

- **Player**
  - Before: "You are quite right. No more delays. To the Master of Seals!"
  - After: "Quite right. To the Master of Seals!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Have patience. You will get your certificate when I find the time."
  - After: "Patience. You'll get your certificate later."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Enough! I have no intention of going anywhere and I do not wish to hear another word about your papers."
  - After: "Enough! I'm going nowhere. No more about your papers."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Shereen! Dargonus is absolutely fabulous this season, wouldn't you agree?" {n}Jae greets you with a familiar pearly smile.{/n} "Incidentally... We've been dealing with the aftermath of the xeno-invasion for three cycles now... And far be it from me to hint at anything... but the ceremony of your succession has long since passed."
  - After: "Shereen!" {n}Jae smiles.{/n} "Three cycles since the xenos... your succession is long past."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "May the Exalted One bless your whole dynasty!" {n}Jae claps her hands and something in her prosthesis clicks in protest.{/n} "Shall we proceed to the shuttles, shereen? I will be right behind you."
  - After: "Bless your dynasty!" {n}Jae claps; her prosthesis clicks.{/n} "To the shuttles, shereen?"
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Of course, shereen! There is no rush. All the time in the world is at our disposal..." {n}Jae rubs her chin with a look of slight worry.{/n}
  - After: "Of course, shereen. No rush..." {n}Jae looks worried.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: {n}Jae says nothing for a while before offering you a saccharine smile.{/n} "But of course! I beg you to pardon my indiscretion, shereen. It does not befit people of your stature to concern themselves with the pleas of lowly... subjects. I dare not trouble you further."
  - After: {n}A saccharine smile.{/n} "Pardon me, shereen. I won't trouble you further."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Will my shereen, perhaps, find the time to visit the Administratum Palace with me? I am worried that, should we sail away on another voyage to the stars, I will never obtain my certificate, the Mercatum Tabula Officiale. And neither will my shereen savour all the benefits that said certificate could offer the von Valancius protectorate."
  - After: "Come to the Administratum Palace? If we sail off, neither I nor the protectorate will get the Mercatum Tabula Officiale."

## World/Dialogs/Ch3/Dargonus_ChapterBeginning/YrlietAskingForHelp/YrlietAskingForHelp

- **Player**
  - Before: "Give me the coordinates, and I shall take you wherever you wish to go."
  - After: "Give me the coordinates; I'll take you there."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Let us discuss this another time, perhaps."
  - After: "Another time, perhaps."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Crudarach's fate is no concern of mine."
  - After: "Crudarach's fate is not my concern."
- **Player**
  - Before: "How were you able to contact those Aeldari?"
  - After: "How did you contact those Aeldari?"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Elantach, at last you have left your ornate cage." {n}Yrliet casts a look over the stone palace walls.{/n} "For many a turn have I sought to meet you, and yet, your servant, the one who is like the silver-haired Abelard but twice as young, has no favour for the requests of a Child of Asuryan. Take me to a place where the hearing of others will not steal the words intended for you."
  - After: "Elantach, at last." {n}Yrliet eyes the walls.{/n} "Your servant keeps me away. Somewhere private, please."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "While you were mending the wounds of this world left by the twisted ones' attack, I was able to discover... no, not Crudarach's fate. Merely traces of it. As Muaran found sanctuary under the boughs of the Lilaethan's forests, so did my other kin find refuge in a system known as the Atlas Reach. We must make a journey there with haste... before new dangers destroy the witnesses who can show me a way to the lost Crudarach, whose fate remains shrouded by the stars!"
  - After: "I found traces of Crudarach's fate. My kin sheltered in the Atlas Reach. We must go quickly, before the witnesses are lost."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I will wait for your decision with great anticipation, elantach."
  - After: "I will await your decision, elantach."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet focuses her piercing gaze on you.{/n} "Their knowledge is the sole thread that may lead me to the truth, elantach. I ask that your metal-winged ship take me along that thread before it tears under the strain of time and circumstance."
  - After: {n}Yrliet stares.{/n} "Their knowledge is my only thread to the truth. Follow it before it tears."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "No, I... I did not contact the Asuryani. I have no means to do so. But I had enough time to explore the stone jungle of your world while you were preoccupied with your urgent matters. The Path of the Outcast has taught me to observe and listen to the world around me — in this case, the throngs of mon-keigh at the port. Errant conversations, rumours, chance words — like parts of a speckled mosaic, they came together to form a hazy image. My kin were seen in the Atlas Reach, and now all we have to do is pull at the web of connections and possibilities to uncover whatever is concealed from the unseeing eye."
  - After: "I didn't; I can't. I listened to rumours in your port. My kin were seen in the Atlas Reach."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "You... will?" {n}The ice in Yrliet's eyes melts away for a moment.{/n} "Thank you, elantach. If this path indeed takes me to the truth... I will be indebted to you. A rare happening between our kinds."
  - After: "You... will?" {n}Yrliet softens.{/n} "Thank you, elantach. I'll be in your debt."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet's gaze burns through you.{/n} "I only joined you to seek out my craftworld, mon-keigh! I helped you overcome adversity and foes, at times turning my weapon against my own kin! The time has come for you to honour our pact! I will leave your palace and wait for you to give the order to embark!"
  - After: {n}Yrliet glares.{/n} "I joined you to find my craftworld! I fought my own kin for you! Honour our pact! I'll wait for your order to embark!"

A curse upon you, mon-keigh!"

  - Before: {n}The construct does not look too different from other creations of the Drukhari you have seen: an angular amalgam of unknown metal, sharp edges, and hints of wriggling living flesh.{/n}
  - After: {n}Typical Drukhari work: angular metal, wriggling flesh.{/n}

  - Before: "What—" {n}Tervantias does not get to complete his question.{/n}
  - After: "What—" {n}He's cut off.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Nonsense!" {n}Tervantias leaps up, his voice ringing with genuine rage.{/n} "This is the work of my genius! The initial data was just a resource transformed into a masterpiece by the brilliance of my mind! How dare you even comment on my creation, you mon-keigh degenerate?"

  - Before: {n}Tervantias's face stiffens into a mask of contempt but his working limbs begin to twitch nervously and his chest heaves with a mechanical creak as if he is suddenly running out of air.{/n}
  - After: {n}He sneers, but his limbs twitch and he gasps.{/n}

Oh, the pains it took me to convince the Archon to bring the spirit warriors into the Dark City. And to then conceal the evidence of the dimensional collapse that had destabilised the spire."
  - After: {n}He chuckles.{/n} "Fear is for weak minds. I got the Archon to bring the spirit warriors here, then hid the collapse that destabilised the spire."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I alone acted without fear. I delved deeper, as a scalpel delves into flesh.   - After: {n}Heinrix laughs darkly.{/n} "A warp breach in their bastion? That makes me smile."

  - Before: "Of course. My masterpiece needed an unthinkable amount of energy, but how could I let something as trifling as 'the unthinkable' stand in my way? The star you call Rykad was stolen at my behest, as were many before it."

How fascinating it is that such a paltry sacrifice as the lives of several million mon-keigh can serve something as great as my masterpiece."
  - After: {n}He gloats.{/n} "I took Santiel's Pride's sun while you fought in the arena. Millions of frozen mon-keigh, a paltry price."

Its chest erupts with a revolting squelching sound, forming a maw with claws in place of a tongue that bites its master's head off, then its serrated tentacles tear the rest of his body to bloody scraps and fall to the floor, still squirming.{/n}

  - After: "I hope you're worth it, Marazhai."
