- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: "An enigma. The project was kept secret from everyone, including the smiths. We forged fragments of it... It was a tool for controlling energies of staggering power, and it was not the Omnissiah's blessed gifts that served as its foundation. It was forbidden knowledge, knowledge that we comprehended."
  - After: "Secret even from us smiths. We forged fragments of a tool for staggering energies, from forbidden knowledge."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Let them celebrate their trifling victory. Little do they know that the Truth has already triumphed, in {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_Eufrates_ChampionOfChaos}bringing forth a mighty champion{/d}." {n}Unseen to anyone but you, Uralon's image surveys the bodies of two lean, scarlet-robed women lying on the floor.{/n} "The lot of the weak is to lay down their worthless lives to pave the way for the strong to ascend their thrones."
  - After: "Let them celebrate. The Truth triumphed, {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_Eufrates_ChampionOfChaos}bringing forth a mighty champion{/d}." {n}Uralon eyes the dead.{/n} "The weak pave the strong's way."
- **Uralon the Cruel**
  - Before: {n}Uralon chuckles.{/n} "The Inquisitor's servants are raising it to the surface as we speak. The full extent of its might is unknown even to me. In the right hands, it will lay the foundation of a new era in which the Great Four will reign in the Expanse as their champion's effort bears fruit. Your effort." {n}Uralon nods toward the two corpses.{/n} "These priestesses knew about the weapon but perished before I was able to get the truth about its nature out of them."
  - After: {n}Uralon chuckles.{/n} "The Inquisitor's servants are raising it. Through you, it will crown the Great Four." {n}He nods at the corpses.{/n} "They died silent."
- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: "A difficult thing to explain... to a {mf|layman|laywoman}. Metamorphosis phenomena occur in the object's vicinity. Sacred technology and even ordinary plasteel start to behave... wilfully. Shifting, restructuring, and altering their fundamental attributes."
  - After: "Hard to explain to a {mf|layman|laywoman}. Near it, even plasteel reshapes itself."
- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: "It's difficult... to process... Have I fulfilled my duty to the Omnissiah? May I rest now?" {n}She looks through you as though she can no longer see you.{/n}
  - After: "Is my duty done? May I rest?" {n}She stares blankly.{/n}
- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: "This place was a shelter. The Lord Inquisitor hid me here... and not only me." {n}A high-pitched groan of pain interrupts her words.{/n} "The Maimed Hunter... A figure of termination, an unknown variable. Amarnat's nemesis. I never met them, but I inferred their existence based on statistical evidence and logical conclusions. The portents of entropy foretell that the Hunter is near."
  - After: "The Inquisitor hid me here, and others." {n}She groans.{/n} "The Maimed Hunter, Amarnat's nemesis, is near."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}There is not a single wound upon her white skin, but there is no doubt that she will soon perish. Her augmetics are failing as if they have been sabotaged by some entropic influence. For a moment you consider it a sign of tech-blight, but then you refute the thought — what you are witnessing is not decay, but transformation of the matter from which the Tech-Priest's True Flesh is made.{/n}
  - After: {n}No wounds, yet she's dying: her True Flesh is transforming, not decaying.{/n}
- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: "We were continuing the work of our mentor, Archmagos Amarnat. It was his wisdom that made our toils possible." {n}Axiomantha's words render Pasqal speechless.{/n}
  - After: "We continued Archmagos Amarnat's work." {n}Pasqal is speechless.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}There is not a single wound upon her white skin. You cannot understand the reason, but she is most certainly dying, like a wilting metal flower.{/n}
  - After: {n}No wounds, yet she wilts like a metal flower.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The unit lacks clear answers. Her cognitive abilities have been damaged, but analytical data suggests a... higher validity to our identifiers being an exact match. It is not a consequence of malicious falsification. It is more akin to an act of purposeful direction."
  - After: "Her cognition is damaged, but our matching identifiers seem purposeful."
- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: "Now this half of me is dead. The rest of my mind... is fading. The sympathetic principle is insurmountable." {n}The Tech-Priest closes her eyes and starts whispering something incomprehensible, sinking deeper into the depths of oblivion.{/n}
  - After: "This half of me is dead. The rest fades." {n}She drifts off.{/n}
- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: "Are my words obscure? That is regrettable. Processing becomes difficult when you only have one half of your mind. Certain notions, data, and logical instruments were left... in the less functional part of me."
  - After: "Regrettable. Half a mind processes poorly."
- **Uralon the Cruel**
  - Before: "His petty desires and ridiculous thirst for revenge obscured the Truth from his eyes. He chose his sacrificial destiny himself when he strayed from the path charted for him and allowed his failures to make way for you, champion."
  - After: "Revenge blinded him. He strayed and made way for you, champion."
- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: "Against... anyone. Its power is absolute. The first experiments with this tech-relic were calamitous. The tech-blight... is merely its echo. Its potential is so much greater." {n}She stops, as if frightened by her own words.{/n} "It never should have fallen into the hands of the laity, but the Lord Inquisitor stole it. Its secret was procured beyond the dimensional gate, beneath the dark stars, and passed over to Amarnat. Calcazar destroyed the Messiah of Discontinuing and robbed him. And claimed the secret for himself."
  - After: "Against anyone. The tech-blight is its mere echo." {n}She stops.{/n} "Its secret came from beyond the dimensional gate. Calcazar destroyed the Messiah of Discontinuing and stole it."
- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: {n}Suddenly something clicks inside the body of one of the Omnissiah's servants. Her eyes open wide. A cramp runs through her thin lips. Her lips twist in an arch. A single word escapes them:{/n} "Yoke!"
  - After: {n}Something clicks; a Tech-Priest's eyes snap open.{/n} "Yoke!"
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "I never even knew there was a weapon! I was told of traitors, and I tracked them down! I claimed no trophies, I had no part in any dark intrigues! You think I would have wished that sneaky, scheming viper to get his hands on something so powerful? I wouldn't even trust him with my axe!"
  - After: "I never knew of a weapon! I hunted traitors. I'd not trust that viper with my axe!"
- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: "Imagine yourself gazing upon a surface of water that was disturbed by a stone an era ago, but the ripples never stop coming. That is what it felt like. The object propagated echoes of change."
  - After: "Like endless ripples from an ancient stone. Echoes of change."
- **Uralon the Cruel**
  - Before: "Wait. The manufactorum's dungeons are vast. I will lie low in them and bide my time until the moment comes for me to appear before you in the flesh again. And while I wait, I will work on this world from the inside to prepare it to accept the Truth when the time is due. One does not need armies to open the world's eyes: all it takes is to sow the seeds of corruption and wait for them to sprout of their own accord."
  - After: "I'll hide in the manufactorum's dungeons until I return in the flesh, sowing corruption meanwhile."
- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: "Knowledge will not have the capacity to be absolute until the coming of the Omnissiah. We do not know of such pre-technology, but can we claim with certainty that it never existed? Do you remember stories about—"
  - After: "Knowledge is incomplete until the Omnissiah comes. Such pre-tech may have existed. Recall—"
- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: {n}The servant of the Omnissiah freezes for a moment. You hear mechanical clicks and binharic chirring, as though unseen mechanisms in her body are struggling to run a diagnostic. After a while, the sounds die down.{/n}
  - After: {n}She freezes, chirring through a diagnostic.{/n}
- **Uralon the Cruel**
  - Before: "You are wasting your effort, champion. The Inquisitor's minions have jammed the vox-transmitters. By the time you reach the surface, his people will have slipped away with the Yoke. But worry not, for this is an outcome the Edge of Daybreak has already told you about. It will be the beginning of your ascent, not an impediment."
  - After: "Futile. His minions jammed the vox and will escape with the Yoke. As foretold, this begins your ascent."
- **Uralon the Cruel**
  - Before: "Intertwining probabilities that will give rise to a new era. The Inquisitor has used you to obtain a weapon with the power to obliterate entire worlds. Or rather a part of that weapon. He knew he was crossing the line, so he concealed his plan even from his allies: both you and the pups who called themselves Wolves. You should follow and track him, champion. The Inquisitor will likely attempt to complete the weapon and that will be the true moment of your triumph. For, when it is completed, you are going to take it."
  - After: "The Inquisitor used you to seize part of a world-killing weapon. Track him. When it's complete, take it."
- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: "He knew." {n}The woman points her finger at Thorbald's body.{/n} "He was there."
  - After: "He knew." {n}She points at Thorbald.{/n} "He was there."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal spews an angry tirade in binharic and glares at the fallen Angel of the Emperor.{/n} "Why is it that even the most capable of laypeople can never be reliable sources of information?"
  - After: {n}Pasqal curses in binharic.{/n} "Laypeople are never reliable."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix casts a grim glance at the mighty warriors, but does not contradict them, either out of agreement, or doubt about his survival were he to raise an objection.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix frowns but stays silent.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix shakes his head in amazement.{/n} "A yoke? A means of restraint... It sounds like a project on a grand, planetary scale — and this is the first I'm hearing of it. Perhaps there was a hidden purpose to my assignment besides combatting the cult and accompanying you, {name}. But why?"
  - After: {n}Heinrix shakes his head.{/n} "A planetary-scale yoke, and I never heard of it. Did my assignment hide another purpose, {name}?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Clicks are heard in the ensuing silence. For a while now, Heinrix has been trying to bring his vox-transmitter back to life — to no avail, judging by the twist to his mouth.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix's vox stays dead.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "The warp take me, what kind of ordeal has the Lord Inquisitor really dragged you into?" {n}Abelard shakes his head.{/n} "Never mind. But what am I talking about? Calcazar's links to House von Valancius obviously go back to your predecessor's time. There is no telling what other secrets Lady Theodora took with her..."
  - After: "Warp take me, what has Calcazar dragged you into?" {n}Abelard sighs.{/n} "Who knows what Lady Theodora hid?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After taking a closer look, you realise that every augment seems to have begun... mutating, developing new forms and functions not envisioned by their creators. It seems probable that this is what caused their demise.{/n}
  - After: {n}Their augments mutated into new forms. Likely what killed them.{/n}
- **Uralon the Cruel**
  - Before: {n}Uralon bares his teeth.{/n} "How I long to see the moment when you cast off your mask as a {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_GreatDeed}'hero of the Imperium'{/d} and let your true power show. Your redoubtable reputation will make your betrayal all the more bitter and unexpected to the corpse emperor's servants. Do not lament the loss of your former renown, for a different kind will take its place, one more befitting a champion."
  - After: {n}Uralon grins.{/n} "I long to see you drop your {d|Encyclopedia:CharGen_MOT_GreatDeed}'hero of the Imperium'{/d} mask. The betrayal will sting all the more."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Yoke... Such a primitive name. And yet what has been said of it piques my curiosity. A secret weapon based on forbidden knowledge and forged by the joint efforts of dozens or even hundreds of people left in ignorance..." {n}Trazyn hums contentedly.{/n} "You should find this thing — I'd like to take a closer look at it."
  - After: "The Yoke... crude name, intriguing weapon." {n}Trazyn hums.{/n} "Find it. I want a look."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "The termination of Opticon-22's life cycle was executed in a most dignified manner, I cannot deny it." {n}The Manipulus gives a slight nod.{/n} "Nevertheless, death, however noble, carries grief in its wake. Let us honour the memory of the fallen with a galvanic hymn." {n}Eogunn's vox emits a solemn, mournful binharic chime.{/n}
  - After: "Opticon-22 died with dignity." {n}Eogunn nods.{/n} "Still, a galvanic hymn for him." {n}His vox chimes mournfully.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "One should not make such hasty decisions. Diagnostic auspexes have revealed to me that the victim's life currents harbour no corruption. The sacred iron within her body functions with complete efficacy; thus, this individual is untainted by entropy."
  - After: "Too hasty. My auspexes find no corruption in her. She is untainted."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Unification... A risky, extremely laborious creation of symbiosis between identical individuals. I believed it to be a legendary technology, deemed lost. Perhaps it could have been the key to the creation of the Triasomata... I regret that we have only met now, upon your deathbed." {n}Eogunn watches the Tech-Priest without looking away.{/n}
  - After: "Unification... a lost legend, perhaps key to the Triasomata. I regret we met only at your deathbed." {n}Eogunn stares.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Astounded, Eogunn turns rigid, letting his hands drop helplessly.{/n} "This means that the laboratory on Amsanct is not the only one? The Inquisition was running a project unsanctioned by the priesthood of the Adeptus Mechanicus? Now the pieces are falling into place... now I see."
  - After: {n}Eogunn goes rigid.{/n} "So Amsanct's lab wasn't the only one? Now I see."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "You have chosen life." {n}Eogunn nods.{/n} "Knowledge is but a meagre toll for the chance to pursue your works."
  - After: "You chose life." {n}Eogunn nods.{/n} "Knowledge is a small toll."
- **Axiomantha**
  - Before: "True." {n}The Tech-Priest smiles weakly.{/n} "I found this concept to be the most rational."
  - After: "True." {n}A weak smile.{/n} "The most rational choice."

## World/Dialogs/Ch4/Eufrates/EPP_PlanetAssault/EPP_PlanetAssault

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Eufrates II lies before you, ravaged by corruption and drained by war. The Skitarii cohorts have boarded the shuttles, and the valiant militia of the Koronus Expanse are inspecting their weapons for the last time before deployment. The fearsome Space Wolves frigate, bristling with weapons, stands ready to unleash its deadly force upon the world overrun with heretics.
  - After: Corrupted Eufrates II awaits. Skitarii, militia and the Space Wolves frigate stand ready.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Shaken by what is to come, Eufrates II awaits its harsh pacification.
  - After: Eufrates II awaits its harsh pacification.

## World/Dialogs/Ch4/Eufrates/KTC_WarCouncil

- **Aishara**
  - Before: "So shall we begin our war council, or shall we wait for heretics to corrupt this planet completely?"
  - After: "Shall we begin the war council, or wait for heretics?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But in order for the threads of chance to allow us to meet and for you to fulfil your purpose, you must bring along the blade shards that wove our destinies together. Goodbye, Child of the Dawn. I will be waiting for you." {n}The voice is gone again, dissolved in the echoes of other people's thoughts.{/n}
  - After: "Bring the blade shards that bound our fates. I'll be waiting, Child of the Dawn." {n}The voice fades.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch4/Eufrates/KTC_WarCouncil/KTC_WarCouncil_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I wish to remind you that the Lord Inquisitor entrusted me with overseeing this war. You will show respect for my status."
  - After: "The Lord Inquisitor put me in charge. Respect that."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Opticon-22, how did you go from overseeing logistics to commanding armies?"
  - After: "Opticon-22, how did logistics become command?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Answer me this, Thorbald: if Opticon-22 were to come to Fenris and start ordering you around, what would you do?"
  - After: "Thorbald, what if Opticon-22 gave you orders on Fenris?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Thorbald is right. However destructive the assault might end up being, it will be nothing compared to the damage that every moment of our hesitation does to the planet."
  - After: "Thorbald is right. Hesitation hurts the planet more than any assault."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are looking at {name} von Valancius, Thorbald Ironhide."
  - After: "I am {name} von Valancius, Thorbald Ironhide."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Heresy runs rampant on Eufrates II, and you two would rather waste all your strength on bickering? Then you are nothing but fools!"
  - After: "Heresy runs rampant on Eufrates II and you bicker? Fools!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have heard enough petty quarrels for one day."
  - After: "Enough petty quarrels."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I shall now present to you the plan of our assault on Eufrates II."
  - After: "Here is my plan for assaulting Eufrates II."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why have you still not commenced a planetary assault?"
  - After: "Why no planetary assault yet?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Opticon-22, what do you propose our plan should be?"
  - After: "Opticon-22, your plan?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Thorbald, what would you do if you were in command of this operation?"
  - After: "Thorbald, what would you do in command?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I require a full report on the situation at the front."
  - After: "Report on the front."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have heard your opinions on this."
  - After: "I've heard your opinions."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What we require is total annihilation. Raze every sacred facility and chapel that our enemies could use as cover."
  - After: "Total annihilation. Raze every sacred facility and chapel they could hide in."
- **Player**
  - Before: "We will begin by bombarding the enemy's positions, then advance cautiously. We must conserve our troops."
  - After: "Bombard, then advance cautiously. Conserve troops."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Send in all our forces even if it means sustaining heavy losses. A swift onslaught is key to our victory!"
  - After: "All forces in, whatever the losses. Speed wins!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "There will be no spitting aboard my ship. Do I make myself clear, esteemed Lord Thorbald?"
  - After: "No spitting on my ship. Clear, Lord Thorbald?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Opticon-22, I must say my curiosity is piqued. The Explorators are hiding something on that planet, something you refused to show to anyone and are now loath to destroy. What is it?"
  - After: "Opticon-22, what are the Explorators hiding on that planet that you won't destroy?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "And what are your responsibilities as a special operative?"
  - After: "What does a special operative do?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You two do not get along too well, do you?"
  - After: "You two don't get along, do you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What troops can you spare to reinforce our army?"
  - After: "What troops can you spare?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The leader of the Explorator warriors appears on the bridge, and the deck trembles beneath his metal gait. He has acquired a new set of fearsome armour since the two of you last met, and his mechadendrites are now fitted with more formidable weapons of destruction.{/n} "Unit Opticon-22 initiating //identification//official greeting// procedure. Unlocking the option of strategic data exchange."
  - After: {n}The Explorator leader enters in fearsome new armour and weapons.{/n} "Opticon-22 //greeting//. Data exchange unlocked."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: {n}The Emperor's Angel who follows in his wake is clad in armour the colour of a tempestuous ocean. You hear his voice, throaty and brimming with untamed boldness and strength:{/n} "Which one of you huskaerls is {name} von Valancius? I am Thorbald Ironhide, and I wish to see the mortal who has been granted the honour of leading my pack into battle."
  - After: {n}A Space Wolf follows.{/n} "Which of you is {name} von Valancius? I am Thorbald Ironhide. Show me who leads my pack."
- **Aishara**
  - Before: "The Lord Inquisitor entrusted me with the task of forging an alliance between the assembled fleet and the forces of the Cognisance Fleet. Once this task is complete, I am to act as an observer and a special operative."
  - After: "To ally us with the Cognisance Fleet. Then I observe, as special operative."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This //command promotion//hierarchy status update// was executed following the //death//decommissioning//deconstruction// of the ship Teeth of the Wrathgear. The fleet's war conclave was operating aboard that vessel. Unit Opticon-22 received premature //rank promotion//modernisation// to Magos Dominus based on his extensive catalogue of recorded combat engagements."
  - After: "After the Teeth of the Wrathgear, the conclave's ship, was //decommissioned//, Opticon-22 became Magos Dominus for his combat record."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "May your service benefit from the updated protocols that were bestowed upon you and the new analytical data that was entrusted to your elucidation."
  - After: "May your new protocols serve you well."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "May the Omnissiah //guide//operate// this unit in his //cause//mission//algorithm// of service to Him."
  - After: "May the Omnissiah //guide// this unit."
- **Aishara**
  - Before: "I happen to have some experience with large-scale bloodshed, Rogue Trader. That, and I never fail to deliver results."
  - After: "I know bloodshed, Rogue Trader. And I deliver."
- **Aishara**
  - Before: "The militia forces have already been transferred to Opticon-22. All I have left under my command is a tactical unit explicitly instructed to carry out the Lord Inquisitor's special assignments."
  - After: "The militia went to Opticon-22. I keep only a unit for the Inquisitor's special tasks."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: {n}Thorbald takes the measure of you and nods in satisfaction.{/n} "I know the habits of a warrior when I see one. You're no indolent hjokke. Good! I give my approval — we will hunt the baseborn heretics together."
  - After: {n}Thorbald nods.{/n} "A warrior, no idle hjokke. Good! We hunt together."
- **Aishara**
  - Before: "The Lord Inquisitor will be delighted at the news that some semblance of order was established in the command. I wish you luck, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "The Lord Inquisitor will welcome some order. Good luck."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "Fenris would never need to be liberated from the Archenemy's servants! Wolf blood is indomitable! And you, {name}, should choose your words carefully lest you provoke my anger!"
  - After: "Fenris would never need liberating! Mind your words, {name}!"
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "You have not changed, Brother Thorbald — high-handed and brazen without measure, and you carry yourself on another's drekkar like it is your own."
  - After: "Still brazen, Thorbald, strutting on another's drekkar."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: {n}The Wolf bursts into booming laughter and bares his long fangs.{/n} "Such is the breed of leaders, Ulfar. We stand out. 'Tis you, Everlost, who cannot find his way when the sun is right over his head." {n}Another explosion of Thorbald's boisterous laughter drowns out Ulfar's stifled yet furious string of curses.{/n}
  - After: {n}Thorbald roars with laughter.{/n} "Leaders stand out, Ulfar. You're the Everlost, lost at noon." {n}Ulfar curses.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Thorbald's face turns purple, but he cannot come up with a retort. Opticon-22 lowers his head repentantly and lets out a binharic trill. Neither of them can find the words to rebuff your pointed accusation.{/n}
  - After: {n}Neither Thorbald nor Opticon-22 can rebut you.{/n}
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "What good is another war council with a cog-priest who knows not the joys of battle, who cut off his parts and replaced them with augments to please his all-knowing master? He will propose again a cowardly plan unworthy of warriors as is the custom of his brethren—"
  - After: "Another council with a cog-priest who'll propose another cowardly plan—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Registering a display of //impertinence//data insufficiency// in regard to the //military craft//eradication methods// of the Adeptus Mechanicus."
  - After: "Registering //impertinence//."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "There is a //conflict//critical error//categorical lack of understanding of the imperatives of this operation// within our chain of command. Unit Thorbald Ironhide is in favour of the strategy of mass destruction, which would constitute an unacceptable violation of the Rite of Operation. Every square metre of the manufactorums is //sacred//of high productivity value//."
  - After: "//Conflict// in command. Thorbald wants mass destruction, violating the Rite of Operation. The manufactorums are //sacred//."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "Which is why the cog-priest is so intent on hindering and sabotaging our assault by refusing us forces and landing drekkars. But Thorbald Ironhide won't fight on the terms of priests! If my battle plan is rejected, the Omnissiah's servants can retake the planet themselves! Maybe they think their lives mean nothing compared to their precious cathedrals, but a Wolf knows what his life is worth!"
  - After: "So he denies us forces and drekkars. Reject my plan and the priests can retake it themselves!"
- **Aishara**
  - Before: "I'm afraid the Lord Inquisitor did not give me the authority to elaborate on this matter."
  - After: "I'm not authorised to say."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Our strategic analysis points toward a full-scale offensive as the optimal course of action. The losses among the //troops//insignificant personnel//laity// will be numerous but will not exceed acceptable parameters. Replenishing such losses will be less arduous than repairing the damage that may otherwise come to the manufactorums."
  - After: "Optimal: full offensive. //Laity// losses acceptable; easier to replace than manufactorums."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Eufrates II is a forge world. Manufactorums and extractiums take up most of its surface. Upon //corrupting them//disrupting their production algorithm//, the heretics enhanced their ranks with possessed mechanisms and //false//defective//traitorous// Skitarii whose protocols were disfigured with indoctrinating scrap-code."
  - After: "This forge world's manufactorums are //corrupted//. Heretics field possessed machines and scrap-coded Skitarii."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "We may outnumber the enemy, but ours is a poor warband. All it has is steel kaerls of the Omnissiah and scantly trained serfs from across the Expanse. While our foe is the detestable but nevertheless deadly putrid-hearted traitors from the ranks of the Word Bearers. And their vessels protect the Machine Cathedral from orbit."
  - After: "We outnumber them, but with steel kaerls and serfs. They have Word Bearers, and ships guarding the Machine Cathedral."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "Choose your strategy wisely. It's not every day you get to heed the advice of a seasoned warrior, one chosen by the Allfather himself to bring death to the foes of Humanity."
  - After: "Choose wisely. Heed the Allfather's chosen warrior."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Analysing... This statement is true. The consequences of the heretical //corruption//disruption of the procedural cycle// are nearing critical levels. In order to prevent them from surpassing those levels, Unit Opticon-22 is prepared to nullify certain protocols related to preservation of //sacred relics//high-priority production facilities//."
  - After: "True. //Corruption// nears critical. Opticon-22 will waive some relic-preservation protocols."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: {n}The Space Wolf bellows with unpleasant laughter.{/n} "I would like to see him try... Fine, I hear you. No one will accuse Thorbald Ironhide of disrespecting the masters of the house where he arrived as a guest. You will hear no more arguing from me — only silence. I will kill the heretics in the manner chosen by the esteemed cog-priest."
  - After: {n}The Wolf laughs.{/n} "Let him try... Fine. I'll respect my hosts and fight the cog-priest's way."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Thorbald looks down on you with an expression of wry amusement. Opticon-22 is silent, but you can still feel the disapproval in the rattles coming from his vox.{/n}
  - After: {n}Thorbald looks amused. Opticon-22's vox rattles.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The first step is obvious — we eliminate the Machine Cathedral's orbital support. But what planetary assault strategy will you choose following the destruction of the enemy void fleet?"
  - After: "First, kill the Machine Cathedral's orbital support. Then, what ground strategy?"
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "Your plan bores me. This is not the Space Wolves' way of war. But such cowardly strategies are the limit of the Omnissiah's cog-kaerls, so you have my approval."
  - After: "Boring, not the Wolves' way. But you have my approval."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "Ha! The Space Wolves respect a good onslaught! Your huskaerls better be loyal enough to charge into the fire without faltering!"
  - After: "Ha! Wolves respect an onslaught! Charge without faltering!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Thorbald merely scoffs in response, and Opticon-22 produces a short binharic litany. Despite their united displeasure at your words, they do not look at all conciliated.{/n}
  - After: {n}Both scoff, unswayed.{/n}
- **Aishara**
  - Before: "Now let us move on to discussing how we intend to kill the heretics."
  - After: "Now, how do we kill the heretics?"
- **Aishara**
  - Before: "The Lord Inquisitor will be pleased to learn that his authority was not questioned at this war council."
  - After: "The Lord Inquisitor will be pleased his authority held."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: {n}Thorbald's face reddens, and he rumbles in a hollow voice,{/n} "I do not wish us to feud on the eve of battle. Very well. The Wolves will fight the way the cog-priest deems fit."
  - After: {n}Thorbald reddens.{/n} "No feuds before battle. We'll fight the cog-priest's way."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Request approved. Unit {name} von Valancius is authorised to issue decisions of the highest execution priority. Unit Opticon-22 standing by for instructions."
  - After: "Approved. {name} von Valancius has top priority. Awaiting instructions."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Analysing... This statement is false. The sacred assembly halls require machine //healing//repairs//, not further destruction." {n}Opticon-22 lowers his head in an unrelenting gesture.{/n}
  - After: "False. The sacred halls need //repairs//." {n}Opticon-22 won't budge.{/n}
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "What's this? A show of character?" {n}Thorbald growls and locks his indignant gaze with yours.{/n} "Fine, I will respect your wishes, warlord. But the bitter taste of suspicion burns my mouth." {n}With pointed contempt, he steps away from Aishara.{/n}
  - After: "Backbone?" {n}Thorbald glares.{/n} "Fine, warlord. But I'm suspicious." {n}He steps away from Aishara.{/n}
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "Hear, hear! I can smell your killer instinct, {name}! Let us break their spirit!"
  - After: "Hear, hear! Let's break them, {name}!"
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "Rein in the impudent priest while there's still time. Or this battle will end in disgraceful defeat."
  - After: "Rein in the priest, or we lose in disgrace."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Are you having another fight, gentlemen? How predictable." {n}A woman in heavy armour walks onto the bridge cloaked in an air of superiority. You remember seeing her before — in the retinue of Xavier Calcazar when he barged into your chambers after your Magnae Accessio.{/n} "Thank you for not starting without me. Acolyte Aishara, dispatched by the Lord Inquisitor to facilitate the operation on Eufrates II. My role on this war council is that of an advisor."
  - After: "Fighting again? Predictable." {n}An armoured woman from Calcazar's retinue enters.{/n} "Acolyte Aishara, the Lord Inquisitor's advisor for Eufrates II."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}{d|Encyclopedia:Conviction_Heretical3OrMore}A silky whisper weaves words{/d} into a kind of unholy pattern in your mind:{/n} "Minions of a false god. Blind in their faith. No unity among them. They will never learn the Truth... but you will. I will show you the path, Child of the Dawn, but in order to walk that path, you must hide our intentions behind a facade of loyalty to the corpse emperor. For now, learn about the false believers' plan and prepare. Now is the time to listen. The time to act will come later, and when it comes, I will tell you."
  - After: {n}{d|Encyclopedia:Conviction_Heretical3OrMore}A silky whisper weaves words{/d}:{/n} "Blind fools. Feign loyalty to the corpse emperor, learn their plan, and wait. I will tell you when to act."
- **Aishara**
  - Before: {n}Aishara raises an eyebrow and chuckles.{/n} "My presence here is entirely unaffected by your approval or your objections, Rogue Trader. But I'm pleased to know you endorse my appointment to this position."
  - After: {n}Aishara chuckles.{/n} "Your approval doesn't matter. But thanks."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest's vox creaks stubbornly:{/n} "Request denied. The Omnissiah's //mysteries//procedures// conducted on Eufrates II are to remain undisclosed according to the //protocol//vow// of preservation of the hallowed from the profane."
  - After: {n}His vox creaks:{/n} "Denied. The Omnissiah's //mysteries// here stay secret."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "This is why on Fenris we have the priests follow the warriors, not the other way around. The priests never think about the battle ahead, only their tenets and taboos. But a Wolf — a Wolf must think only of battle and his enemy's death, not about preserving cathedrals or counting the trophies that await him."
  - After: "On Fenris, priests follow warriors. A Wolf thinks of battle, not cathedrals."
- **Aishara**
  - Before: {n}Aishara casts a suspicious glance at you.{/n} "An interesting reaction, Rogue Trader. Not the kind of reception I've had anywhere else. Granted, I am an acolyte of the Inquisition, but I haven't even begun to get inside your head yet, or indeed considered it. Perhaps some other time. We have work to do right now."
  - After: {n}Aishara eyes you.{/n} "Interesting. I haven't even tried to read your mind. Later. We have work."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A cackle comes from inside your head.{/n} "Only you can hear my voice, Child. Do not talk to me. Just pay attention." {n}You feel the intruding presence recede to the periphery of your mind, to bide its time there.{/n}
  - After: {n}A cackle.{/n} "Only you hear me, Child. Don't speak. Watch." {n}It recedes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You feel the intrusive presence recede to the periphery of your mind, to bide its time there.{/n}
  - After: {n}The presence recedes, waiting.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The unholy cackle fills your mind again.{/n} "The travails of mortals are so amusing. Wandering in the dark, ignorant of the paths open to them and of their own fate. How pathetic! They are not your equals, for you know your way. It is a path littered with the bodies of believers in the Truth: an acceptable sacrifice in the name of your future greatness."
  - After: {n}The cackle returns.{/n} "Blind mortals. Your path is paved with their bodies, a fair price for greatness."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix and Aishara exchange glances, but do not say a word. You cannot help but notice the furrow that forms on the Interrogator's forehead at the sight of his colleague.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix frowns at Aishara.{/n}
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "I would rain down vengeful skies upon the enemy. I would plough the land of Eufrates II with shells, shatter their defences, level the fortified towers, throw their host into disarray... And in that whirlwind of fury, I would lead my glorious pack to pave a path of blood for the cog-kaerls."
  - After: "I'd shell Eufrates II flat and lead my pack to carve a bloody path for the cog-kaerls."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman's words are drowned out by your growing headache: irritation, contempt, and disappointment rack your mind like a three-tailed whip, accompanied by a hundred {d|Encyclopedia:Conviction_Heretical3OrMore}furious whispers{/d}{/n}: "The time of daybreak is almost upon us, and you have failed to make the correct choice at the crossroads of fate! The Truth that is hidden from the unseeing minions of the corpse emperor could have illuminated your sight, granted you... boundless freedom. But you proved to be weak. You would not fight, you would not listen... A child unworthy of the Truth. A {mf|blind boy|lost girl} unworthy of freedom!" {n}The alien presence melts away from your awareness like sticky sludge, no longer willing to waste its word on one such as you.{/n}
  - After: {n}A headache and {d|Encyclopedia:Conviction_Heretical3OrMore}furious whispers{/d}{/n}: "You chose wrong and spurned the Truth! A {mf|blind boy|lost girl} unworthy of freedom!" {n}The presence oozes away.{/n}
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: {n}Thorbald raises his gaze to look at your psyber-raven circling over the bridge. The Wolf smiles broadly.{/n} "On Fenris, only the worthiest are granted the company of such creatures. Since you have the will to handle one, your courage must rival that of a Rune Priest. The two of us should see eye to eye."
  - After: {n}Thorbald grins at your psyber-raven.{/n} "Only the worthiest keep those on Fenris. We'll get along."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "A tragic turn of events leading to a new beginning. May your path of Knowledge, which lies through the thorns of entropy, be blessed by the Machine God."
  - After: "From tragedy, a new beginning. The Machine God bless your path."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Our forces have secured minor footholds on the surface but are unable to deliver an effective blow to the //headquarters//operations centre// of the profaners in the Machine Cathedral at the heart of Manufactorum Sigma-S-13. According to the available data, it is the current location of the //arch-heretic//termination target// — the {g|Encyclopedia:DarkApostle}Dark Apostle{/g} Uralon the Cruel."
  - After: "We hold footholds but can't strike the Machine Cathedral in Manufactorum Sigma-S-13, lair of the {g|Encyclopedia:DarkApostle}Dark Apostle{/g} Uralon the Cruel."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "There is no surprise in my heart — the Inquisition is, as always, too ashamed of its dark deeds to reveal them to honourable fighters." {n}Thorbald makes a show of spitting on the floor.{/n}
  - After: "The Inquisition always hides its dark deeds." {n}Thorbald spits.{/n}
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "You read hearts like they're inscribed with runes, {name}." {n}Thorbald lets out a mocking chuckle.{/n} "'Tis true, my brothers and I grow tired of this cog-priest and his naysaying. For whatever reason, he thinks himself our lord."
  - After: "You read hearts, {name}." {n}He chuckles.{/n} "We're sick of this cog-priest lording it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I concur with this statement. Given that the //military action//sacred purgative crusade//eradication procedure// is taking place on a world devoted to the Machine God, Unit Opticon-22 insists on his privileged status in the matter of strategy selection."
  - After: "Concur. On a Machine God world, Opticon-22 claims priority on strategy."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "Did you think these words would fill me with fear? The Wolves are here because we wish to bring death to the heretics, not because your Lord Inquisitor commands it."
  - After: "Scared? We're here to kill heretics, not for your Inquisitor."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Request denied. Unit Xavier Calcazar lacks the authority to determine the fate of a sacred Adeptus Mechanicus world."
  - After: "Denied. Calcazar has no authority over a sacred Mechanicus world."

## World/Dialogs/Ch4/Eufrates/Torbald_ForgeHeart/Torbald_ForgeHeart_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "What is Uralon after? What is he trying to unearth?"
  - After: "What is Uralon digging for?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Ulfar, we set out to hunt the beast."
  - After: "Ulfar, we hunt the beast."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Have you encountered Uralon before?"
  - After: "Met Uralon before?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Whom did you send your brothers after?"
  - After: "Who are your brothers hunting?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What manner of witchcraft was he attempting back there?"
  - After: "What witchcraft was that?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not approve of this plan."
  - After: "I disapprove of this plan."
- **Player**
  - Before: "How do I get to Uralon?"
  - After: "How do I reach Uralon?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "If Ulfar kills Doomscream, will that prove that the Baleful Howl lives?"
  - After: "Would killing Doomscream prove the Baleful Howl lives?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Don't you dare give me orders!"
  - After: "Don't give me orders!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Ulfar, my party is already full."
  - After: "Ulfar, my party is full."
- **Player**
  - Before: "For the Emperor! Watch yourselves out there."
  - After: "For the Emperor! Be careful."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A glorious fight awaits! Take heed with the silver-tongued traitor, for he is old, sly, and strong. But, by the Allfather, the Wolves will spill rivers of his blood today!" {n}The horrific display of profane sorcery appears to have filled Thorbald with joy and anticipation rather than fear.{/n}
  - After: "A glorious fight! Beware the sly traitor!" {n}Thorbald looks joyful.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Do not ask, for I know not myself. Calcazar treats his allies like a Fenrisian mushroom farmer treats his produce — he keeps them in the dark and feeds them shit. He didn't see fit to enlighten us about the secrets of Eufrates II, but 'tis no matter. Whatever it is, we mustn't let the loathsome malefic claim it."
  - After: "I know not. Calcazar keeps allies in the dark and feeds them shit. The malefic mustn't have it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Halbrandt, you stick to the original plan! Take two brothers and go after Doomscream. Our scouts report that he took refuge here in these depths after being defeated in battle on the approach to the Machine Cathedral. I want to take the unholy tin can that holds his traitorous brain back to Fenris. Good hunting!"
  - After: "Halbrandt, take two brothers after Doomscream. He fled into these depths. I want his tin can on Fenris!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You're a brave one, and not easily deterred! Good! Then find a way to reach the tunnelling platform while we give the mangy sorcerer something to worry about." {n}Thorbald exchanges glances with his warriors, and you could swear they all smile in anticipation inside their helmets.{/n}
  - After: "Brave! Reach the tunnelling platform while we distract the sorcerer." {n}The Wolves grin.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Tread lightly when facing him, young brother. Yes, the beast is mad and hideous, but he is withal mighty, old, and graced with the Archenemy's profane patronage. His hateful sermons abound with malefictions, and his weapon claimed the lives of hundreds during the assault. We grievously wounded him, true, but we haven't seen the last of this foe."
  - After: "Careful, young brother. He's mad, mighty and Archenemy-blessed. Wounded, not finished."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No, or else his head wouldn't still be attached to his neck. But my pack has heard plenty about his strength and ignominious misdoings. One can see the evidence of his malefactions all across the Koronus Expanse like bear tracks upon fresh snow. We stalked him and looked for a chance to clamp our jaws around his throat, but the craven knows well how to hide behind the backs of his heretical lackeys."
  - After: "No, or he'd be headless. The coward hides behind lackeys."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "He wished to wake the tunnelling behemoth. If you hunger for my thoughts, Uralon is searching for something down below, in the manufactorum's deepest halls. My warriors destroyed the energy fount and silenced the drill, but the detestable malefic still found a way to revive it with his heinous magics."
  - After: "He woke the tunnelling behemoth. Uralon seeks something in the deepest halls. We broke its power; his magic revived the drill."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Our mortal foe lurks within this den of heresy. A Helbrute by the name of Doomscream, an ancient and vicious traitor. He barred our advance when we were approaching the Machine Cathedral and felled hundreds of brave champions. A terrible wound he took, but the beast still escaped our grasp. 'Tis time we cornered him and ended his vile existence!"
  - After: "Doomscream, an ancient Helbrute. He killed hundreds at the Machine Cathedral and fled wounded. Time to end him!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That's for you to sniff out, {name}! Perhaps there's a way around. We will give you enough time to look."
  - After: "Sniff it out, {name}! We'll buy you time."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Well, what are we to do, {name}? 'Tis not our place to whimper that the Allfather has sent us a fight different from the one we saw in our sweet dreams."
  - After: "What can we do, {name}? We fight the battle the Allfather sends."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Then you will go with Halbrandt, Ulfar. If fortune favours you in combat, he will be witness to your feat, and if not, he will aid you in battle."
  - After: "Then go with Halbrandt, Ulfar. He'll witness or aid you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And I've regretted it ever since. Brother Ulfar has already marched toward his death a dozen times, and only the Allfather's eye kept him from meeting a gruesome end." {n}Thorbald grins in approval.{/n}
  - After: "And I've regretted it. Only the Allfather keeps Ulfar alive." {n}Thorbald grins.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If it comes to pass, I will be the first to raise a cup to the proud name of that ferocious pack."
  - After: "Then I'll toast that fierce pack first."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You feel a sinister grin blossom somewhere beyond your reason's edge. The familiar voice intrudes upon your train of thought again.{/n} "Blood will be spilt indeed, but the warrior is mistaken as to its source. Allow him to relish that lie born out of ignorance. Allow him to believe that the Dark Apostle will fall by his hand and yours. My hour is drawing near. I will appear again, one last time, when the moment comes to make your mouth speak with the voice of the Truth."
  - After: {n}The familiar voice returns, grinning:{/n} "Blood will spill, but not whose he thinks. Let him believe. I'll return one last time to speak the Truth through you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A fine thing to hear! The sorcerer will fall, for he can't but fall." {n}Thorbald nods his approval, unaware that he wasn't at all who you were talking to.{/n}
  - After: "Good! The sorcerer will fall." {n}Thorbald doesn't know you meant someone else.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Don't let your temper get the better of you, warrior. I had no intention to slight your honour but to warn you." {n}Thorbald frowns, unaware that he wasn't at all who you were talking to.{/n}
  - After: "Easy. It was a warning." {n}Thorbald doesn't know you meant someone else.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Borrowed thoughts clear out of your mind. You know the things they spoke of are true. They will be back one last time at the crossroads of fate where you will have to make the choice that decides everything.{/n}
  - After: {n}The voice leaves. It will return at the final crossroads.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Another blasphemy. They are too many to count now." {n}Pasqal's dry voice is rattling like a heavy vehicle's chain track. His visor lights up a blinding green, then blue, and you hear a metallic moan coming from everywhere. It is as though the manufactorum itself is being tortured.{/n}
  - After: "Another blasphemy." {n}Pasqal's visor flares. The manufactorum moans.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Malignant, blasphemous sorcery, supplanting the pure current of the Motive Force." {n}Wrathful sparks of static flare across Eogunn's beard, and you hear a metallic groan echoing from everywhere. As though the very arches of the manufactorum chime in with the Manipulus, raising a wail fraught with fury and anguish.{/n}
  - After: "Sorcery supplanting the Motive Force." {n}Eogunn's beard sparks. The manufactorum groans.{/n}
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Doomscream? He hides in this den? Step aside, Halbrandt! I will be the one to slay it! I claim this quarry for the Baleful Howl!"
  - After: "Doomscream? Step aside, Halbrandt! He's the Baleful Howl's quarry!"
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Doomscream? He hides in this den? I wish to slay him for the glory of my pack! Aett-Vater, take me into your band! We will track this beast down and fell him before Halbrandt can!"
  - After: "Doomscream? I'll slay him for my pack! Aett-Vater, take me along!"
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "Worry not for the Rogue Trader, Thorbald. I've seen {mf|him|her} in action — it's the heretic who best beware meeting {mf|him|her}."
  - After: "I've seen {mf|him|her} fight, Thorbald. Pity the heretic who meets {mf|him|her}."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "The generous Thorbald honoured me with a place aboard his landing drekkar so that the Baleful Howl could split the skies over Eufrates II."
  - After: "Thorbald gave the Baleful Howl a place on his drekkar."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar laughs heartily.{/n} "Then we have work to do! Do not dally, Aett-Vater, and you might just catch up to us!"
  - After: {n}Ulfar laughs.{/n} "Keep up, Aett-Vater!"

  - Before: {n}The sorcerer does not turn his head as his voice rolls over the room:{/n} "I see you, mortal thing. I sense your meek mind."
  - After: {n}Without turning:{/n} "I see you, mortal. I sense your meek mind."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "Will this do?" {n}Thorbald takes aim and sends a bolt right into the sorcerer's back.{/n} "Hey, you foul-blooded spawn of a worm-ridden womb! We've come to rip your guts out!"
  - After: "Will this do?" {n}Thorbald shoots the sorcerer.{/n} "Oi, worm-spawn! We want your guts!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sorcerer's voice vibrates unnaturally, seething with anger and contempt:{/n} "Ignorant creature. Your pitiful ridicule offends my ears."
  - After: {n}The sorcerer seethes:{/n} "Your ridicule offends me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sorcerer scoffs. His deep, unnaturally vibrating voice causes your insides to shrink:{/n} "What good is the name of a rotting corpse propped upon the Golden Throne? It carries no fear for the disciples of the true faith."
  - After: {n}The sorcerer scoffs:{/n} "A throne-corpse's name doesn't frighten the faithful."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sorcerer reluctantly turns his burning gaze upon you.{/n} "So you are the one who was so eager to meet me and your own demise? Rejoice, Brother Twilight. Today, you become the new Rogue Trader."
  - After: {n}The sorcerer turns.{/n} "Rejoice, Brother Twilight: today you become Rogue Trader."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You know my name well. I am Uralon the Cruel, Breaker of Misbelievers, Truthspeaker, Triumphator of Faith, {g|Encyclopedia:DarkApostle}Dark Apostle{/g} of the blessed Word Bearers Legion. Kneel and offer a prayer of gratitude, for your death could not bear a worthier name."
  - After: "I am Uralon the Cruel, {g|Encyclopedia:DarkApostle}Dark Apostle{/g} of the Word Bearers. Kneel."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Death for the glory of the True Gods is a blessed fate for any believer, so why would I rob them of it? Every martyr who perishes in Their name only empowers their reign. I was tasked with a different mission — to make the Koronus Expanse behold the sheer impotence of its most eminent protector."
  - After: "Martyrs bless the True Gods. My mission: shame the Koronus Expanse's protector."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I will keep this from you so that you may perish in the darkness of ignorance. Pathetic. Your master didn't even tell you the reason why he sent you to face your death. And neither will I make this poisoned cup any easier to drink."
  - After: "Die ignorant. Your master never told you why. Nor will I."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "With joy in my heart!" {n}Thorbald points his weapon, and his shot strikes sparks off Uralon's pauldron.{/n} "You are a negotiator after my own heart."
  - After: "Gladly!" {n}Thorbald's shot sparks off Uralon's pauldron.{/n} "A negotiator after my heart."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sorcerer lets out a chilling laugh.{/n} "Save your feeble lies, for they are unworthy of my ears. I can see into the souls of mortals, and there is nothing in yours but confusion and fear."
  - After: {n}The sorcerer laughs.{/n} "No lies. I see only fear in your soul."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sorcerer's disdainful voice deteriorates into a feral rasp.{/n} "When you fall, I will find your soul in the warp and flay it clean of this cloak of arrogance and obtuseness you have wrapped yourself in."
  - After: {n}The sorcerer rasps.{/n} "When you fall, I'll flay your soul in the warp."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Very well. Kneel and pledge yourself to the True Gods of the warp, for great revelations are a reward for the faithful." {n}He gestures at you imperiously.{/n}
  - After: "Then kneel to the True Gods for revelation." {n}He gestures imperiously.{/n}
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: {n}Thorbald nods at his weapon.{/n} "I doubt you intend to obey, but I will still advise against it..."
  - After: {n}Thorbald nods at his weapon.{/n} "I'd advise against it."
- **Thorbald Ironhide**
  - Before: "I can tell you have tasted the mjod of the skjalds. 'Tis doubly satisfying to kill a foe after shaming him with honourable words of scorn."
  - After: "Skjald's talk! Killing a shamed foe is doubly sweet."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}With a solemn gesture of his hands, Uralon thunders in fury,{/n} "Let those who blaspheme against the True Gods beg forgiveness in vain, let their lips be sealed, let their hands be severed, let their souls be reaped and scourged!"
  - After: {n}Uralon thunders:{/n} "Let blasphemers be silenced, severed, scourged!"
- **Kunrad Voigtvir**
  - Before: {n}No longer able to control his temper, Voigtvir exclaims,{/n} "You did me a favour by coming here! I would like to pass a few words to the late Theodora — will you kindly grant me this request?"
  - After: {n}Voigtvir snaps:{/n} "Good of you to come! Carry my message to the late Theodora?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Silence!" {n}The giant's voice shakes the walls.{/n} "Your witless attempts to insult one another are interrupting my prayer to the True Gods!"
  - After: "Silence!" {n}The walls shake.{/n} "You interrupt my prayer!"
- **Kunrad Voigtvir**
  - Before: {n}Voigtvir's deformed features twist into a bloodthirsty smile.{/n} "Yes, master. I will rectify my mistake and reclaim what was stolen."
  - After: {n}Voigtvir grins.{/n} "Yes, master. I'll reclaim what was stolen."
- **Kunrad Voigtvir**
  - Before: {n}Voigtvir cocks his head sharply like a bird, and laughs mockingly.{/n} "I am on a path to greatness, {name}. True power, of the kind you and Theodora could only dream of. The Edge of Daybreak promised to weave me a truly remarkable fate!"
  - After: {n}Voigtvir laughs.{/n} "To power, {name}. The Edge of Daybreak promised me greatness!"
- **Kunrad Voigtvir**
  - Before: "You don't have the right to offer me pardons or deals. You're a fake!"
  - After: "No deals from you. You're a fake!"
- **Kunrad Voigtvir**
  - Before: "An empty threat. I have the upper hand this time. In my next prayer to the Dark Gods, I will thank them for letting me destroy another Rogue Trader of the von Valancius line."
  - After: "Empty threat. Another von Valancius dies today."
- **Kunrad Voigtvir**
  - Before: "I say it every time I pray to the Dark Gods!"
  - After: "I say it in every prayer to the Dark Gods!"
- **Kunrad Voigtvir**
  - Before: "Indeed. I have nothing to say to a corpse."
  - After: "Indeed. Nothing to say to a corpse."
- **Kunrad Voigtvir**
  - Before: {n}The same cannot be said about Kunrad Voigtvir who stands at his side. His completely mutated turquoise eyes flash upon seeing you. He flinches but remains silent, hesitant to interrupt the ritual.{/n}
  - After: {n}Kunrad Voigtvir, beside him, glares silently.{/n}
- **Kunrad Voigtvir**
  - Before: "If only you knew what powerful weapon awaits us down below! With it, we will make the entire Expanse—"
  - After: "The weapon below will make the Expanse—"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sacred words sustained by your indomitable faith illuminate the air and send a mighty echo across the room. So great is their strength that the sorcerer's words drown within and the currents of heretical power swirling around the drill begin to ebb. Once the final words of the prayer escape your lips, righteous light envelops the drill, washing away the unhallowed taint. The sorcerer, scorched by the radiance of the Emperor Himself, growls in pain and rage.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your prayer drowns his words. Holy light cleanses the drill; the sorcerer growls in pain.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Once Calcazar's treasure has been stolen, his secret hoards plundered, and his name shamed, the dogs of the false emperor will see the Truth. No one will protect them. No one will heed their pleas. Only by bowing to the masters of the Immaterium will they earn the right to live."
  - After: "With Calcazar's treasure stolen and name shamed, the Imperium's dogs must bow to the warp."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The corrupted servants of the Deus Mechanicus scuttle around the heretic, muttering twisted prayers of ignition in attempts to persuade the Omnissiah's majestic beast to awaken and rend the world's flesh.{/n}
  - After: {n}Corrupted Mechanicus servants try to wake the drill.{/n}
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah's earnest laughter resounds through the shaft. She wipes her eyes, ignoring the looks of bewilderment.{/n} "You? Death? Oh, Undying Emperor..."
  - After: {n}Kibellah laughs.{/n} "You? Death? Oh, Undying Emperor..."

## World/Dialogs/Ch4/Footfall/Chaplain/Chaplain_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: "So you have been put in charge? A curious choice."
  - After: "You're in charge? Curious choice."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is your opinion on the situation on the station?"
  - After: "What do you make of the station?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Long time no see, Chaplain. What are you doing here?"
  - After: "Long time, Chaplain. Why are you here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What, Incendia decided to spare you?"
  - After: "Incendia spared you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How fares Denz's young heiress, Adelia?"
  - After: "How is Denz's heiress, Adelia?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "So I'm running things now. I'm running things till some big old reverend of a higher rank than mine shows up, tells me to get lost, and takes over. It's an embarrassment for the head of a mission to have scars all over his face, making it plain for all to see that he did ungodly things in the past."
  - After: "I lead until a higher reverend replaces me. A scarred mission head — embarrassing."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As he sees you, he bows — respectfully but none too gracefully, as if he is not used to making the deferential gesture.{/n} "May Drusus watch over you, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. I never thought I'd see a Rogue Trader in this kind of establishment, especially in these troubled times."
  - After: {n}He bows awkwardly.{/n} "Drusus watch over you, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. A Rogue Trader here, now?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As you approach, he bows deferentially.{/n} "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, it's nice to see that Saint Drusus has protected your neck from the heretics and the xenos since we last met. Shame how it's always sad events that bring us together. The last time was at a funeral, and now it feels like half of Footfall needs a memorial service."
  - After: {n}He bows.{/n} "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, safe still. Last time a funeral; now half of Footfall needs one."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To the children of the Emperor who make generous donations to our godly cause, we gladly gift specks of His gracious light embedded in our relics."
  - After: "Generous donors receive His light in our relics."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Shadows have made their home under Chaplain's eyes.{/n} "If Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship has something to say to the Drusian mission, you can count on having my ear. Reverend Hieronymus's demise has left me... the senior missionary on Footfall, I suppose. I'm authorised to speak on behalf of my brothers and sisters."
  - After: {n}Chaplain looks weary.{/n} "With Reverend Hieronymus dead, I lead the Drusian mission on Footfall, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The imposing man covered head to toe in scars is hard to mistake for anyone else. You are looking at Chaplain, confessor to the late Denz Bellardo, whose funeral now seems like an eternity ago. His arms are crossed as he surveys the room with a gloomy expression.{/n}
  - After: {n}Chaplain, scarred confessor to the late Denz Bellardo, surveys the room gloomily.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Chaplain jerks his chin up defiantly.{/n} "Honestly? Perhaps this began as a cleansing, but since day one, it's looked more like a frenzy of fanaticism. Granted, people with a clear conscience have always been few and far between on Footfall. But is that a reason to exterminate everyone for the pettiest infractions?"
  - After: {n}Chaplain lifts his chin.{/n} "A cleansing turned fanatical frenzy. Footfall's no saint, but exterminate everyone for petty sins?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Same as always, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. Bringing the Emperor's light to the lowly and downtrodden. And I have my hands full here on Footfall — the station's teeming with hungry, maimed, and frightened people."
  - After: "Same as always, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship: the Emperor's light for the downtrodden. Footfall's full of hungry, frightened people."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Ecclesiarchy once tried to make a decent preacher out of me, but fainthearted and brash young brat that I was, I decided that wasn't the life for me. I traded a worthy life in the Emperor's light for greed and what I thought of as freedom at the time. I became a pirate, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship."
  - After: "The Ecclesiarchy tried to make me a preacher, but I chose greed. I became a pirate, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm known simply as Chaplain. I'm a missionary of Saint Drusus. I do sermons, public prayers, and funeral services for the lowly and destitute. I have to say it's been mostly funeral services of late... But perhaps you're more interested to know how a priest got so many battle scars." {n}He chuckles as he looks at his arms, which are covered in pale white stripes.{/n}
  - After: "Just Chaplain, missionary of Saint Drusus. Mostly funerals lately. You'll wonder about the scars." {n}He chuckles at his arms.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I do. A grand man he was, with a strength of character that was only rivalled by the fervour of his faith. It was he who ordained me... ordained me properly, not in the pirate fashion. He taught me a lot, even though I didn't always agree with him. It will be a long time before the Expanse sees another servant of the Emperor quite like him."
  - After: "I do. A grand, fervent man. He ordained me and taught me much. There's none like him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What he did to Her Ladyship and her kin was, of course, cruel and criminal... But he was pursuing a grand goal, a goal of his calibre. He was trying to wrest an entire sector, an entire Rogue Trader dynasty from the clutches of depravity. I hope that one great sacrilege does not taint the memory of his supreme goal and his other good deeds. After all, he never made a secret of having a blemished soul, just like the rest of us. None are unsullied."
  - After: "What he did to Her Ladyship's kin was criminal, but he meant to save a dynasty from depravity. None are unsullied."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I'm going to miss him. I hope I can live up to his memory and be at least half as fervent as him in bringing Saint Drusus's word to those in need of redemption."
  - After: "I'll miss him. I hope to be half as fervent."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A warm smile brightens Chaplain's rough features.{/n} "Safe and sound in my care, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Barely any time has passed, and I already think of her as my own, and the girl herself clings to me. She took to learning the ways of voidfaring with gusto, and she is already better at numbers than me — a true trade captain in the making!"
  - After: {n}Chaplain smiles.{/n} "Safe with me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Like my own daughter — a future trade captain!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I hid her somewhere safe for now. It's a bad time for the girl to be on Footfall — she has seen enough woe and blood as it is. More than enough."
  - After: "Hidden safely. She's seen enough blood."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "The laws of death worlds can be surprisingly unique at times. But for the home of the Space Wolves, the Emperor Himself commanded that special customs be established... ones that may be beyond the understanding of ordinary people."
  - After: "The Emperor decreed special customs for the Space Wolves' home world."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have done many unclean deeds and seen many unsettling things. And I have become a sincere believer — imagine that. Deadly battles and my comrades' nightly confessions of their atrocities did for me what my mentors couldn't. Who else could they confess to? I knew the words of the prayer, if nothing else. That was how I became the ship's chaplain. Then I renounced my criminal ways altogether. I died as a pirate and was reborn as a missionary: thus commanded Saint Drusus, who himself passed away and was resurrected by the Emperor."
  - After: "Hearing comrades' confessions made me a believer, then ship's chaplain. Like Saint Drusus, I died — a pirate — and was reborn a missionary."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You'll hear no argument from me. When we lost Reverend Hieronymus, my brothers and sisters despaired. But I, hardened killer that I am, had seen my comrades die before. So I made... suggestions to them at first, and then gave them instructions. In hard times like these, with so many people suffering, we couldn't afford to wallow in a puddle of grief. My brothers and sisters heeded me, and then somehow got it into their heads that I was in charge now."
  - After: "Fair. When Reverend Hieronymus died, the others despaired. I'd seen death before, so I gave orders, and now I'm in charge."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Saint Drusus teaches us to bring people back to the Emperor's light and only punish by death those who've crossed the forbidden line and turned away from Him irrevocably. I'm my own living proof that even a thoroughly rotten scoundrel can take the path of redemption. Are we in such deep retreat from the heresy we're battling that the flamer and the noose are the only tools we have left?"
  - After: "Saint Drusus teaches redemption, death only for the truly lost. I'm proof. Are flamer and noose all we have?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}His large fists clench into twin mace-heads.{/n} "Her Ladyship Incendia Chorda, in her righteous zeal, doesn't see the atrocities her enforcers commit in the Shadow Quarters, using her name as their shield. I intervene wherever I can, but to be honest, I'm almost spent. Helping everyone is beyond my abilities."
  - After: {n}His fists clench.{/n} "Incendia Chorda doesn't see her enforcers' atrocities in the Shadow Quarters. I'm spent."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Shame that Reverend Hieronymus won't listen to me. He's too zealous. He sees the face of vice too clearly and finds it too abhorrent. Looking at Footfall makes him sick, and so he... welcomes the cleansing."
  - After: "Reverend Hieronymus won't listen. Footfall's vice sickens him, so he welcomes the cleansing."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, it's a curious turn of fate." {n}Judging by the pain and anger that flash in Chaplain's eyes for an instant, he knows full well who instigated the violence against the Drusians. But he contains himself.{/n} "Her Ladyship Incendia judged me herself, and hard as she tried, she saw no darkness in me. It was a bit awkward, as a matter of fact. Not that it's anything to rejoice at. She ordered me to personally carry out her verdicts against my brothers and sisters. A heavy burden... But better me than her executioners." {n}The man falls silent and clenches his fists until they crack.{/n}
  - After: "Curious, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship." {n}Anger flashes in his eyes.{/n} "Incendia found me clean, then made me execute my own brethren. Better me than her men." {n}His fists crack.{/n}
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Shrugging, Ulfar mutters quietly,{/n} "I know piracy is condemned in the Imperium... but on Fenris, participating in a glorious raid on a neighbour is considered a valiant deed, not a shameful one."
  - After: {n}Ulfar shrugs.{/n} "On Fenris, raiding a neighbour is valiant, not shameful."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The priest in front of you looks imposing. He is tall and muscular, and has scars on his face and arms. His whole appearance seems to tell a story of many heretics who met their end at the hands of this adherent of the true faith.{/n}
  - After: {n}A tall, muscular, scarred priest.{/n}

  - After: "Many acquittals?"

  - After: [Whisper the words of the forbidden spell] "If you see corruption in me — indict away!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not see a single tome of the Lex Imperialis in this place, which means that you have spurned the letter of the Emperor's Law and that of Holy Terra — your judgement is your own. How far have you fallen in your hubris, Incendia?"
  - After: "No Lex Imperialis here. You've spurned the Emperor's Law — your judgement is your own. How far has your hubris taken you, Incendia?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I bid you farewell."
  - After: "Farewell."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I haven't the slightest desire to get involved in your petty squabbles."
  - After: "I have no desire to join your petty squabbles."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I wholeheartedly share your indignation. Calligos is a reprobate."
  - After: "I share your outrage. Calligos is a reprobate."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Have you and Calligos lost your minds? The Expanse is in a calamitous state, and you two are busy settling scores! You must cease this at once."
  - After: "Have you and Calligos lost your minds? The Expanse is burning! Stop this feud at once."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If you ask me, you are simply using the situation to plunder his protectorate. Should he call upon House von Valancius for help, we will answer."
  - After: "You're just plundering his protectorate. If he asks House von Valancius for help, we'll answer."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: {n}Incendia Chorda is absorbed in reading a long strip of parchment. Her left hand is holding a silver spoon, with which she is carefully scooping up brain matter from the open skull of the man contorted next to her.{/n} "{name} von Valancius. I was informed of your arrival."
  - After: {n}Incendia spoons brain from a man's skull.{/n} "{name} von Valancius. I expected you."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: {n}Incendia looks up from her parchment and enquires tensely,{/n} "What brings you to me, {name}?"
  - After: {n}Incendia looks up, tense.{/n} "What brings you, {name}?"
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "I never doubted you, {name}. The Emperor protects."
  - After: "I never doubted you, {name}."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: {n}Exhaustion has marked Incendia's features with a criss-cross of lines and deeper furrows. Her cheek is forever twisted in a continuous nervous tic, yet her eyes are ablaze with indomitable resolve. A dazzling aura of power and righteous fury surrounds her like a mantle. She gracefully brings a gold-plated inhaler to her lips, takes a deep breath, and the fire in her gaze flares like a plasma thruster.{/n}
  - After: {n}Haggard and twitching, Incendia inhales from a gold inhaler; her eyes blaze.{/n}
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "Yes, it has, although its journey here took far too long. But never again will it release its grip on this station. I vow it."
  - After: "Yes, belatedly. And it stays. I vow it."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: {n}Incendia cracks her neck, which must have grown stiff after so many hours of reading, before picking up another sheet. Everywhere you look, servants are buckling under heavy stacks of new denunciations, warrants, and other documents.{/n}
  - After: {n}Incendia cracks her neck and takes another sheet.{/n}
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: {n}Incendia jerks her chin up and responds haughtily,{/n} "This IS true justice. Unprejudiced, inescapable, and equally merciless to all."
  - After: {n}Haughtily:{/n} "This IS true justice. Merciless to all."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "The Lord Inquisitor has bestowed upon me the honour of bringing order to this cesspool of pirates and heretics. To rid Footfall of the corruption that has fettered its limbs and turned this Imperial station into a hotbed of freethinking and inefficiency. And I will not rest until all have been judged."
  - After: "The Lord Inquisitor bid me purge this pirate cesspool. I won't rest until all are judged."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: {n}Incendia studies you with a predatory smile.{/n} "It must have been the Emperor's providence that brought you here to my court. It would be my pleasure to indict you for the crimes you have committed."
  - After: {n}She smiles predatorily.{/n} "Providence brought you to my court. I'd gladly indict you."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "It pleases me that you get to share in the triumph of Footfall's purging with me."
  - After: "Good. Share Footfall's purging with me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You swallow the brain matter, and it slips down into your stomach without the slightest issue. You hear a weak moan from the victim — and catch Marazhai's enraptured gaze, who looks like he could faint from sheer exhilaration.{/n}
  - After: {n}You swallow it easily. The victim moans; Marazhai is enraptured.{/n}
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: {n}Incendia touches a panel on the throne's armrest and is immediately shielded by a refractor field. You hear the sounds of alarms going off in the distance. A mocking smile cuts across her face.{/n} "Go ahead, {name}. Give me a reason."
  - After: {n}A refractor field shields Incendia.{/n} "Go ahead, {name}. Give me a reason."
- **Acolyte of the Inquisition**
  - Before: {n}The warrior clad in Inquisitorial armour announces,{/n} "The Lord Inquisitor's instructions were to maintain order and ensure his allies' safety. Using any methods, however extreme they may have to be."
  - After: {n}An Inquisitorial warrior:{/n} "Our orders: keep order and protect his allies. By any means."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "My regards to you, {name}." {n}He glances at Incendia proudly.{/n} "I knew I was right about you."
  - After: "My regards, {name}." {n}To Incendia:{/n} "I was right."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "There, there, {name}." {n}Marazhai's voice is dripping with feigned pity.{/n} "Control yourself. Nevertheless... I cannot say the sentiment does not delight me. Even if you still have much to learn." {n}He graces Incendia with a condescending glance, then looks back at you with repressed pride.{/n}
  - After: "There, there, {name}." {n}Mock pity.{/n} "Still, it delights me." {n}He beams.{/n}
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "Do not hope that mimicking me and listening to your pet inhuman will let you glean the things I have gleaned from the taste of this heretic's thoughts. I do this with disgust and in the Emperor's name, while you are driven by morbid delight and twisted curiosity."
  - After: "Aping me won't teach you what I glean. I do this in disgust, for Him; you, for morbid delight."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "Everyone knows how freely you interpret the strict prohibitions of the Emperor.
