  - After: "Chorda hates Winterscale more than us. I'll drink to that!"
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "Your courage and forthrightness are admirable, my {mf|lord|lady}! Down with Chorda!"
  - After: "Bold, my {mf|lord|lady}! Down with Chorda!"
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: {n}Octaviana grows pale as she shifts her gaze between the bottle shards and you.{/n} "Have mercy, my {mf|lord|lady}! I never knew you, too, were an enemy of the Winterscales. Pray, don't be angry! It won't happen again!"
  - After: {n}Octaviana pales.{/n} "Mercy, my {mf|lord|lady}! It won't happen again!"
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "Badly. But we're in no mood to lie down and die yet. There are still people who can't stand Chorda's regime, and they are fighting. A sting a day, always somewhere new. Vladaym may be on the run, but he still has people loyal to him."
  - After: "Badly. But Vladaym, though on the run, still has loyalists fighting."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "Badly, my {mf|lord|lady}. Her Infallible Ladyship rode into Footfall {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FootfallNotAlly}on the back of the famine{/d} and straight off began running the place her way. Things were just lousy at first, but then there was real carnage. Vladaym tried to start an uprising, but he didn't stand a chance. The people were starving. Half of them enlisted in Chorda's service for a ration pack. The rest were hanged."
  - After: "Badly, my {mf|lord|lady}. Chorda came {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FootfallNotAlly}on the back of the famine{/d}. Vladaym's uprising failed. The starving joined her or hanged."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: {n}With an obedient and world-weary expression, Octaviana opens the bottle and pours its yellowish contents on the floor. She states dryly,{/n} "No more orders for rotgut, then. A glass of water, my {mf|lord|lady}?"
  - After: {n}Octaviana pours it out.{/n} "Water, then, my {mf|lord|lady}?"
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: {n}Octaviana joins in loudly at once:{/n} "All hail {name} von Valancius!"
  - After: {n}Octaviana joins in:{/n} "All hail {name} von Valancius!"
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: {n}Octaviana rubs her jaw augmetic anxiously.{/n} "The silly girl went off on her own to get her people out of Falco's clutches. I told her to wait a little till we sorted out our current business. Then we could've bled him together. But no, not Heydari. That one's as stubborn as a herd of groxes. She said her guys didn't have that much time, and then she vanished."
  - After: {n}Octaviana rubs her jaw.{/n} "The silly girl went alone to free her people from Falco. Wouldn't wait for me. Vanished."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "That ashmag..." {n}Jae's voice is full of anger and thirst for vengeance.{/n} "No, there's still something he needs from me. So not all of them are dead, or at any rate, it will be better for him if some aren't. Where is he, Octy? Speak!"
  - After: "That ashmag..." {n}Jae seethes.{/n} "He still needs me, so some live. Where is he, Octy?"
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: "Got lopped off by a fan blade. There was an enforcer raid and I had to take the ventilation shaft. It used to be a reliable escape route. We'd shorted the fan a while before. Well, the bastards found out about it, and got it working again. Everyone got turned into mincemeat, and I was lucky." {n}Ryzza pats her prosthetic joylessly.{/n} "That was the day I realised the war on Chorda wasn't my war anymore."
  - After: "A fan blade, fleeing a raid through a vent. Everyone else was minced." {n}She pats her prosthetic.{/n} "After that, Chorda's war wasn't mine."
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: {n}Ryzza casts a glance in Octaviana's direction, waits for her to take the hint and look away, then says,{/n} "At Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship's service."
  - After: {n}Ryzza waits for Octaviana to look away.{/n} "At Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship's service."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Ah Octy, I've missed the fiery sunset of your hair, shereen! Sorry I haven't brought any gifts today, but we're certainly going to down another round or two—"
  - After: "Octy, I've missed your fiery hair, shereen! Let's down a round—"
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "You know very well where." {n}Octaviana waves toward a drab-looking door covered by a sheet of metal.{/n} "The sewers are where that rat belongs. You know, he was going to rat us all out to Chorda. Including Vladaym. You should've seen Falco's face when Vladaym led the Inquisitor's dogs to him first, ha ha!"
  - After: "You know where." {n}She points to a door.{/n} "The sewers. He'd have sold us to Chorda, but Vladaym set the Inquisitor's dogs on him first!"
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "I don't have any fighters, but I do have a shipment of xenos weapons. Lethal, but with no guarantee of quality. Figuring out how it even works is tricky enough. But that still beats the junk Vladaym's thugs are armed with. They can have a round on the house."
  - After: "No fighters, but unreliable xenos weapons. Better than what Vladaym's thugs have. On the house."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: {n}The woman looks at you pensively.{/n} "And by 'we,' you mean you and Vladaym? He always has a plan. But it's certainly not always the best plan. Why should I trust in your idea?"
  - After: {n}She studies you.{/n} "You and Vladaym? Why trust your plan?"
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: {n}Octaviana lowers her voice.{/n} "Vladaym has let the station slip away from him. Plenty of people aren't happy about it, not least his business partners. Should something happen to Tocara, come here. {d|Encyclopedia:KasballicaRep_Mid}Your dealings with the Kasballica{/d} shouldn't take a hit because of the old Liege's ambitions."
  - After: {n}Octaviana whispers.{/n} "If something happens to Tocara, come here. {d|Encyclopedia:KasballicaRep_Mid}Your dealings with the Kasballica{/d} needn't suffer."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "You're personally willing to stand against her? That changes things significantly. With you, the resistance has a chance... You certainly know how to turn a situation around, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship."
  - After: "You'll face her yourself? Then we've a chance, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "I'm sorry, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, but if your plan fails, we'll all be strung up while Her Infallible Ladyship won't lay a finger on you. Your risk and ours are poles apart."
  - After: "Sorry, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. If it fails, we hang and you walk."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: {n}Octaviana looks away. It seems your words have touched a sore spot.{/n} "You're right. Time is running out. There's barely any left. I don't give a damn what your plan is. I'm in."
  - After: {n}Octaviana looks away, stung.{/n} "You're right. Time's nearly gone. I'm in."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "Perhaps. Or perhaps tomorrow Her Infallible Ladyship will anger the Lord Inquisitor, set off on a campaign, and fall in battle against the enemies of Humanity, or simply choke on her own spite. And then I'll be alive, and she won't."
  - After: "Perhaps. Or Chorda chokes on her spite first."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "Hmm... It is generous, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. Very generous. If we don't all get killed, the Amasecus will be flooded with thrones. All right then, it's a deal, but I have one condition. Write me a document saying your heirs have no right to go back on the promise. Because, as you can understand, if this doesn't work, there'll be a new Rogue Trader von Valancius in the very near future."
  - After: "Generous, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. Deal, if your heirs are bound to it in writing. If this fails, there'll be a new Rogue Trader von Valancius soon."
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: "It's an honour for old Ryzza to have a conversation with Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, just like that."
  - After: "An honour, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "You're in an enviable position, is all I can say, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. In the Atrium, you'll find hundreds of people who are awaiting trial and would give anything for a dose of lethal poison."
  - After: "Lucky you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. The Atrium's prisoners would beg for poison."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "Don't waste your silver tongue on me, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We're not going to come to an agreement. And what use would I be in this war of yours, anyway?"
  - After: "Save it, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. What use am I in your war anyway?"
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: {n}Ryzza flashes a wicked smile and replies quietly,{/n} "I can assure you I wasn't going to. Vladaym the Vackemo has no future. He doesn't see it, but I do. And you do. When you come for his head, or Her Ladyship Chorda does, you can trust old Ryzza to stand aside... Especially if she can guarantee my safety."
  - After: {n}Ryzza smiles wickedly.{/n} "I wasn't. The Vackemo's finished. When someone comes for him, I'll stand aside... if my safety's guaranteed."
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship is trying to drag old Ryzza into dangerous business. Give it up. I'm much too fond of my own skin."
  - After: "Give it up, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship."
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: {n}The pirate narrows her eyes.{/n} "What, so you're like {mf|Her|the other} Ladyship now? One look, and you can tell the wicked from the righteous? I suppose it's easy enough to guess that a pirate has a misdeed or two to her name, but no one has ever accused me of serving the Archenemy before. You wound me, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship!"
  - After: {n}She narrows her eyes.{/n} "Judging souls like {mf|Her|the other} Ladyship? Me, serve the Archenemy? You wound me, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As much as Ryzza is trying to turn it all into a joke, there is anxiety in her eyes, and her hand is reaching unconsciously for something concealed under her shirt on her chest as if she is trying to further hide it from your gaze.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ryzza jokes, but anxiously hides something under her shirt.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ryzza is clearly trying to turn your question into a joke, but her anxiety is understandable. The situation on the station is not helping to set its inhabitants' minds at ease — especially those involved in illicit activities.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ryzza jokes, but looks anxious, like everyone here.{/n}
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: "Good thing I'm not a heretic then, as you doubtlessly know. I'll be putting my hopes in your mercy, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship." {n}Ryzza smiles darkly, trying to hide her agitation and bewilderment, as her trembling hand brings an empty glass to her lips.{/n}
  - After: "I'm no heretic. I trust your mercy, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship." {n}Her hand trembles.{/n}
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: {n}Ryzza's expression turns to stone. She peers tensely into her glass as if trying to find some answer at the bottom of it. Finally, she raises her eyes to you, looking incredibly tired.{/n} "You're cruel, you know, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. The way you found where this old pirate was hiding her conscience and dragged it kicking and screaming into the light."
  - After: {n}Ryzza looks up, exhausted.{/n} "Cruel, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. You dragged this old pirate's conscience into the light."
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: "I got in over my head and almost took my guys down with me. I'd be a crap captain if I allowed my fear to kill my crew. Thank your esteemed self for talking some sense into me. Got a light?"
  - After: "I nearly took my crew down with me. Thanks. Got a light?"
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: {n}The pirate casually rips some kind of amulet from her neck, bearing a fanged beast crowned with horns. She tosses it into her near-empty glass of rotgut and throws the match you offered her after it. The contents of the glass are immediately engulfed in unholy purple flame. A minute later, all that remains is ash and a nasty puddle of black metal at the bottom. Satisfied with the result, Ryzza smashes the glass on the floor.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ryzza burns her horned-beast amulet in her rotgut with purple flame, then smashes the glass.{/n}
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: {n}The patrons greet your last sentence with an enthusiastic roar. Your heartfelt speech has resonated with the commoners and seems to have stirred Octaviana, too.{/n} "You certainly know how to be persuasive, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. You're right. You're ready to risk your life for us, and here I am being picky like a noble offered a nutribar made of corpse starch. You can count on me."
  - After: {n}The patrons roar.{/n} "You'll risk your life for us, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship? Count me in."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your eyes see through the pirate instantly, and you sense that the burden of her transgressions is so heavy that it will soon drag her under. Pushing her over the edge wouldn't take much effort. The pirate herself seems almost eager to plunge head-first into the murky waters.{/n}
  - After: {n}Her sins are dragging her under. A small push would topple her.{/n}
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "He'd have had more if it weren't for Reverend Hieronymus. Many have fallen for his sermons and taken to repenting and confessing. He's turned so many to the faith, that they don't dare touch him anymore. The old man's a force to be reckoned with now."
  - After: "Reverend Hieronymus draws people away. Nobody dares touch him now."
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: {n}Ryzza's eyes widen.{/n} "You too? I'd never have thought that your esteemed self would... This changes everything. Now I see I made the right choice when I put my trust in... our influential ally."
  - After: {n}Ryzza's eyes widen.{/n} "You too? This changes everything."
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: "You're putting pressure on the most vulnerable spot, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship — the pocket. My fellows will be very disappointed if I ruin our relationship. I'm afraid you leave me no other option but to say yes."
  - After: "You hit my weak spot, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship — the pocket. Fine, yes."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "Reverend Hieronymus is the only one who's flourished amid this madness. He and his missionaries spend days and nights preaching till their throats are sore, talking about the suffering we've brought down upon ourselves. It's almost like he'll grab a flamer himself any day now. And what scares me isn't so much his fiery sermons, but me being on the verge of believing them myself..."
  - After: "Only Reverend Hieronymus thrives, preaching we earned this suffering. Scary thing is, I almost believe him..."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "Give it a rest, Ryzza. I'm not holding you here, so stop trying to drag me away with you."
  - After: "Give it a rest, Ryzza. I'm staying."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: "Trust me, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, if I'd wanted to take part in wars and rebellions, I'd have become a bandit, not a bartender."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, I'm a bartender, not a bandit."
- **Octaviana**
  - Before: {n}Octaviana frowns and shakes her head.{/n} "They won't be pleased. My higher-ups value business partners such as yourself. Which means I ought to help you if I don't want to die an ugly, long, and painful death."
  - After: {n}Octaviana frowns.{/n} "No. So I'd better help."

## World/Dialogs/Ch4/Footfall/ServitorVendor/ServitorVendor_Footfall_c4_dialog

  - Before: "Requesting access to the trading interface."
  - After: "Requesting trading interface access."

  - Before: "I must take my leave."
  - After: "I must go."

  - Before: [Show data-slate] "I have data on planets that will be of interest to your owners."
  - After: [Show data-slate] "I have planet data for your owners."

## World/Dialogs/Ch4/Footfall/Vladaym/Vladaym_Footfall_c4_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: "Liege Tocara. My greetings."
  - After: "Liege Tocara. Greetings."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Who do we have here? A couple of hardened insurgents?"
  - After: "Who's this? Hardened insurgents?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Don't mind me — do carry on."
  - After: "Don't mind me — carry on."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why would I take part in that?"
  - After: "Why would I join that?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What forces do you have at your command?"
  - After: "What forces do you command?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are so docile! But I merely wanted to see how quickly you would renounce your faith and start grovelling. You are obviously not getting out of here alive."
  - After: "So docile! I just wanted to see you renounce your faith and grovel. You won't leave here alive."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What does Ryzza have a problem with?"
  - After: "What's Ryzza's problem?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How is the station faring?"
  - After: "How is the station?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "News of Incendia's death is hardly going to please the Lord Inquisitor."
  - After: "Incendia's death won't please the Lord Inquisitor."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I see no issue in letting Incendia know you are here. Get ready. Your enemies will be here soon."
  - After: "I'll tell Incendia you're here. Get ready; your enemies are coming."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I see your position of authority has not changed you. You remain the bandit you always were."
  - After: "Authority hasn't changed you. Still a bandit."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Laugh] "What a sorry sight — the old outlaw, hounded and hiding like a rat."
  - After: [Laugh] "The old outlaw, hiding like a rat."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Well, between Incendia and you, she has done the better job of imposing order."
  - After: "Incendia imposes order better than you."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Draw your weapon and shout] "In the name of the law, every insurgent present here is under arrest!"
  - After: [Draw your weapon and shout] "In the name of the law, every insurgent here is under arrest!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will go and take a look around."
  - After: "I'll look around."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will help you overthrow Chorda. Each second of her continued rule will cost the lives of hundreds of innocent people."
  - After: "I'll help overthrow Chorda. Her rule costs hundreds of innocent lives."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why has Hieronymus shown up here?"
  - After: "Why is Hieronymus here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Are you aware that Octaviana is already coveting your position in the Kasballica?"
  - After: "Octaviana covets your Kasballica position."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am going to see Calcazar. There are serious things I need to discuss with him."
  - After: "I'm going to see Calcazar on serious matters."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Jae has a few questions for you. Regarding Falco and her gang."
  - After: "Jae has questions about Falco and her gang."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What kind of help do you expect from me?"
  - After: "What help do you expect?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How is the station doing? I can see you have everything under control again."
  - After: "How is the station? You seem in control again."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have understood your plan."
  - After: "I understand your plan."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Down with Chorda. The Emperor's justice has revealed the rot at its core at last. Let us drown it in the blood of self-appointed champions of the faith!"
  - After: "Down with Chorda. The Emperor's justice has exposed its rot. Drown it in the blood of self-appointed champions of faith!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Let us trade. I need your organisation's merchandise."
  - After: "Let's trade. I need your organisation's goods."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You want my help? You can get it — on one condition. In my protectorate, I am worshipped as a deity. Fall to your knees, renounce all other patrons, and swear allegiance to me, the Great Beacon, the living {mf|god|goddess}."
  - After: "My help has one condition. I am worshipped in my protectorate. Kneel, renounce all other patrons, and swear to me, the Great Beacon, the living {mf|god|goddess}."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I would like to make a deal with the Kasballica."
  - After: "I want a deal with the Kasballica."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "You have no other options, Ryzza. If you abandon Footfall to Chorda and flee, where are you going to sell your goods? Or restock your supplies? It will just be a slow death for all of you, with no ammunition, no water, and no air. So quit bargaining with fate and stick to the plan."
  - After: "No choice, Ryzza. Flee, and you'll die slowly without supplies. Stick to the plan."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vladaym slides his glasses down his nose and looks up at you. His eyes are tired but alight with anger.{/n} "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship?"
  - After: {n}Vladaym peers over his glasses, tired and angry.{/n} "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship?"
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: "Plan? More like a suicide pact. You have no allies, no weapons, no... nothing!" {n}Vladaym and Ryzza notice you, and the old pirate grins sarcastically.{/n} "You're a runt trying to play with the big boys, Vackemo. You've taken on a Rogue Trader dynasty with only a handful of heavies and a couple of guns to your name. The way I see it, your march to the gallows is more of a gallop."
  - After: "Plan? Suicide pact!" {n}Ryzza grins at you.{/n} "You're galloping to the gallows, Vackemo."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}Vladaym replies, in a stiff, formal tone,{/n} "My apologies for being unable to receive Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship in my office. My present status imposes certain... limitations on me."
  - After: {n}Stiffly:{/n} "Apologies, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. My status keeps me from my office."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}With a wry smile, Vladaym corrects you:{/n} "Ungodly, lawless rabble-rousers who are a threat to the security of this station. Kindly refer to us using our full titles, please."
  - After: {n}A wry smile.{/n} "Ungodly, lawless rabble-rousers. Full titles, please."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "You are hard to ignore, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. You have a habit of radically altering the state of affairs of whatever situation you wade into."
  - After: "You're hard to ignore, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. You upend everything."
- **Ryzza**
  - Before: "Greetings, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. And as for you, Vackemo... I've got nothing to add. Your plan's utter crap — I don't gamble on those kinds of odds. I'll leave you to think about your prospects. Maybe you'll realise that using my shuttle would be a better idea... while me and my shuttle are still here."
  - After: "Greetings, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. Vackemo, your plan's crap. Consider my shuttle... while it's here."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "A small band of my most daring cutthro— staff members who were by my side when I came to power. Business partners who still remember that any venture is only as reliable as the grip of the venturer's hand on their pistol. Add to that the group of xenos mercenaries which my... colleagues from the Kasballica Mission have provided me with. A radical solution, I know, but they don't care who they kill as long as I pay them, and I have the means to pay them."
  - After: "A few old cutthro— staff, and xenos mercenaries from the Kasballica."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "We would have greater numbers if Ryzza wasn't so damnably cautious, and Hieronymus did us a favour and shut his preaching trap..." {n}Vladaym grits his teeth and adds quietly,{/n} "I would've thrown the good reverend for a loop long ago if it weren't for the fanatical mob that would show up here to avenge him."
  - After: "We'd have more if not for Ryzza's caution and Hieronymus's preaching." {n}Through gritted teeth:{/n} "Damn his mob."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The former Liege looks {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FootfallNotAlly}exhausted{/d}. His glasses cannot hide the circles under his eyes. His coat collar is greasy and unbuttoned, showing the meshwork of the ceramite-reinforced armour hidden underneath. There is a conspicuous dent right beside his throat, left by a bullet. However, as tired as he is, the man is showing no sign of having given up: his lips are pressed together in a hard line; his movements are sharp; and the bandit tattoos under his rolled-up sleeves are a reminder of who Vladaym Tocara was before taking the Liege's throne.{/n}
  - After: {n}The former Liege looks {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FootfallNotAlly}exhausted{/d}, his armour bullet-dented, but unbowed.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The former Liege looks {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FootfallAlly}angry and focused{/d}. His coat collar is unbuttoned, showing the meshwork of ceramite-reinforced armour hidden underneath. He is wearing a gun holster on his side. Now that Vladaym has thrown off the mask of a disgruntled bureaucrat, his sleeves are rolled up, showing his old bandit tattoos. He exudes an aura of imperious cruelty.{/n}
  - After: {n}The former Liege looks {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FootfallAlly}angry and focused{/d}: armoured, armed, bandit tattoos bared. Cruel and imperious.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You note the contraption replacing Ryzza's right leg — a tangle of thick cables around industrial cylinder pistons. A makeshift augmetic, rigged up from whatever was available at the docks. The pirate {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FootfallNotAlly}has not been wearing it for long{/d}, judging by the still fresh stitches on her stump. Every so often, the leg emits sparks.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ryzza's right leg is a sparking scrap augmetic. Fresh stitches show she {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_FootfallNotAlly}has not worn it long{/d}.{/n}
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "It's turned into a kingdom of death. Executing protesters, cracking down on corrupt traders, and suppressing dissent are all good, useful policies within reasonable limits. I've used them myself, in fact. However, with Lady Chorda, reasonable limits are a distant memory at this point."
  - After: "A kingdom of death. I've used executions myself, within limits. Chorda has none."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "And I warned you, didn't I, that this would happen unless you helped us with provisions? When Chorda showed up here, we stood up to her dictatorship, but the ranks of my loyal partners thinned by the day. In the end, a single good punch in the teeth was all it took for the station to roll over and beg for mercy. Few found it in them to resist."
  - After: "I warned you this would happen without provisions. One punch, and the station begged."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "Fortunately, I'd been preparing for that turn of events ever since that hag tried to take Footfall the first time. You helped us then, giving me time to organise. I set up weapons caches, enlisted more fighters, and deleted my agents' data from the cogitator network. When Chorda seized power, she thought she'd won, but the station was still mine... to an extent."
  - After: "But you bought me time before. I hid weapons and agents. The station stayed partly mine."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "My little army is waging war on the enforcers. We slaughter patrols, wrestle back detainees, and punish those who collaborate with the enemy... or are close to someone who does." {n}Vladaym's ruthless smile is like a jagged steel trap.{/n} "Incendia is conducting her reprisals and I am conducting mine. Everyone must remember that there are consequences for collaborating with the occupying force."
  - After: "My army kills patrols and punishes collaborators." {n}A steel-trap smile.{/n} "Incendia has her reprisals; I have mine."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}Vladaym chuckles darkly.{/n} "Surrender? Go crawling on my belly, begging for leniency? If you had any idea how many corpses I've littered across this station's decks on my rise to power, you'd know I would rather die in a void chamber than watch that possessed bitch destroy my station."
  - After: {n}A dark chuckle.{/n} "Beg? I'd sooner die in a void chamber than watch that possessed bitch destroy my station."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}Vladaym smiles tersely.{/n} "Old habits die hard. I'll admit, I wasn't exactly yearning for the days of my youth, but to find myself in the line of fire again is... invigorating."
  - After: {n}A terse smile.{/n} "Old habits. The line of fire is... invigorating."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}Vladaym's presses his lips into a thin line.{/n} "I got into all manner of situations when I was a young man... including desperate ones. This rat has been cornered more than once before. But it always got out of that corner with its belly full of its hunter's flesh. I assure you I have no intention of reneging on my old principles."
  - After: {n}His lips thin.{/n} "This rat's been cornered before. It always escaped fed on its hunter."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}The former Liege grimaces as if from toothache.{/n} "No arguing with that. Here I thought that order should be imposed by killing the people who are harmful to Footfall and protecting the useful ones, hanging rabble-rousers and encouraging traders and explorers. More fool me. Turns out I should've just hanged whoever I could grab, and put all the sector's commerce in front of the firing squad."
  - After: {n}A grimace.{/n} "True. I protected the useful. Should've just hanged everyone."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}Vladaym nods attentively, then looks down at a data-slate showing a map of the station's systems. He scrutinises it with a pensive expression.{/n}
  - After: {n}Vladaym nods and studies a station map.{/n}
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}Vladaym is lightning-fast as he whips his pistol out of its holster and... smiles.{/n} "I've missed this. Everyone — if I pay you thrones, that means you — to battle!"
  - After: {n}Vladaym draws his pistol and... smiles.{/n} "I've missed this. Everyone I pay — to battle!"
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "I'm glad you're with us, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. This is a fight we must be well prepared for. As a... colleague of mine used to say, if your brain doesn't hurt from all that thinking of where to hide, it'll discover even your skull isn't thick enough once the fight is on. Which sounds especially ironic considering how he died. I'd like to ask your opinion on how prepared we are to entertain Lady Incendia."
  - After: "Glad you're with us, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. How ready are we to entertain Lady Incendia?"
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}An unblinking gaze fixes upon you.{/n} "I hope you think it promising."
  - After: {n}An unblinking gaze.{/n} "I hope it's promising."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "Because a critically important station in the Expanse is about to become a graveyard. Once commerce dies, merchants will turn to piracy. What else could they do? Connections between worlds will be weakened, since Chorda will make short work of Astropaths as soon as she gets to them. And Chorda — do you think Footfall will be enough for her? No, she'll march on... perhaps to your worlds as well."
  - After: "A vital Expanse station will die, and Chorda won't stop at Footfall... maybe your worlds next."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Liege — newly restored — looks tired but... {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_Footfall_VladaymLiege}pleased with what is going on around him{/d}. His fingers rap away at his data-slate as he sends out instruction after instruction.{/n} "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship? Is there anything Footfall can do to thank you for its liberation?"
  - After: {n}The restored Liege looks {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_Footfall_VladaymLiege}pleased with what is going on around him{/d}.{/n} "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship? Footfall thanks you."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "She has misgivings about... the prospect of our cooperation. The old rogue prefers not to pick fights unless her victory is a foregone conclusion. And right now she seems to be planning on fleeing rather than fighting. She needs the right kind of motivation... It's a shame there's no one the cold bitch values enough for me to take hostage."
  - After: "She doubts us. The old rogue only fights sure wins and plans to flee."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "He preaches repentance." {n}Vladaym remains stone-faced for a few seconds before giving in and letting a sarcastic smile form on his lips.{/n} "Chorda sent him here to make us lay down our arms and renounce our rebellious ways."
  - After: "He preaches repentance." {n}A sarcastic smile.{/n} "Chorda sent him to disarm us."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}Vladaym is lightning-fast as he whips his pistol out of its holster and... smiles.{/n} "I knew this was exactly how our little war was going to end. All right, then, let's do this the Footfall way. Everyone — if I pay you thrones, that means you — to battle!"
  - After: {n}Vladaym draws his pistol and smiles.{/n} "The Footfall way, then. Everyone I pay — to battle!"
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, you may have little love to spare for me, and you certainly {d|Encyclopedia:KasballicaRep_Min}have not built a strong alliance{/d} with the organisation I represent. But if seeing the new order of things on Footfall gives you even the tiniest suspicion that it's all damned madness, step in and help me stop it."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, you {d|Encyclopedia:KasballicaRep_Min}have not built a strong alliance{/d} with us. But help me stop this madness."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "Considering Calcazar has never once interfered in the station's affairs, he clearly couldn't care less about Footfall. This means he also doesn't care who runs the station, so long as things are quiet here. I'm going to make sure things are quiet. Granted, he did give Chorda a security detail, but if she's already..." {n}Tocara emphasises the last word.{/n} "...dead, and her death doesn't reek of deadly heresy, he likely won't bother to investigate. The Lord Inquisitor will simply entrust governance to someone who won't cause him problems. Someone like me."
  - After: "Calcazar only wants quiet. If Chorda's..." {n}He stresses it.{/n} "...dead, without heresy, he'll pick a harmless governor. Me."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "Besides, the Kasballica Mission — and I'm authorised to say this — sees Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship as a proven and valuable ally."
  - After: "And the Kasballica Mission sees Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship as a valuable ally."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, I'm asking you for help. Not just on behalf of the portion of the station population that isn't already scared shitless, but on behalf of the Kasballica Mission as well. My people and my organisation's assets are in a vulnerable position. Help us protect our interests, and {d|Encyclopedia:KasballicaRep_Mid}we'll help you{/d} protect yours."
  - After: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, the Kasballica Mission asks your help. Protect our interests, and {d|Encyclopedia:KasballicaRep_Mid}we'll help you{/d} protect yours."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "I will send my least important associates to the entrance to take the brunt of the initial assault. That should thin our guests' numbers." {n}Without thinking, Vladaym reaches for his pistol to check how easily it slides out of its holster. Then... he smiles. It's an easy-going, young, and bloodthirsty smile.{/n} "I'd almost forgotten how much I love all this."
  - After: "My expendables take the first assault." {n}He smiles, bloodthirsty.{/n} "I'd forgotten how I love this."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "By the Throne's radiance, Vladaym, if you don't tell me this very moment where you and Falco are keeping my guys—"
  - After: "By the Throne, Vladaym, tell me where you and Falco keep my guys—"
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}The former Liege interrupts Jae with a dry gesture:{/n} "I don't do business with rats, Heydari. And, surprisingly enough, for once I don't mean you."
  - After: {n}Vladaym cuts Jae off.{/n} "I don't deal with rats, Heydari. For once I don't mean you."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "I'm only carrying out the duties imposed upon me by my position as Liege. After the House Chorda forces retreated in a hurry, it turned out that, surprisingly enough, there were unaccounted-for scumbags on the station who wasted no time in seizing the opportunity. I took the smartest and most useful among them under my wing, and told them I didn't want any shenanigans. As for the rest... a hundred or so names were added to the grievous toll Lady Chorda had left behind."
  - After: "A Liege's duty. When Chorda fled, scum rose. I kept the useful ones and hanged a hundred."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "In that case, pray to the Exalted One that Falco backs up your story before he dies." {n}Disappointed, Jae takes her hand off her weapon and bows her head before you penitently.{/n} "Forgive me my brazenness, shereen. He's all yours."
  - After: "Then pray Falco backs your story." {n}Jae bows to you.{/n} "Forgive me, shereen."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}Vladaym grins wickedly.{/n} "Dangerous words. Very dangerous. But powerful. I have no doubt you'll match them with your actions."
  - After: {n}A wicked grin.{/n} "Dangerous, powerful words. Back them with deeds."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "Regretfully, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship, I have nothing to offer you at the moment. My access to the assets you're interested in has been temporarily restricted. It's going to take putting a bullet through a couple of heads for me to once again be able to offer an adequate range of merchandise."
  - After: "Nothing to offer yet, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. A few bullets in a few heads should fix that."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vladaym hesitates. Even this thoroughly unprincipled hustler knows there is no going back after crossing certain lines. He stares at you intently. Despite the dark glasses hiding his eyes and the mask-like expression on his face, you can easily see — no, sense — the exact moment he brutally crushes the last remnants of faith inside him and decides to step into the abyss. Vladaym casts away his doubts and gets down on his knees.{/n}
  - After: {n}Vladaym hesitates, then crushes his last faith and kneels.{/n}
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "But he seems taken aback by the scale of Lady Incendia's purges, which opens up possibilities. If we put pressure on him, he'll bring over zealots who'll tear apart whoever he points his finger at. A useful man. I regret not getting him onside sooner."
  - After: "But the purges shook him. Pressed, his zealots will tear apart whoever he names."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "I renounce all other patrons and pledge my eternal fealty to the Great Beacon, the true {mf|god|goddess} and {mf|master|mistress} of fates. I most humbly beseech you to help me drown Footfall in the blood of Incendia Chorda and her minions." {n}Vladaym looks at you expectantly.{/n}
  - After: "I renounce all patrons and swear to the Great Beacon, true {mf|god|goddess} and {mf|master|mistress} of fates. Help me drown Footfall in Chorda's blood." {n}He waits.{/n}
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "Old nicknames die as hard as old habits. I used to be known by that name on the station. The Vackemo is a myth. A malicious spirit stalking its prey in Footfall's empty sectors." {n}Tocara chuckles.{/n} "I had a terrible reputation when I was young."
  - After: "The Vackemo is a spirit stalking Footfall's empty sectors." {n}He chuckles.{/n} "I had a reputation."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship is too late. The Lord Inquisitor and his people have already left Footfall. They were in a great hurry. That said, you can see I'm in no rush to return to my old abode. I wouldn't like to be thrown out of it, should the esteemed Lord Inquisitor suddenly decide to come back."
  - After: "Too late, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. The Lord Inquisitor left in a hurry."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "She knows we use the Amasecus as our meeting place. If you let the enforcers know I can be found and grabbed in here, she will come — and she will hardly drag her throne with her. We'll lure her into a trap, kill her, and take back Footfall."
  - After: "She knows we meet at the Amasecus. Tell the enforcers I'm here; she'll come without her throne. We kill her."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}Vladaym grins darkly.{/n} "Then Octaviana's bitten off more than she can chew. It's too early to write me off yet. But I appreciate Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship's decision to inform me. I'll keep an eye on that overly feisty bartender."
  - After: {n}A dark grin.{/n} "Octaviana's bitten off too much. Thank you, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. I'll watch her."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "Perhaps some of those gathered in here will support us. Ryzza's people, Hieronymus's zealots... even Octaviana's regulars. We can use whomever we can get. If you think that it may be worth fortifying our positions or preparing a few surprises for our guests, my people and arsenal are at your disposal — all you have to do is say the word. As soon as we're ready, send Chorda a message saying I'm here. Let her come. We'll settle our differences the Footfall way. With a gunfight."
  - After: "Others here may join us. My people and arsenal are yours to fortify. When ready, tell Chorda I'm here. A Footfall gunfight."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}Vladaym nods and stands up.{/n} "Then let's get down to business."
  - After: {n}Vladaym stands.{/n} "To business."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}With a feral snarl, Ulfar says sharply,{/n} "You speak tainted words, Aett-Vater. Yes, the priests here are murderous dogs, but do not dare blaspheme the Allfather." {n}Looming over you, Ulfar brandishes his finger at you in warning.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ulfar snarls.{/n} "Tainted words, Aett-Vater. Do not blaspheme the Allfather." {n}He looms in warning.{/n}
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "A general uprising will be doomed to fail. The enforcers have isolated the asteroids. We can't strike out against Incendia: she has the greater numbers, and her throne's refractor field will protect her from any attack." {n}An insidious smile appears on the Liege's lips.{/n} "So we'll ask Her Ladyship to come to us. Exploiting her overconfidence. If she wants my blood, let her come and spill it."
  - After: "An uprising fails; her throne's refractor field shields her." {n}A sly smile.{/n} "So we invite her here."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}You feel Ulfar's burning gaze directed at you. His face is devoid of emotion, but there is a hostile glint in his eyes.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ulfar glares, eyes hostile.{/n}
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}The word "mercenary" causes Marazhai's eyes to flare in fury.{/n} "Careful with your choice of terms, mon-keigh. Or I will demonstrate my expertise in flaying victims alive, here and now."
  - After: {n}Marazhai's eyes flare at "mercenary".{/n} "Careful, mon-keigh, or I'll flay you here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Vladaym looks over at Marazhai.{/n} "You really aren't picky at all in your choice of mercenaries. Then again, the unholy xenos are too adept in the art of carnage for one to refuse their services out of trivial squeamishness."
  - After: {n}Vladaym eyes Marazhai.{/n} "Not picky about mercenaries. Then, xenos excel at carnage."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Your vanity has crossed the line that divides stupidity from blasphemy." {n}Heinrix clenches his fists. For a moment, you feel as if the air is going cold... but the illusion is dispelled a mere second later.{/n}
  - After: "Your vanity is now blasphemy." {n}Heinrix clenches his fists; the air chills.{/n}
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta stares at you grimly from under her locks of white hair. Her hands on her weapon are trembling with impatience... but the warrior stops herself and looks away.{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta's hands tremble on her weapon... she looks away.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Thank you, Lord Captain." {n}Idira's words are barely audible, breathed out rather than spoken. Her expression is clearly one of relief.{/n} "As filthy of a place as Footfall is... blood and tears won't wash away that filth — they'll only make the stench worse."
  - After: "Thank you, Lord Captain." {n}Idira, relieved.{/n} "Blood and tears only worsen Footfall's stench."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}The Seneschal furrows his thick eyebrows.{/n} "Hmm. I cannot say I approve of antagonising Chorda... but her methods being what they are, I definitely disapprove of assisting her."
  - After: {n}The Seneschal frowns.{/n} "Antagonising Chorda is bad. Helping her is worse."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: {n}Turning away from Ryzza, Vladaym's expression does not change, but an indistinct curse falls from his lips.{/n}
  - After: {n}Vladaym mutters a curse.{/n}
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}The Proctor clenches his teeth with an audible screech.{/n} "Do not equate Chorda's preposterous court with the Lex Imperialis. The God-Emperor's Law remains perfect, even if the judge has erred beyond all hope."
  - After: {n}The Proctor grinds his teeth.{/n} "Chorda's court is not the Lex Imperialis. The Law stays perfect."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "However much Chorda would like to believe she's kicked the Kasballica out of Footfall, she hasn't. We're scattered all over the station, lying low, and there's still enough of us to cause trouble."
  - After: "The Kasballica isn't gone from Footfall. We're lying low, enough to cause trouble."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "Besides, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship has not yet considered the possibilities that working with the Kasballica Mission opens up. Now is the perfect moment for you to gain a new ally. In a time of crisis, every friendship is valuable."
  - After: "And the Kasballica Mission makes a valuable ally, Your {mf|Lord|Lady}ship. In crisis, friends count."
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "I realise it's a bold hypothesis, and the Lord Inquisitor may have me hanged for Chorda's death. But my life is at stake as it is, so I may as well take the risk."
  - After: "Bold. He may hang me for it. My life's at stake anyway."
- **Hieronymus Doloroso**
  - Before: "Enough, Vladaym! I was hoping I could temper your pride, but you are too rooted in your arrogant and heretical ways! All you faithful to the Emperor, let us take a stand for His liege, Rogue Trader von Valancius!"
  - After: "Enough, Vladaym, heretic! Faithful of the Emperor, stand for His liege, Rogue Trader von Valancius!"
- **Vladaym Tocara the Liege**
  - Before: "Alas, most of my people on the station have perished. Incendia had what I couldn't offer — provisions. It's amazing how many people will break their oaths of loyalty for a nutribar... forgetting about the inevitable consequences." {n}Vladaym grins harshly.{/n} "Well then, let's give my modest fighting force a head count."
  - After: "Most of my people broke oaths for Incendia's nutribars." {n}A harsh grin.{/n} "Let's count who's left."

## World/Dialogs/Ch4/HaemonculusLab/HaemonculusQuetzaal/HaemonculusQuetzaal_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "I killed you with my own hands!"
  - After: "I killed you myself!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Draw your weapon] "Trust me, this time I will fell you much quicker than the last!"
  - After: [Draw your weapon] "This time I'll fell you quicker!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I see you have found new company, Tervantias."
  - After: "New company, Tervantias?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why are you here and not in Commorragh?"
  - After: "Why are you here, not Commorragh?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is this place? It does not exactly look like a Drukhari laboratory."
  - After: "What is this place? Not a Drukhari lab."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Am I talking to one Tervantias or several? Is each of you a separate individual?"
  - After: "One Tervantias or several? Is each of you separate?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I saw the body of a dead Tech-Priest in this lab. Where did he come from? Explain."
  - After: "There's a dead Tech-Priest in this lab. Explain."
- **Player**
  - Before: "That hole in the ceiling is a peculiar design choice. What happened here?"
  - After: "Odd hole in the ceiling. What happened?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Draw your weapon] "This meeting shall be our last, Tervantias."
  - After: [Draw your weapon] "Our last meeting, Tervantias."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You are looking at several completely identical Haemonculi at work. A disturbing sight. The indistinguishable, and familiar, faces turn their attention toward you, morosely and almost indifferently.{/n}
  - After: {n}Several identical Haemonculi turn to you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Because of you, specimen! Because of your feeble wits and your deplorably stubborn reluctance to die!" {n}In the thick silence, several clicks are heard as the copies move their limbs in an insect-like fashion.{/n} "But I had to finish what I had started... finish the masterpiece that had been taken away from me! Because of you! All because of you!"
  - After: "Because of you, specimen!" {n}The copies click.{/n} "I had to finish my stolen masterpiece!"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Were you truly a master of the flesh, esteemed colleague, you would have reproduced a single self, rather than a multitude of flawed duplicates." {n}Unveiled, malicious triumph rings in the Manipulus's words.{/n}
  - After: "A true flesh-master would make one self, not flawed duplicates." {n}The Manipulus gloats.{/n}
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}A broad, repulsive grin appears on one of the disfigured faces.{/n} "How would I know? I can't tell one mon-keigh from another."
  - After: {n}A repulsive grin.{/n} "Mon-keigh all look alike."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}The identical faces look annoyed and spiteful. For a moment, it seems the Haemonculi are about to reply in unison, but a barely perceptible electrical impulse stops them. One of them scoffs and mutters through his teeth,{/n} "Just more proof of how unreliable partnerships with lower life forms are."
  - After: {n}One mutters spitefully,{/n} "Lower life forms make poor partners."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You're different from others of your species, specimen. This time around, I want to study you much, and I mean much, more thoroughly, which necessitates your death... I hope dying once isn't enough for you either."
  - After: "This time I'll study you thoroughly. That needs your death."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai clicks his tongue.{/n} "All Haemonculi are endowed with an intellect that is as keen as it is deranged. But this is probably the first coven member I have seen who has well and truly lost his marbles. Dying has not done him any good."
  - After: {n}Marazhai clicks his tongue.{/n} "Haemonculi are deranged, but this one's truly lost it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}An indulgent chuckle rolls like a wave from one Haemonculus to another. They answer all at once, an ominous choir filling up the room:{/n} "Have you forgotten that I am a great master of flesh who has transcended death itself? Do you think it would befit me to let a mon-keigh cut my path short?"
  - After: {n}They answer as one:{/n} "I transcended death. Would a mon-keigh end me?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}One of the Haemonculi starts to talk — with all the usual arrogance:{/n} "Specimen. We {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_HaemonkulusAlive}meet again{/d}. Your escape from Commorragh was both a statistical anomaly and an act of abject cowardice. You should have died in the Dark City, instead of overstepping the limits of your own usefulness. You caused too much commotion."
  - After: {n}One speaks:{/n} "Specimen. We {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_HaemonkulusAlive}meet again{/d}. You should have died in Commorragh."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}The monster falls silent. Barely perceptible electrical charges run through the Haemonculi's bodies. Then the one who spoke continues,{/n} "So you're here. Now what? Are you going to bore me with your questions, mon-keigh?"
  - After: {n}Sparks run through them.{/n} "Now what? Questions, mon-keigh?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The clones look around them in a movement that is almost synchronised. A disembodied voice answers you:{/n} "This dreary vault is lacking in practicality and function but it has served as a passable refuge for me and my research."
  - After: {n}A voice:{/n} "A dreary vault, but a passable refuge for my research."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}You notice one of the Haemonculi glance at the hole in the ceiling. Fury contorts the xenos's face. Tervantias is unable to hide his anger at what happened. Whoever did it and whatever it was they did, it enraged him.{/n}
  - After: {n}One glances at the ceiling hole, twisted with fury.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Tervantias's voice sounds dry. The grim gazes of his hideous copies are fixed upon you, watching.{/n}
  - After: {n}The copies watch you grimly.{/n}
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: {n}The Haemonculi are quiet, and then... they start to giggle. The revolting sound makes your skin crawl.{/n} "Scary, isn't it? The thought that you're not the only mon-keigh who serves me. Try and guess, specimen. Try and guess."
  - After: {n}The Haemonculi giggle.{/n} "Scary? You're not the only mon-keigh serving me. Guess."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You hear the Drukhari's voice again but cannot see who is talking to you.{/n} "'Found'? Don't you mean 'made'? I've had a backup shell stored away for centuries, but the events at the Spire of the Reaving Tempest convinced me one active body was not enough."
  - After: {n}An unseen voice:{/n} "'Made'. After the Spire of the Reaving Tempest, one body wasn't enough."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: "I am obviously here because this is my laboratory containing my research that requires my attention." {n}The familiar voice of one of the xenos sounds as though he is lecturing a child.{/n}
  - After: "My laboratory needs me, obviously." {n}He lectures you like a child.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Haemonculi you can see are silent, and yet, you still hear Tervantias's reply: his voice seems to be coming from every direction at once.{/n} "My new multiple form is intriguing, isn't it? I'll leave your question unanswered, specimen, to give you something to ponder."
  - After: {n}The voice comes from everywhere.{/n} "Intriguing? Ponder it, specimen."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: "I haven't finished yet!" {n}The Haemonculi break into psychotic laughter.{/n} "One corporeal shell is too few! Deplorably, unacceptably few! Once my work is complete, not one mon-keigh in the world will be able to destroy me completely!"
  - After: "I'm not finished!" {n}Mad laughter.{/n} "Soon no mon-keigh can destroy me completely!"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Good. That means I can add a new note of agony to your every death. And I won't repeat myself even once."
  - After: "Good. A new agony for every death."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Your path will not lead you to your goal. This experiment is entirely irrational, and its repercussions will be purged here and now."
  - After: "This irrational experiment will be purged now."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: "One... many... what difference does it make? I'm on my way toward infinity, specimen. Toward genuine, limitless immortality!"
  - After: "One, many? I'm heading toward limitless immortality!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Haemonculi are twitching slightly, as though from invisible electric impulses. They look virtually identical, yet each seems to be missing something: a limb, an implant, even a facial feature or two. The single gaze of the many faces no longer seems full of haughty superiority only. Some kind of a shared defect also shows in it.{/n}
  - After: {n}Each twitching copy lacks something: a limb, an implant, a feature. A shared defect.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Haemonculi appear identical. Their repulsively indistinguishable faces are looking at you with a single condescending gaze, full of haughty superiority.{/n}
  - After: {n}Identical faces, one haughty gaze.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Haemonculi start talking over one another.{/n} "You!" {n}one of them hisses through his teeth.{/n} "How dare you..." {n}echoes another.{/n} "...show up here alive!" {n}a third one finishes.{/n} "This is even better, though..." {n}—{/n} "...now I'll cleanse the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_HaemonkulusKilled}shame of my death{/d} with your blood..." {n}—{/n} "...and then transform you, and the scum you've brought along, into something useful!"
  - After: {n}They overlap.{/n} "You!" {n}hisses one.{/n} "Alive..." {n}another.{/n} "...good!" {n}a third.{/n} "Your blood..." {n}—{/n} "...washes the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_HaemonkulusKilled}shame of my death{/d}..." {n}—{/n} "...then I remake you!"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I'll turn this place inside out to find out who has conspired with the xenos. I've had it with traitors among the ranks of Humanity." {n}Heinrix's voice overflows with anger and bitterness.{/n}
  - After: "I'll find who conspired with the xenos. I'm sick of traitors." {n}Heinrix seethes.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: {n}Jae unconsciously reaches for the augment on her neck to check that it is {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_JaeWasInCommoragh}still there{/d}.{/n} "Bore you, ashmag? Oh, no, no. We'll just stuff your skinny arse full of metal. You love pain, after all, don't you?"
  - After: {n}Jae touches her neck augment, {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_JaeWasInCommoragh}still there{/d}.{/n} "Bore you, ashmag? We'll fill you with metal."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "But you are not immortal, and we both know it." {n}Yrliet clenches her fists and gives the Haemonculus a look that could incinerate him.{/n} "I am going to kill you as many times as it takes. In the name of my fallen kin. And in the name of Crudarach."
  - After: "You're not immortal." {n}Yrliet glares.{/n} "I'll kill you for my kin. For Crudarach."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Look at that despicable ashmag, shereen. He still has hope of surviving our meeting."
  - After: "Look, shereen. The ashmag hopes to survive."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "Haemonculi can create copies of themselves by leaving samples of their body tissues in secret labs. As soon as a Haemonculus breathes their last..." {n}Marazhai clicks his fingers.{/n} "I don't suppose Tervantias shared his secret with Yremeryss."
  - After: "Haemonculi hide tissue to regrow after death." {n}Marazhai snaps his fingers.{/n} "Yremeryss didn't know."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "You are just a coward hiding behind a panoply of masks. I will pluck off every last one."
  - After: "Coward behind masks. I'll pluck off every one."
- **Tervantias the Archmachinator**
  - Before: "A stupid question, the answer to which is of no importance to one who is about to be taken apart."
  - After: "Irrelevant to one about to be taken apart."

## World/Dialogs/Ch4/HaemonculusLab/TracesOfThePast/TracesOfThePast_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Take a closer look around]
  - After: [Look around closely]
- **Player**
  - Before: [Try to surmise what destroyed the lab ceiling]
  - After: [Guess what destroyed the ceiling]
- **Player**
  - Before: [Address your companions] "What do you make of all this?"
  - After: [Address your companions] "Thoughts?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The space around the hollow is littered with lumps of broken rockcrete. A feeble breeze blows through the ugly hole in the ceiling, stirring up whirlwinds of stone dust at your feet.{/n}
  - After: {n}Rockcrete rubble below a hole in the ceiling.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Through the piled-up rocks, dirt, and thick dust, you are able to make out parts of fixtures that were ripped out of their sockets and thrown to the floor. Parts like these are used for fastening industrial girders in place at large manufactorums around the Imperium.{/n}
  - After: {n}Among the debris: ripped-out girder fixtures from a manufactorum.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The pile of rocks, dirt, and thick dust densely covers the entire bottom of the hollow and the entire space around it. There is nothing of note here, just debris that the Haemonculus never bothered to clean up after returning to his lair.{/n}
  - After: {n}Just rubble and dust the Haemonculus never cleared.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The multiple marks on the broken pieces suggest that the ceiling and the layer of rock above it were shattered in an explosion. The details elude you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Marks suggest an explosion. The details elude you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You study the edges of the breach carefully, reflect for a few minutes, and conclude that the hole in the lab ceiling was created by several powerful targeted explosions. After some more time, you note the characteristic marks on the debris and the walls. The ceiling was breached using melta charges.{/n}
  - After: {n}The breach edges show several targeted blasts. Melta charges did this.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "They would if they were going to do business with representatives of Humanity." {n}Heinrix's voice is dull and quiet, as if the Interrogator has suddenly been drained of all his strength.{/n}
  - After: "They would, to trade with Humanity." {n}Heinrix sounds drained.{/n}
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "Tervantias was... robbed? I really wish I could have seen his face the moment he looked upon his lair!" {n}Marazhai laughs mockingly, then looks around the room.{/n} "Although this place... is not a Haemonculus's lair. Too safe. Too shabby. More of a last refuge."
  - After: "Tervantias, robbed? I'd love to see his face!" {n}Marazhai looks around.{/n} "This is no real lair. A last refuge."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The hole in the lab's vaulted ceiling and the hollow underneath it point you to the obvious conclusion: something broke into this room, ripped out a piece of the lab, and dragged it outside. You are, for now, mystified as to what that something was.{/n}
  - After: {n}Something broke in through the ceiling and hauled part of the lab away. What, you can't tell.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}The Seneschal looks around, frowning.{/n} "I don't understand... Drukhari machinery and their toys seem out of place within these walls. They seem positively alien, in fact. These walls... why, this is the standard architecture of an Imperium bunker. Why would a xenos conduct their business in a place like this?"
  - After: {n}Abelard frowns.{/n} "Drukhari machines in an Imperial bunker? Why?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Cold Traders. Privateers. Rogue Traders..." {n}Heinrix breaks off, as if stopping himself at the last moment.{/n} "Mutually profitable commerce with xenos is not that uncommon, Abelard. And that is what went on in this place, a place built by humans and furnished by the Drukhari."
  - After: "Cold Traders. Privateers. Rogue Traders..." {n}Heinrix stops.{/n} "Xenos trade isn't rare, Abelard. Humans built this; Drukhari furnished it."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "My kin were unable to find this place. The Dark Ones... would hardly have been content with a single trophy, even one as great as this. No. This was done crudely and quickly — behaviour more typical of mon-keigh."
  - After: "My kin never found this. The Dark Ones would take more. This was crude — mon-keigh work."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "The work is precise, though not the neatest. Whoever did this clearly knew what they were looking for and where to strike. Just look at the edges of the breach, shereen — they were definitely ripped apart by a targeted blast."
  - After: "They knew where to strike, shereen. See the edges? A targeted blast."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "This world belongs to House Winterscale. But I don't believe... I refuse to believe His Lordship Calligos would ever collaborate with xenos. Dark red and brownish-green would envelop his figure every time the subject of hunting the enemies of Humanity was brought up. He... despised them. Hated them."
  - After: "This is Winterscale's world. But Lord Calligos despised xenos. He'd never deal with them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Whatever contraption this chamber used to house, judging by the size of the fixtures, it could have gone through the hole in the ceiling. The only question is: what was it? Although, given Tervantias's obsession with his "masterpiece," one could venture a guess.{/n}
  - After: {n}Whatever stood here could fit through the hole. Given Tervantias's "masterpiece," you can guess.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch4/Janus_ChapterStart/Janus_ChapterStart_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "How are things in the colony?"
  - After: "How's the colony?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I apologise for intruding upon your hallowed ground. It is where my journey from Commorragh has taken me."
  - After: "Forgive me. My path from Commorragh led here."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am the {mf|master|mistress} of this planet, {name} von Valancius. And I require something of you."
  - After: "I am {mf|master|mistress} of this planet, {name} von Valancius. I need something."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Who am I, you ask? I am Rogue Trader von Valancius! On your knees, knave, while you still have them!"
  - After: "I'm Rogue Trader von Valancius! Kneel, knave!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I suppose I can now call myself an interdimensional traveller."
  - After: "I'm an interdimensional traveller now."
- **Player**
  - Before: "And just who might you be?"
  - After: "And who are you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What world is it?"
  - After: "What world?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Yes. The xenos is coming with me. As my guest."
  - After: "Yes. The xenos is my guest."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Shackle the xenos and keep him imprisoned until my ship arrives."
  - After: "Shackle the xenos until my ship arrives."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Kill the Farseer] "This one? He is of no further use to me."
  - After: [Kill the Farseer] "He's no further use."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Marazhai, aren't you and the Children of Asuryan of the same blood? Why do they loathe you so?"
  - After: "Marazhai, why do your Asuryan kin loathe you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How are things on Janus?"
  - After: "How is Janus?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you know anything about my abduction?"
  - After: "Know about my abduction?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I would say a ransom for his rescue is in order."
  - After: "His rescue merits a ransom."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Draw your weapon] "I wish to challenge your bold statement. He is my prisoner."
  - After: [Draw your weapon] "No. He is my prisoner."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You said Yrliet would serve the Aeldari once more. Are you seeking to use her again?"
  - After: "You'd use Yrliet again?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Well, now. The one about the woman with horns sounds promising. Go on."
  - After: "The horned woman. Go on."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am sure your kin brought their misfortune upon themselves."
  - After: "Your kin brought it on themselves."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your kinsman, Eklendyl, helped us escape from Commorragh."
  - After: "Eklendyl helped us escape Commorragh."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I just cut down a good hundred Aeldari in Commorragh. Keep up that tone, and you will become the hundred and first."
  - After: "I killed a hundred Aeldari in Commorragh. Want to be the hundred and first?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Warm greetings to you as well. You are almost as hospitable as the Dark City."
  - After: "Almost as hospitable as the Dark City."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do the people of Janus say about my abduction?"
  - After: "What does Janus say of my abduction?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Yrliet, kindly explain to your kinsman that there is no reason for him to be so riled up."
  - After: "Yrliet, calm your kinsman."
- **Old Man**
  - Before: {n}A poorly shaved commoner in worn coveralls eyes you with suspicion. He is clutching an autogun that looks like it is one careless reload away from falling apart. The man narrows his eyes and enquires,{/n} "Oi! Who are you lot? Yer not bandits, are you?"
  - After: {n}A scruffy commoner with a battered autogun.{/n} "Oi! You lot bandits?"
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "Vistenza Janus Vyatt ab Aram af Koronus?" {n}The commoner pronounces the governor's florid name flawlessly, but every word makes him flinch like someone is hitting him with a stick.{/n} "We {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusVistenzaAlive}pray for her health{/d} every day!"
  - After: "Vistenza Janus Vyatt ab Aram af Koronus?" {n}He flinches.{/n} "We {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusVistenzaAlive}pray for her health{/d}!"
- **Old Man**
  - Before: {n}The man squints with his weak eyes and finally realises who is standing before him. He collapses to his knees with a whiny grimace and wails,{/n} "Blessed Throne! Mercy, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, have mercy! Blasted old eyes didn't recognise you!"
  - After: {n}He kneels, wailing.{/n} "Mercy, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Didn't recognise you!"
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "The Chem-Princes collect tithes, flog troublemakers, protect us from bandits, and don't fight much among 'emselves... All's well."
  - After: "The Chem-Princes tithe and keep order. All's well."
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "Can't say our lives are all in order, though. The war ended all that. The nobles were so scared of the riots that they abandoned the irrigation facilities and skedaddled to the capital for good. Too afraid there are still conspirators hiding on their estates, waiting to gut them at night."
  - After: "Fearing riots, the nobles fled to the capital."
- **Old Man**
  - Before: {n}The man gives you a puzzled look.{/n} "Wassat? Did some rotter abduct you? Who could perpetrate such villainy? Kidnapping {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}, the nerve! We ain't heard nothing here on Janus!"
  - After: {n}Puzzled.{/n} "Someone abducted {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}? Ain't heard nothing!"
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "Our new masters, the Ultrequisitors, they're a dignified bunch. They fancy the learned type, though, and no good ever comes from scholars. But on the upside, they are paying you thrones for your service. Can you believe it? I hadn't seen a throne in my whole life, and they are giving us two for every month's work!"
  - After: "The Ultrequisitors pay two thrones a month!"
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "Blessed Throne! You're joking me! {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}, in these here backwoods! What an honour, a big ol' honour, this!" {n}The man drops to his knees and tries his best to hide his travesty of a firearm, pretending that he was not just pointing it at your chest a moment ago.{/n}
  - After: "Blessed Throne! {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}, here! What an honour!" {n}He kneels, hiding his gun.{/n}
- **Old Man**
  - Before: {n}The man furrows his shaggy eyebrows and pokes his travesty of a firearm in your direction.{/n} "Trynna pull a fast one on me, eh? Like {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}'d go wandering about this here swamp... Gah! Emperor almighty!"
  - After: {n}He jabs his gun at you.{/n} "Liar! {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}, in this swamp? Gah!"
- **Old Man**
  - Before: {n}The old man flinches in terror, drops his travesty of a firearm, and falls on his knees with a snivelling grimace.{/n} "Throne above! Yer {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, have mercyyy! Didn't recognise ya!"
  - After: {n}He drops his gun and kneels.{/n} "Mercy, yer {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!"
- **Old Man**
  - Before: {n}The old man furrows his shaggy eyebrows and pokes his travesty of a firearm in your direction.{/n} "Trynna scare the pants off me, are you? Well, I'll have none of that! Or I'll call them wardens over the vox, they'll grab ya by the floppers right quick! Them wardens, they don't mollycoddle bandits like yo—"
  - After: {n}He aims.{/n} "I'll vox the wardens on ya—"
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "Do I have anything to say about the life of the mon-keigh? No, your servants are of as little interest to me as they are to you. They simply... carried on in your absence. Some died. Some achieved various insignificant things. Nothing has changed."
  - After: "Your servants bore me. Some died. Nothing has changed."
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "Wassatchusay? Sounds like heresy talk to me..."
  - After: "Wassat? Sounds like heresy..."
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "Will do, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Can't let xenos scum like him walk free." {n}He eagerly points his weapon at the Farseer.{/n}
  - After: "Will do, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!" {n}He aims at the Farseer.{/n}
- **Old Man**
  - Before: {n}The sight of the dying xenos makes the commoner rejoice.{/n} "You show 'em, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Death to the enemies of Humanity!"
  - After: {n}He cheers.{/n} "You show 'em, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Death to xenos!"
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}An iridescent haze momentarily clouds the world around you, and that moment is all it takes for Muaran to hide Eklendyl behind the veil of his xenosorcery.{/n} "We will speak of my kin's fate no longer. All that was meant to be said has been said."
  - After: {n}A haze, and Muaran hides Eklendyl by xenosorcery.{/n} "Enough of my kin's fate."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "Farewell, mon-keigh. I am pleased that our meeting did not spill blood into the Lilaethan's womb." {n}An iridescent haze momentarily clouds the world around you, and that moment is all it takes for Muaran to vanish behind the veil of his xenosorcery.{/n}
  - After: "Farewell, mon-keigh. I'm glad no blood was spilled." {n}Muaran vanishes in a haze.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet nods silently and leaves it at that, as if she is less interested in Muaran's words than in your reaction.{/n}
  - After: {n}Yrliet nods, watching you.{/n}
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "Ours are the souls of the true Aeldari. Our ancestors, whom the craftworld cowards preferred to forget..."
  - After: "We are the true Aeldari. The craftworld cowards forgot that."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "You, despicable, dishonoured, madness-stricken blind renegade, will not speak of what it means to be an Aeldari."
  - After: "Mad renegade, do not speak of being Aeldari."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "Oh, but we are all that keeps their very essence alive, Farseer. You chose to abandon their great legacy at the call of cowardice, so do not embarrass yourself now with your pathetic attempts to justify such a betrayal."
  - After: "We keep their essence alive, Farseer. You fled in cowardice."
- **Eklendyl**
  - Before: {n}Eklendyl shoots you a keen look and asks coldly,{/n} "Will your capital offer protection? I do not wish to exchange one prison for another."
  - After: {n}Coldly,{/n} "Will your capital protect me? I want no new prison."
- **Eklendyl**
  - Before: "The mon-keigh turned out to be a traitor. How shocking!"
  - After: "A traitorous mon-keigh. Shocking!"
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "Oi, keep your wisecracks to yourself! If I hear you badmouth {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}, I'll shoot your floppers clean off!"
  - After: "Badmouth {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} and I'll shoot your floppers off!"
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}{d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusEldarAllies}Muaran{/d}'s silhouette emerges from the dense foliage without disturbing a single blade of grass. He addresses you in an accusatory tone of dissatisfaction,{/n} "I sensed your mind, mon-keigh. Why are you skulking by the Webway Gate? Why have you come to the Lilaethan in secret? Do you intend ill for us?"
  - After: {n}{d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusEldarAllies}Muaran{/d} appears.{/n} "Mon-keigh, why skulk by the Webway Gate?"
- **Old Man**
  - Before: {n}His expression darkens.{/n} "There's this plague going around on Janus, though... Makes your hair fall out, your skin go pale, and your voice disappear. Turns normal, Emperor-fearing people into right freaks, scum of Humanity. We call folks like that retches. Scary to look at — better to put them all down. Well, we do, little by little. With poison."
  - After: {n}Grimly,{/n} "A plague makes folk retches. We poison them."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}After a lengthy pause bordering on insult, Muaran inclines his head slightly.{/n} "I do not seek confrontation, mon-keigh. My words were chosen without proper diligence."
  - After: {n}After a pause, Muaran nods.{/n} "I seek no fight. My words were careless."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "My people are not welcoming of spies and infiltrators." {n}Muaran peers at you, then says thoughtfully,{/n} "However, you, mon-keigh, did not come here to spy on the Webway Gate. You came through it. I can sense its energy lingering on you now. This changes many things."
  - After: "We hate spies." {n}He peers.{/n} "But you came through the Gate. That changes much."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "The news of your disappearance has not reached Janus. My guess is that your close servants decided to conceal this event so as not to beget fear."
  - After: "Janus never heard. Your servants likely hid it."
- **Old Man**
  - Before: {n}With a frowning grimace, the commoner bows and mutters under his breath,{/n} "Oh, this won't end well. With guests like these, better grab 'em by the floppers and to the pyre. Burn them right quick."
  - After: {n}He bows, muttering.{/n} "Won't end well. Should burn 'em."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "The Lilaethan has been charitable to the mon-keigh. She bestows special gifts upon some of your servants; she forges bonds with them. This is the first time I have seen our world so... tolerant of your kind. It reminds me just how much I still do not understand. Alas, your kin do not trouble themselves with contemplating this matter. They fear those gifted by the Lilaethan, they despise them, and seek to kill them. And that does not surprise me at all."
  - After: "The Lilaethan gifts some of your servants. Your kin fear and kill them."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Muaran's voice grows pensive.{/n} "The Lilaethan's slumber is restless. She has guarded a part of herself away from you — it is what the mon-keigh call the isolated region. At first, I thought it was the Lilaethan's attempt to push you away, so she could heal from the wounds your cold iron had inflicted upon her flesh, but... I see something else in what is transpiring. A mystery."
  - After: {n}Pensive.{/n} "She walled off your isolated region. Not to heal. A mystery."
- **Muaran**
