  - Before: {n}Muaran exchanges long looks with Eklendyl, then says gravely,{/n} "This is where Eklendyl's path and yours diverge, mon-keigh. He will stay with us when you leave."
  - After: {n}Muaran glances at Eklendyl.{/n} "Here your paths part. Eklendyl stays with us."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "We will send instructions to our mon-keigh serv— allies to provide you with means of transportation. Farewell, mon-keigh. I am pleased that our meeting did not spill blood into the Lilaethan's womb."
  - After: "Our serv— allies will transport you. Farewell."
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "No bandit or xenos, that's plain to see! Can you say the same? You..."
  - After: "No bandit or xenos, me! Can you say the same?"
- **Old Man**
  - Before: {n}Upon noticing a non-human in your retinue, the old man grimaces with contempt and clutches the Aquila hanging around his neck.{/n} "And chumming around with inhuman scum, no less! Begone, you lanky freak! I compel you in Saint Cognatius's name, in Saint Nicomedes Keefe's name, in Saint Drusus's name..."
  - After: {n}He clutches his Aquila.{/n} "Begone, xenos! In Saint Cognatius's name..."
- **Eklendyl**
  - Before: {n}{d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_EklendylSaved}Eklendyl{/d} casts a weary eye over the commoner and enquires quietly,{/n} "Is this mon-keigh possessed or simply mad?"
  - After: {n}{d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_EklendylSaved}Eklendyl{/d} sighs.{/n} "Possessed or mad?"
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "I'm just a lowborn, a small, humble man! I've only ever seen your lustrous visage on the holy icons in the temples of the capital."
  - After: "I'm a humble lowborn! I've only seen your face on temple icons."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai laughs mockingly.{/n} "Another Farseer who chose to hide from the blades of the Reaving Tempest! Well, it is nothing I cannot rectify, coward."
  - After: {n}Marazhai laughs.{/n} "Another Farseer hiding from the Reaving Tempest! I'll fix that, coward."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Upon noticing {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_EklendylSaved}Eklendyl{/d}, Muaran flinches, then says solemnly,{/n} "Brother Eklendyl, I praise Asuryan for the fortune of seeing you again. Please, step under my protection without delay."
  - After: {n}Seeing {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_EklendylSaved}Eklendyl{/d}, Muaran starts.{/n} "Brother, praise Asuryan! Come under my protection."
- **Eklendyl**
  - Before: "Brother Muaran, I do not feel threatened... not anymore."
  - After: "Brother Muaran, I feel no threat... not anymore."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Muaran looks at Yrliet and says with enmity in his voice,{/n} "Outcast Yrliet, you walk the path paved with your own misdoings. Once more mon-keigh have found their way to our domain, and once more you aid them in doing so!"
  - After: {n}To Yrliet, coldly,{/n} "Outcast, again you bring mon-keigh here!"
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Muaran's voice drops to a venomous hiss when he sees Marazhai.{/n} "Dark Ones have no place here."
  - After: {n}He hisses at Marazhai.{/n} "Dark Ones have no place here."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Neither war nor ill intent follow in our wake, Muaran. Your anger is unwarranted."
  - After: "We bring no ill intent, Muaran."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Muaran's eyes shift from Yrliet to Marazhai, from Marazhai to Eklendyl, then back to Yrliet again. He exclaims indignantly,{/n} "By Asuryan's grace, what is the meaning of this strange visit?"
  - After: {n}He eyes each of you.{/n} "By Asuryan, what is this visit?"
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "I won't shame myself by complaining. We live, thanks be to the God-Emperor and Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We pray for your health every day."
  - After: "No complaints. We live, thank the Emperor and Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **Old Man**
  - Before: {n}The old man lowers his voice.{/n} "Who knows with him. Folks say he doesn't govern us no more at all. They say {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusEldarGovern}forest spirits{/d} have coaxed him, the ones that slip inside his palace at night. Those spirits whisper things into his ears — all their wicked ploys and plots. They almost made him ban expeditions to the islands, but the red priests didn't let him. It's where they live, those spirits. In their old forest shrines."
  - After: {n}Quietly,{/n} "They say {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusEldarGovern}forest spirits{/d} from the island shrines whisper to him at night."
- **Eklendyl**
  - Before: {n}Eklendyl nods.{/n} "I am elated to be once more among those with whom I shared Crudarach's time of bloom, Muaran."
  - After: {n}Eklendyl nods.{/n} "I rejoice to be among Crudarach's kin again, Muaran."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "My people do not bargain for the lives of their kin," {n}Muaran declares angrily.{/n} "We will remember your deed — nothing more."
  - After: "We don't bargain for kin," {n}Muaran snaps.{/n} "We will remember this."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "It is not up for discussion, mon-keigh. It is so."
  - After: "It is not up for discussion."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "We will send instructions to our mon-keigh serv— allies to provide you with means of transportation. You are free to go wherever you wish. But Eklendyl stays with us." {n}Muaran points at the Farseer you rescued.{/n}
  - After: "Our serv— allies will transport you. Eklendyl stays." {n}He points.{/n}
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "I'm a scout, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I wander the woods, I test the soil." {n}Taking great care, the old man reaches into his sack and pulls out a scratched auspex with a long spike, wrapped in a muddy rag.{/n}
  - After: "I'm a scout, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I test soil." {n}He shows a battered spiked auspex.{/n}
- **Old Man**
  - Before: {n}His voice drops to a whisper.{/n} "We also pray that she never sets her sights on us. They say scary things about the capital, about her court, about the missing people. Rumour has it, they host a never-ending ball at her palace. The dancing never stops, not for a moment. Any servant who steps inside the palace never comes out. There must be an awful lot of work to do at that ball of theirs."
  - After: {n}Whispering,{/n} "Servants who enter her palace ball never return."
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "The Tech-Priest told me, 'Once a thousand steps you have walked, thrust the mystical probe into the soil, say a prayer, then press the smaragdine seal. Offer three prayers to the Emperor, then press the ruby seal. Thus will the probe test the land and tell you what minerals dwell therein.'"
  - After: "Every thousand steps, I pray and probe for minerals."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai narrows one eye.{/n} "His body is neither strong enough nor spirited enough to bear torment. I will not waste my efforts on him."
  - After: {n}Marazhai squints.{/n} "Too weak to torment. Not worth it."
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "Can't say I have the foggiest. We've never even heard the governor's name. But it still beats living under that accursed heretic, Vistenza the Bloodsucker."
  - After: "Never heard his name. Still beats Vistenza the Bloodsucker."
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "And some blokes say they saw a woman with horns in these woods—" {n}Despite his excitement at the rare opportunity to tell every possible tall tale he knows to a stranger, the old man suddenly remembers who is standing before him and chokes on his unfinished story.{/n}
  - After: "Some saw a horned woman in these woods—" {n}He remembers who you are and stops.{/n}
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "Oh, it's just groxwash, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, it's nothing. Just some faffers running their mouths." {n}The old man looks down sheepishly.{/n}
  - After: "Just groxwash, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}He looks down.{/n}
- **Muaran**
  - Before: {n}Muaran grimaces contemptuously.{/n} "A mon-keigh cannot comprehend the depth of the tragedy that befell our home, our... Crudarach. The duty of every Child of Asuryan is to do all they can to quell the pain of that loss. And Yrliet the Outcast is no exception."
  - After: {n}Muaran sneers.{/n} "You cannot grasp Crudarach's loss. Yrliet must help ease it."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Unlike you, Muaran, I was able to find the truth. The truth of Crudarach's doom was revealed to me... even though that required me to throw myself in the Dark City's deadly embrace." {n}Yrliet frowns and looks defiantly into the Farseer's eyes.{/n}
  - After: "I found the truth of Crudarach's doom. In the Dark City." {n}She glares.{/n}
- **Eklendyl**
  - Before: "Is the fire of our souls not better directed toward worthy deeds than arguing with our kin?" {n}Eklendyl waves his hands in the air, making several gestures of unknown meaning. Muaran and Yrliet fall into cowed silence.{/n} "I can see that something is troubling your delicate heart, my kinsman Muaran. Share your feelings with me and the Outcast then, and I will reveal the truth of Crudarach's fate to you a little later."
  - After: "Enough quarrelling." {n}Eklendyl gestures; silence.{/n} "Muaran, what troubles you? Crudarach's fate can wait."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "You..." {n}Muaran bows his head, surprised.{/n} "Allow me to see the truth that was revealed to your eyes." {n}The Farseer steps toward Yrliet. He touches her brow lightly with one hand and the faintly glowing spirit stone with the other.{/n}
  - After: "You..." {n}Muaran bows his head.{/n} "Show me." {n}He touches Yrliet's brow and her spirit stone.{/n}
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "Now... I understand." {n}Dark shadows appear on the Farseer's face, and the look in his eyes becomes even sterner than before.{/n} "And that is why I am once again appealing to your sense of duty, Outcast. We did not spend our time on the Lilaethan in fruitless grief. On the contrary, our lost kin have answered my call and are now pleading for help. Driven by revenge, they set out to pursue the one responsible for Crudarach's rueful demise, only to end up as captives on a mon-keigh world."
  - After: "Now I understand." {n}He darkens.{/n} "Outcast, our kin hunted Crudarach's destroyer. Now they're captive on a mon-keigh world."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "We did not spend our time on the Lilaethan in fruitless grief. On the contrary, our lost kin have answered my call and are now pleading for help. Driven by revenge, they set out to pursue the one responsible for Crudarach's rueful demise, only to end up as captives on a mon-keigh world."
  - After: "Our kin hunted Crudarach's destroyer. Now they're captive on a mon-keigh world, pleading for help."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "That I know not. All that my visions showed me was an infinitely green sea... A living sea. And the maddening thirst of a hunter who was pursuing the Children of Asuryan. Outcast, your Path is taking you toward the stars again. Find our kin and do not let them perish."
  - After: "I saw a living green sea and a hunter stalking our kin. Save them, Outcast."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Her emerald-green gaze turns to you and rests on you a little longer than usual.{/n} "Dare I hope that... you will lend me a shoulder to lean on again, elantach?"
  - After: {n}Her green gaze lingers.{/n} "Will you help me again, elantach?"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "They might have... But that does not mean they should pay for their mistakes with their lives."
  - After: "Perhaps. But not with their lives."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah looks up at the Farseer with torment in her eyes.{/n} "You should."
  - After: {n}Kibellah, tormented,{/n} "You should."
- **Old Man**
  - Before: {n}The old man glances at the Farseer suspiciously.{/n} "Will that there chatty mug be flying to the capital with Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}? He's got an awful big mouth, he looks like trouble..."
  - After: {n}Eyeing the Farseer,{/n} "That chatty mug's going with Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}? Trouble..."
- **Muaran**
  - Before: "You come from Commorragh?" {n}Muaran says nothing for a moment, then continues, his voice shocked,{/n} "Now I see. The Gate refused to obey me because it was sealed from within. By the Dark Ones, no doubt. The Lilaethan was meant to become a slaughterhouse for the Drukhari!"
  - After: "Commorragh?" {n}Shocked.{/n} "The Dark Ones sealed the Gate. A Drukhari slaughterhouse!"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "'Riled up'?" {n}Yrliet gives you a confused look, but then nods.{/n} "Elantach and I have travelled a long way, Muaran. We..." {n}She gives you another long look.{/n} "We were prisoners in Commorragh, but followed a Webway thread out. That thread brought us here."
  - After: "'Riled up'?" {n}Yrliet nods.{/n} "We were prisoners in Commorragh." {n}She glances at you.{/n} "A Webway thread led us here."
- **Old Man**
  - Before: "Our good masters, the wise Magi, they take care of us. Every month, we give 'em a drop of blood as payment for protecting us, and they use it to brew potions that can detect freaks. We do whatever mystical tasks they require of us, and for that, the Magi order the irrigation facilities to yield twice as much."
  - After: "The Magi take our blood monthly to find freaks. In return, double irrigation."

## World/Dialogs/Ch4/Quetza_al_Khet/AeldariQuetza/AeldariQuetza_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You invaded this world, and I want to know why."
  - After: "Why did you invade this world?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I need to know more about the Haemonculus."
  - After: "Tell me about the Haemonculus."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am here to resolve this conflict peacefully."
  - After: "I want peace here."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "We have nothing to discuss."
  - After: [Attack] "Nothing to discuss."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not support the methods of the xenos, but I understand their motives. Perhaps they could pay you compensation?"
  - After: "I understand their motives. Could they pay compensation?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You lost your world and are now depriving others of theirs out of vengeance. Why do you think you are different?"
  - After: "You lost your world, so you take others'. How are you different?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "It looks like I can kill two grox with one bullet today."
  - After: "Two grox, one bullet."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What are you talking about? I killed the Haemonculus in Commorragh with my own hands."
  - After: "I killed the Haemonculus in Commorragh myself."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will give you a chance, Yrliet. Stand by my side — or perish."
  - After: "Yrliet, stand with me — or perish."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I... must have misspoken."
  - After: "I... misspoke."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your ships are destroyed, Crudarach is lost, and so are the Farseers. You sacrificed everything to attack this world. Why?"
  - After: "Ships, Crudarach, Farseers — all lost to attack this world. Why?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "By the vastness of space, can we not come to some agreement?"
  - After: "Can we not reach an agreement?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your brothers and sisters are exhausted, you are trapped, and I am the only person who can change that."
  - After: "Your kin are exhausted and trapped. Only I can help."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It is simple, xenos. Tell nothing but the truth if you want to live."
  - After: "Tell the truth if you want to live, xenos."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "Let us get down to business, Calligos."
  - After: [Attack] "To business, Calligos."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack both sides] "I shall just get rid of you all."
  - After: [Attack both sides] "I'll get rid of you all."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You call purging an entire world a decisive action?"
  - After: "Purging a world is 'decisive'?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What if I were to say it was my predecessor who was to blame for Crudarach's demise?"
  - After: "What if my predecessor caused Crudarach's demise?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Yrliet, your kin butchered hundreds of thousands of people on this world in the name of vengeance. Is this the path you see for your people?"
  - After: "Yrliet, your kin butchered hundreds of thousands here for vengeance. Is that your people's path?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Look at yourself, Calligos. You are becoming a monster whose only desire is to kill."
  - After: "Calligos, you're becoming a monster who only wants to kill."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You no longer see profit beyond the thrill of the hunt. You and the xenos can help one another."
  - After: "You see only the hunt, not profit. You and the xenos could help each other."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I presume there is no avoiding the confrontation?"
  - After: "So we must fight?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I do not want to kill you and you know it. You sacrificed everything in the name of your kin, and it is now the time to think about yourself."
  - After: "I don't want to kill you. You gave everything for your kin — now think of yourself."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Enough talk. You will perish on this planet like the rest of the xenos."
  - After: "Enough. You'll die here with the other xenos."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Says the one who has already betrayed me once without a second thought."
  - After: "Says one who already betrayed me."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack the Aeldari] "Calligos, let us butcher these curs until the very ground is a gory mess of their bones and innards! More skulls for the lords of the Expanse!"
  - After: [Attack the Aeldari] "Calligos, let's butcher these curs! More skulls for the lords of the Expanse!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The xenos had a valid reason to attack this world. I see no issue with sacrificing the lowborn if it helps a good cause."
  - After: "The xenos had good reason. Sacrificing lowborn for a good cause is fine."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Yrliet, I will permit your kin to explain themselves."
  - After: "Yrliet, your kin may explain themselves."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack both sides] "I would rather get rid of you all."
  - After: [Attack both sides] "I'd rather kill you all."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Nocturne of Oblivion, it has certainly been a while. What are you doing here?"
  - After: "Nocturne of Oblivion, it's been a while. Why are you here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "We have tracked down the prey, Calligos. It is time to have some fun."
  - After: [Attack] "Prey cornered, Calligos. Time for fun."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "You are guilty before this world and the Imperium. The time of retribution is at hand."
  - After: [Attack] "You're guilty before this world and the Imperium. Retribution is here."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Whisper] [Lie] "I will kill them myself after I find out what I need to know."
  - After: [Whisper] [Lie] "I'll kill them myself once I learn what I need."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Lay down your weapons, and I promise to judge you fairly."
  - After: "Disarm and I'll judge you fairly."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you still think your kin are worth saving?"
  - After: "Are your kin still worth saving?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A stately Aeldari warrior steps forward, calmly looking at the intruders. His armour and its adornments gleam in the sun despite the traces of dried mud and caked-on blood.{/n} "Not a step further, mon-keigh." {n}The smooth voice of the xenos sounds out of place in the rough wilderness of Quetza Temer.{/n} "I grant you the mercy of leaving the emerald halls of the Children of Asuryan — begone and never return."
  - After: {n}An Aeldari warrior steps forward.{/n} "Not a step further, mon-keigh." {n}Smoothly:{/n} "Leave and never return."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Elantach." {n}Yrliet's face is covered with a patchwork of tiny scars. There are dark stains of clotted blood on her, and she holds her leg slightly bent, as if leaning on it would hurt. The {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_Quetza_YrlietRunAway}time she has spent in the woods of Quetza Temer{/d} has not been without consequences.{/n}
  - After: "Elantach." {n}Yrliet is scarred and limping from her {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_Quetza_YrlietRunAway}time in the woods{/d}.{/n}
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: {n}The Solitaire {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ZanniNotEnemy}bows theatrically{/d}.{/n}
"With embers glowing cupped in my two hands,
I bear them through the deluge to the hearth."

  - Before: {n}The Aeldari cast confused glances at their champion.{/n} "A {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}temporary alliance{/d}? So be it. Children of Asuryan, fight with the fury of Kaela Mensha Khaine!"
  - After: {n}The Aeldari hesitate.{/n} "A {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}temporary alliance{/d}? So be it. Fight!"
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: {n}There is no trace of the bored Calligos from a few moments ago. The Rogue Trader is now closely studying the potential battlefield, his enemies... and the heads he intends to claim as trophies.{/n}
  - After: {n}Calligos sizes up the battlefield and his future trophies.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Who would believe you after what you have said, mon-keigh? No. We are not going to rely on someone so weak in spirit."
  - After: "Who would trust you now? Not us."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: {n}Winterscale sneers viciously.{/n} "Let us say I believe you, this once. But there will not be a second time."
  - After: {n}Winterscale sneers.{/n} "Once. Never again."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "I did warn you not to test my patience, new blood." {n}Calligos grabs his axe and charges at you, followed by his entire retinue.{/n}
  - After: "I warned you, new blood." {n}Calligos and his retinue charge.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The warrior brushes Calligos away like a bothersome fly.{/n} "We are not seeking your justice, mon-keigh. We are yearning for retribution."
  - After: {n}The warrior ignores Calligos.{/n} "We seek retribution, not justice."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Aeldari warrior glares at the Solitaire.{/n} "So you knew, Arebennian! We will talk about this later. As for right now... The mon-keigh has left me no choice."
  - After: {n}He glares at the Solitaire.{/n} "You knew, Arebennian! So be it."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "Playing with your prey like a cat? Fine, new blood, you are still young. Just remember that patience is not my strong suit."
  - After: "Toying with prey? Fine, but I'm not patient."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We were reluctant to shed blood on this land, to begin with. But your companion decided otherwise — he shot down our vessels, chased us into the woods, harried and hounded the survivors..." {n}The Aeldari's eyes gleam in the sunlight.{/n}
  - After: "Your companion shot down our ships and hunted us." {n}His eyes gleam.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "I do not need any prophecy to tell you this, Lord Captain... You are in for a fight. A nasty fight."
  - After: "A nasty fight awaits, Lord Captain."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "And I will finish what I started!" {n}Winterscale glares impatiently.{/n}
  - After: "I'll finish it!" {n}Winterscale glares.{/n}
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "I do not believe a single word, xenos."
  - After: "I don't believe a word, xenos."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "But spending enough time among the mon-keigh granted me clarity of vision. Once you stop valuing the lives of others, be they your kin, strangers, or enemies, you gradually become a monster yourself. And one day someone will come to stop you."
  - After: "But I learned: stop valuing lives, and you become a monster someone must stop."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "Throne take you, and all the misfortunes in the galaxy along with you!" {n}Winterscale gives you a clap on the shoulder. The expression on his face is mysterious and almost sad.{/n} "I must confess that all this dismal talk has given me a migraine and made my old wounds ache. So you want to save these xenos? Suit yourself! By my grace, I entrust you with the lives of the enemies of Humanity. Have fun!"
  - After: "Throne take you!" {n}Winterscale claps your shoulder.{/n} "Fine, save your xenos. Have fun!"
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "That can be arranged, xenos." {n}Calligos chuckles nastily.{/n} "The only compensation I accept is blood!"
  - After: "That can be arranged." {n}Calligos chuckles.{/n} "I take payment in blood!"
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: {n}Winterscale looks over the ruins and salutes his entourage with a gesture only he can understand.{/n} "My patience has run out, {name}. Enough words. Drive the prey toward me, and my hounds will assist."
  - After: {n}Winterscale signals his men.{/n} "Enough, {name}. Drive the prey to me."
- **Worten the Grey**
  - Before: "Time to crush skulls!" {n}Worten slams his iron fist against his armour, and Winterscale's vassals draw their weapons.{/n}
  - After: "Crush skulls!" {n}The vassals arm.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Harlequin is being his usual self. His answer only leaves you with more questions that are just as pointless to ask as the previous one.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Harlequin's answer is pointless.{/n}
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: {n}The Solitaire mockingly presses a finger to the mask's lips, indicating that he is {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ZanniEnemy}not going to grace you with an answer{/d}.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Solitaire hushes you: {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_ZanniEnemy}no answer{/d}.{/n}
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "I do not know about you, {name}, but these xenos bastards are giving me the creeps!" {n}Calligos shifts his excited gaze from the Aeldari warrior to Yrliet, and from her to the Solitaire.{/n} "That one, in the motley. I want his head. Now."
  - After: "Xenos give me the creeps, {name}!" {n}Calligos eyes them.{/n} "I want motley's head."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Do you understand now, elantach? The one responsible for the demise of my home. The one to blame for the suffering you had to endure in the streets of the Dark City... He is somewhere on this world. And very close, too. We must find him..." {n}Yrliet pauses, carefully choosing her words.{/n} "And write the closing chapter of this sorrowful tale."
  - After: "The one who destroyed my home and tormented you in the Dark City is here, elantach." {n}Yrliet pauses.{/n} "Let us end this tale."
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: {n}Calligos' mouth foams with rage and anticipation, and his eyes become bloodshot. He emits a guttural scream:{/n} "Blood for the Rogue Trader's throne! Skulls for the lords of the Expanse!"
  - After: {n}Calligos foams with rage.{/n} "Blood for the throne! Skulls for the Expanse!"
- **Worten the Grey**
  - Before: {n}The Arch-Militant smiles so widely you fear his mouth may split and reveal several extra rows of teeth. His deafening inhuman bellow fills you with power and thirst, a desire to rip, tear, and exterminate.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Arch-Militant's inhuman bellow fills you with bloodlust.{/n}
- **Calligos Winterscale**
  - Before: "There has been less good hunting to be had in the Expanse since your arrival, new blood. If the xenos hold useful information about the distant stars... that is a reason to consider your offer."
  - After: "If the xenos know of distant stars... I'll consider it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But his immortality has a limit: resurrection requires reagents, equipment, energy — the fleshmaster had those in abundance in Commorragh, but now he is on the run and vulnerable. And while the Haemonculus has not yet returned to full strength, there is a chance to destroy him forever."
  - After: "But resurrection needs resources. Now he runs, weakened. We can end him forever."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A stately Aeldari warrior steps forward, calmly looking at the intruders. His armour and its adornments gleam in the sun despite the traces of dried mud and caked-on blood.{/n} "My people have {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}heard about you{/d}, elantach." {n}The smooth voice of the xenos sounds out of place in the rough wilderness of Quetza Temer.{/n} "Are you here to help us deliver justice? Or will behave as most mon-keigh would and betray those you once helped?"
  - After: {n}An Aeldari warrior steps forward.{/n} "We have {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}heard of you{/d}, elantach." {n}Smoothly:{/n} "Will you help us, or betray us?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Trazyn's dim projection now flares up with renewed force, and a hint of indignation has seeped into the xenos's usually detached voice:{/n} "It cannot be... Nocturne of Oblivion? That impudent Solitaire has somehow escaped my collection to strut about the backwaters of the galaxy!" {n}Toothless irritation rattles through whatever the Necron has in place of a voice box.{/n} "Well... I will bring him to heel again... someday."
  - After: {n}Trazyn's projection flares:{/n} "Nocturne of Oblivion escaped my collection!" {n}The Necron rattles.{/n} "I will reclaim him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The xenos have made their camp among the ruins of an ancient city of the Imperium. Only the alien growths of the xenotech and the wreckage of the Aeldari ship disturb the picture of centuries-old devastation and rebirth.{/n}
  - After: {n}The xenos camp in Imperial ruins.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Despite their meagre weaponry and flimsy shelters, the xenos are ready to attack at any moment. Their bodies are relaxed, but their minds remain cold and focused.{/n}
  - After: {n}Poorly armed, the xenos remain ready to strike.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No matter how fair the starlight, the star is destined to fade some day. Your fellow mon-keigh was not of the light, for there was darkness clouding his heart. You need not grieve his loss."
  - After: "Darkness clouded his heart. Do not grieve him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You... survived? Asuryan showed you mercy, Outcast, and so did our ancestors from the Alaitoc Infinity Circuit. Tell me, sister, what was their answer?"
  - After: "You survived, Outcast? What did the ancestors answer?"

  - Before: "Oh, yeah. That's much better, thank you!"
  - After: "Oh, much better, thanks!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Before you chide me for my decisions, consider how many of our kin you managed to save in the void between the local stars. And {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_Yrliet_BrokenPromise}how many more you could have saved{/d}."
  - After: "Count the kin you saved. And {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_Yrliet_BrokenPromise}those you didn't{/d}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Aeldari pays no heed to your words... though he may be just pretending.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Aeldari ignores you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I would expect nothing else from a mon-keigh. But one good turn deserves another." {n}Shairenkhei produces an unknown xenodevice and scrutinises it.{/n} "The Farseers could not divine where the master of flesh makes his lair, for an unknown force is hiding him from the penetrating gaze of the wise ones. The Children of Asuryan... have never encountered anything like this before. Having circled the world several times and failed in our search, we ventured to unleash our pent-up fury on the planet in the hope that we would be graced with a fortunate accident."
  - After: "One good turn deserves another." {n}He studies a xenodevice.{/n} "Something hides the master of flesh from our Farseers, so we struck the planet blindly."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I usually do not think about your kind at all." {n}The Aeldari shrugs softly.{/n} "But I am prepared to admit that there are... certain worthy specimens among the millions of your kind."
  - After: "I rarely think of your kind." {n}He shrugs.{/n} "But a few are worthy."
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: "The beast in human guise is tamed, and yet
There does exist no throttling chain to quell
That thirst for blood that slumbers in his veins.
Comes now the hour when rattling links protest,
And, with a grisly roar, he turns once more."
  - After: "The beast in human guise is tamed, and yet
Its bloodlust wakes; it turns on us once more."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}For some reason, your words bring a faint smile to Yrliet's lips.{/n} "Worry not, elantach. It is my turn to rescue you and your people."
  - After: {n}Yrliet smiles.{/n} "Worry not, elantach. It is my turn to rescue you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "After the master of flesh has been dealt with?" {n}Shairenkhei sighs tiredly, a faint shadow of a smile gracing his face.{/n} "We will go home... Not to Crudarach, no, but to our kin from the other craftworlds. The Farseers have already contacted our allies, and they are already on the way to the system."
  - After: {n}He smiles tiredly.{/n} "Then we go to kin on other craftworlds. Allies are coming."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "The Farseers' mistakes doomed Crudarach, Shairenkhei! And their excessive cruelty and thirst for vengeance almost doomed those of us who managed to survive against all odds in the void between foreign stars. You know it just as well as I do, but you continue to do their bidding. Oh, Shairenkhei, you could take the Webway Gate — and go away from the dangers and tribulations of the Expanse. But you have chosen to stay here instead. You are dying. You are feuding with the mon-keigh. Have not the Children of Asuryan spilt enough blood? Is it not enough that we have lost our home? Why do you wish to expose even more of your kin to mortal peril?"
  - After: "The Farseers doomed Crudarach, yet you serve them! You could flee by the Webway Gate. Why risk more kin?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Shairenkhei's iron will falters under Yrliet's relentless pressure.{/n} "It is... it is too late to change anything. The deed is done. Their will carried out. The Outcasts from Alaitoc will come to the local stars, and we will leave with them, sister."
  - After: {n}Shairenkhei falters.{/n} "It is done. The Outcasts of Alaitoc will come, and we leave with them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Once the master of flesh is defeated, we will be relieved to depart this exhausted world... and the Expanse. Is this not what you call this region of space?"
  - After: "Once the master of flesh falls, we leave the Expanse."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Did the darkness of space drive you mad during your exile, sister?" {n}Shairenkhei recoils from Yrliet as if from a scorching flame.{/n} "Even those who walk the Path of the Seer baulk at joining souls with the ancestors inside the Circuit. They are wise and know that the ritual is perilous to the spirit. Your chances of success are... simply non-existent. You would die without achieving anything! And even if you did not die immediately, ask yourself honestly: why should the ancestors listen to a simple Outcast?"
  - After: "Are you mad, sister?" {n}He recoils.{/n} "Even Seers fear the Circuit. You would die for nothing."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "As you said, Alaitoc is a world of my fellow Outcasts. They would not wish harm upon me, which gives wings to my hope. Look me in the eye, Shairenkhei. You must accept it and help me." {n}Though Yrliet's words are addressed to her kinsman, she is watching your reaction closely.{/n}
  - After: "Alaitoc's Outcasts won't harm me. Help me end our kin's suffering." {n}She watches you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It would be humiliating to end up as a game piece in the hands of a mon-keigh... had we been interested in the internecine strife among the lesser species."
  - After: "Being a mon-keigh's pawn would humiliate us, if we cared."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your eagerness is commendable, but we will not abandon our search until the flesh sculptor is destroyed... or until we are presented with proof of his demise.   - After: "We hunt the flesh sculptor until he's dead. If you kill the Haemonculus first, our Farseers will know, and we leave."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Our Farseers paid an insurmountable price to contact a craftworld located billions of stars away from here. Many of them perished to give the rest of us the chance to be rescued. And I will not jeopardise the lives of those who yet remain."
  - After: "Many Farseers died reaching a distant craftworld. I won't risk the rest."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Because they are driven by grief. Sometimes pain and loss blinds even the best of us."
  - After: "Grief blinds them."

  - Before: "More pain? Did you manage to prevent the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusEldarEliminated}death of our kin and Muaran{/d} on the Lilaethan? The Arebennian told me everything that happened."
  - After: "Did you prevent the {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusEldarEliminated}death of our kin and Muaran{/d} on the Lilaethan?"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I am sorry, elantach, but it is not up to you to shape my destiny. Not this time."
  - After: "Sorry, elantach. Not your choice this time."
- **Yrliet**

  - After: "Thank you, elantach." {n}She gestures gratitude.{/n}

  - Before: "With words alone fate cannot be constrained,

And to her will in tribute might respond
The Seers of the Path with bridge outwrought."
  - After: "Words bind no fate; deeds give them weight.

- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I did not think you would let me go so easily, elantach." {n}Yrliet looks at you in surprise, as if expecting a catch.{/n} "But if it really is the pure desire of your soul... so be it."

  - Before: {n}Yrliet cocks her head pensively.{/n} "I think I will return to them some day. But our paths are too tightly interwoven to end them here."
  - After: {n}She muses.{/n} "Someday. But our paths are too entwined to end here."
- **Yrliet**

  - After: "I know they caused this!" {n}Her spirit stone glows.{/n} "But my life's cause teeters. I must speak to the Infinity Circuit. That is my Outcast's Path."

  - Before: "May Asuryan save us from this woe!" {n}Shairenkhei folds his arms on his chest in a graceful gesture, but the horror is obvious on his face.{/n} "No. I will not allow another world to perish at the hands of the mon-keigh, even if this means forsaking my soul!"

  - Before: "A bold statement from one who has not yet forsaken his soul even once."
  - After: "Bold, from one who's never lost his soul."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And I am not going to reveal all the secrets of my kind to you, mon— elantach. You may have helped us in our hour of need, but I trusted you at the Outcast's behest. But I will say this — the warriors of Alaitoc are coming here, to your stars. This is an unalterable truth."
  - After: "Our secrets stay ours, mon— elantach. But Alaitoc's warriors are coming."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The strange energy that permeated the clearing where the paths of humans and Aeldari happened to cross is gradually dissipating. All eyes turn to Yrliet, the Aeldari who managed to survive the deadly ritual, and who awoke looking pensive and enlightened.{/n}
  - After: {n}The energy fades. Yrliet wakes enlightened.{/n}
- **Nocturne of Oblivion**
  - Before: {n}Like a forgotten shadow, the Solitaire steps into the light and leans forward with interest, a spectator watching the culmination of an exciting performance.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Solitaire leans in, rapt.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Elantach, your anger is like the raging winds of desert worlds — restrain it, and listen."
  - After: "Elantach, restrain your anger. Listen."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "During my exile, I met many companions who temporarily joined me on my endless travels." {n}Yrliet closes her eyes.{/n} "One such companion was a fellow Outcast who had already completed many Paths. It was he who told me about the ritual of unity — a great opportunity for one's spirit to reach out and touch the Infinity Circuit of the craftworld known to the Farseers who perform it. Shairenkhei said that the Crudarach Farseers have already contacted Alaitoc. This means... This means I can, too."
  - After: {n}Yrliet closes her eyes.{/n} "An Outcast taught me the ritual of unity: touching a craftworld's Infinity Circuit. Crudarach's Farseers reached Alaitoc. So can I."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Have you already forgotten who is responsible for Crudarach's demise, elantach?" {n}Yrliet's spirit stone glows brightly, but the disapproval in her eyes is even brighter.{/n} "The only thing my kin are guilty of is getting too close to the stars of the mon-keigh. They... We... lost our home. We were hounded by your people. We were tormented by dark ones. No... None of Crudarach's children deserve such a fate. And I will not let those who yet remain perish in darkness."
  - After: "Forgotten who destroyed Crudarach?" {n}Her eyes blaze.{/n} "Hounded by your people, tormented by dark ones. I will not let the rest perish."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What do you mean to do, sister?"
  - After: "What will you do, sister?"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "No! Do this, elantach, and your entire demesne will be drowned in blood. Not only the blood of my kind, but your subjects will also meet a terrible end. And I... I can prevent it. It is my turn to rescue you and your people."
  - After: "No! That drowns your demesne in blood. It is my turn to rescue you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "How can you describe the inevitable demise of your and my own kind so nonchalantly? If you let this happen and leave things as they stand, rivers of blood will flood your demesne. Not only will the Children of Asuryan die, your subjects will also meet a terrible end. So will your worlds and your entire protectorate. And I... cannot allow this. It is my turn to rescue you and your people."
  - After: "You shrug at both peoples' doom? Blood will flood your worlds. It is my turn to rescue you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Unless the warriors of Alaitoc arrive in this part of the galaxy, the sons and daughters of Crudarach will perish among the worlds of the mon-keigh. Is that the fate you wish for us?"
  - After: "Without Alaitoc, Crudarach's children perish here. Is that what you want?"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "It will take the Warriors of Alaitoc many years to discover the Webway Gate capable of bringing their strike force to the Expanse. Perhaps you will be too old by then, and only on your deathbed will you hear the news — the Children of Asuryan have come to exact their vengeance."
  - After: "Alaitoc needs years to find a Webway Gate. You may hear of their vengeance on your deathbed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The strange energy that permeated the clearing where the paths of humans and Aeldari happened to cross is gradually dissipating. All eyes turn to Yrliet, the Aeldari who managed to survive the deadly ritual, but who awoke looking angry and dejected.{/n}
  - After: {n}The energy fades. Yrliet wakes angry, dejected.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet brushes a strand of fiery hair from her forehead and nods appreciatively:{/n} "I know how difficult it is to go against the will of your kin. And yet I cannot hide my joy that we both lived through this moment... and emerged with a tale to tell."
  - After: {n}Yrliet nods:{/n} "Defying kin is hard. I'm glad we survived."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "We will have to find another way. I understand that it is not easy for those who have lived all their lives sheltered within a craftworld to accept that sometimes life leads us down different paths. But the path that you and the Farseers have chosen only leads to more pain."
  - After: "There must be another way. Yours leads only to more pain."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I am fine, elantach." {n}A gracious look and a slight smile underscore Yrliet's words.{/n} "Thanks to you, I have finally reached the end of my Path. This Path. And I am grateful I had you to walk alongside me."
  - After: "I am fine." {n}She smiles.{/n} "My Path has ended. Thank you for walking it with me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Did you prevent the death of Eklendyl, follower of the Path of the Seer, one of the Crudarach Farseers tormented by the master of flesh in the Dark City along with the rest of our kin? Yes, I am aware of {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_EklendylDiedInSpire}his fate{/d}."
  - After: "Did you save Farseer Eklendyl in the Dark City? I know {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_EklendylDiedInSpire}his fate{/d}."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I am an Outcast, elantach. My place is among the stars."
  - After: "I am an Outcast. My place is among the stars."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I would be lying if I said I had not thought about it. But you have helped me and my kin all this time to the best of your ability. Should I not repay you in kind, elantach?"
  - After: "I've thought of it. But should I not repay you?"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Then so be it." {n}Yrliet folds her fingers in a familiar gesture of trust and accord.{/n}
  - After: "So be it." {n}She gestures trust.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet's lips twist and she nods silently.{/n}
  - After: {n}Yrliet grimaces, nods.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "An Outcast returning home? Truly a joyous occasion, considering how many of our kin have been lost. We are glad to welcome you back, Yrliet."
  - After: "An Outcast home! Welcome back, Yrliet."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "However, I dare not complain — for my kin, the hour of triumph has arrived at last. Once the master of flesh is no more, we can go to the edge of this stellar expanse, away from the gaze of mon-keigh. And peacefully await the arrival of our kin from distant stars."
  - After: "Still, we triumph. Then we await kin from distant stars."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "What are you talking about, Shairenkhei?" {n}Yrliet stares intently into the eyes of the Aeldari warrior, but his gaze remains steady and calm.{/n}
  - After: "What do you mean, Shairenkhei?" {n}He stays calm.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The xenos hesitates and adds with slight embarrassment:{/n} "Lesser... {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}allied{/d} species."
  - After: {n}Embarrassed:{/n} "Lesser... {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_AeldariAlly}allied{/d} species."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Outcast Yrliet, I have some good news for you. Our Farseers managed to contact the children of Craftworld Alaitoc, and soon your fellow Outcasts will visit the part of the galaxy that the mon-keigh call the Expanse. They will take us away, give us a new home, and..." {n}Shairenkhei pauses, his gaze on you, wondering if he should continue.{/n}
  - After: "Good news, Yrliet. Our Farseers reached Alaitoc. Your fellow Outcasts will come and..." {n}He pauses, eyeing you.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch4/Quetza_al_Khet/ForestEvents/ForestEvents_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The shuttle disappears in the wild vegetation of the island. Several hours pass before the Rogue Trader finally admits that {mf|he|she} has been aimlessly wandering around in circles. Any attempts to get back on track by retracing {mf|his|her} steps have failed. Vox-communication cannot reach the ship. Now it becomes clear how Calligos Winterscale could get lost on his own world.{/n}
  - After: {n}The shuttle vanishes into the island's jungle. Hours later, the Rogue Trader admits {mf|he|she} is lost; retracing {mf|his|her} steps fails, and the vox cannot reach the ship. No wonder Calligos Winterscale got lost here.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The forest is alive with the constant rustling of thick leaves and the creaking of wood. It is as if the trees themselves are walking around like lumbering, looming people. But surely it is just a trick of the eye — plants cannot walk, can they?{/n}
  - After: {n}The forest rustles and creaks, as if the trees themselves walk. Surely a trick of the eye?{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Quite a few hours pass before something worth noticing finally shows up amid the dense forest: a pile of charred human bones lying in a shallow pit, and in front of it, like a standing stone, a broken fire cultivator with melted nozzles is stuck in the ground. Other corpses can be seen in the grass nearby, just as old and charred, but distinctly non-human. Scattered alongside those are xenos weapons, covered in dirt. Some of the weaponry appears to be in working order, so it is still possible to get some use out of it.{/n}
  - After: {n}Hours later: charred human bones in a pit beside a broken fire cultivator. Nearby lie burnt xenos corpses and dirty xenos weapons, some still usable.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The irresistibly sweet aroma of fruit teases the Rogue Trader's olfactory senses, especially after so many hours spent in the stuffy humidity of the forest. But after locating the source of the aroma, {mf|he|she} decides against tasting the appetising fruits: several mummified corpses lie under the fruit trees, their withered faces a testament to their agony, their bodies covered in dark wounds resembling the bites of giant leeches.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sweet fruit beckons, but {mf|he|she} declines: mummified corpses lie beneath the trees, covered in leech-like bites.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The trek among the monotonous forest landscapes is becoming dull. The Rogue Trader's weary eyes are ready to close of their own accord when the usual sounds of the forest are interrupted by a blood-curdling scream. The cries are drawing closer and closer, then their source finally appears — a small creature with slick black fur and a long tail. As if mocking the Rogue Trader, it lets out another piercing cry and scurries away, its yellow hind paws winking between the tree branches.{/n}
  - After: {n}A blood-curdling scream breaks the dull trek. A small black-furred, long-tailed creature shrieks mockingly and scurries off.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The rich flora of the forest at times staggers the imagination. Among the trees covered in ivy and moss, the Rogue Trader notices a spiralling pattern of small white lumps on one of the tree trunks. Someone has cut the bark, causing the milky sap to flow down the damaged parts of the tree, harden from the heat, and turn into uneven rubbery cocoons.{/n}
  - After: {n}A tree trunk bears a spiral of cuts, its milky sap hardened into rubbery cocoons.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sound of rushing water comes from somewhere close by. After a few more steps, the forest parts, revealing a stepped waterfall. The clear currents flow gracefully from one step to the next, carrying peculiar colourful ribbons, which turn out to be living creatures that latch onto the porous surface of rocks with their flexible bodies, snapping at small fish with their eyeless, toothy heads.{/n}
  - After: {n}A stepped waterfall. Colourful ribbon-like creatures cling to its rocks, snapping at fish with eyeless, toothy heads.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The forest hike lasts an entire day. In the golden rays of dusk, the Rogue Trader sees a small hill crowned with an Aquila — a double-headed eagle totem made from the plasteel and rockcrete components of an ancient ship. The foot of the hill provides a much less scenic view, however: the soil is stained brown from all the flesh smeared upon it, contrasted only by the white specks of bone shards mixed into the dried-up bloody mass.{/n}
  - After: {n}At dusk, a hill crowned with an Aquila built from ancient ship parts. Its foot is caked with flesh and bone shards.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After a day's journey, the smoke of the smouldering fires has been left far behind. The wind has changed, and with it the forests of Quetza Temer, if only subtly. The path the Rogue Trader just followed has become an impassable wall of tangled vines. The rare anomaly of the local florosphere has once again played its insidious trick — the forest has changed, reference points have swapped positions, and paths have become intertwined.{/n}
  - After: {n}After a day, the fires are far behind. The forest has shifted again: the path is now a wall of vines, landmarks swapped.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The now familiar rustle of the centuries-old canopy and barely perceptible movement at the edge of the Rogue Trader's vision announce that the forests are once again in motion — are they fleeing the distant raging fires or simply migrating? It is difficult to say. However, spacious meadows have now been replaced with dense forest, and the trails have changed direction once more.{/n}
  - After: {n}The forest moves again, fleeing fire or migrating. Meadows become thickets; trails change direction.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Part of the forest is obstructed by a thin grey veil emitting barely audible clicks. The translucent curtain ripples and starts moving in the direction of the Rogue Trader. Upon closer inspection, the veil turns out to be woven from many threads carried by fast-flying bugs. The hive attacks the intruder, then retreats into the foliage, leaving behind burning, itching bites and wisps of shredded web.{/n}
  - After: {n}A clicking grey veil of web-carrying bugs swarms the Rogue Trader, leaves itching bites, and retreats.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Hours of wandering bring the Rogue Trader to a tall, sprawling tree. Something shiny is stuck in the foliage. Coming closer, the Lord Captain recognises an obsolete heavy void suit model that has been subsumed among the growing branches. A heavily damaged skull bares its teeth from behind the murky glass — at least their death was quick.{/n}
  - After: {n}An old heavy void suit hangs in a tree's branches, its skull smashed. At least death was quick.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After several hours of traversing the forest, a small mountain blocks the way. Something about the pattern on the stone seems wrong. A few moments later, it becomes clear that there are cogitator parts glinting at the base of the mountain. The machines appear to have grown into the stone itself along with the dirt and grass, with the only proof of their artificial origin being the occasional flashes of lumens powered by some random unknown impulses. A carcass is lying on a flat stone nearby, cut open in sacrifice to an unknown god.{/n}
  - After: {n}A small mountain with cogitator parts grown into its stone, lumens flickering at random. Nearby, a carcass lies sacrificed to an unknown god.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Rogue Trader has never seen an anthill of such size before. But the most disturbing thing about it is a xenos skeleton tied to the anthill with bonds made from some unknown material. The Drukhari weapon stuck in the corpse is the only detail that can point to the perpetrator. Being eaten by ants is a horrific torture that makes the blade in the back seem like an act of mercy — a most uncharacteristic gesture for this race.{/n}
  - After: {n}A huge anthill with a xenos skeleton bound to it. A Drukhari blade in its back was, strangely, a mercy.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The skies break open, the heavy rain penetrating even the dense canopy of the forest. Luckily, the elements relent before long. As the sun emerges once more, the forest comes alive with the singing of birds accompanied by the quiet sound of falling droplets.{/n}
  - After: {n}A brief downpour passes; birds sing as the sun returns.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Rogue Trader requires rest, and {mf|he|she} soon finds a suitable spot for a camp — a meadow with a few fruit trees. A creature with an elongated body and large blunt claws leisurely descends from one of the trees. Its muzzle is red as if stained with blood, but it turns out to be merely the juices of the fruit from the nearby trees. The fruit has a peculiar taste reminiscent of grox meat baked in sweet and sour sauce.{/n}
  - After: {n}Needing rest, {mf|he|she} camps in a fruit-tree meadow. A long-clawed creature, muzzle red with juice, climbs down. The fruit tastes like sweet-and-sour grox.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Halfway through the day, the Rogue Trader discovers a new wonder of Quetza Temer's forests — a spacious stretch of land overgrown with reddish-brown grass covered in sickening yellow blisters. No other plant can be seen among the red blades of grass. The answer to this mystery may have something to do with pale spider-like insects crawling on the underside of the blades.{/n}
  - After: {n}A field of red-brown grass with yellow blisters, nothing else growing. Pale spider-like insects crawl beneath the blades.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}In the shade of the tallest trees in this area of the forest, the Rogue Trader spots mushrooms that come up as high as {mf|his|her} waist. Strands of sponge-like tissue hang from under their pale lilac caps, almost reaching the ground. As soon as the Rogue Trader approaches one of the mushrooms, the strands draw in, the cap rolls up, and the mushroom spews out a cloud of reddish spores. Perhaps it would be wiser to give this place a wide berth.{/n}
  - After: {n}Lilac mushrooms tall as {mf|his|her} waist spew red spores when approached. Best avoid them.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch4/Quetza_al_Khet/QuetzaVillagers/QuetzaVillagers_dialogue

  - Before: "How do you even survive in these forests?"

  - Before: "You think that several gods have set foot on Quetza Temer?"

  - Before: "Was my coming here foretold?"
  - After: "My coming was foretold?"

  - Before: "And how exactly do we conduct the soothing ritual?"
  - After: "How do we do the soothing ritual?"

  - After: "Why does Speaks-With-Gods call us 'Starborn'?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have questions for you."
  - After: "I have questions."

  - Before: "How does your tribe manage to survive in these forests?"
  - After: "How does your tribe survive here?"

  - Before: "Do you know where your brother and the other Starborn are now?"

  - After: {n}Anxious youths surround you. An eagle-branded elder steps forward.{/n}

  - Before: {n}A group of lean young people surrounds you, shooting anxious glances between you, Calligos, the priest, and the grey-headed elder who has stepped forward. Unlike the rest, her skin is completely free of decoration, save for the two-headed eagle branded on her wrinkled forehead.{/n}
  - After: {n}Anxious youths surround your group. An eagle-branded elder steps forward.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Something's calling, it's calling, and calling..." {n}Idira covers her ears with her palms and forces her eyes shut.{/n} "There, in the place of no return, sits the shadow of one who is both alive and dead at once... The voices are calling me there, calling so desperately, but why? WHY?"
  - After: "It's calling..." {n}Idira covers her ears.{/n} "Someone alive and dead, beyond return. Why me? WHY?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Nevertheless... This ruler knows that you will bring Speaks-With-Gods home and soothe the forest of Quetza Temer. The prophecies of the priests have never betrayed our tribe before, and thus this ruler asks you to forget about your worries and rest here, in the heart of the forest."
  - After: "Still, you will bring Speaks-With-Gods home and soothe the forest. Rest here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Because you are the Sky-Herald of the Eagle-God, created by Him from the stars' glow and the night sky's darkness. The one who carries His seal in your image, clad in the armour of our ancestors' most ancient prophecies."
  - After: "You are the Eagle-God's Sky-Herald, bearing His seal, as prophesied."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is an honour for this ruler's tribe to serve you, O Starborn. Follow the path of lights, and you will find your shelter, food, and water. When you decide that it is time to follow the priest and your Starborn kin, this tribe will pray to the Eagle-God Himself for your success."
  - After: "An honour, Starborn. Follow the lights to shelter. We will pray for you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Starborn had lost his priest in battle, so he ordered this ruler's brother to help him trace the spirits' footsteps and cleanse Quetza Temer of their filth. But when Speaks-With-Gods left his home, something enraged the forest. Thus both the Starborn and this ruler's brother were trapped by the ever-changing paths and lurking evil spirits."
  - After: "The Starborn lost his priest and took this ruler's brother to hunt spirits. Then the forest raged, trapping them."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Food and shelter?" {n}Jae's eyes light up.{/n} "So long to our worn-out boots and sodden cape, shereen! My homeworld has a wise rule — never dismiss the hospitality of those who consider you their overlord!"
  - After: "Food and shelter?" {n}Jae brightens.{/n} "Never refuse hospitality, shereen!"

- **Idira**
  - Before: "Like you've never heard that one before, Lord Captain."
  - After: "Like you haven't heard that before, Lord Captain."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "The powers of my kin may have disturbed the wild flora of this world, which then concealed the remnants of the children of Crudarach from the wrath of your rival. That means that they are somewhere in the forest. Surviving. Hiding. Preying on one another."
  - After: "My kin's power may have stirred the forest, hiding Crudarach's survivors somewhere out there."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh yes, Speaks-With-Gods is the priest of this tribe and this ruler's half-brother. He listens to the forest and calls to the earth, wards off the punishing lashes of the skies, and speaks to the Eagle-God on behalf of our tribe. Before disappearing in the wandering forest, he told this ruler to prepare for your arrival."
  - After: "Yes. Speaks-With-Gods, this ruler's half-brother, speaks for us to the forest and the Eagle-God. Before vanishing, he foretold you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It seems that the priest went into the woods with the Starborn's retinue and vanished along with them.{/n}
  - After: {n}The priest seemingly vanished with the Starborn.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I presume this 'priest' is another unsanctioned psyker with the gift of divination." {n}Heinrix tiredly pinches the bridge of his nose.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Everything happened just as Speaks-With-Gods foresaw. The Starborn are back, and with them our—"
  - After: "As foreseen. The Starborn are back, with our—"

One good thing about Quetza Temer is that the fruit here is sweeter than Calixian honey and more tender than the meat of a young grox."

  - Before: "You should get some rest as well, {name}. And remember, it is better to go hunting when you are full of vigour, but slightly hungry. The hunger... adds acuity. Makes the kill more intoxicating, you know?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Our meeting occurred just as Speaks-With-Gods foresaw." {n}The woman's accent grates on your ears — her words sound like a fusion of High Gothic and the most vulgar tongue of the rabble.{/n} "Welcome to the heart of the forest, Starborn. This ruler—"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The name of this ruler is Leads-Ahead, O Starborn.   - After: "This ruler is Leads-Ahead." {n}She gestures around.{/n} "We serve the Eagle-God and guard the Temple of Quetza Temer."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Because you are the Sky-Heralds of the Eagle-God, created by Him from the stars' glow and the night sky's darkness. The ones who carry His seal in your image, clad in the armour of our ancestors' most ancient prophecies."
  - After: "You are the Eagle-God's Sky-Heralds, bearing His seal, as prophesied."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This ruler has lived many of Quetza Temer's seasons for this moment. Please, ask away, Starborn."

  - Before: {n}The sinewy old man bows his head in reverence.{/n} "With your arrival, the blessing of the Two-Headed Eagle-God has descended upon Quetza Temer, O Starborn! - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The priest nods affirmatively.{/n} "The spirits-from-the-darkness brought the fire-rain down on Quetza Temer, killing many of the tribes who had cared for the forests young and ancient. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The priest shudders, his eyes staring into space over your shoulder. His pupils dilate, and his head leans to the side... Then, after dispelling the vision seen by him alone, he gives you a friendly smile.{/n} "Silent questions hang in the air... This servant knows much, and even more is unknown.   - After: "I pray for it with every breath."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Suddenly, the old man throws his head back — his body shudders, and droplets of blood burst from between his clenched teeth.{/n} "The sunset rays will paint the heart of the forest crimson if the darkness leaves it, and the two stars will part, then meet again! - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "One day, you too will grow sick of all the talking, and then you too will choose shooting xenos on a wild planet over endless intrigue." {n}Cheerful notes ring in Calligos's voice.{/n} "Fine, we have plenty of time. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What, all done with your questions?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It's about time indeed, {name}!" {n}Calligos gives you a friendly pat on the shoulder and summons his retinue with a gesture.{/n} "It may take a while to find their trail, but Worten here has a keen eye, and his sense of smell can rival any old dog — we will do just fine!   - After: "About time, {name}!" {n}Calligos pats your shoulder.{/n} "Worten will find their trail. Keep up!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Calligos laughs openly.{/n} "Maybe I will, maybe I won't. Wait around for a couple of decades, new blood, and let others get used to you. It is not often that we have a fresh new Rogue Trader in our circle."
  - After: {n}Calligos laughs.{/n} "Wait a few decades, new blood."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your enquiries are curious, to be sure. Quetza Temer is a planet with a rather dreary backstory. A long time ago, it supplied my great-grandfather with tonnes of succulent fruits and thousands of cargo containers filled with a special building fibre processed from the local forests. The population all lived in large cities a safe distance away from the tangled paths and trees. And then this quiet life was dashed by xenos raids."
  - After: "Quetza Temer once sent my great-grandfather fruit and fibre. Then came xenos raids."
- **Worten the Grey**
  - Before: "The old man was a weakling, and that is why he's dead. That's what happens when you can no longer fulfil your duty to your master." {n}Worten grins in contempt, his entire being expressing his disdain for the Seneschal.{/n}
  - After: "The old man was weak, so he died." {n}Worten grins in contempt.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Winterscale's expression hardens.{/n} "Consider my idiot voidborn nephew dead. Besides... You haven't led me out of the forest yet — you've only brought us into its heart. I still have time to kill all your precious xenos before I become formally indebted to you."
  - After: {n}Winterscale hardens.{/n} "My nephew is dead to me. You haven't led us out yet. I can still kill your xenos first."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Calligos carries himself with an air of indifference, but the sudden furrows on his forehead betray his regret.{/n} "Many fine warriors have perished on this hunt. Raise a toast to their name when you can."
  - After: {n}Calligos's brow betrays regret.{/n} "Fine warriors died here. Toast them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Calligos gives a dismissive wave.{/n} "The unworthy always die during the hunt."
  - After: {n}Calligos waves dismissively.{/n} "The unworthy die."
- **Worten the Grey**
  - Before: {n}The Arch-Militant, previously indifferent to his master's words, raises his head. His burning, curious gaze fixes on Yrliet.{/n}
  - After: {n}Worten stares at Yrliet.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I shall consider your words, and that is all I shall promise."
  - After: "I'll consider it. No more."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "His callous words are painted crimson and purple... and yet bright veneers can never truly mask the deep colours of sorrow."
  - After: "Bright veneers can't mask his sorrow."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A void kraken may eat them both, for all I care!" {n}Winterscale makes a wry face and clenches his fists in anger.{/n} "Acting as if their war on heresy in the Expanse is just starting. Ha! I've been living it for decades. And I don't need an Inquisitorial preacher, and I certainly don't need Incendia's goodwill!"
  - After: "A void kraken can eat them both!" {n}Winterscale clenches his fists.{/n} "I've fought heresy here for decades!"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet gives you a grateful look.{/n} "We all carry the mark of our ancestors' guilt on our shoulders."
  - After: {n}Yrliet looks grateful.{/n} "We all bear our ancestors' guilt."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If I did, {name}, the price would be steep." {n}Winterscale sizes you up with a cunning gaze.{/n} "I have more than enough money and power. I shall need time to consider your offer."
  - After: "The price would be steep, {name}." {n}Winterscale eyes you.{/n} "I'll consider it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Frankly, your desperation excites me, {name}. I shall think on your offer, but that is the only promise you will get from me."
  - After: "Your desperation excites me, {name}." {n}Winterscale scratches his chin.{/n} "I'll think on it. That's all."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The forests of Quetza Temer are not like the jungles of Catachan, new blood.
