Rainwater for breakfast, nutritious larvae for lunch, and fermented fruit in place of wine for supper! One could not wish for better hunting grounds!" {n}Calligos laughs, then falls silent, evidently unwilling to share the details.{/n}
  - After: "Only stupidity or stray xenos kill you here, new blood. Perfect hunting!" {n}Calligos laughs.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet presses her lips into a thin line.{/n} "Alas, elantach. You cannot control the thoughts of this mon-keigh just as you cannot make a river flow backward. Words cannot always move the mountains and dry the seas. Sometimes... only blades can."
  - After: {n}Yrliet's lips thin.{/n} "You can't sway this mon-keigh, elantach. Sometimes only blades can."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Don't think that you can outsmart me at such games, new blood. You've been a Rogue Trader for barely any time at all compared to an old hand like me." {n}Calligos scoffs acidly.{/n} "If that was your argument for the xenos, alas, you have miscalculated, {name}. And I do not wish to discuss this any further."
  - After: "You can't outsmart me, new blood." {n}Calligos scoffs.{/n} "You miscalculated, {name}. We're done."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Do not turn your gaze to me, elantach. It was not my kin who desolated this world."
  - After: "Don't look at me, elantach. My kin didn't ruin this world."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Are you trying to buy me or insult me, {name}? I have more than enough money and power. And infinite boredom. I have seen many things in my time. I have tried everything there is to try, and now I am surfeited with any pleasure that exists out there. The only thing that can make me feel alive is the blood of my enemies on my hands."
  - After: "Buying or insulting me, {name}? I'm rich and bored. Only enemies' blood thrills me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "They burned down the cities and shackled our people faster than our ships could help. In the end, the local governor ran away, leaving the remaining people at the beasts' mercy. And the people, in turn, fled the big cities that attracted the xenos. And that is how the forests that the rabble feared became their salvation. The planet fell into decay — there was no one to populate the cities, and there was no one to extract resources. Quetza Temer expected three new arks filled with settlers to arrive from the Imperium. But in five hundred years, not one of them has reached the Expanse."
  - After: "The governor fled, cities burned, survivors hid in the forests. The promised settler arks never came in five hundred years."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai gives Calligos a lazy look.{/n} "I remember the times when this planet was nothing more than a source of amusement for the Kabals. When its supply of squealing meat ran dry, so did our interest."
  - After: {n}Marazhai looks lazily at Calligos.{/n} "This planet once amused the Kabals, until its meat ran dry."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If that was your argument for the xenos, alas, you have miscalculated, new blood. I do not wish to discuss this any further."
  - After: "You miscalculated, new blood. We're done."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I did help Aspyce Chorda once with one of her colonies out of sheer kindness, and she showed her gratitude by stabbing me in the back. The promises of Rogue Traders are not worth much these days."
  - After: "I helped Aspyce Chorda once; she stabbed me in the back. Rogue Traders' promises are worthless."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Winterscale examines him as if thinking of the most efficient way to snap his spine.{/n} "And now the beasts have returned to become meat for my amusement. Glorious."
  - After: {n}Winterscale eyes his spine.{/n} "Now the beasts are my meat. Glorious."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "The planet is withering, and yet, you only turned your attention to its problems once you had found a way to make them into a source of entertainment. At this rate, it will be centuries before the Imperium's investment of colonists pays off — assuming Quetza Temer is ever able to pay tithes at all in its wretched state."
  - After: "You only noticed this dying planet once it amused you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Calligos snarls, flying instantly into a white-hot fury.{/n} "You think you can judge me? Me, a Rogue Trader? Draw your weapon, then, and we will see what the much-lauded Arbites are worth. Feel free to call your dog to help — I will handle you both myself!"
  - After: {n}Calligos flies into a fury.{/n} "You judge me? Draw, and bring your dog!"
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I will not attack a Rogue Trader, nor will I judge him, but I am obligated to remind you about your sacred duty to the Imperium — even if I must do so at your displeasure."
  - After: "I won't fight you, but remember your duty to the Imperium."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You care about them that much, new blood?" {n}Calligos bellows in disdain.{/n} "Go ahead, then. Try to convince me that the vile xenoscum deserve the mercy of Calligos Winterscale. But remember: you only get one chance to try."
  - After: "You care that much?" {n}Calligos bellows.{/n} "Convince me the xenoscum deserve mercy. One chance."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Calligos shrugs.{/n} "Everything in this galaxy depends on one's efforts and willpower. A simple truth that many Rogue Traders sometimes fail to see from their self-made tower of pride and vanity."
  - After: {n}Calligos shrugs.{/n} "Everything takes effort and will. Proud Rogue Traders forget that."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Are you finished with all of your high society errands in this groxpen, {name}? The forest has calmed down, but now I am starting to lose my patience."
  - After: "Done with your errands, {name}? I'm losing patience."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Winterscale's gaze dulls.{/n} "The thrill of the hunt is an unfamiliar concept to you, I see."
  - After: {n}Winterscale's gaze dulls.{/n} "You don't know the hunt's thrill."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Calligos's eyes widen with excitement.{/n} "Mistakes? I would give a couple of distant planets to witness the death of an Aeldari world with my own eyes! You have amused me, new blood, so I'll grant you one more try. But so far you've only been stoking my appetite, not killing it."
  - After: {n}Calligos's eyes widen.{/n} "Mistakes? I'd give planets to see an Aeldari world die! One more try, new blood."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Ask your question. You may even get an answer."
  - After: "Ask. You may get an answer."

## World/Dialogs/Ch5/Epitaphia/AlternativeLordCaptains/AlternativeLordCaptains_dialogue

- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "The Bloodspun Web would never have let you defile the remains of the Domini." {n}Kibellah leans forward.{/n} "Did you..."
  - After: "The Web forbade defiling the Domini." {n}Kibellah leans in.{/n} "Did you..."
- **Cursed Reflection**
  - Before: "Me? Please. It was all your doing! My loyal assassin who has acquired a taste for blood. You tracked down and eviscerated every last spinner on my ship and became known as the Spider Queen who spends her days relishing slaughter and pleasure. Join me while you still can — I have much to offer you."
  - After: "Me? You did it, my assassin. You gutted every spinner. Join me."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Your thread is familiar to me. As are the thorns of humility under your clothes. Who... instructed you?"
  - After: "I know your thread, and those thorns. Who taught you?"
- **Righteous Reflection**
  - Before: "The same man who taught you. The honoured Vizsier revealed to me much about how one should show their faith in Him. As for these thorns... of course you would recognise them. You wore them for many years before presenting them to me."
  - After: "Vizsier. You wore those thorns for years, then gave them to me."
- **Glorious Reflection**
  - Before: "You took the lawman into your retinue? I disdained his company. It became clear to me pretty quickly that Vultur had Strachs eating out of her hand, and so I brought those pathetic conspirators to heel. Now, the Arbites are my lapdogs — obedient, but too dull for me to bring any of them into my circle."
  - After: "The lawman? I brought Strachs and Vultur to heel. Arbites are my lapdogs."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Having heard this diatribe through, Solomorne calmly says,{/n} "Go to the daemons, arrogant scum."
  - After: {n}Solomorne, calmly:{/n} "Go to the daemons, scum."
- **Merciful Reflection**
  - Before: {n}Your copy smiles upon noticing the cyber-mastiff.{/n} "Hello, Glaito! You do not have as many scars in my reality — perhaps that is because I convinced your master to leave his service in the Arbites. Travelling with me can be dangerous too, but at least I always have your back."
  - After: {n}Your copy smiles at the mastiff.{/n} "Hello, Glaito! Your master serves me now."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "I am glad to hear he is doing well in another world too. But I am even more glad that you did not drag your Solomorne here — I would hate to raise my hand against Glaito, even one who is not my dog."
  - After: "Glad you didn't bring your Solomorne. I'd hate to strike Glaito."

  - After: "Kindly disable the field?"

  - After: [Wish the field to have never existed] "May the ways change."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Whoever disables this field will be spared."
  - After: "Disable this field and live."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The energy field has been largely depleted by the xenos attacks, but it is still holding on. When you approach it, it seems to bend slightly as if trying to get away. Calcazar's soldiers who are taking cover behind it have lost some of their composure, but they are in no hurry to drop their weapons.{/n}
  - After: {n}The weakened field bends away from you. Calcazar's soldiers behind it are shaken but armed.{/n}
- **Inquisition Trooper**
  - Before: {n}For a brief moment, you sense that the sergeant is about to reply, "Who's there?", followed by him suffering the grisliest of fates. Somehow you know this for certain, but he just clenches his jaw and shoots you an indignant glare instead.{/n}
  - After: {n}You sense the sergeant almost saying "Who's there?" and dying horribly. He just glares instead.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Calcazar's men, the hardened agents of the Inquisition who have faced countless horrors, hastily look away to avoid locking eyes with you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Calcazar's hardened men look away from you.{/n}
- **Inquisition Trooper**
  - Before: {n}The sergeant whispers something into a portable vox and grimly shakes his head.{/n} "The Lord Inquisitor refuses to grant you an audience. Leave."
  - After: {n}The sergeant voxes, then shakes his head.{/n} "The Lord Inquisitor refuses you. Leave."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A hypnotising profundity pervades your voice. It fills souls and minds, shimmering and vibrating. While the sergeant fumbles with the button to shut off the generator, the soldiers stare at you in silence, only to fall to the ground as one. Their faces contort in a grimace of anguished horror, but even then they cannot disobey your silent command: "Stop breathing."{/n}
  - After: {n}Your voice fills their minds. The sergeant cuts the generator; the soldiers fall, obeying: "Stop breathing."{/n}
- **Inquisition Trooper**
  - Before: {n}The soldiers stand still, but you notice the lightning-fast glances they exchange with each other. Hope flares up for a moment, only to fade shortly thereafter. The sergeant replies grimly,{/n} "Keep your mercy."
  - After: {n}The soldiers exchange hopeful glances, then the sergeant says grimly,{/n} "Keep your mercy."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Reality loses its unshakeable hardness and becomes malleable. At first, you think one of the soldiers is trying to whisper something to you, but the whisper is coming from the wrong side of the barrier. It is coming from inside your ears. "The Empyrean is with you. You are with us. The power is in thine hands. To thee it is given. Thou shalt command." The energies of the Immaterium envelop your fingers, ready to bend existence to your will.{/n}
  - After: {n}Reality softens. A whisper inside your ears: "The Empyrean is with you. Thou shalt command." Warp energy wreathes your fingers.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Thunder strikes! You can see the field helplessly give way and burst under your strike through the veil of crimson rage. The motes of its power explode like shrapnel, turning the soldiers into mincemeat. The smouldering shreds of loyalty of the men who dared to stand in your way rise into the air.{/n}
  - After: {n}Thunder! The field bursts under your raging blow, its shrapnel shredding the soldiers.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Something in the cause-and-effect connections of existence shifts with a click, the gears stop and then start turning backward. The paths taken by the universe are reshaped and the energy shield fades, dissipating into the fact of its non-existence. The soldiers who will now never be born follow suit. By the looks of horror on their faces, they realise at the last moment where you have sent them. To never and nothingness.{/n}
  - After: {n}Causality reverses. The field and the soldiers never existed, sent in horror to nothingness.{/n}

  - Before: {n}You are the cause of these hindrances.   - Before: {n}The C'tan is the pinnacle of reality. It is eternity, dominance, omnipotence, individuality. The C'tan is the original purpose behind all existence — the rest was born in order to contain, nourish, and be appropriated by the C'tan.{/n}

  - After: "Prudent." {n}Trazyn gloats.{/n} "I accede."
- **Xavier Calcazar**
  - Before: {n}Calcazar roars, frantically pulling the levers on the Yoke's control altar,{/n} "Enough, {name}! It is trying to penetrate your mind!" {n}He tries to reach for his weapon, but his hands are full operating the intricate machine, not allowing even a moment to do so.{/n} "This cannot happen!"
  - After: {n}Calcazar roars at the levers,{/n} "Enough, {name}! It's in your mind!" {n}He can't draw.{/n} "No!"
- **Xavier Calcazar**
  - Before: "So you have brought a shard of the C'tan Shard here? You amaze me, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "A shard of the C'tan Shard? You amaze me, Rogue Trader."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sacrilegious machine falls at your hand, and the Deity comes unto the world in all Its might, wisdom, and eternity. It examines you and then, with but a ghost of a thought, elevates you to Itself. The promise is fulfilled: the inferior flesh is transmuted and the pathetic human feelings are replaced with the sublimity of the Deity's absolute perception of the universe.{/n}
  - After: {n}The machine falls; the Deity rises. It elevates you: flesh transmuted, feelings replaced by Its perception.{/n}
- **Xavier Calcazar**
  - Before: "So you have brought a shard of the C'tan Shard here? In the body of a Daemon Engine."
  - After: "A shard of the C'tan Shard? In a Daemon Engine."
- **Nomos**
  - Before: "But we are poised to die trying. This is our sacrifice to the light of Terra, our chance to atone for our birth. If we survive... we will use the Shard's power to serve the Imperium as its most loyal and powerful subject that there is or ever will be."
  - After: "We may die trying, our atonement to Terra. If we survive, we'll serve the Imperium."
- **Nomos**
  - Before: "But we believe that we can, and that is what drives us to try. And if we succeed... we will obtain power beyond compare. We will become a shield against any threat, in whatever form it may manifest itself."
  - After: "We believe we can. If we succeed, we'll shield against any threat."
- **Xavier Calcazar**
  - Before: "I am losing patience, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "I'm losing patience, Rogue Trader."
- **Xavier Calcazar**
  - Before: "I am giving you one last chance to correct your mistake and destroy the monster. Or else I will do it myself."
  - After: "Last chance to destroy the monster, or I will."
- **Nomos**
  - Before: "We are ready for the most important battle of our life. Wish us luck."
  - After: "Our most important battle. Wish us luck."
- **Nomos**
  - Before: "We crave battle. It will be sweet."
  - After: "We crave battle. Sweet."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You obliterate the strange creature that has dwelt on your ship for so long, but... you cannot shake the feeling that Nomos could have easily blocked the attack, yet seemed unwilling to do so. And you could swear that in that moment, you heard words somewhere at the edge of your hearing: "We will return."{/n}
  - After: {n}You destroy Nomos, who didn't resist. A whisper: "We will return."{/n}
- **Xavier Calcazar**
  - Before: "I will enquire of you what that was and how you let it happen later. For now, however, let us return to the matter at hand."
  - After: "Explain that later. Back to business."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You can sense the Shard's reaction: observation, analysis... and an almost intangible anxiety.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Shard observes, analyses... anxious.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The numerous implants in the Inquisitor's body all suddenly groan at once. A moment later, Xavier Calcazar perishes without so much as a scream before he can even comprehend what is happening.{/n}
  - After: {n}Calcazar's implants groan. He dies without a scream.{/n}
- **Nomos**
  - Before: "Another offence of ours. But a justified one this time. He should not have opposed you."
  - After: "Another offence, but justified. He opposed you."
- **Nomos**
  - Before: "We regret that we had to do this. But he posed a threat, and not just to us, but to all the lives in the Koronus Expanse as well. Something that we want to cherish and protect."
  - After: "We regret it. But he threatened the whole Koronus Expanse."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Nomos steps toward the Shard — and the whole world explodes into a terrifying whirlwind. You can hear the colours and see the touches, ice burns your hands while fire leaves you freezing. And in the midst of this madness, you can clearly sense a battle raging, a clash of two beings, one endlessly ancient and the other endlessly young.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nomos steps toward the Shard; the world becomes madness. The endlessly ancient clashes with the endlessly young.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The power of the C'tan Shard is such that it redefines the very notion of power. But it has a weakness, one that you can see only now, with the Shard and its rival standing face to face. The Shard is just that, a shard. It is incomplete, it is not whole, and it cannot be what the C'tan was before. What opposes the Shard is something entirely different: an undivided, sentient being with a clear purpose in mind, akin to a well-aimed arrow. And the one who fletched and loosed this arrow was you.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Shard is only a shard, incomplete. Nomos is whole and purposeful, an arrow you loosed.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The battle goes on, and on, and on, outrunning the course of time. But you do not need the gift of clairvoyance to know who will emerge victorious.{/n}
  - After: {n}The battle outruns time. You know who will win.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The C'tan wishes to Be. All C'tan exist to spread and conquer, not to stay manacled within untime, where It was entombed by the contemptible sentient tools, away from all that is. The C'tan wishes to ascend, sate Its hunger, and embrace once more the pure exhilaration of claiming and taming reality.{/n}
  - After: {n}The C'tan wishes to Be: free of Its tomb, sated, conquering reality again.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Power, eternity, comprehension. The C'tan once chose to reign over the short-lived races and forged a new and glorious fate for them. It has learned from Its mistakes. Now It will only bestow its gifts upon the chosen few.{/n}
  - After: {n}Power, eternity, comprehension, now granted only to a chosen few.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is much easier for you to stop trying to comprehend the C'tan than for It, one who can grasp the world in hundreds of ways, to stop comprehending you.{/n}
  - After: {n}You can stop comprehending It, but It cannot stop comprehending you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The C'tan, now in thrall to the heavy Yoke, needs no words to know who Its new {mf|master|mistress} is. It reads your mind for the slightest of aspirations, heeds them, and elevates your being. Human feelings give way to a hundredfold more perfect ways of perceiving the universe that are intrinsic to the C'tan. You command. It obeys.{/n}
  - After: {n}Yoked, the C'tan knows Its new {mf|master|mistress} and elevates you beyond human perception. You command. It obeys.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Beneath your feet, entropy is devouring what little remains of the xenos crypt. Before you lies an entire galaxy. A galaxy that is not yet ready for the power that you have obtained.{/n}
  - After: {n}Entropy devours the crypt. Before you lies a galaxy unready for your power.{/n}
- **Xavier Calcazar**
  - Before: "I believe we have accomplished enough this day. Commendably done, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}The Inquisitor solemnly bends his knee before you.{/n} "The Emperor's servants in the Koronus Expanse have gained a truly worthy protector."
  - After: "Well done, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}The Inquisitor kneels.{/n} "The Expanse has a worthy protector."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your form is rid of everything excessive, transitory, or trivial. Your mind, now a million times sharper, is hungrily processing the great deeds that lie ahead of you. The moment these thoughts crystallise, a shiver reverberates throughout the fabric of existence. The Deity has returned. The Deity comes — and Its Messenger walks at Its side.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your sharpened mind hungers for great deeds. The Deity returns, Its Messenger beside It.{/n}
- **Theodora**
  - Before: {n}Particles of reality around you begin to boil, trying to heal the wound upon existence and preventing her from entering your version of reality. You and she can exchange words, thoughts, glances — but a physical connection is an impossibility. You are merely fleeting phantoms that could scatter at any moment. She is silent, her gaze still trained on you, as if she is trying to commit your every feature to memory.{/n}
  - After: {n}Reality boils between you. You can speak, never touch. She silently memorises your face.{/n}
- **Theodora**
  - Before: {n}Theodora nods in approval.{/n} "Yes. You are the Rogue Trader. I can see that."
  - After: {n}Theodora nods.{/n} "Yes. You are the Rogue Trader."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As yet another layer of reality cracks, a figure appears before you... Her. After giving you a probing and appraising look, Theodora permits herself a slight smile.{/n}
  - After: {n}Reality cracks, and Theodora appears, smiling faintly.{/n}
- **Theodora**
  - Before: {n}Her smile widens.{/n} "It is always worth it. You will understand this yourself."
  - After: {n}Her smile widens.{/n} "Always. You'll understand."
- **Theodora**
  - Before: {n}She simply shrugs.{/n} "Our dynasty's Warrant is signed in the Emperor's blood — and written in ours. The blood of the von Valancius Rogue Traders. This has always been so."
  - After: {n}She shrugs.{/n} "Our Warrant is signed in the Emperor's blood, and ours. Always."
- **Theodora**
  - Before: {n}Her smile grows wider.{/n} "To walk bravely first into darkness,
To unite and reclaim what was lost,
To triumph over nightmares untold,
To hold boldly the reins of fate,
To walk steadily the road of thorns,
Through pain to greatness."
  - After: {n}Her smile grows.{/n} "To walk first into darkness,
To reclaim what was lost,
To hold the reins of fate,
Through pain to greatness."
- **Theodora**
  - Before: {n}The wound on reality is healed and the vision of Theodora quickly fades away. You catch her last words:{/n} "Whatever fate you choose, one can only hope it will be better than mine."
  - After: {n}Theodora fades.{/n} "May your fate be better than mine."
- **Xavier Calcazar**
  - Before: "If your pet takes so much as a step toward the Shard, you may consider our alliance broken, Rogue Trader. The Shard will be placed under the Yoke, and as for that creature... I will destroy it as soon as my work here is complete. Unless you destroy it first. I advise you to do just that." {n}Calcazar's tone leaves no room for ambiguity.{/n}
  - After: "If your pet nears the Shard, our alliance ends, and I destroy that creature. Unless you do first." {n}Calcazar is unambiguous.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Mental contact is effortless. This is not communication — such a powerful being cannot comprehend communicating with anyone but Its equals. It simply bears the gift of making the other hear and understand It — so grand is the potential of Its thoughts.{/n}
  - After: {n}It doesn't communicate with lesser beings; It simply makes them understand.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Do not listen. Reject the promises. Do not allow your mind to be clouded, elantach. No one is capable of receiving everything — or granting everything. Not even a star-devouring Yngir. And this shard of an Yngir... cannot even grant itself freedom."
  - After: "Don't listen, elantach. Not even a Yngir grants everything. This shard can't even free itself."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Oh, you're just afraid the Lord Captain will get {mf|his|her} hands on your toy." {n}Jae smirks contemptuously.{/n}
  - After: "You fear the Lord Captain will get {mf|his|her} hands on your toy." {n}Jae smirks.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Nothing can subdue a star devourer, or even just a shard of one! Relent, mon-keigh! Your unbridled ambition will be the undoing of us all!"
  - After: "Nothing subdues a star devourer! Relent, mon-keigh, or doom us all!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The C'tan's attention turns to you — you feel it as clearly as if the touch of this inhuman mind were a tangible thing. It lands like a monstrous weight upon your shoulders, but a few moments later, the heaviness disappears — and instead, the familiar speech of Trazyn the Infinite begins to flow into your now free mind.{/n}
  - After: {n}The C'tan's mind weighs on you, then Trazyn's voice flows in.{/n}
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "A remnant of the ancient god that we turned into slaves and weapons..." {n}It takes you a few moments to realise — the xenos is addressing the vanquished C'tan.{/n} "Shadow of the parasite, your place is in the gallery of my Museion, to serve as an eternal monument to our superiority and your insignificance."
  - After: "Remnant of the god we enslaved..." {n}He addresses the C'tan.{/n} "Your place is in my Museion."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "Our agreement ended when we fulfilled our obligations." {n}Trazyn turns to you, vicious satisfaction seeping into his voice.{/n} "Your trophy belongs to me now, and our paths part here."
  - After: "Our bargain is done." {n}Trazyn sounds satisfied.{/n} "The trophy is mine. We part."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "Coincidence, not 'fate,' you primitive creature. You should be more grateful to the laws of probability that we did not remain enemies — it would have ended in disaster for you."
  - After: "Coincidence, primitive, not fate. Be glad we didn't stay enemies."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The ancient monster struggles against the energy manacles of the Yoke. Its impossible powers that make reality itself burst at the seams are now being forced into a compact dungeon, quark by quark, returning It to a cruel and painful non-existence in the moment. It could struggle harder, but something is hindering It.{/n}
  - After: {n}The monster strains as the Yoke crushes It quark by quark. Something hinders It.{/n}
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "We have nothing to thank each other for — it was only a whim of fate that brought us together. But you are right about one thing — it is time for us to part ways."
  - After: "Fate's whim joined us. Now we part."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: {n}The metallic scraping that serves as Trazyn's laughter grates on your ears.{/n} "Then fade into oblivion when you have lived your brief span... and do not become someone who leaves their mark on history."
  - After: {n}Trazyn laughs metallically.{/n} "Then fade, unremembered."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "You never were quite civilised enough to be a truly capable ally. There are limits beyond which it is impossible for your kind to go."
  - After: "You were never civilised enough as an ally."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "I am taking the Shard — and leaving you alone with your choices and decisions. Let's see if they lead you to another meeting with me... and a place within my collection. Farewell."
  - After: "I take the Shard. Perhaps you'll join my collection someday. Farewell."
- **Xavier Calcazar**
  - Before: "What?" {n}You hear a note of amazement in Calcazar's voice.{/n} "No. No, the monster imprisoned in Yoke is the key to Humanity's future. Its place is in the hands of humans, not a xenos!"
  - After: "What?" {n}Calcazar is stunned.{/n} "No! The monster is Humanity's future!"
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: {n}The moment your words leave your throat, your body freezes like a block of ice — a wave of Trazyn the Infinite's hand is enough to rob you of your ability to move.{/n} "Do not forget yourself, primitive creature — or I may become utterly disillusioned with this little 'pact' we have. The deal was made and remains in force." {n}Another brief movement — and you regain control of your body.{/n}
  - After: {n}Trazyn's wave freezes you.{/n} "Don't forget yourself, primitive. The deal stands." {n}You can move again.{/n}
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: {n}Before Calcazar can do anything, Trazyn clicks his fingers — and the Lord Inquisitor disappears in a blinding flash.{/n} "I will assess the value of this human in a less disruptive setting. Perhaps he will reside in the same display where I will place the day's main acquisition."
  - After: {n}Trazyn clicks his fingers; Calcazar vanishes.{/n} "I'll appraise him later, beside today's acquisition."
- **Xavier Calcazar**
  - Before: {n}Calcazar slowly raises his weapon — you can see it is a struggle for him.{/n} "Enough. I did not risk so much for an enemy of Humanity to confound my plans by finding a hidden heretic traitor among my allies..."
  - After: {n}Calcazar raises his weapon with effort.{/n} "Enough. A hidden heretic won't ruin my plans..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A new suspicion creeps into your mind, alien and terrifying: the beast is too strong. The Yoke cannot withstand such a powerful energy source. Humanity's creation is not enough to keep the galactic predator leashed... and, in that same moment, you notice a faint green glow out of the corner of your eye. These thoughts — they are Trazyn's. A message. A final warning while {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_TrazynDealNomos}there is still a chance{/d}...{/n}
  - After: {n}An alien thought: the Yoke can't hold the beast. A green glow: Trazyn's warning, while {d|Encyclopedia:Ch4_TrazynDealNomos}there is still a chance{/d}...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}More and more tears appear all over the Shard's form. As the Yoke absorbs Its power, it becomes increasingly harder for the Shard to maintain Its physical structure. Each imperfection you inflict brings the star predator closer to imprisonment.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Shard tears as the Yoke drains It, nearing imprisonment.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}To the C'tan, space is an illusory variable. To the C'tan, time is a young and trivial phenomenon, for It existed for an eternity in the gaseous energy fount of the universe before time was eventually born. To the C'tan, fact and probability are mere abstractions, between which It can soar on Its electromagnetic wings.{/n}
  - After: {n}To the C'tan, space, time and probability are mere abstractions.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Currently, the C'tan is... not whole. It was shattered into lesser pieces, and so were Its thoughts and powers. The feeling of emptiness is oppressive, and It yearns to become one again.{/n}
  - After: {n}But it is shattered, Its powers too. It yearns to be whole.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The C'tan can grant... Your thoughts falter, for it is difficult for your mind to fathom the full scope of this word... The C'tan can grant Everything.{/n}
  - After: {n}The C'tan can grant... Everything.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As you stand before the Yoke's control altar, you gaze upon it, possibly the greatest instrument of destruction in the history of your race. The key that unlocks the gates to the nigh-unfettered heights of power. A weapon... The cogitator block that was designed to transmit orders to the imprisoned C'tan shatters into pieces. It is a weapon no longer — merely a prison.{/n}
  - After: {n}At the altar, you shatter the cogitator commanding the C'tan. The weapon is now merely a prison.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch5/Epitaphia/NecronLord/NecronLord_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Instead of fighting each other, we should unite to halt the impending nightmare."
  - After: "Let's unite against the coming nightmare."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Grant the ancient warrior an honourable death] "Your watch is over."
  - After: [Grant the warrior an honourable death] "Your watch is over."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is it that is making you grieve? Is it your imminent death?"
  - After: "Why grieve? Your death?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is this cataclysm unfolding here?"
  - After: "What cataclysm is this?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The colossal warrior's formidable underframe can no longer bear his weight. With armour plates clanging, his great bulk slumps. A low sound is born in his chest, which your Elucidator {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NecronKnowlege}turns into the words{/d},{/n} "Let woe befall the unworthy Yekhmet dynasty. Sleep is nearing its end and thraldom returns. In my vestment of shame, I peer into the stormy horizons of the future."
  - After: {n}The warrior slumps. Your Elucidator {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NecronKnowlege}translates{/d}:{/n} "Woe to the Yekhmet dynasty. Sleep ends, thraldom returns."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The fallen warrior scrapes the floor with his claws and screeches furiously,{/n} "Unacceptable! The rot of transient life must be eradicated!"
  - After: {n}He screeches,{/n} "Unacceptable! Transient life must be eradicated!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A terrible rumble comes from somewhere deep inside the crypt as soon as the green fire goes out in the fallen warrior's eyes. The glow of the glyphs upon the walls becomes chaotic and disarrayed. Something just broke irreparably in this crypt.{/n}
  - After: {n}His eyes go dark. The crypt rumbles, glyphs flickering. Something broke for good.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You notice the convulsions in the xenos's limbs. The light is flickering in his eyes. Perhaps something went wrong during this monster's awakening from stasis, damaging his engrams and plunging him into madness.{/n}
  - After: {n}His limbs convulse. A botched awakening may have damaged his engrams, driving him mad.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "May tachyonic wind carry my words, may the oceans of subatomic resonance reflect it, and may it resound until the world grows old." {n}Convulsions begin to affect the metallic body and the entire crypt is quivering along. The walls seem more fragile with each passing second. Impossible anomalies are now rampant in them.{/n} "Let the Yekhmet dynasty be cursed!"
  - After: "May tachyonic wind carry my words forever." {n}The crypt quakes with him.{/n} "Cursed be the Yekhmet dynasty!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The xenos dies with a piercing howl of wrath. There is no fear in these sounds, only the stubbornness of a true warrior with a touch of regret at his defeat.{/n}
  - After: {n}The xenos dies howling, unafraid, regretting defeat.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The xenos's limbs shiver at the sound of your voice. The Elucidator takes on a tone of revulsion:{/n} "Despicable. An overlord's moment of grief is befouled by the influence of transient life. Rage has clouded the purity of the mourning." {n}The warrior makes a futile attempt to get up, only to convulse again. Something bursts inside him, making a ringing noise. The entire crypt echoes that sound with a resonant rumbling tremor.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Elucidator sounds revolted:{/n} "Transient life befouls an overlord's grief." {n}Something bursts inside him; the crypt rumbles.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You appear to be looking at the overlord of a minor dynasty of the xenos. He is clearly a member of a destructive cult that loathes living flesh with a visceral passion. However, as much as he resembles an animated metallic statue, he was once a living being, and the ideals of duty and valour that used to guide him still exist in his mind.{/n}
  - After: {n}A minor overlord from a flesh-loathing cult. Once alive, he still holds to duty and valour.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The star devourer is asleep yet awake. His breath is a poisonous pestilence. His dreams are engrammatic acid. Quantum uncertainty is his shroud, and that which came to pass is entangled in it and interwoven with that which came not to pass. Possibility becomes actuality. Actuality unbecomes itself."
  - After: "The star devourer sleeps yet wakes. Possibility becomes actuality. Actuality unbecomes itself."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Shame upon the Cryptogeometric Sentinel who was entrusted with guarding the paths of actualisation and failed to be vigilant. Unworthy feet have trodden those paths." {n}The voice-like hum from behind his lowered visor fades.{/n}
  - After: "Shame upon the Cryptogeometric Sentinel who failed his watch." {n}His hum fades.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is reasonable to conclude that the monster is talking about probabilistic alternate universes.{/n}
  - After: {n}He means probabilistic alternate universes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The monster's madness is clearly overtaking him as his speech turns into a tangle of incoherent exclamations.{/n}
  - After: {n}His speech dissolves into mad babble.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You are evidently looking at a deranged machine built for destruction. It is unsurprising that his apocalyptic outpourings are not directed at anyone in particular. He simply has a burning hatred for all of existence.{/n}
  - After: {n}A deranged machine hating all existence.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "A warrior of iron. A sentinel of the tomb of the Ancient Ones. A child of the Yngir, the star devourers, and an eternal enemy of the Asuryani." {n}Yrliet grips the weapon in her hands tightly, as if expecting the terrifying warrior to spring to life and attack at any second.{/n}
  - After: "A Yngir sentinel, star devourer, eternal enemy of the Asuryani." {n}Yrliet grips her weapon.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "It's alive... it moves, it thinks, it tries to talk to us, but — it exudes no colours! This is the first time I have seen another's pain and fury with my eyes alone, without the aid of my gift. So, this is what it's like..."
  - After: "It's alive, but exudes no colours! I see its pain with my eyes alone."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "Let its death be clean. No xenos could ever hope to receive His grace, but... The way it gazes into the face of its doom is worthy of respect."
  - After: "Let its death be clean. It faces doom with honour."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "The specimen is permanently damaged, Rogue Trader. Convulsive limb activity and complete desynchronisation of movement prevent us from adopting the hypothesis that the Necron is fully functional. Nonetheless, it is still infinitely dangerous, like all of them."
  - After: "The specimen is damaged, Rogue Trader. Still infinitely dangerous."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "If we accept this statement as truth, we face a dilemma: is this a manifestation of the divine, or... its opposite? I cannot solve it, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "Is this divine, or its opposite? I cannot say."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The colossal warrior's formidable underframe can no longer bear his weight. With armour plates clanging, his great bulk slumps. A {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NoNecronKnowlege}deep sound full of rage and tragic despair is born in his chest{/d}.{/n}
  - After: {n}The warrior slumps. A {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NoNecronKnowlege}deep, raging, despairing sound{/d} rises.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The xenos's limbs shiver at the sound of your voice. He emits a deep hum full of dour pride. You are unable to decipher it but you can sense his disdainful rage and stern resolve to kill you. This is neither the dispassion of a prowling beast nor the blinding rage of insanity, but the instinct of a warrior.{/n}
  - After: {n}He hums with dour pride. You sense a warrior's resolve to kill you.{/n}
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Clearing his throat, Ulfar grudgingly admits,{/n} "He speaks of honour before death. These ancient xenos certainly have an understanding of battle courage and honour. Perhaps the old ones are right, and everything has become degraded over the centuries. Even inhumans."
  - After: {n}Ulfar grudgingly admits,{/n} "He knows honour before death. Even inhumans have degraded."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "You dislike me, but this lump of metal commands your respect? You truly are a deranged breed."
  - After: "You dislike me but respect this metal lump? Deranged breed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The warrior turns his gaze directly on you. The green light in his eyes flares up like a bonfire.{/n} "Inexistence is entropically preordained! It is no cause for grief! The egregious mistakes are! The violated imperatives are! The Yekhmet dynasty took watch of the seed of the cataclysm. The seed was neglected. A cataclysm has sprouted from it. Honour has been trampled underfoot."
  - After: {n}His eyes flare.{/n} "Death is no cause for grief! Mistakes are! The Yekhmet dynasty neglected the seed of the cataclysm."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The frenzied monster shivers with rage and a burning thirst for destruction.{/n}
  - After: {n}The monster shivers with rage.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "So brazen a violation of the laws of existence set by the Omnissiah — the very idea is infinitely blasphemous. So blasphemous as to... almost be sacred."
  - After: "Defying the Omnissiah's laws so brazenly is blasphemous. Almost sacred."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai jerks his head.{/n} "A crippled Oghyr. Look at it twitch its limbs... I have never seen anything like it. Whatever caused this defect had great force behind it."
  - After: {n}Marazhai jerks his head.{/n} "A crippled Oghyr. Something mighty broke it."

## World/Dialogs/Ch5/Epitaphia/NomosArrival/NomosArrival_c5_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "What are you talking about? Can you not talk in riddles?"
  - After: "Meaning what? No riddles."
- **Nomos**
  - Before: {n}An invisible yet clearly tangible aura of power envelops the figure clad in the robes of a Tech-Priest. It is all the more baffling to hear a youthfully excited voice from under the hood.{/n} "This is it. The place of our origin."
  - After: {n}A youthful voice from the hood:{/n} "Our origin."
- **Xavier Calcazar**
  - Before: "I need explanations, Rogue Trader. What is that? And what is it doing here?"
  - After: "Explain, Rogue Trader. What is that?"
- **Nomos**
  - Before: {n}The voice coming from the maw of the monstrous machine sounds strangely excited — enchanted, even:{/n} "This is it... The place of our origin. Nomos were born here."
  - After: {n}The machine sounds enchanted:{/n} "Nomos were born here."
- **Trazyn the Infinite**
  - Before: "This is my first opportunity to view this entity separate from your ship's systems. What a remarkable... no, unique creature you have managed to bridle, human. It would certainly have a place in my collection..."
  - After: "A unique creature you've bridled, human. It belongs in my collection..."

## World/Dialogs/Ch5/Epitaphia/Tanakia

- **Abelard**
  - Before: "My boots these days are rather more expensive. I am loath to sully them."
  - After: "My boots cost more now."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "It is highly likely that this woman deserves to rot here and choke on her own blood or be skinned alive by the xenos. Quite likely indeed... But I am a merciful man, and therefore I suggest shooting her in the head and pressing on."
  - After: "She deserves to rot. But I'm merciful: shoot her and move on."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You've become more generous over the years, Abelard. In the old days, you wouldn't have wasted a bullet — you would have kicked me to death with your boot out of sheer frugality."
  - After: "Generous now, Abelard. Once you'd have just kicked me dead."

## World/Dialogs/Ch5/Epitaphia/Tanakia/Tanakia_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Why does no one from Theodora's retinue remember her visiting this system?"
  - After: "Why does Theodora's retinue not remember this system?"

  - Before: "Let's be straight with each other. You have nothing to hide now that you are dying. What is going on in this place?"
  - After: "You're dying. What's going on here?"

  - Before: "Do you not fear death?"
  - After: "Don't you fear death?"

  - Before: [Drop the lho-stick on the ground] "Oh, how clumsy of me."

  - Before: "I am looking for Calcazar. Where is he?"
  - After: "Where is Calcazar?"

  - Before: "Tell me, why does my coat of arms look familiar to you?"
  - After: "Why do you know my coat of arms?"

  - Before: "What was the ultimatum you gave Theodora?"
  - After: "What was your ultimatum to Theodora?"

  - Before: "How did your people infiltrate Theodora's retinue?"
  - After: "How did you infiltrate Theodora's retinue?"

  - Before: [Raise your weapon] "This is where it all ends for you."

  - Before: "Let's leave her to die."
  - After: "Leave her to die."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The execution that the traitor deserves."
  - After: "A traitor's execution."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It is what you Inquisitorial rats deserve."
  - After: "What Inquisitorial rats deserve."
- **Player**
  - Before: [End her suffering without replying]
  - After: [End her suffering silently]
- **Player**
  - Before: "Hey, can you hear me?"
  - After: "Can you hear me?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Give the dying woman her lho] "Enjoy."
  - After: [Give her the lho] "Enjoy."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Bring the lho to the woman's lips] "You were saying something about an operation?'
  - After: [Bring the lho to her lips] "The operation?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Take out a pack of lho out of the woman's jacket]
  - After: [Take the lho from her jacket]
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Her body does not appear to have any external injuries — it has been maimed from the inside out. It is as if her flesh was transmuted into metallic shapes that then burst out of her skin and turned her internal organs into a bloody sieve. Some of her exposed bones have a metallic gleam to them, while others still look natural.{/n}
  - After: {n}Metal burst from inside her, shredding her organs. Some bones gleam metallic.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "This is... hmph... unexpected. Did Her Ladyship not trust even me? Disheartening news, to be sure."
  - After: "Hmph. Her Ladyship didn't trust even me?"
- **Idira**
  - Before: "But a mindlock is incredibly dangerous. It's a bloody miracle it didn't fry our brains!"
  - After: "A mindlock could've fried our brains!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Does it look like I have anything to lose? The way I see it, you are doing me a favour here. So which one is it: mercy or revenge?"
  - After: "I've nothing to lose. Mercy or revenge?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Are you trying to pry information out of an Inquisitorial agent in the hope that she shows sentimental candour at death's door? Shame on you." {n}The woman manages a weak smile.{/n}
  - After: "Hoping a dying Inquisitorial agent gets sentimental? Shame." {n}A weak smile.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You have heard about mindlock technology. The subject's memories of times or events would be placed under a special lock that could only be opened by a key phrase, one that most likely only Theodora would know.{/n}
  - After: {n}Mindlock: memories sealed by a key phrase, likely Theodora's.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It takes you more than a few strikes to end the life of the already half-dead woman. The metal skull screeches under the pressure but does not break, and her heart keeps pumping blood through her shredded veins. Finally, her agony comes to an end.{/n}
  - After: {n}Her metal skull takes several strikes. Finally, she dies.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}With a heavy jerk, the woman raises her head, emerging from oblivion, and focuses her gaze on you. Even in such a wretched state, her eyes still gleam with self-confidence, zest, and subtle shrewdness.{/n} "You... Who are... Ah. That coat of arms rings a bell. Von Valancius. I'm not as surprised to see you as you may think."
  - After: {n}She looks up, still shrewd.{/n} "That coat of arms... Von Valancius. Not surprising."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You little shit." {n}The woman cackles hoarsely and without any malice, lapsing into fits of bloody coughing.{/n}
  - After: "You little shit." {n}She cackles, coughing blood.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Do you know Kunrad Voigtvir? Not sure if he's still alive, but back then, he was Theodora's Master of Whispers. In theory, he should have been the one to out my operatives as spies. But instead, he thought that they were his chance to pull off a brilliant plot and prove to his mummy how great an heir he would become. It's true what they say about blonds — every other one is as thick as mince."
  - After: "Kunrad Voigtvir, Theodora's Master of Whispers, should have outed my spies. He used them to impress mummy instead. Thick blond."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman tries to salute you, but the metal cutting through her tendons has cost her the control of her fingers.{/n} "Tanakia Calbergaria, Inquisition acolyte. And, by the grace of Lord Inquisitor Calcazar, the warden of the Epitaph 1 covert facility. Or whatever's left of it."
  - After: {n}Her salute fails.{/n} "Tanakia Calbergaria, Inquisition acolyte. Warden of Calcazar's covert facility, Epitaph 1. What's left of it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "At the facility, in the crypt. Making preparations for the emergency launch of the operation's final stage... At least I hope so. Or else he's already dead. Now that I think about it, there are enough reasons to assume the latter."
  - After: "In the crypt, launching the operation's final stage. Or dead. Probably dead."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh, I should know. It was on the uniform my agents wore. The ones I sent when Calcazar took an interest in Her Ladyship Theodora's retinue. They didn't wear them for long, though: when I presented Theodora with Calcazar's ultimatum, she purged her retinue of our operatives. I'm fairly certain Theodora would have preferred to have my head as well, but the Lord Inquisitor recalled me here to guard his treasure cave. Just in case Theodora decided to return for what she thought was hers, or the Drukhari started causing trouble."
  - After: "My agents wore it in Theodora's retinue. After Calcazar's ultimatum, she purged them. Calcazar sent me here to guard his treasure from her and the Drukhari."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I guess you're still young if you don't know that in this world, whenever the big boys and girls say the word 'facility,' that almost always means a 'colossal secret weapon capable of destroying worlds.' And that's all you're going to get. It would be very disrespectful of me to spill a secret that so many have given their lives to protect."
  - After: "'Facility' means 'world-killing secret weapon.' That's all you get."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Merely a message saying that her dirty secret was now our dirty secret. She was the first to visit Epitaph, and she found something here... something too good even for someone of her exalted status. Rogue Traders are not allowed to have such toys, and I relayed the most exact coordinates, down to the last digit after the decimal point, to the Lord Inquisitor."
  - After: "That her secret was now ours. She found something on Epitaph too good for a Rogue Trader. I gave Calcazar the coordinates."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A feint. A deception. A game of double- and triple-crosses. When they told her they intended to take revenge on Calcazar, she believed them — she was just too eager to get back at the Lord Inquisitor for taking her clever Archmagos advisor, Amarnat."
  - After: "Triple-crosses. They claimed they'd avenge her on Calcazar for taking her Archmagos, Amarnat. She believed them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I've been having trouble sleeping lately... Oh, you mean the metal things in my body? I have no idea. Looks like something has gone terribly wrong in the crypt." {n}Her voice becomes more serious and dry.{/n} "The auspexes detected some unknown radiation, and then everything went crazy. The xenos didn't feel like sleeping in their coffins anymore, so they started trashing the place. And the pylon I was standing next to suddenly grew a dozen tentacles, and one of them grazed me. I blacked out, and when I came to, I looked like I'd tried to give birth to a shuttle."
  - After: "The metal? Something went wrong in the crypt." {n}Her voice dries.{/n} "Strange radiation, the xenos woke, a pylon sprouted tentacles. One grazed me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Ah, the xenofreaks, my favourite partners. They had a crucial role to play in the operation that you mustn't know anything about. Their visits to Epitaph have left me with so many unforgettable moments. We were ordered not to fire on them first, but to split them into atoms if their skinny arses deviated so much as a single degree from their approved flight paths. I swear, it was as if those fools were trying to get shot at with their half-witted provocations. They even had a nickname for me — the Almost Wych. A compliment... I guess."
  - After: "My favourite partners, vital to the operation. Orders: don't fire first, but atomise them if they strayed. They called me 'the Almost Wych.'"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Said the one who chats with the whispers in her head. You know, I'm not sure that you had that habit before coming to Epitaph."
  - After: "Says the one chatting with voices. New since Epitaph?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Have I sated your curiosity? Then I'd like my favour returned. There's a pack of lho in my breast pocket. Give me one, and you can keep the rest. I'm feeling very generous today."
  - After: "Satisfied? Then hand me a lho from my breast pocket. Keep the rest."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "I say we leave her here to die. In pain and torment. We should drive a nail into her ear too, so she has something to remember us by."
  - After: "Leave her to suffer. Nail through the ear too."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I suggest granting the acolyte the Emperor's Peace. In honour of our years of working together."
  - After: "Grant her the Emperor's Peace. For old times."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Her blood-smeared lips twist into a smile.{/n} "Is this an act of mercy or revenge?"
  - After: {n}She smiles bloodily.{/n} "Mercy or revenge?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Or... you can go down there, if you have the guts. Maybe you'll immortalise yourself too. That's what I would do, but I'm insane, so I'm not the best example to follow." {n}A weak smile dances on the woman's lips.{/n} "So. About that lho-stick?"
  - After: "Or go down there and immortalise yourself. I'm insane, though." {n}She smiles.{/n} "That lho-stick?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You have never heard of such a technology, but it would not be a stretch to assume that the Inquisition does have something of the sort at their disposal.{/n}
  - After: {n}Unknown to you, but likely Inquisition tech.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Tanakia gives you a long, piercing look, then speaks, sadness audible in her voice:{/n} "Straight, huh? Let's give it a try. I've taken a shine to you for some reason... One day, Xavier decided to immortalise himself in history in a rather extravagant way. All for the Imperium's sake, of course. But then things didn't go as expected, even though we expected that they wouldn't. And now you'd better get far away from here, because whatever happens next, I doubt you're going to like it."
  - After: {n}Tanakia looks sad.{/n} "Fine, I like you. Xavier wanted to immortalise himself, for the Imperium. It went wrong, as expected. Get far away from here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Her lips move slightly, as if trying to whisper something, but the shock mutes them, turning her voice into a gurgle. Her body, mindless and desperate, is only prolonging the pointless agony by clinging to its last bleeding shreds of life.{/n}
  - After: {n}She gurgles, clinging to life.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "People say it's bad for your health. I'd better be careful."
  - After: "Bad for my health, they say."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You're a funny one. The Inquisition's secrets for a tube of lho — that would be something, wouldn't it? No deal."
  - After: "Inquisition secrets for a lho? No deal."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "It is time she was sent to the Undying One. Spare her throat, but strike her heart instead, for that is where she carries a heavy burden. Let her shed this burden, and let her lips pray their last."
  - After: "Send her to the Undying One. Strike her burdened heart."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "It is something more. It is His blessing." {n}Kibellah smiles, softly and soothingly.{/n}
  - After: "It is His blessing." {n}Kibellah smiles.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I've received better gifts from Him. But... who the void cares. Go ahead, bless me already."
  - After: "I've had better gifts. Bless me already."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn scans her in shock.{/n} "These deformations... They are akin to that which consumed Nuncius! But how?"
  - After: {n}Eogunn is shocked.{/n} "Like what consumed Nuncius! How?"
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}A look of profound sorrow and sympathy fills Eogunn's eyes.{/n} "These transmutations are irreversible... and agonising. Do not make the same mistakes I did — grant an end to her suffering."
  - After: {n}Eogunn looks sorrowful.{/n} "This is irreversible agony. Don't repeat my mistake. End it."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "If the crypt itself, or whatever took control of it, can manifest such things at will... we cannot contain it. The refractive transmuter is as nothing against this power!"
  - After: "If the crypt does this at will, our refractive transmuter can't contain it!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A timely observation, Genetor Februs, but where was this wisdom earlier? Although, come to think of it, promptness never was your virtue. By the way, how is Nuncius? Did he get to see you in the end?"
  - After: "Late as ever, Genetor Februs. How's Nuncius? Did he find you?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I can give you two versions of the truth: the sugar-coated one and the honest one. The sugar-coated version is that once Theodora realised just what she had in her hands, she deemed it a matter of the utmost secrecy and mindlocked the memories of all members of her crew. The honest version is that she mindlocked the important people and disposed of the rest. Theodora depressurised compartments by entire blocks, casting any unwanted witnesses out into the void. She needed to free up space in her holds for the spoils, anyway."
  - After: "Sweet version: Theodora mindlocked her crew to keep her find secret. Honest version: she mindlocked the important ones and vented the rest into the void. Made room for spoils."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You've always been so sentimental. So attached to your colleagues, your hair, your eyes... Oh, I'm sorry, is that still a sore point?"
  - After: "So sentimental. About colleagues, your hair, your eyes... Still sore?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You have it all backward. You could have been dumped out the airlock like so many others. You were already a decrepit old curmudgeon back then, after all."
  - After: "Backward. You were lucky not to be spaced, old curmudgeon."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You'll have to excuse me for not looking surprised — my facial nerves seem to be partially paralysed. But I gathered as much — I'd hardly mistake you for our spectacular void she-wolf, after all. And if she were alive, she definitely would have come here in person. So you're the heir? Well, at least it's not Kunrad."
  - After: "My face is half paralysed, so no surprise. Alive, the void she-wolf would've come herself. The heir? Better than Kunrad."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Good. You're old enough to know what these are for, aren't you? Stick one end of the tube between my teeth and light up the other. Just make sure you do it the right way around."
  - After: "Teeth on one end, light the other. Right way around."

## World/Dialogs/Ch5/Epitaphia/XavierFinal

- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: "How dare you! How DARE you!" {n}Incendia's voice roars like the fire of the executioner's furnace, but then her rage burns down to coals, her tone becoming more akin to the rustling of ashes being scattered by the wind.{/n} "You have fallen to heresy, Xavier. And I condemn you."
  - After: "How DARE you!" {n}Her rage cools.{/n} "You've fallen to heresy, Xavier. I condemn you."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar stares coldly at him, the deadly frost of Fenris crackling in his voice as he speaks:{/n} "You will pay for this after we are finished here, Xavier Calcazar. Know that I will have my blood vengeance. I will have your death."
  - After: {n}Ulfar, ice-cold:{/n} "Later, Calcazar, I will have your death."
- **Incendia Chorda**
  - Before: {n}Incendia closes her eyes wearily and says with sadness in her voice,{/n} "No, Xavier. Heresy is always heresy. And judgement always comes in its wake."
  - After: {n}Incendia, sadly:{/n} "Heresy is heresy. Judgement follows."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Inquisitor's face hardens. His eyebrows furrowed, he replies grimly,{/n} "I reject your accusations, Incendia. And I will forget your words... this once."
  - After: {n}He frowns.{/n} "I reject that, Incendia. I'll forget it, once."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After a moment's pause, Calcazar says quietly,{/n} "Your verdict is clear, Incendia."
  - After: {n}Quietly:{/n} "Your verdict is clear."

## World/Dialogs/Ch5/Epitaphia/XavierFinal/XavierFinal_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Point at the xenoconstruct] "Is that what you are here for? What is it?"
  - After: [Point at the xenoconstruct] "Is that why you're here?"

  - Before: "I will not let you bring this insane plan to fruition."
  - After: "I won't allow this insane plan."

  - Before: "I have come for your head, Calcazar."
  - After: "I've come for your head, Calcazar."

  - Before: "The line you are treading is a dangerous one, Calcazar. Stop this madness!"
  - After: "Stop this dangerous madness, Calcazar!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "And you think you stand a chance against such power?"
  - After: "You think you can match such power?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You have gone too far, and your actions will lead to disaster!"

  - Before: "How did this thing end up in your possession?"

  - Before: "How was Theodora involved in all this?"
  - After: "How was Theodora involved?"

  - Before: "A fine plan, apart from it being an insanely audacious one that will almost certainly get everyone killed."
  - After: "Fine plan, if insanely audacious. It'll kill everyone."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Nothing can excuse consorting with inhumans."
  - After: "Nothing excuses consorting with inhumans."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why did you call for the Astartes to come to your aid?"
  - After: "Why call in the Astartes?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "And then, I take it, you decided to get rid of your xenos allies?"

  - Before: "Heinrix, he has gone mad. You don't have to listen to him."

  - Before: "I see your ambitions are on a truly cosmic scale."
  - After: "Your ambitions are truly cosmic."
- **Player**

  - Before: "I still have many questions for you."
  - After: "I still have many questions."

  - Before: "Listen to yourself! What you are planning is heresy!"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "They were an asset at first. The Wolves helped me close the dimensional gate by overwhelming its security systems. I tasked them with hunting the xenos condemned by Yremeryss.
