- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The obsidian smoothness of the enormous slab begins to ripple and roil. A set of mysterious symbols appears on it, as if impressed on its black surface by an invisible finger. The three brightest ones are {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NecronKnowlege}symbols for "Malefice," "Pestilence," and "Unravelling."{/d} They shimmer forebodingly, like a martyr gasping for air as life drains from them.{/n}
  - After: {n}The black slab ripples. Symbols appear; the brightest are {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NecronKnowlege}symbols for "Malefice," "Pestilence," and "Unravelling."{/d}{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}An inscription above them reads:{/n} "My Lord who hast known eternity, I heed mine guarding words that I spoke at the dawn of the wrathful stars! He who is condemned to torture by imprisonment must languish forever in the labyrinth of many dimensions, lest Their plagues befall us. A minute breach in the impossible prison would suffice for the spiteful will, the destructive thought incarnate in unperishing flesh, to obliterate existence. I lay my hand upon the vessel of the past, and I am revealed the doom that awaits one who breaks the commandments."
  - After: {n}Above them:{/n} "My Lord! The condemned must stay imprisoned in the labyrinth of dimensions, lest Their plagues befall us. One breach would obliterate existence."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Wrinkling his nose in disgust, Ulfar asks,{/n} "Do you go poking your fingers in every kind of xenos filth you encounter, Aett-Vater, or have you just taken a liking to this? Would you like me to chop off that hand before something happens? It will be quick and almost painless. We'll choose a nice augment for it... No?"
  - After: {n}Ulfar wrinkles his nose.{/n} "Must you poke every xenos filth, Aett-Vater? Shall I chop that hand off? No?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You clench your teeth and press your palm harder into the slab. The pain is but an illusion. You overcome it and let the second vision into your mind.{/n}
  - After: {n}You press harder. The pain is illusion. The second vision comes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You cannot stand the pain anymore and jerk your hand out of the slab — unscathed. The flickering symbols freeze at once and begin to fade. The symbol for Pestilence is the last to disappear from the slab's surface.{/n}
  - After: {n}You jerk your hand free, unscathed. The symbols fade; Pestilence vanishes last.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My Lord, I am revealed the nature of the Unravelling: an interminable flow of unmanifested defects of my eternity incarnate. The world known to me is unidentical to the other worlds, nor is it one with them. The other manifestations, the unlikenesses, will wage wars upon me, seeking to absorb and thus obliterate me. I dare not lose my way and doom my eternity to perdition. I am firm in my memory that mine alone is the true eternity whose existence is rightful. I will shatter the mirrored unlikenesses."
  - After: "My Lord, the Unravelling: flawed copies of my eternity will war to absorb me. Mine alone is true. I will shatter them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As soon as your palm touches the symbol, the slab's metal pulls it in, enveloping it like water. The text is transformed:{/n} "My Lord, I dare not divert my gaze from the guarding words! I am revealed the second plague, the Pestilence. It is not enough merely to behold it; I comprehend it, as my own lifeless shell learns the truth of its doom."
  - After: {n}The metal swallows your palm. The text changes:{/n} "My Lord, I am revealed the second plague, the Pestilence. My lifeless shell learns its doom."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The symbol you touched splits into three that are akin to it, similar and yet different from one another. A message materialises in front of you:{/n} "My Lord, Their third plague, the Unravelling, is beyond comprehension; therefore I put before myself a question bearing clarity."
  - After: {n}The symbol splits into three similar ones.{/n} "My Lord, Their third plague, the Unravelling, is beyond comprehension; so I ask myself a question."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}One after another, new inscriptions appear on the slab's surface. They dash around maddeningly fast, overlapping each other. Amid this chaos, only one inscription latches onto your mind, causing it acute pain:{/n} "My Lord, in my measureless eternity, I remember Their doom. I am revealed the first plague, the Malefice: a wormhole that invades the very essence of thought." {n}Your vision goes dark.{/n}
  - After: {n}One inscription burns into your mind:{/n} "My Lord, the first plague, the Malefice: a wormhole invading thought itself." {n}You black out.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Reality cuts through the darkness of eternal sleep like a cold blade. You sense wrongness, and gain a clear understanding of the nature of that wrongness. Your engrams have been tampered with and damaged. You try to move, but in vain — you are buried alive in the metal crypt of your own body. Some of your fellows are faced with the same fate. Almost as soon as they emerge from their stasis sarcophagi, they freeze like mangled statues, tilt sideways, and collapse, crashing to the floor. Maddened legions march mindlessly past them toward a gaping chasm, and tumble obediently into its merciless maw.{/n}
  - After: {n}You wake with damaged engrams, trapped in your metal body. Others collapse leaving stasis. Maddened legions march into a chasm.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My thoughts are sparse, and they are erroneous. I know that the cascade of defects that is my Unravelling has already done its work of destruction. Woe is me."
  - After: "My thoughts are few and wrong. My Unravelling has done its work. Woe is me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The slab withstands your anger stoically and continues its silent display of the same incomprehensible symbols. This calls for less barbaric methods of interaction.{/n}
  - After: {n}The slab doesn't care. Try something less barbaric.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As soon as your hand touches the symbol, new sentences start appearing on the slab's surface. They dash around maddeningly fast, overlapping each other. They seem to be trying to burn alien and unsettling messages into your mind. Discerning these messages, let alone comprehending them, is beyond you. Your nostrils are bleeding. The searing pain inside your head is like dead fingers digging their nails into your brain and trying to squeeze it out.{/n}
  - After: {n}Alien messages swarm the slab, burning into your mind. Your nose bleeds; your head is in agony.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You snatch your hand back in a hurry and look away. You feel nauseous. The sense of being invaded is gone, leaving only its horror behind: a horror you are not sure is your own and not forced upon you by the will of a different mind. The inscriptions freeze and fade away. The symbol you touched is erased from the slab's surface.{/n}
  - After: {n}You pull away, nauseous, left with a horror that may not be yours. The touched symbol vanishes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It seems that the enigmatic text speaks of some distortions of causality, resulting in multiple alternate versions of existence. It also suggests that these versions are hostile to one another.{/n}
  - After: {n}It speaks of broken causality: many hostile alternate versions of existence.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Even while being flooded with xenos visions, your mind remains sound enough to analyse the incoming information. Now you grasp the nature of the pernicious "Malefice." Someone powerful on the outside is broadcasting insidious interferences that disrupt the xenos' awakening from their stasis sleep. Madness is the nearest human equivalent of the effect this has on them.{/n}
  - After: {n}The "Malefice": someone outside broadcasts interference that drives the xenos mad as they wake from stasis.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "Lord Captain! Are you uninjured? Sound of mind? Why am I even asking... the answer has been obvious for a while now." {n}The Seneschal mutters the last sentence under his breath.{/n}
  - After: "Lord Captain! Unhurt? Sound of mind? Why do I even ask..." {n}He mutters.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn's auspex briskly scans you.{/n} "The Rogue Trader is not compromised. Brain cell damage is within the acceptable range." {n}With a greedy look at the slab, the Manipulus adds,{/n} "Repeated interaction is permissible."
  - After: {n}Eogunn scans you.{/n} "Brain damage within acceptable range." {n}He eyes the slab.{/n} "Repeated interaction is permissible."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The symbols begin to change at a frenzied pace. Their light burns your eyes, and their rapid flickering makes you nauseous. You are struck by a splitting headache, like an alien entity squeezing your mind out of shape as if it were soft clay, refashioning it after its own image.{/n}
  - After: {n}The symbols flicker madly. A splitting headache, as if something reshapes your mind like clay.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You see an image of a voidship: a black crescent shape, its plating veined with green lights. Right before your eyes, its various parts start crumbling and flaking away as though gnawed at by invisible termites. It is being consumed by tech-blight. When only a lifeless carcass is left, you feel a searing pain in your hand, as if the Pestilence has spread to your flesh and is now consuming it.{/n}
  - After: {n}A black crescent voidship crumbles to tech-blight. Your hand burns as the Pestilence spreads.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A cyclopean pyramid comes crashing down on the rocky ground. It seems intent on preserving its shape, but tech-blight twists it and eats away at it. An enormous hand cuts short the fortress's death throes as it crumples the pyramid into a shapeless lump and tosses it away. The shining metal giant lifts its little finger and points it at a cohort of mechanical warriors. They are turned into puddles of black metal. The giant clenches its fist, and the soldiers' remains merge into an enormous tentacle that lashes and sweeps at everything around it. Rays of wrath radiate from the giant's face.{/n}
  - After: {n}A blighted pyramid falls. A wrathful metal giant crushes it and melts warriors into a lashing tentacle.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The vision of the vengeful deity ends. The pain subsides at once, and the metal releases your hand unscathed. The flickering symbols freeze instantly and slowly begin to fade. The symbol for Pestilence is the last to disappear from the slab's surface forever.{/n}
  - After: {n}The vision ends. Your hand is freed, unscathed. Pestilence fades from the slab forever.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This I ask myself, my Lord: if my existence were to be reflected in myriad eternities, would they be the same?" {n}Your mind is now drowning in a flood of thoughts and memories, ancient, alien, and indomitable. With a titanic effort of will, you hold on to one of the images and vest it in the sound of borrowed words, and utter it in a strained voice that is not yours...{/n}
  - After: "My Lord, if my existence were reflected in myriad eternities, would they be the same?" {n}You answer in a voice not yours...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The obsidian smoothness of the enormous slab begins to ripple and roil. A set of {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NoNecronKnowlege}mysterious symbols{/d} appears on it, as if impressed on its black surface by an invisible finger. They shimmer forebodingly, like a martyr gasping for air as life drains from them.{/n}
  - After: {n}The black slab ripples. {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NoNecronKnowlege}mysterious symbols{/d} appear, shimmering ominously.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The symbols come together again underneath your palm and then vanish from the slab's animated metal.{/n}
  - After: {n}The symbols gather under your palm and vanish.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Forever frozen in a silent scream, you feel the haze of approaching madness cloud your mind as it is overrun by rows of distorted emerald-green symbols. As soon as their glow becomes unbearable, they go out at once, and you find yourself standing beside the black slab again. Right under your hand, the symbol for Malefice vanishes from the smooth black surface.{/n}
  - After: {n}Green symbols flood you toward madness, then go dark. You're back at the slab. Malefice vanishes under your hand.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As you approach, the black metal of the ancient slab begins to move. Geometric shapes appear on its surface. The three brightest ones are {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NecronKnowlege}symbols for "Star," "Transfiguration," and "Imprisonment."{/d}{/n}
  - After: {n}The slab shifts. Brightest are {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NecronKnowlege}symbols for "Star," "Transfiguration," and "Imprisonment."{/d}{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Above them is another inscription, its flickering as feeble as a dead man's breath.{/n} "My Lord, I have spoken this testament to edify my spirit, so that after my reverie's vision comes to pass eternally, I may shed my oblivion of that, which I lost when I gained all, and that, which I gained when I lost all. I absorb the lifeless images, unheedful of the fleeting moments, for eternity is my worship. I lay my hand and hearken, until my memory is an imperishable tomb wherein the ashes of times past are laid to rest."
  - After: {n}Above:{/n} "My Lord, this testament helps me recall what I lost when I gained all. My memory is a tomb for the past."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The blasphemous and convoluted tales of these xenos are scarcely different from the equally whimsical narratives dreamt up by any other inferior inhumans. They are not likely to contain even a modicum of truth.{/n}
  - After: {n}Baseless xenos fables.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Our artisans harnessed their craft to erect biofurnaces, the gates of indestructible permanence. And we entered the crucibles of immutability, and the tyranny of the withering flesh was cast off, and an eternal existence in bodies of living metal commenced. While They gorged their maws with our souls like carrion-eating beasts, for that was Their fee. Only select Overlords preserved their selfhood tenaciously and fended off the oblivion of their minds and wills."
  - After: "In biofurnaces we cast off flesh for eternal living metal. They devoured our souls as Their fee. Only select Overlords kept their minds."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thus delivered from transient life's decay, we came forth as mighty unity. Guided by Them, who had now sated Themselves, we turned our foes to nought. But Their tyranny had not made us oblivious to deception. Preparations were made and armaments were fashioned. And They were shattered, and Their fragments were engaoled in timeless tesseract prisons. There was war."
  - After: "Guided by Them, we crushed our foes. Then we shattered Them and jailed Their fragments in tesseract prisons. There was war."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The black metal rests silently before you, the rows of mysterious symbols glowing in the dark.{/n}
  - After: {n}The slab glows silently.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The slab's surface wavers and ripples like a bottomless lake. The symbols are washed away and replaced with new ones, their green glow as bright as it is lifeless.{/n} "My Lord, I behold the truth of Them, the rapacious reapers who drank stars dark. Blind was Their eyes' gaze set upon us; futile was Their engorgement, for They would never be sated."
  - After: {n}New symbols glow.{/n} "My Lord, I behold Them, the reapers who drank stars dark, never sated."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A wave of animated metal sweeps away the symbols, and the slab shows you a new set. Their glow cuts through the crypt's darkness, making your eyes sting.{/n} "My Lord, I behold the truth of the rite of Biotransference: the renouncement of our decay-bound bodies, the soul-splitting agony that doomed us to an eternity of triumph. Their messenger manifested among the Overlords of Overlords, bearing the gift of triumphant indestructibility. No fee had been promised, yet a fee was to be paid. There came no refusal, and the gifting was done."
  - After: {n}New symbols blaze.{/n} "My Lord, the rite of Biotransference: we gave up our bodies in agony. Their messenger offered indestructibility. A fee unpromised was paid."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your touch sends the symbols scurrying away like crypt beetles, only for new ones to take their place.{/n} "My Lord, I behold the truth of the fate that befell Them, fashioned by our touches. Their imprisonment is our liberty: this is the enthroned truth that reigns supreme."
  - After: {n}The symbols change.{/n} "My Lord, Their imprisonment is our liberty."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The metal yields and takes in your blade as clay would. You try to pull it out, but to no avail. Forever stuck inside the xenos monument, the blade itself now is a glorious monument to your stubbornness.{/n}
  - After: {n}The metal swallows your blade for good.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The Nephilimechs' books of wisdom. Knowledge received from the Omnissiah Himself by His most beloved children. Knowledge that led to the most terrible betrayal of all." {n}Two of his mechadendrites extend toward the stele with covetous trepidation. Two others coil tensely, as though about to attack it.{/n}
  - After: "The Nephilimechs' wisdom, from the Omnissiah Himself. It led to the worst betrayal." {n}His mechadendrites reach, covetous and tense.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "The tablets that speak through eternity." {n}Eogunn gazes greedily, as if desperate to absorb every detail shimmering in the black metal.{/n} "The secrets they conceal within themselves are sinister, yet they carry the truth across aeons. Do you realise, Rogue Trader, that only a select few among the living have experienced this? The knowledge entombed within this vessel is akin to a double-edged lancet."
  - After: "Tablets that speak through eternity." {n}Eogunn stares greedily.{/n} "Sinister but true. Few living have seen this. A double-edged lancet."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Eogunn's mechadendrite seizes Pasqal's own tentacle-like limb.{/n} "Stop, Magos. The blessing of the Omnissiah has touched neither these slabs nor those intended to use them. The ones you call Nephilimechs are xenos, more insidious and dreadful than Humankind has ever known." {n}Despite his words, he does not look away from the finds.{/n}
  - After: {n}Eogunn grabs Pasqal's mechadendrite.{/n} "Stop, Magos. The Omnissiah never blessed these. Your Nephilimechs are the worst xenos Humankind has known." {n}He keeps staring.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Bathed in the ferocious rays of a deadly star, prisoners of our own brittle bodies, our race was withering, doomed to hurtle toward imminent and inglorious obliteration. War devoured existence within and without, and unity was a spectre of dreams unattainable. Such was the way of things, and we knew nought else till we heard the call of the reapers of deathly stars."
  - After: "Scorched by a deadly star, our brittle race was dying, torn by war. Then the reapers of stars called."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "They made the summons, and we heeded Their call; and we crafted at Their behest indestructible bodies of living metal, for in Their voice we heard a hope of escape from the putrescible nature of existence."
  - After: "We heeded Them and built bodies of living metal to escape decay."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Born before death itself, They were strangers to inexistence. Therefore, my Lord, I place one of these prisons in your immortal custody. For as long as the Yekhmet endures, so too will its impregnable walls."
  - After: "Born before death, They cannot die. So, my Lord, I give one prison into your custody. While the Yekhmet endures, so will it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As you approach, the black metal of the ancient plate begins to move. Strange geometric shapes, symbols of some kind, appear on its surface. A host of smaller symbols glitter above them. They are no less {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NoNecronKnowlege}mysterious and inscrutable{/d}.{/n}
  - After: {n}The plate shifts. Symbols appear, {d|Encyclopedia:Ch5_NoNecronKnowlege}mysterious and inscrutable{/d}.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}At first, the metal feels not much different from plasteel to the touch. But as soon as you apply a little pressure, it becomes pliant and viscous like cold resin. Emerald-green marks linger for a moment where you touch it before being swallowed by the black metal.{/n}
  - After: {n}Hard, then soft as resin under pressure. Green marks fade.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You spend several minutes trying to carve your initials into the ancient xenos artefact with your knife, but the metal instantly heals any damage done to it. The idea seems more pointless with each passing moment.{/n}
  - After: {n}The metal heals every scratch.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You have come across theories that speak of an ancient xenos race that gained a metallic form, of mighty beings that showed said race the ways of unlife, and of a cruel and bitter conflict that subsequently ended their coexistence. Now you have an eyewitness account of those events.{/n}
  - After: {n}Theories told of a xenos race given metal bodies by mighty beings, then war between them. This is an eyewitness account.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You might as well have stabbed a tank — the blade recoils from the monolith with an unpleasant grating sound, slips out of your hand, and flies off.{/n}
  - After: {n}Like stabbing a tank. The blade flies from your hand.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Ch5/Temp_Companions/ChordaFaith_Companion/ChordaFaith_Companion_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "For fortitude, so that my soul may resist the temptations that beset it."
  - After: "For fortitude against temptation."
- **Player**
  - Before: "For strength, so that I may crush His enemies."
  - After: "For strength to crush His enemies."
- **Player**
  - Before: "For mercy upon those who have joined us on this perilous expedition."
  - After: "For mercy on those in this expedition."
- **Player**
  - Before: "There is every chance that our meeting with Calcazar will end in battle. Are you prepared for such an outcome?"
  - After: "Meeting Calcazar may mean battle. Are you ready?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do you make of the systems we have found ourselves in?"
  - After: "What do you make of these systems?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do you suppose was Calcazar's purpose for coming to these accursed systems?"
  - After: "Why did Calcazar come to these accursed systems?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Incendia's eyes blaze with fanaticism against her deathly white features. She rasps in greeting,{/n} "The Emperor protects, {name}. Even in a place as dark and abominable as these stars."
  - After: {n}Her eyes blaze.{/n} "The Emperor protects, {name}. Even here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "May your faith serve as your shield, {name}."
  - After: "May faith be your shield, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You bear this privilege with greater dignity than Theodora did. In this dark hour, the Emperor has sent a worthy leader to guide the Expanse."
  - After: "You're worthier than Theodora."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Let us open our hearts to Him, for even in this fetid darkness of xenos impurity, He hears our voices. What wish you to pray to our Protector for?"
  - After: "He hears us even here. What will you pray for?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You can sense flaws within you and admit to them freely, and that is good. Indeed doubts and temptations are the most terrible of our foes, for they are the bane that turns a righteous warrior into a heretic."
  - After: "Good. Doubt turns the righteous into heretics."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This plea is virtuous, for our lives are insignificant, and all that matters is our service and the condemnation of His enemies."
  - After: "Virtuous. Only service matters."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Very well. Pray that He saves your soldiers, and I shall pray that He graces them with enough conviction and courage to die a righteous death when the hour comes."
  - After: "Pray He saves them. I'll pray they die righteously."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Then join me in asking Him to illuminate our path and show us the wickedness that we have come to exterminate. And to let none hide from our hand, and to see retribution served."
  - After: "Then we ask Him to reveal the wicked, and let none escape."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A battle is imminent, for I am guided by the scent of a crime in the making, and where there is a crime, there is a criminal. If the Lord Inquisitor came here to oppose this malefactor, then we shall help him. If the Warden of the Expanse has erred and abandoned the path of service to the Emperor, then we shall punish him. None are without fault before the Protector, not even Calcazar."
  - After: "I smell a crime coming. If the Lord Inquisitor fights it, we help. If the Warden of the Expanse strayed, we punish him. Even Calcazar."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A hotbed of xenos filth." {n}Her pale lips twist.{/n} "These dark reaches are meant to test us, our faith, and our resolve. From the moment we arrived, I have been tempering my spirit through ascesis and self-denial. I would counsel that you do the same." {n}Incendia's appearance really does look even less healthy than usual. There are deep shadows under her sunken eyes as if she has not eaten for a number of days.{/n}
  - After: "A xenos hotbed." {n}Her lips twist.{/n} "A test. I'm fasting; you should too." {n}She looks gaunt.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "While I cannot approve of your detestable habit of keeping ungodly xenos in your retinue, I will admit that their presence does not dim the fury with which your devotion burns."
  - After: "I despise your xenos, but your devotion burns."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have seen Foulstone burgeon under your hand, and with that, a new beacon for righteous souls was lit in the sector. Such an endeavour takes diligence and patience, and these qualities I, regrettably, lack — mine is the path of a castigator, not a builder."
  - After: "Foulstone flourished under you. I punish; I don't build."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To serve the Emperor, I would hope. I detect the scent of a crime in the making, and pray that the Lord Inquisitor came here to punish and prevent blasphemy against Him."
  - After: "To serve the Emperor, I hope. I smell a crime brewing; may he stop it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Humanity's foes tried time after time to rob us of what we had conquered, but you were always there to stand in their path. Vheabos VI was doomed to fall and become a heathen wasteland, but instead it rose as a bastion of solitude and contemplation for those seeking repentance. This implacability is your great virtue."
  - After: "You held off Humanity's foes. Vheabos VI became a haven for penitents, not a wasteland."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "One day, you will be gone, your flesh will turn to dust, and even your very name will disappear from the memory of the living. But your legacy will live on. At the Schola Progenium on Dargonus, new warriors in His service will be trained to uphold the same ideals that you upheld before them."
  - After: "You'll be forgotten, but the Schola Progenium on Dargonus will train warriors in your ideals."

## World/Dialogs/Ch5/Temp_Companions/ChordaHope_Companion/ChordaHope_Companion_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You seem broken. Do I need such a fighter at my side?"
  - After: "You seem broken. Do I need you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You do realise that our meeting with Calcazar may end in battle, do you not? Are you ready?"
  - After: "Meeting Calcazar may mean battle. Ready?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Has your faith truly wavered so greatly in such a short time?"
  - After: "Has your faith wavered so quickly?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Tell me, why did you choose to come with me, truly?"
  - After: "Why did you really come with me?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}With a neurotic twitch of her pale cheek, Incendia offers you a resolute nod.{/n} "We find ourselves in a grim place, {name}. It frightens me to think of the horrors that dwell here. I only hope that we have the strength to fulfil our duty to the people of the Expanse."
  - After: {n}Incendia nods, twitching.{/n} "A grim place, {name}. May we have the strength to serve."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Emperor protects, {name}." {n}You hear none of the former zeal in Incendia's dry words. She sounds tired.{/n}
  - After: "The Emperor protects, {name}." {n}She sounds tired.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I wish not to speak ill of Theodora, but you treat people with far more grace and nobility than she ever did. Guided by your hand, your protectorate flourishes and your people extol you. And if it is so, then what does my opinion matter?"
  - After: "You're nobler than Theodora. Your protectorate flourishes."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I was impressed by your decision to grant rights to the people of your capital world. Most rulers are afraid of their subjects, but you are not one of them."
  - After: "Granting your capital's people rights impressed me. You don't fear them."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Many in your position would have stopped at watching over their own colonies, especially in an hour as bleak and difficult as ours. And thus I found the mercy that you showed to the refugees from Winterscale's Realm all the more admirable. By allowing them on Janus, you saved millions of lives that Calligos had forsaken."
  - After: "Taking Winterscale's Realm refugees onto Janus saved millions Calligos abandoned."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In a time of trials, the Emperor sent a true leader to the Koronus Expanse. Just as your servants from Foulstone selflessly lit void beacons to save lost souls from death, so have you, through your tireless toils, become a beacon of hope to us all."
  - After: "Like Foulstone's void beacons, you're the Koronus Expanse's beacon of hope."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Keep steadfast, {name}. And be watchful of the temptations infesting our path."
  - After: "Keep steadfast, {name}. Beware temptation."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Lord Inquisitor... I once thought of him as an impeccably pious and devout servant of the Emperor. But he used me as a tool, and when I started doubting myself, I started doubting him. I was a monster, and he... I have a feeling that he may be a monster just as terrible. And monsters must be destroyed."
  - After: "The Lord Inquisitor used me. I was a monster; he may be one too. Monsters must be destroyed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No human should have to journey to a place as dire as this. We are wandering in a graveyard of ancient terrors whose existence strains the mind to acknowledge. Touching their relics, reading their words... Who can say how it will change us? Who can say if we even ought to return to inhabited worlds after this, befouled as we will be by the poison that this xenos darkness is feeding us?"
  - After: "A graveyard of ancient terrors. Who knows how it'll poison us, or if we should return home?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My hands no longer sow murder, but my fingers are forever stained with blood. I had too high an opinion of myself, but shame pierced the shell of my hubris. I do not wish this feeling upon you — to realise that your ideals and deeds were shaped by another's manipulation."
  - After: "I kill no more, but my hands are stained. Shame broke my pride. My ideals were another's manipulation."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Subdue my wrathful spirit. My servants can see to the needs of my protectorate, while I must ensure that my hands hold prayer beads rather than the reins of power. And that, whatever weapon I wield, I use it to protect the people of the Expanse instead of smiting them."
  - After: "Tame my wrath. Hold prayer beads, not power, and protect the Expanse, not smite it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No, I remain truly devoted to Him, but... the fire that once fuelled my faith is gone. I can see the future that I rendered with His name on my lips, and it was akin to a graveyard. A field of towering statues proclaiming His glory, and not a single flaw among them, for all who had been found flawed would be lying dead. And I do not believe that Humanity heading toward such a future is the Emperor's will."
  - After: "I'm devoted, but the fire's gone. My future in His name was a graveyard of flawless statues. That can't be His will."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After a long pause, Incendia says reluctantly,{/n} "I seek forgiveness. I did far too many things that cannot be expiated or corrected. I hope... blast it, {name}, I hope that out there, in the darkness, I shall get a chance to die with dignity and thus absolve myself of even some small portion of my wrongdoing."
  - After: {n}A pause.{/n} "Forgiveness. Blast it, {name}, I hope to die with dignity out there and atone a little."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You see the corner of Incendia's mouth twitch, and a familiar crooked smile appears on her face as a hint of venom creeps into her voice:{/n} "That my pride lies in ruins does not give certain fledgling Rogue Traders the right to look down their nose at me. I have embarked on hundreds of expeditions and fought hundreds of battles, and my heart yet remembers the heat that calls for the Emperor's justice to be served. When the hour comes, that heat will turn into a blaze, which I shall unleash upon His enemies."
  - After: {n}Her crooked smile returns:{/n} "Broken pride doesn't let fledgling Rogue Traders look down on me. My heart still burns for His justice."

## World/Dialogs/Ch5/Temp_Companions/Uralon_Comp/Uralon_Comp_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Why are you known as Uralon the Cruel?"
  - After: "Why 'Uralon the Cruel'?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is that book in your hands?"
  - After: "What is that book?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You betrayed Kunrad. How do I know that you will not betray me next?"
  - After: "You betrayed Kunrad. Why not me?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You call yourself a Dark Apostle. What does it mean?"
  - After: "What is a Dark Apostle?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I must take my leave."
  - After: "I must go."
- **Player**
  - Before: "My path is clear. I shall wear the wreath of the Dawn upon my brow and take what is mine by right."
  - After: "I shall wear the Dawn's wreath and take what is mine."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Not bad, but too plain for my taste. You lack a certain charm of madness. I should ask Idira to show you how it's done."
  - After: "Too plain. Idira could teach you madness."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Is that it? Your prophecies are worthless!"
  - After: "That's it? Worthless prophecies!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are hiding something from me, sorcerer. Answer me: what else did you see?"
  - After: "You're hiding something, sorcerer. What else did you see?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are a prophet, are you not? Reveal the Ways to me."
  - After: "You're a prophet. Reveal the Ways."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Recite the dark prayer you heard on Kiava Gamma] "Are those the words of your lord?"
  - After: [Recite the dark prayer from Kiava Gamma] "Your lord's words?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "And what is the Truth, Uralon?"
  - After: "What is the Truth, Uralon?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have disgraced you more than once, I have killed your brothers and ruined many of your plans. Are you telling me that you harbour no malice toward me at all?"
  - After: "I killed your brothers and ruined your plans. No malice?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Emperor is strong, but that did not stop you from betraying him."
  - After: "The Emperor is strong, yet you betrayed him."
- **Player**
  - Before: "First you betrayed the Emperor, then Kunrad... Old habits die hard."
  - After: "The Emperor, then Kunrad... Old habits."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I see. Let us discuss other matters."
  - After: "I see. Other matters."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The sorcerer's fingers, clad in heavy gauntlets, are leafing through the pages of a grand tome bound in rough, dark leather. Upon hearing your footsteps, Uralon the Cruel looks away from the tome and bares his sharp, uneven teeth.{/n} "I greet you, champion. Is it time to spill the blood of misbelievers? Or has the path of the Truth brought you to me for another purpose?"
  - After: {n}Uralon looks up from his tome, baring sharp teeth.{/n} "Champion. Time to spill misbelievers' blood?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Uralon the Cruel looks away from his tome once more.{/n} "Champion. What is the Truth's reason for this arrival?"
  - After: {n}Uralon looks up.{/n} "Champion. Why are you here?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We have many toils ahead of us, {name}. You are destined to make the Koronus Expanse witness the blaze of the Final Dawn. I will help you in this through word and deed, until the call of the Primordial Truth shows me a different path. For now, leave thoughts of the future to me — you must focus on your deeds in the present."
  - After: "You will bring the Final Dawn to the Expanse, {name}, and I will help. Leave the future to me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is a collection of sermons from the Book of Lorgar. The Truth spoken by our Primarch and carved into human skin, which was then removed and turned into pages. The wisdom and verity of the Primarch's words fill my being with awe whenever I open this scripture. In it, Lord Lorgar casts down the false faith in the Emperor and grants us the tenets of the true faith in the great gods of the Immaterium."
  - After: "Sermons of Lorgar, written on human skin. They cast down the Emperor's false faith for the true gods."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It means that I am the guide of the true faithful. I am their teacher, prophet, and master, who leads the Legion's disciples in their service to the Truth. I share this burden with my brothers on the Dark Council. None but Lord Lorgar and the Great Four can command us."
  - After: "I am teacher and prophet of the faithful, on the Dark Council. Only Lorgar and the Great Four command us."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My sermons have converted entire worlds to the true faith. My hands have brought populations to ruin. Stand proud, {name}, for only those I deem my equal have been allowed to fight at my side."
  - After: "I have converted worlds. Stand proud, {name}: only equals fight beside me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Uralon closes his eyes, and the symbols carved into his face flare like embers.{/n} "I cannot perceive what the watchdog of the Expanse is planning. All I know is that he holds a key, and that key must be yours. Only one path will see you alight with the crimson wreath of the Final Dawn. The rest hold only oblivion and death."
  - After: {n}Uralon's carved face flares.{/n} "The Expanse's watchdog holds a key that must be yours. One path leads to the Final Dawn. The rest, death."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Over thousands of years, I have learned how inconstant fate can be and how often its turns that I perceive as defeats reveal themselves as my resounding victories. I have learned to put my fate in the will of the Changer of Ways and follow the call of the Truth. There is no malice, {name}. Your ascension is one of my greatest triumphs."
  - After: "My defeats often became victories. No malice, {name}. Your ascension is my triumph."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "His strength is feigned and built on lies amplified by the servility of his lackeys. Our actions were not a betrayal, {name}. We were overthrowing a tyrant."
  - After: "His strength is lies. We did not betray, {name}. We overthrew a tyrant."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Do you know what they had in common? Both could only see as far as themselves. Although, even I am loath to compare the corpse emperor to carrion like Kunrad — at least the Imperium's former master had a backbone and a vision, albeit one that was inexcusably deceitful and short-sighted."
  - After: "Both saw only themselves. But the corpse emperor at least had a backbone, unlike Kunrad."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It makes no difference to the Truth whether you find its portents agreeable or not. You asked me to show you the twisted Ways, and I have revealed what you are meant to know here and now, no more and no less than that."
  - After: "The Truth cares not if you like it. You know what you need."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your paltry witch is beneath me. She is a broken vox that spews images and noise, unable to discern the Truth among them. An amusing sight, but that is all."
  - After: "Your witch is a broken vox spewing noise."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "May the blessing of the True Gods be with you."
  - After: "May the True Gods bless you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}For but a moment, you see lines of unease and doubt cross his brow. There is something he is not telling you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Doubt crosses his brow. He is hiding something.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He opens his eyes.{/n} "That is all I can tell you, champion."
  - After: {n}He opens his eyes.{/n} "That is all, champion."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And I will stand at your side when you do, champion. May the faith in the hearts of the devout never waver."
  - After: "And I will stand beside you, champion."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Uralon's long, heavy look presses down on you.{/n} "There is one more path. No, it is not a path — an ancient abyss beyond the edges of fate, a place where no Ways lead. You wear another wreath there. With this wreath, you have everything. With this wreath, you have nothing. Upon accepting it, not only will you renounce your destiny, but life itself will become your enemy. That is my final prophecy to you."
  - After: {n}Uralon stares heavily.{/n} "An abyss beyond fate holds another wreath: everything and nothing. Take it, and you renounce destiny, and life becomes your enemy."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Uralon nods, looking at you expectantly.{/n}
  - After: {n}Uralon nods, waiting.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The general's will was strong, but it was not his will that I had been trying to break — among the children I had brought to the slaughter were the sons and daughters of his closest officers. I was true to my word: I took the general, let the defenders take the children inside the walls, and left. But the Truth had already touched the souls of the youth. The same night, they cut their parents' throats, gutted the sentries, and opened the gates for me and my brothers. The bastion had fallen. The name of that world has long since faded from my memory, but the epithet Cruel I bear to this day."
  - After: "The children included his officers' own. I took the general and let them in. That night they killed their parents and opened the gates. 'Cruel' stayed with me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Once, we were fighting for a planet that was on the verge of embracing the true faith. All that stood in our way was a single bastion whose troops had hidden behind impenetrable walls, refusing to kneel before us. Their commander was a valiant and talented general, an unshakeable protector without a doubt in his heart. My brothers were ready to reduce the city to dust with an orbital bombardment — what did a single stronghold matter when we had already brought the whole planet to heel? But I decided otherwise."
  - After: "One bastion on a world nearly ours held out under an unshakeable general. My brothers wanted bombardment. I chose otherwise."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}He lets out a hoarse laugh.{/n} "Kunrad was weak, pathetic, and vain, and he was nothing compared to you. You spoke the name of the dawns, you spilt the blood of misbelievers, you released the master from his ancient prison. Kunrad could not accomplish even a shred of what you proved capable of. Why would I betray someone as strong as you, champion?"
  - After: {n}He laughs hoarsely.{/n} "Kunrad was weak. You freed the master from his prison. Why betray someone so strong?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "One morning, I walked to the bastion's gates with a hundred children whom we had captured on our triumphant march, and offered the general a trade — his life in exchange for theirs. The general, whose will was stronger than adamantine, refused. I then put the children to death before the defenders' eyes and left. The next day, I came again with another hundred and made my offer once more. Again the general refused, and another hundred screaming, crying children died by my hand. On the third day, when I approached the gates with a hundred more, the general, beaten and wounded, landed at my feet, cast down from the walls by the bastion's defenders."
  - After: "I offered the general a hundred captive children for his life. He refused; I killed them. Again the next day. On the third, his defenders threw him at my feet."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Uralon's torn lips stretch into a satisfied smile.{/n} "You impress me, champion. Yes, that is one of his many sermons. I will gladly share more of Lord Lorgar's wisdom with you, should you so desire. Later, once your ascension is complete."
  - After: {n}Uralon smiles.{/n} "You impress me. Yes, his sermon. More after your ascension."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That the Imperium is a rotting corpse, as is its worthless master. Worms writhe inside its guts, praying to the putrescent husk, believing that it will protect them from the storm. They swallow the damp flesh, smack their lips, and vomit it into each other's throats, gorging, choking. And all the while, the crumbling corpse only continues to rot away. Storms and carrion eaters pick the reeking flesh off its brittle bones, piece by piece, as the frightened worms struggle to mend the gaping wounds with their own flesh."
  - After: "The Imperium is a rotting corpse. Worms gorge in its guts, praying to the husk to shield them from the storm."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Truth is that the corpse is bound to turn into nothing but pus and bonemeal. And the worms, if they wish to survive, must behold the storm of Chaos that rages outside and offer themselves to it. And we, in our endless grace, will accept them into our fold. For the Truth is in the service to the storm."
  - After: "The corpse will rot to nothing. To survive, the worms must offer themselves to the storm of Chaos. The Truth is service to the storm."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I do not blame you for taking great caution, {name}. The paths devised by the Weaver of Destinies are twisted and obscured — it is easy to stumble and lose sight of the Truth. Do not misstep, champion, and we will remain allies."
  - After: "Caution is wise, {name}. The Weaver's paths are twisted. Do not misstep."

## World/Dialogs/Ch5/Temp_Companions/Winterscale_Comp/WinterscaleCompanion_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "What do you think of the way the 'new blood' has handled {mf|his|her} protectorate?"
  - After: "How has the 'new blood' handled {mf|his|her} protectorate?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What are you going to do after Calcazar has been dealt with?"
  - After: "What will you do after Calcazar?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You often talk about your hunt. Will you tell me how it started?"
  - After: "How did your hunt start?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "We are traversing a new part of the Expanse. Do you know anything about it?"
  - After: "Know anything about this region?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "So, you are going to abandon your trade protectorate?"
  - After: "You'll abandon your protectorate?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How are you finding life aboard my ship?"
  - After: "How do you find my ship?"

  - Before: "I shall see you at the hunt, Calligos."

  - Before: {n}Calligos's broad-shouldered figure exudes strength and authority, but his tense jaw muscles belie his impatience.{/n} "Waiting on this rust bucket for the hunt to resume is trying my patience, {name}."

  - Before: {n}Winterscale scorches you with an imperious gaze.{/n} "{name}. How soon will our hunt continue?"

  - Before: "Those poor bastards from Vheabos VI whom you sold to the pirates? Ha! You are an enterprising sort, I'll give you that — you always find a way to turn a profit!"

  - Before: {n}He leans closer and gives you an ominous smile.{/n} "Did you think I wouldn't learn about your little ploy with the Kasballica? I must admit, I'm actually a little... awestruck."

  - Before: "Gladiatorial fights on a pillaged penal world — a bold move, new blood, a very bold move. I am tempted to pay a visit to Vheabos VI myself to place a few bets and enjoy myself... Perhaps later."

  - Before: "It takes a lot of confidence — or nerve — to poach another's subjects and put them to work in the quarries of your own penal world. I can picture the governors' outraged faces when they learned their workforce was now breaking their backs on Vheabos VI!"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Bloodthirst dances in Winterscale's eyes.{/n} "My purpose is to flirt with death in the heat of battle and to tear my enemies to shreds. The list is long, and the degenerate Calcazar will be just another name that I will wash away with blood."

  - Before: "Why, are you already planning to take it for yourself?" {n}Calligos's upper lip twitches in a menacing half-smile.{/n} "The Winterscale dynasty is greater than me alone.   - Before: "Oh, {name}, my hunt began when the blood rivers spilt in the Rifts of Hecaton! - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Rogue Trader pauses before replying.{/n} "While I've never seen anything to like in that bastard, it would be a mistake not to recognise his power. Calcazar is dangerous and far from stupid, which means the hunt for him will be a thrilling one."
  - After: {n}He pauses.{/n} "Calcazar is dangerous and clever. A thrilling hunt."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Lord Inquisitor is a worthy adversary whose skin I'll have made into a fine pair of boots. It pleases me to know I will be trampling him further into the dirt with every step I take."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "{name}." {n}Winterscale's face twists in a predatory grin.{/n}
  - After: "{name}." {n}A predatory grin.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Calligos laughs gleefully.{/n} "Are you calling this rust bucket a ship, {name}? This washtub would pale next to the Emperor's Vow, but I admit that it does bring back memories. I used to command a similar vessel back in the day."
  - After: {n}Calligos laughs.{/n} "A ship, {name}? This washtub? I once commanded one like it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Then again, I do not think your subjects would be very surprised. You yourself enjoy splashing in their blood alongside your pet xenos, do you not?"
  - After: "Though you bathe in their blood with your pet xenos yourself."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This area has been obscured by warp storms for so long that no data about its exploration remains. The diaries of my predecessors briefly mention that something unimaginably dangerous lurks here..."
  - After: "Warp storms hid this area. Old diaries hint at something terribly dangerous..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But that is what you and I want, is it not? There is nothing quite like a new and deadly enemy." {n}Calligos greedily licks his dry lips in anticipation.{/n}
  - After: "Just what we want." {n}He licks his lips.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "After we are done hunting him, I will set out to find a new quarry just as glorious as this one. I will look for a worthy opponent all over the Expanse, enjoying every new skirmish."
  - After: "Then I'll find another glorious quarry."

  - Before: "How the information was reaching his agents, the burned mon-keigh himself did not even know, but based on the units involved and other details it was clear: no mon-keigh in realspace could have gathered such specifics about raid complements and objectives. So I allied with Nazrakhei, who presided over the trial. I promised him that Yremeryss would be humiliated.
