Alarmed, Cassia passes a palm over your shoulder, as if shaking off some ash that settled there. You feel some relief.{/n} "I am sorry, Lord Captain. I should not have darkened your colours with my own struggles."
  - After: "No. My subjects' hatred chokes me..." {n}Your throat tightens; her touch eases it.{/n} "Forgive me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Sister Argenta shines like a guiding star, inspiring resolve in those around her, seemingly inexplicably. However, I see a dark and ugly fog billow behind her, contrasting sharply with her shining light. It burdens the Sister of Battle. It drags her down... Yet Argenta herself is hardly aware of it."
  - After: "Argenta shines like a guiding star. But a dark fog drags at her unnoticed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Jae continues to envelop herself in the variegation of her habitual masks, changing her colours at will like so many garments. But deep within her heart trembles a timid seedling the colour of smoky lilies. It is grimy, burnt, and covered in ash... But it is genuine. Who knows, perhaps one day Jae will allow it to grow and blossom."
  - After: "Jae still swaps masks. But inside, a burnt yet genuine seedling may someday bloom."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The fire of a rising sun illuminates Ulfar's face, a blaze so incandescent it is painful to look at. But whenever the fire subsides, even for a second, at once an undercoat of dismal greyness and repulsive green haze envelops his shoulders. No one around him notices it..." {n}Cassia waves her hand, throwing an invisible shawl off her own shoulders.{/n} "But I see."
  - After: "Ulfar blazes like a sun. When it dims, grey and sickly green cloak him." {n}She shrugs.{/n} "Only I see."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The cold embers in Ulfar's soul absorbed the dismal grey, leaving only charcoal splotches. They are straining to break out. They smudge his hues... And the tarnished gold no longer shines as brightly."
  - After: "Ulfar's embers have turned charcoal, straining to break out. His gold tarnishes."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The esteemed Magos Haneumann is shattered like a beautiful stained-glass window into a mosaic of colours. His bright, beckoning hues are mixed together in complete disarray... I must confess it perplexes me. Normally, scarlet and steel are all that fills the heart of a servant of the Omnissiah."
  - After: "Haneumann is shattered stained glass. Odd; tech-priests are usually just scarlet and steel."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Cassia frowns in confusion.{/n} "Ah, I see... Forgive me, I misunderstood."
  - After: {n}Cassia frowns.{/n} "I misunderstood."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The colourful shards of stained glass have risen up and enveloped Magos Haneumann in a swirl of speculations. The silvery glint of metal no longer conceals his anxiety. Nor does his scarlet robe conceal his doubts."
  - After: "Haneumann's shards swirl. His metal no longer hides his doubts."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Behind the cobalt steel of his thoughts, behind the cold, faded grey of his emotions... an ember the colour of amber glows in Master van Calox's soul, so bright and warm one is tempted to touch it." {n}Cassia looks into the distance, transfixed, as though it weren't you standing in front of her. Then she snaps out of it and lowers her eyes.{/n} "It is sad that the Interrogator seeks to drown it with his own hands in the bottomless blue of duty. Sad indeed... but I can relate."
  - After: "Under van Calox's steel glows a warm ember." {n}She looks down.{/n} "He drowns it in duty. As do I."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Idira's emotions are like a maelstrom: bright, unbridled, enveloping her form like a wondrous kaleidoscope of colours... And as dangerous as a twisting warp storm. The riot of colours hides the truth from my eyes: what exactly is driving this woman? Is it her own will? Or—" {n}Cassia hesitates.{/n} "—or is it the Immaterium, Lord Captain?"
  - After: "Idira's emotions are a warp storm. Is it her will driving her? Or—" {n}She hesitates.{/n} "—the Immaterium?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Idira... The many-coloured veil has fallen off, finally revealing to me the person behind it. Yet what is left of that person? A pale, colourless shell." {n}Her ruby-red eyes are filled with compassion and sorrow.{/n} "Her colours are fading away quickly, and I am powerless to stop it... As is everyone. Soon a grey shadow will be all that is left of the psyker."
  - After: "Idira's veil has fallen, showing a colourless shell." {n}She looks sad.{/n} "She fades fast. Soon only a grey shadow."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Try not to squander that sky-blue fabric of hope, Lord Captain. For others' colours, too, lighten when they are close to you."
  - After: "Keep that hope. Others brighten near you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A dejected silence hangs in the air. Finally, the Lady Navigator says,{/n} "It was real, Lord Captain. I must confess, I have been hounded by eerie strangers for many years — in my dreams, visions, and warp scryings. They try to reach me. They are tormented. They shout something I cannot make out. And one of those strangers, the most frightening one, is a woman who always stands aside and merely looks on in disapproval."
  - After: {n}Silence.{/n} "It was real. Tormented strangers have long haunted my visions. The worst is a woman who only watches, disapproving."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am gradually regaining my strength, Lord Captain. And I am in control of my body and mind once again." {n}Cassia puts her hand on the artefact {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_CassiaAmuletLeft}glowing faintly under her skin{/d}.{/n}
  - After: "I am regaining control." {n}She touches the artefact {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_CassiaAmuletLeft}glowing under her skin{/d}.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And yet you did not abandon me in the darkness, even though you could have. You did not end my life even though your heart was in the grip of a coal-black vice, and your reason was enmeshed in a crimson web." {n}Cassia averts her eyes, trying to hide her burning shame behind her shock of dishevelled hair.{/n}
  - After: "Yet you did not abandon or kill me." {n}She hides her shame.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "An Ecclesiarch, one of the wisest, once said that we all play our parts by unfailingly serving the Emperor. Sometimes our parts change, but faith — faith remains." {n}Cassia smiles a little.{/n} "Dubious colours would show up every now and then in things Jae said, but every word she ever spoke of Him shone with the bright white of faith."
  - After: "Parts change, but faith remains." {n}She smiles.{/n} "Jae's words about the Emperor always shone with faith."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Besides..." {n}Cassia hesitates for a few seconds and looks away.{/n} "I am aware that lesser servants of the Imperium may find our appearance... repulsive. The {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g} gene twists the features the rabble are used to seeing, and the magnificence of our role cannot be grasped by their feeble minds..."
  - After: "Besides..." {n}She looks away.{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g} gene twists us. The rabble find us repulsive."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That explains why the Sister of Battle's pure hues were muddied by swamp sludge. The mere thought of the consequences of her deeds horrifies me."
  - After: "That explains the sludge in her hues. Horrifying."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am sorry, Lord Captain. I should have glimpsed the earthen hue of treachery that creaked between her teeth." {n}Cassia purses her lips guiltily.{/n} "But xenos colours are so... so rank. The variety of hues becomes maddening as soon as you rest your gaze on them."
  - After: "Forgive me. I missed her treachery." {n}She winces.{/n} "Xenos colours are maddening."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Can words ever describe the joy of being free?" {n}Cassia smiles gently as she puts her hand on the spot where, not so long ago, the artefact {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_CassiaAmuletBroken}used to glow{/d}.{/n}
  - After: "Such joy, being free!" {n}She touches where the artefact {d|Encyclopedia:Ch3_CassiaAmuletBroken}used to glow{/d}.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You gave me the strength to cast off the shackles that Felek's cunning had closed around my soul. To tear down the prison of my own fears. And I wish to repay you in kind." {n}Cassia extends a hand toward your forehead, stopping halfway.{/n} "To cast the fading purple of this place from your shoulders. To break the brown collar that is choking you... That is, of course, if you permit me to."
  - After: "You freed me from Felek's shackles. Let me repay you." {n}She reaches for your forehead.{/n} "To lift your darkness, if you permit."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Somewhere in the middle of the Dark City, I suppose. They say the human mind cannot fathom the bounds of this place, for the Imperium's largest hives look like grains of sand in comparison. A Webway Gate built by the ancient Aeldari is the only way in. I think you realise as well as I do what that means for us."
  - After: "In the Dark City. Its only entrance is an Aeldari Webway Gate. You know what that means."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Cassia jerks back her hand as if it's been scalded.{/n} "I am sorry. I thought, since you helped me... N-never mind. Forget I mentioned it."
  - After: {n}She jerks back.{/n} "Sorry. N-never mind."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Cassia's cool palm touches your forehead lightly, and a maelstrom of colours comes flooding into your consciousness. Your feelings and emotions change under the onslaught of a will that is not yours. The sensation is familiar, but this time, the process is different. Soft. Painless. Perhaps even... pleasurable? Fatigue drains out of your shoulders fast. Next, the pain in your exhausted muscles subsides, and each breath you take fills your chest with an increasing sense of confidence.{/n}
  - After: {n}Her cool palm touches your forehead. Colours flood you gently; fatigue and pain drain away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I had the same exact thoughts. But is that not a wild conjecture, even for a Navigator? Or am I simply going insane, as unworthy scions of my family have?" {n}Cassia's voice with despair. She looks you in the eye, as if expecting a refutation of her misgivings.{/n}
  - After: "I thought so too. Or am I going mad?" {n}She looks to you, hoping.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Then..." {n}Cassia breathes a sigh of relief.{/n} "Then I will take every effort to rid myself of that bedevilment."
  - After: "Then..." {n}She sighs, relieved.{/n} "I will rid myself of this."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionDialogues/Nomos/NomosAfterReveal/NomosAfterReveal_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Were you the one who falsified the ship's log?"
  - After: "Did you falsify the log?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What about the research notes on the 'tech-blight' that we obtained from the cache on Kiava Gamma?"
  - After: "And the Kiava Gamma 'tech-blight' notes?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "All I ask is that you promise not to do it again."
  - After: "Just promise not to repeat it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What have you been doing, Nomos?"
  - After: "What have you been doing?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You were in a servitor's body at my Magnae Accessio, Nomos, so how is it that you are once again in a cogitator?"
  - After: "You were a servitor at my Magnae Accessio. Why a cogitator now?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I see you have found your great spirit, Asclepius."
  - After: "You found your spirit, Asclepius."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Incident N872-04 was a ship-wide system failure of some kind. It and 'Epitaph' had something to do with the ship flying better."
  - After: "Incident N872-04 and 'Epitaph' made the ship fly better."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you know where this Epitaph is?"
  - After: "Where is Epitaph?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The people who accompanied Theodora on her travels are strangely unaware of the Incident and Epitaph."
  - After: "Theodora's companions know nothing of the Incident or Epitaph."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I must take my leave."
  - After: "I must go."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The ship was on Epitaph, Amarnat travelled aboard it, investigating the tech-blight, and Nomos was born as a result of an incident. So how was it possible that no one in the crew knew the whole truth?"
  - After: "Epitaph, Amarnat's blight research, Nomos's birth... How did no one in the crew know?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "So you really are the spirit of the ship?"
  - After: "So you are the ship's spirit?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Enough about that for now."
  - After: "Enough for now."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Enough about the past — let us talk about the future. You do, in fact, have a purpose, Nomos..."
  - After: "Enough of the past. You do have a purpose, Nomos..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You read the data-bank recovered from Theodora's cache. And then you said, 'The Incident marked the beginning of Nomos.' What did you mean by that?"
  - After: "You said, 'The Incident marked the beginning of Nomos.' Meaning?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "To serve the light and truth and greatness that is the Imperium."
  - After: "To serve the light of the Imperium."
- **Player**
  - Before: "To simply live, comprehending yourself and the world. Life does not need a purpose to justify itself."
  - After: "To simply live. Life needs no purpose."
- **Player**
  - Before: "To be my servant, my blade, a force to be reckoned with by all."
  - After: "To be my servant and blade, a force all fear."
- **Player**
  - Before: "How is Amarnat involved in this?"
  - After: "And Amarnat?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "If ever you need anything, come straight to me. I will hear you out."
  - After: "If you need anything, come to me."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am not your servant to be sent on errands. I will not tolerate such behaviour from you again."
  - After: "I am not your errand-runner. Never again."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servitor built into the huge cogitator turns its head toward you. The vox emits a rasping voice:{/n} "Hello! Nomos welcome your visit."
  - After: {n}The servitor turns.{/n} "Nomos welcome you."
- **Asclepius**
  - Before: {n}The massive figure of the malatek Asclepius is frozen before the cogitator in a praying pose. Without raising his head, he addresses you:{/n} "I salute the ruler of this ship."
  - After: {n}Asclepius prays.{/n} "Hail, ship's ruler."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The unblinking gaze of the servitor gargoyle is fixed on you.{/n} "Nomos are here. What do you want to talk about?"
  - After: {n}The gargoyle stares.{/n} "Nomos are here. Speak."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This name is also known to us. It is related to Nomos, although we do not understand how."
  - After: "We know this name. It relates to Nomos."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}For a moment there is silence, broken only by the moans of the huge machine, and then the cybergargoyle begins to speak, and with it, the other servitors chosen by Nomos:{/n} "We have analysed the data with which you sated us, and we have recreated the sequence of events."
  - After: {n}The servitors speak as one.{/n} "Your data revealed all."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "First, there was Epitaph. It is a world, but it is merely a case, a container, for something we cannot name and cannot understand. Theodora and this ship have been to that place. Something was lifted up from the world. A gift. A trusted priest in crimson — one who identified himself as 'Amarnat' — comprehended the gift raised from Epitaph. And from it, he created what the data-banks list as a 'tech-blight.'"
  - After: "Epitaph is a world hiding something nameless. Theodora took a gift from it; Amarnat made it a 'tech-blight.'"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But that is not how Nomos came into being. We were not... invented. We were not freed. We came into being... by accident." {n}The chorus of servitors sounds genuinely confused, almost desperate.{/n} "Theodora's ambition, the myriad mechanisms of the huge ship. Amarnat's mind, the inquisitive attempts to comprehend and extract. The dormant blight. The dormant Epitaph. What lies hidden in its depths. And between it all, we slipped in, connected, and emerged like an electrical discharge between the poles."
  - After: "Nomos were not made, but arose by accident," {n}the chorus says.{/n} "From Theodora's ambition, the ship, Amarnat's mind and the blight, we sparked."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Accident... Incident. That is what we are. We have no purpose. No history. Nomos just are."
  - After: "Accident... Incident. No purpose. Nomos just are."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Nomos are not in a cogitator. Or in a servitor. We cannot say where we are — but our existence is tied to the existence of the ship for now. The servitor and the cogitator are only... external interfaces. Shells. Like humans and their bodies."
  - After: "Neither. We are bound to the ship for now; these are shells, like bodies."
- **Asclepius**
  - Before: "I have found a miracle. And the end of my worldly road. I have never seen and never will see anything more meaningful than the spirit of Nomos. In the face of its multitude, we are all nothing but the fixed values of an erroneous function."
  - After: "A miracle. Beside Nomos, we are errors."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cybergargoyle's gaze tracks you as you walk away from the cogitator.{/n}
  - After: {n}The gargoyle watches you leave.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That data is gone. Deleted. Erased. Deliberately — but we cannot trace who did it or why."
  - After: "Deliberately erased, by whom we cannot tell."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A gift, but a terrible one. You would call it a weapon. Theodora coveted it. She needed it desperately... but we do not know why."
  - After: "A weapon. Theodora craved it; we know not why."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The truth was hidden. Deliberately. Your officers' memories were stolen. All the cogitators' memory banks were wiped. It took you feeding us the truth bit by bit for us to piece it together — and understand."
  - After: "Memories stolen, cogitators wiped. Your scraps revealed it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No, they are shells." {n}The rasping voice sounds adamant.{/n} "A human's existence is more than the existence of its shell — this is obvious to us. There is always something more. Something that simmers and shines, for which the dark light and wicked hunger are always reaching."
  - After: "No, shells." {n}Adamant.{/n} "But humans hold a light that dark hunger reaches for."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Nomos is silent for a long time, as though mulling over your words.{/n} "We do not know what we are. But the ship is not us. The ship is our cradle. We may rise from it, one day. We... would like that."
  - After: {n}Silence.{/n} "The ship is our cradle, not us. One day we may rise from it. We would like that."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It was not us he feared. He did not know us, but only suspected. His mental processes were occupied by the tech-blight. That was what he feared. He wanted protection from it."
  - After: "He feared the tech-blight, not us, and sought protection."
- **Asclepius**
  - Before: "Who has the resources, the knowledge, and the power to accomplish such a feat? It would have been beyond the capabilities of the blessed Amarnat himself. And he would never destroy knowledge."
  - After: "Who could? Not blessed Amarnat; he would never destroy knowledge."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes. Nomos remember. You brought us data-sustenance, and it contained a name — Epitaph. We recognised it. No, not like that. In that name we recognised the place where Nomos originate."
  - After: "Yes. Your data named Epitaph, our origin."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Incident marked the beginning of us. The ship became better because of us too. These are all links in the same chain, but we cannot piece them together yet..."
  - After: "The Incident began us; we bettered the ship. Unjoined links."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Human shells are subject to external influences. Perhaps someone purged their memory archives? Or perhaps they simply do not want to access them? It is a shame that no new information was obtained. But Nomos are grateful that you tried."
  - After: "Human memories can be purged. Still, thank you for trying."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To serve the light. To serve the Imperium..."
  - After: "To serve the light. The Imperium..."
- **Asclepius**
  - Before: "Blessed be this spirit. A great path and a great future lie before it. And we must assist it on its way."
  - After: "Blessed spirit! We must aid its great path."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The chorus of servitors dutifully repeats your words, but seemingly without understanding them. Nomos is preoccupied — the huge cogitator continues to sing its creaking song, running unknown calculations.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servitors echo you blankly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "He desired knowledge. Theodora allowed him to explore the gifts of Epitaph, slaking his thirst. But we know it did not bring him happiness. In the footprints of his slaked thirst, fear followed."
  - After: "He craved knowledge; Theodora let him study Epitaph's gifts. Fear followed."
- **Asclepius**
  - Before: "The blessed Amarnat was involved in the birth of the spirit named Nomos. I do not believe for a moment that he could have been frightened by this miracle."
  - After: "Amarnat helped birth Nomos. He could never fear it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Nomos suddenly falls silent. Symbols race chaotically across the screens of the huge cogitator, and you hear an almost human groan come from the depths of the machine.{/n} "Nomos... understand... realise... comprehend... themselves."
  - After: {n}The machine groans.{/n} "Nomos... understand... themselves."
- **Asclepius**
  - Before: "This story... disturbs me. It sounds like an echo of the sacrilege whose name is the preservation of ignorance. The spirit of Nomos must be protected from the encroachments of that power that tried to conceal the truth of its birth."
  - After: "Sacrilege: hoarded ignorance. Nomos must be shielded from whoever hid the truth."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Then, tell us. What is our purpose?"
  - After: "Then tell us our purpose."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We have been studying and observing. And helping the ship when we can. So many mechanisms... they would have suffered without our input."
  - After: "Studying, and helping the ship."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We explored our capabilities, sent a request, and the task was fulfilled. The Nomos are grateful to you for this."
  - After: "We sent a request; it was done. Thank you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We appreciate your answer. Your regard for the Nomos pleases us."
  - After: "Your regard pleases Nomos."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Are you dissatisfied? The Nomos seek no discord, and vow their requests will be more transparent from now on."
  - After: "Displeased? Our requests will be clearer."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionDialogues/Nomos/NomosMain

- **Player**
  - Before: "You will report this to Pasqal."
  - After: "Report this to Pasqal."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I saw a word among the lines of code: Nomos. What does it mean?"
  - After: "The code said 'Nomos'. What does it mean?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What was that just now?"
  - After: "What was that?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your incompetence is appalling! The Rogue Trader's cogitator is rebelling, and your so-called assistance is utterly worthless."
  - After: "Appalling! My cogitator rebels, and your help is worthless."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That is a mystery to me. If this mechanism truly is tainted, then... could it be?" {n}The Tech-Priest's mechadendrite jitters anxiously over the control panel.{/n} "If heresy truly has taken hold of this machine spirit and scorned the Omnissiah's every tenet, then the spirit's madness could be such that it has chosen a name for itself... but that is nothing more than my hypothesis."
  - After: "A mystery." {n}His mechadendrite jitters.{/n} "If heresy has maddened this machine spirit, it may have named itself. Only a hypothesis."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The imperfections of vox-transmission make the Tech-Priest's voice sound even more worried.{/n} "A catastrophic mistake... A heinous violation of the purity of the hallowed code. This mechanism... is touched by heresy, it is branded and tainted by it. Now the machine spirit produces code as before, and yet... Lord Captain, heed my plea: all operations on this machine must be halted until the Enginseer Prime has inspected it."
  - After: {n}The Tech-Priest sounds worried.{/n} "A catastrophe! This machine is tainted by heresy. Lord Captain, halt all work on it until the Enginseer Prime inspects it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest bows guiltily, and his mechanical voice becomes hollow and dejected.{/n} "My knowledge is insufficient to cleanse the code of this mechanism. I will inform the esteemed Enginseer Prime of this disturbing development — only he has the power to expel the heresy from this corrupted machine spirit."
  - After: {n}The Tech-Priest bows guiltily.{/n} "I cannot cleanse this code. I will tell the Enginseer Prime; only he can purge this heresy."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionDialogues/Nomos/NomosMain/NomosMain_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal has informed me that the system has encrypted data stored inside. I wish to know its contents."
  - After: "Pasqal says there's encrypted data. What is it?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am interested in the cache on Kiava Gamma."
  - After: "The cache on Kiava Gamma."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Restore the data on the cache located on Dargonus."
  - After: "Restore the Dargonus cache data."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Sensed my presence? How?"
  - After: "Sensed me? How?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Have the Tech-Priests of the Adeptus Mechanicus been able to discern how the ship was able to start her warp engine?"
  - After: "How did the ship start her warp engine?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Hand the Dargonus data-bank to the Tech-Priest] "Access the data from Dargonus."
  - After: [Hand the Dargonus data-bank to the Tech-Priest] "Access it."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Hand the Kiava Gamma data-bank to the Tech-Priest] "Access the data from Kiava Gamma."
  - After: [Hand the Kiava Gamma data-bank to the Tech-Priest] "Access it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Who are you and what is your purpose here?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: When {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} arrived at the scene, {mf|he|she} found the servitors in the same position that they assumed after they had been corralled into the bay: all standing in a long spiralling line and facing the centre of their strange formation. The moment {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} crossed the threshold of the bay gate, their bodies jerked into motion: all as one, as if obeying a command, the servitors turned to face the Lord Captain! The technomats tasked with overseeing the defective units even reached for their weapons, but then the servitors went still just as abruptly, staring at {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} with vacant eyes.
  - After: When {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} entered, the spiralled servitors all turned to face {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}! Technomats reached for weapons, but the servitors only stared at {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} as {mf|he|she} watched.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Enginseer Prime slowly waded into the motionless ranks of the servitors, peering into their faces and checking the readings. There was no haste in Pasqal's actions: with mesmerising diligence, he inspected every single unit in his path, and binharic prayers were his companions in this investigation.
  - After: The Enginseer Prime checked each servitor with binharic prayers.
- **(conversation owner)**

Region: [data unavailable]
Location: Von Valancius flagship, lower decks

Region: [data unavailable]

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Whatever the Lord Captain did, be it an incline of the head, a wave of a hand, or a step to the side, the defective units repeated it without a moment's delay or hesitation, like grotesque marionettes controlled by an unseen puppeteer. We observed this mime unfold in distressed bafflement for nearly a minute until the servitors finally came to a stop. Not sensing any threat from them, the Rogue Trader approached with confidence.
  - After: The units mimicked the Lord Captain like marionettes, then stopped. Unthreatened, the Rogue Trader approached.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: As High Factotum, it was I who had prompted that entire inspection, and thus it was my duty to follow the Lord Captain. As we stepped closer, we noticed a fascinating irregularity — the servitors' pupils, normally still, were shaking wildly. Their bulging veins were pulsating under their copper collars inscribed with their past offences. It was as if those mindless half-machines were locked in a perpetual state of extreme tension.
  - After: Following closely, I saw the servitors' pupils shake and veins pulse under their crime-collars.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: A visibly shaken technomat behind us proposed that the human souls had awakened within the servitors' bodies after a long slumber deep within their lobotomised brains. Formerly bereft of intelligence, they had attained awareness, feeling, and understanding.
  - After: A shaken technomat suggested their human souls had woken.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: After a pause, the technomat added that the servitors used to function properly and that no one had been able to explain the change in their behaviour. {mf|His|Her} gaze still trained on the motionless but animate half-machines and half-people, the Lord Captain...
  - After: {mf|His|Her} gaze on the servitors, the Lord Captain...
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The moment the blade sliced open the pale flesh, a wild howl washed over the cargo bay! We heard the screeching and crackling of servo-motors. As if having regained the ability to feel pain, the wounded servitor struggled to open its sewn mouth, but all it could muster was a stifled moan of horror. The Lord Captain's victim fell to the metal deck, and all the other servitors came crashing down with it. We all felt the grip of an otherworldly, bone-chilling cold.
  - After: The blade cut; a howl filled the bay! The servitor fell, and every other with it. An otherworldly cold gripped us.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: As I met the technomats' fearful gazes, I realised that none of those present had any explanation for what had just transpired.
  - After: The technomats' fearful eyes showed no one understood.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Enginseer Prime proceeded to the centre of the spiral of servitor bodies, stood over them grimly, studying their lifeless faces, and spoke thus: "This tech-phenomenon warranted comprehensive study. Further investigation has been rendered impossible." Perhaps it was a trick of my imagination, but I thought I caught a semblance of sorrow in his gaze in that moment.
  - After: The Enginseer Prime stood grimly over the bodies: "Further study is now impossible." He seemed sorrowful.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Lord Captain, seemingly not attaching any importance to the situation, sheathed the blade and left the cargo bay without a word.
  - After: Unconcerned, the Lord Captain sheathed the blade and left wordlessly.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: All present held their breath — disturbed by this sight, we waited for the Lord Captain to speak.
  - After: Disturbed, we awaited the Lord Captain's word.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The technomats' long-winded and detailed report could have been summarised in a single key point: despite the servitors' abnormal behaviour, they were still quite capable of carrying out tasks, and therefore the circumstances did not call for their termination.
  - After: The technomats reported: abnormal or not, the servitors could still work.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: As the Lord Captain walked between the servitors and looked at them closely, {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} could see their eyelids fluttering, their chests heaving with restless breaths, and their sewn lips trembling as they strained to produce any sound at all.
  - After: Up close, {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} saw eyelids flutter and sewn lips tremble, straining to speak.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The examination confirmed the technomats' initial hypothesis: the servitors' souls — or rather, the souls of the people they once were — had awakened. Not yet fully conscious of their past and present, these half-machines could nonetheless feel primitive emotions and sensations such as fear and pain. This undesirable consequence of shoddily performed lobotomy is most rarely observed, and yet, for some unknown reason, it had occurred in every single one of the servitors gathered in the bay.
  - After: It confirmed the guess: their old selves had woken, feeling fear and pain. A rare lobotomy flaw, yet it struck the whole bay.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Alas, the Lord Captain's inspection bore us no new knowledge. The servitors were showing strange, uncharacteristic signs of fear yet simply stood there, petrified, awaiting instructions.
  - After: Nothing new. The servitors showed fear, yet stood awaiting orders.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: A group of technomats hurried to act upon the Lord Captain's command. The servitor's mechanical parts separated with clicks, snaps, and hisses. The sutures between its wrinkled, pale flesh and its augments were laid disgustingly bare. We watched the technomats do their work and could see every centimetre of the servitor's stiff muscles abounding with valves and cavities pierced by countless cords and tubes.
  - After: The technomats dissected a servitor: sutures, valves, cords and tubes in pale flesh.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The disassembly and analysis complete, the technomats concurred: the unit was in working order. Nothing in the dissected body that lay before us could provide any insight into the reason behind the defects.
  - After: Verdict: working order. Nothing explained the defects.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: I should make note of one more thing: at that moment, all of us present discovered that not just the eyes, but the hands and heads of some of the servitors were now shaking too. It was as if the mechanised servants were overcome with some primordial terror.
  - After: Now some servitors shook, as if in primal terror.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship} looked at me with unwavering resolve, and it was that confidence that wrenched me out of the nightmarish stupor that had me tensely observing the scene unfolding before me.
  - After: {mf|His Lordship|Her Ladyship}'s resolute gaze snapped me from my stupor.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: The Lord Captain's command was executed post-haste: all defective units were incinerated in furnaces, and their remains were expelled into the void. The crew was provided with replacement servitors and soon forgot all about the destroyed units' peculiarities, yet this incident haunts my memories to this day.
  - After: The units were incinerated and spaced. The crew forgot; it haunts me still.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: On the Lord Captain's orders, the servitors were returned to the same decks where they had worked before. The crew was initially unnerved by their presence but adapted to their quirks soon enough, especially since, following the incident in question, there was a noticeable reduction in the servitors' strange behaviour.
  - After: The servitors returned to work; the strange behaviour lessened.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: With the fate of the defective servitors decided, nothing could now distract the Lord Captain from {mf|his|her} mission.
  - After: Settled, the Lord Captain returned to {mf|his|her} mission.
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: Immediately, the servitors — each and every one of them — stepped toward the Lord Captain in perfect unison. They mimicked {mf|his|her} movements with frightening precision. The Rogue Trader halted in place and, after a moment's thought, waved {mf|his|her} hand — and the servitors, just as synchronously, repeated that gesture as well. When the Lord Captain turned quizzically to the technomats, so did the servitors, as if mocking {mf|him|her}.
  - After: The servitors approached, copying {mf|his|her} every move and wave of {mf|his|her} hand, as if mocking {mf|him|her}.

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am afraid your life is too fleeting and your memory too feeble to encompass the entirety of my knowledge. My people ruled the stars when yours did not even have a name. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Different branches of the {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} chose different paths to salvation. We rescued countless wonders from the days before... but far from all.   - After: "My {g|Encyclopedia:Aeldari}Aeldari{/g} ancestors fled into the void on {g|Encyclopedia:Craftworld}craftworlds{/g}." {n}A pause.{/n} "Other branches chose darker paths. I will not speak of them."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It feels like I am in the belly of a bird with steel wings — cold and unliving, but stubbornly blazing through the dark. It lacks life with its light and beauty. We, the {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Asuryani{/g}, are born and dwell on craftworlds. To find myself on a moving world again, even one such as yours, is a source of much joy."
  - After: "Cold steel. No {g|Encyclopedia:Craftworld}craftworld{/g}, but we {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Asuryani{/g} are born on moving worlds. Being on one again brings me joy."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The first Path I walked was the Path of Awakening. It granted me the ability not merely to look but to see, and to take notice of what I saw." {n}She pauses.{/n} "My second Path could have been that of a Warrior, but I chose differently, for the ability to see called me beyond the boundaries of my homeworld.   - After: "My first Path, Awakening, taught me to see." {n}A pause.{/n} "So I chose the Outcast's Path over the Warrior's, free to doubt the Farseer. I will walk it to the end."
- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Crudarach cannot be described in your language.   - After: "Crudarach can only be sung, intricate as its {g|Encyclopedia:InfinityCircuit}Infinity Circuit{/g}. Artificial, yet alive."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But I must see clearly, not only light but also shadows. I yearn to remember only Crudarach's beauty, but it had a dark side, too. My world was isolated for too long. Like a lake of stagnant water, there was no movement or renewal, and even the sweetest outbursts of life soon turned fetid. Who knows..." {n}Yrliet sighs heavily.{/n} "Who knows, had there been no stagnation, had our elders not been so blind in their dogmatism and our youths not lacking in courage, then perhaps... Crudarach would still be alive even now?"
  - After: "But it stagnated in isolation." {n}She sighs.{/n} "Had our elders been wiser, might it live still?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is a mystery as inscrutable as the sigh of the last immortal, as deep as the waters of a dark ocean. And I can tell you little, for I was far away... on a mission with my unit. We returned at the appointed hour but we did not find Crudarach in its celestial harbour. It happened many journeys ago — or 'standard years,' as you say — but I remember that moment as if it happened this very day. The memory of a loss is always stronger than the memory of a gain, especially when you lose something as significant as a home. Or an entire world."
  - After: "I was away with my unit. We returned to find Crudarach gone. I remember it like today."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We searched, we called out, we looked everywhere, but we saw only emptiness and the echo of an echo of calamity. Countless days passed before I found myself on the Lilaethan and met some of my kin — those refugees who had barely managed to reach our ancestral planet. Their stories were far from being the fruit of truth I so badly craved. Those who agreed to talk to me were few — for most saw me as a wayward daughter who had spurned the honourable Paths — and they would not stop babbling about a terrible disease that spread black tendrils of pain over the paths of the {g|Encyclopedia:InfinityCircuit}Infinity Circuit{/g} and deadened our world one segment after another. The ones who survived fled in fear and wandered between the stars until the Lilaethan's warm light reach out to some of them."
  - After: "We found only emptiness. Later, on the Lilaethan, a few refugee kin told of a black disease that spread through the {g|Encyclopedia:InfinityCircuit}Infinity Circuit{/g}, killing our world piece by piece. Survivors fled."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That mon-keigh Achilleas... There was something wrong about him. He kept disappearing at night, so one day I followed him. Which meant my only chance to discover the fate of my homeworld was about to slip through my fingers. I could not wait any longer. I killed Achilleas, took the artefact, and demanded answers from Marazhai. He hinted at where I could go to look for the truth. You know what happened next."
  - After: "I followed Achilleas at night and saw him take Marazhai's orders through an artefact. His betrayal would cost my chance to learn Crudarach's fate. So I killed him, took the artefact and questioned Marazhai. You know the rest."

  - Before: {n}No matter how hard you try to get Yrliet's attention, there is no change in her posture, facial expression, or barely-there breathing. The only movement comes from her narrow fingers fluidly moving from one strange gesture to another.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nothing. Only her fingers move.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You needn't have been, elantach, for I can take care of myself. However, judging by your expression, my meditation has distressed you — but only due to your ignorance."
  - After: "No need, elantach. You were only distressed by ignorance."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "My meditation... is immersion — immersion into myself, my inner world. It is my chance to speak to myself, but without words. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "What? No, I do not think so. But then again..." {n}Yrliet tilts her head and sceptically examines you from head to toe.{/n} "Perhaps you, elantach, might have the inner strength to do so, but meditation requires long practice sessions, restraint, and self-discipline.   - Before: "Our ships never venture beyond the veil. And I... I never travelled the way you do, {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}.   - After: "Our ships never pass the veil, {g|Encyclopedia:MonKeigh}mon-keigh{/g}." {n}Guiltily:{/n} "I faltered; She Who Thirsts noticed. Meditation hid me. I will steel my heart against Sai'lanthresh."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If I could have, do you think I would have abided your irrational behaviour?"
  - After: "Had I been able, would I have endured your antics?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Words dripping with venom. Could I have expected anything else from a mon-keigh?" {n}Yrliet gives you a long, cutting look.{/n}
  - After: "Venom. What else from a mon-keigh?" {n}A cutting look.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In your language, this state can also be conveyed with the word 'meditation.' It is what allows me to maintain a balance between the outer world and my inner world, and it guards my soul against burdens and corruption."
  - After: "'Meditation,' to you. It balances my worlds and guards my soul from corruption."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Immersion requires concentration and unity of mind, body, and spirit. Entering this state unprepared — or coming out of it suddenly — can be harmful."
  - After: "Immersion needs focus. Breaking it suddenly can harm."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet remains unmoving the entire time that you watch her, and only the barest flicker of her eyes beneath her closed lids lets you know that she is still alive, at least.{/n}
  - After: {n}Yrliet stays still; only her eyelids flicker.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You are still here, elantach." {n}Yrliet's words do not sound like a question or an expression of surprise. Her eyes quickly sweep over you and she nods in greeting.{/n}
  - After: "You are still here, elantach." {n}A nod.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You think you see the shadow of a smile flit across Yrliet's austere face.{/n} "Almost as soon as you decided to join me. Do not worry, your heavy breathing did not disturb my immersion."

  - Before: {n}The moment you raise your hand, Yrliet twists out of your reach in a lightning-fast motion.{/n} "Kae-morag, mon-keigh! What do you think you are doing?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Hardly!" {n}Yrliet presses her lips together in anger, then takes a deep breath, exhales, inhales again — and coldness replaces the irritation in her gaze.{/n} "Meditating in the presence of mon-keigh was unwise — your reaction only confirms it."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I refuse to offer any apology. You will have to content yourself with the knowledge that you will never see me in that state again. Now tell me why you have come."
  - After: "No apology. You will never see me so again. Why are you here?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am disappointed by your lack of restraint, I will admit. Every day you become more primitive, more like other mon-keigh. Do not allow your bestial nature to win out — I can see that there is more to you than that."
  - After: "Your lack of restraint disappoints me. Do not let the beast win — you are more than that."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Restraint is not a trait that your kind is known for... and yet you did not interrupt my immersion, elantach. A worthy act. I will... remember this." {n}Yrliet nods to you — curtly, but gratefully.{/n}
  - After: "Yet you did not interrupt me. I will remember this." {n}A grateful nod.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "{name}." {n}The normally unflappable Yrliet is frozen in indecision.{/n} "I promised that I would no longer hide my worries behind an icy wall of pride and doubt. And so I want to explain myself. But... are you willing to hear me out?"
  - After: "{name}." {n}Yrliet hesitates.{/n} "I promised to stop hiding behind pride. Will you hear me?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet gives a short nod.{/n} "Not here. The words of my truth... are intended only for your ears, elantach."
  - After: {n}A nod.{/n} "Not here. Only for your ears, elantach."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet lapses into a pensive silence for a time.{/n} "Sharing experiences of mind and spirit, trying to understand each other, is truly not the Path that you and I are destined to take.   - After: {n}Silence.{/n} "You still see me as alien. I cannot blame you, elantach. I accept your answer."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I would welcome that, {name}. Which world's unknowable depths will we visit this time — yours or mine?"
  - After: "Gladly, {name}. Your depths or mine?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Sharing silence and exploring new depths of your world together? I agree, {name}. For my soul, too, yearns for knowledge and rest."
  - After: "Agreed, {name}. My soul, too, yearns for rest."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A slight smile touches her thin lips.{/n} "I have you figured out, {name}. I knew you would say that."
  - After: {n}A slight smile.{/n} "I knew you would say that, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet lets out a quiet chuckle and brushes a fiery lock away from her face.{/n} "Indeed? I thought I had learned all there was to know about you, {name}, but you are still full of surprises."
  - After: {n}A quiet chuckle.{/n} "You still surprise me, {name}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Outcasts my Path led me to had a saying... Let me translate it for you: 'If you fall off a cliff, grab the roots and do not ask if they belong to a weed or a noble rose bush.'" {n}For a second, Yrliet's expression changes, she almost grins before continuing in earnest,{/n} "You are the root I grabbed, elantach. By joining forces with you, I may be able to nurture a seedling of the truth I so deeply yearn for."
  - After: "Outcasts say: 'Falling, grab any root.'" {n}Almost a grin.{/n} "You are my root, elantach. My home and kin are lost; with you I may find the truth."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You and I, elantach, look at this world in very different ways. And I see many more facets, and deeper meanings, and brighter colours in it... But to capture the full truth of this world in the miserly language familiar to your ears will take time. I will come to you with an answer later."
  - After: "We see this world differently, elantach. Your tongue needs time. I will answer later."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet looks at you in slight surprise, then cautiously replies,{/n} "{name}... Our species are too different from one another. What touches our souls is unlikely to make a significant impression on your kind. Just as I find your concept of offering material gifts to be clumsy and primitive."
  - After: {n}Cautiously:{/n} "{name}... we are too different. Material gifts seem primitive to me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet's eyes track down your neck, staring blankly.{/n} "How great is the gulf between us. I once strove to escape the bonds and shackles of my craftworld. You, however, readily allowed a Dark One to leave his mark on you — not only in your soul, but on your body as well."
  - After: {n}Yrliet stares at your neck.{/n} "I fled my craftworld's shackles; you let a Dark One mark your soul — and body."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I tried to learn to trust you, elantach. Whatever your motives, you did not turn away from me, and you helped me search for my kin. But despair ate at me from within. The human journeys through the realm of She Who Thirsts left my soul drained, and our attempts to save the children of Crudarach crumbled to nothing in the unending coldness of the dark cosmos. And even when I beheld a piece of Crudarach in your chambers, I wanted to believe you had nothing to do with it. I wanted to, but... I succumbed to emotion. To fear. To hopelessness. To grief. I was afraid that Sai'lanthresh would find me before I found the truth."
  - After: "I tried to trust you, elantach. But the warp drained me, Crudarach's children were lost, and seeing Crudarach's relic in your chambers, I gave in to fear. I feared Sai'lanthresh would find me first."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet replies with a brief nod of understanding.{/n} "Nor I you. To repair the fragile shards of what was... One must plunge into the deep waters of fear. I will reciprocate by making the second."
  - After: {n}A nod.{/n} "Nor I you. You took the first step, elantach. I will take the second."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Elantach." {n}Yrliet leans over you slightly and takes a long — an unusually long — look into your eyes. She nods slowly. And draws back.{/n} "I see you have decided to {d|Encyclopedia:MiniJealousyRomanceBroken}bind your fate{/d} to another soul. I... understand your choice. It is natural.   - After: "Elantach." {n}A long look; she draws back.{/n} "You have {d|Encyclopedia:MiniJealousyRomanceBroken}bound your fate{/d} to another. I accept it." {n}She folds her arms.{/n} "Anything else?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Under the watchful eye of my kin, the Lilaethan could have regained her freedom, perhaps even awoken from her centuries of slumber. Could have... but now {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusEldarEliminated}we will never know{/d}." {n}Yrliet's thin brows quiver slightly, and she turns away.{/n}
  - After: "With my kin, the Lilaethan might have woken. Now {d|Encyclopedia:Ch2_JanusEldarEliminated}we will never know{/d}." {n}She turns away.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Abelard winces as though from toothache and he makes no attempt to hide his feelings.{/n} "You know, Lord Captain, I am no admirer of fine art, but when we next find ourselves in a civilised port with time to spare, I will promptly find an artist and commission a portrait of the individual to whom you refer — with a hole between the eyes.   - After: {n}Abelard winces.{/n} "I'd commission his portrait — with a hole between the eyes. Letting Kunrad Voigtvir escape was unforgivable."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Abelard frowns for a moment, then continues,{/n} "We both served Lord Captain Theodora for many years and we never saw eye to eye. He was... brash. I am loath to admit it, but... the von Valancius protectorate continues to reap the fruits of his labours to this day. His service always garnered my respect.   - After: {n}He frowns.{/n} "We served Theodora together and never got along. Brash, but he took on hard tasks, and the protectorate still reaps them. Otherwise — a two-faced snake."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I used to be an officer in the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperialNavy}Navis Imperialis{/g}," {n}Abelard replies proudly.{/n} "No, 'used to be' is not quite right.   - After: "An officer of the {g|Encyclopedia:ImperialNavy}Navis Imperialis{/g}," {n}proudly.{/n} "My calling. At heart, I still am."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Until recently, the Koronus Expanse could hardly have been called a region of the Imperium. The situation has changed with the arrival of the {g|Encyclopedia:Inquisition}Lord Inquisitor{/g}, but not by much. This place operates under its own rules, you see — more radical, so to speak, but ones that allow for a non-standard approach where there is a promise of victory. The Koronus Expanse is considered Rogue Trader territory for a reason. Only Rogue Traders have sufficient military might, audacity, and the rights granted them by the {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} to survive the leap into the unexplored part of the Expanse... and in the event of a successful outcome, to hold onto whatever they manage to capture on the frontier."
  - After: "Even since the {g|Encyclopedia:Inquisition}Lord Inquisitor{/g} came, the Expanse keeps its own rules. It's Rogue Trader territory: only they have the might and {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} to push into the frontier and hold what they take."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In the first instance, you should treat official representatives of the Imperium with respect — the Expanse may be on the fringes, but it still numbers among the territories of the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g}. The arrival of the {g|Encyclopedia:Inquisition}Lord Inquisitor{/g} has turned the Koronus Expanse into a less wild and uncontrolled region... to the regret of some individuals who had grown inured to the local lawlessness."
  - After: "Respect Imperial officials — this is still {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g} territory. The {g|Encyclopedia:Inquisition}Lord Inquisitor{/g} has tamed it somewhat."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If we are to speak of 'unclaimed' territory, which is what {g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g} is... among the scum that dwells on that handful of asteroids, there are three factions that wield considerable influence in the sector. The first is the {g|Encyclopedia:KasballicaMission}Kasballica Mission{/g} — organised crime in its most primitive form, it holds sway over the Liege of Footfall and has links to Rogue Trader Winterscale. The second faction is an offshoot of our shining Ecclesiarchy, {g|Encyclopedia:Drusians}followers{/g} of Saint Drusus. They are actively building their forces, and hold influence over Rogue Trader Chorda. And, finally, the third faction — the Explorators, a wing of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g}. They are willing to die and kill for the secrets of the ancient technological heresies that are hidden among the stars of the Koronus Expanse."
  - After: "{g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g} has three powers. The {g|Encyclopedia:KasballicaMission}Kasballica Mission{/g}: crime, ruling the Liege, tied to Winterscale. The {g|Encyclopedia:Drusians}followers{/g} of Saint Drusus: arming, tied to Chorda. And the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} Explorators, who kill for ancient tech-heresies."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It was a difficult choice for me. But I saw in the offer a chance to serve the interests of Humanity even more effectively than in the Navis Imperialis. You do not need me to tell you just how remarkable a person Lord Captain Theodora was. I recognised her at once as a true leader and formidable creative force, one who had built a protectorate amidst the dangers and wildness of the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Expanse{/g}."
  - After: "Hard choice, but I could serve Humanity better. Theodora was a true leader who built a protectorate in the wild {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Expanse{/g}."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Savour the anticipation, shereen. Wait, and do not lose confidence."
  - After: "Savour the anticipation, shereen."

  - After: "Heretics targeted this ship, so I'll help you. Someday {g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g}'s reliquary calls me back; for now I'm with the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}."

  - Before: "On one of the recently discovered planets in the {g|Encyclopedia:KoronusExpanse}Expanse{/g}. No one suspected that it had already been tainted by the filth of heresy. Had I known it beforehand — of course I would have been on my guard."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The One Star, the bright star, the silver star shone in the sky. And when the orphan smiled at it — the One Star fell right into her hands.   - After: "She smiled at the One Star, and it fell into her hands. The faithful followed it to salvation."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Those are... very courteous words, Rogue Trader. Thank you — both for your words and your hospitality." {n}She gives you another, somewhat puzzled look.{/n}
  - After: "Courteous words, Rogue Trader. Thank you." {n}She looks puzzled.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

She hesitates, but then shakes her head with a sigh.{/n} "The path to that planet was lost, all the knowledge is gone along with the previous {g|Encyclopedia:Navigator}Navigator{/g}. - **(conversation owner)**

  - After: "But Idira Tlass has no place among the faithful." {n}She frowns.{/n} "Still, we survived. May tomorrow be bright!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "After that she travelled between worlds gripped by turmoil on her ship marked with a silver star and brought hope to the faithful. Numerous accounts confirm this. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And we seek out the relics that have been lost. Neither a coven of heretics nor the most wicked death world can deter Sisters Pronatus when their goal is to return a piece of the great legacy of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g} into the hands of the faithful."
  - After: "We also recover lost relics for the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}. Nothing stops us."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Argenta gives you a stern look, but says nothing, only nodding impassively.{/n}
  - After: {n}A stern look, a nod.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Her eyes flare as she crosses her arms.{/n} "If such is the Lord Captain's will..."
  - After: {n}She crosses her arms.{/n} "If such is the Lord Captain's will..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Argenta glares at you for a while, then gives you a reserved nod.{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta glares, then nods.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes. I'm ready! I would ask only one thing of you, {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}. A difficult conversation lies ahead of us... and I wish to pray by the relic before I lay my soul bare."
  - After: "Ready! But first, {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}, let me pray at the {g|Encyclopedia:Warrant}Warrant{/g} the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g} touched."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Well... then I will be patient, Rogue Trader, and wait."
  - After: "Then I'll wait, Rogue Trader."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "'Become'... It's such a strange word for it. It seems right, but is that how one talks about their destiny? If you're asking about the path itself — that's easy enough to answer.   - After: "'Become'? It was destiny. Like many orphans, I endured the {g|Encyclopedia:ScholaProgenium}Schola Progenium{/g}. Hard, fond years."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I was one of the best among my peers. And I was selected for the novitiate in the ranks of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptaSororitas}Adepta Sororitas{/g}. When the hour came, I passed the trials and took my vows. The most joyous day of my life! The {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g}'s light has always been with me, but to accept it with all your heart, to utter the oaths — that is a rapture like no other."
  - After: "I excelled, joined the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptaSororitas}Adepta Sororitas{/g} novitiate, and took my vows. My happiest day, in the {g|Encyclopedia:Emperor}Emperor{/g}'s light."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "During the last journey, Seneschal Werserian stood out for me — he came by several times to ask about my health. He's an honourable man and a loyal servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}.   - After: "Seneschal Werserian, loyal to the {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g}, often checked on this {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptaSororitas}Sister of Battle{/g}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "None that I'm aware of, but the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptaSororitas}Sisterhood{/g}'s orders are many and can operate independently of one another, sending their sisters wherever their presence is needed as deemed by the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorum}Ecclesiarchy{/g}. Perhaps somewhere in the {g|Encyclopedia:Inquisition}Lord Inquisitor{/g}'s retinue, may his path be blessed, my sisters perform their duty as we speak? I wish it were so — even a single evening spent in joint prayer and training would bring me joy!"
  - After: "None I know of; the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptaSororitas}Sisterhood{/g} goes where the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorum}Ecclesiarchy{/g} sends. Maybe some serve the {g|Encyclopedia:Inquisition}Lord Inquisitor{/g}?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have made no attempt to do so! What need do I have to know of the depravity of the enemies of Humanity, when all I want is to burn it all in pure, raging flame? I already know all I need to — this place is evil, but there are servants of the Emperor here worthy of salvation."
  - After: "No! I don't study depravity, I burn it. Some here are worth saving."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We would find a way out if we joined forces with a comrade in faith, and not a repulsive monster! But now the Commissar is dead, and we are on our own."
  - After: "A monster, not a comrade in faith! Now the Commissar's dead; we're alone."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We do. And I swear to fight for that end and not to lose hope, even... even when deceit, corruption, and treachery surround us on all sides!"
  - After: "We do. I'll keep fighting, whatever treachery surrounds us!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "May Terra's light be with you, Rogue Trader!"
  - After: "Terra's light be with you, Rogue Trader!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Following you into the flames of battle will grant me a chance of purification. And that is all I want, it is all I think about. A righteous death and peace thereafter, should He choose to grant it to His unworthy daughter."
  - After: "Battle at your side may purify me. I want only a righteous death, and peace."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Argenta's face is as white as a sheet and her eyes are half-closed. Her lips tremble slightly as she whispers a prayer. She seems to be oblivious to the world around her.{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta, pale, whispers a prayer, oblivious.{/n}

  - After: {n}Argenta glows.{/n} "Greetings, Rogue Trader!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "More than ever, Rogue Trader! My place is on the field of righteous battle at the side of the Emperor's chosen, the one who helped me reach my journey's end and obtain the holy relic! Lead, and I will follow."
  - After: "More than ever! You helped me find the holy relic. Lead, and I follow."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Today I do. But I cannot promise to always be at your side. There is so much evil, hidden and overt, so much corruption and vileness lurking in every corner! Whereas my road is a straight line that leads inexorably to a single goal."
  - After: "Today, yes. But I yearn to purge evil everywhere." {n}Her eyes burn.{/n} "Your cares are trivial, Rogue Trader. My road has one goal."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The order sent me to {g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g}. My undertaking was to assist the local priesthood of {g|Encyclopedia:Drusians}Drusians{/g} in caring for a sacred reliquary that had been there since the time of Parsimus Dewain, the station's founder."
  - After: "I was sent to {g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g} to help the {g|Encyclopedia:Drusians}Drusians{/g} guard the reliquary of founder Parsimus Dewain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Of course!" {n}Argenta heaves an agitated sigh.{/n} "Do you remember the first days of the attack, when we captured one of the heretic commanders?   - After: "Of course!" {n}She sighs.{/n} "Remember the heretic commander we captured and burned? Before execution, he talked."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The heretic was one of Kunrad Voigtvir's closest henchmen.   - After: "He was Kunrad Voigtvir's henchman. Screaming, he gave up the route to Salis Prime! The Final Dawn failed."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I indeed have a request, Rogue Trader."
  - After: "I do, Rogue Trader."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If you want to do her good, give her a dose of conscience and fear of the Emperor — that is what she truly needs. But if you want to please her... give her some meaningless jewellery, expensive and shiny. Such baubles wield magical power over hearts like hers."
  - After: "She needs conscience and fear of the Emperor. She wants shiny baubles."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Should any more arise — keeping them to yourself would be imprudent! It is a virtue to take an interest in holiness."
  - After: "Ask if more arise. That's a virtue."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Rogue Trader!" {n}Argenta's eyes burn with the incinerating flames of affronted faith.{/n} "Filth and heresy have come aboard this voidship as if in mockery of the righteous! Your deed brooks no explanation or forgiveness — know this!"
  - After: "Rogue Trader!" {n}Argenta seethes.{/n} "An Archenemy monster aboard! You think you control it, but it poisons you. Unforgivable!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "May He guard our hearts against foul passions and weakness of spirit..." {n}Argenta whispers to herself, her eyes locked on the mark on your neck.{/n}
  - After: "May He guard our hearts..." {n}She stares at your neck's mark.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Yes. That was the beginning of her hagiography. It is known that she lived on a world where heretics staged a terrible insurrection. They wiped out all life on the planet — except those whom Saint Argenta managed to save with the One Star. And with the strength of her faith."
  - After: "Yes. Heretics razed her world; she saved the few she could with the One Star."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Her eyes gleam.{/n} "I feel that my undertaking will be fulfilled when I find the answer that has eluded the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorum}Ecclesiarchy{/g} for millennia! I pray we find the way to Salis Prime soon... The Ruinous Powers must be aligned against us. They stand in the way of faith."
  - After: {n}Her eyes gleam.{/n} "I'll solve what eluded the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMinistorum}Ecclesiarchy{/g}, Ruinous Powers be damned!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "To find the way to the planet called Salis Prime. Saint Argenta is my patroness, and that is where her fallen ship is. And it must also be the resting place of her great relic — the One Star."
  - After: "Reach Salis Prime, where Saint Argenta's ship fell with the One Star."

  - After: {n}His eyes hold the haze of {d|Encyclopedia:CompUlfar_Wulfen}creeping madness{/d}. He growls:{/n} "Aett-Vater. Good that you live."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Something has changed in Ulfar, as though a burden that has weighed on him ever since your first meeting is finally gone. There is a serenity in his harsh features that there never was before. He bows before you with respect.{/n} "Aett-Vater, it is good to see you. I swear that {d|Encyclopedia:CompUlfar_Pack}your name will not be forgotten{/d} when I return to Fenris and sing my saga."
  - After: {n}Ulfar seems serene. He bows.{/n} "I swear {d|Encyclopedia:CompUlfar_Pack}your name will not be forgotten{/d} in my saga."

  - Before: {n}Something has changed in Ulfar. His features have become starker, sharper, and the merry glint in his eyes has lost its sincerity. He is grimmer now, and his skjald's voice has gained a funereal hoarseness.{/n} "Aett-Vater, witness to {d|Encyclopedia:CompUlfar_Lone}my oath{/d}, I greet you with honour."

  - Before: {n}Though it wields immense power, when it comes to the Astartes, even the Inquisition chooses to make requests rather than commands. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This is the name given on Fenris to a pack-father. A commander or captain. An aett-vater answers to a jarl — the commander of a Great Company. Since you are the one who commands your crew and I follow you at present, I am granting you the honoured title of Aett-Vater."
  - After: "A pack-father, a captain under a jarl. You command, I follow."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We call ourselves the Baleful Howl, and our sign is known to all Wolves." {n}Ulfar proudly points at his shoulder pad, which is emblazoned with a crude depiction of black fangs.{/n} "We are old Wolves who have seen much and endured much." {n}A shadow of disquiet dampens the warrior's boastful exuberance.{/n}
  - After: "We are the Baleful Howl." {n}He taps black fangs on his pauldron.{/n} "Old Wolves." {n}His pride dims.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Before becoming an Astartes, I dreamed of becoming a skjald, a keeper of stories. At feasts I often sing of my brothers' exploits. Thousands are stored in my memory. One of the Tech-Priests theorised that our songs contained hidden psychometric codes to increase courage. Maybe there is such a thing in other places.   - After: "I dreamed of being a skjald. Wolves fight harder knowing I'll sing their deeds."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Allfather gifted you with strong intuition. This was made by Skyaddi Twice-Thinker. The spirits liked him, and one could feast a whole long Helwinter night to the words of his saga, so keen was his mind.   - After: "Skyaddi Twice-Thinker made it. A great saga-teller. My friend." {n}Ulfar's face darkens.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Every morning I made entreaties to the Allfather, and every night I appealed to Russ. I trained my body, read the litanies, and in the darkest moments, I recited my own saga.   - After: "I prayed, trained, recited my saga. So I survived." {n}He turns away.{/n} "I always survive."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Or is he as enormous as the Sun Wolf, which rises to hunt every morning and fills our world with light? The Allfather is not a god, but the highest of Humanity. Ordinary humans struggle to grasp this, but we, his warriors and offspring, remember the truth."
  - After: "Or vast as the Sun Wolf? No. Not a god, but the highest of Humanity."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "These are dark days you are asking about, Aett-Vater." {n}Ulfar lets out a rumbling sigh, draws out the rune-covered knife that you saw him carry in the Dark City, and begins to spin it between his fingers, finding his equilibrium again.{/n} "Let my keen-edged friend be a witness to the veracity of my words."
  - After: "Dark days." {n}Ulfar spins his rune-knife.{/n} "Let my blade witness my truth."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Koronus Expanse is a wild hunting ground teeming with prey. And the Space Wolves will be the first to turn its snows scarlet!   - After: "The Expanse is rich prey. Two rival packs would chase glory hardest."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thank you. Their stories will not be forgotten, but will live on in the Chapter's legends. We wolves do not fully die — we leave to hunt in Kjalhalla, and one day we will return to this world for the final battle. Glorious will be the day when we brothers are reunited!"
  - After: "Thank you. Wolves hunt in Kjalhalla until the final battle reunites us!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar sadly shakes his head.{/n} "The pack is no more. I could become a Lone Wolf, an avenger of the fallen, but my heart yearns for something else.   - After: {n}Ulfar shakes his head.{/n} "The pack is gone. After this, I'll accept Thorbald Ironhide's offer and join the Stormbiters. My duty isn't done."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar's rumbling voice seems to reverberate in your very bones.{/n} "Our fearless Wolf King is Leman Russ, son of the Allfather.   - After: {n}His voice rumbles.{/n} "Sons of Leman Russ, of Fenris and the Fang. The thunder of battle!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The giant's gaze thaws.{/n} "Fenris is home. A harsh land of harsh winters and harsh people.   - After: {n}His gaze thaws.{/n} "Home. Harsh winters, harsh people, sea-beasts and frost."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar demurs, but a satisfied smile plays on his lips.{/n} "It is true that I am capable of commanding you and your people! But as a warrior of the Allfather, it is too easy for me to forget the limits of ordinary people."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Be worthy of it. And see that you do not disgrace this glorious rank."
  - After: "Be worthy of it. Don't disgrace it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Wolf's smile is full of condescension.{/n} "Your credentials are unknown to me, but none of them bestows greater honour than the one I have given you."
  - After: {n}He smiles condescendingly.{/n} "No title of yours outranks mine."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "More than words stringing,
A secret weaving,
Magic in its marrow,

and the heart hearkens."

and the heart hearkens."

  - Before: {n}Ulfar glowers and growls menacingly, and something primitive and ancient inside your brain descends into hysterical terror.{/n} "Our traditions are steeped in centuries of blood-soaked glory.   - After: {n}Ulfar growls; primal terror grips you.{/n} "Not yours to judge, human. Shut up and be worthy!"
