  - Before: {n}Ulfar responds with an equally firm nod full of meaning.{/n}
  - After: {n}Ulfar nods back firmly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Believe what you wish, Aett-Vater. The Allfather never wanted us to revere him as a god, but we are not ordinary men. I do not know what his intentions were for the rest of you."
  - After: "Believe what you wish. He never wanted our worship."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It makes his deeds all the more glorious. Battling gods is child's play when you yourself are a god. But if you are a man — now that is the stuff that sagas are made of."
  - After: "All the more glorious. A man fighting gods makes sagas."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I could not have done it without you, Aett-Vater. Know that, now and always, you will have friends on Fenris."
  - After: "Not without you. You'll always have friends on Fenris."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is difficult for non-Fenrisians to grasp our wisdom. It comes along with the cold and death."
  - After: "Our wisdom comes with cold and death."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The curse is strong, there is no doubt about that, but my spirit is stronger than a Doppelgrendel. I overcame one in combat, so can I not overcome its magic? No, one day I will find a glorious death on the field of battle!"
  - After: "My spirit beat the Doppelgrendel; it'll beat its curse. I'll die gloriously!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Should you hear a howl of triumph in the night, know that I am on the path of retribution."
  - After: "Hear a howl at night? I hunt for vengeance."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Wolf maintains his own mournful silence.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Wolf mourns silently.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You receive a wolfish grin in response.{/n} "Insightful. We'd had no dealings with this Calcazar before this and we did not trust him. Two packs meant twice as many eyes to watch out for his games and schemes. And then..."
  - After: {n}A wolfish grin.{/n} "We didn't trust Calcazar. Two packs, twice the eyes. And then..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It is strong, but I am not weak. Before, I survived because my duty to my brothers compelled me — to shrug off any wound, to rejoin the fight, to defend, to protect... Now that duty is gone and nothing is holding me here."
  - After: "I survived for my brothers. Now nothing holds me here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Fight, Aett-Vater. I will seek honourable combat and vanquish the Allfather's enemies until the day there is none worthy of defeating me. The name of the Baleful Howl will sail like a drekkar along the rivers of unholy blood that I will spill. Blackmane is no longer my patron — from this day I tread the paths of Lokyar, the Lone Wolf."
  - After: "Fight, till none can best me. I am Lokyar now, the Lone Wolf of the Baleful Howl."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The joy in my heart is dead, Aett-Vater. I feel only rage... But that is a lie. In truth, I feel nothing at all anymore. I simply wish to tear someone asunder. Soon, that feeling will be all that is left inside me, and then even it will fade. And I will be hollow."
  - After: "My joy is dead. Only the urge to kill remains, and soon I'll be hollow."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I no longer want to deceive myself with false hope. Each of us has our own fate. For some, it is an easy one; for others, one full of sorrow. Mine is of the second kind, I think. To be ever lost has been my fate from birth, but only now have I found the nerve to accept that path."
  - After: "No more false hope. My fate is to be ever lost. I accept it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "That arrogant chief thought he could give us orders, but we Wolves have always followed our own instincts and hunted in our own way." {n}The red-haired Space Wolf chuckles smugly.{/n} "I wager that boiled his blood."
  - After: "That chief tried to command Wolves." {n}Ulfar chuckles.{/n} "It boiled his blood."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar says with grim curtness,{/n} "They fell. With honour."
  - After: {n}Ulfar, grimly:{/n} "They fell. With honour."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your counsel, Aett-Vater. It is what gave me strength."
  - After: "Your counsel, Aett-Vater."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I have slain many xenos and feasted on their flesh. My captors have watched me do it, and taken glee in it, while I have been gathering information and planning my escape."
  - After: "I ate xenos while my captors gloated, and planned my escape."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Like a spirit of wyrd itself, you showed me my path, Aett-Vater, while my eyes were still closed to it."
  - After: "Like a wyrd-spirit, you showed me my path."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Every crack was small, but together they shattered the bastion of hopes living within me."
  - After: "Small cracks shattered my hopes."
- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The massive {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} grows out of the metal bulkheads like a grotesque tumour. A hollow roar sounds from deep within the metal housing — whatever spurred the computer into action, it has enough power to supply a small command centre. As soon as your eyes fall upon the cogitator, you feel a tingling in your temples: every nook, every component of the machine radiates a sense of wrongness — one that is difficult to explain but no less palpable for that. It is as though the construct itself defies the laws of physics and perspective.{/n}
  - After: {n}A huge {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} grows from the bulkheads like a tumour, roaring. Every part of it feels wrong.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix makes a warning gesture. His voice, ringing slightly with tension, is threaded with disquiet.{/n} "Stop, {name}. That is a creation of the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Archenemy{/g}, don't go near it. You have done enough for me and my mission — don't put yourself at risk now."
  - After: {n}Heinrix gestures.{/n} "Stop, {name}. It's the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Archenemy{/g}'s work. Don't risk yourself."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}As soon as Heinrix takes another step toward the cogitator, it emits a deafening shriek like hundreds of metal needles driving into toughened glass, as though sensing the stranger. Wincing, Heinrix approaches the control panel and bends down toward the screens. Despite the heat clogging the room, you feel an ice-cold breeze — Heinrix is clearly using his {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g} abilities to try to fend off the pernicious effects of the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} artefact.{/n}
  - After: {n}The cogitator shrieks as Heinrix nears the screens; an icy chill shows his {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g} power warding off the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} artefact.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You study the runes carefully — and suddenly you feel a lancing pain in your eyes, followed by a sharp pang in your chest. You leap away from the cogitator, with your heart pounding and a rushing in your ears.{/n}
  - After: {n}The runes stab pain through you. You leap back.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest raises his uncomprehending gaze to Jae.{/n} "Squeamishness is not a relevant factor. I have conducted the relevant assessments: the risk of spiritual harm is acceptable; the importance of obtaining the information is critical."
  - After: {n}Pasqal looks at Jae blankly.{/n} "Spiritual risk: acceptable. Information: critical."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "You cannot understand this, xenos. Knowing one's enemy is the path toward destroying them. If, in order to prevent countless future calamities, I must perpetrate one of my own... such is my duty to the Golden Throne."
  - After: "Know the enemy to destroy them, xenos. One calamity to prevent many is my duty."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet remains silent for a while, her head tilted to one side.{/n} "Not only do you not keep watch over your kin, you even sacrifice your own souls to your dead god. It is astounding."
  - After: {n}Yrliet tilts her head.{/n} "You sacrifice your souls to your dead god. Astounding."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You take a step backward — and suddenly one of the cogitator screens changes colour, becoming a bright yellow. Your eyes are helplessly drawn to the bilious hue...{/n}
  - After: {n}A screen turns bilious yellow, drawing your eyes...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cogitator displays a wall of text on its screens. The string of symbols is a senseless mixture of numbers, formulas, and unfamiliar characters. There seems to be no logic to it — and yet there is no doubt that the cogitator is computing calculations on a prodigious scale.{/n}
  - After: {n}Senseless symbols fill the screens, yet it is clearly calculating vastly.{/n}

  - Before: {n}One glance is enough to tell you that these are {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} runes, within which lurks a grim threat to mind and soul. You hastily avert your eyes, trying to wipe the foul symbols from your mind.{/n}
  - After: {n}{g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} runes. You look away fast.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A bundle of cables is coming from the broken side panel of the cogitator — they were clearly added after the machine came off the manufactorum's production line. The wires snake along the floor and disappear inside a maintenance hatch that leads to somewhere down below.{/n}
  - After: {n}Added cables run into a hatch to the levels below.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You turn sharply away from the screen — and you can almost feel invisible shackles falling away. The realisation comes a moment later: you were not fighting against your own curiosity, but against someone's malevolent will, which has now lost its hold on you.{/n}
  - After: {n}You wrench away, breaking a malevolent will's grip.{/n}

Staggering back, you can still feel the touch of that icy hand.{/n}
  - After: {n}A claw reaches from the yellow screen into your heart. You stagger back, chilled.{/n}

  - After: "...more sacrifices..." {n}His eyes look black.{/n} "Hecatombe determinans. The enumerator below pours molten waste under the manufactorum. This cogitator feeds on thousands of people, flowing beneath us as slag."

  - Before: {n}He tries to muster a reassuring smile, but it comes out looking more like a grimace.{/n} "I'll be fine."
  - After: {n}He grimaces.{/n} "I'll be fine."

  - After: {n}Heinrix scowls.{/n} "That {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Humane}does not justify{/d} killing more {g|Encyclopedia:Imperium}Imperium{/g} servants."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix's clouded gaze suddenly clears, and he glares at the cogitator.{/n} "No. No, the cult's filthy ravings are {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Humane}not worth that{/d}. What we can extract from its storage drives will be enough."

  - Before: {n}The cogitator screens flash, and the guttural roar in its depths turns into a frantic shriek that seems to contain the death cries of thousands.{/n}

The cursed {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} and his associates created something that went beyond the limits of the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}'s power. This machine is designed to process myriad possibilities using {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} sorcery. It has almost finished its task. It... it predicts the future, {name}."
  - After: "But why so many? That cursed {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} went beyond the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}, using {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} sorcery to weigh possibilities. It's nearly done. It predicts the future, {name}."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Do not attempt to gain any insight into the essence of the machines corrupted by the Archenemy, at least, not if you value your soul! I have encountered the heretics' mechanical abominations before... to truly fathom their nature is to allow a particle of death into your heart." {n}Heinrix is silent for a few moments.{/n} "But the fruit they bear... no matter how abhorrent their instruments, the fruit they bear could be useful."
  - After: "Don't try to understand corrupted machines, if you value your soul." {n}A pause.{/n} "But their fruit could be useful."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix looks at you, his eyes ice-cold.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}, in the name of the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g}, I am requisitioning the population of the lower levels of this manufactorum {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Rough}for the purposes of the Inquisition{/d}."
  - After: {n}Heinrix's eyes go cold.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}, by the {g|Encyclopedia:GoldenThrone}Golden Throne{/g}, I requisition the lower levels' population {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Rough}for the Inquisition{/d}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix's movements are exact and purposeful — unlike his earlier operation of the cogitator. One after another, the cogitator screens begin to fade to black, and the roar coming from inside the machine quietens to a barely perceptible howl... in which you imagine you hear notes of dejection.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix shuts it down; the roar fades to a dejected howl.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix bends over the keys — and flinches as if from an electric shock. His head snaps back unnaturally, and you see his lips moving... The cogitator lets out a roar that grows louder by the second...{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix jerks as if shocked, lips moving. The roar swells...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix is too engrossed in his examination of the control panel to stop you. You draw closer to the side section of the cogitator housing, which has several thick cables running from it. With each step toward the flickering screens, your feeling that the cogitator is watching you with rapidly blinking eyes grows stronger and stronger. Up close, you see that besides buttons, switches, and toggles, the cogitator casing is also covered in strange writing.{/n}
  - After: {n}Near the cabled panel, you feel the machine watching. Strange writing covers the casing.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}When you attempt to study the text being displayed on the screens, your head begins to swim. You look away, but the glowing squares continue to dance before your eyes, as though they have been burned into your retinas.{/n}
  - After: {n}The text makes your head swim.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}'s grace has not touched this object. This mechanism was not desecrated but born flawed and unnatural. Iron most profane." {n}Pasqal unhurriedly produces a data-slate.{/n} "Initiating observation log. Let not fear stand in the path of Knowledge."
  - After: "The {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}'s grace never touched this. Iron most profane." {n}Pasqal takes a data-slate.{/n} "Logging. Fear won't block Knowledge."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "You just said this thing is an abomination. Yet you are going to immerse yourself in it in order to study it? Doesn't the thought repel you?"
  - After: "It's an abomination, yet you'll study it?"
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira suddenly appears by your side and tugs at your sleeve.{/n} "Lord Captain, no. Please don't. Just don't look. The whispers say nothing good will come of it. You really should just step away from that thing..."
  - After: {n}Idira tugs your sleeve.{/n} "Don't look, Lord Captain. The whispers warn against it."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira opens her mouth to speak but then drops her gaze awkwardly.{/n}
  - After: {n}Idira starts to speak, then looks down.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "You intend to let a creation from beyond the veil do what it was designed to do?" {n}Yrliet stares at Heinrix in astonishment.{/n} "Is it not your calling to protect your kind from the schemes and temptations of Sai'lanthresh?"
  - After: {n}Yrliet stares at Heinrix.{/n} "You'd let a thing from beyond the veil work? Isn't your calling to guard against Sai'lanthresh?"

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Interrogator/Interrogator_Q1/EnterForgeWorld_dialogue/EnterForgeWorld

- **Player**
  - Before: "Any suggestions for how to proceed?"
  - After: "Any suggestions?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "We'll learn nothing by standing here. Let's go."
  - After: "Let's go."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Remind me, what is your mission on Kiava Gamma?"
  - After: "Your mission on Kiava Gamma?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix frowns as his eyes sweep over the {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g}'s dark halls.{/n} "No solemn ceremony, no personal meeting with Magi... I fear we are too late and we won't be dealing with clandestine heretics after all."
  - After: {n}Heinrix frowns at the dark {g|Encyclopedia:Manufactorum}manufactorum{/g}.{/n} "No welcome. I fear we're too late."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "You're right, Glaito, something is definitely wrong. And we will know what very soon."
  - After: "Right, Glaito. Something's wrong."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Binharic arias of alarm stream out of Pasqal's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox-synthesiser{/g}. In their neurotic, broken rhythm, you sense a call to arms and a warning of danger.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox-synthesiser{/g} blares binharic alarm.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}The Interrogator nods, continuing to stare into the surrounding gloom.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Interrogator nods, watching the gloom.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "To start, let's look around and find out why the arrival of the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} did not elicit the usual fuss. To speak plainly, I would not count on a warm welcome at this rate. Better keep your weapon at the ready."
  - After: "Learn why the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g} got no welcome. Keep your weapon ready."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I assumed I would conduct an investigation and track down traces of the Cult of the Final Dawn. I believe I can discard that plan now: both the incident with the scrap-code and the manner in which we were forced to land on Kiava Gamma indicate that the situation has taken a turn for the worse."
  - After: "I came for the Cult of the Final Dawn. The scrap-code and forced landing mean it's worse."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Nevertheless, I must use this opportunity and try to determine what the cult was doing on an {g|Encyclopedia:IndustrialWorld}industrial world{/g} and what specifically interested them on a planet full of sacred machines and servants of the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}. First, we must find someone who can tell us what's been going on here..." {n}Heinrix pauses, straining to hear something.{/n} "...if, that is, there is anyone left here to speak to."
  - After: "Why was the cult on an {g|Encyclopedia:IndustrialWorld}industrial world{/g} of the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}? We need a witness..." {n}He listens.{/n} "...if any remain."
- **Glaito**
  - Before: {n}The cyber-mastiff's visors flicker continuously, as if he is trying to process an overwhelming influx of data. The dog leans forward with a slight growl, but then obediently goes still again at his master's side.{/n}
  - After: {n}The cyber-mastiff's visors flicker. He growls, then stills.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Interrogator/Interrogator_Q1/ExperimentalMutant_Dialogue/ExperimentalMutant_Dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Look at the cage closest to you]
  - After: [Look at the nearest cage]
- **Player**
  - Before: "Have you ever seen anything like this before?"
  - After: "Ever seen anything like this?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Why are they hooked up to cogitators?"
  - After: "Why the cogitators?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Study the mutants closely]
  - After: [Study the mutants]
- **Player**
  - Before: "Heinrix, let this go. You are only prolonging their suffering."
  - After: "Let it go, Heinrix. You're prolonging their suffering."
- **Player**
  - Before: "If there is something that will make them talk, we must use it."
  - After: "If something makes them talk, use it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "They're people. Monstrously mutated, but still people."
  - After: "They're still people, however mutated."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Lexmechanic talked about some kind of slag waste disposal and Chaos symbols on machines... What are the Archenemy's minions doing to the people of the lower levels?"
  - After: "Slag disposal, Chaos symbols... What is the Archenemy doing to the lower levels?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What are you going to achieve by prolonging their suffering? Just release them from this nightmare!"
  - After: "Why prolong their suffering? Release them!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I'm not going to argue with you. It seems to me your mind is already made up."
  - After: "I won't argue. Your mind's made up."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It seems to me your mind is already made up. These people need deliverance from their suffering."
  - After: "Your mind's made up. They need deliverance."
- **Player**
  - Before: "These people can still serve the Imperium. Anyone would deem their suffering a fair price to pay."
  - After: "They can still serve the Imperium. A fair price."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Numerous wires and pipes run to the filthy cages, which are filled with what looks like a conglomeration of human bodies. You cannot make out who is in the cage, but bright blue sparks flash intermittently in the darkness, while the mass of flesh twitches and shudders.{/n}
  - After: {n}Wired cages hold fused human bodies, twitching amid blue sparks.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix casts a scrutinising eye over one of the cages, before withdrawing his weapon and approaching to examine what lies inside.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix holsters his weapon and approaches a cage.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The flesh explodes in a fountain of lumps, stinking spray, and bone shards. The gaping wound closes in an instant, and a different face emerges from the fleshy depths in place of the lost head. The mutant's body is pulsing faster, harder, as though the abomination's heart rate has spiked with fear. A many-voiced moan rises up from all the other cages at once — the pain was felt by all who share the mutant's horrific fate.{/n}
  - After: {n}The head bursts; a new face grows back. Every cage moans in shared pain.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Negative. What I am currently observing is not my tech-comrades, but merely their biologically functioning remains fashioned into a specimen of an unnatural perversion of Technology. I am under no directives to feel any affinity for such specimens."
  - After: "Negative. Not tech-comrades, just perverted remains. No affinity required."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Groxseed..." {n}Jae barely breathes the word, not sounding at all like herself.{/n}
  - After: "Groxseed..." {n}Jae barely breathes it.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Through the metal bars, you see it truly is a pile of human bodies — or something that used to be. The monstrously deformed bodies have fused together in places, while others were severed using saws and knives, leaving wounds seeping pus and slime, wounds that are agglutinating and sprouting tendons. Rods connected to wires that run to a nearby {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} bristle across the flesh. One of the human heads turns to you.{/n} "Mercy..."
  - After: {n}Fused, sawn, oozing bodies, wired to a {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}. A head turns.{/n} "Mercy..."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Look at it!" {n}Heinrix gestures toward the cage closest to you.{/n}
  - After: "Look at it!" {n}Heinrix points at the nearest cage.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "The effect of warp energy will likely lead to an explosive reaction. I do not know the precise mechanism of this mutation — the result could be even more monstrous than its current state."
  - After: "Warp energy could make it explode, or worse."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I have seen a great deal, Rogue Trader. That includes mutations caused by the sorcery of {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g}. But what frightens me most is not their repulsive form, but what is hiding beneath it." {n}Heinrix frowns.{/n} "A human soul in torment. Chaos never forgets to ensure its victims retain the ability to suffer."
  - After: "I've seen {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} mutations. Worse is the tormented soul beneath." {n}He frowns.{/n} "Chaos keeps its victims able to suffer."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix carefully studies the screens of the computing machines.{/n} "Lingua-Technis — corrupted by the scrap-code, I'm sure. It's unlikely we will be able to extract anything of value from their data-crypts." {n}Thinking, Heinrix clenches his fist and bites down on a knuckle — and then recoils when the mutant from the nearest cage reaches a hand out to him through the bars.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix studies the screens.{/n} "Lingua-Technis, scrap-code corrupted. Likely useless." {n}He recoils from a reaching mutant.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You examine the pulsating mass of flesh. The creature in the cage seems to be composed of several bodies joined together. You see no sutures or any other means by which the separate parts could have been connected. Among the layers of meat, you can discern large knots of muscle, various limbs, exposed bones, parts of faces, and entire heads... Only {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} sorcery is capable of creating such an abomination while preserving its ability to live on.{/n}
  - After: {n}Bodies joined without sutures. Only {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} sorcery could make this live.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You peer at the pulsating mass of flesh. Beneath the thin film coating the skin of this monstrous creation, you can see the throbbing veins that snake through the flesh and the flowing yellow ichor. The creature looks like a conglomeration of several people, squeezed together by brutal hands into a single whole.{/n}
  - After: {n}Several people crushed into one throbbing mass.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "You're wrong — this is our chance to find out more. Extracting some good from suffering is the only thing that will justify the torment of these unfortunate people. It is how they can serve the Throne one last time."
  - After: "No, it's our chance to learn. Their last service to the Throne."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix nods.{/n} "Yes. It's possible another person would refuse to make such a choice. But we can use this situation to help the investigation."
  - After: {n}Heinrix nods.{/n} "Yes. It helps the investigation."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix nods.{/n} "I am... inclined to relieve their suffering. Every moment of existence in such a state is pure torture for the people locked in these sheaths..."
  - After: {n}Heinrix nods.{/n} "I'm inclined to end their torture."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "You think so? Tiny fragments of data that could prove worthless and even harmful to us... in exchange for participating in this torture?"
  - After: "Scraps of maybe-harmful data, for joining this torture?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix nods grimly.{/n} "Yes, this is what warp sorcery has done to them, to be precise. I have seen many mutants whose features have been distorted under the effects of the {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Archenemy{/g}... but this is something beyond all imagining."
  - After: {n}Heinrix nods grimly.{/n} "Warp sorcery. Beyond any {g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Archenemy{/g} mutation I've seen."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "To know the workings of dark sorcery means allowing corruption into oneself." {n}Heinrix scowls.{/n} "These are warp mutations, no doubt. Perhaps there was some side effect, and that is why they were brought here, to be connected to sensors and cogitators. Even fallen Tech-Priests who have rejected the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g} are driven by a perverted hunger for Knowledge."
  - After: "Knowing dark sorcery invites corruption." {n}He scowls.{/n} "Warp mutations, studied here. Even Tech-Priests who reject the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g} crave Knowledge."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix wavers for another moment, and then leans over the cogitators.{/n} "Each mutant has cables attached. I may not know the nature of these machines, but it isn't too difficult to increase the voltage... Ah, this switch here..."
  - After: {n}Heinrix leans over the cogitators.{/n} "Raise the voltage... this switch..."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix hesitates for a moment, then closes his eyes and raises one hand. You are enveloped by an otherworldly chill. The mass of flesh in the cage suddenly rears up: the mutant wrenches open its glued-together lips and begins wailing frantically. The shrieking is echoed by a chorus of howls and tortured moans coming from the neighbouring cages.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix raises a hand; a chill falls. The mutant wails, and all the cages howl.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "That's that, then. But do you know what bothers me, Rogue Trader? The number of people here — there are too few. The lower levels of similar manufactorums are inhabited by millions — what happened to the rest of them?" {n}Heinrix shakes his head.{/n} "I know I won't like the answer. Let's go. We still haven't done what we came here to do."
  - After: "Done. But too few are here; such levels house millions. Where are the rest?" {n}He shakes his head.{/n} "Let's go."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix takes in his surroundings and once again fixes his attention on the contents of the nearest cage.{/n} "I'm beginning to have some idea. The {g|Encyclopedia:Lexmechanic}Lexmechanic{/g} mentioned the inhabitants of the lower levels who had been imprisoned in their homes. He said some of them were brought here. The cultists did something to those poor people... in their own home... and now they are studying the result."
  - After: {n}Heinrix eyes the cage.{/n} "The {g|Encyclopedia:Lexmechanic}Lexmechanic{/g} said lower-level folk were locked in their homes. Cultists changed them, and now study the result."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "My psyker abilities allow me to affect the human body. It is one of the most effective tools to use against individuals who resist questioning. But if you're suggesting that I 'want' to use it — I think you are getting a little ahead of yourself."
  - After: "My psyker gifts work on bodies, useful in interrogation. But 'want'? Hardly."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I'll be damned! They can still speak! They remember the people who did this to them!" {n}Heinrix balls his fists in powerless rage. Then he frowns in thought.{/n} "Perhaps a little biomancy will allow us to draw the fragments of knowledge out of them. Or it will trigger further... changes."
  - After: "Damn! They remember who did this!" {n}Heinrix clenches his fists.{/n} "Biomancy might draw it out. Or change them more."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The mutant changes before your eyes: the tumours recede like an ebbing tide, revealing an emaciated female face twisted in agony. The woman gasps for air, stretches her now mobile neck, and exclaims,{/n} "LIAR! You promised to kill me! You promised me deliverance! Every one of you, everyone told me to have hope and the pain would go! Accept the Truth, for that is hope! My only hope is to be freed from this pain! Please make it so! MAKE IT S—" {n}A lump of flesh behind her head shudders and sends out smooth, fat tentacles that cover her wailing face and drag it into itself. You feel the pressure in your ears: from the cage you hear a steady, almost imperceptible sound that fills you with despair and horror.{/n}
  - After: {n}An agonised woman's face emerges.{/n} "LIAR! You promised to kill me! Accept the Truth, for that is hope! Free me! MAKE IT S—" {n}Tentacles drag her back in. Despair hums from the cage.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}With a sigh, Heinrix lowers his hand and looks at what the creature within the cage has become. A wetly gleaming mass of meat and gristle that no longer bears any hint of its human origins, it pulses vigorously.{/n} "And that's it? The lamentations of dying people? No. Not just that. What it said about hope sounds like a lie of Chaos, which it uses to take root in weak minds. I believe the corrupted Tech-Priests repeated this phrase like an echo of what had been instilled in them... Whatever the Cult of the Final Dawn is planning, false hope is a key component of their plan. It's a lead. A small one, but still a lead."
  - After: {n}Only pulsing meat remains.{/n} "That line about hope is a Chaos lie the Tech-Priests echoed. The Cult of the Final Dawn relies on false hope. A small lead."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Not missing Pasqal's sober interest in proceedings, which he is dutifully recording in a data-slate, Abelard raises a brow:{/n} "Esteemed Magos, these are your comrades. If I may ask — do you feel any compassion for them? Or, at the very least, regret? Regret for the losses that these poor people represent to the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g}?"
  - After: {n}Abelard eyes Pasqal's notes.{/n} "Magos, these were your comrades. No compassion? No regret for the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g}'s loss?"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah stares at the pile of fused flesh without blinking.{/n} "I do not hear their names in the Undying One's whispers. They have become... too twisted, and He no longer remembers them."
  - After: {n}Kibellah stares.{/n} "The Undying One forgot their names."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "These people are suffering, more so than anyone, anywhere — and you're refusing them deliverance? What is wrong with you?"
  - After: "They suffer worst of all, and you deny them deliverance?"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "They are not people anymore. It does not matter what happens to them." {n}Kibellah turns away from the cage.{/n}
  - After: "They aren't people now." {n}Kibellah turns away.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira curses furiously.{/n} "'A little biomancy'... This is a tangle of flesh and bone that, by some freakish miracle, still happens to have a soul and a mind! Come on, iceman, let them die in peace already!"
  - After: {n}Idira curses.{/n} "'A little biomancy'? They still have souls! Let them die, iceman!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix turns to Idira. You do not see his face, but you do see Idira suddenly shrink and cast her eyes down.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix turns; Idira shrinks.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You hear the crackle of electricity. The wires glow with blue sparks — and the creatures locked in the cages drop lifelessly to the floor. The sharp tang of burned meat hangs in the air.{/n}
  - After: {n}Electricity crackles; the creatures drop dead. Burned meat reeks.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Even attempting to speak causes the mutant pain, but he bears the agony and forces out the words:{/n} "Mercy... Make... make it stop..."
  - After: {n}In agony, the mutant forces out:{/n} "Mercy... Make it stop..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Foreman... from sector... sector... Hurts... Mercy..." {n}The mutant falls silent for a few moments, but then his voice comes back stronger.{/n} "Foreman from Boiler 3... We're... from the lower... levels..." {n}The final words are drowned out by a moan.{/n}
  - After: "Foreman... Hurts..." {n}He strains.{/n} "Foreman, Boiler 3... lower levels..." {n}A moan drowns him.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You..." {n}A female face watches you from within the gloom of the cage. Even though half of her head has been turned into a mess of bones and lumpen growths, her single eye looks at you with a surprising amount of intelligence.{/n} "You promised! You promised us!" {n}Her words are echoed by other voices in the depths of the cages.{/n}
  - After: "You..." {n}A half-ruined woman's eye fixes on you.{/n} "You promised us!" {n}Others echo her.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix leans toward the cage, but at sufficient distance to ensure that the mutant cannot reach him.{/n} "Who are you talking to? What did they promise you? Who are they?"
  - After: {n}Heinrix leans in, out of reach.{/n} "Who promised you what?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You! You took us from the inferno! You promised us a reward! You..." {n}Her face contorts in a grimace, and the creature's lips stick together like melted wax.{/n}
  - After: "You! You took us from the inferno! Promised a reward!" {n}Her lips melt shut like wax.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Interrogator/Interrogator_Q1/FixedLexmechanic_dialogue/FixedLexmechanic_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You don't act like the other priests who were infected with corruption."
  - After: "You're not like the other corrupted priests."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You have nothing to fear from us."
  - After: "Don't fear us."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What's this? Another one of the cultists' minions?"
  - After: "Another cultist minion?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "Death to the slaves of the Archenemy!"
  - After: [Attack] "Death to the Archenemy's slaves!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You mentioned someone imprisoned on the lower levels?"
  - After: "Someone imprisoned below?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How did you manage to avoid the same fate?"
  - After: "How did you escape?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "How did your crazed comrades behave?"
  - After: "How did your comrades act?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You mentioned a 'monster.' Is that some kind of weapon?"

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Interrogator/Interrogator_Q2/InquisitorialDisgrace/InquisitorialDisgrace_dialogue

- **Emelina**
  - Before: {n}The stooped figure draws back the hood of the grimy robe, revealing the emaciated face of a woman. Her skin is stretched taut over her skull and sickeningly protruding augmentations, and her cheek is marred with several open wounds. She looks at you with a feverish gleam in her eyes.{/n} "Hmm... The visual description matches Interrogator van Calox..." {n}The Sage blinks several times and her head twitches.{/n} "You made it here after all."
  - After: {n}A gaunt, wounded woman lowers her hood.{/n} "Matches Interrogator van Calox..." {n}She twitches.{/n} "You came."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: {n}The Sage draws herself upright — as far as her crooked spine will allow — and flicks several switches on her facial augments. Then she turns to you, ignoring Heinrix's words completely.{/n} "Who have you brought with you, Interrogator van Calox? Clearance level?"
  - After: {n}She ignores Heinrix.{/n} "Who is this, Interrogator van Calox? Clearance level?"
- **Emelina**
  - Before: {n}Emelina Lichtenhart inhales through her teeth.{/n} "Hypothesis. Rogue Trader. Most likely the same one Xavier took such an unusual interest in. Von Valancius. Territory to the galactic north of Furibundus. A dynasty noted for its heretical tendencies. Threat level—"
  - After: {n}Emelina Lichtenhart hisses.{/n} "Rogue Trader von Valancius. Xavier's interest. Heretical dynasty. Threat level—"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix turns his livid gaze on you.{/n} "No. For the God-Emperor's sake, {name}, didn't you see the lurid shimmering of the void between the star and the planet? Do you wish this same fate upon other worlds?"
  - After: {n}Heinrix glares.{/n} "No, {name}! You saw that shimmering void. You'd wish it on other worlds?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I... expect that Emelina has chosen to seal the memory block containing data of a personal nature. She does this whenever she is concerned that someone might try to extract information about Calcazar's coterie from her..." {n}Heinrix thinks for a moment, and then in a clear voice says,{/n} "Sigma Prosperity." {n}He pauses before repeating the strange phrase.{/n}
  - After: "She's sealed her personal memories, to protect Calcazar's coterie." {n}He says clearly,{/n} "Sigma Prosperity." {n}He repeats it.{/n}
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "Furthermore, you permit yourself to criticise my methods after having arrived in the company of xenos. Have you forgotten which Ordo you belong to?"
  - After: "You criticise me while travelling with xenos? Forgotten your Ordo?"
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "The reminiscence block you are attempting to access was repurposed — it now contains knowledge of the rituals performed by the shamans of this place. My standard working memory alone was insufficient to record all the nuances I uncovered in my research here."
  - After: "That memory block now holds the shamans' rituals. I needed the space."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix looks as though he has been punched in the gut.{/n} "Emelina, you... you deleted the data about all the members of Calcazar's unit? You... wiped us all?"
  - After: {n}Heinrix reels.{/n} "You wiped Calcazar's unit? All of us?"
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "Of course not. I retained the portion of the reminiscence block's data relating to the operational significance of the Lord Inquisitor's unit. That is how I was able to recognise you, Interrogator van Calox."
  - After: "I kept operational data. That's how I recognised you."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I'm sorry I asked. But {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Humane}what are you trying to achieve here{/d}, Emelina? The ritual we interrupted, what is it supposed to do?"
  - After: "{d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Humane}What are you trying to achieve here{/d}, Emelina?"
- **Emelina**
  - Before: {n}Emelina lifts her gaze upward.{/n} "It will rid this world of its half-year-long night and the Mandrakes of their total advantage over us. It will force a new heavenly body — this one of human making — to rise above the horizon and illuminate the dark side of the planet. If the ritual works... I will have mastered the secret of forging a new sun."
  - After: {n}Emelina looks up.{/n} "To end the half-year night that favours the Mandrakes. I will forge a new sun."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "I came here on the supreme directive of the Lord Inquisitor. An Adeptus Historica mission was established on Phton IV to study the origins of the civilisation that once inhabited the planet. This world was once settled by humans — the mission aimed to discover which colony ship they came from and why they disappeared."
  - After: "The Lord Inquisitor sent me to study this world's vanished human settlers."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "The traces of the ancient culture uncovered in the layers of soil suggested the existence of primitive solar faiths among the dark inhabitants of this world. Faiths that are strikingly similar to worship of the Archenemy. The surviving scrolls indicate that shamans used the gifts of Chaos to protect their people, to secure the harvest, to imbue their warriors with strength and vitality... and that this culture persisted for thousands of years!"
  - After: "Their shamans used Chaos's gifts to protect them — for millennia!"
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "I was cataloguing data when the attacks began at one of the remote outposts. I immediately recognised the enemy by their tactics: Drukhari. They chose an unremarkable, defenceless world where night lasts half the year! By the time five outposts had been swallowed by the darkness, the last Astropath had been torn to pieces, and many calls for help sent to Calcazar's unit had gone unanswered, I realised that no one was going to save these people. Or this... knowledge. And so I put the knowledge to use, for the good of Humanity."
  - After: "Then Drukhari attacked. Calcazar never answered. So I used the knowledge, for Humanity."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "Reason is not what guides the acolytes of the Holy Ordos, von Valancius. We find a tool and we use it to achieve a particular end. And that is exactly what I have done."
  - After: "The Ordos don't run on reason, von Valancius. We find a tool and use it."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "Insanity is maintaining mental rigidity in fluctuating circumstances. This world is important for the Imperium and for our struggle against the enemies of Humanity. To perish along with this world would be the height of wastefulness."
  - After: "Insanity is rigidity. This world matters to the Imperium. Losing it would be wasteful."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "The notion of 'heresy' is {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Humane}hardly applicable{/d} to people in our line of work, {name}. But you are correct about one thing — Emelina has crossed the line that separates a servant of the Imperium from a deluded Chaos worshipper."
  - After: "'Heresy' is {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Humane}hardly applicable{/d} to us, {name}. But she's crossed into Chaos worship."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "If I am to form an {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Rough}assessment of your actions{/d}, I must know the purpose of the ritual we interrupted when we arrived. Answer me."
  - After: "For my {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Rough}assessment of your actions{/d}: what was the ritual's purpose? Answer."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "Buried under silica and granite are knowledge and resources that could repel the enemies of Humanity. We are too afraid of anything labelled 'prohibited.' My memory contains thousands... thousands upon thousands of pages from manuscripts, tomes, and scrolls — contact with any one of these is supposed to guarantee instant death. But the preachers who claim this are liars. I am living proof of their falsehoods."
  - After: "Forbidden knowledge could save Humanity. It's said to kill on contact. I'm proof that's a lie."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "All of the survivors are here in this tunnel. The rest are dead. Or worse than dead — they are in the clutches of the monsters from Commorragh. Our last Astropath died when his mind was invaded by a warp entity — it used his psy-trail to hunt him down. The rest of the people here have been blessed with the protection of those forces that I summoned to our aid."
  - After: "The survivors are here; the rest are dead or taken. My summoned forces protect them."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "That is enough." {n}Heinrix's voice shakes with bridled fury.{/n} "I have heard all the justifications and complaints a hundred times before. No purpose can justify what you have wrought here! Who you have become!"
  - After: "Enough." {n}Heinrix shakes with fury.{/n} "Nothing justifies what you've done! What you've become!"
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "You disrupted the ritual with your untimely appearance. The calculations are based on too many variables to simply repeat the process on another planet... but given resources and time..."
  - After: "You disrupted it. It can't simply be repeated... but given time..."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai sneers.{/n} "So this is the burnt pet's owner. Perhaps we should inform her about the fate of her prized follower..."
  - After: {n}Marazhai sneers.{/n} "The burnt pet's owner. Shall we tell her its fate..."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Do you once more seek to nourish another's pain with your words?" {n}Yrliet sounds tired and slightly vexed.{/n} "By Isha's tears, you are insatiable indeed."
  - After: "Feeding on pain again?" {n}Yrliet sighs.{/n} "By Isha's tears, insatiable."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: {n}Emelina shakes her head.{/n} "You are drawing conclusions based on incomplete knowledge of the situation, Interrogator van Calox. Your judgement is impaired."
  - After: {n}Emelina shakes her head.{/n} "Incomplete data, Interrogator van Calox. Your judgement is impaired."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard's eyes widen in astonishment.{/n} "Create... a star? God-Emperor's grace, what creatures could live in the light of a star born using the powers of the Archenemy?"
  - After: {n}Abelard gapes.{/n} "A star? What could live under a star born of the Archenemy?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "This is madness. Madness, pride, and monstrous, staggering heresy." {n}Heinrix's voice is barely audible, as if his throat has closed up in shock.{/n}
  - After: "Madness, pride, and staggering heresy." {n}Heinrix whispers.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix's usual mask of stoicism has melted away without a trace — he stares around him in undisguised dismay.{/n} "Emelina? What... what is this? You're performing the Archenemy's rituals? But— no. Stop. Right now. Not another move unless I tell you!"
  - After: {n}Heinrix stares, shaken.{/n} "Emelina? The Archenemy's rituals? Stop. Not another move!"
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix's expression scarcely wavers at Emelina's words, but despite this, Marazhai ducks his head sharply and watches the Interrogator with devouring eyes.{/n} "Mmm... fear, and despair, and sorrow... an exquisite palette, mon-keigh..."
  - After: {n}Marazhai eyes Heinrix hungrily.{/n} "Mmm... fear, despair, sorrow... exquisite, mon-keigh..."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "{name}." {n}Heinrix bites out the words through clenched teeth:{/n} "Silence your pet xenoscum... or I will."
  - After: "{name}." {n}Through clenched teeth:{/n} "Silence your xenoscum, or I will."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix stops you with an imperious gesture.{/n} "I am restricting your authority here, Rogue Trader. I have not yet heard everything... everything that Emelina has to say."
  - After: {n}Heinrix stops you.{/n} "Not yet, Rogue Trader. I'll hear Emelina out."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "Even worse. You permit ordinary subjects of the God-Emperor to cross the established line and reduce themselves to consorting with highly dangerous enemies of Humanity."
  - After: "Worse. You let subjects consort with Humanity's enemies."
- **Jae**
  - Before: {n}Jae looks at Emelina, then at Heinrix, then back at Emelina again. She opens and closes her mouth a few times, but the only thing she manages to say in a stifled voice is:{/n} "I'm sorry, shereen."
  - After: {n}Jae stammers.{/n} "I'm sorry, shereen."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: "A fine time to show your true colours, Inquisitor. Let's see if you will do what is right or once again prove that you consider yourself above the rules."
  - After: "Now, Inquisitor: do right, or prove you're above the rules."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Lord Ulfar... With all due respect to you and your Chapter, keep your mouth shut. Your scepticism is the last thing I need right now."
  - After: "Lord Ulfar, with respect — keep quiet."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: {n}Emelina Lichtenhart dips her head.{/n} "Von Valancius. A Rogue Trader dynasty. Territory to the galactic west of Furibundus. The head of the dynasty, Theodora von Valancius, has been flagged for her heretical sentiments. Threat level—"
  - After: {n}Emelina Lichtenhart nods.{/n} "Von Valancius dynasty. Theodora flagged for heresy. Threat level—"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "The Bloodspun Web is familiar with the practice of purging one's memory of all that gets in the way of duty." {n}Kibellah presses her lips into a line.{/n} "But the void that is left in place of the excised memories must be filled with service. Otherwise, corruption will flood the soul, as it has flooded yours."
  - After: "We purge memories too." {n}Kibellah frowns.{/n} "But fill the void with service, or corruption floods in — as in you."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: "You burned away the memory of your comrade? Even if my duty demanded it, I would not want to forget an Arbitrator who fought by my side. And I certainly wouldn't do so for the sake of some dubious knowledge, no matter what benefits it promised me."
  - After: "You erased your comrades for dubious knowledge? I never would."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix gestures at the room.{/n} "I brought the help you requested in your message, Emelina — a voidship under the aegis of the Rogue Trader. I dragged thousands of people and megatonnes of plasteel and ceramite through the bowels of the warp... and for what? To discover that you have sold yourself to the Archenemy?"
  - After: {n}Heinrix gestures.{/n} "I brought the help you asked for... to find you sold to the Archenemy?"
- **Emelina**
  - Before: {n}Emelina glances at you, but she cannot bring herself — or does not consider it necessary — to ask you to elaborate.{/n}
  - After: {n}Emelina glances at you, silent.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Emelina is operating under the assumption that any and all methods are acceptable in the war against the enemies of Humanity. Her reasoning is not... infallible, however, it does contain a {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Rough}grain of truth{/d}."
  - After: "To her any method is fair. Flawed, but a {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Rough}grain of truth{/d}."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: {n}Emelina bows her head.{/n} "A side experiment. A way for exhausted and frightened people to find comfort in a higher power. However, I had the services stopped — several people succumbed to the pernicious influence of the atmosphere and went insane, but the people blamed it on the voices from the vox."
  - After: {n}Emelina bows.{/n} "A comfort experiment. Stopped — some went insane."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Interrogator/Interrogator_Q2/RavorWarpAnomalies/RavorWarpAnomalies_prompt

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Cap'n, we have arrived in Phton IV's system. Our translation from the warp was a little rough — a net loss of about 500 souls on the middle and service decks, and God-Emperor only knows how many wounded. But that's only the half of it: the brainboxes on the augurs are sending me reports that aren't doing my mood any favours. Realspace here's got more holes than a sieve, and all our sensors are playing up — it's got to be sorcery, Lord Cap'n."
  - After: "Lord Cap'n, we're at Phton IV. Rough translation — 500 souls lost. Realspace here's full of holes, sensors failing. Sorcery."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If I was you, Lord Cap'n, I'd do what I came here to do right sharpish and clear out... while we still can. I've seen the likes of this before in this same region. Maybe your sorcerers will be able to explain it better, but here's what I know: shit like this never ends well."
  - After: "Finish quick and clear out, Lord Cap'n. I've seen this before. It never ends well."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Interrogator/Interrogator_Q2/Verdict

- **Player**
  - Before: [Kill Heinrix] "The worlds of the Koronus Expanse will have their suns again, thanks to Emelina. You will not stand in the way of that."
  - After: [Kill Heinrix] "Emelina will give the Expanse its suns again. You won't stop that."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: {n}As Emelina stares at the Interrogator's body, her face reveals no particular emotion save for a tightening around her mouth. Then the Sage looks at you.{/n} "I presume I have no choice but to become your... hostage? Agent? The semantics are unimportant. Answer the question — what will you do with the survivors of Phton IV?"
  - After: {n}Emelina eyes the body, then you.{/n} "Your hostage, then. What of Phton IV's survivors?"
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "Hmm. Good. I will need trained assistants if I am to do what you ask."
  - After: "Good. I'll need trained assistants."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "This will hinder my progress on the work you wish me to complete. If you would make an exception for a few individuals... well, we can discuss it."
  - After: "That hinders my work. Perhaps exceptions..."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: {n}Emelina rises, shaking off the dirt.{/n} "I expect the archives I discovered in the excavation to remain with me — we can be transported to your ship together. It will allow me to begin my calculations and preparations immediately." {n}The Sage holds your gaze.{/n} "Fear holds no power for the bold, Lord Captain. I will restore the stars that have been lost."
  - After: {n}Emelina rises.{/n} "My archives come too." {n}She meets your gaze.{/n} "Fear holds no power over the bold. I will restore the lost stars."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "That will make it difficult to prepare for the ritual you wish me to perform. However, with your resources... perhaps we can accelerate the process."
  - After: "That complicates the ritual."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Interrogator/Interrogator_Q2/Verdict/Verdict_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "What would you advise me to do, Heinrix?"
  - After: "What do you advise, Heinrix?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I have a rather unpleasant suspicion that the witnesses to this conversation are also at risk of being eliminated at a later date..."
  - After: "I suspect the witnesses may be eliminated later too..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Because Emelina's knowledge is just like the archives you were planning to destroy. Coming into contact with it is too dangerous."
  - After: "Her knowledge is like those archives. Too dangerous."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You did not want her to be subjected to your standard 'procedures.' At yours or anyone else's hands."
  - After: "You didn't want her put through your 'procedures.'"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You're a pack of soulless, unhinged animals — you and all your Inquisition cronies. Now, if you have had your fill of violence and death, we are leaving."
  - After: "You Inquisition cronies are soulless animals. If you're done killing, we're leaving."
- **Player**
  - Before: "In other words, you are going to torture her to death."
  - After: "So you'll torture her to death."
- **Player**
  - Before: "First she corrupts her mind with this knowledge, and now you are planning to do the same?"
  - After: "Her knowledge corrupted her, and you'll do the same?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Because you are sick and twisted — just like all of your fellow acolytes."
  - After: "Because you're sick and twisted, like all acolytes."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is this? Some kind of guessing game? I want the truth!"
  - After: "A guessing game? I want the truth!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What will happen to the archives and Emelina?"
  - After: "What happens to the archives and Emelina?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Emelina Iona Lichtenhart. In the name of the Inquisition, you are hereby removed from your post and expelled from the Holy Ordo." {n}Heinrix's eyes are fixed on Emelina, but she does not look at him. Then the Interrogator turns his gaze on you.{/n}
  - After: "Emelina Iona Lichtenhart, you are expelled from the Holy Ordo." {n}He turns to you.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "The fate of its fallen members is a matter for the Ordo. Heretical archives, artefacts obtained in the excavation and other assets in Lichtenhart's possession I hereby declare the property of the Holy Inquisition. However, it is for the Rogue Trader to decide what becomes of Phton IV and its people. What is your verdict?"
  - After: "She and her archives belong to the Inquisition. Phton IV and its people are yours. Your verdict?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "You know my answer — the world has been compromised, its inhabitants touched by corruption.   - After: "The world is corrupted. You won't heed that." {n}He smirks.{/n} "But I'll spare you the archives."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "The archives will be destroyed to prevent this situation from ever reoccurring. Emelina... is my responsibility."
  - After: "The archives burn. Emelina is mine."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "The archives will be sealed and transported to your ship as the official property of the Inquisition — for further study and appraisal. Emelina... is my responsibility."
  - After: "The archives go sealed to your ship, for study. Emelina is mine."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix says nothing for several seconds, staring into space. At last, he begins to speak:{/n} "Emelina Iona Lichtenhart..."
  - After: {n}After a long silence:{/n} "Emelina Iona Lichtenhart..."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "...your knowledge is of particular interest to the Inquisition. Before your fate is decided, I will {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Rough}carry out the necessary procedures{/d} to extract the information from you.   - After: "...I'll {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Rough}carry out the necessary procedures{/d} to extract your knowledge. The sealed block will need force."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix stares at the Sage, saying nothing, then looks down and {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Humane}mutters something{/d} too quietly for you to hear.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix {d|Encyclopedia:CompHeinrix_Humane}mutters something{/d} inaudible.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "You really think my actions are driven by such sentiment?" {n}Heinrix studies you intently. His face is difficult to read, but one of his eyes spasms briefly just before he turns away.{/n}
  - After: "Sentiment? Me?" {n}His eye twitches.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Ha!" {n}Heinrix's laughter sounds like the rasping caw of a dying bird.{/n} "There is a grain of truth to your words, {name}. Yes, there is indeed. A grain of truth."
  - After: "Ha!" {n}A rasping laugh.{/n} "A grain of truth, {name}."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix turns to you.{/n} "Thank you for your assistance in solving my problem, Rogue Trader."
  - After: {n}He turns to you.{/n} "Thanks for your help, Rogue Trader."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "That is an imprecise way to describe the procedure, {name}. You are focusing only on the consequences for Emelina. I am interested in the results of the process."
  - After: "You see her pain, {name}. I see results."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Studying the forbidden is part of my work. I will show greater caution than Emelina did, or else I will suffer the same fate."
  - After: "The forbidden is my work. I'll be careful."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "For you, perhaps. For me, it is my duty, {name}."
  - After: "For you. For me, duty, {name}."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix looks at you, his eyes dark and louring.{/n} "Why don't you answer that question for yourself?"
  - After: {n}He glowers.{/n} "You tell me."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix nods.{/n} "The words of a true citizen of the Imperium." {n}The Interrogator does not even try to hide the caustic edge to his words.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix nods.{/n} "A true Imperial citizen." {n}Caustic.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix makes a sound that could be a cough or a suppressed laugh.{/n} "A less patient acolyte would consider that an insult to the Holy Ordos. Luckily for you, I am very patient."
  - After: {n}A stifled laugh.{/n} "Luckily, I'm patient."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "We are finished here. The planet will be designated unfit for further use — the risks are simply too great. It will take a few hours to deal with the excavation site and what the diggers found there... but it will not delay us. When we return to the ship, find a minute to speak with me."
  - After: "We're done. The planet is declared unfit. Talk to me on the ship."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: {n}Emelina lets out an agonised moan.{/n} "Wasted... all my work, all my preparation... all for nothing..."
  - After: {n}Emelina moans.{/n} "All for nothing..."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "I saw one of Calcazar's documents when I went to receive my new orders. Only a fleeting glimpse... but, with my memory like a pict-recorder, it was long enough for its contents to be imprinted on my mind. I do not know the details, but the document itself... was an interrogation transcript. With a final annotation indicating the removal of the person from the retinue. And we both know how someone leaves the Lord Inquisitor's retinue, Interrogator van Calox."
  - After: "I glimpsed Calcazar's interrogation transcript, marked 'removed from retinue.' We know what that means."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Tanakia is the Lord Inquisitor's top espionage specialist! Wherever Xavier chose to refrain from making a public show of strength, Calbergaria was invaluable! Why would he do this?"
  - After: "Tanakia was Xavier's best spy! Calbergaria was invaluable! Why?"
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "Heinrix... It is Heinrix, yes?" {n}There is a subtle shift in Emelina's voice — she sounds older, wiser.{/n} "You should know... I am sorry to have forgotten you."
  - After: "Heinrix... it is Heinrix?" {n}Softly.{/n} "I'm sorry I forgot you."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix's face is a mask of disbelief and anger.{/n} "You're lying..."
  - After: {n}Heinrix, furious:{/n} "You're lying..."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: {n}Emelina sighs.{/n} "I know, Interrogator van Calox. I know all the procedures used on compromised Sages: interrogation, unsealing of reminiscence blocks... But before we begin..." {n}She stands up, straightening her spine as much as she can, and looks into the Interrogator's eyes with a weak smile.{/n} "I thought Tanakia was your doing. But as your reaction has revealed the truth to me..."
  - After: {n}Emelina sighs.{/n} "I know the procedures, Interrogator van Calox. But first..." {n}She smiles weakly.{/n} "I thought Tanakia was your doing. You didn't know..."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "A reasonable and balanced assessment. An excellent conclusion." {n}Heinrix makes no attempt to inject even the barest hint of conviction into his words.{/n}
  - After: "Reasonable." {n}No conviction.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "You are hereby stripped of your special status as an agent of the Golden Throne and all attendant rights and privileges. I am authorised to use all interrogation measures stipulated in the standard framework for information extraction to ascertain the fate of acolyte Tanakia Calbergaria. Will that be necessary, Emelina?"
  - After: "You're stripped of all rights. I may interrogate you on acolyte Tanakia Calbergaria's fate. Must I, Emelina?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "After all this time, you still have not realised one simple fact about me — I decide whether or not I answer a question. Not you."
  - After: "I decide whether I answer. Not you."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "No, Interrogator van Calox." {n}The Sage's voice is scarcely louder than a whisper.{/n} "I have no intention of concealing that information from you. I am almost certain that Tanakia Calbergaria was eliminated on the orders of Xavier Calcazar after being deemed a volatile element."
  - After: "No, Interrogator van Calox." {n}A whisper.{/n} "Xavier Calcazar had Tanakia Calbergaria eliminated as volatile."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "This world has been compromised. Any attempt to assess the degree of corruption will necessarily be based on weak judgement vulnerable to doubt and sentiment. I would get rid of the planet and its population."
  - After: "This world is compromised. I'd purge it and its people."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix gives you a searching look.{/n} "It is not like you to be so quiet, {name}. I can only guess at the reason."
  - After: {n}Heinrix studies you.{/n} "Quiet, {name}? I can guess why."
- **Emelina**
  - Before: "The nature of her mission — and of Xavier's true purpose here in the Expanse — was likely why he chose to bury this secret, and Tanakia along with it..." {n}Emelina breaks off.{/n} "The operational data indicates that you are the retinue's primary torture specialist, Interrogator van Calox. All this time, I thought you were the one who conducted Tanakia's interrogation. And one of the reasons why I destroyed my personal data block was to ensure that my own sentiments would not prevent me from thinking rationally when I next encountered you or Calcazar's other servants."
  - After: "Xavier's secret purpose likely buried her." {n}She pauses.{/n} "I thought you, his torturer, did it, Interrogator van Calox. So I erased my memories of you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Whether you were joking or being deadly serious, your words fall on the deaf ears of the two acolytes of the Golden Throne: Emelina, weakened by biomancy, is staring fixedly at Heinrix, who seems to be engrossed in intense rumination.{/n}
  - After: {n}Neither acolyte hears you.{/n}
- **Emelina**
  - Before: {n}Emelina looks up at Heinrix, her eyes full of despair.{/n} "I do not know, Interrogator van Calox. Just as I do not know why the Lord Inquisitor sent me to this nondescript planet as soon as I voiced my concerns about his methods. Just as I do not know if I should blame the warp for the lack of responses to my calls for help, or if Calcazar prohibited the others from answering."
  - After: {n}Emelina, despairing:{/n} "I don't know. Nor why he exiled me here, nor who silenced my calls."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Interrogator/Interrogator_Q2/WarpedGuards/WarpedGuards_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "What's happening on the planet?"
  - After: "What's happening here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What a stroke of luck — it seems we have already found who we are looking for."
  - After: "Lucky — we've already found who we seek."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Survey the barricades] "They do not appear to be very sturdy."
  - After: [Survey the barricades] "Not very sturdy."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You mentioned an expedition?"
  - After: "An expedition?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I refuse to find my own way there. You there! Escort me to Emelina Lichtenhart."
  - After: "You! Escort me to Emelina Lichtenhart."
- **Overseer**
  - Before: {n}The sentry rubs her eyes and gawps at you. One half of her face is covered with a bulky, rusty augment of unknown purpose.{/n} "You came... You came to rescue us! Praise the God-Emperor, it reached you! The sorcerer's message reached others like him, may he rest in peace!"
  - After: {n}A sentry with a rusty augment gawps.{/n} "You came! The sorcerer's message reached you!"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix dourly listens to the sentry's speech. He takes a few steps forward and intently peers at her face as the woman herself freezes in fear. Then Heinrix scowls and cuts a glance at you.{/n} "We need to hurry."
  - After: {n}Heinrix studies her face, scowling.{/n} "We must hurry."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "What a life..." {n}Jae chuckles grimly.{/n} "Dragged to a planet in the middle of nowhere. Dumped on a worthless excavation site that everyone else probably forgot about a long time ago. Three out of four children are dead..."
  - After: "What a life..." {n}Jae, grimly.{/n} "Forgotten dig, three kids dead..."
- **Overseer**
  - Before: {n}Even under the wavering lumens, you notice something strange — the slightly skewed proportions, the almost indiscernible asymmetry of her facial features. Looking at the other sentries, you see the same oddity in their faces too — and the fact that they are all wearing the same strange, ramshackle implants, which clearly are not combat augmetics.{/n}
  - After: {n}Her features, like every sentry's, are subtly skewed. All wear the same crude implants.{/n}
- **Overseer**
  - Before: "It's terrible, my {mf|lord|lady}! I don't even know how to describe it. It's been, what... how long has it been... a few months, probably... a few months of being plagued by these sorcerous beasts! As soon as night fell, they came — creeping right out of the shadows, black as soot, there's no stopping them! The only thing that's worked so far is keeping the fires burning and maintaining a constant watch — and even with that, the creatures drag us off in ones and twos the second we drop our guard."
  - After: "Terrible, my {mf|lord|lady}! For months, soot-black beasts creep from the shadows at night. Only fires and watches slow them."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix meets your eyes.{/n} "Noticed, have you? Don't jump to any conclusions. It could be a local genetic anomaly... It could be something else. We can't say anything for sure... yet." {n}Heinrix looks past the sentry.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix eyes you.{/n} "Noticed? Could be genetic. Could be not." {n}He looks away.{/n}
- **Overseer**
  - Before: "You mean Mistress Lichtenhart, my {mf|lord|lady}? We wouldn't have survived without her. It just so happened that she was here, at a local excavation, when the monsters started appearing. We've been losing contact with the other sites on the planet since then, like candles being snuffed out one after another. The rest of them must have all perished. But we're still here... holding on!"
  - After: "Mistress Lichtenhart, my {mf|lord|lady}? She saved us. The other dig sites went dark. We hold on!"
- **Overseer**
  - Before: "Mistress Lichtenhart is inside, in the pit... You go on. Don't be afraid. She will be there to properly greet you! We'll stand guard... Thanks be to the Emperor for delivering you to us..."
  - After: "She's in the pit. Go on. We'll stand guard."
- **Overseer**
  - Before: "Please, my {mf|lord|lady}..." {n}The sentry is on the verge of tears.{/n} "Do you think we are trained Guardsmen? We're from the expedition convoy — we've lived here for generations and, up to now, the God-Emperor has guarded us from misfortune. But now we have to fight. The survivors have all gathered in the tunnel, we've handed out what weapons we have... but how is that supposed to help us against these butchers when we don't always know how to use our weapons?"
  - After: "Please, my {mf|lord|lady}..." {n}Near tears.{/n} "We're expedition folk, not Guardsmen. We barely know our weapons."
- **Overseer**
  - Before: "Yes. About thirty years back, we were brought here with a load of clever people from some high-up Adeptus of something or other. And we've lived here ever since... I've raised four kids here. Two died at the excavations, one was taken by the monsters, but my youngest is still alive..."
  - After: "Thirty years back, with Adeptus scholars. Of my four kids, the dig took two, monsters one. My youngest lives..."
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Excavations? Hmm. Perhaps the expedition, or rather, its objectives, were what Emelina was interested in. Of course, the easiest option would be to ask her directly..." {n}The Interrogator shoots you a pointed, impatient look.{/n}
  - After: "Excavations? Maybe that drew Emelina. Let's ask her." {n}He looks at you impatiently.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix furrows his brow.{/n} "Sorcerous creatures from the shadows... Could they be daemons? That would explain the presence of warp anomalies in the system. A local breach..."
  - After: {n}Heinrix frowns.{/n} "Daemons? That fits the warp anomalies."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Well, I know of other 'creatures from the shadows,' Master van Calox. And so do you — for the Exalted One has granted you extensive knowledge of xenos and everything related to them. This poor soul's description sounded to me like the Mandrakes that lurk in the Webway. I don't know why you didn't come to the same conclusion yourself..."
  - After: "Master van Calox, that sounds like Mandrakes from the Webway. You know xenos — odd you missed it."
- **Overseer**
  - Before: {n}The sentry bows fearfully.{/n} "Of course, of course... one moment, my {mf|lord|lady}..." {n}She signals to her fellows and two more people hurry over to you.{/n}
  - After: {n}She bows.{/n} "Of course, my {mf|lord|lady}..." {n}Two more hurry over.{/n}
- **Overseer**
  - Before: "We are most honoured by your presence. Please, come forward, quickly, out of the darkness." {n}The woman hurriedly checks a nearby lumen, her hands visibly shaking.{/n} "Those creatures come from the dark, you see... but not for much longer, not for much longer! And now you're here, and Mistress Lichtenhart has already found a way to help us..."
  - After: "Come out of the dark, quickly." {n}She checks a lumen, shaking.{/n} "Mistress Lichtenhart has found a way to help us..."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "I can understand the iceman's thinking. Everything here reeks of the warp — as if it has been pricked full of holes deliberately, just like the system itself. No, sorcery is definitely at work on this planet, we just need to figure out where it came from."
  - After: "The iceman's right. This place is pricked full of warp holes. It's sorcery — but whose?"
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai lets out a vicious laugh.{/n} "I would not be surprised if this mon-keigh was speaking of Mandrakes. They come from the shadows... as black as Vect's soul... as savage as an enraged ur-ghul... It is strange that your kin are still alive, {name}. The Mandrakes must be prolonging their own pleasure by terrorising the mon-keigh again and again."
  - After: {n}Marazhai laughs.{/n} "Mandrakes, black as Vect's soul. They're savouring the terror, {name}."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Hey, iceman... No need to lie to yourself. You can feel it. There's no way you can't feel it. I can practically taste it in the air — sorcery. First, we had those flares in the system, now this comely lot... Something here has been poking holes in the veil between realspace and the warp. Something or someone."
  - After: "You feel it, iceman — sorcery. The flares, now this lot. Someone's poking holes in the veil."
- **Overseer**
  - Before: {n}The woman lurches backward under your scrutiny. Her eyes are red and swollen, and there are dark circles under them, suggesting a long run of sleepless nights.{/n}
  - After: {n}She flinches, eyes sleepless.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "I... have noted the system's idiosyncrasies, yes. I cannot yet say how it relates to the person who drew us here... if it is related at all." {n}Heinrix plainly refuses to meet Idira's eyes.{/n}
  - After: "I've noted the oddities. Whether they relate to Emelina, I can't say." {n}He avoids Idira's gaze.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "It is called doing your duty, Mistress Heydari. You may not be familiar with the concept, but for most of the Imperium's subjects, it is the honourable mundanity."
  - After: "It's called duty, Mistress Heydari. Honourable mundanity."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Interrogator/Interrogator_Q2/WorldFate/WorldFate_prompt

  - After: "Collapse the mine and wall up the tainted knowledge forever."

  - After: "Leave this world to the Archenemy."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Jae/Jae_Q1/BusinessTalk/BusinessTalk_JaeQ1_dialog

  - After: "Get to the point! I haven't all day."

  - Before: "A truly wonderful gift. I accept it with gratitude."
  - After: "A wonderful gift. I accept gratefully."

  - Before: "Yet more xenoheresy? You have some nerve trying to peddle this filth to a true servant of the Emperor!"

  - After: "I don't need your help with that."

  - Before: "We are not here to exchange pleasantries. What is it you wanted to discuss?"

- **Player**
  - Before: "I think I follow. You wish to use me?"
  - After: "You wish to use me?"
