  - After: "Mercy? You taught us otherwise."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The dark light, the wicked hunger — do you not fear them? You feared them before."
  - After: "You feared the dark hunger before. Not now?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your secrecy saddens us. We do not like secrets. But... we will stop bothering you."
  - After: "Secrets sadden us. We'll go."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}One can detect with the naked eye the moment when Nomos leaves the bridge — the servitors stop moving in sync and slowly shuffle off to their posts.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nomos leaves.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "All life is inconsistent. We understand that."
  - After: "All life is inconsistent."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Nomos learn. Nomos process streams of data beyond the limits of your imagination. We are certain we understand correctly."
  - After: "Nomos process vast data. We understand."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We were wondering whether you would manage to return."
  - After: "We wondered if you'd return."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We sense that a great deed has been done, a vivid imprint on existence. You did something very important. What was it?"
  - After: "You did something great. What?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Did Nomos say it correctly?" {n}The servitor chorus, which sounds as a single voice, falls silent. Nomos appears to be waiting for your response... in eager anticipation.{/n}
  - After: "Correct?" {n}The chorus waits eagerly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}After a long pause, the servitor chorus responds with unexpected forcefulness,{/n} "Nomos are glad too!"
  - After: {n}Forcefully:{/n} "Nomos are glad too!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We must go now. We will come to speak with you later." {n}Another pause follows, so long that the silence becomes more piercing than a scream. Then the servitors finally break it.{/n}
  - After: "We must go." {n}A long silence, then they speak.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Nomos/TechxorcismNomos/TechxorcismNomos_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "What caused all these failures and peculiarities?"
  - After: "What caused these failures?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Very well. Let us proceed with your ritual."
  - After: "Very well. Proceed with your ritual."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Thank you for your report and service, Drivesmaster."
  - After: "Thank you for your service, Drivesmaster."
- **Player**
  - Before: "And you thought a trifle like that was worth my time? Off with you!"
  - After: "You wasted my time with this trifle? Off with you!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Deliver your report, just do so in a way I can understand. No more than one pearl of tech-wisdom per five sentences of intelligible human speech."
  - After: "Report in plain speech. One pearl of tech-wisdom per five human sentences."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I will not waste my time on this. Deal with it yourself."
  - After: "I won't waste time on this. Handle it yourself."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest makes an elaborate gesture with her upper body and mechadendrites. Her movements bear a closer resemblance to a mechanical marionette than a creature of flesh and blood.{/n} "Lord Captain! In the absence of an Enginseer Prime on board, it falls to me as the Drivesmaster to carry out certain sacred protocols assigned to high-ranking priests of the Omnissiah."
  - After: {n}She gestures like a marionette.{/n} "Lord Captain! Lacking an Enginseer Prime, I, the Drivesmaster, must perform sacred protocols."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's voice pouring out of his vox-system crackles like thin ice under pressure. It is unclear whether this is nothing more than static or an expression of some emotion understandable only to the Tech-Priest himself.{/n} "{name}, following the Omnissiah's guidance, I request permission to execute the report protocol that entails describing suboptimalities within the recent operations of the ship's systems and subsequently proposing the appropriate course of action."
  - After: {n}Pasqal's vox crackles.{/n} "{name}, may I report the ship's faults and propose action?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Presenting report. After registering a large number of malefaction-failures in the operations of maintenance servitors and reports of disturbances in the ship's systems, I arrived at the decision that a rite of techsorcism must be performed. The ritualistic cycles have already begun on all decks and will continue for another forty days." {n}The Drivesmaster hesitates for a moment.{/n} "The rituals are proceeding at a steady pace. However, their first stages were accompanied by taint-phenomena. Dozens of servitors and even several junior tech-acolytes were subjected to disposal."
  - After: "Servitor failures and disturbances prompted techsorcism on all decks, forty days more." {n}She hesitates.{/n} "Taint-phenomena followed. Dozens of servitors and some acolytes were disposed of."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Establishing causality is not part of the standard sancti-response protocol for such anomalies. The protocol dictates that techsorcism must be performed in accordance with the tenets of scripture Epsilon-Rho-12-45."
  - After: "Finding causes isn't protocol. Scripture Epsilon-Rho-12-45 demands techsorcism."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Strings of profane cogitator code, deviations from standard procedures." {n}The Drivesmaster pauses again.{/n} "We have observed numerous messages appear on vid-screens since the very start of the techsorcism rite. These messages call to you, Lord Captain. And, at times, to the exiled Magos Pasqal Haneumann."
  - After: "Profane code." {n}She pauses.{/n} "Vid-screen messages calling to you, Lord Captain. Sometimes to the exiled Magos Pasqal Haneumann."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The frequency of heretici-messages reached its peak during the initial phase of the techsorcism rite. Concurrently, the junior tech-acolytes I mentioned earlier in the report performed acts of arbitrary self-dismemberment. However, as the rituals continued, the frequency of these events declined and eventually the messages stopped displaying altogether. The taint-phenomena have likewise ceased to occur."
  - After: "The messages peaked as acolytes dismembered themselves, then stopped, as did the taint."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Initiating exposition. With the Omnissiah's blessing, I conducted several sessions of tech-meditation in an effort to transpose the available data streams into a matrix of patterns. The data subjected to this analysis comprised evidence of deviations in the operation of the ship's systems and servitors as well as irregularities in the algorithms of the ship's log."
  - After: "I meditated on the system deviations and log irregularities."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Ending report. Departing for the tech-service location."
  - After: "Report ends. Departing."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Request partially approved. Comprehensive processing requires an established definition of the term 'tech-wisdom.' Adjusting speech patterns based on the limited available understanding of the request."
  - After: "Partially approved. 'Tech-wisdom' undefined. Adjusting speech."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "I have arrived at the following conclusion: this vessel's machine spirit is most extraordinary. A full cycle of sacred diagnostics must be performed followed by a complementa-ritual. This ritual will force the spirit responsible for these recent events to reveal itself. Once it does, we will be able to understand its nature and take action applicable to said nature."
  - After: "This machine spirit is extraordinary. Diagnostics, then a complementa-ritual will make it reveal itself."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal pauses before responding.{/n} "Applicable to the entity that appears before us. If it is a machine spirit of great might, we must appease it and humbly ask about the reasons behind the portents it has shown us. If it is the abomination of tech-heresy, the complementa-ritual will help us purge the ship of its unhallowed presence."
  - After: {n}Pasqal pauses.{/n} "A mighty spirit, we appease and question. Tech-heresy, we purge."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Response: affirmative. For the complementa-ritual to take place, activation via the blood of the dynasty is required. All of the ship's high protocols are activated with the key of blood."
  - After: "Affirmative. The complementa-ritual needs dynasty blood as its key, like all high protocols."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "This decision is lamentable. Without your participation, the most we will be able to accomplish is totally purge the data-halls that have demonstrated anomalous behaviour and pray that the good spirit will not be enraged. Nevertheless, on this ship, your decision is law. Therefore, I comply."
  - After: "Lamentable. Without you, we can only purge the data-halls and pray. Your word is law. I comply."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "You have my gratitude, {name}. I will notify my tech-comrades to begin their preparations for the complementa-ritual at once."
  - After: "Thank you, {name}. My tech-comrades will prepare the complementa-ritual at once."

  - Before: "It is an extremely rare and venerated form of statistical augury. But Tech-Brother Abel is adept at this form of appealing to the Deus Mechanicus."
  - After: "A rare statistical augury. Abel excels at it."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The Cycle has the advantage of predictability. Abandoning it will plunge the collective into a perilous space of uncertainty, which will inevitably lead to disasters and the risk of universal annihilation. The doctrine of Discontinuing the Cycle may herald good things to come — or it may be a death sentence. Only the Omnissiah knows all, and comprehends all. Others are mere prophets who interpret His wisdom as far as their own Comprehension permits."
  - After: "Leaving the predictable Cycle risks annihilation, or heralds good. Only the Omnissiah knows."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Abel's voice quivers, and his eyes dart around, desperately avoiding eye contact.{/n} "What was flawed has since been purged... But the shadows of the hunt linger...   - After: {n}Abel avoids your eyes.{/n} "The flaw is purged... but the hunt's shadows linger. Threat remains. Who will judge?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is no easy task to keep up with the scrolling numbers, but you manage to pick out a few equations... schemes... theorems. They are all senseless, for the simple reason that each one is based on an absurd violation of the laws of calculation.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**

- **(conversation owner)**

Do you want me to show you the truth?" {n}His pale lips spread into a smile.{/n}

  - After: "Yet correct."

The Adeptus Mechanicus are hereby officially notifying House von Valancius of having commenced an //investigation into//operation to remove// Fabricator-Censor Cubis Delphim. Estimated time to procedure completion... three point seven solar years."
  - After: "Fabricator-Censor Cubis Delphim blasphemously altered manufactorum rites. We are moving against him. Estimated: three point seven solar years."
- **Opticon-22**
  - Before: "Confirmed. According to the archive entry 1E-99237, Magos Explorator Tarzus Haneumann //served on//maintained// the ship — identifier classified — in the capacity of a reliquary caretaker. He sustained extensive damage to both the organic and the sacred part of his body in //a series of sacrilegious breaches of the Rite of Operation//an assassination attempt//."
  - After: "Confirmed. Archive 1E-99237: Magos Explorator Tarzus Haneumann, reliquary caretaker, maimed in an assassination attempt."
- **Opticon-22**
  - Before: "Request denied. Tech-Brother Tarzus has passed sanctification and has relic privileges. I lack the //authority//access level necessary// to command this unit." {n}There is a hint of animosity toward the bloodthirsty Tech-Priest in Opticon-22's voice.{/n}
  - After: "Denied. Tarzus holds relic privileges; I can't command him." {n}A hint of animosity.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Despite the hood hiding his face, you recognise him as Opticon-22, whom you encountered on {g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g}.{/n}
  - After: {n}It's Opticon-22, from {g|Encyclopedia:Footfall}Footfall{/g}.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Identification codes recognised and confirmed. These units are who they declare themselves to be."
  - After: "Codes confirmed. They are who they claim."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}In contrast, Pasqal speaks quietly and coldly:{/n} "You are malfunctioning, tech-comrade. I deem your logical conclusions questionable."
  - After: {n}Pasqal, coldly:{/n} "You're malfunctioning, tech-comrade."
- **Opticon-22**
  - Before: "The Adeptus Mechanicus regard this act as voluntary //martyrdom//self-destruction// for the glory of the Deus Mechanicus. This battle harness is classified as cogni-armour. The machine spirit living in it is strong and wise, but it took major damage in the course of Magos Gracchus's last battle. Besides sacred litanies and imperatives of service to the Omnissiah, the armour broadcasts a continuous signal of suffering and agony into Tech-Brother Tarzus's mind."
  - After: "A voluntary martyrdom. The armour's machine spirit, damaged in Magos Gracchus's last battle, pours agony into his mind."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Request approved. Ready to work in cooperative mode."
  - After: "Approved. Ready to cooperate."
- **Tarzus**
  - Before: {n}Tarzus gives you a haughty look and lets out a howl of wrath.{/n}
  - After: {n}Tarzus howls in wrath.{/n}
- **Opticon-22**
  - Before: {n}The tall Tech-Priest who spoke to you looks more peaceful and makes a point of not drawing his weapon. There is an air of concern about the way he frequently glances over at his fellow, scrutinising his condition.{/n}
  - After: {n}The tall Tech-Priest glances at his fellow with concern.{/n}
- **Opticon-22**
  - Before: "This statement is true. Brother Tarzus has the //honour of wearing//authorisation to wear// the sacred battle harness that belonged to Magos Militant Auspector Gracchus, one of the first //champions of the faith//holy scouts// to join the cause of conquering the Koronus Expanse. After //his death//the termination of his vital functions// at the hands of xenos, his damaged Goliath-class armour was preserved and given the status of a relic."
  - After: "True. He wears Magos Militant Auspector Gracchus's relic armour. Gracchus helped conquer the Koronus Expanse and died to xenos."
- **Opticon-22**
  - Before: "//Owing to a statistically fortunate coincidence//By the Omnissiah's grace//, enough of his operational capacity was preserved for him to don a Goliath model sacred battle harness, which would preserve his //vital functions//functionality//. Archive entry personally data-sealed by the captain of the — identifier classified."
  - After: "By the Omnissiah's grace, he survived to wear it. Archive sealed by the captain."
- **Opticon-22**
  - Before: "Analysis of the security system showed that the //assassins//heretics// infiltrated the reliquary using Tech-Brother Tarzus's unique identification code. Someone had //stolen//duplicated// Brother Tarzus's identity, which is a Grade Three transgression. And the unit making the allegedly criminal claim of being Pasqal Haneumann is known to have previously //used//entered// the stolen code."
  - After: "The assassins used Tarzus's stolen code. The unit calling itself Pasqal Haneumann used it before."
- **Tarzus**
  - Before: {n}Brother Tarzus lets out a terrifying battle cry and raises his weapon with an amazing alacrity for someone of his size.{/n} "Let those who have spurned the procedure reap the fruits of their sacrilege!"
  - After: {n}Tarzus raises his weapon.{/n} "Let those who spurn procedure reap their sacrilege!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A group dressed in the crimson of the {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Priesthood of Mars{/g} walks toward you. Their gazes are fixed on Pasqal.{/n}
  - After: {n}Crimson-robed {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Priesthood of Mars{/g} approach, eyes on Pasqal.{/n}
- **Opticon-22**
  - Before: "Negative. The data collected by Tech-Brother Tarzus has been deemed sufficiently comprehensive for //the verdict to be passed//termination//."
  - After: "Negative. Tarzus's data suffices for //verdict//termination//."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne folds his arms.{/n} "Your accusation does not follow protocol; you have no authority on the Rogue Trader's ship; you did not account for Pasqal's status as a member of {mf|his|her} retinue — shall I continue, or is the inadequacy of your 'arrest' clear enough already?"
  - After: {n}Solomorne folds his arms.{/n} "No protocol, no authority here, and Pasqal is in {mf|his|her} retinue. Need I go on?"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "These statements are true. However, I am prepared to answer my tech-comrades' accusations. Further intervention from the unit Solomorne is undesirable for ideological reasons."
  - After: "True. But I'll answer them. Solomorne, stay out of it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You note that the group is not monolithic. Some of its members are more heavily armed and follow a large {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} clad in battle armour. Others keep a respectful distance and cast enquiring looks at their own leader, whose hunched posture belies his tall frame.{/n}
  - After: {n}Armed men follow an armoured {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g}; others, a hunched leader.{/n}
- **Tarzus**
  - Before: {n}The slivers of flesh revealed under the steel are marked with terrible chemical burns. Every now and then, convulsions shake the Tech-Priest's body, and a painful-sounding hiss comes from his {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}.{/n}
  - After: {n}Burned flesh shows through. He convulses; his {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} hisses.{/n}
- **Tarzus**
  - Before: {n}Brother Tarzus lets out a terrifying battle cry and raises his weapon with an amazing alacrity for someone of his size.{/n} "Wasting time is sacrilege! The sentence will be carried out immediately!"
  - After: {n}Tarzus raises his weapon.{/n} "Sentence now!"
- **Opticon-22**
  - Before: "Willingness to cooperate recorded. Mandate expanded. I request //the right to conduct//non-interference in// the operation to //detain//arrest//terminate// the unit falsely identifying itself as Pasqal Haneumann."
  - After: "Recorded. Don't interfere with arresting the false Pasqal."
- **Tarzus**
  - Before: {n}In a burst of chattering, the servo-skulls hasten to translate their master's mighty binharic howl:{/n} "An instrument of the Omnissiah authorised to punish and exact vengeance, known by the designation 'Tarzus Haneumann.'"
  - After: {n}Skulls translate:{/n} "The Omnissiah's avenger, Tarzus Haneumann."
- **Opticon-22**
  - Before: "Conflict of authority detected. Official message: the Adeptus Mechanicus //are aware of//respect//recognise// your right of ownership of this territory and declare no intent to commit an act of aggression. This is an operation to //detain//arrest//terminate// a faulty Adeptus Mechanicus unit, the fugitive falsely identifying itself as Pasqal Haneumann."
  - After: "We recognise your territory and intend no aggression. We want only the fugitive calling itself Pasqal Haneumann."
- **Tarzus**
  - Before: {n}The servo-skulls screech:{/n} "Mine is a pure and binharic tongue that preserves only what is true and shuns scrap data."
  - After: {n}The skulls screech:{/n} "Binharic is pure, preserving only truth."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Pasqal/OpticonSorry/OpticonSorry_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "The Messiah of Discontinuing? Is that how you refer to Amarnat?"
  - After: "Messiah of Discontinuing? Amarnat?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal, what did you do to Tarzus?"
  - After: "What did you do to Tarzus?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am sorry that you had to kill a comrade."
  - After: "Sorry you killed a comrade."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I am not tired at all. In fact, I can finish you off too. Do your worst!"
  - After: "I can finish you too. Do your worst!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Now that the conflict has been resolved, you may remain aboard my ship."
  - After: "You may stay aboard my ship."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Clear off. Or I will spill yet more blood and sacred unguents."
  - After: "Clear off, or more blood spills."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Whisper] "Whatever you just did, it's working. Keep going."
  - After: [Whisper] "It's working. Keep going."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal, there is one small point I'm not clear on — what just happened?"
  - After: "Pasqal, what just happened?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is the reason for this act of genuflection?"
  - After: "Why genuflect?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I presume the conflict between you and Pasqal has been resolved?"
  - After: "Conflict with Pasqal resolved?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Is Amarnat's teaching not heretical?"
  - After: "Isn't Amarnat heretical?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you know where Amarnat is now?"
  - After: "Where is Amarnat?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Were you among his followers?"
  - After: "Were you his follower?"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrite{/g} briefly touches the shoulder of Opticon-22, who bows respectfully.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal's {g|Encyclopedia:Mechadendrite}mechadendrite{/g} touches Opticon-22, who bows.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's confused reply comes from his vox in a rasp:{/n} "Unable... to fulfil... request. The Omnissiah granted me an epiphany, and I... muted the maimed {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g} that was filling Tarzus's mind with fury. I do not fully understand the manner of my appeal to it. The situation perfectly mirrors the incident on Rykad Minoris where I appealed to the machine spirit of a malfunctioning mechanism and laid it to rest."
  - After: {n}Pasqal rasps:{/n} "I... muted Tarzus's maimed {g|Encyclopedia:MachineSpirit}machine spirit{/g}. As on Rykad Minoris."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I also //regret//have a negative assessment of// this event."
  - After: "I also //regret//disapprove//."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Requesting diplomacy mode for further communication. I am not authorised to use force against the von Valancius dynasty's supreme leadership."
  - After: "Requesting diplomacy. Force against you is unauthorised."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} still accuse the unit identifying itself as Pasqal Haneumann of criminal theft of a unique identification code. Unlike Tech-Brother Tarzus, I am not authorised to immediately //arrest//execute// the unit, but neither am I authorised to drop the enquiry."
  - After: "The {g|Encyclopedia:AdeptusMechanicus}Adeptus Mechanicus{/g} still charge Pasqal with ID theft. The enquiry stands."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The unit that called itself Tarzus Haneumann //is dead//has been disabled//. This material asset is beyond restoration or reuse as spare parts."
  - After: "Tarzus //is dead//disabled//. Unsalvageable."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Kappa Thread supply line delegation is leaving Dargonus, expresses gratitude for the //hospitality//ceasefire//, and proclaims its intent to return to Footfall to resume performing its regular functions." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} looks over at Pasqal as if waiting for something.{/n}
  - After: "Kappa Thread delegation returning to Footfall." {n}The {g|Encyclopedia:TechPriest}Tech-Priest{/g} eyes Pasqal.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}After a pause, Pasqal bows his head, and a binharic requiem pours out of his {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g}.{/n} "Despite his misconceptions, he was a servant of the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}."
  - After: {n}Pasqal's {g|Encyclopedia:Vox}vox{/g} sings a requiem.{/n} "He served the {g|Encyclopedia:Omnissiah}Omnissiah{/g}."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "There are no apostates among us." {n}The piercing voice from the vox-synth is more overwhelming than Tarzus's thunderous roar:{/n} "Tech-Brother Tarzus and the machine spirit that lived in his battle harness succumbed to the suffering that beset them. Their judgement was rash and erroneous. Now their torment is over. I declare them martyrs, and am requisitioning Tarzus Haneumann's {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}neural augmetic{/g} for the purposes of preserving his blessed memory."
  - After: "No apostates here. Tarzus erred in torment; he is a martyr. I take his {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}neural augmetic{/g}." {n}His vox thunders.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As astonished Tech-Priests look on, Pasqal leans over the slain man's body and extracts the augmetic from his skull. His movements are as precise as they are respectful.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal respectfully extracts the corpse's augmetic.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest makes an imperious gesture, stopping you from continuing.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal silences you.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}With each word, Pasqal's voice grows more powerful and majestic:{/n} "You saw the agony your Tech-Brother Tarzus was in. His unbridled, pain-spurred faith intimidated you, yet you were silent. Reverence stopped you from raising your voices to proclaim that the machine spirit with which his mind had merged was morbidly afflicted."
  - After: {n}Pasqal's voice swells:{/n} "You saw Tarzus's sick spirit, yet reverence silenced you."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}There is a clang as Opticon-22's knee presses into the floor. Crimson-hooded heads are bowed.{/n} "Let the Cycle be discontinued."
  - After: {n}Opticon-22 kneels.{/n} "Let the Cycle be discontinued."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}The radiant light pouring out of Pasqal's visor grows dimmer. Static creeps back into his voice:{/n} "Let the Cycle be discontinued, tech-comrades."
  - After: {n}Pasqal's visor dims.{/n} "Let the Cycle be discontinued, tech-comrades."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's vox-synth crackles somewhat tentatively,{/n} "I decided to sustain my words with an excerpt from one of the blessed Amarnat's sermons, 'On Loss of Internal and External Function,' Verse IV. My analysis deemed it... appropriate."
  - After: {n}Pasqal crackles.{/n} "I quoted the blessed Amarnat. It seemed... appropriate."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The data received provides a basis for calling the fallen Tech-Brother Tarzus's hypothesis into question. //Out of respect for//Due to lack of authorisation to indict// the followers of the Messiah of Discontinuing, we will not proceed with the //detainment//arrest//termination//."
  - After: "Tarzus's claim is doubtful. We won't //arrest//detain// the Messiah of Discontinuing's followers."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It has been a long time since the words of the Messiah of Discontinuing were last spoken //openly//over public communication bands//. We respectfully welcome wisdom's return."
  - After: "The Messiah of Discontinuing, heard again. Welcome."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This statement is false. Contrary to what many servants of the Omnissiah //thought they knew//preferred to believe//, the Fleet's Supreme Conclave never //formulated//issued// an official statement on that decision."
  - After: "False. The Fleet's Supreme Conclave never ruled on it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Data unavailable. No reports have mentioned Archmagos Amarnat since the incident on the Ark Mechanicus Hermetico which led to the //presumed destruction//disappearance// of that voidship."
  - After: "Unknown. Archmagos Amarnat vanished with the Ark Mechanicus Hermetico."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Negative. I had no contact with Archmagos Amarnat and was never a member of his //flock//disciples//retinue//. However, my analysis of the doctrine he outlined inspired in me deep //respect for//trust in// him."
  - After: "Negative. But I //respect//trust// Archmagos Amarnat's doctrine."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The imperative of reverence had paralysed your will, and you watched a tragedy unfold in silence. The Sixth Universal Law states that Comprehension is the True Path to Knowledge. Yet the procedural Cycle has robbed you of your Comprehension. Therefore — let the Cycle be discontinued."
  - After: "The Sixth Law: Comprehension is the True Path. The Cycle robbed you of it. Let it be discontinued."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "So he is not forgotten after all."
  - After: "So he is not forgotten."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "My archive has no data on the Hermetico incident. The vessel was the blessed Amarnat's base of operations. Is it... lost, then?" {n}Pasqal's voice is filled with anxiety.{/n}
  - After: "Hermetico was Amarnat's base. Lost?" {n}Anxiously.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The Omnissiah knows all, comprehends all. Thank you, Tech-Brother Opticon-22."
  - After: "Thank you, Opticon-22."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Thirty-seven percent of the Supreme Conclave's members openly supported Archmagos Amarnat's views and //disappeared//were removed from the chain of command// under circumstances that were classified. The Supreme Conclave has not had a quorum ever since."
  - After: "Thirty-seven percent of the Conclave backed Amarnat and vanished. No quorum since."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Following Archmagos Amarnat's partial //laicisation//removal from the chain of command//, that was the authorship attribution on a series of sermons on Discontinuing the Cycle that were disseminated across the Cognisance Fleet."
  - After: "Amarnat's sermons on Discontinuing the Cycle bore that name."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "It was, in fact, a title used by many. In times past."
  - After: "Many used that title. Once."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Pasqal/Q2/AvelArcShip/AvelArcShip_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Abel, why did you decide to come with us?"
  - After: "Abel, why come?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do you make of this camp?"
  - After: "Thoughts on this camp?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What do you think happened to this ship?"
  - After: "What happened here?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do you understand what is going on here?"
  - After: "Do you understand this?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Quiet and mysterious as always, Abel Haneumann's demeanour is a mixture of cautiousness and curiosity as he inspects the ship's ruined interior. When you approach him, he acknowledges you by saying softly,{/n} "Death's footsteps were heard here."
  - After: {n}Abel warily studies the wreck.{/n} "Death walked here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The Cycle is on the verge of being discontinued. Doubt has opened its maw wide, bidding us enter."
  - After: "The Cycle nears its end. Doubt beckons."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Abel looks upon the tech-barbarians with a moderate degree of curiosity, without attempting to approach or interact with them. Occasionally his gaze rests on some sacred item covered in tribal imagery or otherwise desecrated, and he raises his eyebrows, evidently pained.{/n}
  - After: {n}Abel watches the tech-barbarians, pained by their desecrations.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Abel averts his eyes in embarrassment and says, almost shyly,{/n} "A hunt. The hunter is coming."
  - After: {n}Abel, shyly:{/n} "A hunt. The hunter comes."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Abel shakes his head in shame and hastens to break eye contact with you.{/n}
  - After: {n}Abel looks away, ashamed.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "The hunter? The Maimed Hunter?" {n}Pasqal places a mechadendrite claw on Abel's shoulder, demanding an answer. Abel nods.{/n} "The Maimed Hunter. That persona occurred in the data I decrypted. Unfortunately, the sum total of information on it is very near zero."
  - After: "The Maimed Hunter?" {n}Abel nods.{/n} "He's in the data I decrypted. Little else is known."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The sacred {g|Encyclopedia:Archeotech}Archeotech{/g} and the profane have mixed, like tainted water and sacred unguent."
  - After: "Sacred {g|Encyclopedia:Archeotech}Archeotech{/g} mixed with profane."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Suddenly a smile appears on his face.{/n} "This has happened before. The spirit transcends the body. The matter in which it manifests itself is transformed into something more spirit-like."
  - After: {n}He smiles.{/n} "Spirit transcends body. Again."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "An epiphany. Followed by doubt. Followed by debate. Followed by Judgement— no, a lack of Judgement." {n}Abel's speech becomes fragmentary.{/n} "A contradiction. A dilemma, resulting in antagonism..."
  - After: "Epiphany. Doubt. No Judgement." {n}Fragmented.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "My tech-comrade insisted on taking part in this excursion. This is as much of a priority mission for him as it is for me. We are both expecting to meet our mentor, Amarnat."
  - After: "He insisted. We both hope to find our mentor, Amarnat."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "Now everything is clear. A battle was fought here, and during preparations for it, Amarnat declared the observatorium off-limits. Even to fellow servants of the Omnissiah, the Explorators. It was an internal conflict, and he expected his erstwhile tech-comrades to become his enemies."
  - After: "Before battle, Amarnat sealed the observatorium even from Explorators. He expected betrayal."
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "A conflict. There was a conflict here."
  - After: "There was a conflict here."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Pasqal/Q2/BrassWhisper/BrassWhisper_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Smile at Nihel] "This is my companion, Pasqal Haneumann. And you made a mistake in meddling with him."

  - Before: "We are looking for Archmagos Amarnat. And we want answers."
  - After: "We seek Archmagos Amarnat, and answers."

  - Before: "Locals spoke of a ghost without a face. Did they mean you?"

  - Before: "Are you saying Pasqal is part of that hivemind?"
  - After: "Pasqal is part of that hivemind?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal? What is going on?"
  - After: "Pasqal? What's going on?"

  - After: "All Haneumanns are parts of Amarnat?"

  - After: "Amarnat planned to re-form? Risky."

  - Before: "What was the dilemma Amarnat faced?"
  - After: "What was Amarnat's dilemma?"

  - After: "You're the Maimed Hunter, hunting Haneumanns."

  - Before: "Idiot. Calcazar was harbouring Axiomantha the whole time. She was working for him."
  - After: "Idiot. Axiomantha worked for Calcazar."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You betrayed your brothers and sisters. Such an act is unforgivable."
  - After: "Betraying your siblings is unforgivable."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Yours was a grim duty. But you were unflinching in fulfilling it."
  - After: "A grim duty, done unflinchingly."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What happens now?"
  - After: "What now?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Let us destroy her, Pasqal!"
  - After: "Let's destroy her, Pasqal!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "You must not fight! We are surrounded by enemies. Enough blood has been shed."
  - After: "Don't fight! Enough blood."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are right, Pasqal. You are the decision maker."
  - After: "You decide, Pasqal."
- **Player**
  - Before: "What is going on here?"
  - After: "What's going on?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "If anyone cares to hear a Rogue Trader's opinion on the matter, I—"
  - After: "If anyone wants my opinion, I—"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Think about what she said, Pasqal. Your secret is dangerous."
  - After: "Heed her, Pasqal. Your secret is dangerous."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You are from Calcazar's retinue. Does he have anything to do with this?"
  - After: "You serve Calcazar. Is he involved?"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: "That is your problem. You have always been too sceptical."
  - After: "You were always too sceptical."

  - Before: "The master of this deck, the second most important god after Marnat. Mortals cruelly betrayed his trust once, and he hasn't talked to them or protected them since. Pref only ever answers the shaman's invocations, and only occasionally at that."

  - Before: "I am the Fabricator General. My shoulders bear the sacred burden of leadership." {n}The man shifts his shoulders, bent under the potentia coil resting upon them.{/n} "The others fear you, as ghosts can carry the living away into nothingness. But I am protected by Marnat's grace."

  - Before: {n}The sound of Techna-Lingua makes the man kneel humbly and whistle a reply as if imitating the language of the servants of the Omnissiah.{/n}

  - Before: {n}The man sighs and makes a sign with his hand that is vaguely reminiscent of a Tech-Priest gesture to ward off evil.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Abel lowers his eyes and is silent for a while, then says,{/n} "We have made great sacrifices."
  - After: {n}Abel looks down.{/n} "We have sacrificed much."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And should I exist? That is, we. Amarnat."
  - After: "And should I exist? We. Amarnat."
- **Abel**
  - Before: {n}With a sad sigh, Abel adds quietly,{/n} "Great power has its own answers to the question of who is worthy of it."
  - After: {n}Abel sighs:{/n} "Power chooses who is worthy."
- **Abel**
  - Before: {n}Abel gives you a sideways glance and says sorrowfully,{/n} "Self-sacrifice must not be in vain."
  - After: {n}Sorrowfully:{/n} "Sacrifice must not be in vain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Without waiting for an answer, Pasqal says gravely,{/n} "You have always been inscrutable, tech-comrade."
  - After: {n}Gravely:{/n} "Inscrutable as ever, tech-comrade."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal nods with an air of authority and says,{/n} "I thank you both. The information has been noted and submitted for analysis."
  - After: {n}He nods.{/n} "Thank you both. Noted."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal casts a sorrowful gaze at Nihel's body. His voice is full of wisdom and... weariness:{/n} "We have seen many things over the decades. We have seen true corruption. The distortion of the Omnissiah's design. Kiava Gamma, Eufrates II... the planets of xenos passed into oblivion. Our own crimes. The darkness grows. There must be a fire to burn it away."
  - After: {n}Weary:{/n} "Kiava Gamma, Eufrates II, our own crimes. Darkness grows. Fire must burn it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The graceful dance of the mechadendrites takes on a more comprehensible, symmetrical pattern.{/n} "I am leaning toward the idea that both Eschatos and Amarnat must cease to exist."
  - After: {n}His mechadendrites calm.{/n} "I lean toward ending Eschatos and Amarnat both."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A shower of sparks bursts from the power unit on Pasqal's shoulders, burning holes in his scarlet hood.{/n} "An act of self-sacrifice. I will destroy the data concerning this technology and the methods of reproducing it. I will burn it out of my neural circuits. Along with everything that led to its creation. Amarnat will be no more. Only a damaged and incomplete shard of him will remain: Pasqal Haneumann."
  - After: {n}Sparks fly.{/n} "I burn it from my mind. Amarnat ends. Only a shard remains: Pasqal Haneumann."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The graceful dance of the mechadendrites takes on a more chaotic and unpredictable pattern.{/n} "I am leaning toward the idea that Eschatos must exist. But not in the hands of the Amarnat Collective. In mine alone."
  - After: {n}His mechadendrites writhe.{/n} "I lean toward keeping Eschatos. Not in the Collective. In me alone."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The graceful dance of the mechadendrites takes on a more energetic, wilder pattern.{/n} "I am leaning toward the idea that Eschatos is necessary. That Amarnat is necessary. That the Cycle must be discontinued."
  - After: {n}His mechadendrites surge.{/n} "I lean toward Eschatos and Amarnat both. The Cycle must be discontinued."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This statement is enigmatic. I request an expanded interpretation." {n}Pasqal looks demandingly into Abel's eyes, but he turns away.{/n}
  - After: "Enigmatic. Elaborate." {n}Abel turns away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "In accordance with the Machine God's commandment, I have crafted a tool with which to implement my design. In accordance with His commandment, I have developed a plan and analysed it. Now I will act. By my power as an Archmagos, I hereby effect a Restoration and revive the Amarnat Collective. The servants of the Omnissiah need a Messiah who will discontinue their Cycle, and I will be that Messiah. I am Him."
  - After: "Now I act. As Archmagos, I revive the Amarnat Collective. The Cycle needs a Messiah to discontinue it. I am Him."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You hear echoes of other voices in Pasqal's: a touch of Dementz's anxiety, of Tarzus's zeal, of Axiomantha's pensiveness. They all fuse into a new voice, full of wisdom and confidence in his prerogative to lead — the voice of Archmagos Amarnat. And this voice takes hold of the lips of your companion's new brothers and sisters. The ancient Tech-Priest turns his gaze toward you and says, with gravitas,{/n} "Let the Cycle be discontinued."
  - After: {n}Pasqal's voice merges his old comrades into Archmagos Amarnat's, and his new brethren echo it.{/n} "Let the Cycle be discontinued."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The Acgen tribesfolk, the ignorant fosterlings of the Omnissiah, slip into the observatorium hall like silent shadows. Led by an intuitive grasp of the significance of the moment, they automatically gather in a circle, heeding Pasqal's summons... or perhaps, at this point, someone else's.{/n}
  - After: {n}The Acgen tribesfolk slip in and circle at Pasqal's summons... or someone else's.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Self-doubt drained our strength and made us hesitate, just as the elders, whose testaments we were following, hesitated. Our fear of change drove us to dogma, paralysed us, and made us waste precious moments when we could have altered destiny's course. We fell apart, helplessly fleeing the dilemma. And in scattering we exposed our weakness to the world."
  - After: "Doubt and fear of change paralysed us. We scattered and showed our weakness."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We were consumed by madness and fanaticism, by depravity and paranoia. The old mistake will not be repeated. I, Pasqal Haneumann, will take the entirety of the power and shoulder the entirety of the burden. I alone will preserve the great knowledge of Eschatos and decide the fate of the Cycle that will be discontinued."
  - After: "Never again. I, Pasqal Haneumann, alone will keep Eschatos and decide the Cycle's fate."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}And his voice. A voice born in the nuclear font of a star and hardened in the cold of the interplanetary void.{/n}
  - After: {n}His voice: born in a star, hardened in the void.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Though our fate is implacable, I, Pasqal Haneumann, will follow my sense of duty and become a protector to my tech-brethren, leading them into the future. Alone."
  - After: "I, Pasqal Haneumann, will lead my tech-brethren. Alone."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Cold steel cuts through the fire in his voice.{/n} "But you are right — the danger of heresy is great. I can feel the gift of Eschatos gnawing away at my principles. It is indeed forbidden to possess it... alone. Therefore, I will place chains upon my mind that will bind it with the doubts of the many but protect it from corruption. Let the Amarnat Collective be revived, so the steadfastness of the many may balance out the vulnerability of the individual."
  - After: {n}Coldly:{/n} "But alone, Eschatos corrupts. Many minds will chain mine. Let the Amarnat Collective be revived."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I sentence it to oblivion. I curse the fruit of every labour ever undertaken in its name, and I reformat every particle of memory that contains its knowledge. May the Rite be unshakeable. May the Adeptus Mechanicus priesthood be as one. May Amarnat and the heresy of Discontinuing the Cycle lapse into oblivion forever." {n}The green lightning bolts produced by Pasqal's vox strike his cogitator and turn white-hot. Then... they subside and fade away like ghosts.{/n}
  - After: "I erase it. May Amarnat and the heresy of Discontinuing the Cycle be forgotten." {n}Green lightning flares, then fades.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}Pensively fiddling with the piston on his beard, Eogunn speaks to the room at large,{/n} "Forging the mightiest weapon... Many would deem it a triumph, but only the wise understand that, akin to a double-edged blade, it can smite both enemies and creators alike. Anyone can unleash such a weapon, but the wise make the hardest choice of all — and leave it in its scabbard." {n}He turns his gaze back to the Tech-Priest.{/n} "Pasqal Haneumann understands this, and thus any conclusion that he is defective is false. That is an incontrovertible fact."
  - After: {n}Eogunn muses.{/n} "The wise leave the mightiest weapon sheathed." {n}To Pasqal:{/n} "You are not defective."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Eogunn Februs, I tender an invitation to you as well. We differ on much, and that is where the value lies. Will you come with me?"
  - After: "Eogunn Februs, will you come too? Our differences are valuable."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "I will thoroughly contemplate your offer, Archmagos Amarnat. The potential of such a union is overwhelming, yet I see value in my individual Quest for Knowledge. I am not yet ready to render my decision." {n}He bows respectfully, and Pasqal returns the gesture with a nod.{/n}
  - After: "I will consider it, Archmagos Amarnat. I value my own Quest for Knowledge." {n}They bow.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "It requires formidable willpower to oppose the exhilarating 'I can' with the sobering 'Should I?' By exercising such reflection, you have already surpassed me, esteemed colleague."
  - After: "Asking 'Should I?' takes great will. You have surpassed me, colleague."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "A powerful mind, armed with a deadly weapon and vast ambition. It is hard to predict the outcome of this, yet I yearn to witness it with my own eyes. By any measure, we are bound to behold something unprecedented."
  - After: "Great mind, deadly weapon, vast ambition. I long to see what follows."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We were different. Each one of us considered the prospects of such an experiment, but I was the first to gain the resolve to attempt it. Nihel joined the project to effect control over it: she regarded the experiment as dangerously close to a blasphemous act of creation. The conclave had ordered her to end my research, but she became convinced of the possibility of its success."
  - After: "I dared first. Nihel was sent to end it, but came to believe."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Everything Amarnat was at the moment of the disconnection has now awoken in my mind. We are at the point where we stopped. But the Amarnat Collective was envisioned as a dynamic structure. We need new minds."
  - After: "All Amarnat was has woken in me. But we need new minds."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal remains motionless. Only a short binharic aria comes from his vox. You feel oddly confident that your gesture of respect has been appreciated and received favourably.{/n}
  - After: {n}A short binharic aria. Your respect is received.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "So am I." {n}The Tech-Priest's inscrutable gaze is fixed upon the body once inhabited by Pasqal's shared mind.{/n}
  - After: "So am I." {n}Abel stares at the body.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Whether she deserved it does not matter. I did what was right because it was right."
  - After: "Deserved or not, I did right because it was right."

  - Before: "It is how I venerate the iron spirits who have done their duty and passed into nothingness, ghost. I do this in the hope that I might gain some of their wisdom."

- **Pasqal**

Hypothesis: ignorant as to the true purpose of this litany, they perceived it as a health-replenishing magic spell."
  - After: "False. I just... know. And grieve." {n}He touches the inked skin.{/n} "The tribe wrote the Maintenance Manual on him as a spell."

  - After: "Obscuratoria bans all holy ministry here. It's declared for corruption, battle, or crisis..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}An intricate, monumental, and piercing binharic aria pours from Pasqal's vox. Encoded in its signals is Haneumann's authority to give orders on this ship. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servitor's last words are drowned out by a harrowing screech that rolls across the deck as several shrill voices wail, "SssecuUrrRrity perRrrImmmeter brREeeach! FfForTheOmnissSsiah!"{/n}
  - After: {n}Shrill voices wail across the deck:{/n} "SssecuUrrRrity perRrrImmmeter brREeeach! FfForTheOmnissSsiah!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servitor gives a jolt, raises his head, and fixes his augmented eyes on you. The large black circles of his visors are cloudy and covered in scratches. The Omnissiah knows... what?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The servitor's jerky movement is accompanied by a shower of sparks from his mouth. His optical visor makes a series of clicks.{/n} "Unit's hierarchical rank... not recognised. Authorisation to give orders... unconfirmed. Awaiting... confirmation."

- **Pasqal**

  - After: "I need the exact reason for Obscuratoria to countermand it."

  - After: {n}Pasqal sighs.{/n} "He suffers, kept alive by sacred True Flesh he earned."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A spasm in the servitor's neck makes his chin twitch.{/n}
  - After: {n}The servitor's chin twitches.{/n}

  - Before: {n}A jumble of sounds comes from the servitor's speaker, as if a very old man, who has outlived his faculty of speech, is trying to utter once-familiar words now strange to him.   - Before: "Request denied!" {n}The rattle in the servitor's voice could be easily mistaken for indignation.{/n} "Access to the lift system denied! Service is in Obscuratoria mode."
  - After: "Denied!" {n}He rattles, indignant.{/n} "Lift access denied! Obscuratoria mode."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Psyker/Psyker_Q1/InsaneIdira_dialogue/InsaneIdira_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Idira, snap out of it. For Vigdis. She is going out of her mind with worry about you."
  - After: "Idira, snap out of it. For Vigdis. She's worried sick."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Idira! Snap out of it, or I'll shoot you myself!"
  - After: "Snap out of it, or I'll shoot you!"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Idira! I am your captain, not her! Listen to me and snap out of it!"
  - After: "I'm your captain, not her! Listen!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Watch what happens]
  - After: [Watch]
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}"Theodora" clucks her tongue in sympathy, reaching out to tenderly stroke Idira's hair.{/n} "Poor little Idira... There, there... How could I not come? You were crying for me so desperately, your pleas carried to the very depths of the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g} itself..."
  - After: {n}"Theodora" strokes Idira's hair.{/n} "Poor Idira... Your cries reached the {g|Encyclopedia:Warp}warp{/g}..."

  - After: {n}Argenta silently aims at Idira, merciless.{/n}

  - After: {n}Idira drops. Shrill laughter.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Argenta wrinkles her nose at your shouted command and lowers the weapon by a few centimetres — but she does not put it away.{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta lowers her weapon. Slightly.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira lets out a soul-chilling howl and tries to grab the hand tearing into her, but her fingers pass through the monster's flesh.{/n} "I didn't hear anything! I didn't hear anything that could have had anything to do with you... I'm sorry, Lord Captain, I failed... Aaaah!" {n}Idira breaks into a strangled scream and you feel the air around you grow rapidly colder.{/n}
  - After: {n}Idira howls.{/n} "I heard nothing... I failed, Lord Captain... Aaaah!" {n}The air turns cold.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your blow passes through the illusion. "Theodora" does not react to your shout, but continues to deliberately force her fingers under the {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g}'s skin. Black rivulets of blood seep from the wounds, streaking down Idira's contorted, shrieking face.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your blow passes through. "Theodora" digs into the {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g}; black blood flows.{/n}
- **Idira**

  - After: {n}Childlike:{/n} "Lord Captain... Help me..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Oh, that would have been a real gift to our little Idira... Except her life belongs to me, not you!"
  - After: "A gift to Idira... But her life is mine!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira shudders and goes limp. Then she blinks, disoriented, and looks at you.{/n} "L-Lord Captain..."
  - After: {n}Idira blinks at you.{/n} "L-Lord Captain..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Damn it!" {n}"Theodora" shoves the psyker away with a low snarl. The Rogue Trader's body begins to change, losing its human shape.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} will devour you! It will devour everyone responsible for my death! Die! Die for the delectation of my lord!"
  - After: "Damn it!" {n}"Theodora" loses human shape.{/n} "{g|Encyclopedia:Chaos}Chaos{/g} will devour my killers! Die for my lord!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Don't even bother. She cannot hear you, little {mf|boy|girl}. She doesn't hear anyone but me."
  - After: "She hears only me, little {mf|boy|girl}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Idira's body slides from "Theodora's" claws and sags to the floor. Piercing and shrill laughter suddenly fills the air.{/n}
  - After: {n}Idira falls. Shrill laughter.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Lord Captain?" {n}Idira turns her head to you, but her demented gaze only rests briefly on your face before sliding away. Up close you can see that the base of one of Idira's temple {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g} has blackened and melted.{/n} "No... Wait... Lord Captain... Lady von Valancius!" {n}Idira raises her eyes to "Theodora," who stands before her. Tears stream down Idira's cheeks.{/n} "You... you came back..."
  - After: "Lord Captain?" {n}Her gaze is mad; an {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implant{/g} is melted.{/n} "Lady von Valancius!" {n}She weeps.{/n} "You came back..."

Idira convulses and shrieks in agony. A sound wave hits you in the face, leaving behind the tang of blood and the smell of decaying flesh.{/n}

  - After: {n}Her smile drops.{/n} "Why didn't you save me? Answer, wretch!" {n}Her fingers sink into Idira's scalp.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Psyker/Psyker_Q1/LucidIdira_dialogue/LucidIdira_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Has anything like this ever happened to you before?"
  - After: "Has this happened before?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I eliminated the problem. Neither Idira nor the ghost of the departed Theodora will trouble us again. Once I'm finished here, make arrangements for the disposal of the bodies."
  - After: "Idira and Theodora's ghost are gone. Dispose of the bodies."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I got rid of the warp's illusions. Idira is alive — bring her to the chirurgeons and have them see to her."
  - After: "The illusions are gone. Idira lives — get her to the chirurgeons."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You hear the warp whispering in your head, and you answered? Are you insane?"
  - After: "The warp whispered and you answered? Insane?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The warp tricked you. It played upon your feelings. I can understand why, but that is no excuse for what you did."
  - After: "The warp tricked you. That's no excuse."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Enough. Sister Argenta, carry out the Emperor's will and destroy this heretic."
  - After: "Sister Argenta, destroy this heretic."
- **Player**
  - Before: "This abomination claims that you called her. Is this true?"
  - After: "This abomination says you called her. True?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Your worries do not interest me, but as long as you keep yourself under control and remain useful, you will live."
  - After: "Stay controlled and useful, and you live."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I'm not going to kill you, but keeping you in the crew is dangerous. You'll be put under guard and escorted from the ship at the first orbital stop we come to."
  - After: "I won't kill you, but you'll be guarded and put off at the next orbital stop."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I want to help you, Idira. We'll think of something."
  - After: "I want to help, Idira. We'll find a way."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The previous Rogue Trader has been seen on the ship recently. Was that your doing?"
  - After: "The previous Rogue Trader was seen aboard. Your doing?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "What will happen to my crew while we look for this 'remedy'?"
  - After: "What about my crew meanwhile?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "So what am I supposed to do with you now?"
  - After: "So what do I do with you?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "I got rid of the psyker's creations. Idira is alive — see that she gets medical attention, and then put a guard on her. If she succumbs to the warp's influence again — shoot her without warning."
  - After: "Idira lives — treat her, then guard her. If the warp takes her again, shoot her."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Kill Idira] "Your weakness will be the death of us all. I will not allow it."
  - After: [Kill Idira] "Your weakness will kill us all."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I handled the problems in the bay, although there is one matter outstanding: see to it that Idira Tlass leaves the ship at the next port. I cannot risk keeping her in my crew."
  - After: "The bay is handled. Idira Tlass leaves the ship at the next port."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Everyone who was on the deck is dead, including the attackers. What happened was entirely the fault of Idira Tlass. Dispatch servitors here and put her out through an airlock, I am sick of her antics."
  - After: "Everyone on the deck is dead — Idira Tlass's fault. Put her out an airlock."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira stares at you with crazed eyes while clutching the wounds on her head. At first, no sound comes out of her moving lips, then she coughs weakly and whispers,{/n} "Lord Captain, is it... really you?"
  - After: {n}Idira clutches her bleeding head.{/n} "Lord Captain... is it you?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Sometimes a psyker's first manifestation leads to their death and the deaths of many others. But if a psyker possesses inordinate willpower and discipline, they can stave off their fall for some time. Idira has been alive many years already — a laudable achievement and a stroke of incredibly good fortune — but the forces of the warp will ultimately devour any psyker deprived of the Emperor's protection. The fact that these manifestations are growing more powerful is a clear sign that the end is near."
  - After: "Will can delay a psyker's fall — Idira lasted years — but the warp devours any unprotected psyker. Stronger manifestations mean the end is near."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta trains her weapon on Idira and watches you closely.{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta aims at Idira.{/n}
- **Vox Master Vigdis**
  - Before: {n}For a moment the airwaves are filled with something that sounds somewhat like breathing, somewhat like ordinary interference.{/n} "Of course, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}Breathing, or static.{/n} "Of course, Lord Captain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You hear unconcealed relief in the Vox Master's voice.{/n} "Of course, Lord Captain. As you command."
  - After: {n}Relief.{/n} "As you command."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "You don't know what it's like — the most important person in your life, who's now gone forever, suddenly starts talking to you inside your head! How could I not try to reach her? I had to!"
  - After: "The person I loved most, dead, speaking in my head! I had to answer!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Idira lets out a plaintive scream — and then sags to the ground like a broken toy.{/n}
  - After: {n}Idira screams and collapses.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "I... can barely remember. The voices, my old, good whispers, they suddenly turned red... sharp... They started cutting, tearing, ripping me to pieces. I cried out, I called for help... and she came." {n}Idira groans and clutches her head.{/n} "Damn it, why are the voices making so much noise now? Shut up! Shut UP!"
  - After: "My whispers turned sharp, tore at me. I cried for help... and she came." {n}She clutches her head.{/n} "Shut UP!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira nods and with visible effort forces herself to smile.{/n} "Understood, {name}. I swear I'll be more useful than ever before."
  - After: {n}A forced smile.{/n} "Understood, {name}. I'll be useful."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira covers her face with her hands and tries to hold back her sobs.{/n} "Th-Thank you... Thank you, {name}! I won't let you down!"
  - After: {n}Sobbing.{/n} "Thank you, {name}! I won't let you down!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira shudders in fear and reluctantly nods.{/n} "I... understand. Of course. Thank you, {name}. Forgive me... and farewell."
  - After: {n}She nods, shaking.{/n} "I understand. Forgive me, {name}... farewell."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Me? Did I...? Yes, Lord Captain... I think it was me who called her."
  - After: "Yes, Lord Captain... I think I called her."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Like this — never! Well, there was something... but it was different. It wasn't as strong, or as terrifying. Apparitions appeared. Mechanisms malfunctioned. The crew lost their minds..." {n}Idira breaks off.{/n} "But Lady von Valancius knew about that. She said it was a small price to pay, an acceptable expense! No {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g} is immune to it! But what happened here... it was just a mistake. I won't do it again!" {n}Idira stretches her lips in a helpless smile, looking past you.{/n} "There will be no more mistakes, Lord Captain."
  - After: "Never like this! Before: apparitions, broken machines, mad crew." {n}She stops.{/n} "Lady von Valancius accepted it — no {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g} is immune." {n}A helpless smile.{/n} "No more mistakes."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta grits her teeth.{/n} "This is not the first time this... heretic has caused the death of her crew. Do you remember the incident on the mid-deck, Idira? What did those honest souls ever do to deserve such a fate? To be turned into mutants and attack their own families? You are a monster. A heretic. If you have any humanity left in you, admit what you are!"
  - After: {n}Argenta glares.{/n} "Remember the mid-deck, Idira? Crew turned mutant. You're a heretic. Admit it!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Yes, {name}. I did it a couple of times, when I'd had too much to drink... At the time, I thought I heard her voice among all the whispers in my head. The voice was so sad, so clear... I couldn't help myself — I answered. I hoped I could reach her... there."
  - After: "Yes, {name}, when drunk. I heard her voice in the whispers and answered, hoping to reach her."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira turns sharply to face you.{/n} "{name}... I know after everything I've done, you have no faith in my willpower or my strength, but I can fix everything. It's just I'm not at my best, you see, but maybe we can find a way? To replace my {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g}. Or some other remedy, a better one. Lady von Valancius said that such a thing could be found — if not here, then elsewhere. I just didn't need it before, but... We just need to find it. We need to figure out where to look for it, and we'll get it! And until then, I'll keep myself on a tight leash!"
  - After: {n}Idira turns.{/n} "{name}, new {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implants{/g} or a remedy could fix this. Until we find one, I'll keep myself on a tight leash!"
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira lets out a desperate shriek and tries to hide from the inevitable, but the Sister of Battle's strike finds its target. The {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g}'s body slowly sags to the floor.{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta's strike lands. The {g|Encyclopedia:Psyker}psyker{/g} falls.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira removes her hand from her head and tries to wipe away her tears, leaving bloody marks on her face. Then she touches her burnt-out {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implant{/g}, frowning.{/n} "I... don't know. It should be quiet... but in my head... the whispering's louder. It shouldn't be... like that."
  - After: {n}Bloody tears; she touches her burnt {g|Encyclopedia:Augmentation}implant{/g}.{/n} "The whispering's louder. It shouldn't be."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira swallows and straightens.{/n} "I'll pull myself together, Lord Captain. The death of Lady von Valancius knocked me for six — I'll get myself under control. No more booze, no more obscura, nothing. And I'll stop walking around the lower decks. I'll be stone-cold sober." {n}She determinedly wipes the tears and blood from her face.{/n}
  - After: {n}She straightens.{/n} "I'll get sober, Lord Captain. No booze, no obscura." {n}She wipes her face.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "Why? I've heard enough stories about ways of extending a psyker's life. But I don't think you'll like all of them."
  - After: "There are ways to extend a psyker's life. You won't like some."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira bites her lip.{/n} "Ever since she died... Since I first heard her voice in my head... the whispers have gotten louder. Clearer. Harder to resist."
  - After: {n}Idira bites her lip.{/n} "Since she died, the whispers are louder."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "You did the right thing, Lord Captain. There is no way back for a fallen psyker."
  - After: "Rightly done. A fallen psyker can't return."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "You are making a mistake, Lord Captain. Perhaps you will find something to slow the decline, but it will not stop it. Only a miracle can save Idira Tlass now."
  - After: "A mistake, Lord Captain. Only a miracle can save Idira Tlass."
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}Idira awkwardly shakes out her stained clothing.{/n} "I... I think I'd better... With your permission, Lord Captain..." {n}She sways, takes a step back — and faints.{/n}
  - After: {n}She sways.{/n} "With your permission..." {n}She faints.{/n}
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Forgive me, {name}. I know I let you down. I let everybody down... But it started off well, didn't it? You didn't shoot me or chase me off... All I had to do was keep control of myself and the two of us would have gotten along fine! I threw away my chance!"
  - After: "Forgive me, {name}. You gave me a chance and I threw it away!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Captain... Of course. Consider it done."
  - After: "Consider it done."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Shut up..." {n}Idira moans.{/n} "Quit your preaching, you're the worst out of everyone here!"
  - After: {n}Idira moans.{/n} "Quit preaching, you're the worst!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Lord Captain?" {n}The Vox Master's shaking voice comes over the comm-bead.{/n} "I received a report that the shooting on the lower deck had stopped. I presume you have brought the situation under control. Awaiting further instructions."
  - After: {n}The Vox Master, shaken:{/n} "Lord Captain? The shooting stopped. Orders?"
- **Idira**
  - Before: {n}She falls silent for a moment. When she next begins to speak, it is in a barely audible whisper.{/n} "I know what you're thinking. During the warp jump, when Lady Theodora came out toward us... I keep thinking about that meeting. I keep blaming myself... Why didn't I divine it? Why didn't I stop her killer? These thoughts have been playing at the back of my mind, day after day... choking me with guilt... and do you know what? The one... on the officers' deck... I don't know what that was. But this time... here... this was the product of my guilt. An accuser straight out of my own mind."
  - After: {n}A whisper.{/n} "I blame myself for Lady Theodora's death. This was my guilt — an accuser from my own mind."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Psyker/Psyker_Q1/TheodoraVision_dialogue/TheodoraVision_dialogue

- **Player**

  - Before: "Where's Idira? What have you done with her?"
  - After: "What have you done with Idira?"

  - Before: "You are not Theodora. Theodora is dead. There is no coming back from that."

- **Player**
  - Before: "I'm sorry we could not help you, but you do not belong here."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Seneschal/Seneschal_Q1/AbelardReprimand/AbelardReprimnd_SeneschalQ1_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: "Why are you so angry? I solved the problem."

- **Player**

  - Before: {n}Stopping unexpectedly, Abelard imperiously dismisses the unit to stand at a distance, and addresses your other companions, saying,{/n} "I have an urgent matter to discuss with the Lord Captain. Please give us a moment."

  - After: {n}Abelard's restraint vanishes.{/n} "Pleased with your 'investigation'?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You kowtowed to the disloyal rabble. You believed their lies and showed them leniency. Next time the ship is attacked by cultists, that rabble will welcome them in with open arms and allow them to wreak whatever havoc they like, because they see you as a weak leader."
  - After: "You believed the rabble's lies. They think you weak and will welcome the next cultists."

  - After: "You kowtowed to the rabble and armed them. Their next uprising will be bloodier."

  - After: "And..." {n}Abelard stands at attention.{/n} "I lost my temper. Let me explain."

  - After: {n}Abelard bows his head.{/n} "Yes, Lord Captain." {n}He studies you.{/n} "Admirable resolve. I'll remember it if old habits return."

  - After: "Indeed!" {n}Abelard relaxes.{/n} "You just needed to trust me."

  - Before: "But why did you have to be the one to do it? And did you consider what it might cost you?"
  - After: "But why you? And at what risk?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Is that how you see your future at the helm of the von Valancius protectorate?"
  - After: "Is that how you'll lead the von Valancius protectorate?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And now, please, let us leave the lower decks. If the Rogue Trader desires to stretch {mf|his|her} legs, there are far more suitable places."
  - After: "Now leave. The Rogue Trader can stretch {mf|his|her} legs elsewhere."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Abelard frowns, his affronted dignity clearly at war with his military training, but the latter wins out. He shrugs slightly, juts out his chin, and speaks in a calmer, graver voice,{/n} "I never expected to hear such words after all my years of service. But I suppose I have brought this on myself. Allow me to explain."
  - After: {n}Abelard frowns, but discipline wins.{/n} "I've earned that. Let me explain."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Abelard speaks slowly, the words not coming easily to him.{/n} "The prosperity of the von Valancius protectorate is not just an empty phrase to me. Rogue Traders do not simply forge new routes and capture worlds — they create order out of anarchy. That creative impulse was entirely lacking during my time in the military."
  - After: {n}Abelard speaks slowly.{/n} "I left the Imperial Navy for the von Valancius protectorate, seeing greatness in Theodora. Rogue Traders create order from anarchy."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "I am obliged to speak thus. Who else can point out your errors and offer you counsel?"
  - After: "Who else will point out your errors?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "So I left behind everything I had known, everything my family had known — I come from a long line of officers — and I embarked upon this incredibly reckless venture. Lord Captain Theodora entrusted me with all the concerns she had no time for. She would go off on her flagship for long periods, to distant frontiers, on scouting voyages, and the advancement of the entire protectorate rested on my shoulders. And then suddenly, everything that had been built over years and years began to quake, rattling like a flimsy hangar on a seismically active world."
  - After: "I broke my family's officer tradition for this. While Theodora explored, the protectorate rested on me. Now it's shaking apart."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "One of the senior officers betrayed us all, the Rogue Trader was killed, and who knows what is happening on the planets. I tell you this honestly, without fear of appearing weak. All this has come as a grievous blow to me. I am not panicking or grieving because I cannot allow myself to panic or grieve. I am duty-bound to aid the new Rogue Trader — to aid you — to find your footing as quickly as possible. And to do that, I must insulate you from problems that in the past have been dealt with by tried and tested procedures set out in the ship's regulations. Procedures that were established long ago and have functioned smoothly for decades cannot suddenly be deemed excess to requirements!"
  - After: "An officer betrayed us, the Rogue Trader is dead. I can't allow myself to grieve. I must shield you from problems our decades-old procedures handle. Those can't just be discarded!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Abelard dips his head in a sign of assent. The shadow of incredible strain, which evidently had been wearing on him for some time, finally lifts from his face.{/n} "I am glad you see the value in the foundations laid down by your illustrious predecessor. Why fix what isn't broken? As for me, I shall endeavour not to cause you any further consternation, Lord Captain."
  - After: {n}Abelard nods, relieved.{/n} "Glad you value your predecessor's work. I won't trouble you further."

## World/Dialogs/Companions/CompanionQuests/Seneschal/Seneschal_Q1/AboutRubble/AboutRabble_SeneschalQ1_dialog

  - After: {n}Rivet eyes the old woman.{/n} "Old Nan! The Lord Captain {mf|himself|herself} offers concessions! Nobody in Depot 4 has even met the {g|Encyclopedia:RogueTrader}Rogue Trader{/g}! Back down, you stubborn crone!"
- **Rivet**
  - Before: {n}The tall worker they call Rivet flinches nervously under your gaze, but he casts a glance at the old woman and says nothing.{/n}

- **Stager**

- **Old Nan**
  - Before: {n}The old woman hisses in dissatisfaction.{/n} "You two are ganging up on me, is that it? So brave you are against an old woman! But I'll shut up. I will, indeed. I won't go against two clan leaders on my own. If you want to make peace with the enforcers — make your peace."

- **Stager**
  - Before: "You can count on us, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. We'll find the cultist foulness, if any of our people have taken possession of it."

- **Rivet**

  - Before: {n}Their words seem sincere to you. Their body language and the glances traded between them reveal that the news of the attack has shocked them.{/n}

  - Before: {n}They are too tense and frightened for you to easily read their intentions. They could be telling the truth, but they could also be lying to protect themselves.{/n}

  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, my people have locked down the bay where the strikers are, including their leaders. We have the situation under control as far as resources allow."

- **Abelard**
  - Before: "What begins as petty thievery can turn into a far graver problem. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}For a split second, Vent freezes in fear, but she pulls herself together, straightens, and clips out,{/n} "Forgive me, Lord Captain. I will take steps to ensure such a thing does not happen again."

- **Avrilla Vent**

  - After: "Under control? This is near mutiny! It calls for firing squads! And you, Vent, risk charges!"

  - After: "Give the rabble a grox and they'll take an agri-world. Weapons and no enforcers mean mutiny!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!" {n}Noticing you, the two officers snap to attention and salute, their subordinates following suit a moment later.{/n}
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}!" {n}The officers salute.{/n}
- **Jocasta Sauerback**
  - Before: "The rabble understands only one language, Lord Captain: that of violence.   - After: "True. Only Vent stood up for us." {n}The scarred man throws up his arms.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, we're honest workers. We just want to work unharassed."
- **Old Nan**
  - Before: {n}The old woman's face pales, but she merely grits her teeth and spits on the floor again.{/n}
  - After: {n}The old woman pales and spits.{/n}
- **Stager**
  - Before: "Sorry, Old Nan. I'm not putting my life and my whole clan's lives on the line because of your stubbornness."
  - After: "Sorry, Old Nan. I won't risk my clan for you."
- **Old Nan**
  - Before: "And as for this amulet, or whatever it is — they took it off a dead body. There are no cultists still breathing in our sector, that's for sure. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But on this ship, the word of the Lord Captain carries more weight than a salvo from a hundred bolters. I'm sure that if the Rogue Trader addresses the malcontents directly, {mf|he|she} will quell the unrest."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Depot 4 is poor and troubled. But at worst that means drunken fights and illegal rotgut brewing. We have handled the workers of Depot 4 in the past.
