## World/Dialogs/ExplorationEvents/AncientTrap/Transmitter/Transmitter_AncientTrap_EE_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: "{petname}, grant me access to this cogitator."
  - After: "{petname}, open this cogitator."
- **Player**
  - Before: "A very fitting prank to entertain noble lords! I like it!"
  - After: "A fitting prank for noble lords! I like it!"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Investigate the entire structure]
  - After: [Investigate the structure]
- **Player**
  - Before: "I don't want to believe that this is the work of loyal subjects of the Imperium, whether of noble birth or not. Using cunning traps to exterminate xenos is a good thing. But not killing our own."
  - After: "Not loyal Imperials, I hope. Trapping xenos is fine. Killing our own isn't."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I would bet my money on ordinary thieves. Set a trap and plunder the bodies of those who get caught in it — not a bad scheme."
  - After: "My bet's on thieves. Trap people, loot the bodies."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Right now we don't have enough information to determine who did this."
  - After: "We lack the information to say who did this."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}This unsettling structure adorned in strange masks vaguely resembles the antenna of a powerful transmitter. At its base you see a {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} and a few other devices. It seems that some part of the structure is buried underground.{/n}
  - After: {n}A masked transmitter antenna, a {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g} at its base. Part is buried.{/n}
- **Servo-Skull Swarm**
  - Before: {n}The servo-skull swarm lets out a string of binharic signals, and the largest of the skulls instantly digs its mechanical drill into the side of the structure. A painful screech heralds the breaking of the machine spirit's will.{/n}
  - After: {n}A skull drills in. The machine spirit breaks.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet inspects the construction closely and draws your attention with a graceful gesture.{/n} "Look — there among all the mon-keigh gear — an Aeldari-made device. A beacon, as you would call it. I recognise other components as well. Items from other races, but they are all serving a single purpose — to call for help..."
  - After: {n}Yrliet points.{/n} "An Aeldari beacon. Devices of many races, all calling for help..."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "So, someone loaded this miserable place with transmitters from various races... in the hope that someone would land here and run into their welcoming committee? Clever. I saw similar tactics used in my years in the Navy. True, in a war zone, you are usually on high alert — you don't just hare off after a lone distress signal. But in an isolated place like this — you expect the most likely scenario, just a ship that had to make an emergency landing. It looks like plenty fell for it."
  - After: "Beacons of every race to lure ships in? Clever. Plenty fell for it."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "But who would set such an indiscriminate trap? One intended to lure in Aeldari and humans and anyone else? Who is an enemy to everyone and everything?"
  - After: "Who traps Aeldari and humans alike? Who is everyone's enemy?"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "We have a common enemy, an eternal enemy, one that devours all living things. Have we not already seen its servants on the Lilaethan and elsewhere?"
  - After: "The eternal enemy that devours all life. We saw its servants on the Lilaethan."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "I've seen it all in my life, and I can tell you one thing — this trap could be a malevolent plan by servants of Chaos. Or it could be a prank by some bored offspring of a wealthy lord, one whose parents failed to instil in him the barest speck of self-awareness."
  - After: "A Chaos plot. Or a prank by some bored lord's brat."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Don't pretend your kind wouldn't be saying the same thing about us humans."
  - After: "Your kind would say the same of humans."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "It's possible, very possible... But I'm not convinced. There's something strange about this — it's highly suspicious."
  - After: "Possible... But something's suspicious here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You identify a number of elements of the structure — the long-range antenna of a design standard for Imperial colonies, the {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}, the Aeldari beacon, and half a dozen other devices of varied origin. They all have one thing in common — this tech is designed to transmit basic signals to neighbouring space, the most common being requests for assistance and ship distress codes.{/n}
  - After: {n}An Imperial antenna, the {g|Encyclopedia:Cogitator}cogitator{/g}, an Aeldari beacon: all sending distress codes.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}This mishmash of wires, devices, and decorative details appears to be a mixture of technologies from different eras and even of different races — some of the items show signs of xenos origin.{/n}
  - After: {n}Tech from different eras and races, some xenos.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You manage to penetrate the cogitator's defences. Its function is rather simple — the program is designed to activate the transmitter once every five years and send out a ship distress signal into space.{/n}
  - After: {n}You crack it. Every five years it sends a distress signal.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The cogitator is well protected against unauthorised access. What is more, your attempt to penetrate these defences causes it to turn off and no longer show signs of life.{/n}
  - After: {n}The defences hold. The cogitator shuts down for good.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You destroy the program and disable the transmitter. No one will respond to this sinister signal ever again.{/n}
  - After: {n}You disable the transmitter. No one will answer it again.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You set the charges carefully. Without a doubt, the structure will be destroyed with expert precision along with the underground part.{/n}
  - After: {n}Expert charges. It will all go, underground part too.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You set the charges and hope that it will be enough to destroy the entire structure along with the underground part... without hurting you.{/n}
  - After: {n}You set charges and hope they destroy it, not you.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Noticing the interest with which Pasqal is surveying the construct, Heinrix asks,{/n} "Are you studying the device? Isn't its very existence a violation of the protocols of assembly?"
  - After: {n}Heinrix eyes Pasqal.{/n} "Doesn't it violate the protocols of assembly?"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}The Tech-Priest's tone is pensive, and his visor flashes:{/n} "This statement is true. This construct has been assembled in contravention of canon law and must certainly be disassembled. But not quite yet."
  - After: {n}Visor flashing:{/n} "True. It breaks canon law and must be disassembled. Not yet."
- **Servo-Skull Swarm**
  - Before: {n}The swarm's anxiously flickering lumens signify that it has managed to extract additional information from the device and is eager to share it with you. As soon as you look over at the servo-skulls, they begin to move.{/n}
  - After: {n}The swarm found more. It starts moving.{/n}
- **Servo-Skull Swarm**
  - Before: {n}The swarm hovers near a wall of ice and emits a binharic trill. There must be something hidden behind it.{/n}
  - After: {n}The swarm trills at an ice wall. Something's behind it.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: {n}Abelard shakes his head in annoyance.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, would you like me to set up a shooting gallery on the ship? With live predators as targets? Set in a miniature forest? You can go hunting, satisfy your daring that way. That would be a suitable entertainment for a noble {mf|lord|lady}. But 'pranks' like this one are a disgrace to Humanity, plain and simple."
  - After: {n}Abelard frowns.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, hunt animals, like a noble {mf|lord|lady}. 'Pranks' like this disgrace Humanity."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Ah, I see. Killing xenos who respond to this distress call is acceptable to you."
  - After: "So killing xenos who answer suits you."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The bright daylight cannot pierce the darkness lying over the slopes. The longer you look into its depth, the stronger the feeling grows that this darkness isn't just an absence of light. It is something immeasurably vast, endless, capable of reaching the farthest stars or swallowing a galaxy... Through sheer force of will, you avert your gaze.{/n}
  - After: {n}Daylight can't pierce this darkness. It feels vast enough to swallow a galaxy. You look away.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You lunge forward, but fall, as if someone has grabbed hold of your legs. Your bloodcurdling scream rings in your ears as darkness envelops you in a suffocating wave, pouring into your mouth, nose, eyes, into your very soul...{/n}
  - After: {n}You trip as if grabbed. Screaming, darkness floods into you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You gather your willpower and try to push the thing out of your head. But you and the darkness are still sharing your thoughts, and instead of retreating, it sinks its psychic tentacles even deeper into your brain.{/n}
  - After: {n}You try to expel it. It digs its psychic tentacles deeper.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...you find yourself on the floor of an abandoned estate. You feel someone's disgusting presence behind you, and raspy, foul breath tickles your nostrils.   - After: {n}...you wake in an abandoned estate. Something breathes behind you. The door is open. Now or never.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}At the edge of your consciousness, you sense something slimy and intangible answering your invitation for contact. It seeps into your thoughts, tasting your emotions. Surprise and curiosity envelop you, but these feelings are not your own.{/n}
  - After: {n}Something slimy answers, tasting your emotions with curiosity.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You turn around, intent on killing the Thing with your bare hands, but then exclaim in hesitation — you recognise the disfigured monster that is staring at you balefully from the darkness. You let out a heavy sigh, and a cloud of hot, fetid vapour settles on the smooth surface of the mirror.{/n}
  - After: {n}You turn to fight, then falter. The monster is your reflection.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You gather your thoughts and strike up a conversation with the unseen creature. You tell it about yourself and your crew, about how you do not remember how you got here but would like to avoid conflict. You feel the fear retreat and take the first step toward the creature...{/n}
  - After: {n}You tell the creature you want no conflict. Fear retreats. You step closer...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You clutch the knife in your hand and strike. You are lying on the ground, some distance away from the hole, surrounded by your worried comrades. Looking around, you realise that someone is missing.{/n}
  - After: {n}You stab and gorge on blood... until a slap wakes you by the hole. Someone is missing.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As your brothers and sisters surround you, you release your powers and consume every last one of them. For ten thousand days and as many nights, you battle their souls until you subdue them completely. Immortal, you remain on the throne for thousands of years, watching your civilisation blossom, die, and fade into darkness.{/n}
  - After: {n}You devour your siblings' souls. Immortal, you watch your civilisation bloom and fade.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Solemnly, you are placed on a cold black slab covered in glowing script. You close your eyes and pray as your brothers and sisters rip your seven hearts out of your chest. By the end of the ceremony, they are gnawing on every last bone of your body, shedding tears of sorrow. You join your ancestors within the black monolith, and for many centuries thereafter, you watch from above as your civilisation blossoms.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You approach the altar covered in glowing script and change it to the symbols you saw in the abandoned camp — in some other life of yours.   - After: {n}You alter the altar's script to the camp's symbols. As your seven hearts are torn out, the sky splits and thousands scream. You're already gone.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...you are lying on burning sand, struggling to open your eyes, but your eyelids feel too heavy. You can barely move your arms and legs, your stomach hurts, your throat is bone-dry.   - After: {n}...you lie on burning sand among starving kin. A knife clinks by your hand. You MUST survive. Choose whom to sacrifice.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You are hit by a sudden wave of all-consuming silence. A moment later, the world around you disappears, leaving only black, viscous, boundless darkness. The absoluteness of it is overwhelming, and you slowly sink into the void that is sucking you in.{/n}
  - After: {n}Total silence. The world vanishes into black, boundless darkness, and you sink.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The moment you approach the darkness amassing beneath your feet, something immediately takes root in your thoughts and emotions, much more forcefully this time. Your mind fogs over, and silent insistence spreads throughout your body.{/n}
  - After: {n}As you approach, something seizes your mind. Your thoughts fog.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You turn around and walk away from the ominous pit and its secrets. You run for dear life, get back to your ship, go to a different system... And when you wake up the next morning — the darkness is once again staring at you from beyond the edge of the pit.{/n}
  - After: {n}You leave, play {g|Encyclopedia:Regicide}regicide{/g}, sleep... and wake at the abyss. You flee systems. It finds you again.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...you are looking at a tiny person peeking over the edge of the bottomless darkness. You are looking at yourself. Then you blink and see the same place, except the camp around you is full of life. A moment later, they are all nude, singing and dancing around the pit. The smell of heated bodies, blood, and sweat assaults your nostrils, drowning out your thoughts... one by one, the lunatics fall into the embrace of nothingness.{/n}
  - After: {n}...you see yourself at the edge. Then scholars fill the camp. Then they dance naked around the pit and fall in, one by one.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: {n}Heinrix peers into the darkness in the depths of the pit. You feel the touch of an otherworldly chill. The Interrogator arches an eyebrow.{/n} "Whatever this — hmm — phenomenon may be, there is no warp sorcery within it."
  - After: {n}Heinrix peers in. An otherworldly chill.{/n} "Whatever this is, it's not warp sorcery."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Creepy..." {n}Idira tilts her head to the side, listening to something. Then she scowls and spits on the ground.{/n} "Grox knows what it is. It's beyond my remit."
  - After: "Creepy..." {n}Idira listens, then spits.{/n} "Grox knows. Beyond me."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Again you run, again you change one system after another, you go without sleep for several days... Yet it happens all over again. You spend months, or it could be years, in desperate flight. At some point, you simply give up. With resignation, you sit down at the edge of the pit, no longer moving. Alien satisfaction fills your mind.{/n}
  - After: {n}You flee for months, maybe years. At last you sit by the pit. Alien satisfaction fills you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The streams of fate were changed when you defeated fear and docility. With all your strength, you cling to the vision and do not let go until the darkness yields. The entity shows you the process of an incredible transformation and you cannot hold back tears at the sight of it. And yet, the human brain cannot fully comprehend something like this. As soon as the vision fades, you realise that you remember absolutely nothing. And still, some inscrutable warmth spreads throughout your body.{/n}
  - After: {n}You hold the vision until the darkness yields and shows you a wondrous transformation. You weep, then forget it all. Warmth remains.{/n}

  - Before: {n}You try to cut the beast's flesh again and again, but the blade cannot pierce its thick fur. You raise your knife for a desperate strike... but then a powerful shove brings you back to your senses.   - After: {n}Your blade can't pierce the beast's fur... A shove wakes you at the pit's edge. Ulfar shakes his head.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You raise the knife up high... when the youth suddenly bares his teeth and strikes you first, too quickly for you to react in time. The pain causes your consciousness to come rushing back. You find yourself standing at the edge of the bottomless pit, with a bleeding stab wound on your body, surrounded by your worried companions, one of whom, Marazhai, is staring at you ferociously, clutching a bloodied Drukhari dagger.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...you make out toadlike xenos building a temple around the pit. They are praying, conducting rites, making sacrifices to the darkness in hopes of unimaginable gifts. Then darkness shrouds everything once more. Or rather, you are the darkness. Something immeasurably vast, endless, capable of reaching the farthest stars or swallowing a galaxy. But some will pulls you out of the cosy embrace of the void, toward the light... And you snap out of the vision as sorrow fills you from within.{/n}
  - After: {n}...toadlike xenos worship the pit. Then you are the darkness, vast. A will drags you out, and you wake in sorrow.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You swing to strike, but one of the heads lunges out at an impossible angle and bites you...   - After: {n}A head bites you... You wake at the edge, hand in Glaito's jaws. Solomorne calls the cyber-mastiff off.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...you sit at the apex of a massive onyx pyramid. Your abilities are limitless — with a single thought, you can raise mountains, drain an ocean, or disperse the clouds.   - After: {n}...atop an onyx pyramid, your power is limitless. Soon your siblings will sacrifice you to share it.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You can sense the darkness's triumph. It has been following your thoughts with great interest, rummaging in your memories, studying your emotions, savouring your resolve and rage — its bottomless gut rumbles with satisfaction. At last, grateful, it lets you go and presents a parting reward.{/n}
  - After: {n}Sated by your resolve and rage, the darkness releases you with a reward.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You sense the darkness rampaging inside your mind, unable to fathom humanity. At some point, its desperation gives way to resolve — it needs new specimens for its studies. The darkness retreats, having lost all interest in you as an individual.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Solemnly, you are placed on a cold black slab covered in glowing script, but at the last moment, your love for your people fails you. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As your brothers and sisters surround you, you release your powers, but your attack is met with desperate resistance. When the last of your kind is finished, you feel completely drained and can only watch helplessly as the dark figures of your enemies draw closer and closer...{/n}

  - Before: {n}You feel your way to the barely tangible edges of the entity's consciousness, separate it from yourself, and squeeze it until it is reduced to the size of a bead.   - Before: {n}You bite down on your belt and cut off a piece of your own flesh. The pain is so terrible that your vision darkens. Unable to bear it, you let out a frenzied groan, but you still shove the slimy scrap into your mouth and swallow it.{/n}

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You summon your courage and dash through the open door. Your will to live guides you through the deserted halls of the estate, and the Thing is right at your heels. At some point, you smash open a window and see your crew — unmoving fossils among withered plants...{/n}

## World/Dialogs/ExplorationEvents/HaloDevice/HaloDeviceWear/HaloDeviceWear_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "Did I hear that right? Did you just say immortality?"
  - After: "Did you say immortality?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The ingenious creation of an unknown craftsman shimmers, hypnotising you with its faintly glowing patterns. The trinket is so captivating, you cannot take your eyes off it. When you try to shift it into your other hand, you notice that it can barely separate from your skin — there are thousands of fine flagella stretching between the surface and your palm. You tear the device off with effort and see countless tiny droplets of scarlet left behind.{/n}
  - After: {n}The glowing trinket hypnotises you. Its flagella cling; tearing it off draws blood.{/n}
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "A Halo device." {n}Heinrix reaches out sharply and pries the mysterious object from your hand.{/n} "A cursed xenos creation that twists the mind, and soon the body, of its master. An item subject to the Inquisition's general decree of total annihilation. In this matter, my authority exceeds your privilege, Lord Captain."
  - After: "A Halo device." {n}Heinrix snatches it.{/n} "Cursed xenos tech, marked for destruction by the Inquisition. My authority exceeds yours here, Lord Captain."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet looks at the object in your hands and shakes her head with concern.{/n} "Get rid of it, elantach. This creation is the fruit of ancient and twisted minds that tempt the weak with the promise of eternal youth and life unending. You have seen the price it exacts with your own eyes."
  - After: {n}Yrliet frowns.{/n} "Get rid of it, elantach. It tempts the weak with eternal life. You've seen the price."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai slightly narrows his eyes.{/n} "I have seen similar devices among the trophies of the Kabal. I do not know who created them, but it is hard to deny their devious ingenuity. In exchange for immortality, they turn their prey into something similar to what inhabited these chambers until recently."
  - After: {n}Marazhai squints.{/n} "Kabal trophies. They grant immortality, and turn prey into what lived here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Everything inside you screams in terror, and your body shakes in pain as you try to rip off the device. The area of skin touched by the brooch burns as if it has been grazed by a miniature melta charge, yet you manage to tear the xenos creation from your flesh.{/n}
  - After: {n}In burning pain, you rip it free.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You swing wildly and hurl the mysterious device as hard as you can through one of the broken windows of the hall. Now only the God-Emperor knows where to look for it, and perhaps that is for the best.{/n}
  - After: {n}You hurl it out a window. Only the God-Emperor knows where.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "That is enough, elantach!" {n}Yrliet swiftly knocks the device out of your hand. It tumbles away into the darkness until a distant thud announces that it has fallen into the wreckage.{/n} "I will not allow you to destroy yourself!"
  - After: "Enough, elantach!" {n}Yrliet knocks it away.{/n} "I won't let you destroy yourself!"
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}The Drukhari's movement is almost too swift to be registered by the eye. Marazhai slaps the device out of your hand with a perfunctory swing. The mysterious artefact flies off into the darkness and, judging by the clatter, falls through some crevice. The xenos turns his gaze to you.{/n} "No, {name}. No trinket will ever compete with me for your attention."
  - After: {n}Marazhai slaps it into a crevice.{/n} "No, {name}. No trinket competes with me for your attention."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "If one could call it that. Would you like to become a bloated husk like the one we encountered? I doubt it."
  - After: "Of a sort. Want to be a bloated husk like that one? I doubt it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A shot, a torch, a sharp rock, you go through several ways to break the xeno-artefact, but your efforts are futile. Not a single scratch appears on the smooth surface. All the while you sense something strange — you hear ringing in your ears and the metallic taste of raw meat in your mouth.{/n}
  - After: {n}Nothing scratches it. Your ears ring; you taste raw meat.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The patterns on the device glow brighter the closer you bring it to yourself. The lack of fasteners and the vague visions in your head tell you that the brooch should be placed against your bare skin, not worn on your clothes. As soon as the artefact touches your body, the skin underneath it burns, your heart races, and your head feels like it is being squeezed by an adamantine garrotte.{/n}
  - After: {n}Visions say: bare skin. It touches you. Skin burns, heart races, your skull is squeezed.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The artefact quickly embeds itself in your skin and bliss spreads through your veins. Small scratches heal, and your battle-weary limbs grow strong. You are full of energy, and the only thing bothering you is mild pangs of hunger spurred on by the smell of blood.{/n}
  - After: {n}It embeds itself. Bliss. Wounds heal. Blood smells appetising.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: {n}Yrliet gives you a hard look{/n} "Immortality at a price far worse than death. Cast out the thoughts I am now reading on your face."
  - After: {n}Yrliet stares.{/n} "Immortality worse than death. Cast out those thoughts."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Everything inside you screams in terror, and your body shakes in pain as you try to rip off the device. Your mind yields, and you let the object do its work.{/n}
  - After: {n}You try to rip it off. Your mind yields.{/n}

  - After: "Who are you? Speak!"

  - After: "Fascinating accessory. I'm taking it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "The Halo Device should not have gone to such a weakling. I will take it."
  - After: "Wasted on a weakling. I'll take the Halo Device."

  - Before: "I will put an end to your eternal life and destroy the artefact."
  - After: "I'll end your eternal life and destroy the artefact."
- **Corrupted Noble**
  - Before: {n}A lushly dressed, vaguely human-like carcass sits reclined in a massive Calixian oak armchair. Calloused brownish-blue patches cover the dead flesh, overlapping one another like snake scales. One of the hands, claws of exposed bone, supports a grotesquely bloated face.{/n}
  - After: {n}A bloated, scaled carcass in fine clothes slumps in a Calixian oak armchair.{/n}

  - Before: {n}Heinrix raises a hand, commanding you to stop, and then presses an index finger to his lips. His face is more tense than usual, and there is a semblance of doubt in his eyes. The Interrogator gestures toward the exit.{/n}
  - After: {n}Heinrix signals silence, uneasy, and points to the exit.{/n}

  - Before: "For research purposes, I hope?" {n}The Tech-Priest tilts his head.{/n} "The long-term effects of bearing such a... thing that you may see before you, Rogue Trader. They are, I believe, depressingly illustrative."
  - After: "For research?" {n}He tilts his head.{/n} "Its effects sit before you."
- **Corrupted Noble**
  - Before: {n}The creature's chest remains motionless and its eyes stay tightly closed. And yet the muscles on the distorted face twitch ever so briskly when you approach.{/n}
  - After: {n}Breathless, eyes shut. Its face twitches as you near.{/n}
- **Corrupted Noble**
  - Before: {n}The creature's chest remains motionless and its eyes stay tightly closed. It is hard to say whether it is dead, asleep, or merely lying in wait.{/n}
  - After: {n}Breathless, eyes shut. Dead, or waiting?{/n}
- **Corrupted Noble**

  - After: "Wel-come to my fe-ast..." {n}A glowing scarab brooch is lodged in what was once a man.{/n}

  - Before: "W-what?.." {n}Cassia covers her mouth with both hands, trying to speak quietly even as her body is shaking. The Lady Navigator's wide open eyes are brimming with terror.{/n} "I... I want to leave this place... Right now!"
  - After: "W-what?.." {n}Cassia trembles.{/n} "I want to leave. Now!"

  - Before: {n}Argenta draws her weapon, looks at you, and cocks a questioning eyebrow.{/n}
  - After: {n}Argenta draws, eyebrow raised.{/n}

- **Corrupted Noble**
  - Before: {n}Sharp scales break away from the dense skin with every shot as the creature's flesh explodes, reducing its ugly carcass to a bloody pulp. The mutilated face, completely stripped of skin, and even bones, grins at you with the demented smile of a severed jaw.{/n}

- **Jae**
  - Before: "Light of the Throne..." {n}Jae clutches the Aquila, looking at the creature's corpse with disgust.{/n} "I had to deal with mutants both in the sewers of Footfall and in the depths of the underhives. But this one... Did you see his eyes? They burn like embers in the empty eye sockets."

  - Before: {n}You have heard of the powerful xeno-artefacts from the distant Halo stars, discovered by Humanity millennia ago. - **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The accessory must have been a brooch at some point, but burrowed into the owner's flesh for some inscrutable reason.{/n}

- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Rogue Trader, stay back!" {n}Heinrix grabs his weapon, and the air around you shimmers with otherworldly frost.{/n} "The bearers of the Halo Devices pose a grave threat even to the finest agents of the Inquisition. They are fast, strong, immune to poisons, and..." {n}Heinrix stammers.{/n} "...immortal."
  - After: "Rogue Trader, back!" {n}Frost shimmers.{/n} "Halo bearers are fast, strong, poison-immune, and..." {n}He stammers.{/n} "...immortal."
- **Jae**

The price of immortality..." {n}Jae presses the Aquila to her lips.{/n} "Not even in my own heart does the flame of greed burn hotly enough to betray Humanity and stain my soul forever."
  - After: "Halo Oculus... Cold Trader legends from the Koronus Expanse and Calixis Sector. Wealth and power beyond Rogue Traders." {n}Jae kisses her Aquila.{/n} "No greed would make me betray Humanity."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Bethink yourself, {name}! Every educated nobleman knows of the bloody consequences that befell the Rogue Traders Balastia Irem, Rath Longinus, and Edward Maissus in the fifth century of this millennium. Do not follow in their blood-stained footsteps!"
  - After: "Think, {name}! Remember Balastia Irem, Rath Longinus and Edward Maissus. Don't follow their bloody steps!"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "It is not dead. It is dead, but in the wrong way. It's not—" {n}Kibellah bows her head as if ashamed of her muddled explanation, then places a hand on her weapon.{/n} "I ask your permission to fix... that."
  - After: "It's dead, but wrongly—" {n}Kibellah touches her weapon.{/n} "May I fix that?"
- **Heinrix**
  - Before: "Need I remind you that Halo Devices are highly illegal? And that anyone, from a lowly smuggler to a mighty Rogue Trader, will be burned alive for their possession and use? Such is the fate of all who succumb to the vile temptation of xenoheresy."
  - After: "Halo Devices are illegal. Owners burn alive for xenoheresy."
- **Corrupted Noble**
  - Before: "Brah'ts onk vfsteh'kh omss pk'nglf. E rh'st kho. Am je!" {n}The Elucidator fails to interpret the twisted speech taking root in your mind like a pestilent weed. The creature contentedly smacks its lips.{/n} "I will fi-nal-ly... tas-te the sa-vou-ry fle-sh... a-gain!"
  - After: "Brah'ts onk vfsteh'kh omss pk'nglf. E rh'st kho. Am je!" {n}Untranslatable.{/n} "I will tas-te fle-sh... a-gain!"

  - Before: "The penalty for blasphemy against the Machine God is inevitable annihilation. Initiate the abjuration protocols and commence sanctification through destruction."
  - After: "Blasphemy against the Machine God means annihilation. Destroy it."
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "If you ask my opinion, I would make sure to point out that bringing such rubbish onto a voidship is irresponsible. Leave it to rot on this Emperor-forsaken world."
  - After: "Bringing that aboard is irresponsible. Leave it to rot."
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: "But you did consider it. You appraised the benefit and calculated the price." {n}Kibellah's lips twist into a cold smile.{/n} "And you found the limit of your lust for profit no sooner than hitting the lowest depths of heresy."
  - After: "But you considered it." {n}Kibellah smiles coldly.{/n} "Greed stopped only at heresy."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "The fact that it is operational is a phenomenon, but an ominous one. I advise we retreat, Rogue Trader." {n}Eogunn tightens his mechadendrite around the grip of his weapon.{/n}
  - After: "Operational. Ominous. Retreat, Rogue Trader." {n}Eogunn grips his weapon.{/n}
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "Inconceivable..." {n}Eogunn, however, moves a step closer, forgetting all caution.{/n} "A mythologeme made flesh. I've heard of the Halo Oculus and the immortality it brings, but those were just profane rumours. Should any drop of it prove true, the bearer of this artefact is a priceless specimen for analysis."
  - After: "Inconceivable..." {n}Eogunn steps closer.{/n} "The Halo Oculus made flesh! Its bearer is a priceless specimen."

## World/Dialogs/ExplorationEvents/SpaceScavengers/ChiefScavenger/ChiefScavenger_EE_dialog

- **Player**
  - Before: "I will buy the component."
  - After: "I'll buy the component."
- **Player**
  - Before: "This component doesn't belong to you. I will simply confiscate it."
  - After: "It's not yours. I'm confiscating it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I'm not interested."
  - After: "Not interested."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Think carefully now — are you sure you want to defy a Rogue Trader and all the power {mf|he|she} has at {mf|his|her} disposal? I need but give the order — and there won't be a single cinder left of your entire colony."
  - After: "You'd defy a Rogue Trader and all the power {mf|he|she} commands? One order from {mf|his|her} lips and your colony burns."
- **Player**
  - Before: [Attack] "You have the gall to oppose my will. I will not stand for it."
  - After: [Attack] "You dare oppose my will? I won't stand for it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I must take my leave."
  - After: "I must go."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You take pride in your trade, I see."
  - After: "You take pride in your trade."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Nonsense. There are those who are great and those who are nothing — that is the nature of things."
  - After: "Nonsense. Some are great, some are nothing — that's nature."
- **Player**
  - Before: "There is something to your philosophy."
  - After: "Your philosophy has merit."
- **Player**
  - Before: "You speak as if the world is set in stone and none of us can change anything for the better."
  - After: "You talk as if nothing can be changed for the better."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Do not dare talk back to me. Another word about me thinking too highly of myself, and I'll leave you in no doubt about your place."
  - After: "Don't talk back. One more word and I'll show you your place."
- **Player**
  - Before: "I can take you from this place. It's not safe here, and sooner or later, it will drift somewhere so remote that nobody will ever find you again."
  - After: "I can take you away. This wreck is unsafe and will drift where no one finds you."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Would you believe it — well-spoken rabble! It is rather sweet in its own way. Go on, then, amuse me. Tell me about yourself and this place."
  - After: "Well-spoken rabble! How sweet. Amuse me — tell me about yourself and this place."
- **Player**
  - Before: "It's unlikely, but I want to ask — you haven't come across any Imperial stamps in your 'searching,' have you?"
  - After: "Found any Imperial stamps in your 'searching'?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A tired-looking woman of indeterminate age, clad in work clothes, breaks off from her task to greet you. She freezes momentarily, clearly unsure how to address you, then says simply,{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, please excuse me, I don't really know your name. Welcome to our little colony. May the light of the Emperor be with you — and with us. My name's Reta Machsimova, I'm in charge here."
  - After: {n}A tired worker greets you.{/n} "Welcome, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I'm Reta Machsimova, in charge here."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Hope you don't judge me too harshly and don't take it as insolence, but some people — even big people like you — think too highly of themselves. Let's say your ship hops into the warp someday and doesn't hop out of it in time. And around a thousand years later, another gal like myself, who needs to feed her three ankle-biters somehow, will be rifling through its remains, looking for anything good. That's just the nature of things — each of us comes and goes, but the way the world works stays the same. We all have our lot in life, and mine is just as good as any other."
  - After: "No offence, but big folk think too highly of themselves. Your ship might die in the warp, and some gal like me will pick through it. The world stays the same. My lot's as good as any."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "And about fifteen years ago, back before I had my first little one, a ship took three crews to locations and ran into pirates on the way back. The ships go out on expeditions for years at a time, so it was ages before anyone realised they were missing, and it was even longer before they remembered the scavengers, plus it took some time to find a ship that could check on them and pick them up. Long story short... all three crews had bought it. Yep."
  - After: "Fifteen years back, pirates hit the ship that dropped three crews. Nobody fetched them in time. All three died."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Well, isn't this something! The Emperor Himself must've smiled upon us!" {n}Reta makes a triumphant gesture.{/n} "I mean, uh, thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. You'll be pleased with the results."
  - After: "The Emperor smiles on us!" {n}Reta beams.{/n} "Thank you, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Reta pales a little but lifts her chin with determination.{/n} "We risked our lives to find this thing and pull it out. This is our trade, it's what feeds our families. We can't just give it away, that wouldn't be right — or fair."
  - After: {n}Reta pales.{/n} "We risked our lives for this. It feeds our families. It's not fair."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We just call ourselves Reta's Crew and this place is Reta's Camp, that's it. We're recolligers. Scavengers, in common terms." {n}She does not speak the word "scavengers" with any kind of disdain — on the contrary, there is dignity in her voice, the kind with which one would announce their affiliation with a respected guild or family.{/n}
  - After: "We're Reta's Crew, this is Reta's Camp. Recolligers — scavengers." {n}She says it proudly.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If that'll be all, Y'{mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... you mind leaving us alone?"
  - After: "If that's all, Y'{mf|Lordship|Ladyship}... leave us be?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "This little bird's got all kinds of bells and whistles. Most of the tech is dead, but we do find working pieces now and again. We spent two whole months clearing out this shaft we found — finished just three days ago, actually — and we found this thing, a bit weird-looking but still functional." {n}Reta's expression brightens a little.{/n} "Perhaps Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} would like to buy this component from us? I'll bet that big ship you've got could get plenty of use out of it..."
  - After: "After two months clearing a shaft, we found this — odd, but working." {n}Reta brightens.{/n} "Would Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} buy it for your ship?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Sure do. It takes skill, and luck, and a good head on your shoulders. We risk our lives every day, crawling on top of these old buckets. If something goes wrong — we die, by the scores sometimes. One moment we're there, the next we're gone, kind of like worker ants. But you know what, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}? Our job also has something... how should I put it... poetic about it."
  - After: "Sure do. Takes skill and luck. We die by the scores, like ants. But there's something poetic in it, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It's been a pleasure to serve Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "A pleasure to serve Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Those are some big things you're talking about, way outta my depth. Change for the better? Heck, that'd be nice..." {n}Reta pauses to think.{/n} "If I was younger and didn't have three youngsters back home — maybe I would dream about stuff like that too. But as it is, I've got no time for dreaming — I've gotta work!"
  - After: "Change for the better? Nice..." {n}Reta pauses.{/n} "But with three youngsters home, I've no time to dream."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "It's what my gramps taught me, he was a recolliger and a foreman too. He had some fancy-schmancy thoughts in that head of his, but he lived to a ripe old age with them — in our line of work — which means those thoughts weren't all bad."
  - After: "My gramps taught me, a recolliger foreman. He lived to old age in this trade, so his thoughts weren't all bad."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "If you say so, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I'm a simple woman, living a simple life, having simple thoughts, and if I happen to blurt out some bunkum — that's just because I'm not that bright." {n}Reta shrugs.{/n}
  - After: "If you say so, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I'm simple folk." {n}Reta shrugs.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Not much, we're no eggheads, you know — we're manual labour. It's an ancient thing, pretty dangerous, and we don't really know much beyond that. Before we came here, some Tech-Priests had done their own bit of gutting... I mean ritualling, bowing to the spirits, all that. That lot don't tend to leave a whole lot of valuables behind, it's true, but it's way too scary to go in before them. And hey, we dragged a dozen of their broken servitors out of the mines after. The carcasses smell awful, but you can pluck a decent number of parts out of a servitor and sell them."
  - After: "We're labourers, not eggheads. It's ancient, dangerous. Tech-Priests gutted it first; we salvaged their dead servitors."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Doesn't seem like there's anything nasty living inside the wreck now, but the wreck itself is barely holding together. You go a couple of modules from here — and that's it, you won't take another step without fearing that a broken reactor might cook you alive, or a whole module might depressurise. Well, it's nothing we haven't handled before, so we're having a poke at it. But we don't have a clue what this ship is or who it belonged to."
  - After: "Nothing lives inside now, but it's barely holding — reactors, depressurisation. We manage. No clue whose ship it was."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Reta frowns, but nods cautiously.{/n} "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: {n}Reta frowns, nods.{/n} "As you wish, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "But this... this is our whole livelihood, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! You take us from here, and what are we gonna do — sit in some hold, slaving away? Here, we've got our own colony, our own operation. No, this is our path, and we won't stray from it."
  - After: "This is our livelihood, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}! Slave in some hold? Here we've our own colony. We stay."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "You are amusing, little mon-keigh. Your life is shorter than a moth's, and you spend it digging around in the carcass of dead, malevolent metal. But you speak of eternity and the stars. I like that. It is like seeing starlight reflected in a puddle."
  - After: "Amusing mon-keigh. A moth's life spent in dead metal, yet you speak of eternity. Starlight in a puddle."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: "Disobeying those in power is apostasy. But depriving a poor person of the little they have is no good deed either. Forgive their insolence, {name}! Let them keep what they have managed to scrape together."
  - After: "Defying power is apostasy, but robbing the poor is no good deed. Let them keep it, {name}!"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal's vox crackles to life. Imperiously, he tells her,{/n} "Present the object, laywoman," {n}but curiosity creeps into his voice nonetheless.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal's vox crackles.{/n} "Present the object, laywoman," {n}he says, curious.{/n}
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}Pasqal stares dispassionately at Reta with a hint of disgust. Evidently, he has not even considered the possibility that replying to this creature's words could be anything other than heresy.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pasqal stares at Reta in disgust.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Right now we're gutting this old heap of junk, slowly but surely. That's a recolliger's life for you — they drop us off at some decrepit station or an ancient battlefield, and we just sit there for years on end. We look for working tech, or valuable materials, or whatever else might be useful. If we find anything, we sell it to passing ships. Not the easiest job out there — these wrecks are chock-full of all kinds of dangers. But, and I swear it on my plasma torch, it's an exciting one for sure."
  - After: "Gutting this heap. We live on wrecks for years, selling finds to passing ships. Dangerous, but exciting."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Tossing a glance at Pasqal, she grimly adds,{/n} "And our work is all legal, even though your brethren have no liking for us."
  - After: {n}She glances at Pasqal.{/n} "It's legal, though your brethren hate us."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Reta shrugs.{/n} "We definitely haven't found any stamps here, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I keep a record of all the bits and bobs. Then again... Hang on, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I just remembered something..."
  - After: {n}Reta shrugs.{/n} "No stamps, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. Then again... Hang on, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}. I remember something..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Here you go, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}Reta holds out a weighty seal. There are scratches on the handle where a coat of arms should be.{/n} "I don't know if this is what you're looking for, but we got this thing in a trade with some shady bloke years back. My father thought it was something important, so it's just been gathering dust until today. Take it as a gift — we have no use for it anyway."
  - After: "Here, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}." {n}A heavy seal, its arms scratched off.{/n} "Traded from a shady bloke years back. Take it as a gift."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}..." {n}Reta falters, as if flustered by her own nerve.{/n} "Please don't take it as insolence, but it's not like I have much choice... It's not often that we get well-stocked ships around here, and we could certainly use more provisions and some warm clothes. If it's something you would be willing to provide, we would gladly barter for it with whatever we can dig up inside this here ship. It's just a respectful offer of fair trade." {n}She bows slightly before stepping aside.{/n}
  - After: "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}..." {n}Reta falters.{/n} "We need provisions and warm clothes. We'd barter whatever we dig up here." {n}She bows.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The woman grimly adds as she casts a glance at Eogunn,{/n} "And our work is perfectly lawful, though we are not popular among your fellows."
  - After: {n}She glances at Eogunn.{/n} "It's lawful, though your kind dislike us."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: {n}The Manipulus fixes the woman with a calculating look, as though weighing whether she is a speaker worthy of his time. At last, he speaks:{/n} "I wish neither to confirm nor deny this claim."
  - After: {n}Eogunn regards her coldly.{/n} "I neither confirm nor deny this."
- **Eogunn**
  - Before: "First, present the object for inspection. It might only hold value in your eyes." {n}Eogunn extends his hand with a sharp, commanding gesture of impatience.{/n}
  - After: "Present the object. Its value may be imagined." {n}Eogunn holds out his hand.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "No, not even close. A luxury like that? You could count the recolligers who got their own ship on one hand — an old worker's hand that got sucked into machinery three times and slashed by a plasma cutter twice."
  - After: "Hardly. Recolligers with ships? Count them on one mangled hand."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "We fly with whoever, mostly just taking our chances. Sometimes we hitch a ride on the promise that we'll pay with what we find later, other times we find some other means... Risky business, obviously. Five or so years back, a crew got dropped off at an abandoned station, but something wasn't right with the life support systems. The ship came back to pick them up two years later, and found nothing but bodies."
  - After: "We hitch rides. Risky. Five years back, a crew's life support failed. Their ship found only bodies."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Reta clenches her fists, her eyes narrowing slightly. Her gaze darts over your gear and weapons, as if assessing the threat. When she finally speaks, you can tell she is forcing the words out.{/n} "In that case... take it."
  - After: {n}Reta clenches her fists.{/n} "Then... take it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It is easy to tell by the gritted teeth and narrowed eyes what kind of battle is raging inside Reta — a battle between fear and pride. Pride wins.{/n} "No need to throw your weight around. We may be rabble, rummaging through old, rusted scrap from birth to death, but we value our labour."
  - After: {n}Pride beats fear in Reta.{/n} "No need to throw your weight around. We're rabble, but we value our labour."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Her mood visibly improves.{/n} "You know, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, it's kind of embarrassing to offer you this, but over in that corner there, we keep things we don't rightly understand or can't really use. You could send some of your people to check it out if you'd like... clearly you know more about this stuff than us. You might find something useful."
  - After: {n}She cheers up.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, that corner holds things we can't use. Have your people look."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "A shame, that. But it's your call, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."
  - After: "Shame. Your call, Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}."

## World/Dialogs/ExplorationEvents/StryxShed/ BrainLeaf/ BrainLeaf_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Reach out and touch a leaf]
  - After: [Touch a leaf]
- **Player**
  - Before: [Order somebody else to touch a leaf]
  - After: [Order someone to touch it]
- **Player**
  - Before: "Abelard, kindly pluck a leaf for me."
  - After: "Abelard, pluck a leaf."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Can you help me, Argenta?"
  - After: "Argenta, help?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "Idira, the fate of this plant is literally in your hands."
  - After: "Idira, it's in your hands."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Don't you love nature, Yrliet? Save the poor flower."
  - After: "Yrliet, save the flower."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Lady Cassia, since you have taken an interest in this plant..."
  - After: "Lady Cassia, it interests you..."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Pasqal, can you help? Purely for research purposes."
  - After: "Pasqal, for research?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Pick several leaves for further research]
  - After: [Pick leaves for research]
- **Player**
  - Before: "Marazhai, you will be the one to carry it if you want it so badly."
  - After: "Marazhai, you want it — carry it."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Ulfar, my friend, if you will?"
  - After: "Ulfar, my friend?"
- **Player**
  - Before: [Step away and leave the plant alone]
  - After: [Leave the plant]
- **Player**
  - Before: "Kibellah, I require a sample."
  - After: "Kibellah, a sample."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Solomorne, bring me a leaf, please."
  - After: "Solomorne, a leaf, please."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Eogunn, does such an unusual life form not interest you?"
  - After: "Eogunn, interested in this life form?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A grey, unsightly vine winds through the surviving remnants of the cage, almost merging with the cold stone of the depot. Each tendril of the ragged plant is topped with a single leaf, shrivelled but still alive.{/n}
  - After: {n}A grey vine with shrivelled, living leaves winds through the cage.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You have heard the stories about the unfortunate souls who were careless enough to get too close to the "brain leaf." Its fleshy fronds, each with a semblance of individual consciousness, merge with the nervous system of its victims, turning them into mindless carrier puppets.{/n}
  - After: {n}A "brain leaf." Its fronds merge with victims' nerves, making mindless puppets.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}This is the first time you have encountered such a plant. It is unknown whether the ivy is the last specimen of the native fauna or part of the collection that belongs to the owner of this place.{/n}
  - After: {n}An unknown plant. Native, or collected?{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You cast a glance at your companions.{/n}
  - After: {n}You glance at your companions.{/n}
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai examines the grey leaves with genuine interest, then shifts his gaze to you and back again, keeping a respectable distance from both.{/n}
  - After: {n}Marazhai eyes the leaves from afar.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "How strange... This ivy coloured its surroundings in a caustic green, just like a predator singles out its prey before pouncing. Never before have I seen a plant able to cast its own colour."
  - After: "Strange... It stains things green, like a predator marking prey."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Lord Captain, my friends from the other side are whispering. They say it would be great to shelter this here broom with us. But I will say it is best not to open the door too wide when they start knocking from the other side."
  - After: "Lord Captain, my friends beyond want this broom. Keep the door shut."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The grey vine still hangs sadly from the wreckage just like it did a moment ago.{/n}
  - After: {n}The grey vine still hangs there.{/n}
- **Abelard**
  - Before: "But of course. This is a task for the Seneschal."
  - After: "Of course. A task for the Seneschal."
- **Argenta**
  - Before: {n}Argenta nods eagerly.{/n} "To rescue a living being from a prison of darkness and stone is a small, but noble deed."
  - After: {n}Argenta nods.{/n} "A small, noble rescue."
- **Idira**
  - Before: "Don't say poor Idira didn't warn you." {n}The woman winces and cautiously reaches for the wilted wine.{/n}
  - After: "Idira warned you." {n}She winces and reaches out.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "You are right, elantach. The poor thing has been suffering in the dark for a very long time."
  - After: "Yes, elantach. It has suffered long."
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "Thank you, but I will have to decline such dubious pleasure. My eyes are watering from the acrid green that surrounds its leaves. If it were up to me, I would order to have them chopped up right away!"
  - After: "I decline. Its green stings my eyes. Chop it up!"
- **Pasqal**
  - Before: {n}The mechadendrites swiftly and accurately pluck several fleshy leaves, deposit them in a container, and put it into your hands.{/n} "Organic life forms are not considered a research priority. However, I find your thirst for knowledge impressive."
  - After: {n}Mechadendrites box some leaves for you.{/n} "Organics are low priority. Your curiosity impresses."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}The interest in Marazhai's face vanishes in the blink of an eye.{/n} "I'm not going to waste my time on this. Tell someone else to do it."
  - After: {n}Marazhai's interest vanishes.{/n} "Ask someone else."
- **Ulfar**
  - Before: {n}Ulfar looks at the plant disbelievingly.{/n} "No, Aett-Vater. He who was born on Fenris and has learned its harsh lessons can smell danger. And I say this is a baneful vine. Burn it and be done with it."
  - After: {n}Ulfar balks.{/n} "No, Aett-Vater. This vine is baneful. Burn it."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The meaty leaf falls onto your metal prosthetic with a slap and settles down listlessly. You wait for a while, but nothing happens.{/n}
  - After: {n}The leaf slaps onto your prosthetic. Nothing happens.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}It takes an incredible effort to remain conscious, even though your body is acting against your will. You realise you are reaching for your weapon. You blink and see it in your hand. Then you blink again.{/n}
  - After: {n}Barely conscious, you find your weapon in hand. You blink again.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}And so you leave to do what you must, never to return.{/n}
  - After: {n}You leave to do what you must, never to return.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You stretch out your hand toward the grey vine and touch the wilted leaf. A sharp pain pierces the back of your palm, but after a moment it is gone — and so is everything else. The room wavers, the floor and ceiling change places, and your stomach turns inside out.{/n}
  - After: {n}Pain pierces your palm. Then the room spins, and everything is gone.{/n}
- **Cassia**
  - Before: "N-no, I... Although perhaps you are right." {n}Cassia comes closer and touches one of the leaves with a sharpened claw.{/n} "Ow!"
  - After: "N-no... perhaps." {n}Cassia touches a leaf.{/n} "Ow!"
- **Kibellah**
  - Before: {n}Kibellah carefully wraps her hand in a rag, cuts one of the leaves with her metal claws, and offers it to you.{/n} "Take caution, Domin. Living in the lower bays, one quickly learns not to touch things on a whim. I doubt we should do so in this place."
  - After: {n}Kibellah cuts you a leaf.{/n} "Careful, Domin. Don't touch things on a whim."
- **Solomorne**
  - Before: {n}Solomorne plucks a leaf with two iron fingers and holds it out to you.{/n} "Just this? Hmm, this thing looks nasty. It's a good thing I've made it my habit to touch any suspicious objects with only my augmented hand."
  - After: {n}Solomorne plucks a leaf.{/n} "Nasty. Good thing I use my augmented hand."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "You anticipate my thoughts, Rogue Trader. I was just about to remark that this specimen of flora is quite remarkable." {n}The Manipulus's alembic hisses, spraying an unknown compound onto the plant; its leaves wither even further under the mist, yet do not fully die. Looking thoroughly pleased, Eogunn cuts away a few stems, deftly working his manipulators.{/n}
  - After: "A remarkable specimen, Rogue Trader." {n}Eogunn's alembic mists it, then he cuts stems, pleased.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/ExplorationEvents/StryxShed/CursedBookBIte/CursedBookBite_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: [Burn the suspicious artefact]
  - After: [Burn the artefact]
- **Player**
  - Before: [Step well away from the tome]
  - After: [Step away from the tome]
- **Player**
  - Before: [Turn a few pages]
  - After: [Turn some pages]
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The weighty tome is bound in the skin of a human face, laced with a cord woven from tendons. A sinister crimson symbol dominates the cover, but it is difficult for you to make out. The details elude your scrutiny and the strokes twist and shift, furthering the confusion.{/n}
  - After: {n}A tome bound in a human face. Its crimson symbol shifts under your gaze.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The fiery tongues reluctantly lap away the taint of heresy from the book, their warm colours fading as they engulf the tome. The bloody symbol on the cover melts, and you hear a shriek so loud that the pain pierces your eardrums. The final flash reveals the heretical sigil in full, but only a moment later, you cannot recall what it looked like.{/n}
  - After: {n}It burns. The symbol melts with a piercing shriek; you glimpse the sigil, then forget it.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A hundred hands writhe under your skin, seeking to force their way through, some in and some out. Your eyeballs push at their lids and sizzle, ready to pop. You grit your teeth and remind yourself that all this is just an illusion conjured by the dark sorcery of the warp.{/n}
  - After: {n}Hands writhe beneath your skin; your eyes sizzle. You grit your teeth: warp illusion.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A hundred hands writhe under your skin, seeking to force their way through, some in and some out. Your eyeballs push at their lids and sizzle, ready to pop. You open your mouth to scream, instead spewing out a torrent of dark blood. The agony ends only when you lose consciousness...{/n}
  - After: {n}Hands writhe beneath your skin; your eyes sizzle. You vomit blood until you black out...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Touching the book makes your hands tingle and you feel a spell of dizziness coming on. The symbols on the pages rearrange themselves, vowing vicious torment, and the stretched face on the cover starts to resemble your own.{/n}
  - After: {n}Dizziness rises. The symbols promise torment; the cover's face becomes yours.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Feeling that nothing good can come of it, you slam the book shut.{/n}
  - After: {n}You slam the book shut.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}With every page, the pain in your body intensifies, and an ominous voice echoes in your head, whispering in an unknown dialect.{/n}
  - After: {n}Each page brings more pain and an ominous whisper.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The rustling builds and builds, culminating in a wild, undulating shriek. You feel your skull burst into a thousand bony splinters piercing every inch of your body. An insatiable desire to slash and maim fills your very being. The few moments of struggle feel like an eternity but end in your triumph. The delinquent writings that fill the tome faintly echo in your mind until finally, they fall silent.{/n}
  - After: {n}A shriek. Your skull seems to shatter; bloodlust fills you. You fight it off, and the whispers fade.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You walk away, struggling to suppress the urge to come back and glimpse under the cover.{/n}
  - After: {n}You walk away, resisting the urge to look.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}When you wake up, you still tremble at the memory of the suffering you have endured.{/n}
  - After: {n}You wake, still trembling.{/n}

## World/Dialogs/ExplorationEvents/StryxShed/GiveThemBack/GiveThemBack_dialogue

- **Player**
  - Before: "You may keep the stones, Yrliet."
  - After: "Keep the stones, Yrliet."
- **Player**
  - Before: "Marazhai, what do you need the stones for?"
  - After: "Marazhai, why do you want them?"
- **Player**
  - Before: "The stones are my prize. I am taking them."
  - After: "The stones are my prize."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "What?.." {n}Yrliet's face betrays her surprise. When she speaks, there is sadness in her words:{/n} "How could the spirit stones of my kin end up in such a gods-forsaken place? Elantach, please, allow me to watch over them."
  - After: "What?.." {n}Yrliet looks sad.{/n} "My kin's spirit stones? Elantach, let me keep them."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "I could perform a three-night ballad about the creation of the first stone, but alas, you do not have the luxury of eternity's favour. You should know what is important — the stones shield the spirits of the {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Children of Asuryan{/g} from the insatiable thirst of Sai'lanthresh after they die. They also enable the ancestors to share their wisdom, even sometimes lending us strength to fight our enemies."
  - After: "They shield the spirits of the {g|Encyclopedia:Asuryani}Children of Asuryan{/g} from Sai'lanthresh, and lend us ancestral wisdom."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Your words are like a breath of fresh air, elantach. I will take good care of them."
  - After: "Thank you, elantach."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "Or {name} can give them to me." {n}Marazhai's voice is dripping with dark hunger.{/n} "I will find for them a proper use."
  - After: "Or {name} gives them to me." {n}Marazhai sounds hungry.{/n}
- **Jae**
  - Before: "These smuggler wannabes were hardly aware of the true value of this treasure. If you ask me, shereen, these stones can be sold to a reliable and very rich collector at a profit. And when I say at a profit, I mean it."
  - After: "A rich collector would pay a fortune, shereen."
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "Someday you will trade your soul away for trifles. I just hope I will not be around when it happens."
  - After: "Someday you'll sell your soul for trifles."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: "Imagine you have a heart just ripped from your enemy's breast. It seems fragile and fluttering, but clutch it in your hand, and it will tear open the skin and plunge you into an ocean of sensation. It's a torment and ecstasy that make your blood boil and your soul burn in agony... Oh yes, I will find a good use for the useless spirits powering these stones."
  - After: "Like a torn-out heart in your fist — pure ecstasy. I'll use them."
- **Marazhai**
  - Before: {n}Marazhai's dark eyes light up with a malicious fire.{/n} "It will be my pleasure, {name}."
  - After: {n}Marazhai's eyes gleam.{/n} "My pleasure, {name}."
- **Jae**
  - Before: "I certainly do, shereen! You can be certain of it!"
  - After: "I certainly do, shereen!"
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "No!" {n}Yrliet showers you with a stream of Aeldari speech so fast the Elucidator cannot keep up. Exasperated, she turns away.{/n}
  - After: "No!" {n}Yrliet curses in Aeldari and turns away.{/n}
- **Yrliet**
  - Before: "How long do you intend to torment my kin? The elantach is no fool and {mf|he|she} will not indulge your malice and hatred!"
  - After: "Leave my kin be! The elantach is no fool; {mf|he|she} won't indulge you!"

## World/Dialogs/ExplorationEvents/StryxShed/StryxShedCogitator/StryxShedCogitator_dialogue

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A subdued rumbling comes from under the cover of the ancient cogitator, as if the machine spirits resent being awakened. After a few simple directions from the control panel, the vid-screen flashes to life and starts blinking, waiting for your input.{/n}
  - After: {n}The cogitator rumbles awake, awaiting input.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The mechanism lazily grinds its gears but grants you access to the requested information.{/n}
  - After: {n}Access granted.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Day twenty-one, third month of the cycle...
Now that's what I call good fortune! We hit the jackpot. This xenos peddler, a Stryxis, sure did show up in time, the competitors have been popping up like fleas on a half-dead rat. Merd'Kee has already brought a bunch of rare and exotic shit, and I have never been paid this much for a single order before. Life is good thanks to him (or her?), and is going to get even better!"
  - After: "Day 21, month 3...
Jackpot! Merd'Kee, a Stryxis peddler, brings rare goods. Best pay ever!"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Received: 6 crates of tech upgrades, 4 blocks of T'au firearms, 8 units of miscellaneous Drukhari devices.
Sold: 7 units of Aeldari devices, 5 Ork weapon crates, 3 units of T'au artefacts.
Awaiting delivery."
  - After: "In: 6 tech upgrades, 4 T'au firearms, 8 Drukhari devices.
Out: 7 Aeldari devices, 5 Ork weapons, 3 T'au artefacts."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A relay clicks inside the dusty machine.{/n}
  - After: {n}A relay clicks.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The whirring of the obsolete cogitator's mechanisms grows into a strained whine, and the crackling from the abandoned tracks abruptly stops.{/n}
  - After: {n}The tracks fall silent.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Received: 8 crates of Ork armour, 12 blocks of Drukhari blades, 10 units of Aeldari devices.
Sold: 8 units of Drukhari devices, 3 blocks of T'au firearms, 15 units of devices belonging to an unknown race.
Overhead Costs: disposal of bodies. Keeping an eye on Doe. I've got a bad feeling this won't be the last of it."
  - After: "In: 8 Ork armour, 12 Drukhari blades, 10 Aeldari devices.
Out: 8 Drukhari devices, 3 T'au firearms, 15 unknown devices.
Costs: body disposal. Watching Doe."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Received: 24 units of unidentified artefacts. Let them stay unidentified and in my room.
Sold: 18 units of Drukhari, Aeldari, and Ork firearms.
Stolen: ???
My own people are stealing from me now! What did that scoundrel Merd'Kee promise them? I'm going to find out, and there will be trouble."
  - After: "In: 24 unidentified artefacts.
Out: 18 xenos firearms.
Stolen: ???
My people steal! What did Merd'Kee promise them?"
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Day six of the ninth month of the cycle...
It is time to end this. The thrones are coming in faster than I can spend them, but I am starting to lose count of the people who died. Yesterday, I walked past a dozen of my people and couldn't recognise four. The customers are starting to ask why there's so much blood on the delivery crates.
Damned if I believe that crooked-ass xenos rat again! His deliveries are killing my guys, and there haven't even been any shootouts. Next time Merd'Kee comes here, he won't be leaving this place alive. I'll make sure of it."
  - After: "Day 6, month 9...
Thrones pour in, but my people keep dying. Blood on the crates. Merd'Kee's deliveries kill my guys. Next visit, he dies."

  - Before: {n}The High Factotum bows before you in servile deference.{/n} "Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship}, allow me to steal a few minutes of your precious time! I come to you on behalf of your lowly devotees, who have bestowed upon me the honour of paying you tribute."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Glorious tales of your majesty travel far and wide, not only across the decks of this vessel, but also throughout the protectorate. Your name instils enough fear and awe that people think twice before uttering it without reason... or they call on you in their most desperate prayers. Yes, Lord Captain, at times... your name is spoken instead of His among the commoners. Of course, there are also those who have long since honoured you as a messenger of the true gods."
  - After: "Your name inspires awe. Commoners pray to you instead of Him; some call you a messenger of the true gods."

  - After: "Your cultists sent an altar. It's hidden in your chambers. Will Your {mf|Lordship|Ladyship} see it?"

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As the ship makes its way through the star system, a strange fatigue falls over you. Your eyelids grow heavy, and the quill you have been using to draw up yet another order falls from your hand...{/n}
  - After: {n}A strange fatigue falls over you...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You raise your head with a start: someone else is here, in your study! You stand up and stare at the dozens upon dozens of corpses surrounding you. Among their number, you recognise the disfigured and bloodied faces of those who died on the ship's bridge and those you met in your previous life. How is this possible? Where are the enforcers posted to stand guard? It matters not: you are alone against a horde of heretics risen from the darkness to take your life!{/n}
  - After: {n}You wake among corpses: the dead of the bridge and your past life, risen against you!{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}As if of its own accord, the shard lying on the edge of the desk, the sole remnant of Kunrad Voigtvir's weapon, slips into your hand. The metal is searing cold. The dead sway from side to side, closing in around you in a nightmarishly slow advance.{/n}
  - After: {n}Kunrad Voigtvir's shard slips into your hand. The dead close in.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}A foreign presence rises up out of the deepest, darkest recesses of your mind. The cut on your hand burns like acid, and an alien consciousness in your head greets the pain with a discordant wave of barely intelligible voices.{/n}
  - After: {n}An alien presence stirs in your mind. Voices whisper.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The dead only draw closer, and closer, and... Your fingers involuntarily tighten around the shard, its sharp edge cutting into your palm.{/n}
  - After: {n}The dead draw closer. The shard cuts your palm.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}All you hear in response is unintelligible voices — whispers, moans, and derisive laughter... Anger ignites your chest, and you clutch the shard, which ravenously bites into your palm with its sharp edge.{/n}
  - After: {n}Mocking whispers answer. Angry, you clutch the shard; it cuts you.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The dead remain deaf to your words, creeping ever closer with the inevitability of death itself. You belatedly realise that your trembling hand has found the shard when its razor-sharp edge cuts into your palm...{/n}
  - After: {n}The dead creep closer. The shard cuts your trembling palm...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}An unbearably bright light floods everything around, and you find yourself surrounded by grovelling minions, their bodies shivering in your mere presence. Your hands no longer hold a pitiful shard, but a majestic and intricate weapon — a skilfully crafted sword with strange, unnerving proportions, a curved design, and an unusual hilt adorned with the image of a closed eye.{/n}
  - After: {n}Blinding light. Minions grovel. You hold a strange curved sword, its hilt bearing a closed eye.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The eye opens wide, revealing a gaze so ancient and dark that it steals your breath away. You have felt this gaze before — there, on the bridge... and the voice that appears in your mind only confirms your guess.{/n} "The tapestry is woven. The path is chosen. Accept your fate, champion."
  - After: {n}The eye opens. You felt this gaze on the bridge.{/n} "The tapestry is woven. Accept your fate, champion."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You feel the sword's immense weight pulling you down. You resist its will for a moment longer before collapsing to the ground to the sound of odious laughter. The strain is such that you fear your back could break at any moment.{/n}
  - After: {n}The sword's weight drags you down amid laughter.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Your body refuses to obey your mind. The handle feels as if it has become one with your hands, and the gaze of the daemonic eye sets your very soul ablaze.{/n} "Resisting your fate is futile." {n}You scream as you feel your soul burn away to ash...{/n}
  - After: {n}The hilt fuses to your hands.{/n} "Resisting your fate is futile." {n}Your soul burns...{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}One look at the weapon in your hands makes your very soul tremble — it is a weapon fit for the greatest chosen of the gods, the judge of fates, the tyrant of millions... In the whispers flooding your ears, you hear promises of strength, power, and triumph.{/n}
  - After: {n}A weapon for the gods' chosen. Whispers promise power.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}...you awaken from the vision kneeling next to your desk, clothes drenched in sweat and with a sour taste on your tongue. Your head is ringing, and you struggle to recall those faces and the image of the sword in your hands. Only the deep cut on your palm and the bloodied shard lying on the floor remind you of what just transpired.{/n}
  - After: {n}...you wake by your desk, sweat-drenched. Only your cut palm and the bloodied shard remain.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You reach your shaking hand out to the shard, now slippery with your blood. You wipe its metallic surface and stash your treasure under your clothes, next to your heart and soul forever seared by the great power of the warp.{/n}
  - After: {n}You hide the bloody shard by your heart.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "Vog, the First Dawn, is hereby woven into the tapestry of your fate. Seek the Second Dawn in the hands of she who rises above its future dominion. The former aspirant fell, and thus the new one will become the chosen of the Weaver of Destinies. Make mortals serve you as their god, and become the vessel of the Edge."
  - After: "Vog, the First Dawn, is woven into your fate. Seek the Second Dawn with she who rises above its future dominion. The former aspirant fell; you will be chosen of the Weaver of Destinies. Be a god to mortals, and the vessel of the Edge."

  - Before: {n}The voices fall quiet and then merge into one, ringing and hypnotising.{/n} "This galaxy is an ancient, forgotten battlefield, where the Prince's orphans once stood together against a mighty viceroy of the Realm of the Sorcerer, the embodiment of the Weaver's will in realspace: us. The sword's creators are no more and the sword itself, broken into shards, was lost to oblivion among the stars, where generations of my servants have searched for it. Until now."

- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: "The shards were reclaimed, one after another. The first, Vog, was found in the vastness of the Heathen Stars. The second, Haik, was extracted from the body of a planetoid, where the corpse emperor's lackeys, crawling in the dirt, unearthed it and heeded the whispers. Vog was entrusted to our last aspirant, and the servant named Aurora accepted Haik... but you intervened. You cut the threads of the tapestry by interrupting the aspirant's mission and destroying the prophet. The sword was once destined to be reforged... but the pattern has changed, and now you will become the vessel for the Edge's power."
  - After: "Vog came from the Heathen Stars, Haik from a planetoid. Our aspirant held Vog, Aurora Haik; you slew both. Now you are the Edge's vessel."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The voices burst into screeching laughter.{/n} "The Prince's orphans follow the same paths as the corpse emperor's lackeys — paths woven by the Weaver. The Edge foretold the Final Dawn, and so it came to be, though its makers knew nothing of its design."
  - After: {n}Laughter.{/n} "All walk the Weaver's paths. The Edge foretold the Final Dawn."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The heavy altar looks ancient and out of place in your chambers. Faint whispers surround you as you approach.{/n}
  - After: {n}An ancient altar. Whispers.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**

Let his hopes turn to dust." {n}The voices in your head die down for a moment.{/n} "The future fluctuates and changes. Its interpretation will only tarnish the pattern. Follow the destined path, and all will be revealed in time."
  - After: "Another fool thinks he can tame an ancient horror. Let his hopes turn to dust." {n}A pause.{/n} "Follow your path."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}The voices burst into nauseating laughter.{/n} "It is too late for you to hide behind the tattered curtain of lies. Fulfil your destiny. Find the Third Dawn. Complete... the pattern..."
  - After: {n}Laughter.{/n} "Too late for lies. Find the Third Dawn..."
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}You slowly start regaining clarity of mind. There is no trace of the wounds on your palms. The shards, however, have disappeared as well, which makes you wonder if they ever existed at all.{/n}
  - After: {n}Your mind clears. Wounds and shards are gone.{/n}
- **(conversation owner)**
  - Before: {n}Faint smoke rises from the altar, twisting into intricate shapes and silhouettes...{/n}
  - After: {n}Smoke twists up from the altar...{/n}

## World/Dialogs/TravelPrompts/Chapter2/PredecessorRiots_prompt/PredecessorRiots_prompt

  - After: "What's this about Lady Theodora?"

  - After: "Pacify the whole void shield crew. Those provoked are just as guilty."

So far, no one believes their mad tales, but unrest has begun at the fringes of the compartments. The ship's enforcers are ready to eliminate the instigating clan or pacify the entire void shield crew — the decision is yours."
